coverage: Crossref DOI-indexed metadata; prefix pagination status is reported and full ChemRxiv recall is not guaranteed.

papers.title: Ultrafast Non-Förster Energy Transfer in a DNA-Templated Cy3-Cy5 Assembly
papers.abstract: Controlling electronic coupling between chromophores is central to the design of photonic materials, yet energy transfer at sub nanometer donor-acceptor separations, where the point-dipole Förster approximation becomes unreliable, remains difficult to probe experimentally. Here, we use a doublestranded DNA scaffold to position a Cy3 donor and a Cy5 acceptor within a few ångströms of each other and characterize their energy transfer using steady-state and femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy, microsecond molecular dynamics and umbrella-sampling simulations, and TDDFT-based transition-charge (TrESP) coupling calculations. Absorption changes consistent with H-type heterodimer formation accompany a near-unity (0.96) energy-transfer efficiency, while Cy3 signal depletes and Cy5 signal rises within the ~200 fs instrument response. Simulations show that the Cy3 and Cy5 are moderately-to-strongly coupled in the vast majority of the thermal ensemble, leading to energy transfer lifetimes shorter than 150 fs, consistent with transient absorption measurements. These results establish DNA scaffolds as programmable platforms for accessing non-Förster energy-transfer regimes.

papers.title: Scalable Amidation Reaction by Resonant Acoustic Mixing. Application to the multi-gram scale synthesis of marketed Agrochemicals
papers.abstract: Industrial amide bond formation in agrochemical manufacture still relies on low-molecularweight chlorinating agents and dipolar aprotic solvents. Herein, five marketed SDHI fungicides, Fenfuram (1), Boscalid (2), Mepronil (3), Flutolanil (4) and Fluxapyroxad (5), were prepared by TCFH-mediated one-pot/two-step amidation across three mechanochemical platforms (VBM, PBM and LA-RAM). The optimal reaction environment proved platform-dependent: ball-milling favoured solid K2HPO4, whereas LA-RAM required liquid N-methylimidazole acting as both base and grinding liquid, and added grinding media (GA-RAM) lowered the yield through degradation of the activated acyl intermediate. LA-RAM was the most efficient and most readily scalable platform, delivering 1–5 in 67–99% yield on a 93 mmol scale (up to 34.9 g per batch, a 160-fold scale-up) at room temperature in 2.5 h at η ≤ 0.2 µL mg-1 of ethyl acetate, without re-optimisation. HR-PXRD and microED confirmed the crystalline forms for agrochemicals 2, 4 and 5, and gave the first structures of 1 and 3. DOZN™ 3.0 and CHEM21 assessments showed reduced waste, elimination of POCl3, oxalyl chloride, DMF and CH2Cl2, and PMI halved for 4 (24.5 vs 50.4).

papers.title: Diversity of N-terminal Sequences of Aβ Peptides Governs TDMQ20-Mediated CuII Extraction Efficiency and Kinetics
papers.abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is recognized as the most common form of dementia, with no curative therapies available. One of the current strategies towards an AD drug focuses on the development of copper-binding ligands capable of extracting CuII ions from β-amyloid (Aβ) peptides, among which TDMQ20 has attracted considerable attention. However, previous studies of TDMQ20 have focused primarily on its interaction with Aβ(1–x) peptides, with no consideration given to the molecular heterogeneity of Aβ species present in the AD brain. In this work, we investigated the impact of two biologically relevant N-terminal truncations (4-x) and (5-x) on the formation of the CuIITDMQ20 complex, guided by their known avidity to bind CuII ions. These sequences were represented by water-soluble-(non-aggregating) Aβ(4–16) and Aβ(5–16) peptides. We also reevaluated the CuII-binding properties of TDMQ20 and its interaction with the standard CuIIAβ(1–16) complex. Using stopped-flow kinetics, we confirmed the immediate and complete extraction of CuII ion from CuIIAβ(1–16) complex in the presence of equimolar TDMQ20. Importantly, however, CuIIAβ(4–16) and CuIIAβ(5–16) exhibited marked resistance to TDMQ20-mediated demetallation, revealing strong dependence of CuII extraction on the Aβ sequence. These findings suggest that the heterogeneity of Aβ species in AD-affected brains can be an important factor determining the efficacy of CuII-targeting therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Fine-Tuning a Graph-Transformer ADMET Model Improves Half-Life and Plasma Protein Binding Concordance
papers.abstract: Absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET) models are usually judged on predefined benchmark splits. Those splits are useful, but they do not show whether a model reproduces the pharmacokinetic (PK) numbers that are actually reported for individual drugs. Here we compared ADMET-AI with a fine-tuned NV-KERMT-70M-v2 model (“KERMT”) on the same Therapeutics Data Commons (TDC)-aligned endpoint definitions. KERMT was fine-tuned in two stages: a protocol check on the ChEMBL multitask (ChEMBL-MT) data set, then TDC-aligned regression and classification fine-tuning on merged ChEMBL, Biogen, ExpansionRx/OpenADMET and TDC data. Two retrospective literature comparisons were run. The first used a curated 25-drug oncology panel: for half-life (n = 17) KERMT cut mean absolute error (MAE) from 46.81 to 16.83 h (paired Wilcoxon p = 0.0046, Holm-adjusted p = 0.0139, closer for 13 of 17 drugs); volume of distribution at steady state (VDss, n = 12) and hepatocyte clearance (n = 17) showed no statistically supported difference. The second, reported here for the first time, is an expanded three-way comparison of 53 oncology drugs × 3 endpoints (159 drug-endpoint rows) against curated literature and label values. On the 48 drugs with a usable half-life reference, KERMT more than halved the error (MAE 19.43 vs 43.38 h; median absolute error 12.01 vs 35.30 h; geometric mean fold error, GMFE, 2.72 vs 3.69; within 2-fold 41.0% vs 25.0%), was closer for 34 of 48 drugs (70.8%; 95% confidence interval, CI, 55.9-83.0%), and the paired Wilcoxon test was significant (p = 0.0002; Holm-adjusted p = 0.0004). The advantage persisted after each model's systematic bias was removed (p = 0.0004), so it is not a simple scale offset: ADMET-AI over-predicted half-life for 35 of 48 drugs (mean bias +29.20 h) whereas KERMT was mildly conservative (-13.79 h). For plasma protein binding ratio (PPBR, n = 21) KERMT had lower MAE (7.05 vs 9.44 percentage points) and the only statistically significant rank agreement with literature seen anywhere in this study (Spearman ρ = 0.540, p = 0.012, vs 0.400, p = 0.073), but the paired error difference was not significant (p = 0.157). One endpoint failed outright and we state it plainly: KERMT VDss predictions collapsed to near-baseline behaviour. They occupied a narrow band (46 of 53 drugs between 0 and 10 L/kg; standard deviation 3.64 vs 6.71 L/kg for ADMET-AI), no drug in the panel had an assay-matched VDss reference, and on the six drugs with an approximate reference the per-drug KERMT predictions (MAE 2.18 L/kg) were no better than replacing the entire model with one constant (MAE 2.14 L/kg) and worse than a no-information baseline (1.71 L/kg). KERMT VDss output should therefore not be used. A deliberately strict control bounds the positive findings as well: against a structure-blind constant predictor built by leave-one-out from the reference values, KERMT was statistically indistinguishable on both endpoints (half-life MAE 19.43 vs 16.07 h, p = 0.051; PPBR 7.05 vs 7.24 percentage points, p = 0.812), while ADMET-AI was significantly worse than that constant for half-life (p < 0.0001). We therefore make no claim of accurate numerical point prediction; the supported claims are that fine-tuning removes ADMET-AI's large systematic half-life error and that the PPBR rank correlation is compound-specific signal a constant cannot possess. Physically impossible values occurred in 16 of 159 KERMT rows and 21 of 159 ADMET-AI rows. Across 30 classification endpoints, mean inter-model Pearson correlation was 0.711 and mean binary agreement at 0.5 was 89%, which measures similarity, not accuracy. This version does not yet include official Therapeutics Data Commons benchmark-group evaluation of the fine-tuned models, replicate training seeds, or a training-set overlap audit; those gaps are declared explicitly rather than left implicit. The overall conclusion is endpoint-specific: fine-tuned KERMT is a materially better-calibrated half-life and plasma-protein-binding predictor than ADMET-AI on this panel, it is not yet a demonstrated ranking model for half-life, and its VDss head is unusable.

papers.title: In-silico investigation of small molecule inhibitors of malaria-inducing cycloguanil-resistant Plasmodium falciparum dihydrofolate reductase
papers.abstract: Plasmodium falciparum dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) is the target of antimalarial drugs such as cycloguanil. However, mutations of DHFR, particularly the A16V and S108T variants, induce steric interactions that confer resistance to cycloguanil. It is crucial to find new therapeutics to combat cycloguanil-resistant strains of P. falciparum . We used in-silico methods to investigate possible drug candidates of A16V+S108T DHFR, a key cycloguanil-resistant double mutant. Using a large chemical library, we performed structure-based virtual screening to discover novel small molecule inhibitors of mutant DHFR. Molecular dynamics simulations show that the top-ranked compound from virtual screening, ligand 4, retains a stable binding pose. MM-GBSA calculations rank ligand 4 above cycloguanil and three other known DHFR inhibitors. Through these simulations, we identify a small molecule compound possessing more favorable binding free energies to DHFR than those of cycloguanil.

papers.title: Photoluminescent Ratiometric and Lifetime Thermometry Governed by Water Dynamics in Heterometallic M(s-block)-Ce(III) Tricyanomethanide-Based Coordination Polymers
papers.abstract: It is important to develop novel optical materials combining effective photoluminescence (PL) with a highly sensitive optical response to external stimuli. Cerium(III) complexes, whose efficient luminescence, ascribable to the d-f electronic transitions, is modulated by the coordination environment, are promising in this context. Here, experimental and theoretical studies on achieving the combination of a high room-temperature (RT) visible emission quantum yield (QY) of up to 0.94 (370 nm excitation) with the ratiometric optical thermometry of a relative thermal sensitivity reaching 9.2% K−1 above RT are reported. This was realized by linking Ce(III) centers with anionic tricyanomethanide ligands and s-block metal ions into rigid coordination polymers of the general formula of {AICeIII[C(CN)3]4(H2O)} (ACe, A = Na, K, Rb). They exhibit blue PL of dual ligand–Ce(III) origin, with the chromaticity and QY tuned by alkali metals. Moreover, they reveal strong temperature dependence of optical characteristics, including PL lifetime, which was correlated with thermally activated vibrations of coordinated aqua ligands, as was depicted by the H-to-D exchange and distinct dielectric relaxation processes. This water dynamics influencing PL was utilized for optical sensing of temperature, which was explored through ratiometric and lifetime-based approaches with particularly good performance in the around-and-above RT region.

papers.title: pKasso: Accurate and accessible prediction of small-molecule protonation states
papers.abstract: The protonation states of molecules are tightly linked to their physicochemical properties. Accurately predicting protonation states is therefore important for applications such as docking-based virtual screening in drug discovery. Modern machine-learning models can predict molecular p K a values with good accuracy, but obtaining pH-dependent protonation-state ensembles from available open-source models can cause substantial installation and workflow overhead. Commercial tools provide convenient alternatives but can entail substantial licensing costs. We here present pKasso, an accurate, fast, accessible, extensible, and easy-to-use open-source package to compute pH-dependent protonation-state ensembles of small molecules. pKasso enumerates relevant protonation microstates, integrates the existing p K a -prediction models MolGpKa and Uni-pKa, and converts their predictions into microstate populations and macroscopic p K a values. In addition, pKasso can combine predictions from multiple p K a -prediction models and report their disagreement as a qualitative indicator of predictive uncertainty. We evaluate pKasso on six benchmark datasets, where it achieves prediction accuracy competitive with state-of-the-art models. pKasso supports single-molecule and batch workflows. It is available as a web server ( tools.bindresearch.org/pkasso ), a Python library (pip install pkasso), and a command-line interface ( github.com/bindresearch/pkasso ).

papers.title: When Can a Molecular-Dynamics Simulation Stop?
papers.abstract: Molecular-dynamics (MD) simulations are usually run for a prespecified duration, even when the goal is to estimate an equilibrium observable to a stated precision. Stopping as soon as an estimated uncertainty becomes small enough is attractive, but repeated inspection invalidates uncertainty statements calibrated for a fixed time. We formulate data-dependent stopping as an inferential problem with an explicit precision target and a simultaneous-in-time coverage requirement, and organise it into four gated stages: temporal prediction against strong baselines, uncertainty calibration, an anytime-valid stopping rule, and measured high-performancecomputing (HPC) savings. We report exploratory first-stage results on four incrementally assembled ATLAS cohorts, using sequence-grouped cross-validation and a target computed only from frames after a 20 ns prefix. In the largest cohort (757 systems, 1,243 replicas, 689 sequence groups), ridge regression on 48 prefix summaries and a residual gated recurrent unit (GRU) both reduced RMSD mean absolute error relative to last-value persistence (0.610 and 0.636 versus 0.673 Å; paired bootstrap intervals excluding zero), whereas the GRU–ridge difference was not significant in any cohort. A genuine structure-only baseline, a compatible mdCATH analysis, sequential coverage and HPC cost measurements are still outstanding, so no stopping policy or computational saving is claimed.

papers.title: Mixed-Valence Chemistry without Fractional Electrons in Variational 2-Electron Reduced Density Matrix Theory via Local Integer-Charge Constraints
papers.abstract: The tractable capture of strong, or multi-reference correlation effects continues to present a formidable challenge at the forefront of quantum chemistry. Variational two-electron reduced density matrix (v2RDM) theory presents a polynomially scaling approach to multi-reference calculations, but its use of approximate N-representability conditions yields lower bounds to the true energy and possibly unphysical descriptions. We demonstrate that in mixed-valence transition-metal clusters ([Fe2S2], [Fe3S4], [Co2S2], [Ni2S2]) the common 2-and 3-particle N-representability conditions allow for charge-delocalization error, which affects the ability of v2RDM to both qualitatively and quantitatively describe their properties and redox chemistry, as redox-active electrons may be spuriously spread over multiple metal centers. Here, we introduce local integer-charge constraints that enforce the exact lower bound on the charge variance of metal-centered orbital subspaces and which may be imposed at minimal additional cost. We demonstrate that these constraints remove 22 to 89% of the energy error and 52 to 95% of the error in the metal d-electron populations, resulting in significant improvements to calculated ionization energies.

papers.title: Unlocking the promise of materials AI through application proxies and protected collaboration
papers.abstract: AI-guided and robotic laboratories can accelerate experiments within a company, but materials development still depends on repeated testing across company boundaries. Here we show in controlled simulation how investment in application-relevant private testing reduces that external work. We extend Minimum Knowledge Collaboration with application proxies, calling the extension MKC2. Suppliers develop combinations of physical tests and reference assemblies that capture how their materials respond under relevant product conditions. They train private models on the resulting curves and features, and the product integrator calibrates joint predictions against complete-product tests. Bidirectional MKC messages connect private material selection to the product requirements while raw curves and model parameters remain local. In sixteen paired two-company programs, 72 additional private training curves per program accompany a 93% reduction in subsequent product testing at a target of 90% of the best available combination. Target attainment rises from twelve to all sixteen programs within the fixed test horizon. Including the shared initial product campaign gives a 39% reduction. Matched two- and four-company studies and a reference-training sensitivity study examine the same exchange under prescribed physical response families. The benefit depends on developing informative tests, training useful predictions and acting on them in collaboration. AI and robotics can make the private investment faster. MKC2 connects that application learning to fewer tests across company boundaries.

papers.title: A Graphene Oxide–Coco Pith Fiber–Polyvinyl Alcohol Non-Structural Composite Filter for Lead [Pb(II)] Removal from Aqueous Solution: A Proof-of-Concept Study
papers.abstract: Lead [Pb(II)] in drinking water is a persistent health risk, and low-cost filter media are of interest where centralised treatment is limited. This preliminary proof-of-concept study prepared a filter body from graphene oxide (GO), coco pith fiber and boric-acid-treated polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and tested it once with a nominal 50 mg/L Pb(II) solution under gravity filtration. GO was made by a modified Hummers' method and examined by FTIR only; the composite itself was not characterized. The filtrate was analyzed by flame atomic absorption spectroscopy. The retained reading (0.0054 absorbance units) equalled the reagent blank and lay below the lowest calibration standard (5 mg/L), giving an apparent residual of 0.53 mg/L (apparent removal 98.9%). Because this is at the blank level, the residual could not be quantified; the data support only a residual below 5 mg/L (removal above 90%). Filtered volume, flow rate and pH were not recorded, and no controls, adsorption-parameter studies, replicates or reusability tests were performed. The results are indicative only and define the experiments needed to assess this material.

papers.title: Coupled Condensation–Melting Heat Transfer and Thermal Design Limits of a Steam-Assisted Pipeline Cleaning Crawler: A Probabilistic Modeling Study
papers.abstract: Steam-assisted pipeline cleaning couples condensation heat transfer, melting of a deposit and a thermally protected tool, and the coupling, not any single component, sets its limits. We study a motorized steam-assisted crawler with a probabilistic model: transient conduction through an aluminum–aerogel–titanium wall into a lumped battery pack, film condensation, a melt model with a retained liquid film whose resistance is the dimensionless group Pif=hs/kl, a dynamic film balancing melt production and gravity drainage, an orifice model of the bypass relief, and a steam budget. The conduction and melt formulas are benchmarked against an independent solver 2 and the Neumann solution; no experiment was available for the coupled model. Under assumed input distributions, with 40 mm of aerogel the pack stays at or below 55 °C for 45 min in 98.9% of draws at 25 °C but 22% at 45 °C. The median range per deployment is 138 m if molten deposit leaves at once, 18 m with the dynamic film (0.35 mm) and 2 m with none removed; Sobol indices attribute 55% of the range variance to the film. The condensation correlation changes the instant-removal range by 25%, a Class 150 steam limit of 195 °C by 3%. A 1 km line needs a median of 57 deployments with the dynamic film (8 with instant removal), and the hull does not fit pipes below 8 in. These are model probabilities, not field reliabilities.

papers.title: Pairing manure and lignocellulosic biochars to reduce phosphorus losses from manure fertilisers
papers.abstract: Manures supply less nitrogen relative to phosphorus than crops require, so applying them to meet N demand accumulates P in soils and increases losses to water. Pyrolysis reduces the solubility of manure P, but the fraction that remains soluble is still vulnerable to runoff. This study tested whether lignocellulosic biochars applied alongside manure biochars can recapture that fraction. Poultry litter and dairy slurry were pyrolysed at 300, 500, and 700 °C, and their release of phosphate, ammonium, and nitrate was measured in 30-day batch incubations and in packed beds. Their leachates were incubated for 28 days with cocoa pod and coconut shell biochars produced at the same temperatures. Pyrolysis reduced soluble N release to at most 0.57 mg N/g, and phosphate release fell with peak temperature. Recapture by high-ash cocoa pod biochars rose with peak temperature, while low-ash coconut shell biochars released more phosphate to the leachate as temperature rose. Only cocoa pod biochar produced at 700 °C recaptured net phosphate, removing 0.71 mg P/g from poultry litter biochar leachate, most likely by precipitation, and neither lignocellulosic biochar captured substantial nitrate. A working system must combine a low-temperature manure biochar with a high-temperature, high-ash lignocellulosic biochar, here at a mass ratio of approximately 4:1 for a total application rate of 5 t/ha for winter wheat, costing 30–76 times more than mineral P fertiliser. The strategy’s added value lies in reducing nutrient losses and pollution, alongside biochar’s sterility, sustainability, and contribution to nutrient use efficiency via moisture and microbial communities.

papers.title: Self-Assembled Chiral Lipid Phases for Passive RNA Capture
papers.abstract: Sealed lipid vesicles provide useful models for compartmentalization, but their bilayer boundaries limit post-assembly uptake of hydrated macromolecules such as RNA. Here, we demonstrate that short-chain monoacylglycerides form assemblies that take up RNA. Glycerol monodecanoate (GMD) and glycerol monononanoate (GMN) spontaneously organize in water into sponge phases (L3) with interconnected aqueous channels. RNA uptake into these preformed assemblies is accompanied by restructuring toward vesicular morphologies, suggesting a pathway in which RNA enters through open aqueous channels and becomes retained during and after membrane reorganization. GMD assemblies preferentially retain RNA oligonucleotides over the mononucleotide adenosine monophosphate (AMP). Crucially, lipid stereochemistry (R, S and rac) differentially affects the response of the sponge assemblies to RNA, with R-GMD maintaining higher RNA association over time in comparison to S- and rac-GMD. These findings show how molecular chirality can propagate into self-assembled noncovalent systems providing selectivity for RNA retention.

papers.title: Intrinsic and Extrinsic Factors Governing CO Electro-Oxidation Pathways at Low Potentials on Platinum Single Crystal Electrodes
papers.abstract: CO electro-oxidation on Pt is often interpreted primarily in terms of surface structure and CO coverage, yet the origin of the electro-oxidation processes preceding the main stripping peak remains unresolved. Here, we show that CO pre-oxidation is governed by the coupled effects of Pt surface structure, CO adlayer preparation, and the evolving electrostatic state of the Pt/CO-electrolyte interface. Using Pt single-crystal electrodes spanning the stereographic triangle and different CO adlayer preparation protocols, we demonstrate that long-range structural order in the Pt substrate is the only common structural requirement identified for CO pre-oxidation. The specific conditions under which the process occurs, however, depend strongly on surface orientation. Under potential-controlled CO adsorption, dissolved CO is required for pre-oxidation on Pt(111)-type surfaces but not on Pt(100)-type surfaces. Surface defects do not universally promote pre-oxidation: they inhibit pre-oxidation on Pt(100)-type surfaces and enhance it only on Pt(111)-type surfaces for specific terrace-step configurations when CO is adsorbed at sufficiently low potentials. Their principal role is therefore to modify the reactivity of neighboring terrace domains rather than to act as general active centers. On Pt(111)-type surfaces, the regions made electrochemically accessible during pre-oxidation correspond to extended (111) terraces. Partial electro-oxidation of the CO adlayer also induces structure-dependent relaxation of the remaining adlayer. Most importantly, stepwise CO stripping reveals contrasting coverage-dependent kinetic responses for CO pre-oxidation and the main oxidation process. We attribute this kinetic decoupling to competition between the positive feedback associated with the creation of vacant Pt sites and an opposing electrostatic constraint imposed by the negatively charged CO-covered interface, which likely limits the formation of reactive water-derived species required for CO electro-oxidation. The resulting picture identifies CO pre-oxidation as a collective interfacial phenomenon in which surface structure, adlayer organization, and interfacial electrostatics evolve together as CO is consumed.

papers.title: Molecular Design of Non-Fluorinated Aryl-Extended Carbazole-Based Polymeric Membranes for Anion Exchange and Bipolar Membrane Water Electrolysis
papers.abstract: The development of durable anion-exchange membranes (AEMs) that combine rapid hydroxide transport with restrained hydration and dimensional stability remains a central challenge for alkaline electrochemical technologies. Here, we synthesize a series of ether-free, arylexpanded carbazole-based AEMs bearing systematically varied N-alkyl substituents: N-ethyl (HCz-Et), N-butyl (HCz-Bu), and N-hexyl (HCz-Hex). This systematic modification allows us to investigate how N-alkyl substitution within a common aromatic framework affects the physical, chemical, and mechanical properties of the resulting AEMs. Within this aryl-expanded series, increasing the N-alkyl chain length progressively suppressed water uptake and dimensional expansion while maintaining high hydroxide conductivity at elevated temperature. Specifically, HCz-Hex exhibited a water uptake of 18.7% and swelling ratio of 4.2%, with an OH − conductivity of 178mS cm −1 at 80 ◦C, indicating that this architecture can sustain efficient ion transport with limited membrane swelling. Furthermore, HCz-Hex retained ≈ 91% of its initial ion-exchange capacity (IEC) after 1000 h in 1M KOH at 80 ◦C. This balance of hydration control, conductivity, and alkaline stability translates directly to device performance: HCz-Hex reaches ≈ 2.05V at 2.0A cm −2 in pure-water-fed AEM electrolysis at 70 ◦C and 6A cm −2 at ≈ 2.19V in 1M KOH at 55 ◦C, while sustaining operation at 1.0A cm −2 for ≈ 1000 h. Beyond AEM electrolysis, coupling HCz-Hex with the non-fluorinated cation-exchange polymer SPEEK produces a fully non-fluorinated, Nafion-free bipolar membrane (BPM), enabling BPM water electrolysis at ≈ 2.03V at 1.0A cm −2 with a reported water-dissociation overpotential of approximately 80mV. This study provides a basis for designing non-fluorinated AEMs with tailored membrane properties for high-performance AEM and BPM electrolysis.

papers.title: TEBench: a source-labelled thermoelectric data collection with leakage-safe splits and baselines for machine learning
papers.abstract: Machine-learning thermoelectric scores are difficult to compare when source provenance and split groups differ. TEBench organises Starrydata Experiment-labelled curves (30,530 samples, 1,648,315 points, 6,045 papers), a JARVIS-DFT extract (23,558 structures) and an audited bulk Bi2Te3 workbook (740 records, 151 DOIs) as separate domains. DFT and experiment are never pooled. Canonical composition keys, paper/family/formula grouping and an eight-paper own-data hold-out support leakage review. The original Bi2Te3 Seebeck random forest reaches test R2 = 0.935 but own-paper R2 = −1.21. A κ-specific physical screening rule retains 257,647 Starrydata points before composition parsing and split joining; the rerun gives test R2 = 0.045 (random forest) and 0.232 (gradient boosting). Validation-selected CPU gradient boosting and structure-derived JARVIS tabular features are evaluated beside preserved random-forest references. Composition-to-JID candidate matches are explicitly distinguished from unique structure identity. Extract hashes and transport-unit limitations are documented. These are proposed tasks and transparent baseline comparisons, not a released benchmark or a claim of state-of-the-art prediction.

papers.title: Aromaticity, Electron Delocalization and Pauli Repulsion Explain Singlet and Triplet Energies in π-Systems Containing the Amide Moiety
papers.abstract: Aromaticity has proven an invaluable principle for designing molecular singlet-fission chromophores. However, to effectively leverage aromaticity as part of a series of rational design principles, it is important to understand the interplay between aromaticity, electron delocalization, and singlet and triplet state energies. Here we report a multi-dimensional analysis of the relationship between aromaticity, electron-delocalization, and singlet/triplet state energies in a series of 114 amide-containing π-conjugated fused-ring systems. We show that E(S1) largely depends on the size of the π-system and the local (anti)aromatic character of each of its constituent rings. However, across the entire dataset, calculated E(T1) is less clearly correlated with any of our predictive metrics. In molecules with fewer than four linearly fused rings, E(T1) is correlated with the ground state’s IFDI (inter-fragment delocalization index), a measure of long-range electronic communication. In larger chromophores, this effect is less pronounced, reflecting the more delocalized triplet spin density and thus lower Pauli repulsion. We propose that the rational design of chromophores with narrow singlet-triplet gaps based on aromaticity rules should aim to tune E(S1) using π-system size and local (anti)aromaticity, and E(T1) by manipulating triplet aromaticity to minimize Pauli repulsion. [190/200]

papers.title: GauMon: A Standalone, Cycle-Resolved Monitor for Gaussian Electronic-Structure Calculations
papers.abstract: Electronic structure calculations can produce large and complex log files. Information such as self-consistent field (SCF) convergence, geometry optimization, numerical algorithms, and irregular termination can be found throughout the calculation. GauMon ( https://github.com/devashishdas/GauMon ) is an open-source Python desktop GUI application that monitors Gaussian calculation logs in real-time or allows examination of an existing log file. The software parses log files incrementally to monitor the state of a calculation. Features include numerical summaries, measurements of geometry change, Gaussian links, diagnostics based on the source of failure, and the option for a per-cycle breakdown. Separate windows for each type of calculation allow SCF cycles, quadratic-convergence linear-equation sub-calculations, and harmonic vibration analysis to be monitored. The software can launch a Gaussian executable and attach to the process. It can also be attached to existing or previous calculation processes in a read-only fashion. The Qt native GUI and PyQtGraph plotting require no browser or GPU. The code was tested with dummy input and output, regression testing, and three Gaussian logs provided. The parser was able to extract 19 SCF procedures from an optimization of a water cluster log, 19 incomplete SCF cycles from another calculation, and 5 linear solutions (4 converged and 1 incomplete) from the Fe-S example. This is just to confirm that the parser works and does not indicate any chemical accuracy or speed increases. GauMon provides a focused way to examine lengthy Gaussian calculations with clear indicators of uncertainties in the process, an estimate of the time remaining, and incomplete data.

papers.title: Quantifying the Effectiveness of Independent Manual-Valve Verification in Preventing Product-Transfer Risks: A Monte Carlo Process-Safety Assessment
papers.abstract: Manual valve line-ups before product transfers rely on rounds, radio confirmation and checklists, none of which observes valve position independently. We ask when an additional layer of temporary clamp-on position sensors on existing manual valves reduces transfer risk, and when alarm fatigue, bypass, common-cause failures and incomplete coverage remove the benefit. A Monte Carlo model of the line-up task, verified against closed-form results, an independent analytic model and automated tests, gave with assumed inputs for a 14-valve route an undetected-error probability per transfer of 4.03% with existing checks and 0.29% with direct 2 sensing and NFC identity (14-fold; sampling interval 13.6–14.3), assuming that operators always act on alarms. Varying 13 inputs gave a median reduction of 9.7 (5th–95th percentile 4.4–28); adding uncertain operator response, alarm fatigue and common-cause failures of the sensing layer gave 2.5 (0.9–4.8), with response the strongest driver. A mean response time of 10 min against 20 min available gave a factor of approximately 2. A factor of 10 required a response of at least 97%, bypass below 53% and common-cause probability below 2.3%. An illustrative event tree gave a 14-fold reduction in expected loss. Clustering of validations by valve cut the power of a 1000-validation pilot from 95% to 50%. Inputs, consequence probabilities and losses are assumed: the results are conditional, not credited risk reduction.

papers.title: A Hidden Silver Oxide Layer Rewrites Molecular Fingerprinting in Surface-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Gold (Au) and silver (Ag) are considered as interchangeable plasmonic components based on the implicit assumption that freshly prepared Ag nanomaterials remain metallic. However, we show, using in-situ surfaceaccessible SERS, that a sub-nanometer AgOx layer forms ubiquitously and instantaneously on colloidal Ag nanoparticles, and that this layer fundamentally alters our picture of how molecules interact with silver surfaces. Unlike the welldocumented long-term oxidation that slowly degrades Ag over weeks, this layer is an intrinsic property of a wide range of freshly prepared Ag nanomaterials and persists even in biological environments. This establishes the oxidationmodulated-adsorption (OMA) effect as a tunable parameter and rational basis for material selection in plasmonic technologies. We show that OMA can be quantified via the standard deviation of relative enhancement (𝜎𝑅𝐸) in SERS. Using SERS sensing as a representative application, we demonstrate that OMA causes the same molecule to yield distinct spectral fingerprints on Ag versus Au, and that harnessing OMA improves detection sensitivity by 500-fold, pushes clinically relevant concentrations into reach, and restores machine-learning classification from random chance to perfection. More generally, recognizing the OMA effect not only rewrites the underlying logic for designing plasmonic materials but also implies that the surface chemistry-related mechanisms in previously reported plasmonic technologies should be carefully re-examined.

papers.title: Molecular thermal motion harvester for electricity conversion via contact electrification: Role and effect of design and additives
papers.abstract: Converting the molecular thermal energy to electric energy via liquid-solid interfacial contact electrification was experimentally validated and it presents a promising approach towards a new type of green energy technology. In this work, nylon 66 and polystyrene layers coated on copper foils were employed as positive and negative electrodes, to investigate the effect of electrolytes, saccharides, and surfactants, as additives to water. This study aims to improve device performance and establish some basic design principles for molecular thermal energy conversion systems. Meanwhile, a series of experiments were carried out to investigate the influences of key structural components on the electric output of the device, intending to help refine the design concepts and to gain a better understanding of the working mechanisms. Our work revealed that the electric output of water was significantly enhanced after adding 5% Na 2 CO 3 . This study also attempts to develop new ideas to further enhance the electricity output of molecular thermal motion harvester.

papers.title: BindCraft2 versus RFD4-Proteina for de novo peptide binder design against insecticide targets
papers.abstract: De novo peptide binders are attractive leads for biological pesticides because they can be designed against validated insecticide targets without a small-molecule discovery campaign. Two generative pipelines dominate this space: BindCraft2, an AlphaFold2/ProteinMPNN campaign that accepts designs only after a cascade of structural filters, and RFD4-Proteina, a flow-matching foundation model that generates conditioned backbones and sequences in a single pass. We benchmarked both on three insecticide targets: acetylcholinesterase (PDB 1QON, 540 residues), the ecdysone receptor ligand-binding domain (1R1K, 236 residues) and the ryanodine receptor SPRY2 domain (6KIM, 169 residues). Every design was re-folded with the same AlphaFold2 oracle. RFD4 returned 300 designs in 3.3 GPU-hours, 82 of which passed a common re-folding screen. BindCraft2 returned 10 designs in 58.7 GPU-hours, none on two of the three targets, and 3 of its 10 passed the same screen. The advantage of RFD4 was entirely concentrated on the smallest, contiguous target: there it delivered 82 usable designs in 0.32 GPU-hours, against 3 in 1.95 GPU-hours from BindCraft2. On the two larger targets RFD4 complexes looked bound in the generated coordinates but did not survive re-folding, and BindCraft2 accepted nothing. Generation speed and re-foldable interface quality therefore separated on this target set: RFD4 is the more cost-effective generator, but neither method produced validated binders on two of the three targets.

papers.title: Alchemical Free Energy Methods Reproduce Scaffold Modifications in a Macrocyclic Peptide PCSK9 Series
papers.abstract: Free energy perturbation (FEP) methods are widely used in drug discovery campaigns to optimise the binding affinity of small molecule ligands. Recently, macrocyclic peptides have emerged as an increasingly attractive modality alongside small molecules and biologics. They possess the unique ability to bind to large, flat, and featureless binding sites that are inaccessible to small molecules, while offering a route to oral bioavailability, which antibodies lack. However, modelling macrocycles with FEP presents significant challenges. These campaigns frequently involve complex scaffold changes that extend beyond traditional R-group modifications and often utilise both canonical and non-canonical amino acids, necessitating specialised parameterisation protocols to handle this diverse chemical space. In this work, we address these challenges by benchmarking against the comprehensive structure activity campaign of Tucker et al. [1], which details the development of novel macrocyclic peptide inhibitors targeting PCSK9. We present open-source relative binding free energy (RBFE) protocols and methodological strategies for the range of transformations required by this series, spanning buried backbone N-methylation, olefin transformations, ring-breaking, and changes in net charge. Furthermore, we automatically parameterise these chemically diverse inhibitors using the OpenFF force fields and graph neural network partial charges. We compare three analysis protocols that differ in how equilibration and correlated sampling are treated, and report performance both edgewise and after maximum-likelihood estimation of absolute free energies. Under the most rigorous of these, in which equilibration is detected automatically, the campaign is recovered with an edgewise RMSE of 0.93 kcal mol−1 (95% CI 0.74–1.10 kcal mol−1). Reaching compound 35, the most potent compound considered here, requires five consecutive perturbations, each exercising a distinct modelling challenge and each falling well outside conventional R-group substitution. Every edge along this path is reproduced to within 1.39 kcal mol−1. Overall, this work broadens the applicability of FEP methods in drug discovery while also identifying their current limits.

papers.title: Emergence of Atomic Energy States: Predicting Ionization Energies of One-Electron Systems via Nucleus-Driven Force Propagation in Real Space
papers.abstract: Although probabilistic electron wave-function approaches provide solid mechanistic insights for molecules, their inherent reliance on static, boundary-dependent approximations limits the direct description of real-space molecular dynamics. This study demonstrates the emergence of highly accurate atomic energy states by a single nucleus-driven force-propagating framework within an open system.When compared withNIST ionization energy dataforone-electron systems,our model yields a 0.0000% relative error for the hydrogen atom (Z = 1), where the energy spectrum naturally emerges from the nucleus as wave maximum peaks in real space. Furthermore, by relying solely on the atomic number (Z) as an independent variable alongside fixed global parameters, the model autonomously generates macroscopic energy values across various elements,maintaining relative errors of less than 1% up to Pr (Z = 59) and remaining even for massive nuclei such as Au (1.88%) and Rn (2.59%), with relative errors quite low at 1.88% and 2.59%, respectively. These highly accurate predictions are achieved through the Causal Recording (CR) framework, which tracks the irreversible and continuous propagation of classical nuclear forces. Comparisons with the emergentLagrangianpathconfirmedthatmacroscopictrajectoriesandwavebehaviors autonomously emerge from the collective accumulation oflocalforce events.Ultimately,these results successfully confirm that intra-atomic electron behavior can be described by the classical force of the nucleus in real space.

papers.title: TRIDENT: Three-Lever Privileged Self-Distillation for Audio-Visual Source Separation in Flow-Chemistry Pilot Plants
papers.abstract: Its weakness is that one fume-hood bay runs several unit operations at once, so the pump, the switching valve, the gas bubbler and the agitator arrive as a single mixed channel; the loudest of them owns most of the acoustic energy, and the components that carry the earliest fault signatures are exactly the quiet ones. We cast this as audio-visual source separation in which the viewing window supplies the second modality and the supervision is privileged: single-unit calibration recordings and 15-min at-line HPLC samples exist during training and never at deployment. Dense privileged supervision then reproduces a failure mode already documented for language models: the separator collapses onto the dominant source, and the weak stream is silently abandoned. We treat that collapse as a measurable symptom and govern it with three levers: where the signal is applied (per time-frequency band credit rather than per sample), what the teacher is shown (a ladder of privileged views admitted only after probe-based verification), and when the signal changes (guidance scheduled by a reaction-phase posterior with alarm-triggered refund). On mixtures built from pump, valve, fan and slide-rail recordings, the resulting separator raises weak-source SI-SNRi from 3.9 to 6.4 dB relative to a contribution-balanced baseline, cuts the collapse index from 0.48 to 0.21, and lifts downstream symptom detection from 0.81 to 0.85 AUC, with a distillation budget of 29% of all time-frequency bins.

papers.title: Schiff bases from Sodium alginate and o-phenylenediamine as a water-soluble fluorescent copper(II) chemosensor
papers.abstract: Polymeric Schiff bases derived from aromatic diamines have attracted significant interest due to their potential applications as fluorescent chemosensors. In this study, polymeric Schiff bases were synthesized from oxidized alginates (oxidation degrees of 20%, 40%, and 60%) and o-phenylenediamine. 1 H-NMR and FT-IR confirmed the chemical changes produced in all synthesized polymers. Rheological analysis revealed that the oxidized alginates exhibited Newtonian behavior, with a marked reduction of their thixotropy. In contrast, the synthesized Schiff bases exhibited a slight recovery in viscosity and thixotropic behavior, along with viscoelastic characteristics. All Schiff bases presented a fluorescence emission at nearly 370 nm in aqueous solution, and their fluorescence quenching responses toward Zn 2+ , Co 2+ , Ni 2+ and Cu 2+ ions were evaluated. OSA 20%-OPD exhibited the strongest response to Cu 2+ ; this Schiff base reached a limit of detection of 22.1 μM and a limit of quantification of 73.8 μM, while the Stern-Volmer analysis indicated a static-dynamic fluorescence quenching mechanism between the polymer and Cu 2+. This study offers valuable results of a new water-soluble fluorescent chemosensor for the detection of Cu 2+ .

papers.title: Solid-support photoacids
papers.abstract: Merocyanine photoacids are versatile molecules that allow the control of different processes with visible light, including CO 2 capture, driving molecular machines, and catalyzing reactions. However, high concentrations of the photoacid are needed for large pH changes, which makes observing other changes spectroscopically challenging, as well as requiring the laborious separation of the photoacid afterwards. Herein, we report a solidphase merocyanine-based photoacid that can generate a reversible pH change in bulk solution. The heterogeneous nature of these materials renders them “invisible” in common solution-phase spectroscopic techniques (e.g. UV-vis and NMR spectroscopy), allowing easy monitoring of pH-dependent changes of other components in the system. We demonstrated that these materials are robust through multiple switching cycles and can be used to modulate chemical and enzymatic reactions, showcasing their broad potential for different applications.

papers.title: Comparative QSAR Study of Aquatic Toxicity Prediction Using Molecular Descriptors and Fingerprints with Machine Learning
papers.abstract: To ensure environmental safety, we need to predict aquatic toxicity, but experimental testing is expensive, time consuming and often raises ethical concerns. In this study, we used machine learning to predict the 96-hour lethal concentration (LC50) of 908 organic compounds to fathead minnow ( Pimephales promelas ). We compared four different ways to represent molecular structure: (A) six pre-calculated descriptors from the original dataset, (B) twelve physicochemical descriptors computed from SMILES using RDKit, (C) 2048-bit Morgan fingerprints, and (D) a combined set of original and RDKit descriptors (18 features total). Three regression models were used such as Linear Regression, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting. Results showed that the combined descriptor set with Gradient Boosting gave the best prediction (cross-validation R² = 0.6278), which was about 5% better than using the original descriptors alone (R² = 0.5956). Feature importance analysis showed that lipophilicity (MolLogP) was the most important predictor, which makes chemical sense because fat-soluble molecules cross fish gill membranes more easily. Morgan fingerprints performed poorly, likely because the number of features (2048) was too large for the dataset size. These results show that combining different types of molecular descriptors can improve toxicity prediction

papers.title: Expanding the Covalent Warhead Toolbox: Discovery of the First Covalent PARG Inhibitors Using Bicyclo[1.1.0]butane-Based Warheads
papers.abstract: Poly(ADP-ribose) glycohydrolase (PARG) is the principal enzyme responsible for the degradation of poly(ADP-ribose) chains and has emerged as a promising therapeutic target in oncology within the DNA damage response (DDR) field. Although several reversible PARG inhibitors have recently entered clinical development, covalent inhibition of PARG has not previously been described. Herein, we report the discovery and optimization of the first covalent PARG inhibitors. Guided by structural analysis of the PARG catalytic domain, electrophilic warheads were incorporated into reversible quinazolinedione-based inhibitors to enable selective engagement of Cys872, a residue located within the catalytic pocket. While unsaturated ketone and hydrazide warheads enabled covalent inhibition of PARG, incorporation of a bicyclo[1.1.0]butane (BCB) hydrazide warhead led to the discovery of FORX-175, combining potent biochemical and cellular activity, reduced electrophile reactivity, and improved covalent-labeling selectivity. To the best of our knowledge, this work represents the first application of a BCB hydrazide warhead for selective covalent cysteine targeting. Building on these findings, a hybrid design strategy combining structural elements of the covalent quinazolinedione series with those of a reversible PARG inhibitor series led to the discovery of FORX-425, a covalent quinoline inhibitor bearing an underexplored BCB-carboxamide warhead. FORX-425 displayed potent biochemical inhibition, efficient covalent engagement, and nanomolar cellular activity in PARG-sensitive cancer cell lines. Collectively, these studies establish covalent inhibition as a viable strategy for PARG modulation, identify Cys872 as a tractable site for selective covalent targeting, and further demonstrate the potential of BCB-derived warheads for cysteine-directed drug discovery.

papers.title: Controlled Oxidant Delivery Uncovers Selectivity Branching in Heterogeneous Epoxidation Catalysis
papers.abstract: Heterogeneous catalysis generally features complex speciation of reactive intermediates that limits selectivity control and mechanistic understanding. Olefin epoxidation is a major and highly carbon-intensive process in the chemical industry, yet the molecular origin of selectivity branching causing the competing, CO 2 -emitting combustion reaction remains debated and is obscured by the presence of multiple oxidants on catalyst surfaces. Herein, we selectively generated surface metaloxygen (M–O) species, a commonly proposed intermediate, and discovered clean, O 2 -dependent chemoselectivity: surface M–O alone exhibited up to 100% selectivity toward epoxidation, whereas the co-existence of surface M–O and O 2 could lead to combustion via a novel oxidative C=C cleavage pathway. Further studies uncovered unprecedented insights into selectivity branching, suggesting new strategies for rationally decarbonizing epoxidation catalysis.

papers.title: Stereoelectronic Modulation of Hyperconjugative Networks in Saturated Heterocycles: Bridging Hilbert-Space NBO Perturbations with Real-Space QTAIM Electron Cloud Distortions
papers.abstract: The stereoelectronic modulation of hyperconjugative networks dictates the fundamental parameters of saturated heterocycles. Herein is presented a quantum chemical investigation into the anomeric effect across a matrix of 2-substituted oxygen and sulfur heterocycles utilising a GPU-accelerated pySCF-GPU optimisation pipeline at the CAM-B3LYP-D3(BJ)/def2-TZVPD/PCM level of theory, coupled with orbital perturbation evaluations via Firefly B3LYP-D3(BJ)/def2-TZVPD; QTAIM topology analyses via Multiwfn. For the axial 2-fluoro anomer, the exo -anomeric effect is heavily magnified; NBO maps a massive ( no → σ * C-F ) stabilisation energy ( E (2) = 20.11 kcal/mol). Real-space QTAIM maps confirm the physical consequences of this; compared to a standard C-C baseline (∇² ρ bcp ~= -0.6328 a.u.), the active C3-O2 bond exhibits a π -like charge concentration spike (∇² ρ bcp = -0.8182 a.u., LBO = 0.503, e = 0.1396), while the adjacent C-F bond is thinned and flattened (∇² ρ bcp = -0.3401 a.u., LBO = 0.107, e = 0.1827). Conversely, oxo -protonation triggers the anti -anomeric effect. Sequestering the dominant lone pair into a stable σ O-H bond quenches the exo engine, leaving a residual contribution from the σ -type lone pair and driving an intensive internal ( n F → σ * C-O ) back-donation ( E (2) = 17.38 kcal/mol), that forces the endocyclic bond relaxation to 1.483 Å in the anti -oxonium conformer.

papers.title: Backbone Expansion via Enzyme-Mediated Side-Chain Transfer
papers.abstract: There exists no straightforward strategy to generate protein materials containing internally spliced non-protein matter, especially at lengths and scales that support functional characterization. Here we describe Backbone Expansion via Enzyme-mediated Side-chain Transfer (BEST), a facile and general strategy for generating proteins containing internally spliced, non-protein matter at scale. Protein substrates for BEST contain a reactive glutamine (Gln), a backbone ester linkage, and a non-canonical side chain carrying a bioorthogonal reaction handle; the latter two elements are easily installed using a non-canonical ⍺-hydroxy acid. The bioorthogonal side chain is first extended via a click reaction with an element of non-protein matter that terminates in a primary amine. Treatment of this side-chain extended protein with transglutaminase (TGase) results in an intramolecular reaction between the glutamine side chain and the primary amine, generating an ester-containing macrocycle; selective cleavage of the macrocycle under basic conditions inserts the non-protein matter into the backbone with a minimal scar. Thus rather than excising an internal sequence element to restore polypeptide backbone continuity as in an intein-catalyzed reaction, BEST inserts diverse non-protein matter between two neighboring residues and subsequently cleaves the backbone between them. By transforming the protein backbone itself into an addressable locus for synthetic macromolecular integration, BEST establishes a general framework for constructing protein-polymer hybrids in which abiotic matter is not appended to a protein but structurally encoded within.

papers.title: JAI: Physically Constrained Prediction of Conformer-Averaged Proton–Proton Coupling Constants in Solution
papers.abstract: Machine-learning predictors of proton–proton coupling constants are usually trained on, and evaluated against, couplings computed for single geometries rather than the conformer-averaged values measured in solution. We describe JAI (J-coupling prediction with Artificial Intelligence), a graph transformer for 2J–5J(H,H) of small organic molecules trained on scaled Fermi-contact DFT couplings of about 3700 molecules, computed on geometries from the universal machine-learned potential UMA and averaged over conformers in six solvents, and on more than 25 000 curated experimental couplings annotated with their uncertainty, sign provenance and assignment. A fast mode predicts from the structure diagram; a conformer mode supplies, for each conformer of a reproducible search, the coefficients of Karplus-type expressions that are averaged with predicted populations; and a weighted combination of the two gives the final output, with 68 % and 90 % intervals calibrated on cross-validation errors. Against experimental couplings, the combined output reaches a mean absolute error of 0.43 Hz in cross-validation and 0.55 Hz when all compounds from the same literature source are held out together, our most realistic estimate for new chemistry. It reaches 0.35 Hz on 335 held-out compounds (fast mode: 0.53 Hz in cross-validation and 0.43 Hz on these compounds) and 0.57 Hz on 132 compounds added after the model had been finalized, 37 of them with environments that have very few DFT training examples. For vicinal couplings between sp3 carbons, it lowers the cross-validated error from 0.85 Hz with the fast mode to 0.66 Hz. The intervals hold for compounds like those of the training data but are too narrow for rare chemistry. Ablations on a previous version of the data set show that the physical expressions lower the error by 0.04 Hz overall, with a larger but less certain estimate for coupling types with few training exampl

papers.title: Synthesis of a Molecular Four-Ring Brunnian Link
papers.abstract: Mathematics describes infinitely many distinct knots and links, but translating these topologies into molecular structures remains a major challenge in chemistry. Here, we develop a strategy to bridge mathematical topology and molecular synthesis using single-stranded DNA (ssDNA), with a four-ring Brunnian link (4-BL) as a demanding test case. Because cutting any one ring releases all the others, the Brunnian property can be directly verified by selective cleavage. By surveying existing Brunnian link constructions and screening a census of links with up to fourteen crossings, we identified only one 4-BL type at fourteen crossings. Because a link can may have different diagrams, which impose different constraints on molecular construction, we developed a computational method to search for alternative minimal diagrams. We identified four distinct 14-crossing diagrams for the 4-BL, from which we selected one best suited to molecular construction based on their geometrical properties. The chirality and directionality of ssDNA make all fourteen crossings symmetry-distinct. To achieve precise control over the positions, connectivity and handednesses of these crossings, we reversed the orientation of one helical strand in the canonical DNA tensegrity triangle (cTT), whose crossings all have the same sign, to develop two additional motifs: the reverse TT (rTT), containing parallel junctions, and the inverted TT (iTT), containing bowtie junctions with artificial 5′–5′ and 3′–3′ linkages. We combined cTT, rTT and iTT to synthesize the 4-BL and verified its topology by enzymatic cleaving each ring. We further found that, unlike the three-ring Borromean rings, the 4-BL relaxes through multiple intermediates under the action of E. coli topoisomerase I before complete unlinking, consistent with our computational strand-passage analysis. Our work demonstrates how mathematical link analysis can guide the construction of experimentally verifiable molecular topologies and provides new structural motifs for extending programmable DNA assembly to more complex molecular entanglements.

papers.title: A Staged Reaction Optimisation Workflow for Fragment-to-Lead Elaboration
papers.abstract: Here, we present a reaction optimisation workflow that integrates data mining to generate unbiased, data-led starting points, high-throughput experimentation (HTE) to narrow the reaction parameter space, and closed-loop flow experiments guided by multi-objective Bayesian optimisation for fine-tuning. Designed for early-stage medicinal chemistry, particularly fragment-based drug discovery (FBDD), the workflow was demonstrated in two direct two-step syntheses of potent fragment-derived protein kinase C inhibitor precursors, involving sequential C–C and C–X bond formations. Quantum-mechanical (QM) reactivity prediction was used to inform route redesign improving synthetic efficiency and safety. HTE identified promising categorical starting points, which were subsequently refined within 20-40 autonomous continuous flow experiments per campaign, across 4 reaction steps. The workflow improved reaction yields in both syntheses while minimising simple E-factor and incorporating selectivity as an additional optimisation objective to facilitate downstream purification. An accelerated variant identified comparably productive conditions within a single working week, reducing substrate consumption by approximately 60%. This work demonstrates how staged, data-informed optimisation can accelerate material delivery in early-stage drug discovery while reducing experimental burden and providing valuable insights for subsequent process optimisation.

papers.title: Laser-Assisted Nuclear Thermal Propulsion for Cislunar Logistics: A Monte Carlo Power-Closure Assessment
papers.abstract: Laser-assisted nuclear thermal propulsion (LANTP) would raise the specific impulse of a nuclear thermal tug by adding orbital laser power to the hydrogen. We take performance targets of this kind (specific impulse 1300–1500 s, thrust 50–120 kN, a 1–50 MW laser on a 100–500 MWt reactor, and an initial mass in low Earth orbit, IMLEO, 40% below that of conventional nuclear thermal propulsion, NTP) as hypothetical design targets and test them for Earth–Moon logistics with a coupled model: hydrogen thermochemistry checked against Cantera, a power chain from the wall plug to the propellant, Gaussian-beam capture, finite burns with occultation and link dropouts, tug and laser-node masses, and Monte Carlo and Sobol analyses over assumed ranges. Reaching 1300–1500 s requires a useful laser power of 2.2–3.6 times the reactor power, so a 1–50 MW laser gives at most 1,000 s, and 50–120 kN needs 0.7–1.6 GW of emitted power. Against a conventional tug whose reactor is sized for the payload, the laser-assisted tug has a median IMLEO ratio of 1.44 (5th–95th percentile 1.13–1.94); 0% of the draws are below 1 and none reaches 0.6. Receiver specific mass accounts for 70% of the variance. A technology-threshold map shows that a mass benefit needs a receiver below approximately 11 kg per MW absorbed. 2 The laser nodes (about 18 kt) and the propellant reserve for a single laser fault eliminate this benefit. Results are conditional on the assumed ranges.

papers.title: Atomically Precise Au <sub>22</sub> (Lys-Cys-Lys) <sub>16</sub> Gold Nanocluster as Type I Photosensitizer: ROS Generation Mechanism
papers.abstract: The exceptional response of the gold nanocluster Au 22 (Lys-Cys-Lys) 16 , capable of generating reactive oxygen species (ROS) via electron transfer, was studied from both computational modeling and experimental characterization. An electron density perspective on remarkable features of gold nanoclusters and their photophysical applications provides a comprehensive study of the mechanism the gold nanocluster Au 22 (Lys-Cys-Lys) 16 undergoes as a type I photosensitizer. By means of molecular dynamics simulations, density functional theory for ground state and excited states, and linear response - time dependent density functional theory calculations, the optical properties of the nanocluster and its interactions in aqueous media were studied. Analysis of frontier molecular orbitals of Au 22 (Lys-Cys-Lys) 16 revealed that this nanocluster can transfer an electron from the gold core to a dioxygen molecule in the vicinity, generating ROS by following a spin-flip transition. The results suggest a strong connection between redistribution of electron density in the excited state and the ability of Au 22 (Lys-Cys-Lys) 16 to act as an electron donor rather than as a more commonly studied energy transfer mechanism for gold nanoclusters, mainly reported as photosensitizers type II. This study also probes the underlying mechanism of fluorescence quenching in aqueous media providing a comprehensive description of the experimental detection of ROS at different pH.

papers.title: Predictive Modeling of Friction-Resistant Advanced Coatings using Fluid Dynamics
papers.abstract: Turbulent skin-friction resistance in industrial conduit transport and piping infrastructure accounts for substantial energy dissipation worldwide. Biomimetic shark-skin riblets offer an attractive passive drag-reduction mechanism by constraining cross-stream turbulent momentum transfer and pinning quasi-streamwise vortices aloft. However, optimizing these micro-topographies across high-dimensional parameter spaces (riblet spacing s, aspect ratio h/s, conduit diameter D, and Reynolds number Re) remains experimentally and numerically prohibitive owing to the computational expense of high-fidelity Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD). In this study, we established a deterministic, high-throughput machine learning surrogate framework to accelerate the predictive design of friction-resistant advanced coatings. A space-filling 4-dimensional design matrix spanning s ∈ [10, 120] μm, h/s ∈ [0.20, 1.20], D ∈ [25.1, 249.8] mm, and Re ∈ [10,000, 200,000] was generated via Quasi-Monte Carlo (QMC) Latin Hypercube Sampling (N = 1,000 geometries). An automated execution pipeline coupled Reynolds-Averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) k-ω SST turbulence modeling with near-wall Navier slip boundary conditions, benchmarked against classical Petukhov analytical theory with relative baseline discretization errors below ±0.4%. An ensemble Random Forest regressor (300 bootstrapped decision trees) was trained to predict the continuous Darcy-Weisbach friction factor (f). The surrogate model demonstrated exceptional predictive accuracy on an unseen 20% holdout test set (N = 200), achieving a Coefficient of Determination of R2 = 0.99566 (explaining 99.57% of physical variance), a Mean Absolute Error of 1.487 × 10-4, and a Mean Absolute Percentage Error of 0.819%, with 100% of test predictions strictly bounded within a ±2% error envelope. Gini feature importance decomposition revealed that while macro-scale hydraulics (Re: 71.42%, D: 21.78%) govern global baseline dissipation, microstructural coating dimensions (s: 5.18%, h/s: 1.62%) act as the critical local governing switches determining the drag-reduction margin. The CFD data revealed an optimal drag reduction peak of ηDR,max = +9.253% centered at dimensionless wall spacing s+opt ≈ 16.5 and h/s = 0.55 – 0.65, whereas coarse riblets (s+ > 25) triggered rough-wall vortex penetration penalties down to -24.81%. Crucially, the trained surrogate predicted friction factors in 0.82 milliseconds—achieving an acceleration factor of 4,390,000× (~4.4 million times faster) compared to conventional meshed CFD (3,600 s)—enabling instantaneous 3D response surface exploration. When deployed in continuous industrial transport, the resulting head loss reduction yields electrical savings of up to 14.5 kWh/year per 10 meters of coated pipe, establishing an accurate, ultra-fast computational paradigm for next-generation energy-efficient surface engineering.

papers.title: A Workflow for the Systematic Synthesis and Assessment of Trianguleniums as Optical Probes for G-quadruplex DNA Imaging
papers.abstract: Guanine-quadruplexes (G4s), play critical regulatory roles in genomic processes including transcription, replication, and telomere maintenance. Consequently, there is significant interest in understanding G4 dynamics in live cells. One of the approaches to do this is by using optical probes that have distinct fluorescence lifetime upon binding to different nucleic acid topologies. Such probes can then be used in conjunction with Fluorescence Lifetime Imaging Microscopy (FLIM) for sensing and imaging G4s in cells. However, existing probes often suffer from low brightness, poor cellular uptake, or complex synthesis. In this study, we address these limitations by developing a semi-automated workflow for the parallel synthesis and evaluation of a library of fluorescent probes based on the triangulenium scaffold. Utilizing click chemistry, we produced focused libraries of optical probes that allow for biophysical characterization and cellular imaging directly from reaction mixtures, bypassing laborious purification steps and allowing for direct-to-biology (D2B) approaches. This led to the identification of a novel derivative (DM4) with superior photophysical properties compared to benchmark probes. The new probe displays an increase in fluorescence intensity and lifetime upon G4 DNA/RNA binding. Conversely, both its fluorescence intensity and lifetime decreased upon duplex DNA or total RNA binding. These properties combined with good cell permeability and low cytotoxicity, make DM4 an attractive next generation optical probe for G4 DNA imaging via FLIM.

papers.title: End-to-End Learning from Experimental Data: Integrating the PC-SAFT Equation of State into Neural Networks Training for Improved Polymer Parameter Estimation
papers.abstract: Accurate and computationally efficient thermodynamic models are essential for the design, optimization, and operation of many (bio)chemical processes involving polymer solutions, blends, and membranes. In this work, we combine machine learning (ML) with the PC-SAFT equation of state (EoS) to predict the non-associating pure component parameters for polymers, enabling the rapid evaluation of the pressure–volume–temperature (PVT) behavior of polymer melts and rubbers. Using a dataset of more than 5,400 PVT measurements for 78 chemically diverse polymers, we systematically evaluate the effects of EoS integration in the training process, the molecular representation, neural network architecture, and transfer learning. A baseline approach trained on pre-fitted PC-SAFT parameters is compared with a physics-informed approach that embeds the EoS in the training loop, enabling endto-end training directly on experimental PVT data. Performance is assessed using 6-fold cross-validation. For a feed-forward neural network (FNN) using extendedconnectivity fingerprints (ECFPs), embedding the EoS reduces the average mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) from 8.67% to 5.57%. Replacing the FNN and

papers.title: An Interpretable Chemoinformatics Benchmark for Evaluating Machine Learning Frameworks, Decoy Sensitivity, and Green Catalyst Prioritization
papers.abstract: As descriptor-based machine learning becomes widely used for reaction yield prediction and catalyst prescreening, controlled validation testbeds with known ground-truth data-generating processes (DGPs) are useful for auditing model behavior, cross-validation protocols, and post-hoc explainability methods. Here we construct and evaluate a synthetic chemoinformatics benchmark of N = 5,000 catalytic alcohol oxidation reactions across 20 independently seeded dataset realizations (100,000 total simulated reactions). By pairing a 22-substrate alcohol library characterized by RDKit exact monoisotopic masses (ExactMolWt) with categorical catalyst and terminal oxidant tiers, continuous thermal profiles, and non-causal synthetic decoy variables (Decoy_Cat_Load, Decoy_Rot_Bonds, Decoy_TPSA), we compare four regression models: Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) Linear Regression, eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Random Forest (RF), and Radial Basis Function Support Vector Regression (RBF-SVR). First, we compute the analytical unbounded Gaussian noise floor (3.989% MAE) alongside the 20-seed empirical clamped-oracle benchmark (3.994 ± 0.043% MAE, R² = 0.870 ± 0.003), showing that OLS closely approaches the oracle error floor (4.001 ± 0.044% MAE) under fold-specific standardization. Second, to illustrate how validation splits respond to substrate-level effects, we evaluate a positive-control regime that varies substrate-specific reactivity offsets (σ_sub ∈ {0.0, 4.0, 8.0, 12.0} percentage points), quantifying the divergence between random five-fold cross-validation and substrate-grouped hold-out (GroupKFold). Third, a paired four-model decoy ablation shows that while OLS, XGBoost, and RF exhibit minimal sensitivity to uninformative continuous descriptors (|ΔMAE| ≤ 0.008%, with RF changing by +0.008 ± 0.002%), untuned isotropic RBF-SVR experiences a larger error increase (+0.360 ± 0.026% MAE) consistent with Euclidean distance dilution. Fourth, multi-seed TreeSHAP evaluations show consistent global signal-to-decoy separation across all 20 realizations. Finally, we apply an illustrative multi-criteria Green Performance Index (GPI) to examine the trade-off between thermal activation and environmental penalty in post-hoc reaction ranking.

papers.title: Breaking the Trade-Off – Tilted T-Shaped Bis-Heteroaryl Azo Photoswitches with Near-Quantitative Bidirectional Switching
papers.abstract: Azoheteroarenes provide a versatile platform for controlling the molecular geometry and photochemical reactivity of azo switches through heteroaryl substitution. Here, we describe a family of bis-heteroaryl azo photoswitches combining pyrazole with thiophene or selenophene heterocycles, leveraging the independent success of these classes of azo switch. While T-shaped ( Z )-isomers are currently only established with a phenyl acceptor motif, single-crystal X-ray diffraction confirms the formation of a T-shaped ( Z )-isomer in these new designs where the pyrazole ring acts as the acceptor of a lone-pair–π interaction. Incorporation of pyrazole also substantially improves the bidirectional photoswitching of chalcogen-containing azoarenes by increasing the spectral separation of the ( E ) and ( Z ) isomers. These chalcogenophene azo pyrazoles (CAPs) reach up to 99% ( Z ) under UV/violet irradiation and up to 99% ( E ) under green light irradiation, while the corresponding selenophene derivatives retain efficient bidirectional switching with more red-shifted excitation. The switches show high resistance to photofatigue, with no significant photodegradation observed over multiple switching cycles. Computational analysis of thermal isomerization further reveals interaction-dependent differences in a coplanar transitionstate geometry, allowing for thermal half-lives of seconds to hours. These results demonstrate that heteroaryl-heteroaryl interactions provide an excellent strategy for controlling both metastable-state geometry and the photochemical performance of azo photoswitches and therefore could underpin the further development and application of advanced photoswitches for a range of light-addressable applications.

papers.title: Desalination LLM: Large Language Model Agents Design Efficient Graphene Membranes for Water Desalination
papers.abstract: Graphene nanopores can, in principle, combine high water permeability with strong salt rejection, but finding pore geometries that do both usually requires many molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. We describe a design framework in which a large language model (LLM) grows a nanopore atom by atom, using pretrained predictors of water flux and ion rejection to judge each candidate. Two recent models, Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol, were tested with the same prompt and the same design protocol (30 steps, up to 30 trials per step, at most three atoms removed per trial, and a 90% ion-rejection floor). We wanted to know how much of an agent’s performance comes from the model and how much from the surrounding scaffold, so each model was run twice: once as a tool-using agent with access to the predictors, and once in conversation only, where it chose atoms and estimated performance without any feedback. Three scaffold-only baselines that contain no language model were run for comparison. With tools, both models stayed above the rejection floor at every step. Claude Opus 5.5 produced a single, island-free pore with a predicted flux of 122.3 ns−1 at 93.2% rejection, and GPT-6.1 Sol reached 131.7 ns−1 at 90.2%. Without tools the two models erred in opposite directions. Claude Opus 5.5 overestimated rejection and removed too many atoms, ending at 64.3% rejection, whereas GPT-6.1 Sol was overly cautious and recovered only 30% of the flux reached by its scaffold. A greedy search restricted by simple manufacturability rules matched or exceeded both agents in flux. Compared with the MD dataset and the deep reinforcement learning (DRL) designs of earlier work, the agents placed a larger share of their high-rejection pores above 120 ns−1. Taken together, the results indicate that predictor feedback, rather than the language model on its own, is what keeps LLM-guided pore design on target, and the six-condition protocol gives a simple way to make that attribution for other models.

papers.title: GPU-accelerated analytic Hartree–Fock gradients
papers.abstract: Analytic nuclear gradients underpin much of computational quantum chemistry, driving geometry optimization and supplying the forces of ab initio molecular dynamics. Yet on graphics processing units (GPUs) the gradient has received far less attention than the selfconsistent field (SCF) procedure it accompanies. In current production codes its construction can cost as much as the entire preceding SCF. Here we present a novel, high-performance GPU implementation of the analytic Hartree–Fock energy gradient. The Coulomb and exchange gradients are evaluated by separate engines to exploit their markedly different sparsity. The exchange gradient retains the full eightfold integral symmetry through an in-kernel ring-buffer compaction that eliminates warp divergence. A hybrid Head-Gordon–Pople/Rys quadrature scheme, translational invariance and GPU-resident shell-pair batch construction further accelerate the evaluation. Benchmarked on NVIDIA H200 GPUs across double-and triple-ζ basis sets against TeraChem, GPU4PySCF, QUICK and VeloxChem, EXESS is the fastest code for every system and basis set tested, with average speedups of 12.2×, 15.4×, 222× and 176× respectively on molecules ranging up to ubiquitin (11,577 basis functions).

papers.title: Copper adsorption and release by biodegradable polyester films under field conditions
papers.abstract: In this work we analyze the adsorption of Cu(II) ions on biodegradable mulching films in real conditions by performing a comparison of two commercial PLA/PBAT-based films with a standard olefinic film (LDPE). In particular, in situ tests have been performed at an experimental agriculture center of the Apulian region by miming a real crop cycle. The desorption phenomenon of copper has been also investigated by measuring the amount of metal ions released by the debris of mulching films in the environment at the end of the crop cycle after burying the mulching films under the soil.

papers.title: Chemical Filtering of Thymine over Uracil in Prebiotic Hydrothermal Systems: A Mass-Consistent Stochastic Model with Complementary Insights from UV Photodamage Pathways
papers.abstract: The origin of thymine in DNA remains a central puzzle in astrobiology. While Darwinian evolution may have refined RNA into DNA, the initial selection mechanism must have been purely chemical. Here we present UPDSF v6.1.1—the Unified Prebiotic DNA Selection Framework—a mass-conserving, kineticallyconsistent stochastic model of hydrothermal-vent chemistry. At the optimum (90 °C, pH 11, dark vent), a chemical selection index (CSI) of 6.019× emerges through the multiplicative combination of real (direct) T-preferential hydrolysis and pool-composition drift. The model reproduces all key experimental rates (Lindahl, 1993 ; Cleaves et al., 2010 ; Ferris, 1996 ; Sutherland et al., 2020) with explicit provenance tracking and two environmental channels only. UV damage is negligible (<2 % of CSI) under vent conditions.
