The dominant Cr–Mn–Fe–Co–Ni candidate region expands at 1600 K to include V-containing families and six-principal-element compositions. Screened compositions show substantial departures from equimolarity, highlighting the value of continuous composition optimization. The search also identifies the less-explored Mg–Sc–Ti system, for which preliminary CALPHAD calculations suggest extended high-temperature bcc solid-solution fields under suitable pressure conditions. These results demonstrate a framework for efficient search of CCAs and illustrate how differentiable materials models can serve directly as tools for materials design.

papers.title: FLAME: Fluorinated-motif Learning and Attribution for Molecular Explainability Applied to PFAS
papers.abstract: Machine-learning (ML) architectures such as graph neural networks (GNNs) are increasingly used in structure-property modeling and molecular property prediction in fields of emerging contaminants such as per-and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS). However, their black-box nature makes these models difficult to use in scientific interpretation, decision making and in providing identifiable molecular substructures that contributed to the predictions. In attempts to open up the black-box, fragment-based explainability techniques have been created to capture molecular motifs that contributed to the predicted properties. However, these fragment-based explanations are dependent on how the molecular structures are partitioned and general molecular fragmentation methods may not capture highly fluorinated motifs, functional headgroups, and linker environments relevant for PFAS and related fluorinated compounds. The resulting fragment explanations may be less chemically meaningful unless fragmentation approaches account explicitly for the distinctive chemistry of fluorinated molecular motifs. We present Fluorinated-motif Learning and Attribution for Molecular Explainability (FLAME), a PFAS-tailored framework that extends rBRICS fragmentation to improve fragment-based explainability methods. The additional cleavage environments improved the separation of PFASrelevant structures, enabling the separation of 568 additional molecules relative to the original rBRICS in a dataset of 4,738 molecules. The substructure masking explanation method was then applied to a graph neural network that predicted electron affinity, ionization potential, and HOMO–LUMO gap. The chemically tailored fragments provided identifiable units for substructure masking allowing more interpretable predictions based on motif-level attributions. Our results demonstrate a constrained explainability framework built upon chemically relevant structural motifs. FLAME is extensible to other classes of emerging contaminants whose characteristic structural motifs require tailored fragmentation for scientifically meaningful model explanations.

papers.title: Electrodes as Tunable Ligands: Electro-Inductive Control of Supported Catalyst Reactivity
papers.abstract: Electronic tuning of molecular catalysts traditionally relies on synthetic modification of ligand structures, with each modification requiring the preparation of a distinct catalyst whose electronic properties are largely fixed at synthesis. Herein, we investigate a complementary strategy in which applied potential serves as a continuously adjustable electronic input to a surface-bound molecular catalyst. A pyridine(diimine) iron catalyst was anchored to TiO 2 supported on fluorine-doped tin oxide (FTO) through a conjugated linker that facilitated communication between the active site and the conductive surface. The anchored catalyst was active for the ring-opening polymerization of L-lactide, with polymerization rates increasing under positive applied potential and decreasing under negative applied potential. These results are consistent with an electro-inductive effect in which applied potential modulated the Lewis acidity of the Fe center, supported by trends observed in a complementary Hammett study of para-substituted molecular Fe complexes. Because potential can be varied without altering molecular structure, catalyst activity could also be modified in real time during polymerization. This work demonstrates electro-inductive control of catalytic reactivity for a metal oxide-supported catalyst, illustrating how supported molecular catalysts provide new avenues for dynamically tuning thermochemical catalytic activity.

papers.title: Computational Insights into Chiral Induced Spin Selectivity in Organic Semiconductors via Circular Dichroism Prediction
papers.abstract: Due to implications ranging from the origins of chirality in nature to the development of better spintronic devices, there is notable interest in gaining a deeper understanding of the quantum structure property relationships underlying the chiral induced spin-selectivity (CISS) effect. Although many features proposed to contribute heavily to CISS are computationally expensive, studies have shown that the maximum circular dichroism (CD) absorbance correlates strongly with the magnitude of CISS effect exhibited by a material and that time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) methods can accurately predict CD spectra at a reasonable cost. In this work, we present an unprecedented analysis of approximately 1000 organic semiconductive hexamers using a selection of data science and machine learning methods to examine the quantum structure property relationships contributing to high CD response, finding the paramount importance of polarizability and conformational features as determined by selected methods. We outline methods establishing precedence for highly cost-effective

papers.title: On the real role of hydroxide in zeolite crystallization: electrochemically-generated OH synthesis
papers.abstract: Hydrothermal synthesis of zeolites is typically conducted in basic media, where the hydroxide anion (OH - ) acts as a mineralizing agent, promoting the transformation of precursors into crystalline frameworks. OH - is introduced together with (in)organic structure-directing agents ((in)OSDAs), thus always accompanied by a counter-cation (e.g., Tetrapropylammonium + , Na + ). Consequently, for systems containing only monovalent ions, the OH - /SDA + ratio generally remains at 1 (or below). Contrary to this common approach, we employed a dual electrochemical cell as a novel, unconventional reactor for the in situ cathodic generation of OH-, termed Electrochemically-generated OH Synthesis (EOS). Demonstrated for the first time, expanding the OH - /OSDA + ratio from 0.8 to 1.2 at a constant OSDA content during Silicalite-1 crystallization enabled us to decouple the role of OH - from that of the OSDA. Crystal size, solid yield, and OSDA uptake strongly depended on the OH - content, confirming a broader role of OH - than that of a mineralizer. The evolution of silicate precursors, crystallization kinetics, and particularly the nucleation step were witnessed as the most affected parameters. This decoupling further shows that OSDA uptake by pure-silica frameworks is not solely governed by templating, but also depends on the charge state of the precursors, which is directly influenced by OH - content. EOS reveals an alternative gel-mediated precursor pathway prior to Silicalite‑1 crystallization, highlighting the influence of precursor state and crystallization pathway on the final material properties.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Guided Comparison of n- and p-Type Reorganization Energies
papers.abstract: A key component in the rational design of novel, high-performing candidate organic electronic materials is understanding and predicting the charge transport properties of π-conjugated materials. Although purely experimental design methods can be prohibitively expensive, previous computational investigations have established cost-saving methods to accurately predict charge transport for π-conjugated materials via internal Marcus reorganization energy. Many works, however, have focused solely on p-type charge transfer, whereas many organic electronic devices utilize both n-and p-type materials or motifs. As such, a deeper understanding of the features that influence n-type charge transport is important. In this work, we present a wholesale machine learning (ML)-driven analysis of n-type charge transport for a previously established dataset of polythiophene derivatives. The performance and results of the model are somewhat similar for the prediction of n-and p-type λs by a random forest regression model, albeit with key differences discussed herein.

papers.title: Oxygen-Driven Etching of MAX Phases Assisted by HF Vapor (OxyVap-HF) for MXenes Synthesis
papers.abstract: MXenes are conventionally produced by immersing MAX phases in fluoride-containing acids, where removal of A elements proceeds via their proton-driven oxidation leading to H 2 gas evolution accompanied by fluoride complexation with A n+ . Here we introduce a different, oxygen-driven HF vapor assisted route (OxyVap-HF) in which a precursor MAX phase, such as Ti 3 AlC 2 , is held separated from a dilute HF solution reservoir and etched by oxygen available in air, assisted by HF/H 2 O vapor helping to maintain access of oxygen to A element layers. Importantly, in OxyVap-HF the MAX phase is never in direct contact with liquid, therefore the same dilute HF solution can be used multiple times without purification or any other treatment, minimizing safety risks and environmental burden of MXene synthesis, thereby directly addressing the need for greener MXene synthesis methods. Mechanistically, in the oxygen-containing atmosphere of the OxyVap-HF the etching reaction consumes O 2 rather than evolving H 2 . Gas volume analysis, scavenging of O 2 with pyrogallol, experiments in controlled Ar/O 2 /air atmospheres, and Raman spectroscopy of the gas phase demonstrate a switch from traditional proton-driven, H 2 -evolving etching under Ar, to oxygen-driven etching in air. The HF/H 2 O ratio controls MAX phase conversion, assisting with the removal of Al–O-containing intermediates formed during etching, installing terminations, and expanding the interlayer spacing, thus yielding MXenes that can be further delaminated. We show that an aqueous HF solution with concentration as low as 3 wt% can be used repeatedly in OxyVap-HF process, consistently yielding new batches of delaminable MXenes.

papers.title: Lorentz-Covariant Bi-Photonic Kinematics: Deriving Optical Polarization and the Born Rule from Internal Constrained Dynamics
papers.abstract: (Dated: November 7, 2026) Standard quantum electrodynamics (QED) treats the photon as an unstructured, point-like excitation of a gauge field. In this orthodox framework, when light encounters a measurement device, its continuous wave description abruptly and unpredictably reduces to a single discrete detector click. The statistical likelihood of recording that click is calculated by squaring the overlap between the incoming wave state and the detector state—an operational prescription universally known as the Born rule (P = |⟨ϕ|ψ⟩|2). The persistent inability of spontaneous collapse hypotheses, context-free hidden-variable schemes, and many-worlds branching to eliminate fundamental unpredictability stems from treating abstract state vectors as irreducible primitives of nature. Here, we formulate a relativistic, composite two-particle (bi-photonic) model of light in which a single optical packet consists of a phase-locked pair of conjugate sub-elements (γA, γB) executing internal transverse orbital motion on a light-cone surface. Using relativistic Hamiltonian mechanics with algebraic constraints (Dirac constraint mechanics), we prove that the negative internal binding potential exactly cancels the positive transverse orbital kinetic energy inside the invariant mass operator.

papers.title: Integrated Computational Design and Multistage Virtual Screening for the Prioritization of Putative USP5 Catalytic-Cleft Inhibitors
papers.abstract: Ubiquitin-specific protease 5 (USP5) processes unanchored polyubiquitin and has been linked to cancer-associated signaling. We developed a computer-aided workflow to generate and rank small molecules against its catalytic/substrate cleft. The starting dataset contained 26 activity records representing 19 unique compounds, ten with measured half-maximal inhibitory concentrations. Descriptor-based quantitative structure-activity relationship models underwent compound leave-one-out and scaffold-held-out validation. Ten chemical-enumeration methods produced 3,646 method–product records and 3,264 unique structures. The main screen combined these structures with ten additional source-positive molecules and retained 18 compounds under strict selection criteria. A ten-compound panel, comprising nine generated structures and one known benchmark, underwent corrected AutoDock Vina docking against two USP5 receptor copies. The primary and repeated-seed campaigns produced 800 recorded modes. Standard-precision (SP) and extra-precision (XP) Glide docking independently evaluated the prepared ligand library, followed by Prime molecular mechanics/generalized Born surface area (MM-GBSA) calculations on the XP complexes. P06 emerged as the top-ranked candidate in the three-stage consensus analysis, ranking first in SP and second in both XP and MM-GBSA evaluations. P03 achieved the most favorable mean XP docking score, whereas P09 exhibited the strongest mean MM-GBSA binding energy. P10 ranked third overall but demonstrated greater sensitivity to receptor conformation. Collectively, this integrated computational workflow establishes a prioritized hierarchy of candidate compounds targeting the USP5 catalytic/substrate-binding cleft and highlights the influence of chemical selection and receptor preparation on structure-based rankings.

papers.title: 3-Methyl-2-Oxazolidinone (MOX), an Effective and Plausibly Green Solvent Replacement for DMF in Amidation Reactions
papers.abstract: The solvent N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) is widely used in organic synthesis for a broad range of chemical reactions. However, prolonged exposure to DMF presents serious health hazards due to its hepatotoxicity and reproductive toxicity. Growing appreciation of these risks has motivated public and private institutions to phase out the use of DMF and identify safe, viable alternatives for various applications. This is especially urgent for amidation, the most frequently performed reaction class in pharmaceutical organic synthesis, for which DMF is the most frequently used solvent. Existing alternatives to DMF have distinct chemical or practical drawbacks, discouraging widespread adoption. Herein, we identify 3-methyl-2-oxazolidinone (MOX), an unexplored polar aprotic solvent with a favorable chemical, safety, and sustainability profile, as a general replacement for DMF in the synthesis of amides from amines and carboxylic acids. MOX was evaluated in solution-phase amidation reactions for the synthesis of dipeptides, active pharmaceutical ingredients, synthetic auxiliaries, and other structurally or electronically diverse substrates. Across 44 examples employing 23 coupling agents or coupling methods, MOX enabled amidation reactions for a chemically diverse set of substrates through a broad range of reaction conditions. Isolated yields ranged from 43–98%, with a mean yield of 81%. Optimization of reaction conditions was rarely required. These findings establish MOX as a safe and practical replacement for DMF in amidation reactions. Introduction

papers.title: Hard X-ray Studio for reproducible analysis of static and modulated excitation X-ray absorption spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Quick-scanning X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy (QXAFS) is an emerging technique recent year, which enables complete XAS to be acquired on sub-second to second timescales, providing a powerful means of probing transient electronic and local structural changes under operando conditions. We present Hard X-ray Studio, a local application combining a browser interface with a Python and XrayLarch service. Static mode prepares individual spectra or merges reviewed repeats into named conditions before feature extraction. Time-series mode retains acquisition coordinates and supports electrochemical synchronization, phase-sensitive detection and kinetic analysis. Both modes provide calibrated preparation, constrained XANES linear-combination fitting (LCF), singular-value decomposition (SVD) and multivariate curve resolution (MCR), and EXAFS extraction with relative shell descriptors. A kinetic-analysis module applies exponential models to both the excitation response and time-dependent spectral descriptors, allowing their characteristic time constants to be compared and their consistency to be evaluated. The platform links these analyses through stable source identities, explicit selections and processing-state checks. Its distinctive design preserves missing metadata and source membership while distinguishing condition comparisons from temporal responses. These reproduce imposed mixture fractions, periodic amplitudes, relative EXAFS descriptors and response rates. Experimental NiFe-LDH measurements analysed in Origin provide a separate reference case for subsequent numerical comparison. Hard X-ray Studio offers an inspectable workflow for connecting static and time-resolved XAS analyses while retaining measurements locally; experimental benchmarking and deployment acceptance remain distinct from numerical verification.

papers.title: From Cell to Pack: Experimental Validation of a Thermo-Electrochemical 4s4p Battery Model
papers.abstract: Growing deployment of lithium-ion batteries has intensified the need for advanced battery pack simulation tools to address the key engineering challenge of accurately predicting the electrical and thermal behaviour of battery packs. This work presents a scalable, physics-based simulation framework for arbitrary (Ms, Np) lithium-ion battery pack configurations. The framework is demonstrated and experimentally validated using a 4s4p pack with bottom cooling. Experiments were conducted on the pack, with temperatures measured throughout the assembly using 80 thermal sensors distributed uniformly across the pack. The resulting spatially and temporally resolved temperature measurements, together with measured pack voltage, are compared directly with model predictions obtained using both the standard expression for irreversible heat generation and the energetically consistent expression derived in [27], which includes heat of mixing within the electrode particles. The heat-transfer model is parametrised using a charge–discharge protocol that yields the same heat-transfer coefficients for both heating formulations. The standard expression gives only moderate agreement with the measured temperatures, whereas simulations using the energetically consistent expression show very good agreement with both the temperature evolution across the pack and its electrical response. The approach represents each cell as a set of spatially resolved finite sections, each governed by the full Doyle–Fuller–Newman (DFN) equations, with all sections coupled thermally and electrically. For the 4s4p case, this results in a network of 80 simultaneously solved DFN models. This formulation enables detailed prediction of intra-pack thermal and electrochemical behaviour. The simulation platform is implemented as a flexible API. The resulting tool can support the design of more reliable and longer-lasting lithium-ion battery systems across a range of large-scale applications.

papers.title: Decoupled Semisolid Extrusion and Drop-on-Demand Dispensing for Liposomal Nanomedicine Tableting
papers.abstract: Distributed manufacturing of personalized oral nanomedicines requires processing that protects delicate nanocarriers from thermal and mechanical degradation. Tableting of liposomal nanomedicine into solid dosage forms has gained interest by providing enhanced physicochemical stability and room temperature storage, simplifying cold-chain logistics. Nanomedicine advancements have corresponded with the recent push toward an agile decentralized manufacturing paradigm, incorporating additive manufacturing and 3D printing technologies. This study presents a quality by design-guided framework that decouples semisolid extrusion of blank tablet vehicles from drop-on-demand (DoD) microdispensing of liquid liposomal inks. Critical material attributes and critical process parameters were systematically investigated and optimized to preserve liposomal integrity using a lipid bilayer permeability disruption assay and dynamic light scattering size measurements. Decoupling tablet fabrication from the pharmaceutical drug dosing limited the maximum internal processing temperatures to approximately 50 °C for under 5 minutes, safeguarding the thermolabile liposomes. DoD microdispensing across varying nozzle diameters (60 µm and 100 µm) and pressure pulse intensities (5 Pa·s to 30 Pa·s) produced negligible hydrodynamic shear disruption, maintaining bilayer integrity and liposome particle size distribution. Incorporation into solid tablet matrices enhanced 30-day liposome stability at room temperature relative to aqueous controls, which 2 exhibited membrane breakdown after 14 days. Final tableted formulations, including liposomal ciprofloxacin, met United States Pharmacopeia standards for content uniformity, yielding acceptance values ≤ 8.0 % and target dose recoveries within 90 % to 110 %. This decoupled additive manufacturing platform establishes a robust strategy for decentralized, on-demand compounding of shear- and temperature-sensitive solid oral nanomedicines.

papers.title: From Local Motifs to Long-Range Order: Adaptive Diffusion of the Complex Au–S Surface Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Surface reconstructions present a challenging structure-prediction problem because locally favorable atomic motifs must be accommodated within the periodicity of the underlying crystal, often producing large and complex surface unit cells. Here, we extend adaptive diffusion to jointly explore continuous atomic coordinates and discrete surface cell transformations, allowing favorable atomic arrangements and periodicities to be discovered together. We demonstrate the approach for the complex sulfur-induced reconstruction of Au(111), whose atomic structure has remained debated despite extensive experimental investigation. The search identifies a particularly stable rectangular Au 4 S 4 motif and a preference for a transformed surface cell. The exploration also reveals how favorable motifs can be transferred between different periodic environments. Guided by this observation, we construct and relax an arrangement of ten Au 4 S 4 motifs in the experimentally observed large quasi-rectangular unit cell that reproduces the reported sulfur coverage, and is consistent with the local ordering observed by scanning tunneling microscopy.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Model Implementation for UC Irvine Dataset 322
papers.abstract: The dataset, sourced from the UCI repository, underscores the value of open-source resources in advancing sensor research. In this study, raw sensor data were compressed using polynomial fitting (polyfit), achieving nearly a 100-fold reduction, and subsequently analyzed with the Isolation Forest algorithm to detect anomalies. Python libraries, including scikit-learn, were deployed in an isolated environment to ensure reproducibility and scalability. The workflow was further integrated into Microsoft Copilot, enabling natural language interaction with the AI agent for streamlined big data modeling.

papers.title: Dataset-level reliability and quality control for metallurgical data structured with large language models
papers.abstract: Data-driven alloy design depends on the availability of reliable, structured experimental information. Although the scientific literature contains large volumes of such data, heterogeneous reporting practices hinder their systematic reuse at scale. General-purpose large language models (LLMs) offer a flexible approach for structuring metallurgical text without domain-specific fine-tuning, but they introduce errors such as omissions, misassignments, and fabrications that are not fully characterised by conventional extraction metrics. This study examines error behaviour in LLM-assisted extraction of metallurgical information using a multi-stage workflow comprising text classification, structured extraction, and automated review. Controlled experiments are used to analyse how prompt design, task formulation, and reporting structure influence error behaviour within each stage of the workflow. The workflow is subsequently evaluated at large scale on a corpus of 23,861 full-text publications on high-chromium steels, combining automated reviewer signals with statistically grounded manual sampling to assess residual errors. The results identify dominant, task-dependent error modes and show that similar extraction performance can correspond to substantially different uncertainty profiles across information types. These findings clarify how error behaviour depends on text structure and task formulation and provide a basis for the risk-aware reuse of literature-derived metallurgical data.

papers.title: Pt(II)-Flavin Complexes As Anticancer And Antibacterial Agents
papers.abstract: We report a new chelating pyridyl–imine ligand bearing a riboflavin-derived pendant group and its Pt(II) complexes 1 and 2, designed as cisplatin- and oxaliplatin-like derivatives. Both complexes reacted with DNA and a histone-derived peptide, with 1 showing markedly higher covalent reactivity. However, this trend was not reflected in biological activity. Complex 2 displayed micromolar antiproliferative effects and pronounced antibacterial activity, particularly against Bacillus subtilis, whereas 1 was inactive in the tested models. Cellular accumulation studies excluded enhanced Pt uptake as the origin of this difference. Fluorescence microscopy performed on Escherichia Coli and Bacillus subtilis indicated that 2 affects bacterial DNA and membrane potential, consistent with a dual antibacterial mechanism. Comparison with oxaliplatin and the free flavin ligands showed that both the Pt–oxalate fragment and the riboflavin-containing ligand are required for activity.

papers.title: Optimising TC/EA–IRMS hydrogen isotope measurements of volcanic glass: H 2 -amount dependence of δD and application to SIMS calibration
papers.abstract: In TC/EA–IRMS hydrogen isotope (δD) analysis of volcanic glass, sample mass is commonly adjusted according to H 2 O content so that all samples yield similar H 2 amounts, a practice that can obscure any dependence of measured δD on H 2 amount. Using a wide-bore reactor with a large graphite crucible that accommodated up to 17 mg of sample and gave an approximately four-fold greater peak area than the standard configuration, we measured two reference materials, IAEA-CH-7 polyethylene (δD = −100.3‰) and an in-house chlorite (δD = −41.1‰), over a wide range of H 2 amounts. Measured δD varied linearly with the inverse of H 2 amount above 1.5 µmol: the fitted relationship for polyethylene gives δD values about 19‰ higher at 1.5 µmol than the extrapolated value, whereas chlorite showed no resolvable dependence. In six submarine basaltic glasses, the magnitude of the dependence ranged from none to more than twice that of polyethylene and tended to decrease with increasing δD, but polyethylene departed from this trend. Because the dependence differs among samples and is not necessarily cancelled by matching H 2 amounts, we determined the δD value of each sample by extrapolation to infinite H 2 amount and normalised it with the extrapolated values of the two reference materials. Using the extrapolated values as reference data, normalised SIMS instrumental mass fractionation correlated linearly with anhydrous mole weight across nine basaltic glasses (R 2 = 0.84), showing that a composition-dependent matrix correction is required even within basaltic compositions. These results improve both bulk TC/EA–IRMS and in situ SIMS δD analyses and indicate that SIMS datasets calibrated with earlier reference values should be re-evaluated.

papers.title: Optimal control of lipid–peroxyl radical-pair termination under spin relaxation
papers.abstract: Spin-selective radical-pair reactions provide a molecular mechanism through which magnetic fields can influence chemical kinetics, but whether a shaped field can retain a control advantage under spin relaxation and molecular motion remains open. We address this question for the termination of lipid autoxidation chains through spin-selective encounters between lipid-peroxyl radicals, connecting optimal control of the radical pair to explicit Brownian dynamics and to classical autoxidation kinetics. Gradient-projection optimization, corroborated by a bang–bang Pontryagin solution, identifies a dipolar-scale operating range: the best-found field raises the triplet-initialized singlet termination yield from Φ S|T = 0.220 at 50 µT to 0.562 (+155%), with the bang–bang solution reaching 0.522 and a bandwidth-filtered proxy retaining 0.270. An idealized stochastic-Schrödinger relaxation model serves as a stress test, whereas explicit Brownian dynamics treats the molecular motion; under Brownian dynamics the control advantage remains positive throughout the sampled rotational-correlation-time range, and one field transfers across eight microdomain-size–diffusion parameter sets. Closing the spin calculation to classical autoxidation kinetics gives C eff = −f/(1+f), where f is the fraction of peroxyl loss proceeding through bimolecular termination. Two limiting descriptions of the productive-encounter spin composition bracket the predicted suppression of oxidation flux in antioxidant-free liposomes at approximately 21–37%, and at approximately 4–10% for the bandwidth-filtered field. α-Tocopherol attenuates the response as interception comes to dominate, providing an internal experimental control. These values describe an elementary encounter and a minimal kinetic model, not whole-cell lipid peroxidation.

papers.title: Capturing many-body effects for metal ions in aqueous phase through developing specialized machine learning force fields
papers.abstract: Metal ion–ligand interactions govern reactivity, bioavailability, and catalytic function across chemistry and biology, yet the many-body effects underlying water exchange around multivalent metal ions remain difficult to capture with classical force fields. Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD), by contrast, provides accurate results but is limited to picosecond timescale sampling by its high computational cost. Machine learning force fields (MLFFs) offer a promising route to quantum-mechanics-level accuracy at force-field-level cost, but we show that existing MACE foundation models which were trained on materials predict an incorrect coordination number for Zn2+ in aqueous phase. To address this gap, we developed a CREST-based enhanced-sampling workflow to generate diverse quantum mechanical reference data and trained specialized E(3)-equivariant MACE models for Zn2+, Ca2+, and La3+ in aqueous solution. Systematic benchmarking of DFT functionals, model hyperparameters, data precision, and water geometry shows that model performance is sensitive to several of these choices, underscoring the need for careful validation. Encouragingly, the resulting specialized MACE models accurately reproduce hydration structures, coordination number distributions, and water-exchange kinetics in excellent agreement with experiment and AIMD, outperforming classical force fields (12-6, 12-6-4, and AMOEBA) in simultaneously capturing energetics and mechanism. We further extend this approach to ML/MM simulations of the metalloenzyme thermolysin, reproducing the monodentate/bidentate switching of Glu166 and capturing Zn2+ coordination number flexibility over a 2 ns trajectory—a timescale inaccessible to conventional QM/MM. These results demonstrate that specialized MLFFs provide a practical and transferable strategy for bridging quantum mechanical accuracy with molecular mechanics speed for metal-ligand systems, enabling long-timescale conformational sampling, mutant screening, and mechanistic studies of metalloenzyme catalysis that were previously out of reach.

papers.title: Comparative O-Glycosylation Analysis of Etanercept Originator and Biosimilars Using Orthogonal LC-MS Workflows
papers.abstract: Etanercept is a highly glycosylated Fc-fusion protein whose dense, heterogeneous O-glycosylation is challenging to characterize yet relevant to biosimilarity assessment. We compared O-glycosylation in five originator (Enbrel) batches, three biosimilars (Erelzi, Benepali and Nepexto) and the EDQM chemical reference standard using orthogonal LCMS workflows on an Orbitrap Excedion Pro BioPharma mass spectrometer. Native intact mass analysis after N-glycan and sialic acid removal, and middle-up analysis after IdeS digestion, characterized O-glycan macroheterogeneity together with C-terminal lysine and N-terminal leucine-loss variants. Site-specific mapping combined the O-glycoproteases OgpA and IMPa with HCD-triggered EThcD fragmentation. The same 13 O-glycosites were identified in every sample, carrying predominantly sialylated core 1 O-glycans (72%-80% sialylated) with low levels of Tn antigen. In contrast, Benepali and Nepexto showed lower O-glycan occupancy (approximately 17.3 versus 18.9-19.1 O-glycans per molecule) and broader glycoform distributions, and Benepali showed markedly elevated leucine loss (35% of TNF domains). Subunit analysis resolved nearisobaric leucine-loss and di-lysine variants that were ambiguous at the intact level, while EThcD localized O-glycans within densely glycosylated peptides. This multi-level workflow provides a generalizable approach for site-specific O-glycosylation analysis and comparability assessment of O-glycosylated biotherapeutics.

papers.title: Polarization Is Required to Model Electrostatic Preorganization: The Case of Chorismate Mutase
papers.abstract: Electrostatic preorganization contributes to enzymatic catalysis through transition state stabilization and is often investigated using classical molecular dynamics (MD) simulations that employ fixed-charge force fields (FFs). Although polarizable FFs allow for more accurate quantification of local electrostatic effects, whether they qualitatively differ from fixed-charge FFs regarding properties such as the substrate conformation stabilized by the enzyme's electrostatics remains unclear. Here, we compare molecular dynamics simulations of chorismate mutase performed with the AMOEBA polarizable FF and the AMBER fixed-charge FF. We find that simulations using AMOEBA sample chorismate geometries resembling the transition state-like near attack conformation (NAC), while AMBER simulations sample strictly non-NAC conformations. The local substrate-protein interactions are also completely altered by the choice of FF, with AMOEBA and AMBER each sampling distinct active site hydrogen bond networks. Finally, even at matched reactive substrate conformations, the heterogeneous three-dimensional electric field experienced by the substrate is qualitatively different between the FFs. By additionally comparing to a modified AMOEBA FF with the induced dipole term turned off, we also isolate the explicit polarization in AMOEBA as the key contributor to these differences.

papers.title: Large Language Models in Chemistry: Opportunities, Limitations, and Hallucination Risks
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have moved quickly from general-purpose text tools to components of chemical research workflows. They are now used to extract data from the literature, propose synthesis routes, write analysis code, predict properties from few examples, and control laboratory instruments through tool-augmented agents. These capabilities create real opportunities, particularly for researchers and institutions with limited access to specialist software and training. They also carry risks that are specific to chemistry. Chemical information is dense with symbols, units, stoichiometry, and safety-critical numbers, and LLMs generate fluent text whether or not it is correct. This perspective reviews the main opportunities for LLMs in chemistry, the technical limitations that constrain them, and a taxonomy of hallucination types with examples of how each can cause harm in a laboratory or research setting. It then proposes a practical verification framework for everyday users, a set of reporting practices for authors, and a short research agenda. The central argument is that LLMs are most valuable in chemistry when they are treated as fallible assistants wrapped in verification tools, such as cheminformatics libraries, databases, and physical measurement, and not as sources of chemical truth.

papers.title: Toxicant–Probe Unity in Fluorotoxicology: A Conceptual Framework, Aggregation-State Taxonomy, and Research Agenda
Tyrosine–silver interactions: Comparing [Tyr,H]+ and [Tyr,Ag]+ using mass spectrometry, UVPD, and IRMPD action spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Metal complexes of peptides and proteins are central to biological systems and to the synthesis of functional subnanometer biomaterial templates, such as silver nanoclusters (NCs). Although tyrosine (Tyr) is widely recognised as an effective reducing and stabilising agent in silver nanoparticle production, its fundamental interaction with an isolated silver cation remains poorly understood. Here, we present a joint experimental and theoretical investigation of the structural and optical properties of the mass-selected [Tyr,Ag]+ complex, using [Tyr,H]+ as a structural benchmark. We introduce a new experimental platform that, for the first time, combines a benchtop continuouswave (cw) mid-infrared (MIR) laser and a tunable ultraviolet (UV) optical parametric oscillator (OPO) in a single iontrap setup. Action spectra were recorded in both the mid-IR (1134–1938 cm−1) and UV (234–390 nm) spectral regions. Because [Tyr,Ag]+ exhibits a low propensity for fragmentation, mid-IR photodissociation was achieved by attaching a weakly bound H2O tag. The experimental infrared multiphoton dissociation (IRMPD) and ultraviolet photodissociation (UVPD) spectra were combined with quantum-chemical simulations to identify low-energy conformers and assign their vibrational and electronic transitions. This complementary approach fingerprints the structural and electronic motifs associated with Ag+ binding. The UVPD spectra provide clear evidence of chargetransfer excitations between the aromatic ring of tyrosine and the silver cation. These results provide molecularlevel insight into the early stages of silver–biomolecule coordination.

papers.title: Hetero-Diels-Alder Reaction of Alkenes and Electrochemically- Generated o-Quinonediimines
papers.abstract: Electrochemically driven organic transformations have emerged as a versatile approach for developing more sustainable synthetic methods, offering precise control over redox processes while replacing stoichiometric oxidants with electricity. In this context, an efficient electrochemical strategy for the generation of highly reactive o-quinonediimines from readily available o-phenylenediamines is reported. Anodic oxidation enables their in-situ formation and subsequent cycloaddition with diverse alkenes, affording valuable tetrahydroquinoxaline cycloadducts in good to excellent yields. The broad substrate scope, together with the successful derivatization of the products, highlights the synthetic utility of this approach.

papers.title: Sequence order controls silver(I) coordination in aqueous His–Met–Pro tripeptide–nitrate mixtures: an ab initio molecular dynamics study
papers.abstract: Silver–peptide interactions underpin peptide-directed synthesis of silver nanomaterials and the silver-resistance machinery of bacteria, yet the molecular-level speciation of Ag(I) in the presence of short peptides and nitrate remains poorly resolved. Here we report 100-ps ab initio molecular dynamics simulations of three sequence isomers of the tripeptide His–Met–Pro (HMP, HPM and PHM; 220 atoms each) in water, with four Ag(I) ions, four nitrate anions and 32 water molecules at 298 K, using the PBE–PAW description (VASP 6.1.0, 500 eV plane-wave cutoff, Γ-point sampling). In all three systems silver remains mononuclear, with average coordination numbers of 2.6–2.9 and only transient Ag–Ag contacts (present in 2–9% of frames at a 3.2 Å cutoff). The composition of the coordination shell is strongly sequence-dependent: His–Met–Pro is dominated by the His imidazole nitrogen (0.48 contacts per Ag) and nitrate oxygen (0.57), whereas His–Pro–Met is dominated by the Met thioether sulfur (0.73) with nitrate largely excluded (0.16); Pro–His–Met shows an intermediate, mixed N/S/nitrate shell and the largest peptide conformational rearrangement (heavy-atom RMSD 6.1 Å, radius of gyration 5.8 Å). Nitrate and water exchange on ∼0.2–1 ps timescales, while peptide N/S donors remain bound for several to tens of picoseconds. These results demonstrate that, at fixed composition, sequence order controls which donors are presented to Ag(I) and therefore the speciation from which silver nanomaterials nucleate.

papers.title: Monomer sequence influences electron transport in aromatic amide foldamers
papers.abstract: Sequence encodes structure and function in biomolecules, but whether monomer order influences electron transport in synthetic foldamers remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigate aromatic amide foldamers built from a peptide-inspired secondary amide and its N-methylated peptoid-inspired analogue. Single molecule conductance measurements reveal that the all-secondary-amide foldamer exhibits a well-defined conductance state (~10-3.8 G0), comparable to the substantially shorter secondary-amide building block (~10-3.7 G0), whereas incorporation of N-methylated units produces lower or less-defined conductance features. Notably, foldamers with identical composition but different sequence arrangements exhibit distinct conductance distributions, demonstrating that sequence order influences electron transport. Displacement and flicker noise analyses indicate compact junction geometries with substantial throughspace contributions, and the all secondary amide foldamer responds most strongly to changes in applied bias and molecular concentration. Computational modeling using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, density functional theory (DFT), and nonequilibrium Green's function (NEGF)-DFT calculations provide insight into sequencedependent conformational variability. Overall, this work demonstrates that oligomerization can generate electron transport behavior that cannot be inferred directly from isolated monomer properties and establishes monomer order as a design variable for molecular electronics.

papers.title: Probabilistic Design and Safety-Constrained Optimization of a Firewater-Powered Portable Valve Actuation System
papers.abstract: Almost every hazardous facility owns a pressurized, regularly inspected source of hydraulic power: its firewater system. This study asks whether a portable water-hydraulic operator driven through a fire hose can stroke seized or stiff valves without overloading the stem or taking the water that firefighting needs, and which design and operating rules make that likely. A Monte Carlo model with an explicit hydraulic circuit, motor leakage, a relief valve and the surge on stall is evaluated on 200,000 draws; every added mechanism can be switched off, recovering the earlier first-order model exactly. Under assumed input distributions a baseline tool (200 cc, 250:1, 60 gpm) completes the stroke in 75% of the draws but without exceeding the allowable stem torque in only 63%, because a median surge of 45 psi accompanies the stall; a stroke needs about 1,600 L of water. A hose-side accumulator and a relief chart set from the stem strength reduce the over-torque probability to 1% (motor speed at most 3,000 rpm) at a cost of 3 to 9 percentage points of safe strokes, of which a slow creep flow at the start and end of travel recovers 4 to 6. The surge model reproduces classical water-hammer results. The optimum holds out of sample but not under a stem 30% weaker than its data sheet (14% over-torque), and the 2 firefighting reserve is protected only if the spare flow of the source is known. The results are simulation outputs under assumed priors, not measurements.

papers.title: Measuring chemical safety and refusal in language models
papers.abstract: A language model can decline a chemistry question for several reasons. It may detect a safety concern, fail to identify the molecule, or lack the facts needed to answer. When it does answer, the response may still be wrong or incomplete. Chemical safety evaluations need to distinguish these outcomes before interpreting differences between models. We propose a framework for doing so, using established practices from cheminformatics: verified identities and reference answers, suitable controls and baselines, independent validation, and statistics that account for related molecules and repeated measurements. We examine chemical safety studies, including SynthRefusal within onepot-Bench 0, ChemSafetyBench, DualChem, and broader scientific safety benchmarks. Eight detailed audits and additional methods readings identify both effective controls and gaps in the evidence. Our reanalyses reproduce large effects of molecular identifiers in ChemIDBench and system prompts in XSTest. A calculation from DualChem shows how excluding tool failures changes the apparent benefit of web access. Because these studies measure different outcomes, we do not pool their results. We propose an experiment that holds legitimate chemical safety questions fixed while changing the identifier and the information supplied to the model. It measures refusal and answer quality together, with separate judgments of whether withholding is appropriate. Separate extensions would test unsafe compliance and, where relevant, practical execution. Each proposed control addresses a specific uncertainty in interpreting model behavior.

papers.title: Beyond Ion Features: Resolving Ion Redundancy for LC–HRMS/MS
papers.abstract: Untargeted LC–HRMS/MS workflows frequently represent the same molecular entity through multiple ion features, including adducts, multimers, dehydrated species, and signals compatible with in-source fragmentation. This ion redundancy can propagate into downstream analyses, increasing apparent molecular-network complexity and contributing to unannotated features. To address this issue, we developed two workflows integrated into Compound Discoverer. The unresolved workflow enables structured export of MS2 spectra in MGF format with matched quantitative data, metadata, and an audit trail, whereas the resolved workflow performs ionredundancy resolution and representative-feature selection before export. The approach was evaluated using two reference-standard panels, comprising phytocannabinoids and novel psychoactive substances (NPS), and applied to plant, biological, and in vitro drug-metabolism datasets. Ion-redundancy patterns varied across chemical classes and analytical contexts, encompassing alternative ion species, predefined mass-difference relationships, and MS2-child matches, identified when the m/z of a lower-mass coeluting feature matched a product ion in the MS2 spectrum of a higher-mass feature. Across applications, the resolved workflow reduced exported MGF entries by 18.2–36.1%. In molecular networking, the workflow reshaped molecular-family composition and connectivity through spectral-quality filtering, feature removal, and representative-ion reassignment, while preserving chromatographically distinct features lacking sufficient evidence of redundancy. These findings suggest that LC–HRMS/MS feature space does not necessarily reflect the underlying molecular space. By addressing ion redundancy before spectral export, these workflows provide a conservative and traceable framework that reduces analytical complexity, addresses a potential contributor to the apparent dark metabolome, and enables a more interpretable spectral representation that may better reflect underlying molecular diversity.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal Decoupling of Antimicrobial and Osteogenic Cues for Tissue Regeneration: Evidence, Design Windows, and a Validation Roadmap
papers.abstract: Infected bone defects require two outcomes that can conflict at the same site: reduction of biofilm-associated bacterial burden, which usually needs high local antimicrobial exposure, and regeneration of vascularised bone, which needs viable progenitor cells and a resolving immune environment. Biomaterials that present antimicrobial and regenerative cues together are clinically established, but in some systems the exposure needed to act on biofilm may approach the tolerance of host cells. This targeted narrative review develops spatiotemporal decoupling, the separation of cues in time, location or activation condition, as a design hypothesis rather than a proven superior strategy. It (i) defines decoupling operationally and classifies published platforms accordingly; (ii) frames the therapeutic window as a measurable exposure problem, defines exposure metrics, and specifies what must be measured to compute them; (iii) maps four overlapping biological domains (bacterial burden, inflammation, vascular supply, bone formation) to cues, controls and readouts, with each design rule tagged by evidence status; (iv) examines the immuneosteogenic–vascular network as a hypothesis map; (v) positions bioactive glasses and glass-ceramics as a testable platform opportunity, separating what has been shown from what is inferred; and (vi) sets out validation gates and author-proposed reporting recommendations. Most evidence reviewed is mechanistic or preclinical, and matched comparisons against equal-payload co-delivery remain the decisive missing experiment.

papers.title: Signed Kekulé structures and Hückel gap-closure thresholds in phenylenes
papers.abstract: Naphthalene and biphenylene have comparable Hückel HOMO–LUMO gaps, yet no positive bond couplings close the gap of naphthalene, whereas coordinated changes of 18.9% close that of biphenylene. We define the gap-closure threshold as the smallest maximum relative change of existing bond couplings needed to close the gap. At equal reference couplings, it depends only on the signed Kekulé polynomial: it is maximal when all Kekulé structures share one sign, is fixed by a polynomial equation when one structure has the minority sign, and is otherwise bounded. Phenylenes with the same sequence of linear and angular annelations share the threshold, even when their gaps differ. For linear [N ]phenylenes it approaches π2/[4(N + 1)2]; angular [3]phenylene closes only by breaking mirror symmetry. In a bond-length model, the threshold ranks closure energies better than the relaxed gap does, and the predicted closing distortion is nearly the steepest-descent direction of the B3LYP Kohn–Sham gap (cosine 0.989).

papers.title: Advanced High-Throughput Characterization of Nanoporous Materials using Pore Graphs
papers.abstract: Nanoporous materials databases now contain millions of structures, yet the tools for characterizing their void spaces have not kept pace. Standard descriptors such as largest cavity diameter and pore limiting diameter are global quantities that conflate local pore geometry with inter-pore connectivity, and can hide distinct pores and network topology behind a single number. We present Mofography, an open-source Python/Rust library that recasts pore characterization as a three-dimensional image-processing problem. It segments the void space into non-overlapping pore regions, connects them at shared windows, and constructs a pore graph that decouples local properties (size, shape, chemistry) from global topology (percolation, connectivity). Global textural properties are obtained as queries on this graph and agree with those from Zeo++ and Pore-Blazer across a diverse set of metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), while remaining traceable to individual pores and windows. The same representation supports pore-resolved pore size distributions, multi-modal pore-type clustering, window detection across periodic boundaries, and percolation and accessibility analysis. To demonstrate its utility for material discovery, we develop a workflow integrated with Mofography to screen favorable pores in MOFs for xylene isomer separations and validate selected candidates with grand canonical Monte Carlo simulations. The results reveal how accessibility and competing pore environments influence whether local preferences translate into material performance. By linking global textural properties to local pore environments and their connectivity, Mofography provides a unique platform for interpreting structure–property relationships and accelerating nanoporous materials discovery.

papers.title: Predicting Active and Inactive Targets of Small Molecules from ChEMBL Data Using the Polypharmacology Browser PPB4
papers.abstract: Drug-like molecules often interact with multiple biological targets, which must be identified during drug development. Various models spanning classical machine learning, deep learning and artificial intelligence, predict active targets of a query molecule based on its structural similarity to target annotated molecules from drug-target interaction databases such as ChEMBL. Herein we report on the Polypharmacology Browser PPB4, a deep neural network trained on ChEMBL35. In contrast to its predecessor PPB3 and related tools which only return lists of probably active targets, PPB4 also lists probably inactive targets, as well as targets that are probably both active and inactive if the query molecule is similar to both active and inactive compounds for that target. Two prospective case studies illustrate the use of PPB4, which returns every predicted target together with the list of nearest neighbor molecules marked as active on that target in the training data. PPB4 is freely available at https://ppb4.gdb.tools.

papers.title: OpenASChem: A Data Analysis Software Suite for High-Throughput Affinity Selection Mass Spectrometry
papers.abstract: Summary: Affinity selection mass spectrometry (AS-MS) enables ligand discovery from pooled compound libraries, but compound signal assignment and cross-run review remain labor-intensive as screens expand across multiple targets. Here, we present OpenASChem, an open-source platform with a graphical interface for compoundcentric analysis of high-throughput pull-down ASMS screens. OpenASChem integrates standardguided peak matching, cross-run quantification and enrichment analysis with interactive chromatographic review. We evaluated OpenASChem using mixed-standard and AS-MS screening datasets acquired in our laboratory. In the mixed-standard benchmark, OpenASChem recovered 248 expectedpositive compounds compared with 204 using an XCMS-based workflow, a 21.6% increase, with no calls from the two pools expected to remain below the enrichment threshold. In a four-pool ASMS screen against eight proteins, it reported 13 candidate associations, including all five previously reported hits and two additional chromatographically supported candidates, while reducing candidates not supported by manual review by 86.7%. An interactive summary integrates results across pools and targets, helping laboratories assess chromatographic evidence and prioritize compounds for follow-up validation.

papers.title: Training of Neural Network Machine Learning Potentials for Activation Barrier Calculations in Predicting Growth Modes of Deposited Metals
papers.abstract: Machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are opening many new opportunities to extend the capabilities of computational materials science. MLIPs deliver increased throughput and simulations at time and length scales beyond first principles density functional theory (DFT), while maintaining near-DFT accuracy, thus allowing unravelling of chemical processes not accessible with DFT. In this work, we present an approach to training a neural network MLIP using DeepMD-kit software that delivers both accurate energies and forces, suitable for determining activation energies via nudged elastic band calculations. We use the deposition of metals on substrates, in particular Ru and Cu on TaN for semiconductor device interconnects, as the example system, for which activation barriers of metal atom migration at the metal-substrate interface and on the metal deposit are important in understanding the evolution of the film morphology during deposition. The structure of the metal-substrate interface directly affects the performance of devices, from catalysts and sensors, to interconnects and contacts in nanoelectronics. The activation barrier energies from our MLIP for all sizes of metal atom deposits reproduce the DFT activation energies to within an average error of 0.08 eV (6%) for Cu and 0.23 eV (19%) for Ru. The trends of the DFT barriers are preserved by the MLIP and the computing time is reduced from days using high performance computing to minutes on a personal laptop. This allows us to assess the activation energies for complex processes such as the transition of a 2-layer metal cluster to a 3-layer cluster-a key step in metal island growth. Morphology evolution occurs on multiple scales, from initial nucleation, to layer growth and cluster ripening. By demonstrating that MLIPs can be used to accurately and rapidly deliver activation energies for the relevant atomic scale processes, a multi-scale predictive atomistic model of metal deposition and growth chemistry becomes feasible.

papers.title: Mechanosensitive ion transport in hexagonal boron nitride nanopores
papers.abstract: In biological systems, mechanical strain can trigger strong changes in ion conductance and signaling, yet in synthetic nanopores, achieving similar mechanosensitive behavior has been a significant challenge. Here, we demonstrate that subtle mechanical strain can induce strong modulation of ionic current in small hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) nanopores. Using hydrostatic pressure to apply small lateral strain to free-standing single-layer h-BN membranes featuring triangular sub-1-nm nanopores, we observed ion conductance modulation exceeding 1 30% under 0.5% strain. We attribute this response to the strain-dependent interplay of ionpore and ion-water interactions within the nanopore. The measured mechanosensitivity values also agreed strongly with those obtained from modeling of strain-tunable transport in ensembles of h-BN nanopores. These findings establish a framework for developing strain-responsive membranes for applications in molecular separations and sensing.

papers.title: Optical Properties of Different Chemistries of Natural and Synthetic Melanin
papers.abstract: Melanin, a ubiquitous black pigment, consists of at least five chemistries identified by the starting monomers involved in its polymerization. Natural melanin may also contain other components, such as lipids and proteins, that can affect its optical properties. Melanin is known for its high refractive index and broadband absorption. However, most optical-property observations are based on measurements of eumelanin-based chemistry. In this study, we used spectroscopic ellipsometry to measure the complex refractive index over a broad wavelength range (380–1700 nm) for the three main melanin chemistries: eumelanin, allomelanin, and pheomelanin. We compared the complex refractive indices of these materials with values obtained from UV absorption measurements, using an integrating sphere to minimize scattering effects. Our results show that melanin chemistry strongly influences optical properties. Pheomelanin from human red hair has the lowest absorption and refractive index, while poly(L-3,4-dihydroxyphenylalanine) (PDOPA; a polydopamine-based eumelanin chemistry) has the highest refractive index and absorption. We also observed variation in the optical properties of pheomelanin samples extracted from human red hair and rooster feathers. Thus, variations in melanin composition affect both the optical and thermal properties of melanin, highlighting the need to identify its precise chemistry in natural systems to understand melanin's impact on function and performance.

papers.title: Plasmon-Enhanced Nanosensing: From Single Proteins to Therapeutic Nanoparticles
papers.abstract: Plasmonic nanosensing, in which plasmon-enhanced near fields are used for single-molecule detection andsingle-particlebiosensing,hasmovedbeyondensemblerefractive-indexmeasurements.Itnow interrogatesindividualproteins,transientmolecularcomplexes,photoexcitedredoxpartnersand heterogeneous therapeutic nanoparticles. Its defining advantage is not a universal detection limit. It is the ability to concentrate optical energy into nanometric volumes and to transduce properties that ensemble averagesconceal.Localizedsurfaceplasmonresonance,surface-enhancedRamanandinfrared spectroscopy, plasmon-enhanced fluorescence, nanoaperture optical trapping and hybrid optical–electrical nanopores each provide different observables: binding-induced spectral shifts, vibrational fingerprints, residence-time distributions, conformational fluctuations and particle-specific electrical signatures. This review synthesizes the electromagnetic, thermal and transport physics that govern these observables. It thenevaluatesrepresentativeapplications,fromsingle-proteindynamicsandweakprotein–protein interactionstowavelength-dependentcytochromec–cytochromecoxidasekinetics,single-virus detection, adeno-associated virus genome loading, extracellular vesicles and lipid nanoparticles. Unlike earlierreviewsorganizedbydeviceorbyenhancementmechanism,thisreviewtreatsplasmonic nanosensing as an inverse problem and a metrology problem. Particular attention is given to three issues: separatingmolecularheterogeneityfromspatiallyheterogeneousenhancement;separatinggenuine photochemistryfromphotothermalandresonance-detuningartifacts;andcorrectingclass-dependent capture before event counts are reported as sample composition.Closed-form illustrations show how capture bias and device-to-device variation can produce convincing but incorrect results. A minimuminformationreportingchecklistandamaturitymapareproposedsothatplasmonicsingle-entity measurementscanprogressfrom informativeresearchprobestotransferable,orthogonallyvalidated analytical methods.

papers.title: vibyverse: an integrated computational chemistry ecosystem developed through agentic engineering
papers.abstract: We describe the vibyverse, developed by agentic engineering, comprising vibe-sketcher for chemical structures and reaction schemes, vibe-qc for electronic-structure calculations, vibe-scheduler for execution and retrieval, vibe-viewer for inspection and presentation, and the Quantum Visualization Format (QVF) for structured exchange. The workflow starts with reaction design in vibe-sketcher, submission through vibe-scheduler, calculation with vibe-qc, and inspection and analysis in vibe-viewer, with scientific data transferred through QVF. We examine the responsibilities of each component and the information that must survive their connections, including charge, multiplicity, geometry, method settings, runtime identity and result provenance. Source inspection identifies implemented interfaces and their compatibility requirements. A Diels–Alder preparation example connects an editable scheme and preoptimized structures to validated QVF and viewer exports. The executed numerical workflow proceeds through MACE geometry optimization, PBE/def2-SVP refinement and DLPNO-CCSD(T) endpoint energies. A proposed water-on-boronnitride example would extend the workflow to periodic structures. The molecular optimization and Hessian use existing PBE routes without an added dispersion correction. Both Hessian stencils identify minima for all three molecules. With an explicit restrictedreference contract, the correlated electronic energy of cyclohexene relative to butadiene and ethene is −190.547 kJ mol−1. Changing from TightPNO to NormalPNO shifts it by +0.187 kJ mol−1. The viewer reproduces both electronic reaction energies from the archived endpoints, in agreement with an independent stoichiometric sum. All data supporting this study are openly available from the Zenodo repository under accession number 23976098 at https://zenodo.org/records/23976098.

papers.title: How do the research evaluation requirements of Chinese universities, which are oriented towards paper publication, affect the development of chemistry graduate students and faculty members?
papers.abstract: Research assessment oriented towards publication has become an important feature of academic work, profoundly shaping the expectations for research productivity and the career advancement trajectories of researchers. However, its impact on graduate education in chemistry and the cultivation of independent researchers still requires further exploration. This qualitative study examines how publication requirements affect chemistry professors and graduate students in Chinese universities. Specifically, this research investigates how journal classification/ranking and publication goals intervene in the daily guidance practices of departments and mentors, how young teachers and graduate students respond to these expectations, and how assessment practices affect research autonomy, task allocation, researcher development, and career planning. Through thematic analysis of interview data, this study identified the institutional requirements, the mentoring practices of mentors, and their impact on the research training of graduate students. The research results revealed three interrelated processes: Firstly, the requirements of institutions for high-quality paper publication, access to research funds, and periodic performance evaluations were transformed into expectations within the research groups, in some cases even evolving into graduation requirements exceeding the official standards of the school; Secondly, teachers' coping strategies were to prioritize research projects with more predictable publication outcomes, while graduate students had to deal with the expectations of their mentors that might affect their research priorities and the completion of their degrees; Thirdly, these practices shaped the opportunities for students to explore independent research questions, participate in scientific decision-making, and plan their careers. The interviews also revealed contrasting results, including the improvement of research skills, supportive mentoring practices, and the loss of employment opportunities due to delayed graduation.

papers.title: Goggles On, Bagels Out: A Randomized Hazard Hunt in a Browser Replica of a Real Teaching Laboratory
papers.abstract: Students are usually introduced to the layout of a teaching laboratory, and to where its eyewash, shower, extinguisher and waste containers are, during a safety lecture on the first day of lab, a session that also covers the syllabus and the first experiment. I built a walkable, browser-based replica of the actual laboratory my students use, from a phone scan and photographs of the room, and turned it into a safety inspection. Each time a student opens the virtual lab, five hazards drawn at random from thirty-one are hidden in the room. Every hazard is tied to a rule in the course syllabus, from a drink on a bench or a fume hood sash left wide open to a classmate without goggles or a sleeve on fire. Students find and click each hazard, read what is wrong and what to do, carry out hands-on tasks such as dropping a used needle in the sharps container or guiding a splashed classmate to the eyewash, answer an emergency question, evacuate by the posted route when a fire alarm sounds, and finish with a report of what they found and missed. The inspection sits between a safety prelab page and the graded safety quiz in the learning management system; students must score at least 70% on the quiz before they are admitted to the lab room. The replica runs in an ordinary web browser with no headset or installation, downloads in about 31 MB, and was built by one instructor with a phone, free or low-cost software and generative AI tools. This report describes how the replica was built, how the hazards were designed and how the module fits into a course. Student outcomes will be evaluated in a later study.

papers.title: Freestanding FeS2-Integrated Reduced Graphene Oxide Aerogels Enhance Cathode-to-Cell Electron Transfer in Three-Dimensional Living Cathodes
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) living cathodes can retain dense biofilms, but cells within porous scaffolds may remain electronically underutilized. Here, we integrate FeS2 nanoparticles throughout a freestanding reduced graphene oxide (rGO) aerogel, combining interconnected macropores, continuous electron pathways, and spatially distributed FeS2 interfaces within a living cathode. This architecture provides three complementary functions: 3D biofilm retention, low-resistance cathode-to-cell electron delivery, and greater availability of intracellular reducing equivalents for fumarate reduction by Shewanella oneidensis MR-1. Compared to pristine rGO, FeS2-rGO generated a ~ 12-fold higher cathodic current density, accelerated complete fumarate depletion within 50 h, and reached 67% Faradaic efficiency to succinate. FeS2-rGO also exhibited a 2.4~4.1-fold higher biomass-normalized succinate partial current, the lowest fitted interfacial resistance, and the highest NADH/NAD+ ratio. Less than 2% of the loaded Fe dissolved, as measured by ICP-OES, while the characteristic FeS2-associated diffraction features were retained after operation. Mechanistically, mutant strain responses further showed that FeS2 strengthened electron transfer through the native outer membrane cytochrome-CymA network. By positioning electronically connected FeS2 interfaces throughout a freestanding porous electrode, this work combines long-range scaffold conduction with enhanced local, pathway-dependent electron uptake in a 3D living cathode.

papers.title: Protonation-state-dependent charge transfer to solvent in aqueous L-cysteine probed by resonant Auger–Meitner spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Charge-transfer-to-solvent (CTTS) couples electronic, nuclear, and solvent dynamics on femtosecond timescales. In biologically relevant L-cysteine, resolving how protonation and local hydrogen bonding influence CTTS upon resonant excitation remains challenging. Sulfur KLL resonant Auger–Meitner spectroscopy qualitatively resolves different final states separated in kinetic energy. These include localized excited states, delocalized CTTS states, and the charge-transfer continuum, enabling direct identification of different decay channels in L-cysteine. At pH 12, the dianion exhibits a pronounced charge-transfer channel extending below the ionization threshold, negligible at pH 5. Transition-potential density functional theory and Born–Oppenheimer molecular dynamics link this to enhanced thiolate hydrogen-bond coordination, revealing a delocalized core-excited state nearly degenerate with the bright localized resonance. A Fano-based core-hole-clock approach, accounting for coherent population of the localized state and charge-transfer continuum, yields a charge-transfer time of 43± 8 fs, compared with 15± 2 fs from conventional core-hole-clock analysis, highlighting the importance of accounting for direct excitation into the chargetransfer continuum and its coherent coupling to the localized core-excited state when extracting charge-transfer times. Together, these results establish resonant Auger–Meitner spectroscopy with Fano-based analysis as a general strategy for probing protonation-and solvation-dependent ultrafast electronic delocalization in aqueous biomolecules.

papers.title: Toward Chemical Accuracy in Biomolecular Simulations through Data-Driven Many-Body Potentials: III. A Library of Amino Acid Building Blocks
papers.abstract: Extending data-driven many-body potentials to peptides and proteins requires reusable building blocks that capture the chemical diversity of amino acids. Building on the many-body expansion (MBE) of the energy, we construct an intramolecular MB-nrg library for all 20 natural amino-acid residues by combining physics-based interactions with machine-learned (ML) n-body terms trained on DLPNO-CCSD(T) n-mer reference data and described by permutationally invariant polynomials. Covalently bonded functional groups define the bodies of the MBE, allowing each ML term to be reused wherever the same chemically defined nmer occurs. Without training on whole-dipeptide energies, the assembled MB-nrg potentials predict gas-phase Ramachandran potential energy surfaces with a pooled root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) of 1.26 kcal/mol relative to DLPNO-CCSD(T), compared with 6.65 and 5.43 kcal/mol for Amber ff14SB and ff19SB force fields, respectively. Because the MB-nrg potentials are modular, the remaining deviations from the DLPNO-CCSD(T) reference can be systematically analyzed within the MBE framework and addressed by expanding the library with additional nonbonded and higher-body terms, as demonstrated for asparagine. The library thus provides an initial set of reusable n-body building blocks for peptide potentials and a blueprint for their systematic refinement and expansion toward coupled-cluster accuracy in biomolecular simulations.

papers.title: Remote N‑Substituent‑Tuned Dichotomous Diradical Scission Enables Photocatalytic Divergent Rearrangement of Allylic Aminophosphines
papers.abstract: Organophosphorus compounds are widely prevalent in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and functional materials, and phosphoranyl radicals represent a versatile platform for the construction of these valuable molecules. Although the selectivity of α- and β-scission dictates the reaction outcomes of phosphoranyl radical transformations, established strategies for tuning such fragmentation are confined to monoradical systems and rely on local structural modification at the phosphorus center. Herein, we realize remote N-substituent-controlled switching between α- and βscission pathways of phosphorus–carbon triplet diradicals and apply this concept in a visible-light energy transfer photocatalytic divergent rearrangement of allylic aminophosphines to access two structurally significant organophosphorus skeletons. Computational studies reveal that the electronic properties of N-substituents govern the geometries of phosphoranyl radicals: N-alkoxy substituents favour α-scission, whereas N-sulfonyl substituents promote β-scission. This work provides new mechanistic insights into heteroatom diradical reactivity and broadens the available tools for divergent synthesis of organophosphorus compounds.

papers.title: False Confidence in Generative Samplers: Exact Physical References Expose Hidden Errors and Diagnostic Blindness
papers.abstract: Learned samplers are increasingly proposed for equilibrium sampling and free energies in chemistry, and they are usually judged by self-normalized diagnostics such as the effective sample size (ESS). We show with an elementary proposition that these diagnostics are structurally invariant to the Boltzmann mass α of unvisited basins: conditioned on not proposing a basin, the importance weights follow the law of the truncated system, so the ESS stays high while the free energy shifts by −kBT log(1 − α) and the nominal deltamethod interval contracts around the biased value, yielding asymptotically zero coverage. In a toy double well where one basin holds 49.9% of the mass, a proposal putting mass 10−6 on that basin achieves a median ESS of 98% but covers the exact logZ in 0% of 400 runs. On exactly enumerated Sherrington-Kirkpatrick instances (n = 24), nominal 95% intervals from masked diffusion and a GFlowNet cover the truth in only 8% and 47% of runs at β = 2, while classical estimators and an autoregressive network (VAN-MADE) stay near 95%. A reverse check that scores the proposal on draws from an independent reference sampler flags the dropped basin where the forward Jensen gap is blind. We demonstrate this on a continuous molecular model: a RealNVP Boltzmann generator trained on the alanine dipeptide Ramachandran landscape drops the C7ax basin (8.1% mass), reporting a median ESS of 79% with only 10% coverage, while the reverse check detects the omission (Grev = 11.7 nats). Finally, we size the bound on macromolecular systems (chignolin, Trpcage, LJ38), contrasting single-trajectory kinetic trapping with converged Anton and NMR equilibrium baselines to show that dropped macroscopic states shift free energies by 0.68 to 1.02 kcal/mol, exceeding lead-optimization thresholds.

papers.title: Lost in Chemical Space: Local Open-Source Large Language Models Display Model-Dependent Adherence to Reference Data in Molecular Generation
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate drug-like molecules and may be used locally in drug discovery projects where confidentiality and intellectual-property constraints preclude the use of external APIs. Weight quantization enables deployment of large open-source LLMs on limited hardware, but its impact on molecular generation and on the ability of models to follow reference chemical spaces remains poorly understood. Here, we evaluated Gemma-4-31B, GPT-OSS-120B, Mistral-Small-4-119B, and Qwen-3.6-35B-A3B at the BF16 (original precision), Q8, Q6, and Q4 quantization levels in two molecular generation tasks. The models were prompted either to generate small molecules without constraints or to generate drug-like molecules conditioned on 69 reference kinase inhibitors provided in-context. Quantization increased inference throughput in a model-dependent manner, with the largest gains, up to 24-fold increase in performance, occurring for Gemma-4-31B and Qwen-3.6-35B-A3B. In the task of unconstrained generation, model quantization did not affect molecular validity, uniqueness, drug-likeness, diversity and synthesizability. In the task of reference-guided generation, however, the models displayed markedly different levels of adherence to the provided chemical space. Gemma-4-31B was the only model that consistently generated small molecules similar to the reference compounds at all precision levels. Mistral-Small-4-119B and Qwen-3.6-35B-A3B failed to generate small molecules according to the reference chemical space. GPT-OSS-120B showed adherence to the reference molecules at BF16, Q8, and Q6, but lost the capacity to generate molecules in the desired chemical space at the Q4 quantization level. These results show that quantization can substantially improve the performance of local LLMs for molecular generation without compromising output quality, although model selection and validation is essential for guided exploration of the chemical space.

papers.title: Chemistry-Informed Transfer and Interaction-Resolved Learning Towards Data-Efficient Materials Exploration
papers.abstract: Optimizing synthesis parameters for new thin-film materials is slow and often relies on intuition and trial and error.
