XinPilot addresses this project-level interoperability problem through a chemist-designed Windows desktop workspace that brings together chemical stock information, synthesis records, reaction schemes, expected products, and analytical evidence within a portable project. Working alongside existing instrument-control systems, XinPilot generates worklists for the Tecan Fluent and Opentrons Flex and OT2 liquid handlers, records manual reagent additions, and imports transfer records from other liquid-handling workflows in Excel, CSV, and JSON-compatible formats. These results can be combined into a unified reaction map when they use the same plate format. Chemical IDs and reaction-to-analysis well mappings preserve the relationships among reaction compositions, expected products, and analytical samples. Integrated PyParse-based analysis allows chemists to inspect UV chromatograms, mass spectra, and integrated peaks. Chemists can also reassign product peaks for individual experiments while retaining the automated assignments for other experiments, without requiring coding knowledge. Experimental records, original imported files, and supported analytical inspection data can be retained in portable .xinpilot.zip projects for subsequent review, handover, and synthesis planning. An experimentally executed Suzuki–Miyaura campaign combining Tecan dispensing, manual additions, Opentrons aqueous workup and LC-MS review is presented as a tutorial-style demonstration of the workflow. Additional experimental examples independently performed by other chemists are provided in the Supporting Information. A separate demonstration uses published experimental data from 192 Chemspeed reactions. These data were converted into XinPilot-compatible transfer records and imported into two projects. Reaction structures were also generated using XinPilot's Cheminformatics tools, and both projects were exported as portable .xinpilot.zip files. Overall, XinPilot provides an integrated open‑source workspace for generating worklists for parallel synthesis and workup using Tecan and Opentron liquid handlers, facilitating the purity analysis and maintaining traceable links between experimental conditions, reaction products, and analytical results.

papers.title: LiteratureAgent: Linking Perovskite Literature to Database Expansion, Knowledge Graphs, and Predictive Modeling
papers.abstract: Scientific literature contains experimental knowledge that is difficult to combine and reuse across publications. Here, we present LiteratureAgent, a workflow that retrieves publications, extractsstructuredexperimentalinformation,retainssourcelinks,integratesrecordsintoa database, and supports knowledge-graph analysis and predictive modeling. Applied to perovskite photovoltaics, the final web-expansion campaign processed 910 publications. Across the researchgroupPDFcollectionandallweb-expansionstages,LiteratureAgentadded1,843records, expanding the Perovskite Database from 43,398 to 45,241 records. These additions came from 1,396 source identities: 1,373 identified by DOI and 23 by source filename. Adding accepted literature-derived training records improved power conversion efficiency (PCE) prediction on a separate test set of newly extracted records and produced little change on the historical test set. Stability-prediction changes were smaller and depended on the outcome being predicted. The workflow connectspublished experimentalinformation with database integration,knowledge graphs, and modeling while retaining links that allow the extracted information to be checked.

papers.title: Detection of Tiludronic Acid in Equine Hair and Its Segmental Analysis Following Administration
papers.abstract: A method for the detection of tiludronic acid in equine hair was developed and applied to investigate its distribution in hair following administration of Tildren®. Hair samples collected from seven horses at 2-7 months post-administration were analysed using ultra-performance liquid chromatography tandem high-resolution mass spectrometry (UPLC–MS/HRMS). The method achieved an estimated limit of detection of 0.1 pg/mg. Tiludronic acid was detected in all hair samples collected following administration. Segmental analysis revealed non-uniform distribution along the hair shaft, with the highest concentrations observed in discrete segments corresponding to the time of drug exposure. The position of the concentration peak shifted towards distal end with increasing post-administration time according to the normal hair growth rate. These findings demonstrate the incorporation of tiludronic acid into equine hair via systemic circulation and suggest that segmental hair analysis may provide information regarding the timing of bisphosphonate exposure in horses.

papers.title: Enhanced Quantum Simulations Reveal Conformation-Controlled, Site-Resolved Proton Binding in Biliverdin
papers.abstract: For a molecule with several titratable sites, a measured pKa reports a change in the number of bound protons, but not the population of each tautomer. The biological chromophore biliverdin (BV) is a longstanding example: the protonation of its four pyrrole nitrogens controls its photoactivity, yet the reported pKa values vary by about two units, and ring C is typically assumed deprotonated in neutral BV without a site-resolving measurement. BV is also flexible, so its protonation microstates and its conformers form coupled ensembles: the shape of the molecule changes how tightly it binds the proton. Here, we compute the macroscopic pKa of BV in explicit water and the populations of its four neutral tautomers, from the site-resolved pKa of the four rings. Enhanced quantum-mechanical simulations follow a proton into bulk water, and the free energies of proton transfer between rings and of ring rotation connect all protonation states in one thermodynamically consistent network. In the locked-helix conformation that dominates in water, BV has a macroscopic pKa of 4.0, and its four nitrogens are almost equally basic (site pKa values of 4.5 for rings B and C and 4.9 for rings A and D). No single tautomer dominates: the tautomers deprotonated at rings B and C each make up 36% of neutral BV, and those deprotonated at rings A and D 14% each. Opening the helix at ring D, as in bacteriophytochromes, raises the macroscopic pKa to 6.4 and shifts the neutral form almost entirely to the ring B (71%) and ring C (27%) tautomers. The conformation of BV thus controls its proton binding more than the choice of ring.

papers.title: Plasma-Enhanced Atomic Layer Deposition and Substrate Engineering of Low-Resistivity Ultrathin MoCx Films for Advanced Interconnect Applications
papers.abstract: As Copper (Cu) interconnect dimensions continue to shrink, conventional tantalum/tantalum nitride (Ta/TaN) liner/barrier layers occupy an increasing fraction of the available interconnect volume and introduce additional electrical resistance because of their relatively high resistivity. Therefore, a key challenge is to develop ultrathin liner/barrier materials that can maintain low resistivity while providing effective Cu diffusion-barrier performance. In this work, we demonstrate MoC x as a liner-free barrier material using plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD). For this PEALD-grown film, cycloheptatriene molybdenum tricarbonyl, (η 6 -C 7 H 8 )Mo(CO) 3 , was first introduced as a precursor to synthesize ultrathin molybdenum carbide (MoC x ) films. The effects of plasma reactants, plasma power, deposition temperature, film thickness, and substrate types were systematically evaluated to clarify how PEALD process conditions and substrate chemistry influence the electrical performance of ultrathin MoC x films. We observed nucleation differences during the growth based on the substrate; MoC x films deposited on Al 2 O 3 consistently exhibited lower resistivity than those grown on SiO 2 . Using the optimized deposition process, amorphous MoC x films thinner than 5 nm showed resistivities as low as ~230 μΩ·cm without any post-deposition annealing. For reference, current Ta/TaN liner/barrier layers typically exceed 500 μΩ·cm resistivity in the sub-5 nm thickness regime. Sub-5 nm MoC x film also showed good Cu adhesion and effective Cu diffusion-barrier behavior after thermal annealing of up to 500 °C. These results demonstrate the potential of ultrathin amorphous MoC x as a low-resistivity liner-free barrier material for advanced Cu interconnects.

papers.title: Air pollution sensing to urban air quality insight: review of spatially interpolated data products from sensor networks
papers.abstract: Air pollution adversely impacts health globally, disproportionately affecting urban populations. Regulatory monitoring is often too spatially coarse to capture true intra-urban variability, needed to prioritize and guide localized interventions and policies. High-density lower-cost sensor (LCS) networks, mobile monitoring, satellite-derived products, and advanced interpolation techniques are emerging to support higher spatial resolution characterization. However, results from related studies are varied, disconnected across different fields, and as yet with no defined standards or guidance. This review examines the literature from 2005-2025 to systematically compare data collection and modeling pipelines for accuracy and application to the intra-urban challenge. 166 studies from regional to neighborhood scale were analyzed quantitatively on monitoring network characteristics (geographic location, spatial density, target pollutants, study duration) and interpolation modeling approaches (algorithms, predictive covariates, performance metrics). Studies from Europe, Asia, and North America dominated the literature, with particulate matter being the most studied pollutant. While 95% of studies had measurement density below 20,000 km2/device (metro scale), none had sufficient resolution for capturing intra-urban heterogeneity. Modeling approaches shifted over time from primarily geostatistical methods toward increasingly sophisticated machine learning and deep learning techniques incorporating diverse covariates, including meteorology, land use, traffic patterns, and satellite data products. More than measurement density or model complexity, strategic use of both static and dynamic covariates in data driven models was most consistently associated with performance improvement for interpolation of both PM2.5 and NOx. However, major gaps remain including (1) imbalance in data availability geographically, temporally, and across pollutant species, leading to major challenges in assessing and achieving transferability of models globally, (2) limited data availability at appropriate intra-urban scale for most metro areas, (3) lack of evaluation and reporting standards necessary to truly compare performance of different data-model pipelines, and (4) general lack of generating or reporting uncertainty quantification on model outputs, critically needed for interpretability and sensitivity analyses. These gaps point to an urgent need for not only interdisciplinary collaboration and innovation but also discipline-wide guidance that will enable objective assessment of model performance and state-of-the-art, including shared benchmark datasets, standardized evaluation metrics, mandatory unit reporting, and guidelines for complete model specifications.

papers.title: Ensemble of ∆-ML Models for Quantum Chemistry Level of Theory Selection for Interaction Energies
papers.abstract: Ab initio quantum chemical approaches for computing interactions between molecules are useful in a wide range of applications but can be difficult to apply effectively. In particular, variations in cost and accuracy across different levels of theory (method and basis set combinations) makes it challenging to select an appropriate level of theory for a given chemical system. In this work, we train ∆-machine learning models to predict interaction energy errors for 81 levels of theory versus a reference and simple polynomial models to quantify computational cost for a meaningful subset of these methods. We demonstrate how a large language model (LLM) can leverage these models to select appropriate levels of theory and run computations autonomously on distributed resources, significantly reducing the barrier to obtaining accurate interaction energies.

papers.title: Can Two Metals Be Chosen Independently for Electrochemical C–N Coupling?
papers.abstract: Electrochemical C–N coupling could produce urea directly from CO or CO2 and nitrogen oxides under mild conditions. Bimetallic catalysts offer neighboring sites with different binding preferences, but choosing a suitable metal for each intermediate does not necessarily identify the most active pair. We screen 80 ordered A3B surfaces and investigate how metal selection affects reactivity at Zn3M interfaces using DFT transition-state calculations and comparative kinetic modeling. Although *CO and *N preferentially bind to different metals, both retain their metal coordination in the C–N bond-forming transition state. Changing the CO-binding metal therefore affects both CO availability and the coupling barrier. Stronger CO binding can increase coverage while making bond formation more difficult. Zn3Cu has the lowest coupling barrier, but its low CO coverage limits the rate. Zn3Pt has a higher barrier yet gives the highest predicted comparative coupling rate among the alloys studied at U = 0 V versus RHE. This comparison shows how evaluating adsorption or bond-forming kinetics alone can misidentify the preferred metal pair. Considering their combined effects provides a mechanistic basis for prioritizing Zn-based bimetallic catalysts for experimental testing.

papers.title: Brewing Coffee in Ethanol Instead of Water: A Multi-Technique Pilot Study
papers.abstract: Water extracts chlorogenic acids, which contribute to the sourness and bitterness of coffee, together with caffeine. We examined whether a less polar solvent changes that balance. Coarse-ground coffee was brewed for 20 minutes at 75 degrees Celsius in deionized water or 95 percent denatured ethanol and the extracts followed by UV-Vis and infrared spectroscopy; spent grounds from earlier brews were examined by electron and optical microscopy. The caffeine-region band near 275 nm grew about three times faster in water, while the chlorogenic acid region near 320 nm was suppressed proportionally more in ethanol, raising the ratio of the two bands from about 1.2 to 1.5 to 1.7 within a large reading uncertainty, and only the ethanol extracts showed a scattering baseline. Infrared spectra of the undiluted extracts were dominated by the solvents, identified isopropanol as the ethanol’s denaturant and showed no coffee band above the detection limit, and ethanol-brewed grounds more often showed exposed cell walls. These pilot data point to slower, partially selective extraction in ethanol, a direction relevant to lower-acid coffee concentrates, although acidity and caffeine were not measured directly. We also report the measurement problems the data revealed.

papers.title: Making Complete-Basis-Set Extrapolation Visible: A Spreadsheet-Based Activity for Upper-Division Computational Chemistry
papers.abstract: Complete-basis-set (CBS) extrapolation is widely used to estimate electronic energies beyond finite-basis calculations. However, students may encounter it primarily as a formula or automated correction, which obscures how a CBS value is constructed from a sequence of finite-basis energies. We describe a scaffolded Excel activity that makes this process visible by linking energy tables, component extrapolations, and convergence plots. Students first examine Hartree-Fock and correlation-energy convergence in the hydrogen chloride heteronuclear diatomic molecule, compare CBS estimates obtained from alternative extrapolation choices, and then apply the same workflow to the hydrogen fluoride molecule HF. The activity culminates in the calculation and justification of CBS-derived atomization energies and comparison to experiment. This activity is implemented in an upper-division computational chemistry course, and was evaluated through a pre-activity quiz and rubric-based analysis of completed student work. In general, students executed the component extrapolations successfully, yet evaluating sensitivity and justifying a final reported value proved more challenging. The activity offers a transparent and adaptable approach for teaching students to evaluate, rather than merely obtain, computational chemistry results.

papers.title: Probing the dimensionality of confinement in soft nanoreactors through plasmonic nanoparticles nucleation
papers.abstract: Soft nanoscale confinement fundamentally alters the thermodynamic and kinetic landscape of chemical reactions, yet a predictive understanding of how nanoreactor geometry dictates reactivity remains elusive. In this work, we demonstrate that the dimensionality of soft confinement governs the onset of nanomaterial formation. By systematically tuning the water-to-surfactant molar ratio () in self-assembled lecithin reverse micelles, we decoupled the geometry of the host template from its chemical composition. We utilized the in situ nucleation of gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) as an active optical and structural probe across isotropic, anisotropic, and bulk-like spatial domains. Correlating UV-Vis spectroscopy with small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) analyses, we reveal that confinement dimensionality acts as an ON/OFF switch for the reduction of gold ions. Under extreme isotropic confinement (), where the interfacial water network is severely restricted, AuNP formation is suppressed for at least 30 days. Conversely, a hydration-induced structural transition toward anisotropic, wormlike domains () coincides with the onset of AuNP nucleation and yields the highest reaction extent. Finally, further expansion into bulk-like regimes () dilutes the gold precursor within the aqueous domains, attenuating the reaction yield. We rationalize these trends within a phenomenological framework based on classical nucleation theory, highlighting confinement dimensionality as a design parameter for soft nanoreactors and tailored plasmonic nanomaterials.

papers.title: Deposit optics, film thickness and acquisition date confound Raman spectra of dried droplets
papers.abstract: Laboratory mixtures of known composition serve as ground truth for explainable AI (XAI) in vibrational spectroscopy, on the assumption that the class difference is the spectrum of the added molecule. We tested this assumption on a public Raman dataset (785 nm) of 16 dried droplets in a 2 × 2 design: a phosphatidylcholine–phenylalanine–lactate base with or without collagen–mucin and with or without DNA. Besides the 16,107 spectra, we used three records stored with the data but not analysed before: white-light images, LiveTrack focus heights and acquisition timestamps. All inference was at the droplet level. DNA raised the base bands more than any DNA band, and the two added components were not additive (p = 0.032). DNA doubled the Raman yield of the deposit (×1.97, p = 2 × 10-4). Deposit optical density in the white-light images predicted yield across droplets (r = 0.93) and within most droplets, and with optical density in the model the DNA effect fell to ×1.05 (95% CI 0.77–1.44). Focus heights agreed with a thicker film: yield rose with local height in DNA-free deposits but much less with DNA (p = 3 × 10-4). Band ratios to phenylalanine still changed with DNA after adjustment for optical density. Five maps had been acquired 8–15 days after the rest; they showed a 3.2-fold higher background, and acquisition date was predictable from held-out droplets. The DNA class therefore combines deposit optics, a modest compositional change and a date-dependent background. Attributions should be judged against this decomposed effect rather than against reference bands of DNA.

papers.title: Emergence of Glass-like Thermal Transport through Anion-Engineering in Complex Silver Gallium Germanium Chalcogenides
papers.abstract: Designing crystalline materials with ultralow thermal conductivity remains an important challenge for optimizing thermoelectric energy conversion and thermal barrier coatings. Crystalline solids exhibiting glass-like thermal transport are of special interest because they approach the minimum thermal conductivity achievable in an ordered structure. Here, we investigate the ultralow thermal conductivity of crystalline AgGaGeS8-8xSe8x and Ag2-xGa2-xGe2+xS8-8xSe8x (x = 0.00, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00). In these systems, selenium incorporation strongly suppresses crystalline thermal transport, leading to glass-like properties while preserving structural crystallinity. Across all compositions, the ultralow thermal conductivity is associated with a disordered silver substructure characterized by weak Ag–Ch interactions and pronounced anharmonicity, where selenium substitution promotes softening of the silver dynamics. Heat-capacity measurements reveal boson peaks in the endmember compounds, which for AgGaGe3Se8 is significantly more intense and shifted to lower temperature. Together, these results suggest that selenium promotes low-frequency silver vibrations that drive the emergence of glass-like thermal transport. Furthermore, selenium exhibits a pronounced preference for the chalcogen site most strongly interacting with silver, demonstrating that local anion chemistry, rather than average composition, governs the thermal transport response. This selective occupancy provides a structural basis for the emergence of glass-like thermal conductivity at remarkably low selenium contents.

papers.title: Opposite Effects of Removing Ethylene Carbonate from the Electrolyte on Ni-Rich Layered Oxide and Mn-Rich Olivine Phosphate Cathodes
papers.abstract: Ethylene carbonate (EC)-free electrolytes are promising for high-voltage lithium-ion batteries. However, their benefits have been demonstrated primarily for layered oxide cathodes, while their effects on olivine phosphates remain unclear. Here, we show that EC removal accelerates the degradation of LiMn 0.6 Fe 0.4 PO 4 (LMFP64), in contrast to LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 (NCM811). Experiments and first-principles calculations suggest that these opposite responses reflect distinct degradation pathways associated with transition-metal–oxygen (TM–O) covalency. On NCM811, strongly hybridized O 2 p states near the Fermi level favor EC dehydrogenation, initiating degradation; EC removal eliminates this pathway. In contrast, olivine models exhibit weaker TM 3d–O 2 p hybridization, more ionic TM–O bonding, and stronger PF 6 − adsorption at TM sites. Without EC, experiments on LMFP64 reveal salt decomposition before cycling and accelerated degradation; EC otherwise limits anion access to TM sites. These findings show that the effect of EC removal is cathode-dependent and can be rationalized by TM–O covalency.

papers.title: Patent Landscape of Gemini (Dimeric) Surfactants: Cationic Dominance in Intellectual Property versus the Emerging Green Surfactant Narrative
papers.abstract: Gemini (dimeric) surfactants, molecules bearing two hydrophobic tails and two head groups joined by a spacer, have been developed across cationic, anionic, nonionic, zwitterionic, sugar-based, and amino acid-based chemistries over several decades. To the author's knowledge, this review is the first to combine a systematic patent landscape analysis spanning all major charge classes with a survey of current academic research trends to ask a direct question: Does patent activity track academic attention in this field? Drawing on 41 patent families listed in this review (Supporting Information S1) and over 20 peer-reviewed sources, the answer is no. Cationic quaternary ammonium gemini surfactants, driven mainly by enhanced oil recovery, corrosion inhibition, antimicrobial, and personal care applications, account for 25 of the 41 patent families identified here. In contrast, recent academic reviews describe amino acid- and sugar-based gemini surfactants, rather than cationic quaternary ammonium chemistry, as the field's emerging green surfactant direction; searches specifically for arginine- or lysine-specific gemini surfactant patents returned no on-point results. This review further documents a recurring definitional ambiguity between "two hydrophobic tails" and "two charge centres" in patent claim language, a near absence of true single-molecule zwitterionic gemini surfactants, and no agricultural or pesticide adjuvant application identified for any gemini surfactant charge type in either the patent or the academic searches. These findings identify several concrete, evidence-based directions for future synthetic, formulation, and intellectual property work.

papers.title: Radical‑Mediated Formal Anti‑Markovnikov Hydroalkenylation of Unactivated Alkenes Enabled by a Functional Alkenyl‑Radical Surrogate Strategy
papers.abstract: Although alkenyl radicals are conceptually desirable for anti‑Markovnikov hydroalkenylation, their direct addition to unactivated alkenes is kinetically inaccessible owing to their intrinsically low electrophilicity and competing strong hydrogen atom abstraction reactivity. Herein, we establish a novel strategy to realize the first radical‑mediated formal anti‑Markovnikov hydroalkenylation of unactivated alkenes. This approach utilizes the combination of highly electrophilic triphenylphosphonium methyl (TPPM) radicals with weak H atom abstraction reactivity and carbonyl compounds as practical alkenyl‑radical surrogates. The transformation begins with the photocatalytic reduction of bromomethyl triphenylphosphonium bromide to generate TPPM radicals, which add to unactivated alkenes to form carbon-centered radicals that abstract a hydrogen atom from thiophenol. The resulting phosphonium salts subsequently undergo an in‑situ Wittig reaction with carbonyl compounds to furnish the devised hydroalkenylation products. This protocol exhibits good functional group tolerance, broad substrate scope covering both activated and unactivated olefins, and allows late‑stage functionalization of natural product derivatives.

papers.title: Regioselective sugar epimerization to rare sugar on ruthenium surface
papers.abstract: Rare sugars, monosaccharides that occur only rarely in nature, exhibit physicochemical and biological properties distinct from those of naturally abundant sugars such as D-glucose. Their widespread utilization has been hindered by limitations in existing production methods, which rely primarily on equilibrium-constrained biocatalytic cascades or on synthetic approaches requiring multiple steps or organic reagents. Here we show the one-pot heterogeneous catalytic epimerization of methyl glucosides into rare sugar derivatives over supported Ru catalysts under hydrogen atmosphere in water. Among the supported metals examined, Ru uniquely promotes regioselective stereoinversion of 1- O -methyl β-D-glucopyranoside at the C3 position to produce 1- O -methyl β-D-allopyranoside without requiring additional reagents or multistep reactions. Isotopelabeling experiments reveal that dehydrogenation and hydrogenation proceed substantially faster than net epimerization, identifying surface-confined molecular rotation of a keto intermediate as the rate-determining step. Computer simulations further show that the experimentally observed regioselectivity originates from the low rotational free energy barriers and relatively high stability of the keto intermediate on the Ru surface. These findings identify molecular rotational dynamics on catalyst surfaces as a governing principle for stereochemical inversion reactions.

papers.title: Revealing Phase-Controlled Surface Structure in PtNi Nanocatalysts via In-situ Gas Cell Transmission Electron Microscopy
papers.abstract: The rational design of catalysts capable of efficiently utilizing CO2 is critical for sustainable chemical processes. The Super-dry reforming of methane (Super-DRM), which couples dry reforming of methane (DRM) with the reverse water gas shift (RWGS) reactions, offers a promising route to maximize CO2 conversion. Modulating the crystal phase of nanocatalysts offers a powerful strategy to enhance catalytic performance, yet the relationship between bulk phase and catalytic behavior remains poorly understood. A significant obstacle in resolving this issue is obtaining atomic-level insights on the surface structure of phase-controlled catalyst under reaction conditions. In this study, we employ in-situ gas cell transmission electron microscopy to investigate the surface structure of faceted PtNi nanoparticles during Super-DRM at moderate temperatures (550 ℃). Atomic-resolution in-situ observations reveal that the reaction environment induces a pronounced nickel segregation and subsequent coke formation on the surface of disordered A1-PtNi nanoparticles. In contrast, the ordered L10 phase exhibits remarkable resistance to such segregation on its {111} facets. This structural rigidity effectively suppresses coke formation and lowers the kinetic barrier for CH4 activation by 27 kJ/mol compared to the disordered phase. Complemented by in-situ spectroscopy and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, our findings demonstrate that the bulk crystal ordering acts as an anchor for surface structures, governing the catalytic behaviors. This study unveils a direct atomic-level link between crystal ordering, surface reconstruction, and catalytic performance, offering valuable design principles for robust intermetallic catalysts in CO2 utilization.

papers.title: Electrochemically driven thermomechanical energy harvesting
A database-wide atlas of single-crystal filters for thermal neutron beams
papers.abstract: Single-crystal filters that pass thermal neutrons and remove epithermal and fast neutrons and γ rays have been chosen from a handful of materials. For 18 449 inorganic crystals of the Materials Project, the thickness L₀.₈ at which a large single crystal oriented away from Bragg reflections transmits 80% of a 300 K Maxwellian beam over 0.5–3 Å was computed, together with its rejection −ln T of a 1/E neutron spectrum (1 eV–100 keV), of a fission spectrum and of 1 and 6 MeV photons at that thickness; 3 437 crystals have density-functional and 1 279 machine-learned phonons. A composition-only proxy reproduces the bulk order of L₀.₈ (Spearman ρ = 0.83 at 293 K, 0.95 at 77 K) but not the top of the ranking, which a single elastic Debye temperature largely recovers. Against measured total cross-sections the acceptance criterion fixed in advance was not met (6 of 13 crystals fail); restricted to single-crystal data, 4 of 11 fail, or 6 of 11 without an allowance for the spread between datasets; and the model lies above all four sapphire datasets. With a model uncertainty of 0.138 in ln L₀.₈ propagated by 20 000 Monte Carlo draws, the Pareto front of commercially grown crystals (epithermal against 1 MeV photon rejection) consists of known filters alone with probability 0.10 at 293 K and 0.04 at 77 K, and cooling reorders it. No grown crystal that is not a known filter beats sapphire with probability above 0.90, the level fixed for a statement. 6H-SiC and chrysoberyl are candidates on the epithermal axis: the probability that 6H-SiC rejects the 1/E spectrum better than sapphire is 0.85 at 293 K and 0.88 at 77 K (chrysoberyl: 0.66 and 0.85); with an error component shared by all compounds it rises to 0.93 and 0.95, and with sapphire corrected by its measured residual it falls to 0.69 and 0.73. On the fission spectrum neither candidate is distinguishable from sapphire. Counting every transmitted particle instead of the uncollided ones changes the epithermal rejection by −0.23 to −6.28 and reorders the front, so uncollided figures of merit rank filters optimistically for uncollimated beams. The pipeline that produces the atlas is openly available; the atlas and its uncertainties will be archived openly on acceptance.

papers.title: Diastereoselective Synthesis of Hetero-[2]-Ladderanes
papers.abstract: Conformationally rigid heterobicyclic motifs with well-defined exit vectors have emerged as valuable isosteric replacements for pyridine. While these rigid 3D structures successfully mimic 3,5-disubstituted pyridine derivatives, no isosteric analogues of 2,3-disubstituted pyridines have been reported, despite their widespread occurrence in bioactive compounds. Herein, we report the first diastereoselective synthesis of hetero-[2]-ladderanes, representing a new class of potential 2,3-disubstituted pyridine isosteres, via carbonyl photoexcitation. This protocol is amenable to a variety of 2-azetines and isatins, with remarkable functional-group tolerance, enabling rapid construction of complex spiro-oxa-aza-[2]-ladderanes as single diastereomers. Notably, benzaldehyde derivatives could also participate, affording oxa-aza-[2]-ladderanes with high stereoselectivity. Exit-vector analysis of an oxa-aza-[2]ladderane and a 2,3-disubstituted pyridine-based drug demonstrated the potential of this scaffold as a possible isosteric mimic of 2,3-disubstituted pyridine. Experimental-based mechanistic studies combined with density functional theory have rationalized the observed reactivity and selectivity. Finally, we explored an unprecedented strainenabled, aromaticity-driven Grob-type fragmentation of a hetero-[2]-ladderane, yielding synthetically valuable αhydroxy-β-amino ketone and aminotriol derivatives.

papers.title: Non-structural proteins 2 (nsP2) in Alphavirus: a useful target for drug discovery studies
papers.abstract: The Alphavirus genus consists of single-stranded positive-sense ribonucleic acid (RNA) viruses belonging to the Togaviridae family. They are considered arthropod-borne viruses (arboviruses) and the medically most important are: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), Sindbis virus (SINV), and the three American equine encephalitis viruses, i.e., the Eastern equine encephalitis virus (EEEV), Western equine encephalitis virus (WEEV), and Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus (VEEV). There is currently no approved direct-acting antiviral for the treatment of these diseases. As part of our antiviral drug discovery program focused on Alphaviruses and the non-structural protein 2 (nsP2). We employed diverse in silico methods, ranging from static scanning to temporal pocket evaluation, to assess the druggability of the alphaviral nsP2. Our results suggested that cryptic sites could be better explored for drug discovery campaigns, as current efforts have focused only on the nsP2 active site.

papers.title: Direct Access to α-Aryl-β-Amino Aldehydes via Hypervalent Iodine-Mediated Oxidative Rearrangement of Cinnamyl Amines
papers.abstract: Selective synthesis of α-aryl-β-amino aldehydes remains less developed despite considerable progress in Mannich reactions, aza-Michael additions and asymmetric hydroformylation. Here we report a phenyliodine(III) bis(trifluoroacetate) (PIFA)-mediated oxidative rearrangement of cinnamyl amines through formal 1,2-aryl migration. The reaction proceeds at 0 °C under ambient air and accommodates diverse nitrogen substituents, migrating aryl groups and pharmaceutical-derived substrates. A 6-gram preparation and subsequent transformations to β-amino acids, 1,3-amino alcohols, 1,3-diamines and azetidines, together with the synthesis of a valifenalate isomer, demonstrate the synthetic utility of the aldehyde products. Mechanistic experiments suggest a pathway involving a bis(trifluoroacetate) intermediate. An initial asymmetric variant using chiral iodine(III) reagents furnished a celecoxib-derived chiral aldehyde, with up to 77% ee measured for its reduced chiral alcohol derivative.

papers.title: Machine learning–driven inverse design of nanofiltration membranes for selective Mg2+/Na+ separation
papers.abstract: Desalination brine, a byproduct of seawater desalination, contains valuable resources, including magnesium. Recovering magnesium requires selectively retaining Mg 2+ while allowing the dominant monovalent cation, Na + , to permeate. Nanofiltration (NF) membranes fabricated by interfacial polymerization are promising for this Mg 2+ /Na + separation, but their performance depends on coupled formulation and processing variables that are inefficient to optimize through trial and error. Here, we demonstrate a workflow integrating dataset curation, forward prediction, and inverse design of thin-film composite NF membranes. A dataset of 1,253 entries, comprising literature and in-house records, was cleaned, imputed, and augmented through chemically constrained permutation of interchangeable polymer, solvent, and salt variables in the training split only. Optimized extremely randomized tree regressors predicted pure water permeability, solute rejection, and intermediate membrane properties, achieving test-set coefficients of determination above 0.79. Shapley analysis indicated that permeability was governed primarily by formulation and processing variables, whereas rejection depended mainly on solute identity and charge, as well as membrane tightness. Using Bayesian optimization with a scalarized objective, two membrane recipes with favorable Mg 2+ /Na + selectivity were identified and experimentally validated. The inversely designed membranes exhibited the required Mg 2+ /Na + selectivity, demonstrating the capability of this workflow to design Mg 2+ -selective NF membranes for resource recovery from desalination brine.

papers.title: Schizotrins B-E from the Cultured Cyanobacterium CCIBt3280 - Unique Biosynthetic Signatures and Evidence for an Antibacterial Target
papers.abstract: We report the discovery and chemical structures of schizotrins B-E (1-4) isolated from cultures of Phormidium sp. CCIBt3280. These peptides were identified by spectroscopic and spectrometric analyses. Their absolute configuration was established by Marfey’s and advanced NMR analysis, computational modeling, and Phormidium sp. CCIBt3280 genome analysis. Conserved A- and B-type ketoreductase motifs revealed a stereochemical control of αketoreduction in polyketide natural products. Phylogenomic analyses placed Phormidium sp. CCIBt3280 within the Floridanema family-level clade, indicating that its current assignment to Phormidium should be reassessed. Genome mining uncovered numerous previously unknown schizotrin-like biosynthetic gene clusters in publicly available genomes. The antibacterial activity of peptides 1-4 were also investigated. Schizotrin B inhibited the growth of Bacillus anthracis Sterne at 1 µM. Whole-genome sequencing of spontaneous resistant mutants of B. anthracis revealed a loss-of-function mutation in psd (phosphatidylserine decarboxylase), implicating membrane phospholipid homeostasis in schizotrin B activity. Our results expanded the chemical diversity of the schizotrin family, provided new insights into the biosynthesis of αcarbonyl-containing amino acids, supported the placement of the schizotrin-producing lineage within a potentially novel cyanobacterial genus, and provided insights into the potential mechanism of schizotrins antibacterial resistance.

papers.title: Identification and Experimental Validation of Repurposable Drugs Targeting the Essential ClpP1 Protease of Mycobacterium tuberculosis
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major global health challenge, necessitating the identification of novel therapeutic targets and accelerated drug discovery strategies. The caseinolytic protease (ClpP) complex of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) is essential for proteostasis, stress adaptation, and bacterial survival, making it an attractive yet underexplored drug target. Comparative structural analysis also revealed significant differences between mycobacterial and human ClpP S1 pockets, suggesting opportunities for selective inhibition. In this study, a structure-based drug repurposing approach was employed to identify approved drugs targeting the S1 pocket of the ClpP1 subunit, a key regulatory site involved in proteolytic activation. Virtual screening of the approved drug library against the ClpP1 crystal structure (PDB ID: 4U0G) identified Saquinavir and Raltegravir as the most promising candidates, exhibiting binding affinities of –9.1 and –9.5 kcal/mol, respectively, and favorable interactions with critical S1 pocket residues. Molecular dynamics simulations over 200 ns confirmed stable ligand binding and persistent occupancy within the S1 pocket. In vitro evaluation against M. tuberculosis H37Ra demonstrated potent concentration-dependent antimycobacterial activity, with Saquinavir showing superior efficacy (IC50 = 0.01 ± 0.007 μM; MIC = 64 μM) compared with Raltegravir (IC50 = 0.1 ± 0.09 μM; MIC ≥ 128 μM). Growth kinetics, REMA, and statistical analyses further validated their inhibitory activity. These findings validate Saquinavir and Raltegravir as potential repurposable anti-tubercular agents for further mechanistic and preclinical evaluation.

papers.title: Constraint-guided equal-strut growth generates a tunable family of DNA-realizable wireframe filaments
papers.abstract: Wireframe DNA nanostructures are built from edges of prescribed length meeting at vertices of prescribed valency, which makes their design space a geometric one: which equal-edge frameworks can be built at all, given a maximum vertex degree, a minimum edge angle and a steric clearance. We apply a constrained growth construction—each new vertex placed by trilateration at a fixed strut length from at least three placed vertices, accepted only if the resulting framework still satisfies the design constraints—and report three results. First, under a degree cap of six the construction is extremely selective: of all periodic face-choice patterns tested, only the Boerdijk–Coxeter tetrahelix grows without stalling, and it does so because its interior vertices have degree exactly six, saturating the budget. Second, raising the cap to seven unlocks a one-parameter family of kinked variants indexed by the defect spacing k, whose radius is programmable from 0.52 to 1.13 strut lengths and whose handedness alternates with k, while straightness stays above 0.99. Values k ∈ {3, 5, 8} stall for an identifiable reason—the capped vertex lands at unit distance from a fourth earlier vertex—and run freely at a cap of eight. Both caps are within demonstrated multi-arm junction capability. Third, two members of the family, the pure tetrahelix and a k = 6 variant, were routed into DNA, energy-minimised and run for 5×105 oxDNA steps at 30◦C: both are stable, with second-half mean energies −1.4919±0.0017 and −1.5004 ± 0.0019 per nucleotide and shape changes under 4%. The kinked variant routes into 8 strand cycles against the tetrahelix’s 22. We also report what did not survive checking: a twist–stretch coupling that vanished under length convergence, and a circular-dichroism sign rule that its own descriptor failed to predict.

papers.title: Polarization Is Required to Model Electrostatic Preorganization: The Case of Chorismate Mutase
Exciton Diffusion Drives Efficiency Roll-off in TADF OLEDs
papers.abstract: 2 Abstract Despite their potential to deliver high-efficiency organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs), those using thermally activated delayed fluorescent (TADF) emitters often suffer from a large drop in efficiency at high luminance. This effect is known as efficiency roll-off and is a longstanding issue for these devices, which has limited their commercial deployment. We have discovered that the degree of overlap between the photoluminescence (PL) and absorption spectra drives singlet exciton diffusion and is a strong predictor of the magnitude of efficiency roll-off in TADF OLEDs. This effect is especially important in OLEDs made with multiresonant (MR)-TADF materials given their intense low-energy short-range charge transfer absorption bands. MR-TADF OLEDs are very appealing due to their narrow emission spectra; however, their small Stokes shift leads to large spectral overlap and contributes to these devices showing severe efficiency roll-off. Developing TADF materials that have a larger Stokes shift whilst maintaining their bright, narrow emission would help minimize efficiency roll-off while securing high internal quantum efficiencies, features particularly relevant for displays.

papers.title: Enzymatic Conversion from a Vicinal Diol to a Vicinal Diketone: Computational Study of the Conserved 6-Pyruvoyltetrahydropterin-Forming Stage in Mammalian and Bacterial PTPS
papers.abstract: As a zinc- and magnesium-dependent triphosphatase, 6-pyruvoyl tetrahydropterin synthase (PTPS) catalyzes the conversion of dihydroneopterin triphosphate (H2NTP) to 6-pyruvoyltetrahydropterin (PPH4) and a triphosphate ion, representing a typical reaction for vicinal diketone biosynthesis from vicinal diol. The molecular mechanism of PTPS remains elusive owing to the lack of structural data containing native substrate H2NTP and magnesium ion. Here, we performed a quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) investigation based on a predicted PTPS structure, elucidating the complete atomistic reaction mechanism for triphosphate ion formation and stereoselective product generation. The overall catalytic reaction of PTPS proceeds via two half-reactions, each comprising four sequential proton-transfer steps. Both half-reactions involve the conversion of a hydroxyl group on the substrate into a carbonyl group, ultimately furnishing the pyruvoyl-containing product PPH4. The third proton transfer in the first half-reaction occurs preferentially on the Si-face of the critical carbanion intermediate, yielding the (R)-configured product, in agreement with the reported experimental detection results. These calculations not only unveil the structural origins of stereoselective vicinal diketone product formation, but also uncover a non-canonical triphosphate elimination pathway driven by a charge-center shift that facilitates C–O bond cleavage. These findings broaden the mechanistic paradigm of triphosphatase-mediated phosphate chemistry and offer foundational insights for synthesizing vicinal diketones from vicinal diols.

papers.title: Redox-active ligand facilitates HNO generation in a super-reduced dinitrosyl iron complex
papers.abstract: Dinitrosyl iron complexes (DNICs) are widespread biological nitric oxide (NO) storage and delivery motifs, yet their highly delocalized electronic structure generally resists NO-centered reductive chemistry. Here, we establish ligandcentered reduction as a strategy for unlocking nitroxyl (HNO)-generating DNIC reactivity. A redox-active formazanate ligand (L) stabilizes a super-reduced formal {LFe(NO) 2 } 11 state beyond the conventional {Fe(NO) 2 } 9/10 redox pair. EPR and Mössbauer spectroscopy, together with density functional theory calculations, identify predominantly ligand-centered reduction, yielding an {Fe(NO) 2 } 10 unit coupled to a formazanate radical dianion, L 2−• . Electronic communication between the reduced ligand and the [Fe(NO) 2 ] unit enhances Fe-to-NO π backbonding, consistent with experimental ν(NO) redshifts. Importantly, protonation triggers HNO release, representing an unprecedented example of HNO generation from the super reduced DNIC scaffold. Isotopically distinct H 14 NO/H 15 NO is trapped with PPh 3 , along with the 14/15 N 2 O characterization. Calculations support direct nitrosyl protonation to form an Fe-bound HNO intermediate, followed by solvent-assisted HNO release and subsequent N 2 O formation. These findings establish that ligand-centered electron accommodation coupled to nitrosyl protonation enables HNO generation from a formally super-reduced DNIC, extending DNIC reactivity beyond conventional NO donation.

papers.title: Polarization-Driven Hydride Transfer Promotes Cobalt Tetrasulfophthalocyanine-Catalyzed Hydrogen Evolution by Five Orders of Magnitude
papers.abstract: The hydricity of M–H intermediates is a key descriptor and optimization target for the rational design of molecular hydrogen evolution electrocatalysts. Adsorption to an electrode surface is known to augment catalytic rate, but it remains unclear how adsorption affects M-H hydricity. Herein, we quantitatively compare the catalytic activity and mechanism of the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) from cobalt tetrasulfophthalocyanine (CoTSPc) in a dissolved aqueous form (CoTSPc (aq) ) and when adsorbed to the surface of a carbon electrode (CoTSPc/C). At the same electrode potential, CoTSPc/C catalyzes HER at a rate that is over five orders of magnitude faster than CoTSPc (aq) . Mechanistic studies indicate that both CoTSPc/C and CoTSPc (aq) catalyze HER via a rate-limiting hydride transfer to a proton donor in solution to form H 2 . Hydride transfer from Co-H in CoTSPc (aq) is a purely chemical step defined by a constant hydricity of 22.4 kcal mol −1 that is independent of applied potential. In contrast, hydride transfer from Co-H in CoTSPc/C is strongly polarization dependent, decreasing hydricity by ~23 kcal mol −1 V −1 to values as low as 1.2 kcal mol −1 at −1.1 V vs SHE, leading to the observed rate promotion. We attribute this mechanistic change to the positioning of the CoTSPc-H intermediate within the electrochemical double layer, such that the hydride traverses the interfacial electrostatic potential difference during the RLS. These results demonstrate the power of surface adsorption to generate highly reactive molecular hydrides and fundamentally reshape the free energy landscape of electrocatalysis.

papers.title: A bipartite quantum-acoustic architecture stabilizes multi-exciton solitons at 323 K
papers.abstract: A fundamental thermal paradox has constrained the physical viability of quantum coherent Davydov solitons in quasi-one-dimensional (1D) peptide helices for over 50 years. At 323 K (0.0278 eV), ambient thermal noise disrupts the localized amide I self-trapping resonance, rapidly scattering multi-quanta excitations into delocalized thermal states on femtosecond timescales. Here, a non-equilibrium, bipartite quantum-acoustic stabilization architecture resolves this long-standing decoherence veto via a two-scale viscoelastic coacervate boundary that opens a terahertz transverse acoustic pinning gap, extending three-exciton coherence half-lives from 6.5 fs to 42.6 fs—a pre-thermalization window sufficient to outpace non-radiative intramolecular vibrational energy redistribution (IVR) prior to classical mechanical stepping. By examining the continuous α-helices of eukaryotic F/V-type rotary ATPase c-rings as an evolutionary proof-of-concept archetype and directly simulating both biological α-helical and synthetic 3₁₀-helical manifolds in a 136 × 136 three-exciton open quantum system master equation, we demonstrate that a cooperative, reaction-field-polarized variable-dipole linactant (6.0 D) induces a 0.058 eV single-quantum vibrational Stark–polaron trap (2.1 k B T ) and a > 0.25 eV cooperative three-exciton well. Incorporating exact nearest-neighbor Lang–Firsov polaron coupling alongside three-body single-bond Morse/Pauli over-compression repulsion stabilizes the dipole-active |2₁₅,1₁₆⟩ ± |1₁₅,2₁₆⟩ charge-shared ground doublet 57 meV below the super-dephasing |3,0⟩ manifold, locking the soliton core onto the central defect dimer with 88% spatial localization fidelity. Finally, we map each term of the bipartite Hamiltonian directly onto an orthogonal click and fluoride-exchange (CuAAC/SuFEx/GeFEx-S/PFEx) synthetic blueprint to establish a falsifiable, room-temperature quantum-acoustic metamaterial.

papers.title: Ligand-Length Asymmetry Controls Nanoscale Heat Flow in Gold Janus Nanorods
papers.abstract: Plasmonic nanoparticles play a crucial role in enabling technologies used in medical, catalytic, and imaging applications. Introducing particle heterogeneity in Janus nanoparticles provides a route for molecular-level control of heat transport across nanoscale length scales. Here, we show that the temperature field generated by gold Janus nanorods in water can be tuned by engineering the length of one of the ligand layers. Using non-equilibrium molecular dynamics simulations, we investigate nanorods coated via self-assembly with a hydrophobic octanethiolate monolayer and a hydrophilic hydroxy-terminated alkanethiolate monolayer of varying lengths (3 to 13 carbon atoms). Increasing the hydrophilic ligand length from 3 to 13 carbon atoms,at comparable heat rates of ∼1 μW, decreases the temperature of the water adjacent to the hydrophilic domain by approximately 16 K and reduces the temperature contrast between the hydrophobic and hydrophilic regions by a factor of three, from ∼23 to ∼7 K. Simulations at constant coverage show that chain length accounts for most of this reduction by increasing ligand–water Kapitza resistance and shell thickness, whereas the lower grafting density of long-chain monolayers mainly increases gold–ligand resistance. The hydrophobic domain shows no systematic variation within the statistical uncertainty. The temperature contrast persists near the hydrophobic–hydrophilic–water three-phase boundary, indicating weak lateral heat transfer along the ligand coating. Our findings establish ligand-length asymmetry as a molecular strategy for designing materials to control anisotropic heat flow and nanoscale temperature contrast in Janus nanorods.

papers.title: Tetrathiafulvalene-Based Molecular Qubit Frameworks with Room-Temperature Quantum Coherence
papers.abstract: Molecular qubits, owing to their designability and tunability, have emerged as fundamental units for quantum technologies. Among them, molecular qubit frameworks (MQFs) offer unique advantages in long-range ordered lattices and microporosity that provide well-defined phonon environments and guest-tunable spin dynamics. These features greatly enhance qubit performance and enable room temperature quantum operations, holding promise for quantum sensing applications. Herein, we compare the qubit performance of 2,3,6,7,10,11-hexahydroxytriphenylene (HHTP) and tetrathiafulvalene tetrabenzoic acid (H4TTFTB), which form stable radicals upon spontaneous oxidation in the air. We found that optical phonons dominate spin relaxation in HHTP, whereas H4TTFTB exhibits stronger spin-orbit coupling and higher acoustic phonon population that account for its shorter spin relaxation time. Meanwhile, H4TTFTB features a nuclear-spin-free core and in turn a prolonged phase memory time, making it a favorable qubit candidate. Furthermore, we synthesized three MQFs using H4TTFTB as the ligand, which not only retain the superior room-temperature qubit performance but also possess porous channels, establishing a viable platform for future quantum information applications.

papers.title: The Importance of Base and Solvent in the Ni-Mediated Decarboxylation of Pentafluorobenzoic Acid
papers.abstract: An experimental kinetic study of the decarboxylation of pentafluorobenzoic acid is reported. This work demonstrates a thermal decarboxylation pathway that is operative under conditions commonly employed for catalytic decarboxylative coupling reactions. This work also reveals a dramatic rate enhancement for the benzoate salt relative to the neutral acid and the importance of basic additives in accelerating the decarboxylation of the pentafluorobenzoic acid. Additionally, decarboxylation of the acid displays a strong solvent dependence with the polar aprotic solvent DMA leading to more rapid thermal decarboxylation as well as an increased influence of Ni additives.

papers.title: A dual-targeting nitrogen mustard-class I HDAC inhibitor hybrid molecule is superior to the combination of an HDAC inhibitor plus chlorambucil in glioblastoma cells
Acetylcholinesterase Activity Modulation by Proteinogenic Amino Acid Ester Ferulates salts with Enhanced Solubility and Antioxidant Properties
papers.abstract: Ferulic acid (FA) is a phenolic antioxidant whose potential applications are limited by poor aqueous solubility and bioavailability. Novel ferulate salts of ethyl, propyl, and isopropyl esters of L-tyrosine and L-phenylalanine were synthesized and characterized in terms of their physicochemical properties, antioxidant activity, and acetylcholinesterase (AChE) inhibition. All synthesized ferulates exhibited improved aqueous solubility compared with FA, with tyrosine ethyl ester ferulate, [TyrOEt][FA], showing the highest solubility. The salts retained or enhanced antioxidant activity, with tyrosine-derived compounds exhibiting nearly twofold higher activity than FA in the ORAC assay. The ferulate salts also demonstrated stronger AChE inhibition than FA, with phenylalanine isopropyl ester ferulate, [PheOiPr][FA], showing the greatest inhibitory potency among the ferulates. Comparison with the corresponding chloride salts indicated that the amino acid ester cations were primarily responsible for AChE inhibition. Kinetic analysis revealed a mixed inhibition mechanism with a predominant competitive component for the most active compounds. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations identified interactions with key aromatic residues within the AChE binding gorge, while MM/GBSA calculations supported favorable binding of the amino acid esters. The synthesized compounds generally had limited effects on L929 fibroblast viability, although tyrosine propyl ester salts showed greater cytotoxicity. These findings demonstrate that salt formation with amino acid esters improves the physicochemical properties of FA while preserving its antioxidant potential, whereas AChE inhibitory activity is primarily determined by the structure of the amino acid ester moiety and its interactions with key residues within the enzyme's active-site gorge.

papers.title: Uniform Gel Networks with Amide-Rich Crosslinking Domains Amplify Weak Interactions for Growth of Ultrasmall Nanoparticles without Added Strong Ligand
papers.abstract: Synthesizing ultrasmall thermoresponsive nanoparticles within poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPA) hydrogels without the use of strong ligands remains challenging, as intrinsically weak interfacial interactions and structural heterogeneity in conventional networks often lead to poor size control and aggregation. Here, we report a programmable PNIPA-based hydrogel constructed from star-shaped polymers via living radical polymerization, in which a homogeneous network containing locally reinforced crosslinking domains enables ligand-free in situ formation of ultrasmall metal nanoparticles. The uniform network provides a spatially consistent reaction environment, allowing synchronized and controllable particle growth across length scales. Nanoparticle size is governed by network architecture rather than by synthetic conditions, and the resulting hydrogel composites exhibit exceptional stability under thermal cycling and harsh chemical environments, despite relying solely on amide functionalities. Stabilization does not arise from rigid immobilization or strong ligand coordination along the polymer chains; instead, it emerges from the collective engagement of multiple spatially distributed, amide-enriched crosslinking domains. These reinforced domains generate a cooperative multiple-anchoring effect, creating a soft yet adaptive chelation-like confinement. This work establishes a versatile platform for strong-ligand-free yet robust and controllable nanoparticle synthesis, extendable to colloidal dispersions, diverse polymer matrices, and various metal nanoparticles.

papers.title: Hierarchical Copper-Based Metal-Organic Frameworks for Improved Catalytic Performance
papers.abstract: Introducing additional meso- or macroporosity into traditionally microporous metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) can greatly improve the catalytic performance of these materials, by reducing diffusional barriers during reactions. In this study, we demonstrate that HKUST-1 synthesized via supercritical CO2-assisted crystallization (referred to here as “scCO2-HKUST”) forms a hierarchically porous structure, combining intrinsic microporosity with newly formed macropores. X-ray diffraction (PXRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and gas sorption analyses confirmed the preservation of the crystal structure alongside macropore formation. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) revealed a higher proportion of low-valent copper species (Cuo/Cu+) in scCO₂-HKUST compared to conventional HKUST-1, indicative of increased coordinatively unsaturated metal sites. In catalytic CO oxidation, scCO2-HKUST achieved higher conversion rates than normal HKUST-1 between 220 and 260 oC, with complete CO conversion at 260 °C versus 280 °C for the conventional sample. This enhanced activity is attributed to faster molecular diffusion through the macropores and greater accessibility of reactive copper sites.

papers.title: Ligand-Based Design of Lyn-Selective Type II Kinase Inhibitors by Rational Tail Modification of Imatinib
papers.abstract: Lyn is a tyrosine kinase that plays critical roles in immune signaling and neurodegenerative diseases but is difficult to target selectively because of high homology within the Src-family of kinases. Here, we report ligand-based optimization of the type II inhibitor imatinib through systematic tail modification to enhance Lyn potency and selectivity. This approach yielded potent inhibitors, including compound 22 with low-nanomolar Lyn inhibition and compound 27 with 500-fold selectivity over Hck. Compound 22 showed a limited off-target kinase profile under low-ATP conditions that was further narrowed at 1 mM ATP while retaining submicromolar Lyn inhibition. Complementary 3D-QSAR and Markov state modeling linked tail-region steric features to ligand-dependent activation-loop conformational ensembles. In human microglia, 22 suppressed Aβ-induced Lyn autophosphorylation and increased CD163 high CLEC7A high DAM-like and Aβ-positive DAM-like populations. These findings establish compound 22 as a novel molecular probe for interrogating Lyn catalytic function across diverse disease-relevant contexts.

papers.title: Open Ontology of Polymer Chemistry: Accumulation and Self-Improving Memory Mechanisms for Polymer Research
papers.abstract: Memory systems for AI agents are a valuable component of long-running workflows. They are also a strong form of lock-in for model providers, because the memory system that makes a model better with use may be inaccesible to users. An ideal memory system would accumulate both factual knowledge and the relationships of that knowledge to recurring tasks performed by the researcher. People accumulate particular and general knowledge through experience, the latter often through periodic reflection on what is working and isn’t working at a higher level of abstraction. Here, we introduce an open-source harness for polymer research meant to heuristically mimic (i) knowledge accumulation across research tasks, (ii) the review of new knowledge against existing knowledge, and (iii) performing periodic updates to task-knowledge relationships through reflection. The system, which we call the Open Ontology of Polymer Chemistry (OOPC, pronounced ‘oopsie’), is initialized with a knowledge base consisting of an open-source wikipedia with entries for most known polymers. From this starting point, the knowledge base was enriched by running a 1,092 task campaign across different areas of polymer chemistry, producing 8,899 distinct findings extracted from 1,679 sources on 157 different polymers. GPT-6.1 Sol and Opus 5.5 comparisons were run with and without the accumulated memory from this campaign on 60 held-out tasks with varying overlap in terms of polymer and properties being researched. The performance improvements tracked with research topic similarity to prior work researched from the harness, with token reductions of up to 19% and 48% and web search reductions of up to 80% and 72% (10.3 to 2.1 and 7.6 to 2.1 per answer) for Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol, respectively. The harness was tested through five independent restarts of 500 tasks each with reproducible performance gains. An independent review of the performance caught rare contradictory claims and occasionally unsubstantiated claims depending on the underlying model (up to a few percent of all claims by claude on withheld tasks, none by codex). The reflection heuristic was tested as an update to the knowledge ontology after the accumulation period. These updates mainly consisted of extended lists of property names with marginal improvements to finding recall. The roles of review and ontology updates require further study as after knowledge accumulation these tests had little room to show appreciable gains given the consistently strong evidentiary basis for findings within the harness. Looking forward, domain-specific memory systems are likely to be valuable and ideally transferable research artifacts that can be shared at the group, community, and organizational levels.

papers.title: The study of secondary isotope substitutions on adjacent carbon atoms affecting the tunnelling rate in acetylacetone
papers.abstract: Heavy-atom isotope effects on hydrogen-tunnelling splittings have been reported for malonaldehyde and tropolone but not for acetylacetone, where the splitting has not yet been measured. We predict the effects of 13C substitution at positions not directly attached to the transferring proton on its tunnelling splitting. The model is a relaxed one-dimensional reaction path on a semiempirical GFN2-xTB surface that is scaled to the coupled-cluster barrier, with the parent splitting fixed by a diffusion Monte Carlo calculation. It is tested against instanton calculations and the experimental 13C effects in malonaldehyde, and against a fulldimensional ring-polymer instanton calculation for acetylacetone on the same GFN2-xTB potential energy surface, free of the model’s fitted parameter. Substitution of 13C at both carbons bonded to the oxygens decreases the splitting by 2.1% (model range 1.5–2.5%; instanton 2.3%), and a single oxygen-bonded 13C by 1.1%. The central-and methyl-carbon isotope effects are not established. These two oxygen-bonded carbons move with the proton during tunnelling, but the instanton fluctuation prefactor cancels about a third of this kinematic effect. In malonaldehyde the model reproduces the instanton results for substitution at the oxygen-bonded carbons and the measured total effect for all three carbons, although the only positionresolved measurement gives about half as much for the oxygen-bonded pair. Predicted shifts of 0.69 cm−1 (20.5 GHz) for 2,4-13C2-acetylacetone and about half that for the naturally abundant singly labelled species present an experimental test.

papers.title: Revealing Hidden Exposures: Multi-omic and Mass Spectrometry Approaches for Decoding the Chemical Exposome
papers.abstract: Human-made chemical pollutants pose a pervasive threat to environmental and human health, yet global chemical production continues to rise while toxicological data often remains unavailable. Since regulations lag behind innovation, much of our understanding of real‑world chemical exposure frequently comes from observed biological consequences such as infertility, chronic disease, neurocognitive decline, and threats to food security. These knowledge gaps therefore illuminate major limitations in our current ability to evaluate chemical risks and highlight the need for analytical strategies capable of capturing the complexity of environmental exposures and their biological effects. The exposome provides a framework for characterizing the totality of exposures across the lifespan. Within this framework, the chemical exposome focuses specifically on exposures and effects from exogenous small molecules. Traditional targeted mass spectrometry and single-omic approaches have offered valuable but limited insights into this chemical space but often overlook co‑occurring contaminants and perturbations in interconnected molecular pathways. In contrast, multi‑omic measurements enable a more comprehensive assessment of both exposure and biological response, revealing mechanistic links between contaminants and adverse health outcomes. Developments in these areas position chemical exposomics and multi‑omics as essential tools for environmental precision health, an emerging paradigm that seeks to identify exposure‑specific molecular signatures, predict susceptibility, and guide targeted interventions. This review highlights how multi-omics, advanced analytical chemistry techniques, and sophisticated computational tools are collectively advancing a more holistic understanding of the chemical exposome.

papers.title: Increasing Adhesion via Strong Dipoles: Oxazolidinone-containing Polyolefins as Nonreactive Tie Layers in Polymer Laminates
papers.abstract: Multilayer films are widely used to combine the properties of multiple polymers but often require tie layers to achieve interfacial adhesion between the substrates. To adhere polar and nonpolar polymers, common tie layers are polyolefins containing reactive functionalities, which limit their application space and potential methods for multilayer recycling. By contrast, nonreactive tie layers require chemical modification to achieve suitable performance due to their relatively weak dipoles. To address this limitation, we synthesized a series of hydrogenated copolymers between 1,5-cyclooctadiene and an oxazolidinone-fused cyclooctene monomer (Oxa, 10–100 mol %) to form “polyethylene” functionalized with strong dipoles (~5 Debye). We tested these copolymers as nonreactive tie layers between high-density polyethylene (HDPE) and polyamide 6 (PA6), achieving adhesive strengths up to 881 N/m with moderate dipole incorporation. We observed a change in the interface of adhesive failure from PA6 to HDPE with increasing Oxa content, demonstrating a change in substrate affinity with increasing polarity. Overall, this work provides the first evidence of strong dipoles increasing interfacial adhesion for nonreactive tie layers, introducing a new adhesive design strategy for multilayer polymeric materials.

papers.title: BigFingerprint: A Topology-aware Extended-connectivity Fingerprint for Polymers
papers.abstract: Machine learning-driven polymer design and property prediction require molecular representations that encode not only local chemistry but also the statistically distributed monomer sequences and connectivity patterns and global topology that distinguish polymers from small molecules. Existing fingerprinting workflows often fail to capture global polymer architecture, as well as connectivity across repeat units, end groups, and linking groups. This work develops BigFingerprint, a topology-aware extended-connectivity fingerprint for polymers represented by BigSMILES. BigFingerprint consists of two components, a polymer extended-connectivity fingerprint, p-ECFP, that encodes atom-centered substructures within and across stochastic molecular fragments, and a polymer topology fingerprint, p-TFP, that encodes global architectural features such as block, statistical, graft, star, branched, and network topologies. Through representative structural examples and polymer property prediction tasks, BigFingerprint retains the chemical interpretability of circular fingerprints while extending their applicability to complex polymer architectures. As a critical component of the BigSMILES-centered ecosystem, BigFingerprint integrates local substructural information with global topological descriptors to provide a general and chemically interpretable representation for substructure analysis, similarity

papers.title: Exploration of Particle Swarm Optimization for Parameter Identification in Phase-Field Modeling
papers.abstract: To address the issue that phase-field (PF) simulation parameter calibration has long relied on manual experience and comparisons with static final-state results, a frame-by-frame parameter identification framework was developed. Three strategies were designed: standard Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), a hybrid PSO incorporating elitism and random reset mechanisms, and Elitist Random Search (ERS). A composite cost function was established, which combined the Dice coefficient and Chamfer distance through a weighting ratio. Hybrid PSO converged earlier and achieved a superior final global optimum cost, demonstrating that this strategy effectively mitigated the risk of entrapment in local optima. Finally, hybrid PSO went through extended validation with longer duration (15s) and larger simulation scale (400 µm × 1700 µm), the average error of the key parameters identified is approximately 2.8%. This work combined frame-by-frame dynamic comparison with hybrid PSO for PF parameter identification for the first time, fundamentally resolving the long-standing problem of degradation in this field.

papers.title: Decarboxylative radical C–C coupling of ⍺-(oxy/thio)acetic acids with electron-poor alkenes
Development of a Microfluidic Droptode Sensor for Detection of Heparin in Citrated Human Plasma
papers.abstract: Heparin, a large, negatively charged macromolecule, is an anticoagulant widely used in extracorporeal procedures. Methods to quantitate the amount of heparin in blood are therefore essential to ensure correct dosing, thus avoiding unwanted side effects such as thrombosis and hemorrhage. Electrochemical and optical methods have been developed for the detection of heparin in plasma and whole blood; however, deterioration of sensor response from matrix fouling and optical interference, respectively, are limitations of these technologies. Furthermore, methods that require minimal sample input are also desirable so as to limit consumption of blood during these procedures. Motivated by needs for a new, low volume and non-fouling clinical sensor, we developed a droplet microfluidic form of an ionophore-based optode. This method involves sub-nanoliter aqueous sample aliquots spaced by oil segments containing analyte-selective ionophore and pH-sensitive chromoionophore. Partitioning of the analyte from the aqueous droplet to the oil segment, facilitated by interactions with the ionophore, results in fluorescence changes that track with analyte concentration. Fluorescence measurements are recorded from sub-nanoliter oil segments adjacent to aqueous droplets, therefore components of the sample do not interfere with the measurement. Furthermore, reagent-conservative oil segments are continuously generated at tens of Hz in the droplet microfluidic device, eliminating the need to regenerate the oil phase for reuse. Here we report the application of this droplet optode (e.g. droptode) technology for the quantification of heparin in citrated human plasma samples over relevant clinical ranges.

papers.title: A geometry-matched structure generator outperforms basin hopping for silicon cluster global optimisation at fixed relaxation budget
papers.abstract: In cluster global optimisation the cost is dominated by local relaxations, so the number of relaxations—not wall-clock time—is the natural budget whenever each relaxation is a first-principles or machine-learned potential evaluation. We ask how much of that budget can be saved by the initial structure generator alone. We study a motif-agnostic generator that places each new atom by trilateration at a fixed bond distance from at least three alreadyplaced atoms, subject to a steric admissibility test, and we benchmark it as a drop-in initialiser for Stillinger–Weber silicon clusters with n = 24–60 atoms against three baselines: random structure search, a specialised basin-hopping implementation with single-atom, collective and surface moves and an adaptive step, and a growth-pattern beam search in the spirit of GOALS and GrowPAL. At equal relaxation budget the generator reaches lower minima than specialised basin hopping at every size from n = 32 upward, winning 8/8 paired replicates at n = 48 and n = 60 with complete distributional separation at n = 48, and it beats growth-pattern search in 7/8 paired replicates at both sizes. It also exhibits markedly lower run-to-run variance, and it was the only method to locate the deepest structure found at n = 32, n = 40 and n = 60. The advantage is absent at n = 16, marginal at n = 24, and clean from n = 32; a structural analysis of the resulting minima shows that they are more highly coordinated than the baselines’ but not more tetrahedral in bond angle, so we report the size onset as an unexplained empirical observation rather than attribute it to angular matching. We report the opposite accounting as well: because growth-pattern relaxations start from an already-optimised sub-cluster they are roughly an order of magnitude cheaper in wall-clock, and on equal CPU time the two methods are comparable, while the advantage over basin hopping persists on both accountings.

papers.title: Global potential of decentralized waste biomass to solid carbon for scalable carbon removal
papers.abstract: Livestock manure and crop residues are abundant agricultural by-products whose mismanagement releases ~1.56 Gt CO2-eq yr-1, about 22% of agricultural greenhouse gas emissions. Here, we propose a circular bioeconomy system to recover their energy, nutrients, and carbon. The proposed solar-powered, farm-scale system integrates anaerobic digestion, biomethanation, and methane pyrolysis to convert these residues into stable solid carbon, recycling hydrogen internally and returning nutrients to the soil as digestate. We apply a coupled mass, energy, and cost model globally using spatially explicit biomass and solar datasets. We estimate a sequestration potential of ~596 Mt C yr-1 (~2.2 Gt CO2-eq yr-1, ~6% of global fossil CO2 emissions), with a median levelized cost of 926 USD t-1 C for crop residue (5th–95th percentile: 904–980 USD t-1 C), and 1,534 USD t-1 C for manure (5th–95th percentile: 1,510–1,589 USD t-1 C), assuming no revenue from the carbon product. Capital expenditure dominates (~89% of cost, led by anaerobic digestion) while solar electricity contributes only ~11%. Under tailored process conditions, the product can be recovered as carbon black, graphite, carbon nanofibers, graphene, or nanotubes; both its market prices and carbon-credit prices could exceed the sequestration cost, making distributed carbon removal a potential source of farm income.

papers.title: Diastereoselective synthesis of glycosyl-1-thiophosphates as reporters for nucleotide diphosphate sugar metabolism
papers.abstract: Glycosylation controls key physiological processes such as cell-cell recognition, signal transduction, and protein folding/trafficking within subcellular compartments. Glycans are often assembled by Leloir glycosyltransferase enzymes, which use nucleotide diphosphate monosaccharides (NDP-monosaccharides) as substrates. Cells produce NDP-monosaccharides through metabolic transformation of corresponding glycosyl-1-phosphates (G1Ps). Existing LC-MS-based approaches to study NDP-monosaccharide metabolism in living cells are limited due to the mass degeneracy of the epimeric physiological pyranoses that populate the NDP-monosaccharide pool. Technology that enables tracking of NDP-monosaccharide metabolism from chemically defined metabolic precursors would illuminate these challenging-to-study pathways that are central to immunity, signal transduction, and cellular homeostasis.
