To circumvent this challenge, we have developed a series of cell-permeable glycosyl-1- thio phosphates (G1TPs) in which a single oxygen atom is replaced with a sulphur atom at the phosphorus centre. This chalcogen substitution generated a mass-unique signature that enabled tracking of select NDP-monosaccharide metabolites. To generate G1TPs, we leveraged a cyclic thiophosphorochloridate reagent to selectively install a 1,3,2-dioxaphospholane group at the anomeric centre of per- O -acetyl-D-pyranoses. Our approach included anomeric stereocontrol, which provided access to both native (α) and non-physiological (β) diastereomers at C1. Next, we leveraged the intrinsic strain of the dioxaphospholane system to efficiently install an S -acetyl-2-thioethyl (SATE) group by direct ring opening with thioacetate. LC-MS analysis confirmed that the resultant per- O -Ac- and SATE-protected G1TPs were cell permeable and could be deprotected to free G1TPs once inside. Importantly, metabolomic analysis revealed that an archetypal G1TP – α-galactosyl-1-thiophosphate – was metabolized to the corresponding NDP-(S)-galactose in cellulo , whereas the β-counterpart was not. Finally, we demonstrated that α-galactosyl-1-thiophosphate G1TP was non-toxic, did not perturb native glycan biosynthesis, and did not impact gene transcription. Combined, these results establish G1TPs as biologically silent reporters for NDP-monosaccharide metabolism.

papers.title: How Metal-to-Linker Ratio and Concentration Govern the Nucleation Mechanism of MOF-5-inspired Crystals: Insights from Multiscale Modeling
Temperature Mediated Balance of Singlet Fission and Symmetry-Breaking Charge-Transfer in a Polycrystalline Perylene Bisimide Thin Film
papers.abstract: Singlet fission (SF) and symmetry-breaking charge transfer (SBCT) are competing, and often concurrent, pathways observed in photoexcited organic semiconductor systems: a photoexcited molecule electronically coupled to a neighbor can yield two triplet excited states (SF) or a charge-separated radical ion pair (SBCT). The branching ratio of SF and SBCT is determined largely by the intermolecular electronic coupling, which depends on the relative orientation of neighboring molecules. In a solid thin film, this orientation is defined by the molecular packing, which is typically a static condition established during film formation, and difficult to change with external stimuli. Here, we show that intermolecular coupling in a solid thin film of an asymmetrically substituted perylene bisimide (mXPBI) can be reversibly modulated by temperature alone. Oblique π-stacking in mXPBI produces Davydov-split excitonic states with mixed Coulombic and charge-transfer (CT) coupling character. Temperature-dependent X-ray diffraction reveals modest changes in intermolecular distance and relative molecular orientation. Time-dependent density functional theory calculations demonstrate that these subtle changes to the molecular packing alter the balance between long-range Coulombic and short-range CT coupling, which is expected to influence the competition between SF and SBCT pathways. Transient absorption spectroscopy confirms this prediction, showing that the branching ratio between triplet (SF) and SBCT shifts from approximately 30:70 at 300 K to 50:50 at 100 K. These results demonstrate that excitonic coupling of mXPBI can be reversibly tuned by temperature in the solid state, thereby shifting the balance of competitive photophysical pathways.

papers.title: FROST: certified Hartree–Fock limits of helium and beryllium to hundreds of significant figures
papers.abstract: We report rigorous upper bounds on the closed-shell Hartree–Fock (HF) energies of helium and beryllium whose first 503 and 501 significant figures are correct, EHF(He) = −2.861 679 995 612 238 878 775 543 740 022 563 429 412 879 776 752 447 053 906 864 . . . Eh, EHF(Be) = −14.573 023 168 316 399 582 411 447 359 870 014 453 877 721 357 . . . Eh, against previous records of 66 and 43. The method, which we call FROST (Fock radial orbital shooting with Taylor series), uses no basis set. When every occupied orbital is an s orbital, the HF equations reduce to coupled radial differential equations for the orbitals and for one potential per pair of orbitals. We integrate them with Taylor series of order up to 873 in arbitrary-precision arithmetic, sizing every step from the local radius of convergence. The orbital energies and normalisations are fixed by nested secant shooting to a hard wall, which is the only truncation and whose error decays as e−2κR. For beryllium each orbital has its own wall, and the canonical equations are solved without enforcing exact orthogonality, which costs energy far below the wall error. The orbitals are piecewise polynomials with dyadic rational coefficients. An independent program therefore evaluates the exact determinant energy in integer arithmetic, and by the variational principle the result is an upper bound free of rounding error. The orbitals are as accurate as the energies. Their nuclear cusp is exact, and for helium the density at the nucleus and ⟨rk⟩ are obtained to about 500 significant figures (previously 32 to 65), with a pointwise error given in closed form by Whittaker functions. On a laptop, the 503-digit helium calculation takes 7.4 minutes and beryllium to 500 digits 4.0 hours. The same code gives the HF energies of H− through Ne8+ to 100 significant figures in about 15 seconds each. We locate the nearest singularities of the helium HF orbital in the complex plane at r∗ = −1.099 ± 0.577 i. This explains why single-exponent Laguerre-type bases converge sub-geometrically and predicts the optimised exponent of the previous record to within 3%. Combined with our FLAKE energy, the correlation energy of helium follows to 58 significant figures.

papers.title: Thermally Induced Structural Transformation in a Two-Dimensional Conductive Metal-Organic Framework
papers.abstract: A long-standing structural question in triphenylene-based conductive metal-organic frameworks is why closely related materials adopt either fully extended honeycomb lattices or intercalated structures containing alternating extended layers and discrete metal–ligand clusters. Ni(II)–HHTP and Co(II)–HHTP (HHTP = 2,3,6,7,10,11-hexahydroxytriphenylene) have both been reported to have the latter “intercalated structure”, but here we discover that thermal activation and dehydration convert both frameworks to the fully extended structures. Focusing on Ni(II)–HHTP, we show that this structural transformation is reversible, with roomtemperature hydration restoring the intercalated structure. Variable-temperature synchrotron powder X-ray diffraction supports the intercalated-to-fully-extended structural transformation, while solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, thermal analysis, and elemental analysis provide evidence for the accompanying dehydration. Rehydration of Ni(II)–HHTP restores the intercalated structure, establishing reversible structural switching through removal and reincorporation of water. The resulting change in interlayer architecture alters electrical conductivity, gas response and adsorption properties in Ni(II)–HHTP. Importantly, common sample pre-treatment and testing conditions can themselves change the type of framework structure, meaning that measured properties may not correspond to the initially assigned structure. Because thermal and hydration history determine structure and function, careful structural verification under measurement conditions is, therefore, essential for establishing reliable structure–property relationships. Ultimately our findings resolve a persistent structural ambiguity in this family of materials and allow access to new fully extended electrically conductive framework materials.

papers.title: Folding and Function as Two Sides of One Coin: Statistical Mechanics, Information Theory, and Deep Learning of Binding, Catalysis, and Allostery in an Exactly Enumerable Lattice Protein
papers.abstract: Folding and function depend on the same conformational ensemble, but they need not favor the same population distribution. We examine this relationship in a 27-residue lattice protein with 103,346 exactly enumerated compact conformations, combining statistical mechanics, information-theoretic analysis, and variational autoencoders. Exact identities separate binding into native-site recognition and population terms, distinguish transition-state complementarity from reorganization in catalysis, and express allosteric coupling as a conformational covariance. Under composition-conserving selection, binding and turnover optimization favor a dominant compact fold, whereas strong allostery can coexist with a distributed ensemble: pure coupling optimization gives a median native population of 0.47, compared with 0.85 when designs with additional stability rewards are pooled. Composition-free binding and catalytic selection provide further counterexamples to an unconditional function-to-folding implication. Rényi divergences quantify the shortfall from the best available binding or transition-state-recognition conformation; allosteric coupling instead depends on the magnitude and alignment of two ligand-induced responses. A sequence VAE generates target-fold-compatible sequences more frequently than an independent-site baseline and partially retains binding and catalytic properties, but not allosteric coupling. Time-lagged VAEs resolve additional basin information in selected allosteric trajectories, although incomplete interconversion prevents inference of equilibrium switching kinetics. Together, these results identify a conditional relationship between functional selection and fold specificity, and distinguish population concentration for recognition from population redistribution for allosteric communication.

papers.title: Volumetric self-assembly of addressable DNA frames
papers.abstract: The ability to organize distinct molecular components at prescribed positions throughout a three-dimensional volume remains a central challenge in programmable self-assembly. Although DNA nanotechnology has enabled both highly addressable structures and assemblies of considerable size, combining these capabilities is limited by the growing number of unintended interactions between components. Here, we develop a sequence-encoded strategy for the volumetric assembly of uniquely addressed DNA origami cubes. Each cube carries 24 programmable address codes that determine its position through cooperative interactions with neighboring cubes. We formulate address generation as a coding problem, derive its theoretical capacity and develop computational methods to identify and suppress incorrect multivalent binding configurations. Using this approach, we assemble a range of three-dimensional architectures, including a 6 × 6 × 6 cuboid that contains 216 unique cubes, spans 300 nm and is encoded by a single scaffold and 361 distinct oligonucleotides. We further demonstrate site-specific organization of 18-nm gold nanoparticles into prescribed three-dimensional patterns and use single-molecule DNA-PAINT to resolve spatially encoded features at the level of individual cubes. These results establish a framework for large-scale volumetric self-assembly in which molecular identity, spatial position and cargo placement can be independently programmed, providing a route toward aperiodic nanomaterials with designed three-dimensional organization.

papers.title: Exciton Diffusion Drives Efficiency Roll-off in TADF OLEDs
papers.abstract: 2 Abstract Despite their potential to deliver high-efficiency organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs), those using thermally activated delayed fluorescent (TADF) emitters often suffer from a large drop in efficiency at high luminance. This effect is known as efficiency roll-off and is a longstanding issue for these devices, which has limited their commercial deployment. We have discovered that the degree of overlap between the photoluminescence (PL) and absorption spectra drives singlet exciton diffusion and is a strong predictor of the magnitude of efficiency roll-off in TADF OLEDs. This effect is especially important in OLEDs made with multiresonant (MR)-TADF materials given their intense low-energy short-range charge transfer absorption bands. MR-TADF OLEDs are very appealing due to their narrow emission spectra; however, their small Stokes shift leads to large spectral overlap and contributes to these devices showing severe efficiency roll-off. Developing TADF materials that have a larger Stokes shift whilst maintaining their bright, narrow emission would help minimize efficiency roll-off while securing high internal quantum efficiencies, features particularly relevant for displays.

papers.title: Thermal expansion of the Martian mineral starkeyite (MgSO4·4H2O) and the effect of synchrotron X-ray radiation damage on its lattice parameters
papers.abstract: Starkeyite, MgSO4·4H2O, is one of the few hydrated sulfate minerals identified by X-ray diffraction on the martian surface, yet its structure and lattice parameters are known only at room temperature, whereas the material is exposed to much colder conditions on the surface of Mars. We report the crystal structure of perdeuterated starkeyite at 10 K and 300 K from high-resolution neutron powder diffraction, including freely refined deuterium positions, and its lattice parameters over 10–370 K, providing the first reference data for this mineral across the full Martian temperature range. Thermal expansion is strongly anisotropic and near-uniaxial, with α1 : α2 : α3 = −0.12(4) : 0.89(5) : 1.00 at 305 K and the negative direction lying in the ac plane; the volume expansion is identical within uncertainty to that of the polymorph cranswickite despite their different topologies. At ~245 K, a temperature crossed daily at the surface of Gale crater on Mars a shoulder emerges on the 212 reflection that cannot be accounted for by the P21/n model, possibly indicating a hitherto unrecognised low-temperature modification. A synchrotron X-ray experiment on protiated starkeyite yields lattice parameters that diverge progressively from the neutron data, show cooling–heating hysteresis and negative expansion of the a-axis; snapshot patterns on irradiated and fresh sections of the capillary demonstrate that this is due to radiation damage. We describe the radiation-induced strain by a second-rank X-ray expansion tensor rij which in starkeyite is strongly anisotropic, reaches a volumetric value of 11.8 TGy-1 at an absorbed dose of 0.39 GGy, and largely anneals out on reheating to room temperature. Such doses cannot be reached on Mars, but they are routinely exceeded in synchrotron studies of minerals, where radiationinduced strain is indistinguishable from the thermal or pressure response within a single dataset and can bias lattice parameters, V–T relations and equation-of-state fits, particularly for hydrates and other beam-sensitive phases and in diamond-anvil-cell experiments where the sample cannot be moved to a fresh spot. We recommend that dose be recorded as a routine experimental variable and that thermal expansion be cross-checked against neutron or low-flux reference data.

papers.title: Structure – Stability Relationships in Aryl- and Heteroarylmethanesulfonyl Chlorides and Fluorides
papers.abstract: Sulfonyl chlorides are among the most widely used yet least storable building blocks in medicinal chemistry, and arylmethanesulfonyl chlorides in particular remain poorly represented in commercial catalogs because of their limited stability. In this work, the long-term stability of 23 aryl- and 36 heteroarylmethanesulfonyl chlorides and fluorides was evaluated systematically. Decomposition was monitored by 1 H NMR spectroscopy in THF- d 8 solution at 4 °C and 23 °C for up to 12 months; the solvent was chosen to avoid solvolysis and acidic admixtures, and to minimize water uptake. Whereas at least one batch of each compound remained unchanged in neat form for up to 14 years (median 5.5 years), their stability in solution varied widely, i.e., from complete decomposition of a pyridine derivative within one month to no detectable change over more than 12 months, and was governed by both the electronic nature and the position of the substituent. Notably, both strongly electron-withdrawing and strongly electron-donating substituents proved destabilizing, and the decomposition products differed accordingly: sulfonic acids for electron-poor and benzyl chlorides for electron-rich substrates. Sulfonyl fluorides proved considerably more robust: all heteroaromatic derivatives studied, except isothiazole (8% after 12 months) and pyridine (15% within one week), showed no detectable decomposition over 12 months. We believe that the resulting stability map, which assigns each compound to a defined storage class, will make arylmethanesulfonyl halides practical building blocks for early drug discovery in the near future.

papers.title: Metal Nanocluster-Based Metal-Organic Frameworks for Catalysis
papers.abstract: 2 Metal nanoclusters (MNCs) are a class of ultrafine metal nanoparticles, comprising several metal atoms that possess distinctive electronic and geometric structures. In addition to these intrinsic properties, MNCs have various structural parameters that can be precisely tuned, such as the number of constituent atoms, geometric configuration, and heteroatom doping with other metal species. Because MNCs exhibit unique catalytic performance that is highly dependent on these structural factors, their synthesis and application in catalysis have been actively investigated in recent years. Notably, metal nanocluster-based metal-organic frameworks (MNC-MOFs) have emerged as a novel class of porous crystalline nanomaterials. These frameworks not only retain the unique characteristics of the parent MNCs that serve as their secondary building units but also acquire enhanced structural stability and additional functionalities derived from the bridging organic linkers. In this review, we summarize the catalytic performance of MNC-MOFs and discuss the outlook of this rapidly developing research field.

papers.title: Photoinduced C–S Cleavage in Thiols and Oligopeptides to Initiate Controlled Radical Polymerization
papers.abstract: Conjugating synthetic polymers to therapeutic peptides is a powerful strategy to improve their stability and enable less frequent dosing. While numerous methods have broadened the chemical space of accessible polymers, many rely on multi-step syntheses that reduce the overall yield of the final conjugate. Herein, we report a user-friendly, photocatalyst-free method to initiate polymerization via photoinduced cleavage of C–S bonds in native cysteine residues, coupled with reversible addition-fragmentation chain transfer (RAFT) polymerization. Under optimized conditions, a variety of acrylate and acrylamide monomers underwent controlled polymerization from monomeric cysteine units and unprotected (oligo)peptides. We also extended this method to initiate polymerization from other thiol-containing small molecules, including those that yield non-stabilized C-centered radicals. The resulting polymers have narrow mass distributions, good agreement between theoretical and experimental molar masses, and exceptionally high α-chain-end fidelities (>99%). Collectively, these results establish an efficient, selective approach to initiating controlled radical polymerization via C–S cleavage, which can be broadly applied to designing peptide-polymer conjugates and other functional composite materials.

papers.title: Accuracy, Reliability, and Efficiency of a MACE Machine-Learning Interatomic Potential for Aspirin: A Reproducible Benchmark for Molecular Simulation
papers.abstract: Machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) can reproduce density functional theory (DFT) energies and forces at a small fraction of the computational cost, yet an average benchmark error is an incomplete measure of their reliability in molecular simulation. This study presents a reproducible workflow that assesses prediction accuracy, error heterogeneity, and dynamical stability together, using aspirin (C9H8O4), a widely used pharmaceutical compound, as an initial molecular benchmark en route to metal-containing systems. A MACE equivariant graph neural network potential is trained on the MD17 dataset and deployed for molecular dynamics through the Atomic Simulation Environment (ASE). Across 210 762 held-out configurations the potential attains a force root-mean-square error of 15.30 meV Å−1, within the published MACE benchmark range, with a validation-to-test generalization gap of 7.6%. Force error correlates positively with configuration energy (Pearson r = 0.51), the carboxyl carbon emerges as the least reliable atomic site, and 90% of force predictions lie within 23.5 meV Å−1 of the DFT reference. Microcanonical simulations conserve total energy and canonical trajectories remain stable, while single-configuration evaluation is approximately four orders of magnitude (a roughly ten-thousand-fold) faster than the corresponding DFT calculation. By combining aggregate accuracy with configuration-and atom-resolved error analysis and explicit dynamical tests, the workflow exposes behavior that a single error metric conceals. The resulting aspirin benchmark establishes a documented baseline for subsequent validation on metal-containing systems and illustrates the value of assessing error distributions and dynamical behavior alongside mean prediction accuracy.

papers.title: A spectral law for blackbody radiation without temperature or Planck’s constant
papers.abstract: Planck introduced the constant h in 1900 to fit the blackbody spectrum but for years questioned whether it implied that energy is quantized or was merely a feature of its mathematical description. Here we show that his reservation was justified. The shape of the spectrum is determined by a single measured spectral rate, either its peak frequency ν max or its spectral width D , the rate at which the radiation loses phase correlation (its decoherence rate). Their ratio, D /ν max = 4.7368, is a dimensionless constant of the blackbody, internal to its spectrum. The shape follows from two relations among frequencies: the profile is a sum over integer harmonics of each frequency, as required for a recurrence rate, and each harmonic is weighted exponentially in its own frequency on the scale of D . The measured spectrum thus contains the structure needed to predict itself. A mathematical control without the recurrence constraint returns the Rayleigh–Jeans limit. On the COBE/FIRAS spectrum of the cosmic microwave background (CMB), the measured width alone predicts the shape with no fitted parameter, to a median absolute error of 0.005% of the maximum intensity, and the peak frequency ν max to 0.03%. A width–temperature calibration recovers the CMB temperature to 0.01%. Beyond spectral shape, a second spectral constant , governs the fourth-power relation between integrated intensity ( I ) and decoherence rate. Mapping the intensity–decoherence relation into temperature recovers the Stefan–Boltzmann constant 𝜎. The constants h , kB (Boltzmann’s constant) and 𝜎 appear only when the measured spectral relations are expressed in terms of temperature, energy, or absolute radiance, quantities assigned from outside the spectrum. The variable of the blackbody is therefore its coherence, not its temperature: for blackbody radiation, temperature is the decoherence rate expressed in kelvin. For other thermal radiation the two separate: structured thermal emitters at the same temperature emit with decoherence rates 7 to 150 times below the blackbody value. The discreteness the blackbody spectrum requires is the integer order of harmonics, a relation among frequencies, and not quantized energy.

papers.title: A spectral law for blackbody radiation without temperature or Planck’s constant
Charged Interface in Battery Breaks Molecular Chiral Symmetry
papers.abstract: Molecular events occurring within a few solvent layers at a charged electrode surface govern the rate and reversibility of reactions in electrochemical devices, yet such interfacial mechanism was never sufficiently understood at atomistic-level. Here we report a counter-intuitive discovery that charged interface breaks down the mirror symmetry between R - and S -enantiomers of propylene carbonate (PC), which expresses at graphite surface into distinct interphasial chemistries. Using enantiopure R - and S -PC as a chemically identical model pair against their racemic mixture, we find interphase at graphite diverges sharply at high lithium salt concentration, where R -PC enables reversible graphite lithiation with a LiF-rich interphase, while S -PC exfoliates graphite. Simulations and spectroscopies identify the combination of high salt concentration and charged interface collectively responsible for inducing the collapse of enantiomerism into diastereomerism. This knowledge not only establishes a hitherto-unknown dimension for electrolyte design, but also introduces a new concept of broad implications beyond battery applications.

papers.title: Choosing a DFT Protocol That Ranks Deep-Blue TADF Emitters and Pairs Them with Hosts
papers.abstract: Computational screening of deep-blue thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) materials decides which emitters are made and which host each is paired with, yet the descriptors behind these decisions are rarely tested against measurement. We test them on 50 molecules (39 published emitters, eight references and three phosphine-oxide hosts) against measured data for 27 emitters. The range-separated ωB97X-D3 functional overestimates every singlettriplet gap (∆EST) and fails to rank the emitters because its error differs between molecular families; a family offset restores the ranking, and the global hybrids PBE0 and B3LYP rank the gaps directly (Spearman ρ = 0.59 and 0.58). Rate constants built on computed gaps are unreliable, but become accurate once the measured gap is used. For host–emitter pairing, the triplet energies of host and emitter must be computed on one footing: a calibrated host combined with as-computed emitters misclassifies almost every confined pair. A tiered, costed protocol turns these findings into selection rules for screening campaigns.

papers.title: The Curious Case of tBu-Cz-TPA-bis-DPPO: Lowest Structural Order Among Three Deep-Blue Hosts, Yet a Smooth Hole-Only Device Response
papers.abstract: Deep-blue phosphine-oxide hosts are compared by energy levels and photophysics, almost never by microstructure—yet order and film morphology are routinely read as proxies for how well a host will carry charge. Here three related hosts are compared from primary particles to film relief with documented, protocol-tested descriptors. The tert-butyl-substituted S3 host emerges as the least ordered on every scale: the lowest X-ray ordered fraction at every baseline setting, the shortest film correlation length at matched scan size, micrometre-scale relief and the lowest decomposition temperature, while only the S1 host shows lattice fringes. This structural disorder coexists with a smooth hole-only device response. The S3 hole-only device shows a single, nearly ideal relaxation with a capacitance close to the geometric value and an apparent hole mobility of about 5 × 10⁻⁷ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹, comparable to that of the far better-ordered S1 host, although a bias-independent relaxation time is also consistent with the RC response of the layer stack. Long-range disorder in these hosts is therefore compatible with a clean hole-only response, and microstructure alone is not a reliable screen for transport.

papers.title: The film, not the molecule, decides how deep-blue TADF hosts rank on gap and thermal robustness
papers.abstract: Deep-blue host materials for thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) are usually ranked on a few molecular numbers, on the assumption that the isolated molecule anticipates the film. We test that assumption for three phosphine-oxide hosts, S1, S3 and S4, by reading protocol-locked descriptors of the dilute solution, the evaporated film, the powder and the bulk side by side, each with its uncertainty, next to a separate density-functional layer. The descriptors fall into families that rank the hosts differently: film-gap and thermal descriptors place the multi-arm S4 host first, emission and order descriptors place the compact carbazole S1 host first, and band-tail and voltammetric descriptors do not separate the two. The split appears between the molecule and the film: the two hosts emit alike as dilute molecules, yet the S4 film absorption edge lies 0.33 eV higher. Calculations validated against the measured infrared and NMR spectra show frontier levels that move far more with the functional than between hosts. Film gap and thermal robustness must therefore be measured and assessed separately from emissive quality.

papers.title: Ni/TiO <sub>2</sub> Interfaces Enhance Benzaldehyde Selectivity in the Photocatalytic Dehydrogenation of Benzyl Alcohol
papers.abstract: The selective conversion of alcohols to carbonyls (ketones and aldehydes) plays an important role in chemical manufacturing. Photocatalytic acceptorless dehydrogenation offers a light-driven alternative for producing value-added aldehydes and H 2 under mild conditions and with easy separation and high molar efficiency. However, using semiconductor photocatalysts to achieve high selectivity and long-term stability under prolonged high-intensity illumination remains challenging. In this work, we developed CdS/TiO 2 /Ni photocatalysts by depositing TiO 2 onto CdS nanoparticle panels via atomic layer deposition (ALD), followed by Ni cocatalyst photodeposition, for the acceptorless dehydrogenation of benzyl alcohol to benzaldehyde and H 2 . Diluting the benzyl alcohol concentration to a practical range of ~10 vol% (1 M) further increased benzaldehyde selectivity to ~95%. Ni photodeposition and zeta-potential measurements suggest that TiO 2 coatings progressively modify Cd 2+ -associated surface sites through Ti 3+ /Ti 4+ incorporation, altering adsorption kinetics and contributing to the reduced activity. This extends the photocatalyst’s lifespan from ~23 to 60 hours and increases cumulative benzaldehyde and H 2 production. TiO 2 thin-film coatings have emerged as a promising strategy to protect semiconductor photocatalysts while modifying surface active sites and reaction kinetics, and their stability-activity trade-off showing lower initial-stage activity beyond 15-cycle ALD will be discussed alongside proposed mechanisms. This work establishes a semiconductor/coating/cocatalyst design architecture that highlights the importance of engineering surface adsorption and active-site environments, alongside charge-separation strategies based on band-edge energetics and charge-carrier dynamics, to jointly optimize photocatalytic activity and product selectivity for targeted chemical synthesis.

papers.title: Inhibiting LINE-1 retrotransposons therapeutically in disease
papers.abstract: The LINE-1 retrotransposon is a virus-like genomic element that can activate in diseased cells. It has been implicated in cancer, autoimmunity, developmental disorders, infectious disease and neurodegeneration. LINE-1 can be inhibited by reverse transcriptase inhibitors, small molecules originally developed for HIV. The correlation between HIV and LINE-1 inhibition is ∼0.9 on a log scale, in spite of >450 Mya of evolutionary history since retroviruses diverged from retrotransposons. Suppression of HIV requires prevention of a completed 9.7 kb virus insertion into the genome in immune cells. However, every cell in the body already contains >100 copies of LINE-1 that can potentially activate. Even incomplete LINE-1 mediated insertions can cause damaging mutations and genome instability. Furthermore, partial HIV and LINE-1 products in the cytoplasm of cells can contribute to an inflammatory immune response. Preclinical studies have shown LINE-1 inhibitors slow the progression of otherwise unrelated diseases. LINE-1’s contribution to these diseases can potentially be quantified using single-nucleus whole-genome sequencing on diseased tissue, enabling prioritization of disease selection for therapeutic development. Furthermore, LINE-1’s ORF1p protein can be measured in the blood of individuals with certain cancers. LINE-1 inhibitors could therefore be extended to various diseases. Potentially used both as an anti-inflammatory and prophylactically to help preserve genome integrity. Reverse transcriptase inhibitors are available at low cost for HIV, and higher doses of some could be used to inhibit LINE-1. However, reverse transcriptase inhibitors do not prevent DNA cutting by LINE-1’s endonuclease. Novel inhibitors may therefore be required. This, combined with novel diagnostics opens up possibilities for inhibiting LINE-1 therapeutically in disease

papers.title: Orochi: A Physics-Grounded Python Package for Pair Distribution Function Analysis of Crystalline and Low-Dimensional Materials
papers.abstract: Atomic pair distribution function (PDF) analysis from X-ray total scattering is a powerful methodology for determining atomic structure and arrangements across crystalline, disordered, nanostructured, and low-dimensional materials on both laboratory and synchrotron instruments. Fundamentally, PDF analysis relies on two core pillars—PDF data reduction from one-dimensional (1D) total scattering profiles and real-space structural modeling—often accompanied in rapid-acquisition experiments by upstream two-dimensional (2D) detector image processing. However, conventional workflows remain fragmented across disconnected software tools, forcing researchers to manually combine multiple programs and preventing the simultaneous optimization of measurement reduction parameters and crystal structure parameters that is standard in X-ray Rietveld refinement. Furthermore, mainstream PDF modeling engines rely on legacy physical approximations: they enforce three-dimensional (3D) periodic boundary conditions (requiring artificial vacuum supercells for 2D nanosheets), treat atomic scattering factors as angle-independent constants (causing peak distortions in compounds with large atomic number contrast), and approximate number density baselines using macroscopic bulk volume assumptions. Here, the open-source, pure-Python architecture of Orochi (version 4.0) is presented, implementing physical calculations from scratch in Python (accelerated via Numba) to unify total scattering data reduction, symmetry-aware crystallographic modeling, and real-space PDF simulation alongside a dedicated high-Q 2D detector processing module within a self-contained Python environment. Originally developed for laboratory total scattering studies of pharmaceutical glasses and deployed as compiled executable (β-version) tools at SPring-8 beamlines, Orochi has been completely redesigned around an externalized parameter management core (orochi.base) in which parameters are stored in standardized Python dictionaries and accessed via hierarchical string addresses. By bringing parameters outside the calculation engines rather than locking them inside built-in optimizers, this architecture allows multiple module instances across data reduction and structural modeling to be optimized simultaneously by modern optimization algorithms, machine learning libraries, and autonomous AI agents. For structural simulation, intra-cell atomic pair vectors are decoupled from lattice translation vectors to natively support arbitrary periodic boundary conditions across 3D crystals, 2D nanosheets, 1D nanowires, and 0D clusters. The simulation engine incorporates the full scattering vector (Q) dependence of atomic form factors, enabling accurate modeling of heavy/light-element oxides and permitting direct instrumental calibration using standard CeO2 powder rather than monoatomic nickel substitutes. Furthermore, a sinc-convolution density formulation is established to accurately reproduce baseline ripples arising from finite Qmin cutoffs in nanostructured systems. Complete mathematical formulations for all reduction and simulation algorithms are consolidated to establish a rigorous foundation for automated crystallographic analysis.

papers.title: Interaction without an interaction module
papers.abstract: The prevailing way to model a many-body system is to encode every component and then let a module capture interaction. We show that the explicit interaction module is harmful when the number of components increases. We use a simple plastic encoder that compresses a component’s interaction contribution into its representation, and combine the representations by linear aggregation. This modelling approach is simple in form yet delivers unexpectedly excellent performance: it matches the prevailing explicit route under most conditions and exceeds it when a mixture carries more components than the training set covered. Moreover, an encoder produced this way has a clear advantage over per-component descriptors when it is transferred to a similar task: it greatly reduces the data requirements.

papers.title: Bio-derived ionic conductive Guar Gum hydrogels as distributed circuit elements for analogue signal processing: the case of Resistor-Capacitor filters
papers.abstract: Developing functional electronic materials from renewable resources is a key challenge toward more sustainable electronics. Here, we report on a bio-derived ionic conductive hydrogel based on guar gum and demonstrate its direct integration as a functional circuit element for analogue signal processing. Ionic conductivity is introduced by incorporating sodium chloride into the polysaccharide matrix and systematically tuned through the glycerol and salt contents. Increasing glycerol loading enhances conductivity, while varying NaCl concentration produces a non-monotonic response, with maximum conductivities in the 10-2 S cm-1 range and an optimum salt-loading window. The conductive formulation is subsequently combined with pristine guar gum, used as a dielectric, to fabricate guar gum-based resistor-capacitor elements. Their integration into low-pass and high-pass filters demonstrates frequency-selective operation in the audio range, with cut-off frequencies of 658 and 576 Hz and transition slopes of −17 and +15 dB dec-1, respectively. These results demonstrate that guar gumbased ionic hydrogels can move beyond conventional roles as substrates or electrolytes and directly perform circuit-level functions, providing a simple materials platform for low-frequency analogue electronics.

papers.title: Polarization-Driven Hydride Transfer Promotes Cobalt Tetrasulfophthalocyanine-Catalyzed Hydrogen Evolution by Five Orders of Magnitude
papers.abstract: The hydricity of M–H intermediates is a key descriptor and optimization target for the rational design of molecular hydrogen evolution electrocatalysts. Adsorption to an electrode surface is known to augment catalytic rate, but it remains unclear how adsorption affects M-H hydricity. Herein, we quantitatively compare the catalytic activity and mechanism of the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) from cobalt tetrasulfophthalocyanine (CoTSPc) in a dissolved aqueous form (CoTSPc (aq) ) and when adsorbed to the surface of a carbon electrode (CoTSPc/C). At the same electrode potential, CoTSPc/C catalyzes HER at a rate that is over five orders of magnitude faster than CoTSPc (aq) . Mechanistic studies indicate that both CoTSPc/C and CoTSPc (aq) catalyze HER via a rate-limiting hydride transfer to a proton donor in solution to form H 2 . Hydride transfer from Co-H in CoTSPc (aq) is a purely chemical step defined by a constant hydricity of 22.4 kcal mol −1 that is independent of applied potential. In contrast, hydride transfer from Co-H in CoTSPc/C is strongly polarization dependent, decreasing hydricity by ~23 kcal mol −1 V −1 to values as low as 1.2 kcal mol −1 at −1.1 V vs SHE, leading to the observed rate promotion. We attribute this mechanistic change to the positioning of the CoTSPc-H intermediate within the electrochemical double layer, such that the hydride traverses the interfacial electrostatic potential difference during the RLS. These results demonstrate the power of surface adsorption to generate highly reactive molecular hydrides and fundamentally reshape the free energy landscape of electrocatalysis.

papers.title: Late-Stage Functionalization of Hydroxamic Acid Pharmaceuticals through Oxidative C-N Bond Formation
papers.abstract: A mild, copper-catalyzed protocol is used for the oxidative activation of pharmaceuticals bearing hydroxamic acid functionalities. The aerobic dehydrogenation generates reactive nitroso intermediates that smoothly and selectively undergo trapping with olefins leading to the N -allylated products through ene-type reactions. Moreover, in presence of 1,3-dienes, [4+2]-cycloadditions provide access to bicyclic hydroxamate derivatives. The methodology is effective across a set of structurally diverse active pharmaceutical ingredients covering a broad application range from inflammation to cancer and neuromuscular diseases.

papers.title: High-Performance Chemiresistive Humidity Sensing and Quantum Isotopic Differentiation with Single Crystals of a Conductive MOF Hosting Electron Spin Qubits
papers.abstract: Conductive metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) offer a versatile platform for chemiresistive humidity sensing, a capability vital for industrial and biomedical applications. However, grain boundaries and uncontrolled crystallite orientations in commonly used polycrystalline devices limit sensing performance, while electrical responses alone lack specificity for distinguishing H2O from D2O. Here, we report high-performance chemiresistive humidity sensing and quantum isotopic differentiation using single crystals of a representative conductive MOF, Cd2(TTFTB) (TTFTB4− = tetrathiafulvalene tetrabenzoate). Leveraging intrinsic charge transport modulated by a solvent screening effect, the single-crystal devices significantly outperform polycrystalline counterparts that exhibit negligible sensing capability. Specifically, they achieve an ultralow detection limit of 100 ppm, a broad dynamic range up to 100% relative humidity, and a high average on/off response exceeding 3 × 106. Comparative measurements across solvent vapors reveal selectivity for water vapor and relate current modulation to solvent dielectric constant, hydrogen-bonding ability, and molecular volume. Furthermore, we harnessed the electron spin coherence of embedded TTF⋅+ radical qubits in a collection of Cd2(TTFTB) crystals to unambiguously distinguish H2O from D2O via hyperfine spectroscopy, complementing high-performance single-crystal chemiresistive detection with quantum-enabled isotopic identification. Taken together, these results demonstrate the feasibility and considerable promise of a dual-mode sensing approach that integrates chemiresistive and quantum sensing.

papers.title: Model Dependence and Cancellation in a Fixed-Geometry Lactone Energy Cycle
papers.abstract: A small signed energy response can conceal larger individual changes and may not transfer between computational models. We compare fixed lactone and methanolysis-product conformers through a balanced eight-state protonation-response cycle. Existing density-functional calculations give gas and implicit-methanol cycles of +18.327235 and +4.381410 kJ/mol. Matched 0.020 Å H-only displacements lower every cation energy but change the solvent cycle by −0.072625 kJ/mol. The four-arm first-order force-work prediction is −0.237920 kJ/mol, with a signed finite-step remainder of +0.165294 kJ/mol. A prospectively frozen challenge of 184 single-point calculations preserves qualitative medium attenuation in both tested approximate Hamiltonians but fails the complete predefined local-response rule: their solvent cycle changes become +0.047132 and +0.127370 kJ/mol. This distinguishes medium-response agreement from local-response transferability without establishing optimized structures or experimental accuracy. Original ωB97X with separately specified D3 dispersion and Becke–Johnson damping, def2-TZVP/def2-universal-jkfit density fitting and the solvation model based on density were used in PySCF 2.14.0. Stored gradients and accepted endpoints define the force-work analysis. GFN1-xTB and GFN2-xTB in xTB 6.7.1 evaluate gas and analytical linearized Poisson–Boltzmann methanol models across nine signed displacements, with 974/2030-point endpoint surface-grid controls. An independent raw-output reader and actual moved-package reproductions check the deterministic analysis; no fitting, optimization or uncertainty calibration is performed.

papers.title: Multi-Scale Light-Based Biofabrication of Acrylate-Free Magnetic Gelatin Composites for Transient Vascular Navigation
papers.abstract: Photocurable hydrogels derived from native proteins offer high bio-functionality for biomedical micro-devices; however, traditional approaches require chemical functionalization such as methacrylation, altering native bio-activity. Here, an acrylate-free photocurable magnetic composite ink is developed using native gelatin photocrosslinked via ruthenium-mediated di-tyrosine coupling and loaded with zinc-substituted iron oxide (ZFO) nanoparticles. Incorporating magnetic nanoparticles introduces an inherent trade-off between magnetic responsiveness and light penetration during light-based fabrication. By systematic optical and photorheological mapping, an upper processing window of 6 wt% nanoparticle loading under the standard irradiation conditions is established, preserving hydrogel network density at stiffness of ~2 kPa while maintaining printability. The precursor ink is capable of printing structures across length scales via mold casting, digital light processing (DLP), and two-photon polymerization (TPP). The ZFO nanoparticles show dose-dependent cytocompatibility, with cell viability above the ISO 10993-5 threshold (70%) up to 150 µg mL−1, and the dried ZFO-loaded hydrogels show superparamagnetic-like behavior, reaching about 42% of saturation (8.4 emu g−1) at 25 mT. Electromagnetic navigation demonstrates shape-programmed directional alignment, gradient-driven translation, selective Y-junction branch navigation, and 3D out-of-plane friction reduction. Finally, the composites exhibit passive disintegration under simulated physiological conditions within two weeks, presenting a versatile platform for transient bio-hybrid medical micro-devices.

papers.title: Toward the Synthesis of Verteporfin from Hemin and Protoporphyrin IX
papers.abstract: This report describes two approaches toward verteporfin (benzoporphyrin derivative monoacid), a photosensitizer used in photodynamic therapy. One starts from hemin and the other from commercial protoporphyrin IX (PpIX). The hemin route first converts hemin into PpIX dimethyl ester, by reductive removal of iron and concomitant acid-catalyzed esterification. The benzoporphyrin skeleton of verteporfin is then built from PpIX dimethyl ester by a Diels-Alder cycloaddition with dimethyl acetylenedicarboxylate (DMAD). The vinyl group and the neighboring pyrrole double bond of ring A or ring B act as the diene, and the activated alkyne adds to them to form a new six-membered ring carrying two methyl ester groups. Throughout the sequence, reaction progress was monitored by UV-visible spectroscopy, thin-layer chromatography, HPLC, and 1H NMR spectroscopy. The Diels–Alder step was studied under three activation conditions: reflux in 1,2-dichloroethane (bp 83.5 °C) and in 2-methyltetrahydrofuran (bp 80 °C), both in an oil bath set to 85 °C, and microwave irradiation at 100-140 °C. The HPLC, NMR and UV-visible data are consistent with partial conversion to benzoporphyrin products, but the products were not isolated and their structures were not confirmed at this stage. The work provides a critical assessment of the reaction parameters governing the key cycloaddition and identifies the main limitations encountered in each step, with a view to informing future optimization of the process.

papers.title: Data-Driven Analysis of C–F Bond Lengths in Two-Dimensional Fluorinated Carbon Materials
papers.abstract: The C–F bond length is an important structural descriptor of fluorinated carbon materials, but its reported values remain widely scattered across the literature. Here, a compilation and statistical analysis of C–F bond lengths is presented, focusing on two-dimensional (2D) fluorinated carbon materials and comparing them with fluorinated low-dimensional and molecular systems. The 2D dataset comprises 176 entries spanning C0.86F to C200F and covering publications from 1934 to 2026. It includes bulk, single-layer, and double-layer architectures, with carbon conformation in bulk structures also taken into account (e.g., puckered, planar, and mixed sp2/sp3). Mean C–F bond lengths decrease progressively from bulk graphite fluorides and fluorine–graphite intercalation compounds (~1.42 Å) to single- and double-layer fluorographenes (~1.40 and ~1.38 Å, respectively). They are generally longer than those of conventional molecular fluorides, fluorocarbonium ions and fluorocarbenium ions, but shorter than those in three-center fluoronium ions. Experimental determinations from the literature, including solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance and X-ray/neutron pair distribution function analysis, give broadly consistent mean bond lengths. Computational results from the literature likewise show broadly consistent values across exchange–correlation functionals. Decreasing fluorine content increases the mean C–F bond length by ~9% from ~1.39 Å for CF to ~1.51 Å for C16F. Puckeredchair structures generally show longer C–F bonds than puckered-boat structures, with a difference of ~0.04 Å in bulk materials. Together, these results provide an accessible reference that brings scattered C–F bond-length data together, revealing statistically supported trends that are difficult to identify from individual reports.

papers.title: Metal-Organic Frameworks as Single-Particle Contrast Agents for Localization Optoacoustic Tomography
papers.abstract: Localization optoacoustic tomography (LOT) resolves microvascular networks beyond the acoustic diffraction limit by detecting and tracking individual absorbing particles in the bloodstream. Single-particle detection in LOT remains challenging for clinically acceptable contrast materials, typically requiring particle diameters of ~5 μm to overcome the strong absorption background of blood. Here, we show that metal-organic framework (MOF) microparticles overcome this limitation. Rods (3.43 × 0.36 μm) and ellipsoids (1.03 × 0.53 μm) of the porphyrinic zirconium MOF PCN-222 take up 16 to 18 wt% indocyanine green (ICG), which is retained in the framework. Both morphotypes are resolved as isolated optoacoustic (OA) point sources in vitro, with single-particle signal-to-noise ratios of 13 to 82, which would still allow the detection of particles with 22 to 42% of the present volume, down to ~0.4 μm in equivalent diameter. The combined emission of framework and dye allows each particle to be counted by flow cytometry, which sets absolute concentrations for dosing. The particles retain ≥96% of their ICG in water and ≥88% in undiluted serum, keep their per-particle ICG signal in serum, and leave the calcein AM retention of murine dendritic cells at 97 to 103% of the untreated control after 48 h at up to 75.9 (PCN-222-R@ICG) and 15.9 (PCN-222-E@ICG) particles per cell. After intravenous injection at 800 nm excitation and ~35 mJ cm−2, both morphotypes were individually localized in the mouse brain, yielding super-resolved cortical microangiograms and blood flow velocity maps. By enabling LOT with particles one to two orders of magnitude smaller in volume than previous ICG-based agents, PCN-222@ICG microparticles, to our knowledge the first MOFbased contrast agents for LOT, extend single-particle optoacoustic imaging to smaller particle sizes.

papers.title: Ensemble RMSD-Driven Metadynamics for Electrolyte-Reduction Pathway Discovery
Machine Learning-Guided Design of Cu-Based Single-Atom Alloy Nanoclusters for Selective CO2 Electroreduction
papers.abstract: Metal nanoclusters are highly promising for the electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (eCO2RR) due to their abundant low-coordination sites and size-dependent electronic properties. Alloying these clusters with isolated transition metal atoms to form Cu-based single-atom alloys (Cu-SAAs) provides a powerful strategy to finely tune their local structures and electronic properties. Because the dopant element identifies and its specific surface site strongly dictate *CO adsorption and subsequent eCO2RR pathways, systematically mapping this combinatorial space is critical. To clarify these effects, we synergistically couple high-throughput density functional theory (DFT) calculations and machine learning (ML) to evaluate *CO adsorption across 1,944 small Cu-SAAs nanocluster candidates. Using reliable DFT-derived adsorption data, we developed an iterative Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model capable of rapidly predicting binding energies by identifying the governing structural and electronic descriptors. Analysis of these large-scale predictions highlights how specific combinations of dopant elements and geometrical sites modulate *CO adsorption strength, directly influencing catalytic trajectories. This work establishes an interpretable, data-driven framework for the rational design of Cu-SAAs nanoclusters tailored for targeted eCO2RR products.

papers.title: Czochralski Growth of YSGAG Crystals: Experimental, Numerical, and Data-Assisted Analysis of Solid–Liquid Interface Shape
papers.abstract: Yttrium scandium gallium aluminum garnet (YSGAG) is a promising diamagnetic substrate for yttrium iron garnet thin films, but scalable Czochralski growth requires control of the solid–liquid interface. Here, growth experiments, thermophysical-property measurements, and CGSim simulations are combined to analyze interface-shape control in YSGAG. The Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) model was constrained and assessed using experimentally observed interface profiles from early, middle, and late stages of the constant-diameter regime. The resulting model was used to generate a 190-point CFD dataset spanning crystal diameter, rotation rate, growth rate, initial melt charge, and crystallized fraction. A Gaussian-process surrogate, combined with Sobol sensitivity analysis, accumulated local effects, Spearman correlations, and SHAP attribution, was used to identify process correlations controlling interface deflection. Crystallized fraction was the dominant variable, while crystal diameter and rotation rate showed secondary, interaction-dependent effects. The results show that interface flattening in YSGAG should be treated as a coupled, growth-stage-aware control problem rather than as an isolated single-parameter adjustment.

papers.title: Predicting Regulator-Listed N-Nitrosamines from API Structure: A Rule-Based Method with a Retrospectively Corrected FDA and EMA Evaluation
papers.abstract: Regulator lists of N-nitrosamines include assessed and hypothetical impurities as well as detected compounds. We evaluate a deterministic rule-based method that proposes N-nitrosamine structures from an active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) through direct nitrosation, selected nitrosative dealkylation pathways and nitrosation after one degradation step. The engine was refined against the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) list and frozen. An external European Medicines Agency (EMA) set excludes all FDA API identities using standardized parent connectivity. Source parsing, identity grouping and analysis were corrected after the initial results had been seen; this is a retrospective evaluation. A unique API identity and reference connectivity pair is the evaluation unit. The method recovered 55 of 112 external pairs across 88 APIs, recall 0.491 (Wilson 95% interval 0.400-0.582; API-cluster bootstrap 0.398-0.588). A post hoc ablation limited to direct secondary-amine nitrosation recovered 26 pairs (0.232); the paired gain was 0.259 (cluster bootstrap 0.186-0.336). The method proposed a median of 1 and mean of 1.48 candidates per API, versus 0.33 for the ablation. Degradation routes contributed 21 hits. Development recall was 247/272 (0.908). Of 57 external misses, 29 were positive and 25 negative in a fragmentwise cleavage substructure proxy; separate adjudications identified 2 reference/name disagreements and 1 ring-hydrolysis implementation defect. These cases remain scored misses. Incomplete reference lists prevent a precision estimate, and structural matches do not establish actual impurity formation. Deposited outputs support statistical recomputation and candidate-membership checks; prediction generation requires the proprietary frozen engine.

papers.title: Polymer interface-driven perovskite crystallization in electrospun fibers
papers.abstract: Polymer incorporation into metal halide perovskite films is an effective strategy to control perovskite nucleation and crystallization, passivate defects and suppress humidity-induced degradation. In this work, we use enthalpic interactions between insulating polymers and formamidinium lead iodide (FAPbI 3 ) to control FAPbI 3 crystal size, quality and location. Specifically, we electrospin interconnected networks of FAPbI 3 precursor/poly(vinylpyrrolidone) (PVP) composite nanofibers, then encapsulate the fibers in a poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) or poly(phenylene oxide) (PPO) scaffold prior to thermal annealing to induce α-FAPbI 3 crystallization. Polar PMMA nucleated dense, polycrystalline FAPbI 3 crystals at the PMMA/fiber interface. Non-polar PPO scaffolds, on the other hand, suppressed FAPbI 3 nucleation at the interface, suggesting enthalpically unfavorable perovskite-polymer interactions. Transmission electron microscopy revealed that PPO drives FAPbI 3 crystallization within fiber interiors to form FAPbI 3 core/PVP shell structures. PPO-confined FAPbI 3 fibers exhibited long excited carrier lifetimes of ~1200 ns, surpassing those of bulk single crystals, but poor charge transfer to a hole transport layer due to the presence of an insulating PVP shell. Unconfined and PMMA-confined FAPbI 3 fibers, in contrast, showed rapid, defect-induced photoluminescence decay and fast charge transfer, the latter of which contributed to improved photodetector responsivity compared to PPO-confined fiber photodetectors. Polymer incorporation into these perovskite films improved their environmental stability, with α-FAPbI 3 persisting for more than seven weeks of storage in air. Collectively, these results demonstrate the use of perovskite-polymer interactions to dictate perovskite crystallization outcomes, including size, location and defect density.

papers.title: New Oxygen Sensor with Polyaniline Spin Probe and Low Frequency EPR (L-Band) Detection System
papers.abstract: Our research demonstrates the potential of certain PANI samples to serve as sensitive and reliable spin probes for oxygen detection, while also highlighting the advantages of the lowfrequency EPR technique. Compared to other methods of measuring oxygen concentration, the new sensor—based on a PANI spin probe and a low-frequency EPR detector—offers unique benefits: it ensures high sensitivity to changes in oxygen concentration and does not require direct contact between the EPR detector and the sensor itself (the polyaniline probe). This sensor can be placed in isolated environments, including biological samples (tissues), and - thanks to the use of nanodispersed polyaniline - even inside living cells.

papers.title: Hybrid Joining Technologies for Composites: Mechanisms, Performance, Challenges, and Perspectives
papers.abstract: Fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) composites are increasingly used in aircraft structures with their high specific strength, stiffness, corrosion resistance, and lightweight nature. However, reliably joining FRP components is challenging because mechanical joining can create stress concentrations, fiber damage, and delamination, while adhesive bonding can cause peel stress, environmental degradation, and inspection challenges. This review systematically covers hybrid joining approaches for FRPs, emphasizing joint designs, load-sharing mechanisms, mechanical performance, surface treatment, interlayer engineering, aerospace applications, certification concerns, and emerging technologies. This systematic literature review focused on bolted-bonded, riveted-bonded, welded-bonded, and friction-based hybrid connections. The review analyzed the evaluated research for static strength, fatigue behavior, impact resistance, failure mechanisms, joint design parameters, surface modification, interlayer engineering, aerospace implementation, inspection, repair, and certification. Other emerging themes included structural health monitoring, thermoplastic composites, automated joining, and bio-inspired interfaces. Based on the literature, this study shows that hybrid joining provides load-transfer mechanisms and progressive failure behavior comparable to those of single-joining approaches. Reported impact testing suggests that hybrid joints absorb roughly 45% more energy than adhesive joints. Moreover, surface treatments such as abrasion, plasma treatment, laser ablation, and chemical etching, as well as toughening interlayers, can further improve interfacial performance and damage tolerance. Aircraft applications include thermoplastic control surface components, wing-box joints, and fuselage splices. The performance of hybrid FRP joints depends heavily on controlled load sharing between the adhesive and mechanical or friction-based joints. Therefore, adhesive layer thickness, fastener torque, edge distance, overlap length, and fastener spacing are important in reducing stress concentrations and progressive failure. Tailored interlayers and surface activation may further improve fracture resistance and adhesion. However, the following are restricted: certification, non-destructive assessment, long-term durability, repair techniques, and uniformity of repair procedures. Future work should develop new solutions for monitoring, automation, production efficiency, and damage tolerance by combining embedded sensors, machine learning, thermoplastic welding, robotic joining, and bio-inspired interfaces. Hybrid joining methods provide an integrated approach to enhancing the structural performance of FRP composite connections, including damage tolerance, fatigue endurance, and reliability, particularly in aerospace applications. This is achieved through complementary joining techniques that enable gradual load transfer and maintain load-carrying capacity after local damage. Future research should also focus on standardized qualification procedures, standardized processes for reliable non-destructive inspection, environmental durability, automated process control, intelligent health monitoring, and scalable certification procedures to enable the wider application of hybrid composite joining technologies in next-generation aerospace structures.

papers.title: Computational Exploration of Dopamine Adsorption on Carbon Nanotubes for Electrochemical Sensing
papers.abstract: Dopamine (DA), has a variety of impacts on human health. Due to the high cost and labor-intensity of its current measurement methods, sensitive and low-cost electrochemical sensors with carbonaceous substrate materials have been proposed as an alternative. Single-chirality single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) have gained interest for their chirality-dependent properties. In a recent study, we demonstrated that the sensing response of DA varies for SWCNT chiralities. In this study, we performed density-functional theory (DFT) simulations to identify low-energy conformers of DA and to gain atomic-level understanding of the interactions upon DA adsorption on (6,6) SWCNTs. We utilized Bayesian Optimization Structure Search (BOSS) to sample energy landscapes and identify the lowest-energy DA conformers and adsorption configurations. As a result, we found 6 low-energy conformers of DA and one adsorption configuration type of DA on the (6,6) SWCNT, where the aromatic ring of DA adsorbs flat on the SWCNT and the flexible side chain is oriented away from the substrate. Analysis of its electronic structure revealed that DA physisorbs on the (6,6) SWCNT via the aromatic ring. The present workflow can be expanded to other chiralities and molecules to support substrate material development for electrochemical sensors with applications in healthcare and environmental monitoring.

papers.title: Comparative Analysis of Basic Machine Learning and Rigorous Free-Energy Calculation on Benchmarking Datasets of Protein-Ligand Binding Affinity
papers.abstract: Rigorous free-energy methods based on molecular dynamics simulations like free-energy perturbation (FEP) are nowadays widely applied in lead optimization in pharmaceutical companies. Due to sampling restrictions and potential force-field deficiencies, it is common practice to first validate the applicability of FEP to a target/chemical series using a small number of known compounds, before applying it prospectively. As rigorous methods require significant computational resources, we want to explore how basic machine learning (ML) methods perform under the same conditions, i.e., training on a small number of known compounds and estimating the affinity of novel variants in the same chemical series. We apply classical ML models using 2D and 3D molecular descriptors, alongside two implementations of 3D quantitative structure–activity relationship modeling, and integrate the predictions through meta-learning. For many of the standard benchmarking datasets, we find that one of the ML models matches or exceeds the performance of FEP. Interestingly, ML-based predictions generally exhibit flatter slopes in parity plots, but without substantial effect on the relative rank ordering of compounds. Given their lower computational cost and ease of deployment, basic ML methods, particularly the meta-learner, emerge as a powerful complement to rigorous free-energy methods for estimating binding affinities within chemical series.

papers.title: Dynamics of oxygen and hydrogen species at the surface Ru/Al <sub>2</sub> O <sub>3</sub> revealed by advanced operando spectroscopies
papers.abstract: The microscopic evolution of supported Ru-oxide nanoparticles under reducing conditions remains a central challenge in hydrogenation catalysis. In 5 wt% Ru/Al2O3 catalyst, the transformation of oxidized Ru species into metallic Ru, the formation of hydrides, and hydrogen exchange with the support are closely related but difficult to resolve simultaneously. Here, operando IR and O K-edge NEXAFS, supported by quantum chemical DFT calculations, show that the initially hydroxylated Ru-oxide surface contains *OOH and *OO-H species at unsaturated Ru sites characterized by a distinct O K-edge electronic signature. Upon dehydration, removal of neighboring surface groups strongly stabilizes a bridged η2-peroxo species with a characteristic vibrational fingerprint. Subsequent exposure to H2 drives a low-temperature multistep reduction to metallic Ru and leads to the transient formation of terminal Ru–H species. Inelastic neutron scattering (INS) measurements independently reveal multi-coordinated hydrides under hydrogen-rich conditions, while H/D isotope exchange shows reversible hydrogen exchange between Ru nanoparticles and the support. The concomitant recovery of alumina hydroxyl groups upon H2 exposure further supports hydrogen transfer to the support. These results provide insight on the evolution of the catalyst, showing that surface dehydroxylation, Ru-oxide reduction, hydride formation, and hydrogen transfer are closely connected during activation of Ru/Al2O3 catalysts.

papers.title: A spectral law for blackbody radiation without temperature or Planck’s constant
Breaking Linear Scaling Relations for Regioselective Phenol Hydroxylation via SiC-Supported Dual-Atom Catalysts
papers.abstract: The electrochemical hydroxylation of phenol offers a sustainable route to valueadded dihydroxybenzene isomers, yet rational catalyst design remains limited by 2 poor regioselectivity and structural instability. This study investigates silicon carbide (SiC) monoliths as exceptionally robust supports for dual-atom catalysts, utilizing density functional theory and operando ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) to screen 45 bimetallic combinations. Mechanistic analysis reveals that phenol undergoes site-specific activation directly at the Si-lattice, dictating regioselectivity toward catechol (ortho-pathway) or hydroquinone (para-pathway). Crystal Orbital Hamilton Population analyses and energetic span modeling demonstrate that macroscopic turnover is strictly governed by dynamic orbital overlap and precise d-band alignment. The TiFe configuration optimally minimizes the energetic span for ortho-hydroxylation, while TiMn provide the most competitive pathways for para-hydroxylation. Two-dimensional microkinetic mapping confirms that optimizing surface binding thermodynamics and bimetallic electronics successfully circumvents traditional linear scaling relations. Furthermore, operando AIMD simulations at 298 K validate these models, confirming that aromatic 𝜋-electron disruption constitutes the kinetic bottleneck (0.70 eV) and highlighting the critical role of interfacial potassium cations in electrostatically shielding polarized radical transition states.

papers.title: Spatial Inhomogeneity of Thermal Degradation of Semi-Crystalline Polymers
papers.abstract: The thermal degradation of polymers is typically interpreted as a uniform chemical process involving molecular weight reduction and oxidation. However, the role of localized microstructural changes as defect sites that deteriorate polymer mechanical performance remains underexplored owing to the limitations of conventional bulk characterization techniques. We applied an isotope-labeled Raman mapping technique with molecular weight selectivity to visualize the structural evolution of semi-crystalline polyethylene during long-term thermal exposure under conditions in which the bulk molecular weight and carbonyl index remained nearly unchanged. In this material, mechanical deterioration is induced by spatially localized structural changes. Despite the negligible average chemical change, the ductility decreased drastically upon heating. High-resolution mapping revealed discrete domains of enhanced crystallinity and conformational ordering, which emerged with spherulite-scale correlation lengths that expanded with the aging time. These domains spatially coincide with the fracture-origin regions after tensile deformation. Molecular weight-resolved analysis showed that high-molecular-weight chains preferentially underwent degradation-induced crystallization (chemi-crystallization), suggesting that regions rich in tie molecules are the primary transformation sites. Our findings show that thermal exposure is a defect nucleation process governed by structural heterogeneity, providing a new framework for predicting the long-term reliability of semi-crystalline polymers. This mechanism provides a predictive foundation for a wide range of engineering thermoplastics.

papers.title: Benchmarking a fast energy model for predicting the stability of solvated surface sites for organic molecular crystals: The paracetamol–water interface
papers.abstract: Crystallisation of molecular materials is important for a range of industries including the pharmaceutical and agrochemical sectors. Prediction of the crystal growth and dissolution of such systems requires detailed knowledge of the thermodynamics, and ideally kinetics, of surface sites in contact with solvent. The most reliable method for obtaining the free energy of solvated kinks, step edges and terraces with molecular resolution is often via computer simulation using molecular dynamics, as this includes explicit solvent interactions and entropy changes, but comes at a significant computational cost. Here this approach is used to provide a series of benchmark standard free energies for dissolution of different types of surface sites at the paracetamol form I (001) interface with water. A modified GAFF force field is used that is calibrated to predict the solubility of paracetamol in good agreement with experiment. These reference free energies are then used to examine the accuracy of a faster, more approximate method that has been previously tested primarily for solubility and morphology prediction, namely the CrystalClear protocol. Results show that not only do both approaches have the same qualitative trends, with removal of the first molecule from the terrace at the aqueous interface having a significantly higher thermodynamic cost relative to removal from kink sites, but both approaches are in quantitative agreement to within the uncertainty of the molecular dynamics results for nearly all surface sites. The only site that exhibits a noticeable difference is for the removal of the final molecule from a step and occurs due to relaxation effects. The excellent agreement between the two methods examined here provides confidence that the CrystalClear approach represents a reliable and efficient means of predicting the thermodynamic stability of individual molecular binding sites at solvated interfaces, which can then be used for coarse-grained methods such as Monte Carlo simulation of crystal growth and dissolution.

papers.title: Enhancing Interfacial Exciton Conversion in Blue Upconversion OLEDs through Oligomer-Controlled Molecular Orientation
papers.abstract: Controlling molecular orientation is central to high-performance organic optoelectronics. Anthracene oligomers provide an orientation-tunable platform for elucidating orientation effects in upconversion organic light-emitting diodes (UC-OLEDs), which generate blue emission at exceptionally low driving voltages through interfacial charge-transfer (CT) states, CT-to-triplet (CT-to-T1) conversion, and triplet–triplet annihilation. Across anthracene derivatives, increasing horizontal orientation enhances external quantum efficiency (EQE) beyond that expected from light outcoupling alone. To identify the underlying processes, the randomly oriented monomer 1,2-ADN and the preferentially horizontally oriented dimer p-ADN-1 serve as representatives. Both interface-exchanged devices, in which interfacial and emitting-layer anthracene species are varied independently, and transient absorption measurements consistently show that horizontal orientation enhances interfacial CT-to-T1 conversion. Overall, a more horizontal orientation of the host molecules improves light outcoupling by only ~4% but enhances interfacial CT-to-T1 conversion efficiency by 1.3–1.5-fold. Beyond its ultralow turn-on voltage of 1.5 V, the optimized p-ADN-1 device achieves an EQE of 2.61%, a 1.5-fold improvement over the 1,2-ADN device, and a LT50 (time to 50% of the initial luminance) exceeding 1750 h at 1000 cd m−2. To our knowledge, these values represent the highest EQE and longest operational lifetime reported for blue OLEDs with turn-on voltages below 2 V. These findings establish molecular orientation as an active structural parameter governing both light outcoupling and interfacial exciton conversion.

papers.title: Helicene-Blade Molecular Propellers
papers.abstract: Molecular propellers have attracted intense interest as a fascinating class of chiral molecules, as exemplified by hexaphenylbenzene derivatives bearing peripheral point-chiral substituents. However, these molecules typically show limited chiral configuration stability, hindering applications that require stable chiroptical responses. Herein, helicenes are introduced as blades to construct molecular propellers for the first time, achieving enhanced chiral stability. A stereospecific synthesis from enantiopure aza[7]helicene (A7H) is employed to obtain a propeller-shaped A7H hexamer (HA7H), which shows a high critical temperature (Tc) of 23 °C for chiral inversion. Such a high Tc sets a new record among molecular propellers (typically from –50 to 10 °C), highlighting the advantage of helicenes as blades for acquiring configurationally stable molecular propellers.

papers.title: Beyond Atom Pairs: Multicenter Crystal Orbital Hamilton Populations for Molecules and Solids
papers.abstract: The Crystal Orbital Hamilton Population (COHP) is a standard tool for energyresolved bonding analysis in solids and also applies to molecules, but it assigns the band energy only to atom pairs. A multicenter bond therefore has no energy of its own: across the five molecules and solids studied here, pairwise integrated COHP reports strong two-center bonding (−1.8 to −3.5 eV) and cannot distinguish an electrondeficient bridge from an electron-rich unit. We here formulate a multicenter COHP from the idempotency of the zero-temperature density matrix P in each spin channel, P 2 = P , which gives Tr(HP ) = Tr(HPn−1) for every n ≥ 2. Projecting the resulting cyclic matrix products onto ordered n-atom groups and replacing one density-matrix factor with the spectral function A(E) yields COHP (n) C1,...,Cn (E). Its energy integral, summed over all n-tuples, recovers the band energy independently for every n, and the n = 2 expression reduces to standard COHP without approximation. Across these systems, the three-center energy spans about 1320 meV: it is bonding in the B–H–B bridge of diborane (−820 meV), near zero in the Cr–O–Cr pathway of half-metallic

papers.title: Targeted Covalent Inhibition of Pyk2 via a Paralog-Specific Cysteine for Selective Antiplatelet Action
papers.abstract: Focal adhesion kinase 2 (FAK2, also known as Pyk2), a focal adhesion kinase (FAK) family member, has emerged as a promising antiplatelet target with minimal impact on normal hemostasis. However, the development of Pyk2-selective inhibitors has been constrained by limited paralog selectivity and suboptimal in vivo pharmacokinetics. Here, we report compound 2-1, a first-in-class covalent inhibitor that selectively targets Pyk2 by hijacking a unique cysteine residue (Cys545) absent in the sister kinase FAK1. Using structure-guided design, we modified the reversible inhibitor PF-4594755 with an acrylamide electrophile and a methylazetidine spacer to enable covalent engagement of Cys545. Intracellular NanoBRET assays and an alkyne-tagged analogue of 2-1 validated its covalent mechanism and kinome-wide selectivity. Functionally, 2-1 impaired platelet responses to the thromboxane A2 analog U46619, while showing moderate-to-minimal effects on adenosine diphosphate- and thrombin-induced aggregation. Under microfluidic simulated arterial and venous flow conditions in human whole blood, 2-1 reduced platelet adhesion comparably to aspirin. In an electrolytic carotid artery thrombosis model, 2-1 tripled the thrombolytic efficacy of recombinant tissue plasminogen activator without increasing bleeding risks. This work provides a foundation for the development of selective Pyk2 inhibitors as a new class of safe, bleeding-sparing antiplatelets for thrombotic disorders.
