papers.title: Controlled Competition Reduces Errors in Nanostructure-Based DNA Data Storage
papers.abstract: DNA nanotechnology offers a promising route toward molecular data storage with exceptional density, longevity, and energy efficiency. Unlike sequence-based approaches that rely on large-scale synthesis and sequencing, structural DNA data storage encodes information into spatial architectures readable at the single-molecule level. However, practical implementation is hindered by substitution errors -particularly 0-to-1 “bit flips” - that arise during pooled readout and compromise data fidelity. Here, we introduce and systematically benchmark a set of thermodynamically-tuned error protection strategies for DNA ‘hard drive’ nanostructures, based on controlled competition between a label strand and a protector strand. By rationally modulating hybridisation stability through toehold truncation, internal mismatches, or self-complementary clamping, we identify a protector strand with a single cytosine-thymine (C-T) mismatch as an optimal design. This straightforward modification yields >90% readout fidelity and increases the information-theoretic channel capacity 25-fold relative to unprotected overhangs. The 1 C–T mismatch protector will enable accurate data writing and pooled readout using solid-state nanopore sensing, demonstrating scalable, high-fidelity molecular data retrieval. Overall, our findings establish new design principles for error suppression in structural DNA data storage and represent a key step toward practical, sustainable molecular information technologies.

papers.title: Data-driven discovery and substrate scope mapping of dual-ligand nickel catalysts for C(sp2)–C(sp3) cross-electrophile coupling
papers.abstract: Dual-ligand nickel catalysis has emerged as an effective strategy for improving C( sp 2 )–C( sp 3 ) cross-electrophile coupling (XEC), yet the systematic studies identifying productive ligand combinations and mapping their target scope remain limited. In this work, we combine high-throughput experimentation (HTE) with a simple, interpretable data-analysis workflow to identify and validate synergistic bidentate–tridentate ligand pairs for Zn-mediated Ni-catalyzed XEC. An HTE screening campaign spanning nine model reactions and 77 ligand combinations per plate enabled simultaneous evaluation of performance, robustness, and non-additive behavior of the catalytic systems. Statistical analysis revealed six ligand pairs that combined strong overall activity with measurable positive synergy, including combinations related to previously reported systems as well as new productive pairings. Using a diverse panel of 96 pharmaceutically relevant (hetero)aryl bromides, we demonstrated that dual-ligand systems often outperformed the best single ligand and could cover the studied substrate space more efficiently. Critically, for certain dual-ligand catalysts, these benefits tracked with interpretable electronic descriptors, providing a practical basis for prioritizing which substrate classes are most likely to profit from the usage of ligand pairs. Together, these results demonstrate that HTE coupled with lightweight statistical analysis provides an efficient route to the discovery of complex catalytic systems, their prioritization and mapping their scope. Our findings also establish dual-ligand Ni catalysis as a practical strategy for expanding the scope and increasing the success rate of thermally driven XEC relevant to pharmaceutical synthesis.

papers.title: Tailoring Pt-CeO <sub>2</sub> Interactions to Bypass Activity-Selectivity Trade-Off for C <sub>2</sub> H <sub>2</sub> Semi-Hydrogenation
papers.abstract: CeO 2 -supported platinum-group metals with small nanoparticles allow fine-tuning of their electronic properties through enhanced electronic interactions with the support. Here, we modify the electronic properties of a Pt/CeO 2 catalyst with 1.5 nm Pt nanoparticles by varying the near-surface oxygen vacancy concentration. In-situ infrared, X-ray photoelectron, and X-ray absorption spectroscopies show that roomtemperature oxidation followed by re-reduction at 100 o C decreases near-surface oxygen vacancies by ∼3-fold without altering Pt size, resulting in ∼25-fold increase in C 2 H 2 hydrogenation turnover frequency while C 2 H 4 selectivity remains unchanged at ∼90%. These findings are exceptional for C 2 H 2 semi-hydrogenation since C 2 H 4 selectivity typically decreases with increasing C 2 H 2 activity due to the well-known linear scaling relationship and Brønsted-Evans-Polanyi relation. X-ray absorption spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations reveal that lowering subsurface oxygen vacancy concentration unevenly depletes Pt d -electron density, altering projected density of states exclusively for apex Pt sites. Competitive adsorption modeling reveals that apex Pt sites preferentially adsorb C 2 H 2 , while basal Pt sites favor C 2 H 4 , leading to a stronger effect on C 2 H 2 binding and resulting in the observed deviation from the typical activity-selectivity trade-off. Our study demonstrates that tailoring Pt-CeO 2 interactions enables site- and molecule-specific adsorption modulation to overcome the conventional activity–selectivity trade-off.

papers.title: Intramolecular Hydride Migration Enables Ring Substitution in a Diphosphacyclobutadienyl Complex
papers.abstract: While substitution reactions at coordinated carbocyclic π-ligands are well established, similar examples of direct substitution at the ring carbon atoms of mixed carbon-phosphorus π-systems have remained scarce, owing to the intrinsic bias towards P-centered reactivity. Herein, we report a hydride-for-phosphonium substitution at a coordinated phosphorus heterocyclic π-system: protonation of the complex [W(CO)3{η 4-(PPh3)2C2P2}] bearing a zwitterionic diphosphacyclobutadienyl ligand affords a tungsten hydride complex which undergoes a selective rearrangement to [W(CO)3(PPh3){η 4-(PPh3)HC2P2}][OTf] upon dissolution in acetonitrile. A combined experimental and computational investigation reveals a multistep pathway, in which a tungsten-mediated intramolecular hydride migration serves as the key step. Acetonitrile plays a crucial role in driving the reaction by stabilizing the coordinatively unsaturated intermediate generated upon hydride migration. Remarkably, despite its negative charge, the resulting phosphonium-hydro-diphosphete-diide ligand combines strong π-donor and pronounced π-acceptor properties, resulting in stronger binding to the tungsten carbonyl fragment than the cyclopentadienyl ligand, as evidenced by EDANOCV calculations and IR spectroscopy.

papers.title: Machine Learning for NMR Observables Sensitive to Nuclear Quantum Effects
papers.abstract: Nuclear quantum effects (NQEs) are essential for an accurate description of systems containing light elements. Their omission in classical simulations can lead to significant deviations between theoretical predictions and experimental measurements, particularly for nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) observables that are highly sensitive to quantum nuclear motion. Although NQEs can be treated rigorously by using ab initio path-integral molecular dynamics (AI-PIMD), the substantial computational cost associated with these simulations continues to limit their applicability to large systems and long timescales. To address this limitation, we developed a machine learning-driven PIMD (MLPIMD) workflow for the accurate and efficient prediction of NMR observables, in which NQEs at finite temperature are explicitly included. As a demonstration, we investigate the experimentally measured isotropic chemical shifts, δ iso , of the 3 He monomer ( 3 He@C 70 6- ) and dimer ( 3 He 2 @C 70 6- ) endohedral fullerene hexaanions. The resulting predictions show excellent agreement with the experiment and reveal a pronounced influence of NQEs on the 3 He chemical shifts in both systems. In particular, NQEs are found to play a key role in determining the chemical-shift difference between the monomer and dimer species. The methodology introduced here is broadly applicable and provides a general framework for investigating NMR observables sensitive to NQEs in complex molecular systems.

papers.title: From Azirinyl Radicals to Azirinium Cations: Small-Ring N-Heterocyclic Reactive Intermediates
papers.abstract: Late-stage functionalization via reactive intermediates has recently emerged as an efficient way to access structurally diverse small rings, as illustrated with cyclopropyl radicals or cyclopropenium cations, which have opened valuable new synthetic opportunities. Their nitrogen counterparts, however, remain underexplored despite the importance of heterocycles in synthetic and medicinal chemistry. Herein, we demonstrate that azirinyl radicals and azirinium cations can be reliably accessed from a common N-hydroxyphthalimide ester azirine precursor under blue light irradiation, without the need for a metal catalyst. Under reductive conditions, azirinyl radicals can be added to electron-poor alkenes and using a radical polar-crossover approach, azirinium cations can be trapped with nucleophiles. Both pathways are high-yielding, chemically robust and scalable to give azirines with a wide range of substituents previously inaccessible and can be applied to complex drug-derived molecules. The obtained azirines could be converted to the corresponding aziridines diastereoselectively.

papers.title: Cobalt-Catalyzed Dual Construction of peri-(C–C) and (C–N)/(N–N) Atropisomerism via C–H Activation
papers.abstract: Axially chiral biaryls bearing an atropisomeric C–C axis at peri-substituted positions are difficult to access, and this difficulty compounds when the same scaffold must also carry a second, independent C–N or N–N axis, a combination that remains largely unexplored. Here we report an efficient, cost-effective route to these dual-axial atropisomers through enantioselective Co(II)/Salox-catalyzed C–H/N–H annulation. Arylbenzamide substrates bearing two distinct classes of directing groups react with peri-substituted alkynes to install both stereogenic axes in a single step. The reaction tolerates a broad range of substituents, proceeds in good yield, and delivers excellent stereocontrol (up to >99% ee, >20:1 dr). Mechanistic studies, supported by density functional theory (DFT) calculations, clarify the origin of the observed stereoselectivity. The resulting dual-axial atropisomers are fluorescent, and their photophysical properties point to potential applications in optoelectronic materials.

papers.title: Gold deposition on surfaces using small organic molecules: effects of preparation conditions on morphology and Raman response
papers.abstract: Reduction and subsequent deposition of noble metals from simple salt solutions on solid surfaces remains challenging. We describe deposition of gold (nano)-particles from an aqueous chloroauric adic solution on glass and polyethylene surfaces at ambient temperature by adding simple primordial organic molecules. The deposited gold structures showed differences in morphology, size and Raman response across the preparation conditions examined, motivating further investigation of their potential as functional surface coatings with distinct properties for various applications. Green foundation 1 This work examines gold deposition on glass and plastic, hydrophobic and hydrophilic, surfaces using aqueous solutions of simple organic compounds at room temperature; mild reaction conditions relevant to green chemistry. 2 Light and electron microscopy revealed differences in deposit morphology across conditions with different organic compounds and reagent concentrations. 3 Cancer cell and rhodamine 6G Raman measurements were used to explore the potential of the deposited gold structures as substrates for surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy to detect biofilm compounds.

papers.title: Chemical Synthesis and Immunological Evaluation of Archaeal Rare Sugar L-TalNAcA and Its Derivatives
papers.abstract: Human-associated archaea, such as Methanobrevibacter smithii and Methanosphaera stadtmanae, have attracted increasing attention for their potential involvement in the modulation of host immune responses. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying these interactions remain poorly understood. Pseudopeptidoglycan (pPG), a major component of the archaeal cell wall, is a potential mediator of such immunomodulatory effects. Although N-acetyl-L-talosaminuronic acid (L-TalNAcA) has been proposed as a constituent of pPG, both its precise structural context within the archaeal cell wall and the immunological properties of its glycoconjugates remain largely unexplored. In this study, we established a synthetic route to L-TalNAcA and its derivatives, including mono- and disaccharide glycopeptides. LC-MS/MS analysis using synthetic L-TalNAcA as a reference standard supported the presence of this rare sugar in archaeal cell wall hydrolysates. Furthermore, immunological evaluation using reporter cell lines revealed that the M. smithii-type monosaccharide glycopeptide induced hNOD2-dependent activation. These findings provide molecular evidence of host receptor recognition of an archaeal cell wall-related glycopeptide motif and establish a chemical platform for further investigating archaeal-host immune interactions.

papers.title: Adaptive Hydration-Shell ML/MM Simulations Recover Full ML Accuracy in Biomolecular Conformational Description
papers.abstract: Residue-specific backbone conformational preferences govern the conformational ensembles of intrinsically disordered proteins, yet their accurate description using classical force fields is limited by prescribed functional forms that cannot fully represent environment-dependent many-body interactions. Machine-learned force fields (MLFFs) learn complex atomic interactions directly from quantum-mechanical reference data, providing a systematic alternative to classical parameterisations. Here, we employ a pretrained MLFF to simulate nine cationic Gly-x-Gly tripeptides in water and compare the resulting conformational ensembles against experimental NMR scalar J-couplings. To improve computational efficiency, we develop and assess hybrid Machine Learning/Molecular Mechanics (ML/MM) protocols as computationally tractable alternatives to full ML simulation. Mechanical-embedding ML/MM is found insufficient for accurate conformational sampling, as the classical treatment of peptide–solvent interactions fails to adequately represent solvation effects on backbone conformational preferences. We therefore implement an adaptive ML/MM scheme that incorporates the immediate solvation environment into the ML description and recovers near-full-ML accuracy at a reduced computational cost.

papers.title: Tight binding of optically innocent bisphosphonate ligands to robust Tb3+-doped HfO2 nanocrystal surfaces
papers.abstract: Lanthanide (Ln3+)-doped nanocrystals feature photostable, long-lived emission, making them attractive probes for in vitro and in vivo imaging. Their translation, however, hinges on a surface chemistry that confers colloidal stability under physiological conditions without compromising their photophysical properties. Here, we benchmark three classes of PEGylated anchoring groups—nitrocatecholates, phosphonates and bisphosphonates—on core and core/shell Tb3+-doped HfO2 nanocrystals. Nitrodopamine-based ligands quench Tb3+ luminescence in water on both core and core/shell particles, whereas phosphonic and bisphosphonic acids are optically innocent and leave the emission intact. Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) and dynamic light scattering (DLS) reveal that only the bisphosphonates remain tightly bound and keep the nanocrystals dispersed across a wide pH range and in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS). Nanocrystals capped with PEGylated bisphosphonate (bisPA−PEG250) retain their luminescence after prolonged incubation in PBS, with no detectable Hf or Tb leaching. Thus, PEGylated bisphosphonates emerge as robust, non-perturbing ligands for Ln3+-doped HfO2 and as a practical entry point to biomedical application, since Tb3+-doped HfO2 can be used as probes in bio-imaging of leukemia cells.

papers.title: Automated Full-Spectrum Multivariate Calibration for Quantitative Glow Discharge Optical Emission Spectrometry
papers.abstract: Glow discharge optical emission spectrometry (GD-OES) enables rapid bulk and depthresolved multi-elemental analysis of solid materials with minimal sample preparation. Conventional quantification, however, relies on preselected analyte emission lines and, if sputtering-rate variations must be compensated, on matrix reference lines or sputtering-rate correction, requiring matrix composition or sputtering rates as input. Modern CCD-based instruments simultaneously record broadband spectra containing thousands of spectral variables, yet most of this information remains unused in conventional calibration based on a few selected lines. Here, we investigate a full-spectrum calibration strategy based on Variable Importance in Projection-selected Partial Least Squares (VIP-PLS) regression for the quantitative determination of individual alloying elements. Al-Si and Cu-Zn alloys were selected as metallurgically and spectrochemically distinct model systems, with Si and Zn as target analytes, respectively. The VIP-PLS models predicted Si and Zn with Root Mean Square Error of Cross-Validation (RMSECV) values of 0.38 wt% and 0.50 wt%, compared with 1.05 wt% and 1.41 wt% for univariate calibration of a single preselected line, and 0.24 wt% and 0.63 wt% for normalized ratio-based calibration using a reference line and the matrix mass fraction. VIP-PLS thus achieved performance comparable to the ratio-based calibration, implicitly compensating for sample-specific intensity variations, such as the sputtering rate, without matrix composition as input and without manual line selection. Time-resolved evaluation further showed that model performance reflects the transient and steady-state stages of the glow discharge, while VIP analysis revealed which spectral features contribute most strongly to the calibration and how they evolve during sputtering. Full-spectrum multivariate calibration therefore provides an automated, spectrum-driven and interpretable route for matrix-specific quantitative GD-OES that exploits information already contained in broadband measurements.

papers.title: SandCat: OpenMM Framework for Prospective Cryptic Pocket Discovery
papers.abstract: Proteins are dynamic biomolecules, yet often in drug discovery they are treated as static entities. A relevant example of this are cryptic pockets, which are pockets that are not present in the apo structure but reveal themselves upon binding to a particular ligand. Methods based on molecular dynamics (MD) simulations can dynamically probe the protein structure and have been validated on known cryptic pocket sites. SWISH-X is one of the most prominent methods in this field. Previously, it was only available with GROMACS and PLUMED, which limited its speed. Here, we present SandCat, an OpenMM-based toolkit that implements this enhanced sampling method for cryptic pocket discovery. SandCat reproduces previous results from SWISH-X with twice the computational speed. Furthermore, SandCat provides standardised protocols for prospective use on targets where cryptic pockets are not known. We tested the SandCat pipeline on challenging targets, and recovered every characterised cryptic site within the top six candidate sites, with no sites detected for a negative control. We believe that the increased speed and the implementation of a prospective toolkit will enable SandCat to be used at scale to unlock previously undruggable targets.

papers.title: A Pharmacophore-Based Virtual Screening Approach for the Discovery of Novel P2Y <sub>12</sub> Receptor Ligands
authors: Anne van der Schatte van der Schatte Olivier
papers.abstract: Microglia play key roles in neuroinflammation, which is a hallmark of neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson’s disease, Alzheimer’s disease and Multiple Sclerosis. To strengthen our understanding of the molecular mechanisms of these disorders, we need to understand the complex dynamics in microglial states. Developing new positron emission tomography (PET) tracers is exceptionally useful for this purpose, as they enable the assessment of microglia dynamics and function in the living human brain. The purinergic receptor P2Y12 (P2Y 12 R) is highly expressed in the homeostatic microglial states, and thus makes for a promising biomarker. In particular, P2Y 12 R PET tracers could complement translocator protein (TSPO) and P2X 7 receptor tracers, which image microglial density or target the pro-inflammatory state, respectively. Unfortunately, current high-affinity P2Y 12 R ligands do not enter the brain because they are charged in vivo or because they are substrates for efflux transporters. Attempts to increase brain uptake by improving their physicochemical properties have not yet resulted in a successful P2Y 12 R PET tracer. This emphasizes the need for novel chemotypes. Herein, we applied a pharmacophore-based virtual screening strategy to a library of about three million compounds. As a result, we identified the imidazo[1,2- b ]pyrazolone scaffold as a promising structural class to use as a starting point for developing P2Y 12 R ligands. After extensive hit expansion and structure-activity relationship studies, the two best ligands displayed excellent binding affinity for human P2Y 12 R ( 96 : K i = 9.61 ± 1.70 nM; 109 : K i = 3.10 ± 0.34 nM) and rat P2Y 12 R ( 96 : K i = 65.6 ± 25.9 nM; 109 : K i = 17.9 ± 12.8 nM) in a radioligand binding assay. Furthermore, imidazo[1,2- b ]pyrazolone [ 18 F] 91 was successfully radiolabeled as a proof-of-concept in sufficient radiochemical yields. Future work will assess whether the more potent ligands can be radiolabeled and used to image the P2Y 12 R in the brain. Together, these results highlight the use of pharmacophore-based strategy in PET tracer development and provide a robust basis for further hit exploration.

papers.title: Disentangling protein confinement from surface adsorption in hierarchical zirconium metal-organic frameworks
papers.abstract: A persistent challenge in protein immobilization within metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) is distinguishing genuine internal confinement from surface adsorption and interparticle voids, which can mimic encapsulation despite fundamentally different spatial microenvironments. Incorporating mesochannels to produce hierarchical UiO-66-NH 2 and MOF-808 nanoparticles, prepared by micelle templating, offers a strategy to overcome this ambiguity while preserving their intrinsic microporosity. Evidence from pore accessibility, pulsed field gradient NMR, and small-angle X-ray scattering is consistent with protein association within mesochannel environments. In the hierarchical hosts, loaded bovine serum albumin shows enhanced resilience to thermal stress. Together, these results are consistent with internal mesochannel confinement contributing to protein stabilization while preserving molecular accessibility in MOFs. Extending confinement to function, Candida antarctica lipase B immobilized in these hosts remains catalytically active at elevated temperature. In contrast to a commercial immobilized preparation, it retains a larger fraction of its activity in the first reuse cycles.

papers.title: Multinuclear High-Field FlowNMR for Real-Time Monitoring and Analysis of Biocatalytic Reactions in Batch and Flow
papers.abstract: Online high-field nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy in continuous or recirculating flow (FlowNMR) offers a powerful yet underutilised approach for monitoring biocatalytic reactions, particularly in challenging aqueous and low-concentration systems. Herein, we demonstrate the application of multinuclear high-resolution FlowNMR at 500 MHz for real-time analysis of both batch and continuous flow biotransformations. Across four case studies run at the typical low concentrations associated with biocatalysis including alcohol oxidation, nitroreductase-mediated reduction, a two-stage enzymatic cascade and a nucleoside phosphorylation, high-resolution spectra were obtained without interference from enzymes or reaction media. This technique enabled direct observation of key reaction intermediates, rapid optimisation of conditions and structure elucidation at sub-millimolar concentrations. Overall, this work demonstrates online high-field NMR as a versatile and information-rich tool for biocatalysis, providing real-time insight and significantly accelerating reaction development, with strong potential for integration into automated flow systems.

papers.title: Stepwise Condensation to Diversify Cyano-Substituted Vinylene-Linked COFs for Boosting H2O2 Photosynthesis
papers.abstract: Driven by growing demand for structural diversification and practical application of vinylene-linked covalent organic frameworks (COFs), it is critical to develop sustainable routes to monomers with highly tunable connectivity and functionality. Herein, we report an efficient route to a new class of aromatic DCP derivatives (DCP = 2,6-dimethyl-3,5-dicyanopyridine) via Hantzsch-type condensation from low-cost commodity chemicals. Using arene-bridged DCP dimers (arene = phenyl, biphenyl, naphthalenyl) as tetratopic monomers, we constructed three new vinylene-linked COFs via Knoevenagel condensation with 4,4'-biphenyldicarbaldehyde. Thorough characterization reveals their long-range ordered structures and high porosity. Their semiconducting properties are finely tuned by varying the monomer arene bridges. In pure water, these COFs deliver excellent photocatalytic H2O2 production up to 7020 μmol g-1 h-1, outperforming the cyano-free counterpart. This phenomenon can be directly attributed to the abundant cyano substituents with strong dipolar and π-extended character in the as-prepared COFs. These cyano moieties enhance light harvesting and photogenerated charge utilization, and provide strong hydrogen-bonding interactions to stabilize the key *OOH intermediate, thereby facilitating oxygen reduction, as supported by theoretical investigations. This work provides an economical strategy to tailor vinylene-linked COF structures and functions for broader practical applications.

papers.title: Shell-nested virtual spaces from atomic natural orbitals
papers.abstract: Selecting a compact molecular virtual space requires deciding which radial and angular freedom can be removed while retaining a useful description of electron correlation. A correlated molecular density can guide this choice, but obtaining it requires a preliminary correlation calculation. Here we examine whether tabulated atomic natural orbitals (ANOs) can provide radial guidance within the previously introduced shell-nested framework. Complete multicenter overlaps select directions available in the molecular parent basis, while adaptation uses the restricted Hartree–Fock reference and earlier layers remain fixed. The resulting shell-nested virtual spaces, SNVS(ANO), improve the average energy recovery over density-guided shell spaces in the tested second-order Møller–Plesset (MP2) and coupled-cluster singles and doubles (CCSD) panels. ANO guidance narrows the mean raw-energy differences from equally sized MP2-based frozen natural orbital spaces, although the latter retain smaller parent truncation errors. The prescribed shell content also makes the successive additions of spatial flexibility explicit. These results show that correlated atomic radial functions can guide molecular virtual-space selection before a correlated molecular density is available. The molecular reference controls their adaptation, and the correction and extrapolation tests show that retention of finite-parent correlation must still be distinguished from accuracy against an independent explicitly correlated reference.

papers.title: Ladderane as a Saturated Bioisostere of ortho-Benzene
papers.abstract: Previously, we proposed a hypothesis that ladderanes could mimic ortho-benzene in bioactive compounds. In this work, we have proven this hypothesis experimentally. In particular, 2,3-disubstituted ladderanes were efficiently synthesized and extensively characterized. These cores were then incorporated into six bioactive compounds instead of the benzene ring. The corresponding patent-free ladderane derivatives of Thalidomide and Oxatomide showed improved physicochemical profiles and similar biological activities compared to those of the original drugs. These results confirm that ladderanes can act as saturated bioisosteres of ortho-benzenes.

papers.title: Chemical Editing of DNA-Mediated Nanoparticle Superlattices through a CRISPR-inspired Strategy
papers.abstract: Biological systems employ molecular machinery to organize matter into functional structures and dynamically modify their organization in response to external signals. Translating such capabilities into synthetic nanomaterials requires strategies to selectively modify the interactions that define their structure. DNAbased assembly exploits sequence-specific molecular recognition to organize nanoscale components into prescribed architectures, yet post-assembly modification of structural DNA bonds remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate that enzymatic reactions, such as DNA-backbone covalent scission using CRISPRmediated editing of DNA linkers, provide targeted chemical modification of assembled 3D nanomaterials. Guide RNAs (gRNAs) direct Cas9 and Cas12a nucleases to selectively cleave DNA duplexes linking nanoparticles within ordered superlattices. Fluorescence measurements, optical microscopy, and timeresolved small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) reveal how molecular bond cleavage propagates into domain erosion, fragmentation, and loss of long-range lattice order. We extend this strategy to superlattices assembled from DNA-origami frames, demonstrating programmable disassembly through chemical cleavage of interframe DNA linkages. Importantly, sequence-selective disassembly can be realized within mixed populations of DNA-origami lattices, where Cas9 selectively disrupts lattices containing the recognized linker sequence, while non-targeted lattices retain their structure within the same reaction environment. These results establish sequence-specific chemical modification of DNA bonds as a strategy for selectively transforming DNA-based nanomaterials. This approach extends DNA programmability beyond encoding the initial assembly to directing post-assembly transformations, providing a pathway toward nanomaterials whose organization can be selectively modified through guided enzymatic processes,

papers.title: Isolable silyl- and germyl-thioketones dearomatize their own benzene rings at room temperature
papers.abstract: Although dearomatization of benzene converts flat molecules into three-dimensional (3D) frameworks, the stability of the benzene ring makes this transformation difficult. Main-group compounds that achieve it are typically highly reactive low-valent species or contain weak multiple bonds and usually require elaborate design. Thioketones engage an adjacent aryl ring only with strongly electron-poor partners or fused arenes, and the products rearomatize. Whether a simple, isolable main-group functional group can dearomatize a non-fused benzene ring under mild conditions has remained unclear so far. Here, we introduce a substituent-based strategy that switches on this reactivity, i.e., thioketones bearing a σ-donating silyl or germyl group dearomatize their own benzene rings at room temperature without the need for metals, light, or redox reagents. Whereas conventional thioketones are inert toward alkenes under identical conditions, these compounds, including the first structurally characterized silyl-thioketone and the first isolable germyl-thioketones, undergo cascade cycloadditions with alkenes and alkynes to give air-stable 3D frameworks. Rather than strengthening frontier-orbital interactions, the group-14 substituent polarizes the C═S bond and renders bond formation highly asynchronous, thus markedly reducing the distortion required to disrupt the aromatic ring. These results establish main-group substitution as a design strategy for unlocking latent dearomative reactivity under mild conditions.

papers.title: Correcting the Liquid Densities of Universal Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials Using Local-Number-Density Repulsion
papers.abstract: Universal machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) such as UMA, trained on reference data from meta-generalized gradient approximation or hybrid functionals that incorporate dispersion interactions, often overestimate molecular-liquid densities, thereby placing every property computed at constant pressure at the wrong state point. This study proposes a correction that adds to the MLIP a repulsive energy quadratic in the local number density of each atom, with two coefficients fitted only to the equations of state of water and ethanol; the forces and stresses follow analytically, so neither electronic-structure calculations nor retraining is required. For UMA, the correction reduces the density mean absolute error (MAE) of 22 liquids from 10.8% to 2.5%, lowering the error for every liquid and bringing 20 of them within ±5% of experiment, while improving the bulk modulus (MAE from 71.6% to 22.1%), heat of vaporization, and second hydration shell of water, none of which was calibrated. Applied to SevenNet-Omni without recalibration, the same coefficients reduce the density MAE from 8.2% to 1.8%, with 21 of 22 liquids within ±5% of experiment.

papers.title: SKIER: A Scientific Skills Framework for Evidence-Grounded AI Reasoning
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to interpret experiments and propose mechanisms, but its mechanistic claims often lack traceable evidence. Here we introduce SKIER (Skills for Evidence-grounded AI Reasoning), a scientific skills AI framework that combines AI orchestration, researcher-defined analytical procedures, deterministic calculations, and versioned records. Using 49 records from a published methanol-oxidation case study, the framework recovered an m/z 48 signal exceeding 60% of the combined m/z 44, 46, and 48 signals in the H218O experiment, which was assigned to C18O18O. This observation supported the previously reported C–O cleavage pathway. AI then used the processed data to propose three competing mechanisms and design CH318OH-labelling, oxygen-exchange, and residence-time experiments to distinguish them. Those follow-up experiments further refined the published mechanism by locating C–O cleavage before formic acid formation. With shared skills, all 11 AI configurations completed data processing, compared with none without them. In the 100 expert-designed questions evaluating mechanism inference and validation-experiment design, GPT-5.6-sol achieved 100% accuracy. Together, these results demonstrate how a scientific skills framework connects reproducible data analysis with experimentally testable mechanistic reasoning across AI models.

papers.title: Direct Synthesis of CdSe Quantum Dot Inks in Polar Solvents with Conductive Ligands
papers.abstract: Colloidal quantum dots (QDs) have unlocked advancements in technologies like displays and light detectors, thanks to their tuneable photoelectronic properties and scalability. However, several device schemes based on electronically conducting QD layers, such as photodetectors and LEDs, require processing QDs as concentrated inks with short, conductive ligands. Currently, this is only achievable after replacing the insulating ligands used during their colloidal synthesis, a process that is both time-consuming and resource-intensive. Direct synthesis of QD inks with short ligands remains underdeveloped in non-aqueous medium, yet such straightforward synthesis route would immensely facilitate QD device integration. In this study, we focus on cadmium selenide (CdSe), a well-understood QD system with established syntheses and surface chemistry, to showcase a strategy for directly synthesising inks with conductive ligands. We report a one-step synthesis of inorganic-passivated 3.4 nm wurtzite CdSe QDs in polar aprotic solvents. Our findings reveal a non-classical nucleation pathway with 1.5 nm magic-size clusters as intermediates. We demonstrate that highly Lewis-basic solvents and weakly coordinating cadmium counteranions are essential for producing high-quality CdSe QDs, particularly with hexamethylphosphoramide as a solvent and tetrafluoroborate counteranions for cadmium. Surface characterisations, including solid-state NMR, Raman, and IR spectroscopy, and ζ-potential measurements, reveal a disordered QD surface rich in cadmium-oxygen bonds and phosphates, which quenches the photoluminescence.

papers.title: Advances in OLED Technology: From Fundamental Materials, Device Architectures to Emerging Applications
papers.abstract: Organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) have emerged as a leading optoelectronic platform, owing to their high efficiency, tunable emission, and mechanical flexibility, yet key questions remain about which molecular design strategies and device architectures are advancing commercial performance, and where persistent bottlenecks, such as blueemitter instability, continue to limit progress, Here, we address these questions through a data-driven analysis of approximately 86 thousand OLED-related documents from the CAS Content CollectionTM spanning 2016–2026, a period chosen to capture recent developments in this rapidly evolving field. This data-driven study provides a comprehensive assessment of advances across multiple dimensions of OLED technology. Global innovation trends reveal a pronounced concentration of intellectual property and technological development in East Asia, reflecting strong alignment between research activity and manufacturing infrastructure. Materials-level analysis highlights diverse molecular motifs governing key processes such as charge transport, exciton management, and emission. Concurrently, device architectures, including tandem structures, micro‑OLED platforms, flexible form factors, and hybrid integration, demonstrate a clear shift toward application-driven optimization. The application landscape indicates widespread commercialization in consumer electronics and display technologies, with expanding roles in lighting, automotive systems, wearable devices, medical technologies, and immersive platforms such as augmented and virtual reality. Despite ongoing challenges related to emitter stability, efficiency roll-off, and manufacturing complexity, emerging approaches in data-driven materials discovery and scalable fabrication are expected to enable further performance enhancements. Overall, OLEDs represent a mature yet continuously advancing platform with significant potential for next-generation display and integrated optoelectronic applications.

papers.title: (iso-bpy)Ni: Isomeric Bipyridine Ligands in Nickel-Catalyzed Coupling of Aryl Chlorides and Alcohols Under Thermal Conditions.
papers.abstract: In search of more active and robust catalyst systems for the nickel-catalyzed coupling of aryl halides and heteroatom nucleophiles, a core scaffold modification of the conventional 2,2’-bipyridine ‘bpy’ ligand was explored. Transposition of one of the N-atom donors of bpy into the ligand backbone results in the isomeric bipyridine ligand ‘iso-bpy’, an N,Cdonor containing a highly electron-donating, strong-field 2-pyridylidene group. A series of (iso-bpy)Ni complexes were synthesized by a directed C–H metalation or C–Cl oxidative addition approach using N-(2-pyridyl)pyridinium salt ligand precursors. (iso-bpy)Ni complexes were investigated as precatalysts for the coupling of aryl chlorides and aliphatic alcohols under thermal conditions. Precatalysts of the general structure [(iso-bpy)Ni(Cl)(2-picoline)]BF4 efficiently catalyzed C–O coupling for a range of aryl chlorides, including those bearing electron-donating substituents, and were found to provide synthetically useful yields of product at lower catalyst loadings compared to their established (bpy)Ni counterparts. This work lays the foundation for further comparative studies of bpy and iso-bpy ligands within other transition metal catalyst systems.

papers.title: Processing-and cell-stage thermodynamic screening of nacre-and bone-inspired carbonate and phosphate phases on aluminium current collectors in fluorine-free lithium-ion cells with an open screening framework
papers.abstract: Water-processed, fluorine-free lithium-ion cathodes avoid fluorinated binders and organic solvents, but their alkaline slurry attacks the aluminium current collector, and the cell lacks the protective AlF3 layer that fluorinated salts form. Water-processed (bio-)binders do not protect the collector; the current fixes are pH control with H3PO4 and carbon-coated foil. We ask which nacre- and bone-lineage mineral phases can survive both the alkaline aqueous slurry and the oxidising potential of a fluorine-free cell, and which measurements would decide the rest. We compare nacre-lineage calcium carbonate, bone-lineage calcium phosphates, condensed calcium phosphates and aluminium phosphates as biopolymer-templated coatings, in the slurry (processing stage) and at cell potential (cell stage). Our open, extensible screening framework uses sourced thermochemistry with propagated uncertainty, and reports which phases are excluded, which remain open, and how precise a measurement must be to decide each. Calcite is thermodynamically stable against dissolution at pH 10.0–13.0 for total calcium from 1×10−4 mol dm−3. In a LiClO4-saturated electrolyte, carbonate is thermodynamically excluded above about 4.02 V, and hydroxyapatite and the tricalcium phosphates (upper bounds on oxidation onset 3.98 V–4.07 V) at 4.3 V and above. Condensed calcium phosphates are not excluded at any cutoff-voltage class, and aluminium phosphates are undetermined. Carbonate and bone mineral therefore cannot serve as the cell-stage barrier, and the condensed calcium phosphates remain the open bone-inspired candidates. One slurry-immersion and potential-hold experiment, with two measurements (the Ca2+ transfer free energy into the cell solvent and the template–nucleus interfacial energy), would decide them. No phase can pass the oxidation test while these transfer free energies are unmeasured, and the nucleation model failed its check against literature cases with known outcomes.

papers.title: Processing-and cell-stage thermodynamic screening of nacre-and bone-inspired carbonate and phosphate phases on aluminium current collectors in fluorine-free lithium-ion cells with an open screening framework
papers.abstract: Water-processed, fluorine-free lithium-ion cathodes avoid fluorinated binders and organic solvents, but their alkaline slurry attacks the aluminium current collector, and the cell lacks the protective AlF3 layer that fluorinated salts form. papers.title: Poly(pentafulvalene)s: One-Dimensional Conjugated Hydrocarbons toward Stable and Narrow-Bandgap Polyenes
papers.abstract: Polyacetylene is the archetypal narrow-bandgap conjugated polymer, yet its high-lying HOMO renders it air-sensitive, and aromatic alternatives sacrifice the small bandgap inherent to a polyene backbone. Here we show that embedding the polyene in a dibenzopentafulvalene (DBF) framework affords a stable, narrow-bandgap polyene analog. Poly(dibenzopentafulvalene) (polyDBF) was synthesized by Kosugi–Migita–Stille polycondensation; its thin film absorbed up to 995 nm (optical bandgap 1.25 eV) and, unlike polyacetylene, persisted for days in air. Because intermolecular interactions in the solid state and chain-length dispersity preclude isolating the intrinsic electronic structure of each polymer, we synthesized soluble, monodisperse oligomers [1]DBF–[5]DBF up to the pentamer. Extrapolation of their longest-wavelength absorptions yielded an intrinsic optical bandgap of 1.64 eV for the ideal polymer, which is substantially narrower than that of polyene (2.03 eV) and even than PEDOT (1.92 eV), a benchmark narrow-bandgap homopolymer, as obtained by the same analysis. Quantum-chemical calculations trace this narrowing to the combined effects of cross-conjugation and five-membered-ring cyclization, which selectively lower the LUMO. Consistent with our earlier oligomer series up to [3]DBF, the longer oligomers further sustain reversible multi-electron reduction, reaching an eight-electron reduction in [4]DBF. These results establish DBF as a building block that narrows the polyene bandgap while conferring ambient stability, and provide a design principle for stable narrow-bandgap hydrocarbon homopolymers grounded in their intrinsic electronic structure.

papers.title: Lactonization of Acyloxy Radicals
papers.abstract: Carboxylic acids have been used extensively as weak nucleophiles in lactonization and esterification processes involving activated electrophiles. Conversion of these building blocks into carboxyl radicals furnishes reactive species that are electrophilic in character but susceptible to decarboxylation. This high propensity for fragmentation, assessed to proceed at rates of 10 9-11 s -1 in the case of acyloxy radicals, has facilitated access to carbon radicals but impeded exploration of umpolung C–O bond forming reactions through non-decarboxylative pathways. Herein, we report an anti -Markovnikov lactonization of acyloxy radicals with unactivated alkene coupling partners initiated through proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) catalysis. The associative nature of PCET facilitates carboxyl radical stabilization through hydrogen bonding, suppressing typical decarboxylation pathways to enable competitive cyclization. This reactivity provides a mechanistically orthogonal entry to γ- and δ-lactone products complementary to existing nucleophilic functionalization strategies. Notably, a number of secondary and tertiary acids, which possess greater thermodynamic drivers for fragmentation, preferentially undergo radical lactonization under the reported conditions. Luminescence and NMR titration studies were performed to support the intermediacy of acyloxy radicals generated through PCET.

papers.title: A Molecular View of the Osmotic Response of Polyelectrolyte Complex Coacervates
papers.abstract: Synthetic polyelectrolyte complex coacervates are a ubiquitous class of liquid–liquid phase-separated (LLPS) systems that closely mimic the dynamic condensates often seen in cellular environments, where macromolecular crowding fundamentally shapes their physicochemical properties and biological function. For synthetic systems, neutral crowding agents, such as poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG), enhance coacervation, although the direct impact of osmotic stress on the structural and thermodynamic stability of the dense coacervate phase remains incompletely understood. Here, we utilize coarse-grained molecular simulations alongside systematic experimental studies to reveal the intrinsic compressibility and hydration dynamics of the coacervate phase under controlled osmotic perturbations. This framework establishes quantitative design principles for engineering synthetic condensates with programmable mechanical stability in macro-molecular crowded environments, with direct implications for developing biomimetic organelles that maintain structural integrity within the crowded cellular environment.

papers.title: Systematic Evaluation of Mixture-Design for Multi-Oxide Magnesium Aluminosilicate Glass Development: Model Comparison, Modifier Interactions, and Predictive Limitations
papers.abstract: A constrained ternary mixture design (Design of Experiments, DoE) was applied to four magnesium aluminosilicate (MAS) glass series to evaluate the predictive capability of Scheffé mixture polynomials for the specific Young’s modulus (spE = E/ρ), the key figure of merit for lightweight glass-fibre reinforcements. Two base compositions (V, Al2O3-rich; T, MgO-rich) were each modified with a 14 wt.% Y2O3–ZnO–CeO2 or La2O3–ZnO–CeO2 block. Linear, quadratic and special-cubic models were fitted to ten design points per series and ranked by R2, R2(adj) and the leave-one-out coefficient R2(pred). Three distinct regimes emerge: the V-series requires a special-cubic model with a dominant ternary Y2O3·ZnO·CeO2 term (β = −47.2, p = 0.001; R2(pred) = 97 %); the T-series is strictly linear (R2(pred) = 55 %), higher orders overfitting; and both La-series show a significant La2O3·CeO2 interaction absent in their Y-analogues. Three additive property models (Makishima–Mackenzie, an extended variant, and Yamane–Sakaino) deviate systematically from measured spE (absolute errors 6.9–12.2 × 106 N·m·kg-1, negative R2), most strongly where DoE detects interactions. The study delineates where additive approaches suffice, where binary synergy dominates, and where genuinely ternary cooperative effects must be resolved.

papers.title: Electronic Descriptors Lower Oxygen-Vacancy Formation-Energy Error Relative to Crystal Structure Alone in Non-Magnetic Oxides
papers.abstract: Oxygen vacancies control conduction, catalysis and ion transport in oxides, and an error of 0.3 eV in their neutral formation energy changes their concentration at 1000 K thirty-fold. Graph networks predict this energy from structure alone, but whether electronic descriptors of the pristine host from density-functional theory help is untested at matched training oxides. We compared a structure-only network (S) with one also given 22 such descriptors (D) on 1726 vacancy sites in 818 non-magnetic oxides of the Kumagai database, testing on unseen formulas. S reached 0.297 eV, the published accuracy. With 654 training oxides and equal tuning, D lowered the site error by 0.033 [0.021, 0.045] eV (95% interval), inside a 0.05 eV tolerance (1.8-fold in concentration). Tuned alone in a wider search, D* gained 0.069 [0.060, 0.078] eV, above it, but 0.039 [0.030, 0.048] eV over default-initialised S. The descriptors remove 11 to 23% of the error of S, depending on tuning. Within oxides the gain is concentrated in hosts whose cations have an empty valence s shell: empty-shell post-transition hosts gain 0.075 [0.050, 0.102] eV more than lone-pair hosts. Descriptors predicted from structure never surpass S, so the gain requires computed descriptors; where these are unavailable, S suffices for neutral vacancies.

papers.title: One-Electron Modulation of Photophysics in a Through-Space Donor–Acceptor System
papers.abstract: Through-space donor–acceptor interactions provide an attractive strategy for controlling molecular electronic structures and excited-state properties. However, the influence of one-electron transformations on the photophysical behavior of such systems remains relatively unexplored. Herein, we report an isolable carbazole–xanthylium cation (5+) and its corresponding neutral radical (5•), in which the donor and acceptor units are held in close spatial proximity. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals short donor–acceptor contacts of approximately 3.37 and 3.45 Å for the cation and radical, respectively. The cation exhibits a broad nearinfrared absorption extending to approximately 930 nm, whereas one-electron reduction affords a neutral radical displaying visible absorption and red photoluminescence with a quantum yield of 3.7 %. Density functional theory calculations and natural transition orbital analyses reveal pronounced through-space charge-transfer (TSCT) character in both species, despite their substantially different excitation energies. Excited-state geometry optimizations further support the distinct energetic landscapes associated with their charge-transfer excited states. These findings demonstrate that one-electron reduction can substantially modulate the photophysical properties of a spatially confined donor–acceptor system while preserving its underlying TSCT character.

papers.title: Cellulosic fibers coated in mineral sheaths for flame-retardant nonwovens
papers.abstract: While plant-based materials composed of cellulosic fibers have a favorable sustainability profile in several respects compared to synthetic alternatives, they are flammable and often require treatment for safe use. Many traditional flame-retardant finishes are toxic, while others are difficult to integrate with fibers or fabrics. In this work, cellulosic fibers (cotton, lyocell, jute, and hemp) were coated with crystalline calcite (calcium carbonate) or gypsum (calcium sulfate dihydrate) using a “polymer-induced liquid precursor” strategy. During this process, supersaturated solutions of insoluble minerals are induced by additives to form metastable intermediate droplets before crystallizing. These droplets wet the fibers via capillary action before nucleating to form crystalline sheaths that surround the fibers; calcite coatings were notably smooth and conformal, whereas gypsum coatings were faceted and less durable. Following mineralization, fibers were assembled into nonwoven sheets using carding/needlepunching or wetlaid techniques, then subjected to flame testing. While unmineralized cellulosic nonwovens burned readily, most nonwovens derived some degree of flame-retardancy from the mineral coatings, which serve as a heat/mass transfer barrier hindering flame propagation; further, gypsum endothermically loses its waters of hydration at low temperatures. Most mineralized nonwovens either self-extinguished or were consumed very slowly by the propagation of a flameless smoldering front.

papers.title: Polariton-Mediated Electron Transfer Rate Constant from Non-Equilibrium Fermi’s Golden Rule
papers.abstract: We provide a time-domain derivation of the population transfer rates for the polariton-mediated electron transfer (PMET) reaction under the collective coupling regime. Our theoretical analysis leads to the corresponding Marcus theory rates under the high-temperature and Markovian bath approximations. In addition to including the non-Markovian effect and the low-temperature limits, the theory is also generalized to include the multiple donor-to-acceptor case, as well as including multiple cavity modes. The derivations reveal a comprehensive framework of master equation-based reduced dynamics methods for PMET and other polariton-mediated reactions, providing a promising balance between numeric accuracy and computational efficiency, as well as a step closer to fully scalable simulations of realistic PMET processes.

papers.title: Tailored Nitrone [3+2] Dipolar Cycloaddition Enables the Elusive Synthesis of Structurally Complex Seven-Membered Heterocycles
papers.abstract: Intramolecular [3+2] nitrone cycloadditions have seldom been used to construct 7-membered heterocycles as the formation of the competing 6-membered heterocycles is favored almost exclusively. Herein, we report an intramolecular nitrone cycloaddition that proceeds with a strong preference for the formation of seven-membered 2-benzazepines. The reaction tolerates electronically diverse substrates, including heterocyclic variants, delivering a variety of structurally diverse and synthetically challenging 2-benzazepines in yields up to 76% with diastereomeric ratios up to 20:1. DFT calculations provide mechanistic rationale for both the observed regio- and diastereoselectivity and reveal the interplay of the Pauli repulsion and distortion as key selectivity-driving structural effects. The utility of the cycloadducts, especially by exploiting the N−O bond to increase molecular complexity further, is demonstrated through a concise total synthesis of (±)-caulophine A.

papers.title: Chiral H2S Ice
papers.abstract: Spontaneous symmetry breaking and the emergence of homochirality have been long-standing mysteries in chemistry and physics. The observation of symmetry breaking in simple triatomic molecules, such as hydrogen sulfide (H2S), is challenging owing to rapid molecular motion and structural relaxation, it provides a fundamental yet poorly understood pathway to molecular handedness in the prebiotic universe.We reportthe firstexperimentalcharacterization of emergent chirality in H2S clusters using vibrational circular dichroism (VCD) in cryogenic matrices (4–40 K). By quenching molecular motion, we resolved a temperature-dependent structural bifurcation: at 10 K, H2S assembles into helical trimer-based strands, characteristic of amorphous ice,whereas at40 K, the system undergoes a cooperative reorganization into crystalline cage-like pentameric networks, characteristic of Phase III crystalline ice. Quantumchemicalsimulationsrevealedthatenthalpiccooperativityinthesethree-dimensional pentameric architectures through S–H⋯S hydrogen bonding and S⋯S interactions provides the criticalstabilizationrequiredforlong-rangecrystallineorder.Kineticanalysesfurther confirmed that the intrinsic chirality of the assemblies remained preserved due to cryogenic trapping, demonstrating the role of directional hydrogen-bonded supramolecular architectures insymmetrybreakingandprovidingexperimentalbenchmarksfortheoreticalmodels developed to treat chirality signatures and prebiotic life in interstellar icy mantles.

papers.title: Charged Interface in Battery Breaks Molecular Chiral Symmetry
papers.abstract: Molecular events occurring within a few solvent layers at a charged electrode surface govern the rate and reversibility of reactions in electrochemical devices, yet such interfacial mechanism was never sufficiently understood at atomistic-level. Here we report a counter-intuitive discovery that charged interface breaks down the mirror symmetry between R - and S -enantiomers of propylene carbonate (PC), which expresses at graphite surface into distinct interphasial chemistries. Using enantiopure R - and S -PC as a chemically identical model pair against their racemic mixture, we find interphase at graphite diverges sharply at high lithium salt concentration, where R -PC enables reversible graphite lithiation with a LiF-rich interphase, while S -PC exfoliates graphite. Simulations and spectroscopies identify the combination of high salt concentration and charged interface collectively responsible for inducing the collapse of enantiomerism into diastereomerism. This knowledge not only establishes a hitherto-unknown dimension for electrolyte design, but also introduces a new concept of broad implications beyond battery applications.ed electrode

papers.title: Framework-Templated Single Clathrate Hydrate Cages in Metal–Organic Frameworks
papers.abstract: Molecular simulations identify metal–organic framework (MOF) pores that retain single methane hydrate cages and, for a nonstandard 16-water cage, support its assembly from disordered water. In smooth spherical pores, a methane molecule assembled twenty waters into the pentagonal dodecahedron of structure I hydrate and sixteen waters into a 435661 cage, a polyhedron that no known hydrate crystal contains. These idealized models were built by language-model agents and then walked back toward real materials, an approach referred to here as agentic doodling, and they guided a screening of 120,419 experimental MOF structures. Most size-matched pores pulled the cage apart, but a small set of frameworks kept it intact at 216 K, better with methane than without, and ELOZIQ kept the dodecahedron up to 270 K, near the melting temperature of the water model. In XODDED and GUQMAH, the nonstandard cage was held at least as well as in an ideal spherical pore, and it self-assembled around methane from randomly placed water, with nearly all of its edges hydrogen bonded. The pores template the cages through a moderate attraction spread over the cage corners rather than through strong binding sites placed at the corners. These results open a route to designing MOFs that hold single hydrate cages, including cages that do not occur in bulk hydrates.

papers.title: Electrolyte-derived interphases control nonuniform charging in battery particle networks
papers.abstract: In an ensemble of battery particles, dynamic interactions among individual particles give rise to emergent behavior like nonuniform charging. Yet, its origins have remained contested due to the challenge of directly measuring the current into each particle. Inspired by neuronal potential recordings in brain-computer interfaces, we present Multichannel Acquisition of Parallel-particle Level Electrochemistry (MAPLE) to map dynamic current distributions in real time. We demonstrate that asynchronous charging in layered oxide cathodes does not originate from bulk properties but instead results from a fluorinated cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI). This CEI forms upon electrolyte exposure before cycling and impedes Li + transport. Counterintuitively, intergranular cracking rescues these passivated particles by exposing pristine internal surfaces, whereas single-crystal particles without grain boundaries are more vulnerable to this Li + -impeding CEI.

papers.title: Anti-Parallel Dimer Structure of p-Cyanophenol Adsorbed at the Aqueous Solution Surface Probed by Sub-1 cm-1 High Resolution
papers.abstract: Sub-1 cm-1 High Resolution Broadband Sum-Frequency Generation Vibrational Spectra (HR-BB-SFG-VS) in different polarization combinations and experimental configurations was used to measure the spectral lineshape in the -CN stretching vibration region of p-cyanophenol (PCP) molecules at the air/water interface. The HR-BB-SFG-VS with a spectral resolution of ~ 0.6 cm-1 provides accurate and nearly intrinsic SFG spectral lineshape with excellent signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). From analyzing the high-resolution spectra in the 2160-2300 cm-1 range, we found that there are two closely overlapping peaks with opposite phases, implying the existence of two -CN groups with opposite orientations at the interface. This finding is unexpected from the conventional perception that PCP molecules at the air/liquid interface forms single Gibbs monolayer at the air/PCP solution interface. In addition, we also found that the -CN spectral intensity dependence on the bulk PCP concentration does not follow the typical Gibbs adsorption layer behavior, that is to follow the Langmuir isotherm, nor follow the anti-parallel double layer adsorption behavior, that is to follow the double-layer adsorption model (DAM) isotherm. By comparing with the -CN signal intensity and lineshape of the 4-(Octyloxy) benzonitrile (C8-PCP) monolayer, as well as orientation analysis of the two opposite peaks with polarization data, we further validated the anti-parallel dimer structure regarding the interfacial configuration of the PCP molecules. These findings not only provided detailed information about the adsorbed organic molecular layers, such as PCP, at the liquid interfaces, but also demonstrated the power of HR-BB-SFG-VS as a uniquely powerful interfacial selective spectroscopy in resolving and discovering detailed and unexpected molecular structure at interfaces.

papers.title: Foldability Is an Intrinsic Property of Protein Sequences: A Lattice Model Study with Information-Theoretic Approach and Unsupervised Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Protein structure prediction has been largely solved, but why a given sequence is foldable has not. We address this question for 27-, 48- and 64-residue lattice heteropolymers with statistical thermodynamics, the informationtheoretic approach (ITA) and a variational autoencoder (VAE). Native populations, folding probabilities and freeenergy surfaces are reproducible and independent of the initial denatured ensemble, so foldability is an intrinsic property of the sequence at a given temperature and solvent. We then ask where the observed regularities come from. Stability is governed by an information balance: the information content (self-information) of the native energy relative to the maximum-entropy description of compact alternatives, ℐtail, must exceed their Shannon entropy, 𝑆c = ln𝛺c. This is the random-energy-model condition for a folding transition, and ℐtail/𝑆c fixes the ratio of folding to glass temperatures, recasting minimal frustration in information units. Foldable sequences have smooth funnels, minimal Shannon entropy and minimal Fisher information in the native state, and a single sharp maximum of Fisher information at melting (cooperativity). Mutual and conditional information show that stability is an approximately sufficient statistic for kinetic accessibility of compact 27-mers. No hierarchical folding order is found. Variational autoencoders trained without labels distinguish sequences by their folding ensembles, supply a six-variable reaction coordinate that retains 91% of the kinetic information in the full native-contact map, and rediscover the native energy gap from the density of compact states.

papers.title: Reference Conventions and Structure Types, Rather Than 4f Occupancy, Shape Lanthanide Errors in Universal Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials
papers.abstract: Compounds that pair a lanthanide with a d-block metal and a p-block anion sit behind permanent magnets, catalysts and energy-storage materials, yet large parts of this chemical space have not been computed. Universal machine-learning interatomic potentials now make it possible to screen such spaces for stability at a small fraction of the cost of density functional theory, and they are increasingly used to decide which candidates are worth calculating properly. Their training data, however, hold few lanthanide compounds, describe the same element with different pseudopotentials from one database to the next, and carry empirical energy corrections fitted on compound sets from which lanthanides were excluded, so their reliability for felectron chemistry has not been established. Here we benchmark five universal potentials against density functional theory computed with Materials Project settings on 82 lanthanide–d-block–anion ternaries covering the lanthanide series (excluding Pm) and seven anions. Apparent accuracy turns out to be set mainly by the energy convention of the reference: judged against the quantity each model was trained to predict, all five reach mean absolute errors of 0.07 to 0.10 eV per atom, while the wrong convention inflates the error by more than a factor of three. Error does not follow 4f occupancy or the 4f pseudopotential treatment assigned to each element. It is larger for intermetallic than for ionic compounds and concentrates in two structure types, the CeNiC2-type carbides and the PbFCl-type phosphides, which most models miss even though these compounds have Materials Project entries. For ytterbium, every model follows the divalent convention of the older Materials Project data rather than the trivalent one now in use, a singleelement inconsistency of roughly 0.2 to 0.3 eV per atom. These results indicate where lanthanide chemical space can be screened with current potentials and where explicit DFT validation is still required, and they point to structural and data-provenance diagnostics, rather than elemental ones, for the next generation of models.

papers.title: A General Cobalt-Catalyzed Oxidative Radical-Polar Crossover Platform for Secondary and Primary Alkyl Radicals
papers.abstract: Along with recent advances in photoredox-mediated radical generation, oxidative radical–polar crossover (ORPC), involving single-electron oxidation of an alkyl radical to the corresponding carbocation, has emerged as a promising strategy for carbocation generation without use of strong acid mediators. However, current photoredox-mediated ORPC systems are not applicable to secondary and primary alkyl radicals due to their short lifetimes and high oxidation potentials, thereby hampering the development of general synthetic platforms for radical/cation-mediated alkylation of heteroatom nucleophiles and rearrangement reactions. Herein, we develop a cobalt-catalyzed ORPC system for secondary or primary alkyl radicals. It involves the radical capture of an alkyl radical by a cobalt(II) complex followed by oxidation of the resultant alkyl cobalt(III) complex to the alkyl cobalt(IV) complex, which participates in an SN2 reaction with heteroatom nucleophiles or rearrangement reactions. Following this strategy, we design a triple photoredox/cobalt/Brønsted acid catalysis and apply it to secondary or primary alkylation of heteroatom nucleophiles. The cobalt-mediated ORPC system could merge with various radical processes, such as b-cleavage and radical addition, which dramatically enables to expand accessible structures.

papers.title: Probing ionomer distribution in PEMFC catalyst layers: AFM and DEM enabled microstructure analysis
papers.abstract: Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell (PEMFC) catalyst layers have been probed experimentally and theoretically for decades. However, existing microscopy techniques lack the ability to perform quantitative analyses on the catalyst and ionomer distributions of catalyst layers. Since the microstructure of the catalyst layer has an influence on the electrochemical performance, the simulation of catalyst layer microstructures is of great importance. A physics-based simulation model was recently reported to predict the microstructure of the catalyst layer as a function of ink composition. We propose a workflow to characterize catalyst layers with the utilisation of Atomic Force Microscopy. The novelty of the workflow lies in the calculation of a statistical description of the catalyst layer (CL). This statistical metric is then used as a validation metric for a microstructural physics-based simulation model. The resulting simulation workflow can be used to predict the ink composition required to obtain catalyst layers with desired microstructural properties, paving the way towards more efficient PEMFCs.

papers.title: A General Approach for the Generation of alpha-Thioalkyl Radicals from Pinacol Boronic Ester Precursors
papers.abstract: A straightforward and effective method to produce alpha-thioalkyl radicals using stable and readily accessible pinacol boronic ester precursors is described. The generation of alpha-thioalkyl radicals proceeds via in-situ transesterification with MeOBcat or 3-methoxycatechol (MOC), and subsequent nucleohomolytic substitution at the boron atom with an oxygen-centred radical. The alpha-thioalkyl radicals can be trapped intermolecularly using a variety of conjugated enones and sulfonyl-based radical traps or subjected to intramolecular cyclisation.

papers.title: Selective Adsorption Processes in Mordenite-Catalysed Ethanol Dehydration
papers.abstract: Ethanol dehydration offers a promising solution to improve the sustainability of ethene production, using biomass-derived feedstocks and a heavy-metal-free zeolite catalyst. To improve understanding of the key chemical steps in this reaction, the adsorption of key species in acid-catalysed ethanol dehydration have been investigated on Brønsted Acid (BA) sites in protonated mordenite (MOR). The strength of the BA sites has been characterised using adsorption enthalpies of NH 3 , revealing that the proximity of the zeolite framework at each BA site is important for stabilisation through van der Waals interactions. Ethanol is found to adsorb more exothermically to the BA sites than the reaction products of ethene and H 2 O, suggesting that reactant adsorption is not thermodynamically hindered. Reaction selectivity can be tuned by introduction of pyridine. Calculated pyridine adsorption enthalpies indicate that pyridine preferentially occupies specific BA sites, thereby influencing the distribution of active sites available for reaction. In particular, pyridine binds significantly stronger at 12-membered-ring BA sites, which are associated with lower ethene selectivity, than to the more selective 8-membered-ring side pocket BA sites. The results of this paper show that additives may increase reaction selectivity by controlling access to different BA sites, highlighting a potential strategy for improving the performance and versatility of zeolite catalysts.

papers.title: DFT Studies of Coherent States in Triphenylamine Trimers
papers.abstract: Density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent DFT (TDDFT) calculations were performed to investigate the degree of coherence in two triphenylamine trimers: restricted and unrestricted. The B3LYP/6-31+G(d,p) level of theory was employed in this study. Toluene and dichloromethane were used as solvents to understand the effects of the solvent environment on the properties of the trimers. The unrestricted trimer exhibits a larger HOMO-LUMO energy gap and a shorter absorption wavelength than the restricted trimer, indicating a lower degree of coherence. The solvent effects on the HOMO-LUMO energy gap and UV-Vis absorption spectra are minimal, whereas the intensities of the IR absorption peaks are affected more significantly.

papers.title: Synthesis of zigzag-type carbocationic nanobelts
papers.abstract: Belt[n]arenes correspond the shortest belt segments of zigzag carbon nanotubes. Their closed cyclic π-conjugated topologies and distinct size-dependent electronic configurations render them platforms for the construction of quantum materials and devices. Here, we report the synthesis of a fully conjugated carbocationic zigzag-type belt consisting of four linearly fused benzotropylium units. Belt[4]arene[4]tropylium salt was synthesized from resorcin[4]arene via a sequence featuring fjord-stitching olefin metathesis reactions, selective bromination and heterolytic C–Br bond cleavage reaction. Single crystal X-ray diffraction analysis confirms that the synthesized molecule is a rigid C4v-symmetric belt with all positively charged seven-membered rings adopting a boat conformation. Combined evidence from 1H and 13C nuclear magnetic resonance spectra, electronic absorption spectra, single crystal structural characterization and theoretical calculations demonstrates the global aromatic nature of belt[4]arene[4]tropylium.

papers.title: Can existing or future pathways reduce green ammonia production costs?
papers.abstract: Many scenarios for the energy transition consider green ammonia. The technologically most mature production process combines water electrolysis and Haber-Bosch process (EHB). Its costs are dominated by electrolyzer investment costs and electricity. Emerging pathways researched in academia, start-ups, and industry try to reduce costs by changing sub-processes and chemistry. However, it remains unclear which pathways have the potential to outperform EHB, if any. We assess relevant emerging pathways, compare to EHB in terms of costs and energy demand, and derive performance targets. Many pathways investigated in the literature, such as metalmediated electrolysis, have theoretical minimal energy demands well above the actual energy demand of EHB; consequently, they cannot produce ammonia at competitive costs due to the high influence of electricity costs. Any novel pathway must employ simple and energy-effective chemistry to substantially reduce costs. Identified performance targets are applicable to novel pathways and can guide research, industry, and policy makers.

papers.title: Adsorption of cations at electrochemical interfaces revisited
papers.abstract: At electrochemical interfaces, alkali-metal and alkaline-earth metal cations are usually described as solvated species that nonspecifically adsorb, whereas specifically adsorbed anions interact more directly with metal electrodes. However, the mode of cation-surface interaction remains poorly defined at the atomic scale because experiments typically measure averaged interfacial responses. Distinguishing hydration modulated polarization from localized ion-surface coupling therefore requires access to both the atomic structure and the redistribution of electronic charge. Using density functional theory molecular dynamics, we reexamine this distinction for hydrated K+, Na+, Ca2+, oand Mg2+ at Pt(111), Au(111), and Ag(111) metal-water interfaces. Charge neutral, symmetric 3 × 3 cells containing one cation and five to seven water molecules at each interface allow for the study of compact, ion-rich layer configurations, rather than dilute electrolytes or electrodes maintained at an applied potential. Within the sampled compact layer configurations, structural sampling and charge density difference analysis indicate that cation adsorption spans a continuum of interfacial responses, ranging from diffuse, hydration modulated polarization to localized, compact layer coupling. Divalent cations exhibit the most persistent direct contact, and the selected divalent configurations show localized electronic redistribution, while monovalent cations are more sensitive to water coverage and substrate identity. Even predominantly non-contact cations can remain electronically relevant by polarizing the interfacial water layer and metal surface. These results suggest that cation adsorption within the compact interfacial region requires a local, structure dependent description that goes beyond simple specific or nonspecific classifications.

papers.title: Enzymatic Conversion from a Vicinal Diol to a Vicinal Diketone: Computational Study of the Conserved 6-Pyruvoyltetrahydropterin-Forming Stage in Mammalian and Bacterial PTPS
papers.abstract: As a zinc- and magnesium-dependent triphosphatase, 6-pyruvoyl tetrahydropterin synthase (PTPS) catalyzes the conversion of dihydroneopterin triphosphate (H2NTP) to 6-pyruvoyltetrahydropterin (PPH4) and a triphosphate ion, representing a typical reaction for vicinal diketone biosynthesis from vicinal diol. The molecular mechanism of PTPS remains elusive owing to the lack of structural data containing native substrate H2NTP and magnesium ion. Here, we performed a quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) investigation based on a predicted PTPS structure, elucidating the complete atomistic reaction mechanism for triphosphate ion formation and stereoselective product generation. The overall catalytic reaction of PTPS proceeds via two half-reactions, each comprising four sequential proton-transfer steps. Both half-reactions involve the conversion of a hydroxyl group on the substrate into a carbonyl group, ultimately furnishing the pyruvoyl-containing product PPH4. The third proton transfer in the first half-reaction occurs preferentially on the Si-face of the critical carbanion intermediate, yielding the (R)-configured product, in agreement with the reported experimental detection results. These calculations not only unveil the structural origins of stereoselective vicinal diketone product formation, but also uncover a non-canonical triphosphate elimination pathway driven by a charge-center shift that facilitates C–O bond cleavage. These findings broaden the mechanistic paradigm of triphosphatase-mediated phosphate chemistry and offer foundational insights for synthesizing vicinal diketones from vicinal diols.

papers.title: Dataset-specific retention time adjustment and multi-evidence lipid annotation: a reproducible R workflow for untargeted LC–MS lipidomics
papers.abstract: Background and Objective: Untargeted lipid annotation by liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry is challenged by structural isomers, multiple ion forms, and retention time differences between analytical datasets.
