We developed an open-source computational workflow combining dataset-specific retention time adjustment with experimentally characterized lipid information to restrict candidate assignments while preserving unresolved identities. Methods: The R workflow uses a curated database of 592 lipid species derived from a human plasma reference material. It combines monotonic retention time adjustment, accurate-mass matching, isotope-pattern assessment, empirical adduct profile, and ambiguity resolution. Developed using a 40-sample MICROSAMPLING study, it was applied to an independent 189-sample METFORMIN-HIIE study acquired under compatible chromatographic conditions. Annotation stages were evaluated against fixed workflow-derived references, including a comparison with unadjusted database retention times. Results: Unadjusted retention time matching recovered 55.4-77.2% of reference feature-lipid pairs, whereas adjusted matching recovered all reference pairs under identical tolerances. RT adjustment reduced candidates on non-reference features by 69.5-83.2% relative to mass-only matching and increased within-reference candidate discrimination from 69.1-70.9% to 88.5-92.6%. Isotope filtering and ambiguity resolution further restricted assignments. Integration across ionization modes yielded 433 and 379 endogenous feature records, respectively; 93 and 100 retained multiple compatible lipid identities rather than forcing unsupported unique assignments. Conclusions: Dataset-specific adjustment improves agreement with workflow-curated assignments while restricting candidate space. The approach supports reproducible lipid annotation and transparent uncertainty handling. Because the reference assignments originate from the workflow itself, complete retention does not establish independent annotation sensitivity or accuracy.

papers.title: Ni/TiO <sub>2</sub> Interfaces Enhance Benzaldehyde Selectivity in the Photocatalytic Dehydrogenation of Benzyl Alcohol
papers.abstract: The selective conversion of alcohols to carbonyls (ketones and aldehydes) plays an important role in chemical manufacturing. Photocatalytic acceptorless dehydrogenation offers a light-driven alternative for producing value-added aldehydes and H 2 under mild conditions and with easy separation and high molar efficiency. However, using semiconductor photocatalysts to achieve high selectivity and long-term stability under prolonged high-intensity illumination remains challenging. In this work, we developed CdS/TiO 2 /Ni photocatalysts by depositing TiO 2 onto CdS nanoparticle panels via atomic layer deposition (ALD), followed by Ni cocatalyst photodeposition, for the acceptorless dehydrogenation of benzyl alcohol to benzaldehyde and H 2 . Diluting the benzyl alcohol concentration to a practical range of ~10 vol% (1 M) further increased benzaldehyde selectivity to ~95%. Ni photodeposition and zeta-potential measurements suggest that TiO 2 coatings progressively modify Cd 2+ -associated surface sites through Ti 3+ /Ti 4+ incorporation, altering adsorption kinetics and contributing to the reduced activity. This extends the photocatalyst’s lifespan from ~23 to 60 hours and increases cumulative benzaldehyde and H 2 production. TiO 2 thin-film coatings have emerged as a promising strategy to protect semiconductor photocatalysts while modifying surface active sites and reaction kinetics, and their stability-activity trade-off showing lower initial-stage activity beyond 15-cycle ALD will be discussed alongside proposed mechanisms. This work establishes a semiconductor/coating/cocatalyst design architecture that highlights the importance of engineering surface adsorption and active-site environments, alongside charge-separation strategies based on band-edge energetics and charge-carrier dynamics, to jointly optimize photocatalytic activity and product selectivity for targeted chemical synthesis.

papers.title: Inhibiting LINE-1 retrotransposons therapeutically in disease
papers.abstract: The LINE-1 retrotransposon is a virus-like genomic element that can activate in diseased cells. It has been implicated in cancer, autoimmunity, developmental disorders, infectious disease and neurodegeneration. LINE-1 can be inhibited by reverse transcriptase inhibitors, small molecules originally developed for HIV. The correlation between HIV and LINE-1 inhibition is ∼0.9 on a log scale, in spite of >450 Mya of evolutionary history since retroviruses diverged from retrotransposons. Suppression of HIV requires prevention of a completed 9.7 kb virus insertion into the genome in immune cells. However, every cell in the body already contains >100 copies of LINE-1 that can potentially activate. Even incomplete LINE-1 mediated insertions can cause damaging mutations and genome instability. Furthermore, partial HIV and LINE-1 products in the cytoplasm of cells can contribute to an inflammatory immune response. Preclinical studies have shown LINE-1 inhibitors slow the progression of otherwise unrelated diseases. LINE-1’s contribution to these diseases can potentially be quantified using single-nucleus whole-genome sequencing on diseased tissue, enabling prioritization of disease selection for therapeutic development. Furthermore, LINE-1’s ORF1p protein can be measured in the blood of individuals with certain cancers. LINE-1 inhibitors could therefore be extended to various diseases. Potentially used both as an anti-inflammatory and prophylactically to help preserve genome integrity. Reverse transcriptase inhibitors are available at low cost for HIV, and higher doses of some could be used to inhibit LINE-1. However, reverse transcriptase inhibitors do not prevent DNA cutting by LINE-1’s endonuclease. Novel inhibitors may therefore be required. This, combined with novel diagnostics opens up possibilities for inhibiting LINE-1 therapeutically in disease

papers.title: Constructive chemical discovery through autonomous reasoning and experiment
papers.abstract: Making a new reaction often requires chemical knowledge that does not yet exist. Self-driving laboratories and language-model agents now plan, run and optimize experiments rapidly, but deciding what to ask next still requires a chemist in the loop Here we report AIChemist, a robotic chemist for what we call constructive chemical discovery. It decides what to ask next from its own results, settles each question by calculation or experiment, and builds the next design on the answer. Given a silyl-radical-relay concept, AIChemist developed an asymmetric three-component silylcyanation: it established that the solvent effect depended on the oxidant formulation and built the next formulation on this finding, raising the yield from 20% to 67% at 88% enantiomeric excess. For an intermediate of the insecticide broflanilide, it designed a photoredox/nickel C–N coupling route free of nitro-group transformations, at lower estimated cost than the conventional route. When the base favoured by calculation performed poorly, it withdrew that premise and rebuilt the search around the reaction medium, where non-polar toluene raised the product's HPLC yield from 43% to 86%. In both cases, each conclusion extended what the system knew and became the starting point for the next. These results demonstrate a framework for autonomous chemical discovery in which chemical understanding and experimental design evolve together within a closed loop.

papers.title: Benchmarking thermoelectric property extraction from scientific text
papers.abstract: We compare five methods for extracting thermoelectric property records from paragraphs of the literature (regular expressions, the ChemDataExtractor thermoelectric parsers, MaterialsBERT named-entity recognition with rule-based linking, a single-prompt large language model (LLM) and an LLM agent) on one corpus of 311 papers with one scoring rule, with all methods frozen before the 200-paragraph test sample was annotated. A record counts as correct only if property, value, temperature and material all match the gold standard. On the 160 in-scope test paragraphs (241 core records), the single-prompt LLM reached F1 = 0.79 (95% CI 0.71–0.87) and the agent 0.73 (0.64–0.83), against 0.22 for the regular-expression baseline and 0.06 for the ChemDataExtractor and NER pipelines; both LLM methods recover property, value and temperature with F1 above 0.94, and most of their remaining errors concern the material. We found no evidence of an accuracy improvement from the tested agent configuration, and we release the protocol, code, gold standard and all method outputs.

papers.title: Phosphorus-Mediated Optical Defect Engineering in Single-walled Carbon Nanotubes
papers.abstract: Defect engineering of single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) offers a versatile strategy for tailoring their optical properties through localized chemical modification. However, expanding the range of accessible defect chemistries beyond established oxygen- and aryl-based functionalities remains an important challenge. Here, we report a straightforward, light-driven strategy for introducing phosphorus-derived defects into (6,5)-enriched SWCNTs using triphenylphosphine (TPP) and a photosensitizing dye. Ultraviolet irradiation in the presence of TPP and eosin Y generates a new near-infrared emission feature centered at 1125 nm, assigned to a defect-associated emissive state (E11*), alongside the intrinsic nanotube emission at 997 nm. The formation of this state depends on the TPP concentration, photosensitizer concentration, and irradiation time, and is accompanied by attenuation of the intrinsic optical transition and an increase in the Raman D/G intensity ratio, indicating progressive structural modification of the nanotube framework. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveals a phosphorus-associated chemical state and changes in the carbon chemical environment, supporting phosphorus incorporation and the formation of modified carbon sites. Control experiments further demonstrate that defect formation requires both photosensitization and irradiation, is enhanced under oxygen-depleted conditions, and is suppressed by radical scavenging, consistent with a radical-mediated photochemical pathway. Complementary density functional theory calculations support the formation of a covalent carbon–phosphorus bond, accompanied by a change in phosphorus coordination from three- to four-coordinate, and reveal a phosphorus-associated electronic trap state near the valence-band edge. These findings establish phosphorus-mediated defect engineering as a complementary approach to tailoring SWCNT optical properties and provide a foundation for investigating the relationships between defect chemistry, localized electronic states, and near-infrared emission.

papers.title: Revisiting Artifact Suppression in Electrospray Ionization Deconvolution
papers.abstract: Charge state assignment is a critical step in many workflows for intact protein analysis by mass spectrometry. Computational deconvolution algorithms are increasingly used to automate data analysis, but conventional approaches can present artifacts. Here, we explore several approaches to remove artifacts by limiting the charge state assignments for each data point. One approach removes satellite charge states surrounding local maxima. Another removes harmonics at double a more probable charge assignment. The last two limit either the total number of allowed charge state assignments or the minimum relative charge state assignment probability for a given data point. These new features are as effective as the prior SoftMax artifact removal in UniDec, but they enable easier tuning by the user. Although the new set of features introduces additional complexity and an expanded number of parameters, these tools enable users to more precisely reduce artifacts in deconvolution results.

papers.title: Antisolvent precipitation of Zinc Porphyrin Hydrogen-Bonded Organic Frameworks Enables J-Aggregation Mediated Electrochemiluminescence for Synthetic Cannabinoid Sensing
papers.abstract: Zinc porphyrin hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (ZnTCPP HOFs) represent attractive electrochemiluminescence (ECL) luminophores; however, their tendency to undergo uncontrolled short-range π–π stacking at solid/liquid interfaces induces aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ) and severely limits the ECL efficiency. Existing strategies for suppressing ACQ rely mainly on covalent or coordination-mediated ligand engineering and often require laborious multi-step synthesis. From the perspective of colloid and interface science, we herein report a chitosan (CS)–DMF antisolvent precipitation strategy that reorganizes the interfacial hydrogen-bond network between CS and the carboxyl groups of ZnTCPP HOFs, enabling a controlled transformation of bulk crystals into short-range aggregates with local J-type coupling. Such synergistic colloidal-interface regulation suppresses short-range π–π stacking while enabling J-aggregates to enhance the ECL emission, boosting the peak ECL intensity without the need for an additional co-reaction promoter. On this basis, an aptamer-based ECL sensor was constructed for the ultrasensitive detection of the synthetic cannabinoid 5F-EDMB-PINACA, achieving a limit of detection of 8.61 × 10 ⁻16 g/L together with satisfactory selectivity and reliable determination in e-cigarette liquid samples. These findings demonstrate that colloidal-interface regulation provides an efficient and synthesis-free route toward high-performance ECL sensing.

papers.title: The infinitesimal machine surgeon: prospects for upconversion nanoparticles driving molecular motors/nanomachines
papers.abstract: The concept of the “infinitesimal machine surgeon” was envisaged by Feynman in 1959 and 1983, describing a miniature, human-controllable machine capable of being directed to biological tissue to perform a physical intervention. This perspective explores the potential of combining Feringa-type rotary molecular motors (nanomachines) with upconversion nanoparticles (UCNPs) to realise the vision of the infinitesimal machine surgeon. In this approach, UCNPs convert near-infrared (NIR) excitation into ultraviolet/visible (UV/Vis) emission to activate molecular nanomachines within biological tissue. The fundamental operating principles are outlined, recent experimental advances in powering molecular motors and UCNPs in organic solvents are reviewed. Simple biophotonic calculations based on the Beer–Lambert law suggest that upconversion from 808 nm to 450–475 nm may offer a promising excitation strategy for activating molecular motors in biological tissues. Key challenges to biological implementation are identified, including permissible tissue light-exposure levels and the effects of tissue absorption and multiple scattering on the photon budget available to drive UCNPs and molecular motors. Finally, experimental strategies for evaluating these systems in biologically relevant environments are proposed, in accordance with the 3Rs principles of biomedical research.

papers.title: Anisotropic Strain Enhances Oxygen Reduction Catalysis in Pt-Based High-Entropy Intermetallics
papers.abstract: The oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) remains a major bottleneck for the efficiency of proton exchange membrane fuel cells. While alloying Pt with 3d transition metals can reduce Pt loading and improve catalytic activity of ORR catalysts, Pt-based solid solutions suffer from reduced activity and stability at Pt fractions below 75-80 at. %. Here, we investigate the role of atomic ordering in multimetallic Pt catalysts by comparing high-entropy solid solutions (HESOSO) and high-entropy intermetallics (HEI) with identical nominal composition, Pt5MnFeCoNiCu. Gas diffusion electrode (GDE) setup measurements at industrially relevant current densities (>1 A cm-2 geo) show that catalysts containing the intermetallic phase outperform solid solution counterparts in both specific and mass activity despite their larger particle sizes. Density functional theory calculations attribute this improvement to anisotropic strain arising from the tetragonal intermetallic lattice, which generates distinct adsorption environments with near-optimal *OH binding energies. These results identify strain anisotropy in ordered multimetallic intermetallics as a promising catalyst design principle for independently tuning adsorption energetics and Pt loading. On-line inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) measurements reveal reduced 3d-metal dissolution in the HEI sample compared to HESOSO sample and binary PtNi reference. Operando X-ray total scattering and pair distribution function analysis further demonstrate that both crystallographic structure and local atomic arrangement are retained during accelerated stress testing, indicating that nanoparticle structural collapse is not the dominant degradation pathway. Instead, the observed activity losses are primarily associated with catalyst-layer degradation and mass transport limitations. Overall, the results identify atomic ordering and strain anisotropy as key parameters for designing low-Pt ORR catalysts with enhanced activity and structural stability under operating conditions.

papers.title: A growth-based screening method to detect defluorinating enzymes
papers.abstract: Organofluorines are persistent, widespread contaminants, yet enzymes that cleave carbon-fluorine (C-F) bonds remain scarce, creating demand for methods to discover or engineer defluorinating enzymes. However, screening enzymes that break C-F bonds is difficult because most defluorination assays test one clone or enzyme at a time. To address this problem, we developed a growth-based screening method in Escherichia coli that links fluoride production to tetracycline resistance. We constructed a selection plasmid, pRS-tet, by placing tetA under the control of a fluoride-responsive riboswitch so that fluoride allows tetA expression and cell growth under tetracycline selection. BL21(DE3) E. coli carrying pRS-tet were co-transformed with plasmids encoding either active RPA1163 fluoroacetate dehalogenase (FAcD) or its D114N variant (ΔFAcD). Active FAcD produced higher mean fluoride concentrations from ethyl fluoroacetate (EFA) and ethyl difluoroacetate (EDFA) than ΔFAcD and cell-free controls. Exogenous fluoride increased colony formation up to 5 mM in both strains, whereas growth declined at 10 mM. Under tetracycline selection, active FAcD colony counts increased with EFA, difluoroacetate, and EDFA concentrations (p < 0.01), while ΔFAcD did not exhibit the same dose response. These results show that fluoride released during defluorination can activate tetA expression and support cell growth. Because the selection responds directly to fluoride, it could be adapted to screen enzyme or environmental gene libraries against other fluorinated compounds, including recalcitrant per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS).

papers.title: Foundation interatomic potentials learn the practical chemistry they were never taught
papers.abstract: Chemists understand molecular reactivity through simplified concepts such as substituent effects, acidity, and aromaticity, which are compact descriptors of the potential energy surface and of the electronic structure that shapes it. Universal machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are transforming applied computational chemistry by learning the same surface from atomic structures, energies, and forces, making atomistic simulations of complex systems practical. Like chemists, MLIPs build compact internal representations of that surface, yet these are usually treated as a means to faster, larger-scale molecular dynamics simulations. Here we show that they also contain directly recoverable chemical information: simple models applied to the invariant per-atom embeddings of pretrained universal MLIPs recover Hammett substituent constants, Brønsted and Lewis acidity, and ring aromaticity with Spearman ρ = 0.8–0.99. The same representations predict the yield of a four-component palladium-catalyzed cross-coupling at ρ = 0.96, matching models built from curated descriptors, while pinpointing the aryl halide as the reaction’s key substrate and ranking isoxazole additives by catalyst-poisoning strength. Universal MLIPs are therefore not only fast engines for energies and forces but also chemically meaningful representations of molecular reactivity, opening a route to extracting chemical insights directly from the learned potentials themselves.

papers.title: Transfer learning on universal interatomic potential embeddings improves generalization in structure-property defect models
papers.abstract: Oxygen vacancy formation energies govern the performance of metal oxides across energy conversion, catalysis, and electronics, yet predicting them accurately without density functional theory calculations for novel chemical systems remains challenging. Here, we show that frozen 256-dimensional embeddings extracted from a pretrained MACE universal machine-learning interatomic potential encode information sufficient to predict vacancy formation energies obtained from density functional theory without requiring supercell construction, vacancy creation, or geometry optimization. A lightweight multilayer perceptron trained on these embeddings (MACE-dGNN) achieves an element-wise cross-validation mean absolute error of 0.38 eV, halving the error of a baseline graph neural network trained from scratch (0.72 eV) and offering a modest advantage over direct MACE relaxation calculations (0.51 eV). Because the embedding approach decouples representation from the prediction task and generalizes well with limited data, it will (1) extend naturally to fine-tuning and prediction of properties (e.g., charged defects) that are inaccessible to generic energy-and force-output interatomic potentials and (2) be trainable on necessarily small datasets, potentially enabling the use of more expensive but accurate tools for generating training data (e.g., hybrid functional calculations) for which training or fine-tuning of interatomic potentials will be difficult. We demonstrate practical impact by revisiting a prior screening of thermochemical water-splitting materials, where improved generalization alters ∼45 % of candidate classifications.

papers.title: Computer-Guided In-situ Screening of Poly(acetylene)s for Gene Delivery
papers.abstract: We report a new methodology for the discovery of polymer-based gene vectors that enables the simultaneous optimization of polymer composition and polyplex formulation, while bypassing the need to prepare, isolate, and characterise new candidates using conventional polymer synthesis. At the core of this approach is the combination of computer-aided experimental design, in situ screening of polymer composition and polyplex formulation, and machine learning, which allows us to treat polymer synthesis and formulation as a single optimizable problem. Central to this methodology is a new reactive and water-soluble poly(acetylene), poly(N-(propargyl)-2-(aminooxy)-acetamide), which can be functionalized in aqueous conditions with readily available aldehydes. This provides candidate polymers under biologically compatible conditions, which are then directly complexed with nucleic acids and evaluated within the same workflow. Iterative modelling then correlates inputs readily controlled by the operator—such as reagent concentrations and ratios—with the key performance metric, transfection efficiency, guiding subsequent rounds of candidate generation. In doing so, we move beyond post hoc correlations of physicochemical properties to establish an iterative, data-driven methodology for materials discovery. Ultimately, this methodology has unlocked the potential of poly(acetylene)s, a polymer family not previously explored in this context, to move beyond compositional mimicry and capture the dynamic helicity that underpins nucleic acid complexation and delivery in natural systems.

papers.title: Theoretical characterization of hydroxyfuranones related to biomass burning and their tautomers
Visible Light Enables NHC–Nickel-Mediated Carbonyl Deletion from Carboxamides
papers.abstract: Electron-rich N -heterocyclic carbene- (NHC-) supported nickel complexes are prized for their reactivity with weak polar functional groups, especially acyl electrophiles. However, synthetic applications leveraging this potent nucleophilicity have been limited to reactivity on the ground-state energy surface, thereby constraining the feasibility of downstream mechanistic steps. Herein, we report the development of a light-driven, NHC-nickel-mediated transformation that takes advantage of the complementary strengths of ground- and excited-state reactivity of NHC-nickel complexes. The carbonyl-deletion protocol enables intramolecular N -arylation from readily accessible carboxamides for the synthesis of di- and triaryl amines under mild conditions (ambient temperatures, additive-free). Combined density functional theory, organonickel intermediate isolation, single-crystal X-ray diffraction, spectroscopy, and radical-probe experiments reveal the origins of substrate-dependent reactivity and the role of light in C–N bond formation. The results support a dinuclear pathway for decarbonylation followed by photoinduced Ni–aryl bond weakening and in-cage C–N-forming radical rebound. These findings establish a mechanistic framework for developing direct photochemical reactivity from electron-rich NHC–nickel complexes relevant to organic synthesis.

papers.title: A Review of Migraine Treatments and the Significance of CGRP Inhibitors
papers.abstract: Migraines are not only a common neurological disorder, but also very debilitating. Migraine disorders cause significant financial, social, and mental burdens for patients. Despite its prevalence and impact, very few medications have been developed to treat migraines specifically. Previous treatments used medications prescribed for other conditions, and most of these treatments have low efficacy or tolerability, resulting in high percentages of patients who stop these medications. In recent years, a new class of medication, known as CGRP inhibitors, has been developed specifically for migraine treatment. These medications provide both preventative and acute treatment options with high efficacy and tolerability. Additionally, these medications are available to a wider range of population, unlike other treatments that cannot be used by individuals with preexisting conditions. This paper aims to serve as a review of previous studies on past treatment options and CGRP inhibitors to draw conclusions on the shortcomings of previous treatments and highlight the significance of CGRP inhibitors for migraine treatments. Based on the mental and socioeconomic impact of migraines, one can see that access to effective, tolerable treatment is imperative to improving the lives of those with migraines. Patients should not have to sacrifice other aspects of their health for relief from migraines. This comprehensive comparison gives important background information of migraines and asserts that CGRP inhibitors are the most effective and tolerable migraine treatment.

papers.title: Lewis Acid Catalyzed Cyclizative Rearrangement Strategy for One-Step 3-SF5- Furoquinoline and Furopyridine Synthesis
papers.abstract: Pentafluorosulfanyl (SF5)-substituted polyheterocyclic architectures hold significant promise across pharmaceutical and materials science applications. Nevertheless, the lack of a general, modular synthetic strategy to convert readily available SF5-building blocks into structurally diverse SF5-polyheterocycles remains a persistent and unsolved challenge in modern heterocyclic chemistry. To address this gap, we report a single-step, atom-economical synthesis of 3-(pentafluoro-λ6-sulfanyl)-2-arylfuro[3,2-b]quinolines and 3-(pentafluoro-λ6-sulfanyl)-2arylfuro[3,2-b]pyridines. This transformation is catalyzed by inexpensive ZrCl4 and promoted by NaI, proceeding via a cascade cyclizative rearrangement: (i) regioselective 1,3-dipolar addition of quinoline or pyridine N-oxides to SF5-alkynes, (ii) sequential 1,3-oxygen transfer, and (iii) rearomatization—affording the target 3-SF5-polyheterocycles in yields up to 99%. The methodology exhibits broad functional group tolerance and practical utility, enabling late-stage diversification of drug-like molecules, modular assembly of value-added heterocyclic scaffolds, and rational construction of D–π–A-type push–pull fluorophores with enhanced photophysical properties. Collectively, this work provides a scalable, operationally simple route to SF5polyheterocycles, thereby advancing their accessible chemical space for discovery in medicinal and materials chemistry.

papers.title: The Unique Vinylidene-Like Global Minimum of the Si <sub>2</sub> H <sub>2</sub> <sup>-</sup>
papers.abstract: This study presents a high-level computational investigation into the structural, vibrational, and energetic properties of neutral and anionic Si 2 H 2 structures. Through rigorous focal-point analysis at the CCSD(T) level and beyond, we demonstrate that electron attachment fundamentally reshapes the potential energy surface with computations using basis sets as large as quadruple zeta, and correlation treatments as sophisticated as CCSDT(Q). While the neutral butterfly is lowest in energy and has been identified experimentally, the anionic surface is fundamentally different. Our results remarkably identify the vinylidene structure as the lowest-energy anionic minimum, significantly preferred over the butterfly structure, which fails to support an anion minimum. The anion supports two minima: the vinylidene-like and monobridged; the vinylidene structure is lower in energy by 12.2 kcal/mol. The electron adiabatic affinity, the energy difference between the neutral butterfly and the anion vinylidene-like structure is 27.6 kcal/mol. This structural rearrangement upon electron attachment is related to behavior observed in isoelectronic hydrocarbons and other silicon hydrides, where charge accommodation forces a collapse to a more favorable semi-bridged ground-state minimum. By characterizing the distinct geometric, vibrational, and energetic signatures of these isomers, this research provides a definitive basis for the experimental detection of the anionic Si 2 H 2 species and adds a new chapter to the unique bonding behavior that distinguishes silicon from its lighter group 14 counterparts.

papers.title: Limits of geometric packing descriptors in molecular crystal energy ranking
papers.abstract: Simple packing descriptors do not consistently reproduce molecular crystal energy rankings across chemically distinct compounds. A retrospective benchmark of 98 deposited crystal structure prediction candidates from seven molecules was assembled from published relative r²SCAN-D3 electronic energies. Forty entries from four earlier systems were combined with 58 entries for indomethacin, nicotinamide and aspirin. Density, heavy-atom proximity, N–H···O/N geometry and planar-ring proximity were evaluated individually and through an equal-weight rank composite, without fitting feature weights. An implementation audit identified incomplete periodic-image enumeration affecting at least one descriptor in 23 structures. Recalculation with geometry-dependent complete image bounds changed 3.5 Å contact counts in 13 structures. On the three additional molecular systems, the corrected four-feature composite gave a macro-averaged Spearman correlation of 0.187, compared with 0.501 for density and −0.004 for 3.5 Å contacts. The composite improved on density for indomethacin but underperformed for nicotinamide and aspirin. Fifty-four of 813 within-molecule pairs had reference energy differences below 0.2 kJ mol⁻¹. This retrospective threshold does not provide calibrated predictive uncertainty or a prospective abstention rule. Metadata-verified energy joins, exact input hashes, representative invariance tests and reproducible numerical outputs accompany the analysis. The results document representation and implementation sensitivities and heterogeneous transfer between molecules. Neither superiority over established energy-ranking approaches nor prediction of experimental thermodynamic stability is demonstrated.

papers.title: Coarse-Graining in Drug Discovery: Opportunities and Challenges for Martini 3 in Small-Molecule Binding
papers.abstract: Accurate simulation of protein–ligand interactions remains a central challenge in drug discovery. Coarse-grained (CG) molecular dynamics offers a route to broader system coverage and efficient sampling by reducing molecular resolution. Here, we examine the potential of Martini 3 for drug discovery, reviewing methodological advances in simulation setup and addressing persistent challenges in sampling, model parameterization, and the reliable estimation of binding thermodynamics. Finally, we discuss priorities for translating CG simulations into robust, scalable drug discovery workflows.

papers.title: Compliance Mismatch Drives Mechanochemical Reactivity in Diels-Alder Reactions
papers.abstract: Mechanical forces can alter chemical reactivity by reshaping the potential energy surface landscape, but the relationships between force direction, molecular structure, and barrier structure remain poorly understood. Here, we develop a compliance-based framework for understanding primary mechanochemical activation by means of the compliance matrix and test it across a systematically designed chemical space of cyclopentadiene-based Diels-Alder reactions. Under the harmonic approximation, the force-induced change in a barrier height is determined by the difference in the compliances along the direction of force between the reactant complex and the transition state. We then evaluate this model across 233 Diels-Alder reactions, generating 1,271 reaction profiles and performing over 284,448 force-modified critical point calculations enabled by frontier machine-learned interatomic potentials. When deformation is restricted to a single coordinate, where the compliance matrix is effectively diagonal, the mechanochemical response depends strongly on the selected distortion, with dihedral motions providing a particularly effective mode of activation. However, upon optimizing in the presence of force, including the off-diagonal elements of the compliance matrix, the barrier-lowering behavior becomes widespread and is substantially less sensitive to the initial force direction. This behavior arises from the finding that reactant complexes are generally more compliant than their corresponding transition states. We show that a global reactant compliance descriptor captures this trend and identifies substituent-dependent differences in mechanochemical susceptibility, including candidate reactions for observing changes in stereoselectivity. These results show that mechanochemical activation for this reaction class does not require the force to be aligned with the traditional reaction coordinate. Instead, differential distortability across the reactant and transition states provides a general physical principle for understanding and potentially designing force-sensitive reactions. Finally, by extending this model to understand reactions under hydrostatic pressure conditions, this work provides insight into primary mechanochemistry across all distortion modes of molecular systems.

papers.title: A Modular Strategy for Collagen-Mimetic Peptides Using Diastereoselective Ugi Reactions
papers.abstract: Here, we report a highly efficient and modular strategy to synthesize characteristic tripeptide units via diastereoselective Ugi multicomponent reactions and use them to construct collagen-mimetic peptides (CMPs). Biocatalytic desymmetrization of prochiral cyclic amines provides optically pure chiral imines, which are combined with readily available isocyanides and amino acid building blocks to generate stereodefined tripeptide modules for solid-phase peptide synthesis. Monoamine oxidase N (MAO-N) mediated desymmetrization afforded imines in excellent enantiomeric excess (>99% ee), while the corresponding tripeptide modules were obtained with high diastereomeric ratios (>92:8 d.r.). After assembly into medium-sized CMPs, Circular Dichroism (CD) spectroscopy confirmed triple-helix formation. The synthetic analogues exhibited melting temperatures (Tm) of up to 39.2 °C, corresponding to a decrease of only 3.2 °C relative to the parent Hyp CMP sequence. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed that the bicyclic substituents optimize local packing via enhanced inter-chain van der Waals interactions and localized desolvation, rendering the fully folded analogues thermodynamically indistinguishable. This strategy enables the modular introduction of unnatural proline analogues into CMPs and provides a platform to rapidly evaluate how proline-analogue structure and stereochemistry influence triple-helix formation and stability.

papers.title: Protein-State Editing through Proximity-Induced Targeted Delactylation
papers.abstract: Selective manipulation of protein post-translational modifications without eliminating the modified proteins represents an emerging strategy for controlling protein function. Here, we introduce Delactylation Targeting Chimeras (DeLacTACs), a class of heterobifunctional molecules designed to redirect endogenous histone deacetylases (HDACs) toward lactylated proteins through chemically induced proximity. As a proof of concept, we targeted the oncogenic transcriptional coactivator YAP, whose lactylation at Lys90 promotes YAP–TEAD signaling. Through modular synthesis and systematic linker optimization, we developed a series of DeLacTACs and identified Y3CH and Y1PH as active compounds in gastric and liver cancer cells. Immunoprecipitation and quantitative mass spectrometry demonstrated reduced YAP K90 lactylation, accompanied by decreased lactylation of its transcriptional partner TEAD1 at Lys108 and Lys57, without substantial changes in their total protein abundance. Co-immunoprecipitation experiments further supported enhanced association between YAP and endogenous HDAC machinery following DeLacTAC treatment. These molecular changes were accompanied by reduced YAP nuclear accumulation, attenuated YAP–TEAD1 colocalization, suppression of downstream genes including CTGF, CYR61, and AARS1, and pronounced inhibition of tumor-cell proliferation and colony formation. The substantially weaker effects of the individual recognition components highlighted the importance of the bifunctional molecular architecture. Together, these findings establish DeLacTACs as a proximity-based chemical strategy for targeted modulation of protein lactylation and provide a foundation for programmable protein-state editing without target degradation.

papers.title: IMPLICIT LEARNING: REACTION OUTCOME PREDICTION FROM POSITIVE-ONLY DATA
papers.abstract: Machine learning models for reaction product prediction have largely been trained and evaluated on datasets of successful reactions. While this setting allows reaching high accuracy scores, these models generally struggle to discriminate between successful and unsuccessful transformations due to the lack of negative training data. This critically limits their practical use, as reliably recognizing unproductive substrate combinations in silico is required to accelerate experimental campaigns and save resources in the laboratory. While the availability of negative reaction data remains limited to date, we show that even purely positive datasets implicitly contain a significant amount of information about cases in which no reaction occurs. To exploit this, we introduce TACIT (TAckling Chemistry through ImpliciT negative learning). While trained on positive-only data, TACIT learns to distinguish between productive and unproductive transformations. On two published high-throughput experimentation datasets, it outperforms all evaluated reaction outcome prediction models in separating successful from failed reactions. Crucially, TACIT’s accuracy on the popular USPTO-MIT benchmark remains competitive, despite its added ability to predict negative reaction outcomes.

papers.title: Electric-field control of hydrogen-bond ordering in monolayer ice on graphite
papers.abstract: Hydrogen-bond (HB) networks govern molecular structure and function across chemistry, biology and materials science, yet their deterministic control at the atomic scale remains a central challenge. Here, we directly visualize and control HB ordering in monolayer ice on graphite by an external electric field and how this control arises from interfacial charge redistribution. Low-temperature scanning tunnelling microscopy reveals a field-driven two-dimensional (2D) liquid-to-solid transition from a mobile, non-wetting water adlayer to an ordered hexagonal monolayer ice. Systematic field variation is accompanied by a continuous change in apparent lattice spacing, while bias-resolved imaging reveals discrete conductance states set by the 2D-ice band edge, exposing coupled structural and electronic responses. At higher fields, we observed a 2D solid-solid phase transition between hexagonal and square ice. First-principles computation and biasdependent imaging support that the 2D transitions and physical effects arise from fieldinduced interfacial charge redistribution, thereby providing a field-tunable parameter for electrically programming HB networks and electronic properties at interfaces.

papers.title: Highly Selective Ionophore-Based Bilayer Emulsion Membranes
papers.abstract: Biological channels have been seen as ideal membrane components due to their high throughput and ion-ion selectivity, but their promise is often not realized in engineered biomimetic membranes. However, one recently-developed class of materials that has shown promise in this area is jammed interconnected bilayer emulsions (JIBEs), which are comprised of aqueous droplets joined together by amphiphilic bilayers that contain channels. Here, we investigate the use of ionophores in JIBEs as alternatives to biological channels and develop a crosslinked analog of this material with enhanced mechanical stability. Unlike biological channels, which provide a continuous pathway for ion transport through amphiphilic bilayers, ionophores partition into the bilayers and shuttle ions across them via facilitated transport. Various ionophores were studied to demonstrate the tunability of ionophore-containing JIBEs towards different separations. Most interestingly, JIBEs containing nonactin, an ammonium-selective ionophore, had an NH4+/Na+ selectivity up to 133, and JIBEs containing lithium ionophore VIII had an Li+/Na+ selectivity up to 180. Additionally, a crosslinked interconnected bilayer emulsion (crosslinked IBE) membrane with enhanced mechanical stability was synthesized by photopolymerizing monomers in both phases of an emulsion. Microscopy and capacitance measurements verified that networks of water droplets and the amphiphilic bilayers between these droplets were preserved after crosslinking. Furthermore, crosslinked IBE membranes containing nonactin exhibited an NH4+/Na+ selectivity of 54, which is similar in magnitude to what was observed in JIBEs. Overall, this work demonstrates the implementation of ionophores into biomimetic membranes to achieve highly-selective ion-ion separations and improves the scalability of JIBE membrane platform.

papers.title: Borrowing the fold, building the site: non-catalytic protein scaffolds in the age of computational metalloenzyme design
papers.abstract: The design of novel metalloenzymes has gained its motivation and momentum less from what enzymes already do well rather than from what they do not do at all, that is, the organic chemistry outside any biosynthetic pathways. In search for starting points to create proteins that are active in new-to-Nature transformations, computational design in particular offers powerful solutions by supplying folds made to order en route to inventing tailor-made de novo biocatalysts. Nature, however, rarely invents; it decorates. A large share of biological catalysis sits on backbones whose original role was structural or recognition-based, and in which the metal center occupies no more than a handful of side chains within an otherwise unchanged fold. In this Perspective we make the case that especially in systems addressing abiological catalysis, promising and successful approaches oftentimes adapt non-catalytic scaffolds as their foundation, taking binding modules, small disulfide-locked domains and synthetic miniproteins as hosts. We organize the discussion around the minimal functional site: the smallest ligand set that, placed on a rigid and pre-organized backbone, holds a metal in a defined geometry. Whether a given scaffold is able to offer such a site is a structural question before it is a chemical one. We examine how far current structure prediction can guide the placement of such sites, where its confidence scores mislead, and which spectroscopic and computational evidence remains indispensable. Scaffold repurposing, we conclude, offers organic synthesis a route to catalysts that enzymology alone would not deliver.

papers.title: Modeling CO2 absorption in aqueous monoethanolamine with ePC-SAFT
papers.abstract: We examine whether one explicit-ion electrolyte perturbed-chain statistical associating fluid theory (ePC-SAFT) formulation with carbamate chemistry can represent the equilibrium, caloric and density properties of loaded aqueous monoethanolamine (MEA). After separate water, CO2–water and dielectric fits, sixteen parameters are fitted jointly to pressure, species, integral absorption heat, density, heat capacity and binary equilibrium data. For nominal 30 wt% MEA, one parameter set thus represents CO2 pressure, the amine and carbamate fractions, integral heat at 313.15K and loaded density through 353.15K. Pressure average absolute relative deviations are 11.86 % over 47 fitted observations at 313.00–333.15K and 20.55 % over 159 observations at 313.00–393.15K, including 112 not fitted but examined during model development. The shared subset of 94 fitted species fractions gives 7.10 % at 293.15–333.15K. The fitted integral-heat root-mean-square error is 1.84 kJmol−1 CO2; the average absolute relative density deviation is 0.18 % over 47 fitted loaded densities, calculated without volume translation, with 44 within twice the assigned scale and three accepted misses at 353.15K. The 159-pressure deviation lies within the range of pressure deviations reported for related MEA models, which use different data sets and fitting roles. A fit with wider bounds on the protonated-amine diameter and its water interaction matches the properties similarly but predicts a second liquid phase at some states; narrowing these bounds removes the detected instabilities in a finite search at 162 states between 313.15 and 393.15K, with a 0.45 % higher fitting cost. Carbonate shares, titration bicarbonate, the 0.51MPaArcis integral heats, loaded densities above 353.15K and the unloaded heat capacity at 318.15K remain discrepant, and pressure deviations reach 29.5 and 56.0 % at 15 and 45 wt% MEA. The available comparisons do not yet establish suitability across absorber and stripper temperatures.

papers.title: Matrix Confinement Governs Competing Heavy‑Atom and Hydrogen Tunneling Pathways
papers.abstract: 1-Methylcyclobutylfluorocarbene (MFC) has served as a benchmark for ground-state carbon tunneling, yet its conformer-dependent tunneling competition in the matrix has remained unresolved for two decades. Here, we constructed three independent, channel-specific, highly accurate machine-learning potential energy surfaces and employed full-dimensional ring-polymer instanton theory to compute gas-phase tunneling rates. Our calculations reveal that rapid exo↔endo equilibration strongly favors endo-MFC, which decays exclusively via hydrogen tunneling. This intrinsic kinetic branching ratio sharply contradicts matrix experiments, where only heavy-atom tunneling was detected and the predicted hydrogentunneling product was not reported. This discrepancy can be rationalized by the dual regulatory effects exerted by rigid matrix cages: they sterically block large-amplitude conformer interconversion to trap exo-MFC, while simultaneously distorting the endo-MFC geometry to suppress its hydrogen tunneling. Dedicated spectroscopic searches over an extended spectral range could test the predicted hydrogen-tunneling pathway. This computational framework quantitatively disentangles how matrix confinement tunes competing heavy-atom and hydrogen quantum tunneling, resolving the longstanding mechanistic ambiguity of the MFC benchmark carbene system.

papers.title: ePC-SAFT: an electrolyte equation-of-state engine with exact derivatives for phase and reaction equilibrium and parameter estimation
papers.abstract: Electrolyte parameter estimation and equation-oriented process models require properties of a solved phase and reaction equilibrium and their responses to temperature, pressure, feed and molecular parameters. The ePC-SAFT package supplies these calculations in native C++ through a Python interface. Published hard-chain, dispersion, association, polar and electrolyte contributions define a selected Helmholtz energy; association and pressure closure, constrained equilibrium and exact derivatives share its mathematical implementation. One equilibrium driver handles declared neutral, charged and reacting phase specifications, while explicit tangent-plane searches test additional phases. Implicit derivatives of the defining equations supply observation Jacobians, least-squares and guarded minimax parameter estimation, and first and second derivatives for process models. Comparisons span pure-fluid saturation, neutral and associating mixtures, aqueous and mixed electrolytes, solvent transfer, liquid splits and reacting systems, with calibration, withheld prediction and published-model reproduction identified separately. With fixed published parameters, propane saturation pressures and liquid densities deviate from measurements by 2.70 % and 0.305 % on average; on 19 temperatures withheld from a threetemperature refit, the refit gives 1.00 % and 0.180 %, against 1.07 % and 0.228 % for the published parameters. The comparisons also expose failed mixed-salt transfer, large reactive-amine pressure discrepancies and unresolved source conventions. Numerical verification gives liquidliquid mole fractions within 4.62 × 10−9 of an independent matched electrolyte implementation and selected solved-state derivatives within 3.40 × 10−10 relative. Settler and hydrogen-mixture examples show how the same calculations enter engineering models, with physical accuracy bounded by the stated parameter domains and data.

papers.title: Engineering Receptor-Directed Intracellular Palladium Catalysis
papers.abstract: Directing abiotic chemical activity toward cells defined by surface receptors remains difficult because a metal complex must combine recognition with reactivity in biological media. Integrin-, epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-, and CD44-binding peptides were joined to a bis(histidine) Pd(II)-binding zinc-finger scaffold to create three receptor-directed Pallado-fingers. Each construct retained depropargylation reactivity in an equimolar cell-free assay. In paired cell models, the integrin- and EGFR-directed complexes showed >2.5-fold greater cellassociated fluorescence in receptor-enriched cells, while the CD44-directed complex showed 1.45-fold enrichment. Antibody profiling, receptor competition, mixed-cell discrimination, and αvβ3 knockdown connected this bias to receptor engagement. Receptor-enriched cells then generated greater fluorescence from a masked dye, and cell-associated-Pd-normalized apparent turnover numbers of 3.81–5.76 supported catalysis at the whole-cell level. The same design increased nuclear accumulation of a masked nuclear localization sequence and enhanced the Annexin V response of propargyl-protected temporin in A549 cells. These results establish a modular route from surface recognition to receptor-biased intracellular unmasking.

papers.title: Escape Rooms, Arcades, and a Grain of Salt: Five Original Games for Introductory Chemistry, Built by One Instructor with Generative AI
papers.abstract: Five browser games for a one-semester introductory chemistry course (CHM 1025, Daytona State College) are described: a four-stage retro arcade game on balancing equations, stoichiometry, and Lewis structures; a Halloween escape room on bonding, molecular shape, polarity, and intermolecular forces; a 3D game in which the player shrinks by factors of a thousand from a laboratory bench to the ions in a grain of salt, practicing scale, atomic structure, isotopes, light, and electron configurations; a six-stage arcade game on the textbook's key terms; and a first-week game that sends students to read the syllabus. The games are offered as optional extra credit or for nothing at all; their purpose is to get students to open the chapter one more time and to make the course feel friendlier, not to replace instruction. I built all five in about a month, as side projects; I am a chemist with no programming background and used a generative AI coding assistant, in HTML or in Unity depending on what each concept needs to be seen. Every character, image, sound, and tune is original or used with permission; completion is verified by a code the game issues, so extra credit can be awarded without trusting a screenshot. The games are free, run in any browser with no account, and are published with their source. No learning outcomes are claimed; evaluation is future work.

papers.title: Frozen sequence encoders with gradient boosting match the state of the art on drug–target affinity domain generalization, and a sequence defect in the Davis kinase benchmark
papers.abstract: We report two results on public kinase drug–target interaction (DTI) benchmarks. First, a deliberately simple model — frozen pretrained encoders for molecules and proteins, with gradient-boosted trees on top and no end-to-end training — reaches PCC 0.591 ± 0.004 on the Therapeutics Data Commons DTI-DG benchmark (BindingDB_Patent), evaluated with TDC’s own split and evaluator over five seeds. This is statistically indistinguishable from the best published entry (0.588 ± 0.002; difference 0.003 against a combined standard error of 0.0045, 0.67 SE) and separated from the second entry (0.538 ± 0.008) by 5.9 SE. The result reproduced exactly on an independent run. Second, we document a defect in the widely used Davis kinase dataset that affects any work using its mutant kinases. Davis lists 442 protein names but contains only 379 distinct sequences: all 45 mutation-labelled entries are assigned the wild-type sequence of their gene. ABL1 and ABL1(E255K) have bit-identical ESM-2 embeddings (L2 = 0.0000, cosine = 1.000000). The affinity labels differ while the model input does not, so these pairs are irreducible contradictions in training — 9.63% of all Davis rows. Reconstructing the mutant sequences from the names raises the distinct-sequence count to 423, reduces contradictory rows to 3.97%, and improves concordance index on mutant proteins by +0.0173 (5/5 seeds, t = 23.16) under an otherwise identical protocol.

papers.title: Navigating the STORM of Structural and Stereochemical Systematization of Monosaccharides
papers.abstract: Carbohydrate complexity stems largely from the number and structural diversity of monosaccharides, many differing only in stereochemistry. Trivial names and systematic names resulting from stereochemistryaffecting modifications obscure structural relationships, creating barriers for newcomers and sometimes puzzling experts. Systematic Tables of Relevant Monosaccharides (STORM) addresses these issues by organizing monosaccharides in tables, aligned by corresponding stereochemistry and grouped by analogous modifications. STORM comprises five tables for reference, systematization, and education: major monosaccharides, branched monosaccharides, ulosonic acids, heptoses, and atypical monosaccharides, totaling 351 distinct monosaccharides in 336 cells. Color-coded property marks visualize relationships and reveal monosaccharides not yet described. STORM tables are extensible and customizable.

papers.title: PyFMO: A Python Framework for Fragment Molecular Orbital Calculations
A Fluorescent Nucleosome Platform for High-Throughput Sirtuin Kinetic Analysis and Inhibitor Discovery
papers.abstract: The class IV sirtuins SIRT6 and SIRT7 are epigenetic protein lysine deacylases identified as targets for cancer treatment, including pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). However, small molecules to study their regulatory roles or modulate their function in disease remain scarce. A major reason is that class IV sirtuins require nucleosomal substrates to be active, and current peptide-based assays therefore fail as tools for activity profiling and inhibitor development. Here, we develop a translatable kinetic assay platform by engineering a fluorescence-based activity sensor directly into semi-synthetic nucleosomes. This enables activity profiling and screening of modulators of epigenetic eraser enzymes. For both SIRT6 and SIRT7, we measure enzyme kinetics in real time, yielding an assay with nanomolar Michaelis-Menten substrate constants and Z’ values over 0.8. For SIRT7, we provide a mechanistic model of nucleosomal substrate selectivity and activity regulation, and for SIRT6, we use the platform to assay hits selected from an in-cell DNA-encoded library screening campaign. As a result, we identify vpc03898 as a potent, selective, and cell-permeable competitive inhibitor of SIRT6 with activity against PDAC cell migration at single-digit µM concentration. Together, this work establishes a translatable strategy for kinetic screening of nucleosome-targeting eraser enzymes toward cancer therapeutic development.

papers.title: 1 ̸= 0: A Thermodynamic Alternative to the Navier–Stokes Equations via Extended 14-Moment Hyperbolicity and Scale-Space Regularization
papers.abstract: For nearly two centuries, the classical Navier–Stokes equations have served as the foundational governing model of continuum fluid mechanics. Despite their engineering utility, the equations harbor unresolved mathematical pathologies—most notably the open question of finite-time blow-up of smooth solutions in three dimensions—and require empirical closure hierarchies to approximate high-Reynolds-number turbulence. In this work, we demonstrate that these pathologies are not intrinsic features of physical fluids, but mathematical artifacts resulting from treating an instantaneous local spatial derivative as a fundamental physical law. By enforcing the Local Thermodynamic Equilibrium (LTE) truncation (De = τmicro/τmacro → 0), the classical Newton–Stokes closure (τ dev = 2µDdev) discards the finite relaxation memory and non-local phase-space contraction of irreversible energy dissipation. We formulate a rigorous alternative grounded in the 1 ̸= 0 Non-Equivalence Principle: a dissipative continuum with strictly positive entropy production (σ > 0) cannot be topologically reduced to a memoryless sequence of equilibrium tangent projections. Expanding the state space to a 14-moment Extended Irreversible Thermodynamic (EIT) manifold M = {ρ, u, e, Π, τ dev, q} equipped with the trace-preserving, frame-indifferent corotational Jaumann derivative

papers.title: Tacticity Engineering: Decoupling Bond-Formation from Stereochemical Control in the Design of Poly(Vinyl Ethers)
papers.abstract: Tacticity in synthetic polymers governs local chain conformations and intermolecular packing, thereby exerting itself as a primary determinant of emergent material properties. However, despite its transcending effects, tacticity is generally treated as an immutable synthetic outcome rather than a variable that can be independently designed and manipulated. To isolate tacticity as a fundamentally tunable macromolecular variable, we have developed a tacticity engineering platform that decouples chain growth from stereochemical control in the design and synthesis of poly(vinyl ethers). This platform leverages photocatalytic post-synthetic hydrogen atom abstraction and transfer to controllably manipulate tacticity in pre-formed polymer scaffolds without altering other defining material characteristics, such as molecular weight, dispersity, or cross-linking density. Leveraging the photocontrol of our approach, we show that precise tacticity levels can be reliably accessed by controlling irradiation duration. We highlight that this synthetic method can be broadly applied to a library of differentially substituted poly(vinyl ethers). To showcase the utility of our tacticity engineering platform, we systematically manipulated emergent macromolecular properties and established structure-property relationships correlating tacticity to thermomechanical behavior. Rheological characterization of poly(vinyl ethers) links local packing density to the zero-shear viscosity, revealing that viscosity increases by six orders of magnitude as stereoregularity decreases. Collectively, these findings establish post-polymerization tacticity engineering as a general strategy for decoupling bond formation from stereochemical programming in synthetic matter, while forging a direct link between tacticity and viscoelastic properties and indicating its promise for designing next-generation functional materials.

papers.title: Dataset-specific retention time adjustment and multi-evidence lipid annotation: a reproducible R workflow for untargeted LC–MS lipidomics
papers.abstract: Background and Objective: Untargeted lipid annotation by liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry is challenged by structural isomers, multiple ion forms, and retention time differences between analytical datasets. We developed an open-source computational workflow combining dataset-specific retention time adjustment with experimentally characterized lipid information to restrict candidate assignments while preserving unresolved identities. Methods: The R workflow uses a curated database of 592 lipid species derived from a human plasma reference material. It combines monotonic retention time adjustment, accurate-mass matching, isotope-pattern assessment, empirical adduct profile, and ambiguity resolution. Developed using a 40-sample MICROSAMPLING study, it was applied to an independent 189-sample METFORMIN-HIIE study acquired under compatible chromatographic conditions. Annotation stages were evaluated against fixed workflow-derived references, including a comparison with unadjusted database retention times. Results: Unadjusted retention time matching recovered 55.4-77.2% of reference feature-lipid pairs, whereas adjusted matching recovered all reference pairs under identical tolerances. RT adjustment reduced candidates on non-reference features by 69.5-83.2% relative to mass-only matching and increased within-reference candidate discrimination from 69.1-70.9% to 88.5-92.6%. Isotope filtering and ambiguity resolution further restricted assignments. Integration across ionization modes yielded 433 and 379 endogenous feature records, respectively; 93 and 100 retained multiple compatible lipid identities rather than forcing unsupported unique assignments. Conclusions: Dataset-specific adjustment improves agreement with workflow-curated assignments while restricting candidate space. The approach supports reproducible lipid annotation and transparent uncertainty handling. Because the reference assignments originate from the workflow itself, complete retention does not establish independent annotation sensitivity or accuracy.

papers.title: Chemically Programmed Albumin–Enzyme Conjugates to Induce Microenvironment-Responsive Metabolic Disruption
papers.abstract: Glucose oxidase (GOx)-mediated glucose depletion is an attractive intervention strategy that can address the abnormal tumor metabolism characterized by elevated glycolysis. But its efficacy is limited by inefficient cellular delivery and hypoxia-induced stabilization of HIF-1α, which is associated with adaptive metabolic responses. Here, we report a chemically programmed albumin–GOx conjugate that couples microenvironment-responsive uptake with reductive release of acriflavine (ACF), a small molecule reported to interfere with HIF-1 signaling. Human serum albumin was used as the core carrier platform and engineered to include (1) dimethylmaleic anhydride groups to sense tumor-relevant acidic conditions and induce charge reversal for concomitant cellular delivery of both GOx and ACF payloads and (2) self-immolative disulfide linkage to release ACF under reductive conditions. The resulting GOx–albumin–ACF conjugate preserved GOx-mediated glucose oxidation and attenuated HIF-1α accumulation. Consequently, stronger metabolic disruption including suppressed lactate production and reduced adenosine triphosphate (ATP) levels was observed, together with enhanced cell death in two-dimensional cultures and three-dimensional tumor spheroids. By integrating chemical activation with modulation of the GOx-associated HIF-1α response, this work establishes a biomacromolecular design strategy for a protein-based, microenvironment-responsive therapeutic system that senses, responds, and acts within the tumor microenvironment to achieve enhanced metabolic disruption and cytotoxicity

papers.title: Choosing a DFT Protocol That Ranks Deep-Blue TADF Emitters and Pairs Them with Hosts
papers.abstract: Computational screening of deep-blue thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) materials decides which emitters are made and which host each is paired with, yet the descriptors behind these decisions are rarely tested against measurement. We test them on 50 molecules (39 published emitters, eight references and three phosphine-oxide hosts) against measured data for 27 emitters. The range-separated ωB97X-D3 functional overestimates every singlettriplet gap (∆EST) and fails to rank the emitters because its error differs between molecular families; a family offset restores the ranking, and the global hybrids PBE0 and B3LYP rank the gaps directly (Spearman ρ = 0.59 and 0.58). Rate constants built on computed gaps are unreliable, but become accurate once the measured gap is used. For host–emitter pairing, the triplet energies of host and emitter must be computed on one footing: a calibrated host combined with as-computed emitters misclassifies almost every confined pair. A tiered, costed protocol turns these findings into selection rules for screening campaigns.

papers.title: DNA Origami Welding Sticks Enable Dielectrophoretic Growth of Gold Nanowires
papers.abstract: Electric fields can gather metal nanoparticles between electrodes, but turning them into continuous conductors at a chosen site remains difficult: at kilohertz frequencies free particles grow branched aggregates, and at the megahertz frequencies that favor straight wires, free DNA-coated particles were not collected at all under our conditions. Here, DNA origami tubes holding three 13 nm gold nanoparticles serve as carriers that deliver gold to the gap and then give it up to form wires. The tubes roll from a 72 × 89 nm sheet around particles bound by A20:T20 tethers and carry three particles, 25 nm apart. Three-dimensional field calculations show that at this spacing the peak field is only 1.14 times that of an isolated particle, so the scaffold creates no hot spots. At 1.2 MHz, hybrids form particle lines between Ti/Au tips where free particles leave no wire, and fronts grow from one or both tips to bridge 0.35–2.2 µm gaps. The products are polycrystalline gold with rounded grains up to about 60 nm; 13 of 17 structures conduct, with linear current–voltage curves and length-independent two-terminal resistances of 60–360 Ω. A circuit model accounts for this: after bridging, about 40 mA flows, and Joule heating melts any constriction that drops more than about 0.4 V, so growth should end when the wire is a few ohms and the leads dominate the measured value. DNA origami thus serves as a field-trappable carrier and consumable feedstock for bottom-up interconnects.

papers.title: The Least-Ordered of Three Deep-Blue Phosphine-Oxide Hosts Still Conducts Holes Cleanly
papers.abstract: Deep-blue phosphine-oxide hosts are compared by energy levels and photophysics, almost never by microstructure—yet order and film morphology are routinely read as proxies for how well a host will carry charge. Here three related hosts are compared from primary particles to film relief with documented, protocol-tested descriptors. The tert-butyl-substituted S3 host emerges as the least ordered on every scale: the lowest X-ray ordered fraction at every baseline setting, the shortest film correlation, micrometre-scale relief and the lowest decomposition temperature, while only the S1 host shows lattice fringes. Disorder, however, does not spoil its hole transport. The S3 hole-only device shows a single, nearly ideal relaxation with a capacitance close to the geometric value and an apparent hole mobility of about 5 × 10−7 cm2 V−1 s−1, comparable to that of the far better-ordered S1 host. Long-range disorder in these hosts is therefore compatible with clean hole transport, and microstructure alone is not a reliable screen for transport.

papers.title: Autonomous discovery of reaction networks from active-learning-driven reactive molecular dynamics
papers.abstract: Reaction networks underlie complex chemical systems such as combustion, catalysis, and atmospheric chemistry and can comprise thousands of elementary reactions. Ab initio nanoreactor molecular dynamics explores such networks efficiently by accelerated sampling of the potential energy surface, but computational cost limits how far it can sample. This work presents a transferable methodology coupling nanoreactor molecular dynamics with active learning to autonomously generate reaction networks from starting molecules. An agentdeveloped parser extracts elementary reactions from trajectories, and a large-language-model coding agent improves transition-state search strategies. Applied to the atmospheric oxidation of dimethyl sulfide, the methodology yields 980 nanoseconds of simulation, requiring only 290,195 quantum-chemical calculations. Initializing reaction discovery from already discovered species drastically speeds up reaction network exploration leading to 13,271 elementary reactions and 6,995 species. The reaction network covers most of the established mechanism but also unveils novel species such as an isomer of the key intermediate HPMTF.

papers.title: The film, not the molecule, decides how deep-blue TADF hosts rank on gap and thermal robustness
papers.abstract: Deep-blue host materials for thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) are usually ranked on a few molecular numbers, on the assumption that the isolated molecule anticipates the film. We test that assumption for three phosphine-oxide hosts, S1, S3 and S4, by reading protocol-locked descriptors of the dilute solution, the evaporated film, the powder and the bulk side by side, each with its uncertainty, next to a separate density-functional layer. The descriptors fall into families that rank the hosts differently: film-gap and thermal descriptors place the multi-arm S4 host first, emission and order descriptors place the compact carbazole S1 host first, and band-tail and voltammetric descriptors do not separate the two. The split appears between the molecule and the film: the two hosts emit alike as dilute molecules, yet the S4 film absorption edge lies 0.33 eV higher. Calculations validated against the measured infrared and NMR spectra show frontier levels that move far more with the functional than between hosts. Film gap and thermal robustness must therefore be measured and assessed separately from emissive quality.

papers.title: Hydrogen bonding, thermal expansion, and phase transition of cranswickite (MgSO4 · 4H2O)
papers.abstract: Cranswickite, the rarer of the two natural polymorphs of MgSO4·4H2O, has until now been known only from its type locality and characterized solely by X-ray powder methods, leaving its hydrogen-atom positions undetermined. The crystal structure of perdeuterated cranswickite, MgSO4·4D2O, prepared by controlled-humidity dehydration of the heptahydrate, has been refined by Rietveld analysis of time-of-flight neutron powder diffraction data at 10 K and 295 K, with all deuteron positions and displacement parameters refined without restraints, yielding the first complete hydrogen-bond geometry for this phase. Variable-temperature measurements (10–340 K) reveal strongly anisotropic thermal expansion: one principal axis of the expansion tensor is negative over the entire temperature range, reaching α1 = −3.7(3) × 10-5 K-1 at 335 K, which is balanced by positive expansion of similar magnitude within the ac plane, such that the principal expansivities [α1:α2:α3 = −1.04(4):2.90(4):1.00(5) at 295 K] yield zero area expansion of the ac plane. At 330 K cranswickite’s transformation to starkeyite accompanied by a volume reduction of 4.72% was observed, which is among the largest known density increases associated with a phase transition. The relevance of these findings to MgSO4 hydrates as candidate rock-forming minerals on Mars and the icy Galilean satellites is discussed.

papers.title: Learning Chemoselectivity in a Low-Data Regime: Bayesian Optimization of the NBS-Activated Selenocyclization of α-Allenols
papers.abstract: The activation of diaryl diselenides with N-bromosuccinimide generates two competing electrophiles, and with α-allenols as the π-nucleophiles, product mixtures of brominated and selenylated dihydrofurans can arise. This selectivity challenge was quickly resolved through a Bayesian optimization campaign over seven reaction parameters covering >2000 discrete combinations. Fifteen randomly sampled experiments were sufficient for Gaussian-process surrogate models that, when asked to simultaneously maximize yield and selectivity, recommended conditions that delivered the 3-selanyl-2,5-dihydrofuran in up to 74% yield with complete suppression of the vinyl bromide. The identified protocol for the 5-endo-trig cyclization transferred without re-optimization to a range of structurally diverse α-allenols (50–81% isolated yield) and proved to be applicable to other dichalcogenides, as well as to the 6-endo-trig cyclization of related allene homologues.

papers.title: From Processing to Programmable Properties: A Review of Artificial Intelligence in Metal Additive Manufacturing
papers.abstract: Machine learning has accelerated process–structure–property (PSP) prediction in metal additive manufacturing (AM), but a predicted optimum is useful only if it can be realized through processing and verified experimentally. This review examines that transition by connecting physics-based simulation, data curation, microstructure representation and reconstruction, and inverse design. We assess the information each stage retains, the assumptions it introduces, and the uncertainty it passes to subsequent decisions. Three tests organize the synthesis: structural fidelity, independently evaluated property performance, and accessibility through a specified processing route. Using these tests, we compare forward and inverse methods in terms of their data requirements, physical constraints, and validation evidence, distinguishing metal-AM demonstrations from transferable approaches developed in adjacent fields. Recurring limitations include simulation–experiment mismatch, incomplete dataset provenance, representation-dependent ambiguity, and insufficient testing outside the training domain. We outline benchmarks and reporting practices that make these limitations visible and connect them to priorities in physics-informed, multifidelity, interpretable, and multimodal learning. The resulting roadmap places experimental feedback at the center of the design workflow and identifies the evidence needed to translate rapid predictions into reproducible control of microstructure and properties.

papers.title: Ni/TiO <sub>2</sub> Interfaces Enhance Benzaldehyde Selectivity in the Photocatalytic Dehydrogenation of Benzyl Alcohol
papers.abstract: The selective conversion of alcohols to carbonyls (ketones and aldehydes) plays an important role in chemical manufacturing. Photocatalytic acceptorless dehydrogenation offers a light-driven alternative for producing value-added aldehydes and H 2 under mild conditions and with easy separation and high molar efficiency. However, using semiconductor photocatalysts to achieve high selectivity and long-term stability under prolonged high-intensity illumination remains challenging. In this work, we developed CdS/TiO 2 /Ni photocatalysts by depositing TiO 2 onto CdS nanoparticle panels via atomic layer deposition (ALD), followed by Ni cocatalyst photodeposition, for the acceptorless dehydrogenation of benzyl alcohol to benzaldehyde and H 2 . Diluting the benzyl alcohol concentration to a practical range of ~10 vol% (1 M) further increased benzaldehyde selectivity to ~95%. Ni photodeposition and zeta-potential measurements suggest that TiO 2 coatings progressively modify Cd 2+ -associated surface sites through Ti 3+ /Ti 4+ incorporation, altering adsorption kinetics and contributing to the reduced activity. This extends the photocatalyst’s lifespan from ~23 to 60 hours and increases cumulative benzaldehyde and H 2 production. TiO 2 thin-film coatings have emerged as a promising strategy to protect semiconductor photocatalysts while modifying surface active sites and reaction kinetics, and their stability-activity trade-off showing lower initial-stage activity beyond 15-cycle ALD will be discussed alongside proposed mechanisms. This work establishes a semiconductor/coating/cocatalyst design architecture that highlights the importance of engineering surface adsorption and active-site environments, alongside charge-separation strategies based on band-edge energetics and charge-carrier dynamics, to jointly optimize photocatalytic activity and product selectivity for targeted chemical synthesis.

papers.title: Inhibiting LINE-1 retrotransposons therapeutically in disease
papers.abstract: The LINE-1 retrotransposon is a virus-like genomic element that can activate in diseased cells. It has been implicated in cancer, autoimmunity, developmental disorders, infectious disease and neurodegeneration. LINE-1 can be inhibited by reverse transcriptase inhibitors, small molecules originally developed for HIV. The correlation between HIV and LINE-1 inhibition is ∼0.9 on a log scale, in spite of >450 Mya of evolutionary history since retroviruses diverged from retrotransposons. Suppression of HIV requires prevention of a completed 9.7 kb virus insertion into the genome in immune cells. However, every cell in the body already contains >100 copies of LINE-1 that can potentially activate. Even incomplete LINE-1 mediated insertions can cause damaging mutations and genome instability. Furthermore, partial HIV and LINE-1 products in the cytoplasm of cells can contribute to an inflammatory immune response. Preclinical studies have shown LINE-1 inhibitors slow the progression of otherwise unrelated diseases.
