LINE-1’s contribution to these diseases can potentially be quantified using single-nucleus whole-genome sequencing on diseased tissue, enabling prioritization of disease selection for therapeutic development. Furthermore, LINE-1’s ORF1p protein can be measured in the blood of individuals with certain cancers. LINE-1 inhibitors could therefore be extended to various diseases. Potentially used both as an anti-inflammatory and prophylactically to help preserve genome integrity.

papers.title: WITHDRAWN
papers.abstract: Withdrawn by ChemRxiv because it was posted prematurely.

papers.title: OPRD-100: An Expert-Curated Dataset of Organic Reactions for Benchmarking Reaction Data Mining Tools
papers.abstract: The increasing use of AI in chemical research requires reliable reaction data to support efficient synthetic route design and reaction discovery. We present OPRD-100, an expert-curated and cross-validated dataset of 3,878 reactions extracted from 100 Organic Process Research & Development articles published between 1999 and 2024. Each entry captures detailed reactivity information, including yield, stereochemistry, temperature, time, solvents, and reagents. Analysis of the dataset reveals the relative importance of reaction data reported in tables versus text—particularly for reactions with low or no yields—and highlights the challenges of consistently capturing information from complex studies. Comparison with Reaxys showed systematic omissions and a strong bias toward high-yield reactions, underscoring the risks of relying on uncurated data. OPRD-100 thus provides a robust benchmark for training and evaluating AI tools in industrially relevant organic synthesis. Reaction data, data mining, benchmarking dataset

papers.title: A Negatively Curved Porphyrin [10]Circulene
papers.abstract: A curved five-porphyrin circulene has been synthesized through oxidative fusion of a cyclic precursor, prepared by Yamamoto coupling. The saddle-shaped geometry of this molecule was confirmed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. In solution, it undergoes a rapid saddle-to-saddle inversion, even at 200 K, resulting in a simple 1 H NMR spectrum. Despite its pronounced negative curvature (Gauss curvature: –0.30 Å –2 ), it exhibits efficient electronic delocalization, with an electrochemical band gap of 0.88 eV and near-infrared absorption (λ max 1200 nm). It has a high affinity for C 60 and C 70 , in toluene at 298 K. There is no significant bond length alternation around the central 10-membered ring, and computational studies reveal a substantial diatropic current around this ring, establishing the porphyrin circulene as a globally aromatic curved nanographene.

papers.title: Non-Monotonic Structural Response of Co3O4 during Calcination
papers.abstract: Calcination is widely applied to adjust crystallinity and defects in metal oxides. However, structural evolution is often assumed to follow a monotonic temperature dependence. Here, we demonstrate that the structural response of Co3O4 to calcination is significantly more complex. Using a multi-modal approach combining diffraction, microscopy, spectroscopy, and defect-sensitive analysis, we track the structural evolution across multiple scales from 300–600 °C. While average crystallographic descriptors evolve monotonically with temperature, defect-associated features exhibit pronounced non-monotonic behaviour, revealing asynchronous evolution across structural levels. A distinct structural turning emerges at 400 °C, where found the metastable Co3O4. This state is characterized by enhanced local disorder and a distinct combination of various defects within spinel matrix. The results reveal that calcination does not induce a monotonic ordering pathway but activates coupled asynchronous structural processes. Our work highlights the importance of multiscale structural characterization for understanding and controlling the complex structures of oxide nanomaterials.

papers.title: Disinfection of Onsite Sewage Treatment and Disposal Systems: A Critical Review of U.S. State Regulations and Field Evidence
papers.abstract: Onsite sewage treatment and disposal systems (OSTDS) serve approximately one in five U.S. households and hundreds of millions of people worldwide, yet the scientific basis for regulating onsite wastewater disinfection has not been comprehensively evaluated. This review compares statewide regulations from all 50 U.S. states with field evidence for chlorination and ultraviolet (UV) disinfection under actual OSTDS conditions. Only 24 states include specific disinfection provisions, with substantial variation in allowable technologies, certification, operational criteria, microbial standards, and maintenance requirements. Prescribed operating conditions, including chlorine residual and UV fluence, generally fall within ranges associated with successful field performance. However, available evidence is insufficient to confirm that minimum regulatory requirements consistently achieve adequate microbial reduction under routine conditions. Field studies show that treatment failures commonly result from inadequate maintenance, declining chlorine delivery or UV output, inadequate pretreatment, and failure to verify required operating conditions. These failure pathways are only partially addressed by current regulations. State policies could be strengthened through technology-specific requirements for routine performance verification, preventive maintenance, and early failure detection. Future research should prioritize long-term field validation of regulatory criteria and improved monitoring and maintenance strategies for OSTDS.

papers.title: Ultracompact Biomimetic High-Performance CO2 Membrane Contactor
papers.abstract: 12 Achieving net-zero carbon emissions will require compact, energy-efficient CO2 capture 13 technologies, yet conventional membrane contactors are limited by mass transfer. Here, we 14 report a lung-inspired three-dimensional gyroid membrane contactor (3D-GMC) that integrates 15 a nanoporous membrane with an interconnected microchannel networks. At contact times 16 below one second, the contactor achieves >90% CO2 removal from simulated flue gas and >80% 17 removal from ambient air. Its volumetric CO2 capture flux exceeds that of the best reported 18 flue-gas capture systems by more than 2.7-fold and that of current DAC technologies by 5.8-19 fold. For DAC at a capture capacity of 1 ton of CO2 per day, this perfrmance translates to a 20 ≈10-fold reduction in required contactor volume relative to conventional air-liquid contactors.

papers.title: Neural quantum states for non-Markovian open quantum dynamics in bosonic environments
papers.abstract: Condensed-phase quantum dynamics are strongly shaped by vibrational, solvent, and protein environments, yet their nonperturbative, non-Markovian description requires a rapidly growing high-dimensional representation as environmental complexity increases. Here, we extend neural quantum states (NQS) to the dissipaton-embedded quantum master equation (DQME) for bosonic environments using a complex-valued restricted Boltzmann machine adapted to nonbinary bosonic occupations. An explicit filtering scheme further concentrates the neural representation on dynamically relevant dissipaton configurations. The resulting NQS-DQME approach reproduces representative quantum dissipative dynamics while effectively compressing the reduced density tensor (RDT). For an anharmonic model of condensed-phase hydrogen transfer, the method also reproduces weak-coupling tunneling dynamics. At stronger system-bath coupling, however, errors become localized in a small subset of RDT elements, showing that a small global variational residual does not necessarily ensure accurate chemically relevant observables. This limitation identifies observable-level error control as a key challenge for reliable long-time NQS propagation.

papers.title: Noise Ceilings for Molecular Potency Benchmarks: Measuring Label Noise from Independent ChEMBL Documents
papers.abstract: The same compound measured against the same target in different laboratories often receives different potency values, which limits how well any model can be scored against such labels. For 17 potency tasks (target × Ki or IC50) from ChEMBL 37, we estimate this limit per task from 3,292 molecules reported in at least two source documents and express model scores as a fraction of ceiling f (0: predicting the training mean; 1: reaching the estimated noise floor). The floors range from 0.31 to 0.79 pChEMBL units, but for some tasks the replicates come from a few document pairs, and a bootstrap over document pairs then gives intervals several times wider than one over molecules. After removing molecules found in MoleculeNet and TDC, we benchmark ECFP-based gradient boosting, random forest and MLP models and frozen ChemBERTa-77M and MoLFormer-XL embeddings with a boosted-tree head under random, scaffold and temporal splits. ECFP with a random forest reaches a mean f of 0.90, 0.73 and 0.36 on the three splits (random: median 0.82, range 0.80–1.03 over the floor’s uncertainty). The frozen embeddings reach 0.69/0.66, 0.55/0.54 and 0.25/0.25 (ChemBERTa/MoLFormer) and are below ECFP with gradient boosting on every split (Wilcoxon over tasks, Holm-adjusted p < 0.05); on five tasks, a D-MPNN and a fine-tuned ChemBERTa do not close the gap on random and scaffold splits. On five task–split combinations ECFP models score below the estimated floor (f > 1), which shows that the floor is uncertain for these tasks; we discuss mis-estimation and learnable document-level offsets as explanations. We report single-test-set minimum detectable effects and a reporting protocol, and release code and data.

papers.title: Mobilis: an open-source toolkit for charge transport in organic semiconductors, from crystal structures to temperaturedependent mobilities with dynamic disorder and active learning
papers.abstract: Computing a charge mobility for an organic semiconductor involves a chain of steps: monomer site energies, intermolecular couplings, the thermal fluctuation of those couplings, and a transport model whose validity depends on the ratio of coupling to reorganization energy. These steps are usually carried out with separate scripts and different quantum-chemistry codes, which makes results hard to reproduce and models hard to compare. Mobilis is an open-source Python package (GPL-3.0) with a graphical interface and a command-line interface that runs the whole chain from a CIF file or an MD morphology. It prepares and reads Gaussian and ADF calculations (and xtb from the command line), and contains its own extended-Hückel and ZINDO couplings, a polarizable site-energy model, Marcus–Jortner hopping with kinetic Monte Carlo, and transient localization theory. For dynamic disorder it builds coupling surfaces over the six rigidbody intermolecular coordinates and samples them by full-crystal rigid-body molecular dynamics. A Gaussian-process active-learning loop chooses the DFT dimer calculations needed for these surfaces and stops when the posterior uncertainty of the coupling fluctuation σV falls below a target. For pentacene, 24–40 DFT dimers per pair reproduce σV within 4%, against 273 points for a quadratic fit. Chiral molecules in centrosymmetric crystals, such as mer-Alq3 and Ir(III) emitters, are treated by mirror-image fragments. The code is tested by 34 automated test scripts, including an exact-solution check of the kinetic Monte Carlo, and is archived on Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23593488).

papers.title: Portfolio Search with Precedent-Based Selection for Multi-Step Retrosynthesis
papers.abstract: Computer-aided synthesis planners propose routes from a target molecule back to purchasable starting materials, and they are usually compared by how often they find such a route. A route that reaches purchasable stock, however, often contains steps that have no precedent in the chemical literature and that a chemist would not run. We present P*, a planner that searches with a portfolio of complementary strategies and then keeps, for each target, the route whose every step has literature precedent. Each strategy pairs a reaction score with an estimate of how hard an intermediate is to make. The reaction scores are built from chemical heuristics, such as how common a transformation is and how many of its precursors are purchasable. We find that the strategies that reach stock most often produce the fewest precedented routes, because rewarding purchasable precursors favors multicomponent disconnections that are rarely reported. Different strategies therefore find different precedented routes, and together they find precedented routes for about twice as many development targets as the best single strategy. P* produces fully precedented routes for 61% of approved drugs and clinical candidates, 41% of novel expert-curated targets and 49% of USPTO-190 targets, more than any published planner on all three sets. It exceeds the strongest of them, and it improves route validity with every single-step model we tested. Its best single strategy is also an effective route finder and solves 88.0% of ChEMBL-1000 targets.

papers.title: Model-Kernel Corrected DIIS: Cheap Response Information for the Roothaan Step
papers.abstract: Nearly all Kohn–Sham density functional theory (DFT) and Hartree–Fock calculations solve the self-consistent field (SCF) equations with the direct inversion in the iterative subspace (DIIS). Their cost is set by the number of Fock builds that DIIS needs. Each DIIS cycle diagonalizes an extrapolated Fock matrix as if this matrix stayed fixed while the electrons move. The charge that the step moves, however, changes the Coulomb potential, and the next cycle has to undo part of the step. This charge sloshing makes DIIS slower as molecules grow. We correct every step with a model kernel, an inexpensive approximation of this Coulomb response that is built from a few Gaussian functions on each atom and contains no fitted parameters. The resulting method, MK-DIIS, needs no extra Fock build, converges to the same solution as DIIS and adds about 1% to the run time. On 170 transition-metal complexes and organic molecules it needs about one third fewer Fock builds than DIIS, fewer than any SCF algorithm of a production code that we compared with. On molecules with up to 300 atoms it needs about half as many, and on linear acenes its number of Fock builds does not grow with length. The saving is smaller with more exact exchange and in a continuum solvent, both of which screen the Coulomb response. For open-shell molecules, a delayed start keeps the reliability of DIIS. Because only the diagonalization step changes, the correction can be added to existing SCF codes and combined with other convergence aids.

papers.title: Sustainable Surface Metallurgy for Public Health: A Review of Barrier Degradation, Structural Heterogeneity, and Aluminum Leaching Dynamics in Low-Income Country Cookware
papers.abstract: Aluminum (Al) consumer cookware remains a cornerstone of global food preparation due to its exceptional thermal efficiency and low cost. However, in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), the widespread reliance on low-purity, informally recycled artisanal alloys creates severe public health risks due to heavy metal migration into dietary pathways. This review explicitly links materials engineering for sustainable development with global safety frameworks by evaluating surface modification technologies designed to mitigate aluminum ion leaching under aggressive thermal and chemical cooking conditions. This review systematically synthesizes the thermodynamic, kinetic, and mechanical performance of three dominant protective systems: electrochemical anodization, sol-gel quasi-ceramic matrices, and fluoropolymer barriers. The chemical stability of these systems is analyzed using mass transport models, chelation-assisted coordination mechanics, and the Arrhenius activation energy framework. Furthermore, a sequential technical characterization workflow is established—linking Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM-EDX), X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS), and Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry (ICP-MS)—to evaluate barrier performance against the strict specific migration limits (SML) enforced by the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) and the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA). While hard anodization and ceramic coatings offer excellent thermal stability, their long-term barrier performance is often compromised by interfacial shear stresses driven by mismatched coefficients of thermal expansion (CTE) and mechanical wear. This issue is particularly severe in informal metallurgical sectors. Artisanal castings feature high structural porosity and iron/copper micro-impurities that create localized galvanic micro-cells (Δ E > 1.0 V), accelerating the breakdown of surface oxide barriers and leading to heavy metal migration that routinely exceeds international safety standards by factors of 10 to 50. Critical commercial research gaps are identified, specifically the development of cost-effective, bio-based non-stick barriers (e.g., cross-linked green nanocomposites) and the implementation of decentralized circular economy scrap-sorting upgrades. Resolving these material vulnerabilities is essential for advancing UN Sustainable Development Goals related to good health and well-being (SDG 3), clean manufacturing (SDG 9), and responsible consumption and production (SDG 12). This work provides a clear roadmap for scalable, non-hazardous cookware manufacturing tailored for vulnerable populations.

papers.title: Accelerating characterization of conformational stability for biologics in Discovery space by combining SEC‑HDX‑MS with molecular modeling
papers.abstract: Conformational stability is a critical attribute for biologics discovery and manufacturability assessment, yet conventional approaches often require substantial material, extensive preparation, or lack sufficient structural resolution for early decision-making. Here, we present a native size-exclusion chromatography hydrogen–deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (SEC-HDX-MS) workflow integrated with molecular modeling to rapidly characterize conformational stability of therapeutic proteins in the discovery space. The workflow was evaluated across monoclonal antibody and bispecific antibody modalities. From a sequence variant comparison, SEC-HDX-MS showed that elevated aggregation did not uniformly reflect global conformational instability; instead, only one variant displayed increased deuterium incorporation, which modeling linked to an elongated, solvent-exposed CDR-H3 loop with increased hydrophobicity. In a representative proprietary mAb (“mAb X”), SEC-HDX-MS revealed that thermally-induced isoaspartate accumulation reduced conformational stability, whereas high-pH stress showed behavior comparable to controls despite higher overall deamidation. Molecular dynamics simulations explained this destabilization through disruption of a backbone Asn43–Ala40 hydrogen bond and altered local coordination after isoAsp formation. Finally, application to a complex bispecific antibody confirmed the workflow’s sensitivity for detecting conformational differences in more complex formats. Collectively, this integrated approach connects global HDX measurements with molecular-level interpretation, requires minimal preparation and limited material, and is compatible with partially purified samples. The workflow enables rapid conformational stability assessment to support candidate ranking, protein engineering, formulation development, and CMC risk assessment during biologics discovery.

papers.title: Removal of Cu(II) and a PET Glitter Microplastic Surrogate by Alginate, Alginate–Opuntia, and Chitosan-Treated Alginate–Opuntia Beads
papers.abstract: The use of alginate-only beads, alginate–Opuntia (AO) beads, and chitosan-treated AO beads for the removal of Cu(II) and a PET glitter (a microplastic surrogate) from water has been investigated. Each bead type was made from the previous one by the addition of one component. Batch experiments were carried out in water containing glitter, Cu(II), or both, and AO beads soaked in dilute acetic acid without chitosan served as a control for the acid. The removal of Cu(II) in copper-only water was 45.71 ± 1.97%, 59.44 ± 2.28%, and 84.19 ± 2.65% for the alginate-only, AO, and chitosan-treated beads, respectively (mean ± SD, n = 12, 6 h, 140 rpm). Opuntia increased the Cu(II) removal by 13.72 percentage points and chitosan by a further 24.75 points (paired t-test, p < 0.001 for both, and p ≤ 0.0013 for the batch means). In the presence of 2.00 g of glitter, the chitosan-treated beads still removed about 84% of the Cu(II). Meanwhile, the glitter removal increased by about 7 points with Opuntia but changed by less than 0.25 points with chitosan (p = 0.648 and 0.231). No significant difference was found between the acid-soaked and the untreated AO beads. It can be concluded that Opuntia was responsible for the increase in glitter capture and chitosan for most of the increase in Cu(II) removal.

papers.title: Heavy Metal-Binding Peptide Phytochelatin Drives Membraneless Compartmentalization and Biomineral-Like Structures via Nanoparticle Formation within Condensates
papers.abstract: Phytochelatin is a heavy metal-binding biogenic peptide found across different organisms that helps cells mitigate cytotoxicity by chelating metal ions. Yeasts produce phytochelatin to chelate intracellular cadmium and sequester it as cadmium metal sulfide nanoparticles. These nanoparticles were proposed to be stored within cytoplasmic microcompartments, although it remains unclear whether they are stored within membrane-bound or membraneless compartments. Here, we focused on the structure of phytochelatin and hypothesized that it can form membraneless compartments with positively charged biomolecules, which are capable of internal cadmium sulfide sequestration. Indeed, mixing phytochelatin with natural polysaccharide chitosan led to the instant formation of membraneless condensates. Moreover, Cd and S were preferentially accumulated within the condensates relative to other elements and CdS nanoparticles formed inside them. These nanoparticles exhibited crystalline features, with sizes of 2–3 nm and structures comparable to those of the CdS particles observed in cells, which predominantly correspond to the hawleyite structure. This study demonstrated that heavy metal-binding peptides can participate in the formation of membraneless compartments and internal sequestration of nanoparticles. Our findings further indicate a potential role of phytochelatin-based membraneless compartments in spatially controlled intracellular biomineralization and heavy metal sequestration for cellular detoxification, which remains to be explored in vivo.

papers.title: The Oxidation of Drug Molecules Using the Peroxygenase Activity of a Bacterial Family of Cytochrome P450 Enzymes
papers.abstract: Cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzymes with peroxygenase activity can use H2O2 as the sole oxidant which is beneficial for biocatalytic applications. We investigated the peroxygenase activity of CYP105D18 from Streptomyces laurentii. The modification of the acid-alcohol pair in the I-helix through protein engineering reduced the peroxygenase activity for papaverine oxidation by 6-fold compared to the wild-type (WT) enzyme. We identified the oxidation metabolites as papaverine N-oxide, and two newly identified metabolites that arise from O-demethylation. The major O-demethylation metabolite was characterized as 6-O-desmethyl papaverine. Given the higher peroxygenase activity of the unmodified CYP105D18 enzyme we explored if another enzyme from the same CYP subfamily had similar activity. We produced and purified CYP105D41 from Streptomyces thermoviolaceus and found that this enzyme also has significant peroxygenase activity. CYP105D41 could catalyze the oxidation of papaverine and diclofenac. For this enzyme the oxidation of diclofenac was the more efficient reaction and generated 4′-hydroxydiclofenac, 5-hydroxydiclofenac and a doubly hydroxylated metabolite. Overall, we demonstrate that two CYP105 enzymes are effective natural peroxygenase biocatalysts and could efficiently oxidize drug molecules to generate human drug metabolites. These drug molecules are also emerging contaminants, and their oxidation would facilitate their removal from or breakdown in the environment.

papers.title: Partial Pressure Modulation as a Method to Access Non-Equilibrium States in Heterogeneous Catalysis
papers.abstract: Under steady-state conditions, heterogeneous catalyst surfaces are often represented by thermodynamically favoured surface configurations defined by temperature and pressure. However, catalyst surfaces are inherently dynamic and can populate non-equilibrium states that differ from those expected based on the reaction environment. Herein, we show how partial pressure modulation can be utilised to sustain access to non-equilibrium states. Using CO oxidation over Pd/Al 2 O 3 as a model system, we demonstrate how oscillating the partial pressures of CO and O 2 drives the catalyst surface into a non-equilibrium state, accessing CO* coverages and reactivities unattainable under steady-state conditions. We find that accessing this state enhances catalytic rate up to three times above the steady-state maximum at a given temperature and induces activity under conditions where no steady-state activity can be recorded. Numerical simulations reproduce similar rate enhancements, demonstrating that accessing non-equilibrium states via dynamic operation can enhance activity without invoking catalyst reconstruction or alternative kinetic pathways. We conclude that the rate enhancement is directly related to disrupting the thermodynamically expected relationship between the gas and surface concentrations. More broadly, these findings suggest that dynamic reactor operation provides a powerful strategy for accessing non-equilibrium states and revealing otherwise inaccessible catalytic behaviour.

papers.title: Mitigating Catalyst Leaching and Deactivation in Heterogeneous Hydrogen-Bonding/Tertiary Amine Chiral Organocatalysts
papers.abstract: The heterogenisation of chiral organocatalysts remains a key strategy for developing sustainable and recyclable chemical processes. However, long-term stability is often compromised by catalyst leaching and deactivation. In this work, we present a combined computational and experimental study of the deactivation pathways in an ester-linked heterogeneous thiourea/tertiary amine organocatalyst. By identifying the fundamental causes of activity loss, we establish a rational design framework for developing a more robust, high-performance triazole-linked heterogeneous catalyst with extended lifetime and improved reusability.

papers.title: A Non-equilibrium Statistical Mechanics-Based Diffusion Theory: A Unified Model for Diffusion in Porous Media (II)
papers.abstract: Starting from the linear response theory of non-equilibrium statistical mechanics, this study establishes a unified model that comprehensively describes bulk diffusion, Knudsen diffusion, and interface diffusion. The diffusion process within porous media is decoupled into a bulk–Knudsen diffusion process and an interface diffusion process, and the flux expressions corresponding to each process are derived separately. The influence of the geometric structure and physicochemical properties of porous media on the Onsager phenomenological coefficients is analyzed, and the variation of the ratio of the chemical potential gradient to the concentration gradient is revealed. On this basis, the ratio of interface diffusion to bulk–Knudsen diffusion is derived and proposed as a criterion for the transition of diffusion mechanisms. The influence of the geometric structure and physicochemical properties of porous media on this criterion is further discussed. Finally, the relationships between this model and the classical theories are analyzed. The proposed model captures the constitutive relationship between the geometric structure and physicochemical properties of porous media and their diffusion capacity, providing a new theoretical paradigm for the construction of diffusion models in porous media.

papers.title: A New Perspective in Chemical Probe Discovery: Expanding Virtual Screening into Metal Complex Chemical Space
papers.abstract: Transition metal complexes provide rigid, shape-defined molecular architectures in which the coordination geometry precisely organizes ligand functionality in three dimensions, making them attractive scaffolds for target-based chemical probe discovery. Yet, their broader and prospective use in structure-based virtual screening has remained largely unexplored, due to the absence of structurally diverse, computationally tractable screening libraries. Here, we address this by curating MOSAIC (Metal complex library for Structure-Aided In silico screening), a first collection of 16,901 neutral, drug-like metal complexes assembled directly from experimentally determined geometries deposited in the Cambridge Structural Database. Using MOSAIC , we perform a high-throughput virtual screening campaign against the allosteric pocket of methionine adenosyltransferase 2A (MAT2A), identifying the copper complex Cu1-Complex , for which nano differential scanning fluorimetry (nanoDSF) confirmed strong binding in vitro . The diamagnetic zinc analogue Zn1-Comple x allowed orthogonal binding characterization with ligand-observed and competition NMR studies. Along with Hydrogen–deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS), site-directed mutagenesis and molecular dynamics (MD), these studies show that Zn1-Complex engages the MAT2A through an allosteric pocket, inhibiting enzymatic activity. Together, this establishes MOSAIC as a scalable and generalizable virtual screening platform for transition metal complexes and demonstrates the potential of these metal-based scaffolds as chemical probes to uncover new modes of protein recognition.

papers.title: Physicochemical and Structural Determinants of BACE1-Selective Inhibition: An Integrative Modeling Study using A Combined Ligand-and Structure-Based Approach
Post-Polymerization Editing of Polymer Tacticity
papers.abstract: The tacticity of polymers impacts their macroscopic properties. Methods to precisely 10 control polymer tacticity prior to or during polymerization are well known; however, postpolymerization editing of tacticity remains underexplored. Here, we report a strategy for visible light-driven polymer tacticity editing through continuous C–H exchange at stereogenic sites along the polymer backbone. This approach can transform isotactic polymers into a library of products with varying tacticities and can provide access to stereoenriched polymers from atactic starting 15 materials. Spatiotemporal control over tacticity editing enabled the patterning of heterogeneous mechanical responses within a compositionally uniform material. This platform establishes postpolymerization tacticity editing as a complementary paradigm to stereocontrolled polymerization that provides access to stereoenriched and stereopatterned materials that are challenging to access through conventional synthetic routes.

papers.title: Phase-Controlled Synthesis and Low Thermal Conductivity in Cu <sub>4</sub> TiTe <sub>4</sub>
papers.abstract: The synthesis of phase-pure Cu-based multinary tellurides remains challenging due to the competitive formation of stable Cu–Te binary phases, which frequently intercept the reaction pathway as secondary products. In the Cu 4 TiTe 4 system, rapid synthesis temperature mapping reveals the synthesis window, whereas precise compositional control suppresses secondary Cu–Te binaries to unlock non-equilibrium phase selection. We demonstrate that addition of 2 wt% excess Ti shifts the reaction chemistry toward Cu 4 TiTe 4 , suppressing detectable Cu–Te secondary phases and yielding phase-pure Cu 4 TiTe 4 over the identified 623–873 K synthesis window. Cu 4 TiTe 4 crystallises in a ‘stuffed sulvanite’ type structure, similar to Cu 4 TiSe 4 , and exhibits an order–disorder phase transition, in which partial ordering of the Cu sublattice induces structural transformation primarily governed by Cu sublattice ordering. Bulk Cu 4 TiTe 4 is a p-type narrow bandgap semiconductor that achieves a low lattice thermal conductivity of 0.63 to 0.68 W m -1 K -1 between 300 and 423 K. Transport calculations attribute the low observed thermal conductivity to Cu-sublattice disorder, local symmetry breaking, and localized Ti-dominated vibrations that collectively suppress phonon transport.

papers.title: A Refined cDICE Platform for the Controlled Production of Lipid Giant Unilamellar Vesicles
papers.abstract: Continuous Droplet Interface Crossing Encapsulation (cDICE) is well known to be an effective alternative to the manual reverse emulsion method to produce giant unilamellar vesicles (GUV). It provides high encapsulation efficiency and enhanced user control over process variables, comparable to that offered by microfluidic approaches, without involving extensive infrastructure requirements such as clean rooms or lithography. The cDICE method can be challenging to implement because its performance depends on the precise configuration of the experimental setup and careful adherence to protocol details that are easily overlooked. The aim of this paper is to provide a practical, comprehensive, step-by-step guide to operating an improved cDICE system, covering the design of the rotating chamber through to the extraction of the resulting GUVs. This paper will also quantify the influence of ambient humidity, an often-mentioned factor in vesicle generation, and compare small molecule encapsulation efficiency and vesicle size characteristics with the manual reverse emulsion phase transfer method. The often overlooked influence of sonicator choice for lipid oil solution preparation will be examined, highlighting the downstream effects that the pre-cDICE preparation steps can have on the overall effectiveness of the vesicle generation technique demonstrate the applicability of the improved cDICE set up to synthetic-cell research, a protocol is presented for producing GUVs, containing a cell-free protein synthesis system that expresses eGFP. GUVs containing cell-free expression systems are widely used as model synthetic cells because they provide a membrane-bound compartment in which genetic constructs can be expressed and studied under controlled conditions.

papers.title: Sonochemical synthesis of imine- and aminal-linked porous organic polymers for efficient CO2 separation
papers.abstract: The practical deployment of porous organic polymers (POPs) in gas separation applications remains challenging, in large part due to the limited scalability and time-consuming nature of conventional solvothermal synthesis. Herein, we report a facile and scalable sonochemical approach for the synthesis of POPs from cost-effective monomers. The resulting materials exhibit high BET surface areas of up to 664 m2/g and good CO2 separation performance for both CO2/N2 and CO2/CH4 mixtures. Scale-up to multigram quantities was achieved with a space-time yield more than 50-fold higher than that of conventional solvothermal synthesis. This study therefore provides a time-efficient and scalable synthetic strategy for highly porous POPs for gas separation.

papers.title: PLANTMETBENCH: A MULTIMODAL KNOWLEDGE GRAPH BENCHMARK FOR BIOSYNTHESIS PREDICTION
papers.abstract: Plant metabolism produces a vast diversity of molecules, yet identifying the enzymes that catalyse biosynthetic reactions remains a major open problem. Existing benchmarks typically reduce this problem to isolated enzyme–reaction pairs, overlooking pathway and metabolite context that determines biological plausibility, leaving no standardised way to evaluate approaches that exploit this richer multimodal and relational structure. We present PlantMetBench, a multimodal graph benchmark built on PlantMetWiki, a curated knowledge graph of plant metabolism spanning 424 organisms. The resulting benchmark graph comprises 13,682 proteins, 2,741 genes, 4,577 metabolites, and 11,980 experimentally curated enzyme–reaction pairs. PlantMetBench frames enzyme–reaction prediction as an organism-disjoint link-prediction task and provides graph-native dataset splits, precomputed multi-modal node features, and evaluation protocols. Using PlantMetBench, we evaluate heterogeneous graph neural networks, standard architectures (HeteroSAGE, GAT, HGT, and R-GCN), alongside residual and jumping-knowledge variants, against non-graph models. Most heterogeneous graph architectures consistently outperform non-graph baselines on our rank-based evaluation, suggesting the value of relational context for enzyme–reaction prediction. Yet, performance remains far from saturated, indicating substantial room for improved representations and modelling strategies. Also, we show that benchmark design choices (shortcuts, splits, and metrics) are key to aligning evaluation with biologically meaningful tasks. PlantMetBench provides a standardised, reproducible framework to evaluate multimodal biosynthetic data, establishing a foundation for future work on graph-based architectures for enzyme–reaction prediction. Code and data are publicly available.

papers.title: Spectro-Electrochemical Decoding of Metals, Alloys, and Buried Interfaces
papers.abstract: Metal-electrolyte interfaces govern corrosion, catalysis, energy-conversion and storage technologies, yet resolving their chemical evolution under operating conditions remains challenging. Electrochemical measurements report an integrated response, while post-mortem characterization can lose the transient sequence and spatial distribution of dissolved species. Here, we introduce the In-Situ Corrosion Monitoring Technique (ICMT), an operando spectro-electrochemical platform that converts interfacial metal dissolution into spatially and temporally resolved optical concentration fields. Under an applied bias, dissolution products migrate through a transparent gel electrolyte that suppresses convection and restricts mixing, thereby retaining dissolved species for interrogation by UV-visible spectroscopy. Using Cu and Ni as model systems, ICMT establishes element-specific absorption fingerprints and distinguishes active Ni dissolution from passivation-influenced Cu corrosion while enabling estimation of recession rates and apparent transport coefficients. Applied to Cu-coated Ni, ICMT sequentially detects Cu and Ni-associated species, revealing degradation from the outer coating to the buried substrate and detecting dissolution from a Cu overlayer as thin as 100 nm. Applied to a Cu-Zn-Ni ternary alloy, the platform resolves constituent-specific dissolution signatures that remain convoluted within the total electrochemical current. Collectively, ICMT provides a simple and accessible benchtop approach for determining how material interface evolves, which constituent dissolves and from which layer it arises, while preserving the transient chemical history of electrochemical interfaces.

papers.title: In-Situ Corrosion Monitoring via Gel-Confined Operando Spectro-Electrochemistry
papers.abstract: Corrosion causes trillions of dollars in economic loss annually, yet real-time observation of interfacial alloy dissolution remains challenging due to rapid convective mixing, dynamic pH gradients, and post-dissolution side reactions. Here, we present in-situ corrosion monitoring technique (ICMT), a simple spectro-electrochemical approach that transforms buried interfacial corrosion into directly observable optical signals. By confining ionic transport within a transparent, ion-conductive gelatin gel, ICMT suppresses convection while stabilizing dissolved metal species, enabling real-time UV–Vis spectral resolution of Fe, Ni, and Cr dissolution kinetics. Diagnostic absorption features are identified for distinct metal-ion species, with corrosion rates from 0.14 to 14.4 nm s-1 across nearly two orders of magnitude in dissolution flux. By establishing a direct link between Faradaic dissolution, mass transport, and chemical speciation, this platform provides a generalizable framework for operando interrogation of dynamic metal–electrolyte interfaces.

papers.title: Is characterization worth the cost in data-driven catalyst discovery?
papers.abstract: New catalysts are often discovered by trial and error, a search in which most candidates fail. Machine learning now shortens that search by predicting how untested formulations perform from composition alone. Measuring the physicochemical properties that govern performance should shorten it further, yet this expectation remains untested in a discovery campaign. We tested it on Pt-based propane dehydrogenation catalysts, evaluating discovery speed, prediction accuracy, and physical insight on the same materials. Here we show that measured properties neither accelerate the search nor improve predictions beyond composition alone. However, they resolve deactivation into separable contributions from exposed platinum and surface acidity. These results explain why brute-force screening dominates industry and define, in catalysis and beyond, when to characterize a material rather than test the next one.

papers.title: Self-Driving Microscopy with Agents: Progress and Prospects
papers.abstract: Agentic AI, powered by large language models, has increasingly been applied within self-driving laboratories and here we review its emerging role in self-driving microscopy. Microscopy is an unusually demanding target as each experiment is a sequence of interdependent decisions about where to measure, at what resolution, through which modality, and often on ambiguous evidence. We review recent demonstrations across atomic force, scanning tunneling, and transmission electron microscopy and examine how agentic systems can lower the expertise barrier to advanced characterization, transfer strategies between platforms, mine laboratory records for reusable protocols, generate and screen hypotheses, and bring simulation into the experimental loop. We also highlight and examine the limitations that currently constrain these systems. Agents can lose track of the scientific goal as a session outgrows their context window. They also remain poor judges of their own competence, making failure particularly difficult to anticipate in open-ended research. Flexible reasoning must therefore sit on deterministic, physically constrained control, with safety limits enforced outside the model. Human oversight can be the safeguard, but a human acting only as an approval or rejection gate risks forfeiting what scientists contribute most — questioning how the problem was framed in the first place. Designing agentic systems that preserve that contribution and address the current limitations is, in our view, the defining challenge for the field.

papers.title: Phase transitions in multicomponent systems relevant to atmospheric new particle formation
papers.abstract: Typically, molecular clusters containing sulfuric acid, water, ammonia, and/or amines initiate particle nucleation, followed by particle growth through condensation of highly oxidized organic molecules. The coexistence of multiple organic and inorganic components in these particles can lead to variations in morphology and phase state. In this study, optical and Raman microscopy were used to study multicomponent model aerosol particles representative of new particle formation and growth. We focused on 2-methylglutaric acid, sulfuric acid, and ammonium sulfate systems with different amines; and dipropylamine, sulfuric acid, and ammonium sulfate systems with various dicarboxylic acids. Liquid-liquid phase separation occurred in many systems, while amine functionality and molecular structure affect morphology and phase state. Systems containing dipropylamine along with sulfuric acid underwent liquid-liquid phase separation in several mixtures that remained homogeneous in its absence. These particles formed an inorganic-rich core surrounded by an organic-rich shell containing both the dicarboxylic acid and dipropylamine, with slight dipropylamine enrichment at the air-water interface. Their deliquescence relative humidity was generally the same or lower, while efflorescence relative humidity was similar to the corresponding dicarboxylic acid/ammonium sulfate systems. These results demonstrate that the chemical identity of atmospheric amines and overall compound activity should be considered when predicting the phase state, morphology, and water uptake of newly formed particles, which is important for their heterogeneous chemistry and cloud droplet formation.

papers.title: Nucleotides trigger the spontaneous emergence of hierarchical nanolamellar architectures in coacervate-like polyelectrolyte multilayers
papers.abstract: Spontaneous generation of hierarchical order over multiple length scales remains a major challenge in soft materials because it typically relies on external patterning or multistep fabrication strategies. Here we show that a coacervate-like, exponentially growing poly(L-lysine)/hyaluronic acid (PLL/HA) multilayer autonomously reorganizes into a hierarchical architecture following simple exposure to ATP under aqueous conditions. Within minutes, the initially homogeneous film evolves into a sponge-like network of micrometer-sized cavities separated by thin walls containing PLL, HA and ATP. Cryogenic scanning electron microscopy and small-angle X-ray scattering independently reveal that these walls possess a short-range one-dimensional lamellar paracrystalline organization, demonstrating the emergence of structural order at both the micro- and nanoscales. The extent of this reorganization depends on the ATP concentration: 2 mM concentration of ATP produces a stable hierarchical morphology, whereas high ATP concentration drives complete film dissolution. Comparison with guanosine and uridine triphosphate (GTP and UTP) demonstrates that the self-organization process depends on the chemical nature of the nucleobase since, under exactly the same conditions, only ATP and GTP lead to a mesostructured formation. All our observations are consistent with a mechanistic framework in which a suitable nucleotide, i.e. ATP or GTP, progressively remodels the coacervate-like network, leading to an internal phase separation that may evolve into a lamellar structure through a surface-directed process. More broadly, this work identifies hydrated polyelectrolyte assemblies such as exponentially growing polyelectrolyte films, as a simple experimental platform in which diffusion-driven compositional changes can generate hierarchical periodic micro- and nanostructures without external templating.

papers.title: Reactive dye adsorption and recovery using a PVA/TiO2 film containing Saccharum spontaneum flower-fibre cellulose: kinetic model discrimination beyond pseudo-second-order
papers.abstract: Reactive dyes are difficult to remove from textile effluent, and adsorbents made from discarded plant fibres offer a low-cost option. Cellulose microcrystals were isolated from the flower fibre ofSaccharum spontaneum (catkin) and incorporated with TiO2 nanoparticles into a citric acid-crosslinked poly(vinyl alcohol) film prepared by solution casting. The film was characterized by FTIR, XRD, particle size analysis, FE-SEM with EDX, DSC, swelling, tensile and color measurements. In batch tests with the anionic reactive dye Avitera Light Red SE, 0.5 g of film in 50 mL removed 37 to 41 % of the dye at 20 to 60 mg L−1 after 170 min. The kinetic and equilibrium data were analyzed by nonlinear model discrimination over eleven rate laws and three isotherms, with leave-oneout validation and propagation of calibration uncertainty. Fast initial uptake followed by slow intraparticle diffusion described the kinetics best (Akaike weight 0.77), and pseudo-second-order kinetics received little support once the definitional origin point was excluded from the fit. Equilibrium uptake followed a near-linear Freundlich isotherm (1/n = 1.21, 95 % profile interval 1.06 to 1.38) with no saturation in the tested range. A preregistered simulation of 95,000 synthetic kinetic experiments showed that the eight-point sampling design identifies single-rate laws reliably but cannot fix the form of a slow second phase, and that a physics-informed neural network did not improve on the classical description at this data density. Adsorbed dye was released by heating the film in water at 80 °C, and the film could be reused.

papers.title: Small-data pH-resolved kernel modelling of flotation collectors
papers.abstract: Small, heterogeneous datasets are common in chemometrics, yet their predictive ceiling is rarely quantified. We assembled 19 flotation collectors from 15 literature sources (116 pH-resolved recovery points) and asked how much of the label, curve maximum and full pH curve can be predicted from molecular descriptors. The model combines DFT, Mordred and local descriptors in an additive molecule/pH kernel with a target branch for the label and maximum and a shape branch for the normalized curve. Whole-molecule leave-one-out gave label R2=0.821 (RMSE 7.79 pp), maximum R2=0.801 (8.07 pp) and full-curve R2=0.635 (19.59 pp). The pooled curve value is misleading: the per-molecule median R2 was 0.138 and the minimum −114.9, and correcting the M04/M13 structures did not rescue these failures. A post hoc source-group test (pooled R2=0.549) and six held-out congeners (R2=0.110; MAE 26.7 pp) further limited the claim. The model can rank training-like collectors, but it cannot certify a new molecule, a new source or a full curve. The study shows why pooled R2 and random splits are insufficient for small chemometric datasets, and provides a benchmark and validation protocol for more honest claims.

papers.title: Sustainable and Scalable Electrochemical Decarboxylative Cyanation of an Amino Acid Using KCN as Both Cyanide Source and Base
papers.abstract: Organic nitriles are an important class of compounds found in pharmaceuticals and agrochemicals, as well as useful intermediates in synthesis. Decarboxylative cyanation as a method to generate nitriles enables the use of widely available carboxylic acids as starting materials. Although this method has been well-explored synthetically, current methodologies often feature poor atom economy or require harsh reaction conditions. Herein, an electrochemical method for the decarboxylative cyanation of Cbz-protected alanine that uses inexpensive KCN as the cyanide source has been developed. The operationally simple procedure only requires electrolyzing a mixture of the amino acid with the cyanide in DMSO/EtOH as the solvent, without any additional chemicals such as base or supporting electrolyte, resulting in excellent green chemistry metrics. Using inexpensive graphite and stainless-steel as electrodes, excellent conversion and selectivity towards the desired nitrile product were obtained. Translation of the process to a flow electrolysis cell confirmed that the electrochemical protocol is scalable. Thus, gram amounts of material were obtained in a parallel plate reactor, with a space-time yield of 1026 g L-1 h-1. The space-time yield in the flow system was ca. 70 times larger than its batch counterpart, confirming the suitability of flow electrolysis cells for scale-up purposes.

papers.title: Autonomous Experimentation Enables Rapid Optimization of Photochemical Continuous-Flow Synthesis of Diazaxanthilidene Fluorophores
papers.abstract: Photoconvertible diazaxanthilidene dyes enable optical labeling and tracking in live cells, but the batch photocyclization that generates them requires days of irradiation and analog-specific optimization. Here we report a closed-loop continuous-flow platform that uses Bayesian optimization to tune light intensity, temperature, flow rate, and concentration. In campaigns on the parent diazaxanthilidene and four analogs, the platform improved throughput for four of five compounds. For the parent diazaxanthilidene, photoconversion yield rose from approximately 69% in batch to 79%, while throughput increased from 0.52 to 87 nmol min-1. The platform autonomously performs >40 optimization experiments to turn a multiday, analog-specific batch synthesis into a same-day flow synthesis.

papers.title: Method for Measuring Solid-State Diffusivity: Part 1. Theoretical Introduction
papers.abstract: The reliable determination of solid-state lithium diffusivity is essential for parameterizing physics-based lithium-ion battery models. However, conventional methods misattribute electrolyte concentration polarization to solid-state diffusion, introducing systematic errors in the inferred diffusivity. This study introduces a resistance-decomposition method that explicitly accounts for electronic conduction, electrolyte transport, charge transfer, and solid-state diffusion within the Doyle–Fuller–Newman (DFN) framework. The diffusion coefficient is calculated from the residual polarization resistance after independently determining the other contributions and accounting for the equilibrium potential dependence on the state of lithiation. The method is evaluated using synthetic voltage data generated with the DFN model implemented in PyBaMM. The results demonstrate accurate recovery of the prescribed diffusivity across most of the investigated parameter space under idealized conditions.. These findings establish the theoretical basis and numerical feasibility of the proposed method while identifying key limitations that require experimental validation.

papers.title: HRnSiH3: A Radon Hydride with Near-Zero Dissociation Energy, Benchmarked Against HRnF
papers.abstract: HRnSiH3 is a genuine minimum on the PBE0/ZORA potential energy surface, but at coupled-cluster level it is not meaningfully bound against loss of its atoms. We optimised the C3v structure (H–Rn 2.008 Å, Rn–Si 2.876 Å; all harmonic frequencies real) and computed dissociation energies with a CCSD(T)/def2-TZVP plus MP2(QZ–TZ) composite, using a 60-electron effective core potential on Rn, with counterpoise and zero-point corrections. For HRnSiH3 → Rn + H + SiH3 the result is +1 kcal/mol, with an es mated uncertainty of ±3 kcal/mol, so the molecule is thermoneutral against radical fragmentation. The control molecule HRnF, computed identically, is bound by about 51 kcal/mol against Rn + H + F. Both molecules lie 84–90 kcal/mol above Rn + HX, so metastability toward HX loss is shared and does not separate them. The silyl group therefore does not support the H–Rn bond that stabilises known radon hydrides, and HRnSiH3 could at best be a matrix-isolation target. Spin–orbit coupling and the complete-basis-set limit are not included.

papers.title: MATCHERS: a ‘chemistry-infused’ representation bridging molecular graphs and strings
papers.abstract: Molecular graphs and molecular strings are two well-established molecular representations for deep learning, with complementary strengths: while graphs make atom and bond properties explicit, strings are sequential and straightforward to generate. Here, we introduce a novel molecular representation than bridges these two representations: Multichannel Atom and Topology for Chemical Representation Series (MATCHERS). In a single representation, MATCHERS encode user-defined atomic properties, explicit molecular topology, as well as bond properties, while maintaining the sequential character typical of molecular strings. In this proof-of-concept, we show that MATCHERS outperform sequential string representations (SMILES and SELFIES) for bioactivity prediction, and that they can be used for de novo molecular design. MATCHERS illustrate the untapped opportunity of explicitly encoding chemical knowledge into new molecular representations that remain compatible with deep learning.

papers.title: Deuteration favours the polymorph with shorter O-H bonds: a stretch-bend rule tested across 220 inorganic polymorph pairs
papers.abstract: Deuteration can change which polymorph of a hydrogen-bonded crystal is stable. We derive a rule for the direction and size of this effect and test it across compounds. The H/D free-energy difference between two polymorphs is, to first order, ΔΔF ≈ S_str(1 − C)Δr̄, where Δr̄ is the difference in mean O-H length, S_str ≈ ½hc(1 − 1/ρ)s at room temperature comes from the softening s of the O-H stretch with bond length, and C is the fraction of the stretch term cancelled by bend and libration. While C < 1, deuteration favours the polymorph with the shorter O-H bonds, that is, with the weaker hydrogen bonds; where C(T) crosses unity the preference reverses. In harmonic calculations with three universal machine-learned potentials on 220 inorganic polymorph pairs, ΔΔF rises by 0.11 to 0.13 meV per H per mÅ at 300 K, with C about one half. For moderate to strong hydrogen bonds (a boundary chosen after inspecting the data) the rule is right in 74 of 84 pairs and 27 of 28 formulas; the exceptions share one Al(OH)₃ structure in which bend and libration outweigh the stretch at room temperature (C > 1 in two of the three models). The rule fails for weak hydrogen bonds and did not transfer in a prospective test on new pairs. Exploratory quasi-harmonic calculations put the diaspore to δ-AlOOH transition about 1 GPa higher for AlOOD than for AlOOH, a shift that high-pressure experiments can test.

papers.title: Achieving Stimuli-responsive Spin-state Switching in Potassiuminserted Molecular Replica of Prussian Blue
papers.abstract: Diving into the age-old three-dimensional Prussian blue network, we opted for a “complex-as-a-ligand” strategy to design and synthesise a soluble molecular replica of alkali-inserted Fe8 cube, {K ⊂ [FeIIILS(Ttp)(CN)3]4[FeIILS(POPy3)]4}2.(BF4)9.[FeIIILS(Ttp)(CN)3], referred to as K⊂Fe8. This mixed-valence cyanide-bridged molecular cube, hosting a potassium cation, was structurally characterised by temperature-dependent X-ray diffraction. Insertion of the potassium cation and its strong interaction with the cyanide bridges impart additional stability to the cationic cubic motif. Magnetic measurements on the crystal in mother liquor suggest thermally induced spin state switching, partially converting the {FeIIILS−CN−FeIILS} pairs into {FeIIILS−CN−FeIIHS} pairs, a feature that is lesser-known for alkali-inserted molecular Prussian blue so far. Additionally, K⊂Fe8 displays a reversible photoinduced LIESST effect under light irradiation (ON: 808 nm laser light and OFF: 532 nm laser light), confirmed by (photo)magnetic measurements. The photoinduced metastable state relaxes back to the ground state at 50 K (TLIESST = 50 K). Temperature-dependent Mössbauer spectroscopy further confirms the thermo-induced switching of {FeIIILS−CN-FeIILS}  {FeIIILS−CN-FeIIHS} pairs.

papers.title: Living cells reshape dynamic covalent chemical space via selective intracellular disulfide exchange
papers.abstract: Dynamic covalent chemistry (DCC) enables adaptive molecular systems, yet whether dynamic covalent networks can operate selectively inside living cells remains largely unknown. Here we show that living cells reshape dynamic covalent chemical space through selective intracellular disulfide exchange. A disulfide-based dynamic combinatorial library (DCL), previously characterized in vitro, undergoes cysteine-directed redistribution in cellular lysates and intact living cells. Fluorescence spectroscopy and live-cell ratiometric imaging reveal functional network reorganization, whereas UPLC–ESI-MS identifies specific species that provide orthogonal consistency with the optical response, including enrichment of a cysteine-containing heterotrimer and a fluorescent homodimer. Notably, this redistribution occurs despite millimolar glutathione and other competing intracellular thiols. These results establish living cells as chemically selective environments capable of biasing dynamic covalent networks, expanding DCC into functional intracellular contexts and providing a framework for target-guided molecular selection in situ.

papers.title: Where to Site Direct Air Capture? Optimal Global Supply Chains from Capture to Storage
papers.abstract: The cost and net removal efficiency of direct air capture with CO2 storage (DACCS) depend strongly on siting, power supply, and how captured CO2 reaches storage. Here, we present a globally resolved (1° × 1°) assessment of solid-sorbent DACCS supply chains for near-term and mid-century scenarios, coupling hourly techno-economic optimization, (prospective) life-cycle assessment, and multimodal CO2 transport to storage to estimate net levelized costs of carbon dioxide removal that account for cradle-to-grave greenhouse gas emissions. In the near-term, the cheapest sites require ∼1,100–1,200 USD/tCO2 in the central United States and western Australia; cost is governed less by CO2 capture than by access to CO2 transport and storage and the regional cost of capital, while local wind resources enable the cheapest sites. A siting hierarchy emerges: proximity to geological storage is preferred, and a well-connected port is a near-equivalent substitute where storage is distant. By 2050, a lower-carbon global economy, cheaper CO2 transport, and technological learning broaden low-cost deployment, with ∼98% of sites below 1,000 USD/tCO2 (cheapest ∼370) at a median ∼93% removal efficiency. Near-term first-mover regions remain the lowest in cost, indicating low risk of stranded assets.

papers.title: Stereochemical and electronic complementarity drives both arene and facial selectivity for carbohydrate CH–π Interactions
papers.abstract: CH-π interactions between a sugar and an aromatic amino acid play an important role in carbohydrate recognition by proteins. Glycoconjugate model systems have been instructive in highlighting the importance of electronic and dispersive effects in driving carbohydrate-arene association in aqueous solution. These interactions have been probed using NMR, leveraging ring current-induced magnetic fields in arenes to effect chemical shift perturbations (CSPs) in select glycoside proton resonances upon association with aromatic rings. In this work tryptophol and phenethyl alcohol were identified as improved aromatic surrogates that overcome previous solubility limitations and allow a greater dynamic range of shift perturbations to be observed and interpreted. Armed with these aromatic probes, we examined the CSPs of a panel of methyl glycosides of biological and configurational interest to identify CH-p interaction preferences for common pyranosides. We identified clear trends that correlate the strength of the CH-π interactions with the identity of both the carbohydrate and arene. Indole and phenyl rings exhibit variations in the affinity and selectivity of their CH-π interactions, highlighting different components of the CH-π interaction driving carbohydrate-arene contacts. Our results underscore the interplay of stereoelectronic effects, arene electron density, and dispersion forces on the facial selectivity and arene interaction preferences in the carbohydrate CH-π interaction. This work highlights the role of carbohydrate conformation and the importance of carbohydrate-aromatic interfacial complementarity for effective CH-π interactions in water.

papers.title: Beyond Candidate Generation: A Validation-First Protocol for AI-Assisted Transition-State Discovery
papers.abstract: Machine-learned models can now propose three-dimensional transition-state (TS) geometries in seconds, but a candidate geometry is not a validated TS. The gap between a plausible structure and a mechanistically meaningful barrier—one imaginary frequency, the intended atom pair, the correct connectivity, and a consistent electronic state—remains the bottleneck in AI-assisted computational chemistry. We present a validation-first protocol that separates candidate generation from physical validation. The protocol combines (i) a chemical preflight that fixes reactive pairs, spin surfaces, connectivity, and conformers; (ii) a per-point independent scan that localizes the barrier without fragile collective scans; (iii) a constrained reference calculation that produces the Hessian; (iv) an OptTS stage that reuses that Hessian; and (v) a validation stage based on imaginary-mode localization, key bond lengths, IRC endpoints, spin diagnostics, and energy-convention checks. The protocol is implemented as a portable, open-source skill package for local ORCA/xtb and Gaussian/Slurm execution. Case studies from Ni/Fe catalysis illustrate the failure modes the protocol is designed to catch: a generative model produced candidates with 3.6–4.4 Å heavy-atom RMSD for an 84-atom broken-symmetry organometallic system, a collective scan failed three times where a per-point strategy completed 16/16 points, and a single-conformer R/S comparison would have misread a conformerdominated difference. The reported gains of multi-sampling and conformer enumeration are taken from the published benchmark, not measured here. We argue that the near-term role of AI is not to replace electronic-structure judgment but to shrink the search space before it and to make the validation layer reproducible.

papers.title: Metal Centered Cleavage of E≡E Bonds (E = Si, Ge): The Mononuclear Rhodium Bis(Tetrylidyne) Complexes [Rh(≡ER) <sub>2</sub> (PMe <sub>3</sub> ) <sub>2</sub> ] <sup>+</sup>
papers.abstract: Mononuclear bis(carbyne) complexes featuring two multiply bonded carbyne ligands at a single metal center, are an exceptionally rare class of organometallic compounds. Despite considerable advances in multiple bonding involving heavier group 14 elements, the synthesis of their heavier congeners, bis(tetrylidyne) complexes [L n M(ER) 2 ] (E = Si–Pb), remains extremely challenging owing to the lack of suitable synthetic strategies. Herein we report experimental and theoretical studies of the Rhodium bis(tetrylidyne) complex salts [Rh(ETbb) 2 (PMe 3 ) 2 ][B(Ar F ) 4 ] ( [2-E][B(Ar F ) 4 ] ; E = Si, Ge; Tbb = C 6 H 2 -4- t Bu-2,6-(CH(SiMe 3 ) 2 ) 2 ; Ar F = C 6 H 3 -3,5-(CF 3 ) 2 ). The complexes [2-E][B(Ar F ) 4 ] were obtained by chloride abstraction of the tetrylidyne-chlorotetrylidene complexes [Rh(ETbb)(EClTbb)(PMe 3 ) 2 ] ( 1-E ) with Na[B(Ar F ) 4 ]. Complexes 1-E were prepared by a E≡E triple bond cleavage reaction of the ditetrylynes E 2 (Tbb) 2 with [RhCl(PMe 3 ) 2 ] 2 . The molecular structures of [2-E] + feature two almost linearly coordinated tetrel centers, that are bonded to the Rh center via two very short Rh−E bonds (Rh−Si1 = 2.1310(7) Å, Rh−Si2 = 2.1240(7) Å; Rh−Ge1 = 2.2093(2) Å, Rh−Ge2 = 2.1976(2) Å). The electronic structure calculations in combination with the assessment of the thermochemical properties corroborate the presence of two highly polar Rh≡E triple bonds in [2-E][B(Ar F ) 4 ] . Cyclic voltammetric studies show a reversible electrochemical oxidation and reduction of the cations [2-E] + . The electrophilic character of the tetrel center is reflected in the reactions of [2-E][B(Ar F ) 4 ] ] with LiMe yielding the tetrylidyne-methyltetrylidene complexes [Rh(ETbb)(EMeTbb)(PMe 3 ) 2 ] ( 5-E ).

papers.title: Extraction and Analysis of Aroma Components from Four Types of Citrus Peels
papers.abstract: The peels of citrus fruits are a valuable source of natural fragrances. However, due to extraction difficulties and the complexity of their chemical components, these natural fragrances are relatively rarely applied in skincare products. In this study, essential oils from the peels of four citrus varieties—Pomelo, Shatang Mandarin, Baba Mandarin, and Sweet Orange—were successfully extracted using steam distillation to investigate their characteristic aroma components. The chemical structures of these volatile organic compounds were identified and comparatively analyzed using Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (GC-MS). By examining structural features, the relationships between the molecular structures of the aroma compounds and their specific scents were discussed. GC-MS analysis revealed that the content of D-limonene in Shatang Mandarin peel essential oil reached up to 82.3%, whereas in Pomelo peel essential oil, it was only 57.5%. Conversely, the content of γ-terpinene in Pomelo oil was unexpectedly high at 13.2%. Furthermore, the Pomelo peel extract contained unique components such as δ-elemene, germacrene D, and nootkatone, which are sesquiterpenes and sesquiterpene ketones. Because these components possess cyclic structures and relatively large molecular weights, their volatility is reduced, endowing the Pomelo essential oil with a much more long-lasting aroma. Finally, these natural organic fragrances were incorporated into homemade cleansing mousses, and user acceptance was evaluated through a questionnaire. Results indicated that Pomelo peel extract achieved the highest public acceptance due to its pure, fresh, and richly layered scent, making it the optimal natural fragrance ingredient for skincare.

papers.title: Interplay of Aromaticity and Coulomb Repulsion in the Electronic Structure of a Dimeric Pentafulvalene Upon Multi-Electron Uptake
papers.abstract: Multielectron reduction of finite one-dimensional (1D) π-conjugated hydrocarbons remains poorly understood because such frameworks are usually unstable due to charge accumulation in the absence of electron-withdrawing substituents. Here, we investigate the reduction of dibenzopentafulvalene dimers ([2]DBFs), a rare class of quasi-1D conjugated hydrocarbons that exhibit unusual stability toward multi-electron reduction and contain four indenylidene subunits that can each become aromatic upon reduction, raising the question of where the excess electrons reside. Chemical reduction of [2]DBFs with alkali metal-based reductants afforded dianionic and tetraanionic species, which were characterized by electronic absorption spectroscopy, NMR spectroscopy, single-crystal X-ray diffraction, and complementary quantum chemical calculations. The dianions accommodate excess negative charge at the outer indenylidene subunits, where Coulomb repulsion is minimized by charge separation while gaining 10π Hückel aromaticity. In contrast, upon four-electron reduction, all four indenylidene subunits become aromatic, and the excess charge becomes more broadly distributed and can extend to the end-capping phenyl groups even at the expense of the aromatic character of the end-capping benzene rings. The solid-state structures further reveal that the observed charge distributions are strongly influenced by the spatial arrangement of counter cations. These results identify local aromatization, Coulomb repulsion, and countercation position as competing factors that determine where electrons reside in multiply charged finite 1D π-conjugated hydrocarbons.

papers.title: Bath-to-System Timescale Dependence of Bloch−Redfield−HEOM Corrections in a DASA Photoswitch
papers.abstract: Solvent effects on donor−acceptor Stenhouse adducts (DASAs) involve both changes in electronic structure and changes in the timescale of environmental response. Here, solvent-dependent vertical excitations are characterized using linear-response and state-specific TD-DFT continuum-solvation calculations while the early photodynamics are examined separately with an independently specified reduced two-state open-quantum-system model. The two analyses share the same solvent set, but the calculated excitation energies do not determine the effective coupling, energetic bias, or bath reorganization parameter used in the dynamical model. Across the five solvents, the LR and nonequilibrium state-specific descriptions differ by approximately 38−43 nm for the S1 transition, whereas the solvent-to-solvent variation within the state-specific results spans only about 9.35 nm. Solvent-derived longitudinal relaxation rates are then used to define the bath timescale of a Drude−Lorentz environment, and matched Bloch−Redfield and hierarchical equations of motion (HEOM) dynamics are compared under otherwise controlled conditions. The principal diagnostic is the maximum absolute difference in the effective reactive-state population over the 0−15 ps propagation window. Across the converged scan points, the BR−HEOM discrepancy shows an overall decrease from slow- to fast-bath conditions, superimposed on a nonmonotonic broad crossover when bath and system rates become comparable. Varying the effective energy bias changes the discrepancy magnitude but preserves the slow-crossover-fast ordering over the tested biases and bath rates. These results distinguish static solvent-response effects from dynamical solvent-relaxation timescales and identify bath-to-system rate competition as a useful organizing coordinate within the tested reduced-model parameter range and stated numerical-convergence criteria.

papers.title: Portfolio Search with Precedent-Based Selection for Multi-Step Retrosynthesis
papers.abstract: Computer-aided synthesis planners propose routes from a target molecule back to purchasable starting materials, and they are usually compared by how often they find such a route. A route that reaches purchasable stock, however, often contains steps that have no precedent in the chemical literature and that a chemist would not run. We present P*, a planner that searches with a portfolio of complementary strategies and then keeps, for each target, the route whose every step has literature precedent. Each strategy pairs a reaction score with an estimate of how hard an intermediate is to make. The reaction scores are built from chemical heuristics, such as how common a transformation is and how many of its precursors are purchasable. We find that the strategies that reach stock most often produce the fewest precedented routes, because rewarding purchasable precursors favors multicomponent disconnections that are rarely reported. Different strategies therefore find different precedented routes, and together they find precedented routes for about twice as many development targets as the best single strategy. P* produces fully precedented routes for 61% of approved drugs and clinical candidates, 41% of novel expert-curated targets and 49% of USPTO-190 targets, more than any published planner on all three sets. It exceeds the strongest of them, and it improves route validity with every single-step model we tested. Its best single strategy is also an effective route finder and solves 88.0% of ChEMBL-1000 targets.

papers.title: Model-Kernel Corrected DIIS: Cheap Response Information for the Roothaan Step
papers.abstract: Nearly all Kohn–Sham density functional theory (DFT) and Hartree–Fock calculations solve the self-consistent field (SCF) equations with the direct inversion in the iterative subspace (DIIS). Their cost is set by the number of Fock builds that DIIS needs. Each DIIS cycle diagonalizes an extrapolated Fock matrix as if this matrix stayed fixed while the electrons move. The charge that the step moves, however, changes the Coulomb potential, and the next cycle has to undo part of the step. This charge sloshing makes DIIS slower as molecules grow. We correct every step with a model kernel, an inexpensive approximation of this Coulomb response that is built from a few Gaussian functions on each atom and contains no fitted parameters. The resulting method, MK-DIIS, needs no extra Fock build, converges to the same solution as DIIS and adds about 1% to the run time. On 170 transition-metal complexes and organic molecules it needs about one third fewer Fock builds than DIIS, fewer than any SCF algorithm of a production code that we compared with. On molecules with up to 300 atoms it needs about half as many, and on linear acenes its number of Fock builds does not grow with length. The saving is smaller with more exact exchange and in a continuum solvent, both of which screen the Coulomb response. For open-shell molecules, a delayed start keeps the reliability of DIIS. Because only the diagonalization step changes, the correction can be added to existing SCF codes and combined with other convergence aids.

papers.title: trans -Rich Skeletal Transformation of a Cross-Conjugated Polymer via 1,4-Selective Hydrothiolation
papers.abstract: Previous skeletal transformations of cross-conjugated polymers into linear-conjugated structures have been limited to methods involving cyclization, which form only a cis structure on the main chain. In this study, cross-conjugated polymer containing 2,3-linked 1,3-butadiene was successfully converted into a linear-conjugated polymer with cis / trans -isomeric main chains via 1,4-selective hydrothiolation, achieving up to 71% trans -selectivity. In addition, the factors influencing the regio- and stereoselectivities were examined using density functional theory calculations.

papers.title: Dual-Function Organic Emitters for Plastic Scintillators Enabled by Integration of Photocatalytic Controlled Radical Polymerization and Sensitive X-Ray Detection
papers.abstract: Organic scintillators are attractive for X-ray detection and imaging because of their solution processability and compatibility with large-area fabrication. However, their development is limited by the trade-off between X-ray attenuation and photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY), as well as by the lack of mild fabrication methods for plastic scintillator screens. Herein, we report a brominated donoracceptor–donor molecular platform with hybridized local and charge-transfer (HLCT) character that addresses both challenges. Peripheral bromination of a benzo[c][1,2,5]oxadiazole-based scaffold produces a pronounced anti-heavy-atom effect, simultaneously enhancing X-ray attenuation and PLQY. This strategy is extended through chalcogen substitution to afford BOTBr, BTTBr, and BSeTBr, among which BTTBr shows the best overall performance, delivering a PLQY of 77%, a light yield of 37,851 photons MeV-1, and a detection limit of 54 nGy s-1. Notably, BTTBr also acts as a photocatalyst for photoinitiated atom transfer radical polymerization (PhotoATRP), enabling the in situ fabrication of transparent and uniform poly(methyl methacrylate) scintillator screens under mild conditions. The resulting screens afford high-resolution X-ray imaging with a spatial resolution of 13.2 lp mm-1. This work establishes an anti-heavy-atom-effect strategy for dual-functional scintillatorphotocatalyst materials and provides a light-driven route to integrated plasticscintillator fabrication.

papers.title: Predicting molecular crystal growth: Automated surface terminations, interchangeable interaction energy models and finite particles in the CrystalClear protocol
papers.abstract: The incorporation of crystal growth processes extends the utility of predictive techniques beyond simply crystal geometry and a thermodynamic ranking with the ultimate goal being actionable information to target specific crystallisation. Pairwise model interaction energies with implicit solvation have been previously demonstrated in the CrystalClear protocol to provide a computationally efficient route to incorporate such processes, though some limitations restricted its use.
