papers.title: Methodological Optimization of ATR-IR Spectroelectrochemistry for Powdered and Poorly Conductive Electrocatalysts
papers.abstract: In-situ infrared spectroscopy combined with electrochemistry has become a key tool for studying the processes that govern the activity of electrocatalysts under operating conditions. However, its application has been limited almost exclusively to model electrodes, which are either electronically conductive or specifically designed to maximise the ATR optical signal, thereby limiting its use for a family of emerging heterogenous catalysts typically available in powder form and exhibiting poor electrical conductivity. Extending ATR-IR spectroelectrochemistry to this type of catalyst requires simultaneously reconciling optical, adhesion and electrochemical requirements which, until now, have rarely been addressed systematically. Rather than focusing on the elucidation of electrocatalyst mechanisms, this paper presents a structured and transferable methodology for optimising ATR-IR spectroelectrochemical measurements on emerging classes of electrocatalyst. Three groups of interrelated parameters that mostly affect the feasibility of the technique, namely spectroscopic, interfacial and electrochemical parameters, are discussed proposing a step-by-step workflow that enables their methodological standardization and balance. The proposed workflow is validated by applying this methodology to three different materials (Ni(OH) 2 , ZnO and Zn-Al LDH) showing distinct spectroscopic, electrochemical and interfacial properties. The results demonstrate that, following appropriate optimisation, ATR spectroelectrochemistry can be extended to more challenging powdered catalyst layers, providing a practical and generalisable guide for future robust mechanistic investigations of this broad family of materials and contributing to the rational understanding and development of new electrocatalysts for reactions of energy and chemical interest.

papers.title: Elucidating permselectivity mechanisms in polyamide membranes through controlled chlorination and hydrolysis
papers.abstract: Polyamide membranes are widely used in freshwater production because of their high water permeance and water–salt selectivity, but emerging applications require tunable permselectivity. We investigate the structure–property–performance relationships governing membrane behavior by modifying permselectivity through sequential chlorination and alkaline treatment. Chemical, structural, and transport properties are examined using X-ray characterization, free-energy barrier analysis, and molecular dynamics simulations. We find chlorine–alkaline modification more than doubles water permeance through hydrolysis, which enhances swelling, increases water–membrane interactions, and promotes water transport. Despite the resulting looser structure, the hydrolyzed membrane maintains water–salt selectivity because of entropic barriers to salt transport, likely caused by the presence of bulky chlorine groups on the aromatic rings. These findings identify distinct mechanisms by which chemical modification alters water and salt transport, challenge the prevailing view that swelling is detrimental to selectivity, and provide new design insights for tuning polyamide membrane performance.

papers.title: Low Energy Electron Attachment to Catechin Sulphate
papers.abstract: Low energy electron (LEE) attachment can initiate molecular fragmentation through temporary negative ion states, in which autodetachment competes with nuclear motion toward dissociation. We apply an improved local complex potential time-dependent wavepacket (LCP-TDWP) workflow to catechin sulphate, a metabolically relevant catechin conjugate for which, to our knowledge, no dissociative electron attachment (DEA) study has been reported. The model follows a one dimensional C--O bond extension coordinate, whose fragmentation yields a C5-centered catechin-derived radical and the stable bisulphate anion, HSO 4 - . Neutral and anionic potential energy curves were computed at the CAM-B3LYP/6-311++G(2d,2p) level, and vibrational eigenfunctions were obtained with the Fourier grid Hamiltonian method. The coordinate dependent resonance width was defined by an exponential envelope centered at the Franck--Condon coordinate, a Wigner type energy factor built from the local anion--neutral energy difference, and a smooth switch near the curve crossing. Propagation employed a symmetric split-operator scheme with a 0.1 fs time step for 1.0 ps and a complex absorbing potential (CAP) starting at 7.25 a 0 . The Franck--Condon coordinate and the neutral--anion curve crossing lie at R FC =2.659 a 0 and R cross =3.327 a 0 , respectively. The autocorrelation spectrum shows a doorway feature near 0.4512 eV, whereas the DEA cross section peaks at 1.113 eV with a maximum of 4.608 Mb. The cumulative CAP loss from the initial packet at 1.0 ps is 0.003162 (0.3162%). These results characterize the competition between autodetachment and the chosen dissociation channel.

papers.title: CuPd Dilute Alloys Enhance Stability During CO2 Electroreduction in Zero-Gap Electrolyzers
Volatile-element depletion in rocky planets as a purity spectrum of a single information field: An information-dynamics reinterpretation of hybrid accretion
papers.abstract: Wang et al. (2026, Nature Astronomy) showed that the moderately-volatile lithophile element (MVLE) depletion patterns of Earth and Mars record different formation pathways: Earth accreted ≳75% of its mass via pebble accretion, Mars ∼73% via collisions of volatile-depleted planetesimals. We reinterpret this result in the information-dynamics (ID) framework, in which self-organization (ε) and dissipation (γ) compete through a single information field of local purity p. A numerical experiment on the published source data (13 elements for bulk silicate Earth, bulk silicate Mars and Vesta) shows that, within the tested formulation, a single mean purity cannot describe the two planets: the fit escapes to unphysical solutions. A purity spectrum fits instead: each planet’s pattern is a mixture over one universal single-purity response law S(T;p), with only the mixture weights differing between bodies. A joint fit with a 4-parameter universal law reproduces all 36 data points with χ²/N = 0.35 (all residuals within 2σ). The inferred spectra mirror the published multi-component decomposition (Earth: 59% strongly-processed + 24% Vesta-like + 17% volatile-rich; Mars: Vesta-like bin dominant), and Vesta concentrates 99% of its weight at a processing temperature of 1116 K, close to the published 1135 ± 35 K. This is an in-sample consistency check, not an independent validation. Read this way, pebble accretion and planetesimal collision occupy different regions of one organizing spectrum. We do not claim this proves a single mechanism. We offer it as a coherent reading that translates the published decomposition into testable predictions for rocky exoplanets and the Moon.

papers.title: FRACTAL: A Ratiometric-based Fingerprinting Framework for Robust Spectral Classification and Ratio-based Spectroscopic Marker Discovery
papers.abstract: Spectral classification is conventionally performed on band intensities, yet ratios between bands have long served as diagnostic indices in vibrational spectroscopy, from lipid-to-protein markers of membrane composition to amide ratios reporting protein secondary structure. Their use, however, has remained confined to a handful of expert-selected pairs, leaving most of the ratio information contained in a spectrum unexamined. Here I present FRACTAL (Full Ratio Combinatorial Analysis for Classification and Analytical Interpretation), which computes every pairwise log-intensity ratio among detected peaks to form a complete ratiometric fingerprint, grounded in compositional data analysis. Each component is a contrast between two assigned bands and is invariant to the multiplicative factors that scale spectral intensities. Applied to serum Raman spectra from 103 donors (53 with COVID-19, 50 healthy controls), FRACTAL screened all 91 ratios among 14 reproducible peaks and identified 44 discriminant contrasts. A ten-ratio fingerprint reached a mean internal AUC of 0.93–0.96 across six classifier architectures spanning linear, kernel-based and ensemble methods, exceeding the corresponding peak intensities for every classifier and are within 0.04 AUC of the full 457-point spectrum. It generalized to a withheld 20-donor cohort (AUC 0.94–0.96) with the narrowest spread across classifiers of any representation tested, whereas the single most discriminant ratio, despite performing well internally, detected only half of the withheld COVID-19 donors. The top-ranked contrasts include a well-known lipid-to-protein ratio (1451/1662 cm⁻¹) and are consistent with the altered protein composition and aromatic amino acid metabolism reported in COVID-19. FRACTAL establishes exhaustive ratiometric fingerprinting as a compact, robust and interpretable representation for spectral classification and spectroscopic marker discovery.

papers.title: Revisiting Artifact Suppression in Electrospray Ionization Deconvolution
papers.abstract: Charge state assignment is a critical step in many workflows for intact protein analysis by mass spectrometry. Computational deconvolution algorithms are increasingly used to automate data analysis, but conventional approaches can present artifacts. Here, we explore several approaches to remove artifacts by limiting the charge state assignments for each data point. One approach removes satellite charge states surrounding local maxima. Another removes harmonics at double a more probable charge assignment. The last two limit either the total number of allowed charge state assignments or the minimum relative charge state assignment probability for a given data point. These new features are as effective as the prior SoftMax artifact removal in UniDec, but they enable easier tuning by the user. Although the new set of features introduces additional complexity and an expanded number of parameters, these tools enable users to more precisely reduce artifacts in deconvolution results.

papers.title: Classical infrared correlation rules as diagnostic tests: likelihood ratios from 6,663 experimental spectra
papers.abstract: Infrared correlation tables give, for each functional group, a wavenumber window and an adjective. They do not say how often a band is found in that window when the group is absent, and that is the number that decides whether the observation is evidence. We treated every published rule as a diagnostic test. A set of 101 rules for 60 functional groups, transcribed from one widely used interpretation course and frozen before any confirmatory analysis, was scored on 1,539 ATR spectra from the Chemotion repository and replicated on 5,124 transmission spectra from the NIST Chemistry WebBook, with the deposited structure as ground truth and sensitivity, specificity and likelihood ratios as the metrics. Each rule was scored by band position alone and with the intensity and shape words the source attaches to it; 26 combinations of rules from the same table were scored as well. The main result is a division of the spectrum into two regimes. Above 1500 cm-1 most rules carry real evidence (median positive likelihood ratio 2.8 and 3.0 in the two collections, up to 43 for the saturated ester carbonyl); at or below 1350 cm-1, band position alone is close to uninformative (median 1.1 and 1.2), because almost every spectrum has a band in almost every window, and combining fingerprint bands with each other does not change this. The rankings agree across the two collections (Spearman 0.79; 87% of rules within a factor of two) and are unchanged when spectra flagged for atmospheric, saturation or baseline artefacts are removed. Intensity qualifiers and combinations cost more sensitivity than they buy specificity (the nitrile band reaches the stated intensity in one nitrile in ten), the benzene substitution patterns do not reach a likelihood ratio of 5, and several rules are far more useful for ruling a group out than for ruling it in. The quantified table, the frozen rule set and the scripts are provided.

papers.title: A Minimal Tetrazine Linchpin for Cysteine Bridging and Bioorthogonal Ligation
papers.abstract: Site-selective bridging of cysteines and native disulfide bonds represents a powerful strategy for peptide and protein modification. However, most bis-electrophilic reagents rely on azide-alkyne cycloadditions for downstream bioconjugation, while existing tetrazine-based cysteine linkers can generate undesired byproducts, such as peptide cyclodimers, or incorporate additional components that are not directly involved in conjugation or ligation. Here, we report divinyl- s -tetrazine ( DvTz ) as a minimal linchpin in which the electron-deficient tetrazine core activates the vinyl groups as Michael acceptors for efficient cysteine conjugation, while simultaneously serving as a bioorthogonal handle for subsequent inverse-electron-demand Diels-Alder (IEDDA) ligation. DvTz enables high-yielding, cysteine-selective stapling of unprotected peptides, tolerates all twenty canonical amino acids, and accommodates a broad range of sequences and stapling distances. A one-pot stapling-IEDDA sequence enables facile installation of functional tags without intermediate purification. The chemistry was extended to antibody Fab fragments, achieving site-specific disulfide rebridging and subsequent IEDDA ligation across three distinct Fab proteins, with exclusive formation of singly conjugated species. A Fab-drug conjugate was constructed with retained antigen-binding activity and selective potency against HER2-positive cell lines, showcasing the application of DvTz in therapeutically relevant settings. Collectively, this work establishes DvTz as a simple and versatile linchpin for peptide and protein bioconjugation.

papers.title: Twin Ag10 Clusters Assembled into a Discrete Complex via Direction-Tuned Cooperative Coordination
papers.abstract: The spatial organization of multiple atomically precise metal nanoclusters has emerged as a promising strategy to amplify and diversify their properties and to create functional supramolecular materials based on these materials. Here, we report the construction of a discrete complex encapsulating dimerized Ag10 clusters, whose structure in the crystalline state was observed by X-ray diffraction experiments. Such a self-assembly is achieved by modifying cooperative coordination approach that integrates acetylide protection and metal–pyridyl coordination, as confirmed through the stepwise X-ray observation of the related acetylide-protected monomeric Ag8 clsuter and its partial transformation via Ag–pyridyl capping. Photophysical measurements and quantum-chemical calculations demonstrated that the Ag10 dimer showed cluster-based photoluminescence mediated by electronic coupling between the silver cluster core and the carbazole moieties in the ligand framework, with quantum yields of 0.04 in CH2Cl2 solution and 0.10 in the solid state. This work thus suggests that the combination of discrete coordination self-assembly and acetylide-based cluster formation may indeed represent a new way to the oligomerization of large metal clusters to generate structurally precise assemblies.

papers.title: Visible-light-Enabled O-Selective Radical Etherification of 1,2-Dicarbonyl Compounds for the Synthesis of Sterically Congested Ethers
Beyond the Exchange Picture of Singlet–Triplet Gaps
papers.abstract: Molecules with inverted singlet-triplet gaps are promising candidates for next-generation organic light-emitting diode emitters, but identifying general principles that explain and guide singlet-triplet inversion remains challenging. Here, we investigate substituted heptazines, vibrational ensembles of azupyrene and isopyrene, and a chemically diverse molecular set using CIS, EOM-CCSD, and wavefunction-based state matching. The CIS analysis reveals an intermediate level of electronic response between direct exchange and correlation: state-specific configuration relaxation redistributes the gap among exchange, orbital-energy, and electron-hole Coulomb contributions. Correlation beyond CIS generally lowers the gap, with a larger reduction associated with greater relative double-excitation character in the singlet. However, the final gap also depends on the positive CIS baseline, so similar doubles content can occur in systems with either positive or negative gaps. Within related molecular datasets, a larger CIS baseline is accompanied by a stronger correlation-driven reduction, but this relationship does not hold across chemically diverse molecules. These findings establish the importance of balancing the full state-specific singles baseline against correlation-driven gap reduction when interpreting and designing singlet-triplet energetics.

papers.title: Lithium-Ion Battery Electrolyte Structural Transport: Anion Dependent Exchange Mechanisms
papers.abstract: Li + moves through an electrolyte both by diffusing with its intact solvation shell (vehicular transport) and by exchanging its solvent partners (structural transport). Structural diffusion depends on the frequency of solvent dissociation from Li + and how far the ion moves when it does, yet neither is well characterized experimentally. Li + transport in propylene carbonate solutions of LiTFSI, LiBF 4 , and LiPF 6 , from battery-relevant to superconcentrated levels, was studied via a vibrational probe molecule, phenyl selenocyanate, with ultrafast two-dimensional infrared chemical exchange spectroscopy. Li + diffusion coefficients significantly exceed the Stokes-Einstein prediction. Combining this excess diffusion with solvent dissociation times yields the the step length Li + moves per exchange event. Dissociation times correlate with the reorientation time of unbound probe molecules, indicating that productive exchange requires reorganization of the surrounding solvent. For all salts, the step length decreases with concentration. In relatively dilute LiTFSI it is ~1.3 Å, matching the distance predicted from an associative mechanism through a five-coordinate intermediate, whereas in LiPF 6 it is 0.7–0.8 Å at every concentration, consistent with a predominantly dissociative mechanism through a three-coordinate intermediate. Because PF 6- forms the fewest contact ion pairs, it leaves the least free solvent available to act as an entering group, suppressing the associative pathway. Combined with the longest dissociation times, these short steps make LiPF 6 electrolytes generally the most reliant on vehicular transport despite their high viscosity. Thus, the anion influences not only how often Li + exchanges solvent but also the mechanism, and therefore how far Li + moves with each step.

papers.title: Conformational Soft Hash (CSH): A Rotation-Invariant Molecular Fingerprint for Conformation-Sensitive Similarity Search and Blockchain-Based Conformational Registry
papers.abstract: Many molecular descriptors are currently available, but each has its limitations. One group, such as the Morgan and ECFP fingerprints, encodes only the connections between atoms. Those that do take the 3D structure into account either reduce the geometry to a few summary values, as USR, USRCAT and 3DAPfp do, or describe only the environments of individual atoms, as E3FP does. The present work uses the Conformational Soft Hash (CSH), a simple method for representing a 3D conformation as a 256-bit binary hash. Each conformer is described by a feature vector containing the distances between pairs of heavy atoms at least three bonds apart, together with the sine and cosine of each torsion angle. Because interatomic distances and trigonometric functions span different ranges of values, they were brought to a common scale. The length of the vector varied with the size of the molecule, so its dimensionality was reduced to 32 components and the result was converted into a 256-bit string by SimHash, yielding the CSH. CSH was compared with USR, USRCAT, 3DAPfp and E3FP on 28 drug molecules and on a separate set of twelve approved drugs of varying size and flexibility, selected after the method had been finalised. For every pair of conformers of a molecule, the similarity of their hashes was correlated with the geometric difference between them, measured as the root-mean-square difference between their interatomic distance matrices (DM-RMSD). At a common budget of 256 bits, CSH reached a mean Spearman correlation of ρ = 0.508 on the first set and 0.637 on the second. It performed better than USR, while the results for USRCAT and 3DAPfp were similar. 3DAPfp has the advantage, however, of reaching the same accuracy without a transformation fitted to each molecule, which allows different molecules to be compared, something CSH does not offer. E3FP, on the other hand, encodes local atom environments rather than global shape and reflected the geometric differences between conformers poorly. A conformational registry was also implemented on the Ethereum blockchain, which timestamps an identifier of a conformer on a public chain without disclosing its coordinates. Eighty conformers of four molecules were recorded. Records belong to the registry of a particular molecule, so all of its hashes can be retrieved at once, browsed and compared with one another. No registry of this kind has been described before for molecular conformations.

papers.title: Exploiting Differences in Molecular Interactions for Selective PFAS Separation from Natural Organic Matter during Ion-Exchange Regeneration
papers.abstract: Ion-exchange resins effectively remove per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) from water but generate concentrated brines co-loaded with natural organic matter, complicating downstream PFAS destruction. Here, we present a sequential selective regeneration strategy exploiting differences in adsorption mechanism and desorption kinetics between PFAS and humic substances to recover them in separate streams. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that perfluoroalkyl carboxylic acids bind to the resin through dual hydrophobic and electrostatic interactions disrupted by organic solvents, while humic substances bind predominantly electrostatically and are selectively displaced by Cl⁻ ions, desorbing 3–5 times faster than PFOA in sodium chloride solutions. A sequential protocol combining propanol regeneration with a rapid low-contact-time NaCl step recovers over 60% of loaded PFAS in an organic fraction essentially free of humic substances, while humic substances are quantitatively eluted in a separate brine. The PFAS-enriched organic fraction is directly compatible with incineration and emerging destruction technologies, where co-concentrated organic matter would otherwise increase energy demand and reduce treatment efficiency. This work demonstrates that solvent composition, ionic strength, and contact time can be systematically tuned during regeneration to engineer selectivity, a powerful but underexplored dimension of sorption-based water treatment.

papers.title: Steering Solid–Solution Equilibria to Tame Phase Complexity and Instability in Dion-Jacobson Quasi-2D Halide Perovskites
papers.abstract: Dion-Jacobson (DJ) quasi-two-dimensional (2D) halide perovskites (HPs) have emerged as a robust platform for optoelectronic applications, yet their crystallization pathways and subsequent phase evolution remain insufficiently understood. Herein, we integrate robotic high-throughput synthesis with automated spectral diagnosis and multimodal characterization to investigate 1,4-butanediammonium-based HPs containing methylammonium (MA) or formamidinium (FA) across composition and temperature. Tracking phase evolution and cation partitioning reveals competition between lattice stabilization, coarsening, and reconstruction within a coupled heterogeneous reaction system. Continued MA incorporation changes both the solids and surrounding solution, whereas greater initial FA capture does not ensure higher- n phase retention. Comparative extraction and spacer-treatment experiments support an additional pathway linking δ-containing FAPbI 3 structures to FA release and lower- n reconstruction. These findings provide experimental insight into the intricate solid–solution chemical equilibria underlying crystal maturation beyond nucleation. Exploiting this understanding, machine-learning-assisted multi-objective screening identifies synthesis conditions that sustain homogeneous, spectrally ‘frozen’ emission, guiding the formation of chemically stabilized, structurally robust HP frameworks. Applying the selected formulation to HP interfaces yields efficient solar cells with markedly improved thermal stability. Overall, this integrated experiment-analysis workflow translates solid–solution equilibrium chemistry into data-guided control of phase complexity, offering a strategy for durable HP optoelectronics.

papers.title: The Evolution of Electronic Structure in Conjugated Molecules Revealed by Mixed-Reference Spin-Flip Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory and Density-Based Analyses: I. Polyenes
papers.abstract: Spin-flip time-dependent density functional theory (SF-TDDFT) extends linear-response TDDFT to diradicals, bond breaking, conical intersections, and excited states with doubly excited character. The mixed-reference SF-TDDFT (MRSF-TDDFT) formulation provides spin-purified states while keeping the simplicity of the original formalism. Previous benchmarks of MRSF-TDDFT have focused on energies, structures, and permanent and transition dipole moments. Here we look at the state and transition densities. Using natural orbitals, natural transition orbitals, natural difference orbitals, and exciton descriptors, we examine the number of effectively unpaired electrons, the singly excited character of the transitions, exciton sizes, and electron–hole correlation in conjugated molecules of increased sizes. Here we consider all-trans polyenes and in a companion paper we consider polyacenes. In polyenes, the ground state remains predominantly closed shell, the bright 1 1Bu+ state remains singly excited, and the covalent 2 1Ag− and 1 1Bu− states gain progressively more doubly excited character. Exciton descriptors, in particular electron–hole separation and correlation, highlight the differences in state characters arising due to differences in treatment of electron correlation. MRSF-TDDFT captures the main trends in state ordering as compared to the high-level correlated methods as well as the evolution of states’ characters. The results illustrate the utility of MRSF-TDDFT and density-based analyses in describing electronic structure of large conjugated systems.

papers.title: DFT Studies of the Structural and Electronic Properties of Fluorinated and Methoxylated 3-Amino-2-CyclopropylQuinazolin-4(3H)-one Molecules
papers.abstract: DFT B3LYP/6-31+G(d,p) calculations were performed on the twelve fluorinated and methoxylated 3-amino-2-cyclopropylquinazolin-4(3H)-one molecules, which are abbreviated as FMACQs, in toluene, the gas phase, and aqueous solution. Among the twelve isomers, ten of them are positional isomers and two are rotational conformers. The DFT results show that the electronic properties, the HOMO, LUMO, and other five descriptors, i.e. chemical potential, electronegativity, global hardness, global softness, and electrophilicity index, are all similar among the twelve isomers and are therefore less critical in determining the bioactivity of these molecules. However, the dihedral angle between the fluorinated and methoxylated benzene ring and the quinazolinone ring is strongly correlated to the bioactivity. The three isomers with fluorine at the 2-position and no methoxy at the 6-position (FMACQ-42, FMACQ-36, and FMACQ-32) have a dihedral angle larger than 40o but smaller than 45o and are potent REV-ERBα antagonists, whereas that in FMACQ-26 is 57o or the dihedral angles of the molecules with neither functional group present at the 2- and 6-position are about 37o.

papers.title: Binary MOF micropatterns enabling spatially defined dual dye encapsulation
papers.abstract: We report a patterning strategy that combines X-ray lithography with ceramic-to-MOF conversion for the fabrication of binary metal-organic framework (MOF) micropatterns composed of the pillar-layered MOF Cu 2 (BDC 0.5 (Br 2 BDC) 0.5 ) 2 DABCO and HKUST-1. The fabrication protocol enables spatially controlled integration of two MOF phases within defined microscale architectures. Further, the selective encapsulation of distinct fluorescent dyes within each MOF results in micropatterns exhibiting localized dual-wavelength emission. This work establishes a platform for the design of multifunctional MOF-based micropatterns with spatially programmable optical properties.

papers.title: Molecular Mechanics-Based Symmetric Two-State Energy-Gap Estimation of Binding Free Energies
papers.abstract: We examine a symmetric two-state energy-gap (STEG) approximation for binding free energies using a molecular mechanics/Poisson–Boltzmann surface area (MM/PBSA) energetic baseline. An endpoint linear-response approximation, together with a negligible OFF-state mean gap, yields an estimate equal to one-half of the MM/PBSA energetic baseline. The numerical protocol requires one 50 ns bound trajectory per complex and no simulations at intermediate coupling states. For eight neutral cucurbit[7]uril host–guest complexes, MM-STEG gives mean absolute/root-mean-square errors of 1.41/1.64 kcal mol−1, compared with 5.36/6.52 kcal mol−1 for MM/PBSA with interaction entropy (IE), and reproduces the experimental rank order, as does raw MM/PBSA. Across fifteen T4 lysozyme complexes with experimental affinities, MM-STEG reduces every absolute error relative to MM/PBSA+IE, giving errors of 3.04/3.21 versus 7.02/7.58 kcal mol−1. The T4 predictions show persistent overbinding and a pooled Spearman coefficient of 0.375, with the narrow experimental affinity range making accurate ranking particularly challenging. Raw MM/PBSA and MM/PBSA+WEIE give T4 errors of 11.15/11.40 and 7.13/7.59 kcal mol−1, respectively. Within MM-STEG, WEIE affects only the optional enthalpy inference; the inferred 1-adamantanol binding enthalpy differs from experiment by 1.48 kcal mol−1. For eight L99A ligands, inferred enthalpies give MAE/RMSE of 3.58/4.35 kcal mol−1 against calorimetry at a 4 K higher temperature, with no consistent advantage over ordinary IE at the same free-energy baseline. These results support further evaluation of

papers.title: CFD Evaluation of a Tesla-Type Micromixer for Chemical Processing
papers.abstract: Passive Tesla-type micromixers achieve very good mixing in published studies, yet they are rarely found in industrial flow reactors. This study evaluates whether a modified Tesla micromixer could be suitable for continuous chemical processing by considering mixing quality together with pressure drop and throughput. A three-dimensional model with four pairs of Tesla units (channel width 200 µm, depth 110 µm) was built from published dimensions and simulated as a transient, incompressible, laminar water flow in SimScale at Reynolds numbers of 10, 50 and 70. Mixing of the two inlet streams was tracked with a passive scalar. At Re = 10 the streams mixed gradually, while at Re = 50 and Re = 70 they were fully mixed after about two of the eight units, consistent with a transition from diffusion- to convection-dominated mixing. However, as Re increased from 10 to 70, the flow rate increased about 7 times while the pressure drop increased about 29 times (from 2.7 to 78.2 kPa), so the pumping power increased about 200 times. One mixer processed at most about 80 mL per hour, and at Re ≥ 50 low-velocity regions formed inside the bends. The results suggest that the Tesla micromixer is limited not by mixing but by low throughput per unit, rapidly rising pressure drop and possible blockage, and that operation near Re = 50 with fewer units would be the most efficient choice.

papers.title: An Automated Scholarly Literature Collection Workflow Using Official Services for AI for Science
papers.abstract: AI for Science depends on scientific corpora that can be acquired, checked, and updated reproducibly. This work presents a Python literature collection workflow based on official scholarly services. Crossref and Europe PMC support journal identification and record discovery, NLM PMC Cloud supplies eligible article files and supplementary materials, and separate Elsevier and Wiley adapters use the publishers' official APIs where the operator has the required access. The PMC implementation records provenance and licenses, validates file integrity, checkpoints completed records, and resumes using verified local files. A historical smoke test documents one article PDF and one supplementary DOCX from 11 search hits. A live check of the current release downloaded one 13-page Chemical Science PDF from 21 query hits and confirmed reuse on a second run, while also exposing ambiguity between the query term Mg and the mass unit mg. The release passed 38 offline regression tests and a desktop interface smoke test. File downloads default to an interval of 10 min, with longer intervals recommended where required by the service. The workflow provides a reference implementation for local corpus preparation; corpus completeness and downstream extraction accuracy remain outside the present validation.

papers.title: Graphene–ZnO Nanohybrid Synthesis via Wheat Germ Lipase Exfoliation for Environmentally Compatible Antimicrobial Applications
papers.abstract: A graphene-supported ZnO bionanohybrid material (G@WG-ZnO) was prepared through an aqueous synthesis approach using immobilized wheat germ lipase (WG) as a natural biotemplate. The strategy enabled the in-situ formation of ZnO nanoparticles within the graphene-based material. X-ray diffraction, surface and elemental analyses confirmed the formation and incorporation of ZnO, with a Zn content of approximately 6 wt.%. The re-sulting G@WG–ZnO bionanohybrid exhibited significantly enhanced antibacterial activity compared with G@WG, which showed no detectable inhibition under the tested conditions, producing inhibition zones of 13.2 ± 2.0 and 9.8 ± 1.5 mm against Shewanella oneidensis and Staphylococcus aureus , respectively. The larger inhibition zone observed for S. oneidensis indicates a greater susceptibility of the Gram-negative strain to the nanohybrid, while the inhibition zones were comparable to those obtained with ZnO nanoparticles alone at a comparable ZnO amount. In addition, the G@WG–ZnO bionanohybrid reduced the growth of the sulfate-reducing bacterium Desulfovibrio vulgaris by 92 %, indicating potential relevance for controlling microbiologically influenced corrosion (MIC). Ecotoxicological assessments showed a moderate response in Daphnia magna and no acute toxicity in Vibrio fischeri exposed to the leachates at the tested concentrations. Overall, these findings support immobilized WG as a biotemplate for the aqueous synthesis of graphene-supported ZnO nanohybrid material and demonstrate that ZnO incorporation provides antibacterial activity comparable to that of ZnO nanoparticles alone, highlighting the potential of the resulting nanohybrid for aquatic microbial control and MIC-related applications.

papers.title: A green and sustainable incorporation of bi- and ter-thiophenes into 1,4-dihydropyridines: synthetic, mechanistic and photophysical investigations
papers.abstract: Bi- and ter-thiophene moieties have been incorporated into 1,4-dihydropyidines (DHPs) via a novel and green, solvent- free, one pot multi-component Hantzsch reaction. Effect of catalyst, solvents and temperature were studied to optimize the reaction condition. Tetra noctyl ammonium bromide (TOAB) was used as a promoter and trace amount of water inadvertently trapped in ammonium acetate acted as catalyst to facilitate the reaction. A combined experimental and quantum chemical mechanistic study was carried out to elucidate how only trace amount of water is central to the success of the proposed synthetic protocol, while bulk water actually inhibits the reaction. A combined experimental and quantum chemical photophysical study was carried out to assess the impact of conjugation extension for bi- and ter-thiophene DHPs compared to mono-thiophene DHP. It was found that the DHP moiety determined the photophysical behavior for monothiophene incorporated products, but the behavior of terthiophene incorporated DHPs reflected that of the corresponding thiophene moieties.

papers.title: Transforming Biogenic Iron Oxide into Zero-Valent Iron for Sustainable Doxycycline Removal from Water
papers.abstract: The study of biogenic iron oxide (BIOX) produced by Leptothrix bacteria plays a crucial role in sustainable environmental management. As a naturally abundant material, BIOX offers a green alternative to synthetic iron oxides, with promising applications in water treatment, pollution control, and resource recovery. However, its efficacy in removing antibiotic contaminants, specifically doxycycline (DOXY), has not been systematically investigated, representing a clear knowledge gap. Here, we demonstrate that reducing BIOX under either pure H2 or a H2/N2 gas mixture significantly enhances its adsorption capacity for DOXY in both synthetic solutions and real water samples collected from the River Clyde. An increased intensity of zero-valent iron (Fe0) reflections, achieved by extending the reduction duration or raising the temperature, generally correlated with superior performance across various pH levels. A prolonged reduction process lasting 10 hours at different temperatures (700°C, 400°C, and 500°C) achieved adsorption capacity of 455 mg/g. Furthermore, this reductive strategy successfully enhanced the performance of other waste-derived adsorbents, including red mud (RM) and RM-derived α-Fe2O3. These results demonstrate the broad potential of reduced biogenic and waste-derived materials for environmental remediation, highlighting the need for further studies across a wider spectrum of aquatic pollutants.

papers.title: Mechanism-Driven Optimization of Proton Transfer in Mn-Catalyzed Amine-Boranes Dehydrogenation: The Way to Turbo Mode
papers.abstract: Improving the efficiency of the individual steps in catalytic cycles is one of the main cornerstones of homogeneous catalysis. In particular, optimization of proton transfer processes by the incorporation of nitrogen donor moieties in the second coordination sphere of transition metal constitutes a privileged strategy to boost the rate and modulate the selectivity of electrocatalysts for small molecules activation. However, proton-relay strategies remain largely unexplored in homogeneous (de)hydrogenation, particularly through the use of exogenous nitrogen bases. We report herein that the rational choice of amine additive as proton transfer mediator can largely improve efficient Mn-based catalytic system for amine-borane dehydrogenation working through the cooperation between Mn + and MnH species. Addition of 1.0-5.0 mol% of simple tertiary amine such as Et 3 N led to 7-45-fold rate acceleration and the increase of TON values by 65-420% for all substrates. This upgrade is due to a combination of lower activation barrier for the rate-determining deprotonation of Mn-coordinated amine-boranes and a higher amount of catalytically active cationic metal species Mn+ present in solution under these conditions. In addition, meticulous mechanistic investigations revealed the crucial role of ammonium salt concentration in this catalytic process thus paving the way for further improvements. Accordingly, the use of a binary Et 3 N/Et 3 NH + mixture instead of pure Et 3 N again speeds up Mn-catalyzed Me 2 NHBH 3 dehydrogenation by a factor of ten to achieve unprecedented TOF of 125 s −1 and TON of 105 at 60°C. Beyond achieving the best performance reported to date for this substrate, our results highlight how the judicious optimization of a priori trivial elementary steps in the catalytic cycle, without altering the intrinsic reactivity of the metal center, can dramatically enhance the activity of an already highly efficient transition metal catalyst.

papers.title: Mechanism-Driven Optimization of Proton Transfer in Mn-Catalyzed Amine-Boranes Dehydrogenation: The Way to Turbo Mode

papers.title: Accessible-State Descriptors Transfer Across Families but Fail at Larger Scales
papers.abstract: Can descriptions of the states visited during quantum dynamics predict product-formula simulation requirements beyond physical and Hamiltonian controls, and do those relationships survive a change of scale? In a frozen nested leave-one-family-out evaluation of ﬁnite matter–light models, normalized accessibility and a combined state-space representation reduced equal-family mean absolute step-count error from 7.4512 to 5.5334 and 4.6771, respectively, although eﬀects were heterogeneous and the primary accessibility increment on a separately registered external family was marginal. On the subsequent strict large-simulation-dimension endpoint, frozen R6 and the later R7 representation each performed worse than the already inaccurate Phase IV physical baseline, with the resolved-fraction support gate remaining inconclusive. These results support a bounded predictive association within the tested ﬁnite regime, not a state-space complexity law, a causal explanation, or an extrapolatable hardware-resource estimate.

papers.title: Ranking versus Absolute Accuracy in Matter–Light Simulation Cost Prediction
papers.abstract: Ordering quantum-dynamical simulations by diﬃculty is not equivalent to pre-dicting their absolute computational requirements. We examine this distinction using frozen matter–light product-formula benchmarks and descriptors of accessible support, state-space geometry, ﬁnite-time Krylov evolution, control-algebra dimension, analytic suﬃcient steps, and empirical symbolic predictions. Eﬀective Krylov dimension has a median error-stratiﬁed Spearman association of 0.8158 with measured steps, but the descriptor comparisons use diﬀerent eligible populations and cannot establish condi-tional superiority. On its strict dimension holdout, a frozen symbolic predictor retains rank correlation 0.9363 while incurring mean absolute error 626.5785 steps. Analytic suﬃcient-to-measured step ratios have medians 46.6087 and 7.6583 for the respective formula orders; these measure conservative looseness, not point-prediction error. The benchmark illustrates a domain-limited separation of ranking, absolute accuracy, and conservative error control. Censoring, approximate Krylov bases, and unavailable cir-cuit domains preclude a uniﬁed or hardware-level complexity interpretation.

papers.title: Near-Infrared-Responsive Au Nanorod/UiO-66-NH2 Hybrids for Photocatalytic Carbon Dioxide Conversion
papers.abstract: The efficient conversion of carbon dioxide into value-added chemicals using solar energy remains a critical scientific and technological challenge, particularly due to the limited utilization of the near-infrared (NIR) region of the solar spectrum. In this study, we report the design and synthesis of an ultrabroadband plasmonic–metal–organic framework (MOF) hybrid photocatalyst capable of driving the carbon dioxide reduction reaction under NIR irradiation. Gold nanorods with tuneable longitudinal surface plasmon resonance were successfully integrated into a UiO-66-NH2 framework through an in-situ encapsulation strategy followed by mild thermal treatment to enhance interfacial coupling. The resulting composite exhibits strong and continuous light absorption across the 300–1200 nm range, enabling efficient harvesting of low-energy photons. Under 808 nm irradiation, the optimized catalyst demonstrates a CO production rate of 152.3 μmol g-1 h-1 with a selectivity exceeding 90%. Detailed spectroscopic and electrochemical analyses reveal that plasmon-induced hot carrier generation and efficient interfacial charge transfer play a decisive role in enhancing photocatalytic performance. This work provides a viable pathway for extending photocatalytic activity into the NIR region and contributes to the advancement of solar-to-chemical energy conversion technologies.

papers.title: Redox-active ligand facilitates HNO generation in a super-reduced dinitrosyl iron complex
papers.abstract: Dinitrosyl iron complexes (DNICs) are widespread biological nitric oxide (NO) storage and delivery motifs, yet their highly delocalized electronic structure generally resists NO-centered reductive chemistry. Here, we establish ligandcentered reduction as a strategy for unlocking nitroxyl (HNO)-generating DNIC reactivity. A redox-active formazanate ligand (L) stabilizes a super-reduced formal {LFe(NO) 2 } 11 state beyond the conventional {Fe(NO) 2 } 9/10 redox pair. EPR and Mössbauer spectroscopy, together with density functional theory calculations, identify predominantly ligand-centered reduction, yielding an {Fe(NO) 2 } 10 unit coupled to a formazanate radical dianion, L 2−• . Electronic communication between the reduced ligand and the [Fe(NO) 2 ] unit enhances Fe-to-NO π backbonding, consistent with experimental ν(NO) redshifts. Importantly, protonation triggers HNO release, representing an unprecedented example of HNO generation from the super reduced DNIC scaffold. Isotopically distinct H 14 NO/H 15 NO is trapped with PPh 3 , along with the 14/15 N 2 O characterization. Calculations support direct nitrosyl protonation to form an Fe-bound HNO intermediate, followed by solvent-assisted HNO release and subsequent N 2 O formation. These findings establish that ligand-centered electron accommodation coupled to nitrosyl protonation enables HNO generation from a formally super-reduced DNIC, extending DNIC reactivity beyond conventional NO donation.

papers.title: Dual-Channel Solvation Forces at Polymer-Brush Interfaces
papers.abstract: Integrating statistical-mechanical pole theory with molecular dynamics simulations, we extend asymptotic correlation theory to polymer-brush-grafted soft interfaces, achieving quantitative, parameter-free predictions of oscillatory solvation free energies. We uncover a dual-channel physical mechanism governing inter-surface forces: interactions across disordered brushes are governed entirely by bulk-liquid correlations (the oscillatory channel), whereas dense, crystalline brushes induce capillary freezing of the confined solvent, opening a monotonic attraction channel of interfacial phase-transition origin.

papers.title: ML/MM
papers.abstract: Electrostatic embedding allows a local machine-learning potential to respond to an extended molecular environment without including every environmental atom in its message-passing graph. We construct a fixed-charge machine-learning/molecular-mechanics (ML/MM) interface for the pretrained MACE-POLAR-1-M model. Analytic Gaussian monopole and dipole operators supply the environmental potential, the internal electrostatic features, and the interaction energy. Differentiation through both field-conditioned density updates gives forces on the model fragment and the environment, which are combined with a subtractive classical energy and exact link-atom force redistribution. A reciprocal-space extension treats three-dimensional periodicity at fixed cell. We assess the implementation using fixed-geometry numerical checks and 24 matched QM/MM reference calculations for a 2589-atom rhodopsin model, with 54 atoms in the neural-network graph. The analytic model gives a relative-energy root-mean-square error of 8.62 kJ mol−1 after one constant energy shift, and force-component errors of 0.07345 and 0.00797 eV Å−1 on the 53 real high-level atoms and 2536 environmental atoms, respectively. Analytic operators substantially reduce rotational errors while leaving the QM/MM accuracy essentially unchanged. A nearby water accounts for approximately 74% of the environmental squared force error. Matched charge-density and frozen-density force comparisons identify limitations of both the local multipole representation and its predicted coefficients. The results establish the numerical consistency of the embedding implementation and delimit the single-point accuracy of the transferred pretrained model.

papers.title: Time-Resolved Dynamic Assembly and Disassembly of Fueled Peptide Systems
papers.abstract: Many molecules can self-assemble into higher order structures. Depending on the environment, the molecules will either assemble or disassemble towards their equilibrium (lowest) free energy state. Fueled molecular systems allow for a fundamentally di!erent behavior, namely an assembly into a higher free energy state (via the consumption of fuel) and a subsequent disassembly, allowing for new material properties. Here we quantify the fueled assembly and disassembly for structures formed by Lphenylalanine acyl ethyl phosphate (FEPs) and contrast this with the equilibrium self-assembly of diphenylalanine (F2). Importantly, we derive kinetic and thermodynamic parameters, e.g., e!ective (dis)assembly rates, phase coexistence points, and chemical potential biases for this system by fitting a mean-field model for chemical fueling of transient states (CFTS) to time-resolved atomic force microscopy (AFM) data. This quantitative framework provides a physical basis to define and analyze the lifetime of transient states, establishing how initial fuel concentrations and internal thermodynamic parameters dictate such non-equilibrium systems. Additional ex-situ AFM experiments yield molecular structural information and delineate the influence of substrates. Understanding the underlying mechanisms for fueled molecular systems is essential for further developing this growing field.

papers.title: Electrochemically assembled oligovalent glycomimetics as potent inhibitors of bacterial sialidases
papers.abstract: Gut microbiota dysbiosis is a hallmark of Crohn’s disease (CD), with increased availability of host-derived nutrients contributing to the expansion of pathogenic bacteria such as adherentinvasive Escherichia coli (AIEC). Microbial sialidases play a key role in mucin degradation by releasing N-acetylneuraminic acid, thereby promoting bacterial nutrient scavenging and colonization. Here, we report a new strategy for targeting intestinal sialidase activity through the development of multivalent glycomimetic inhibitors generated by electrochemically promoted bioconjugation (eY-click). S-linked Neu5Ac and transition-state analogue Neu5Ac2en derivatives were equipped with phenylurazole or N-methylluminol electroactive handles and efficiently conjugated onto tyrosine-containing peptide scaffolds under mild aqueous conditions. This approach enabled the formation of oligovalent sialidase inhibitors with varied ligand density. The resulting compounds displayed potent inhibitory activity against gut microbiota sialidases from Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron and Bacteroides vulgatus, demonstrating strong multivalent enhancement despite their relatively low valency compared with previously reported polymeric inhibitors. Notably, Neu5Ac2en-based oligovalent inhibitor effectively suppressed AIEC LF82 growth driven by sialidase-mediated Neu5Ac release from mucin, outperforming a previously described high-valency polymeric inhibitor. Beyond sialidase inhibition, this work establishes eY-click as a versatile method for constructing multivalent biomolecular inhibitors and provides a new avenue for targeting microbial carbohydrate metabolism in inflammatory bowel disease.

papers.title: Oxalyl Halide-Mediated Synthesis of Halogenated α,β-Unsaturated γ-Lactams from Amino Acid Derivatives
papers.abstract: An oxalyl halide-mediated conversion of amino acid derivatives to halogenated α,β-unsaturated γ-lactams is reported. The metal-free transformation provides functionalized γ-lactams from readily available amino acid derivatives. Variation of the amine substituent, oxalyl halide, amino acid side chain, and external nucleophile enables independent diversification at N1, C3, C4, and C5, respectively. Mechanistic studies support an activation-cyclization-halogenation sequence involving multiple modes of oxalyl halide reactivity.

papers.title: Peptide Stapling: A Strategy for Enhanced Molecular Recognition of C-Reactive Protein
papers.abstract: In our previous studies, we identified three linear CRP‑binding peptides (P2, P3, and P9), which were subsequently characterized using experimental approaches and in silico analysis. The P3 peptide was successfully used as a sensing element in a microfluidic sensing device for CRP recognition 1. However, linear peptides have some limitations, such as conformational instability. Thus, in our study, we constrained the peptide structure using a stapling approach (P1) to address this problem. In silico analysis showed that only the P9 peptide retained CRP-binding activity after the stapling reaction among other CRP-binding peptides reported in our previous studies 1. Calculations indicated that the staple-bound peptide P1 has a higher affinity for CRP than the linear peptide P9, which lacks a staple. Furthermore, the calculated binding energy for P1 was lower than that obtained for the stapled peptides P2 and P3. The staple in peptide P1 was formed via ring-closing olefin metathesis (RCM). Structural differences between the new stapled P1 peptide and the linear P9 peptide were demonstrated using transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and circular dichroism (CD) measurements. The stapled P1 peptide was applied to recognize CRP on silicate-modified indium tin oxide-coated glass electrodes. The electrodes obtained with P1 exhibit a greater affinity for CRP, even in the presence of proteolytic enzymes, than those modified with the linear P9 peptide. The thermal and proteolytic stability of the peptides was evaluated using electrochemical analyses and CD.

papers.title: Stereoselective N-Glycosylation by Iron-Catalyzed Cross-Coupling of Glycosyl Phosphates
papers.abstract: Herein, we report an iron-catalyzed glycosyl cross-coupling strategy for stereoselective β-N-glycosylation through activation of glycosyl phosphate donors under mild conditions. Inspired by the reactivity of enzymes and the biological relevance of phosphate leaving groups, this biomimetic glycosyl phosphate enables efficient coupling of diverse Naglycones with both armed and disarmed sugars. The methodology exhibits broad substrate scope with excellent functional-group tolerance and high β-stereoselectivity. The synthetic utility of the protocol is demonstrated with over 58 examples, including late-stage functionalization of pharmaceutical and biologically relevant scaffolds, offering new opportunities to advance chemical biology, glycochemistry, and therapeutic discovery.

papers.title: Noncollinear Mixed-Reference Spin-Flip TDDFT: Removing the Dependence on High Exact Exchange
papers.abstract: Collinear mixed-reference spin-flip TDDFT (MRSF-TDDFT) omits the transverse exchange–correlation (xc) response from its spin-flip channel, making large fractions of exact exchange practically necessary. We remove this restriction by incorporating the multicollinear transverse xc kernel into MRSF-TDDFT without empirical rescaling. The U(1) spin-rotation selection rule confines the added response to the matrix blocks within each triplet reference and leaves the inter-reference spin-pairing coupling unchanged. The resulting noncollinear MRSF-TDDFT (nc-MRSF-TDDFT) reduces the offset between the spin-lowered MS = 0 response root and the bare MS = ±1 references by 86–99%, from 0.75–2.9 to 0.03–0.11 eV, and restores the diagonal spin-rotation condition without imposing an exact zero mode. Thiel and QUEST benchmarks show that B3LYP and PBE0 give the most balanced singlet, triplet, and singlet–triplet gap errors, whereas BH&HLYP tends to overcorrect the absolute excitation energies after the transverse response is restored. Ethylene torsion separates the complementary roles of the theory: the mixed-reference configuration space describes the continuous development of open-shell character, while the NC kernel corrects the relative spin-state energetics. The same correction improves diradical singlet–triplet gaps at published state-specific geometries. The transverse kernel increases the response-step cost, but the unchanged SCF and other shared steps make the relative overhead smaller for the total calculation. By restoring the missing xc response rather than compensating for it with high exact exchange, nc-MRSF-TDDFT extends the practical functional and chemical scope of MRSF-TDDFT while retaining its description of multiconfigurational and doubly excited states.

papers.title: Yielding Enhanced Gas Sensing in WO3 Thin Films via p-n Heterojunction Formation
papers.abstract: Semiconductor nanostructures have attracted considerable attention for developing high-performance gas sensors for the high-level detection of highly flammable and toxic gases. Herein, the present work integrates n-type WO3 with p-type Ag2O to form a p-n heterojunction by DC reactive magnetron co-sputtering technique. The CH4 sensing performance of the p-n heterojunction with Ag content is correlated with the crystalline structure, surface morphology, elemental composition, optical band gap, and chemical states of the thin film. The p-n heterojunction thin film with 3.63 at. % Ag exhibits a maximum CH4 sensitivity of 70.61 % towards 25 ppm at a low operating temperature of 75 °C. The optimised CH4 sensor also demonstrates a fast response/recovery time of 28 s/106 s with a low detection limit of 1 ppm, excellent repeatability, and long-term stability. The effectiveness of the p-n heterojunction is validated by comparing the sensing performance with that of pristine n-type WO3. Moreover, the utilisation of our optimised p-n heterojunction thin-film-based sensor is further extended towards CO, H2S, H2 and NH3 gas detection, with a detection limit of 25 ppm. This easily implementable approach to designing p-n heterojunctions could pave the way for advanced next-generation sensing technology.

papers.title: When do machine-learning potentials need a configuration-dependent kernel? Learning long-range interactions with Fourier neural operators
papers.abstract: Long-range interactions in machine-learning interatomic potentials are commonly treated by coupling learned sources through either a prescribed electrostatic kernel or a learned but configurationindependent one. Whether such a kernel suffices depends on the underlying screened interaction. We address this question by using Fourier neural operators (FNOs) to learn how latent source fields, built from the descriptors of a local backbone (here MACE), interact across the simulation cell. For a synthetic ionic system with tunable screening, a prescribed Coulomb kernel underestimates the longwavelength charge fluctuations by 43% under strong screening, whereas the FNO reproduces them within 3% and recovers 95–99% of the variance of the residual left by the local backbone. A linear FNO, which learns a configuration-independent kernel, performs equally well in the homogeneous case. Under inhomogeneous screening, rearranging the remote medium modulates the coupling between distant ions, a dependence that no configuration-independent kernel can represent. Among the models tested, only the nonlinear FNO responds to this modulation, and its force errors are 27–41% lower than those of configuration-independent models. In first-principles benchmarks of liquid water, lithium lanthanum zirconate, and Au 2 /MgO(001), MACE–FNO is comparable to a prescribed-kernel model for the bulk systems and more accurate for the interface. It further captures the reversal of the Au 2 wetting preference induced by remote Al dopants, with deviations below 5meV per cell from density functional theory. These results indicate that a configuration-dependent kernel becomes necessary once the screening medium varies, even though the energy remains quadratic in the charges for a fixed medium. Nonlinear FNOs, which learn such a kernel from energies and forces alone, offer a flexible route to environment-dependent long-range interactions.

papers.title: Perspective on the Feasibility of Near-Term Quantum Simulation for Industrially Relevant Catalyst Materials
papers.abstract: Quantum simulation has been proposed as a route to treating strongly correlated electronic structure problems relevant to catalysis, but most existing studies focus on faulttolerant algorithms beyond current hardware capabilities. Here we assess the feasibility of near-term quantum simulation for catalytic materials through industrially relevant use cases. We consider zeolite clusters from classical QM/MM simulations relevant to NH3-SCR, and construct electronic active-space and embedding-based models of the catalytic active site. Using variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) ansätze, we estimate qubit requirements and circuit depths to produce the ground-state for both full and reduced Hamiltonians. Direct simulation of the full system is intractable on near-term devices, but fragmentation and active-space approaches, combined with low-rank Local Unitary Cluster Jastrow ansatz constructions, substantially reduce resource requirements. These results indicate that, while full catalytic models remain out of reach, reduced representations of chemically relevant fragments begin to approach the capacity of near-term quantum hardware. This highlights the role of physically informed model reduction in applying quantum simulation to applied materials problems.

papers.title: Geometries are forgiving, basins are not: a practical guide to optimizing chemical structures
papers.abstract: A calculated molecular or materials structure is the input to almost every later number in a computational study, yet the step that produces it is usually reported in one line. Two kinds of failure are distinguished here, and the heuristic that follows is offered with its range of validity. Within a basin of the potential energy surface, and for the stiff modes and well-behaved closed-shell systems covered by the benchmarks reviewed, geometries are forgiving in energy: for well-chosen methods, bond lengths converge to a few tenths of a picometer and rotational constants to a few megahertz, and the coordinate system and Hessian guess mainly change the cost of the optimization; they can also change convergence behavior and, in difficult cases, the stationary point reached. Between basins, the answer can change qualitatively, because a wrong conformer, cluster isomer or polymorph can shift energies and properties by more than a change of functional or basis set in the examples examined. The heuristic fails for properties that depend on the geometry to first order, for very soft modes and weak interactions, and for systems in which the level of theory changes the topology of the surface. Published benchmark data on coordinates and optimizers, local and global search, wave-function and density-functional levels, basis sets and composite methods are replotted in a common graphical style; this does not make them statistically commensurable, and directly comparable results are distinguished from illustrative comparisons across studies. The review covers molecular optimization, conformer and cluster search, transition-structure location and machine-learned potentials, with periodic relaxation treated briefly. Worked examples show where a wrong basin or an unbalanced level changed a conclusion. Universal machine-learned potentials are assessed as pre-optimizers, a reporting standard is proposed, and a decision scheme by system class is given. Where the literature contains no benchmark, this is stated explicitly.

papers.title: An Evaluation of Modern Density Functionals for the Bond Dissociation Energies of Diatomic Transition Metal Complexes.
papers.abstract: Two benchmark sets of dissociation energies of diatomic transition-metal complexes have been assembled from previously published data, with selected reference values reassessed or updated where necessary, and used to evaluate a variety of density functionals. The BDE41 set of 41 3d complexes based on both experimental data and phaseless auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo reference data is the statistically more robust of the two sets. A number of local hybrid functionals top the list with the smallest deviations, including the strong-correlation (sc) corrected scLH22t and scLH22ta, and the range-separated variant ωLH23tP, followed by the previous top-performing global hybrids B97 and B97-1. While global hybrids and local hybrids without sc-corrections tend to underbind on average, sc-corrections may shift this to moderate overbinding. Nitride and oxide complexes account for much of the underbinding. Functionals based on neural-network local mixing functions underbind more clearly also in other cases, confirming that for these very flexible constructions a lack of transition-metal training data is more harmful to transferability than for less flexible functionals with heuristic mixing functions. The smaller and somewhat less reliable HBDE17 set of 4d/5d complexes reinforces several of the observations but appears to disfavor large exact-exchange admixtures even more strongly. In this case carbide and oxide complexes provide the most pronounced challenges. Nevertheless, several functionals perform not much worse than the most sophisticated post-Hartree-Fock reference calculations currently available based on CCSD(T) with multi-reference corrections. These benchmark sets may also prove useful for training and evaluating new approximate methods, an application we intend to explore in future work.

papers.title: NMRSCOUT: Automated Annotation of Complex Mixtures from Multidimensional NMR Spectra Using Predictive Modelling and Statistical Filtering
papers.abstract: Fast multi-dimensional NMR methods are increasingly used in untargeted metabolomics studies. By mitigating overlap, they offer improved statistical discrimination and/or facilitated biomarker annotation compared to 1D NMR. However, annotating the resulting spectra remains difficult due to limited databases and annotation tools supporting such methods. We introduce NMRSCOUT, an automated workflow for annotating 1D and 2D NMR spectra, including conventional and fast 2D experiments. Using a user-provided library of candidate structures, NMRSCOUT predicts 1H and 13C chemical shifts via a hybrid model combining Morgan fingerprints and a graph neural network, reconstructs corresponding 1D/2D spectra, and compares them to experimental data. Statistical filtering (STOCSY, RANSY) leverages signal relationships across sample series to reduce false matches, while complementary NMR experiments are integrated into a unified annotation score. NMRSCOUT was evaluated using 20 Aspergillus chevalieri extracts analyzed via 1D 1H, 13C-INEPT, ultrafast COSY (UF-COSY), and HSQC-SYMAPS, using a library of 3,250 candidate structures. Combining all four experiments narrowed high-scoring candidates (scores in the [90-100] range) to 1.8% (57 structures), significantly reducing ambiguity. Top-ranked candidates aligned with compounds previously reported for A. chevalieri, and most of them were also observed in the LC-HRMS profiles of the same extracts. Thus, NMRSCOUT provides a versatile tool for annotation of NMR spectra from highly complex mixtures, taking advantage of the convergence of spectra from multiple NMR acquisition sequences. The NMRSCOUT software is available at https://github.com/serignebamba398pixel/NMRSCOUT.

papers.title: Photochemical Synthesis of Planar-to-Helical BN Acenes
papers.abstract: BN-isosteric acenes offer new opportunities for structural and property modulation, but the synthesis and conformational control of highly fused BN acenes remain challenging. Here we develop a photochemical strategy to convert BN heterocyclic precursors into highly fused BN acenes. By varying substituent positions and ring-fusion orientations, we achieve a conformational evolution from planar to double-helical structures. Despite pronounced backbone distortion, the six-membered BN rings retain substantial local aromaticity. Conformational modulation gives rise to diverse photophysical properties, including long-lived phosphorescence and persistent afterglow. Enhanced air stability arises from the synergistic effects of steric shielding of the boron centres by the double-helical architecture and HOMO energy lowering upon π-extension. This work establishes a new route to highly fused BN acenes and provides opportunities for tuning their three-dimensional structures and properties.

papers.title: Engineering Bi2WO6 /NiFe-LDH Heterostructure for Enhanced Water Splitting: Activity, Interfacial Properties and Durability
papers.abstract: Developing efficient and durable electrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is essential for advancing sustainable hydrogen production. In this study, we have developed Bi2WO6/NiFe-LDH (BWL) heterostructure as an electrocatalyst toward hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). The catalytic activity was assessed using linear sweep voltammetry (LSV), Tafel analysis, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), electrochemical double-layer capacitance (Cdl), charge-transfer studies and long-term chronopotentiometric measurements. The BWL composite exhibited the lowest overpotentials of 64, 161 and 222 mV at current densities of 10, 50 and 100 mA cm-2, respectively, outperforming the individual components. Furthermore, BWL demonstrated a lower Tafel slope of 99 mV dec-1 compared with 165 mV dec-1 for Bi2WO6 and 111 mV dec-1 for NiFe -LDH, indicating more favorable HER kinetics. The BWL also exhibited the highest Cdl value of 4.5 mF cm-2, suggesting an increased electrochemically accessible interfacial area. Charge-transfer studies revealed a higher current response for BWL than for the individual components. Moreover, the composite sustained electrochemical operation for 40 h, with the HER overpotential increasing only from 64 to 68 mV following the stability test. These results highlight the promising electrochemical performance and durability of the BWL composite and support further investigation of Bi2WO6, NiFe-LDH hybrid materials for electrocatalytic hydrogen production.

papers.title: Hybrid Kernel/Bath Quantum Dynamics Reveal Conical Intersection Signatures in X-ray Raman Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Quantum dynamical (QD) descriptions of the coupled electronic and nuclear dynamics can deliver full information on photochemical reactions providing a firm basis for the simulation of their time-resolved spectroscopic signatures. Yet, treating all vibrational degrees of freedom explicitly rapidly becomes computationally intractable. Here, we introduce a hybrid reactive-kernel/bath (RK/B) partitioning of the vibronic Hamiltonian into an anharmonic reactive kernel and a parametrically coupled harmonic bath. Using the cis–trans photoisomerization of a minimal retinal chromophore model PSB3, we perform nonadiabatic QD simulations on a hierarchy of models of increasing dimensionality and simulate two representative N K-edge X-ray Raman signals, resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) and TRUECARS, to assess how the vibrational bath shapes them. We observe that RIXS, which is sensitive to the electronic populations, is governed almost entirely by the reactive coordinates and is already reproduced by the bare reactive kernel. Conversely, TRUECARS, which is sensitive to the electronic coherence, is shaped by the coupling modes, whose explicit inclusion is indispensable and is accurately captured by a quadratic bath treatment. These results suggest that RIXS and TRUECARS provide complementary, mode-selective views of photochemical dynamics, and establish the RK/B strategy as a computationally affordable route to investigate multimode effects on the quantum dynamics and nonlinear X-ray signals of complex photoactive systems.

papers.title: Temperature- and matrix-dependent excited state equilibria in pyrene-linked ruthenium and iridium complexes
papers.abstract: The triplet reservoir effect is an established concept to extend triplet state lifetimes in molecular transition metal complexes. However, the delicate balance between the excited states is impacted by various parameters such as ligand design, the central metal ion, but also the solvent environment. In this study, we present an in-depth investigation of the excited-state nature and relaxation pathways of structurally related Ru(II)- and Ir(III)-based dyads bearing a pyrene moiety in the ligand backbone to serve as triplet reservoir in two different matrices, (frozen) methanol and potassium bromide. By temperature-dependent luminescence spectroscopy and excited-state lifetime measurements, pronounced sensitivity of the energetic position of the 3 MLCT state relative to the pyrene 3 ππ* state to the environment is revealed, resulting in an inversion of the excited-state ordering in dependence of the surrounding medium in the Ru(II) dyad. Nevertheless, the triplet reservoir effect can be exploited in both investigated surroundings. In contrast, the lowest-lying excited state in the Ir(III) dyad is found to be of 3 ππ* pyrene character independently of the environment, as confirmed by transient absorption spectroscopy and temperature-dependent emission measurements, showing a characteristic spectral position and long lifetime of phosphorescence. Moreover, three simultaneously emissive states were revealed in (frozen) solution, whereas pyrene-based phosphorescence is the dominating emission pathway if embedded in KBr. This implies limited interaction of the different excited state manifolds and limited back energy transfer to the 3 MLCT/ 3 LLCT state due to an increased energy gap to the pyrene triplet state. The solvent environment tunes the energy gap, though never reaching efficient back electron transfer necessary to exploit the triplet reservoir. Our work demonstrates the importance of the intricate design of such dyads as well as the complex interplay of steric, electronic, and environmental effects.

papers.title: The unifying Role of the “Oxo Wall” concept in Oxygen Evolution Catalysis
papers.abstract: The rational design of catalytic active sites on the surface of solids enables efficient interfacial proton-electron transfer processes in the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and is thus essential for high-performance water splitting on electrolyzer anodes. Popular examples of rational catalyst designs include the Sabatier principle associated with solid-state quantum-chemistry volcano-type reactivity predictions. The use of molecular unifying concepts to predict and rationalize the design of catalytic active OER sites on solid surfaces is rare. Here, we develop an a priori, chemically informed catalyst-design principle by transferring the oxo-wall concept of molecular coordination chemistry to bimetallic solid catalysts. The molecular “oxo wall” rule essentially states that tetragonal metal complexes with multi-bonded M=O ligands do not exist for metals to the right of group 8. We hypothesize that pairing metals located on opposite sides of the oxo wall creates complementary electronic functionality and leads to enhanced catalytic activity relative to combinations in which both metals lie on the same side. We show that this framework – although rooted in molecular ligand-field effects and developed and validated in coordination chemistry – is capable of predicting and rationalizing reactivity trends of solid-state mixed-metal layered double hydroxides OER catalysts. The very predictive character of the molecular “oxo wall” concept as to reactivity and stability of multiple-bond M-O cores makes it a unifying guiding principle for molecular and solid-state OER catalysis. We anticipate that the cross-disciplinary findings that bridge molecular chemistry and solid-state electrochemistry will help to better design of O 2 -based technologies with improved performance.

papers.title: trans -1,2-Disubstituted Cyclopropanes with CH 2 -Extended Functional Groups: Synthesis and Physicochemical Properties
papers.abstract: An efficient multigram synthesis of trans -1,2-disubstituted cyclopropane derivatives bearing two functional groups (including fluoroalkyl substituents), with one or both of them attached to the ring through a CH 2 spacer, was developed. The strategy was based on a Michael-initiated ring closure reaction (MIRC), followed by functional group transformations to provide a series of over 70 structurally diverse building blocks, including free carboxylic acids, amines, and other synthetically relevant derivatives, on up to 370 g scale. The methodology also enabled the preparation of fluorinated derivatives bearing CH 2 CF 3 , CH 2 CHF 2 , and CH 2 CH 2 F substituents. The combined effect of fluorination and the CH 2 spacer on key physicochemical properties was investigated through acidity/basicity (p K a ) and lipophilicity (Log P ) measurements. It was found that insertion of the spacer between the fluoroalkyl group and the cyclopropane ring increased pKa by 0.5–0.7 units for the carboxylic acids and by 1.1–1.5 units for the protonated amines, whereas its contribution to lipophilicity was lower than expected from additivity. Enumeration of a virtual library based on the proposed building blocks allowed us to demonstrate their potential for lead-oriented synthesis in drug discovery.

papers.title: Multimodal Spectroscopy–Driven Reconstruction of Three-Dimensional Molecular Structures via Conditional Diffusion Model
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) molecular structures underpin molecular function and dynamics. Spectroscopy can encode rich structural information via energy-level transitions, but existing data-driven approaches have largely focused on predicting symbolic representations such as SMILES, or molecular topology rather than reconstructing full 3D structures. Here, we introduce SpecDiffMol, the first generative framework to directly reconstruct full molecular 3D structures from molecular formulae and multimodal spectroscopic data, including infrared, Raman, UV–vis, and NMR spectra. SpecDiffMol integrates a Transformer-based topology inference module with an E(3)-equivariant conditional diffusion model, enabling the inference of molecular connectivity, global structure, and fine-grained conformational geometry in a unified framework. Extensive experiments on large-scale theoretical spectroscopic benchmarks comprising about 400,000 molecules systematically elucidate the complementary roles of individual spectroscopic modalities in determining molecular connectivity, backbone topology, and detailed 3D conformations. By explicitly incorporating spectroscopically informed topological priors, the framework substantially constrains the chemical search space and enables robust structure generation. Meanwhile, SpecDiffMol remains effective under realistic experimental conditions. Using automated experimental spectroscopic measurements, we demonstrate its ability to track Z↔E isomerization dynamics in bridged azobenzenes, capturing conformational transitions and key dihedral angle evolution with high accuracy.
