Central to our strategy is a gold(I)-catalyzed cascade cyclization of a silyl enol ether containing an enyne motif, which simultaneously constructs the fused tricyclo[5.3.1.04,8]undecane core and sets three remote stereocenters. A systematic ligand screening revealed that, in contrast to prior reports, both NHC-type ligands and bulky Buchwald-type phosphines promoted exclusive 5-exo-dig cyclization, indicating a strong substrate-controlled preference that overrides steric and electronic ligand effects. The full sequence proceeds in nine steps from commercially available materials, and the key cyclization step was successfully scaled up to the gram scale. Access to enantioenriched material was achieved via a stereoselective methylcuprate addition catalyzed by a chiral NHC-Ag complex. This work establishes a practical and modular strategy for the synthesis of complex terpenoids and offers new mechanistic insight into ligand-substrate interplay in gold-catalyzed enyne cyclizations.

papers.title: Water-Model Dependence of Absolute Binding Free Energies across the Bromodomain Family
papers.abstract: The choice of explicit water model may affect absolute binding free energy (ABFE) predictions for bromodomains, whose conserved acetyl-lysine pockets contain structured waters. We assembled a benchmark of ten distinct bromodomain–ligand complexes with experimental isothermal titration calorimetry thermodynamics and compared four TIP-family water models, TIP3P, TIP4P, TIP5P, and TIP7P, using a common alchemical protocol. TIP3P gave the lowest point-estimate mean unsigned error (MUE), 1.56 kcal mol−1, against 1.89–2.11 kcal mol−1 for the other models, at the lowest cost. TIP7P correlated best with experiment (r = 0.73), but the experimental affinities span only 2.1 kcal mol−1, about the size of the errors of the models. The 0.55 kcal mol−1 MUE difference between TIP3P and TIP7P had a nominal 95% paired bootstrap interval that excluded zero when only the benchmark composition was resampled, but not when the calculated affinities were perturbed by their sampling-sensitivity measures or the four charged ligands were left out. No other paired difference was resolved, including after finite-size corrections for the charged ligands. The leg decomposition shows that solvent and complex contributions can compensate, so water-model effects must be judged over the complete binding cycle. With one calculation per complex and model, the higher-site TIP models gave no demonstrated accuracy benefit with this force field for 1.4–2.7 times the cost.

papers.title: Second-generation tau PET tracer in situ binding assessed with fluorescence imaging
papers.abstract: Brain positron emission tomography (PET) imaging is a valuable tool which allows visualization of the pathological structures inside the living patients’ brains. While amyloid-β PET tracers have been in use with Alzheimer’s disease patients in clinics, tau PET tracers have still not entered the clinical routine. Second-generation tau PET tracers have been developed with the aim to overcome the limitations of the first-generation tau PET tracers, such as low sensitivity and off-target binding. However, the detailed pathological characterization of these tracers’ binding is still needed for fully understanding their potential as accurate markers of pathogenic tau. Herein, we focused on the second-generation tau PET tracer Genentech Tau Probe 1 ([18F]GTP1) and made use of the fluorescent properties of its non-radioactive unlabeled variant GTP1 for correlative fluorescence microscopy. The results show that GTP1 binds to tau tangles and neuropil threads (NPTs), but not amyloid-β plaques. Importantly, our results indicate that there is a strong correlation between the fluorescent GTP1 signal and the [18F]GTP1 signal detected with autoradiography, which is currently the standard way of studying the tau PET tracer binding in situ. Together, this data shows the robust application of a non-radioactive tau PET tracer in binding studies in post-mortem tissue and sheds new light on the tau binding properties of GTP1.

papers.title: Methyl-Induced Hydrophobicity and Electronically Tuned Copper Nanocluster COF for Highly Selective Nitrate to Ammonia Electrosynthesis
papers.abstract: Electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction (eNO3-RR) offers a promising route for sustainable ammonia production while mitigating nitrate pollution. Yet high NH3 selectivity remains challenging owing to proton-coupled multi-electron transfer pathways and competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Herein, we report a trinuclear Cu nanocluster-based covalent organic framework (CuMePh) featuring methylfunctionalized π-conjugated extended porous framework that provides a molecular-level strategy for modifying the interfacial wettability and electronic environment of the catalytic framework. Benefiting from this modulation strategy, CuMePh exhibits a maximum faradaic efficiency (FE) of 98% for nitrate to ammonia conversion, with an NH3 production rate of 2161 μg h-1 cm-2 (5402.5 μg h-1 mg-1 cat.) at -0.5 V versus RHE under the investigated alkaline conditions. Compared with the non-methylated CuPh analogue, CuMePh also exhibits a higher water contact angle. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the electronenriched Cu3-cluster nodes in CuMePh facilitate nitrate activation and sequential hydrogenation by lowering the free-energy requirement and optimizing intermediates binding, while simultaneously suppressing the competing HER. This work highlights a molecular-level design principle that couples electronic-structure engineering with interfacial-property regulation in nanocluster-based COFs, offering new opportunities for developing highly selective electrocatalysts for sustainable nitrogen-cycle transformations.

papers.title: Programming of Dissipative Networks and Transient Vesicles Using Intrinsic Kinetic Discrimination of Thiol Oxidation
papers.abstract: Programmable dissipative systems that mimic life’s ability to execute timed functions—such as apoptosis triggered by inherent reactivity contrasts—remain a fundamental challenge, as most synthetic designs lack the kinetic complexity to orchestrate multi-step, autonomous sequences. Here, we introduce a synthetic dissipative network in which the intrinsic oxidation kinetics of mono- and dithiols serve as an embedded reaction window to program a cascade of thiol-thioester exchange reactions. This autonomous mechanism dictates reaction timing and sequence, translating molecular-scale kinetic differences into a programmed, system-level response. By extending this principle to the material scale, we further construct fuel-driven, self-assembled vesicles that undergo a life-like cycle of formation, functional execution (as catalytic microreactors), and dissipation. This work establishes intrinsic kinetic hierarchies as a general design paradigm for programming temporal order in non-equilibrium systems, inspiring the development of time-evolving functional materials.

papers.title: Influence of Divalent Cations on the Mechanical Properties of DNA Origami Six-Helix Bundles
papers.abstract: The mechanical behavior of DNA origami nanostructures (DONs) is governed by both design parameters and ionic environment, yet their coupled effects remain poorly understood. Here, atomic force microscopy (AFM)-based contour analysis is used to quantify the persistence length (Lp), contour length (Lc), and end-to-end distance (Ree) of DON six-helix bundles (6HBs) with different staple crossover densities. Non-ligated and ligated 6HBs are compared in the presence of MgCl2 and SrCl2, while oxDNA simulations employing implicit monovalent salt screening help distinguish design-dependent from ion-specific effects. While providing comparable diffuse electrostatic screening, Mg2+ and Sr2+ interact differently with DONs and produce distinct design-dependent mechanical responses. For non-ligated 6HBs, lower Lp values are obtained in Sr2+ than in Mg2+, with the magnitude of the difference depending on crossover density. Paired Ree-versus-Lc analysis further indicates greater bending heterogeneity in Sr2+. In the presence of both cations, ligation may lead to an increase or a decrease in Lp depending on crossover density. Simulations reproduce the opposite ligation responses of the two designs but not the Mg2+-associated behavior, supporting an additional contribution from specific divalent cation interactions. These results establish crossover density, backbone continuity, and cation species as coupled variables whose interplay controls DON mechanics.

papers.title: Improved Prediction of Mössbauer Quadrupole Splitting at High and Low Temperatures with a Quantum Chemical Ensemble Approach
papers.abstract: Mössbauer spectroscopy is a key method for characterizing the electronic structures of iron compounds. The resulting Mössbauer parameters show a well-established temperature dependence. For quantum chemical calculations that are often used to aid in the interpretation of Mössbauer spectra, this poses a major challenge: they commonly employ a single, rigid equilibrium structure that is assumed to deliver good results for low temperatures up to ca. 80 K. In this work, we reveal this approach to be a rather severe approximation. We use a structural sampling approach that captures the effect of temperature dependent molecular vibrations on the quadrupole splitting. Even for low temperatures, this approach delivers a significantly improved agreement with experimental data. In addition, the T-dependence of the quadrupole splitting can be qualitatively reproduced for four iron(II) high spin complexes. The results are analyzed in terms of the individual EFG tensor contributions, which shows the origin of the temperature dependence being rooted in different electronic structures with varying contributions at different temperatures. Limitations in the sampling approach and electronic structure method are discussed. The approach presented herein may provide better agreement with experiment in future in situ and operando studies at low, ambient and elevated temperatures.

papers.title: Charge-Transfer-State Descriptors from Donor–Acceptor Interfaces Enable Improved Prediction of Indoor Organic Photovoltaic Efficiency
papers.abstract: Organic photovoltaic (OPV) devices have attracted significant attention as lightweight, flexible, and solution-processable alternatives to conventional solar cells. In this work, a novel computational workflow was developed to generate donor–acceptor interfacial adducts for non-fullerene acceptor (NFA)-based indoor OPV systems and to investigate their charge-transfer (CT) characteristics using density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent DFT calculations. Molecular docking followed by excited-state analysis enabled identification of important CT descriptors, including excitation energies, electron–hole separation, participation ratios, and charge-transfer characteristics. A dataset containing 30 donor–acceptor pairs were subsequently constructed by combining these CT descriptors with molecular fingerprints and frontier molecular orbital (FMO) parameters. Machine learning (ML) models based on ElasticNet and XGBoost algorithms were then trained to predict OPV power conversion efficiency (PCE). Our results demonstrate that incorporating physically meaningful CT descriptors derived from donor–acceptor interfaces significantly improve the ML-based prediction of OPV efficiencies from a small dataset.

papers.title: Synthesis of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural using sulfonated calix[4]arene in brine and rapid reaction monitoring with micellar capillary electrokinetic chromatography
papers.abstract: The acid-catalyzed dehydration of D-(−)-fructose into 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) and side product levulinic acid (LA) in saturated aqueous sodium chloride was investigated with 1 H quantitative nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy (qNMR) and micellar capillary electrokinetic chromatography (MEKC). The highest isolated HMF yield of 32.7 ± 5.4 % was obtained with 2 mol% sulfonated calix[4]arene (sC4A) from 0.3 M fructose over 4 hours at 140 °C showing modestly improved performance over p -toluenesulfonic acid, methanesulfonic acid, p-hydroxybenzenesulfonic acid, sulfuric acid and hydrochloric acid. Host-guest interactions between sC4A and HMF were investigated with 1 H NMR titrations at different temperatures revealing supramolecular complexation at 30 °C, whereas p -hydroxybenzenesulfonic acid bearing same functional groups but lacking the macrocyclic cavity of sC4A did not show interactions with HMF. A MECK method for the HMF analysis from acidic reaction mixtures was developed reaching limit of detection and limit of quantification values of 0.003 mM and 0.009 mM, respectively. Here we demonstrate that MEKC can be used to track the production of HMF at the concentration range 0.1–10 mM within a total analysis time of 2 minutes.

papers.title: A Physics-Informed Fourier Neural Operator Framework for Zero-Plating Fast Charging of Lithium-Ion Batteries via Real-Time Electrochemical State Estimation and Barrier-Riding Optimal Control
papers.abstract: Extreme fast charging of lithium-ion batteries is critically limited by internal lithium plating at the negative electrode-separator interface, driving rapid degradation and thermal hazards. Real-time mitigation is fundamentally impeded because the interfacial plating overpotential (ηplating) is inaccessible to non-invasive sensors, leaving conventional protocols blind to metallic lithium deposition. While high-fidelity Doyle–Fuller–Newman (DFN) models resolve these dynamics, their computational cost (∼ 8 s) precludes embedded closed-loop control, whereas empirical equivalent circuit models lack the spatial resolution to detect plating. To resolve this trade-off, we develop a physics-informed 1D Fourier Neural Operator (FNO-1D) surrogate incorporating an explicit cumulative charge integral Q(t) = ∫ I dt to preserve mass conservation. Trained on 7,771 continuum DFN trajectories, the surrogate achieves a 4, 349× speedup (1.84 ms inference) with high fidelity (V RMSE = 5.40 mV, η plating , RMSE = 2.24 mV). Coupled with an Ensemble Smoother with Multiple Data Assimilation (ESMDA), the framework filters sensor noise (±10 mV to 5.94 mV) and reconstructs unobservable plating dynamics (RMSE = 4.12 mV, 95% CI = ±3.22 mV), establishing continuous closed-loop observability. A Barrier-Riding Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) policy then maximizes charging current along the degradation boundary. Across a 10% - 80% SOC window, it cuts charging time by 21.7% (33.7 min vs. 43.0 min CC-CV)while strictly preventing lithium plating (η plating ≥ +14.81 mV > +5.0 mV), limiting peak temperature to 38.5◦C, and decreasing SEI growth by 21.5%. Finally, transferability is experimentally validated across two phys ical cycler benchmarks: cross-chemistry transfer on Oxford pouch cells, and chemistry-matched validation on commercial RWTH Aachen Sanyo 18650 NMCcells, achieving a terminal voltage tracking RMSE of 33.02 mV (86.0% error reduction over zero-shot transfer) providing an experimentally grounded paradigm for degradation-free fast charging.

papers.title: Fluoroalkynes: The Last Frontier of Organofluorine Chemistry?
papers.abstract: Molecules containing carbon-fluorine bonds are of global importance in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals and polymers and are widely studied. However, little is known about fluoroalkynes where a fluorine atom is directly bonded to a carbon atom that forms part of a carbon-carbon triple bond. Pioneering studies in the 20th century established that these compounds are typically unstable, but their chemistry has remained largely unexplored to date. Here, we outline methods to prepare a diverse range of fluoroalkynes for the first time, rationalize the reasons behind their low stability, and demonstrate six different classes of reactions of fluoroalkynes and their difluorocyclobutadiene dimers.

papers.title: Copper-Catalyzed Asymmetric Remote ε-Arylation/Cyclization of Yne-Indole Esters with 5-Aminopyrazoles toward Polycyclic Fused Seven-Membered Azaheterocycles
papers.abstract: Chiral Cu-catalyzed asymmetric remote ε-arylation/cyclization of yne-indole esters with 5-aminopyrazoles is reported to construct polycyclic fused seven-membered azaheterocycles. After systematic screening of copper sources, chiral ligands, bases and temperature protocols, the optimized CuCl2/L12/DABCO system delivers products in good yields and high enantioselectivities. This transformation exhibits broad substrate compatibility, and steric/electronic effects on stereocontrol are discussed.

papers.title: High-Valent Copper(III) Cyanide Tetramer Stabilized by Trifluoromethyl Ligands and its Multifaceted Reactivity
papers.abstract: High-valent neutral copper(III) complexes are highly elusive species with strong Lewis acidic properties and high effective nuclear charge. Herein, an unprecedented copper(III) cyanide [Cu(CF3)2(CN)]4 stabilized in a tetrameric square-like scaffold with bridging cyanide ligands was isolated and fully characterized in the form of tetrahydrate [Cu(CF3)2(CN)(H2O)]4, including X-ray crystallography. This tetrameric scaffold is stable to Lewis bases, while the apical ligands easily undergo substitution to acetonitrile and cis-trans isomerization in the presence of acetone. Lewis acidity of copper(III) cyanides – hypothetical Cu(CF3)2(CN) and a tetrameric scaffold [Cu(CF3)2(CN)]4 – was evaluated by experimental and computational methods. Relevance of the [Cu(CF3)2(CN)(solv)]4 scaffold for carbon-carbon bond formation was demonstrated by spontaneous reductive elimination of CF3CN at room temperature in high yield, and trifluoromethylation of a boronic acid.

papers.title: Phosphorus-Mediated Optical Defect Engineering in Single-walled Carbon Nanotubes
papers.abstract: Defect engineering of single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) offers a versatile strategy for tailoring their optical properties through localized chemical modification. However, expanding the range of accessible defect chemistries beyond established oxygen- and aryl-based functionalities remains an important challenge. Here, we report a straightforward, light-driven strategy for introducing phosphorus-derived defects into (6,5)-enriched SWCNTs using triphenylphosphine (TPP) and a photosensitizing dye. Ultraviolet irradiation in the presence of TPP and eosin Y generates a new near-infrared emission feature centered at 1125 nm, assigned to a defect-associated emissive state (E11*), alongside the intrinsic nanotube emission at 997 nm. The formation of this state depends on the TPP concentration, photosensitizer concentration, and irradiation time, and is accompanied by attenuation of the intrinsic optical transition and an increase in the Raman D/G intensity ratio, indicating progressive structural modification of the nanotube framework. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveals a phosphorus-associated chemical state and changes in the carbon chemical environment, supporting phosphorus incorporation and the formation of modified carbon sites. Control experiments further demonstrate that defect formation requires both photosensitization and irradiation, is enhanced under oxygen-depleted conditions, and is suppressed by radical scavenging, consistent with a radical-mediated photochemical pathway. Complementary density functional theory calculations support the formation of a covalent carbon–phosphorus bond, accompanied by a change in phosphorus coordination from three- to four-coordinate, and reveal a phosphorus-associated electronic trap state near the valence-band edge. These findings establish phosphorus-mediated defect engineering as a complementary approach to tailoring SWCNT optical properties and provide a foundation for investigating the relationships between defect chemistry, localized electronic states, and near-infrared emission.

papers.title: Non-Markovian Memory Kernels in Condensed-Phase Chemical Dynamics: From Dipole Dephasing and Conical Intersections to Spin Crossover and Radical-Pair Magnetoreception
papers.abstract: Standard theoretical formulations of ultrafast condensed-phase molecular processes rely heavily on Markovian master equations and time-local Lindblad semigroups that assume memoryless bath relaxation (t ≫ τB). However, in viscous solvents, structured protein binding pockets, and biomolecular matrices, environmental fluctuations exhibit power-law algebraic memory tails K(t) ∝ t−µ (µ ∈ (0, 1)) where Markovian approximations break down. In this work, we develop an analytical and computational framework for non-Markovian chemical dynamics governed by the causal Caputo fractional memory kernel of the Multi-Electron Unified Wave Equation (MEUWE). We apply this framework across five benchmark regimes of contemporary chemical physics. First, in molecular dipole autocorrelation dynamics, fractional dephasing replaces exponential Markovian damping with Mittag-Leffler decay Eµ (−Γ0 τ0µ tµ), extending the 10% electronic coherence lifetime by 13.40× (134.15 fs vs. 10.01 fs in H2), while coupled-channel Volterra equations achieve a benchmark vertical excitation mean absolute error (MAE) of 37.85 meV across pyscf Full Configuration Interaction (FCI) benchmarks with exact zero self-interaction error on one-electron ions (0.00 meV vs. TD-B3LYP 1884.37 meV). Second, at the 2D two-state conical intersection governing ultrafast rhodopsin retinal photoisomerization, viscoelastic solvent memory generates a +24.75 fs delay in non-adiabatic transition onset while suppressing coherent recoil back-transfer by up to 99.7% and preserving an all-trans photoproduct quantum yield of 62.625%. Third, in avian cryptochrome magnetoreception, fractional sub-Ohmic spin-bath relaxation delays singlet-triplet dephasing, producing an anisotropic magnetic compass contrast gain of 11.27× (and up to 266.94× at low fields) relative to standard exponential models. Fourth, in [Fe(bpy)3]2+ spin crossover, exact Stieltjes–Laplace inversion yields an asymmetric Fuoss–Kirkwood distribution of relaxation lifetimes spanning 2.288 decades of full-width at half-maximum (FWHM). Finally, on chemical reaction barriers, fractional Grote–Hynes transmission theory predicts a non-monotonic Kramers turnover with enhanced dynamic barrier transmission κGH = 0.513620 (vs. Markovian Kramers 0.242536). These results establish a unified, non-Markovian foundation for condensed-phase photochemistry, quantum biology, and barrier-crossing kinetics.

papers.title: PerMix: Algorithmic Pathway Planning for Multicomponent Halide Perovskite Synthesis
papers.abstract: The reproducible growth of multicomponent halide perovskite single crystals depends critically on the stoichiometry of the precursor solution: even small deviations introduced during weighing or dissolution can change phase purity, defect density, and the lattice parameters of the resulting crystals. Today, recipes for such systems are still planned largely by hand in spreadsheets, which are error-prone, difficult to audit, and impractical for the compositional spaces of multicomponent solid solutions. We present PerMix, an open-source Python framework that formalizes precursor planning as a constrained mass-balance problem and solves it transparently. The stoichiometric model, the combinatorial enumeration of precursor pathways based on a rigid/flexible partition of cations, tolerance-based validation, deduplication of identical salt formulations, deterministic ranking of pathways, geometric stability indicators (Goldschmidt tolerance and octahedral factors), and the SQLite reference database are described in full, with every governing equation stated explicitly. The tool was used to grow nine (MA1−xCsx)Pb(Br1−zYz)3 (Y = Cl, I) single crystals by antisolvent vapor-assisted crystallization; X-ray diffraction shows the systematic lattice expansion and contraction expected from the nominal substitutions. We also discuss the limits of the approach explicitly: precursor stoichiometry does not account for ion segregation, and quantitative composition analysis as well as homogeneity profiling are identified as future work.

papers.title: An [Fe32] molecular metal oxide
papers.abstract: Reaction of [Fe16] with 3-chloropyridine results in formation of an [Fe32] cluster, whose magnetic skeleton describes interwoven triangular and square tilings, demonstrating that pre-formed molecular iron oxides can be used as starting materials to access new species. Magnetic measurements reveal competing antiferromagnetic exchange interactions, resulting in significant spin frustration.

papers.title: VHH-Bench: A Benchmarking Framework for Evaluating Nanobody–Antigen Complex Predictions Across CDR3 Conformations
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of nanobody–antigen complex structures is critical for the development of diagnostic, therapeutic and biosensing applications. However, progress in this area have been constrained by the limited availability of experimentally determined nanobody–antigen complex structures. Recent advances in deep learning have enabled highly accurate prediction of protein structures and protein-protein complexes, yet accurate modelling of nanobody–antigen interactions remains challenging due to the diverse binding modes exhibited by nanobodies. Here, we present VHH‑Bench, a benchmarking workflow for the systematic evaluation of nanobody–antigen complex structure prediction methods. We curated a non-redundant dataset of experimentally resolved nanobody–antigen complexes and evaluated six state-of-the-art models: AlphaFold3, Boltz-2, Chai-1, ESMFold2, HelixFold3 and Protenix-v2. Complexes were stratified according to CDR3 conformation, enabling separate assessment of kinked and extended nanobody classes. Prediction performance varied substantially between models and conformational classes. Protenix-v2 achieved the highest overall docking accuracy, success rate and proportion of high-quality predictions, with its advantage most pronounced for nanobodies with extended CDR3 conformations. In contrast, all evaluated models showed reduced accuracy and higher failure rates for complexes containing kinked nanobodies. While increased stochastic sampling provided slight improvements in some cases, its overall impact was limited and did not substantially affect the relative performance ranking of the evaluated models. VHH-Bench provides an extensible and reproducible benchmarking workflow for standardised dataset curation, nanobody classification, model evaluation and confidence analysis, facilitating the rigorous assessment and future development of nanobody–antigen complex prediction methods. The VHH-Bench framework is available at https://github.com/haiboyugroup/VHH-Bench.

papers.title: Precursor Formulation Redirects Phase Competition and Thermal Evolution in Silver Multinary Chalcogenide Ag-M-Ch (M = Zr, Cr, Sn, Sb) Nanocrystals
papers.abstract: Multinary nanocrystal synthesis requires chemically dissimilar metals to enter a common framework while competing with binary crystallization and metal reduction. We examine this competition through 31 preparation records spanning nominal Ag8SnS6, Ag4Zr3S8, AgZrSe2, AgCrSe2, and Ag3SbS3 targets in an oleylamine–octadecene platform. In a matched Ag–Zr–S comparison at 240 °C for 20 min, replacing an elemental-sulfur-derived stock with trioctylphosphine sulfide redirects a dense diffraction fingerprint toward a sparse fcc-Ag-compatible series. Comparison with independently identified crystallographic records further reveals substantial overlap of the sulfide and selenide fingerprints with acanthite Ag2S and published metastable P21/n Ag2Se, respectively. Microscopy resolves condition-dependent morphology, local lattice order, and elemental association within selected fields. Calorimetric heating and cooling traces reveal preparation-dependent responses, with ten individually resolved higher-temperature events at 88.63–176.33 °C. Annealing at 300 °C for 2 h under Ar yields composition-dependent morphological endpoints; two interpretable diffraction pairs distinguish persistence of an Ag-compatible component from redistribution of a more complex Ag–Sb–S fingerprint. The results identify precursor formulation as a control over competing crystalline pathways and show why thermal sensitivity must be interpreted in the context of those pathways. This comparative library connects reaction design with structural discrimination and subsequent processing response in silver-containing chalcogenides.

papers.title: Homogeneous–Heterogeneous Hybrid Oxidation Catalysis Based on Multiple Adsorption Enabling Efficient Aerobic Amide Oxygenation
papers.abstract: Homogeneous–heterogeneous combined catalysts, such as immobilized homogeneous catalysts and single-atom catalysts (SACs), have been developed to improve catalytic performance and practicality and elucidate catalytic mechanisms. However, achieving new catalytic functions beyond those of the individual components remains challenging. Homogeneous–heterogeneous hybrid catalysis offers a contrasting approach: homogeneous catalysts can coordinate/adsorb onto heterogeneous catalysts, allowing the two components to cooperate and potentially enable new catalytic processes for efficient molecular transformations. Nevertheless, reports of such hybrid catalysis remain limited, particularly for oxidation catalysis. We achieved effective homogeneous–heterogeneous hybrid oxidation catalysis by adsorbing a homogeneous phthalimide N-oxyl (PINO) radical catalyst onto a supported heterogeneous Pd nano-(hydr)oxide catalyst, enabling efficient aerobic α-oxygenation of structurally diverse amides (up to 99% yield; 15 examples). This hybrid oxidation system also accommodated amides that possess α-C–H bonds with high bond dissociation energies and are challenging substrates for previously reported amide α-oxygenation systems, including those involving direct hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) by PINO. Comprehensive characterization, control experiments, kinetic studies, and detailed comparisons with Co-catalyzed systems and Pd SACs support that the hybrid radical species formed on the Pd nano-(hydr)oxide surface through PINO adsorption efficiently facilitate HAT of amides via their coadsorption at nearby Pd sites.

papers.title: UNDERSTANDING THE ROLE OF AROMATICITY IN TAUTOMERIC EQUILIBRIA
papers.abstract: Tautomerism, the interconversion of small molecules via proton and π-electron shifts, poses a fundamental challenge in drug discovery, as different tautomers can exhibit distinct physicochemical properties and receptor-binding profiles, while computational approaches have been widely applied to predict tautomeric equilibria, most methods often overlook electronic properties such as aromaticity, which are critical to molecular stability. Here, we explore the role of aromaticity in tautomeric equilibria using a computational framework that integrates density functional theory (DFT) calculations with interpretable machine learning (ML) models. Aromaticity, which is challenging to measure experimentally, is quantified via Harmonics Oscillator Model of Aromaticity (HOMA) values and incorporated as a molecular descriptor. To enhance interpretability, we employ shallow ML models and assess feature contributions both intrinsically and using post-hoc explainability techniques. Our results demonstrate that both intrinsic and post hoc feature importance approaches capture similar trends associated with aromaticity. This highlights the complex influence of aromaticity on tautomeric equilibria and suggest that ML models, when combined with quantum-mechanics-based descriptors and explainable feature analyses, could be applied more broadly to capture important trends in other physicochemical properties beyond tautomer stability.

papers.title: HF· · ·H2S Hydrogen-Bonded Clusters as a Model for Probing Subtle Cooperative Effects
papers.abstract: Hydrogen-bond (HB) cooperativity is usually analysed for whole networks, and its variation between individual HBs is poorly understood when strong and weak donors coexist. We resolve 126 HBs in 20 neutral cyclic (HF)m(H2S)n clusters (Nmon = m + n = 3–7). The molecular tailoring approach (MTA) at the MP2/aug-ccpVTZ level splits each in-cluster HB energy into an isolated-dimer part and a network-associated (cooperative) part. The mean MTA energies of the F–H· · ·F, F–H· · · S, S–H· · · F and S–H· · · S bonds are 9.03, 8.47, 2.57 and 2.45 kcal mol−1, respectively. The cooperative part averages 2.11 kcal mol−1 per HB and is positive for nearly all HBs. In these structures, it correlates more strongly with HF content than with cluster size and changes little beyond five monomers. The cooperativity gain index, the cooperative part divided by the isolated-dimer energy, identifies fluorine-accepting HBs as the most enhanced, and S–H· · · F bonds stand out among the weakly bound dimers. For HF-donor HBs, the MTA energy correlates strongly with the H· · ·A distance and the electron density at the bond critical point. By the criteria of the quantum theory of atoms in molecules, these HBs are medium-strength interactions with partial covalent character, whereas the H2S-donor HBs are weak closed-shell interactions that local descriptors predict less well. The HB-resolved energies provide reference data for testing interaction models and machine-learning potentials; applying them to atmospheric or astrochemical systems requires further work.

papers.title: Chemoselective Copper(l)-Catalyzed 1,2-Reduction of Conjugated Amides by a Molecular Recognition Strategy
papers.abstract: The selective 1,2-reduction of conjugated amides represents an elusive transformation, owing to the intrinsically low reactivity of the amide group and competing conjugate reduction. Here, we report an unprecedented copper(I)-catalyzed hydrogenation of conjugated amides that selectively furnishes allylic alcohols using molecular hydrogen as the terminal reductant. A bifunctional copper catalyst exploits molecular recognition of a privileged amide motif to enable reduction of the amide functionality while preserving the conjugated alkene, thereby reversing the chemoselectivity commonly associated with copper hydride catalysis. The method provides access to a range of aromatic, heteroaromatic, aliphatic, and conformationally restricted allylic alcohols and tolerates additional reducible functionalities. Mechanistic studies reveal a decisive interplay between base-mediated E/Z isomerization and selective recognition and hydrogenation of the E-configured substrate. Moreover, isolation of a conjugated aldehyde intermediate supports a stepwise pathway involving amide reduction, C–N bond cleavage, and subsequent aldehyde hydrogenation. These results establish molecular recognition as a strategy to unlock otherwise inaccessible chemoselectivity in catalytic hydrogenation.

papers.title: Hydroxyurea synthesis using resonant acoustic mixing in ethanol
papers.abstract: Hydroxyurea derivatives have important medicinal utility acting as enzyme inhibitors and anticancer agents. Their syntheses have, however, entailed low yielding routes employing long reaction times and toxic reagents such as phosgene. Towards sustainable and environmentally benign hydroxyurea synthesis, a one-step hydroxycarbamoylation approach is described employing resonant acoustic mixing (RAM) to expedite reactions at higher concentration. Eighteen medicinally relevant hydroxyurea were synthesized in 68-91% yields using ethanol as green solvent.

papers.title: Adsorption–Absorption Polymer Purification (AAPP): A Mass Transfer Strategy for Removing Residual Monomer from Synthetic Polymers
papers.abstract: After polymerization, synthetic polymers frequently contain residual monomers, solvents, and other low molar mass compounds that can adversely affect material properties and subsequent applications. Their removal remains challenging, as conventional purification methods such as precipitation and dialysis are often time-consuming, difficult to standardize, and generate substantial amounts of solvent waste. Herein, an Adsorption–Absorption Polymer Purification (AAPP) method that combines a polymer immobilization through physisorption with a selective extraction of the corresponding residual monomer (or compounds) into a nonsolvent phase is introduced. Model polymers were employed to evaluate the performance of AAPP and to identify suitable operating conditions. Quantitative proton nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy (1H NMR) demonstrated near-complete removal of residual monomers within comparatively short purification times while preserving the molecular characteristics of the polymers. Furthermore, the purified polymers were recovered in high yields and successfully employed as precursors for subsequent block copolymer syntheses, confirming the retention of their functionality. It is also demonstrated that AAPP can be efficiently utilized for, at least, the multigram scale production of specialty polymers. These results demonstrate that AAPP provides an effective and versatile strategy for polymer purification and highlight the potential of coupling absorption and adsorption to mitigate transport limitations in purification processes.

papers.title: Resolving Ultrafast Carrier-to-Exciton Conversion in CsPbBr3 Nanocrystals Formed from Solid-State Photochemistry
papers.abstract: Photoinduced conversion provides an alternative pathway to form CsPbBr3 nanocrystals from their twodimensional analogues, nanoplatelets, using optical excitation in the solid phase. Although this transformation has been previously observed, it is unclear how the ultrafast dynamics of excitons in the resulting nanocrystals compare with those of CsPbBr3 nanocrystals synthesized in solution. In this study, we used femtosecond pump-probe spectroscopy to monitor the photoinduced conversion of n = 2 CsPbBr3 nanoplatelets in real time and investigate the charge carrier dynamics of the resulting nanocrystals. To investigate the processes that dominate the excited-state dynamics, we performed excitation-density-dependent pump-probe measurements and analyzed the transient kinetics using singular value decomposition methods. From this analysis, we identified two characteristic decay associated spectra connected to charge carrier cooling following photoexcitation. Comparison of these spectra with literature reports indicates that nanocrystals generated through photoinduced conversion exhibited carrier relaxation pathways similar to those of CsPbBr3 nanocrystals prepared by conventional colloidal synthesis. Our results provide insight into the ultrafast photophysics of photoinduced CsPbBr3 nanocrystals and established a connection between their formation through photoinduced conversion in the solid-state and the excited-state dynamics of similar materials synthesized through conventional solution-phase methods.

papers.title: Wigner Momentum Estimation and Sampling with Local Modes: A Second-Moment Approximation to High-Frequency Momentum Marginals
papers.abstract: Instantaneous local Gaussian approximations assign nuclear momentum widths from the curvature of the potential at each sampled configuration. Strongly compressed bonds can consequently acquire large momentum widths even when their positions are drawn from an anharmonic path-integral ensemble. We estimate momentum covariances from pathintegral coordinates and forces in local modes that follow molecular deformations. These covariances define Gaussian approximations to high-frequency Wigner momentum marginals without evaluating a Hessian at each configuration. The resulting sampling recovers the Maxwell momentum distribution in the classical limit. A rotating bond model with harmonic stretching and periodic torsion agrees with an independent quantum reference within statistical uncertainty. For trans-azobenzene at 300 K with 32 beads, the most compressed C–H bond receives a mass-weighted momentum variance of 36.53 kJ mol−1 from LGA and 19.55 kJ mol−1 from the local covariance along the same physical stretch direction. Temporal holdout errors in C–H second moments are 7.2–7.6%, compared with 2.2–5.1% for LGA relative to the finite-bead reference; the demonstrated benefit concerns the suppression of local width spikes. The largest collective C–H width remains sensitive to estimator noise. These results support the method as an approximation to high-frequency momentum widths without a frequency cap. Position-conditioned quantum correlations, non-Gaussian tails, and the continuum-bead molecular limit remain outside the demonstrated accuracy.

papers.title: Deterministic Preparation of Intermolecular Spin States Through Collective Light Emission in Copper Porphyrin Aggregates
papers.abstract: The coupling of electron spins in open shell systems drives formation of distinct singlet and triplet states whose transitions possess unique coherence properties relative to those of doublets. Here we show that exchange interactions couple the electron spins on neighboring Cu cations within porphyrins macrocycles that participate in aggregate formation. Following photoexcitation, we find a ‘low field’ EPR signal whose peak position and shape are reproduced by simulations of anti-ferromagnetically coupled electron spins. We use time-resolved light emission and EPR results to propose that this ‘low field’ peak appears due to a singlet to triplet transition that results in selective, deterministic population of the lowest energy state in the coupled spin system. Our results highlight how enhanced radiative relaxation in molecular aggregates ligated with open shell transition metal cations can be used to design the coupled spin states that participate in EPR transitions. This design principle could be used to further extend the use of molecular chromophores in quantum information science and technology applications.

papers.title: Predicting excess solvation in binary solvents toward green organic semiconductor processing
papers.abstract: Replacing halogenated solvents in organic semiconductor inks benefits from binary mixtures that balance dissolution and film drying, yet mixing changes solvation beyond the pure-solvent contributions. Here, we introduce ShellEx, a three-dimensional contact-shell model distilled from openCOSMO-RS that predicts this endpoint-fixed excess solvation from force-field geometries. Trained on 10,640 calculated curves for aromatic cores resembling organic semiconductors, ShellEx reduces the error by 27% on held-out curves relative to a zero-excess reference, which interpolates linearly between pure-solvent free energies. On 148 measured curves of eight solutes, its error, averaged with equal weight per solute, is similar to that of openCOSMO-RS and below that of simpler baselines. An openCOSMO-RS map of 200 solvent pairs for 35 cores ranks limonene–γ-valerolactone first among six predefined candidate-green pairs, with a median 1.35-fold concentration gain over the zero-excess reference. ShellEx selects the same pair and reproduces the pair ranking with a Spearman correlation of 0.85. ShellEx thus offers a route to prioritize green binary solvent pairs and compositions for halogen-free organic semiconductor inks before experimental testing.

papers.title: Interstitial Oxygen and a Two-Dimensional Migration Pathway in Mo-Substituted Palmierite Ba <sub>3</sub> V <sub>2−x</sub> Mo <sub>x</sub> O <sub>8+x/2</sub>
papers.abstract: Palmierite oxides are promising oxide-ion conductors, with conductivities exceeding those of related hexagonal perovskite derivatives. However, aliovalent Mo6+ substitution in Ba 3 V 2 O 8 has previously been demonstrated only at high substitution levels. Here, the Ba 3 V 2-x Mo x O 8+x/2 series (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.3) was investigated using X-ray and neutron powder diffraction, 51 V and 17 O solid-state NMR spectroscopy combined with density functional theory (DFT), and bond-valence site-energy (BVSE) calculations. Combined Rietveld refinement reveals that Mo6+ substitution introduces a charge-compensating interstitial oxygen site (O3) at x = 0.3, transforming isolated (V, Mo)O 4 tetrahedra into corner-sharing polyhedra with mixed coordination. DFT-supported 17 O NMR identifies additional oxygen environments associated with Mo in four- and five-fold coordination, suggesting oxygen bridges between adjacent MoO5 polyhedra. 51 V NMR confirms predominantly tetrahedral vanadium coordination, alongside a minority V environment , distorted by occupation of a nearby O3 site. BVSE calculations indicate that O3 bridges neighboring polyhedra in the abplane, enabling a low-barrier, two-dimensional oxide-ion migration pathway involving apical O1 and interstitial O3 sites. These findings establish interstitial oxygen incorporation as the key structural mechanism facilitating low-barrier two-dimensional oxide-ion transport at low Mo substitution levels in the palmierite family, with broader implications for hexagonal perovskite ionic conductors.

papers.title: Imbalanced burner heat release for enhanced ethylene yield in industrial-scale cracking furnaces
papers.abstract: Symmetric burner arrangements with uniform heat release are the default design for cracking furnaces. However, the present study reveals that this symmetric layout leads to inferior heating conditions and reduced ethylene yields in specific coils. Therefore, an imbalanced heating strategy is proposed: side burners are grouped by location, with the fuel flow rate of Group L set to four times that of Group R while maintaining the same total fuel consumption. This approach increases the heat load on the disadvantaged coils by up to 2.65% and boosts their ethylene yields by nearly 10%, improving the overall average yield by 4.09%. Remarkably, even with Group R fully shut off, the averaged ethylene yield increases by 3.86%, demonstrating that highly imbalanced heating strategy outperforms the conventional symmetric arrangement. Given the limited yield improvements achieved under the conventional framework over decades, a new operational philosophy for high-efficiency cracking furnaces is warranted.

papers.title: The Multi-Electron Unified Wave Equation in Quantum Chemistry: Symmetrized Riesz Exchange Kernels, Sobolev Domain Classification, and O(N4) Quasiparticle Electronic Structure across Bond Dissociation
papers.abstract: A central challenge in ab initio electronic structure theory is capturing both short-range dynamic electron correlation (the Kato inter-electronic cusp) and long-range static multireference correlation across covalent bond dissociation without incurring the exponential O(exp N) cost of Full Configuration Interaction (FCI), the O(N⁶) cost and single-reference breakdown of Coupled Cluster Singles and Doubles (CCSD), or the one-electron self-interaction error (SIE) of Density Functional Theory (DFT). In this work (the first of two companion papers on the Multi-Electron Unified Wave Equation, MEUWE), we formulate and rigorously analyze the closed-system stationary sector of MEUWE as an ab initio two-electron correlation theory. First, we establish a foundational No-Go result against nonlinear state powers Ψᵖ (p ≠ 1) and unscaled nonlocal kernels (Proposition II.1), and establish operator uniqueness of the Jordan-symmetrized Riesz exchange kernel K̂sym = ½ ∑ᵢ₍ⱼ₎ {Ŵᵢ, r₀ᵅ|rᵢ − rⱼ|⁻ᵅ P̂ᵢⱼ} within the bilinear screening-permutation pencil P_W,K, showing that unsymmetrized operators ŴᵢV̂ᵅP̂ᵢⱼ violate Hermiticity (ΔHerm ∈ [1.68, 3.76]) and leak fermion states outside the Pauli sector ∧ᴺL²(R³) (Theorem III.1). Second, we establish a four-regime functional-analytic self-adjointness classification of Ĥ₀ + ΛK̂sym on ∧ᴺL²(R³): operator Kato–Rellich self-adjointness on H²(R³ᴺ) for α ∈ (0, 3/2), quadratic-form KLMN self-adjointness on H¹(R³ᴺ) via Hardy’s inequality for α ∈ [3/2, 2) (including our canonical α = 3/2), the critical Hardy threshold at α = 2, and bounded-density L¹ ∩ L∞ expectation finiteness for α ∈ (2, 3) with ultraviolet divergence at α ≥ 3. Third, for closed bound states below the excitation threshold (Eₙ < Eₜₕ), we prove via Feshbach–Schur resolvent projection that integrating out the virtual excitation continuum yields a strictly real, Hermitian, energy-dispersive quasiparticle self-energy Σₘₑₘ(E) = Λγₘₑₘ(E)K̂sym whose self-consistent fixed point converges geometrically via Banach contraction (qₘₐₓ = 0.091226 < 1, error 4.44 × 10⁻¹⁵ Ha in ≤ 13 iterations, matching exact Stinespring resolvent poles to 5.82 × 10⁻⁷ Ha, Theorem III.5). Fourth, using exact 6D Mellin–Laplace Gaussian integrals implemented in PySCF/libcint, we verify that MEUWE is 100% self-interaction-free on all one-electron ions Z = 1 … 6 (|ΔE| ≤ 2.66 × 10⁻¹² mHa) and achieves an overall correlation RMSE of 0.3824 mHa across the Z = 2 … 6 two-electron isoelectronic series (7.31× more accurate than MP2, Section III C 1). Finally, freezing all parameters strictly at the two-electron Helium calibration (α = 1.50, μ = 0.606503, Λ₀ = 0.01150) with zero molecule-fitted parameters and zero FCI calls, our standalone O(N⁴) Dyson pair solver reproduces exact FCI potential energy surfaces across H₂, HeH⁺, and LiH (R ∈ [0.5, 3.0] Å) with mean absolute errors of 0.1382, 0.1618, and 0.1302 mHa, captures the avoided-crossing ionic-to-neutral dipole turnover in LiH (μ(3.0 Å) = 5.0398 D vs. FCI 5.0265 D where RHF diverges to 9.1647 D, Section III C 2), and resolves atomic K/L shell structures and Coulson–Neilson Coulomb holes across H–Ne (Section III C 3).

papers.title: ChemEidos: Synthesis-Aware Multimodal Foundation Models for Domain-Specific Generative Design
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence models for de novo drug discovery often suffer synthetic tractability issues and lack fidelity in underrepresented chemical domains. This white paper highlights ChemEidos, a novel multimodal generative design platform that utilizes the underlying patterns, forms, and organizing principles of chemical space (eidos) by incorporating expert domain knowledge in focused training sets and at inference time.

papers.title: Transferable Quasiparticle Correlation, Subtractive Multireference Embedding for Biradicaloid Ozone, and Retarded Casimir–Polder Dispersion in Multi-Electron Systems
Airborne Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons (PAHs) in 20 Homes Several Months After the 2023 Maui Wildfires
papers.abstract: Exposure to polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) is associated with adverse health outcomes, including cancer. PAHs are emitted by wildfires and may persist in indoor environments following smoke events. To better understand post-wildfire PAH persistence inside residences, we sampled for 16 airborne PAHs at 20 homes in Lāhainā, Hawaiʻi, 5-7 months after the 2023 Maui wildfires, both before and after deploying an additional air purifier on top of existing indoor filtration and purification systems. Additionally, we surveyed building occupants about pollution-relevant behaviors. Concentrations of all indoor airborne PAHs fell below risk-based screening levels. Estimated cumulative cancer risks and hazard indices were all below 1 × 10-6 and 1, respectively. We found higher concentrations of low-molecular-weight PAHs than highmolecular-weight PAHs. The results of source attribution using indoor/outdoor ratios, principal component analysis, and diagnostic ratios are somewhat equivocal, but we could not clearly identify a biomass-combustion-related source of the indoor airborne PAHs. We found little association between self-reported occupant behaviors and PAH levels, and we found no significant effect of the air purifier on indoor PAH concentraties. These results suggest that there was not substantial fire-related airborne PAH contamination inside local residences several months after a major wildfire event.

papers.title: mzView : visualizing mass spectrometry data in the browser
papers.abstract: Routine inspection of raw mass spectrometry data is limited to installed desktop software which often needs high memory, security updates, compatible operating system, and hard-drive space. Existing web-based tools require uploading raw data files to a server. To address this, we introduce mzView, a zero-installation web application featuring client-side modules for visualizing mass spectrometry data files covering Data Dependent Acquisition (DDA), Data Independent Acquisition (DIA), Imaging, and Ion-mobility acquisitions. mzView supports mzML, imzML, MSP, Bruker (.d) file formats. It enables multi-target extraction ion chromatograms (EICs) with MS2-event overlays and isotope- and adduct-driven EIC visualization ; global filtering of DDA MS2 spectra by precursor and fragment ions; DIA fragment EICs by isolation window and fragment co-occurrence; and rapid in-browser MSP library parsing and filtering. Ion-mobility and imaging data are visualized using WebGL GPU based faster rendering. To assist in spectra annotation, mzView searches spectra against the IDSL spectral database of over 50,000 compounds curated from publicly available mass spectral databases, scored by spectral entropy and cosine similarity with interactive mirror plots. Accepted hits can be saved to a browser-local annotation library, edited, re-searched, and exported as MSP files. Demonstrated on publicly available DDA and DIA data files of NIST SRM 1950 plasma acquired on a SCIEX ZenoTOF 8600, and additional data collected using Bruker timsTOF Metabo and MALDI- Pro Ultra 2 instruments, mzView readily handles files up to 35 GB, with indexing, filtering, and EIC extraction completing in less than 60 seconds. mzView is freely available at https://mzview.org (License: CC-BY).

papers.title: Disentangling Between-Target and Within-Target Signal in PPI Benchmarking
papers.abstract: Pooled correlation, the metric usually reported when predicting mutation effects on protein–protein binding affinity (ΔΔG), mixes two different capabilities: placing targets on a common binding scale and ranking mutations correctly within a target. We formulate an exact between-/within-target covariance decomposition for PPI ΔΔG benchmarking, r = C_B + C_W, and apply it to matched, provenance-filtered evaluation sets. In a controlled comparison that changes only the split regime, on identical 7,523 mutation rows and identical model configurations, median pooled Pearson falls from 0.6844 under random splitting to 0.1508 under family-out-of-distribution evaluation, with ΔC_B = −0.4347 and ΔC_W = −0.1011; the between-target component accounts for 81.1% of the summed absolute component change. Target weighting changes how the components should be read: across five schemes C_B reverses sign in 40/109 configurations and in 34/109 even above |C_B| > 0.005, whereas C_W reverses in only 5/109. Fixed-K shortlist metrics are constrained by candidate-set geometry: a rank-linear discriminability surrogate is zero when n ≤ K and peaks near n* ≈ 20.5 for K = 10, and 40.8% of targets with n ≥ 5 fall in that degenerate regime. A matched retrospective ablation separated modifications that improve pooled scores only from those that also improve within-target ranking. External evidence from five methods is underpowered and its apparent cross-axis agreement is not robust to score orientation. Benchmarks should therefore report both components under declared weighting and candidate-set geometry.

papers.title: Aromaticity Hidden in Magnetically Antiaromatic Macrocycles
papers.abstract: Global paratropic ring currents give norcorrole and rosarin a familiar antiaromatic label and account for their characteristic pattern of deshielded inner and shielded outer protons. Translating that magnetic picture into a perimeter of alternating double bonds, however, assigns the occupied 𝜋 electrons to a bonding pattern that the current pathway alone does not determine. Here we ask how much of the ground-state bonding the magnetic response actually reveals. For a diaza[16]annulene model series and for free-base and metal-coordinated porphyrinoids, we compare occupied bonding domains, resolved with the electron density of delocalized bonds and the bond delocalization function, with orbital-resolved magnetic response. A global paratropic pathway persists when the model bonding changes from a delocalized 16𝜋 perimeter to localized double bonds or two pyrrolic sextets. In norcorrole and rosarin, fixed sextets give way to migrating patterns upon coordination, again without changing the paratropic classification. Orbital decomposition reveals local diatropic contributions beneath the global response. Isomerizations involving the pyrrolic units of norcorrole cost more than the rim control, although their energies also contain structural and stereochemical effects. A paratropic ring current is therefore not, by itself, a bonding formula. Annulene-based aromaticity assignments should retain Hückel’s energetic logic, with electron counts and magnetic or spectroscopic fingerprints interpreted through the complete molecular electronic structure rather than substituted for appropriate energetic and, where relevant, thermodynamic characterization.

papers.title: What Information Is Required to Learn Molecular Pauli Potentials? A Nonlocal Descriptor Hierarchy for Orbital-Free Density Functional Theory
papers.abstract: Practical orbital-free density functional theory (OF-DFT) for molecules remains limited by the unknown Pauli contribution to the noninteracting kinetic energy. Here, we ask what information a density representation must contain for a machine-learned (ML) Pauli potential to drive an orbital-free Euler solution toward its Kohn–Sham (KS) reference. For C2H2, a frozen KS-derived Pauli-potential oracle yields an OF energy within 3.15 mHa of the KS reference, establishing the numerical accuracy attainable within the chosen finite representation. Coordinate-conditioned neural networks demonstrate that the Paulipotential field is learnable but do not provide a density-functional representation. Replacing coordinates with semilocal density descriptors leads to severe failure for both multilayer perceptron (MLP) and Kolmogorov–Arnold network (KAN) models. A descriptor-space identifiability analysis reveals the underlying cause: sparse representations leave approximately 14% of grid points ambiguous, whereas an atom-reaching 60-component nonlocal environment reduces this fraction to approximately 1.4%. Correspondingly, progressively adding nonlocal density information reduces the KAN energy deviation from −4594 to −16.0 mHa, while geometry-informed bond-centered descriptors further reduce it to −0.9 mHa. Applied independently to C2H4, the same descriptor strategy remains effective, yielding deviations of +24.0 and −13.5 mHa for KAN and MLP, respectively. Companion models also recover the principal spatial features of the Pauli energy density and strong covalent interaction profile. These results identify the resolution of descriptor ambiguity through extended and chemically structured nonlocal density information as a central representational requirement for molecular OF-DFT.

papers.title: Accelerating characterization of conformational stability for biologics in Discovery space by combining SEC‑HDX‑MS with molecular modeling
papers.abstract: Conformational stability is a critical attribute for biologics discovery and manufacturability assessment, yet conventional approaches often require substantial material, extensive preparation, or lack sufficient structural resolution for early decision-making. Here, we present a native size-exclusion chromatography hydrogen–deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (SEC-HDX-MS) workflow integrated with molecular modeling to rapidly characterize conformational stability of therapeutic proteins in the discovery space. The workflow was evaluated across monoclonal antibody and bispecific antibody modalities. From a sequence variant comparison, SEC-HDX-MS showed that elevated aggregation did not uniformly reflect global conformational instability; instead, only one variant displayed increased deuterium incorporation, which modeling linked to an elongated, solvent-exposed CDR-H3 loop with increased hydrophobicity. In a representative proprietary mAb (“mAb X”), SEC-HDX-MS revealed that thermally-induced isoaspartate accumulation reduced conformational stability, whereas high-pH stress showed behavior comparable to controls despite higher overall deamidation. Molecular dynamics simulations explained this destabilization through disruption of a backbone Asn43–Ala40 hydrogen bond and altered local coordination after isoAsp formation. Finally, application to a complex bispecific antibody confirmed the workflow’s sensitivity for detecting conformational differences in more complex formats. Collectively, this integrated approach connects global HDX measurements with molecular-level interpretation, requires minimal preparation and limited material, and is compatible with partially purified samples. The workflow enables rapid conformational stability assessment to support candidate ranking, protein engineering, formulation development, and CMC risk assessment during biologics discovery.

papers.title: Universality of Lithium Metal and Solid Electrolyte Interphase Descriptors of Coulombic Efficiency Governed by Lithium Connectivity
papers.abstract: Coulombic efficiency (CE) is a key metric governing the cyclability of lithium metal anodes, motivating efforts to identify physicochemical descriptors that correlate with CE. Diverse descriptors spanning electrolyte thermodynamics and interphase properties have been proposed, but their interrelationships and underlying physical origins remain unclear. Here we show that, when evaluated across a consistent electrolyte set, these descriptors exhibit a common hockey-stick relationship with CE that can be unified through the mesoscale connectivity of lithium deposits. A percolation-like transition from isolated deposits to interconnected networks sharply suppresses inactive Li0 formation during stripping, which underlies the common CE transition across descriptors. Tuning plating current density reproduces this transition within individual electrolytes, demonstrating that connectivity is not uniquely determined by electrolyte chemistry. These findings establish lithium connectivity as a common mechanistic basis for diverse CE correlations and provide a framework for interpreting these correlations across distinct capacity-loss regimes.

papers.title: Conformal Chemical Vapor Deposition in the Thermodynamically Limited Temperature Range
papers.abstract: Perfectly uniform and conformal thin films of materials are routinely deposited by chemical vapor deposition (CVD) for a range of applications, especially in the semiconductor industry. The most common way to enable highly conformal deposition is to operate the CVD process in the kinetically limited temperature regime, i.e., at the lower temperature range where the deposition chemistry is active. Here, we present the unexpected finding that a conformal CVD process is also available at very high temperatures. When doing CVD of boron carbide on freestanding carbon nanotubes (CNT) at 1000 °C, i.e., in the thermodynamically limited temperature regime, the process afforded fully conformal layer of boron carbide on the CNTs. In contrast, depositions at 700 and 850 °C afforded sub-conformal depositions. This result indicate a lower reaction probability caused by the enhanced desorption of growth species at higher temperatures.

papers.title: Eliminating the remaining spin contamination of MRSF-TDDFT by completing its core–virtual block
papers.abstract: We introduce a core–virtual-complete variant of mixed-reference spin-flip time-dependent density functional theory (MRSF-TDDFT), CV-MRSF, which completes the block of core-to-virtual (CV) excitations. For each CV excitation, the four determinants missing from MRSF-TDDFT are recovered by imposing exact spin adaptation, which makes every singlet and triplet spin pure and gives the proper singlet–triplet splitting of CV states without spin-pairing couplings. In addition, invariance under a rotation of the two singly occupied molecular orbitals (SOMOs) O1 and O2 adds the configurations C¹O₁²V¹ and C¹O₂²V¹. The number of CV configurations per excitation thus grows from one to four in the singlet and to five in the triplet configuration state function (CSF) response, and one quintet CSF also arises within the same CV block, instead of from a separate spin-flip-up calculation. As a result, the CV excitations properly couple to the complete set of open-to-open (OO) configurations, both singlet and triplet, as well as to the core-to-open (CO) and open-to-virtual (OV) configurations, which relaxes the excited states and accounts for most of the changes in excitation energy. For hybrid functionals, a spin-scalar one-body correction keeps the response matrix covariant under separate rotations of the core, open-shell, and virtual orbitals. For the Thiel benchmark set it lowers the mean absolute error of MRSF-TDDFT from 0.53 to 0.40 eV for the singlets and from 0.40 to 0.29 eV for the triplets. The largest gains are for n→π* states by excitation character and nucleobase singlets by molecule class. The CV block also describes the spin-pure triplet-pair states ¹(TT), ³(TT), and ⁵(TT) of chromophore dimers on the same footing, the essential requirement for the description of singlet fission processes.

papers.title: Tunable Emission from Quasi-2D Perovskites via Electrospinning
papers.abstract: Quasi-2D Ruddlesden-Popper halide perovskites are promising materials for light-emitting applications. They comprise corner-sharing metal-halide octahedra separated by bulky, insulating organic spacers and exhibit tunable bandgaps by varying the number of octahedral layers, n . Isolating a single n -phase within a film remains challenging, with spin-coated films generally containing a broad distribution of n phases. Their emission is dominated by the largest n -number present due to energy funneling towards narrow bandgap phases. Here, we electrospin phenylethylammonium (PEA + )/methylammonium (MA + ) lead bromide quasi-2D perovskites into 140 - 400 nm nanofibers to restrict molecular diffusion. We observe progressive redshifts in absorption and photoluminescence from blue (410 nm) to cyan (470 nm) to green (530 nm) with decreasing PEA + :MA + molar ratio. In contrast, spin-coated films with the same PEA + :MA + ratios exhibit green emission (524 - 532 nm) across all MA + containing compositions. Transient absorption spectroscopy reveals energy transfer within 80 ps from low n phases to MAPbBr 3 domains in spin-coated films, which are absent in electrospun fibers. Electrospun fibers are also highly emissive compared to spin-coated films, with average photoluminescence quantum yields up to 77±1%. These results suggest that electrospinning limits organic cation diffusion to selectively stabilize intermediate n phases, providing a scalable route to achieve tunable solid-state emission.

papers.title: Direct C(sp3)–H/C(sp2)–F Cross-Coupling of Methylpyridines with Aryl Fluorides
papers.abstract: Direct C(sp3)–H functionalization of methylpyridines is intrinsically challenging. Herein, we report a transition-metal-free, silylboronate-mediated heterobenzylation of methylpyridines with aryl fluorides. The combination of a silylboronate and KOtBu enables direct C(sp3)–H/C(sp2)–F coupling under mild conditions, providing efficient access to structurally diverse azaarylmethanes. The reaction accommodates π-extended aryl fluorides, polyfluoroarenes, and various 4-alkylpyridines, including substrates bearing multiple potentially reactive C–H or C–F bonds, with useful levels of chemo- and regioselectivity. The method is also applicable to the late-stage functionalization of structurally complex molecules. Alkyl fluorides are also compatible via the C(sp3)–H/C(sp3)–F coupling reaction. Mechanistic studies, including aryl-halide comparison, radical-trapping, investigation of pronucleophile, Hammett plot, competition experiments, and DFT calculation support an ionic pathway involving generation of a heterobenzylic nucleophile followed by nucleophilic substitution of the C–F bond. For electronically neutral and electron-rich aryl fluorides, the observed reactivity is consistent with a concerted SNAr pathway. This strategy provides a complementary approach to conventional transition-metal-catalyzed heterobenzylic arylation and expands the synthetic utility of organofluorine compounds as coupling partners for C–C bond formation.

papers.title: Multi-Agent Scheduling of Instrument-Time for High-Throughput Palladium-Catalysed Cross-Coupling
papers.abstract: NMR time and a shared liquid-handling robot are scarce, noisy and only partially observable, so the practical question is which experiment to run next on which instrument. Existing reaction-optimisation benchmarks measure budgets in experiments rather than instrumenthours, and they learn chemical feasibility only by paying for infeasible runs. We present CHASE, a centralised-training decentralised-execution scheduler with three coupled modules: a belief encoder (PEB) infers per-instrument throughput and channel health from local event histories and exchanges only low-bandwidth summaries; a chemistry feasibility gate (CFG) masks chemically impossible actions with a four-layer compatibility graph; and a counterfactual attribution module (CFA) converts delayed campaign reward into per-step credit through leave-one-experiment-out surrogate scoring. On the Buchwald–Hartwig (3,955 reactions) and Suzuki–Miyaura (5,760 nanomole-scale conditions) HTE datasets, the ten Olympus benchmarks and a plant-wide Tennessee Eastman process, CHASE reaches 94.1% best-found yield under a shared 60 instrument-hour budget, +3.3 points over the strongest same-setting baseline, attains 90% of the attainable optimum with 25.6% fewer experiments, and cuts infeasible actions to 0.7–1.6% across plate, flow and fault-injection settings.

papers.title: Risk-Priced Radio Resources for In-Line Spectroscopy and Reaction Monitoring in Chemical Plants
papers.abstract: In-line spectroscopy now carries the chemical plant’s quality decisions over shared industrial wireless links, yet the schedulers distributing those links optimize throughput, fairness or delay and are blind to chemistry: an MIR quantification stream survives compression, while a runaway precursor confined to a narrow wavenumber window disappears with it. We present ChemRAN, a chemistry-aware orchestration framework for wireless process analytical technology networks. ChemQoI predicts how an allocation changes a stream’s analytical error, detection sensitivity and measurement-failure probability, and converts them into an expected chemical risk reduction using a sparse spectral sketch and a process cost matrix. SCARF allocates each window by marginal risk reduction under a hard safety floor for hazard streams, and RECAP couples allocation with offloading through a shared adaptation tensor and asynchronous updates conditioned on chemistry descriptors. On the Tennessee Eastman process, Buchwald–Hartwig and Suzuki–Miyaura screens and in-line MIR soft sensing, ChemRAN attains 0.9755 F1, 0.966 yield 𝑅2 and 1.08 g L−1 𝜅-casein RMSECV, cuts the risk-weighted chemical loss by 19% and the hazard miss rate from 2.31% to 0.88%, and retains over 90% of its performance on unseen plants and campaigns.

papers.title: Quantum Graph-Theoretic Docking of Multiple Ligands Targeting CMG Helicase: Analysis of Interaction Patterns and Ideal Ligand Composition
papers.abstract: Molecular docking and compound screening can overlook and biochemically relevant binding configurations of molecules, limiting the ability to identify true functional poses of potential drug candidates. To address this, we apply the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) to improve the evaluation of target–ligand interaction patterns. As a proof of concept, we focus on the CDC45–MCM2-7–GINS (CMG) helicase, which is essential for DNA replication and represents a potential therapeutic target in cancer due to mutant KRas-induced vulnerabilities in the CMG and its MCM hexameric core. In this study, docking of three ligands: methylbiocin, novobiocin, and BL_C43, to one of the ATP-binding regions of the CMG was formulated as a combinatorial optimization problem. Pharmacophore interactions were encoded in a Binding Interaction Graph and mapped to a Maximum Independent Set problem, allowing exploration of all feasible docking configurations. The quantum workflow identified ligand-dependent interaction patterns and biologically relevant binding orientations that classical docking methods failed to predict, demonstrating superior agreement with experimental biochemical outcomes for CMG inhibitors. These findings establish QAOA as a promising approach for overcoming limitations of classical molecular docking and advancing the rational design of improved inhibitors targeting CMG and other cancer-associated proteins.

papers.title: Lewis Acid-Activated Bathophenanthroline Photoredox System for Chlorine Radical-Mediated C(sp³)–H Alkylation
papers.abstract: Despite major advances in photoredox catalysis, photocatalysts capable of oxidizing substrates with E ox > +2.0 V vs SCE remain limited. Herein, we report that a Lewis acid-activated bathophenanthroline (bphen) photoredox system with ZrCl 4 enables intermolecular single-electron oxidation of chloride ( E ox = +2.03 V vs SCE). Under visible-light irradiation, this system promotes Giese-type alkylation of electron-deficient alkenes with a broad range of C(sp 3 )–H donors through chlorine radical-mediated hydrogen atom transfer (HAT). Detailed spectroscopic, electrochemical, kinetic, and computational studies reveal that Lewis acid activation of bphen enhances the excited-state oxidizing power and enables the intermolecular oxidation of chloride to generate a chlorine radical.

papers.title: Polyamide Reverse Osmosis Membranes Are Less Crosslinked Than Previously Thought
papers.abstract: Polyamide membranes are central to industrial separations, including desalination and water treatment. They are typically described as comprising crosslinked and linear units. Molecular dynamics simulations and topological analysis find branched units to be similar to or more prevalent than crosslinked units, and ignoring them can mischaracterize polyamide membranes. 2 Crosslinked polyamide membranes are widely used as selective layers in thin film composites (TFC) for reverse osmosis, forward osmosis, and nanofiltration.1 The most common desalination membranes are formed by reacting m-phenylenediamine (MPD) with trimesoyl chloride (TMC);

papers.title: Mediator-Assisted Energy Release Enabled by Positional Isomerism in Norbornadiene/Quadricyclane Systems
papers.abstract: Molecular solar thermal (MOST) systems store solar energy in metastable photoisomers and release it on demand through triggered back-conversion. Here, we show that mixtures of MOST compounds enable a distinct energy-release strategy in which one component mediates the activation of another. Using methoxyphenyl-substituted norbornadiene/quadricyclane (NBD/QC) positional isomers, we show by in situ photoelectrochemical infrared reflection absorption spectroscopy (PEC-IRRAS) and density functional theory (DFT) that substituent position shifts the electrochemical onset potential by up to 0.6 V and controls switching selectivity, largely independently of thermal stability, a trend rationalized by calculated ionization potentials. Crucially, in a mixture, the electrochemically facile QC isomer triggers back-conversion of a second QC isomer below its intrinsic onset potential, consistent with a radical-chain mechanism. Mediator-assisted triggering thus decouples the requirements for molecular energy storage and electrochemical activation and opens new opportunities for tuning energy release strategies through multicomponent MOST systems.

papers.title: Mass Balance-based Computational Frameworks for the
papers.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent anthropogenic contaminants widely 20 detected in aquatic environments. Conventional wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) are major 21 emission sources that discharge PFAS via effluent and the land application of biosolids, yet they 22 are ineffective in removing PFAS. Understanding PFAS distribution and transformation in 23 WWTPs is important for the development and integration of PFAS remediation technologies. 24 However, identifying the mechanisms governing each PFAS mass flow change across a treatment 25 compartment remains challenging, and parameters quantifying PFAS transformation and 26 distribution in the field are difficult to measure. To address these problems, we developed novel 27 mass balance-based computational frameworks for PFAS distribution and transformation in 28 WWTP. We demonstrated that they are robust tools for identifying the mechanisms driving 29 changes in PFAS mass flow and for estimating unobservable parameters describing PFAS 30 distribution and transformation. Also, based on these frameworks, we found that the impacts of 31 PFAS partitioning on PFAS concentrations in the aqueous phase were two to three orders of 32 magnitude higher than those of precursor transformation. These frameworks are extensible, and 33 remaining limitations in parameter uncertainty and transformation pathway completeness are 34 discussed. 35 36

papers.title: Enhancing Ethylene Yields and Energy Efficiency in Industrial Cracking Furnaces via Spatial Heat-Flux Optimization
papers.abstract: Steam cracking furnaces are conventionally operated by raising the coil outlet temperature (COT) via increased fuel input, yet this approach yields diminishing selectivity gains while accelerating coking. Using a high-fidelity 3D coupled furnace–reactor model consistent with industrial design parameters, we demonstrate that COT is not the primary control lever. Instead, at a fixed total heat input, the spatial distribution of heat flux along the coil axis governs ethylene yields and cracking severity. By aligning the heat-flux profile with the axial endothermicity of the cracking reactions, relative ethylene yield increases by 5.86% while COT decreases by 3.94 K, effectively decoupling yield enhancement from fuel consumption. The causal effect of the heat-flux profile on ethylene yield makes it a more physically rigorous control variable than COT. This shifts the operational paradigm from temperature-driven to spatial heat-flux-driven control, offering a practical retrofit pathway for current industrial-scale cracking furnaces.

papers.title: Substituted Catechols as H-Bonding Organocatalysts in Conjugated Addition Reactions of (Hetero-)Arenes to Nitroolefins
papers.abstract: Hydrogen-bond donor organocatalysts based on thioureas, silanols, amidines and diols have been studied in-depth. However, catechols – as prototypical diol catalysts – are comparatively underexplored despite their structural simplicity, straightforward accessibility, and tunability. Here, we systematically investigate substituted catechols as hydrogen-bond donor catalysts for the conjugate addition of indoles to nitroolefins. Screening of the catechol substitution pattern identified 4bromocatechol as the most active derivative. Comparison with related diols established the importance of the vicinal arrangement and phenolic nature of the hydroxy groups.
