The modular and adaptable design provides a versatile platform for advanced spectroelectrochemical investigations and can be extended to a wide range of electrochemical systems and complementary spectroscopic techniques.

papers.title: Chiral Octahedral Metallomesogens with Δ/Λ Core Chirality: Extending Wallach's Rule from Crystals to Liquid Crystals
papers.abstract: Chirality often induces marked structural changes in liquid crystals (LCs) and can even induce new phases. Where chirality resides in a mesogen is thus a fundamental question, but because mesogens favor planar structures, the effect of chirality at the molecular center (core chirality) on their assemblies has remained poorly understood. This Account explores this question with the octahedral tris(β-diketonato) family M-Cn (M = Ru, Ir), whose Δ/Λ configuration proves to be a decisive design element. Enantiopure Ru-C8 builds helical hexagonal columns, whereas its racemate assembles ΔΛ-alternating paired columns, and longer alkyl chains switch the system to a micellar cubic phase. Strikingly, the racemate is the more stable form: Wallach’s rule, known for crystals, also governs the LC state. This Δ–Λ recognition can be harnessed: pairing Δ-Ru-Cn with Λ-Ir-Cn gives quasi-racemic LCs with emergent chiroptical properties, such as stereoselectively enhanced vibrational circular dichroism.

papers.title: Distribution Function Analysis of Crystalline and Low-Dimensional Materials
papers.abstract: Atomic pair distribution function (PDF) analysis from X-ray total scattering is a powerful methodology for determining atomic structure and arrangements across crystalline, disordered, nanostructured, and low-dimensional materials on both laboratory and synchrotron instruments. Fundamentally, PDF analysis relies on two core pillars—PDF data reduction from one-dimensional (1D) total scattering profiles and real-space structural modeling—often accompanied in rapid-acquisition experiments by upstream two-dimensional (2D) detector image processing. However, conventional workflows remain fragmented across disconnected software tools, forcing researchers to manually combine multiple programs and preventing the simultaneous optimization of measurement reduction parameters and crystal structure parameters that is standard in X-ray Rietveld refinement. Furthermore, mainstream PDF modeling engines rely on legacy physical approximations: they enforce three-dimensional (3D) periodic boundary conditions (requiring artificial vacuum supercells for 2D nanosheets), treat atomic scattering factors as angle-independent constants (causing peak distortions in compounds with large atomic number contrast), and approximate number density baselines using macroscopic bulk volume assumptions. Here, the open-source, pure-Python architecture of Orochi (version 4.0) is presented, implementing physical calculations from scratch in Python (accelerated via Numba) to unify total scattering data reduction, symmetry-aware crystallographic modeling, and real-space PDF simulation alongside a dedicated high-Q 2D detector processing module within a self-contained Python environment. Originally developed for laboratory total scattering studies of pharmaceutical glasses and deployed as compiled executable (β-version) tools at SPring-8 beamlines, Orochi has been completely redesigned around an externalized parameter management core (orochi.base) in which parameters are stored in standardized Python dictionaries and accessed via hierarchical string addresses. By bringing parameters outside the calculation engines rather than locking them inside built-in optimizers, this architecture allows multiple module instances across data reduction and structural modeling to be optimized simultaneously by modern optimization algorithms, machine learning libraries, and autonomous AI agents. For structural simulation, intra-cell atomic pair vectors are decoupled from lattice translation vectors to natively support arbitrary periodic boundary conditions across 3D crystals, 2D nanosheets, 1D nanowires, and

papers.title: Synthesis of Clickable Pyrazolo-fused N -heterocycles using a Diversity Oriented Clicking Strategy
papers.abstract: Diversity-Oriented Clicking (DOC) provides a powerful platform for the rapid assembly of structurally complex, SuFEx-enabled molecules. Here, we report a regioselective, catalyst-free [3+2] cycloaddition between 2-substituted-alkynyl-1-sulfonyl fluorides (SASFs) connectors and N -iminium ylides to access a library of sulfonyl fluoride functionalized fused N-heterocycles. Under mild conditions, N -iminopyridinium ylides react smoothly with a range of aromatic and aliphatic SASFs to furnish pyrazolo[1,5- a ]pyridinyl sulfonyl fluorides as single regioisomers. The methodology is applicable to N -iminoisoquinolinium and N- iminoquinazolium ylides, enabling access to pyrazolo[2,1- a ]isoquinoline and pyrazolo[1,5- c ]quinazoline sulfonyl fluorides, respectively, expanding the structural diversity accessible from SASF hubs. The transformation proceeds without additives or transition metals and tolerates diverse functional groups. Importantly, the sulfonyl fluoride moiety enables rapid late-stage diversification with phenols and amines, demonstrating the utility of these fused heterocyclic scaffolds as clickable connective hubs. Finally, we propose a detailed stepwise reaction mechanism.

papers.title: Defect Chemistry and Electronic Structure of α-Pu2O3: A Hybrid DFT Study of Charged Vacancies, Interstitials, and Antisites
papers.abstract: Using state-of-the-art hybrid density functional theory, we systematically investigate the formation energetics and electronic structure of native charged point defects in α-Pu2O3, including plutonium and oxygen vacancies, interstitials, and antisite defects. We find that these defects induce significant local structural distortions and modify the magnetic properties of neighboring Pu ions. Furthermore, they lead to a redistribution of electronic states near the band edges and induce in-gap states, resulting in notable variations of the band gap. Defect formation energetics are found to be strongly governed by both the chemical potentials of the constituent elements and the electron chemical potential, resulting in distinct defect stability regimes under different chemical potential conditions. These defects, in general, are found to generate deep electronic levels within the band gap, suggesting their potential role as carrier trapping centers. Overall, this study provides critical insight into the role of point defects in α-

papers.title: Spontaneous Emergence of Homochiral Halogen-bonded Helices from Achiral Components
papers.abstract: Biological systems selectively use chiral molecules, such as L-amino acids and D-sugars, to construct single-handed helical structures including proteins, collagen, and DNA. Reproducing such handedness selection using synthetic systems remains a major challenge because achiral molecules generally form racemic helices. Here, we show that supramolecular halogen-bonded complexes assembled entirely from achiral molecular components spontaneously form either left- or right-handed helices. Structural analysis reveals that helix formation is driven by cooperative hydrogen-bonding interactions within the halogen-bonded assemblies, while their handedness is determined solely by the solvent. Remarkably, homochiral helices emerge without the need for chiral catalysts, chiral solvents, or other external chiral influences. These findings provide experimental evidence for spontaneous symmetry breaking in an achiral molecular system and offer a simple platform for exploring the origins of homochirality.

papers.title: Functional-Group Effects in Biopolymer Binders for Sodium-Ion Battery Electrodes: Interfaces, Rheology, and Electrochemical Performance
papers.abstract: Binders, though typically only a few weight percent of a battery electrode, play an outsized role in determining cell performance and sustainability. Water-soluble green binders have emerged as eco-friendly alternatives that enable aqueous slurry processing and easier recyclability. In this work, we leverage biopolymer-based binders (CMC/SBR, Guar Gum and ι-carrageenan) in sodium-ion battery electrodes (Prussian white cathodes and hard carbon anodes) to demonstrate a new paradigm of sustainable electrode design. Our findings highlight that biopolymer binders (Guar Gum and ι-carrageenan) can effectively “glue” sodium-ion battery electrodes together forming a robust structural network and refine the composition of the passivation layer on electrode interface through the functional groups (hydroxyl, carboxyl, and sulfate bonding). By replacing conventional binders with these green alternatives, high-capacity retention and rate capability were achieved when paired with hard carbon electrodes, all with the added benefits of aqueous processability and sustainability.

papers.title: Atom-precise nanocluster architectures programmed by biomolecular assembly
papers.abstract: Ligand-protected metal nanoclusters hold promise as atomically precise building blocks for nanoscale materials. However, it remains challenging to achieve ligand chemistries that control higher-order organization while still retaining the nanocluster’s atom-precise properties. Here, we present two biomolecular approaches for higher-order organization of silver nanoclusters stabilized by DNA (DNA-Ag N ). First, using strategies from DNA nanotechnology, we develop complementary DNA-Ag N that oligomerize upon toehold-mediated strand displacement reactions. Second, we exploit biotin-streptavidin interactions to oligomerize biotinylated DNA-Ag N . Higherorder assembly is confirmed by native polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis and cryo-electron microscopy. Optical spectroscopy shows that the nanoclusters retain their optical properties upon assembly, supporting the integrity of their atomically precise structures during biomolecular organization. These results demonstrate the utility of programmable biomolecular interactions for the higher-order assembly of atom-precise inorganic nanoclusters.

papers.title: Improving Molecular Dynamics of Aqueous Electrolytes through Data-Driven Sensitivity-Guided GFN2-xTB Reparameterization
papers.abstract: Semiempirical tight-binding methods such as GFN2-xTB enable efficient molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, but their performance is strongly system dependent. The default GFN2-xTB parameterization overestimates equilibrium densities of liquid water and aqueous NaCl, and it underestimates the bond length for Na+–water pairs in the radial distribution function. To correct these deficiencies, we develop a sensitivity-guided stepwise approach to reparameterize GFN2-xTB against cluster-based and periodic revPBE0-D3 data. We find that the GFN2-xTB fitting problem is ill-conditioned, with many compensating parameter changes that reduce fitted errors but yield unphysical densities in MD simulations. Fisher information matrix (FIM) analysis reveals that only a few parameter combinations dominate the sensitivity of fitted observables, suggesting a reduction of the parameter space for efficient optimization. Optimizing those FIM-selected parameter subsets first for H/O and then for Na improves the equilibrium densities and shifts Na+ hydration distances into the experimental ranges without compromising the remaining properties. We achieve these improvements without directly fitting densities or hydration distances. While the best agreement with experiment for densities is achieved by optimizations on periodic datasets that include virials in the objective function, inclusion of targeted scans of essential geometric degrees of freedom in either a periodic or cluster dataset also improves optimization. Our results identify cluster data as a practical route to correct ion-solvation structure via inexpensive reference calculations, while periodic virials provide complementary control over bulk properties. These findings demonstrate that sensitivity-guided parameter selection, combined with carefully selected reference data describing the relevant interactions, enables GFN2-xTB reparameterizations whose improvements in the static fit translate to bulk MD and provides a general strategy for improving dynamical properties from low-cost electronic structure methods.

papers.title: Mechanical versus thermal amorphization of ZIF-4: from local rearrangements to network disorder
papers.abstract: There is mounting evidence that different amorphization routes can produce metalorganic framework (MOF) glasses with distinct structures and properties, yet the microscopic origins of these differences remain difficult to establish experimentally. Focusing on the two main synthesis methods, which are melt-quenching and ball-milling, we use molecular dynamics simulations with a machine-learning interatomic potential to compare different glasses obtained from ZIF-4. While both routes largely preserve tetrahedral zinc coordination, mechanical deformation generally produces more distorted local environments, showing that average coordination numbers alone do not capture the structural differences between these glasses. At smaller applied strain, mechanical glasses retain substantial memory of the crystalline network topology, despite pronounced changes in ring geometry. Larger strains erase this topological memory, yielding ring-size distributions similar to those of melt-quenched glasses, while differences in local geometry and porosity persist. Simulations of larger systems reveal a heterogeneous amorphization mechanism, involving the formation and growth of disordered domains. These findings from in silico amorphization support process-dependent polyamorphism in ZIF glasses and identify local geometry, topological memory, and spatial heterogeneity as complementary features needed to characterize their structure and understand the influence of mechanical processing.

papers.title: Dynamic Anionic Speciation and Proton Transfer in Choline/Geranic Acid Mixtures Revealed by Machine-Learned Molecular Dynamics
papers.abstract: In carboxylate/carboxylic acid-containing ionic liquid systems, oligomeric complex anions have been shown to substantially alter transport properties; yet whether such persistent pairing survives in the presence of water remains an open question. The 1:2 choline/geranic acid mixture (CAGE12) provides an ideal case study: a promising therapeutic solvent unavoidably hydrated in biomedical use. Although hydrogen-bonded geranic acid (AGE)–geranate (GE) oligomeric motifs have been proposed and recently characterized spectroscopically, their prevalence and dynamical relevance in the liquid remain unclear, particularly in application conditions. Here, we employ DFT-trained NeuralIL machine-learned molecular dynamics to investigate hydrated CAGE12 containing 8 wt% water. The simulations reveal a highly dynamic hydrogen-bond network centered on GE, in which AGE, water, and choline continuously compete for coordinating the GE. AGE–GE associations are frequently observed but exhibit sub-picosecond lifetimes, indicating that they are transient structural motifs rather than persistent complex anions. Proton-transferred configurations are found to depend strongly on the local hydrogen-bond environment. Rare AGE-rich coordination environments are associated with proton-transferred configurations that remain stable, whereas the more abundant water-coordinated AGE–GE pairs are associated with reversible proton-transfer events and proton rattling. Overall, hydrated CAGE12 is best described as a dynamically evolving hydrogen-bond network in which transient local coordination, rather than persistent oligomeric anions, governs proton transfer and anionic speciation. These results highlight the critical role of water in disrupting complex anion formation in nonstoichiometric ionic liquids, with direct consequences for their transport and physicochemical properties.

papers.title: Two-photon-enabled near-infrared proximity labeling maps protein neighborhoods in vivo
papers.abstract: Native molecular neighborhoods govern biological processes and disease, yet existing approaches trade off penetration, precision, and native compatibility. Photocatalytic proximity labeling (PL) offers nanoscale, genetics-free precision but is limited by visible-light activation in optically opaque tissue. Here, we report 2PMap, a two-photon near-infrared PL platform driven by a sensitizer with a twophoton absorption cross-section nearly two orders of magnitude above conventional photocatalysts, enabling 850 nm continuous-wave excitation without pulsed lasers. In optically opaque samples, 2PMap achieved higher proteome coverage than conventional visible-light PL. In an early-stage Alzheimer’s disease mouse model, peptide-guided 2PMap produced the first proximity scale map of connective tissue growth factor (CTGF) in living brain tissue, capturing an 80-node network spanning extracellular-matrix, vascular, immune, and neuronal components within a microenvironment inaccessible to existing PL methods. 2PMap thus provides a genetics-free, modular platform for spatial proteomic mapping, extending molecular cartography to previously inaccessible living systems.

papers.title: Morgan Fingerprint Classification Prioritizes Autophagy Modulators While Transcriptome Regression Fails to Distinguish Opposing Modulators
papers.abstract: Autophagy is a conserved lysosomal degradation and recycling pathway with established roles in aging, neurodegeneration, cancer, and metabolic disease. Computational prioritization of autophagy modulators is difficult: autophagy modulators have a variety of mechanisms and the analysis of perturbational transcriptomes could confound pathway-specific effects with generic stress responses. Here, we evaluated four formulations of the prioritization task: full transcriptome regression, gene-signature matching, binary modulator classification, and activator-versus-inhibitor direction prediction, using LINCS L1000 transcriptomics, the Human Autophagy Modulator Database (HAMdb), and a 99,433-compound ChEMBL library. We found that a Uni-Mol neural network trained to predict 12,328-gene expression responses assigned near-identical profiles to Rapamycin and Wortmannin, two compounds with opposing effects on autophagy (predicted Spearman ρ = +0.97 versus +0.43 observed), and that genome-wide diagnostics detected no association between molecular structure and expression. In contrast, XGBoost on 2,048-bit Morgan fingerprints distinguished modulators from non-modulators with compound-level AUROC 0.845 using L1000 context and 0.84 to 0.88 (95% bootstrap CI) from structure alone, ranking held-out canonical controls at the top of the score distribution, and enriched autophagy and mTOR/PI3K annotations up to ~36× and ~58× over baseline on the ChEMBL library. Direction prediction remained near chance (macro F1 0.532), limited by the lack of samples in the HAMdb compounds that are marked as autophagy inhibitors (only 132 inhibitors). Taken together, these results suggest that binary structure-based classification can prioritize autophagy modulators, while transcriptome regression and structure-based direction prediction are not supported by current data.

papers.title: Generative discovery, symmetry-aware membership screening, and device-level evaluation of six-member-ring MoS2 polytypes
papers.abstract: Six-membered-ring (SMR) inorganic materials were recently unified into a class, but the class-level perspective lacks two enabling tools: an operational test of “SMR-ness” and a path from newly generated crystals to device-level figures of merit. Here we couple conditional generative modelling (MatterGen; Mo–S, Ti–S, W–Se; 512 cells per system) to a novelty/stability funnel, a symmetry-aware membership checker that casts the SMR definition as three calibrated criteria (6/6 positives, 6/6 trap negatives), full DFT relaxation with composition-anchored hull analysis, and a contract-based device evaluation injecting literature-anchored OCV and diffusivity into an electrochemical cell model. The campaign maps the AA-stacked polytype manifold across five TMD chemistries, confirming 61 candidates (12 MoS2, 7 TiS2, 18 WSe2, 16 MoSe2, 8 NbS2; e.g. the MoS2 series P6̄m2, c = 7.1–40.8 Å, Ehull = 0.019–0.022 eV atom−1), 56 of them novel against every queried database. A dedicated spin cross-check (ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic and unpolarised initialisations) collapses to zero moments in every tested channel, and a three-probe stability screen (phonons, annealing dynamics, hull distance) shows the layered frameworks robust while the AA registry is metastable toward layer sliding, sharpening the synthesis list into kinetically stabilisable targets with two registry-robust entries. Two methodological findings transfer to any SMR screening effort: minimum-ring statistics collapse on TMD coordination (four-rings swallow six-rings), and membership is adjudicable only after relaxation. At the device end, material classes are discriminated by 0.639 V and polytypes by computed Li barriers (a 1.6× 10 8 diffusivity ratio separates fast from frozen at 0.5C); every number is traceable to a versioned experiment record.

papers.title: Accelerating Catalyst Discovery with Artificial Intelligence Using Molecular Dual-Atom Site Catalysts as a Case Study
authors: Bruno Ina cio da Silva Roux Leite
papers.abstract: We test whether researchers can delegate the writing of a complete catalyst study to a large language model while retaining scientific judgment. Our case study concerns molecular dual-atom site catalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction, where stabilizing an adsorbed intermediate can make its subsequent reduction less favorable. Using density functional theory calculations on 88 catalysts, we explain this balance through adsorption free energies and the overpotential volcano. We then use adsorbate specific ridge models to predict adsorption energies for 1,260 additional structures and identify candidates for further study. Among candidates with low predicted overpotentials, we find predominantly Fe adsorption centers, with separate structural patterns associated with S bridges and 1,2phenylenediamine. To communicate the reasoning behind these choices, we guided a large language model with explicit scientific writing instructions and refined its explanations through repeated scientific and editorial review. The resulting article is the demonstration: we delegate manuscript preparation while retaining responsibility for its scientific meaning. This approach to accelerating catalyst discovery with artificial intelligence offers researchers an opportunity to concentrate on scientific investigation while guiding how their results are communicated.

papers.title: Toward Interpretable Graph-Based Machine Learning for Combustion Kinetic Model Generation
papers.abstract: This work presents an atom-conserving and interpretable graph neural network (GNN) for combustion kinetic model generation, where atoms are represented as nodes, covalent bonds are represented as edges, and reactions are represented as bond-rearrangement operations. Its artificial-intelligence (AI) contribution is a reaction generator that extends a standard Graph Isomorphism Network with Edges (GINE) architecture through reaction-context embeddings, reaction branching & third-body reaction inputs, Arrhenius-rate-parameter prediction, pairwise decoding, and stochastic inference over evolving reactant pools. Trained on the Li–Dryer hydrogen combustion kinetic model (8 species and 21 reactions), the GNN reproduces trained chemistry and generates element-balanced new reactions and intermediate species outside the training dataset, many of which have experimental analogues. When trained on a subset of the Li–Dryer dataset, the model recovered most held-out reactions and revealed relationships between samples (reactions) in the model’s latent space. The results suggest that the model learns transferable local reaction structures and generates valid species and reactions. As with any reaction generators, the generated reaction models require thermochemical and kinetic verification; the intended engineering application is low-cost reaction-pathway exploration for new fuels and prioritization of experiments and first-principles calculations to develop new combustion kinetic models.

papers.title: What a low-bias filter leaves out: measured performance on the excluded negatives of a drug–target interaction benchmark
papers.abstract: Eligibility rules define which interactions contribute to a benchmark score. The low-bias BindingDB benchmark retains a drug only when it has both positive and negative labels, excluding measured inactive pairs involving drugs without a measured active. We reconstructed this rule in a declared BindingDB population and evaluated retained and excluded negatives against the same positive reference. After cleaning and an additional connectivity-overlap restriction, the excluded region contained 78.4% of the measured negative pairs. DrugBAN and MolTrans were trained in three evaluation designs with five seeds; a released BioT5 checkpoint was evaluated on its published split. Across these evaluations, pooled AUROC was 0.072–0.136 lower on excluded negatives. Lower performance also occurred within proteins with sufficient observations in both regions. DrugBAN remained ahead of MolTrans, but the change in their advantage depended on aggregation: it generally increased under pooled AUROC, whereas equalprotein weighting produced smaller or oppositely directed changes. Cross-protein comparisons accounted for approximately 99.8–99.9% of pooled AUROC's pair-comparison weight. The closer BioT5–DrugBAN comparison additionally depended on scoring convention. These results measure regional performance differences, conditional on the chosen positive reference; they do not estimate a causal filter effect or deployment performance. Benchmark reports should specify eligibility, coverage at the evaluated unit, metric aggregation, and performance on excluded regions where labels are available.

papers.title: Fabrication and Microstructural Analysis of ZnO and In2O3 MOS Thin Film Sensors with Embedded Microheaters for Methane Sensing
papers.abstract: Methane detection is essential for both environmental monitoring and industrial safety due to its greenhouse impact and explosive potential. Conventional sensing approaches, such as electrochemical, infrared, and catalytic bead sensors, are limited by stability and sensitivity constraints. Metal oxide semiconductor (MOS) sensors, particularly those based on ZnO and In2O3, provide an attractive alternative owing to their stability, high sensitivity, compactness, and fabrication compatibility. In this work, compact MOS chip sensors were developed using a six-layer architecture that integrates a microheater for localized thermal control. Thin films of ZnO and In2O3 were deposited via magnetron sputtering with photolithographically defined geometries, followed by annealing under inert gas conditions. Microstructural and surface morphological characterization was performed using atomic force microscopy (AFM), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS). Results revealed that ZnO films undergo significant surface restructuring upon annealing, exhibiting increased roughness, grain coarsening, and oxygen vacancy formation, whereas In2O3 retained compact morphology and stoichiometric stability. These findings establish a sensitivity–stability trade-off between the two materials, with ZnO showing higher surface activity favourable for methane adsorption, and In2O3 offering reproducibility and long-term stability.

papers.title: Chemical Representation Dependence of Quinone Reduction Energetics: Site-Specific Limits of Methylthio Surrogates for Cysteine-Derived Conjugates
papers.abstract: Methylthio substituents are compact models for larger sulfur-linked quinone conjugates, yet their fidelity for calculated one-electron reduction-energy shifts is uncertain. We audited a historical survey of 38 methylthio attachment sites in 26 quinones; four source-energy outputs remain unreconciled, leaving 34 archive-corroborated site shifts across 25 parents. In a historical matched comparison of ten SMe and N-acetylcysteine methyl ester-derived (AcCysOMe) conjugate models, the original median absolute mismatch was 0.175900 eV. An explicitly retrospective, source-corroborated eightsite subset retained a median mismatch of 0.162917 eV, above the prespecified 0.05 eV screening tolerance, with category agreement of 1/3 among decisive SMe cases. Four separately conformercorrected case studies included opposite-sign shifts for benz[a]anthracene-3,4-dione and its 7-methyl analogue. An alternative-functional PBE0-D4 fixed-geometry analysis retained both numerical sign differences, although the 7-methyl analogue's AcCysOMe shift (−0.037065 eV) was near zero under the original category rule. Retrospective spin-population checks indicated predominantly quinonecentered radical-anion states. Thus, sulfur-fragment truncation can materially alter a computed site-

papers.title: Pyrrolidinium-Assisted Proton and Cation Exchange Enables Near-Quantitative Rare Earth Extraction from Synthetic NdFeB Leachate
papers.abstract: Diglycolamide (DGA) extractants offer strong affinity for rare-earth elements (REEs), tunable coordination, and phosphorus-free chemistry. Incomplete use of their molar capacity limits extractant utilization efficiency (EUE), while low distribution ratios (D) require larger organic-phase volumes. Ionic liquids (ILs) can stabilize DGA–REE complexes and modify extraction pathways, with proton exchange reported in some imidazolium ILs and IL-mediated cation or anion exchange in others. Combining exchange pathways within a single system could improve extraction and EUE, but this remains underexplored. Screening five ILs with N,N-dioctyldiglycolamic acid (DODGAA) identified [C2mpyrr][NTf2] as the best-performing formulation, outperforming the tested pyridinium- and imidazolium-based ILs and achieving an Nd3+ distribution ratio of approximately 7,000 at an organic-to-aqueous volume ratio of 0.1 with near-quantitative extraction. Slope analysis (~3.3), proton balance (~1 H+ per Nd3+), and aqueous 1H NMR support coupled proton and IL-cation exchange. The maximum EUE of 17.0% is comparable to several organophosphorus extractants. In synthetic NdFeB leachate, Nd3+ and Dy3+ were extracted at >99%, with low boron transfer and iron removed by hydroxide precipitation. Over five extraction–stripping cycles, the organic phase retained ~73% of its initial extraction efficiency, limited by incomplete single-stage stripping. Pyrrolidinium-assisted coupled exchange offers an efficient route to REE extraction.

papers.title: Spatially Separated NO Capture and Hydrogenation for NH <sub>3</sub> Synthesis from O <sub>2</sub> -Containing Streams
papers.abstract: The selective conversion of nitric oxide (NO) in combustion flue gases to ammonia (NH 3 ) is a promising strategy for sustainable nitrogen management. However, this conversion remains challenging in O 2 -containing exhaust gases because coexisting O 2 strongly inhibits catalytic hydrogenation. Here, we developed a tandem NO capture and hydrogenation system for NH 3 production from O 2 -containing streams. Various adsorbents were examined for NO capture in the presence of O 2 , and Li-impregnated β zeolite with 1.2 wt% Li, denoted as Li(1.2)/β, was selected as a representative adsorbent owing to its high NO x adsorption capacity. In situ IR spectroscopy showed that NO x species formed from NO + O 2 on Li(1.2)/β were mainly present as [NO + ][NO 2 ] adducts, which subsequently desorbed as NO 2 upon heating. By coupling the Li(1.2)/β-based temperature-swing adsorption unit, operated between 30 and 200 °C, with a downstream Cu(5)/CeO 2 hydrogenation reactor operated at 450 °C, the tandem system maintained an NH 3 yield of 55–60% during a 7 h cyclic operation. These results demonstrate the feasibility of spatially separated NO capture and downstream NO x hydrogenation for converting NO in O 2 -containing streams into a valuable nitrogen resource.

papers.title: Cationic surfactant-modified cotton and cotton/polyester textile-derived biochar for hexavalent chromium removal via ion-exchange
papers.abstract: Biochar derived from textile waste presents an opportunity in the circular economy for contaminant remediation from industrial wastewater. In this study, biochars derived from cotton and cotton-polyester blended textiles were assessed for the removal of the toxic and pervasive aqueous contaminant, hexavalent chromium (Cr(VI)). Unmodified textile-derived biochars exhibited some adsorption capacity for Cr(VI) under environmentally relevant pH conditions, but removal improved substantially once modified with the cationic surfactant cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB). Adsorption experiments conducted at 50–100 mg/L as Cr showed equilibrium capacities of about 1.6–2.0 mg Cr/g BC for unmodified biochars, increasing to 10–15 mg Cr/g BC for CTAB-modified materials, with rapid adsorption in the first 5 minutes. Maximum adsorption capacity for CTAB-modified cotton and cotton-polyester biochar prepared at 450 o C was determined to be 72 and 32 mg Cr/g BC, respectively, comparable to established adsorbents. Adsorption-desorption experiments conducted using low (10 mM NaCl) and high (500 mM NaCl) ionic strength showed apparent anion exchange capacities of ~0.08 to 0.09 meq/g, suggesting that chromium retention involves ion exchange with CTAB-derived quaternary ammonium sites in addition to electrostatic attraction. Similar adsorption behavior between feedstocks suggests that surfactant modification played a larger role in overall performance than feedstock composition. These findings demonstrate that textile-derived biochar can be engineered through surfactant modification to enhance the removal efficiency of industrially-relevant anionic contaminants like Cr(VI), supporting their potential use as low-cost sorbents for industrial wastewater treatment.

papers.title: Data-efficient molecular and nanoparticle design via fine-tuned large language models
papers.abstract: Designing molecules with prescribed properties is central to pharmaceutical and materials innovation, but vast chemical design spaces make development lengthy and costly. Generative artificial intelligence can accelerate molecular discovery, but its deployment in many real-world domains remains limited by the need for large task-specific training datasets. To enable generative design when property-labeled data are scarce, we present a data-efficient foundation-model adaptation strategy combining complementary positive and negative property prompts with parameter-efficient fine-tuning. Generated molecules are then ranked by molecular graph-kernel Gaussian process regression for structure-aware prioritization. In a controlled computational setting, the platform generated candidates with novel scaffolds satisfying multiple design objectives, including predicted target binding, synthesizability, and drug-likeness. Although only a few hundred training molecules per target met all three criteria, the model generated thousands of new molecules matching the desired profiles. For prospective validation, we applied the model to nanoparticle design, a domain of high clinical potential but limited excipient diversity. Fine-tuning on only 1,521 labeled drug-excipient pairs - including just 139 nanoparticle-forming examples identified new nanoparticle-forming excipients for the anticancer drug sorafenib. The model proposed lithocholic acid and the sorafenib metabolite M6, and experiments confirmed that both form stable sorafenib nanoparticles with high encapsulation efficiency and increased in vitro potency. These findings show that foundation-model fine-tuning with complementary prompts and graph-based prioritization enables data-efficient molecular design in low-data chemical domains.

papers.title: Resolving the Methanol-Promoting Alloy–Oxide Ensemble in Pd–Zn/C Catalysts for CO2 Hydrogenation
papers.abstract: Pd–Zn bimetallic catalysts are a promising alternative to traditional Cu-based systems for the hydrogenation of CO2 to methanol. Yet a complete understanding of their structure-activity relationships has been hindered by methodological limitations, such as high-temperature synthesis and the use of bulk characterization techniques. Here, we use an inert graphitic carbon support to prepare a Pd–Zn/C catalyst library with systematically varied Zn:Pd ratio and pre-treatment temperature. In situ Pd and Zn K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), coupled with multivariate curve resolution, resolves the coexisting Pd–Zn and Zn-derived oxide components, including Pd-rich FCC α-PdZny, ordered tetragonal Zn-rich β1-PdZnz, crystalline ZnO, and disordered ZnOx. The components identified by XAS provide a reference database for the detailed chemical speciation across the catalyst library. In situ XAS showed that catalysts pre-treated in H2 at 250-450 °C do not restructure during catalysis, and therefore it is sufficient to analyze their structure before catalysis to uncover structure-activity correlations. Combined with kinetic measurements and statistical correlation analysis, this framework identifies the structural motifs associated with methanol and CO formation. Methanol productivity is linked to the coexistence of ordered tetragonal β1-PdZnz (z > 1) and disordered ZnOx, whereas CO forms across a broader range of Pd-containing bimetallic environments. In situ restructuring experiments for the catalysts pre-treated at mild conditions (50 °C) further show that the hydride-forming FCC α-PdZny phase acts as a precursor that can evolve toward the more methanol-selective β1-phase to form an active interface under catalytic conditions in the presence of Zn oxide. These results resolve the methanol-promoting alloy–oxide ensemble in Pd–Zn catalysts and show that selective methanol synthesis depends on stabilizing the appropriate local oxidic environment at the alloy boundary, rather than simply maximizing Zn loading or alloy fraction.

papers.title: Photocatalyst-Free Visible-Light-Induced Trifluoroalkylation of Electron-Deficient Heteroaromatics via a Three-Component Minisci-Type Reaction.
papers.abstract: The combination of electron-poor heterocycles and trifluoromethyl motifs is widely found in pharmaceuticals, making the development of methods for the simultaneous introduction of these two features highly desirable. Herein, we report a fast, acid-free, metal-free, photocatalyst-free, and operationally simple multicomponent approach for the trifluoroalkylation of electron-poor heterocycles under open-air conditions. The method relies on the ability of trifluoromethyl thianthrenium triflate to generate CF3 radicals and proceeds through a polarity-reversal cascade strategy employing electron-rich alkenes as linkers. A broad range of alkenes and heterocycles was evaluated, and the chemo-and regioselectivity of the process were thoroughly investigated. Furthermore, mechanistic studies revealed that multiple pathways contribute to the formation of the desired products.

papers.title: One-Pot Synthesis of Oxazolines from Carboxylic Acids and Amino Alcohols using Phosphorus(V) Catalysis
papers.abstract: Oxazolines are important heterocycles for a range of industrial applications, and yet their synthesis from simple carboxylic acid and amino alcohol substrates requires multiple steps and stoichiometric reagents. Here, we demonstrate the one-pot direct synthesis using a bifunctional boronic acid/phosphorus(V) catalyst that is shown to catalyze both the amidation and cyclodehydration steps. Different classes of carboxylic acid coupling partners are surveyed, the mechanism for cyclodehydration investigated, and a variety of 2-substituted oxazolines prepared without the addition of stoichiometric reagents.

papers.title: Ion Pairing and Electrochemical Behavior of Al(OTf)3 in Propylene Carbonate Bilal Overton
papers.abstract: The development of practical aluminum-ion batteries requires electrolytes capable of stabilizing multivalent aluminum species while maintaining sufficient ionic conductivity and electrochemical activity. Here, we investigate aluminum trifluoromethanesulfonate (Al(OTf)3) dissolved in propylene carbonate (PC) as a potential halide-free aluminum electrolyte using a combined computational and experimental approach. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations were employed to optimize coordination structures and predict speciation, redox potentials, and vibrational signatures of solvated aluminum complexes. Cyclic voltammetry reveals electrochemical activity with a reduction onset near 0 V versus Al/Al3+, consistent with computational predictions. Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy indicates significant ionic association between aluminum and triflate anions, suggesting the coexistence of free and coordinated species in solution. Scanning electron microscopy of copper substrates after chronoamperometric deposition shows surface features consistent with metal deposition, while X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy confirms the presence of aluminum-containing species. The electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of approximately 5.4 mS cm-1 at ~0.6 M. These results demonstrate that Al(OTf)3/PC solutions support electrochemical activity of aluminum species but exhibit strong ion association, highlighting key challenges and opportunities for halide-free aluminum battery electrolytes.

papers.title: Discovery of Nanomolar CDK2 Inhibitors Using Boltz-2
papers.abstract: The computational design of small-molecule ligands for pharmaceutical targets has historically been hindered by a strict trade-off between screening throughput and predictive accuracy. While next-generation cofolding affinity models like Boltz-2 hold immense promise for bridging this gap, their utility in prospective medicinal chemistry campaigns remains largely unexplored. To date, virtual screens leveraging these models have been overwhelmingly restricted to standard commercial catalogs, leaving their capacity to navigate novel, synthetically tailored chemical spaces unevaluated. Here, we present a novel hit discovery platform that integrates Boltz-2’s affinity module with a custom screening space of stereochemically complex tetrahydroquinolines, accessed efficiently via a single-step multicomponent approach. Boltz-2 successfully guided both the initial high-throughput virtual screening of these targeted scaffolds and subsequent hit optimization, rapidly yielding nanomolar inhibitors of cyclin-dependent kinase 2 (CDK2).

papers.title: A Novel Reactive Incipient Wetness Impregnation Assisted by H <sub>2</sub> O <sub>2</sub> for Vanadium Catalysts: the Case of V/Silicalite-1 zeolites in Oxidative Propane Dehydrogenation
papers.abstract: Metal deposition in zeolites is often interpreted using concepts developed for relatively open support surfaces, overlooking the consequences of precursor transport and deposition within confined microporous environments. Here, we introduce an H 2 O 2 -mediated reactive impregnation strategy for supported vanadium catalysts reactive vanadium impregnation mediated by H 2 O 2 and that avoids organics complexing agents (carbon-free) exploiting vanadium-peroxo chemistry to dissolve in situ the precursor into smaller complexed soluble species and modify its interaction with Silicalite-1. The resulting catalyst displayed still detectable vanadium aggregates compared with conventional impregnation. The materials tested under oxidative propane dehydrogenation exhibited comparable catalytic activity (slightly higher) but improved stability during repeated reaction-regeneration cycling. The in situ coke accumulation within a cycle was tracked in the intermediary regeneration steps by using online MS, and showed similar amounts for both preparation routes, suggesting that carbon deposition is governed predominantly by the structural and pore-capacity characteristics of Silicalite-1. Structural characterization revealed distinct vanadium-support interactions in the H 2 O 2 -assisted materials, while microscopy and H2-TPR indicated different evolution of the support and vanadium phase during cycling. Under representative OPDH conditions, the H 2 O 2 -assisted catalyst reached 41% propane conversion and 90% propylene selectivity, with a 30% lower deactivation rate over ten cycles. These results identify precursor chemistry and metal-support interaction, rather than dispersion alone, as key design parameters for supported vanadium catalysts.

papers.title: Comparable Trifluoroacetic Acid Deposition in Guyana and Canada: Evidence of Atmospheric Formation and Remobilization
A Dioxasilepane-Functionalized Styrenic Monomer as a Platform for Novel Silicon-Containing Polystyrenes
papers.abstract: A dioxasilepane-derived styrenic monomer, 2,4,4,7,7-pentamethyl-2-(4-vinylphenyl)-1,3,2-dioxasilepane (St-Si(pan)Me), is introduced as the first polymerizable representative of the recently developed Si(pan) platform, a seven-membered cyclic dialkoxysilane motif combining high stability with controllable silicon reactivity. The monomer combines the exceptional kinetic stability of the seven-membered cyclic dialkoxysilane with a polymerizable styrenic functionality, enabling direct incorporation of the Si(pan) motif into polystyrene-based polymers and materials. Following multigram-scale synthesis, the compatibility of St-Si(pan)Me with conventional free-radical polymerization was systematically investigated. Among the investigated polymerization temperatures (70 - 90 °C), 90 °C provided the best balance between molar-mass distribution, structural fidelity, thermal stability, and photophysical performance while fully preserving the integrity of the Si(pan) framework. Beyond free radical polymerization, Reversible Addition-Fragmentation Chain-Transfer (RAFT) polymerization showed compatibility with controlled radical polymerization, while preliminary emulsion polymerization revealed distinct behavior under aqueous conditions, suggesting opportunities for future siloxane network formation. Copolymerization with styrene afforded silicon-functionalized copolymers with tuneable compositions and systematically adjustable molecular, thermal, and photophysical properties. Comprehensive characterization by various techniques confirmed successful incorporation of the Si(pan) functionality throughout the polymer series. This work establishes St-Si(pan)Me as a versatile platform monomer that expands the toolbox of silicon-functionalized styrenes and provides access to a new class of thermally robust and intrinsically luminescent silicon-containing polystyrenes.

papers.title: Conditional latent distillation enables controllable molecular generation in data-limited soft materials
papers.abstract: De novo molecular generation is particularly difficult when materials-specific datasets are too small to support reliable training of a new generative backbone. We develop a framework for controllable molecular generation based on conditional latent distillation and chemistryconstrained construction. A variational autoencoder (VAE) pretrained on more than 20,000 polymer molecules supplies a starting molecular representation, reducing reliance on training a new generator from approximately 1,600 surfactant or 200 anion-exchange-membrane (AEM) records. A compact conditional student learns to predict teacher latent coordinates from molecular descriptors and property-associated inputs, while molecular exploration and chemistry-aware editing govern which candidate structures are constructed and retained. In the primary surfactant application, Bayesian optimization produced 841 cleaned novel structures and retained 118, compared with 205 and 15 from nearest-neighbor exploration under equal 20,000-attempt mutation budgets. An independent distillation-guided teacher-latent retrieval benchmark yielded 2.32 more retained candidates per request than anchor-count-matched random selection (95% confidence interval (CI), 1.78–2.86). The conditional mapping also reduced teacher-coordinate prediction error by 40.3% and decoderdistribution divergence by 59.1% relative to the strongest tested regression baselines, validating the distillation-based interface. Molecular dynamics characterized selected surfactants at a water–decane interface. We then applied the chemistry-constrained construction and screening workflow to AEM-related building blocks, obtaining 125 screened candidates and assessing selected cations in water. These results demonstrate controllable molecular exploration and structural selection in data-limited settings, without claiming experimentally verified control of final materials properties.

papers.title: Synthesis of Leaching-Proof Single-Site Catalysts Based on Metallolinker MOFs
papers.abstract: The creation of single-site catalysts, for which all active sites have the same structure, is a key goal in contemporary heterogeneous catalysis. Many MOF linkers present well-defined binding sites for transition metals and may thus provide access to single-site catalysts. Depending on how the metal is introduced into the linker-based binding site, however, additional undesired species such as pore-confined nanoparticles or node-bound metal centers may be formed that can be difficult to locate. Here, we introduce catalytic interrogation as a diagnostic workflow for identifying the types of active sites that contribute to the catalytic activity observed for MOF catalysts. Using a suite of MOFs with porphyrin linkers as a case study, we combine catalytic interrogation with extensive electron microscopy to shed light on the rhodium-based active sites present in the MOF. We show that for strongly coordinating binding sites that furnish leaching-proof MOF-based catalysts, post-synthetic metalation carries a significant risk of undesired nanoparticle incorporation. MOF assembly from metalated linkers, on the other hand, generates MOFs that behave as single-site catalysts.

papers.title: An open-source electrosynthesis platform for reaction screening enables a nickel-catalyzed electroreductive aryl cyanation
papers.abstract: The application of electrochemistry to synthetic organic chemistry has resulted in the development of more efficient and sustainable synthesis methodologies. However, the costs and technical burdens of electrochemical instrumentation impose barriers towards the wider adoption of electrochemistry. Herein, we report a modular, open-source platform for electrosynthesis screening built around a low-cost miniaturized potentiostat. The platform supports electrosynthesis and electroanalytic methods, and its open design readily allows for customization. We demonstrate this utility of the platform by the development of a zinc-free, nickel-catalyzed reductive cyanation of aryl bromides with an electrophilic cyanating agent (2-methyl-2-phenylmalononitrile, MPMN). Replacing stoichiometric zinc reductant with a sacrificial tertiary amine allows the cyanation of aryl bromides incompatible with the original zinc-based conditions. In addition, acetonitrile can be used in place of typical hazardous amide solvents. This work provides a blueprint for non-expert practitioners to integrate electrochemistry as an accessible and affordable technique in their research programs.

papers.title: Picking a Pucker: Excited-State Charge Redistribution Navigates the BN-Reshaped Conical-Intersection Landscape in Azaborine Photochemistry
papers.abstract: Photoexcited benzene yields multiple isomers, whereas its BN isostere 1,2-azaborine selectively forms BN-Dewar benzene (BN-DB), despite both decaying through ringpuckered S1/S0 conical intersections (CIs). This selectivity is puzzling given that BNinduced asymmetry in 1,2-azaborine creates six distinct puckering sites and potentially multiple CIs, yet only a single photoproduct is observed. Here, we map the S1/S0 CI landscape of 1,2-azaborine using CASSCF and XMS-CASPT2 and identify eight N-, B-, and C-puckered CIs that open channels to various isomers including BN-DB and BN-benzvalene (BN-BV). BN incorporation therefore does not remove the excitedstate pathways of benzene but multiplies them. Of these CIs, only the N-puckered CIs leading to BN-DB lie below the S1 minimum, a preference we trace to S1 N→B charge redistribution. We then examine whether structural modifications that alter this redistribution can change CI accessibility, considering CH3 and F substitution and changes in B and N positions. Notably, 1,4-azaborine exhibits a qualitative shift from N→B to C→B charge redistribution. Consistently, C-and B-puckered CIs lie below the S1 minimum and may provide access to BN-BV, a versatile synthetic intermediate currently obtained through two photochemical steps. Together, these results suggest that S1 charge redistribution may be a key lever for steering azaborine photochemistry and for designing more direct routes to BN-BV.

papers.title: Chiral Organic Single Crystals as a Platform for Chirality-Induced Spin Selectivity
papers.abstract: The chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) effect has attracted increasing attention for its unique ability to generate spin-polarized currents without magnetic components, with promising applications in spintronics, optoelectronics, and electrocatalysis. Although a wide range of chiral materials have been demonstrated to exhibit the CISS effect, most reported systems are based on amorphous films, self-assembled monolayers, or supramolecular assemblies, where structural disorder and aggregative traps compromise reliable evaluation of the CISS effect and obscure the structure-property relationship. Here, we overcome these limitations by constructing high-quality single crystals of chiral BN-embedded double helicenes, which feature a rigid chiral backbone and ordered molecular packing. Using magnetic conductive atomic force microscopy, we show that the single-crystal platform yields significantly improved current uniformity and measurement reproducibility compared with spin-coated thin films. Taking advantage of this enhanced reliability, we systematically investigated spin-selective transport in single crystals with thicknesses ranging from 18 to 330 nm. The spin polarization initially increases rapidly with crystal thickness, reaches a broad maximum, and remains pronounced over transport distances of up to 330 nm. This thickness-dependent behavior provides direct evidence for the cumulative spinselective transport along the long-range ordered structure, thereby distinguishing intrinsic bulk spin polarization from interfacial contributions. Our results thus establish chiral organic single crystals as a robust platform for investigating the CISS effect and unveiling clear structureproperty correlations.

papers.title: Mechanochemically Accelerated Defluorosilylation of α-Trifluoromethyl Styrenes
papers.abstract: We report a mechanochemical copper-catalyzed defluorosilylation of α-trifluoromethyl styrenes with silylboranes. Mechanical activation dramatically accelerated the C–F bond transformation, reducing the reaction time from 8 h to only 30 min at room temperature while substantially decreasing solvent consumption. The reaction exhibits broad substrate compatibility and scalability, highlighting mechanochemistry as an effective strategy for accelerating selective C–F bond functionalization.

papers.title: Self-Sustained Sabatier Reaction via Submerged Photosynthesis
papers.abstract: CO 2 methanation is a promising route for carbon utilization, yet conventional processes remain constrained by their reliance on externally supplied H 2 and specialized catalysts. To overcome these limitations, this study introduces a self-sustained Sabatier reaction based on the submerged photosynthesis of crystallites (SPSC). In this single aqueous system, metallic Fe and Mg powders react with carbonated water to generate H 2 and CH 4 near room temperature without an added methanation catalyst. Light irradiation accelerates the production of both gases. CH 4 production scales approximately in proportion with H 2 generation across diverse reaction conditions, with both gases exhibiting similar apparent activation energies. During the reaction, plate-like FeCO 3 forms on the Fe surface, while Mg addition modifies this carbonate structure to enhance relative CH 4 formation at longer reaction times. Scavenger experiments confirm the pivotal role of electron transfer in gas production. These results demonstrate that metal oxidation, electron transfer, and surface-bound carbonate reactions drive SPSC-methanation, successfully integrating in situ H 2 generation, CH 4 formation, and metal carbonate crystallization without external H 2 input.

papers.title: Mechanistic Insights into the Non-Equilibrium Synthesis of Highly Fluorinated Cation-Disordered Rock-Salt Cathodes: Solid-State Thermal vs. Mechanochemical Reactions
papers.abstract: Fluorination is an effective strategy to improve the stability of high-capacity cation-disordered rock-salt (DRX) cathodes, yet incorporating substantial fluorine through conventional thermal synthesis remains challenging. Although mechanochemical milling enables highly fluorinated compositions, the reaction pathways underlying this capability remain poorly understood. This study compares the thermal and mechanochemical synthesis of Li2Mn0.5Ti0.5O2F from identical precursors using in situ thermal and custom-made quasi in situ mechanochemical synchrotron X-ray diffraction. Thermal synthesis proceeds through a Ti-rich DRX intermediate followed by Mn incorporation. Subsequent LiF incorporation coincides with MnO segregation, while further heating induces phase decomposition and substantial fluorine loss. In contrast, mechanochemical milling generates a transient amorphous intermediate that coexists with Ti-rich DRX during progressive MnO incorporation and subsequently transforms into highly fluorinated DRX. Elemental analysis combined with 19F solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance shows estimated fluorine contents of 1.00–1.06 F per formula unit of DRX after mechanochemical synthesis, compared with 0.32–0.41 after thermal synthesis. These findings support an amorphous-mediated pathway for accommodating Mn and F within metastable DRX, highlighting control over transient intermediates as a strategy for accessing highly fluorinated oxyfluoride cathodes.

papers.title: SpectraFit-Core: a Rust-cored nonlinear curve-fitting library validated against the NIST Statistical Reference Datasets
papers.abstract: Nonlinear least-squares fitting of parametric line shapes is routine in the analysis of spectra, and the analyst often knows relationships between the parameters before the fit starts, such as a shared width or a fixed intensity ratio. SpectraFit-Core is an open-source curve-fitting library in which this knowledge is part of the model. A model is a graph of named components, and each relationship is an expression edge on that graph, within one spectrum or across several spectra fitted jointly in one call. On a measured Fe L2,3 energy-loss spectrum, four such relationships leave the fitted values unchanged and make the edge-step amplitude 28 times more precise. Because the model is a description rather than code, the same graph can be fitted by other implementations and their parameters compared name by name. The parameters and standard errors of the library are checked against certified values: on 22 of the 27 nonlinear-regression problems of the NIST Statistical Reference Datasets, the least accurately recovered parameter agrees to more than six significant figures, and the standard errors agree nearly as well except on Lanczos1. Kernels, analytic Jacobians, and solver iteration run in compiled Rust behind a typed Python interface, which also makes the library faster than lmfit, SciPy, and JAX on its benchmark. A companion repository regenerates the results from the published release. SpectraFit-Core is released under the MIT license, distributed on PyPI and archived on Zenodo.

papers.title: A hydrochromic porous aromatic framework for self-reporting, high-capacity atmospheric water harvesting
papers.abstract: Atmospheric water harvesting materials are typically optimised for sorption performance alone, despite the practical importance of monitoring sorbent loading. Here, we report a hydrochromic porous aromatic framework that integrates water capture and self-reporting within a single adaptive material. Sulfonation of PAF-1 affords the hydrophilic framework PAF-1-S that adsorbs 0.18 g·g-1 of water at only 10% RH and reaches 1.87 g·g-1 at 90% RH, combining exceptional low-humidity capture with the highest total capacity among the porous sorbents surveyed here. Water adsorption simultaneously induces a reversible, graded colour change, enabling direct visualisation of sorbent loading without external sensing hardware. Spectroscopic analysis indicates that this response arises from hydration-driven acid–base equilibria within the modified framework. Combined with rapid sorption kinetics, low-temperature regeneration and robust cycling stability, these findings establish responsive porous adsorbents as a strategy for intelligent sorption materials.

papers.title: A bipartite quantum-acoustic architecture stabilizes multi-exciton solitons at 323 K
Directional Electric Fields at Designed MOF Sites: Implications for Electrostatic Preorganization and Catalysis
papers.abstract: Enzymes achieve their enormous catalytic power in part through electrostatic preorganization: non-covalent interactions arrange an electric field that is preorganized to stabilize the change in dipole moment between a reaction's ground and transition states. Thus, the catalytic relevance of an electric field depends not only on its magnitude but also on its orientation. Here we use the enforced rigidity of a metal–organic framework (MOF), PCN-521, to demonstrate this orientation dependence directly. We introduce an aldehyde carbonyl vibrational Stark probe in situ, first as a protected ketal, then deprotect it to reveal a carbonyl at the same node-capping site as a previously reported nitrile probe, extending field measurements to a field reporter of greater relevance to enzymatic catalysis. Electric field- vibrational frequency calibrated probes using the vibrational Stark effect report a trifluoroacetate field donor that projects nearly its full destabilizing field onto the collinear nitrile (sp, C≡N) but only a fraction onto the off-axis aldehyde (sp2, C=O) — a geometric effect. Because the framework's non-covalent contacts, unlike an enzyme active site's, cannot reorganize, this controlled, single-site comparison isolates alignment from magnitude. While electric fields are often invoked to explain observations near electrodes or droplet interfaces, these results show the importance of alignment which is often neglected.

papers.title: Predictive Design of Greener Ultrafast Chromatography for Accelerated Discovery and Development Chemistry
papers.abstract: Liquid chromatography (LC) is the analytical workhorse of pharmaceutical research and, at the same time, one of its largest sources of organic solvent waste and energy consumption. High-throughput experimentation amplifies this burden by generating thousands of samples per campaign, each conventionally analyzed by methods that consume milliliters to liters of solvent per system and keep instruments running for hours. Because solvent consumption and instrument energy demand scale directly with run time, accelerating these analyses is both a throughput and a sustainability priority. Routine implementation of ultrafast LC, however, has been limited by two related barriers: the experimental effort required to identify high-speed conditions that retain decision-critical selectivity, and the solvent-intensive nature of method development itself. Herein, we introduce a predictive in silico framework that transforms ultrafast LC assay development from empirical screening into a model-driven design workflow. Experimental retention data are used to model chromatographic selectivity across temperature, gradient slope, flow rate, and column geometry, enabling rapid identification of the fastest separation conditions that preserve the information required for decision-making. Retention modeling is further combined with fit-for-purpose resolution criteria and in silico peak clustering to selectively resolve critical components while intentionally grouping noncritical analytes to maximize throughput. The approach is demonstrated across closely related isomers, chiral analyses, and high-throughput reaction screening, where model-predicted separations translated directly into reliable experiments, substantially shortened analysis cycle times, and required minimal manual intervention. The resulting methods give lower analytical method greenness scores, in some cases by more than 10-fold. Together, this framework establishes a general strategy for systematically deploying greener ultrafast chromatographic assays while reducing method-development burden, solvent consumption, and energy demand, with broad applicability to biocatalysis, natural products, metabolomics, high-throughput experimentation, and modern synthesis.

papers.title: Electrostatic preactivation, a missing step in dioxygen activation
papers.abstract: For decades, dioxygen activation has been understood primarily in terms of reduction: the transfer of the first electron from a metal centre, flavin or other reducing species to O 2 , followed by the formation of reactive oxygen species. Here we identify and quantify a preceding stage, electrostatic preactivation , across organozinc complexes and enzyme active sites. The surrounding field splits the π* manifold of neutral O 2 and makes electron attachment energetically favourable at unchanged O–O geometry; point charges alone reproduce this response before charge moves. In dialkylzinc systems, additional Lewis-acidic centres lower the electron-attachment energy and the charge-transfer state, while the electron originates from the same Zn–C bond. A relation calibrated on organozinc systems, with a correction for metal charge and distance, predicts the π* splitting in four enzyme active sites to within 7%, without refitting, including one with crystallographically located O 2 but no metal, cofactor or available electron source.

papers.title: Effective Directionality in Electron-Transfer-Driven Reactions on Bifurcating Multidimensional Potential Energy Surfaces
papers.abstract: Electron transfer (ET) is microscopically reversible under a closed, finite, Hermitian Hamiltonian, yet ET-driven reactions are strongly directional: of several possible products, one is formed and kept. Standard theories explain this through thermodynamic driving forces, free-energy surfaces, or coupling to a continuum of environmental modes. We ask whether the geometry of a multidimensional Born-Oppenheimer surface, combined with relaxation into the molecule's own vibrational modes, can supply this directionality without an external bath. On model surfaces with a reaction coordinate and an orthogonal branching coordinate, the shape of the surface after the transition state decides which product forms within about one vibrational period, independently of barrier heights. Relaxation into a closed, energy-conserving set of internal harmonic modes, an idealized model of intramolecular energy redistribution, keeps that decision for hundreds of vibrational periods, even where the microcanonical equilibrium of the full system (reacting coordinates and modes together, at the same energy) favors the other product almost completely. When the branching follows an electron-transfer crossing between coupled diabatic surfaces, the decision can be quantum, and the same internal modes keep it. The decision is kept when the internal modes drain the exchange coordinate, the motion that carries one product into the other, faster than the products exchange. Across random surfaces, spectral densities and coupling patterns, an a priori estimate of this competition predicts most outcomes, and its failures trace to which coordinate holds the energy. Thermal and quantum modes remove the kept decision before they remove commitment. The irreversibility supplied by the internal modes is statistical, as for any finite bath; the geometry fixes the direction, both which product forms and which motion must be drained for it to be kept.

papers.title: Cholesterol-Dependent Membrane Fluidity in Sindbis Virus Governs Viral Particle Stability and Infectivity
papers.abstract: Cholesterol is a key biomolecule that regulates lipid bilayer fluidity, and cholesterol-rich domains in host cells and virions are critical for virion entry and egress. Here, using Alphavirus Sindbis virus (SINV) as a model, we combine new experimental methods and single-particle biological characterization to revisit how envelope cholesterol affects particle stability and the biological consequences for infectivity. To this end, we generated two SINV populations with a 3-fold difference in envelope cholesterol levels (SINV LC and SINV HC ) to assess how cholesterol affects SINV stability and infectivity. Transmission electron microscopy and dynamic light scattering showed minimal differences in morphology and size, indicating that cholesterol minimally alters virion structure. Electrochemical measurements between SINV LC and SINV HC particles revealed similar Zeta Potentials (ζ-potential ~ -31 mV), which implies that the surface distribution of the E1-E2 glycoprotein heterotrimers within the envelope is cholesterol-independent. Titer measurements showed that SINV HC retains nearly an order of magnitude more infectious particles than SINV LC when pre-exposed to 30 minutes of thermal stress, corresponding to a 1.25-fold faster decay rate for the low-cholesterol virions, with SINV LC and SINV HC showing values of 0.34/min and 0.27/min, respectively. Single-particle fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy analysis using the fluidity-sensitive dye DI-8-ANEPPS revealed a statistically significant increase (≥ 0.2 ns; p < 0.0001) in photon arrival times in the SINV HC population, indicating that elevated cholesterol enhances membrane rigidity. Because virion size and ζ-potential remained unchanged while fluorescence lifetimes increased with cholesterol level, these findings indicate that membrane fluidity is the primary parameter governing viral stability and subsequent infectivity.

papers.title: Inverse-Polarity Approach Towards Modular, Red-Shifted, and Soluble Polymethine Fluorophores
papers.abstract: Polymethine dyes are widely used for NIR and SWIR imaging, yet their synthesis still relies on a single coupling paradigm that limits structural diversity and functionalization. Herein, we report a versatile, modular synthesis of heptamethine dyes based on an inverse-polarity approach. Readily available building blocks are converted into a ketone intermediate, which allows independent selection of heterocycles and the central ring system, as well as installation of 4′-substituents via organolithium addition. This intermediate can also be extended by aldehyde homologation to access undecamethine and longer red-shifted scaffolds. The method enables access to polymethine dyes that were previously inaccessible or difficult to synthesize, including dyes with varied central rings, alkyl substitution, and a tri-alkyne scaffold for multivalent bioconjugation. Notably, introducing a localized positive charge on the central ring greatly reduces aggregation and enhances aqueous solubility, allowing direct administration in saline for in vivo imaging without formulation. More than a route to tailored fluorophores, this inverse-polarity platform provides a general alternative to conventional polymethine synthesis and a design framework for engineering soluble, red-shifted, and targetable imaging probes.

papers.title: Direct Access to Carbenoids from Alkyl and α-Acyloxy Halide`s for Boron Homologations: Method Development and Mechanistic Insights
Cellulose Coating Altered the Electro-Chemo-Mechanical Evolution of Sodium Thioantimonate Electrolyte in Solid-state Sodium Batteries: An Operando Raman Study
papers.abstract: All-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) attracted increasing attention due to their improved safety and energy densities; yet electrolyte decomposition and subsequent contact loss limited the interfacial stability of ASSBs. Herein, we report an operando Raman characterization that provides high voltage, time, and spatial resolutions, which enables simultaneous analysis of interfacial decomposition mechanism and morphological evolution. Using Na3SbS4 electrolyte (NSS) and its carboxymethyl-cellulose-encapsulated analogue (NSS-CMC) as exemplars, we precisely contrasted the subtle differences in the two-step reduction mechanism of the two electrolytes. In both systems, Na3SbS3 formed as an intermediate, and Na3Sb binary as one major final product; while the CMC coating altered the kinetics of Na3SbS3 formation and consumption, and extended the formation potential of Na3Sb from 1.35 V (seen in NSS) to 0.50 V (vs. Na/Na+). Oxidation of NSS and NSS-CMC both occur near 2.20 V, although CMC coating altered the crystallinity of the oxidative products. Simultaneously, we captured phenomena that are unique to solid-state electrochemical systems such as particle relocation, morphological change, and reversed reactions. We inferred CMC’s dual role as a voltage barrier and a mechanical buffer in suppressing the electro-chemo-mechanical decomposition of NSS electrolyte. The deep mechanistic insights unravel the exact modification needed for improved interfacial stability.

papers.title: The Illusion of Chemical Continuity Limits Machine Learning Generalization
papers.abstract: The central dogma of materials informatics is the "Scaling Hypothesis": the assumption that chemical space is a continuous manifold, and that, with sufficient data, deep learning models can approximate any structure-property relationship. While this strategy has achieved near-DFT accuracy for thermodynamic properties like formation energy, prediction accuracy for bandgaps suffers from a fundamental, non-converging error floor (~0.4 eV). By analyzing a comprehensive dataset of binary semiconductors and state-of-the-art Graph Neural Networks (including coGN and foundational embeddings), this work isolates the root cause: unlike the smooth, transferable landscape of total energy, the electronic bandgap manifold is topologically disjoint. Consequently, increasing dataset size fails to improve predictions, instead resulting in negative learning, where increasing the structural diversity of the training set (e.g., adding rocksalt data to zincblende models) degrades prediction accuracy for unseen chemistries. This can be traced back to the discrete quantization of atomic orbitals and the resulting band crossings, which create non-differentiable cusps in the property surface. This work establishes a boundary condition for the "Big Data" paradigm: simple regression on atomic coordinates cannot resolve the intrinsic discontinuities of eigenvalue phenomena. Instead, a more detailed integration of quantum mechanics is required, such as direct entrainment of Hamiltonians as descriptors.

papers.title: Vibrational Excitation of Water Drives Proton Reactivity with Native Proteins During Mid-Infrared Laser Desorption Coupled to Mass Spectrometry.
papers.abstract: We discovered a vibrational-excitation-driven proton reactivity between proteins and their surrounding aqueous environment during mid-infrared laser Desorption by Impulsive Vibrational Excitation (DIVE). We show that this process, when coupled directly to high resolution mass spectrometry (MS) without secondary ionization sources, produces intact gas-phase ions of proteins retaining their compact conformations. The unexpected multiple protonation states of protein ions are generated through a series of concerted proton transfer processes to protein surface residues. We propose that laser-induced ionization via DIVE is facilitated by sub-nanosecond transient superheating and Grotthuss proton hopping processes. By coupling to high-resolution MS, protein ionization via DIVE opens up an avenue for chemical and structural characterization of proteins and their complexes directly from aqueous and physiological buffer environments.

papers.title: Sterically Shielded Cations Decouple Ion-Exchange Capacity from Water Uptake in Anion Exchange Membranes
papers.abstract: Anion exchange membranes (AEMs) for electrochemical devices must combine high ion-exchange capacity (IEC) with controlled hydration and dimensional stability. Water uptake is commonly rationalized in terms of IEC and intrinsic cation hydrophilicity, but this picture fails when the cationic site is locally shielded by the polymer architecture. Using the poly(bis-imidazolium) ionene Aemion+® as a model backbone-embedded AEM, we find that it absorbs only ~40% of the water taken up by pendant-cation analogues at matched IEC, reversing the trend expected from solution thermodynamics, which identifies its embedded dimethylimidazolium cation as the more hydrophilic one. All-atom molecular dynamics simulations reveal that adjacent aromatic rings create a three-dimensional steric envelope around the embedded cation, reducing first-shell water coordination by 69% and chloride coordination by 62% relative to the free cation in solution. Restricted access to the cation persists for the membrane in hydroxide form. To separate cation chemistry from architecture, we synthesize poly(phenylene oxide) (PPO) membranes bearing four pendant cations—tetramethylammonium (TMA), dimethylimidazolium (DMIm), piperidinium (Pip), and pyrrolidinium (Mpy)—at matched IEC and find that PPO–TMA and PPO–DMIm have indistinguishable hydration despite the substantially higher intrinsic hydrophilicity of DMIm⁺ in solution, with all four cations falling within a narrow hydration window. These results establish local steric accessibility — the ability of water and counterions to occupy the cation's first solvation shell — as a controlling descriptor for AEM hydration. Engineering cation accessibility therefore offers a molecular design strategy for high-IEC AEMs with controlled hydration and swelling.

papers.title: PARAMAGNETIC SUPRAMOLECULAR POLYMERS OF METAL-METAL BONDED DIRUTHENIUM COMPLEXES
Spectroscopic–Catalytic Onset Decoupling in Energy Electrocatalysis: Evidence, Mechanistic Hypotheses and Research Priorities from 250 Studies
papers.abstract: Spectroelectrochemical methods can be used to reveal the chemistry that governs energy conversion and storage at operating interfaces. The review represents 250 primary studies that employed in situ or operando spectroscopy across carbon dioxide reduction, oxygen evolution, hydrogen evolution, battery interfaces and organic electronics. Three findings stand out. First, only five studies in the entire corpus provide paired surface and bulk onset potentials and these reveal offsets from zero to nearly 300 mV. Second, the magnitude of this offset tracks the binding strength of the catalytic intermediate rather than the prominence of its spectroscopic signature.
