Third, dynamic surface reconstruction creates active phases that differ from the as-prepared material in 147 of 250 systems. The central construct that emerges is onset decoupling: spectroscopic detection of an intermediate does not guarantee catalytic turnover, because binding energetics and site density govern whether accumulated species convert to products. This construct predicts that catalysts with strong intermediate binding will show large offsets and poor activity, while weak binding will produce coupled onsets and high activity.

papers.title: Structural pillar effect of Sn substitution in SrFe 1‒ x Sn x O 3‒ δ catalysts for oxidative decomposition of 1,2-dichloroethane
papers.abstract: Chlorination-induced structural degradation limits the durability of perovskite catalysts for the oxidative decomposition of chlorinated organic compounds. Here, a series of SrFe 1−x Sn x O 3−δ (x = 0, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75 and 1.0) was investigated for oxidation of 1,2-dichloroethane (1,2-DCE), with emphasis on the relationship between activity, structural stability and regenerability. Partial Sn substitution improved light-off performance relative to SrFeO 3−δ , whereas SrSnO 3 exhibited little catalytic activity. Although SrFe 0.50 Sn 0.50 O 3−δ gave the highest conversion during temperature-programmed oxidation, SrFe 0.25 Sn 0.75 O 3−δ (SFSO75) exhibited a more favorable balance between activity and structural stability. Independent exposure tests to CO 2 and HCl revealed that Sn substitution enhanced resistance to carbonate and chloride formation, particularly after oxidative pretreatment. Under a dry reaction feed at 450 °C, SFSO75 retained approximately 40% conversion of 1,2-DCE after 12 h, exceeding that of unsubstituted SrFeO 3−δ . Calcination of spent SFSO75 in air effectively restored its perovskite structure, and the regenerated catalyst maintained conversion at approximately 60% during a subsequent reaction of 12 h despite its lower surface area compared with the fresh catalyst. These results demonstrate the roles of Sn in enhancing activity and stabilizing and regenerating the perovskite structure as an effective approach to sustaining the performance of strontium ferrate for 1,2-DCE oxidation. Furthermore, with cofeeding 2.7% water vapor, fresh SFSO75 maintained conversion near 70% over 12 h and largely preserved the perovskite structure.

papers.title: Quantum Coherence in Guest-Controlled Endohedral Fullerenes: Hierarchical Equations of Motion and a Neural-Network Model.
papers.abstract: Light-harvesting efficiency hinges on how long an excitation stays coherent, yet in natural antennae the environment that destroys that coherence, the protein scaffold, cannot be redesigned at will. Here we invert the architecture and place the bath inside the chromophore: a C60 cage acts as the absorber while an encapsulated guest (CH4, N2, O2 or H2O) supplies a tunable internal environment. Combining B3LYP/6-31G* excitation energies, transition-electrostatic-potential (TrESP) couplings and hierarchical equations of motion (HEOM), we find that the choice of guest alone dictates the character of the dynamics. The guest acts through three parameters: the excitonic coupling to the neighbouring cage, the shift of the cage excitation energy and the reorganisation energy (λ). The damping of quantum beats grows in proportion to λ, coherent exchange gives way to incoherent hopping once λkBT/ℏγ becomes comparable to the coupling, and the guest-induced shifts of the excitation energy set the direction of net energy flow. Pairs containing the polar H2O guest, with λ above 40 cm−1, lie in the incoherent regime, whereas O2@C60, 5750 cm−1 below the other cages, is isolated from them. Two-dimensional electronic spectra of the all-system endohedral fullerenes show beats at the exciton gaps and spectral diffusion on the 100 fs time scale of the bath. We further demonstrate that this mapping can be inverted. A feed-forward neural network trained on a corpus of 3000 HEOM trajectories recovers a dimer’s site-energy gap, excitonic coupling and λ from a single 2 ps trace, with mean absolute errors of 3.45, 1.87 and 1.13 cm−1 on 600 unseen realisations. The coherence must accompany the population, because the sign of the coupling is reversed by a gauge transformation that leaves the populations unchanged; supplied with ρ12(t), the network recovers it in every held-out case. Internalising the bath thus renders coherence both tunable by design and readable from the dynamics.

papers.title: Machine Learning for Ionic Conductivity Prediction in Polymer Electrolytes: A Benchmark on Lithium Systems and a Feasibility Study on the Data-Scarce Multivalent (Mg, Zn, Na) Frontier
papers.abstract: Solid and gel polymer electrolytes are central to safer, more flexible batteries, and machine learning has been used to predict their ionic conductivity directly from composition and processing variables. Almost all of this work targets lithium-ion systems, for which large, curated datasets exist. Polymer electrolytes conducting multivalent or non-lithium cations (magnesium, zinc, sodium) are promising lower-cost alternatives but remain comparably underexplored, in part because no public, ML-ready dataset of their measured ionic conductivities exists. Here we validate a standard composition-to-conductivity pipeline (Random Forest and XGBoost regression) on OBELiX, a published dataset of 599 lithium solid-state electrolytes, reaching R2 = 0.79 against a mean-predicting baseline near zero. We then construct, to our knowledge, the first ML-ready dataset of Mg-, Zn-, and Na-conducting polymer electrolytes, systematically mined from the primary and review literature: 135 data points across 105 distinct host-polymer/salt systems. Applying the same pipeline to this new dataset, a tuned Random Forest reaches R2 = 0.47 under leave-one-out cross-validation, or 0.36 under a more conservative 5-fold estimate, well below the lithium benchmark. Through chemistry-informed feature engineering and a nested cross-validation check, we show this gap is driven primarily by data scarcity and literature measurement heterogeneity, not by model or feature choice. We argue the scarcity is itself the central finding: it puts a number, for the first time, on how far behind the multivalent and non-lithium polymer electrolyte literature sits relative to the lithium-ion mainstream. We release the curated dataset and pipeline to support future community data collection.

papers.title: ICl-Mediated Iodocyclization of Electron-Deficient 1,5-Enynes to Functionalized Iodonaphthalenes
papers.abstract: Iodine-induced cyclizations of 1,5-enynes are generally limited to electron-rich alkenes. We report an ICl-mediated iodocyclization of 1,5-enynes bearing strongly electron-withdrawing vinyl-bis(perfluoroalkanesulfonyl)amide groups. A range of aryl-substituted enynes cyclized under mild conditions to give iodonaphthalenes in good yields with tolerance of halogen and carbonyl substituents. The products retain both the iodine atom and the bis(perfluoroalkanesulfonyl)amide unit. Suzuki-Miyaura coupling at the iodine site proceeds without cleavage of the sulfonimide moiety, demonstrating the utility of the products as precursors to functionalized naphthalenes.

papers.title: Expanding Non-Natural Prenyl Diphosphate Chemical Space through Promiscuous yet Regioselective C2-Methylation
papers.abstract: Prenyl diphosphate methyltransferases are emerging as powerful biocatalysts that bypass the classic isoprene rule, installing methyl appendages directly onto standard (iso)prenyl diphosphate substrates and transforming conventional terpene architectures into non-canonical terpenoids. Although their activity toward natural precursors is well documented, their biocatalytic tolerance toward non-natural analogs remains largely underexplored. Here, we systematically probe the substrate scope of the C2-geranyl diphosphate methyltransferase from Streptomyces coelicolor A3(2) (ScGPP-MT) using a library of 40 structurally diverse synthetic allylic, benzylic and heterocyclic diphosphate (alkyl-PP) analogs spanning 4–15 carbons. Direct screening revealed that 10 analogs serve as substrates, including the natural substrate geranyl diphosphate (GPP), establishing a minimum linear chain length of seven carbons for acceptance. To expand this scope, we developed a coupled enzymatic cascade with Lithospermum erythrorhizon GPP synthase (LeGPPS), in which non-natural GPP derivatives are generated by condensation of synthetic alkyl-PP analogs with isopentenyl diphosphate (IPP) and subsequently methylated by ScGPP-MT. This cascade successfully processed 25 additional analogs, including the natural substrate. Collectively, ScGPP-MT accommodates allylic substrates spanning 7–11 linear carbons from diphosphate headgroup, enabling modification of 33 distinct non-natural analogs. To investigate the regiochemistry of ScGPP-MT-catalyzed methylation, which cannot be directly determined because methylated prenyl diphosphates and their alcohol derivatives are difficult to isolate, we coupled the methylation reaction with an engineered aromatic prenyltransferase, NphB(M31S), affording an array of structurally unique, non-canonical cannabinoid precursors. Scale-up and subsequent structural characterization of selected cannabinoid precursors revealed that ScGPP-MT is strictly regio-specific, performing C2-methylation of non-natural substrates just as it does with GPP. Together, these results establish a versatile biocatalytic platform that circumvents traditional biosynthetic constraints, offering a powerful toolkit for the de novo synthesis of diverse unnatural terpenoids with potential pharmaceutical value.

papers.title: Hexanitrogen (N6) formation via direct dinitrogen activation
papers.abstract: Dinitrogen (N2), the major component of air is the only nitrogen allotrope found in nature. Due to its exceptional stability, its activation is rather challenging but a key step in N2 fixation as, for example, in the Haber-Bosch process.1–3 In Earth’s atmosphere, N2 is continuously activated through energetic processes that drive its chemistry away from equilibrium toward reactive nitrogen species. This activation has long inspired efforts to synthetically replicate these energetic processes and elucidate the underlying activation mechanisms. Here we present the formation of the C2h-N6 nitrogen allotrope (in short N6) through direct N2 activation. N6 was previously prepared starting from metal azides.4 In the present work, we continuously irradiated gaseous N2 with an electron beam at 200 eV under flow conditions, followed by co-deposition onto a cold window at 3.5 K. In such experiments, we detected N6 alongside oxygen-containing and atmospherically relevant nitrogen-oxo species and O3. The formation of N6 under such conditions establishes a new route to its formation directly from N2, thereby providing direct access to a neutral nitrogen allotrope that holds potential as a high-energy-density material.

papers.title: Electrochemically-driven dynamic surface chemistry breaks the selectivity-conversion tradeoff in the oxidative coupling of methane
papers.abstract: The partial oxidation of methane to C2 products such as ethylene (C2H4) and ethane (C2H6) is a notoriously challenging catalytic reaction since the key properties, namely the C2 selectivity and CH4 conversion, scale inversely with each other. Despite decades of research on catalyst design, this fundamental C2 selectivity-CH4 conversion tradeoff remains a preeminent challenge.1 While traditional thermochemical catalyst design approaches seem inadequate to surmount said challenge, the electrochemical oxidative coupling of methane (EOCM) presents an alternative approach to enhance catalytic performance by dynamically altering the working state of the catalyst. In this study, we use (La, Sr)1-xTiO3±δ as a model system to demonstrate how electrochemistry enables one to dynamically tune the surface chemistry for enhancing C2 selectivity. Depending on the bulk composition, we observe either step changes in C2 selectivity or even a continuously increasing C2 selectivity trend by using La0.24Sr0.60TiO3-δ: this composition, once electrochemically activated, can break the traditional OCM tradeoff. We demonstrate that any C2 selectivity enhancement effects are determined by the surface La/Ti and Sr/Ti ratios which dynamically evolve under electrocatalytic conditions. The enrichment of La at these surfaces is central to enhanced C2 selectivity values and is crucially modulated by both the initial surface and bulk composition. The results presented herein highlight the potential of electrochemical materials activation for overcoming traditional challenges in partial methane oxidation and provide guidance on materials design for maximizing the C2 selectivity of EOCM.

papers.title: Beyond heuristics: structure-aware screening reveals the limits of composition-based cathode design
papers.abstract: Composition-level heuristics based on transition-metal identity are widely used to anticipate lithium-ion cathode durability, but their physical basis is rarely tested against structure-resolved data. Screening 2,774 Li insertion electrodes from the Materials Project, we compare a metal-identity heuristic with a transparent Degradation Screening Index (DSI) built from three structure-resolved descriptors: delithiation volume strain, charged-phase energy above hull and band gap. Against 11 experimentally characterised cathodes the DSI ranks durability better (Spearman ρ = 0.76, p = 0.007) than the metal-identity heuristic (ρ = 0.55, p = 0.08) or a single volume-strain descriptor (ρ = 0.55, p = 0.08), and at database scale the heuristic correlates only weakly with the DSI (ρ = 0.37, n = 787). Resolving LiCuO2 into its polymorph-specific electrode entries shows delithiation strain from 4.7 to 47% and DSI values spanning three of four durability categories at fixed composition. For energy-density prediction, neither compositional descriptors (R2 = 0.39, 132 Magpie features) nor structural descriptors alone (R2 = 0.36; 0.27 under grouped cross-validation) are predictive, and the accuracy of an 8-feature model (R2 = 0.95) is fully accounted for by voltage, capacity and density, the arithmetic constituents of the target; its role is therefore confined to coverage and uncertainty estimation. Multi-objective Pareto analysis over energy density, DSI and supply-chain criticality shows that no single material is universally optimal. All durability estimates are reported as relative DSI categories rather than cycle counts, and structure-resolved descriptors, not composition alone, should anchor durability screening.

papers.title: Tribology at the Flip of a Switch: Dynamic Control of Friction and Adhesion with Surface Phonon Polaritons
papers.abstract: Advanced applications of robotics and haptics require the ability to modulate friction and adhesion in a dynamic fashion, in real time. Existing technologies, however, suffer from the need for high voltage circuitry, slow response times, and poor spatial resolution, limiting their utility. Moving away from traditional approaches, here we demonstrate that tuned interfacial interactions involving surface phonon polaritons (SPhPs) can control friction and adhesion in real time at surfaces. SPhPs are hybrid light-matter states formed by the coupling of photons and phonons, which can be excited in polar dielectrics. Since phonon coupling is a primary mechanism for frictional energy dissipation, optically gating SPhPs provides a pathway to controlling this. Moreover, the dipolar nature of the polaritons can modify adhesion in response to localized surface electric field confinement. Here, using atomic force microcopy (AFM), we demonstrate that when SiC thin films are optically pumped in the Reststrahlen (RS) band, the friction and adhesion between a Pt probe tip and a SiC surface can be turned “on” and “off’ with light, with a nearly 3-fold increase in friction and 4-fold increase in adhesion, when illuminated. The influence of SiC film thickness, local interfacial dielectric, and optical excitation energy are described.

papers.title: From Catalytic Networks to Activity Landscapes: A Hierarchical Nonequilibrium Framework for Catalysis
papers.abstract: Catalysis is commonly described in terms of free-energy profiles, elementary steps, barriers, intermediates, adsorption energies, turnover frequency (TOF), and selectivity. These quantities are essential, yet they do not fully answer a deeper question: what makes a system catalytic? Here we retain the waterwheel picture for catalysts as an organizing model and develop it into a hierarchical framework connecting microscopic kinetics to macroscopic turnover. In this framework, the established correspondence between productive steady-state flux and TOF is used to recast catalytic performance as a nonequilibrium activity landscape, linking rate constants and catalyst-state populations to observable performance. A catalyst is viewed as a hierarchical system with accessible multistate capacity, regenerative closure, kinetic and thermodynamic compensation, and productive nonequilibrium steadystate (NESS) current. The catalyst provides the structured wheel, while reaction conditions provide the thermodynamic driving force. The framework recovers classical catalytic principles as limiting cases and motivates catalyticity as a condition-dependent capacity defined over an explicitly declared operating or design domain, rather than as a new observable replacing TOF. A literature-inspired Pd(PPh3)4/Pd-PEPPSI Suzuki–Miyaura model illustrates how the framework converts barrier data into NESS currents, ratecontrol coefficients, Hessian modes, frustration indices, and domain-level activity capacities. A Gaussianprocess surrogate and an active-learning workflow further show how sparse evaluations of the activity landscape can reconstruct and navigate such landscapes, suggesting a practical route toward DFT- and experiment-guided catalyst design.

papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware Techno-Economic Assessment of Calcium-Based Treatment and Caustic Recovery from Refinery Spent Caustic
papers.abstract: Refinery spent caustic is difficult to treat because of its high alkalinity, sulfur species and dissolved organics. Independent electrolyte-model calculations (PHREEQC; not experimental validation) show that lime treatment cannot both recover caustic and precipitate sulfate as gypsum: gypsum fell below 0.1% of the sulfate once the equilibrium hydroxide exceeded 0.08–0.23 mol/kg (25–90 °C; up to 0.31 with solubility-product shifts of ±0.5 log units), while carbonate causticization stayed favorable (97% conversion at 25 °C, 1 M initial NaOH). Sulfate removal as a solid therefore needs a separate environment from caustic recovery, which defines when neutralization, causticization with recycle or a staged hybrid applies. A Monte Carlo model (10,000 draws; 720 to 1,320 designs) carries this constraint into process design, a sulfate-limited recycle loop and an economic screen against third-party disposal. Oxygen supply is the physical limit: at 80 °C with atmospheric air the required oxygen-transfer rate exceeds the achievable one by a median factor of 23, so the kinetics-only optimum (median NPV $11.7M for Route B, $5.4M for neutralization) is an upper bound. The preferred design is conditional on oxygen enrichment: with 90% oxygen, 60 °C and 12 h, Route B has a median NPV of $6.4M (P10 −$1.3M; P(NPV>0) = 84%) against $0.2M for neutralization, but it meets the sulfide-removal requirement in only 39% of draws without chemical enhancement of transfer and 67% with half the assumed kLa; with air it is not viable. Results are conditional screening values, not forecasts; no experimental data are reported.

papers.title: Photoresponsive Co3S4 Nanocrystals
papers.abstract: Colloidal semiconductor nanocrystals offer opportunities for solution-processable optoelectronic devices, although their functionality depends on electrical transport across interparticle junctions. Co3S4 has been explored largely for electrochemical applications. Here, we investigate optoelectronically active colloidal Co3S4 quantum dots (QDs) for lightresponsive electrical devices. Structural characterization confirms crystalline spinel Co3S4 nanoparticles with a mean diameter of 8.8 ± 3.1 nm. Optical absorption extends into the infrared region, with an estimated optical band gap of 0.35 eV. Films deposited onto Au interdigitated electrodes exhibit unstable current–voltage characteristics and no discernible photo response before post-deposition treatment. Following treatment with a butylamine–isopropanol mixture, the films show improved electrical reproducibility and a measurable photo response under broadband illumination, with rise and decay times of 15.8 and 31 s, respectively. These findings establish that structurally pure Co3S4 QDs grown through the colloidal route, could be used for optoelectronics.

papers.title: Complementary Roles of Iodide-Mediated Pathways and Anion Dynamics in Lithium-Ion Transport in Li <sub>3</sub> PS <sub>4</sub> -LiI Glasses
papers.abstract: LiI addition enhances lithium-ion transport in sulfide glasses, yet the microscopic mechanisms linking halide incorporation to faster conduction remain unclear. Here, we investigate how LiI promotes Li+ migration in (100−x)Li3PS4–xLiI glasses by resolving changes in local structure, migration energetics, and anion dynamics. A machinelearning potential trained on newly generated ab initio molecular dynamics data and an existing sulfide-electrolyte dataset enables 10 ns simulations of approximately 5000atom glass models at 300 K over a LiI content range of 0–50 mol%. The potential is validated against density functional theory calculations, experimental densities, and X-ray total scattering profiles. Although the PS4 3–units remain intact and their time-averaged inter-unit correlations change little, Li+ diffusivity more than doubles across this composition range, accompanied by increased migration beyond local cage-like regions. To characterize the energetics of these pathways in a disordered environment, we introduce an analysis that combines Voronoi partitioning into P-and I–-centered domains with atomic potentialenergy fluctuations along Li+ trajectories. The resulting statistical local energy-barrier indicators allow comparisons between domain transitions without assigning absolute activation energies. This analysis reveals two complementary effects of LiI addition. Transitions involving I–-centered domains exhibit lower barrier indicators than direct transitions between P-centered domains, identifying favorable I–-mediated migration pathways. LiI addition also lowers the barrier indicators for direct P-to-P transitions, extending its influence beyond pathways that pass through I–-centered domains. Enhanced local translational and rotational dynamics of PS4 3–units accompany this broader reduction, suggesting that anion motion helps facilitate Li+ migration. These findings explain how LiI can enhance transport while largely preserving the average glass structure and highlight the combined roles of local migration pathways and anion dynamics in designing sulfide glass electrolytes.

papers.title: Development and Validation of Low-Temperature Partitioning Extraction Methods for Multiresidue Determination of Pesticides in Soil and Surface Water
papers.abstract: Two complementary low-temperature partitioning methods were systematically optimized and validated for the multiresidue determination of five chemically diverse pesticides in soil and surface water by HPLC-UV. A 23 factorial design was used to evaluate the effects of extraction solvent volume, agitation time, and ionic strength on pesticide recovery. Acetonitrile volume was the primary factor, and the optimization established harmonized conditions for solid–liquid (SLE-LTP) and liquid–liquid (LLE-LTP) extraction: 6 mL acetonitrile, 1 min vortexing, and no salt addition. The simplified procedures reduced solvent consumption by 25–50% compared with selected previously reported methods, while achieving recoveries of 78–106% and relative standard deviations ≤13%. AGREEprep scores of 0.54 (SLE-LTP) and 0.53 (LLE-LTP) indicated comparable environmental performance. The applicability of both methods was further evaluated using real environmental samples, demonstrating the feasibility of harmonizing sample preparation across distinct matrices while maintaining satisfactory analytical performance.

papers.title: Generic OH• Scavenging Constants in UV/H2O2 Screening: Size and Direction of the Error Across Four Published Datasets
papers.abstract: Generic literature rate constants are widely used to estimate hydroxyl-radical (OH•) scavenging in UV/H2O2 screening when no matrix-specific probe measurement is available. The reliability of that shortcut is usually assumed rather than tested. Using four independently published datasets, this study compares generic-constant scavenging estimates with experimentally informed references to establish the size and direction of the error. On a common basis, the ratio R of the generic to the reference matrix scavenging rate, generic constants overestimated probe-derived background scavenging in all three waters of Rosenfeldt and Linden (2007), by 2.5- to 11.8-fold. Against a rate-implied reference from Xiao et al. (2015), the generic model overestimated the matrix sink by 1.05- to 1.31-fold in all six conditions (equivalently, it underestimated matrix OH• by the same factor, if primary generation is correctly predicted). In four waters from Katsoyiannis et al. (2011), the sign of the error differed between matrices (R = 0.81–1.26; geometric mean 1.02, interval including unity). A one-parameter sweep shows that the DOM rate constant that reconciles the generic and measured sinks ranges from 1.97 to 3.50 × 104 L (mg C)-1 s-1 across these waters, bracketing the generic value of 2.5 × 104, and neither bulk DOM nor alkalinity ordered the error monotonically. A reconstruction of the steady-state balance against Wu and Linden (2010) reproduces the published direction and hierarchy of the CO3•- contribution. The probe-based method yields very different outcomes in the two datasets that use it, and the other methods are each represented by one dataset, so the contribution of the inference method cannot be separated from that of water and study. The findings argue against a single transferable correction factor and in favor of reporting generic-constant estimates with a matrix-specific uncertainty range.

papers.title: The Ferenczy Dataset Revisited: How HIV Protease Inhibitors Created an Illusion of Universal Size Dependence in Ligand Binding
papers.abstract: The Size‑Independent Enthalpic Efficiency (SIHE) metric normalizes binding enthalpy by molecular size and is used to compare ligands across different sizes. Re‑analyzing the Ferenczy dataset after cleaning and stratification reveals that the aggregate data exhibit an unphysical compensation slope of –1.04, which resolves into plausible slopes of –0.86 (General) and –0.75 (HIV) upon stratification. For non‑HIV targets, pKH_90 shows no meaningful correlation with molecular size (linear R2 = 0.12; power law R2 = 0.13, exponent –0.23). SIHE achieves size independence trivially because pKH is already size‑independent. The apparent size dependence in the original analysis is driven by HIV‑1 protease inhibitors, which are confined to HA = 35–50 and exhibit a distinct entropy‑driven, endothermic binding mode. Structural analysis attributes this entropy‑driven behavior to HIV‑1 protease’s non‑canonical binding site architecture (interfacial pocket, aromatic‑poor/Asp‑rich composition, glycine‑rich flap network). Formal statistical comparison (Hotelling's T2 p < 10-140) and geometric ellipse overlap (2.6%) confirm that the two subsets are largely separate. SIHE should not be used as a general metric for enthalpic efficiency.

papers.title: A Single-Li+ and Electron Mixed Conductor via Intrinsic Ion-Carrier Implantation in a Metal–Organic Framework
papers.abstract: We report a crystalline metal–organic framework (MOF) that enables efficient Li+ and electron conduction, where a triphenylene ligand functionalized with a propylsulfonate group is designed and utilized to introduce mobile Li+ ions while forming extended conjugation for electron transport. The resulting MOF exhibits a mixed conduction behavior in the solid state with a Li+ conductivity of up to 1.10 mS cm−1 and an electronic conductivity of 15.81 mS cm−1 at room temperature, together with a Li+ transference number close to 1.0. Mechanistic studies reveal that the conformationally dynamic propylsulfonate groups facilitate Li+ transport with low energy barriers in a manner resembling wobbling paddle wheels, and the rigid, conjugated scaffold promotes electronic conduction through in-plane π–d orbital coupling and interlayer interactions. This work establishes an effective bottom-up route for constructing crystalline, porous mixed Li+-electron conductors, offering a new platform for solid-state electrochemical devices requiring synchronized ion and electron transport.

papers.title: Cellulose-Derived Cu-N-C Hybrid for Potential-Regulated CO2-to-CH4 Electroreduction
papers.abstract: Electrochemical CO2 reduction to methane (CH4) offers a promising route for carbon utilization and renewable fuel production, yet achieving high-rate and selective CH4 formation remains challenging because of the complex multi-electron reaction pathway and the competing hydrogen evolution reaction. Herein, marine biomass-derived carbon (MBC) obtained from sea pineapple tunics is integrated with copper phthalocyanine (CuPc) to construct a CuPc/MBC hybrid for CO2 electroreduction. The optimized catalyst achieves a CH4 selectivity of 67.9%, a maximum CH4 partial current density of −538.4 mA cm-2, a CuPc-normalized mass activity of 13,460 A g-1, and stable operation for over 49 h, outperforming most previously reported Cu–N–C catalysts. Structural and spectroscopic characterization shows that the highly crystalline cellulose nanofibers form an interconnected carbon framework after vacuum carbonization, while the local Cu–N4 coordination of CuPc is largely preserved. The resulting hybrid structure promotes CuPc dispersion, electron transport, and intimate catalyst–support interfacial contact, accompanied by interfacial electronic coupling and charge redistribution. Electrochemical measurements further reveal a distinct potential dependence of CH4 selectivity, with CH4 formation and H2 evolution exhibiting opposite trends as the applied potential becomes increasingly cathodic. Density functional theory calculations indicate that more negative potentials thermodynamically favor CO2 hydrogenation toward CH4 while simultaneously enhancing the competing hydrogen evolution reaction, leading to an optimal potential window for CH4 production. This work demonstrates a sustainable molecular catalyst/carbon hybrid platform for high-rate CO2-to-CH4 electroreduction and highlights the combined roles of biomass-derived carbon architecture, catalyst–support coupling, and applied potential in regulating catalytic selectivity.

papers.title: Unified reductive synthesis of pyrrole and indole under acid-free conditions
papers.abstract: Reductive functionalization of nitrogen-bearing carboxylic acid derivatives represents a powerful yet underexplored platform for assembling value-added nitrogen heterocycles. Herein, we describe an iridium-catalyzed unified reductive manifold that converts acyclic hydrazides into pyrroles and indoles under acid-free conditions. This transformation realizes sigmatropic rearrangement via in-situ formed N,N’-dialkyl bisvinylhydrazine intermediates, circumventing key limitations of classic Piloty-Robinson and Fischer syntheses. Excellent functional-group compatibility and scale-up capability underscore its potential to expand the synthetic toolbox for carboxylic-derived nitrogen-containing molecules.

papers.title: Improving computer-aided retrosynthesis of chemically intuitive disconnections
papers.abstract: Reliability in computer-assisted retrosynthesis relies on each architectural component. In template-based retrosynthesis, defining components include the precursor library, the trained model, and the templates. In this work, we evaluated open-source retrosynthesis tools (with default parameters), against a benchmark of 19 common disconnection strategies. An accompanying open-source dataset, template library, and trained model were developed to target simple chemistries. We investigated how precursor libraries, training data and network underfitting affect the reliability of retrosynthetic routes. A method for enumerating reaction SMIRKS into reaction SMILES is also described, providing a route to generate additional training data. The combination of an improved template library, retrained model, and expanded stock file increased the proportion of correctly solved simple case examples from 37% to 84%, outperforming all the other open-source tools. Analysis of the results showed that template presence alone is insufficient: successful retrosynthesis also depends on whether relevant templates are ranked within the search space and whether the search favours the expected route over shorter alternatives. These results highlight the importance of treating template coverage, model ranking, stock definition, and search behaviour as interacting components of retrosynthetic performance. The stock file, template library and model have been implemented into our open-source electronic lab notebook (ELN), AI4Green.

papers.title: Atomic-level structure of an amorphous solid dispersion
papers.abstract: Amorphous materials play a pivotal role across condensed-matter physics, materials science, and pharmaceuticals, for example enabling increased dissolution rates and higher in-vivo exposure for poorly bioavailable molecules. In particular, amorphous solid dispersions (ASDs), disordered multi-component mixtures of an active ingredient within a polymer matrix, are widely used to trap molecules in metastable high-energy states. However, because these systems lack longrange order, directly observing their atomic-level spatial arrangements has remained an outstanding challenge, rendering their long-term physical stability unpredictable and leaving formulation science reliant on empirical screening. Here we report the first complete three-dimensional, atomic-level structure elucidation of an amorphous solid dispersion. By combining solid-state NMR crystallography with machine-learning-accelerated quantum chemical calculations, we determine the structural ensemble of the drug AZD5462 within a copovidone matrix. We show that the polymer drives a total reconfiguration of the hydrogen-bonding network, substituting self-association with API–polymer interactions and fundamentally altering the local conformational energy landscape by raising the kinetic barriers to rearrangement. The structure explains why the formulation remains physically stable for over two years, whereas the pure amorphous drug recrystallizes within hours. These findings establish a rigorous structural framework for disordered multi-component materials, paving the way for the rational, structure-directed design of amorphous matter.

papers.title: THz Calorimetry of Electrolyte Solutions Links Water’s H-Bond Network to Macroscopic Properties
papers.abstract: Understanding the macroscopic properties of aqueous electrolyte solutions over their full solubility range requires a detailed microscopic picture of water-ion interactions. We combine THz calorimetry and dimensionality-reduction techniques to demonstrate that two to four spectroscopic markers are sufficient to describe ion-specific variations in mixing entropies and enthalpies, viscosity, and limiting conductivity across 19 electrolytes. Those markers allow us to classify electrolytes as ’strong’ or ’weak’ and report on changes in the water’s H-bond network. As concentration increases, spectroscopic nonlinearities due to ion aggregation appear that, based on a multipole expansion model for activities, are correlated with density changes. For CsI and LiCl, as prototypes of weak and strong electrolytes, respectively, the multipole expansion model accurately describes their conductivities, viscosities, and surface tensions. THz spectroscopy in combination with an activity coefficient model directly correlates macroscopic solution properties with changes in the H-bond network, paving the way towards efficient machine-learning approaches.

papers.title: A grouped split silently removes the chemistry entangled with its grouping variable: the case of MOF topology hold-out
papers.abstract: Machine learning screens metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) for CO2 capture, and 2026 studies on enumerated databases have converged on topology hold-out as a test of topological transferability, presupposing untested separability of topology and chemistry. They are not: on hMOF (324,426 structures), 74.7% of coarse compositions (61.3% of structures) occur in a single topology, and for seven of hMOF's eleven topologies removing one topology leaves every structure with no chemical counterpart in training; the confound replicates on ARC-MOF (99.3% coarse single-topology), which is not independent of hMOF, so only a leave-one-source-out bound (98.6–99.8%) is claimed. On the isoreticular pcu ↔ nbo pair, removing the matched topology degrades nbo-side MAE by 70.0% while a sizematched control leaves it unchanged, and across the shared 25,000-sample support set the top-1% hit rate falls from 50.4% to 19.3% (five seeds). Yet the topology penalty is not explained by chemistry alone: holding out the composite chemistry key instead retains R2 = 0.674 against topology's 0.379, so the composition counts fix the identity of the withheld chemistry, not its cost. Topology hold-out should therefore not be read as a clean test of topological transferability, and grouped-split reports should first disclose the confound structure and chemical granularity, for which we provide a reporting checklist.

papers.title: Grassmannian Density Learning for Physically Consistent Kohn–Sham Electronic Structure Prediction
papers.abstract: Deep-learning electronic-structure models show great potential to accelerate first-principles calculations, with broad implications for materials science, biology and drug discovery. Yet no consensus has emerged on which physical quantity should be modeled to represent electronic states. As two fundamental quantities that arise naturally in Kohn–Sham density functional theory, the Kohn–Sham Hamiltonian and electronic density have attracted the most attention. Hamiltonian prediction, however, devotes substantial modeling capacity to degrees of freedom that do not affect the occupied electronic subspace, whereas direct regression of density matrices or real-space densities removes this redundancy but cannot ensure that the prediction represents a physically admissible electronic state. Motivated by the fact that electronic states themselves reside on a constrained manifold, we observe that predicting coordinates directly on this manifold can simultaneously eliminate redundant degrees of freedom and preserve physical admissibility. Here we introduce GeoK, a framework that predicts compact occupied–virtual orbital-rotation generators as coordinates on the manifold of electronic states, thereby ensuring each prediction corresponds to a valid electronic state of the target molecular system. We further develop a neural-network architecture tailored to this geometric prediction task. Across in-distribution and out-of-distribution benchmarks, as well as downstream applications, GeoK consistently improves electronic-state prediction over the evaluated Hamiltonian and unconstrained densityregression baselines, while supporting robust deployment in downstream first-principles workflows. These results establish orbital-rotation generator prediction as a principled and reliable paradigm for intrinsic electronic-state modeling, opening a route towards more accurate and transferable deep-learning electronic-structure models.

papers.title: Classical 1H NMR correlation rules as diagnostic tests: likelihood ratios from 168,211 experimental spectra
papers.abstract: How much does a signal between 3.3 and 4.5 ppm say about a proton on a carbon bearing oxygen? The correlation tables used to read 1H NMR spectra state where each proton type resonates, but not how much observing, or failing to observe, a signal in that range should change a chemist’s belief. We measured this for 42 single-signal correlation rules and coupling rules transcribed from two open teaching sources, treating each rule as a diagnostic test and computing positive and negative likelihood ratios (LR+ and LR−) on two independent collections of experimental spectra with known structures: 160,038 literature peak lists from NMRexp and 8,173 atom-assigned spectra from nmrshiftdb2. Rules and scoring were frozen before the confirmatory data were examined; the sources state positions and coupling ranges, and the integration and multiplicity clauses we scored are our formalisation of what those rules imply. The rules fall into two regimes. Windows in uncrowded regions carry real evidence (aldehyde C-H LR+ 34 and 20 on the two collections, carboxylic acid O-H 11), while no window between 1.0 and 4.5 ppm exceeds LR+ 3.5 by position alone (median 1.6 and 2.3 on the two collections), because the protons of other environments occupy it: the environment a window describes accounts for a median of 20% of the assigned signals inside it. A reported integration recovers part of the crowded region (alkyl methylene LR+ 2.5 to 38), and several of the strongest effects are negative observations that the tables do not quantify (no reported signal between 6.5 and 8.0 ppm, LR− 0.011 for an aromatic C-H). The published windows are narrower than the environments they describe, and LR+ agrees between the two collections (Spearman ρ = 0.92). A coupling constant considered without regard to which signal carries it holds little information; tied to the shift region of the protons the rule concerns, in an analysis added after the confirmatory run, it gains up to thirteen-fold. In a secondary analysis in the reciprocal direction, from structure to expected shift, the additive increment rules of the standard reference tables, audited on 73,049 assigned protons, predict benzene ring protons to 0.14 ppm and protons on sp3 carbon to 0.35 ppm, with heavy-tailed errors that call for a robust likelihood. Together the results give the qualitative tables a quantitative form, measured on the information that published peak lists actually carry, that can be encoded in automated interpretation.

papers.title: ProtBed: a streamlined web platform for exploratory statistics and predictive modeling in quantitative mass spectrometry
papers.abstract: Mass spectrometry proteomics and metabolomics generate high-dimensional quantitative matrices requiring rigorous statistical and machine learning evaluation, yet existing analytical workflows typically depend on programmatic scripting or remote cloud servers that introduce datagovernance constraints. ProtBed is a client-side web application that executes post-extraction data exploration directly in the browser runtime. The platform integrates deterministic preprocessing, pairwise and omnibus hypothesis testing, six-model cross-validated machine learning, and publication-ready visualization while preserving complete local custody of quantitative abundance matrices and clinical metadata. Empirical validation was conducted across four diverse cohorts totaling 250 clinical specimens. On an untargeted GC-MS urine cohort (𝑛 = 40; 356 metabolites), stratified five-fold cross-validated classifiers discriminated diabetic kidney disease with AUC = 0.90 (89% sensitivity, 82% specificity). In a deep-coverage post-mortem substantia nigra tissue cohort (𝑛 = 30; 9,606 quantified proteins), full-matrix modeling achieved out-of-fold AUC = 0.99 using logistic regression (AUC = 0.96 for linear support vector machines) and prioritized neuroinflammatory mediators including SAA1, CRP, and GFAP. ProtBed further resolved multiclass diagnostic arms in plasma extracellular-vesicle proteomics (𝑛 = 124) and characterized dysregulated lipid classes in Alzheimer's disease plasma (𝑛 = 56). ProtBed is freely accessible at https://protbed.com/ .

papers.title: Fast Liquid Chromatography for Real-Time Process Monitoring of Chemical Reactions in Batch and Flow
papers.abstract: Process analytical technologies (PATs) are increasingly vital tools in process research and development, enabling realtime monitoring of a reaction’s chemical and physical parameters. Although numerous commercial PATs exist, many are limited by sampling frequency, material consumption, or requiring unique chemical labels for spectroscopic analysis. Herein, we report a rapid, label-free analytical sampling platform that integrates fast high-pressure liquid chromatography (HPLC) with electrospray ionizationmass spectrometry (ESI-MS) for the direct, real-time monitoring of chemical reactions. Reactions are pumped into a four-port nanovolume injection valve and are injected onto short LC columns at high mobile phase flow rates, which enables chromatographic separations on the time-scale of 6–20 seconds. We demonstrate the utility of this technology by monitoring two rapid reactions relevant to the pharmaceutical industry: a photocatalytic thiol–ene reaction and a metallaphotoredox aryl sulfonamidation reaction. In each case, data-rich reaction progress profiles are obtained for monitoring the reaction progress in real-time, demonstrating the platform’s capability to deliver detailed reaction insights with minimal sample consumed (4 nL injection-1). Its modular design is adaptable to different reactor geometries and scales, while maintaining device simplicity to enable straightforward integration into existing workflows in industrial settings.

papers.title: Contact organization separates biological from crystal protein interfaces matched on area and disjoint in sequence
papers.abstract: Interface area can dominate discrimination between physiological protein interfaces and crystal contacts. We tested whether local contact organization remains informative after area matching and sequence-cluster separation. In 2,000 balanced BioMany/XtalMany interfaces, sequence cluster aware cross validation gave ROC AUC 0.904 for area and 0.937 after adding five normalized contact descriptors (difference 0.033; bootstrap 95% interval 0.015–0.058). We then fixed 40 biological and 40 crystal homomeric interfaces from the Duarte–Capitani collection, matched pairwise on area within 800–2000 Å2 and sharing no 30%-identity cluster with development. Area reached AUC 0.523; the frozen contact score reached 0.849 (dependency-component bootstrap 95% interval 0.751–0.927) and average precision 0.812. Biological interfaces carried 2.5 times the hydrophobic carbon-pair density of crystal contacts, 1.91 versus 0.76 pairs per 100 Å2. Post hoc analysis identified hydrophobic density as the main contributor; this descriptor alone reached AUC 0.829. On the same panel, unchanged PRODIGY-cryst reached AUC 0.8475 and the lineage-linked current EPPIC score reached 0.876. Contact organization therefore discriminated the curated classes after area matching and sequence-cluster separation. The inference applies to EPPIC-derived labels; protein chain size remained unmatched and associated with the score.

papers.title: Developing Efficient and Hyperthermostable Heme Peroxygenase Enzymes as a Biocatalytic Platform for Selective C-H bond Oxidation Reactions
papers.abstract: There is intense interest in using enzyme biocatalysts for chemically challenging oxidation reactions involving the activation of inert carbon-hydrogen bonds in organic molecules. The cytochrome P450 family of heme monooxygenase enzymes can catalyse selective C-H bond hydroxylations and epoxidation reactions. However, the complex and costly nature of these multicomponent systems and the low stability and activity of these systems make larger scale reactions challenging. Thermophilic P450s from bacteria and archaea have been identified but have low activity when reconstituted using electron transfer partner proteins and surrogate oxygen donors. We demonstrate that two cytochrome P450 enzymes (CYP119A1 and CYP119A2) from hyperthermophilic archaea can be engineered to be efficient peroxygenase enzymes requiring only hydrogen peroxide to function. Catalytic oxidation was achieved through modification of three residues in the dioxygen binding groove, including the important addition of a proline residue after the glutamate acid/base residue which significantly enhanced the activity (8-fold over the double mutant and three orders of magnitude over the natural enzyme). These peroxygenases oxidised tridecanoic acid with high activity and enabled further investigation of the substrate range of these enzymes. Both enzymes could oxidise fatty acids and related compounds as well as styrene and the norisoprenoid β-ionone. The oxidation of these substrates occurred with excellent regioselectivity. The CYP119A2-QEP variant was stable to heating at 85-90 °C, had higher activity at 70 °C, could tolerate up to 20 % v/v acetonitrile and was able to catalyse ≥1000 total turnovers across the range of substrates tested. These new peroxygenase biocatalysts, provide hyperthermostable enzyme scaffolds to enable selective and catalytic oxidation of inert C-H bonds using a single enzyme system and cheap cofactors.

papers.title: Prediction of Singlet-Triplet Gaps Using Self-Attention–Based Regression with Model Integration into a Molecular Editor
papers.abstract: The singlet–triplet gap (STG) is an important property of photofunctional materials, but obtaining reliable values can be challenging. Experimentally, its determination often requires a combination of advanced spectroscopic techniques, while computational approaches can be time-consuming and demand specialized expertise. Therefore, a low-cost and user-friendly approach for obtaining reasonable STG estimates could make this property more accessible to non-experts. In this work, we evaluate regression models based on different molecular representations using the INVEST dataset from the Aspuru-Guzik group that contains ADC(2) energy gaps for ~70K molecules. We compare transformer models operating on SMILES representations, graph-based models (AttentiveFP), and fingerprint-based models. While AttentiveFP performs best for molecules similar to those in the training set, pre-trained transformers generalize better to unseen chemical space after fine-tuning. Motivated by these complementary strengths, we integrate our best-performing models into an online 2D chemical structure editor, enabling users to obtain STG estimates directly from drawn molecular structures. The editor can be accessed at http://ketcher-predict.ttk.hu/.

papers.title: Cristobalite-Type Compounds for Rechargeable Potassium-Ion Batteries
papers.abstract: Potassium-ion batteries have emerged as high-voltage and economically advantageous electrochemical energy storage systems with promise to viably complement and/or augment lithium-ion technology owing to the natural abundance, projected low cost and favourable redox potential of potassium. Their continued advancement, however, is primarily predicated upon the discovery of electrode and electrolyte materials adept to delivering high energy density, long-term cycling stability and rigorous safety performance. Cristobalite-type compounds have recently garnered traction as prospective candidates, for these materials not only combine theoretically high energy density with structural robustness but can also be designed exclusively from earth-abundant and low-toxicity constituent elements. This Review provides a critical assessment of the rapidly expanding family of cristobalite-type compounds, which exhibit pronounced structural versatility and the capacity to reversibly intercalate two potassium ions per formula unit, thereby enabling high theoretical energy densities. We particularly survey recent advances in their structural chemistry, electrochemical behaviour and potassium-ion transport properties, and elucidate the mechanistic principles that govern their electrochemical performance. Finally, we outline future research directions, encompassing rational materials design, advanced characterisation methodologies and large-scale computational screening, to optimise cristobalite-type compounds as high-performance electrode materials and solid-state electrolytes for potassium-ion batteries.

papers.title: Non-Symmetric Stapling of Tyrosine-Containing Peptides Driven by Intramolecular Non-Covalent Interactions
papers.abstract: Non-symmetric stapling of native peptides that crosslinking two distinct residues is a valuable tool for enriching diversity of peptide macrocycles, yet it is less achieved due to the high demand for chemo- and siteselectivity control, as well as the competitive intermolecular peptide crosslinking. Herein, we reported a noncovalent interaction activation strategy for non-symmetric stapling of tyrosine-containing peptides by employing ethenesulfonyl fluoride (ESF) as a bifunctional crosslinker. Once covalently anchored to peptide, the sulfonyl fluoride motif is activated by non-covalent interactions, which triggers an intramolecular SuFEx click reaction with tyrosine to afford peptide macrocycles. This approach efficiently crosslinks diverse residue pairs, including Cys–Tyr, His–Tyr and Pro–Tyr. Notably, the protocol is scalable and can be performed in solid-phase synthesis, providing a robust access to tyrosine-bridged peptide macrocycles with excellent diversity.

papers.title: IMPECCABLE: A Digital Twin Drug Discovery Workflow Comprising AI, Physics and Experiment & the Creation of Nanomolar-Potent Inhibitors
papers.abstract: The traditional drug discovery process is slow, costly and prone to high failure rates. To address this, we have developed IMPECCABLE, an integrated, heterogeneous in silico workflow combining physics-based methods and artificial intelligence to explore small-molecule chemical space. Operating on Frontier and Aurora exascale supercomputers, the workflow rapidly screens, generates and evaluates candidate compounds. Promising candidates enter a generative, multi-objective active learning loop where reliable binding free energies from ESMACS and TIES guide REINVENT to predict diverse, novel and synthesizable molecules. Unlike conventional approaches, this tightly coupled architecture integrates hit identification together with hit-to-lead optimisation and expansion within a single automated pipeline. Crucially, and uniquely, IMPECCABLE also integrates human medicinal chemistry input based on experiments, creating a molecular digital twin. We applied IMPECCABLE to two disease-related targets, WDR91 and TNKS2, demonstrating its ability to produce viable binders, while also performing prospective experimental validation for WDR91. Following multi-objective optimisation via an iterative REINVENT-TIES cycle, we identified four potent hits for WDR91 exhibiting nanomolar binding affinity with KD values between 129 ± 1 nM and 287 ± 1 nM. Remarkably, these four hits emerged from a selection of just ten synthesized compounds, demonstrating an exceptional ca 40% success rate.

papers.title: Interfacial Engineering of 2D/2D BiVO4/V2CTx Heterostructures for Enhanced Symmetric Supercapacitor Performance Across Various Electrolytes
papers.abstract: Engineering well-defined heterostructured composites is an effective strategy for improving the electrochemical performance of energy storage systems. In this study, a 2D/2D BiVO 4 /V 2 CT x heterostructure was synthesized via a simple hydrothermal method and, for the first time, systematically tested as a symmetric supercapacitor electrode in neutral (1 M Na 2 SO 4 ), alkaline (1 M KOH), and acidic (1 M H 2 SO 4 ) electrolytes. The composite showed better electrochemical performance compared to pristine V 2 CT x , with specific capacitances of 191.5 F g -1 , 107 F g -1 , and 239 F g -1 in Na 2 SO 4 , KOH, and H 2 SO 4 , respectively, at 0.016 A g -1 . A high energy density of 83.3 Wh kg -1 at 147.5 W kg -1 was achieved in the neutral electrolyte, along with excellent rate capability and Coulombic efficiency. These improvements arise from the synergistic interaction between BiVO 4 and V 2 CT x , which increases active site accessibility and promotes efficient ion and electron transport. Overall, the results show that the BiVO 4 /V 2 CT x heterostructure is a promising and versatile electrode material for high-performance supercapacitors.

papers.title: Effect of Cyclodextrin Type on the Photopolymerization and Network Properties of Oligo(L-lactide)-Extended Poly(ethylene glycol) Formulations
papers.abstract: Cyclodextrins (CDs) are widely used as supramolecular components to provide a platform for designing material properties through non-covalent interactions. In this study, we report how the CD type influences the photopolymerization and network properties of a methacrylated telechelic oligo(L-lactide)-extended poly(ethylene glycol) precursor (PLA-PEG-PLA), denoted MPL with three different cyclodextrins (α-CD, β-CD and 2-hydroxypropyl-β-CD (HP-β-CD)) prepared at a 1:2 MPL:CD molar feed ratio. The effect of cyclodextrin type on the chemical structure, inclusion geometry, thermal behaviour, and physicochemical properties of the resulting material, as well as on their photopolymerization process, was systematically studied using FTIR spectroscopy, 1D and 2D proton (ROESY/NOESY) 1 H NMR techniques, and differential scanning calorimetry. Molecular docking was used to visualize plausible inclusion geometries. The influence of photoinitiator type and concentration on polymerisation efficiency was examined, and the cytocompatibility of the cured materials was assessed against L929 fibroblasts. The results showed that the nature of cyclodextrin affects the strength of supramolecular association and systematically influences photo-initiated polymerization kinetics, network formation, and macroscopic material properties. Overall, this work highlights the design of cyclodextrin-mediated supramolecular macromonomer materials and outlines their potential as a tunable photo-curable host-guest polymer network.

papers.title: Metasurface information processor based on 4D bionic hardware and software for ultralow energy consumption computing
papers.abstract: As AI technology faces an energy crisis, one promising solution is bionic ultra-low energy computing hardware, which can operate at a power level as low as sub-20-watt based on the 4D model of Ca 2+ channels recently verified in brain information processing. Inspired by this model, here we design and fabricate a 4D bionic computing system based on information metasurface array with the powerful capability of electromagnetic controls. Paired with specific algorithms, each metasurface cell functions as a multifunctional unit, capable of storing, regulating, transmitting, and computing information simultaneously. The metasurface array also has high energy efficiency and precision required for high-performance bionic computing. Integrated with the DNA computing, this system is expected to achieve a variety of functions including DNA replication, DNA logical computation, and DNA produce/readout. We aim to pave the way for a new paradigm in advanced computational materials that meet the evolving demands of AI and robotics.

papers.title: In situ observation of ultra-giant spherulites in perovskite hydrates
DeImmu-MPNN: Reducing Immunogenicity in De Novo Protein Design
papers.abstract: De novo-designed proteins lack an evolutionary history of immune tolerance, making antidrug antibody (ADA) responses a barrier to their clinical translation. ProteinMPNN is widely used to design sequences for a given protein backbone, but it does not account for immune tolerance, which is important for therapeutic applications. The ADA response to injected proteins is driven principally by MHC class II presentation of protein-derived peptides to CD4+ T-helper cells. We fine-tuned ProteinMPNN using direct preference optimization to reduce ADA-relevant class II epitopes across a six-allele HLA-DRB1 panel, while also reducing class I epitopes. The resulting model, DeImmu-MPNN, reduces NetMHCIIpan-predicted MHC class II presentation by 41.4% relative to the baseline model, bringing predicted presentation to the level of length-matched human proteins, and NetMHCpan-predicted MHC class I presentation by 33.0% on the same designs, for 2.1 points of sequence recovery and no detectable structural cost. The reduction transfers without retraining to unseen DRB1 alleles, the DRB3/4/5 paralogs, and HLA-DQ. It generalizes to 11 published de novo binder complexes, with mean reductions of 50.4% for class II and 30.2% for class I and no systematic predicted cost to interface confidence. DeImmu-MPNN provides a framework for incorporating immune presentation into protein sequence design and may dramatically facilitate the design of proteins with reduced immunogenicity.

papers.title: FluorCast: Solvent-aware 2D-3D feature fusion for predicting fluorophore photophysics
papers.abstract: Machine-learning (ML) models can accelerate the prediction of fluorescence properties, but their apparent performance depends strongly on molecular representation and on the evaluation strategy. Here we present FluorCast, a solvent-aware ML framework assembled from three public datasets—ChemFluor, Deep4Chem, and FluoDB-Lite—comprising 66,820 standardized records, 33,965 unique chromophores, and 1,368 nonmissing canonical environment identifiers. Conventional Morganfingerprint models were benchmarked for absorption and emission maxima, photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY), and Stokes shift under random, molecule-grouped, and scaffold-grouped splits, revealing substantial performance degradation with increasing structural novelty. To incorporate three-dimensional (3D) molecular information, we evaluated frozen 512-dimensional ConforFormer embeddings alone and in feature-level fusion with Morgan fingerprints. On matched test sets, fusion reduced the mean absolute error (MAE) relative to Morgan fingerprints alone in 11 of 12 target-split combinations, although molecule-grouped PLQY prediction worsened and several scaffold-grouped gains were small. An external set of five recently reported fluorophores with no exact training-set match provided a further test; fusion reduced absorption MAE from 65.67 to 24.49 nm, whereas Morgan-only models performed better for emission and Stokes shift, and PLQY performance was comparable. These results indicate that learned 3D conformational embeddings provide complementary, target-dependent information rather than a universal replacement for two-dimensional (2D) molecular fingerprints.

papers.title: Evaluation of Reusable Monolithic Silica Columns for Sustainable Liquid Chromatography in Organic Synthesis
papers.abstract: Liquid chromatography (LC) is essential for compound purification in synthetic organic chemistry. However, single-use particle-packed columns using silica gel result in substantial solvent and solid waste. We herein evaluate reusable monolithic silica gel columns as a practical and sustainable alternative, based on 370 purification runs conducted by 14 researchers over one year under routine laboratory conditions. Compared to conventional particle-packed columns, the monolithic system was estimated to reduce annual LC solvent consumption by 74% and solid silica waste by 95%, while maintaining high separation performance even for challenging separations (e.g., ΔRf < 0.1). A modeled life cycle assessment (LCA) further indicated that total CO2 emissions and energy consumption per purification were reduced by over 80%, primarily due to reduced solvent use. A modeled workflow analysis indicated an approximately 40% reduction in purification time relative to manual purification using self-packed particle columns. Analysis of the recorded monolith data showed no clear relationship between user experience and solvent consumption. The plate efficiency of the monolithic columns was comparable to that of preparative high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) columns packed with 10 μm particles, despite operating at a low gauge pressure of 0.1 bar. Requiring only standard laboratory equipment, this reusable system combines high separation performance with reduced solvent consumption, minimal solid waste, and improved operational efficiency. By substantially reducing the resources and labor required for routine purification without sacrificing separation performance, this technology has the potential to make synthetic organic chemistry more efficient and environmentally sustainable.

papers.title: Approaching the Two-Dimensional Limit of the S = 1/2 Kagome Magnet via Metal-Organic Framework Exfoliation
papers.abstract: Realising chemically programmable two-dimensional magnetic materials is a major challenge in the development of next-generation quantum technologies. Layered magnetic metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) provide an attractive platform because their reticular design enables systematic control over composition, topology, and magnetic interactions while offering the possibility of exfoliation into atomically thin nanosheets. Here, we investigate the layered S = 1/2 kagome MOF, Cu 3 (CO 3 ) 2 ( bipy ) 6 · 2 ClO 4 , whose bulk magnetic structure is most consistently described by ferromagnetic kagome layers that are ferromagnetically correlated to adjacent ones. We develop a micromechanical Scotch tape exfoliation strategy capable of producing few-layer nanosheets and combine synchrotron X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) and X-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) to demonstrate that the Cu 2+ oxidation state and ferromagnetic behaviour are retained following exfoliation. By showing that magnetic functionality is preserved in the exfoliated kagome MOF nanosheets, this work establishes the promise of layered magnetic MOFs as tuneable platforms for low-dimensional quantum magnetism and provides an important experimental route toward realising the archetypal S = 1/2 kagome magnet in the two-dimensional limit.

papers.title: Myxobacterial terpene synthases produce structurally diverse sesquiterpenes
papers.abstract: Myxobacteria represent an underexplored source of terpenoids with relatively few terpenoids and terpene synthases known from this phylum. Thirteen sesquiterpenes (1–13) representing ten distinct carbon skeletons were identified from eight myxobacterial terpene synthases. Twelve of these natural products (1–10, 12, and 13), including enantiomers of known brasilane-type sesquiterpenes (1–3) and the humulene analog viticumulin A (4), were previously unknown from myxobacteria. Moreover, ten (i.e., 1–4, 7–10, 12, 13) have not been previously reported from bacterial sources. These data demonstrate that myxobacteria represent a rich and largely untapped reservoir of terpenoids that should be further investigated.

papers.title: Lithium Polysulfide Speciation in Lithium–Sulfur Batteries: A First-Principles Benchmark of Thermodynamics, Bonding, and Solvent Control
papers.abstract: Lithium–sulfur cycle life is limited by dissolved LiyS q x polysulfides whose speciation remains disputed. We benchmark the complete matrix (y = 0–2, q = 0 to −2, x = 1–8) in the gas phase, tetraglyme and dimethyl sulfoxide: 248 M06-2X/SMD thermochemistries, 132 refined by single-point CCSD. The convex hull, S8 → Li2S6 → Li2S4 → Li2S3 → Li2S2 → Li2S, is identical in both solvents, and every exergonic long-chain comproportionation delivers Li2S6. QTAIM analysis of the CCSD densities separates covalent S–S from electrostatic Li–S bonding, transferably between solvents. Solvation makes S 2–x the dominant lithium-free 1 charge state and places both legs of the shuttle on that branch. Infrared and Raman spectra of prepared solutions test the vibrational predictions and track the chain-length distribution through one band envelope. The open dataset is a calibrated reference for force-field, machine-learned and continuum battery models.

papers.title: A Hierarchical Latent Architecture of the Chemical Bond Revealed
papers.abstract: The chemical bond has no unique quantum-mechanical observable, and energetic, orbital/wavefunction, 9 and electron-density analyses can therefore agree, specialize, or apparently conflict. In this work, we ask 10 whether unsupervised machine learning can reveal a simpler physicochemical organization beneath this 11

papers.title: Vegetation-Rainfall Relationship within the Caatinga Biome
papers.abstract: With drought and extreme weather events increasing in frequency, it has become crucial to understand the relation between weather and biome responses. The semi-arid Caatinga biome of Brazil is highly sensitive to climatic variability, and particularly to changes in precipitation and drought frequency. This study explores a remote-sensing workflow to estimate green vegetation cover and assess its relationship with precipitation using satellite imagery. Monthly satellite composites were processed to distinguish green and non-green vegetation, comparing the efficacy between a convolutional neural network (CNN) and a python classification method. We match the computational measurements of green vegetation cover with monthly precipitation data from the four nearest weather stations. Green cover analysis shows a lagged positive relationship with precipitation, with wetter months generally exhibiting greater green vegetation coverage. The study demonstrates the potential of combining satellite imagery, CNN classification and climatic data for longterm remote ecosystem monitoring.

papers.title: Solvotaxis: Gel Motion Against Gravity via Autonomous Solvent Exchange
papers.abstract: Molecular gelation, where a low-molecular-weight gelator (LMWG) self-assembles into a network of fibers, has long obeyed a simple rule: a solvent can be gelled only if the gelator is at least partially soluble in it. In this work, we overturn this paradigm and show that the disaccharidebased gelator 4′,6′-O-benzylidene amygdalin (BA) forms stable gels in solvents where it is completely insoluble. BA dissolves in aqueous media upon heating and forms hydrogels upon cooling, but it is insoluble and does not form gels in oils. When an immiscible nonpolar oil is placed atop a BA hydrogel, the network spontaneously absorbs the oil, expels the water, and migrates upward against gravity. At steady state, a stable BA organogel sits atop liquid water. We refer to this process as Autonomous Solvent Exchange (ASE) and it reveals a strong preference of BA fibers for oil over water (whereas BA molecules prefer water). ASE thus leads to the unusual phenomenon of solvotaxis, i.e., migration of the gel toward its preferred solvent without disrupting the fibrous network. BA organogels with tunable strengths can be formed by solvotaxis across a range of oils (e.g., n-alkanes, natural oils, fuels). Overall, by decoupling molecular solubility from gelation, solvotaxis expands the landscape of gelation to previously inaccessible liquids. Our work also establishes new principles for designing materials that respond autonomously to chemical gradients, with potential applications in environmental remediation and oil recovery.

papers.title: Does Endocrine State Gate Proteoform-Induced Synaptic Vulnerability? A Metaplasticity Framework for Menopause and Early Neurodegeneration
papers.abstract: This is a hypothesis-driven conceptual review, not a systematic review or meta-analysis, integrating two largely independent bodies of neuroscience literature — the neuroendocrinology of the menopause transition and the molecular synaptotoxicity of soluble amyloid-β (Aβ) oligomers — to ask whether they converge on a shared synaptic mechanism. Estrogen (17β-estradiol) and the neurosteroid allopregnanolone regulate hippocampal excitatory-inhibitory balance through ERβ, GPER1, and GABA-A δ-subunit-containing receptors, although not uniformly through “anti-LTD”: GPER1 mediates its own distinct form of long-term depression (LTD). Separately, soluble, preplaque Aβ oligomers facilitate NMDA receptor- and mGluR1-dependent hippocampal LTD via convergent calcineurin/AKAP150 spine elimination signaling, independent of amyloid plaques. We situate both literatures within Bienenstock–Cooper–Munro (BCM) metaplasticity theory, in which a sliding modification threshold, not a fixed switch, governs whether a synaptic input produces potentiation or depression. We propose a specific, falsifiable hypothesis: that decreasing estrogen/allopregnanolone tone and increasing proteoform burden act on convergent postsynaptic machinery to jointly lower this threshold in the hippocampal and limbic circuits. We explicitly distinguish this synaptic-level claim from the clinically separate phenomena of perimenopausal mood symptoms, subjective cognitive complaints, mild cognitive impairment, and Alzheimer's disease and weigh it against four competing models, including the possibility that endocrine decline and proteinopathy are both downstream of a shared upstream process. We present a structured, falsifiable research agenda specifying the experiments needed to confirm, partially confirm, or refute the proposed convergence. We do not claim that the central hypothesis is established; our contribution is to make an underexplored cross-disciplinary link explicit and testable.

papers.title: Obstructions to four-body perimetric coordinates
papers.abstract: Pekeris’ perimetric coordinates make the three-body Coulomb problem tractable. They are linear in the interparticle distances, range independently over [0,∞), and turn the Schrödinger equation into a sparse recursion. Whether a four-body analogue exists has been debated since 1966, with claims in both directions and no agreed definition. We formulate a hierarchy of definitions and settle each level of it. (i) No linear coordinates exist, because the configuration domain is not convex. (ii) No coordinates smooth up to the boundary, in the sense of a diffeomorphism of manifolds with corners, exist even locally, because the domain has a round tangent cone at collinear configurations. (iii) Independent coordinates on the closed orthant whose squared distances are polynomial do exist. They cover the whole domain and are bijective on its interior. Degree 4 is attained. (iv) No independent coordinates exist in which the six distances themselves are rational functions, for instance polynomials. The proof of (iv) shows that the variety of coplanar configurations, written in the distances, is birational to a quotient (X ×X)/G of the square of a Kummer K3 surface. It therefore carries a nonzero holomorphic 4-form and cannot be parametrized rationally. Finally, we identify an exact Galois symmetry in a broad class of Pekeris-type sparse schemes, the coefficientwise graded schemes. If one distance enters only through its square, such a scheme computes identical spectra for repulsion and for attraction in that pair, so it cannot converge for both. If it is consistent for the attractive problem, it has spurious eigenvalues below the true ground state of the repulsive one. A helium calculation exhibits this behaviour. Within this class, uniform convergence for four-body Coulomb systems therefore requires rational distances, which (iv) excludes. Every computational step is accompanied by a runnable check.

papers.title: TENKi: counting the value of borrowed knowledge to a materials campaign in measurements saved
papers.abstract: Materials campaigns draw on data of very different cost: a band gap costs almost nothing from a database, core-hours from a hybrid-functional density functional theory (DFT) calculation, and instrument time from a measurement. No calibration carries values from low-cost to costly sources, and multi-fidelity methods do not state how many costly evaluations an imported ordering of the candidates replaces. We test whether that ordering, with its margins, reduces the evaluations needed to reach a given ranking quality, and whether the saving can be measured for each route. TENKi (Transfer-ensemble Knowledge Inheritance) records ranking agreement against budget while a ranking model is fitted to queries that order several candidates at once, with the donor ordering entered as a prior whose trust is learned from incoming results. The evidence is 261,053 archived band-gap records from eight sources, 171 semiconductors with gaps computed on demand, and an aluminium–magnesium–silicon (Al–Mg–Si) alloy pool computed with DFT and molecular dynamics. Queries ranking four candidates outperform pairwise comparisons on every source, a donor prior replaces nearly half of the early measurement budget, and a trained query-selection policy reaches the ranking quality of random selection with fewer evaluations on held-out sources, whereas hand-written rules do not. An ordering from the generalised gradient approximation cuts hybrid-functional compute about sixfold, while an archived ordering that lacks the alloys gives no saving at fixed trust; for Al–Mg–Si, a foundation-potential ordering lowers the DFT compute needed to find eight of the ten most stable compounds from 19% to 5%. The saving depends on direction and coverage, and the agreement-versus-budget curve separates disagreement that further sampling removes from gaps that remain, so a campaign can use these curves to decide which source to compute first, how far to trust it, and when further evaluations stop improving the ranking.

papers.title: Graded revision lets autonomous campaigns update symbolic laws of SiGeC semiconductors from mixed-fidelity evidence
papers.abstract: Autonomous materials campaigns combine published measurements, simulations at several levels of theory and curated compilations whose errors are known in kind but not in size. A value off the current law may be an error, a measurement under a special condition, or a lead to missing physics, and an outlier filter discards all three alike. Machine unlearning removes data from neural networks by costly or approximate retraining, and provenance records locate data origins without identifying which conclusions to revise. We tested whether nine graded revision actions on sourcetagged evidence, from labelling or reweighting rows to forgetting them, confine each correction to conclusions named in advance. The actions operate on symbolic laws fitted by HG-SR, a symbolic-regression engine whose terms record their supporting evidence, and were applied to the lattice thermal conductivity of Si 1-x Ge x and SiGeC, which limits heat removal from SiGe transistors. The pipeline corrected an undesigned unit error, caught mislabelled and amorphous simulation rows from their structure, split the literature by microstructure and issued a conductivity law with a declared validity domain. Of twelve decisions on flagged values, four found errors; the other eight kept the value, five as special conditions (microstructure, another alloy, melting, box size, nonlinear response) and three as leads to physics the law lacked.
