For SiGeC it showed that carbon leaves the lattice as SiC and named in advance the one weak input of the germanium-saving claim; pre-registered tests of that input changed only the named conclusions for a leg operated from 300 to 1100 K, leaving its composition and carbon content unchanged. Because the SiC scattering contrast fell with particle radius roughly as R −4 , 2.5 nm SiC replaces 14–16% of the germanium at equal lattice thermal conductivity (8–9% at 5 nm). Corrections become targeted errata, not rebuilds, and less germanium eases demand for a by-product metal of constrained supply.

papers.title: Processing history attached to each value separates conflicting evidence on metastable (Si)GeSn semiconductors
papers.abstract: GeSn and SiGeSn with several per cent Sn are metastable direct-gap group-IV semiconductors: anneals, contact sinters or hot measurements can move Sn out of the lattice, so a value describes the film at one point in its processing, not its composition alone. Published values rarely carry that history, and machine-learned simulations add values whose errors are known in kind but not in size; two disagreeing values may reflect an error or two different samples. The hypothesis tested was that recording the processing history with every value separates conflicting evidence that composition and temperature leave unresolved. Each value was stored as one event of a time-resolved evidence hypergraph, whose entries link states before and after, defect species, process step, source and time window on separate clocks for sample processing and campaign decisions; defect reactions must balance. The record held 551 literature values from 163 anneal series, 3028 defect events from molecular dynamics with the machine-learned potential MACE-MP-0, and 159 campaign entries. MACE-MP-0 kept Ge 0.88 Sn 0.12 crystalline for 0.5 ns only at 500 K; at 600 and 700 K the model lattice disordered, so a 0.13 eV hop activation energy across 500 to 700 K measures disorder, not a barrier. The same potential bound Sn to a vacancy by 0.43± 0.08 eV. Literature activation energies for Sn diffusion in Ge-rich material spanned 1.13 to 3.10 eV but fell into groups no wider than 0.7 eV once anneal regime and starting state were recorded, and an oxide cap alone decided whether a Si 0.08 Ge 0.88 Sn 0.04 film degraded at 550 °C. These conflicts follow processing history rather than composition, and a foundation potential’s dynamics hold only within a stated temperature range. Anneals of metastable films between 380 and 650 °C therefore call for the low-temperature film activation energy, not the implanted-bulk value.

papers.title: Provenance records predict which multi-scale conclusions a foundation-potential release can change in SiGeC semiconductors
papers.abstract: Multi-scale simulations of semiconductor alloys rest on foundation interatomic potentials (machine-learned force models trained on large density-functional databases), re-released as training data grow. A release changes defect energies and phonon stiffness and, through them, the recipes and design verdicts downstream; recomputing everything is costly, and recomputing nothing leaves conclusions that may no longer hold. Workflow records list every result downstream of a calculation, not which could change a decision. We tested whether the conclusions a release can change are predictable from a campaign’s provenance record (a record of which calculation fed which result) before any rerun and settled by recomputing only the predicted units. The chain served a SiGeC design question (germanium content, carbon content and SiC particle size for low lattice thermal conductivity), with MACE-MP-0 replaced by MACE-MPA-0 and all predictions and decision rules fixed in advance. From the record, 49 of 128 record entries were reached, 24 conclusions were classified by their margin to a decision threshold, and four recompute units were named. Recomputing those units (70 relaxations, 91 molecular-dynamics runs) settled 20 conclusions: none changed outside the predicted set (exact 95% upper bound on the miss rate 0.24), eight of nine flagged as at risk held, and one, Ge attraction to the first shell around a SiC particle, reversed by less than a millielectronvolt past its threshold, while the conclusion it served (no germanium-depleted zone forms) held. Magnitudes moved more than assumed: the energy carbon gains by precipitating as SiC grew by 0.65–0.75 eV against an assumed 0.3 eV; the recipe and the germanium saving held. Recomputation cost 3.5 CPU-task-hours and 354 GPU-hours, 2.2 times the GPU estimate scaled from the recorded runs. Decisions whose margins exceed a measured release shift can be carried across a release with a recorded check; magnitudes need recomputation, and explicit records of each result’s inputs and code would make the prediction a lookup.

papers.title: Covering and loss-tolerant batch designs guarantee what autonomous campaigns sample in SiGeC semiconductors
papers.abstract: Self-driving laboratories plan experiments in batches and lose runs to cracked pellets, tripped furnaces and cancelled compute jobs. Their planners give no guarantee about which combinations of processing variables a batch has sampled, so an interaction between two variables can go unnoticed. The hypothesis tested was that covering designs from software testing supply that guarantee at a run cost known in advance. A covering batch samples every pair of variable levels at least once, or twice so any single lost run leaves the guarantee intact; greedy follow-up batches touched every uncertain region with few runs; and eight evidence sources were assigned to composition and temperature regimes at least cost. In a pre-registered study of heat transport in the boron-or phosphorus-doped nanostructured SiGeC semiconductor (six coupled variables, 9000 combinations), a covering batch sampled every two-factor combination with 33 runs, the doubled batch kept that property under any single loss, and one-factor-at-a-time screening, which never varies two factors together, picked a recipe 33% above the best (22% under the SiC contrast measured later). On 16 molecular dynamics recipes the planner never saw, covering kept its guarantee but predicted no better than random batches, because only Ge content and temperature moved the response there. A covering-designed molecular dynamics campaign on strained SiGe device films found heat flow across a film grown on Si 12 to 18% above relaxed bulk, with heat flow along it unchanged. Covering is valuable while the relevance of each factor is unknown: an autonomous campaign can state, before its first run, which combinations its conclusions speak to.

papers.title: Hash-committed pre-registration and exact unlearning make belief revisions in autonomous SiGeC semiconductor campaigns checkable
papers.abstract: Autonomousmaterials laboratories revise conclusions fromevidence sources (calculations,machine-learned potentials, databases, furnace runs) whose errors are known in kind but not in size. These revisions are self-reported, so a reader cannot check that no batch was dropped or that a retraction removed what it claims; verifiable unlearning covers only erasure from trained machinelearning models. The aim is a record that lets anyone check every revision without trusting the campaign. Full checkability is hypothesised to be affordable when beliefs are compact symbolic models, whose clean retrain takes seconds. Designs are hashed onto an append-only campaign record before runs start, raw outputs are committed before analysis, and revisions are verified by deterministic re-execution. Four pre-registered campaigns on heat transport in SiGe and SiGeC semiconductors (molecular dynamics, machine-learned relaxations, phonon transport, an experimental database) test the scheme. The record keeps failed checks, refuted predictions and set-aside evidence in view, and an independent verifier re-checks it in about three seconds. It meets pharmaceutical data-integrity rules; separating a measurement’s influence on fitted laws from the measurement reconciles the European right to erasure with mandatory retention. Materials claims, such as howmuch germanium carbon can replace, can thus be adopted and extended on an inspectable record.

papers.title: How the fruit fly connectome can help autonomous materials discovery
papers.abstract: Autonomous laboratories for two-dimensional semiconductors pair a recipe planner with instruments that return in situ spectra every few seconds. Some decisions are too fast for the planner: stop a failing selenization anneal, flag a flake that is not the logged material, or end an ion irradiation at a set vacancy density, from a few examples, on a small computer at the instrument. The fruit fly takes decisions of this form with two structures whose wiring is measured at synapse level: the mushroom body, a one-shot memory for odours, and the ventral nerve cord, which turns a few descending commands into local reflexes. We asked which instrument jobs models wired from these connectomes do better than engineered tools. A mushroom-body model of 685 projection neurons and 5,177 Kenyon cells read one Raman band per glomerulus; over 20 paired seeds, on simulated selenization Raman streams and on Ar + irradiation anchored in published in situ spectra, it lost the fewest flakes when one failed run taught a stop rule (3.3 of 30, against 3.9 for a nearest neighbour), read vacancy density from its sparse code with less error than from the raw spectrum (5.5 % against 6.4 %), and ran in 0.30 ms on a Raspberry Pi 5 within 152 kB. A stop decided at the furnace, as the nerve cord decides reflexes, prevented the losses of a planner that needed 60 s per turn (0.15 against 10.7 flakes of 30). It did not choose recipes. In three animals and after training, measured wiring matched a degree-preserving shuffle, and the nerve-cord wiring matched a ridge regression: the connectome contributes an architecture and wiring statistics, not a partner map. As hardware, the fixed wiring can be binary and each plastic synapse needs about 64 levels. The connectome supplies a low-cost reflex layer under the planner, not a replacement.

papers.title: Compound-specific memory demand determines when a research group and a computing centre benefit from sharing information in two-dimensional semiconductor screening
papers.abstract: Screening two-dimensional semiconductors with density functional theory (DFT), the standard electronic-structure method, involves two parties who know each other only qualitatively: a research group holding the candidate list and a computing centre that knows its nodes. Sharing information helps either party only if a calculation’s demand on the node depends on the compound. Thirty transition-metal dichalcogenide layers (MX2; M = Ti, Zr, Hf, Mo, W; X = S, Se, Te) in 1T and 2H structures were screened with Quantum ESPRESSO at the PBE level, recording each calculation’s duration and memory, then supercells up to 3328 electrons and preregistered paired comparisons of no sharing against a job-placing broker. Nine layers have PBE gaps in the 1.0–2.0 eV window of transistor channels and photodetectors, seven after spin–orbit coupling; single-layer 2H cells keep the same nine, and chalcogen-vacancy hop barriers follow the gap, also in Janus layers. In primitive cells and 3×3 supercells, demand followed calculation stage and cell size, which the centre already knows, and no arrangement raised throughput. At 8×8 supercells, compounds of equal electron count differed in memory by 23–32% near node capacity; one disclosed memory-class bit per job raised the centre’s throughput 1.133-fold under memory-reservation charging, but not on single-layer pools, whose memory classes nearly coincide. The group gained no resolvable advantage and job timings revealed the compound, so the hypothesis that the broker benefits both parties was rejected. A gap screen needs batching rather than disclosure; defect and heterostructure supercells justify disclosing one memory class per job.

papers.title: Simple Modification to Minimize Ionomer Poisoning in Carbodiimide Synthesized Pt-Rare Earth Catalysts
papers.abstract: Platinum rare earth (Pt-RE) alloys show promise as oxygen reduction reaction catalysts due to their improved activity and durability over conventional Pt-based catalysts. However, their synthesis has remained relatively complicated due to REs high affinity for oxygen. Recently, carbodiimide-mediated synthesis has shown promise under relatively moderate conditions, although it results in nanoparticle formation mostly on the carbon support exterior. We introduce a simple “wet-mix” modification that allows metallic precursors to diffuse into the pores of the Ketjenblack support as nucleation sites, affording a larger proportion of nanoparticles inside of the pores of the carbon black. XRD, HR-TEM, XPS and XAS, indicate higher Pt 2 Gd formation for the conventional carbodiimide route; our synthesis produces Pt 2 Gd with a small fraction of polycrystalline PtGd. Rotating-disk electrode studies showed that a high ionomer loading does not depress the mass activity, specific activity, or ECSA of the wet-synthesized catalyst. We validate this work in 12 cm 2 single-cell PEMFC studies under H 2 /O 2 , with specific activity improvement of 2.27×, and mass activity improvement of 3.04×. While the durability of the catalyst has not significantly improved, we propose reduced ionomer poisoning of the Pt 2 Gd catalyst resulting from our simple “wet-mix” modification to the carbodiimide route improves ORR activity.

papers.title: An artificial macrophage reveals the impact of nitric oxide microenvironments on bacterial viability
papers.abstract: Nitric oxide (NO) emitted from immune cells such as macrophages plays an important role in combating bacterial pathogens. Yet studying ephemeral NO-mediated interactions in real time, quantitatively, and at the single-cell level has been technically challenging. Here we present an “artificial macrophage”: a live-cell imaging platform that overcomes these challenges by leveraging electrochemistry to generate micropatterned NO gradients at infection-relevant concentrations. We achieve this capability using a biocompatible electrocatalyst that selectively transforms ammonia into NO in biological media. Using Pseudomonas aeruginosa as a model NO-responsive pathogen, we show that the NO microenvironment, influenced by both extracellular NO concentrations and NO gradients experienced by cells, underpins NO’s bactericidal efficacy for individual surface-associated cells. Our results highlight that considering NO’s reaction-diffusion, rather than just its local concentration, is key to understanding how the extracellular microenvironment affects single-cell bacterial viability. Spatiotemporal control of NO microenvironments using our live-cell imaging platform will advance studies of diverse cell types that regularly encounter NO.

papers.title: Steroid Thioesters to Target Golgi Apparatus
papers.abstract: Despite Golgi apparatus plays a central role in lipid and protein trafficking, the biomedical potential of Golgitargeting supramolecular assemblies remains underexplored. While recent studies showed that peptide thioesters localize to the Golgi, it is unclear whether steroid thioesters can exhibit similar targeting behavior. Here, we designed and synthesized steroid-based thioesters by conjugating a thioester group and an NBD fluorophore to bile acids (BAs). Live-cell fluorescence imaging revealed that steroid thioesters localize to the Golgi apparatus, further confirming the utility of thioesters as a reactive warhead for Golgi targeting via localized S-palmitoylation. While BA-thioesters accumulate at the Golgi, their accumulation is slower than peptide thioesters. Unlike the peptide thioesters, these steroid conjugates displayed excellent cellular compatibility, showing minimal cytotoxicity. O-acetylation of BAs also modulates the dynamics of Golgi targeting. Our findings demonstrate that steroid thioesters can serve as Golgi-targeting motifs, expanding the pool of organelle-directed bioconjugates and providing a new scaffold for the design of functional molecules to reprogram palmitoylation-associated processes.

papers.title: Galvanic Coupling Links Heterogeneous and Molecular Palladium Catalysis in Aerobic Alcohol Oxidation
papers.abstract: Thermochemical catalytic reactions are often composed of coupled electrochemical redox reactions, which may even generate the active catalyst itself. Here we show that oxygen reduction on heterogeneous palladium drives corrosion of Pd(0) through galvanic coupling: electrons released by Pd(0) oxidation are consumed by oxygen reduction on the same catalyst, and the soluble Pd(II) forms a homogeneous complex which catalyzes benzyl alcohol oxidation. Combining corrosion measurements with quantification of Pd(II) and reaction products, we find that supplying more oxygen raises the catalyst potential and accelerates Pd(II) generation and alcohol oxidation. Applying equivalent electrochemical potentials in the absence of oxygen reproduces Pd(II) generation and alcohol oxidation with similar sensitivity to the catalyst potential. Diverting the anodic reaction to a sacrificial anode suppresses Pd(II) supply and thus the thermochemical reaction rate. Hence, the primary role of oxygen is to set the potential for generating the active catalyst, while palladium corrosion is the kinetic link to thermochemical turnover. Together, our results show that galvanic coupling provides a framework that links electrochemistry and thermochemical catalysis.

papers.title: Triple Atom Transfer-Enabled α-C(sp3)-H Aminomethylation of Aliphatic Amines: General and Modular Access to Vicinal Diamines
papers.abstract: Vicinal diamines are prevalent structural elements in organic molecules. In particular, those featuring a tertiary alkylamine motif are commonly found in biologically active molecules and therapeutic agents. However, methods for the efficient construction of these architectures from inexpensive and readily available feedstocks remain scarce. Here, we report a mild photocatalytic protocol for the modular synthesis of vicinal alkyl diamines via triple atom transfer-enabled α-C(sp3)–H aminomethylation. This transformation integrates halogen-atom transfer (XAT) and intramolecular 1,5-hydrogen-atom transfer (HAT) processes to furnish key α-amido alkyl radicals, which subsequently add to in situ-generated iminium ions. Critical to the success of the reaction is the cooperative action of a nickel complex and a zinc salt, which jointly promote the aminomethylation process. Utility of this method is demonstrated through late-stage modification of complex amine molecules, scale-up experiments, and ready access to scaffold-diverse free vicinal diamines. In addition, compatibility with aromatic aldehydes and the ability to functionalize alternative C–H sites further expand the chemical space of diamine architectures, highlighting the robustness and synthetic versatility of this protocol.

papers.title: Two extrapolation axes decide whether interaction needs a module in many-body systems
papers.abstract: We separate the extrapolation problem in many-body systems into two axes: toward combinations with more components (the composition axis), and toward components unseen (the identity axis). The prevailing pipeline—encode then interact—performs poorly when extrapolating in composition count. We open an interaction-free route to interaction by strengthening its encoder until a component’s representation can carry what it contributes across the mixtures it appears in. Where component identities are bounded while their combinations are not, this route performs better along the composition axis, while the prevailing route is better along the identity axis; both differences follow from the functional forms rather than from the data. Chemical mixtures are the main example, synthetic tasks isolate the two axes, and the same structure recurs in other fields.

papers.title: Nature skips the 3/2 rung: point group selects the orientational exponent
papers.abstract: The low-temperature orientational heat capacity of an interacting multipole pair is conventionally taken to be two-valued: 3/2 k_B for axially symmetric moments and 2 k_B otherwise. Here I evaluate it for all 101,666,280 molecular geometries of the OMol25 dataset and show that this is the bottom rung of a staircase: the exponent is a count, not a case split, γ = C_v/k_B = Σ_i 1/p_i, which for two rigid nonlinear molecules is exactly γ = D/2 and leaves only the rungs 3/2, 2 and 5/2. Of 11,325,000 pairs drawn uniformly from the whole dataset none occupies the 3/2 rung (P < 3.26×10⁻⁷), and the rest split 12.05% and 87.95% between γ = 2 and 5/2, so nearly the whole molecular world shares one coefficient: (5/2) k_B = 20.79 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ per mole of pairs. The rung is deleted structurally rather than thermally suppressed: axiality is forced only by a C₃ or higher rotation axis in the equilibrium point group, and a census of equilibrium structures weighted by the dataset's own size distribution bounds the branch at 2.07×10⁻⁵ — a limit set by symmetry rather than by a numerical threshold, and therefore independent of how the geometries were sampled; and which rung a pair occupies is settled by its point group at the dominant multipole rank rather than by temperature, coupling or size — a C₃ axis supplies axiality only at rank two, so the bottom rung needs σ_h or S₆ as well.

papers.title: Polarization-Driven Hydride Transfer Promotes Cobalt Tetrasulfophthalocyanine-Catalyzed Hydrogen Evolution by Five Orders of Magnitude
papers.abstract: The hydricity of M–H intermediates is a key descriptor and optimization target for the rational design of molecular hydrogen evolution electrocatalysts. Adsorption to an electrode surface is known to augment catalytic rate, but it remains unclear how adsorption affects M-H hydricity. Herein, we quantitatively compare the catalytic activity and mechanism of the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) from cobalt tetrasulfophthalocyanine (CoTSPc) in a dissolved aqueous form (CoTSPc (aq) ) and when adsorbed to the surface of a carbon electrode (CoTSPc/C). At the same electrode potential, CoTSPc/C catalyzes HER at a rate that is over five orders of magnitude faster than CoTSPc (aq) . Mechanistic studies indicate that both CoTSPc/C and CoTSPc (aq) catalyze HER via a rate-limiting hydride transfer to a proton donor in solution to form H 2 . Hydride transfer from Co-H in CoTSPc (aq) is a purely chemical step defined by a constant hydricity of 22.4 kcal mol −1 that is independent of applied potential. In contrast, hydride transfer from Co-H in CoTSPc/C is strongly polarization dependent, decreasing hydricity by ~23 kcal mol −1 V −1 to values as low as 1.2 kcal mol −1 at −1.1 V vs SHE, leading to the observed rate promotion. We attribute this mechanistic change to the positioning of the CoTSPc-H intermediate within the electrochemical double layer, such that the hydride traverses the interfacial electrostatic potential difference during the RLS. These results demonstrate the power of surface adsorption to generate highly reactive molecular hydrides and fundamentally reshape the free energy landscape of electrocatalysis.

papers.title: Directional Control of Droplet Motion via Geometric Gating
papers.abstract: We explore new methods for inducing the movement of water droplets on elastomeric substrates, such as polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS). Our approach builds upon the well-known phenomenon that water droplets move easily across these substrates when swelled with silicone oil. While designing shallow open channels and traps on a PDMS film offers a simple way to control a droplet's trajectory by tilting the substrate in two orthogonal directions, this method is poorly suited for manipulating multiple droplets simultaneously. To address this limitation, we introduce two new methods. The first method utilizes a piano-concave PDMS platform with a radius of curvature significantly larger than the size of the droplet and its translation distance. When the system's configuration is altered, this curved substrate consistently guides the droplet along a curved geodesic. The second method incorporates diode-like gates on the PDMS. These gates are created on either flat or piano-concave PDMS films by embedding thin, rigid plates into the elastomer prior to crosslinking, followed by swelling in silicone oil. This process generates sigmoidal steps that restrict droplet motion to a single direction. Finally, we demonstrate how combining these two strategies enables various forms of directed motion for both single and multiple droplets.

papers.title: Single-Ion Hydration Through the Lens of Data-Driven Many-Body Potentials
papers.abstract: Single-ion hydration provides a stringent test of molecular models because local ionwater interactions, collective polarization, nuclear quantum effects, and long-range electrostatics all contribute to experimentally measurable structure, spectra, and thermodynamics. Here we discuss how data-driven many-body potentials, in particular MB-pol for water and MB-nrg for hydrated ions, provide a physically transparent route from correlated electronic structure data to predictive simulations of ion hydration from clusters to bulk water and aqueous interfaces. We emphasize how this framework transforms single-ion hydration from a parameterization problem into a hierarchy of many-body observables, and we outline opportunities for connecting simulations directly with interfacial spectroscopy, hydration free energies, and complex electrolyte environments.

papers.title: Combinatorial Steiner Methodology for Efficiently Exploring Chemical Space in CO 2 Hydrogenation to Fischer-Tropsch Reactivity via High-throughput Experimentation
papers.abstract: High-throughput experimentation (HTE) and machine learning (ML) have accelerated discovery in molecular chemistry. Meanwhile, such advances in heterogeneous catalysis are hindered by the complexity of materials and the vast chemical space. We present a mathematically optimized methodology using Steiner coverings to explore multi-component catalysts and access lower-dimension interactions through higher-dimension blocks. From 21 elements, we designed a library of 70 trimetallic mixed-metal-oxide catalysts, covering all 210 possible bimetallic pairs. The experimental workflow was automated by a robotic platform and applied to thermocatalytic CO 2 hydrogenation, critical for achieving a circular carbon economy. In just 70 materials we successfully recovered and uncovered trends in methanation, reverse water–gas shift (RWGS), and methanol synthesis, while discovering a highly active FeGaRu catalyst for CO 2 –Fischer–Tropsch synthesis that retains this reactivity when simplified to binary FeRu, Ga providing improved performances. Our combinatorial optimization methodology replaces thousands of manual experiments with strategic exploration, improving the discovery rate for complex, multi-component heterogeneous catalysts.

papers.title: Electrolyte Switching Reveals Electric Double Layer Dynamics and Electrocatalytic Electrolyte Effects
papers.abstract: New insights into the electric double layer (EDL) under strongly driven electrocatalytic (EC) conditions are obtained by measuring its rearrangement kinetics in response to abrupt switching of bulk electrolyte composition (55 ms for complete exchange up to the ordered layers of the EDL) The aqueous alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is used as a model EC system, motivated by its opposite alkali metal hydroxide effect: catalyst activity decreases with increasing cation radius on Pt (Li + > Na + > K + > Cs + ) whereas the trend is opposite for Au and Ag. Monitoring the constant potential HER current as the electrolyte composition is switched between two different cations (e.g. Li + and Cs + ) provides an overall kinetic picture as the EDL rearranges to accommodate the new cation. For both Pt, Au, and Ag, the transition time is asymmetric; switching from a smaller ionic radius to a larger one is faster than the reverse (e.g. 95 ± 31 ms for Li + → K + compared to 352 ± 38 ms for K + → Li + on Pt at -200 mV vs RHE). Transition times also increase with greater ionic radius difference between the cations and at more negative potentials. The transition time trends are consistent with more weakly hydrated cations having stronger electrostatic ion-electrode interactions and hence being slower to leave. EDL rearrangement kinetics appear unaffected by the simultaneously occurring HER. Mixing LiOH with the stickier K/CsOH electrolytes produced a smooth, continuous variation in HER kinetics with increasing K/CsOH fraction on Pt, Au, and Ag, even though we expect the closest ion plane (CIP) to be mostly K + /Cs + over the range. This shows that EDL structure beyond the CIP can also influence HER kinetics on Pt, Au, and Ag. Our work emphasizes the spatial extent of electrolyte influence which needs to be captured by theory.

papers.title: Martini 3 Coarse-Grained Models for Steroid Hormones
papers.abstract: Steroid hormones are central to the development, metabolism, homeostasis and reproduction of animals and have been the subject of many evolutionary, ecotoxicological and human health studies. Coarse-grain molecular dynamics (CG MD) simulations are a powerful tool to study the structural and dynamic behavior of steroid hormones and their interactions. Here, we expand the capabilities of the widely used Martini 3 CG framework by parameterizing and validating a set of 20 steroid hormone models — including both endogenous and synthetic molecules — to enable their study across diverse targets, systems, and fields of interest. Hormone parameterization followed Martini 3 guidelines, while leveraging the similarities with the parent cholesterol molecule, for which a Martini 3 model is available. Notably, we were able to base our parameterization on the hundreds of experimental structures in the protein data bank that contain steroid hormones, instead of relying on atomistic simulations as is typical with Martini. The parameterized models match to within 5% target molecular volumes, and recover the overall hydrophobicity trend of the hormones, although higher hydrophobicities tended to be overestimated. In free simulations of protein-hormone systems the experimentally known binding poses could be recovered for 89% of the cases, indicating a successful parameterization also from a functional standpoint. Since several Martini 3 protein models were tested, we also incidentally show that the flexibility of the OLIVES and GōMartini models makes them best suited for this type of protein–ligand recognition. Finally, models were validated in interaction with membranes by comparison to reference atomistic data. We expect that the availability of our fully validated Martini 3 CG steroid hormone models will contribute to new studies, collaborations, and applications across different scientific fields.

papers.title: Controlling Vertical and Lateral Growth of Copper and Ruthenium on Tungsten Dichalcogenide Monolayers for Interconnects and Metal Contacts
papers.abstract: The unique properties of tungsten based transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers (TMDs) drive significant interest for their use in a variety of applications, from heterogeneous catalysis, to future generation semiconductor device technologies. In these technologies the TMD monolayers are necessarily interfaced with a metal, such as a source and drain contact for use as a channel material in sub-nm transistors, an interconnect metal when used as a diffusion barrier, or as a support for a metal catalyst. The control of the morphology of the interfaced metal is critical to ensure optimal material performance for these target applications. Therefore, an atomic level description of how metals interact and grow on TMDs is needed. First principles studies of metal-TMD monolayer interactions have primarily focussed on the behaviour of single metal atom adsorption, substitutional metal doping, or pristine metal-monolayer interfaces. Consequently, there persists a clear gap in the understanding of metal growth on TMD monolayers and the drivers of vertical versus lateral growth. In this work, we present a density functional theory and ab initio molecular dynamics investigation of the adsorption, preferred morphology, and dynamics of Cu and Ru metal deposits on WS2 and WSe2 monolayers. Using metal cluster models of sufficient size to display a variety of potential morphologies, and by characterising the behaviour of the metal deposits with an ensemble of analytical shape descriptors derived from the gyration tensor, we develop a comprehensive and quantitative understanding of the structure, stability, dynamics, and morphology of deposited metals on tungsten TMD monolayers. We find that on both TMDs Cu prefers to form compact, vertically growing clusters, with molecular dynamics simulations showing a transition to a more compact metal shape and a further promotion of 3D growth over time. In contrast, Ru prefers to grow laterally on WS2. Ru present on WSe2 displays a preference for a lateral morphology as on WS2, but makes noticeably more compact deposits on WSe2 than on WS2. Dynamics simulations show that temperature further promotes growth in the preferred direction, thus driving both island growth and lateral deposition depending on the inherent preference for a growth mode. These results demonstrate clearly how the identity of the metal and the TMD layer contribute to the preferred growth mode and morphology. Additionally, we reveal the critical importance of dynamic cluster evolution over time in determining the final structure.

papers.title: Evaluating transfer across modalities in autonomous materials systems
papers.abstract: A power device needs a wide-gap semiconductor and a heat-treated Al–Mg–Si alloy to cool it, and both draw on sources that disagree: band gaps from several levels of density functional theory (DFT) and from measurement, alloy formation energies from DFT and interatomic potentials. Multi-fidelity methods combine such sources only through paired values on a common scale and do not state in advance whether one source’s guidance holds in another. We test whether the relative differences between candidates, which lead and by how much, are preserved across sources whose values disagree. PEGKi infers relative ratings of decision bodies (any rule that ranks candidates) from comparison outcomes within each source, and scores every donor-to-receiver route with a robustness certificate or a refusal. The evidence is 261,053 archived band-gap records from eight sources and an Al–Mg–Si pool where every query runs a DFT or molecular-dynamics calculation. Orderings alone recover the accuracy ladder of the DFT levels, and experiment spreads material classes about twice as widely as the generalised gradient approximation. Transfer follows the database of origin more than the functional, and routing learned from measured campaigns outperforms the fixed default at every query size. For the alloy, the score picks each potential’s room-temperature run as donor at heat-treatment temperatures, the best measured choice in five of six cases, and discounts the two potentials that predict Mg 2 Si to be unstable. Relative margins therefore transfer where values do not, so a campaign can rate whose knowledge to reuse before committing compute or instrument time.

papers.title: Spin-chemistry modulation of ATP synthesis via vibronic reorganisation
papers.abstract: Coordination between adenosine diphosphate (ADP) and a magnesium (Mg) ion is a key prerequisite step in the synthesis of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), and in the last few decades it has been proposed that ATP synthesis yields may be sensitive to magnetic fields. Prior studies have invoked the radical-pair mechanism to explain magnetic field effects (MFEs) and magnetic isotope effects (MIEs) in ATP synthases; however, the microscopic conditions required for such effects have not been clearly established. Here, we investigate the mechanistic constraints under which MFEs and MIEs may emerge in the ADP-Mg precursory complex through spin-orbit coupling (SOC) and the hyperfine interaction. Enhanced triplet populations, key to preventing recombination, are observed only upon isotopic enrichment. We find that isotope-dependent vibronic reorganisation dominates spin evolution in the ADP-Mg radical pair, contrary to the conventional interpretation that magnetic isotope effects originate from nuclear-spin-dependent hyperfine interactions. While the MFE was found to be negligible, spin-dynamics simulations reveal a 45% enhancement in projected ATP yields due to MIEs. Molecular dynamics simulations show that perturbations to the dimer conformation and Mg coordination environment do not strongly alter the spin chemistry. These results reconcile the conflicting observations of magnetosensitivity in ATP synthesis and establish experimentally testable criteria for assessment of field-sensitive bioenergetic systems.

papers.title: In Situ Mapping of Aqueous CO2 during the Electrochemical CO2 Reduction Reaction
papers.abstract: Electrochemical interfaces feature dynamically evolving local reactant distributions that strongly influence catalytic behavior. In electrochemical CO 2 reduction (CO 2 RR), the low solubility and limited diffusion of CO 2 generate highly non-uniform local reaction environments near electrochemical interfaces. However, the actual spatial distribution of dissolved CO 2 within the interfacial structure under operating conditions remains poorly understood due to limited experimental visualization methods that probe interfacial structure. Here, we introduce an in situ ratiometric fluorescent labeling strategy with a CO 2 -sensitive chemosensor to directly visualize dissolved CO 2 distributions during CO 2 RR. Using a pyrene-modified fluorescent chemosensor, we directly visualize the spatial distribution and dynamic evolution of local dissolved CO 2 concentrations near electrochemical interfaces. The measurements reveal pronounced spatial heterogeneity in the CO 2 RR microenvironment, dynamic evolution of gas-liquid-solid interfaces, and unexpectedly strong local CO 2 enrichment. Dissolved CO 2 concentrations near the interface approached ~84.4 ± 27.5 mM. Beyond CO 2 RR, this work establishes fluorescent labeling as a general operando visualization strategy for probing local reactant distributions and interfacial mass transport processes in electrochemical systems.

papers.title: Symmetry-adapted perturbation theory for cavity-modified intermolecular interactions: QED-SAPT0 theory and implementation
papers.abstract: We develop a cavity quantum electrodynamics symmetry adapted perturbation theory (QED-SAPT) formalism that directly models intermolecular interactions in quantized cavity environments. By formulating the zeroth-order problem in a coherent state basis, we define the inter-monomer perturbation as the sum of the standard Coulombic contribution and an inter-monomer dipole self energy contribution. This yields a particularly convenient structure whereby the new inter-monomer cavity components can be incorporated through a simple augmentation of the dressed integrals that arise in standard SAPT theory. We also leverage this structure in a density fitted implementation and demonstrate the performance advantage over an implementation that utilizes the full electron integral tensor. Finally, we utilize this formalism to explore several representative molecular clusters from the S66 data set and provide comparison to QED-CCSD and QED-DFT formalisms.

papers.title: WITHDRAWN
papers.abstract: Withdrawn at the authors' request because it was posted without the approval of all contributors.

papers.title: From Notch-Tip Stress to Mechanophore Activation - A Multiscale Study of Mechanochromic PMMA
papers.abstract: Mechanophore-functionalized polymers enable optical readout of molecular-level stress under macroscopic deformation. Spiropyran (SP)-doped poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) provides a well-established platform for mechanochemical stress sensing, yet molecular stress fields around defined geometric stress concentrators remain largely disconnected from continuum mechanics. To bridge this gap, we develop a geometry-matched molecular dynamics (MD) and finite-element (FE) approach for PMMA containing two opposing semi-elliptical notches of systematically varied depth and width. Molecular simulations employ a hybrid coarse-grained/all-atom (CG/AA) PMMA model with atomistically resolved, quantum-chemically (QC) informed SP, while the FE models use the MD-derived stress–strain response of bulk PMMA as input. Under uniaxial tension, both approaches capture notch-tip stress localization, plastic-zone propagation toward the ligament center, and the characteristic butterfly-shaped stress field. FE simulations reproduce MD notch-tip stresses, demonstrating that suitably parameterized continuum models capture key notch mechanics, whereas defect-mediated rearrangements require molecular resolution. Notch geometry strongly enhances SP activation to its merocyanine (MC) form, lowering the onset strain and localizing activation in highly elongated chains and around deformation-induced voids near the notch edges. These results link defect geometry and molecular stress concentration to mechanophore activation and directly connect molecular and continuum notch mechanics.

papers.title: Geometrical Constraints Weaken a Nickel–Hydrogen Bond and Enable the Homolytic H2 Evolution Mechanism
papers.abstract: Mechanistic studies of the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) are helping advance catalysis towards energy storage technologies based on water splitting. Homolytic H–H bondforming pathways are one of the fundamental mechanisms of HER, yet well-defined examples of bimetallic coupling in molecular HER catalysts remain extremely rare. A planar tetradentate bipyridine diphosphinite ligand (PONNOP) is reported that constrains the geometry of nickel complexes, weakening the Ni–H bond dissociation free energy and enabling H2 evolution via the homolytic pathway. Crystallography, magnetism, absorption spectroscopy, and computational studies provide insight into the electronic structure enforced by the rigid tetradentate PONNOP ligand, which results in a very weak Ni–H bond in a transiently formed metal hydride. Cyclic voltammetry and chronoamperometry studies are consistent with electrocatalytic HER via the homolytic mechanism. The ability of a tetradentate ligand to induce M–H bond-weakening is discussed as a possible design element in HER by Earth-abundant catalysts.

papers.title: (ImRN)2Fe: An Elusive Complex and the Limits of Its Ferrocene Analogy
papers.abstract: The isolobal relationship between imidazolin-2-iminato and cyclopentadienyl ligands makes the iron bis(imidazolin-2-iminato) complex (Im R N) 2 Fe an attractive target as a potential ferrocene analog, yet reported efforts toward its isolation have been unsuccessful. Herein, we report the synthesis of (Im Dipp N) 2 Fe ( 1 ) by protonolysis of Fe 2 Mes 4 with Im Dipp NH, affording a linear, two-coordinate, high-spin Fe(II) complex (S = 2). Its coordinative unsaturation permits binding of THF, an aryl isocyanide, and TEMPO, affording complexes with varied geometries. Unlike ferrocene, the electrochemical properties of 1 depend strongly on its ancillary ligands. Oxidation with AgPF 6 affords a Ag-bound Fe(II) intermediate 1-Ag that undergoes photochemical conversion to the Fe(III) complex [(Im Dipp N) 2 Fe(Solv) 2 ][PF 6 ] ( 2 ). These results establish 1 as a distinct low-coordinate iron complex whose coordination and redox chemistry extend beyond its proposed ferrocene analogy.

papers.title: HFO-1234yf as a Source of the 3,3-Difluoropropynyl Group
papers.abstract: Dimethyl(phenyl)(2,3,3-trifluoroallyl)silane, the defluorosilylation product of HFO-1234yf, reacts with KHMDS to form 3,3-difluoro-1-dimethyl(phenyl)silylpropyne. The mechanism of this transformation was rationalized through DFT calculations. Deprotonation and subsequent β-fluoride elimination leads to an allene intermediate. A base-catalyzed 1,3-proton migration from the allene then results in the difluoromethylated alkyne product. This alkynyl silane can undergo transmetalation with NHC-ligated Group 11 transition metal chloride complexes to form novel metal acetylide compounds with a 3,3-difluoropropynyl motif.

papers.title: 3H-1,5-Benzodiazepine Derivatives as Novel Antimalarial Agents: Synthesis, Biological Evaluation and Computational Target Exploration
papers.abstract: Malaria remains a major global health challenge worldwide and the emergence of resistance to frontline antimalarial drugs, including artemisinin-based combination therapies, underscores the need for novel antimalarial agents with distinct mechanism of action. Herein, eighteen novel 3H-1,5-benzodiazepine derivatives (5a-r) were synthesized and evaluated against chloroquine-sensitive (PfD10) and chloroquine resistant (PfW2) strains of Plasmodium falciparum. Cytotoxicity was assessed against human hepatocellular carcinoma (HepG2) cells to determine preliminary selectivity. Compound 5e, 5k, 5m, 5n, and 5o exhibited promising anti-plasmodial activity. Compound 5o was the most potent, with IC50 values of 5.88 ± 0.36 and 6.68 ± 2.03 µM against PfD10 and PfW2, respectively, whereas 5k and 5n displayed the most favourable selectivity profiles. Considering the potency of compounds 5k and 5o, we further evaluated them against human G9a, a histone lysine methyltransferase which showed exhibited weak inhibition relative to the reference inhibitor BIX-01294. Computational studies that include frontier molecular orbital analysis, molecular docking, MM-GBSA calculations, molecular dynamics simulations and post-simulation analyses were performed to support their binding modes and stability within the active sites of parasite-specific PfSET3 and human G9a. Thus, this study identifies 3H-1,5-benzodiazepine scaffold as a promising and underexplored starting point for new antimalarial agents, with PfSET3 emerging as an interesting target worth further investigation.

papers.title: Conformational Control and Charge Separation Dynamics in Perylene Bisimide-based Donor-Acceptor Polymers
papers.abstract: The development of organic electronic materials is fundamentally influenced by the electronic structure of π-conjugated polymers. Precise positioning of donor and acceptor (D-A) units plays a crucial role in tailoring electronic properties to meet desired requirements. In this study, we report the synthesis and investigation of a novel class of D-A polymers. Four polymers, two with hanging and two with linear configurations of perylene bisimide, were designed and synthesized using Hay-Glaser and oxidative coupling polymerization methods. These polymers differ in the length of the saturated spacer connecting a bithiophene, thiophene-acetylene “donor” core to a bay-substituted perylene bisimide “acceptor”. Femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy enabled the correlation of the variations in charge separation and stabilization with conformational preferences and the folding behavior of the polymers. AFM images show that the polymer forms a maximum chain length of up to ~175 nm (up to ~140 monomers) and self-assembles on the hexagonal graphite lattice with a distinct threefold orientation. Notably, this study establishes a direct correlation between molecular conformation (linear vs. hanging configurations) and optoelectronic properties, deepening the understanding of how spatial orientation influences charge separation and stabilization dynamics.

papers.title: Spatially Encoding Fluorescence by Tailoring Clustering-Triggered Emission in Polymer Networks
papers.abstract: Spatially programmable fluorescence has widespread potential for display, sensing and security applications, but current patterning strategies remain primarily limited to simple binary systems or methods that require locally varied chemical composition. The design of electron-rich clusters allows for a direct and facile method to induce controlled clusteroluminescence. However, achieving the necessary control over intermolecular interactions has required the design of polymers with new backbones or end groups, limiting the opportunity to spatially vary the luminescence. In this study, intermolecular interactions and therefore fluorescent emission are controlled in a single step by the photopolymerization of a methacrylate-based monomer system. The emission wavelength and intensity can be facilely tuned by varying the crosslinking density within the polymer, and further modulated through processing parameters, such as irradiation time and intensity. Moreover, the monomer system can be integrated within a multimaterial direct-ink writing setup. By selectively depositing monomer mixtures with different crosslinker concentration, structures can be printed with locally-controlled emission for patterned fluorescence images. Achieving the spatial encoding of clusteroluminescence with an approach generalizable for a broad range of monomers allows for design of new polymer-based optical devices with complex photonic responses.

papers.title: DNA-programmed nanogels as dynamic membraneless compartments for synthetic cells
papers.abstract: Bottom-up synthetic biology aims to engineer minimal systems that mimic and expand upon biological structures and functions. Programmed and dynamic organisation of intracellular components into membraneless organelles is being uncovered as vital to many cellular processes. Current approaches to introduce such membraneless compartmentalisation into bottom-up synthetic cells have focused on biomolecular coacervates, which are generally highly sensitive to environmental conditions and limited in their ability to controllably interact. A major benefit of synthetic cells, over living cellular systems, is that non-biological components can be incorporated to expand their functionality. Here, we present DNA-coated nanogels as a new membraneless compartment that can be interfaced with vesicle membranes in a dynamic and programmed manner. Nanogels are well-defined nanoscale cross-linked polymer networks. The selection of the constituent polymers gives rise to tuneable size, excellent biostability, stimuli-responsiveness, and versatile cargo loading. The ability to covalently and non-covalently load a wide variety of cargoes into nanogels has led to them being widely investigated as drug-delivery devices and nanoreactors. By functionalising nanogels with DNA, we achieved specific assembly and localisation of the nanogels onto DNA-coated vesicle membranes, creating a new type of synthetic cell. We then achieved selective disassembly and release of the DNA-nanogels by using enzymatic and DNA triggers. This approach introduces DNA-nanogels as a new membraneless platform to dynamically control the compartmentalisation state of synthetic cells. Combined with nanogel biocompatibility and loading capacity, DNAnanogels might be exploited to spatiotemporally organise biomolecular reactions and introduce entirely new functions to synthetic cells.

papers.title: Probing Molecular Chirality from Vibrational to X-ray Energies in Cr(III) and Co(III) Complexes
papers.abstract: The expression of molecular chirality across widely separated energy regimes was investigated in enantiomeric Cr(III) and Co(III) tris(trans-1,2-cyclohexanediamine) complexes using vibrational circular dichroism (VCD), electronic circular dichroism (ECD), and X-ray natural circular dichroism (XNCD), supported by single-crystal X-ray diffraction and density functional theory (DFT). Crystallographic analysis establishes the Λ-δδδ/lel3 and Δ-λλλ/lel3 configurations in the solid state, while the ECD spectra and comparison of experimental and DFT-calculated VCD spectra support retention of the lel3 stereochemical arrangement in solution. At the Co K-edge, pronounced opposite-sign XNCD responses are observed in the pre-edge region, with an amplitude approximately 1.5 times that previously reported for the Co(III)–ethylenediamine system measured in axial geometry, corresponding to an estimated threefold enhancement under equivalent axial conditions. At the Cr K-edge, a clear, reproducible and well-resolved enantiomer-dependent XNCD response, featuring several distinct dichroic contributions, is observed, despite its lower amplitude relative to the Co analogue. To the best of our knowledge, this constitutes the first clear experimental observation of XNCD at the Cr K-edge. The distinct XNCD responses of these structurally related Cr(III) and Co(III) complexes demonstrate the sensitivity of K-edge XNCD to differences in the local chiral electronic environment of transition-metal centers.

papers.title: Systematically Constructing QM regions for Calculating QM/MM Absorption Spectra
papers.abstract: Hybrid simulations utilizing both quantum mechanics and molecular mechanics (QM/MM) are widely used to model complex problems, such as the electronic excitation of chromophores embedded in a protein environment. Its success requires a careful choice of the portion of the system to include in the QM region to obtain accurate results. Chemical intuition and/or proximity arguments are often used to select the QM region for excited state calculations aiming to compute absorption spectra, but such choices do not guarantee accuracy. We compare four schemes for selecting the minimal set of protein residues that must be treated quantum mechanically to reproduce a reference spectrum: distance analysis, charge shift analysis, point charge variation analysis, and subtractive analysis. Charge shift analysis is the most robust: in both systems studied it identifies the smallest QM region that reproduces the reference spectral shape and absorption maximum, at moderate computational cost, using a threshold that transfers between systems. Because the resulting regions are both accurate and minimal, converged excited state calculations become affordable at scale, laying a foundation for large, internally consistent datasets of excited state properties in extended systems. We release an open-source implementation that automates the full workflow, including residue selection and determination of the QM/MM boundary, so a converged QM region can be built for a new system without manual intervention.

papers.title: The curious case of COF-300: One framework, Seventeen years of structural reinterpretation
papers.abstract: Few frameworks have changed the meaning of their own structural description as profoundly as COF-300. Over seventeen years, this archetypal three-dimensional covalent organic framework has evolved from a powder-derived interpenetrated model into a condition-dependent structural landscape. Successive studies revealed that conserved covalent connectivity can accommodate different interpenetration states, pronounced geometrical distortion, guest-selected conformers and large-amplitude breathing through coupled linker rotation, node deformation and interframework displacement. The structural problem subsequently expanded beyond the unit cell: crystal size, facets, local disorder, surfaces and composition alter mechanical response, while amorphous polymers, ordered molecular intermediates, classical growth and oriented attachment expose multiple routes by which crystallinity emerges. Recent advances go further, enabling crystallization trajectories, defects and even covalent linkages to be deliberately manipulated without necessarily erasing crystallographic identity. COF-300 is therefore better understood not through a single CIF, but as a history- and environment-dependent ensemble of states connected by kinetic pathways and energetic barriers. Its seventeen-year evolution reframes a broader challenge for dynamic reticular materials: structural determination must progress toward structural cartography, and reticular design from programming connectivity toward programming landscapes—the accessible states, transitions and histories through which a crystal acquires its behaviour.

papers.title: Are Molecular Foundation Models Ready for Free Energy Simulations?
papers.abstract: Foundation models for atomistic simulations offer broadly applicable potentialenergy surfaces that can either be applied in a zero-shot manner (without domainspecific retraining) or fine-tuned to the task at hand. Their accuracy is typically judged by energy and force errors on near-equilibrium data, yet it remains largely unclear whether these metrics translate into reliable free-energy landscapes. Here, enhanced sampling can be a particularly demanding test: simulations are driven far from equilibrium into sparsely trained regions and held there over long trajectories, so that small systematic errors in forces or relative energies can accumulate and distort predicted populations, transition pathways, and barriers. We assess several molecular foundation models trained on different dataset sizes and architectures (including models with explicit long-range electrostatics) in prototypical metadynamics and umbrella sampling simulations. Our results show that recent foundation models can reproduce simple gas-phase free-energy profiles with near-reference accuracy, while more complex multidimensional and solvated free-energy landscapes remain challenging. However, assessing their performance in these systems is further complicated by limitations in current sampling protocols and the lack of well-defined reference data. These findings highlight the need for more rigorous sampling protocols and reliable benchmarks to systematically assess the accuracy of future molecular foundation models in free-energy calculations.

papers.title: Polymethylsilsesquioxane Aerogel-like Xerogels via a Surfactant-Free Base-Catalyzed Process
papers.abstract: Highly insulating polymethylsilsesquioxane (PMSQ) aerogel-like xerogels were prepared from methyltrimethoxysilane in 2-propanol (IPA)/water using 10 wt % aqueous tetraethylammonium hydroxide in a one-step reaction without an acid step or surfactant. Fine interconnected skeletons were obtained after ambient-pressure drying. Infrared spectroscopy and solid-state 29Si nuclear magnetic resonance indicated fewer residual silanols in the dried material than in a two-step reference. A 20-fold scale-up gave effective thermal conductivities of 0.018 W m−1 K−1 for granular material and 0.021 W m−1 K−1 for a PMSQ-filled panel with a polycarbonate casing at 20 °C. This provides a simple route to insulating granular PMSQ.

papers.title: Information Dynamics Explains Chemical Reactions: A Unified Framework from NaI Photodissociation to H2 Formation
papers.abstract: Chemical reactions are fundamentally the motion of atomic nuclei on potential energy surfaces. However, there is a methodological gap between quantum chemistry calculations and dynamical simulations: constructing potential energy surfaces is complicated, non-adiabatic couplings are difficult to treat, and different reaction types lack a unified language. In this work we introduce the information dynamics framework, reformulating chemical reactions as a three-element system: virtual space (potential energy surface rules), real space (initial wave packet data), and coupling matrix (projection mechanism). The virtual space defines the absolutely allowed region for nuclear motion, the real space provides the observed distribution of initial positions and momenta, and the coupling matrix drives the system toward a steady-state product according to the virtual space topology (gradient flow for a single surface or Landau-Zener transitions for two crossing surfaces). We validate the framework with three classic reactions: (1) NaI photodissociation (nonadiabatic, two crossing surfaces)—simulated dissociation yield 65.3% ± 1.5%, matching Zewail’s femtochemistry experiment (65%); (2) Cl2 photodissociation (adiabatic, single repulsive surface)dissociation yield 100%, mean relative kinetic energy 3.84 eV, in agreement with literature values;

papers.title: Ligand Protonation Tunes Hydride-Transfer Thermochemistry in an Iron Metal-Ligand Cooperative Catalyst
papers.abstract: Cyclopentadienone iron complexes are established metal-ligand cooperative hydrogenation catalysts, yet their bifunctional reactivity complicates the independent evaluation of proton- and hydride-transfer thermodynamics. Here, room-temperature H 2 -splitting enables deconvolution of these contributions, affording a new anionic hydride with a hydricity of 39.0 kcal·mol -1 . Ligand protonation weakens hydride-donor strength by 10 kcal mol -1 , highlighting protonation-state control of reactivity in MLC catalysis.

papers.title: Optical Design of Low-Haze Transparent Wood
papers.abstract: Transparent wood (TW) composite is a structural optical material for light‑transmitting applications. TW with low haze (scattering) remains challenging due to multiple light‑scattering mechanisms at different length scales. Interfacial debonding, limited polymer accessibility in the cell wall, and refractive index (RI) mismatch between wood and polymer phases contribute to forward scattering and haze. Here we establish an optical design strategy to reduce haze/scattering in TW composites by suppressing scattering sources. Chemical modification through NaOH swelling and acetylation is employed to reduce optical defects, while the polymer phase is tailored by tuning the RI. A series of TW composites enables decoupling of different scattering mechanisms and analysis of their contributions through transmittance, haze, angular light‑distribution, and ultra-fast time resolved measurements. RI tuning combined with chemical reduction of interfacial optical defects leads to a strong decrease in haze (down to ~ 45% for a 1mm thick sample). A more isotropic transmitted light distribution confirms suppression of refraction-based scattering. The study provides a mechanism-based framework for designing low-haze TW and other cellulose-based optical composites.

papers.title: Site-Selective Gaussian Accelerated Molecular Dynamics and Its Integration with Replica-Exchange Methods
papers.abstract: We developed site-selective Gaussian accelerated molecular dynamics (ssGaMD), which selectively enhances molecular motions associated with a specified region or set of interactions. The method allows selected dihedral, electrostatic, and Lennard–Jones energy terms to be biased independently or in combination, while limiting direct biasing of the rest of the system. ssGaMD can be combined with replica-exchange umbrella sampling (ssGaREUS) or temperature replicaexchange molecular dynamics (ssGaREMD) to further enhance the sampling of association and dissociation processes and conformational changes. We implemented these methods in the GENESIS MD simulation software and applied them to aspirin binding to β-cyclodextrin, PP1 binding to Src kinase, and Trp-cage folding. Selectively boosting interactions involved in binding efficiently promoted molecular association and dissociation, while combining ssGaMD with replica-exchange methods accelerated the convergence of binding and folding free-energy landscapes. These methods offer a flexible approach to studying ligand binding and other biomolecular processes in which slow dynamics are governed by specific local interactions.

papers.title: Looking Beyond KD for Aptamer Validation: Disentangling Specific Aptamer Binding from Electrostatic Association for Basic Protein Targets
papers.abstract: Nucleic acid aptamers provide a simple, cost-effective alternative to antibodies for targeting biomolecular analytes from ions to large protein complexes. However, the interactions of these nucleic-acid based structures in vivo remains largely uncharacterized. Here, we report the seemingly pervasive electrostatic association between nucleic acids and high isoelectric point proteins under biological conditions. Such non-specific binding runs the risk of convoluting aptamer selection and validation, while also potentially interfering with nucleic acid-based nanotechnologies in vivo. Through our explorations, we identify several methods to disentangle sequence-specific aptamer interactions from non-specific electrostatic association, allowing for discrimination between binding modes. We also identify dissociation rate (koff) and equilibrium binding response (Req) as potentially better discriminators than KD for isolating and validating true sequence-specific aptamers.

papers.title: Enantiopure Telluronium Complexes through Bidentate Chalcogen Bonding: From Solid and in Solution Studies to Chiral Recognition
papers.abstract: This work demonstrates that tetravalent telluronium salts constitute versatile chalcogen bonding (ChB) receptors for polydentate phosphine oxide ligands. A range of bidentate phosphine oxides form highly stable 1:1 complexes with telluronium salt 1BArF in solution. Multinuclear NMR spectroscopy revealed that bidentate coordination occurs through simultaneous interaction of the two phosphine oxide groups with the telluronium centre, while variable-temperature experiments evidenced a dynamic ligand-exchange process involving the third accessible σ-hole. The formation of the enantiopure telluronium complex with (S)-BINAPO was further confirmed by ECD spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction, which highlighted the bidendate coordination mode while preserving one available σ-hole capable of binding an external Lewis base. Exploiting this remaining ChB donor site, host-guest complexes were formed with DMSO and a series of racemic chiral substrates. The resulting diastereomeric adducts produced clear NMR signal splitting, demonstrating the ability of these chiral telluronium complexes to discriminate between enantiomers through ChB.

papers.title: Enantiopure Telluronium Complexes through Bidentate Chalcogen Bonding: From Solid and in Solution Studies to Chiral Recognition
papers.abstract: This work demonstrates that tetravalent telluronium salts constitute versatile chalcogen bonding (ChB) receptors for polydentate phosphine oxide ligands. A range of bidentate phosphine oxides form highly stable 1:1 complexes with telluronium salt 1BArF in solution. Multinuclear NMR spectroscopy revealed that bidentate coordination occurs through simultaneous interaction of the two phosphine oxide groups with the telluronium centre, while variable-temperature experiments evidenced a dynamic ligand-exchange process involving the third accessible σ-hole. The formation of the enantiopure telluronium complex with (S)-BINAPO was further confirmed by ECD spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction, which highlighted the bidendate coordination mode while preserving one available σ-hole capable of binding an external Lewis base. Exploiting this remaining ChB donor site, host-guest complexes were formed with DMSO and a series of racemic chiral substrates. The resulting diastereomeric adducts produced clear NMR signal splitting, demonstrating the ability of these chiral telluronium complexes to discriminate between enantiomers through ChB.

papers.title: Mild acid promoted bromination with H2O2/NaBr at room temperature inspired by flavin-dependent halogenase (FDH)
papers.abstract: Bromination is an important and frequently used organic transformation. Many elegant and reliable bromination methods have been well established; however, limitations still exist, thus calling for more sustainable approaches with broader substrate scope, better selectivity, milder condition and lower cost. In this manuscript, an effective bromination method has been established utilizing low-toxic and cost-friendly carboxylic acid/NaBr/H2O2, including bromination of (hetero)arenes, decarboxylative bromination of (hetero)aryl/vinyl carboxylic acid, ipsohydroxylation-bromination of (hetero)aryl boronic acids/esters, hydroxybromination of alkyne/alkene, and 𝛼-bromination of ketone. Broad substrate scope, good functional group tolerance, operation-friendly procedure, moderate to excellent yields, and late-stage bromination of small molecule natural products and drugs have been achieved. The carboxylic acid was hypothesized to play dual roles as providing H-bond, proton donor and acceptor in this reaction. Compared many previously reported bromination methods, this method shows evidently better sustainability, and can serve as a useful synthetic tool for related research.

papers.title: Describing the Fluxional Dynamics of Sub-nanoscale Clusters with Markov State Modeling
papers.abstract: Fluxionality, or the population of and interconversion between multiple structures, has long been suggested to be relevant for understanding the physical and catalytic behavior of sub-nanoscale metal clusters on an oxide support. Much of this treatment has, however, been thermodynamic, neglecting direct exploration of the timescales for interconversion between di!erent isomers. Previously, we exploited machine-learned interatomic potentials, combined with automatic process exploration (MLIP-APE) to identify isomerization networks for MgO-supported Pd clusters, capturing all barriers for cluster restructuring. In the current work, we demonstrate a new analysis approach based on Markov State Modeling (MSM) which captures the complex contribution of multiple timescales on the overall fluxional dynamic behavior over a range of cluster sizes. This overall fluxional behavior can then be classified between the extremes of highly dynamic “labile” clusters, to “rigid” clusters which exhibit much less dynamic behavior. These dynamics are of particular interest when using fluxional clusters for catalysis, as these dynamics could influence the observed catalytic reactions. Ultimately, this work demonstrates a rigorous and general approach to investigate the dynamics of reaction networks of well-defined states.

papers.title: Thioethers as alkyl donors in electrochemical C–O and C–N bond forming reactions
papers.abstract: A catalyst- and fluoride-free electrochemical method for the use of readily available thioethers as alkyl donors in C-O and C-N bond formation to furnish ethers, esters, and N-alkylated products is reported. The protocol exhibits broad functional group tolerance and is compatible with structurally complex substrates. Cyclic voltammetry studies rationalize the distinct behaviour of oxygen and nitrogen nucleophiles and guide the optimization of the electrochemical conditions, enabling the formation of coupled products from starting materials with both matched and mismatched redox potentials.

papers.title: Cold Plasma Induced 3D Printing of Hydrogels
papers.abstract: Control over when and where gelation occurs is central to the fabrication of structured soft materials, yet most approaches rely on chemical additives or uniform bulk triggers. Here, we show that cold plasma provides an external, reagent-free route to spatial and temporal control over gelation in low molecular weight hydrogel systems. Plasma exposure induces a localised decrease in pH at the plasma–liquid interface, triggering self-assembly and gel formation only in the treated region. This external plasma-induced self-assembly method enables direct writing of gel features from precursor solutions without embedded triggers, construction of three-dimensional architectures, and control over local mechanical properties through plasma dose. Our approach also allows simultaneous formation of metal nanoparticles within gels, yielding spatially confined composite and catalytic soft materials.

papers.title: Nanoscale Phase Engineering and Magnetic Property Enhancement in High-Entropy Alloy Nanoparticles by Continuous Microparticle Laser Fragmentation in Liquid
papers.abstract: High-entropy alloy nanoparticles (HEA NPs) offer compositional and structural tunability for applications, like water splitting, H2O2 production, or magnetocaloric technologies. Therefore, the interplay between composition, structure, and functionality is of significant interest for materials´ functionality optimization. Microparticle laser fragmentation in liquid flow (MP-LFL) is an emerging scalable method for nanoalloy production, but remains underexplored for HEA NPs. Here, we investigate CrFeCoNiX (X = Ga, Cu, Mo) HEA NPs fabricated by MP-LFL in ethanol and examine how compositional variations affect elemental homogeneity, size, phase structure, and magnetic properties. Microscopy, diffraction, size analysis, and magnetometry reveal particle sizes of 6-7 nm and pronounced differences in phase structures, ranging from single-phase fcc and biphasic fcc/bcc to amorphous structures, partially contrasting the initial feedstock microparticle structures. The low saturation magnetization (Ms, 310 K) of the as-synthesized superparamagnetic NPs increases strongly after in situ annealing by approximately 4-, 3-, or 24-fold for Ga-, Cu-, and Mo-containing NPs, respectively, coinciding with structural and elemental rearrangements. In contrast, the feedstock microparticles show no comparable increase, highlighting the role of the initial phase constitution in determining magnetic properties. Moreover, MP-LFL enables production of ~0.4 g h-1, with a record picosecond MP-LFL mass yield of ~60%, leaving room for further optimization and high throughput.

papers.title: Ring Opening of Oxiranes with Amines Using Iodolium Salts as XB-Precatalysts
papers.abstract: Herein, we report the nucleophilic ring-opening of oxiranes with substituted amines using N-heterocycle-substituted iodolium salts (NHISs) as Lewis acid pre-catalysts. Using the ring-opening of styrene oxide by aniline as a model reaction, we demonstrate that NHISs enable efficient β-aminoalcohol formation at room temperature and with pre-catalyst loadings as low as 2.5 mol%. The optimized protocol was successfully applied to a broad range of substituted oxiranes and amines, affording the corresponding β-aminoalcohols in isolated yields of up to 98%. Based on control experiments and recent literature examples, we show that the iodolium salt is not a simple spectator but, under the reaction conditions, undergoes an amine-induced intramolecular aryl–aryl coupling to generate an electron-deficient iodoarene and an ammonium borate salt in situ. On this basis, we propose a dual activation mechanism in which halogen-bond (XB) donor activation of the epoxide operates in concert with an in situ generated β-hydroxyammonium co-catalyst.

papers.title: Molybdenum and Tungsten Dinitrogen Complexes Supported by Modified pentaPod Ligands: Implications on the Activation of N2 and its Conversion to NH3
papers.abstract: The pentaPod (pentadentate tetrapodal phosphine) ligand P5R with PMe2 or phospholane (Pln) donors offers the opportunity to investigate how small changes in the ligand framework affect the properties of the corresponding transition-metal complexes. Here, we examine the influence of replacing the propyl with ethyl groups in the trident part of the pentaPod ligand with regard to N2 activation as well as N2-to-NH3 conversion by the corresponding Mo(0)N2 and W(0)N2 complexes. A comparison of the DFT-optimized structures of the original P5R and the shortened etP5R pentaPod complexes reveals important structural differences that influence N2 activation. The geometric and electronic structure results obtained from DFT are checked by comprehensive spectroscopic and electrochemical studies of the new etP5R-supported molybdenum and tungsten systems as well as through an investigation of their ability to (catalytically) generate NH3.

papers.title: Central Atom Driven Modulation of Electron Transfer in Alkyne-Protected Ag <sub>14</sub> Nanoclusters
papers.abstract: Single-atom doping at the cluster core is an effective strategy for modulating the molecule-like properties of monolayer-protected nanoclusters. In this study, we systematically synthesized a pair of alkyne-protected silver nanoclusters, in which the central template anion of one nanocluster was replaced by a copper atom in the other. Incorporation of copper significantly quenched the photoluminescence of the nanocluster while enhancing its electron-transfer capability through modification of the electronic structure. Theoretical calculations further revealed that the central copper atom contributes directly to the frontier molecular orbitals. This work represents an important step toward the development of atomically precise nanochemistry, demonstrating how precise structural tailoring of alkyne-protected silver nanoclusters can be used to regulate their functional properties.

papers.title: How to tame your bromine: bandgap tuning of solvent-free hybrid perovskites in a vapor transport deposition process
papers.abstract: We present a sequential physical vapor and gas phase transport deposition process for batchcapable formation of metal halide perovskite films, applicable to single- and multi-junction solar cells. After evaporating porous Cs-containing Pb halides via physical vapor deposition onto the substrate or bottom cell, we use a quartz furnace to deposit the organic precursor, formamidinium iodide (FAI), onto this inorganic scaffold via vapor transport deposition. Ammonia is used as carrier gas to prevent decomposition of FAI. The resulting perovskite is already present in the photoactive alpha phase. The process time can be minimized down to 15 min, depending on the scaffold, as no subsequent annealing is required. Notably all contacting layers in this work, including self-assembled molecules and passivation, are also fabricated with solvent-free processes. We note an occurring halide exchange reaction between the FAI in vapor phase and Br in the scaffold and present a proposed reaction scheme. By utilizing this reaction, we can vary the resulting bandgap of the perovskite to fit to the requirements for tandem applications, showing a broad process window. The resulting champion cell (1.66 eV) created with this approach reaches 18.3% power conversion efficiency, with a photoluminescence quantum yield of 1.6 % on full cell stacks.

papers.title: Compartmentalized Microgels with Programmed Acoustic Anisotropy for Orthogonal Ultrasound-Triggered Motion and Cargo Release
papers.abstract: Compartmentalization is a fundamental organizational principle in nature, enabling anisotropy required for controlled locomotion and spatiotemporal regulation of biological processes. Inspired by this principle, we present a one-step strategy to fabricate compartmentalized anisotropic microgels via liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) in aqueous droplets. Upon sodium chloride addition, concentrated N-isopropylacrylamide (NIPAAm) solutions spontaneously separate into NIPAAm-rich and NIPAAm-poor phases. Integrating this process into microfluidic droplets followed by photopolymerization enables continuous fabrication of anisotropic PNIPAAm microgels with two compartments of distinct stiffness. Synthetic and biological macromolecules can be selectively loaded into different compartments according to their polarity. Crucially, LLPS-generated acoustic contrast enables two independently addressable functionalities under biocompatible ultrasound (US).
