Lowfrequency, low-intensity US induces propulsion at speeds of approximately 10 microgel diameters per second without cargo release, whereas high-frequency, higher-intensity US at biocompatible settings selectively degrades one compartment, enabling on-demand cargo release. Complementary computer simulations further elucidate the physical mechanisms underlying acoustically driven motion. This work establishes LLPS-driven compartmentalization as a design principle for multifunctional colloidal microrobots with independently programmable propulsion and cargo release, opening new avenues for targeted drug delivery and soft robotics.

papers.title: Genome Mining-Guided Discovery of Polyketide-Tropolone Hybrids Reveals Their Biosynthetic Logic and Antitumor Activity
papers.abstract: 2 ABSTRACT: Tropolone-containing natural products display diverse biological activities, yet characterized fungal tropolone hybrids are dominated by sesquiterpene-derived systems, leaving polyketide-tropolone hybridization largely unexplored. Here, genome mining guided by conserved tropolone biosynthetic enzymes and an unusual dual-polyketide synthase architecture led to the discovery of fusariolones A–E and semifusariolone A from Fusarium sp. WA57, defining a distinct family of fungal polyketide-tropolone hybrids. Heterologous pathway reconstitution supported fusABCDEF as the minimal gene set for scaffold assembly and revealed a biosynthetic logic in which a canonical tropolone pathway converges with a highly reducing polyketide synthase. The resulting linear pentaene hydrocarbon represents, to the best of our knowledge, the first such intermediate identified in fungal natural product biosynthesis and supports a proposed FusF-mediated dehydration/hetero-Diels-Alder cascade in scaffold construction. Fusariolone A displayed low-nanomolar antiproliferative activity with pronounced selectivity toward K562 and HT-29 cells. In HT-29 cells, it suppressed DNA synthesis, altered cell cycle progression, and increased apoptosis, while also reducing xenograftassociated fluorescence in zebrafish. Together, these findings establish a distinct biosynthetic strategy for polyketide-tropolone hybrid assembly and expand the chemical and functional space of fungal tropolone natural products.

papers.title: RetroMol: Knowledge Distillation of Energy-Based Retrosynthesis Models
papers.abstract: Retrosynthesis prediction is a central task in computer-aided synthesis planning, and synthesizability remains a persistent bottleneck in AI-driven molecular and materials discovery. We introduce RetroMol, a family of compact text-based models that transfers an energy-based critic’s ranking of candidate reactant sets into the generator itself. RetroBase, an 11M-parameter transformer encoderdecoder trained on two-reactant USPTO reactions, achieves Top-1 and Top-5 accuracies of 46.8% and 67.8% on a held-out test split. RetroERM, an energybased model over molecular fingerprint counts, scores RetroBase’s candidates, and its ranking preferences are distilled back into the generator. The distilled model, RetroDistil, reaches 52.6% Top-1 and 73.5% Top-5 under identical data and evaluation, improving on RetroBase by 5.7–6.8 points at Top-1/3/5 with no reranking stage at inference and no increase in model size. Distilling a critic is therefore a practical way to improve a compact retrosynthesis generator without larger or more complicated architectures.

papers.title: TAPERSS-MoCa: A Physics-Based Monte Carlo Framework for 3D RNA Structure Prediction from Sequence
papers.abstract: Ribonucleic acid (RNA) function is intrinsically linked to its three-dimensional architecture, yet experimental structure determination remains challenging. Here, we introduce TAPERSS-MoCa (Theoretical Analyses, Prediction, and Evaluation of RNA Structures from Sequence using a Monte-Carlo Simulator), a physics-based fragment assembly framework for predicting RNA tertiary structures directly from sequence. By utilizing a novel fragment library grounded in dinucleoside monophosphate (DNMP) energetics parameterized via Discrete Path Sampling (DPS), TAPERSS-MoCa efficiently samples low-energy conformational landscapes. Evaluated across 6-, 10-, and 12-nucleotide RNA test sets, TAPERSS-MoCa consistently recovers native-like global minima with canonical Watson–Crick base pairs adopting near-planar geometry. By combining dinucleoside fragment energetics with an angularly constrained hydrogen-bonding potential, TAPERSS-MoCa accurately captures A-form structures in 6-nucleotide linear RNAs, outperforming traditional fragment-assembly algorithms that frequently misfold these flexible sequences. Thermodynamic evaluations based on ensemble partition functions (Δ G folding ) and macrostate basin free energies (Δ F folding ) demonstrate strong predictive performance for rigid, well-stacked GNRA tetraloops. Furthermore, TAPERSS-MoCa systematically reproduces key physical stability trends predicted by empirical nearest-neighbor models. This physics-based approach provides a robust platform for structural prediction and thermodynamic profiling of short RNA motifs, supporting RNA-targeted drug discovery and functional design.

papers.title: Programmable Formic Acid Decomposition in Flow on an Interdigitated Internal Catalytic Condenser Beyond the Sabatier Limit
Breaking the Potency Barrier: A Practical Recipe for QSAR Extrapolation
papers.abstract: Predicting compounds that are more potent than those represented in the training data remains a difficult and practically important problem for quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) modeling. This challenge is particularly relevant during lead optimization, where the goal is to design or identify analogs that are more potent than compounds already measured. To address this problem, we developed a new Pairwise-Difference QSAR (PD-QSAR) approach that learns changes in biological activity from differences in molecular descriptors between compound pairs. We evaluated three strategies for aggregating the resulting PD-QSAR predictions: mean aggregation, k-nearest-neighbor aggregation (k = 3), and 10% quantile aggregation, and compared their performance with Direct QSAR and Chemprop using a benchmark derived from publicly available ChEMBL 35 data. The primary benchmark included 103 human single-protein target datasets, comprising 33,707 activity records. For each target, the 10% most potent activity records were withheld for external validation. Among the approaches evaluated, 10% quantile aggregation provided the lowest median external validation RMSE (0.518) and outperformed mean and kNN aggregation on external validation RMSE for 100 of 103 targets, Direct QSAR for 102 targets, and Chemprop for 94 targets. These results support PD-QSAR with quantile aggregation as a useful strategy for prioritizing analogs expected to extend beyond the potency range represented by previously measured compounds.

papers.title: Machine Learning Identifies an Information-Sufficiency Regime for Critical-Mineral Recovery
papers.abstract: The recovery of critical minerals from spent lithium-ion batteries is governed by coupled feedstock chemistry, solvent composition, and processing conditions, yet heterogeneous experimental reporting makes it difficult to determine which information is essential for reliable prediction across heterogeneous experimental systems. Here, using deep eutectic solvent-based recovery as a representative resource recovery platform, we curate 814 experimental observations from 38 publications and develop an interpretable machine learning framework to identify an informationsufficiency regime. Five descriptors, including temperature, electrode material type, leaching time, target metal, and hydrogen-bond donor identity, retain 98.3% of the predictive performance of the full 13-descriptor model while reducing the descriptor space by 61.5%. Reducing the representation from five to four descriptors causes a pronounced performance loss, whereas adding a sixth provides negligible additional benefit. Descriptor removal and domain ablation analyses further show that temperature and target metal identity contain the least replaceable predictive information, while material identity, solvent chemistry, and processing conditions provide complementary information. These results identify a compact, chemically structured information core for critical-mineral recovery and provide a quantitative basis for prioritizing experimental measurements, improving cross-study data consistency, and developing more transferable datadriven frameworks for battery resource recovery.

papers.title: Methodology for Fabricating and Testing Carbon Molecular Sieve (CMS) Dense Film Membranes for Reproducible Permeation Experiments
papers.abstract: Carbon molecular sieve (CMS) membranes are promising for demanding gas separations, but their brittleness after pyrolysis makes dense-film permeation testing difficult and often irreproducible. Membranes that appear defect-free after pyrolysis can crack during handling, masking, permeation cell assembly, vacuum evacuation or gas pressurization. This work presents a practical procedure for fabricating and testing CMS dense films prepared from fluorinated polyimide-based CMS membranes. We investigated several experimental factors such as polymer concentration, membrane casting in glove bag, epoxy selection, filter paper support, masking and pressure loading, and their resulting impact on the mechanical stability of the membranes Careful control of these steps reduced or entirely mitigated film cracking, gas bypass during testing, and epoxy seal failure during permeation measurements. This study provides a reliable method for casting, masking and testing of fragile CMS dense film membranes and addresses practical details that are often not reported, but are important for successful and reproducible gas permeation data with CMS membranes.

papers.title: Photocatalytic dehydrogenation enables divergent access to functional polyolefins
papers.abstract: Polyolefins are among the most widely used plastics, yet their chemically inert hydrocarbon backbones severely limit opportunities for chemical modification and value-added reuse. Introducing carbon–carbon double bonds offers a powerful way to transform these otherwise unreactive materials into versatile intermediates for downstream chemistry. Here we report an acceptorless photocatalytic/cobalt-catalyzed dehydrogenation that operates across a broad range of polyethylene- and polypropylene-based materials, including post-consumer plastics. Notably, polypropylene undergoes dehydrogenation with near-exclusive selectivity for terminal alkene formation. The resulting unsaturated polyolefins serve as versatile platforms for diverse transformations, enabling access to functionalized polyolefins, telechelic polyethylene, as well as block and graft copolymers. These products further demonstrate utility as compatibilizers for immiscible polymer blends and as strong adhesive materials. By converting inert C–H backbones into chemically addressable alkene-containing polymers, this strategy transforms commodity polyolefins into diverse polymer architectures with practical functions.

papers.title: High-Resolution MRT-TOF Mass Spectrometry Enables Simultaneous Carbon and Nitrogen Tracing in Stable Isotope Resolved Metabolomics
papers.abstract: Stable isotope-resolved metabolomics (SIRM) using dual-isotope tracers, such as [U- 13 C 5 , 15 N 2 ]glutamine, provides complementary insight into carbon and nitrogen metabolism and their integration across interconnected metabolic pathways. However, distinguishing closely spaced 13 C- and 15 N-containing isotopologues requires resolving power that conventional quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometers (QTOF MS) may not provide. In this study, we evaluated the performance of a multi-reflecting time-of-flight (MRT) mass spectrometer for dual-isotope SIRM using [U- 13 C 5 , 15 N 2 ]glutamine-infused patient-derived tumor xenografts and compared its performance with that of a conventional SYNAPT™ XS QTOF Platform operated at a resolving power of approximately 15,000. A total of 113 metabolites were detected on both platforms, and dual-isotope labeling patterns were evaluated for 29 carbon- and nitrogen-containing metabolites. The Xevo™ MRT Mass Spectrometer, operating at a resolving power of approximately 100,000, resolved closely spaced 13 C- and 15 N isotopologues that remained unresolved on the SYNAPT™ XS Instrument under the acquisition conditions used. This separation enabled composition-specific isotopologue assignment, independent peak integration, natural-abundance correction, and isotopologue-specific fractional-enrichment analysis. The higher sensitivity of Xevo™ MRT Mass Spectrometer improved detection of low-abundance isotopologues, increasing isotopologue coverage when compared to SYNAPT™ XS MS Instrument. Together, these results demonstrate that MRT-TOF mass spectrometry provides a practical high-resolution platform for dual-isotope SIRM and enables simultaneous assessment of carbon incorporation and nitrogen-transfer reactions within a single experiment.

papers.title: Confinement-Controlled Cluster Percolation Shifts the Widom Crossover in Supercritical Methane
papers.abstract: Supercritical fluids undergo significant structural and dynamic changes near the Widom line, which separates gas-like and liquid-like regimes. These phenomena are well understood for bulk fluids, but their evolution under nanoscale confinement remains poorly understood. Using a Grand Canonical Monte Carlo and Molecular Dynamics simulation framework, we show that confinement of supercritical CH4 in clay slit nanopores shifts the Widom crossover to lower pressures, with the shift increasing as pore size decreases. Energy-based cluster analysis reveals that this shift is associated with the emergence of system-spanning molecular clusters. Confinement promotes the percolation of these clusters at lower pressures, extending liquid-like behaviour into regimes that are gas-like under bulk conditions. The crossover is also reflected in transport properties as an inflection in both the effective mean distance between free molecules and clusters and the molecular diffusion coefficient. These results establish a direct link between confinement-controlled cluster percolation and the Widom crossover.

papers.title: An Annotation Consistency Checker for Evidence-Based Evaluation of Untargeted LC-MS/MS Metabolite Annotations
papers.abstract: Untargeted LC-MS/MS metabolomics routinely produces complex annotation landscapes in which individual spectra can yield multiple candidate metabolite annotations. Although spectral similarity provides an essential foundation for library-based annotation, determining whether a candidate annotation is consistent with the available evidence and whether alternative explanations remain plausible requires integration of multiple lines of evidence. In current practice, this evaluation is largely embedded in expert judgment, making annotation review difficult to teach, standardize, and reproduce. Here, we introduce an annotation consistency checker that aids this expert review process by generating a user-inspectable report for spectral library matches. The framework integrates complementary evidence dimensions, including spectral agreement, structural relationships among candidate annotations, and competing library matches to highlight annotations that are supported by, or inconsistent with, the available data. Biological context is provided separately to aid interpretation of metabolite occurrence across organisms, tissues, and sample types but is not incorporated into the annotation score. By enabling systematic evaluation of multiple evidence streams, this approach provides a transparent workflow that helps users critically assess metabolite annotations, reduce overinterpretation of spectral matches, and make informed decisions beyond only accepting the top-ranked library match.

papers.title: Growth-Triggered Nano-vesicle Budding via Leaflet Area Asymmetry in Fatty-Acid Protocells
papers.abstract: CORRECTION NOTICE (version 2). Three results reported in version 1 do not survive a more careful treatment of the bud geometry, and a one-page correction notice has been prepended to the document; the original text follows it unaltered. (1) The self-consistency condition x_extra = 0 of Sec. 2.3 describes a bud drawn from the outer leaflet alone. A closed vesicle has two leaflets, and matching the removed areas to those of a closed spherical bud fixes x_extra at about -2 for every radius between 60 nm and 1 micrometre, so no non-negative value is admissible. (2) The predicted bud radius of 60-90 nm therefore does not follow. It came from equating the excess outer-leaflet area with the bud's total area; a closed bud instead withdraws 8 pi h r of area difference, giving r = R x Delta a_c, which is 500 nm to 1 micrometre for a parent of 1 micrometre. The corrected behaviour is growth followed by division-scale budding rather than sustained growth punctuated by nano-shedding. (3) The reduced imbalance Delta a used here counts the excess accumulated during growth, whereas the O(1) criterion quoted from the area-difference-elasticity literature is stated in the normalisation where a sphere already carries unit reduced area difference; the two are related by Delta a_ADE = 1 + Delta a. The kinetic scheme and its steady state are unaffected, as is the qualitative prediction that shed vesicles are enriched in recently inserted material. Derivations are given in doi:10.26434/chemrxiv.15010117/v3. ORIGINAL ABSTRACT (version 1). Fatty-acid vesicles growing by monomer uptake, as demonstrated experimentally for Szostak-type protocells, insert new amphiphiles predominantly into the outer leaflet. Because transbilayer flip-flop is not instantaneous, this generates a growing area mismatch between the two leaflets. We show, using the area-difference-elasticity (ADE) framework for vesicle shape, that this mismatch crosses a threshold beyond which the vesicle relieves it by shedding small, high-curvature nano-vesicles rather than by symmetric division – with no external mechanical forcing required. A leaflet-resolved kinetic model shows that sustained parent growth over many such cycles requires the shed nano-vesicles to be compositionally enriched in the destabilizing (outer-leaflet) material rather than ordinary bilayer: a specific, falsifiable prediction. For illustrative growth and flip-flop rates the model predicts nano-vesicles of radius 60–90 nm, above the stability floor of fatty-acid vesicles. This mechanism, and its central prediction, match independent experimental observations on fatty-acid and lysolipid-containing vesicles. In an earlier work [1] we explored periodic environmental mechanical forcing (tidal, geyser and vortex-driven shear) as an alternative trigger for vesicle instability; that mechanism rests on poorly constrained assumptions about Hadean orbital dynamics and produces, in its simplest form, no resonance, only a low-pass response. The present mechanism requires no assumption about the early Earth’s mechanical environment at all.

papers.title: Directional Electric Fields at Designed MOF Sites: Implications for Electrostatic Preorganization and Catalysis
papers.abstract: Enzymes achieve their enormous catalytic power in part through electrostatic preorganization: non-covalent interactions arrange an electric field that is preorganized to stabilize the change in dipole moment between a reaction's ground and transition states. Thus, the catalytic relevance of an electric field depends not only on its magnitude but also on its orientation. Here we use the enforced rigidity of a metal–organic framework (MOF), PCN-521, to demonstrate this orientation dependence directly. We introduce an aldehyde carbonyl vibrational Stark probe in situ, first as a protected ketal, then deprotect it to reveal a carbonyl at the same node-capping site as a previously reported nitrile probe, extending field measurements to a field reporter of greater relevance to enzymatic catalysis. Electric field- vibrational frequency calibrated probes using the vibrational Stark effect report a trifluoroacetate field donor that projects nearly its full destabilizing field onto the collinear nitrile (sp, C≡N) but only a fraction onto the off-axis aldehyde (sp2, C=O) — a geometric effect. Because the framework's non-covalent contacts, unlike an enzyme active site's, cannot reorganize, this controlled, single-site comparison isolates alignment from magnitude. While electric fields are often invoked to explain observations near electrodes or droplet interfaces, these results show the importance of alignment which is often neglected.

papers.title: The Regularized Frozen Natural Orbital approach to CASPT2: extension to Restricted Active Space wave functions, different multiplicities and assessment of correlation effects
papers.abstract: The frozen natural orbital (FNO) method is a well-known approximation that significantly reduces the cost of many-body perturbation theory treatments for obtaining correlation energies in a systematic and controlled manner, enabling the simulation of larger and more realistic molecular systems. Here, we implement FNO on top of restricted active-space self-consistent field (RASSCF) wave function within second-order perturbation theory, leading to the FNO-RASPT2 method. To account for the additional approximations incurred when using restricted RASSCF wave functions, as well as to apply it to states of different molecular charge and spin multiplicity, we introduce a regularisation approach via a level-shift in the orbital deletion procedure, which helps avoid singularities resulting from vanishing denominators due to the reduced occupation of restricted (active) virtual orbitals and that we show does not significantly influence the final energies obtained. Numerical results on vertical excitation energies showcase the FNO to be up to ∼3.5 faster than the parent computation while retaining ∼95% of the dynamic correlation energy and being within 0.1 eV of the reference calculation, with the CASPT2 equations-the main bottleneck in large molecular systems-registering over an order of magnitude speed-up. An in-depth analysis shows the regularized FNO approach to retain electron correlation appropriately for internal and semi-internal contributions, while displaying larger deviations for the external term, which originates from the initial FNO truncation based on an approximated one-electron reduced density matrix. Ongoing efforts are directed towards improving and extending our current implementation to the calculation of analytic gradients and non-adiabatic couplings to enable faster non-adiabatic molecular dynamics simulations in larger and more realistic molecular systems.

papers.title: Accelerating the deployment of nitrogen diversion and recovery technologies in water resource recovery facilities
papers.abstract: Nitrogen recovery from human excreta is advancing rapidly at the laboratory scale, yet its potential in full-scale water resource recovery facilities (WRRFs) remains unrealized. To expedite the deployment of nitrogen recovery technology across diverse WRRF configurations, an agile and standardized framework is needed to predict plant-wide operational impacts and prioritize deployment pathways. Here, we developed and applied an open-source benchmarking framework comprising 18 representative WRRF configurations to evaluate three early-stage nitrogen recovery upgrades – upstream urine diversion (UD), mainstream hydrogel adsorption (HA), and sidestream electrochemical stripping (ECS). WRRFs’ operational performance is configuration-dependent: biological nutrient removal configurations, particularly the Johannesburg process and modified Bardenpho membrane bioreactor with anaerobic digestion, exhibit the largest operating expenditure savings for WRRFs across all three upgrades. Approaches that recover >40% of total nitrogen (UD covering 100% served population, or 100% UD, and HA) from the influent can reduce OPEX by 31% to 56%, whereas lower recovery (10% UD and ECS) still reduce OPEX by 10% to 15%. Together, these results identify promising deployment pathways for early-stage nitrogen recovery technologies and provide a scalable approach for evaluating other resource recovery upgrades.

papers.title: Correlative Analysis of Individual Suspended Photocatalyst Particles Enabled by Optical Particle Trapping with Electrochemical Sensing
papers.abstract: In particulate photocatalysis, typical experiments involve billions to trillions of particles that possess highly heterogeneous properties, making it difficult to uncover mechanisms and structure-property relationships at the single-particle level. Additionally, existing single-particle measurement techniques become limited by the need to anchor particles to substrates and lack the ability to control interparticle spacing and interactions. Herein, we describe a multi-modal technique called optical particle trapping with electrochemical sensing (OPTECS), whereby the distributions of product generation rates from fully wetted, individual photocatalyst particles are measured using microelectrode sensors while simultaneously recording their luminescent characteristics. Using doped bismuth vanadate and strontium titanate as model particulate photocatalysts towards overall water splitting, OPTECS is used to reveal (i) hidden correlations between single particle luminescence intensity and photoactivity, and (ii) the presence of optically stimulated electrochemiluminescence (OSECL), which is leveraged to quantify rates of undesired back reactions, a key loss mechanism in particulate photocatalysis.

papers.title: Surface-Confined Steric Frustration Directs One-Dimensional BisNHC Assembly
papers.abstract: Sterically demanding ligands are widely used to control coordination geometry and stabilize otherwise inaccessible metal complexes, yet how steric repulsion influences metal–ligand coordination and periodic molecular assembly under surface confinement remains underexplored. Here, we show that a tert -butyl-substituted bis(N-heterocyclic carbene) (bisNHC) assembles into a one-dimensional metal-organic lattice. Steric constraints give rise to an asymmetric NHC–adatom–NHC arrangement, generating dipolar bisNHC–adatom units whose dipole-dipole interactions contribute to their organization into periodic chains. The lattice decomposes upon mild annealing, showing that direct deposition of the free bisNHC is essential for preserving this coordination motif. Despite chemisorption through metal adatoms, the lattice exhibits reduced electronic coupling to the substrate. It also defines sterically protected cavities for individual metal atoms. Lanthanide atoms accommodated within these cavities show higher-energy spin-flip excitations and enhanced positive-bias stability compared with graphene-supported atoms. These findings demonstrate that steric congestion under surface confinement can prevent conventional covalent chain formation without precluding periodic metal–organic assembly. This approach offers a strategy for constructing ordered molecular architectures with tailored coordination sites for individual metal atoms.

papers.title: Iridium-Catalyzed Regio- and Enantioselective Hydroamination of Allenes: Direct Access to α-Tertiary Chiral Allylic Amines
papers.abstract: We disclose a highly regio- and enantioselective Ir(I)-catalyzed hydroamination of 1,1-disubstituted allenes, providing a broadly applicable access to α-tertiary chiral allylic amines, very relevant structural motifs that are mostly inaccessible through other enantioselective strategies. The method employs an a-aminopyridine as nucleophile, and displays a broad substrate scope, accommodating both aryl- and alkyl-substituted allenes. Removal of the pyridine moiety of the products yields synthetically challenging primary allylic amines bearing α-tetrasubstituted stereocenters. Notably, addition of i -PrOH after completion of the hydroamination enables an in situ transfer hydrogenation of the generated alkene to deliver the corresponding a-tertiary saturated amines with equally high selectivities. The use of trisubstituted allenes in the hydroamination protocol is also feasible, affording in this case a-secondary allylic amines, also with high selectivities. Finally, experimental and computational mechanistic studies support a hydrometalation/C–N bond-forming sequence as the preferred reaction pathway, with the C-N reductive elimination step identified as enantio- and TOF-determining.

papers.title: Electrochemical Reduction of Acetonitrile to Gaseous C2 Products and Implications for Small Molecule Transformations
papers.abstract: Acetonitrile (CH3CN) is a polar aprotic solvent that is widely used in electrochemistry due to its large dielectric constant, strong ability to solubilize numerous substrates and catalysts, and stability under a wide range of applied potentials. In the context of electrocatalysis, reaction rates and product selectivities can differ markedly in CH3CN relative to other solvents, but the possibility of solvent reduction remains poorly explored. Herein, we report that CH3CN is reduced electrochemically in the presence of organic acids to form ethylene, ethane, ethylamine and ammonia. To our knowledge, this study constitutes the first report of electrochemical acetonitrile reduction to ethylene and the first molecular system to generate ethane. These reactions are catalyzed by iron tetraphenylporphyrins but also occur on plain glassy carbon electrodes, highlighting the generality of this reduction to a variety of other catalyst systems. Isotopic labelling coupled with high‐resolution gas chromatography-mass spectrometry shows that CH3CN is the source of ethylene and ethane and offers insights into plausible mechanistic pathways. Because the observed hydrocarbons and amines are also desired products of CO2 or N2 reduction or C‒N coupling reactions, these observations motivate increased scrutiny as to the origin of unusual reduction products when electrocatalytic reactions are performed in CH3CN.

papers.title: Harvesting photosynthetic reducing power stored
Imaging of ultrafast electronic and chemical dynamics in biological systems
papers.abstract: Ultrafast electron microscopy (UEM) has enabled real-space visualization of dynamics in inorganic nanomaterials on fundamental timescales, but its application to functional biological nanostructures remains largely unexplored. Here, we use time-resolved UEM and electron energyloss spectroscopy (EELS) to probe the photoinduced electronic response and the light-induced chemical modification of the conductive periplasmic nanofiber network extracted from filamentous cable bacteria. Low-loss EELS reveals a feature at 3.6 eV, assigned to π→π* excitations, that is absent in non-conductive bacterial controls. Upon femtosecond near-infrared excitation (800 nm, 4.8 mJ cm−2), the spectral weights of this π feature and of the collective valence excitation at 23.1 eV decrease by ~10% and ~8%, respectively, within the first ~2 ps and largely recover within a few picoseconds, leaving a small long-lived component. A comparison with the expected photothermal response indicates that this transient is dominated by electronic excitation. Power-dependent core-loss EELS and elemental mapping under quasi-continuous illumination show that cumulative exposure irreversibly depletes nitrogen and oxygen, relatively enriches sp2bonded carbon and causes partial mass loss, while the outline of the nanofiber network is preserved. These results establish time-resolved EELS as a probe of the electronic photoresponse and photostability of biological conductors, and show how transient electronic and cumulative chemical light-induced effects can be distinguished in such systems.

papers.title: Off-the-Shelf ReaxFF Parameter Sets Underestimate O–O Bond Strengths in Organic Peroxides: A Static and Kinetic Benchmark for Thermal-Hazard Assessment
papers.abstract: ReaxFF reactive molecular dynamics (MD) is increasingly used to study organic peroxide decomposition, although the parameter sets supplied with common MD codes were developed for other chemistries. We benchmarked the six C/H/O ReaxFF parameter sets distributed with LAMMPS against CBS-APNO O–O bond dissociation enthalpies (BDEs) of 13 peroxides and tested whether the static error carries over to the kinetics. All six sets underestimate the O–O BDE (mean signed errors of −11.9 to −30.5 kcal mol-1) and correlate only weakly with the references (r = 0.14–0.50). The newer CHO-2016 set (not distributed with LAMMPS) gives −19.5 kcal mol-1, whereas the same protocol yields 85–90 kcal mol-1 for the ethane C–C bond (experiment, about 90 kcal mol-1). The errors increase with alkyl and acyl substitution. For di-tert-butyl peroxide (DTBP), the sets predict 0.4–16.7 instead of 42.4 kcal mol-1, four of them stretch the O–O bond to 1.68–1.76 Å, and a fifth breaks it. Isothermal MD of DTBP at 575–1480 K with three sets gave activation energies of 45.0–76.5 kJ mol-1, consistent with each set’s static BDE (48.7–69.9 kJ mol-1) but 2.0–3.4 times lower than the experimental 153 kJ mol-1. At 121 °C, the extrapolated rate constants exceed manufacturer data by factors of 3.4 × 108 to 5.0 × 1012, and the predicted 10 h half-life temperatures (−147 to −59 °C) lie 180–270 °C below the measured 121 °C. Calculating the O–O BDE of the target peroxide is therefore a simple but necessary check before using a ReaxFF parameter set for hazard assessment.

papers.title: Structure-Based Virtual Screening of Enantia chlorantha Stem Bark Constituents Reveals Candidate Pancreatic Alpha-Amylase Inhibitors
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) remains a major global health burden, and inhibition of pancreatic alpha-amylase is an established strategy for limiting postprandial hyperglycaemia. Enantia chlorantha stem bark is widely used in Nigerian ethnomedicine, but its alpha-amylase-inhibitory phytoconstituents have not been characterised at the molecular level. This study applied structure-based computational screening to identify candidate alpha-amylase inhibitors from E. chlorantha stem bark, using a previously reported GC-MS phytochemical profile of a carbonated stem-bark extract as the source of the screened ligand library. The GC-MS-identified constituents were docked against human pancreatic alpha-amylase (PDB ID: 1B2Y) using Glide, followed by induced fit docking (IFD) of the top-ranked hits and ADMET prediction (SwissADME, ProTox-III). Neoisolongifolene-8-ol emerged as the most promising hit, with a docking score of −6.201 kcal/mol. To assess the physical plausibility of this predicted interaction, a 10 ns all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulation of the enzyme–Neoisolongifolene-8-ol complex was performed in GROMACS 2024.5 with the CHARMM36m force field. The complex remained conformationally stable throughout the simulation (mean backbone RMSD = 1.17 ± 0.13 Å; mean radius of gyration = 2.352 ± 0.008 nm), with a well-maintained intramolecular hydrogen-bonding network (384.8 ± 8.7 bonds) and narrow solvent-accessible surface area fluctuation (201.5 ± 2.4 nm2). The ligand hydroxyl group formed a persistent hydrogen bond with the active-site residue His305, and principal component analysis indicated smooth, non-oscillatory conformational sampling consistent with a stable binding mode. These findings provide converging docking- and dynamics-level evidence that Neoisolongifolene-8-ol is a computationally predicted, structurally stable ligand of pancreatic alpha-amylase. As a purely in silico prediction, this finding does not establish therapeutic efficacy; in vitro kinetic and in vivo validation of this and related E. chlorantha stem bark constituents remain necessary before any candidate can be considered for T2DM management.

papers.title: Mechanochemically Accelerated Defluorosilylation of α-Trifluoromethyl Styrenes
papers.abstract: We report a mechanochemical copper-catalyzed defluorosilylation of α-trifluoromethyl styrenes with silylboranes. Mechanical activation dramatically accelerated the C–F bond transformation, reducing the reaction time from 8 h to only 30 min at room temperature while substantially decreasing solvent consumption. The reaction exhibits broad substrate compatibility and scalability, highlighting mechanochemistry as an effective strategy for accelerating selective C–F bond functionalization.

papers.title: Residue Protonation States Shape the Photodynamics of Red Fluorescent Proteins
papers.abstract: Understanding the protonation equilibria of key residues in fluorescent proteins, particularly those buried and involved in hydrogen bonding with the chromophore, is crucial for modeling their photodynamical behavior. Using mCherry as a model system, we investigate the protonation effects of two ionizable residues, GLU 215 and LYS 70, located within 4 Å of the chromophore, on the protein's photodynamics. Although GLU and LYS should be fully deprotonated and protonated respectively at pH=7.5 and 300K in water, constant pH molecular dynamics simulations reveal that the fractions of protonated GLU 215 and LYS 70 are both near 50% in mCherry at pH=7.5 and 300K. These co-existing protonation microstates modulate chromophore geometry and hydrogen bonding patterns on the ground state, affecting the accessibility of different non-radiative decay pathways on the first singlet excited state (S1). Upon deprotonation of GLU 215 and loss of its hydrogen bond with the chromophore, the protein environment both sterically restricts chromophore twisting and removes the electrostatic driving force for this motion on S1. These findings provide valuable insights for designing brighter red fluorescent proteins by selective stabilization of residue protonation states that block non-radiative decay pathways.

papers.title: Supramolecular Eutectogels Based on Mangiferin, a Glucose-Appended Natural Herbal Compound
papers.abstract: Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) have attracted considerable attention as sustainable, next-generation solvents. In this study, we report the formation of supramolecular eutectogels using mangiferin (MF), a naturally occurring C -glucosyl xanthone. MF successfully induced gelation in typical DESs composed of choline chloride and various hydrogen-bond donors, including urea, ethylene glycol, and glycerol. The gelation behavior was dependent on the hydrogen-bond donor, with significant differences observed in the time required for gelation. Furthermore, microscopic observations and XRD measurements revealed that MF formed distinct self-assembled network structures depending on the DES composition. Rheological measurements revealed the viscoelastic properties of the eutectogels, which supported the formation of three-dimensional supramolecular networks. These findings highlight the potential of MF as a bio-based gelator for DES-based soft materials and provide valuable insights into the rational design of sustainable supramolecular eutectogels for future applications.

papers.title: Lithographically Patterned Cobalt Nanoribbons as Magnetic Artificial Pinning Centers in REBCO-Coated Conductors for Continuous-Wave Accelerator Magnets
papers.abstract: We investigate a lithographically patterned cobalt-nanoribbon array as a magnetic artificial pinning center (APC) architecture for REBCO-coated conductors intended for continuous-wave (CW) superconducting accelerator magnets, using accelerator-driven subcritical (ADS) fission-waste-transmutation injectors as the motivating application. A long-wavelength magnetostatic model (the Wallace/Karlqvist spacing-loss approximation used in magnetic-recording physics) is used to estimate the periodic stray-field harmonic produced above the array as a function of the ribbon fill fraction and cobalt-to-REBCO separation and is combined with the standard flux-lattice matching-field relation Bphi = 2*Phi0/(root3 * p^2) to fix the lithographic pitch required for a given target field. This calculation shows that the 13 nm feature size inherited from a prior magic-angle-graphene proposal corresponds to a matching field of approximately 14 T, which is well outside the 0.4–2 T range of published ADS injector solenoid and corrector designs; a pitch of 45–80 nm is required to place the matching field in the ADS-relevant range, and we adopt that corrected target here. This revision replaces the previously illustrated Figure 3 pinning-force bump with a closed-form calculation: the same periodic stray field is combined with the local (Pearl-length) leading-order approximation to the London-theory vortex-ferromagnet interaction energy U_v-Co(x) and force F_v-Co(x) = -dU_v-Co/dx, yielding a nonfitted estimate of the magnetic pinning-force contribution across the 0.4-2 T design range (Section 5.1). That estimate exceeds typical core-pinning energy and cuprate depairing-current scales, which we read as evidence that the local approximation is an upper bound in this regime — expected, since the calculated Pearl length (~45 nm) is comparable to the design pitch — rather than a validated quantitative prediction; the full nonlocal London-theory treatment of the vortex–magnetic-dipole interaction developed by Erdin, Lyuksyutov, Pokrovsky and Vinokur remains the necessary next calculation to convert this upper bound into a quantitative prediction (Section 9). A Rayleigh-law model of minor-loop hysteresis dissipation under near-DC ripple and a toy superposition model of the ribbon orientation-tunable Jc(theta) are presented explicitly as first-order, nonfitted illustrations of the expected functional behavior, not as predictions of specific measured values. The Rayleigh analysis indicates that hysteresis dissipation should be small under strict DC operation but increases as the cube of any residual field ripple, making the power-supply ripple specification a first-order design constraint rather than a negligible detail. No device has been fabricated, and no finite-element or micromagnetic simulation has been performed; together with the full nonlocal London calculation, these remain the specific open questions identified explicitly in Section 9.

papers.title: Recycling of PFAS using magnesium through mechanochemical process
papers.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are widely used a class of organofluorine compounds whose high chemical and thermal stability has motivated the development of strategies for their chemical conversion and fluorine recovery from the perspective of effective fluorine resource utilization. Herein, we report a mechanochemical strategy for the recovery and utilization of fluorine using alkaline-earth metals. Mechanochemical treatment of polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) with Mg rapidly converted the fluoropolymer into MgF2, and the method was extended to various PFAS. We further established a method for converting poorly soluble MgF2 into water-soluble NaF by ball milling with NaOH. The poorly water soluble Mg(OH)2 formed during this conversion, which enabled the selective recovery of NaF without additional metal oxide additives. These two transformations were subsequently integrated into a single-step process, enabling the direct conversion of fluoropolymers and perfluoroalkanes into water-soluble and reaildy usable NaF under mechanochemical conditions. The recovered NaF was directly utilized as a fluoride source for one-pot fluorination reactions of sulfonyl chlorides and acyl chlorides, affording the corresponding fluorinated products. This protocol was also scaled up, highlighting important considerations for reaction scale and operational safety. This study provides a useful approach to recovering PFASderived fluorine as a reusable fluoride source and demonstrates its potential for the circular utilization of fluorine resources.

papers.title: Methodology for Fabricating and Testing Carbon Molecular Sieve (CMS) Dense Film Membranes for Reproducible Permeation Experiments
papers.abstract: Carbon molecular sieve (CMS) membranes are promising for demanding gas separations, but their brittleness after pyrolysis makes dense-film permeation testing difficult and often irreproducible. Membranes that appear defect-free after pyrolysis can crack during handling, masking, permeation cell assembly, vacuum evacuation or gas pressurization. This work presents a practical procedure for fabricating and testing CMS dense films prepared from fluorinated polyimide-based CMS membranes. We investigated several experimental factors such as polymer concentration, membrane casting in glove bag, epoxy selection, filter paper support, masking and pressure loading, and their resulting impact on the mechanical stability of the membranes Careful control of these steps reduced or entirely mitigated film cracking, gas bypass during testing, and epoxy seal failure during permeation measurements. This study provides a reliable method for casting, masking and testing of fragile CMS dense film membranes and addresses practical details that are often not reported, but are important for successful and reproducible gas permeation data with CMS membranes.

papers.title: Photocatalytic dehydrogenation enables divergent access to functional polyolefins
papers.abstract: Polyolefins are among the most widely used plastics, yet their chemically inert hydrocarbon backbones severely limit opportunities for chemical modification and value-added reuse. Introducing carbon–carbon double bonds offers a powerful way to transform these otherwise unreactive materials into versatile intermediates for downstream chemistry. Here we report an acceptorless photocatalytic/cobalt-catalyzed dehydrogenation that operates across a broad range of polyethylene- and polypropylene-based materials, including post-consumer plastics. Notably, polypropylene undergoes dehydrogenation with near-exclusive selectivity for terminal alkene formation. The resulting unsaturated polyolefins serve as versatile platforms for diverse transformations, enabling access to functionalized polyolefins, telechelic polyethylene, as well as block and graft copolymers. These products further demonstrate utility as compatibilizers for immiscible polymer blends and as strong adhesive materials. By converting inert C–H backbones into chemically addressable alkene-containing polymers, this strategy transforms commodity polyolefins into diverse polymer architectures with practical functions.

papers.title: Self-Sustained Sabatier Reaction via Submerged Photosynthesis
papers.abstract: CO 2 methanation is a promising route for carbon utilization, yet conventional processes remain constrained by their reliance on externally supplied H 2 and specialized catalysts. To overcome these limitations, this study introduces a self-sustained Sabatier reaction based on the submerged photosynthesis of crystallites (SPSC). In this single aqueous system, metallic Fe and Mg powders react with carbonated water to generate H 2 and CH 4 near room temperature without an added methanation catalyst. Light irradiation accelerates the production of both gases. CH 4 production scales approximately in proportion with H 2 generation across diverse reaction conditions, with both gases exhibiting similar apparent activation energies. During the reaction, plate-like FeCO 3 forms on the Fe surface, while Mg addition modifies this carbonate structure to enhance relative CH 4 formation at longer reaction times. Scavenger experiments confirm the pivotal role of electron transfer in gas production. These results demonstrate that metal oxidation, electron transfer, and surface-bound carbonate reactions drive SPSC-methanation, successfully integrating in situ H 2 generation, CH 4 formation, and metal carbonate crystallization without external H 2 input.

papers.title: Sequential Adaptive Natural Density Partitioning (AdNDP) Systematically Produces Non-N-Representable Densities
papers.abstract: Adaptive natural density partitioning (Ad-NDP) sequentially extracts fragment natural orbitals from the one-electron density matrix. Herein, we show, with an exact and basisindependent argument, that the residual density left behind after two non-orthogonal bonding elements are extracted is not guaranteed to be N-representable. The breakdown has a precise, traceable origin: whenever two sequentially depleted orbitals carry a nonzero overlap, S12 ̸= 0, the second extraction re-subtracts density along a direction the first depletion step has already emptied, driving a diagonal element of the compressed 2 × 2 residual block negative independently of basis set, correlation treatment, or system size. At CCSD/cc-pVTZ, five benchmark multicenter systems (diborane, B−

papers.title: Atomic-level visualization of local tacticity and steric structures of polymer chains
papers.abstract: Since Staudinger's demonstration of the macromolecular concept a century ago, polymer science has been built upon the fundamental concept of chain configuration and conformation, which primarily determine polymer properties at both molecular and macroscopic levels. However, direct atomic-level visualization of individual polymer chains has remained a challenge, leaving the fundamental question of how local chain configuration/conformation are involved in the preferred overall chain morphology experimentally unexplored. Here, we present a novel approach combining atomic-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy, molecular mechanics simulation, and a genetic algorithm to determine the atomic-level structures of single polymer chains. This hybrid experimental-computational method successfully visualizes both the local stereochemical configuration, i.e., tacticity, and backbone conformations (dihedral angles) of a single chain adsorbed on a substrate at the atomic level. Significantly, we demonstrate experimentally that chain shapes result from a balance between intrinsic local conformational energy, influenced by local tacticity, and extrinsic environmental factors, including substrate adsorption energy and surface geometric constraints. Our approach extends fundamental experimental insights into single-chain physics, enabling the rational design of polymeric materials with more precisely controlled molecular architectures.

papers.title: Volatile-element depletion in rocky planets as a purity spectrum of a single information field: An information-dynamics reinterpretation of hybrid accretion
papers.abstract: Wang et al. (2026, Nature Astronomy) showed that the moderately-volatile lithophile element (MVLE) depletion patterns of Earth and Mars record different formation pathways: Earth accreted ≳75% of its mass via pebble accretion, Mars ∼73% via collisions of volatile-depleted planetesimals. We reinterpret this result in the information-dynamics (ID) framework, in which self-organization (ε) and dissipation (γ) compete through a single information field of local purity p. A numerical experiment on the published source data (13 elements for bulk silicate Earth, bulk silicate Mars and Vesta) shows that a single mean purity cannot describe the two planets: the fit escapes to unphysical solutions. The data instead require a purity spectrum: each planet’s pattern is a mixture over one universal single-purity response law S(T ; p), with only the mixture weights differing between bodies. A joint fit with a 4-parameter universal law reproduces all 36 data points with χ2/N = 0.35 (all residuals within 2σ). The inferred spectra mirror the published multi-component decomposition (Earth: 59% strongly-processed + 24% Vesta-like + 17% volatile-rich; Mars: Vesta-like bin dominant), and Vesta independently concentrates 99% of its weight at a processing temperature of 1116K, reproducing the published 1135±35K without being given it. Pebble accretion and planetesimal collision thus emerge as two projections of the same field at different purities, rather than two independent mechanisms. We give testable predictions for rocky exoplanets and the Moon.

papers.title: Dry-drawn Bi2Te3-on-paper thermoresistive devices for respiration monitoring
papers.abstract: Dry deposition on paper offers a simple route to resistive sensing devices. Here, micronized Bi2Te3 powder is rubbed onto copier paper through a tape mask, charcoal electrodes are drawn over the deposited layer, and copper leads are attached with conductive silver paste; the active layer requires no solvent, binder, vacuum processing or annealing. X-ray diffraction identifies rhombohedral Bi2Te3 with preferred (00l) orientation, while electron microscopy shows particles and platelets distributed over the fibrous substrate. Between 25 and 60 °C, the resistance of three devices follows an Arrhenius relationship with an apparent activation energy of 0.121 ± 0.005 eV, corresponding to a temperature coefficient of resistance (TCR) of −1.6 % °C−1 at 25 °C, several times larger in magnitude than that of pencil-drawn graphite. A room-temperature air puff onto a device held at 40 °C produces a 10–90 % response within ≈0.2 s, limited by the sampling rate of 10 readings s−1. Covering the channel with adhesive tape reduces the resistance change between 30 and 90 % relative humidity from ≈−30 % to less than 1 %. In a self-experiment by one of the authors, a tape-covered device positioned ≈1 cm below the nostrils exhibits resistance modulations of 2.3–7.2 % during bilateral and single-nostril breathing, with dominant spectral frequencies of 22–23 min−1. These results establish dry-drawn Bi2Te3 as a simple, solvent-free thermoresistive sensing material on paper and demonstrate its feasibility for respiration monitoring.

papers.title: A Broadly Deployable Method for Repeated Hyperpolarized <sup>13</sup> C Metabolic Imaging in Living Animals
papers.abstract: Hyperpolarized 13 C-MRI enables real-time imaging of metabolic conversions in vivo, but remains largely restricted to specialized sites with superconducting high-field MRI and polarization infrastructure. Here we present a broadly deployable method for preclinical hyperpolarized 13 C-metabolic imaging, which combines signal amplification by reversible exchange (SABRE), a parahydrogen-based hyperpolarization technique, with detection of [1- 13 C]pyruvate-d 3 in a compact 436 mT permanent-magnet small-animal MRI system. SABRE yields 13 C-pyruvate polarization of 13% at ~30 mM in a purified, biocompatible solution, with a T 1 relaxation time of 140 s. In a transgenic breast cancer mouse model, 13 C-chemical shift imaging after injection resolves pyruvate, pyruvate hydrate and lactate in vivo, maps elevated lactate-to-pyruvate ratios in mammary tumors and images three freshly prepared pyruvate doses sequentially in the same animal in less than one hour. This compact SABRE-to-low-field method makes repeated hyperpolarized 13 C-metabolic imaging mobile and accessible in standard preclinical research environments.

papers.title: Hybrid Photoactive Lignin Based Magnetic Nanomaterials for Antimicrobial Application
Direct Photo- and Electrothermally Regenerable Adsorbents for Carbon Dioxide Capture Using Conjugated Metal−Organic Frameworks
papers.abstract: Adsorbent regeneration in carbon dioxide capture systems primarily relies on external temperature and pressure swings, posing critical challenges of intensive energy penalties and low cycling rates. Here we demonstrate a direct photo- and electrothermal swing method for CO 2 capture using two-dimensional conjugated MOF Cu 3 (2,3,6,7,10,11-hexahydroxytriphenylene) 2 (Cu 3 (HHTP) 2 ) and its derivatives. Cu 3 (HHTP) 2 releases CO 2 captured at room-temperature through photo- or electrothermal effects by directly applying one-sun irradiation or a voltage of 10 V. The capture-release process operates across 1%-50% CO 2 with a cyclic frequency of 4-5 h -1 and adsorption capacities of 0.04-1.11 mmol g -1 . Incorporating alkylamine groups into Cu 3 (HHTP) 2 further enhances CO 2 adsorption capacity by more than three-fold, with corresponding energy consumptions down to 145 and 60 kJ mol -1 for 1% and 10% CO 2 , respectively, via photothermal regeneration. Structurally integrating energy conversion functions and CO 2 adsorption sites within a single, porous material establishes a new blueprint for solar-driven and electrified carbon management.

papers.title: Mayer’s Effective Minimal Localized Molecular Orbitals
papers.abstract: Roughly thirty years ago Mayer presented a theory leading to the concept of an effective minimal atomic basis. A set of a posteriori defined, fragment-localized molecular orbitals (LMOs) was obtained as a byproduct. In this work, a new set of LMOs, termed Mayer’s effective minimal LMOs, is derived from this byproduct; it can be viewed as arising from a compactification of atomic orbitals projected onto the occupied space. The procedure is fully self-contained, requiring no input beyond that of the underlying quantum chemical calculation. The resulting LMOs are orientation invariant, computationally economical, and can be partitioned into disjoint subsets assigned to atoms or multiatomic fragments. Mayer’s effective minimal LMOs span the occupied space, but their number exceeds its dimension; they therefore form a frame rather than a basis in the strict sense. The size of the set does not grow with the original AO basis but remains at a value prescribed by the user, a prudent choice being the minimal atomic orbital basis dimension.

papers.title: Nonadiabatic Semiclassical Polariton Dynamics: Excited State Proton Transfer of Aminopropenal
papers.abstract: The interplay between strong light-matter coupling and nonadiabatic molecular dynamics provides a promising route to control chemical reactivity. Here, we develop a framework for simulating polaritonic chemistry with on-the-fly semiclassical nonadiabatic molecular dynamics, employing the linearized semiclassical initial value representation. With this approach, we simulate the nonadiabatic molecular dynamics under strong light-matter coupling, presenting results for excited state proton transfer of aminopropenal. Light-matter interactions are described using a Jaynes-Cummings Hamiltonian formulated in the adiabatic electronic basis, where the electronic energies, transition moments, and nuclear forces are evaluated on the fly. We characterize how light-matter coupling reshapes reaction pathways and redistributes photonic and electronic character of individual states along the trajectory, finding that photonic character of the lower polaritonic state decreases in time as the molecular geometry relaxes, demonstrating that the cavity effect is strongest during the initial dynamics. We find that for aminopropenal, the main effect of cavity coupling on the dynamics is not altering the proton transfer barrier, but instead altering the excited-state relaxation network by introducing an additional polaritonic state with favorable proton transfer energetics. By analyzing the population transfer between excited states, we find that cavity coupling leads to population being temporarily redirected into this intermediate state, delaying population relaxation to a high-barrier excited state. This change in timing results in a higher fraction of trajectories undergoing proton transfer. Our new computational protocol that connects on-the-fly semiclassical nonadiabatic dynamics and polaritonic frameworks provides trajectory-resolved insight into how cavity coupling modifies nonadiabatic population transfer and proton-transfer dynamics.

papers.abstract: The interplay between strong light-matter coupling and nonadiabatic molecular dynamics provides a promising route to control chemical reactivity.
