papers.title: Heteroatom Engineering Enables Oxygen-Tolerant Electrochemical Direct Air Capture
papers.abstract: Electrochemical direct CO2 capture using redox-active carriers offers an alternative to thermal amine scrubbing but requires molecules that combine strong CO2 binding with tolerance toward oxygen and water. Here, we show that incorporating pyridinic nitrogen into an ortho-quinone framework provides this combination in 1,10phenanthroline-5,6-dione (PD). Comparison of PD with phenanthrenequinone (PQ) and the analogue 1,10phenanthroline (PT) isolates the role of pyridinic nitrogen in tuning the redox potential and CO2 capture behaviour of the quinone core. Electrochemical measurements, density functional theory (DFT), in situ FT-IR, and 13C NMR spectroscopy support strong and reversible CO2 binding through the electrochemically reduced dianion (log𝐾 = 9.8). The capture chemistry established in homogeneous electrolyte was subsequently translated to PD immobilised on a carbon-felt electrode and demonstrated in a near-neutral aqueous electrolyte. Under a 9.3% CO2 feed, the PD-modified electrode sustained reversible CO2 capture and release over 16 h with an electron-utilisation efficiency of 96% and a minimum energy requirement of 44-56 kJ mol-1 CO2. Isotope-sensitive in situ FT-IR measurements and the pH response during aqueous cycling further support cation participation in charge compensation. These results establish heteroatom engineering as a molecular design strategy for developing oxygen- and water-tolerant quinone redox carriers and provide a pathway toward electrochemical CO2 capture from dilute emission streams.

papers.title: Aryne-Enabled Synthesis of 1,8-Disubstituted Thioxanthones for Conformationally Gated Metal-Ion Sensing
papers.abstract: Conformational changes in a chromophore can strongly influence its fluorescence properties. Here, we report the development of thioxanthone-based fluorescent sensors designed to suppress the characteristic butterfly-like deformation of the thioxanthone core upon metal-ion binding. To access the required 1,8-disubstituted scaffolds, we developed an efficient aryne-based synthesis of multisubstituted thioxanthones from readily available o -iodoaryl triflates and N , N , N’ , N’- tetramethylthiourea. Subsequent functionalization provided a series of thioxanthones bearing metal-coordinating substituents at the 1,8-positions. Evaluation of the resulting compounds identified a probe exhibiting pronounced and spectrally distinct fluorescence responses to Zn 2+ and Ca 2+ with high ON/OFF ratios, enabling clear discrimination between the two metal ions. Time-dependent DFT (TD-DFT) calculations for a simplified Zn 2+ complex indicated that coordination stabilizes a nearly planar thioxanthone structure and enhances the oscillator strength of the emissive transition. These results demonstrate the utility of controlling the butterfly-like deformation of the thioxanthone core for metal-ion-responsive fluorescence sensing.

papers.title: Synthesis of Amphiphilic Polymer Co-Networks via the Growth of a Living RAFT Network. Part III: Effect of DMSO Content
papers.abstract: Owing to their distinctive nanophase-separated, co-continuous morphology, Amphiphilic polymer co-networks (APCNs) have attracted considerable attention in the past four decades. In 2024, a RAFT-mediated network growth strategy for the synthesis of APCNs was reported. This approach involves first preparing a parent RAFT network, typically a hydrophilic network containing dormant network-RAFT agents, followed by the diffusion and polymerization of hydrophobic monomers within the parent network. This process generates a secondary hydrophobic nanophase within the pre-existing hydrophilic continuous phase, yielding an amphiphilic polymer co-network that fulfils the defining structural characteristics of APCNs. This work reports a systematic study of the effect of DMSO content (10%, 50%, and 75%) on the synthesis of amphiphilic polymer co-networks (APCNs) using the above-mentioned RAFT-mediated network growth strategy. The resulting APCNs comprise a hydrophilic parent network based on oligo(ethylene glycol) methyl ether acrylate (OEGA, Mn = 480) and the crosslinker N, N′-methylenebisacrylamide (Bis), into which hydrophobic n-butyl acrylate (BA) segments are incorporated through RAFT-mediated network growth. Network chemical composition, thermal properties, and morphology were characterized using FT-IR, TGA, DSC, and SEM, while amphiphilicity was assessed through equilibrium swelling measurements in water and toluene. The DMSO content employed during parent network synthesis was found to exert a pronounced effect on the properties of the resulting APCNs. Among the systems investigated, the APCN derived from a parent gel prepared in 75% DMSO and subjected to 5 h of photogrowth exhibited the most balanced amphiphilic character, displaying swelling ratios of 10.30 in water and 18.24 in toluene.

papers.title: Scalable Synthesis and Processing of Porous Organic Polymers for Continuous-Flow Noble Metal Recycling and Catalysis
papers.abstract: Porous organic polymers (POPs) hold great promise for separations and catalysis but remain limited by costly syntheses and poor processability. Here we report the scalable synthesis of freestanding imine/aminal-linked POP gels from inexpensive monomers under mild conditions. The gels can be molded into diverse architectures and converted into mechanically robust monoliths with high surface areas of up to 1055 m2/g. The POPs exhibit high adsorption capacities of 3225 mg/g for [AuCl4]- and 1375 mg/g for [PdCl4]2-. Integrated into continuousflow columns, they enable the treatment of electronic-waste leachates at a throughput of 1 L/h, achieving a gold recovery efficiency of 99%. The noble-metal-loaded POP column can be operated as a continuous-flow Suzuki reactor, delivering a space–time yield of 2.75 kgbiphenyl/LPOP·day. This work establishes a practical platform for fabrication of scalable, processable POPs that integrate noble-metal recovery with continuous-flow catalysis, advancing their application toward circular resource utilization and sustainable chemical manufacturing.

papers.title: Fe-dopant site occupancy in Co3O4: evidence of isovalent substitution and short-range association at octahedral sites
papers.abstract: Understanding how dopant site occupancy influences the behavior of spinel oxides is essential for tailoring their functional properties. Here, we combine DFT+U calculations with computational and experimental Co K-edge XANES spectroscopy to investigate the structural, electronic, and magnetic effects of Fe incorporation into Co3O4. The results indicate a strong energetic preference for isovalent substitution, with Fe3+ preferentially occupying octahedral Co3+ sites. This preference becomes more pronounced with increasing dopant concentration, leading to a clear stability hierarchy in which short-distance double-octahedral configurations are energetically favored. Dopant–dopant interactions further influence this stability landscape, promoting attractive coupling for octahedral and mixed-site configurations, while tetrahedral Fe3+ exhibits weak or slightly repulsive interactions. These trends are reflected in the magnetic properties, with octahedral Fe inducing stronger local magnetic moments compared to tetrahedral substitution. The calculated XANES spectra reveal site-dependent modifications of the Co pre-edge features that can be related to changes in the local electronic structure induced by Fe doping. However, these spectral changes should be interpreted qualitatively in light of known limitations of the theoretical approach. Overall, this study highlights the central role of dopant site occupancy, in addition to dopant concentration, in tuning the structural, electronic, and magnetic properties of Co3O4 spinels.

papers.title: Microstructural, Energy-Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy, and Fourier-Transform Infrared Analysis of Inorganic-Platelet Polymer Composites for Sustainable Infrastructure
papers.abstract: Polymer matrix composites used in wet or thermally variable environments may change through moisture diffusion, polymer relaxation, swelling and plasticization, hydrolysis or leaching, microcracking, and progressive weakening of the reinforcement–matrix interface. This paper focuses on understanding the composition and morphology of a reinforcing phase, and determining whether its incorporation produces additional bulk-resolvable chemical features, which is important for interpreting composites used in wet or aggressive environments. The study presents a structural and spectroscopic characterization of a commercial glass-flake-reinforced unsaturated-polyester composite by combining energydispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) with full-range Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) against a neat unsaturated-polyester-resin control. EDS gives a composition consistent with a sodium–calcium silicate glass phase for the flake (17.4 wt% Si, 5.0 wt% Na, 2.2 wt% Ca, 1.1 wt% Al, 1.0 wt% Mg and 55.6 wt% O), whereas the polyester matrix and coat regions are dominated by carbon and oxygen (70–75 wt% C and 23–26 wt% O). Two representative flakes (n = 2) have apparent length-to-width ratios of 21.9 and 43.9. FTIR spectra collected over 428–4500 cm-1 show the same principal polyester-resin-associated bands at essentially identical wavenumbers in the composite and neat resin. Polymer-associated band intensities are 12–28% lower in the composite, while the band near the Si–O–Si network bending region changes by only −0.6%. No additional resolvable bulk absorption bands are observed. The results support a physically dispersed silicate-glass phase within the polyester matrix but do not exclude weak or spatially localized interfacial interactions below the resolution of the measurements. The spectra and elemental tables are released as a reusable dataset.

papers.title: Stable triorganoiodine complexes
papers.abstract: The first examples of air stable acyclic triorganoiodine compounds, phenyliodine bis(1-(2-R)-o-carborane)s have been isolated from reactions of PhIL2 reagents with lithio-o-carboranes and crystallographically characterized. When R = H or Si(CH3)3, the complexes are predisposed to form o-carboryne through β-elimination as confirmed by a trapping reaction with naphthalene, where the R = H variant degrades during formation. The latter Si(CH3)3 derivative is isolable in modest yield, while for R = CH3, the resulting phenyliodine bis(1-(2-methyl)-o-carborane)s can be obtained in high yields. The complexes known so far appear to behave as nonnucleophilic bases, and treatment with strong protic acids affords more electrophilic phenyl(1-o-carboranyl) iodonium salts. Compared with our previous synthesis of an aryl(1-o-carboranyl) iodonium salt, this method is simpler and offers broadened scope. Less is known of these salts than previously assumed as earlier reports have now also been found incorrect. A preliminary study finds they can either arylate or 1-o-carboranylate a chloride nucleophile with chemoselectivity tuneable by electronic modification of the oCb ligand, providing a rare example of an o-carborane C atom reacting as an electrophile.

papers.title: Predicting Glass Transition Temperature of Polyimide Homopolymers and Copolymers Using Interpretable QSPR-Based Machine Learning: The MFKit Framework
papers.abstract: In this work, we address the problem of predicting the glass transition temperature of polyimides, a class of high-performance engineering thermoplastics, with an emphasis on both homopolymer and copolymer systems. While machine learning approaches have been widely applied to polymer property prediction, their extension to copolymers remains limited and often lacks the interpretability required for rational materials design. To overcome these limitations, we develop an interpretable QSPR-based framework (MFKit) that combines physically grounded descriptors for monomer featurization with Gaussian Process Regression (GPR). The model is trained on a dataset of polyimide homopolymers from PoLyInfo and achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art approaches (R2 = 0.856, MAE = 20.7 °C on the test set). Causal inference and SHAP analysis reveal key structure–property relationships, identifying aromatic content, backbone flexibility and rotation, side chain volume and hydrogen bonding as dominant factors governing Tg. The framework is subsequently extended to polyimide copolymers by constructing copolymer representations through combination of monomer descriptor vectors using several aggregation schemes. The best-performing approach yields R2 = 0.832 and MAE = 23.3 °C on an external dataset compiled from the literature. Furthermore, guided by the identified structure–property relationships, polyimide copolymers are designed, synthesized, and experimentally characterized, each exhibiting increased Tg compared with the parent homopolymer. Validation against DSC measurements demonstrates strong agreement with predictions (MAE = 16.3 °C). Overall, the proposed approach provides a unified and interpretable framework for Tg prediction for both homopolymer and copolymer systems, enabling physically grounded and data-driven design of polyimide-based materials.

papers.title: Terminal Acceptor-Substitution Controls Optoelectronic Properties in Triphenylamine Based Donors for Organic Solar Cells: A DFT Approach
papers.abstract: Organic solar cells offer opportunities for lightweight and flexible solar energy conversion, motivating development of molecular systems with tunable optoelectronic properties. In this study, six novel triphenylamine-based small-molecule donors (RD1-RD6) having donor-πacceptor (D-π-A) design, where dimethoxy triphenylamine-donor, thiophene-bridge, and phenyl with 1,3-indandione derivatives-acceptors are investigated to understand how the terminal acceptor regulates their molecular, electronic and excited state properties. Density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent DFT (TD-DFT) calculations are employed to understand their structural, optoelectronic and charge-transfer properties. Terminal acceptors via different substitutions systematically modulate frontier orbital energies, with HOMO-LUMO gaps ranging from 1.62 to 2.23 eV, absorption maxima of 396-469 nm, and pronounced intramolecular charge transfer characteristics reaching 69.57%. RD6 exhibited the deepest HOMO (-4.96 eV), highest calculated dipole moment (21.33 D) in methanol, and substantial electron-hole separation, whereas RD3 exhibited the narrowest HOMO-LUMO gap (1.62 eV). All the molecules showed low reorganization energies especially for electrons (0.02 - 0.08 eV), high light-harvesting efficiencies (0.89 - 0.98), and favorable intrinsic charge-transfer characteristics. A Scharber-type model applied to RD6 predicts theoretical PCEs of 18.50% and 19.83% for the binary RD6:Y6-2Cl and ternary RD6:L8-BO:Y6-2Cl configuration. Overall, the results demonstrate that terminal acceptor engineering provides an effective way for tuning electronic and excited-state properties of triphenylamine-based donors.

papers.title: De novo design of photoenzymes with substrate-recognition-encoded enantioselectivity
papers.abstract: Photoenzymes enable stereoselective excited-state transformations beyond the chemical space accessible to natural enzymes, yet their development remains largely dependent on repurposing few privileged protein scaffolds and extensive directed evolution. Although de novo protein design enables tailor-made catalytic architectures, its prevailing transition-state stabilization paradigm is not readily transferable to photoenzymes. Here we establish a substrate-recognition-guided strategy for de novo photoenzyme design, in which the computational construction of substrate-tailored catalytic environments determines stereoselectivity and the genetic incorporation of abiotic thioxanthone photosensitizer endows excited-state reactivity. This approach generated customized photoenzymes for the deracemization of 4-alkenylcyclohexanols that exhibit nanomolar substrate affinity, catalytic efficiencies exceeding 1.5 × 105 M-1 s-1, and up to 99% enantiomeric excess. Crystal structure and kinetic analyses validate the designed model, revealing substrate-recognition-dependent enantioselective energy transfer within the tailored active site. This work establishes substrate recognition as a general design principle for extending de novo enzyme design to excited-state biocatalysis.

papers.title: De Novo Circularly Polarized Emission and Greatly Enhanced Circular Dichroism in Cationic Naphthalene Diimide Dye Supramolecular Assembly on 2-D Laponite Nanoclay
papers.abstract: This study reveals a surprising finding that a chiral cationic pyrrolidine-substituted naphthalene diimide (cNDI-Py + ), which shows no circular dichroism (CD) or circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) in its monomeric form, exhibits strong CD and broad, intense CPL when electrostatically bound to a 2D synthetic laponite nanoclay nanoplatelet (cNDI-Py + _Laponite) in an aqueous environment. This supramolecular alignment of the electrostatically anchored dye on laponite platelets leads to a chiral assembly that produces distinctive chiral excimer emission, stemming from an excited-state slip-stacked arrangement of preorganized dye molecules. The new hybrid emission band at 480 nm comes from the excited cNDI-Py+_Laponite assembly, as evidenced by a high quantum yield (Φ) of 0.40, luminescence dissymmetry (g lum ) of -0.013, and an outstanding CPL brightness of 88 M -1 cm -1 . We demonstrate that chiral dye-nanoclay assemblies serve as an underused platform for excimer-based CPL by nanoscale confinement of dye molecules. Bright circularly polarized emissions can play an important role in establishing experimental space-to-ground telecommunication links, enabling full-color 3D holographic displays, and supporting other applications that rely on chiral control of light-matter interactions. This approach provides oxygen-tolerant control with inorganic templates, enabling enantioselective excimer emission and opening new paths for CPL-active materials.

papers.title: Robust and Reusable Waveguide-Enhanced Raman-on-a-Chip for Sensing Complex Fluids
papers.abstract: Integrated photonic sensors offer a pathway toward compact chemical analysis, but their use in unprocessed complex fluids is limited by surface fouling, chemical compatibility, and the need for stable optical coupling. Here, we develop a reusable waveguide-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (WERS) platform based on chemically resilient silicon nitride waveguides and a permanently packaged fiber-to-chip interface. The sensor incorporates a spiral sensing waveguide and a robust optical input/output architecture designed to provide reproducible coupling without active alignment. Reusability was evaluated following exposure to commercial gasoline and sequential cleaning treatments. Raman signal recovery using isopropanol as a reference analyte demonstrated improved spectral performance after solvent and oxidative cleaning. As a representative application in a chemically complex matrix, the sensor was directly immersed in commercial gasoline for quantitative ethanol determination without extraction or additional sample preparation. A ratiometric signal based on the ethanol band at 885 cm-1 and a reference band at 1000 cm-1 provided a linear calibration over 10.00–21.74% v/v ethanol (R2 = 0.9323). Independent external validation across 10.00–20.00% v/v yielded 100% prediction-interval coverage, an RMSEP of 0.46% v/v, and an MAE of 0.36% v/v. These results demonstrate that chemically robust WERS with stable packaging can support reproducible, reusable Raman sensing directly in complex fuel matrices, providing a foundation for field-deployable photonic chemical analysis.

papers.title: Enantioselective [3+3] Formal Annulation of Anilines via Carbene Catalysis
papers.abstract: An efficient preparation of highly enantioenriched cyclic compounds from readily available synthons via stereocontrolled organocatalytic processes remains a significant challenge in modern synthetic chemistry. Herein, we report a highly stereoselective N -heterocyclic carbene (NHC)-catalyzed [3+3] annulation of anilines using α-bromocinnamic aldehydes as convenient acyl-azolium precursors. This protocol offers a straightforward route to valuable chiral lactams in high yields (up to 98%) and excellent enantioselectivities (up to 97:3 er ), featuring broad functional group tolerance. Moreover, the reaction is easily scalable and enables versatile downstream derivatizations, further demonstrating the synthetic utility of the developed methodology.

papers.title: Quantum-Entangled Four-Proton Waltz of Anomalous Transport in Water Hydrogen Bond Network
papers.abstract: Proton transfer mechanism along water hydrogen bond network lies in the fundamental question in chemical dynamics. The mechanism remains challenge due to nuclear quantization and many-body correlation. We develop a quantum dynamical model framework that treats electrons and multiple transferring protons on equal footing, and integrate it with isotope measurement by scanning tunneling microscopy of a surface‑bound water tetramer. The simulations reveal the importance of quantum correlation among stepwise electron–proton intermediate states, which quantum coherently drives a synchronized, concerted four‑proton switch between two chiral hydrogen‑bond configurations. Populations periodically decay from one chiral arrangement and reappear in the other, whose oscillation amplitude is strongly suppressed by modest symmetry breaking from isotopic substitution. This mechanism accounts for an anomalous isotope trend experimentally in which the low‑symmetry, singly deuterated tetramer (H2O)3(D2O) switches as slowly as the high‑symmetry, fully deuterated (D2O)4 that eludes semiclassical tunneling kinetics. The framework establishes a practical route to study multi-proton quantum correlation in hydrogen-bond networks on surfaces.

papers.title: Graph Theory-Based De Novo Strategy for Automated Generation of Organic Molecular Cage
papers.abstract: The current design and construction of organic molecular cages (OMCs) remain largely constrained by established topological library. To address this challenge, we established a de novo, graph-theory-based strategy that enables the automated generation of OMCs architectures, which require only the chemical structures of building blocks. By decomposing OMCs into distinct topological geometric elements, a system of equations can be established using graph theory to describe the mathematical relationships and geometric constraints for their architectures. Solving these equations yields the numerical composition of the topological geometric elements for each candidate OMC, allowing the potential rotational symmetries of their architectures to be inferred. Based on the inferred rotational symmetries, a database of OMC topologies was systematically established by applying symmetry operations to define the connectivity between geometric elements. Subsequently, different molecular building blocks were incorporated into these topologies, followed by geometry optimization to generate a large space of chemically realistic three-dimensional OMC structures. This strategy enabled the generation of OMCs with previously unexplored topologies, substantially expanding the structural diversity of the OMCs’ chemical space. To further enrich this chemical space, we extended our strategy to encompass isomers arising from mixed or prochiral building blocks. This strategy enables the systematic exploration of previously overlooked OMC topologies and their corresponding isomers, providing a foundation for the targeted design of molecular cages with tailored cavity geometries, pore sizes, and chemical environments for applications in molecular recognition, selective separation and catalysis.

papers.title: One-step synthesis of α-fluoroarylacetic acids from trifluoromethyl arenes via photocatalytic reduction
papers.abstract: A photocatalytic reduction strategy for the direct synthesis of α-fluoroarylacetic acids from readily available trifluoromethyl arenes has been developed. In contrast to conventional approaches, this reaction does not generate undesired oxidation byproducts associated with the use of fluorinating reagents. Investigation of the substrate scope revealed that the reaction tolerates a wide range of functional groups, including dimethylamino, alkynyl, alkenyl, and ether functionalities. Trifluoromethyl-substituted pyridine derivatives were also compatible with the reaction conditions. Mechanistic studies suggested that the reaction proceeds via an initial hydrodefluorination to form a difluoromethyl arene intermediate, followed by further reductive C–F bond cleavage and carboxylation. The observed selectivity for the monofluorinated products originated from the selective carboxylation during product formation together with the slow hydrodefluorination of the resulting α-fluoroarylacetic acids. The reaction proceeds without the need for an external CO2 atmosphere.

papers.abstract: Withdrawn by ChemRxiv because it is an unintentional duplication of 10.26434/chemrxiv.15010502/v1

papers.title: Investigation of NaxFePO4 systems prepared by a modified Pechini sol-gel method as possible cathode materials for high voltage Na-ion batteries
papers.abstract: An uncomplicated modification of a Pechini assisted sol-gel process in water-polyol solutions is proposed for the synthesis of Na-Fe phosphate powders with different Na-ion content as cathode materials for sodium ion batteries (SIBs). Depending on the pH-values, X-ray diffraction detected the formation of Na-poor olivine-like o-NaFePO4 orthorhombic phase and o-FePO4 nanocrystalline structure. The cyclic voltammetry of the SIBs shows reduction peaks at ~2.23 V (x = 1.0) and ~2.12 V (x = 1.2) vs. Na/Na+ for pH < 3, and between 2.8 V - ~3.0 V (x = 1.0) for pH = 5 respectively. For x = 1.2, several redox peaks observed for pH=5 are assigned to a single-phase reaction (at ~2.5 V vs. Na/Na+) and two-phase reactions (at 3.0–3.25 V). Redox peaks above 4.5 V are more likely associated with Fe3+/Fe4+ redox coupling. A good cyclability is observed for the cathodes synthesized at both the pH values even by charging the batteries to the upper cut-off 4.8 V. The Na-cathode materials prepared under milder conditions showed the highest specific capacity of 40 mAhg-1.

papers.title: Transition state to minimum conversion in the Cope rearrangement under gigapascal pressure
papers.abstract: Converting a transition state (TS) into a minimum is a challenging, yet possible, task, commonly achievable via chemical substitution. Pressure is expected to favor TSs that correspond to volume minima, yet experimentally or computationally demonstrated TS-to-minimum conversions remain rare. Here, we demonstrate a pressure-induced TS-to-minimum conversion in the Cope rearrangement at ∼18 GPa. Extreme pressure polarizable continuum model (XP-PCM) optimizations and vibrational analyses reveal the gradual conversion of the TS imaginary mode into a real vibrational mode. Helium compression chamber (HeCC) simulations unveil a pressure-driven inversion of the reaction-path curvature at the TS in the Gibbs free energy profile. Cyano substitution produces effects on bond distances and vibrational frequencies similar to those induced by pressure, highlighting parallels between chemical and mechanical stabilization. Although compression also accelarates the open-shell pathway, the closed-shell pathway remains thermodynamically favored up to 31 GPa. These findings highlight pressure as a powerful means of reshaping reaction landscapes, effectively enabling new chemistry.

papers.title: Inverse Design of Optical Metamaterials Assembled from Plasmonic Nanoparticles
papers.abstract: Self-assembly of strongly coupled plasmonic nanoparticles is a scalable and promising route for producing optical metamaterials with emergent photonic properties. Understanding, controlling, and designing the light-matter interactions of these components is crucial to improving their performance. In this paper, we formulate optical metamaterials design as an inverse problem, where we first specify a target optical behavior and then use numerical optimization to autonomously discover self-assembled nanoparticle metamaterials possessing the desired features. We use a coupled dipole method for electromagnetic simulation to efficiently compute gradients of optical figures of merit with respect to nanoparticle position, size, and parameters of the dielectric function analytically for gradient-based iterative optimization. Our design framework rapidly iterates through candidate materials self-assembled from tens of thousands of nanoparticles, and specifies the position, size, dielectric properties, and other physical features of each nanoparticle within an optimal metamaterial, subject to arbitrary constraints on the choices of design parameters. We use our tool to perform simulated annealing optimization to propose nanoparticles metamaterials with optical features tunable over an enormous range. In particular, we have inverse designed nanoparticle metamaterials with: 1) tunable extinction spectra of complex lineshape and 2) electric nearfield intensity with spatial profiles matching targeted patterns. By examining libraries of metamaterials with similar optical features, we can describe the key structure-property relations governing their optical responses.

papers.title: Synthesis of Amphiphilic Polymer Co-Networks via the Growth of a Living RAFT Network. Part II: PEGDA-Based Parent Networks
papers.abstract: This work represents the second part of our series on the synthesis of amphiphilic polymer co-networks (APCNs) via the growth of a living RAFT (reversible additionfragmentation chain transfer) network. In this work, we explore the photogrowth behavior of crosslinked polyethylene glycol diacrylate 700 (PEGDA 700) as a hydrophilic parent RAFT network. The model hydrophobic monomers—butyl acrylate (BuA) and methyl methacrylate (MMA)—were incorporated into the parent network via photogrowth, ultimately forming APCNs. The parent networks, daughter networks, and resulting APCN gels were thoroughly characterized using Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), water absorption and dehydration, and swelling experiments.

papers.title: Interfacial Assembly of 2D Superlattices and Quasicrystals in Binary Nanoparticle Systems with Strong Unlike Interactions
papers.abstract: Two-dimensional nanoparticle (NP) superlattices assembled at fluid–fluid interfaces offer a versatile platform for creating novel materials with applications in plasmonics, spectroscopy, photonics, and catalysis. Recently, we implemented a basin-hopping Monte Carlo approach to identify ground-state configurations of binary NP assemblies at fluid interfaces, which helped predict a range of ordered superlattices, several of which have been observed experimentally. Here, we extend this approach by allowing unlike-particle interactions to vary independently of like-particle interactions, an experimentally relevant feature not considered in our previous work that captures systems such as oppositely charged or chemically dissimilar NPs. We systematically map the resulting phase behavior as a function of particle size ratio, NP-fluid interaction asymmetry, and unlike-interaction strength. The resulting structural transitions reveal how preferred immersion depths, geometric packing, and particle coordination collectively govern assembly. Strengthening unlike-particle attraction shifts phase boundaries toward structures with greater unlike-particle coordination, suppresses phase-separated and like-contact-dominated regions, and stabilizes new crystalline phases inaccessible when unlike interactions are constrained by the like-particle interactions. At strong unlike attraction, additionally varying particle composition gives rise to periodic approximants and quasicrystalline structures with 12-fold and 8-fold symmetry. Collectively, these results establish how particle size asymmetry, differential interfacial affinity, and independently tunable like and unlike interactions can be used to direct structural selection in binary NP assemblies at fluid interfaces.

papers.title: Synthesis and characterization of polyazomethines – Towards a semiconducting paper
papers.abstract: Novel organic semiconductor poly(azomethine) materials were synthesized via the polycondensation of terephthalaldehyde with two distinct diamines: para-phenylenediamine and 4,4’-diaminodiphenylmethane. These synthetic routes yielded a fully conjugated polyimine (P1) and a polyimine featuring a more restricted conjugation domain interrupted by a methylene spacer (P2), respectively. A comparative study was conducted to evaluate the influence of the conjugation length on some of their properties, mainly optoelectrical. Hydrochloric acid was employed as a dopant to enhance the electrical performance of the synthetized macromolecules. Furthermore, in alignment with eco-design principles to promote renewable and sustainable solutions, these polymers were integrated onto cellulosic supports either through physical deposition on cellulose filaments or via covalent grafting onto propargylated Kraft pulp fibers using copper(I)-catalyzed azide-alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC). Structural, morphological, and optical characterizations, including Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) and UV-Visible spectroscopies, solid-state 13C NMR, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and atomic force microscopy (AFM), confirmed the successful synthesis, functionalization, and fabrication of the biocomposite materials. Conductivity measurements and optical band gap (Eg) estimations revealed that the conformational flexibility of polymer P2 promotes tighter molecular packing and effective inter-chain interactions (π-π stacking), thereby enabling the development of bio-based semiconductor materials with promising potential for organic electronics.

papers.title: A General Suzuki–Miyaura/[2+2] Photocycloaddition Approach to 2-Oxabicyclo[2.1.1]hexane Biaryl Mimetics
papers.abstract: Herein, we report a modular approach to monosubstituted, (hetero)arylated 2-oxabicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes (oxa-BCHs). The strategy combines facile Suzuki–Miyaura cross-couplings to assemble suitable diene precursors that can undergo [2+2] photocycloadditions. Nineteen novel (hetero)aromatic building blocks and fragments are constructed from their respective (hetero)aryl boronates, conveniently accessed from commercial sources. Next, a high-throughput enabled synthetic sequence is performed, demonstrating the gram-scale conversion of 6-quinoline bromide to the corresponding 4-(quinolyl)oxa-BCH adduct. Finally, the physicochemical properties and aqueous stability of the new oxa-BCH biaryl mimetic was compared with those of other medicinally relevant substituents, demonstrating its promise as a robust, three-dimensional, polarity-enhancing motif for medicinal-chemistry applications.

papers.title: Natural abundance isotopomics reveals coordinated amino acid metabolic alterations in human lung cancer
papers.abstract: Background Metabolic reprogramming in cancer is usually characterized through changes in metabolite levels, yet pool size alone does not reveal how elements are routed through tumour metabolism. We investigated whether natural abundance isotopomics could resolve this metabolic organization in human lung cancer from bulk tissue to individual protein-bound amino acids. Methods Paired tumour and adjacent non-tumour lung tissues from 35 patients with non-small cell lung cancer (25 adenocarcinomas and 10 squamous cell carcinomas) were analysed for elemental composition (C, N, S) and bulk δ13C, δ15N and δ34S by elemental analysis–isotope ratio mass spectrometry, together with amino acid specific δ15N and δ13C and protein-normalized amino acid concentrations by gas chromatography–combustion–isotope ratio mass spectrometry. Changes between tumour and adjacent non-tumour tissues were assessed using paired statistics, correlation analysis, ANOVA-simultaneous component analysis and multilevel partial least squares discriminant analysis. Results Lung tumours showed a reproducible multi-isotope phenotype characterized by lower bulk δ13C and δ15N, higher δ34S, reduced N content and modest increases in C and S content. At the molecular level, glycine showed the strongest δ15N depletion and a parallel decrease in protein-normalized abundance, whereas proline and glutamate were relatively 13C-enriched. Glycine, proline and hydroxyproline concentrations were reduced in tumour tissue. Despite pronounced inter-patient variability, the multivariate tumour effect remained highly significant (permutation p = 0.0008), and multilevel modelling separated tumour from adjacent tissue with a cross-validated area under the curve of 0.922. Compound specific isotope changes were not systematically coupled to pool size, indicating that isotopic composition captures metabolic information not contained in concentration alone. The coordinated glycine, glutamate, proline and hydroxyproline responses further pointed to glycine related N handling and a glutamate–proline–collagen axis linking tumour metabolism to extracellular matrix organization. Conclusions Natural abundance isotopomics reveals a coherent metabolic phenotype of human lung cancer across C, N and S metabolism. By resolving bulk isotope signals into molecule specific responses, this approach identifies pathway level metabolic organization. This information is not apparent from level measurements alone. It highlights glycine metabolism and glutamate–proline–collagen remodelling as biologically relevant features of the lung tumour microenvironment.

papers.title: The Role of Metacognitive Skills in Decision-Making using Type I/II Thinking
papers.abstract: Strong reasoning skills are vital in a variety of academic and everyday contexts, requiring strong metacognitive awareness to be strategic and efficient. However, relatively little is known about how metacognitive abilities and skill-building relate to making purposeful choices about reasoning. We investigated the role of metacognition in Dual Process theory, including learners’ awareness and self-description of their cognitive engagement. Dual-process theory describes that most reasoning results from the interaction of two cognitive processes: Type I (fast/intuitive thinking) and Type II (slow/analytical thinking). The purposeful use of reasoning types is complex, including metacognitive awareness of the Type being used, identifying the optimal type, deciding if there is a need or benefit to switching, desire/motivation to switch, and the ability to do so (e.g., cognitive resources). This mixed-methods study examined how a metacognition intervention influenced awareness of and engagement with Type I/II thinking, and the impacts of training in discipline agnostic and discipline specific contexts (organic chemistry). Using an experimental design that included pre- and post-tests, participants completed a worksheet targeting Type I/II reasoning three times over two weeks. Participants in the treatment/intervention group completed a metacognition learning module, while the controle group completed an unrelated activity. In the worksheets, participants identified the thinking type they engaged with for questions and explained their thought process. We found that having an organic chemistry background and/or belonging to a particular group (intervention/control) were correlated with differences in analytical engagement. Participants in the treatment group demonstrated more deliberate monitoring and regulation of their reasoning, whereas participants in the control group relied on rigid, superficial distinctions between thinking types. Metacognitive accuracy and regulation varied across groups.

papers.title: Divergent Two-Carbon Insertion of Alcohols
papers.abstract: Carbon-chain extension enables systematic modification of molecular frameworks, yet general two-carbon homologation of alcohols remains underdeveloped. Herein, we report a divergent two-carbon extension of primary, secondary, and tertiary alcohols through a radical–polar relay. Photocatalytic radical C–O bond cleavage merged with vinylsulfonium salt enabled a subsequent nucleophilic substitution to afford divergent two-carbon insertion products with oxygen-, nitrogen-, sulfur-, and carbon-based nucleophiles. The method tolerates alkenes, esters, carbamates, acetals, and complex molecular frameworks. Both two-carbon, and formal three-carbon homologation of alcohols are demonstrated. Intramolecular substitution provides substituted pyrrolidines or piperidine from amino alcohols. A quick access to fluspirilene, pimozide, and lidoflazine from 2,2-bis-4-fluorophenyl ethanol further demonstrated the synthetic utility.

papers.title: From Cancer to Infection: An amphiphilic ABAC Phthalocyanine for Versatile Phototherapy
papers.abstract: The development of photosensitizers capable of operating across multiple therapeutic photoprocesses remains a major challenge in photomedicine. Herein, we report a cationic amphiphilic ABAC zinc(II) phthalocyanine (ZnPc-Me) obtained by a direct [3+1] mixed cyclization strategy followed by post-functional quaternization/transalkylation. The controlled amphiphilic architecture promotes optimal membrane anchoring while suppressing aggregation in lipid environments. Due to its optimized physico-chemical and photophysical properties, ZnPc-Me acts as a multimodal photodynamic platform whose biological activity can be switched between photodynamic therapy (PDT), vascular-targeted PDT, photodynamic inactivation (PDI) or photochemical internalization (PCI) by adjusting the administration, irradiation and dosing protocols. The compound exhibits high activity in cancer models (with EC50 in nM), surpasses clinically used photosensitizers under identical conditions, and retains activity in 3D tumor spheroids. In parallel, it efficiently inactivates multidrug-resistant ESKAPE pathogens and enables photochemical internalization of a model drug through both light-before and light-after protocols, producing dose-dependent synergistic effects. Despite its high photodynamic efficacy, ZnPc-Me shows negligible dark toxicity, no hemolysis, and no epidermal penetration, ensuring a favorable safety profile for both topical and systemic applications. Overall, this work introduces a versatile design strategy for amphiphilic phthalocyanines that enables adaptive photodynamic activity across diverse biomedical applications, opening new avenues for the development of multifunctional light-responsive therapeutic systems.

papers.title: Stereospecific Conversion of Alkenyl and Epoxy Carbamates into Cyclic Carbonate Alcohols
papers.abstract: We have thoroughly explored the conversion of alkenyl and epoxy carbamates into cyclic carbonate alcohols. The substrate scope is robust, and the products are amenable to further transformations. In almost all cases, the reactions are predictably regioselective and stereospecific. The reactions can be run open to air and without precautions to exclude moisture. Indeed, H2O plays a critical role in the transformations and is added to the reactions as a key reagent.

papers.title: Directing group-free site-selective and stereoretentive C-H amination of alkanes with phenyl triazolinedione (PTAD) as a σ-acid
papers.abstract: 4-Phenyl-1,2,4-triazoline-3,5-dione (PTAD) is known as the most reactive commercially available dienophile, as it rapidly reacts with dienes at low temperatures and high dilution. In general terms, PTAD is a very soft Lewis acid, with a strong affinity towards electron rich alkenes. In this work, we report that the potent π-acid PTAD also shows a very useful and general σ-acid reactivity towards electron rich C(sp3)-H bonds, opening up its use in alkane amination reactions, as well as in late stage functionalization applications. The experimental observations over a wide range of alkanes, as well as in more functionalized substrates, indicate a carbocationic mechanism involving a hydride ion transfer of the alkane substrate to PTAD. The carbocation is very transient, as C-N bond formation proceeds generally with retention of the original configuration of a stereogenic carbon. The reaction can be run at high conversion of the alkane substrate using a catalytic amount of a gold(I)-catalyst combined with a mild proton donor such as hexafluoroisopropanol (HFIP). The reaction can often fully discriminate between very similar C-H bonds, such as cyclic alkanes over linear ones, equatorial C-H bonds over axial ones and tertiary over secondary ones. These observed reactivity orders closely follow expected trends in carbocation stability, offering a conveniently predictability. This novel C-H functionalization method does not require extensive catalyst or reagent design and offers good complementary to more conventional C-H activation or amination methodologies.

papers.title: Immunodetection of a Cell-Surface Biomarker via the Freezing of Supercooled Water Droplets
papers.abstract: Immunolabels traditionally detect biomarkers via a color change or fluorescence. The frequently weak signals from low biomarker concentrations prompted the development of numerous enzymatic amplification strategies. Although very effective for signal generation, these strategies increase the complexity, cost, and time required for immunoassays. What if water itself could generate and self-amplify a signal to detect a biomarker? Here, we demonstrate that it is possible to detect a cell-surface protein biomarker by inducing the phase change from water to ice in supercooled water droplets. Relative to enzymatic amplification, this phase change has the potential for orders-of-magnitude larger amplification factors on orders-of-magnitude shorter time scales. We engineered a recombinant ice-nucleating protein (rINpro), based on the bacterial protein InaZ, that binds to an antigen via a tetrameric antibody complex. Breast cancer cells expressing the Human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (HER2) antigen were adopted as a model system. Arrays with 96 × 10 μL droplets containing cells immunolabeled with rINpro froze at a higher average median freezing temperature (–11.2 ± 0.5 °C) than droplets with unlabeled cells (–23.4 ± 1.3 °C) and non-target cells (–25.1 ± 0.6 °C). High-speed videos of freezing droplets confirmed that the labeled cells triggered the freezing and nucleated macroscopic ice formation. As few as ca. 500 target cells were successfully detected among 10,000 non-target cells, and selective naked-eye detection of target cells was possible with a household freezer and fixed cooling period. The “cryo-assay” in this study represents a completely new approach to sensitive biomarker detection. With further development, it has vast potential for the detection of low-abundance biomarkers in research, clinical, and point-of-care immunoassay applications.

papers.title: Gas-Conditioned Message Passing Graph Neural Network for Permeability Prediction in Polymeric Membranes
papers.abstract: Designing polymeric membranes for diverse gas-separation applications remains a critical challenge. Machine learning (ML) models can significantly accelerate this effort by capturing complex relationships between polymer-gas pairs and enabling permeability prediction over an extended chemical space of gases and polymers. In this work, we present a novel ML framework, the gas-conditioned message passing neural network (GC-MPNN), that jointly combines gas descriptors and polymer chemistry in a fused neural network model. Polymers are represented at the monomer level and encoded as molecular graphs, where node and edge information is propagated through message-passing layers. Six gas species (He, H2, N2, O2, CH4, and CO2) are represented using multiple descriptor sets spanning thermodynamic, kinetic, and electrostatic properties, along with one-hot encodings and combined feature sets that include kinetic plus thermodynamic descriptors and the full physicochemical descriptor set. For each descriptor combination, model hyperparameters are optimized using Bayesian optimization within a leave-one-gas-out (LOGO) validation framework. Test performance is then evaluated on the gas species excluded entirely from the corresponding training fold (out-of-training set) and compared across descriptor sets. For most gas species, the model achieves strong predictive performance (R2 ∼ 0.86–0.96), while CO2 remains more challenging in terms of absolute prediction accuracy (R2 ∼ 0.44). Active learning sampling further improves model performance by adding a few labeled samples from the test gas species into the training set. Among the three strategies tested, deep ensemble-based sampling and random sampling show strong improvement, with R2 reaching approximately ∼ 0.95 for all gas species, while evidential regression shows less consistent improvement. The model is further evaluated on a smaller polymer-gas dataset containing hydrocarbon species (C2H4, C2H6, C3H6, C3H8, and n-C4H10) using the GC-MPNN trained only on the six base gases, achieving moderate to strong Pearson correlations (r ∼ 0.77–0.89) for these out-of-training gases. Overall, this work presents a machine learning model that can learn transferable polymer-gas relationships from known gas species and extend them to previously unseen gases.

papers.title: Probing the Softer-acid Nature of 102No2+ Compared to Alkaline Earth Metal ions via Synergistic Extraction with Sulfur Donor on Crown Ether Supported Resin
papers.abstract: Unlike other f block elements that typically exhibit +3 or higher oxidation states, nobelium (No, atomic number = 102) exists predominantly as the divalent cation in aqueous solutions. While No2+ has long been considered chemically analogous to Ca2+ and Sr2+, strong relativistic effects are predicted to alter its reactivity. In our previous study, the soft metal ion behavior of No2+ was demonstrated through complexation with crown ethers. Prompted by this implication, in this study, we performed online solid-liquid extraction experiments of 255No by employing diethyl dithiophosphate (DEDTP−) as a soft sulfur-donor ligand to probe the softer Lewis acid character of No relative to alkaline earth metals via No–S bonding. Here we report the results of the experiments and relativistic DFT calculations. In the Sr resin/HDEDTP (aqueous) system, No2+ behaves in a manner distinct from Ca2+ and Sr2+, resembling Ba2+ and Ra2+. No2+ exhibits a significantly higher extraction efficiency in the HDEDTP system than Sr2+, confirming enhanced soft Lewis acid character. The computed Gibbs free energies of extraction-complex formation are consistent with the experimental ΔG trend, validating the theoretical model. The optimized geometry revealed a No–S bond shorter than ionic radius trends, indicating stronger bonding. We attribute this distinctive behavior to unique electronic states of No. Specifically, higher electron gain in the d-orbital, stronger relativistic 7s stabilization, and closer 5f energy matching synergistically enhance covalent character of No–S bonding.

papers.title: Lewis acid-mediated borodegermylation grants access to donor- and acceptor-substituted azaboraspirobifluorenes
papers.abstract: Boron-centered spiro compounds represent a prominent platform for the design of optoelectronic materials. The orthogonally arranged π-conjugated systems around boron enhance stability toward air and moisture, facilitate processing, and allow electronic tuning through donor and acceptor substitution. Synthetic methods reported to date for the preparation of these compounds suffer from low efficiency and poor functional group tolerance, limiting the diversity of accessible electronic materials with tailored properties. Herein, we present a synthetic method leveraging the “Goldilocks” reactivity of germoles among Group 14 analogues to achieve a highly efficient and versatile AlCl3-catalyzed borodegermylation reaction, granting access to donor- and acceptor-functionalized azaboraspirobifluorenes. Furtheremore, the reaction efficiency can be enhanced by employing the sublimed catalyst and the use of an additive. Owing to their high stability, comparatively low toxicity and non-pyrophoric nature, the use of organogermanium compounds provides a more robust and safer alternative to methods that rely on other organometallic reagents.

papers.title: Imitation and Accuracy in Automated Electronic-Structure Method Selection
Research Progress and Applications of the Fundamental Principles of Soft Ionization Mass Spectrometry
papers.abstract: (1. Guangdong Huisheng Testing Technology Co., Ltd.) Abstract: Soft ionization mass spectrometry is widely applied in fields such as pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, environmental monitoring, and food safety; however, its fundamental principles remain subject to considerable debate, rendering it a "black-box" technology. This review summarizes the basic principles of electrospray ionization (ESI), matrix-assisted laser desorption (MALDI), and desorption electrospray ionization (DESI), and establishes "one theory, two equations, and three instruments" as the theoretical and practical foundation for soft ionization mass spectrometry. Furthermore, this study discusses the electromagnetic applications of soft ionization mass spectrometry, thereby expanding its scope of research and application.

papers.title: Tension-Limited Leaflet-Asymmetry Budding Predicts the Size and Rate of Tumour Ectosome Shedding
papers.abstract: Fatty-acid protocells growing by outer-leaflet monomer uptake accumulate a transbilayer area imbalance that is relieved by budding once the reduced imbalance Δa exceeds a critical value, as described by area-difference elasticity (ADE). It is tempting to read modern tumour ectosome shedding as the same physics. We show that the naive transfer fails, and derive the version that does not. A protocell is osmotically relaxed; the plasma membrane of a cancer cell is under tension (σ ≈ 0.01–0.1 mN/m), which imposes an area cost absent from the protocell treatment. Replacing the shape-instability criterion with an explicit energy balance for bud formation gives a threshold in the differential leaflet tension, Δτ_c = sqrt(8κΣ)/h with Σ = σ + K_A h^2/R^2, and a bud radius at threshold r* = sqrt(2κ/Σ) that is independent of both h and K_A. Retaining the finite-parent term K_A h^2/R^2 is essential: in the tension-free limit it acts as an effective tension, so the threshold does not vanish but tends to Δa_c → sqrt(2κ/K_A)/h = 0.21–0.87, equivalently 1.21–1.87 in the convention where a sphere carries unit reduced area difference. The O(1) ADE criterion assumed for protocells is thereby recovered as a derived result. The stored imbalance at threshold pays for exactly 1 + R^2 σ/(K_A h^2) buds, independent of κ: one for a tension-free vesicle, which therefore divides, and 11-2600 for a tense plasma membrane, which sheds a burst of nano-vesicles. The protocell growth kinetics map exactly onto flippase/scramblase imbalance under γ → 2a_L j. Using bending rigidities measured on giant plasma membrane vesicles (κ = 5.4–35 k_BT, including the metastatic line MDA-MB-231), the model predicts bud diameters of 43–346 nm, overlapping measured cancer extracellular vesicles, at a threshold requiring translocation of only 0.09–0.76 mol% of plasma-membrane lipid. Because a single TMEM16F scramblase translocates 45 000 lipids per second while the critical net flux is below one lipid per second per square micron, the thermodynamic threshold is not the regulated quantity: the shedding rate is. Reported secretion rates of 60–80 EV per cell per hour correspond to a net outward flux of 0.2–1 lipid per square micrometre per second, a calibration rather than a test of the model. Two falsification tests on the threshold locus, to which shedding pins the membrane — the bud radius falls as the inverse square root of the membrane tension, and grows as the square root of the bending rigidity — distinguish this mechanism from ESCRT-dependent biogenesis. We argue explicitly against reading the size agreement between protocells and tumour vesicles as evolutionary atavism.

papers.title: Meropenem degradation does not necessarily eliminate antibacterial activity: responses of model and environmental bacterial isolates
papers.abstract: Carbapenems can degrade rapidly in aquatic systems, and disappearance of the parent compound is often interpreted as loss of antibacterial activity. Here, we compared the antibacterial effects of intact meropenem with those of a meropenem mixture incubated for eight days in the presence of biofilm-covered moving-bed biofilm reactor carriers. During incubation, parent meropenem became undetectable, while several transformation products (TPs) retaining a closed β-lactam ring, a key structural feature for antibacterial activity, formed and persisted through the incubation period. The intact antibiotic and the incubated meropenem mixture containing TPs were tested against Escherichia coli, Pseudomonas fluorescens and two environmental isolates, CIS1 and CIR3, using optical density and viable cell counts. While intact meropenem strongly reduced viable counts of E. coli, P. fluorescens and CIS1, CIR3 was able to grow in its presence. In contrast, the incubated meropenem TPs mixture exhibited lower toxicity overall. Little or no TP inhibition was detected for P. fluorescens and E. coli, while CIS1 showed a weaker and time-dependent response. CIR3 was not suppressed by the mixture. Although the observed responses were subtle, the results show that disappearance of parent meropenem does not necessarily coincide with complete loss of meropenem-derived biological effects. The findings highlight that meropenem TPs should be considered when evaluating the environmental relevance of meropenem degradation and its potential contribution to selective pressure of antibiotics.

papers.title: MaRs: A Universal Python Library for Steady-State and Time-Resolved EPR Simulations
papers.abstract: MaRs is an open-source Python library for the simulation and fitting of electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectra. MaRs supports simulations of field-swept and frequency-swept continuous-wave EPR, accounting for various spin-sublevel polarizations. Moreover, MaRs is capable of simulating complete 2D time-resolved EPR spectra (in field-time domain). The latter can be computed in different levels of theoretical complexity. First, the time evolution can be computed either with kinetic rate equations, which describe population transfer, or in full Liouville space, which captures coherence dynamics. Second, the relaxation pathways in timeresolved simulations can be specified either through intuitive rate parameters that are automatically expanded into the Lindblad master-equation form, or derived microscopically using the Bloch-Redfield formalism. To handle physically complex relaxation scenarios, MaRs provides automatic thermal-balance enforcement and composition operations that allow multicomponent relaxation models to be assembled from simple building blocks. Built on PyTorch (popular platform for machine learning development), MaRs leverages operations on both CPU and CUDA (GPU) backends. We demonstrate MaRs time-resolved EPR capabilities as well the differences and limitations of each built-in approach to time-domain simulations on the examples of coupled triplet-doublet pairs and systems exhibiting the reverse intersystem crossing phenomenon. Separately, we validate stationary EPR simulations across diverse spin systems, including high-spin complexes, achieving excellent agreement with established packages. We also show the possibilities of parameter fitting framework, applicable to all spectrum types implemented in MaRs, that supports multiple optimization strategies and uncertainty quantification.

papers.title: Non-Isobaric Is Not Enough: Gap-Merge Safety for Unambiguous Peptide Readout
papers.abstract: Selecting a set of non-isobaric amino acids is the standard way to guarantee unambiguous readout when peptide sequences are used to carry information. We show it is insufficient. Because tandem MS reads residues as differences between consecutive fragment masses, a single missing b/y ion merges two adjacent residues into one observed gap; if that merged gap aliases a single residue mass, the decoder does not register a dropout but emits one confident, wrong residue. Non-isobaricity cannot prevent this, because the colliding quantity is a sum rather than a residue. We formalize the missing condition—gap-merge safety, |m(a) +m(b)−m(c)| > τ for all a, b, c in the alphabet—as a decidable predicate with a machine-checked soundness proof in Lean 4, and characterize the collision structure of the proteinogenic alphabet exhaustively: beyond the Leu/Ile isobar and the Gln/Lys near-isobar, exactly two summed-gap collisions exist, Gly + Gly = Asn and Gly + Ala = Gln, making glycine disproportionately expensive. In simulation, alphabets satisfying gap-merge safety produce zero silent errors at every fragment dropout rate from 0 to 0.4, where alphabets chosen by non-isobaricity alone produce 1.0% to 6.9%; every failure becomes a detectable erasure rather than a silent substitution.

papers.title: From Promotion to Poisoning: Temperature- and Coverage-Dependent Effects of Trace Fe on the Hydrogen Evolution Activity of Pt
papers.abstract: Trace iron impurities can strongly alter the alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), yet how temperature governs their surface accumulation and kinetic consequences remains poorly understood. Here, the influence of 0–60 ppb Fe impurities on polycrystalline Pt was systematically examined in 0.1 M KOH over 280–336 K. Fe addition progressively suppressed the hydrogen underpotential-deposition (Hupd) charge, indicating blockage of Pt sites by Fe-derived surface species, while this suppression was substantially mitigated at elevated temperature. Despite this site blocking, 10–20 ppb Fe enhanced the HER current, whereas further Fe addition caused pronounced deactivation, particularly at 280–298 K. Wide-potential-range voltammetry revealed electrochemical responses consistent with hydroxide-like Fe species undergoing an Fe(II)/Fe(III)-type redox transition, with the Fe-associated anodic charge decreasing markedly at 336 K. Apparent thermodynamic analyses further indicated that Fe-induced site blocking cannot be described by adsorption on a single population of independent, equivalent sites. Most importantly, correlation of the Hupd-derived blocked-site fraction with the Tafel slope revealed three coverage-dependent regimes: kinetic promotion at low Fe coverage, predominantly site-number-limited deactivation at intermediate coverage, and severe kinetic inhibition at high coverage. These results demonstrate that trace Fe does not behave as a simple inert poison but dynamically modifies the Pt/Fe-derived interface in a coverage- and temperature-dependent manner. The findings establish electrolyte temperature and trace-impurity coverage as coupled parameters controlling alkaline HER kinetics on Pt.

papers.title: The pH effect in hydrogen evolution is a consequence of creating a solvated hydroxide ion
papers.abstract: The hydrogen evolution reaction is orders of magnitude faster in acid than in base on the same electrode, a pH effect that first-principles calculations have not quantitatively reproduced. We trace this failure to the treatment of the ions: standard density functionals with standard solvation treatments undersolvate hydroxide–the ionic product of alkaline hydrogen evolution–by more than 1 eV against experiment and coupled cluster benchmarks, an error that tracks the functional’s self-interaction error. A screened hybrid functional with reduced self-interaction error yields Au(111) Volmer barriers whose acidalkaline difference falls within the measured range of onset-potential separations, whereas semi-local functionals predict zero to three times the measured value. Quantitative computational electrocatalysis therefore demands functionals benchmarked jointly against ion solvation thermochemistry and molecule-surface energetics.

papers.title: WITHDRAWN
papers.abstract: Withdrawn at the authors' request because it did not comply with journal policies.

papers.title: Crystal-to-crystal solar energy storage in a hydrogen bonded dianthracene lattice retrocyclized by heat or e-beam
papers.abstract: Solid-state (SS) systems for molecular solar thermal (MOST) energy storage are desirable for their simplicity and higher energy storage density compared to solution-based MOST systems, but it is difficult to design systems that both achieve high conversion to the metastable photoproduct and undergo thermally-driven release of the stored heat without melting. Anthracene (An) photocycloaddition to dianthracene (diAn) can proceed to high conversion in the solid state, but few crystalline Ans are appropriately aligned for dimerization, and even fewer diAns thermally retrocyclize without melting. By combining 9-pyridyl anthracene and 9-anthracenecarboxylic acid, we form hydrogen-bonded (H-bonded) and π-stacked chains that undergo high-conversion single-crystal-to-single-crystal photocycloaddition under simulated sunlight. Disordered packing in the lattice produces a mixture of the pyridyl-carboxylate “heterodimer,” the pyridyl homodimer, and the carboxylic acid homodimer. Calorimetry reveals that the H-bonded diAn product has a large separation between its thermal retrocyclization and melting temperatures, allowing the material to be cycled in the solid state. The H-bonded diAn lattice is also shown to undergo crystal-to-crystal retrocyclization under e-beam exposure. This work presents an easily-assembled all-SS crystal-to-crystal cyclable MOST system and demonstrates that H-bonding can be leveraged to increase the gap between thermal retrocyclization and melting.

papers.title: Whole-Enzyme Reactive Free-Energy Simulations with a Universal Machine Learning Interatomic Potential: Catalytic Mechanism and Mutational Effects of PETase
papers.abstract: Universal machine learning interatomic potentials (uMLIPs) have emerged as powerful tools for atomistic simulations that achieve quantum mechanical accuracy at significantly reduced computational cost. Yet, their direct application to complex enzymatic reactions remains challenging owing to the immense size of solvated enzyme systems and the scarcity of transition-state structures in training data. In this study, we demonstrate that PFP (PreFerred Potential), a pretrained uMLIP across 96 elements in nature, simulates the complete hydrolytic cycle of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) catalyzed by PETase as a single reactive domain of approximately 20,000 atoms, without multiscale partitioning or system-specific fine-tuning. Umbrella-sampling simulations revealed stepwise mechanisms for both acylation and deacylation through distinct tetrahedral intermediates. The computed rate-limiting deacylation barrier of 20.5 ± 0.3 kcal/mol is in agreement with the range of 18.0–18.7 kcal/mol inferred from experimental turnover numbers. The PFP-based simulations further capture catalytic consequences of point mutations from loss of function (D177N, M132A) to predicted activity enhancement (D157N) and reveal that simultaneous neutralization of three distal acidic residues which are located more than 10 Å from the active site raises the activation barrier due to a collective long-range electrostatic effect that emerges naturally in the partition-free treatment. These findings demonstrate that the pretrained uMLIP, PFP, can provide physically plausible free-energy profiles for enzymatic reaction mechanisms and capture mutational effects, providing a powerful platform for rational enzyme design.

papers.title: Mechanistic characterization of a bacterial terpene synthase that bifurcates to produce both 6/10- and 5/11-bicyclic diterpenes
papers.abstract: The mechanism of the bacterial diterpene synthase ChtS from Chitinophaga japonensis was investigated. ChtS was found to produce two major diterpenes, 5/11-bicyclic chitino-2,5,9-triene (11) and the previously uncharacterized 6/10-bicyclic chitinoeunicellene (12). Deuterium labeling experiments, site-directed mutagenesis, and isolation of minor products cembrene C (13), cembrene A (14), and chitinol (15) support initial 1,14-cyclization, two sequential 1,2-hydride shifts, prior to bifurcation to 11 or 12, ultimately retaining the E-configured C-2/C-3 alkene.

papers.title: When Does MMLCT Emerge? The Role of Crystal Packing in the Photophysics of Pt(II) Polymorphs
papers.abstract: Aggregation-induced metal-metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MMLCT) is widely used to rationalize the red-shifted and broadened emission observed in Pt(II) complexes. However, the underlying mechanism of MMLCT formation and its exact relationship with photoluminescence remain poorly understood. Polymorphism provides an ideal platform to isolate aggregation effects from molecular structural changes, because the same molecule can pack into different packing arrangements leading to strikingly different photophysical properties. By combining QM/MM calculations, excited-state electronic structure analysis, vibronic spectral simulations, and radiative rate constant calculations, we investigate two polymorphs exhibiting distinct photophysical behaviors. For the investigated compounds, the formation of the excimeric MMLCT species is only possible for one polymorph and that the trimer is the minimum aggregate needed for the MMLCT formation. The MMLCT species possess distinct properties from those of the rest of aggregates and the monomer, including vibronically unresolved redshifted absorption and emission spectra and larger photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQY). An in-depth analysis of the computed results evidences that the redistribution of the electronic density in the MMLCT states leads to a different electron-vibrational coupling scenario, where the contributions of high-frequency ligand vibrations to the total reorganization energy are reduced and low-frequency Pt···Pt···Pt stretching modes become more prominent. The MMLCT species also enhances the radiative decay through enhanced spin-orbit coupling and transition dipole moments. These findings establish a direct relationship between aggregation structure, electronic structure, and photophysical properties and provide a modelling framework for understanding the formation of excimers in Pt(II) complexes in their solid states.

papers.title: Steroid Thioesters to Target Golgi Apparatus
papers.abstract: Despite Golgi apparatus plays a central role in lipid and protein trafficking, the biomedical potential of Golgitargeting supramolecular assemblies remains underexplored. While recent studies showed that peptide thioesters localize to the Golgi, it is unclear whether steroid thioesters can exhibit similar targeting behavior. Here, we designed and synthesized steroid-based thioesters by conjugating a thioester group and an NBD fluorophore to bile acids (BAs). Live-cell fluorescence imaging revealed that steroid thioesters localize to the Golgi apparatus, further confirming the utility of thioesters as a reactive warhead for Golgi targeting via localized S-palmitoylation. While BA-thioesters accumulate at the Golgi, their accumulation is slower than peptide thioesters. Unlike the peptide thioesters, these steroid conjugates displayed excellent cellular compatibility, showing minimal cytotoxicity. O-acetylation of BAs also modulates the dynamics of Golgi targeting. Our findings demonstrate that steroid thioesters can serve as Golgi-targeting motifs, expanding the pool of organelle-directed bioconjugates and providing a new scaffold for the design of functional molecules to reprogram palmitoylation-associated processes.

papers.title: Helium Inclusion in a Mixed-Anion Framework Under Pressure: Discovery of Tetragonal BaFClHe and the Diamond Anvil Cell Sensor Paradox
papers.abstract: Helium has the highest ionization potential among all elements (24.59 eV) and is notoriously chemically inert. Here, utilizing density functional theory (DFT-PBE-PAW) and density functional perturbation theory (DFPT), we report the discovery of a stable quaternary helium insertion compound in a mixed-anion matrix, BaFClHe, synthesized under moderate pressures of 35 GPa. In the tetragonal matlockite-derived framework (𝑃 4 𝑛𝑚𝑚, 𝑍 = 2), neutral helium atoms reside in square antiprismatic cavities (2𝑏 sites) without covalent charge transfer (𝑞 = +0.0395𝑒, 1𝑠1.962𝑝0.00). The phase is thermodynamically protected against binary decomposition (2 BaFClHe → BaF2 + BaCl2 + 2 He) by a substantial enthalpy barrier of +67.22 kJ/mol, while DFPT calculations confirm complete dynamical stability with zero imaginary phonon modes across the Brillouin zone. The four isolated high-frequency optical modes (417.9cm−1[𝐵1𝑔], 443.0cm−1[𝐴2𝑢], 548.3cm−1[𝐸𝑢], 567.9cm−1[𝐸𝑔]) provide distinct spectroscopic fingerprints for in situ detection. Strikingly, while pure host BaFCl undergoes a transition to an ultra-dense hexagonal phase (𝑃 63 𝑚𝑚𝑐, ZrBeSi-type) at 35 GPa, helium insertion completely reverses the polymorph stability by over 186.2 kJ/mol, demonstrating guest-induced structural templating. Because Sm2+:BaFCl crystals have served as standard luminescence pressure sensors with helium as the hydrostatic pressure-transmitting medium for four decades, this discovery demonstrates that helium is not an inert spectator fluid, resolving an overlooked fundamental interaction in experimental high-pressure physics.

papers.title: Galvanic Coupling Links Heterogeneous and Molecular Palladium Catalysis in Aerobic Alcohol Oxidation
papers.abstract: Thermochemical catalytic reactions are often composed of coupled electrochemical redox reactions, which may even generate the active catalyst itself. Here we show that oxygen reduction on heterogeneous palladium drives corrosion of Pd(0) through galvanic coupling: electrons released by Pd(0) oxidation are consumed by oxygen reduction on the same catalyst, and the soluble Pd(II) forms a homogeneous complex which catalyzes benzyl alcohol oxidation. Combining corrosion measurements with quantification of Pd(II) and reaction products, we find that supplying more oxygen raises the catalyst potential and accelerates Pd(II) generation and alcohol oxidation. Applying equivalent electrochemical potentials in the absence of oxygen reproduces Pd(II) generation and alcohol oxidation with similar sensitivity to the catalyst potential. Diverting the anodic reaction to a sacrificial anode suppresses Pd(II) supply and thus the thermochemical reaction rate. Hence, the primary role of oxygen is to set the potential for generating the active catalyst, while palladium corrosion is the kinetic link to thermochemical turnover. Together, our results show that galvanic coupling provides a framework that links electrochemistry and thermochemical catalysis.

papers.title: Deactivation of SrTiO3 slurry and model photocatalysts during overall water splitting: Impact of Sr leaching on stability
papers.abstract: Photocatalytic hydrogen evolution has been investigated for over five decades as a potential route to sustainable hydrogen production. SrTiO 3 (STO) is a benchmark photocatalyst because its band-edge positions enable overall water splitting. However, rapid charge-carrier recombination and sluggish interfacial redox kinetics limit light-to-product conversion efficiency, requiring suitable reduction and oxidation cocatalysts. While extensive research has addressed the activity and stability of cocatalysts, the stability of STO itself under reaction conditions has received less attention. Here, we investigate the deactivation of Pt-modified STO slurry and model photocatalysts during overall water splitting under UV illumination. Pt was used as stable hydrogen-evolution cocatalyst while the oxygen-evolution cocatalyst was deliberately omitted to assess how hole transfer affects photocatalyst stability. Both slurry and model photocatalysts exhibit pronounced activity decay within tens of minutes under irradiation at 365 nm and 20 mW cm -2 . STO single crystals modified with dewetted Pt nanoparticles were used as a model photocatalyst and characterized by ex situ and in situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy and inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry, and by scanning electron microscopy, scanning transmission electron microscopy, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The results show that photoinduced Sr leaching into the aqueous phase contributes substantially to photocatalyst deactivation. We propose that, in the absence of oxygen-evolution cocatalyst and hole scavenger, sluggish hole transfer at the STO/liquid interface initially favors lattice-oxygen oxidation and O 2 evolution, thereby destabilizing the SrTiO 3 surface and promoting Sr dissolution. Whereas STO regions covered by Pt nanoparticles remain compositionally unchanged (and enable electron transfer for Pt-mediated H 2 generation), exposed STO regions become Sr-depleted due to Sr leaching under UV irradiation and transform into a Ti-rich, TiO 2 -like surface phase. Unfavorable band alignment between bulk and Sr-depleted STO together with a high defect density within the Sr-depleted STO surface phase are proposed as main cause for charge recombination, hindering interfacial hole transfer, which ultimately suppresses photocatalytic activity.

papers.title: Heterotypic Imine Cross-links Reshape Phase Behavior and Relaxations in Polystyrene/Poly(ethylene glycol) Vitrimer Blends
papers.abstract: Converting an immiscible polymer blend into a vitrimer is a powerful strategy for enhancing miscibility while still preserving viscoelasticity. In vitrimer blends, the chains bear dynamic covalent cross-links that undergo associative exchange – new bonds form before old bonds break, permitting the blend to maintain both network connectivity and topological fluidity. Recent studies have demonstrated that vitrimer blend phase behavior results from competition between homotypic cross-links between identical polymers and heterotypic cross-links between dissimilar species. In this work, we investigate binary vitrimer blends in which the two polymer components exclusively form heterotypic linkages. The blends are composed of a polystyrene (PS) copolymer and a telechelic poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) connected by dynamic imine linkages. We prepare blends with varying PEG weight fractions and chain lengths. In contrast to classical Flory-Huggins theory, which predicts PS and PEG are immiscible at ambient temperature, hybrid molecular dynamics/Monte Carlo simulations, experiments, and theory demonstrate that PS/PEG vitrimer blends assemble into a stoichiometrically balanced network that coexists with a PEG-rich domain – phase behavior analogous to off-eutectic metal alloys. Dynamic cross-linking produces fast and slow relaxation regimes, enhancing the vitrimer blend elasticity relative to linear and graft copolymer blend controls.
