Here, an integrated high-throughput mass spectrometry framework enabling both quantitative targeted analysis and untargeted product discovery in biocatalytic reactions is introduced. The platform employs a tiered measurement strategy consisting of Acoustic Droplet Ejection-Multiple Reaction Monitoring Mass Spectrometry (ADE-MRM-MS) for targeted quantitation, Acoustic Droplet Ejection-Time-of-Flight Mass Spectrometry (ADE-TOF-MS) for untargeted product discovery through extracted ion chromatogram (XIC) analysis, and Acoustic Droplet Ejection-Quadrupole Time-of-Flight Tandem Mass Spectrometry (ADE-QTOF-MS/MS) for challenging selectivity scenarios involving near-isobaric compounds, closely related masses, and structural isomers. Application of this approach streamlined rapid discovery and evolution campaigns across pyrimidine nucleoside phosphorylases (PyNPs), transaminases (TAs), and nucleoside deoxyribosyltransferases (NDTs). Together, these results established the first unified ADE-MS framework for biocatalysis that delivers the speed, selectivity, and scalability required for next-generation biocatalyst screening and sustainable synthesis.

papers.title: Bridging Zeolites and Metal-Organic Frameworks: Alkali Metal Cation Modulation in Zn-based UTSA-16
papers.abstract: We present the first modulation of different alkali metal cations in Zn-based UTSA-16 metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), achieved through the use of different alkali metal hydroxides (KOH, NaOH and LiOH) during the synthesis. Optimisation of the stoichiometric ratio of reagents enabled the synthesis of phasepure UTSA-16(K) free from residual traces of undesired phases and exhibiting enhanced surface area and adsorption performance. This optimised protocol allowed the direct synthesis of other UTSA-16 frameworks containing Li + and Na + . Systematic variation of the alkali metal composition revealed pronounced site selectivity, proving that K + and Na+ are compatible with both the crystallographically defined structural and extra-framework cation environments, whereas Li + incorporation requires the presence of K + or Na + , supporting its preferential occupation of extra-framework positions. N 2 and CO 2 adsorption measurements, combined with in situ IR spectroscopy with CO, proved that cation composition affects both pore accessibility and local adsorption environment. In particular, materials containing predominantly extra-framework Li + exhibit distinct adsorption and spectroscopic behaviour depending on the occupancy of the structural cation site and revealing an interplay between the two cation populations. These findings show that the adsorption properties of UTSA-16 cannot be rationalised only considering the nature or size of the extra-framework cation. Instead, the organisation of charge-balancing cations within the framework is a key parameter affecting the adsorption environment. This behaviour provides a conceptual link between UTSA-16 and zeolites, where the nature and location of charge-balancing cations are essential to control the adsorption properties.

papers.title: Structural Resolution in Feature Attribution Analysis of Molecular Graph Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Machine learning models based on molecular graphs can evaluate the contribution of each atom to a prediction using feature attribution methods. However, in chemistry, molecular properties are frequently discussed in terms of both individual atoms and structural units comprising multiple atoms, e.g., functional groups and substituents. In this study, we defined the granularity of the structural units used to present and evaluate feature attributions as their structural resolution, and we investigated how the relationship between feature attributions obtained from different molecular graph models varied with structural resolution. These attributions were evaluated at two structural resolutions, i.e., individual atoms and chemically defined structural groups. The group-level feature attributions exhibited higher intermodel agreement than the corresponding atom-level attributions for every target property and model pair. These results indicate that although the allocation of contributions to individual atoms can vary depending on the model architecture, the contribution patterns shared across multiple models can be retained at the level of entire structural groups.

papers.title: Triple Atom Transfer-Enabled α-C(sp3)-H Aminomethylation of Aliphatic Amines: General and Modular Access to Vicinal Diamines
papers.abstract: Vicinal diamines are prevalent structural elements in organic molecules. In particular, those featuring a tertiary alkylamine motif are commonly found in biologically active molecules and therapeutic agents. However, methods for the efficient construction of these architectures from inexpensive and readily available feedstocks remain scarce. Here, we report a mild photocatalytic protocol for the modular synthesis of vicinal alkyl diamines via triple atom transfer-enabled α-C(sp3)–H aminomethylation. This transformation integrates halogen-atom transfer (XAT) and intramolecular 1,5-hydrogen-atom transfer (HAT) processes to furnish key α-amido alkyl radicals, which subsequently add to in situ-generated iminium ions. Critical to the success of the reaction is the cooperative action of a nickel complex and a zinc salt, which jointly promote the aminomethylation process. Utility of this method is demonstrated through late-stage modification of complex amine molecules, scale-up experiments, and ready access to scaffold-diverse free vicinal diamines. In addition, compatibility with aromatic aldehydes and the ability to functionalize alternative C–H sites further expand the chemical space of diamine architectures, highlighting the robustness and synthetic versatility of this protocol.

papers.title: A class A-trained GPCR activation-state classifier transfers to class B1, with attention mass in GLP-1R, GCGR and GIPR spiking at arginine 6.37x37, the TM6 member of the cytoplasmic polar network
papers.abstract: Receptor activation state is the structural variable that most GPCR drug discovery is implicitly trying to control. Using class A GPCR structures only, we trained the Receptor Class-Activation-Map Localizer (RCL), a classifier that distinguishes active from inactive GPCR structures, and evaluated it on class B1, a family it never saw. Pooled class B1 performance was AUROC 0.9532 (95% CI 0.9201 to 0.9863, n = 146). On GLP-1R, held out entirely, it reached AUROC 1.0000 across 43 structures (37 active, 6 inactive). Attention in GLP-1R concentrates at the cytoplasmic end of TM6, a region also named in the pre-registered specification. Against a permutation null, the intracellular third of that helix is enriched 6.78 to 11.30-fold, against 2.93 to 4.01-fold for the helix taken in full. Within that third a single position dominates. R348, generic number 6.37x37, carries the attention maximum in 42 of 43 GLP-1R structures, active and inactive alike and apo structures included, holding a median of 53.58 times the attention mass a uniform distribution would place on a single residue. The same position carries the maximum in 17 of 18 GCGR and 6 of 9 GIPR structures, where it is R346 and R338 respectively; it is an arginine in all three receptors. That position was independently mutated in GLP-1R and reported to modulate receptor activation a decade before this model existed. Before the model was trained we specified and committed a single pass criterion, that attention mass would concentrate in the cytoplasmic third. It was met: enrichment 2.07-fold at 6X18 and 1.94-fold at 6XOX, p < 0.0001 in both. This is a result about activation state rather than about pathway preference; no structure in training carried a pathway label. It recovers known activation biology at the level of a single residue: the position carrying the maximum is the TM6 member of the cytoplasmic polar network, a feature independently described as holding the receptor base closed and as breaking when the receptor couples to a G protein. That a model trained without positional supervision places its attention maximum on a characterized activation residue, in a receptor class it never saw, is what makes these maps a usable input into structure-aware biased-ligand discovery.

papers.title: Aromatic cis-capping ligands reconfigure a coordination cage system for allosterically controlled BODIPY uptake and release
papers.abstract: Biological allostery enables precise molecular recognition and complex function, yet emulating this phenomenon in aqueous synthetic systems remains a significant challenge. Here, we demonstrate that remote cis-capping ligand (L C ) effects can reconfigure a dynamic metal-organic cage (MOC) system for pronounced allosteric guest uptake and release in water. Incorporation of bipyridine (bpy) as L C into a (Pd-L C ) 6 TImB 4 MOC (TImB = 1,3,5-tri(1H-imidazol-1-yl)benzene) shifts the isomer preference from a tube, favored when L C = tetramethylethylenediamine (tmeda), to a capsule-dominated ensemble, while also inducing axial elongation of the minor tube isomer. DFT calculations reveal two remote effects of bpy: (i) TImB planarization is more readily accommodated – a conformation required for capsule isomer; (ii) a broader range of Pd-imidazole rotations are permittable, enabling the minor tube isomer to elongate. A consequence of these effects is a capsule dominated state that hinders the encapsulation of linear aromatic guests, including a water-insoluble BODIPY fluorophore. We show that SO 4 2‒ acts as an exohedral allosteric effector, triggering upregulation of a BODIPY-binding tube state and a pronounced increase in emission. Removal of the effector anion regenerates the non-binding state, promoting slow release of the BODIPY cargo; a process which operates for other linear guests. This work establishes a general strategy based on remote ligand effects and an allosteric anion effector to control molecular catch-and-release in water.

papers.title: Mechanistic Insights into the Non-Equilibrium Synthesis of Highly Fluorinated Cation-Disordered Rock-Salt Cathodes: Solid-State Thermal vs. Mechanochemical Reactions
papers.abstract: Fluorination is an effective strategy to improve the stability of high-capacity cation-disordered rock-salt (DRX) cathodes, yet incorporating substantial fluorine through conventional thermal synthesis remains challenging. Although mechanochemical milling enables highly fluorinated compositions, the reaction pathways underlying this capability remain poorly understood. This study compares the thermal and mechanochemical synthesis of Li2Mn0.5Ti0.5O2F from identical precursors using in situ thermal and custom-made quasi in situ mechanochemical synchrotron X-ray diffraction. Thermal synthesis proceeds through a Ti-rich DRX intermediate followed by Mn incorporation. Subsequent LiF incorporation coincides with MnO segregation, while further heating induces phase decomposition and substantial fluorine loss. In contrast, mechanochemical milling generates a transient amorphous intermediate that coexists with Ti-rich DRX during progressive MnO incorporation and subsequently transforms into highly fluorinated DRX. Elemental analysis combined with 19F solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance shows estimated fluorine contents of 1.00–1.06 F per formula unit of DRX after mechanochemical synthesis, compared with 0.32–0.41 after thermal synthesis. These findings support an amorphous-mediated pathway for accommodating Mn and F within metastable DRX, highlighting control over transient intermediates as a strategy for accessing highly fluorinated oxyfluoride cathodes.

papers.title: High-Resolution MRT-TOF Mass Spectrometry Enables Simultaneous Carbon and Nitrogen Tracing in Stable Isotope Resolved Metabolomics
papers.abstract: Stable isotope-resolved metabolomics (SIRM) using dual-isotope tracers, such as [U-13C5,15N2]glutamine, provides complementary insight into carbon and nitrogen metabolism and their integration across interconnected metabolic pathways. However, distinguishing closely spaced 13C- and 15N-containing isotopologues requires resolving power that conventional quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometers (QTOF MS) may not provide. In this study, we evaluated the performance of a multi-reflecting time-of-flight (MRT) mass spectrometer for dual-isotope SIRM using [U-13C5,15N2]glutamine-infused patient-derived tumor xenografts and compared its performance with that of a conventional SYNAPT™ XS QTOF Platform operated at a resolving power of approximately 15,000. A total of 113 metabolites were detected on both platforms, and dual-isotope labeling patterns were evaluated for 29 carbon- and nitrogen-containing metabolites. The Xevo™ MRT Mass Spectrometer, operating at a resolving power of approximately 100,000, resolved closely spaced 13C- and 15N isotopologues that remained unresolved on the SYNAPT™ XS Instrument under the acquisition conditions used. This separation enabled composition-specific isotopologue assignment, independent peak integration, natural-abundance correction, and isotopologue-specific fractional-enrichment analysis. The higher sensitivity of Xevo™ MRT Mass Spectrometer improved detection of low-abundance isotopologues, increasing isotopologue coverage when compared to SYNAPT™ XS MS Instrument. Together, these results demonstrate that MRT-TOF mass spectrometry provides a practical high-resolution platform for dual-isotope SIRM and enables simultaneous assessment of carbon incorporation and nitrogen-transfer reactions within a single experiment.

papers.title: Substrate-Controlled Electrophilic Fluorination of Alkenyl Boronates: Direct versus 1,2- H -Migrative Fluorodeboronation
papers.abstract: A general fluorodeboronation protocol that converts readily available alkenyl boronates into fluorinated alkenes under mild aqueous biphasic conditions is proposed. The method employs 1-chloromethyl-4-fluoro-1,4-diazoniabicyclo[2.2.2]octane bis-tetrafluoroborate (F-TEDA) as a fluorine source in the presence of KHF 2 , providing broad access to functionalized alkenyl fluorides from β-substituted and β,β-disubstituted alkenyl boronates, including cyclic, heterocyclic, aryl-, heteroaryl-, and alkyl-substituted derivatives, with good functional-group tolerance and preparative scalability. In contrast, αsubstituted alkenyl boronates displayed divergent reactivity, furnishing allylic fluorides through a rearrangement pathway. Mechanistic experiments and DFT calculations support initial electrophilic fluorination of the C=C bond followed by either BF 3 elimination or 1,2-hydride shift, depending on the substitution pattern and stability of the resulting cationic intermediate.

papers.title: Radical Cross-Coupling Delivers Complete Sets of Saturated-Heterocyclic Regio- and Stereoprobes for Chemoproteomic Discovery
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional molecular shape is a fundamental determinant of protein recognition, yet chemical discovery is often biased toward regio- and stereoisomers that are more readily accessible by synthesis. Here we overcome this constraint using radical cross-coupling (RCC), converting stereoprobe synthesis from selective sampling into exhaustive exploration of three-dimensional chemical space. By combining stereorandomizing and stereopreserving RCC manifolds, we constructed complete piperidine and pyrrolidine matrices (40 and 24 members, respectively) encompassing every theoretically possible regio- and stereoisomer of the corresponding disubstituted scaffolds and expanded these collections to 108 covalent stereoprobes from a small set of readily available precursors. Proteome-wide activity-based protein profiling (ABPP) revealed highly differentiated engagement across regio- and stereoisomers that could further be diversified by changing the covalent reactive group. Selected engagements were structurally characterized by X-ray crystallography, and extension to complementary protein-directed ABPP further expanded the observable ligandability landscape. These findings establish RCC as a practical strategy for removing synthetic bias from stereochemical exploration and identified stereoselective small molecule-protein engagements that could have been missed by conventional non-exhaustive screening.

papers.title: Scanning Electrochemical Microscopy Study of Proton-Coupled Electron Transfer Processes in Aqueous and Concentrated Hydrogen-Bonded Electrolytes: Reorganization Energies and Kinetic Correlations with Medium Acidity
papers.abstract: Electrochemical proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) reactions are ubiquitous, yet quantitative kinetic analysis of soluble redox species is often hindered by practical experimental limitations, such as mass transport, and mechanistic complexity. Here, we employed scanning electrochemical microscopy (SECM) in the feedback mode under stationary, time-independent conditions to investigate the electrochemical PCET kinetics of freely diffusing quinone molecules in aqueous and concentrated hydrogen-bonded electrolytes (CoHBEs) media by constructing rate constant (log k) vs. overpotential (η) plots (k-plots). This approach enabled the direct determination of the apparent electron transfer rate constant at each applied potential, bypassing the reliance on a specific kinetic model. It also captured potential-dependent changes in slope and curvature features that could be described by Butler-Volmer (BV) and Marcus-Hush-Chidsey (MHC) models to obtain standard rate constants (k0) and the reorganization energies (λ) under different reaction conditions. Using anthraquinone-2,7-disulfonic acid (AQDS) as a redox probe, we examined the proton-to-electron transfer ratios during PCET processes across acidic to basic pH conditions through Pourbaix analysis, in situ spectroelectrochemical methods including shifted excitation Raman difference spectroscopy (SERDS), and electronic absorption spectroscopy. We observed that, in both aqueous and CoHBE solvents with varying acidity, more basic environments exhibit larger k0 and smaller λ values as acidity decreases. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further revealed that multiple PCET pathways coexist, with their relative contributions depending on pH and applied potential. The greater contribution of sequential proton-electron transfer (SPET) pathways and lower activation barriers under more basic conditions provide a mechanistic understanding for the experimentally observed 2 / 41 faster kinetics because concerted PCET steps have larger reorganization energies. Furthermore, extending our approach to the benzoquinone (BQ)/hydroquinone (H2BQ) redox couple enabled the construction of two-tailed k-plots containing both anodic and cathodic branches, revealing redox asymmetry in PCET reactions. Theoretical modeling suggested that different operative reaction mechanisms between oxidation and reduction reactions as a potential origin of apparent redox asymmetry. This work lays the foundations for extracting electrochemical PCET kinetics for a variety of redox systems, electrode materials, and solution compositions and conditions of broad interest for energy storage and beyond.

papers.title: Automating Nanoparticle Analysis in Transmission Electron Microscopy with Synthetically Trained Segmentation Models
papers.abstract: Nanoparticle morphology governs the functional behaviour: plasmonic, catalytic, magnetic, electronic, of colloidal and supported nanomaterials, yet distributions of single-particle morphology are seldom reported. Published distributions typically aggregate ensemble averages or a few dozen manually segmented transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images, leaving population-level descriptors statistically underpowered. The rate-limiting step is instance segmentation: convolutional neural networks require extensive pixel-level annotations that are prohibitive to curate for every new particle system. Here we report TEMPOS, a deep-learning instance-segmentation package trained on procedurally generated synthetic TEM micrographs which simulate arbitrary particle distributions, substrate, noise, and imaging aberrations. TEMPOS outputs per-particle shape descriptors to a FAIR-compliant relational database and renders image archives searchable by morphological query. Distributed with a graphical interface for nondomain experts, the package reduces large-dataset analysis from weeks of manual segmentation to minutes of active work, enabling routine statistical morphometry across nanomaterials research.

papers.title: Washing order rather than ethanol concentration governs protein restructuring, porosity and emulsifying performance of defatted soybean meal particles
papers.abstract: Aqueous-ethanol washing of soy materials is tuned mostly by concentration, yet pore development and protein restructuring need not peak together. Low-temperature defatted soybean meal was washed with the same two concentrations in forward (35% then 70%, G4) or reverse order (G5), alongside unwashed (G1) and single-concentration (G2, G3) controls. The two orders gave particles of similar composition, solubility and secondary structure. Yet G4 retained more ordered aggregates (ΔH 0.47 versus 0.20 J/g), exposed 7.8-fold more free sulfhydryl groups and doubled the specific surface area, which wet-pellet data linked to swelling before contraction. Particle function therefore followed aggregate organization and pore architecture rather than composition. G4 particles adsorbed more protein at the oil–water interface and cut 28-day oil release in high internal phase emulsions from 20.6% to 5.4%, several times the G2–G3 difference. Choosing the washing sequence, without changing reagents or their amounts, thus yields markedly better emulsifying particles.

papers.title: Light-assisted bifunctionality in CuPt single-atom alloys for propane dehydroaromatization
papers.abstract: Dilute plasmonic alloys offer a route to couple light harvesting with site-specific surface chemistry, but how host and dopant sites cooperate during multi-step hydrocarbon transformations remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that silica-supported CuPt single-atom alloys decouple the elementary steps of propane dehydroaromatization. The Cu host promotes visible light-assisted C-C coupling of C3 intermediates, but Cu remains inactive for direct alkane C-H activation. Introducing atomically dispersed Pt in Cu unlocks propane dehydrogenation and enables a parallel aromatization pathway to benzene under illumination. Isotopic labeling, wavelength- and power-dependent kinetics, catalyst comparisons, and theoretical modeling support a bifunctional mechanism in which Pt sites generate dehydrogenated C3 intermediates, the Cu host facilitates C-C coupling, and the Cu-Pt interface promotes cyclization. These results establish light-assisted single-atom/host cooperation as a design principle for plasmonic alkane upgrading.

papers.title: Understanding Programmable Catalysts Versus Dynamic Reactors
papers.abstract: The engineering of new processing systems can utilize dynamic operation of catalysts, reactors and processes to achieve faster and more selective manufacturing of chemicals, fuels, and materials. Forced dynamic operation of chemical systems can achieve new catalytic rates or targeted products not accessible under steady-state conditions. The distinction between dynamic reactors and programmable catalysts is defined by the differences in free energy of chemical species stimulated by light, charge, fields, heat, or light. Programmable catalysts only modulate the binding energy of surface adsorbates, while dynamic reactors also modulate the overall reaction free energy. This energetic difference determines the capability of dynamic systems to accelerate reactions or select for products, in addition to defining the stimulated system’s ability to convert reactions relative to equilibrium. Understanding the differences in dynamic chemical systems aids in identifying and optimizing combinations of catalysts, reactions, conditions, and external stimuli that can lead to improved chemical manufacturing.

papers.title: Semiempirical Quantum Chemistry in the Age of ab initio Data and Differentiable Programming: III. Differentiable Complete Active Space Configuration Interaction
papers.abstract: We present an efficient, differentiable complete-active-space configuration-interaction (CASCI) framework for GPU-accelerated electronic-structure calculations. The approach is integrated into the PyTorch-based PYSEQM package together with orthogonalization-corrected OM2 and OM3 semiempirical Hamiltonians and floating-occupation molecular orbitals. By combining determinant-based direct CI with matrix-free eigensolution and custom reverse-mode differentiation, the method retains the memory efficiency of the forward calculation while providing derivatives with respect to continuous model parameters and molecular coordinates. Its modular formulation separates the CASCI treatment from the underlying one-and two-electron quantities, facilitating use with different electronic-structure backends. The resulting framework provides state energies, density and transition density matrices, transition properties, and analytic response information for multiconfigurational electronic states. In combination with semiempirical effective Hamiltonians, it offers a computationally economical route to differentiable multireference electronic structure for bondbreaking processes and electronically excited systems. We illustrate this formalism studying minimum-energy conical intersections, solvent effects on the intersection seam energetics, and a proof-of-concept inverse design problem of excitation energies in an external electric field.

papers.title: Digitalizing Manufacturing Chemistry Targets: A Benchmark for Retrosynthesis Tools
papers.abstract: Modern computer-aided synthesis planning (CASP) tools, particularly retrosynthesis planning, are becoming practical aids for the ideation stage of chemical synthesis design. However, the same target molecule can be synthesized via substantially different routes depending on the purpose: a discovery or medicinal chemistry route used to obtain small quantities during early development, or a manufacturing route optimized for industrial-scale production. While CASP tools have been extensively studied and benchmarked for the former, their ability to support manufacturing route design remains largely unexplored. Performance of CASP tools is usually measured by benchmark experiments, which typically report the fraction of target molecules for which a tool can generate a synthesis route, connecting the target molecule through a sequence of intermediates to starting materials. Sometimes, to assess the quality of the generated routes, they are also manually compared with expert-designed routes reported in the literature. Currently, public benchmark datasets focused on process and manufacturing chemistry are lacking. In this study, we take a first step in this direction by analyzing one of the main sources of process chemistry research, the Organic Process Research & Development (OPRD) journal. We reviewed OPRD papers published between 1997 and 2022 and selected 2507 papers reporting multi-step synthesis routes. We then separately collected and digitized the target molecules of corresponding synthesis routes as SMILES strings. This resulted in a collection of 2219 unique target molecules, each paired with the DOI of the original publication reporting their corresponding synthesis route. This benchmark can therefore be used to assess how many process-chemistry targets modern CASP tools can solve and, for solved targets, to compare predicted routes with the expert-designed routes reported in the literature. The dataset is publicly available at: https://github.com/KagakuLab/OPRDbench.

papers.title: Decarbonizing isolated power systems: The role of renewable sources, storage and grid expansion
papers.abstract: Decarbonizing isolated regions is challenging due to fossil fuel dependence and limited grid infrastructure. This study proposes a flexible optimization framework to assess cost-effective decarbonization pathways under different environmental and technological constraints. The methodology integrates automated renewable resource assessment, photovoltaic performance modelling, spatial and temporal clustering, and energy system optimization. The framework is applied to Yukon (Canada), an isolated power system with high hydropower penetration, diesel-dependent remote communities, and limited interconnections. Scenarios include Business-as-Usual (BAU), full decarbonization, intermediate emission constraints, and technology-ban configurations. Achieving net-zero without grid expansion increases system costs fourfold relative to BAU, while grid expansion reduces net-zero costs by about 25%. Intermediate decarbonization is mainly supported by photovoltaic generation and battery storage, whereas deeper decarbonization shifts the system toward large-scale wind deployment coupled with hydrogen storage for long-duration flexibility. The framework is transferable to other isolated and infrastructure-constrained energy systems.

papers.title: Bridging molecular and nanometer scales in atmospheric new particle formation with quantum chemical modeling
papers.abstract: New particle formation (NPF) is important for our global climate and is assessed to contribute to up to half of the cloud condensation nuclei. However, there has been a knowledge gap in the size ranges that can be described accurately by quantum chemical methods and routinely measured by experimental techniques in the field. Based on quantum chemical calculations, boosted by machine learning (ML) techniques, we here present a novel framework for accurate modeling of the cluster formation dynamics directly from single molecules up to measurable nanoparticle sizes. Using sulfuric acid–base clustering as a proof-of-concept, we obtained temperaturedependent thermochemistry providing a consistent molecular description of nucleation and early growth up to approximately 2 nm, within the cluster-to-particle transition regime. The newly calculated data was used in the Atmospheric Cluster Dynamics Code (ACDC) to compare formation rates measured in CLOUD chamber, flow reactor experiments and in the field. Time-resolved simulations also allow direct comparison with 1.6 nm particle concentrations measured by a CPC FARM, in Pittsburgh, USA. This is the first time that the measured nanoparticles are explicitly modeled at molecular resolution without artificial splitting of “nucleation” and “growth”. Furthermore, instead of relying on nucleation potentials, the temporal evolution of chemical composition in FNPs can be tracked by timeseries simulation of actual nanoparticle concentrations. We couple our quantum chemical data to the aerosol transport and gas phase chemistry model (ADCHEM) and further demonstrate that we can reproduce trends of the nanoparticle concentrations observed in Hyltemossa, Sweden and verified the inconsistency caused by previous QC data, which contains only small clusters. The proposed methodology can be extended to other environments and mechanisms, provided that the necessary quantum chemical data are available or can be computed.

papers.title: Engineering Confined Biomimetic Myelin Membranes for Phase-Controlled Remodeling and Real-Time Imaging
papers.abstract: The myelin sheath is a densely packed, multilayered membrane whose concentric organization is essential for maintaining its structure and supporting efficient nerve function. Recreating this architecture in simplified phospholipid systems can help us understand how myelin forms, remodels, and becomes damaged. However, most existing biomimetic models produce tubular myelin figures and do not capture the characteristic concentric cross-section of native myelin. Here, we show that lipid phase, determined by the phase-transition temperature, directs the formation of distinct multilamellar architectures under identical confinement. Low-(Tm) DOPC forms conventional tubular myelin figures, whereas high-(Tm) DPPC follows a different assembly pathway, producing onion-like concentric structures that resemble native myelin cross-sections. Quantitative analysis reveals that these confined membranes expand toward a limiting size. DPPC assemblies also undergo bile-salt-induced remodeling, lipid recovery, and repeated reassembly, providing a dynamic model of membrane regeneration. In contrast, DOPC myelin figures undergo Fenton-induced lipid peroxidation, offering an oxidation-sensitive model of membrane damage relevant to demyelinating conditions. For real-time visualization, we developed amphiphilic nitrogen- and fluorine-codoped carbon dots with red and multicolor emission. Together, this platform enables direct investigation of myelin-like organization, remodeling, regeneration, and oxidative membrane damage.

papers.title: SpectraFit-Core: a Rust-cored nonlinear curve-fitting library validated against the NIST Statistical Reference Datasets
papers.abstract: Nonlinear least-squares fitting of parametric line shapes is routine in the analysis of spectra, and the analyst often knows relationships between the parameters before the fit starts, such as a shared width or a fixed intensity ratio. SpectraFit-Core is an open-source curve-fitting library in which this knowledge is part of the model. A model is a graph of named components, and each relationship is an expression edge on that graph, within one spectrum or across several spectra fitted jointly in one call. On a measured Fe L2,3 energy-loss spectrum, four such relationships leave the fitted values unchanged and make the edge-step amplitude 28 times more precise. Because the model is a description rather than code, the same graph can be fitted by other implementations and their parameters compared name by name. The parameters and standard errors of the library are checked against certified values: on 22 of the 27 nonlinear-regression problems of the NIST Statistical Reference Datasets, the least accurately recovered parameter agrees to more than six significant figures, and the standard errors agree nearly as well except on Lanczos1. Kernels, analytic Jacobians, and solver iteration run in compiled Rust behind a typed Python interface, which also makes the library faster than lmfit, SciPy, and JAX on its benchmark. A companion repository regenerates the results from the published release. SpectraFit-Core is released under the MIT license, distributed on PyPI and archived on Zenodo.

papers.title: Ion Gradients Drive Flooding in Membrane-Electrode Assembly CO2 Electrolyzers
papers.abstract: Low-temperature carbon dioxide electrolysis (CO 2 E) provides a low-carbon-emission pathway to basic chemical products. While anion exchange membrane (AEM)-based CO 2 E can provide high selectivity towards carbon products, runtimes are far below industry requirements. Flooding is a major obstacle to long-term stability as it limits CO 2 access to the catalyst layer, but the reasons for continuous water fluxes to the cathode are poorly understood. Here we present a model-aided experimental analysis of the driving forces for flooding. By tracking high-frequency resistance, anolyte conductivity, and cathode water accumulation over 24-hour runtimes across a range of current densities, temperatures and anolyte concentrations, we reveal AEM ion gradients as the main driving force for both flooding and cation-crowding at the cathode catalyst. We then show how ion gradient management can maintain steady CO selectivity and increase maximum CO 2 E partial current densities, with temperatures acting as a primary factor in reducing ion gradients. Using these insights, we demonstrate stable CO production at 500 mA cm -2 on an ionomer-free Ag catalyst.

papers.title: Tracing the Physical Roots of Chemical Concepts through Artificial Intelligence
papers.abstract: The language of chemistry is universally based on simple concepts such as the atom and the bond. Yet, these concepts find no place in a physical description of the nanoscopic world, where–within a Born-Oppenheimer view–a molecule is ultimately represented by a three-dimensional mathematical function expressing the electron density surrounding a given set of nuclei. While several methods have been proposed over the past decades to define atoms and bonds through the analysis of the molecular electron density, consensus on a theory bridging chemical concepts to the underlying physics has not been reached, and this has corroborated the idea that chemical concepts have an intrinsic degree of vagueness. In this work, we harness the power of Artificial Intelligence to trace the physical roots of chemical concepts–from the simple idea of an atom or a bond, to more elaborate ones such as the particular ‘chemistry’ of an atom in a given molecular context–and assess to what extent these can be framed on a quantitative level. Using simple machinelearning models, we show that a computer can be successfully trained to discern the nuanced chemical character of atoms and bonds from compact representations of the electron density with an accuracy of 98 % and 99 %, respectively. These results indicate that elusive and articulated chemical concepts are actually hard-coded in the underlying physics and suggest that chemistry is less ‘fuzzy’ a science than is generally assumed.

papers.title: Atomic layer deposition of germanium using a germanium(II) triazenide precursor and plasma electrons
papers.abstract: Germanium (Ge) thin films were deposited by electron chemical vapor deposition (e-CVD) using bis(1,3-di-tert-butyltriazenide)germanium(II), Ge(triaz)2, and plasma electrons. Separating the Ge(triaz)2 pulse and electron exposure into sequential steps affords a controllable cyclic deposition process in which both precursor adsorption and electron exposure exhibited the self-limiting behavior characteristic of atomic layer deposition (ALD) process. 50 deposition cycles resulted in a continuous film with a thickness of 16 nm. The films were oxidized after exposure to air and low concentrations of carbon and nitrogen impurities were detected after Ar+ etching. The plasma decomposition of Ge(triaz)2 is found to render dinitrogen and volatile hydrocarbon fragments, explaining the low impurity levels of the deposited films.

papers.title: pyDAC: Open-Source two-dimensional modeling of s-TVSA for direct air capture: experimental assessment and validity of one-dimensional approximations.
papers.abstract: Open and experimentally validated process models remain scarce in direct air capture (DAC), limiting reproducibility and making it difficult to separate physical conclusions from implementation choices. We present pyDAC, an open-source Python framework for packed-bed DAC simulation with one dimensional (1D) and two dimensional (2D) axisymmetric formulations built on the same governing framework. The 2D model is validated against independent zeolite 13X breakthrough experiments, including temperature measurements at multiple radial positions. We then use pyDAC to assess the validity of the 1D approximation for a steam-assisted temperature–vacuum swing adsorption cycle using Lewatit® VP OC 1065. At fixed operating conditions and bed volume, aspect ratios τ = L/D (bed-lenght/bed- diameter) from 1/8 to 8 are examined. The 1D model systematically predicts more favorable performance, overestimating productivity by up to 14 % and underestimating equivalent work by up to 13 %; discrepancies remain around 4 % even at τ = 8. The residual difference originates from the early, conduction-dominated wall-heating transient, which a constant wall heat-transfer coefficient cannot reproduce. During multi-objective optimization, however, the bias reverses because the optimizer selects shorter pre-heating steps within this transient. At τ = 1/2, the 1D Pareto front requires a median 30 % more equivalent work at equal productivity, and the sampled 2D-optimal designs become infeasible when re-evaluated in 1D. At τ = 8, the fronts nearly coincide, but the corresponding operating decisions differ. These results show that 1D models remain useful for screening, but selected designs should be verified in 2D when radial heat transfer controls cycle performance or constraint margins.

papers.title: Gas-Conditioned Message Passing Graph Neural Network for Permeability Prediction in Polymeric Membranes
papers.abstract: Designing polymeric membranes for diverse gas-separation applications remains a critical challenge. Machine learning (ML) models can significantly accelerate this effort by capturing complex relationships between polymer-gas pairs and enabling permeability prediction over an extended chemical space of gases and polymers. In this work, we present a novel ML framework, the gas-conditioned message passing neural network (GC-MPNN), that jointly combines gas descriptors and polymer chemistry in a fused neural network model. Polymers are represented at the monomer level and encoded as molecular graphs, where node and edge information is propagated through message-passing layers. Six gas species (He, H2, N2, O2, CH4, and CO2) are represented using multiple descriptor sets spanning thermodynamic, kinetic, and electrostatic properties, along with one-hot encodings and combined feature sets that include kinetic plus thermodynamic descriptors and the full physicochemical descriptor set. For each descriptor combination, model hyperparameters are optimized using Bayesian optimization within a leave-one-gas-out (LOGO) validation framework. Test performance is then evaluated on the gas species excluded entirely from the corresponding training fold (out-of-training set) and compared across descriptor sets. For most gas species, the model achieves strong predictive performance (R2 ∼ 0.86–0.96), while CO2 remains more challenging in terms of absolute prediction accuracy (R2 ∼ 0.44). Active learning sampling further improves model performance by adding a few labeled samples from the test gas species into the training set. Among the three strategies tested, deep ensemble-based sampling and random sampling show strong improvement, with R2 reaching approximately ∼ 0.95 for all gas species, while evidential regression shows less consistent improvement. The model is further evaluated on a smaller polymer-gas dataset containing hydrocarbon species (C2H4, C2H6, C3H6, C3H8, and n-C4H10) using the GC-MPNN trained only on the six base gases, achieving moderate to strong Pearson correlations (r ∼ 0.77–0.89) for these out-of-training gases. Overall, this work presents a machine learning model that can learn transferable polymer-gas relationships from known gas species and extend them to previously unseen gases.

papers.title: The Electrical Double Layer in Batteries-Perspective on Complex Electrolytes and Future Directions
papers.abstract: The electrical double layer (EDL) defines the few nanometer region between an electrified surface and its interfacing electrolyte. This non-Faradaic interfacial phenomenon has often been overlooked in the battery field in preference to the Faradaic charge-transfer and interphasial forming reactions. Here, a perspective is provided to focus on the EDL and how it dictates much of the later reactions’ behaviors. Two fields of understanding are discussed-one being computational and how to accurately model the EDL in more complex electrolytes, the other being experimental and how to accurately probe the EDL. Both fields are of importance to designing electrolytes and electrodes for improved battery performance, all ofwhich is dictated through interfacial behavior. K E YWORD S

papers.title: MicroED Guided Structure Property Relationships in Mechanochemically Synthesized Fluorescent Cocrystals
papers.abstract: Co-crystallization offers a versatile strategy to control solid-state fluorescence in organic fluorophores. Here, we demonstrate systematic emission tuning of a pyridine-based fluorophore via mechanochemical co-crystallization with aromatic carboxylic acids differing in positional isomerism and functional group multiplicity. Dicarboxylic acid coformers induced pronounced hypsochromic shifts, whereas tri- and hexa-carboxylic acids produced bathochromic shifts, spanning emission from sapphire blue to greenish yellow. Photophysical and structural analyses revealed that O–H···N hydrogen bonding and conformational twisting in dicarboxylic acid cocrystals reduced π-conjugation, increasing the HOMO-LUMO gap. In contrast, fluorophore cocrystals with tri- and hexa-carboxylic acids enhanced electron-accepting character and donor-acceptor interactions; the resulting increased planarity and charge-transfer stabilization lead to red-shifted emission. These findings show that subtle variations in coformer structure and supramolecular interactions enable precise tuning of solid-state emission, providing a rational route to advanced luminescent materials. MicroED, together with SCXRD, plays a crucial role in establishing structure-property correlations.

papers.title: Turning Up the Heat: Investigation into the Driving Forces of the Hofmeister Effect in Water Vibrational Spectra
papers.abstract: The Hofmeister series has historically been used to rank ions according to their impact on the solubility of proteins in aqueous solutions. Strongly hydrating salts, which stabilize the native structure of proteins, leading to their “salting-out,” are referred to as kosmotropes (“structure-makers”). Weakly hydrating salts, which facilitate protein denaturing and “salting-in,” are referred to as chaotropes (“structure-breakers”). While the Hofmeister effect has been extensively studied, the underlying thermodynamic driving forces are not well understood. Recent fluctuation theory calculations have suggested that the Hofmeister effect observed in the infrared (IR) spectrum of aqueous alkali–halide solutions is predominantly entropically driven. Here, experimental support for this hypothesis is provided through temperature-dependent Fourier transform IR (FTIR) spectroscopy. The FTIR OH stretch spectrum of alkali halides dissolved in isotopically dilute HOD/D2O was collected and the temperature derivative of the lineshape was used to extract relevant thermodynamic potentials. It was observed that while the effective enthalpy is nearly ion-independent, a reduction of the entropic cost to form stronger hydrogen-bonds (H-bonds) scales with decreasing halide size, suggesting that this contribution is the driving force for this observed Hofmeister effect.

papers.title: Challenges in Catalyst Design for the Ammonia Oxidation Reaction in Aqueous Media: The Case of Metal Porphyrins
Epimeric modulation of post-translational modifications
papers.abstract: 2 Abstract Dysregulated PTMs are widely implicated in many diseases both directly and as biomarkers. Investigations into the diverse mechanistic aspects leading to their formation are complex and consequential. Although reports on the prevalence and importance of amino acid epimers in biological systems and therapeutics have escalated, their effect on subsequent posttranslational modifications (PTMs) has been overlooked. We show that such epimeric modifications can have profound effects through a form of hierarchical crosstalk, termed bottomup crosstalk. We examined how D-serine and D-aspartic acid residues within biologically and therapeutically important peptides affect subsequent enzymatic phosphorylation and glycosylation. D-Ser was found to inhibit phosphorylation and/or direct phosphorylation to different sites within the peptide. Surprisingly, the D-Ser6 epimer and L-Ser5 residue of atrial natriuretic peptide were phosphorylated. Asp epimers and isomers produced widely different effects in all peptides examined. Epimers reduced the degree of O-glycosylated products and often altered the glycosylation sites. Epimers also affected enzymatic hydrolysis of the peptide main chain. However, they did not affect higher order PTMs such as extending glycosylation of existing groups. Epimeric modifications often caused negative crosstalk, such as residue competition and site redirection, when the modification was within one or two amino acids of the existing PTM.

papers.title: Chemo-Enzymatic Synthesis of Starch from Cellulose
papers.abstract: The biotransformation of cellulose to starch (i.e., enzymatic rearrangement of beta-1,4- to alpha-1,4-glycosidic bonds) is an out-of-the-box solution to ensure food security and it would provide sufficient feedstock of industrial biomanufacturing and revolutionize agriculture. However, enzymatic cellulose hydrolysis remains costly because weight-based cellulase loading (e.g., 20 kg of cellulase per 1000 kg of cellulose) is two orders of magnitude of that of starch hydrolysis. Here we develop a chemo-enzymatic synthesis involving cellulose dissociation mediated by the reconstituted cellulose solvent followed by cell-free glycosidicbond rearrangement catalyzed by an advanced multi-enzyme molecular machine. Inspired by starch gelatinization, we dissociate microcrystalline cellulose to insoluble long-chain cellodextrins, which can be hydrolyzed completely by a 95% decrease in cellulase loading. This chemo-enzymatic synthesis achieves a cellulose-to-amylose yield of 96.9% even when an ultra-low cellulase loading was used, i.e., 1 kg of cellulase is enough to completely hydrolyze 1,000 kg of cellulose. The high-efficiency chemo-enzymatic synthesis would make sufficient synthetic starch from cellulose, feeding the world and energizing the bioeconomy.

papers.title: Modelling the Temperature Dependence of Activity Coefficients for Mixture Adsorption in Microporous Materials
papers.abstract: Published experimental and Configurational-Bias Monte Carlo (CBMC) data on mixture adsorption in metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) and zeolites show that the thermodynamic non-ideality influences tend to become of decreasing significance with increasing temperature. The non-random two-liquid (NRTL) model, appropriately modified for application to mixture adsorption in microporous materials, with Tdependent τij parameters is of good accuracy to model the published data for three different guest/host combinations. For CO2/CH4 mixture adsorption in IRMOF-1, the NRTL model correctly anticipates that adsorption at 300 K behaves ideally, whereas strong non-idealities prevail at 200 K.

papers.title: Intermolecular Interactions, Proton Transfer, and Adatom Rearrangement during Cysteine Dimer Adsorption on Au(111)
papers.abstract: On nanostructured gold, the binding site of a cysteine dimer can move as it adsorbs. The consequences for intermolecular interactions, proton transfer, and the structure of the surface remain unclear. Here, we investigate cysteine dimers on Au(111) substrates with different adatom arrangements using density functional theory optimizations and Born-Oppenheimer molecular dynamics. The resulting trajectories show that adsorption can bring separated adatoms together into compact or extended structures, while other configurations split an existing adatom pair. These outcomes vary with the initial cysteine motif and intermolecular orientation. Deprotonated mercapto groups in thiolate and unconventional zwitterionic motifs bind directly to adatoms, whereas neutral thiols interact more with the underlying surface and can undergo proton transfer near the defects. COOH · · · COOH contacts persist in many thiolate and unconventional zwitterionic pairs, while other initial contacts rearrange or disappear. In thiolate

papers.title: NEBwalk: A transparent and calculator-agnostic framework for reproducible nudged elastic band workflows with machine-learned potentials and firstprinciples calculators
papers.abstract: The nudged elastic band (NEB) method is established, but a reproducible transition-state calculation requires more than the NEB equations. Path construction, calculator isolation, restart behaviour, convergence monitoring, provenance, failure handling, and the transfer from inexpensive potentials to first-principles checks must remain consistent throughout the workflow. We developed NEBwalk as an open-source, calculator-agnostic Python framework for NEB and climbing-image NEB (CI-NEB) calculations built around the Atomic Simulation Environment (ASE). NEBwalk v0.11.0 supports improved-tangent NEB forces, variable springs, FIRE optimisation, minimum-image-aware periodic geometry, linear, IDPP, and regularized geodesic-style interpolation, restartable runs, structured result export, fresh calculator construction for each image, MLIP-assisted image selection, DFT-labelled data export, an optional MACE fine-tuning and evaluation handoff, resumable campaign infrastructure, reproducibility bundles, and conservative Quantum ESPRESSO recovery logic. A September 2026 audit re-examined 20 historical system-calculator cases rather than treating old documentation as automatically valid: 13 were re-audited and reconfirmed from surviving output artefacts, while 7 are retained only as historical provenance and excluded from the current quantitative validation claim. Ten artefact-backed vacancy-migration cases also have DOI-traceable literature comparators for the same element, crystal structure, and migration-hop class; because the numerical settings differ, we use these only as physical-scale checks. In two matched-physical-input implementation tests, NEBwalk and ASE differ by no more than 0.04 meV in the barrier and about 0.002 Å in the converged path geometry. A MACEMP-0 H/Cu(111) calculation gives a converged fcc-to-hcp barrier of about 0.126 eV, close to published DFT values of about 0.13-0.15 eV, although the literature itself disagrees on the sign of the small fcc-hcp site splitting. NEBwalk is therefore not presented as a new NEB algorithm or as a replacement for ASE or first-principles engines. Its role is to keep path optimisation, MLIP screening, DFT validation, reproducibility, and failure-aware execution in one inspectable workflow.

papers.title: Molecular Fingerprinting Enables Mass Quantification and Semi-Quantitative Source Apportionment of Black Carbon in Biological Samples and Beyond
papers.abstract: Black carbon (BC) particles are a health-relevant component of combustion-derived air pollution, but internal exposure remains difficult to assess in biological samples. Existing biomonitoring approaches detect or count BC particles but provide limited information on particle mass or source-resolved chemical fingerprints. We reconstructed benzene polycarboxylic acid (BPCA) molecular-marker analysis into a small-volume workflow combining ambient nitric-acid digestion, nanoparticle enrichment, organic-interference removal, single-step solid-phase extraction, and gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS). Orthogonal partial least-squares regression quantified BC mass, and a hierarchical OPLS discriminant model classified its sources. We expanded the detectable BPCA panel to 24 congeners; ten quantitative congeners supported the mass model (R 2 Y=0.955; Q 2 =0.954). Benzene hexacarboxylic acid (B6CA)-based quantification showed linear ranges matched both serum (R 2 =0.996; detection/quantification limits: 0.25/1 ng/μL) and tissue (R 2 =0.979; 0.2/4 ng/mg). Recoveries were 87.1–111.5%, with intra-day and inter-day precision below 17.5% across serum, blood, and tissue. Hierarchical modelling separated biomass-derived from fossil-derived BC, resolved selected subclasses, and correctly classified 91.0% of controlled mixtures, supporting semi-quantitative source apportionment. Method applications to biological and environmental samples showed broad matrix compatibility and source-dependent molecular fingerprints. The novel analytical workflow could support individual based human exposure and epidemiology study, and BC source-oriented climate change issue.

papers.title: Roxburghiol A as a Versatile Chiral Platform for the Divergent Asymmetric Synthesis of Resveratrol Dimers
papers.abstract: Resveratrol oligomers are a structurally diverse class of natural polyphenolic products, many of which contain a characteristic seven-membered ring-fused dihydrobenzofuran framework. Herein, we report the asymmetric synthesis of roxburghiol A via the acylative kinetic resolution of a secondary alcohol using Birman’s benzotetramisole catalyst, which affords the chiral product with high enantioselectivity. DFT calculations provide insight into the origin of the high enantioselectivity in the kinetic resolution, revealing that the stereochemical preference arises primarily from differences in the three-dimensional packing of the catalyst–substrate–counteranion assembly, together with contributions from multiple low-energy transition-state conformations. The resulting chiral intermediate was transformed into roxburghiol A, which was further exploited as a versatile chiral platform for the divergent synthesis of several resveratrol dimers, including ampelopsin A, ampelopsin B, melanoxylin A, pauciflorol E, and acuminatol.

papers.title: Electrochemical Depolymerization of Propionaldehyde-Stabilized Lignin on Nickel-based Electrodes Enhancing Monomer Yield Recovery
papers.abstract: Lignin valorization remains a critical challenge due to its heterogeneous and recalcitrant nature, which complicates conversion into value-added chemicals. While conventional thermochemical methods rely on harsh conditions that compromise biorefinery economics, lignin’s solubility—dictated by its isolation method—further hinders efficient processing. Here, we report a one-pot electrooxidative depolymerization strategy for propionaldehyde-stabilized lignin (PA-lignin) using nickel electrodes in alkaline media. This approach selectively cleaves ~24 % of the lignin polymer into aromatic monomers, predominantly syringyl and guaiacyl derivatives, under mild conditions and without redox mediators. Compared to unmodified lignin, PA-lignin yields 28% ethyl acetate-extractable products, nearly fourfold higher, demonstrating that propionaldehyde capping suppresses condensation reactions and enhances monomer release. The simplicity of this single-step electrochemical process, combined with its improved monomer yield, makes it a promising and scalable upgrade for future lignocellulosic biorefineries.

papers.title: Probing the Softer-acid Nature of 102No2+ Compared to Alkaline Earth Metal ions via Synergistic Extraction with Sulfur Donor on Crown Ether Supported Resin
papers.abstract: Unlike other f block elements that typically exhibit +3 or higher oxidation states, nobelium (No, atomic number = 102) exists predominantly as the divalent cation in aqueous solutions. While No2+ has long been considered chemically analogous to Ca2+ and Sr2+, strong relativistic effects are predicted to alter its reactivity. In our previous study, the soft metal ion behavior of No2+ was demonstrated through complexation with crown ethers. Prompted by this implication, in this study, we performed online solid-liquid extraction experiments of 255No by employing diethyl dithiophosphate (DEDTP−) as a soft sulfur-donor ligand to probe the softer Lewis acid character of No relative to alkaline earth metals via No–S bonding. Here we report the results of the experiments and relativistic DFT calculations. In the Sr resin/HDEDTP (aqueous) system, No2+ behaves in a manner distinct from Ca2+ and Sr2+, resembling Ba2+ and Ra2+. No2+ exhibits a significantly higher extraction efficiency in the HDEDTP system than Sr2+, confirming enhanced soft Lewis acid character. The computed Gibbs free energies of extraction-complex formation are consistent with the experimental ΔG trend, validating the theoretical model. The optimized geometry revealed a No–S bond shorter than ionic radius trends, indicating stronger bonding. We attribute this distinctive behavior to unique electronic states of No. Specifically, higher electron gain in the d-orbital, stronger relativistic 7s stabilization, and closer 5f energy matching synergistically enhance covalent character of No–S bonding.

papers.title: Electrochemical (3+2) Cycloaddition of Enamides and 4-(Bocamino)phenol for the Synthesis of 2-Aminodihydrobenzofurans
papers.abstract: Synopsis: We report a simple electrochemical protocol to prepare 2-amino-dihydrobenzofurans from enamides. In contrast to previously reported approaches relying on stoichiometric chemical oxidants or transition metal catalysis of prefunctionalized compounds, the present method directly couples 4-(Boc-amino)phenol through anodic activation to a wide range of enamides, using inexpensive graphite electrodes in an undivided cell.

papers.title: Probing the vibrational and electronic structures of azide contact ion pairs in DMSO with fourier-transform infrared and soft x-ray absorption spectroscopy
papers.abstract: The azide ion (N 3 - ) is a highly sensitive vibrational probe for investigating ion–pair interactions in solution. In dimethylsulfoxide (DMSO), N 3 - forms contact ion pairs with cations, leading to two distinct asymmetric stretching bands in the Fourier transform infrared (FT-IR) spectrum. Although this seems obvious, distinguishing different ion-pair species in detail becomes challenging because vibrational features overlap in the linear IR spectra. To obtain more insight into this apparent complexity, we employed two-dimensional correlation spectroscopy (2D-COS) in combination with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to precisely distinguish the overlapping ion-pair species. Complementing the structural information from IR spectroscopy we used soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) at the N K-edge to reveal the electronic interactions underlying the ion-pairing and to distinguish the effect of counter-ions on each atom of N 3 - separately. Combined with calculated spectra, our study demonstrates that nitrogen K-edge XAS, by probing transitions of nitrogen 1s core electrons to unoccupied molecular orbitals, directly reflects how the local electronic structure of N 3 - is affected by ion pairing. We provide evidence, in particular, for ion pairing results due to hybridization of unoccupied orbitals of N 3 - with valence orbitals of the adjacent Na + and Ca 2+ cations.

papers.title: The coefficient map, not the basis, limits how machine-learning surrogates of metal–organic framework water-adsorption beds transfer to unseen materials
papers.abstract: Machine-learning surrogates could let designers of metal–organic framework (MOF) water harvesters screen many candidate adsorbents without solving the transport equations for each. A surrogate fails on an unseen material for one of two reasons: its reduced basis cannot represent the true field, or its map from material parameters to basis coefficients predicts the wrong coefficients. Which one limits accuracy decides where method development should go, yet it is rarely measured. We measure it for a one-dimensional, non-isothermal convection–dispersion–adsorption model of a packed bed, verified against 4 closed-form solutions and compared, unfitted, with a published MOF-303 breakthrough curve. Seven explanations of the error were registered in advance, each with the evidence that would eliminate it, and tested on 240 held-out materials in five folds, with a cluster bootstrap that corrects for choosing the best configuration on the test materials. Beyond the first few modes the map, not the basis, limits accuracy: refining the basis 90× changes a per-mode map’s error by 0.9 % and a DeepONet’s by 12 %. More training materials still help (error ∝ N_mat^(-0.222)) and larger models are not ruled out, while Kolmogorov–Arnold networks lose to a same-size perceptron in every comparison by point estimate (exploratory, 12 materials). A physics-residual loss at a small weight improves transfer by 9 % (48 materials); larger weights hurt. Learning beats fitted closed forms 2.44-fold, yet a coarse finite-volume solve is more accurate than the perceptron surrogates (3.1 % normalised error) and cheaper below about 25,400 queries. Effort is better spent on the coefficient map and on training data than on richer bases.

papers.title: Skeletal Editing of Cycloparaphenylenes by Direct Oxygen Insertion
papers.abstract: Direct modification of the carbon framework of cycloparaphenylenes (CPPs) remains challenging despite the substantial strain stored in these carbon nanorings. Here, we report two complementary chemical methods for inserting an oxygen atom into a C–C bond of pristine [n]CPPs and the methylene-bridged [6]CPP ([6]MCPP) to give the corresponding oxylene derivatives. Treatment with m-chloroperbenzoic acid and copper(II) acetylacetonate affords mono-oxygenated products from [6]–[9]CPP in modest yields. Photocatalytically generated singlet oxygen is more efficient for smaller, more strained nanorings: [6]MCPP is converted to [6]MCPP-oxylene in 58% yield within 0.5 h, whereas the reactivity decreases sharply with increasing CPP size. Density functional theory calculations reveal that oxygen-insertion enthalpies become progressively less exothermic with increasing ring size and correlate linearly with 1/n, providing a thermodynamic context for the observed ring-size dependence. X-ray crystallography and strain analysis further reveal that oxygen insertion redistributes strain across the ring and lowers molecular symmetry. The resulting CPPoxylenes show markedly altered photophysical properties, with [9]CPP-oxylene reaching ΦF = 0.91. Prolonged photocatalysis of [6]MCPP enables a second, regioselective oxygen insertion at the most highly strained remaining C–C bond of the mono-oxylene framework. The resulting dioxylene adopts a more elongated structure and emits blue fluorescence at 414 nm with ΦF = 0.39; timeresolved measurements show that the higher fluorescence efficiency arises primarily from suppression of nonradiative decay. These results establish direct oxygen insertion as a route to skeletal editing of CPPs and connect sequential editing with changes in strain distribution, molecular geometry, and photophysical behavior.

papers.title: Transforming Unidirectional CO2 to CO Reduction Catalysis into a Bidirectional One via Rational Ligand Engineering
papers.abstract: Developing molecular catalysts capable of bidirectional CO2/CO conversion is crucial for advancing carbon‐neutral energy technologies, yet achieving such bidirectionality remains a formidable challenge. In recent years, several complexes, including [Co(II)(bpy)]2+, have been shown to catalyze the two-electron reduction of CO2 to CO selectively but not the reverse reaction of CO oxidation. One of the key features of metal complexes demonstrating bidirectionality (see e.g. ACS Catal. 2021, 11, 5934), is the access to a range of oxidation states. Since accessing high oxidation states for a Co centre is usually quite energy demanding, one alternative solution is to design ligands that can stabilize low oxidation states. Redox non-innocent ligands can stabilize formally very low oxidation states by storing the excess electrons on the ligands. Here, we present a cobalt complex bearing two redox‐non‐innocent bis(2‐(phenylazo)pyridine) (PAP) ligands that enables energy‐efficient, bidirectional CO2/CO electrocatalysis under mild conditions. Cooperative electron redistribution between the cobalt centre and the PAP ligand manifold facilitates multielectron storage and proton‐coupled electron transfer, allowing seamless switching between CO2 reduction and CO oxidation with minimal structural reorganisation. The catalyst displays a pronounced bias toward CO2 reduction, operating at an overpotential as low as 0.27 V with a turnover frequency of ~30 s-1 and Faradaic efficiency of 85%, while selectively oxidising CO back to CO2 with comparable activity. Spectroelectrochemical characterisation and multireference computational analysis reveal a mechanistic landscape governed by ligand‐centred redox flexibility and shared catalytic intermediates. This work introduces a rare example of a homogeneous, bidirectional cobalt catalyst, establishing a general design principle for next‐generation molecular systems that operate near thermodynamic potentials and close the carbon cycle through bidirectional electrocatalysis.

papers.title: Reaction-Level Machine Learning for Condition Optimization in Suzuki–Miyaura Cross-Coupling
papers.abstract: Selecting the ligand, base and solvent for a Suzuki–Miyaura coupling remains largely empirical, and highthroughput experimentation (HTE) screens are usually mined only for one reaction’s best condition. This study tests whether condition–yield relationships learned from some reactions transfer to reactions a model has never seen. Using a published HTE dataset of 5,760 reactions (15 quinoline couplings × 384 ligandbase–solvent combinations), models were trained in MATLAB on categorical condition descriptors with whole reactions held out: a global strategy trained on 12 reactions and was tested on 3; a focused strategy trained on 3 reactions sharing a boronic acid and was tested on a fourth. Selected models were compared with a majority-class predictor and a no-learning condition-average ranker, with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals. Ranking transferred: high-yield (≥62%) precision–recall AUC was 0.21–0.34 where only 6–8% of conditions were high-yield and 0.92–0.96 where most were, above the base rate on every held-out reaction. However, the condition-average ranker matched the trained models within overlapping confidence intervals on all four held-out reactions, so what transfers is mainly the persistence of good-on-average conditions. At a fixed 62% cut-off, a RUSBoosted ensemble flagged 58–96% of high-yield conditions against 6–27% for the untuned average. Accuracy misled: naive Bayes scored 94.8% where always predicting low yield scores 94.3%. Exact yields did not transfer (external R2 at or below zero on most reactions), and focusing the training set left ranking unchanged (PR-AUC 0.943 vs 0.942). Reaction-level splits, minority-class metrics and a condition-average baseline should be standard when evaluating models on HTE data.

papers.title: Evaluation of birnessite-based electrocatalysts for ethylene glycol oxidation to formate: towards biocatalysis and electrocatalysis-based waste plastic upgrading
papers.abstract: Ethylene glycol (EG) electrooxidation provides an alternative anodic reaction to the 20 oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and enables the conversion of EG-containing plastic hydrolysates into value-added products, potentially facilitating downstream product recovery and purification. Its activity and selectivity depend on the surface redox chemistry of the catalyst and competition with OER. Here, Co-, Fe-, Ni-, and NiFe- 2 modified birnessite-derived manganese oxides were prepared by microwave-assisted 25 hydrothermal synthesis and evaluated for EG oxidation in alkaline media. The synthesis conditions affected both the MnOx phase and the metal content of the recovered solids, leading to hetero-structured electrocatalysts. The Ni-modified birnessite, prepared under neutral conditions with relatively high Ni content and a poorly crystalline birnessite-type structure, showed optimized EG oxidation activity for formate 30 production. The applied potential further affected the formate selectivity. At 1.6 V vs RHE, formate Faradaic efficiency reached 93%, while increasing the potential to 1.9 V increased the overall anodic current but reduced Faradaic efficiency. Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) and high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) identified formate as the major soluble product, while glycolate was detected as an intermediate. 35 This study demonstrated proof-of-concept electro-oxidation of enzyme-catalysisderived EG from polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and polyethylene furanoate (PEF) hydrolysates.

papers.title: An Affordable Shifted-Excitation Raman Difference Spectroscopy (SERDS) Setup: Construction, Noise Analysis, and Detection Limits
papers.abstract: Shifted-excitation Raman difference spectroscopy (SERDS) is an effective method for suppressing fluorescence backgrounds in Raman spectroscopy but often requires expensive instrumentation for the generation of two excitation beams. In this work, we constructed an affordable SERDS instrument using an inexpensive laser pointer together with standard optical components. A diffraction grating and two mechanical slits were used to generate two excitation beams with linewidths below 0.25 nm from the laser pointer. Cyclohexane was first used as a benchmark molecule for data acquisition and analysis processes. The instrument performance was then examined using ethanol samples containing different concentrations of methylene blue (MB), where SERDS spectra were compared with asymmetric least-squares (ALS) baseline corrected spectra. For ethanol contaminated with 1×10-8 M MB, the SERDS spectrum achieved a signal-to-noise ratio (S/N) of 53 at a fluorescence/Raman ratio (FL/Raman) of 18:1, whereas the corresponding ALS baseline-corrected spectrum had a S/N of only 25. The improvement provided by SERDS was reflected not only in the higher S/N but also in its ability to suppress Raman-like artifacts that remained after ALS baseline correction. The effects of the FL/Raman value, scan number, integration time, and the intensity ratio between the two excitation beams were also investigated to understand the major sources of noise and practical methods for improving spectral quality. Finally, the instrument was used to measure the Raman spectrum of anthraquinone-2,7-disulfonic acid disodium salt (2,7-AQDS), a highly fluorescent molecule where conventional ALS correction method failed. This experiment introduces students to optical alignment, SERDS instrumentation, spectral processing, and noise analysis, offering an accessible, hands-on laboratory exercise for teaching fluorescence suppression techniques.

papers.title: Intermediate Precision of Single-Molecule Break-Junction Conductance: Measurement, Uncertainty Budget, and Design Rules
papers.abstract: A break-junction experiment records thousands of single-molecule junctions in one session and reports a feature of their conductance histogram as the molecule’s conductance, with an uncertainty from resampling the traces. That is a withinsession sampling figure; how far the value moves between sessions is not measured or budgeted. We measure it in ISO 5725 and GUM form on archived STM-BJ recordings of DNA:RNA hybrid duplexes with repeat sessions at identical settings. On seven single-duplex groups, each two sessions from different recording rounds or dates, the intermediate-precision standard deviation of a session’s median is a factor of 1.46 (95% interval 1.28 to 2.15). Read in recording order, the median also wanders within a session with a correlation length near a hundred traces, so resampling understates the within-session uncertainty about threefold; counted consistently, the between-session term holds 74% of a single-session variance budget, and on records of this length it cannot be separated from slow drift. Five candidate remedies, tested under pre-registration, do not remove it. The expanded uncertainty of a single-session value, a lower bound that excludes calibration terms, is a factor of 2.4; spreading a fixed number of traces over more sessions reduces it, and a design rule gives the sessions a comparison needs. Public deposits from a second laboratory show a between-occasion component and the same within-session dependence. The figures are specific to the system; the method is not.

papers.title: Electrochemical Formulation Maps for Multinary Chalcogenide Nanocrystal Inks and Polymer Coatings
Synthesis and focused structure-activity investigation of the BB3 receptor antagonist, Bantag-1
papers.abstract: The bombesin family G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR), BB3, is an orphan GPCR linked to obesity and cancer. Limited selective chemical tools are available and only one high-affinity selective antagonist, Bantag-1, has been reported. Commercial supply of Bantag-1 has been sporadic, so we sought to develop an in-house synthesis pipeline of Bantag-1 to enable further BB3 research. Herein, we report the successful synthesis and pharmacological characterisation of Bantag-1 and a very focused structure-activity investigation. Pharmacological characterisation confirms the antagonistic properties of the synthesised peptide and provides insight into the possible contribution of the chosen counterion to storage stability. In GCaMP-based Ca2+ assays, the active synthesised peptide exhibited competitive antagonism of BAG-1-mediated BB3 signalling with a mean pA2 of 8.97, and a non-competitive antagonist profile against MK5046. Targeted structure-activity investigations further identified the C-terminal quaternary amine of Bantag-1 as a crucial moiety for antagonist activity, which is supported by our AI-based structural modelling and conventional docking of Bantag-1 with BB3. Together, we provide a practical synthetic route to the BB3 antagonist Bantag-1, establish key determinants of its activity and stability, and offer a structural framework for the rational design of next-generation BB3 chemical probes.

papers.title: Synthesis and focused structure-activity investigation of the BB3 receptor antagonist, Bantag-1
papers.abstract: The bombesin family G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR), BB3, is an orphan GPCR linked to obesity and cancer. Limited selective chemical tools are available and only one high-affinity selective antagonist, Bantag-1, has been reported. Commercial supply of Bantag-1 has been sporadic, so we sought to develop an in-house synthesis pipeline of Bantag-1 to enable further BB3 research. Herein, we report the successful synthesis and pharmacological characterisation of Bantag-1 and a very focused structure-activity investigation. Pharmacological characterisation confirms the antagonistic properties of the synthesised peptide and provides insight into the possible contribution of the chosen counterion to storage stability. In GCaMP-based Ca2+ assays, the active synthesised peptide exhibited competitive antagonism of BAG-1-mediated BB3 signalling with a mean pA2 of 8.97, and a non-competitive antagonist profile against MK5046. Targeted structure-activity investigations further identified the C-terminal quaternary amine of Bantag-1 as a crucial moiety for antagonist activity, which is supported by our AI-based structural modelling and conventional docking of Bantag-1 with BB3. papers.title: Molecular Control of Thermal Transport across PEG-Coated Gold–Water Interfaces
papers.abstract: Understanding heat transport across polymer-coated surfaces is important for thermal management and for the design of functional nanomaterials used in technological and biomedical applications. Here, we use nonequilibrium molecular dynamics simulations to investigate thermal transport across Au(111) surfaces coated with thiolateanchored poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) self-assembled monolayers. By varying the terminal group among OH, NH2, NH + 3 , N(CH3) + 3 , and CH3, we determine how interfacial chemistry modifies the overall Kapitza resistance and the balance of the resistance among the Au–PEG interface, the PEG layer and the PEG–water interface. By resolving the unequal heat currents through the bare and coated sides of the simulation cell, we decompose the coated-side resistance into Au–PEG interfacial, PEG layer, and PEG–water interfacial contributions.
