Applications to two post-transition-state bifurcation reactions—deuterated methoxy radical isomerization with density functional theory and nitrene insertion with g-xTB—yield product ratios of 64:68 and 7.9:1, respectively, consistent with the previously reported ratios of 1:1 and 8.3:1.

papers.title: Rapid mechanochemical dinitrogen fixation for single-atom skeletal editing
papers.abstract: Direct utilization of dinitrogen (N2) in organic synthesis remains an unmet challenge in sustainable chemistry, particularly under mild conditions. Conventional transition-metal-mediated N2 functionalization typically requires elaborately designed catalysts under harsh conditions, limiting operational practicality. Here, we report a mechanochemical strategy that achieves rapid, lithium-mediated N2 reduction at ambient pressure and temperature in under two minutes, delivering polymorphic mixtures of α- and β-lithium nitride. The resulting metal nitride serves as a versatile platform for single nitrogen-atom transfer: applied to skeletal conversion reactions, it enables direct O-to-N transmutation of furans and aromatic oxonium salts into the corresponding pyrroles and pyridine derivatives, establishing a formal incorporation of N2 into N-heterocycles. The photophysical consequences of the single-atom edit on excited-state properties of the molecular chromophores were evaluated.

papers.title: Classical Nucleation Induced Intrafibrillar Mineralization of Collagen
papers.abstract: Collagen mineralization is fundamental to bone formation, and this process is widely believed to proceed via an amorphous calcium phosphate (ACP)-mediated non-classical nucleation pathway. Here we investigated this paradigm using cryogenic electron tomography. The results reveal that the intrafibrillar mineralization of collagen does not rely on the infiltration of ACP, but occurs through a classical heterogeneous nucleation mechanism, which can be accelerated both in vitro and in vivo by increasing the density of the collagen template. The finding not only updates our understanding of collagen mineralization mechanisms, but also provides critical insights for the design of bone regeneration materials.

papers.title: From Molecular Building Blocks to Corrugated Graphitic Carbon Nitride: Chemical Origins of Structural Preference and Electronic Diversity
Harnessing remote weak interactions for fine-tuning the catalytic activity of rotaxane-superbases
papers.abstract: Mechanically interlocked molecules offer a distinct strategy for controlling molecular function by translating subtle differences in noncovalent interactions into changes in molecular conformation and reactivity. Here, we show that remote weak interactions can be harnessed to fine-tune the basicity and catalytic activity of mechanically interlocked secondary amines. To this end, we synthesized two bistable rotaxanes, featuring a primary ammonium/amine binding site and either a triazole or a methyltriazolium unit as the secondary binding site. In the base-catalysed Michael addition of malononitrile to beta-nitrostyrene, both deprotonated amine-rotaxanes exhibit substantially higher catalytic activity than both the corresponding non-interlocked thread and the benchmark organobase proton sponge, demonstrating that the mechanical bond can enhance the reactivity of the embedded amine. Importantly, the triazole based-rotaxane shows a twofold higher catalytic activity than that of the triazolium-rotaxane, although the secondary amine as the catalytically active unit is structurally unchanged. Thus, the increased reactivity is caused by the difference in weak noncovalent interactions at the secondary binding site: Weaker binding to the triazole translates into higher basicity of the secondary amine, which in turn increases the catalytic activity of the rotaxane. Collectively, these results demonstrate that weak, remote interactions transmitted through a mechanical bond can modulate the proton-accepting ability and catalytic performance of an interlocked amine, establishing remote co-conformational control of basicity as a design principle for fine-tuning the reactivity of rotaxane superbases.

papers.title: Absorption and Emission Spectra in Aqueous Solution with Coupled-Cluster Accuracy
papers.abstract: Quantitative prediction of electronic spectra in water requires an accurate treatment of electronic excitation, nuclear structure, and state-specific solvation including effects from hydrogen bonding. Here, photoacids and photobases in aqueous solution are used as stringent test systems for statespecific embedded cluster reference interaction site model calculations combined with the iterative coupled cluster models CC2 and CC3. Wigner nuclear-ensemble and adiabatic Hessian Franck-Condon calculations reproduce absorption and emission band maxima on an absolute energy scale with typical errors of 0.1–0.2 eV without empirical shift or scaling corrections; the energies of resolved 0–0 transitions in photobases are even reproduced within a few hundredths of an eV. The simulations also resolve contributions from different excited states and changes in the emitting species. Derived excited-state acidity changes, ∆pK∗ a , show similar accuracy for photoacids and photobases, with residual errors governed by cancellation or accumulation between protonation states.

papers.title: Aggregation-Induced Polarization (AIP) of Racemic and Achiral Organic Molecules Leading to Asymmetric Elliptical Polarization Displaying Optical Rotation
papers.abstract: Aggregation-induced polarization (AIP) was found to enable racemic and achiral molecules to show optical rotation in clear and transparent solutions. It also leads to the specific rotation of chiral molecules to be affected by their concentrations instead of being nearly consistent as documented in literature and textbooks. In this work, we examined AIP effect in a series of solutions containing small racemic, achiral and chiral molecules. After being irradiated with UVvis in prolonged periods inside polarimeter, racemic compounds of rac-BINOL, rac-BINAP, rac-BINAP oxide and achiral aggregation-induced emission (AIE) luminogens and 4CzIPN showed transient optical rotations in cosolvents of THF and water, i.e., the optical rotation appeared during an induction period and later returned toward baseline. Specific rotations of chiral cinchona derivatives and R or S BINOL/BINAP retained their intrinsic sign but showed their concentration dependence. Dynamic light scattering (DLS) directly revealed concentration-dependent aggregates’ populations, while Photoluminescence (PL) also provided complementary evidence for aggregation-dependent behavior in the racemic and cinchona series. Changes in solution state organization can therefore appear as a transient net rotation in racemic or achiral samples, and as specific rotation changes of an existing chiral response. The asymmetric polarization induced by

papers.title: Strategy for the activation of porous molecular crystals using organic vapors
papers.abstract: Porous molecular crystals (PMCs), i.e., crystalline solids with permanent, virtual, or flexible porosity, are usually synthesized by crystallization from solution, with the solvated molecules included in the pores as guests. To use such crystals as porous materials, the guest molecules must be removed. Typically, thermal treatment is used to promote their desorption, but this method often leads to the loss of crystallinity and catastrophic collapse of the porous structures due to the weakness of the intermolecular interactions. Therefore, methods for guest desorption under mild conditions are in high demand. The present study reports exposure to organic vapors as an unprecedented strategy for this purpose. Specifically, we demonstrate that exposure to vapors of dimethyl sulfoxide, n-butanol, or tert-butanol at room temperature can induce the removal of ethanol molecules encapsulated in crystalline phenylbis(benzothiazol-2-yl)methanol while maintaining its single-crystallinity. Furthermore, this method was found to be applicable for guest desorption from a hydrogen-bonded organic framework based on phenylbis(benzimidazol-2-yl)methanol.

papers.title: Confinement-Controlled Cluster Percolation Shifts the Widom Crossover in Supercritical Methane
papers.abstract: Supercritical fluids undergo significant structural and dynamic changes near the Widom line, which separates gas-like and liquid-like regimes. These phenomena are well understood for bulk fluids, but their evolution under nanoscale confinement remains poorly understood. Using a Grand Canonical Monte Carlo and Molecular Dynamics simulation framework, we show that confinement of supercritical CH4 in clay slit nanopores shifts the Widom crossover to lower pressures, with the shift increasing as pore size decreases. Energy-based cluster analysis reveals that this shift is associated with the emergence of system-spanning molecular clusters. Confinement promotes the percolation of these clusters at lower pressures, extending liquid-like behaviour into regimes that are gas-like under bulk conditions. The crossover is also reflected in transport properties as an inflection in both the effective mean distance between free molecules and clusters and the molecular diffusion coefficient. These results establish a direct link between confinement-controlled cluster percolation and the Widom crossover.

papers.title: Imitation and Accuracy in Automated Electronic-Structure Method Selection
Evaluation and Health Risk Analysis of Residual Pesticides in Some Cereal Crops in Mangu Market, Plateau State, Nigeria
The Impact of Linker Disorder in Multivariate Metal-Organic Frameworks on Mechanical and Phonon Properties
papers.abstract: While the reticular nature of metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) allows incorporating highly symmetric building blocks, it also supports linker asymmetry and linker mixing within a single material. These imperfections impact both the framework structure and, crucially, its underlying physical properties. However, microscopic configurations of organic linkers are challenging to detect experimentally and we lack accurate atomistic models computationally. This work investigates the impact of orientational and compositional linker disorder on the emergent macroscopic behaviour of UiO-type MOFs with asymmetric linkers, based on azobenzene and stilbene compounds with different mixedlinker compositions. Atomic interactions in these multivariate MOFs are modelled using an accurate machine-learning potential (MLP) derived with a recent cluster-based learning algorithm. We find that axial linker rotations occur below the millisecond time scale and are hindered for asymmetric linkers, thereby leading to geometric frustration of the linker backbone within the cubic crystal system of the MOF. Flat bands in the phonon band structures corroborate the latter effect. We predict bulk moduli of a series of mono- and multivariate Zr-MOFs and uncover a nonlinear trend with linker composition. This work demonstrates that individual structural models fail to capture the complexity of realistic MOFs with mixed-linker compositions, and a structural ensemble approach is necessary to estimate representative properties. Combining an ensemble description with accurate MLPs holds promise to more generally model spatially disordered framework materials with multiple linkers and establish novel structure-function relationships.

papers.title: Computational design and prioritization of database-absent small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist candidates from public bioactivity data
papers.abstract: Public bioactivity data were used to construct a reproducible workflow for the computational prioritization of small-molecule glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) agonist candidates. Exact IC50, EC50, and Ki measurements were standardized, converted to pActivity, and deduplicated after structural exclusion of peptide-like records. The resulting dataset comprised 337 compounds and 155 Murcko scaffolds. Morgan fingerprints and physicochemical descriptors were evaluated using ridge regression, random forest, and XGBoost with scaffold-based validation. Random forest provided the lowest mean five-fold cross-validation root-mean-square error (RMSE; 0.497 pActivity units). Its scaffold-disjoint holdout performance was R2 = 0.236, RMSE = 0.760, and mean absolute error = 0.499. Local modifications of orforglipron generated 1,701 valid, unique analogs. Composite prioritization incorporated predicted activity, quantitative estimate of druglikeness, synthetic accessibility, and database absence. All 146 queried structures were absent from ChEMBL and PubChem under the implemented identity criteria. Of these, 46 passed an exploratory physicochemical filter, and 20 were shortlisted. No generated candidate passed the stricter drug-likeness filter. The leading candidate, GLP1R-01162, had predicted pActivity 7.677 and composite score 0.5400. These results defined an auditable set of computational hypotheses; they did not establish agonism, experimental potency, synthetic feasibility, or global novelty. Functional testing and independent novelty assessment remained necessary.

papers.title: Finding a small cytokine inside complex biological matrices using nanobody-functionalized plasmonic metasurfaces
papers.abstract: Interleukin-6 (IL-6) is a key inflammatory cytokine involved in numerous physiological and pathological processes, including cancer progression, fibrosis, and immune regulation. Rapid and label-free detection of IL-6 in complex biological environments is challenging due to its small size, which is overshadowed by the presence of large numbers of competing biomolecules. In this work, we develop a method to detect the spectroscopic signature of IL-6 in complex matrices using a nanobodyfunctionalized plasmonic metasurface that acts as a surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) sensor. Machine-learning-based spectral analysis enables identification of subtle molecular signatures of IL-6, despite the presence of competing species. We measured binary protein solutions containing IL-6 and bovine serum albumin (BSA), followed by IL-6-spiked cell culture medium and fibroblastconditioned culture medium. The mixed IL-6/BSA experiments show that elevated IL-6 scores can be recovered even at BSA-to-IL-6 ratios up to 100:1. In cell culture medium, the IL-6 score depends on the concentration and the observed trend deviates from the well-known Langmuir isotherm model. We developed a model that considers IL-6 binding on the nanobodies as a two-site adsorption problem that accounts for the metasurface geometry and steric effects. The model agrees well with the experimental data. Transforming growth factor beta (TGF-β)-stimulated fibroblast samples show a modest shift toward higher IL-6 scores than medium samples without TGF-β stimulation. Our approach is versatile and applicable to analyzing other biomolecules in a complex biological ‘soup’ of molecules and proteins.

papers.title: BRACE: Bayesian Residual-covariance Adaptive Calibration for Multi-Endpoint ADMET Prediction
papers.abstract: Deciding which ADMET assays to run on a compound requires a calibrated probability that it will pass each assay not yet measured, given those already run. A multi-task predictor supplies these via the cross-assay covariance of its prediction errors (residuals), but this covariance is usually estimated once, from historical data. It therefore misses correlations specific to a program’s chemical series (scaffolds) and knows nothing about assays unique to the program. With only hundreds to thousands of program compounds, we adapt this covariance rather than retrain the predictor. BRACE merges historical and program residuals by expectation–maximization into one covariance covering every assay, then corrects it per scaffold series with an Inverse-Wishart hierarchical model; an optional copula handles non-Gaussian data. A closed-form identity makes its posterior-mean covariance equal the Ledoit–Wolf shrinkage estimator exactly, so its prior strength comes from the data, without cross-validation. On a semi-synthetic 36-assay benchmark built from the residual covariance of about 780,000 real ADMET compounds, BRACE cuts the pass-probability mean absolute error by up to 76% versus the QComp multi-task baseline. Its always-on merging step matches or beats QComp in all 29 settings of a robustness sweep; the optional per-scaffold step helps when series-specific structure exists and hurts when it does not, and we map when to use it (chosen with hindsight here; an automatic rule is future work). On a real temporal split, the per-scaffold steps raise AUC-ROC from 0.789 to 0.860 and MCC from 0.37 to 0.53, and lower Brier from 0.187 to 0.152. However, about 96% of that gain comes from recalibrating each series’ mean and variance, which simple untuned shrinkage also achieves; BRACE’s distinctive cross-assay term adds about 4% here and matters mainly under strong cross-assay structure.

papers.title: Revisiting Spin Contamination in Mixed-Reference Spin-Flip Time-Dependent Density-Functional Theory
papers.abstract: Mixed reference spin-flip time-dependent density-functional theory (MRSF-TDDFT) has achieved widespread adoption as a computational method for describing photochemistry beyond the Franck–Condon region, as it removes most of the spin contamination limiting previous spin-flip (SF-)TDDFT approaches. The C → V excitation space, in which an electron from a doubly occupied (closed) orbital is promoted to an unoccupied (virtual) orbital, remains spin-incomplete in MRSF-TDDFT. The contamination induced by this incompleteness has consistently been reported as negligible, since the missing configurations are expected to be high in energy, thus barely coupling to low-lying vertical excitations. We show that the expression for 〈Ŝ 2 〉, which these assessments are based on, is erroneous and misses a key contribution of C → V excitations in singlet states, while triplet states always remain spin-pure. We derive and implement a corrected equation for 〈Ŝ 2 〉 and show that low-lying excited states with significant spin contamination become unavoidable if the singly occupied orbitals (SOMOs) localize onto a subsystem, decouple by symmetry, or if the density of orbitals around the Fermi level is high. We find that these results are virtually independent of the choice of density-functional approximation, but do not seem to impact the accuracy of excitation energies and spectroscopic properties. Nonetheless, these results show that severe spin contamination in MRSF-TDDFT becomes unavoidable when describing extended systems or the collective behavior of many chromophores.

papers.title: Structural Non-Identifiability of Photochemical Reaction Yields from Linear Optical Observables
papers.abstract: Identical time-resolved and steady-state optical observables can correspond to different reaction quantum yields when reactive and non-reactive dark exits are not independently resolved. We formulate linear photochemical networks as stable input-output systems with kinetic matrix K, observation matrix B, and reaction output vector q. Complete integrated yields are Φobs = BRu and ΦR = q⊤Ru, where R = (−K)−1 is the cumulative residence-time matrix. Pulse-steady-state equivalence and common rate scaling are treated as auxiliary linear-system facts. The central result is a structural non-identifiability theorem: if a reactive exit qj and a dark-loss exit lj from state j are not independently observed, then any redistribution q′ j + l′j = qj + lj leaves K, all non-reactive optical observables, and all spectral signals unchanged, while the reaction yield changes by ∆ΦR = δ (Ru)j . A one-state counterexample and a Jacobian analysis of the two-state thermally activated delayed fluorescence model with eight independent parameters θ = (kF , kP , kS,nr, kT,nr, i, r, qS, qT ) show that the luminescence observation map including fluorescence and phosphorescence, Y = (kF , kS, kT , ir, kP i), has rank 5 and a three-dimensional null space. Two directions reallocate reactive and dark-loss exits on the singlet and triplet states while leaving all luminescence observables unchanged; the third reallocates internal coupling and phosphorescence, and changes ΦR if and only if the triplet reaction exit qT is nonzero. A conditional experimental design table shows how direct product detection, state-selective observations, and multi-condition quenching restore identifiability. The results clarify when lifetime, delayed fluorescence, and transient absorption can be used to infer reaction quantum yields, and when they cannot.

papers.title: ARGUS: A Four-Signal Joint Model for H5N1 Neuraminidase Inhibitor Resistance Prediction
papers.abstract: Oseltamivir and zanamivir are the primary antivirals against H5N1 influenza, yet resistance profiles at the structural level remain incompletely characterized. Phenotypic screening requires one to two weeks in biosafety level 3 containment; during an active spillover event, this timescale is incompatible with clinical decisions. We present ARGUS (Affinity-and Representation-Guided Unified Scoring), a learned joint model combining four independent structural signals into a unified resistance risk framework: molecular docking affinity, protein language model evolutionary likelihood, perturbation response scanning, and all-atom pocket volume analysis. This work comprises two major components: (1) a comprehensive dual-drug saturation mutagenesis of the H5N1 neuraminidase binding pocket (1,102 mutations, 551 per drug) revealing a striking 166:1 asymmetry between oseltamivir-specific and zanamivir-specific resistance mutations, reflecting zanamivir’s substrate-mimicking pharmacophore; and (2) a novel four-signal learned joint model validated against 37 published fold-resistance measurements spanning H5N1, H1N1pdm09, H3N2, and H7N9 backgrounds (oseltamivir fold-resistance was the fitting target). The four-signal model achieves leave-one-out Spearman ρ = 0.628 (p = 0.000032), with a 95% bootstrap interval of [0.428, 0.845] for the in-sample correlation and a permutation p < 0.001. The earlier two-signal linear blend reached ρ = 0.659 (p = 0.0142) on only n=8 mutations, so the two figures are not directly comparable. The learned weights make docking the dominant signal (96.3% of the total weight) with ESM-2 LLR at 3.7%, which fits the view that protein language models alone conflate evolutionary constraint with drug-resistance specificity. Applied to the 2024 US H5N1 B3.13 outbreak, all 21 outbreak mutations are pocket-distal for both drugs, predicting maintained efficacy of both antivirals. ARGUS provides immediate structural assessment of any novel neuraminidase mutation without experimental work, and the full saturation landscape and trained models are released as a public resource on Zenodo.

papers.title: Adsorption regime changes the information needed for data-driven metal–organic framework screening
papers.abstract: How much fitting evidence, and which materials descriptors, are needed to prioritize porous materials? We analyze archived computational uptake labels for 279,010 metal–organic frameworks at four CO2/CH4 conditions (298 K). In retrospective experiments using target-informed example selection, each condition reaches at least 90% of its B = 1000 top-5% recall endpoint by B = 500. Local-chemistry RAC descriptors improve methane top-5% recall by 0.175 at 5.8 bar but only 0.039 at 65 bar, consistent with a pressure-dependent balance between chemical and geometric signals. These values describe predictor-fitting budgets, not total acquisition cost: the random-split setting also uses approximately 44,642 labeled structures for conformal calibration. Missing historical split identities and reference-informed candidate selection constrain transfer and shortlist claims. Thus, adsorption conditions appear to modify representation utility, while prospective label efficiency and physical attribution require independent, leakage-audited validation.

papers.title: Permutation-inversion insensitive comparison of three-dimensional molecular structures
papers.abstract: We present a new approach to compare molecular geometries from a purely geometric perspective. The first step of our algorithm uses permutation-insensitive alignment of two molecules with a Gaussian-kernel-damped analog of the mean-squared deviation (MSD) between two structures. Using this procedure, we restore a proper atom-to-atom mapping between two structures. This circumvents the factorial growth of permutation sampling in root-MSD analysis by globally optimizing a nonlinear function to find the best overlay of the structures. Then, we use a physics-driven approach to derive a dimensionless criterion for comparing two structures. This criterion uses the idea of quantum fluctuations in atomic positions and requires computing the mass-weighted MSD as a measure of proximity between structures. We also provide an implementation of our approach in a Python software and numerical examples of its performance.

papers.title: Machine learning prediction of bismuth recovery from literature data: publication-grouped validation, anchored calibration and chemical interpretation
papers.abstract: Machine learning models trained on published leaching data often report high accuracy from random splits that place runs of one study in both training and test sets. This study tested whether reported operating conditions can predict bismuth recovery for a study that the model has not seen. A data set of 485 runs from 82 sources was compiled across six unit operations; runs designed to retain bismuth, plate part of a bath or recover another metal were set aside, leaving 375 recovery runs from 72 studies. Thirteen models, including a mean baseline, were compared under random, publication-grouped and feedstock-grouped validation, and six of them under temporal validation. Random splits gave R2 up to 0.57, whereas publication-grouped validation gave at most 0.09 (95% interval −0.22 to 0.28); about half of the residual variance lay between publications. Three measured runs from a new study raised R2 for its remaining runs from about zero to 0.48, and Gaussian-process predictions were positively rank-correlated with measured recovery in 83% of studies. Within studies, recovery rose with acid concentration and temperature, although the temperature trend tended to reverse across studies. Literature data can therefore rank conditions for a new feed, but absolute prediction needs a few local measurements; an offline browser tool that applies this approach to leaching is provided.

papers.title: Iron Tetraphenylporphyrin for Electrocatalytic AmmoniaOxidation in Solution and Carbon-Supported Films
AriadneX: Unknown Crystalline Phase Discovery from Anomaly-Aware Unmixing of Powder X-Ray Diffraction Patterns
papers.abstract: Accelerated materials discovery produces experimental characterization data at a scale that requires evaluation to assess the chemical outcomes. For example, high-throughput materials synthesis approaches generate large arrays of powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) patterns from complex phase assemblages, in which signals from known and unknown products overlap. Identifying unknown crystalline phases still relies on expert assessment of unexplained reflections and does not scale with data generation. We introduce AriadneX, a tool for high-throughput multiphase PXRD analysis that curates a diffraction basis library appropriate to the chemistry, assigns known phases to each sample, and extracts structured diffraction signal unaccounted for by the library as an anomaly pattern. The coupled task of phase recovery and anomaly detection is formulated as a mixed-integer optimization problem with crystallographic constraints and constraints inspired by optimal transport (OT). In controlled leaveone-out tests, the method prioritizes samples containing deliberately withheld known phases. Applied to a realworld discovery dataset, AriadneX resolves two families of distinct unexplained diffraction patterns and estimates their Bragg diffraction patterns, consistent with the two unknown crystalline phases identified by human experts.

papers.title: WITHDRAWN
papers.abstract: Withdrawn by ChemRxiv because the content was truncated. A full copy is available at 10.26434/chemrxiv.15011293/v1

papers.title: Mechanistic basis of μ-opioid receptor allosteric modulation from molecular simulations
papers.abstract: The μ-opioid receptor (μOR) is a central mediator of analgesia and opioid-induced adverse effects, yet the molecular basis by which allosteric modulators reshape receptor signaling remains poorly understood. Here, we integrate all-atom molecular dynamics with unbinding kinetics simulations to resolve the mechanistic basis of positive and negative allosteric modulation of μOR. We show that the positive allosteric modulator BMS-986122 enhances signaling not through uniform stabilization of canonical active microswitches, but by selectively remodeling the sodium pocket and, critically, stabilizing the μOR–G protein interface. This stabilization increases interfacial interactions and buried surface area, providing a G protein–dependent mechanism for enhanced efficacy despite increased agonist conformational flexibility and weakened orthosteric contacts. In contrast, the negative allosteric modulator compound 368 broadly enforces inactive-like microswitch conformations while simultaneously stabilizing antagonist binding. Unbinding kinetics simulations reveal that 368 exerts a dominant kinetic effect, restricting naloxone egress pathways and increasing residence time by approximately three orders of magnitude. Together, these results establish a unified framework in which μOR allostery operates through modulation of receptor and ligand conformational dynamics, G protein engagement, and ligand dissociation kinetics. This work provides an atomistic foundation for the rational design of next-generation opioid therapeutics that exploit allosteric mechanisms to enhance efficacy and safety.

papers.title: Prediction of MOF Adsorption Isotherms and High-Throughput Screening Using a Physics-Informed Membranes Graph Neural Network
papers.abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are prime CO 2 -capture candidates, but grand canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) screening is costly when full isotherms, not single uptakes, are required; machine learning surrogates rarely resolve the continuous pressure response. We report a physics-informed pressure-aware multi-task graph neural network (PI-MGNN) to predict CO 2 uptake at arbitrary pressure and reconstruct isotherms from structure. From ~130,000 candidates, PCA and K-means select 5,023 representative MOFs, each simulated by GCMC at five pressures spanning 0.1-5.0 MPa, enforcing a continuous pressure response. Crystal graphs are processed by decoupled geometric and electrostatic graph-attention branches with auxiliary supervision, while a Gaussian-expanded pressure query is fused by cross-attention. PI-MGNN attains R 2 = 0.977 and MAE = 0.291 mol kg -1 ; isotherm MAEs are 0.428/0.312/0.330 mol kg -1 for high/medium/low-uptake MOFs, and cross-attention improves accuracy by 6.3%. Attention weights recover the pressure-resolved physics, enabling accurate and interpretable high-throughput screening.

papers.title: Descriptor-Based Regression Analysis Enables the Discovery of Highly Selective Ligands for Palladium-Catalyzed Siloxycyclopropanation
papers.abstract: A palladium-catalyzed siloxycyclopropanation of alkenes using acylsilanes as carbene precursors provides a distinctive catalytic approach to structurally diverse cyclopropanes through a siloxycarbene–palladium intermediate. Although the reaction scope and major mechanistic features have been established, the origin of its ligand-dependent diastereoselectivity has remained unclear, limiting the rational development of more selective catalysts. Here, we combine density functional theory (DFT) calculations, molecular parameterization, and statistical modeling to elucidate the steric and electronic factors governing the stereochemical outcome. DFT calculations of a series of NHC ligands and their corresponding siloxycarbene–palladium complexes provided a diverse set of molecular descriptors, which were used to construct a multivariate linear regression (MLR) model against experimental activation energies. The refined model identified complementary descriptors reflecting ligand steric demand, directional steric effects, and metal–ligand electronic interactions as key factors associated with the observed selectivity. MLR-guided virtual screening of 21 NHC ligands identified L24 and L30 as promising candidates for enhanced syn- and anti-selectivity, respectively, and their predicted selectivities were experimentally validated. The newly identified ligands not only improved the selectivity in their respective directions but also enabled a pronounced switch between syn- and anti-selectivity relative to the previously optimized ligand. Furthermore, L24 and L30 exhibited 2 complementary stereocontrol across a range of acylsilanes and alkenes beyond the benchmark reaction. Mechanistic analysis of the corresponding transition states revealed the roles of anisotropic steric environments and ligand-specific electronic interactions in determining the distinct stereochemical preferences of L24 and L30. These findings provide a mechanistic basis for ligand-controlled stereoselectivity in siloxycarbene–palladium cyclopropanation and establish molecular-level ligand features as useful parameters for improving and redirecting stereochemical

papers.title: When Ethylene Meets Sulfur: Direct Synthesis of Minimal Ethylene-Sulfur Copolymers
papers.abstract: In inverse vulcanization chemistry, research has predominantly focused on multifunctional unsaturated comonomers to stabilize sulfur-rich structures, whereas the direct copolymerization of elemental sulfur with simple olefins has remained comparatively unexplored. Extending this concept to the simplest olefin, we report Minimal Ethylene-Sulfur Copolymers (MinESC), synthesized through the direct reaction of gaseous ethylene with elemental sulfur via a base-mediated inverse vulcanization approach under mild conditions. These materials are viscoelastic fluids of tunable viscosity reaching exceptionally high values. They exhibit a peculiar sheet-like morphology, polar surfaces, elevated electrical conductivity, and high permittivity, and can be reprocessed into predominantly elastic structures following thermal treatment. Our approach provides a straightforward route to a distinct class of sulfurethylene-derived functional materials and demonstrates that inverse vulcanization chemistry can be extended to the simplest olefin under industrially relevant pressures and temperatures.

papers.title: Core-to-rim chemical zoning of a Paraíbatype tourmaline from Abulo, Ethiopia: Implications for origin determination
papers.abstract: Copper-bearing tourmaline of Paraíba type is now mined at Abulo in southern Ethiopia. We report the core-to-rim characterisation of one colour-zoned crystal attributed to this locality, obtained in Bangkok in June 2026. A sawn slab about 12 mm across and 5 mm thick was e x t e n s i v e l y analysed by electron microprobe (113 points), LA-ICP-MS analysis (45 spots on two traverses and 58 isotopes, totaling 2,565 concentration values with silicon as internal standard and GSE and NIST 610 as external standards), LA-ICP-TOFMS imaging (13,500 measuring spots of 24 µm and 55 isotopes, totalling 729,000 concentration values with silicon as internal standard and GSE and NIST 610 as external standard, about 505,000 of them above limits of detection), Raman spectroscopy (24 spectra) and a screening test by ED-XRF. The crystal is an Al–Li tourmaline of the elbaite series, including elbaite, fluor-elbaite, and elbaite with a liddicoatite component. Fluorine at the W site is 0.385 apfu in the core and exceeds the 0.5 apfu boundary to fluor-elbaite in the zones next to the core (0.51–0.53 apfu); 25 of 111 points lie within 1of that boundary. Ca/(Ca + Na) increases from core to rim but never exceeds σ 0.43. Lithium, measured by LA-ICP-MS, increases from about 7,840 µg/g in the core to about 10,000 µg/g in the outer zones. With this lithium taken zone by zone, boron and H O taken from 2 the formula and the unanalysed trace elements added as oxides, the analytical totals of the microprobe are 99.2 ± 0.5 wt.% over 111points.The trace elements are quantified on this measured matrix, with silicon measured by microprobe as internal standard using GSE and NIST610 as external standards. To our knowledge for the first time, silicon concentrations were measured across a growth profile of this material, in each of the five growth zones of the crystal. Themeasurementsprovide36.3 wt.% SiO2 in the core, 35.2–35.4 wt.% in the dark-blue zone, 35.5–35.8 wt% in the "neon"-blue zone, 35.9 wt% in the pink zone and 36.0 wt% in the yellowbrown zone. The concentrations of the trace elements are significantly zoned. Copper zone averages decrease from 16,200–25,700 µg/g in the core and the dark-blue zones around it to 1,420–1,820 µg/g in the yellow-brown outer zone. The iron concentration d e c r e a s e sfrom 4,130–4,150 µg/g to below detection. The bismuth concentration increases from 26–27 to 1,370 µg/g and the lead concentration from 146–160 to 1,650–1,810 µg/g. I nc o n t r a s t ,Gallium (629–741 µg/g as zone averages) and vanadium (58–158 µg/g at all 45 spots) vary far less. The element ratios used in origin determination therefore change by up to an order of magnitude inside this one crystal. For example, Cu/Ga changes from 2.3 to 41, Pb/Bi from 1.2 to 5.9 Peretti, Oberholzer, Allaz and Günther: Colour-zoned Paraíba-type tourmaline from Ethiopia. Draft of 9 October 2026 2 / 78 and Fe/Mn starts below detection to 1.1 w h i c ha r ecalculated as zone averages. The imaging confirms the element ratios of the spot analyses and separates the elements that are present in the tourmaline's composition from those carried by inclusions, which are detected above the matrix composition of the tourmaline. Of the rare earth elements, only the light rare earths, La to Sm, are present in the tourmaline's composition. Yttrium is also present in the tourmaline, at about 0.6–0.9 µg/g outside the core and lower in the core. The other elements found in the tourmaline include Li, Be, Sn, Ga, Nb, Ta and B, all of which are typically found in LCT pegmatites. Compared with our 2009 reference profiles for Brazil, Mozambique and Nigeria, the crystal from Ethopia has higher vanadium and gallium concentrations and evolves toward bismuth rather than manganese. A high vanadium concentration is independently reported for Ethiopian material by other laboratories, and the vanadium test proposed there holds across the growth zones of this crystal, with the core at the limitofdetection. The gallium difference from Mozambique is small, whereas the published Ethiopian gallium concentration extends to 280 µg/g. Because the comparison is based on a very detailed analysis of five growth zones, the reported observations are very significant and represent more information than the analyses of larger sample sets. Therefore, this information is crucial as origin criteria. Individual analyses of samples could represent mixtures of various growth zones and would not easily be identified withoutknowledgeaboutthegrowth stage. Any discriminant therefore has to be implemented into the growth-stage concentration profiles of this study as reference. A limited Raman data set, placed on the element maps, shows that the framework bands shift with the copper concentration and that the OH bands follow the fluorine and lithium concentrations; these relations are shown for one crystal.

papers.title: Photocatalytic CO <sub>2</sub> Conversion Driven by UV Light Above 300 nm Using Ammonia as an Electron Donor
papers.abstract: Efficient utilisation of solar UV light ( λ > 300 nm) is essential for practical photocatalytic CO 2 conversion. However, in conventional systems using water as an electron donor, slow water oxidation kinetics present a critical bottleneck that severely limits the CO production rate. Here, we demonstrate an efficient CO 2 conversion system that overcomes this kinetic limitation by employing ammonia as an alternative electron donor over Mg-doped SrTiO 3 loaded with Ag and Fe as dualcocatalysts (Ag–Fe/Mg–SrTiO 3 ). Under UV irradiation ( λ > 300 nm), the optimised photocatalyst achieved a remarkable CO produc on rate exceeding 200 μmol h −1 . Mechanistic investigations revealed that the Fe cocatalyst played a crucial role in promoting ammonia oxidation, facilitating the rapid consumption of photogenerated holes, and significantly enhancing CO 2 conversion activity. Furthermore, nitrite (NO 2 − ) was successfully quantified as the primary oxidation product of ammonia, yielding a calculated e − / h + balance of approximately 1.2, validating the stoichiometric relationship of the reaction. This study offers a promising strategy for simultaneously achieving the upcycling of CO 2 and effective utilisation of ammonia as both an energy source and an electron donor.

papers.title: Mechanistic Classification of Multicatalysis
papers.abstract: Multicatalysis combines two or more catalytic functions within a single reaction network and can unlock reactivity, selectivity, and synthetic efficiency that are difficult to achieve with an individual catalyst. Its mechanistic description, however, remains fragmented across partially overlapping terms such as tandem, relay, cooperative, synergistic, double-activation, and bifunctional catalysis, among others. Here, we propose a mechanism-first classification based on the relationship between catalytic functions and, specifically, on the catalytic ‘currency’ exchanged between them. When the currency is substrate-derived, the coupling is classified as tandem, cooperative, or double activation. When the exchanged currency controls catalyst state rather than contributing to the substrate framework (e.g. electrons, cofactors), the relationship is gated or regenerative, distinguished by whether activation is required only once or repeatedly during turnover. Importantly, the classification is additive, so complex reaction networks are represented as combinations of pairwise relationships. Representative reactions illustrate how this framework resolves mechanistic distinctions that are hidden by conventional labels. By linking nomenclature to the elementary connection between catalytic functions, the classification provides a compact language for comparing multicatalytic systems and a basis for more deliberate catalyst and reaction-network design.

papers.title: Substituent Effects on Anion Bonding and Disassembly of Hypervalent Iodine Macrocycles
papers.abstract: A series of phenylalanine-derived hypervalent iodine-based macrocycles (HIMs) bearing electron donating and withdrawing substituents were prepared. The HIM associations with the anion of tetrabutylammonium chloride (TBA-Cl) were systematically investigated using binding isotherms generated via NMR spectroscopy. The association constants of the resulting I-Cl bond were found to linearly correlate with the electronic substituents via Hammett analysis. Electron-withdrawing substituents strengthened the I–Cl bond and disassembled the macrocycle more readily. In addition, the shifting of HIM carbonyl frequencies obtained by Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy were found to correlate with the binding affinities and provide an alternative predictive methodology to determine HIM disassembly and anion binding affinities.

papers.title: Conformational Heterogeneity and Local Electronic Structure in Wild-Type and Arctic Amyloid-Β42
papers.abstract: Amyloid-𝛽 42 is a heterogeneous system, widely known as an intrinsically disordered protein, or IDP, sampling a variety of conformations. However, how ensemble redistribution affects the underlying local electronic structure remains less well understood. In this study, classical molecular dynamics simulations are combined with population-aware density functional theory and reduced active-space calculations to compare the LVFFA fragment of the wild-type and Arctic (E22G) variants. Common-space principal component analysis, clustering, and Ramachandran plot analysis depicted distinct trajectory distributions and greater conformational heterogeneity for the E22G trajectory. Population-ranked conformations representing 60.58% of WT and 54.98% of Arctic populations yielded conditional population-weighted B3LYP/def2-SVP HOMO-LUMO separations of 5.81 and 5.95 eV, respectively. The 0.14 eV Arctic–WT shift remained positive across moving-block bootstrap analyses. Fragment expansion altered frontier-orbital ordering, although the spatial character of LVFFA-associated states was preserved. CASCI tested active-space sensitivity, and matched UCCSD-VQE calculations reproduced CAS(4,4) CASCI reference energies for the reduced Hamiltonians. Together, these results demonstrate the importance of population-aware conformational sampling and model-definition sensitivity when relating heterogeneous biomolecular ensembles to quantum-chemical properties.

papers.title: Assessing the Limits of He Isotope Separation Under
papers.abstract: Separation of helium isotopes is of interest owing to the critical importance and limited supply of helium-3 (3He). Nanoporous materials offer a viable route for gas-phase isotope separation through either selective adsorption or quantum sieving. Here, to maximize the isotope selectivity of quantum sieving we propose coupling a strongly attracting open-metal site for He adsorption to a surrounding nanopore acting as a confining potential. We demonstrate that upon tightening the pore, the zero-point energy (ZPE) elevates up to a point where 3He detaches while 4He remains bound. Our model shows that 100% isotope-selective adsorption of 4He is achieved when pores of diameter 4.8-5.3 Å are coupled to metal sites with He binding energies of 2-20 kJ/mol. At 20 K, operating pressures between 0.3-30 bar are estimated, which increase to 2-6 kbar at 77 K. Even if the exact pore size for 100% isotope-selective adsorption cannot be realized, our results provide a rational design strategy for materials with unprecedentedly large He isotope separation factors at elevated temperatures.

papers.title: Defining the Catalytic Boundaries of N -Nitrosourea-Forming StzF/SznF and Related Metalloenzymes through Genome Mining and Mechanistic Analysis
papers.abstract: Enzymatic N–N bond formation is a rare and chemically challenging transformation in natural product biosynthesis. The non-heme iron metalloenzyme SznF catalyzes the formation of the N -nitrosourea pharmacophore of streptozotocin via the coordinated action of a diiron heme-oxygenase-like (HDO) domain and a mononuclear iron cupin domain. Although recent computational studies have advanced mechanistic models for this transformation, the determinants governing substrate specificity within this enzyme family remain poorly understood. Here, we employed a multi-pronged approach combining genome mining, substrate scope screening, protein engineering, structural analysis, and biochemical characterization to define the catalytic boundaries of SznF and related homologs. Genome mining identified a previously uncharacterized homolog displaying higher activity toward the native substrate N ω -methyl-L-arginine than SznF, expanding the known repertoire of N-nitrosourea-forming metalloenzymes. Comprehensive substrate screening further revealed the first non-native substrate accepted by this enzyme family, N ω -propyl-L-arginine, whereas all other modifications in carbon chain length, guanidino substitution, alkylation state, or stereochemistry did not result in detectable turnover. Structure-guided engineering that targeted the binding pocket surrounding the terminal alkyl substituent increased the activity of several variants toward N ω -propyl-L-arginine compared to wildtype SznF. Furthermore, cascade experiments, and nitric oxide supplementation further demonstrate that productive catalysis requires a precise combination of steric, electronic, and geometric features that cannot readily be compensated by alternative substrates. Together, these findings show that the substrate specificity of SznF and related homologs is governed by mechanistic constraints arising from the tightly coupled hydroxylation and rearrangement chemistry underlying N–N bond formation. More broadly, this work defines the catalytic boundaries of enzymatic N -nitrosourea formation while identifying new opportunities for the discovery and engineering of N–N bond-forming metalloenzymes for biocatalytic synthesis of structurally diverse N -nitrosourea derivatives.

papers.title: A study of the valence shell photoionization dynamics following core level resonant excitation in imidazole
papers.abstract: The photoionization and subsequent Auger decay dynamics of core-excited states in imidazole have been investigated at the carbon and nitrogen K-edges using linearly polarized synchrotron radiation. Ion yield measurements in the pre-edge regions were used to locate core-level transitions into either unoccupied valence or Rydberg states, and assignments were made through comparison with simulated spectra obtained using the RASPT2 method. Valence shell photoelectron spectra were recorded at photon energies coinciding with these core-level transitions, using two polarization orientations to allow the photoelectron angular distributions to be determined. The interpretation of these resonantly excited photoelectron spectra was guided by RASPT2 simulations that helped distinguish between participator and spectator contributions. Autoionization strongly affects the photoelectron intensity and angular distributions of the outer valence 1h states. Spectator contributions become evident at binding energies above 15 eV, and some of the intense 2h-1p states are well-described by the calculations, allowing assignments to be proposed. The non-resonantly excited C(KVV) and N(KVV) Auger spectra have been measured and some of the features at high kinetic energies have been assigned.

papers.title: Density Functional Theory Bond Dissociation Energies of Model Compounds Relevant to LDL Oxidation: Bis-Allylic C–H, Phenolic O–H and Hydroperoxide O–H Bonds
papers.abstract: Background : Oxidative modification of low-density lipoprotein (LDL) contributes to atherogenesis, with polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) as its main chemical target. Vitamin E is an effective chainbreaking antioxidant in vitro, yet large clinical trials showed no cardiovascular benefit. We calculated bond dissociation energies (BDEs) of model compounds to quantify the underlying thermodynamics. Methods : Density functional theory calculations (PySCF; B3LYP/6-311+G(d,p)//B3LYP/6-31G*, scaled zero-point energy, 0K) were performed for butane, 1,4-pentadiene, phenol, catechol and methyl hydroperoxide. Vitamin E was not calculated at the relaxed level; published values were used. A truncated tocopherol model (5,7,8-trimethylchroman-6-ol) was run at screening level only (B3LYP/6-31+G*, unrelaxed geometries, no zero-point correction), with phenol at the same level. Results : The bis-allylic C–H bond of 1,4-pentadiene (68.2 kcal/mol) was 28.3 below that of butane (96.5). Catechol O–H (73.4) was 8.4 below phenol (81.8). The hydroperoxide model (79.6) fell 2.2 below phenol, opposite to the approximate literature order; the cause was not investigated. In screening calculations the tocopherol model was 9.0 below phenol. Published values place α-tocopherol O–H at about 77 to 78 kcal/mol, about 10 below phenol, the same direction as our screening gap. Computed values were 1.7 to 8.6 kcal/mol below approximate literature values, so gaps and ordering, not absolute values, are interpreted. Conclusions : The calculations quantify the thermodynamic basis for PUFA vulnerability and for the stronger hydrogen donation of polyphenol-type O–H bonds. They do not by themselves show donation to peroxyl radicals. Bond energies cannot explain the clinical trial results; kinetics, LDL localization and tocopherol-mediated peroxidation must be considered. No clinical outcomes or biomarkers were computed.

papers.title: Enhanced Sodium Metal Anode Cycling Stability via an Organometallic Electrolyte Additive
papers.abstract: Despite the high theoretical capacity of sodium metal anodes, practical application is limited by the general instability of the solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) leading to dendritic growth and capacity fade. Here we report that the dimolybdenum paddlewheel complex, Mo2(mea)4 (1, mea = 2-(2-methoxyethoxy)acetate), functions as an effective electrolyte additive for Na metal anodes at millimolar loadings, enabled by self-assembly on the anode surface upon formation of aggregates involving 1 and Na+. In symmetric Na||Na cells, additive 1 was found to increase cycling stability and attenuate overpotential growth and impedance rise over 450 cycles compared to additive-free controls. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy revealed that 1 promotes early formation of an inorganic-rich SEI that also contains intact 1 and its downstream products. Scanning electron microscopy confirmed suppression of morphologies associated with dendrite growth. Full-cell Na||Na3V2(PO4)3 testing demonstrated improved Coulombic efficiency relative to an additive-free control and served to validate cathode compatibility of the additive. This work establishes organometallic complexes as an effective “third class” of Na metal battery additives, complementing purely organic or inorganic systems.

papers.title: Detection and Characterization of the Cosmological Neutrino Background by EPR Spectroscopy on Molecular Hydrino with Implications for Telecommunications
papers.abstract: A hydrino atom, H(1/p) solved using a Maxwellian electrodynamics and relativistic mechanics, is atomic hydrogen with state energy En = -13.598/n2 eV, in which n = 1/p, and p is limited by the energy in the electric field of the proton to 126 whereafter the proton and electron decay. Electron transitions to hydrino states involve an initial non-radiative energy transfer to a catalyst that serves as an energy hole or sink of a quantized amount of energy, 2mE1 (m is integer) to be transferred to a catalyst such as HOH, a free or nascent water molecule. Furthermore, hydrino atoms can react to form the corresponding diatomic molecule referred to as molecular hydrino H2(1/p). In contrast to molecular hydrogen (H2), the molecular hydrino (H2(1/p)) is paramagnetic with S = ½ comprising a paired and unpaired electron in the same MO wherein the lower energy state central field is provided by photons akin to gluons in nucleons in addition to the field of the protons. Due to its unique structure, H2(1/p)) interacts with the neutrinos in the energy range of the cosmological neutrino background (𝐶𝜈𝐵) as confirmed by the neutrino mediated observations of predicted fine structure, predicted high magnetic field Paschen Beck effect, large downfield shifts, temporal changes of EPR spectra due to accumulated changes in fine structure state populations, extraordinary broadened signals, zero order absorption occurring in the perpendicular and parallel modes, and the observation of magnetic dipole-dipole interactions of H2(1/4)-H2 dimer requiring intramolecular angular momentum transfer from a neutrino excited fine structure state in H2(1/4) as well as unique temperature and matrix dependences of the EPR signals. EPR was used to detect and characterize the 𝐶𝜈𝐵 for the first time. The isotropic and parallel propagation nature of 𝐶𝜈𝐵 can be exploited for line of site telecommunications requiring no transmission power to transmit signals in any direction unattenuated and undispersed through any physical barrier, including the Earth.

papers.title: Size-Controlled HgTe Nanocrystals Achieve Near-Unity Shortwave Infrared Emission
papers.abstract: The near-infrared (NIR, 700-1000 nm) and short-wave infrared (SWIR, 1000-2000 nm) regions of light are privileged for optoelectronic applications due to the decreased scattering and diminished autofluorescence arising from the few natural chromophores which absorb or emit in these windows. We demonstrate a two-stage, size-resolved synthesis of spherical HgTe quantum dots (QDs) with narrowband photoluminescence tunable across the NIR and SWIR which combine exceptionally high photoluminescence quantum yields (QY > 80%), low polydispersity (<10%), and stability in air. Using this synthetic control, we determine the size-dependent bandgap and molar extinction coefficients of HgTe under extreme confinement, and show conclusively that separating nucleation from growth — via a fast injection followed by a slow one — suppresses Ostwald ripening. Post-synthetic incubation with zinc salts further improves optical stability, pushing QY to near unity across the SWIR, including at telecom-relevant wavelengths. We then formulate water-soluble HgTe QD micelles as contrast agents for in vivo mouse imaging in the SWIR, achieving 100 frame/s video-rate imaging above 1400 nm with contrast and temporal resolution that substantially exceed those of indocyanine green. Together, these results establish that even without a protective shell, HgTe QDs offer a near-optimal, air-stable platform for optoelectronic applications at telecom-relevant wavelengths .

papers.title: Density Functional Theory of Dion-Jacobson Double Perovskite Halides
papers.abstract: First-principles density functional theory was used to study six (four unreported) hybrid layered double perovskites of the Dion-Jacobson A2MM ′′′ X8 family. All 6 compounds consist of organic diamines that bridge rock-saltordered inorganic octahedra, with Ag+ as the M ′ site and Bi+3/Sb+3 as the M′′′ site. Both aliphatic (1,3-diaminopropane [PDA], 1,4-diaminobutane [BDA], 1,8-diaminooctane [ODA]) and aromatic (para-phenylenediamine [PPDA]) spac-ers are investigated, revealing how composition affects the band gap character and magnitude. Formation energy analysis using the DFT-D3 method reveals negative formation energies with respect to relevant precursors. Furthermore, calculations using the complex dielectric function reveal key optical properties, including absorption coefficients, refractive indices, and complex permittivity.

papers.title: Phosphorus(V) Umpolung Converts Electrophilic Phosphates into Nucleophilic H-Phosphonates
papers.abstract: Ubiquitous in chemistry, biology and medicine, phosphate groups form the backbone of DNA and RNA, and their analogues like phosphorothioate antisense oligonucleotides provide frontier therapies for challenging genetic disorders. However, the inherent electrophilicity of phosphorus(V) and thermodynamic stability of native P–OH bonds preclude their direct, latestage conversion into phosphate analogues. Here, we introduce a polarity-reversal (umpolung) strategy for converting electrophilic phosphates into nucleophilic H-phosphonates. This approach proceeds through two stages: P–OH thiolation into a thiophosphate followed by radical P–S cleavage, which generates the P–H bond. This sequence converts diverse phosphate substrates, such as complex drug scaffolds and nucleotides, into H-phosphonates that can undergo further phosphorus functionalization. The thiolation step also enables direct, one-pot conversion of P–OH into P–SH in nucleotides, providing a chemical route to the phosphorothioation of native phosphate backbones associated with bacterial and archaeal DNA defense. Therefore, phosphorus(V) umpolung reverses the polarity of phosphate chemistry, transforming otherwise stable P–OH bonds into synthetically versatile phosphorus functionalities.

papers.title: Complementary Roles of Iodide-Mediated Pathways and Anion Dynamics in Lithium-Ion Transport in Li3PS4-LiI Glasses
papers.abstract: LiI addition enhances lithium-ion transport in sulfide glasses, yet the microscopic mechanisms linking halide incorporation to faster conduction remain unclear. Here, we investigate how LiI promotes Li+ migration in (100−x)Li3PS4–xLiI glasses by resolving changes in local structure, migration energetics, and anion dynamics. A machinelearning potential trained on newly generated ab initio molecular dynamics data and an existing sulfide-electrolyte dataset enables 10 ns simulations of approximately 5000atom glass models at 300 K over a LiI content range of 0–50 mol%. The potential is validated against density functional theory calculations, experimental densities, and X-ray total scattering profiles. Although the PS4 3–units remain intact and their time-averaged inter-unit correlations change little, Li+ diffusivity more than doubles across this composition range, accompanied by increased migration beyond local cage-like regions. To characterize the energetics of these pathways in a disordered environment, we introduce an analysis that combines Voronoi partitioning into P-and I–-centered domains with atomic potentialenergy fluctuations along Li+ trajectories. The resulting statistical local energy-barrier indicators allow comparisons between domain transitions without assigning absolute activation energies. This analysis reveals two complementary effects of LiI addition. Transitions involving I–-centered domains exhibit lower barrier indicators than direct transitions between P-centered domains, identifying favorable I–-mediated migration pathways. LiI addition also lowers the barrier indicators for direct P-to-P transitions, extending its influence beyond pathways that pass through I–-centered domains. Enhanced local translational and rotational dynamics of PS4 3–units accompany this broader reduction, suggesting that anion motion helps facilitate Li+ migration. These findings explain how LiI can enhance transport while largely preserving the average glass structure and highlight the combined roles of local migration pathways and anion dynamics in designing sulfide glass electrolytes.

papers.title: Customizable Approach to Conformer Space Discretization using Torsion Angular Bin Strings (customTABS)
papers.abstract: Conformational ensembles of small organic molecules are primarily determined by the rotameric states of their torsional or dihedral angles. The previously introduced concept of torsion angular bin strings (TABS) is a discrete vector representation of a molecule’s dihedral states, which therefore offer a quantitative description of such ensembles. Discretization of the torsional-angle space allows us to count distinct conformational states, giving an estimate of the upper limit of the expected conformational ensemble size (nTABS). In addition to nTABS being used as a qualitative measure of molecular flexibility, TABS itself is a way of grouping conformers of a molecule without picking thresholds. In the initial version of the TABS application, the discretization was based on crystal-structure derived torsion preferences, which may not be fully transferable to the conformational preferences in other environments. Here, we present the extension of the TABS framework to consider observed, system-specific distributions for the discretization of the conformational space. CustomTABS can be used to decompose the given conformational ensemble into the torsional states, which can be useful for clustering, importance ranking of dihedrals, or convergence analysis. We present the algorithmic solutions developed for the customTABS extension and demonstrate their application in clustering molecular dynamics (MD) trajectories and monitoring the convergence of the observed torsional space.

papers.title: Chromoselective Control for Aminoalkylation of CF3‑Alkenes through Low-Energy Photoredox Catalysis
papers.abstract: Recent advances in chromoselective photoredox catalysis have demonstrated that light wavelength can serve as a powerful and orthogonal reaction parameter, enabling divergent reactivity from a single catalytic system. Building on recent advances in the sequential decarboxylative/defluorinative aminoalkylation of trifluoromethyl-substituted alkenes, we report a divergent, wavelength-dependent strategy for the site-selective functionalization of N-arylglycines. High-throughput experimentation (HTE) was used to systematically screen photocatalysts and irradiation wavelengths to identify the most suitable divergent conditions. Interestingly, using [Ru(bpy)3]2+ as photocatalyst, irradiation with blue light promotes efficient difunctionalization of CF3-alkenes with N-arylglycines, affording monofluoroalkenyl-1,5-diamines, while switching the irradiation to red light enables selective monofunctionalization, delivering the corresponding gem-difluoroalkenyl amine intermediates exclusively under otherwise identical conditions, via a spin-forbidden transition pathway. This wavelength-governed switchable reactivity provides a powerful and tunable platform for the controlled radical modification of amino acids, expanding the synthetic utility of visible-light photoredox catalysis in divergent amine synthesis. Mechanistic investigations using photoelectrochemistry and TD-DFT have revealed notably a photo-excitation of intermediates, allowing for the second functionalization to whether happens or not, based on the irradiation wavelength used.

papers.title: Solvent Dynamics and Multiconfigurational Treatment Drive the Anomalous Stokes Shift of HINA
papers.abstract: The 3-hydroxyisonicotinaldehyde (HINA) anion is one of the smallest known green-emissive fluorophores, yet the origin of its anomalously large Stokes shift (0.87 eV) remains unexplained. Given the well-established influence of the surrounding environment on the photophysical properties of fluorescent dyes, we examine its role in this shift by simulating the anion's absorption and emission spectra with four computational protocols that differ in configurational sampling, solvent treatment, and electronic-structure method. Wigner sampling protocols capture less than half of the experimental Stokes shift, whether the solvent is treated implicitly or explicitly, whereas QM/MM molecular dynamics sampling improves it significantly. Structural analysis associates this improvement with coupling between the first solvation shell and the intramolecular interaction between the aldehyde hydrogen and the hydroxyl oxygen, which is captured by molecular-dynamics sampling but not by the corresponding frozen-solute Wigner-sampling protocol. When combined with RMS-CASPT2, this sampling quantitatively reproduces the experimental spectra and Stokes shift (0.85 versus 0.87 eV), showing that quantitative description of the Stokes shift of HINA requires both solvent-induced conformational dynamics and a multiconfigurational electronic-structure treatment.

papers.title: Free induction decay-detected high-field electron spin resonance for accurate monitoring highly polarized spin dynamics
Solid-phase synthesis and structure-degradation relationships of VHL-recruiting PROTACs for preferential histone deacetylase 6 degradation
papers.abstract: This work reports on a series of von Hippel-Lindau (VHL)-recruiting histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6) PROTACs based on a vorinostat-inspired HDAC inhibitor. Systematic variations of the VHL ligand, the exit vector, and the linker architecture revealed that longer, semi-rigid linkers promoted efficient HDAC6 degradation. Compounds 12-15 emerged as potent HDAC6 degraders, with 15 exhibiting a half-maximal degradation value of 26 nM with 12 showing particularly rapid degradation kinetics. The lead compounds induced pronounced and preferential HDAC6 degradation in MM.1S and FLT3-ITD-positive MV4-11 cells. Notably, 13-15 displayed submicromolar antiproliferative activity in MV4-11 cells and significantly induced apoptosis. Compound 13 was markedly more active than its non-degrading control nc-13, despite nearly identical HDAC1 and HDAC6 inhibitory activities, which underscores the important contribution of targeted HDAC degradation to the antiproliferative activity. Overall, this study supports VHL-mediated targeted degradation as a promising strategy to translate HDAC6 targeting into pronounced antileukemic activity.

papers.title: Pathway Reweighting in DNA Reaction Networks Enables Adaptation to Environmental Pressures
papers.abstract: Adaptive biochemical reaction networks must respond to environmental changes while maintaining function, yet synthetic networks typically rely on predefined pathways and stimulus–response relationships. Here, we introduce pathway reweighting as a strategy for adaptivity in DNA strand-displacement reaction networks. We design a splitting network in which two competing pathways connect a shared initial state to a common output. This allows environmental perturbations to redistribute reaction flux between the pathways while preserving overall network function. We showcase environmental sensitivity by integrating pHresponsive i-motif and ATP-binding aptamer motifs that enable selective and proportional adaptation. Combining these pressures demonstrates pathway reweighting under more complex, biologically relevant environmental conditions. Beyond proportional adaptation, we introduce a distinct, history-dependent mechanism based on an enzymatic feed-forward loop. The loop progressively modifies the Input strand, creating delayed pathway reweighting and encoding a memory of prior environmental exposure. A deep-learning reaction-network framework resolves the resulting interconnected dynamics and identifies changes in pathway utilization without requiring complete mechanistic parameterization. Our experimentalnumerical framework enables the rational design of synthetic CRNs whose adaptive behavior emerges from network organization rather than explicit reaction-by-reaction programming.

papers.title: Drug Molecular and Route Similarity-Aware Retrieval-Augmented LLM Generation with Knowledge Graph for Semantic Reasoning
papers.abstract: To address the inherent limitations of large language models (LLMs) in chemical synthesis—hallucinations, and low knowledge dense—this study presents a Knowledge Graph–enhanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework (KG-RAG-LLM) with a multi-scale calculation of molecular and route similarity. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that KG-RAG-LLM significantly mitigates hallucinations, increasing the proportion of concrete chemical information in generated responses to 39.52%–40.87%, drastically outperforming baseline LLMs and standard literature-based RAG pipelines in response completeness and accuracy. To overcome the inability of traditional 2D linear fingerprints to capture 3D spatial properties and reaction path variations, we further developed a multidimensional molecular and route similarity calculation combining SimHash, core similarity, and FCFP, as an alternative to Route CGR representations coupled with UMAP dimensionality reduction. This formulation accurately distinguishes between subtle and distinct synthetic strategies, demonstrating superior precision over traditional clustering methods for fuzzy retrieval of synthetic routes. Overall, this work provides a reliable, knowledge-dense solution for intelligent retrosynthetic Semantic Reasoning.

papers.title: Commit: Automated Scale-Up Crystallisation DataFactory for model-based pharmaceutical process development: a data-driven, mechanistic and hybrid model case study
papers.abstract: In 2025, we introduced the Scale-Up Crystallisation DataFactory, an automated platform for crystallisation experimentation and Bayesian optimisation. However, the initial case study used a relatively simple three-parameter, single-objective optimisation problem. In this Commit paper, we extend the platform to a five-dimensional, multi-objective cooling-antisolvent crystallisation of lovastatin and benchmark data-driven, mechanistic and hybrid optimisation approaches. Sixteen screening experiments were followed by model-guided experiments targeting yield and particle size (D90). Bayesian optimisation produced continued improvements in hypervolume, while mechanistic and hybrid approaches did not improve experimental performance beyond screening. The results demonstrate the value of experimentally benchmarking optimisation strategies for autonomous process development.

papers.title: Removal of Cu(II) and a PET Glitter Microplastic Surrogate by Alginate, Alginate–Opuntia, and Chitosan-Treated Alginate–Opuntia Beads
papers.abstract: The use of alginate-only beads, alginate–Opuntia (AO) beads, and chitosan-treated AO beads for the removal of Cu(II) and a PET glitter (a microplastic surrogate) from water has been investigated. Each bead type was made from the previous one by the addition of one component. Batch experiments were carried out in water containing glitter, Cu(II), or both, and AO beads soaked in dilute acetic acid without chitosan served as a control for the acid. The removal of Cu(II) in copper-only water was 45.71 ± 1.97%, 59.44 ± 2.28%, and 84.19 ± 2.65% for the alginate-only, AO, and chitosan-treated beads, respectively (mean ± SD, n = 12, 6 h, 140 rpm). Opuntia increased the Cu(II) removal by 13.72 percentage points and chitosan by a further 24.75 points (paired t-test, p < 0.001 for both, and p ≤ 0.0013 for the batch means). In the presence of 2.00 g of glitter, the chitosan-treated beads still removed about 84% of the Cu(II). Meanwhile, the glitter removal increased by about 7 points with Opuntia but changed by less than 0.25 points with chitosan (p = 0.648 and 0.231). No significant difference was found between the acid-soaked and the untreated AO beads. It can be concluded that Opuntia was responsible for the increase in glitter capture and chitosan for most of the increase in Cu(II) removal.

papers.title: The role of membrane properties and environmental footprint in shaping the cost-climate optimal carbon capture processes
papers.abstract: Membrane development for carbon capture is typically guided by CO2 permeability and CO2/N2 selectivity, although these properties alone cannot determine whether a material will deliver economically and environmentally favourable performance at scale. Herein, we develop a multi-criteria optimization framework that integrates a machine-learning surrogate model of a multi-stage membrane process with techno-economic analysis and life cycle assessment. By applying this framework to mixed matrix membranes, we investigate the interplay of membrane properties and membrane-specific inventories in defining process-level costs and environmental indicators. For the capture from flue gases produced by a waste incinerator plant and a cement plant, electricity is mostly driven by CO2/O2 selectivity within the investigated range and is the dominant contributor to process costs and climate change impacts. This makes the climate benefits of membrane-based capture strongly dependent on the electricity supply: high-performance membranes supplied with carbon-intensive electricity can have climate change impacts comparable to or even higher than those of low-performing membranes supplied with low-carbon electricity. Therefore, we show for the first time how the system-level context shapes the properties that must be prioritized and their target values to unlock economic and environmental benefits: membrane synthesis and lifetime have a substantial impact in the presence of clean electricity, whereas increasingly high CO2/O2 and CO2/N2 selectivity are needed in the presence of moderate to high carbon intensity. Overall, with this work, we identify priorities for improvement in membrane production and performance that could only be revealed by jointly considering process-level costs and environmental impacts.

papers.title: Cholesteric Liquid Crystals for Ultratrace PFAS Detection
papers.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent, mobile water contaminants associated with adverse effects on human health and ecosystems. Current analytical methods require specialized instrumentation, complicating their on-site detection at ultratrace concentrations across distributed water infrastructures. Here we integrate fluorophilic partitioning and proton-responsive recognition within a cholesteric liquid crystal (CLC). The fluorinated component promotes selectivity over non-fluorinated structural analogues, whereas the pyridine receptor transduces protonation into changes in helical organization and reflected color. The formulation was confined within monodisperse spherical droplets and processed as a photocurable photonic ink to produce sensing strips with a strong reflection signal readable by portable fiber-optic spectroscopy. The platform detected five PFAS through concentration-dependent blue-shifts, reaching detection limits of 5.9 parts per trillion (ppt) without sample preconcentration and maintaining comparable performance across three water matrices. Coupling molecular recognition to collective supramolecular reorganization establishes CLCs as promising sensing materials for on-site ultratrace PFAS detection.

papers.title: Building the Data Foundations for the Design and Discovery of Transition Metal Complexes
papers.abstract: The unique chemistry of transition metal complexes (TMCs) enables several advanced technologies in diverse fields including renewable energies, medicine, and catalysis. Machine learning methods can accelerate their rational design but are bounded by limited dataset sizes, restricted chemical scopes, and insufficient quality. This Perspective surveys the current landscape of TMC datasets and investigates how they seek to address these challenges. The analysis focuses on the data curation processes as well as the scope of the properties provided, and their level of theory. Furthermore, the applications and methodological advancements enabled by TMC datasets are reviewed, including the generative design of metal ligands and the evolutionary optimization of TMCs. The Perspective concludes by outlining future directions, with particular emphasis on extending data to broader chemical scopes including non-equilibrium geometries, establishing community-wide data formats and benchmarks, and developing strategies to effectively integrate heterogeneous data sources.

papers.title: Electrochemical Capture of Microplastics via Reversible Metal Deposition in Aqueous Solutions
papers.abstract: Microplastics are persistent aqueous contaminants for which effective removal strategies remain needed. Here, we investigate electrochemical deposition as a means of capturing suspended polystyrene (PS) particles. The purpose of this study is to understand the plausibility of electrochemical deposition as a means for removing microplastics from aqueous systems. The central hypothesis guiding this work is that ramified solid metallic deposits created during electrodeposition can mechanically capture plastic particles suspended in the liquid phase. PS particles of 200 nm and 250 μm were evaluated in ZnSO4 electrolyte under applied potentials from 0 to −4 V, with surfactant conditions also examined. Electrochemical treatment resulted in visibly reduced turbidity, suggesting a decrease in suspended particle concentration. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) showed particles attached to or incorporated within deposited zinc.
