Particle capture was not observed at 0 V but was evident under active zinc deposition at −2 V, supporting the role of electrodeposited zinc in particle capture. The observed particle–electrode interactions differed with particle size: larger particles were partially embedded within rough, dendritic zinc deposits, whereas nanoscale particles were densely distributed across the deposited structure. These observations demonstrate the ability of electrodeposition to facilitate particle capture through distinct particle–deposit interactions and support its potential as a tunable approach for investigating microplastic capture in aqueous systems.

papers.title: COSMO-RS-Based Theoretical Investigation of Equilibria in Protic Ionic Liquids
papers.abstract: Ionic liquids have become an increasingly important field of research. A subgroup, protic ionic liquids, have been shown to be excellent solvents even for poorly soluble materials such as cellulose or polyamides. Still, the composition of such liquids, e.g., their ionicity and the nature of formed aggregates, is mostly unknown and experimental attempts to shed light on this have been mostly unsuccessful. Herein, we report the development of the Python-based COSMOPIL program (COnductor-like Screening MOdel for Protic Ionic Liquids) to analyze the composition of protic ionic liquids via theoretical methods based on density functional theory (DFT) and the COSMO-RS (COnductor-like Screening MOdel for Real Solvents) implicit solvation model. The inputs of experimental data such as dielectric constants is not necessary. The COSMO-PIL program demonstrates the influence of acid/base ratios and residual water on the ionic liquid composition and allows the understanding of the reported poor ionicity of those liquids. Most notably, we explain this “ionicity gap” in protic ionic liquids, as even superbases fail to achieve full acid deprotonation, with a polarity mismatch between anion and cation, requiring residual acid as mediator.

papers.title: Characterisation of thermostable CYP116B reductase domains as modular electron transfer units for redox biocatalysis
papers.abstract: Electron transfer is a common bottleneck in redox biocatalysis. Here, we report the isolation of five cytochrome P450 reductase (CPR) domains from the thermophilic, self-sufficient CYP116B family. These enzymes have considerable industrial potential because their CPR and haem domains are naturally fused, yet the catalytic properties of the individual components remain poorly understood. EPR and UV–Vis spectroscopy confirmed the canonical FMN and [2Fe–2S] cofactors were present, although occupancy varied (FMN, 30–62%; [2Fe–2S], 10–33%). The isolated CPRs were generally stable, robust and electron-transfer competent, supporting electrochemical NADPH/NADP+ oxidation/reduction and NADPH-driven reduction of ferric cytochrome c. All homologues were more thermostable than the CPR from non-thermophilic CYP116B2, with stability showing an apparent correlation with [2Fe-2S] occupancy. Separating the CPR and haem domains generally reduced the ability to perform hydroxylation on a model substrate (diclofenac). However, isolated AxCPR and AxHAEM formed a productive non-covalent combination with activity comparable to the full-length enzyme (TON 439.38 ± 5.19 versus 416.43 ± 12.11). Given the widespread use of CYP116B CPR domains as surrogate redox partners in P450 catalysis, these findings provide valuable insight into their catalytic performance. Furthermore, the results demonstrate the potential of the isolated CYP116B CPRs as modular electron-transfer units for redox biocatalysis more widely.

papers.title: A hydrochromic porous aromatic framework for self-reporting, high-capacity atmospheric water harvesting
papers.abstract: Atmospheric water harvesting materials are typically optimised for sorption performance alone, despite the practical importance of monitoring sorbent loading. Here, we report a hydrochromic porous aromatic framework that integrates water capture and self-reporting within a single adaptive material. Sulfonation of PAF-1 affords the hydrophilic framework PAF-1-S that adsorbs 0.18 g·g-1 of water at only 10% RH and reaches 1.87 g·g-1 at 90% RH, combining exceptional low-humidity capture with the highest total capacity among the porous sorbents surveyed here. Water adsorption simultaneously induces a reversible, graded colour change, enabling direct visualisation of sorbent loading without external sensing hardware. Spectroscopic analysis indicates that this response arises from hydration-driven acid–base equilibria within the modified framework. Combined with rapid sorption kinetics, low-temperature regeneration and robust cycling stability, these findings establish responsive porous adsorbents as a strategy for intelligent sorption materials.

papers.title: Late-Stage Ligand Prioritization by Combining Rapid-Dissociation Filtering with MM/GBSA
papers.abstract: Accurate and efficient prediction of binding free energies remains a central challenge in computational chemistry, largely due to the complexity of solvent effects and the trade-off between accuracy and computational cost. Explicit solvent molecular dynamics (MD) simulations provide detailed thermodynamic and kinetic insight, now routinely reaching microsecond timescales, while end-point methods such as MM/GBSA offer high efficiency but are sensitive to model parameters. In particular, the accuracy of MM/GBSA strongly depends on the atomic radii used to define the dielectric boundary within the implicit solvent framework. Here, we introduce an explicit–implicit hybrid workflow for late-stage ligand prioritization that integrates the strengths of both approaches. In this framework, microsecond-scale explicit solvent MD simulations act as a rapid-dissociation filter, flagging weak or unstable binders through spontaneous dissociation within the simulation window. MM/GBSA is then used to rank the remaining candidates. To improve the accuracy of the implicit solvent stage, we employ optimized atomic radii sets (OPTBIND), specifically designed for binding free-energy calculations. On the protein–ligand complexes of Curated32-4 set , a new curated benchmark of 32 complexes including 4 congeneric series, the entropy-free MM/GBSA stage with OPT- BIND 6D achieved Pearson r = 0.82 and Spearman ρ = 0.84, with 100% recovery of the experimental rank ordering across all four congeneric series, while a single-replica consistency test of the rapid-dissociation filter yielded an AUC of 0.88 and retained all 15 sub-micromolar binders. Finally, as a real-world drug design application, we apply the workflow to halogen substitutions in SARS-CoV-2 main protease inhibitors, demonstrating its ability to identify favorable chemical modifications. Notably, the approach prospectively identifies F→Cl and F→I as affinity-enhancing substitutions; the predicted enhancement for the chlorine analog is subsequently confirmed experimentally, while the iodine analog remains a testable prediction, highlighting its predictive power in guiding chemical optimization. Together, these results establish a practical framework for detailed studies of receptor–ligand binding and for late-stage ligand prioritization in drug discovery.

papers.title: UpKast: Method, Model, and Database for Large-Scale Cross-Solvent Determination of pKa Values
papers.abstract: The acid dissociation constant, commonly written as p K a , plays a key role in chemistry. However, most p K a measurements have been conducted in only a handful of solvents, resulting in data scarcity for many relevant solvent systems. Herein, we introduce the UpKast-DB, which comprises of p K a estimates for around 3,000 acids and bases in 29 solvents. We constructed UpKast-DB using a quantum-chemical method that integrates solvation free energy calculations with experimental data. Furthermore, we trained a surrogate machine learning model UpKast-ML on the computed values, allowing for rapid and accurate prediction of p K a values beyond the acids and bases presented in UpKast-DB. The quantum-chemical and machine learning methods result in RMSEs of approximately 1 p K a unit relative to experimental values, slightly higher than the typical aleatoric uncertainty of underlying experimental data, but more accurate than many existing experimental measurements (which can have uncertainties up to, and sometimes beyond, 3 p K a units). The data and modeling approaches provide a means of productively augmenting existing p K a data sources, and represent a significant step toward general determination of p K a in any solvent. The dataset and models can be found on Zenodo: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23239570

papers.title: CP-GFM-SGX: Topology-Aware Cyclic Peptide Generation and Design with Receptor-Conditioned Structural Evaluation and Experimental KRAS Affinity Optimization
papers.abstract: Cyclic-peptide discovery requires molecular topology, atomic structure, receptor-associated evidence and computational decisions to remain consistent across a multistage workflow. We present CP-GFM-SGX, an all-atom generative AI model for cyclic-peptide design that integrates a topology-aware generative core with a Unified Evidence State Machine (UESM) to track candidate identity, chemical validity, provenance, typed failures and bounded computation. We evaluated three distinct aspects of the system. In Track A, a frozen five-complex known-ligand benchmark with 100 scheduled poses per complex, the native-free FULL route selected a ligand-backbone pose with root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) below 2 Å in four of five systems; retrospective best-of-100 evaluation found a sub-2-Å pose in all five (median selected RMSD, 1.72 Å). In Track B, matched true-pocket versus shuffled-pocket comparisons favored the specified pocket in all seven main targets (median of target medians, +172.6 Rosetta energy units; weakest margin, +3.9 for MCL-1–9CDT). An exploratory post-protocol assessor admitted 42/42, 42/42 and 40/42 selected top-K slots in the full, condition-masked and post hoc head-to-tail arms, respectively. In Track C, FULL UESM produced the specified protective outcomes for six deterministic synthetic fault fixtures and one additional missing-evidence case; targeted ablations isolated the roles of provenance and failure propagation. In a separate KRAS G12D–GDP experimental-feedback series, synthesis and SPR/BLI testing of cyclic-peptide analogues guided position-2 basic-side-chain selection and dual-basic-group placement, advancing the reported SPR affinity from approximately 60 µM for CRO-748 to approximately 6 µM for 748-R1 and approximately 1 µM for 748-RK. Comparisons using the 31-dimension Structured Capability and Evidence Grid (SCEG-31D) demonstrate that CP-GFM-SGX exhibits certain superiority over other design platforms in multiple aspects. Together, we evaluate a topology-aware generative artificial intelligence workflow for receptor-focused cyclic-peptide design and show, in a KRAS feedback series, how binding measurements guide iterative chemical optimization.

papers.title: Zr-MOF/Quinone Multicatalysis Enables Programmable Aerobic Synthesis of Benzimidazoles
papers.abstract: Selectivity control in aerobic oxidation reactions containing several oxidizable functional groups remains challenging. Herein, we show that the chemoselectivity of a Zr-MOF/quinone 2 multicatalytic platform can be controlled through modulation of the organic redox co-catalyst. In contrast to previously reported Zr-MOF-808/(hydro)quinone combinations that promote direct oxidation of anilines or thiols, Zr-MOF-808/1,8-dichloroanthraquinone unlocks a different reaction pathway to selectively oxidize primary alcohols in the presence of aromatic diamines and aminothiophenols. This pathway enables the one-pot synthesis of 2-substituted benzimidazoles and benzothiazoles under atmospheric air. Mechanistic experiments support coupled catalytic cycles in which Lewis-acidic Zr sites facilitate quinone-mediated alcohol oxidation, while the MOF/semiquinone interface regenerates the oxidized mediator using oxygen. This method furnishes a highly sustainable synthesis of 31 benzimidazole and benzothiazole products, permitting recovery and reuse of both catalytic components.

papers.title: Directional Prediction Errors Reveal Systematic Underprediction of Low-Pressure Carbon Dioxide Adsorption in Compact Metal–Organic Frameworks
papers.abstract: A prediction residual has both magnitude and sign, yet materials-screening studies usually treat only its magnitude as informative. Here we show that residual sign localizes systematic underprediction of low-pressure carbon dioxide (CO2) adsorption to a compact, low-accessibility region of metalorganic-framework (MOF) descriptor space. We analyze 7,306 MOFs in a topology-held-out test set, keeping related framework topologies out of training. A one-sided 90% calibration defines the expected underprediction tail; critically, that tail is not distributed uniformly across materials space. Strong-underprediction incidence falls from 27.6% to 4.0% across accessible-volume-fraction quintiles and from 26.5% to 2.7% across accessible-surface-area quintiles, while rising from 4.2% to 24.7% with density. Individual discrepancies reach 6.35 mmol g−1. Literature-derived structural annotations of leading Mg-and Ca-containing cases motivate the testable hypothesis that global geometric descriptors can miss favorable first adsorption environments in compact frameworks; they do not establish a distinct microscopic adsorption mechanism. A calibrated lower-bound screen provides a separate practical corollary for conservative candidate prioritization. The central result is not the expected size of a positive-error tail, but its structured location in descriptor space. Retaining residual direction therefore provides a chemically interpretable diagnostic of model failure and identifies the next discriminating calculation or experiment.

papers.title: Stoichiometric Control in H <sub>2</sub> S-Mediated Nitrite Reduction at a Zn-site: Intercepting SNO <sup>1−</sup> , SSNO <sup>1−</sup> and HONO Intermediates
papers.abstract: Hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S) and nitrite participate in intertwined signaling chemistry, yet the factors governing product selectivity between nitric oxide (NO) and nitroxyl (HNO) and the underlying reaction pathways remain poorly defined. Here, we establish that reduction of a zinc-nitrite complex by H 2 S follows stoichiometry-dependent product selectivity. With 2 equiv of H 2 S, the reaction generates NO and HNO-derived nitrous oxide (N 2 O) trapped in 46.3% ± 2.1% and 19.7% ± 1.5%, yields, respectively. UV-vis and 15 N NMR spectroscopy along with phosphine-based intermediate trapping and DFT studies support a nucleophilic attack pathway involving zinc-bound thionitrite (SNO − ) and perthionitrite (SSNO − ) intermediates. We independently synthesize and crystallographically characterize the zinc-perthionitrite complex, identifying isomers with cis-ĸ 2 -S,O and unprecedented Y-shaped ĸ 2 -S,S coordination modes in the solid-state. In contrast, 5 equiv of H 2 S favors an acidbase pathway involving spectroscopically intercepted nitrous acid (HONO) intermediate and affords NO in 94.6% ± 1.5% yield, with only trace N 2 O. Reaction with hydrosulfide (HS − ) instead, generate a zinc-hydrosulfide-nitrite adduct without nitrite reduction; subsequent protonation produces NO exclusively. Together, these findings establish H 2 S stoichiometry and proton availability as complementary determinants of competing nitrite reduction pathways that control NO versus N 2 O selectivity at a redox-inactive zinc center.

papers.title: De novo Rewriting DNA Identity into Functional RNA via Genetic Information Compiler
papers.abstract: Genetic information is expressed through the molecular products encoded by DNA. Synthetic systems can regulate these outputs, but retain the original link between DNA identity and function. Re-engineering this link could assign new functions to existing DNA identities. Here we present a genetic information compiler (GIC) that converts selected double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) identities into user-defined RNA outputs. GIC exploits the nontrivial activity of λ exonuclease to interrogate dsDNA and release predefined activators. These activators restore T7 promoters and drive programmable transcription. This modular architecture enables orthogonal and concurrent routing, logic processing, and control of RNA identity, amplitude, composition and timing. Spatial compartmentalization further reveals activator-mediated information transfer between separated compartments. By programming functional gRNAs as outputs, GIC enables tunable, sequence-dependent, and selective regulation of Cas9, Cas12a and Cas13a. GIC establishes a new programmable information layer in which existing dsDNA identities can be interpreted de novo as user-defined functional RNAs.

papers.title: Topology-Dependent Glass Formation Behavior in Poly[n]catenane Melts with Variable Ring Size and Chain Length
papers.abstract: Poly[n]catenanes consist of cyclic subunits that are connected by mechanical bonds rather than covalent bonds, which gives them internal degrees of freedom and permanent topological constraints that are absent in conventional polymers. How these features affect the glass transition is not known. Here, we employ molecular dynamics simulations of the Kremer–Grest bead–spring model to determine the glass transition temperature, Tg, of poly[n]catenane melts with ring sizes of m = 8–50 beads and chain lengths of n = 5–40 rings. Each melt is compared with a bonded-ring analogue in which the mechanical link between neighboring rings is replaced by a covalent bond. Mechanical interlocking raises Tg by up to 0.44 εk B -1 , nearly a factor of 2, for the smallest rings, whereas the effect vanishes for m ≥ 20. This crossover coincides with the ring size at which the free aperture of a ring, measured in the melt, falls below one bead diameter. The topological contribution to Tg scales as 1 − n end /n with n end ≈ 2.1 for all tightly interlocked chains, indicating that the two singly interlocked terminal rings act as topological chain ends. The Debye–Waller factor, the generalized localization model, and the non-Gaussian parameter show that tight mechanical bonds restrict bead motion at a given temperature, make the relaxation time grow more steeply as the cage tightens, and add a broad, slow, and strongly non-Gaussian component to segmental relaxation. In contrast, the dynamic fragility and the large-scale Gaussian chain statistics are nearly unaffected, and the modest increase of the characteristic ratio cannot account for the rise of Tg. Our work identifies ring size as the primary molecular parameter controlling the glass transition of poly[n]catenanes and shows that it acts through local topological confinement rather than global chain stiffness.

papers.title: Automated Extraction and FAIRification of Chemical Structures from Scientific Publications
papers.abstract: Chemical structures are published predominantly as images, which makes them inaccessible for database indexing, structure-based search and computational reuse. While Optical Chemical Structure Recognition and PDF-extraction tools attempt post-publication recovery, they cannot restore the information lost during image rendering. To address this, we present BChemXtract, an open-source Java library that extracts chemical structures directly from the CDX and CDXML files that authors already submit with their manuscripts. BChemXtract parses the CDX object hierarchy to isolate chemical fragments from graphical annotations and expands abbreviations using a community-curated lookup table. The structures are then converted via the Chemistry Development Kit into standard machine-readable formats. BChemXtract is integrated into the production workflow of the Beilstein Journals, where extracted structures are manually validated before being embedded in article metadata as Schema.org JSON-LD, deposited in PubChem and offered for download. Applied to the 2993 ChemDraw figures and schemes of volume 20 of the Beilstein Journal of Organic Chemistry, it yielded 23,320 structures with InChIs in under two minutes. On a 225-file benchmark corpus, it generated valid InChIs for 98.2% of extracted unique substances, compared with 14.2% for Open Babel, at comparable per-file speed. BChemXtract makes published chemistry FAIR at the point of publication without altering author workflows. It is available under the MIT license together with a web application and the benchmark corpus.

papers.title: Process and Systems Modeling of Hydrothermal Liquefaction for Fuels and Bioproducts from Wet Organic Wastes
papers.abstract: Hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) can convert wet organic waste into fuels and bioproducts, but variation in feedstocks and operating conditions can propagate from product yields to system performance and deployment. This study linked machine learning based HTL yield prediction with process simulation, techno-economic analysis (TEA), life cycle assessment (LCA), uncertainty analysis, and surrogate modeling. A literature data set of 402 experiments was used to predict biocrude, aqueous, gas, and solids yields, with 71.8% of predictions within ±5 wt% of experimental values. The predicted yields reproduced 77.1% of internal rate of return (IRR) and 83.2% of GWP 100 estimates within ±5% and ±10 kg CO 2 e/kg, respectively, and were integrated into two deployment configurations (centralized and decentralized HTL) and two product pathways (biobinder/biofuel and sustainable aviation fuel [SAF]). Process and system scale analyses showed that operating conditions strongly affecting HTL performance could have weaker or competing economic effects due to tradeoffs among product yields, water handling, energy requirements, and capital costs. Across representative feedstocks, decentralized biobinder systems achieved median IRRs up to 35.8%, compared with up to 8.0% for decentralized SAF systems. Feedstock price, followed by biocrude quality, and biocrude yield emerged as the leading economic drivers. Monte Carlo filtering identified waste tipping fee thresholds $25.1–196.7 per wet metric tonne for achieving the 10% IRR target. These results show that existing tipping fee structure can support HTL deployment in some cases, while higher tipping fees or additional financial incentives can expand viability and enable higher investment returns.

papers.title: Tension-Limited Leaflet-Asymmetry Budding Predicts the Size and Rate of Tumour Ectosome Shedding
papers.abstract: Fatty-acid protocells growing by outer-leaflet monomer uptake accumulate a transbilayer area imbalance that is relieved by budding once the reduced imbalance Δa exceeds a critical value, as described by area-difference elasticity (ADE). It is tempting to read modern tumour ectosome shedding as the same physics. We show that the naive transfer fails, and derive the version that does not. A protocell is osmotically relaxed; the plasma membrane of a cancer cell is under tension (σ ≈ 0.01–0.1 mN/m), which imposes an area cost absent from the protocell treatment. Replacing the shape-instability criterion with an explicit energy balance for bud formation gives a threshold in the differential leaflet tension, Δτ_c = sqrt(8κΣ)/h with Σ = σ + K_A h^2/R^2, and a bud radius at threshold r* = sqrt(2κ/Σ) that is independent of both h and K_A. Retaining the finite-parent term K_A h^2/R^2 is essential: in the tension-free limit it acts as an effective tension, so the threshold does not vanish but tends to Δa_c → sqrt(2κ/K_A)/h = 0.21–0.87. The O(1) ADE criterion assumed for protocells is thereby recovered as a derived result, and a tension-free vesicle is found to bud at a sizeable fraction of its own radius rather than shedding nano-vesicles. The protocell growth kinetics map exactly onto flippase/scramblase imbalance under γ → 2a_L j. Using bending rigidities measured on giant plasma membrane vesicles (κ = 5.4–35 k_BT, including the metastatic line MDA-MB-231), the model predicts bud diameters of 43–346 nm, overlapping measured cancer extracellular vesicles, at a threshold requiring translocation of only 0.09–0.76 mol% of plasma-membrane lipid. Because a single TMEM16F scramblase translocates 45 000 lipids per second while the critical net flux is below one lipid per second per square micron, the thermodynamic threshold is not the regulated quantity: the shedding rate is. Reported secretion rates of 60–80 EV per cell per hour correspond to a net outward flux of 0.2–1 lipid per square micrometre per second, a calibration rather than a test of the model. Two sharp falsification tests — the bud radius falls as the inverse square root of the membrane tension, and grows as the square root of the bending rigidity — distinguish this mechanism from ESCRT-dependent biogenesis. We argue explicitly against reading the size agreement between protocells and tumour vesicles as evolutionary atavism.

papers.title: Utilization of heuristic approaches and molecular modelling to visualise chemical reactivity in small student groups
papers.abstract: According to current psychometric analyses, a vast majority of novices in universities mostly utilize algorithmic mental processes to solve given tasks and tests. Although algorithmic thinking is an essential part of brain functions, experts on didactics call for methods which also develop conceptual thinking in beginners. In this sense, heuristic molecular modelling plays an important role in chemistry education since it inherently employs several conceptual thinking principles. Herein, we present eight different molecular modelling tasks of Diels-Alder reactions to develop understanding of the concept of chemical reactivity in undergraduate students of chemistry. The aim of this study is to provide teachers of chemistry with an example lesson utilizing heuristic education techniques and molecular modelling. The present study was evaluated in a university course on advanced organic chemistry for students in the third year of a chemistry master program. Interviews with the involved students and analyses of the applied pre/post didactical tests show that the proposed lesson has a positive impact on the understanding of basic chemical concepts related with chemical reactivity and Diels-Alder reaction.

papers.title: Reductive insertion of a trivalent metal leading to the isolation of Prussian blue-type EuIIIFe3[Fe(CN)6]3
papers.abstract: Reductive insertion reactions selectively modify three-dimensionally bonded solid-state structures through the addition of an elemental metal by electronation of the host structure and insertion of the metal cation into the host cavities for charge balance. However, with rare exceptions, this class of reactions has been largely restricted to insertions of monovalent metals. The reductive insertion of divalent and trivalent metal ions is intrinsically limited by their very slow diffusion through a host lattice at low temperatures and instability of a host lattice in the presence of these metals at high temperatures. These limitations originate from strong coordination of multivalent guest species to anions within the host lattice. By using coordinatively saturated anions such as cyanide in Prussian blue analogues, only relatively weak coordination modes to guest cations are available within the host structures, suggesting these host structures may participate in multivalent metalations. Herein, we report reductive insertion of europium into Berlin green Fe[Fe(CN) 6 ] under relatively mild conditions by reaction with EuI 2 at 150 °C in N-methyl-2-pyrolidone. The formation of the half-ferrous product, Eu III Fe 3 [Fe(CN) 6 ] 3 , is an exceptionally rare reductive insertion of a trivalent metal, and the first example of a phase pure Prussian blue (A n+ 1/n Fe[Fe(CN) 6 ]; A = metal cation) isolated with either a lanthanide or multivalent A-site metal. The resulting compound exhibits a distribution of iron oxidation and spin states not observed in previously reported Prussian blue phases of the form M I Fe[Fe(CN) 6 ]. The valence of Eu 3+ was confirmed by a combination of X-ray absorption, 57 Fe Mössbauer, and magnetic susceptibility measurements, which informed a possible reaction mechanism invoking redox exchange between the ferrous host, Eu 3+ guest ions, and excess Eu 2+ in solution.

papers.title: Comparative Characterization of Nitrogen–Nitrogen Bond-Forming Piperazate Synthases to Improve Activity and Precision
papers.abstract: Piperazate synthases (PZSs) have recently gained attention as enzymes that catalyze the formation of nitrogen-nitrogen bonds, offering a sustainable alternative to traditional synthesis of substituted hydrazines. Although progress has been made in elucidating their structure and mechanism, an exhaustive study characterizing multiple PZSs regarding their activity or tendency toward side reactions under varying conditions has yet to be conducted. In this study, we profiled the activity of eight purified PZSs under 80 different conditions each, covering pH, buffers, salinity, temperature dependence, and thermal stability, using automated liquid handling and a colorimetric substrate consumption assay. We also performed kinetic and structural analysis of the two most promising PZSs and used LC-MS to quantitatively investigate the substrate scope and side reactions. Among the investigated enzymes, we identified two highly active synthases, SbPZS from Streptomyces sp. B93 and SgPZS from Streptomyces griseochromogenes. Both enzymes tolerated a broad range of reaction conditions, but differed in their side-product formation rates. We found this tendency to be sequence-dependent and controlled by pH. These findings provide detailed information regarding the in vitro applicability of PZSs and will improve their use in (chemo-)enzymatic cascades for synthesizing pharmaceutical building blocks.

papers.title: Tuning the Anchoring and ORR Activity of Sub-Nano Pt Clusters on HOPG via Ion Implantation and Oxygen Functionalization
papers.abstract: Sub-nanometer supported clusters are of interest in catalysis due to nearly complete precious metal atom utilization, generally high catalytic activity, and attractive tunability via size and clustersupport interactions. The stability of such clusters remains a challenge, however. We demonstrate anchoring and stabilization of size-selected Ptn, n = 2 - 10 clusters soft-landed on HOPG, achieved 2 by modifying the HOPG with 100 eV kinetic energy N(𝑛 1, 2) and Ar+ ions, with and without O2 oxidation of the ion-modified surfaces, prior to Ptn soft-landing. Ion modification is found to significantly improve the sticking probability for soft-landed Ptn, implying increased adsorption energies, and O2 exposure prior to cluster deposition increases the sticking probability to ~unity. DFT finds that Ptn bind preferentially to under-coordinated carbon sites created by the ion impacts, rather than to implanted N atoms, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and scanning tunneling microscopy both show that the defect-anchored clusters are stable against sintering. There is net electron transfer from the defect-bound clusters to the support, and the local defect structure may undergo significant restructuring due to Pt-C bond formation. To probe the effects of ion-modified HOPG on the chemical properties of the adsorbed Ptn clusters, we tested electrodes prepared by Ptn deposition on ion-modified HOPG for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). The ion-modified electrodes showed ORR activity consistent with cluster size being maintained, and O2 modification enhanced both cluster anchoring and ORR activity. Thus, ion modification provides means to stabilize sub-nano cluster electrodes, while oxygen functionalization of the anchoring sites tunes the electrocatalytic activity.

papers.title: Molecular Symmetry Decomposition by Graph Automorphism: Fast, Symmetry-Aware RMSD, Structure Alignment, and Canonical Atom Ranks
papers.abstract: The root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) is among the most widely used metrics in computational chemistry. However, computing a chemically meaningful RMSD requires solving a combinatorial “atom mapping” problem: finding the RMSD-minimizing and chemically acceptable correspondence between atoms in two structures. Existing methods force a trade-off. Graph-isomorphism enumeration is exact but can be computationally prohibitive. The faster (cubic scaling with molecular size) Hungarian assignment algorithm disregards the bonding topology and can return chemically invalid mappings and spuriously low RMSD values. We eliminate this trade-off by recasting the assignment problem in the language of graph automorphism, where the bond-preserving permutations form a group whose internal structure (orbits, stabilizers, and product decompositions) mirrors molecular topology. This yields a complete classification of molecular graph symmetry into coupled core and independent peripheral symmetry (falling into exactly two graph-theoretic classes), reducing the search from a product of local symmetries to a sum. The resulting algorithm, snapRMSD, produces assignments that are bond-preserving by construction and recovers the global RMSD minimum under mild conditions satisfied by most molecular structures. We demonstrate that snapRMSD is significantly faster than existing methods, often by orders of magnitude. As a byproduct, the same machinery yields exact canonical atom ranks, a rigorous alternative to the refinement heuristics used since the 1960s.

papers.title: Toward bio-circular, fully organic batteries from non-toxic and bio-derived materials
papers.abstract: The development of biodegradable energy storage systems is essential for enabling environmental monitoring devices that can degrade after stable operation. In this work, we present a fully organic, bio-circular battery that uses materials selected using a framework based on their natural occurrence and hazard classification according to the Globally Harmonized System of Classification and Labelling of Chemicals (GHS). We use redox-active organic molecules, aloe-emodin and luteolin, immobilized on activated coconut charcoal, together with an agarose/carboxymethyl cellulose gel polymer electrolyte and current collectors based on graphite flakes, carbon black, and agarose. The resulting battery delivers 0.7 V and stable electrochemical performance, supplying 8.8 mAh/g after 200 cycles, with 73.6% capacity retention and 98% coulombic efficiency. All components are further integrated into a pouch cell with an agarose packaging and beeswax coating. This prototype exhibits a discharge capacity of 7.1 μAh and 77.9% capacity retention over 20 cycles. Under simulated aerobic composting conditions, the pouch cell shows rapid and substantial disintegration, highlighting its potential for environmentally benign end-of-life scenarios. This work establishes a comprehensive design strategy for bio-circular batteries and demonstrates the applicability of bio-derived, GHS-non-toxic, fully organic materials for sustainable energy storage solutions.

papers.title: Synthesis of Large-area Two-Dimension Metal-Organic Framework Films via Chemical Vapour Deposition
papers.abstract: Synthesizing uniform and large-are two-dimensional (2D) metal-organic framework (MOF) films directly on substrates is highly desirable and important for MOF-based electronics, but it still remains great challenge. Here, a simple chemical vapour deposition (CVD) growth strategy with controllable-thickness and large-area capabilities has been developed to directly prepare them on substrates, in which 2,3,6,7,10,11-hexahydroxytriphenylene (HHTP) ligand films pre-deposited on substrates react with copper (II) acetylacetonate (Cu(acac) 2 ) vapor, resulting the structure transformation from small molecule thin film to Cu 3 (HHTP) 2 MOF films. The MOF films have high crystalline quality with uniform surface, large area (4 inches wafer) and controllable thickness (15 nm to 100 nm). And Replacing Cu(acac) 2 with nickel (II) acetylacetonate (Ni(acac) 2 ) and platinum (II) acetylacetonate (Pt(acac) 2 ) as metal ion source, the method can also be used to synthesize uniform Ni 3 (HHTP) 2 and Pt 3 (HHTP) 2 MOF films, suggesting the generic applicability of this method. When employed the Cu 3 (HHTP) 2 MOF films as an active material for optoelectronic devices, it simulates light-stimulated and synaptic memory properties, making it exhibit promising application in artificial biological synapse.

papers.title: Realising a Poschenrieder dual-sector electrostatic analyser for charge-detection mass spectrometry
papers.abstract: Megadalton biomolecular assemblies, including viral vectors, synthetic nanoparticles and protein aggregates, are increasingly important chemical and therapeutic entities, yet their heterogeneity often exceeds the resolving power and space charge tolerance of conventional mass spectrometry. To overcome these limitations, here we report the first realisation of a Poschenrieder dual-sector electrostatic analyser as a charge-detection mass spectrometer. The instrument traps individual ions in a continuous closed trajectory between two spherical electrostatic sectors, enabling induced-current detection over extended transients without end-cap deceleration. Coupled to a high-mass ion-transfer interface, the analyser supports both ensemble m/z measurements and single-particle charge detection of large biomolecular ions. We validate the platform using protein standards and demonstrate megadalton mass analysis of adeno-associated virus capsids, distinguishing empty and genome-containing populations in agreement with orthogonal mass photometry and Orbitrap-based measurements. Although charge-detection noise remains the principal performance constraint in this first-generation prototype, the dual-sector architecture offers a simple, high-capacity route to charge-detection mass spectrometry with substantial scope for improved resolution through miniaturisation and reduced detector capacitance.

papers.title: Lipid Matrix-Dependent Effects of Ceramide Enrichment on Cholesterol-Containing PSM and DLPC Membranes
papers.abstract: Ceramide is a bioactive sphingolipid that can reorganize cholesterol-containing membranes, but how membrane properties change with increasing ceramide content in different lipid matrices remains unclear. Using Martini 3 coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations, we examine cholesterol-containing PSM and DLPC membranes across a controlled palmitoyl ceramide (PCER) composition series at a single liquid-phase temperature. Increasing PCER fraction generally decreases area per lipid and increases lipid ordering, consistent with membrane condensation. However, the responses differ between matrices. In PSM/CHOL, PCER is accommodated within an already ordered environment, producing only modest membrane stiffening. In DLPC/CHOL, PCER leads to greater changes in local packing heterogeneity and lateral organization, accompanied by a nonmonotonic mechanical response. PCER enrichment also changes the positional and orientational distributions of cholesterol in a matrix-dependent manner. These results show that ceramide-induced condensation does not necessarily produce monotonic membrane stiffening and highlight the importance of the host lipid matrix in determining membrane structure and mechanics.

papers.title: Site-selective Halogenation of Aromatic C-H Bonds via Electrocatalytic Flavin Adenine Dinucleotide Cofactor Regeneration
papers.abstract: Flavin-dependent halogenases (FDHs) catalyze site-selective C–H halogenation of electron-rich aromatic compounds but rely on multienzyme cofactor-recycling systems to continuously supply reduced flavin (FADH 2 ). Here, we establish an overpotential-driven, mediator-assisted bioelectrocatalytic strategy for FADH 2 regeneration that eliminates auxiliary reductases, nicotinamide cofactors, and enzyme immobilization. Cyclic voltammetry confirmed the proton-dependent FAD/FADH 2 redox couple (-0.42 V vs Ag/AgCl, 3.5 M KCl) and the competing oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). Bulk electrolysis involving the FDH RebH revealed that L-ascorbic acid suppresses ORR-derived species more effectively than conventional catalase/glutathione/superoxide-dismutase systems, increasing conversion of tryptophan to 7-bromotryptophan from 20% to 46% after 24 h at -0.7 V. Increasing the cathodic potential to -1.1 V improved yields to 64% without substantially improving the faradaic efficiency (FE~ 5%). Introducing redox mediators such as 2-hydroxy-1,4-naphthoquinone (HNQ) and methyl viologen (MV 2+ ) enabled the HNQ/FAD pair to achieve quantitative halogenation within 10 h (FE ~ 14%) and the MV 2+ /FAD pair within 12 h (FE ~ 9%), enabling production of 8.8 mg of 7-bromotryptophan in a scale-up reactor. Moreover, the HNQ/FAD system exhibited a kinetic isotope effect (KIE) of ( k H / k D = 1.8) for product formation in H 2 O versus D 2 O, supporting proton involvement in productive FAD regeneration and potentially reflecting cooperation between mediator-assisted electron transfer and surface-adsorbed hydrogen (H ads ) produced during the hydrogen evolution reaction in accelerating FADH 2 formation. Extending this method to engineered RebH variant 4-V enabled halogenation of larger substrates, establishing a scalable electrochemical platform for FDH catalysis. These results establish how electron delivery, proton availability, and competing oxygen reduction govern productive electrochemical flavin regeneration and provide a scalable platform for FDH catalysis.

papers.title: PolycIMS: Polymers for Automated Cyclic Ion Mobility Spectrometry Calibration
papers.abstract: The development and commercialization of cyclic ion mobility spectrometry (cIMS) instruments has considerably expanded the level of structural details that can be accessed for gaseous ions. Commercial cIMS instruments rely on travelling wave ion mobility spectrometry (TWIMS), a technique that requires calibration of the measured arrival times to enable the determination of collisional cross sections (CCS). Most calibration strategies use peptide mixtures that span a CCS range of approximately 100 – 400 Å2, which can introduce significant inaccuracies when extrapolating to larger ion structures. In addition, TWIMS calibration remains a tedious data processing step that would greatly benefit from automation. Here, we introduce polycIMS, a command-line tool that automates cIMS calibration and generates charge-independent calibration curves covering a broad CCS range from 100 – 1500 Å², within just 3 minutes on a standard laptop. Calibrated CCS can be determined in He or N 2 ( TW CCS N2→He , TW CCS N2→N2 ) using inexpensive, commercially-available polymer standards and are validated against reported values for more than 50 reference ions. Furthermore, the derived calibration parameters are largely insensitive to collisional activation, making it possible to calibrate multistage cIMS workflows such as slice collision induced unfolding (CIU n ). We anticipate that the simplicity and accessibility of polycIMS will encourage its adoption as a new standard for cIMS calibration.

papers.title: Emergence of Temporally Irreversible Hierarchical Solid Patterns through Information-Bearing Field Evolution and History-Dependent Growth Arrest
papers.abstract: Patterns are widespread in natural and synthetic systems. Their formation is often interpreted through diffusion-driven instabilities or static geometric constructions. While successful in many contexts, these frameworks struggle to encode the spatiotemporal growth history of independently nucleated domains and their resulting collective behavior, including temporal asymmetry and hierarchical pattern formation with progressive solidification. This study shows that the TRACE (Temporal Recording through Arrested Coupled Evolution) mathematical model can generate intricate hierarchical patterns of solidifying and growing domains from simple, local growth rules through a phase information event-driven discretization operator within continuously evolving spatial information-bearing fields. The framework reveals how competition between growing domains can transform simple initial conditions into diverse final patterns, offering a new perspective on the emergence of spatial complexity from local growth processes, as observed experimentally in hierarchical pattern formation with solidification from fixed nuclei. This model suggests that complex patterns can emerge from the interaction of local, time-evolving growth, kinetic arrest rules with irreversible solidification embedded in front propagation. Numerical simulations reveal emergent patterns from the only TRACE equation, such as cell-like domains, stripes, banded structures, and hierarchical boundaries arising from variations in spatial confinement, nucleation timing, and domain density. The TRACE model also qualitatively reproduces the reported hierarchical macroscopic pattern formation observed in a chemical system. With these results, a phenomenon for growth-based natural patterns with solidification, and the featured characteristics of resultant patterns via growth and exclusion of each local cell are proposed.

papers.title: Molecular Engineering of Fano Resonances for Enhanced Single-Molecule Thermoelectrics
papers.abstract: Enhancing the thermoelectric power factor of single-molecule junctions requires simultaneously achieving high electrical conductance and thermopower, which are often mutually constrained. The sharp and asymmetric transmission features produced by Fano resonances offer a promising strategy for mitigating this trade-off. However, quantitative molecular structure–line-shape relationships linking molecular modifications to the resonance valley position and peak-valley energy width remain underexplored. Here, we demonstrate a molecular engineering strategy based on electronically tunable 9-fluorenylidene derivatives to tailor Fano resonance line shapes in single-molecule junctions. Systematic density functional theory and non-equilibrium Green’s function (DFT-NEGF) calculations reveal that substituent-induced variations in local orbital energies, backbone-side-chain coupling and localized-delocalized state detuning control the resonance valley position and the peak-valley energy width. Specifically, the valley position correlates linearly with the energy level of the side-group-localized LUMO, whereas the width is governed by the combined effect of main-side-chain coupling and localized-delocalized state detuning. Together, these two orbital descriptors provide a practical basis for the predictive molecular engineering of Fano resonance line shapes. To experimentally validate this strategy, we synthesized and characterized the designed dicyanomethylene-substituted derivative C -(CN) 2 alongside a control molecule A -O . Electrochemically controlled scanning tunneling microscope break-junction (EC-STM-BJ) measurements confirm the emergence of Fano resonance features near the Fermi level for C -(CN) 2 , in agreement with the DFT-NEGF prediction, whereas no comparable features is observed for A -O. Crucially, statistical single-molecule conductance and thermopower measurements reveal that C -(CN) 2 simultaneously exhibits higher conductance ( G ) and Seebeck coefficient ( S ) than A -O , overcoming the usual trade-off between these two parameters. This synergy effect yields a 97.6% enhancement in thermoelectric power factor ( GS 2 ) relative to control systems. By establishing explicit structure–line-shape–property relationships, this work provides a practical molecular engineering strategy for engineering Fano resonances in single-molecule thermoelectrics.

papers.title: From MOF to polyMOF: Incorporation of Poly(itaconic acid) into a Cu-Ellagate Framework
papers.abstract: The incorporation of flexible coordinating polymers into crystalline metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) remains challenging because the conformational freedom of macromolecular ligands can interfere with the development of long-range order. Here, we report IEF-35(Cu), a new Cu–ellagate MOF whose crystal structure was resolved by electron diffraction, and its extension to a polymer-containing framework, PolyIEF-35(Cu), through the incorporation of poly(itaconic acid) (PIA) as a co-ligand. The resulting hybrid retained the characteristic features of the parent framework while displaying pronounced changes in particle morphology and gas sorption. Variation of the ellagic acid (EA) to PIA ratio showed that the crystalline hybrid could be obtained over a relatively broad compositional range. Both materials retained their crystallinity upon heating up to 250 °C and exhibited substantial stability toward the investigated solvents. Finally, biological studies showed cytocompatibility under the investigated conditions and antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus epidermidis .

papers.title: Unleashing AI for preclinical drug development
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping preclinical drug development across target discovery, therapeutic design, synthesis, functional characterization and safety assessment. In this review, we present an integrated view of AI across the preclinical pipeline, beginning with target identification, modality selection and representation learning for molecular, protein, structural, cellular and multimodal data. We then examine major generative modeling paradigms including autoregressive, latent-variable, diffusion, flow-based and guided approaches and their applications across small molecules, peptides, enzymes, antibodies, Tcell receptors and mRNA therapeutics. We discuss how these methods support de novo design, structure- and pocket-conditioned generation, sequence–structure co-design, affinity and activity optimization, developability engineering and synthesis-aware discovery. We further review AI-enabled retrosynthesis, reaction prediction and closed-loop experimental optimization, emphasizing the distinction between computational synthesizability and experimentally executable chemistry. Beyond molecular generation, we organize functional prediction from binding and kinetics through target engagement, pharmacological activity, mechanism of action, pathway response and phenotypic outcome. We also examine singlecell perturbation modeling, organoid-based drug-response prediction, toxicity and off-target assessment, and prospective validation across therapeutic modalities. Across these areas, we highlight the importance of uncertainty estimation, out-of-distribution generalization, reproducibility and experimentally grounded benchmarking. Finally, we discuss how integrating generative AI, mechanistic biology and iterative design–make–test–analyze cycles could transform AI from isolated predictive tools into decision-support systems for preclinical drug development.

papers.title: From Vacuum Geometry to Solution-Phase Electronic Properties and Thermodynamics via Equivariant Neural Networks
papers.abstract: We introduce a general framework for predicting solution-phase quantum-mechanical (QM) properties of drug-like molecules directly from gas-phase geometries, without solvent-specific structural optimization or property calculations. Using current equivariant neural network (ENN) architectures, such as MACE and Allegro, we demonstrate that they can also predict extensive and intensive QM properties in implicit water at a high level of theory. Direct-and ∆-learning strategies are employed for this prediction task using the Aquamarine dataset, which provides QM properties for the same molecules in both environments. The developed models are systematically evaluated for scalability to larger molecules, transferability across chemical space, and generalization to out-of-equilibrium configurations. Our results show that, despite substantial differences between gas-and solution-phase conformational ensembles, the models can accurately reconstruct ensemble-averaged solution-phase properties from gas-phase molecular dynamics. We further integrate the learned QM properties into the QUEDsol framework (“QUantum Electronic Descriptors in SOLution”) as electronic descriptors for hydration free-energy prediction. A simple and interpretable quadratic regression model trained on the FreeSolv dataset achieves state-of-the-art performance on the challenging and chemically diverse FlexiSol benchmark, outperforming previously reported QM-and ML-based approaches. These results establish ENNs as a versatile approach for inter-phase molecular property prediction and demonstrate that environment-specific QM descriptors generated from gas-phase geometries can provide transferable inputs for complex thermodynamic modeling.

papers.title: The Chemical Bond in the Age of Quantum Information: Atoms in Molecules as Entangled Open Systems
papers.abstract: The chemical bond is among the oldest ideas in chemistry and still among the least settled: chemists continue to disagree about what a bond is. We argue that the recurring controversies (ionic versus covalent, dative versus shared-electron, hypervalent versus metavalent, whether metal–metal contacts are genuinely collective) are not disputes about the physics but about an unstated reference against which a bond is declared. Removing the reference forces a change of viewpoint: an atom in a molecule is not a fixed piece of electron density but an open quantum system, a mixed state that is a probabilistic superposition over how many electrons it owns. From this vantage the electronnumber fluctuations that the theory of electron distribution functions has long measured acquire a sharp meaning: they are the quantum correlation, the entanglement, shared between the atoms of a molecule. Measured directly between the Bader basins chemists already draw, this entanglement yields a single, reference-free bond order in which the electron pair of Lewis, the resonance of Pauling and the delocalization of Mulliken reappear not as assumptions but as consequences. We outline the open-systems formulation of Quantum Chemical Topology that makes the picture exact, and sketch how the same quantity is the natural readout of molecular quantum computation.

papers.title: Gold nanofibers as scaffolds for neuron differentiation in a 3D microtissue
papers.abstract: Engineering neuronal tissues requires biomaterials that provide structural support while actively directing cell fate. Here, high-aspect-ratio gold nanofibers are explored as bioinstructive scaffolds for neuronal organization and differentiation. In a 2.5D paper-based model, the nanofibers guide Neuro-2a cell organization and promote neurite-like extensions through topographical interactions. Building on these findings, a printable composite bioink comprising a gelatin/alginate liquid phase and gelatin microstrands is fabricated. The resulting inks exhibit shear-thinning behavior, rapid structural recovery, and sufficient mechanical stability for extrusion-based 3D bioprinting. Incorporation of SH-SY5Y cells generates viable and proliferative progenitor microtissues, with increasing gelatin microstrand content favoring neuronal-like morphologies. Integration of the gold nanofibers further enhances neuronal differentiation, as supported by cell morphology, immunostaining, and expression of neuronal markers, with differentiation occurring even in the absence of retinoic acid, a common chemical differentiation factor. Spatial separation of the gold nanofibers from the cells reduces this effect, highlighting the importance of direct cell-material interactions. Together, these results establish high-aspect-ratio gold nanofibers provide structural cues capable of promoting neuronal differentiation within 3D bioprinted tissues and provide a strategy for engineering neuron-like microtissues without relying exclusively on chemical differentiation agents.

papers.title: Enhanced Spin-Forbidden Excitation of Ru(II) Polypyridyl Complexes for the Promotion of Red-Light Photocatalysis
papers.abstract: Photoredox catalysis, mainly occurring under blue light, has emerged as an indispensable tool in modern organic synthesis. However, some limitations remain, mostly due to the high energy inherent to the irradiation wavelengths used. Red-light excitation of transition-metal photocatalysts is attractive for expanding the synthetic utility of visible-light photochemistry. Here, we report a strategy to enhance spin-forbidden red-light absorption in Ru(II) polypyridyl complexes through ligand tuning. [Ru(Br2-bpy)3](PF6)2 exhibits a substantially intensified spin-forbidden absorption band in the red region, with a molar extinction coefficient approximately 10-fold higher than that of [Ru(bpy)3]2+. The enhanced red-light absorption results in markedly improved photocatalytic activity under 660 nm irradiation in a range of electron- and energy-transfer transformations. Comparison with the parent complex demonstrates that modulation of the spin-forbidden absorption pathway can directly influence red-light photochemical reactivity. These findings support ligand modification as an effective approach for enhancing spin-forbidden excitation and provide a molecular design strategy for redlight-responsive Ru(II) photocatalysts, establishing Ru(II) polypyridyl complexes as an efficient family of photocatalysts activated via a spin-forbidden transition pathway.

papers.title: Defining Applicability Domains for Metal–Ligand Selectivity Prediction: Predictive Uncertainty vs. Molecular Similarity
papers.abstract: Applicability domains are widely used to determine whether a machine-learning prediction can be trusted, yet they are commonly defined by similarity to the training data rather than by evidence that similarity predicts error. Here, we treat an applicability criterion as a testable claim and evaluate whether it identifies predictions with lower error than an equally sized random subset on a common held-out population. We test 23 criteria on a context-dependent metal–ligand selectivity problem, comparing molecular fingerprints, descriptor-space distances, learned embeddings, training support and predictive uncertainty. At 50% retention, predictive uncertainty reduces mean-of-pairs RMSE by 65%, compared with 32% for the best molecular distance and 18% for the best ligand-only distance. Fingerprint nearest-neighbour and learned-embedding distances provide no useful error ordering, whereas uncertainty remains informative after accounting for training support and predicted magnitude. In a prospective-style selection task, ranking ligands by their standardized predicted margin above a selectivity threshold increases single-ligand success from 0.639±0.035 under random selection to 0.831± 0.059. These results show that, at least for the context-dependent metal-ligand selectivity task studied here, structural similarity to the training data is not, by itself, evidence of predictive reliability in context-dependent molecular prediction. Applicability criteria can instead be treated as empirical hypotheses and tested directly against held-out error before being used to define reliable prediction regions or benchmark difficulty.

papers.title: Application-Specific Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis of Source-Optimized Nanoparticle Textile Formulations: Trade-offs in Washing Durability, Antibacterial Performance, and Laboratory-Scale Raw-Material Cost
papers.abstract: Nanoparticle-functionalized textiles offer antibacterial and self-cleaning functions, but their practical suitability is difficult to compare because laundering protocols, reported performance measures, and formulation costs vary across studies. This study develops an application-specific multi-criteria decision-analysis framework using harmonized secondary data from eight source-optimized TiO2-, ZnO-, Ag-, and hybrid-based textile formulations under a school sports-bib scenario. Washing durability and laboratory-scale raw-material cost were evaluated for all eight formulations, while antibacterial performance was included for the six formulations with sufficiently comparable data. Laundering results were converted to a common ten-reference-wash horizon, normalized criterion scores were evaluated across the full feasible weight space, and targeted sensitivity analyses examined uncertainty arising from washing normalization, incomplete Ag laundering conditions, sparse ZnO evidence, and possible cost underestimation. Under baseline conditions, Hybrid ZnO-TiO2 applied by padding-squeezing and Ag deposited through two-step grafting and reduction formed the Pareto frontier in both the two-and three-criterion models. The hybrid formulation was preferred under cost-oriented priorities, whereas the Ag formulation was favored when durability or antibacterial performance received greater weight. This principal decision structure remained stable across the tested uncertainty scenarios. In the Ag-excluded metal-oxide subset, Hybrid Padding-Squeezing remained the budget-sensitive option, while Hybrid In-Situ became more competitive when performance was prioritized. Substantial within-material variation indicated that formulation and deposition route were important sources of practical performance variation within the selected dataset. The framework provides a transparent method for translating heterogeneous published textile data into conditional, application-specific formulation decisions.

papers.title: Tunable Aza-BODIPY Photocatalysts for Near-Infrared Metallaphotoredox Atom Transfer Radical Polymerization
papers.abstract: The merger of photoredox and transition-metal catalysis has significantly advanced radical and redox transformations, yet its reliance on UV or visible light continues to limit applications in optically complex and spatially confined environments. Herein, we introduce a modular family of tetraaryl aza-boron-dipyrromethene (aza-BODIPY) organic photocatalysts (PCs) for near-infrared (NIR) metallaphotoredox atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP). We systematically modulated peripheral electronics and core bromination, evaluating the dyes through quantum-chemical, electrochemical, and spectroscopic methods. This approach identified the key parameters governing catalytic performance: a delicate interplay between triplet-state accessibility, redox properties, and photostability. The optimized aza-BODIPY dye enables well-controlled ATRP of diverse acrylates and methacrylates at ultralow catalyst loadings, down to 5 ppm PC and 50 ppm copper complex. The system is further translated to open-air aqueous conditions, enabling rapid, high-throughput synthesis of water-soluble polymers in a 96-well plate format. Taking advantage of the enhanced penetration of NIR light, we demonstrate controlled polymerization through challenging physical barriers, including ex vivo tissue. Overall, this work defines design principles for far-red/NIR-absorbing aza-BODIPY PCs and expands the scope of NIR-mediated polymer synthesis to optically turbid, spatially restricted, and aqueous environments.

papers.title: Beyond Materials Rankings: When Adsorption or Membranes Win for CO2/CH4 Separation
papers.abstract: Choosing between adsorption and membranes for carbon dioxide removal from methane is often reduced to a contest between material metrics, even though an industrially meaningful answer emerges from the coupled material, flowsheet, pressure, composition, recovery, and economic context. Here we compare the technologies on a common process boundary, allowing each to select its process-optimal material, equipment size, and membrane architecture while meeting identical methane-product and recovery constraints. The resulting atlas spans 300 ARC–MOF adsorbents, 220 experimental polymers, and 864 matched biogas-and natural-gas-like scenarios. Among 676 mutually feasible cases, adsorption minimizes annualized cost in 73.4% and membranes in 26.6%; choosing the wrong technology incurs a median cost regret of 19.4%. Crucially, the boundary is not a single pressure threshold. Four pressurized-natural-gas slices exhibit clean adsorption–membrane–adsorption re-entry as the optimal material and membrane flowsheet switch with operating conditions. Material and architecture ablations isolate this mechanism. Cost-based choices disagree with energy, methane-loss, and footprint choices in 30.8–46.0% of paired comparisons, while cost and operational-climate choices disagree in 25.4%; joint uncertainty creates an explicit abstention region in 18.3% of boundary-focused cases. The framework converts high-throughput materials screening into conditional, auditable technology-selection rules and a compact agenda for cycle and mixed-gas validation under realistic process conditions and quantified uncertainty ranges.

papers.title: Next Generation NPK Slow Release Hydrogel Fertilizers: A Critical Review of Material Design, Performance, and Field Translation
papers.abstract: Climate variability, water scarcity, declining soil quality, and inefficient fertilizer use are increasing the need for nutrient-delivery systems that support climate-resilient agriculture. Slow-release fertilizer hydrogels (SRFHs) are promising because they can retain water and control nutrient transport. This critical review examines SRFHs within conventional and enhanced-efficiency fertilizer strategies. It covers matrix, coated reservoir, and multilayer systems, along with their preparation methods and functional properties. The available evidence shows that polymer composition, crosslink density, pore structure, particle size, fertilizer loading, and environmental conditions affect swelling, mechanical behavior, and nutrient release. Important environmental factors include soil confinement, pH, ionic strength, and temperature. Kinetic models and response surface methodology can help explain release mechanisms and formulation trade-offs. Moisture-, pH-, and temperature-responsive systems may also support more adaptive nutrient delivery. However, high swelling or prolonged release in deionized water does not demonstrate improved nutrient uptake, crop yield, water-use efficiency, reduced nutrient loss, or environmental safety under field conditions. Translation is limited by inconsistent protocols, inadequate dose-matched controls, few multi-season trials, and limited evidence on degradation, residual materials, batch reproducibility, scale-up, and farm-level value. To address these gaps, this review proposes a target product profile that links crop, soil, and climate conditions with nutrient-specific release, mechanical service life, environmental fate, manufacturability, and economic performance. Model-guided responsive formulations could eventually be combined with sensor- and IoT-enabled monitoring for precision agriculture. However, this remains a prospective rather than field-validated approach. SRFHs should therefore be judged by reproducible and context-specific agronomic and environmental performance rather than maximum laboratory performance alone.

papers.title: Direct-Write Printing of Freestanding Prussian Blue Analogue Fibers with Tunable Redox Potentials
papers.abstract: Prussian blue (PB) and its analogues (PBAs) are attractive electrode materials for energy storage because of their chemical tunability, open-framework structures, fast ion transport, and rich redox chemistry. Yet, their practical implementation remains limited due to the challenging processability and the discrete set of redox potentials accessible through conventional compositions. Here, a 3D flow-focusing microfluidic strategy is used for directly synthesizing and printing freestanding PB and PBA composite fibers in a single step, coupling particle formation with their integration into an alginate/carbon-nanotube matrix. The method yields continuous, self-supporting fibers incorporating PB and multiple PBAs (Co, Ni, Cu, Zn), which can be directly written into functional electrode architectures and assembled into working energy storage cells. Beyond processability, the platform enables two complementary routes for voltage design: high-entropy PBAs, which access redox responses distinct from those of conventional single-metal PBAs, and spatially encoded fibers in which different PBAs are integrated within one fiber to generate intermediate and deliberately tuned electrochemical behavior. By exploiting the inherent spatial and temporal control afforded by microfluidic flow focusing, the approach establishes a versatile route toward printed, application-tailored PB and PBA electrodes with programmable operating voltages.

papers.title: Lipid-Phase Access Does Not Explain P-Glycoprotein Substrate Selection in Matched Pairs
papers.abstract: The hydrophobic vacuum cleaner model holds that P-glycoprotein intercepts substrates within the lipid bilayer, which makes lipid-phase access to the transporter a candidate determinant of efflux, but the proposition has never been tested on compounds matched for the properties that otherwise dominate. We simulated nine matched molecular pairs—matched simultaneously on calculated lipophilicity, hydrogen-bond donors, polar surface area and molecular weight, and differing 5.9-to 30.1-fold in measured MDR1-MDCK efflux ratio—in a coarse-grained blood–brain barrier membrane containing human P-glycoprotein, and applied a pre-registered observable: enrichment E of substrate over non-substrate within 3.5 nm of the lateral portal axis. E bears no relation to efflux (ρ = −0.100, p = 0.80, n = 9), and the slope of unity predicted if access governed efflux lies outside the 95% interval [−0.51, +0.79], while five matched replicas put the measurement error at 3.65 times below the pair-to-pair spread, so the null is informative rather than underpowered. Selection is therefore decided after arrival at the transporter rather than during delivery to it.

papers.title: Photochemical Aminomethylation of C(sp <sup>3</sup> )–H Bonds via Hydrogen Atom Transfer
papers.abstract: Direct installation of an aminomethyl group onto aliphatic C–H bonds provides an attractive route to valuable amine-containing building blocks but remains challenging with conventional polar approaches. Here, we report a photochemical aminomethylation of C(sp3)–H bonds enabled by hydrogen atom transfer (HAT). Photoexcited benzophenone directly abstracts hydrogen from αamino, α-oxy, and α-thio C–H bonds, generating carbon-centered radicals that are intercepted by an in situ-formed N-protected formimine. This strategy provides direct access to protected vicinal diamines, amino alcohol derivatives, and related aminomethylated products without requiring prefunctionalization of the C–H donor. Notably, the C–H substrate can be employed as the limiting reagent, while selective radical generation suppresses overfunctionalization. Translation to continuous flow reduces reaction times from 20 h to 3 h, while improving yields for the investigated substrates, and enables scalable synthesis. Subsequent deprotection and functionalization further demonstrate the synthetic utility of the resulting aminomethylated products.

papers.title: Catalytic C–O Bond Cleavage of Vinyl Ethers via Dehydrovinylation and Tandem Tishchenko Coupling
papers.abstract: The cleavage of ether C–O bonds by transition-metal complexes has attracted considerable attention, but catalytic cleavage of vinyl ether C(sp²)–O bonds is largely unexplored. Herein we report the dehydrovinylation of alkyl vinyl ethers catalyzed by a pincer-ligated osmium complex. Primary alkyl vinyl ethers undergo C–O bond cleavage to afford ethylene and the corresponding aldehydes, which undergo tandem Tishchenko coupling to yield esters. Secondary alkyl vinyl ethers undergo dehydrovinylation to afford ethylene and ketones. Experimental observations and density functional theory calculations support a mechanism involving insertion of the vinyl ether C=C bond into an Os–H bond, followed by β-alkoxy elimination and β-hydride elimination to form the carbonyl product. These results establish a new mode of catalytic C(sp²)–O bond cleavage and demonstrate its application in a tandem dehydrovinylation–Tishchenko transformation.

papers.title: Atomic-Scale Insights into the Surface Chemistry, Surface Stability, and Floatability of Spodumene and Montebrasite with Fatty Acid Collectors
papers.abstract: Spodumene and montebrasite are minerals that contain significant quantities of lithium and are often found together in phosphate-rich lithium pegmatites. Separating these two minerals by flotation is key to efficient downstream lithium extraction from each. Understanding the crystal and surface properties of both minerals is an important step towards their separation by flotation. We present a systematic study of the surface properties of spodumene and montebrasite, and their interactions with fatty acid collectors, using density functional theory calculations. Our results showed that, for montebrasite, the most dominant surfaces were (110) ≈ (012̅) > (102̅) > (12̅0) > (212̅), with (110) ≈ (012̅) being the most represented (56 %). The Al-terminated (110) surface was the dominant surface on spodumene, accounting for 70 % of the crystal surface area, followed by (111̅) > (111) > (101̅) > (001), consistent with available experimental data. The Wulff equilibrium morphology showed that both minerals are elongated/prismatic, consistent with their naturally occurring crystals, but spodumene is less reactive to flotation reagents than montebrasite. Surface electronic density of states showed that Li and Al states dominate the bottom of the conduction band of spodumene (110) and montebrasite (110) and are available to hybridize with oxygen states of the COO- functional group of fatty acid collectors. Energetics calculations show that both minerals interact with fatty acid collectors via surface Al and Li, but more strongly for montebrasite than spodumene (–18.6 kcal/mol vs +11.05 kcal/mol). Therefore, montebrasite is more floatable with fatty acid collectors than spodumene, making it convenient to separate these two minerals by first recovering montebrasite to the flotation concentrate, resulting in a spodumene-enriched tailings product. Less favorable adsorption energies explain the need to activate/pretreat spodumene before flotation to overcome the energy barrier for fatty-acid adsorption, with spodumene activation by high-density conditioning performed only after montebrasite flotation. This study further demonstrates that the interaction energy of fatty acids with mineral surfaces does not depend on chain length, regardless of mineral type. Our findings open a new direction for efficient lithium production from phosphate-rich lithium pegmatites by generating a montebrasite concentrate while simultaneously upgrading the feed to the spodumene flotation circuit.

papers.title: Rational construction of semi-clathrate-like water networks on engineered ferritin cages
papers.abstract: Understanding and controlling the organization of water at molecular interfaces is a longstanding goal in both biological and materials sciences, as it controls the biophysical properties of the surfaces. For example, semi-clathrate waters containing polygonal hydrogen-bonded water clusters found in some antifreeze proteins (AFPs), are thought to play key roles in interacting with ice. Despite this significance, the lack of well-defined design principles makes it difficult to rationally construct such ordered hydration architectures. Here, we report the rational construction of a semiclathrate-like water network in an engineered ferritin cage. We designed a series of alanine (Ala) mutants on the internal surface of the ferritin cage and analyzed the formation of semi-clathratelike water networks using X-ray crystal structure analysis. Our results indicate that the continuous hydrophobic surface formed by the Ala mutation organizes water molecules on its surface, forming semi-clathrate-like water networks. Specific hydrogen-bonding networks involving the main-chain carbonyl group were found to play a key role in initiating the formation of semi-clathrate-like water networks. These findings are significant for organizing water molecules on the protein surface to control biophysical properties.

papers.title: CAN it work? Using hydroxyethyl acrylate or methacrylate to turn epoxy-amine thermosets into covalent adaptable network materials.
papers.abstract: Epoxy-amine thermosets can be converted into covalent adaptable networks (CANs) by adding β-aminoester-based curing agents to the formulation. This is achieved by utilizing commercially available di- or trifunctional acrylate monomers, which react with the amine component via an aza-Michael addition. Consequently, this approach is inherently scalable and holds high industrial relevance. In this study, the fundamental applicability of two commodity chemicals—namely 2-hydroxyethyl acrylate (HEA) and 2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate (HEMA)—for this purpose is investigated, aiming to provide an additional handle to mitigate the rapid viscosity increase of the formulations. Using a model epoxy resin consisting of bisphenol A diglycidyl ether (DGEBA) and 1,3-bis(aminomethyl)cyclohexane (BAC), it was demonstrated that a Lewis-base catalyst (1-methylimidazole) is necessary to incorporate the hydroxy groups of HEA and HEMA into the network. Contrary to expectations, this incorporation proceeds predominantly through a condensation reaction that liberates ethylene glycol. Finally, a formulation consisting of 1 equiv. DGEBA, 0.5 equiv. BAC, 1 equiv. HEA, and 0.025 equiv. 1-methylimidazole was found to offer a good compromise, providing both satisfactory reprocessability and a sufficiently high glass transition temperature (74 °C). Compared to a reference formulation made with a trifunctional acrylate monomer, the CAN made with HEA is characterized by a lower glass transition temperature, a similar flow activation energy, a lower storage modulus, and distinctly longer relaxation times. Both acrylate-based CAN materials aged under thermal stress, which resulted in higher storage moduli and glass transition temperatures upon reprocessing. A protocol for characterizing such modulus changes under thermal stress is suggested, consisting of performing repeated frequency sweeps for at least 1 h at temperatures slightly exceeding the maximum temperature of the stress relaxation measurements.

papers.title: Lithium Plating-Induced Fracture of Individual Graphite Platelets Revealed by Operando
papers.abstract: Lithium plating is a key barrier to achieving faster charging of lithium-ion batteries; however, fundamental and nanoscale understanding of plating is still being developed, largely due to the dynamic nature of the process. Here, we perform operando electrochemical atomic force microscopy on individual graphite platelets to observe the morphology evolution of plated lithium and graphite electrodes simultaneously. We observe plating-induced fracture of the graphite platelets even in the absence of a porous electrode structure. Unexpectedly, fracture occurs through preferential lithium deposition beneath the particle surface despite lithium-ion transport limitations, pointing to lithium in graphite as the lithium source. Our findings deepen the understanding of the lithium plating process and offer pathways to improvement for fast-charged negative electrodes.
