papers.title: A dimension staircase for orientational heat capacity: nature skips the 3/2 rung
papers.abstract: The low-temperature orientational heat capacity of an interacting multipole pair is conventionally taken to be two-valued: 3/2 k B for axially symmetric moments and 2 k B otherwise. Here I evaluate it for all 101,666,280 molecular geometries of the OMol25 dataset and show that this is the bottom rung of a staircase: the exponent is a count, not a case split, γ = C v / k B = Σ i 1/ p i , which for two rigid nonlinear molecules is exactly γ = D / 2 and leaves only the rungs 3/2, 2 and 5/2. Of 11,325,000 pairs drawn uniformly from the whole dataset none occupies the 3/2 rung ( P < 3.26 x 10 -7 ; structural bound 4.187 x 10 -7 ), and the rest split 12.05% and 87.95% between γ = 2 and 5/2, so nearly the whole molecular world shares one coefficient: 5/2 k B = 20.79 J mol -1 K -1 per mole of pairs. The 3/2 rung is deleted rather than thermally suppressed (a 0.129 Å C-H bending amplitude exceeds the 0.1 Å scale at which a C 3v rotor saturates its axiality defect), so no temperature recovers it.

papers.title: Advancing Targeted Nanoparticle mRNA Delivery Using Machine Learning
Resolving Month-Long Nanostructural Evolution in Degrading Anion Exchange Membranes
papers.abstract: Chemical degradation reshapes the hydrated ion-transport channels of anion exchange membranes (AEMs), but conventional aging measurements do not reveal how their nanostructure evolves toward functional failure. Here we resolve this structural evolution using high-resolution kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC) simulations. The simulations are calibrated to reproduce the experimental ion exchange capacity (IEC) and water uptake (WU) over a month degradation of a PPO-TEA membrane. The ionomer-peak position remains essentially unchanged even after 70% cation loss, while the water channels narrow from approximately 0.8 to 0.6 nm and progressively fragment. The hydrated network loses percolation at a critical hydrophilic volume fraction 𝜙!≈ 0.26, close to the threshold (𝜙!≈ 0.25) inferred from experimental conductivity using a percolation power law. Two complementary descriptions, a percolation law and a connected-carrier model, reproduce the normalized conductivity decay without using conductivity to calibrate the degradation kinetics. These results link conductivity failure to the loss of connected transport pathways within a membrane that retains its characteristic phase-separation length scale. The structural predictions are similar for two kinetic models with different dependencies on local hydration. Thus, a persistent ionomer-peak position can conceal substantial deterioration of the ion-transport network. Resolving channel connectivity along the aging trajectory provides a structural measure of membrane durability that complements conventional characterization of phase separation.

papers.title: The Dopant Cage Sets the Phonon Count of Lanthanide Emitters
papers.abstract: Multiphonon relaxation decides whether a lanthanide ion emits light or heats its host. Since 1968 it has been predicted from the host’s maximum phonon energy, although the excitation resides on a single ion. First-principles force constants and five decades of relaxation measurements show that the accepting vibration is the stretch of the dopant’s coordination cage, a site property set by local chemistry. Aliovalent substitution stiffens the cage by up to 27%, and across seven halide hosts the cage frequency departs from the host frequency by −21% to +19%. It predicts measured effective phonon frequencies three times more accurately than the host frequency, and in its quanta the seven energy-gap laws share one room-temperature slope. The site-resolved laws map the lattice limits of optical refrigeration from 2 to 6 µm. The phonon count of a lanthanide emitter becomes a site property that chemistry can tune and theory can compute before synthesis.

papers.title: Diverse Remote Difunctionalization of Enyne-type Propargylic Carbonates: Regio-, Chemo-, and Stereoselective Access to Highly Functionalized Multisubstituted 1,3-Dienes
papers.abstract: Herein, we report the first catalytic heterodifunctionalization and homodifunctionalization of readily available 1-substituted enyne-type propargylic derivatives, proceeding via a multicomponent remote C2,C5-addition/substitution pathway. This palladium-catalyzed protocol enables the modular and straightforward assembly of tri-, tetra-, and penta-substituted 1,3-dienes with diverse functional groups from two heteroatom nucleophiles or one heteroatom nucleophile and one carbon nucleophile. The reaction exhibits high chemo-, regio-, and stereoselectivity, accommodates a broad spectrum of O-, N-, S-, and C-nucleophiles, and delivers highly substituted (Z, E)-1,3-dienes with precise stereocontrol. Notably, switching from O- to S-nucleophiles triggers a nucleophile-directed stereodivergence. The synthetic utility is further demonstrated through diverse downstream transformations, efficient synthesis of bioactive molecules, and late-stage functionalization of natural products. Mechanistic studies reveal the involvement of heteroatom-containing pentacoordinate π-allyl palladium and π-alkynyl palladium intermediates in this heterodifunctionalization process.

papers.title: An alternative equation for effective nuclear charge that is applicable to all atoms
papers.abstract: Although the advent of ionization energies predated Slater’s rule, there was unawareness of the utilitarian value of the former for the computation of effective nuclear charge (ENC for short) until recently and in this research. The study aimed to derive another equation in which the average ionization energies of hydrogen and any other multielectron atom are independent variables. The objective was to answer the question in the literature that states, "Are Slater’s Rules the Best Approach for Calculating Effective Nuclear Charge for Undergraduates?" (Moore & Birnbaum, 2014) and compare the graphical portrayal of chemical periodicity between outcomes using data generated using Slater's rules for some elements and data generated in this research. By exploring theoretical and computational methods and the data in the literature, the study showed that ENC (1.34458-3.32446) for the first 30 elements computed using the 2021 CODATA fine structure constant (FSC, for short) was higher than those (1.34402-3.32309) without it; however, the equation containing the computed FSC using e^2/20hc and other equations gave the same value of ENC. The use of Slater’s result (atomic radii) for the computation of ENC (1.29859-5.06996) and average ionization energy, IE (553.21-2108.13 kJ), gave higher values than other methods. All plots using Slater’s values of ENC and IE versus atomic number (Z) did not show chemical periodicity (greater linearity), unlike the use of other values (less linearity or lower R^2). The use of Slater’s result (atomic radii) for the computation of ENC (1.29859-5.06996) and average ionization energy, IE (553.21-2108.13 kJ), gave higher values than other methods. All plots using Slater’s values of ENC and IE versus Z did not show chemical periodicity (greater linearity), unlike the use of other values (less linearity or lower R^2). The new equation was derived, and with earlier equations, ENC can be accurately computed; they should therefore be part of the school curriculum at all levels without ceasing to teach Slater’s rule, which is not the best approach. A future study should include 30 other elements of the periodic table.

papers.title: Data-Driven Approach to Predicting Durability and Property Retention in Polymer Matrix Composites
papers.abstract: Predicting the long-term performance of reinforced polymer composites from short-duration accelerated aging data remains a central challenge in composite durability engineering. This work presents a data-driven kinetic and mechanical-performance characterization of a glass-flake reinforced unsaturated polyester composite exposed to deionized water at 20, 40, 60 and 80 °C for up to 14.5 months, integrating long-term gravimetric sorption, flexural testing, and dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA), including substantial portions of the dataset that have not previously been analyzed or reported. The initial moisture sorption rate constant obeys an Arrhenius relationship across all four temperatures (activation energy Ea = 45.1 kJ/mol, R2 = 0.97), providing a kinetic basis for estimating uptake behavior within the tested temperature range. Extended gravimetric monitoring reveals a two stage hygrothermal response: an initial Fickian-like uptake stage reaching an apparent plateau (4.4-7.5 wt% depending on temperature and replicate), followed by a degradation-associated mass-loss stage, with weight gain at 60 °C falling from a 4.5% plateau to 1.8% after 14.5 months, and markedly greater coupon-to-coupon variability at 80 °C. Flexural modulus and strength retention under wet conditions (22-50% and 28-60% of dry values, respectively) is reported across all four temperatures at 2 and 6 months, alongside DMA glass transition temperature data showing an initial rise with exposure temperature followed by a decrease at 80 °C. No meaningful relationship between initial moisture sorption kinetics and 2-month mechanical retention could be established from the present four temperature-matched averages (Pearson r = 0.43, n = 4; retention is non-monotonic in ln(k)); the 6-month data instead indicate that degradation kinetics and exposure duration, rather than the initial sorption rate, are what track mechanical performance loss. The study does not establish a validated model for predicting mechanical-property retention; rather, it provides a quantitative experimental basis and structured dataset for future data-driven and machine-learning-based durability models of this and structurally similar glass-flake-reinforced polyester and related polymer matrix composite systems.

papers.title: Enabling Optoelectronics in Cu2S/Co9S8 Heteroassembly
papers.abstract: Semiconductor heteroassembly can integrate complementary properties through nanoscale interfaces, but structural integration alone does not necessarily yield optoelectronic functionality. Here, we demonstrate an optoelectronically active Cu2S/Co9S8 heteroassembly for photodetection, obtained through higher-temperature nucleation and growth conditions that may promote enhanced crystallization and structural ordering of Co9S8. Structural characterization reveals crystalline Cu2S nanostructures decorated with dense 3–5 nm Co9S8 nanocrystallites, providing extensive interfacial contact. HRTEM, electron diffraction, XRD, and elemental mapping confirm the coexistence and spatial integration of the two phases. Controlled antisolvent processing reduces residual organic content and enables formation of uniform films. A vertical Cu2S/Co9S8/n-Si device exhibits broadband photoresponse with rise and fall times of 2.7 and 2.3 s, respectively. At 2 V bias, the device achieves a responsivity of 1.93 mA W-1 and a shot-noise-limited detectivity of 6.3 × 107 Jones. The bias-dependent response is attributed to field-assisted photocarrier separation and extraction, with the Cu2S/n-Si junction and Cu2S/Co9S8 interfaces influencing carrier transport. These results highlight the combined importance of structural ordering and interfacial architecture in converting nanoscale heteroassembly into functional optoelectronic devices.

papers.title: Transformation product bottleneck: Photo-recalcitrance of rotenolone limits the aquatic degradation of rotenone in a temperature-dependent manner
papers.abstract: The environmental fate and toxicity of transformation products (TPs) are frequently overlooked. However, in many cases, TPs are functional analogs that exhibit similar, and often greater, toxicity as the parent compound. In cases where the TP is persistent in the environment, the rate of TP degradation can influence the overall environmental fate. Rotenolone (12𝛼-hydroxy-rotenone, ROH) is the primary TP of rotenone (ROT), a pesticide utilized ubiquitously and highly popular in cold regions. Both ROT and ROH are mitochondrial NADH inhibitors, however ROH is more persistent than ROT and remains unregulated. 2 This work investigated the aquatic photochemical pathways and transformation products of ROH, including simulated Subarctic (low-temperature) conditions. Given that ROT degradation is driven by photolysis, we hypothesized that inhibited photochemical activity of ROH accounts for its persistence. Our results suggest ROH persistence is largely attributed to significantly reduced triplet state lifetimes, absorbance, and apparent quantum yields. Temperature was identified as a significant driver of ROH photolysis, accelerating the direct photochemical transformation rate, with half-lives ranging from approximately 115 h (6 °C) to 66 h (19 °C). This suggests that the cool temperatures of Subarctic surface waters further contribute to ROH persistence. Degradation was accelerated in the presence of chromophoric dissolved organic matter (CDOM); Fenton experiments confirmed ROH reacts with hydroxyl radical at near diffusion-limited rates (2.9×1010 ± 1.1×109 M-1 s-1 at 20 °C). Nontarget analysis of ROH photoproducts revealed novel transformation intermediates not previously identified. These were observed to further transform to smaller products, suggesting that ROH photochemical transformation represents the final step in detoxification. Thus, the photochemical recalcitrance of ROH is involved in limiting the detoxification of ROT following aquatic pesticidal use. These results strongly suggest including ROH monitoring during ROT pesticide applications.

papers.title: 3D DLP Printing of Multi-Responsive Cellulose Derivatives with Tunable Structural Color
papers.abstract: Polymer systems exhibiting structural color represent a promising class of materials for 3D printing due to their capability to adapt their properties in response to external stimuli. Hydroxypropyl cellulose (HPC) stands out for its ability to form cholesteric liquid crystalline phases that exhibit vivid structural colors. In this work, we introduce a digital light processing strategy to fabricate complex 3D structures with tunable, stimuli-responsive structural color using methacrylated HPC (HPC-MA). By formulating an aqueous ink system containing 58 to 70 wt% HPC-MA and establishing a pre-print equilibration protocol, cholesteric order is developed and covalently locked into the printed architecture via photopolymerization. The resulting 3D printed structures display bright, iridescent structural colors, tunable within the entire visible spectrum. The thermoresponsive properties of the printed structures are investigated both in a dried and a water-swollen state. Notably, the thermochromic behavior exhibits opposing trends in both environments with increasing temperature inducing a redshift in the dry state but a blueshift in the aqueous state. Finally, we demonstrate the practical utility of this approach in zero-power visual humidity sensing and biomimetic adaptive camouflage. The integration of structural color, stimuli-responsiveness, and 3D geometric freedom opens avenues towards next-generation 4D printing, adaptive materials, and autonomous sensing.

papers.title: Beyond Bulk Grade: Mineral–Flow Accessibility Controls Pore-Scale Copper Recovery
papers.abstract: Mineral dissolution in porous media is driven by fluid flow, solute transport, and geochemical reactions, yet reactive transport models commonly use bulk mineral abundance and specific surface area as proxies for mineral reactivity. This neglects a key constraint: dissolution occurs only where reactants can access minerals through connected fluid-flow pathways. Here, we use pore-scale PFLOTRAN simulations of acid-driven chrysocolla dissolution to isolate the effect of mineral accessibility at fixed initial mineral volume fraction. Across pore-network ensembles and flow–reaction conditions, copper recovery varied substantially (9–21%) despite identical bulk copper content. Recovery depended on the fraction of mineral accessible to connected flow and on mineral proximity to inlet-connected pores, even when cumulative pore volumes flushed during the 48 h acid pulse were nearly identical. In contrast, Péclet and Damköhler numbers characterized transport–reaction regimes but did not uniquely predict copper recovery because they do not encode pore-scale accessibility. An accessibility-weighted pore-volume metric combined with intrinsic dissolution kinetics explained recovery with R2 ≈ 0.95. Thus, our results show that mineral–flow accessibility and reaction kinetics jointly control pore-scale copper recovery and provide a physically interpretable basis for accessibility-aware reactive transport upscaling.

papers.title: Spirocyclic Azetidines as Lactam Bioisosteres in Isoindolinones Through Facile C1 Stitching Enabled by Dual Energy- and Electron-Transfer Photocatalysis
papers.abstract: Bioisosteric replacement of nitrogen-containing cyclic structures with smaller, more conformationally rigid ring systems such as azetidines and spirocyclic azetidines has emerged as an effective strategy to improve the physicochemical and pharmacokinetic profiles of nitrogen-bearing drug candidates. Despite extensive studies, the use of spirocyclic azetidines as bioisosteres has been limited to simple ring systems and has not been extended to medicinally relevant complex pharmacophores. Herein, we introduce benzo-fused spirocyclic azetidines as three-dimensional bioisosteres of lactam moieties in isoindolinones, significant structural motifs present in >40,000 bioactive compounds. Our synthetic strategy is to “stitch” in one step a broad range of oxadiazoline carbene precursors and substituted 1-azabicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (ABBs), thus accessing structurally diverse spirocyclic azetidines. This reaction is mechanistically novel, merging strain-release activation of ABB with a dual energy-transfer/single-electron-transfer photocatalytic cascade, enabling formal C1-insertion under mild conditions. The physicochemical and metabolic profiling suggests that these spirocyclic azetidine bioisosteres retain key physicochemical properties while improving metabolic stability. Moreover, docking studies indicate conserved recognition with the potential for interaction rewiring at selected targets. Given the ubiquitous presence of lactam and amide-containing motifs in bioactive molecules and drug candidates, this work opens new avenues for drug discovery and clinical development.

papers.title: Following Nature’s Lead – Pillar[n]arene Phosphates as Versatile Molecular Hosts
papers.abstract: Phosphates are ubiquitous natural recognition motifs. Their charge, hydrogen bonding, variable substitution, and reversible enzymatic installation uniquely enable complex tasks in Biology. However, they are not used extensively in supramolecular systems. Herein, we combine Nature’s modulator with supramolecular rational design, creating rim-functionalised pillar[n]arene phosphates, which act as highaffinity molecular hosts. Using robust phosphoramidite chemistry, we prepared P5Max and P6Max, based on pillar[5]arene and pillar[6]arene cores in four high yielding steps. We developed a high-throughput fluorescence displacement assay enabling us to explore a biologically focused screening panel and so rapidly investigate the recognition properties of our new hosts. P5Max and P6Max bind a series of structurally diverse chemotherapies, neuromuscular blockade agents, anaesthetics and antibiotics, with P6Max proving the more general host. We used functional assays to explore P6Max’s ability to control the biological effect of different drug classes, including highly toxic chemotherapy drugs and antibiotics. The use of high-throughput assays in host-guest systems provides a simple, rapid, and scalable route to translating supramolecular interactions to functional effect.

papers.title: FMS2Lib: A Machine Learning-Ready Tandem Mass Spectral Library for Nontargeted Analysis of Non-conventional PFAS
papers.abstract: Nontargeted identification of non-conventional per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), including fluorinated pharmaceuticals and pesticides, remains challenging. Existing machine learning models for nontargeted analysis, primarily trained on tandem mass spectra of nonfluorinated compounds, may not generalize well to non-conventional PFAS because of their distinct mass spectrometric chemistry. Here, we established FMS2Lib, an experimental tandem mass spectral library containing 34,686 fluorinated drug-like compounds (F 1-4 ), to support machine learning-based nontargeted PFAS analysis. We demonstrated that training with FMS2Lib substantially improved the performance of existing models for both molecular formula prediction and structure annotation. We further applied these models to identify PFAS in passive samplers from wastewater effluents and surface waters and in high-throughput laboratory biotransformation experiments, revealing dozens of non-conventional PFAS and their biotransformation products. Collectively, FMS2Lib addresses a major data bottleneck in machine learning-based nontargeted analysis of non-conventional PFAS.

papers.title: Case Studies of Homemorphic Isomerization: Interconversion of In/Out Isomers of Bicyclo[6.5.1]tetradecane and Related Bicyclic Hydrocarbons
papers.abstract: Homeomorphic isomerization is equivalent to turning a molecule inside out in the same manner as a reversible article of clothing. Manifestations include the interconversion of (a) in,in and out,out isomers, or (b) in,out and out,in isomers of bicyclic molecules, but without inverting the configurations of the bridgehead atoms. In this preprint, this topological process is probed computationally for the title molecules. For the in,in/out,out manifold, the CH 2 tether is able to transit through the CH(CH 2 ) 6 CH tether with a barrier of ~26 kcal/mol, in good agreement with an experimental measurement. The geometries of the ground and transition states are analyzed in detail and the process of isomerization is visualized in animations.

papers.title: FoldX interface ΔΔG depends on which structure it starts from, and a learned predictor does not: a cautionary analysis on glutaryl-CoA dehydrogenase
papers.abstract: FoldX and related methods are widely used to interpret missense variants, and their sensitivity to the input structure is documented: repair of the coordinates is mandatory, averaging over structural ensembles improves agreement with experiment, and the uncertainty of a FoldX folding ΔΔG has been put at roughly ±3 kcal/mol, with binding stability worse. What has not been asked is whether that uncertainty is spread evenly over a protein. We took 258 ClinVar missense variants in glutaryl-CoA dehydrogenase, a homotetramer, verified every reference residue against the 1SIQ structure and computed ΔΔG for the 124 classified pathogenic. Eighteen variants were then recomputed on three molecular dynamics snapshots of the same complex: six interface variants selected on their monomer-to-tetramer difference, six interface variants drawn at random, and six at least 10 Å from any contact. The displacement between the crystal-based value and the relaxed-frame mean had a median of 1.10, 1.38 and 0.20 kcal/mol in the three groups (random interface against distant, Mann-Whitney p = 0.0130), while frame-to-frame scatter was indistinguishable between them (Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.385). The variation is therefore positional, and it is not explained by noise in the mean. SAAMBE-3D, a learned interface predictor, run on the same eighteen variants and the same four structures, moved by a median of 0.075 kcal/mol at the interface and by nothing at all away from it, so the instability is largely a property of FoldX. It also depends on magnitude: G171R, scored at +22.53 kcal/mol, moved 2.7%, whereas A421V moved from +0.18 kcal/mol, which reads as tolerated, to +4.37 ± 2.22. Along the way we found that ThermoMPNN given a chain selector on a tetramer returns values identical to the isolated monomer at all 7,800 scanned positions. For variant interpretation the consequence is specific: at a subunit interface, in the range where a classification is actually in doubt, a single starting structure does not support a single number.

papers.title: A bipartite quantum-acoustic architecture stabilizes multi-exciton solitons at 323 K
papers.abstract: A fundamental thermal paradox has constrained the physical viability of quantum coherent Davydov solitons in protein α-helices for over 50 years. At 323 K (0.0278 eV), ambient thermal noise disrupts the localized amide I self-trapping resonance, rapidly scattering multi-quanta excitations into delocalized thermal states on femtosecond timescales. A non-equilibrium, bipartite quantum-acoustic stabilization matrix resolves this long-standing decoherence gap by inducing a transverse acoustic viscoelastic phonon gap, extending exciton coherence lifetimes from 6.5 fs to 42.6 fs—a pre-thermalization window sufficient to outpace non-radiative dissipation and electrostatically prime catalytic interfaces prior to microsecond motor stepping. Utilizing non-Markovian open quantum system simulations, we demonstrate that a highly polarizable variable-dipole linactant at the lipid raft interface induces localized electrodynamic Stark defects, breaking lattice translation symmetry to anchor the wave packet. Sustaining this protective boundary against passive diffusive loss mandates a strict kinetic equilibrium that arrests uncoupled proton leaks, directly coupling the continuous, hydrogen-bonded α-helices of eukaryotic F/V-type rotary c-rings to a hyper-rigid viscoelastic membrane locked in a far-from-equilibrium state. Finally, we present a definitive pathway to bypass thermal decoherence by establishing three physical boundary conditions to translate these biological principles into a predictive blueprint for synthetic quantum-acoustic metamaterials.

papers.title: Surface hydroxyls act as key intermediates in the selective oxidative dehydrogenation of 2-propanol on Co3O4
papers.abstract: Transition-metal oxides typically catalyze aerobic oxidation reactions with high activity even at low temperatures, but rarely with high selectivity. Owing to the complexity of competing surface processes on such catalysts, the rational design of selective low-temperature catalysts still requires a deeper mechanistic understanding of the active surface and reaction intermediates. In this work, we combine operando modulation-excitation infrared spectroscopy with density functional theory and molecular dynamics to mechanistically investigate 2-propanol oxidation over Co3O4 with a focus on surface hydroxyls, acting as hydrogen acceptors during alcohol adsorption. We identify two chemically distinct hydroxyl populations: linear hydroxyls, which actively participate in acetone formation and can be considered part of the active surface ensemble, and bridged hydroxyls, which behave largely as spectators. Together, these results provide a molecular-level mechanistic picture of alcohol oxidation on Co3O4 and establish the dynamic role of surface hydroxyl species as active players in heterogeneous oxidation catalysis.

papers.title: Collective vibrational strong coupling triggers dissociation reaction by overcoming energy threshold
papers.abstract: Ground-state reactions under vibrational strong coupling (VSC) have emerged as one of the central topics in polariton chemistry, yet how the energy redistribution under collective VSC translates into chemical reactivity remains an open question. Here we investigate vibrational predissociation in dilute ensembles of water trimers coupled to an optical cavity using full-dimensional cavity quasi-classical trajectory (cav-QCT) simulations with ab initio-quality potential-energy and dipole-moment surfaces. We demonstrate that collective VSC directly induces an otherwise energetically forbidden dissociation of the water trimer through cavity-mediated intermolecular VET. Remarkably, the enhancement of reactivity remains observable with increasing ensemble size despite reduced effective single-molecule light–matter coupling strength. Trajectory analyses identify collective energy transfer as the microscopic mechanism and reveal largely consistent quantum-state distributions of the reaction products. These findings establish a microscopic link between collective polaritonic energy transport and chemical reactivity, and suggest collective VSC as a route toward simultaneously manipulating reactivity and preserving product-state selectivity.

papers.title: Direct Mechanochemical Aryl Amination of Polystyrene for Creep Resistant Imine Elastomers
papers.abstract: Imine-based covalent adaptable networks (CANs) hold promise for the development of recyclable thermoset materials, but due to low barriers for dynamic exchange, such networks typically suffer from significant material creep. Incorporating linear polymers into imine CANs can improve creep resistance by introducing physical crosslinks, while reactive variants further mitigate through chemical crosslinks. Herein, we directly aminate polystyrene (up to 1.1 mol%) using ball mill grinding mechanochemistry with liquid-assisted grinding for inclusion into dynamic materials. This post-polymerization modification technique allows us to avoid excess solvent while preserving high molar mass. Incorporating aminated PS (aPS) in representative polyimine elastomers enhances creep resistance relative to unmodified PS, while generally maintaining comparable mechanical properties. These findings establish waste PS grafted with low densities of reactive primary amines as an effective additive for improving deformation resistance in polyimines, thus offering a route to give post-consumer plastic waste renewed value.

papers.title: Zwitterionic Acyl Anion Equivalents from Carboxylic Acids via Acylsulfonylhydrazides: A Practical Organocatalytic Umpolung
papers.abstract: The development of mild and practical acyl anion equivalents remains a cornerstone challenge in modern organic synthesis, as traditional umpolung strategies often rely on moisture-sensitive reagents, strong bases, or specialized N-heterocyclic carbene catalysts. Here we report that readily available N,N-acylsulfonylhydrazides serve as efficient acyl anion surrogates under operationally simple organocatalytic conditions. Using DMAP as a nucleophilic catalyst, these stable hydrazide precursors readily provide acylation products of a wide range of carbon electrophiles, including aromatic and aliphatic aldehydes, activated ketones, olefins, and imines. Mechanistic investigations, supported by DFT calculations and HRMS analysis, reveal an unconventional pathway wherein DMAP adds to the acyldiazene intermediate, triggering nitrogen extrusion and generating a zwitterionic nucleophile. This dual role of DMAP in enhancing both the stability and nucleophilicity of the reactive species circumvents the hydroxycarbene rearrangement pathway, offering a practical and scalable alternative to existing acyl anion methodologies.

papers.title: NEVPT2 Multiple Spawning Molecular Dynamics Simulations for Uracil
papers.abstract: The quasidegenerate n-electron valence state second-order perturbation theory (QD-NEVPT2) for complete active space reference wavefunctions has been implemented in the OpenMolcas package. The implementation utilizes the efficient formulation of Kollmar et al. for the electronic energy, which is extended here to the calculation of analytic derivatives. To demonstrate its utility, the method is applied to classical and non-adiabatic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of uracil. The non-adiabatic MD simulations describe the ultrafast deactivation of the initially excited bright ππ∗ state through the S 2 /S 1 conical intersection, demonstrating the applicability of the method to photochemical processes. Furthermore, a machine learning-based analysis of the trajectory data extracts key geometrical parameters that are associated with the magnitude of the time-derivative coupling.

papers.title: Formamidine-Linked Covalent Organic Frameworks
papers.abstract: Formamidine has been established as a versatile molecule in agriculture, organic solar cells, and as a ligand in organometallic catalysis. Despite, formamidine-based materials have remained largely unexplored due to challenges in achieving controlled polymerization. In this direction, we introduce a one-pot microwave-assisted diamine-orthoformate condensation strategy to synthesize formamidine-linked conjugated covalent organic frameworks (FOF-2 and FOF-3). Interestingly, the formamidine units of FOFs enable affinity towards urea, and that allowed us to use as metal-free electrocatalysts for the urea oxidation reaction (UOR) in alkaline media. FOF-2 demonstrates an onset potential value of 1.47 V (vs RHE) and a lower overpotential. The ordered microporous conjugated backbone facilitates charge and mass transport in FOFs. These findings demonstrate that metal-free FOFs can serve as a platform for UOR and open new directions toward organic framework-based electrocatalysts for sustainable energy conversion.

papers.title: A Scalable One-Pot Strategy for Porphyrin Metal–Organic Frameworks via In situ Linker Synthesis
papers.abstract: Porphyrin metal–organic frameworks (pMOFs) are highly versatile materials for catalysis, energy, and environmental applications, yet their widespread use is limited by the cost and multistep synthesis of porphyrin linkers. Here, we report a one-pot synthetic strategy that integrates porphyrin formation and MOF crystallization, enabling the direct assembly of zirconium-based pMOFs from simple molecular precursors. This approach eliminates the need for linker isolation and purification, significantly reducing synthetic complexity and resource consumption. The method is demonstrated for the benchmark framework PCN-224 and its zinc metalloporphyrin analogue, yielding crystalline, porous materials at multigram scale. Notably, the resulting materials exhibit enhanced mesoporosity, which improves mass transport and enables superior adsorption of large organic dyes, despite lower BET surface areas compared to conventionally synthesized analogues. Importantly, we further demonstrate the generality of this approach by synthesizing USTC-9(Fe), a framework with distinct metal nodes and porphyrin linker geometry. This work establishes a versatile platform for coupling complex linker synthesis with framework assembly, offering a sustainable and scalable route to functional pMOFs and broadening the scope of in situ linker formation in reticular chemistry.

papers.title: Selective Ligand Replacement Leads to Carbene Complexes as Catalysts in Proteins
papers.abstract: Artificial metalloenzymes (ArMs) that incorporate organometallic fragments through direct metal–protein coordination open the door to unlock the full evolutionary potential of the protein scaffold to modulate catalysis. This work builds on our previously published work, in which Ru(II) piano stool complexes bearing bipyridyl ligands were used to deliver [Ru(Arene)]2+ fragments into a naïve protein scaffold, generating a transfer-hydrogenase artificial metalloenzyme. Here we systematically explore Ru(II) piano stool complexes bearing pyridyl–N-heterocyclic carbene (Pyr–NHC) bidentate ligands as active-site precursors for metathases and transfer hydrogenases. In this work we describe the synthesis and characterisation of five novel Ru(II) piano stool complexes bearing a hexamethylbenzene (HMB) arene cap and Pyr–NHC bidentate ligands, in which systematic variation of the NHC wingtip substituent (R′ = Me, Et, iPr, Ph) and the pyridine ring substituent (R = H, F) tunes the steric and electronic properties of the complex. Single-crystal X-ray analysis and electrochemical studies show that the strong σ-donation from the carbene lowers the Ru(II/III) redox potential and elongates the Ru–HMB bond relative to their bipyridyl counterparts. This supports displacement of the arene as opposed to the bidentate ligand in the presence of protein. Systematic comparison between Pyr–NHC and bipyridyl complexes also provided an insight into the influence of the arene and the bidentate ligand on the structural and electrochemical properties of these complexes.

papers.title: Metalsurfer: Fast Generation of Realistic Substrate-Adsorbate Interfaces
papers.abstract: Realistic adsorbate–substrate geometries are essential for meaningful electronic-structure calculations at interfaces, yet constructing them remains slow and generally ad hoc for bulky molecules, high coverages, and irregular surfaces. This challenge limits systematic exploration of adsorption configurations across many problems in catalysis, surface chemistry, and materials design. We introduce metalsurfer, a Python package that generates density functional theory (DFT)-ready interface models from simplified molecular input line-entry system (SMILES) strings and a substrate. The workflow combines chemistry-aware, CPU-parallel placement enumeration with TorchSim GPU-batched relaxation under a machine-learned interatomic potential (MLIP), molecular integrity filters, sequential coverage growth, and optional Bayesian acquisition. We demonstrate these capabilities on three chemically distinct systems. For camphor on Cu(111), a ∼1.2 h search recovers neighbors to all eight published weak-adsorption minima and provides a set of plausible basins for refinement. For bipyridine on defected Au(111), offline fixed-batch replays on saved saturation pools show that probability-of-improvement acquisition identifies the first committed motif much faster than random sampling. Transfer from earlier coverage steps also accelerates later searches, with a trust gate that can fall back to a cold model if the prior fails current-step validation. For CO/Pt(111), fixed-coverage n-tuplet searches locate all four ordered adlayers reported in the literature. In each case, a few hours of GPU screening produce a compact shortlist for DFT refinement. metalsurfer thus provides a practical route through the combinatorial problem of interface construction.

papers.title: Formation Pathways of Cyanocoronene (C24H11CN) in the Interstellar Medium and its Detectability with JWST
papers.abstract: Cyanocoronene, the currently known largest cyano-substituted polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH), has recently been discovered in the molecular cloud TMC-1. In this work, we investigate its possible formation pathways using density functional theory (DFT) together with multireference CASSCF and NEVPT2 quantum chemical calculations. Six distinct formation mechanisms are explored, including HAVA-type growth pathways as well as alternative bottomup routes. To facilitate astronomical searches, anharmonic infrared spectra of cyanocoronene are computed and compared with continuum-subtracted JWST/NIRSpec observations. Our calculations indicate that, among the bottom-up growth pathways considered, early incorporation of the nitrile group generally facilitates subsequent PAH growth, while direct cyanation of an already formed coronene framework is also energetically favorable, exhibiting a submerged barrier. Comparison of the theoretical spectra with the available JWST observations does not reveal any convincing spectral signatures attributable to cyanocoronene in the different astrophysical environments examined.

papers.title: Research Progress and Applications of the Fundamental Principles of Soft Ionization Mass Spectrometry
papers.abstract: (1. Guangdong Huisheng Testing Technology Co., Ltd.) Abstract: Soft ionization mass spectrometry is widely applied in fields such as pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, environmental monitoring, and food safety; however, its fundamental principles remain subject to considerable debate, rendering it a "black-box" technology. This review summarizes the basic principles of electrospray ionization (ESI), matrix-assisted laser desorption (MALDI), and desorption electrospray ionization (DESI), and establishes "one theory, two equations, and three instruments" as the theoretical and practical foundation for soft ionization mass spectrometry. Furthermore, this study discusses the electromagnetic applications of soft ionization mass spectrometry, thereby expanding its scope of research and application.

papers.title: MolSanitizer: An open-source pipeline to prepare small-molecule databases for large-scale virtual screening
papers.abstract: Accurate preparation of small-molecule databases for virtual screening is crucial for the success of computer-aided drug discovery. Although numerous free software options are available, they often underperform compared to commercial alternatives. Here, we introduce MolSanitizer, an open-source molecular preparation pipeline built on RDKit and designed for large-scale virtual screening. MolSanitizer extends existing open-source functionality through curated, chemical-environment-aware rules for protonation and tautomerization, systematic stereoisomer enumeration, and a dedicated conformer generator that combines knowledge-based structural preferences with stochastic torsional sampling. Our benchmarking results show that MolSanitizer achieves better performance than several free software alternatives while achieving performance levels comparable to commercial software. MolSanitizer features a modular and open-source design, allowing users to easily customize the tool to meet their specific needs. MolSanitizer also generates output files compatible with several widely used molecular docking programs, thereby facilitating a streamlined workflow for users. MolSanitizer is available for free at https://github.com/carlssonlab/MolSanitizer and via a web server at https://carlssonlabtools.icm.uu.se/molsani.

papers.title: Ultra-lightweight Flexible Perovskite–Perovskite–Organic Triple-Junction Tandem Solar Cells
papers.abstract: Triple-junction photovoltaics offer a promising route to surpass the efficiency limitations of single-junction solar cells, yet existing high-performance architectures are predominantly rigid and relatively heavy, limiting their use in weight-sensitive applications. Here, we report, to the best of our knowledge, the first ultra-lightweight and flexible monolithic perovskiteperovskite–organic triple-junction tandem solar cells. The devices integrate 2.05 eV and 1.62 eV perovskite front and middle subcells with a 1.33 eV organic bulk-heterojunction rear subcell on a 10 μm flexible polyethylene terephthalate substrate. The champion tandem device achieves a power conversion efficiency of 24.1%, with an open-circuit voltage of 3.27 V, a short-circuit current density of 9.32 mA/cm2, and a fill factor of 79.0%, corresponding to a power-per-weight of 11.2 W/g. The device exhibits a stabilized PCE of 24.6% under maximumpower-point tracking and negligible hysteresis between forward and reverse voltage scans. External quantum efficiency measurements yield closely matched integrated photocurrent densities of 9.39, 9.39, and 9.21 mA/cm2 for the three subcells, confirming efficient spectral utilization and current matching. These results establish flexible perovskite–perovskiteorganic triple-junction tandems as a promising platform for high-specific-power photovoltaics and open opportunities for lightweight energy harvesting in aerospace, unmanned aerial vehicles, wearable electronics, and portable power systems.

papers.title: Indium-Catalyzed Deaminative Coupling of Propargylamines with Terminal Alkynes: A Mild Approach to Conjugated 1,3-Dienones
papers.abstract: A mild and efficient indium-catalyzed coupling of propargylamines with terminal alkynes has been developed, affording a diverse array of conjugated 1,3-dienones in good to excellent yields. The reaction proceeds via in situ hydrolysis of propargylamines to generate the corresponding enones, followed by an indium(III)-promoted syn-selective alkyne insertion. Using InCl3 as the catalyst and DBU as the base, the protocol features broad functional-group tolerance and operates under mild conditions. Mechanistic investigations indicate that indium activation is crucial for facilitating the addition of alkynes to enones, enabling selective construction of conjugated 1,3-dienones frameworks. This transformation represents a rare example of indium-catalyzed C–C bond formation and provides a practical and versatile approach to structurally diverse 1,3-dienones from readily available propargylamine precursors.

papers.title: Quantitative Characterization of Pharmaceutical Powder Surface Interactions Using Inverse Gas Chromatography-Derived Surface Energy Profiles
papers.abstract: Quantitative characterization of surface and interfacial properties is important for understanding the behavior of pharmaceutical powders, but conventional approaches to powder wettability and surface free energy can be influenced by measurement procedures and sample-specific factors. Inverse gas chromatography (IGC) provides a sensitive approach for characterizing powder surface energetics as a function of fractional surface coverage; however, the reproducibility and interpretation of IGC-derived surface energy profiles require careful evaluation. In this study, the reproducibility of IGC-derived surface energy profiles was examined using pharmaceutical excipients, and the resulting energetic characteristics were compared with wettability measurements obtained using sessile drop and Washburn methods. Surface-energy profiles were further used to calculate thermodynamic work-of-adhesion profiles for powder–water interactions and for drug–excipient systems. Distinct differences in surface-energy profiles were observed among pharmaceutical excipients, including materials with identical nominal chemical compositions but different grades. Drug–excipient work-of-adhesion profiles further demonstrated coverage-dependent differences in calculated interfacial interactions among pharmaceutical materials. The results demonstrate that IGC-derived surface-energy profiles can provide reproducible characterization of pharmaceutical powder surfaces and can be extended to quantitative evaluation of solid–liquid and solid–solid interfacial interactions. These findings support the use of surface-energy profiles as a quantitative framework for characterization of pharmaceutical powders and for comparison of potential interfacial interactions among formulation components.

papers.title: Pd-Cu-Ag Trimetallic Synergistic Catalysis for Decarboxylative/Deaminative Coupling of Carboxylic acids with Tertiary Amines
papers.abstract: Palladium-catalyzed coupling reactions, such as the well-established Suzuki and Hiyama couplings of benzylic ammonium salts, have been widely employed for the synthesis of diphenylmethanes. In contrast, the decarboxylative coupling strategy for constructing such scaffolds remains largely unexplored. This paper reports a Pd-Cu-Ag trimetallic synergistic catalytic system that enables efficient access to diphenylmethane derivatives through C(sp3)–N bond cleavage of amines and decarboxylation of carboxylic acids. This innovative methodology involves the in situ generation of carbene precursors via Pd-catalyzed, electron-deficient alkyne-mediated deamination of tertiary amines, along with the formation of activated nucleophilic species through Cu/Ag-catalyzed decarboxylation of carboxylic acids. The protocol features mild reaction conditions, high efficiency, and excellent functional group tolerance.

papers.title: Mixed Ionic–Electronic Memory in a Conjugated Polymer Composite for Retrospective Optical Event Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Coupling a light-responsive conjugated polymer to an ionic matrix and oxide interfaces offers a materials strategy for retaining complementary information about completed optical events. A PEDOT:PSS/Nafion/TiO 2 composite implements this approach through an irradiance-dependent conductance amplitude and a wavelength-dependent fading trajectory. At matched nominal polymer loading, TiO 2 incorporation reduces the light-OFF amplitude by 70–77% while extending the half-decay time by 1.56–2.01-fold. Post-illumination optical spectra reveal persistent, composition-dependent changes consistent with electronic-state redistribution coupled to slower matrix and interfacial relaxation. The peak conductance change remains linear with irradiance over 10–40 mW cm −2 (R 2 = 0.9981–0.9993), enabling 91.7% leave-one-condition-out wavelength accuracy and an irradiance mean absolute error of 0.86 mW cm −2 . Same-batch devices show strong kinetic fidelity (median relaxationtime coefficient of variation = 10.02%), but zero-shot transfer to a device from an independently prepared batch fell to 58.3% wavelength accuracy (7/12; p = 0.066 versus three-class chance), making cross-batch kinetic variability the principal barrier to calibration-free transfer. With readout delay withheld, 50 s segments yield 88% wavelength accuracy and a conditional event-age error of 5.5 s. This work demonstrates retrospective decoding of completed optical events in a conjugated polymer composite. A stored conductance peak and a post-illumination relaxation trajectory enable calibrated reconstruction of irradiance, wavelength, and elapsed event age.

papers.title: Depth-resolved operando grazing-incidence diffraction reveals non-equilibrium Cu-Pt alloy restructuring under glycerol electrooxidation
papers.abstract: Alloying Pt with Cu enhances activity towards hydrogen generation and valueadded products during the electrooxidation of glycerol, but the most active alloys typically require electrochemical activation, during which their structure and composition evolve in poorly understood ways. Here we use synchrotron-based operando, angle-dependent grazing incidence X-ray diffraction in a custom dual-chamber electrochemical flow cell to follow, in real time, the depth-resolved structural evolution of Cu-Pt thin-film catalysts under glycerol electrooxidation in alkaline media. Our approach allows us to monitor the temporal evolution of lattice parameter, phase composition and microstrain during cyclic voltammetry and chronoamperometry while varying the X-ray penetration depth from the topmost tens of nanometres into the underlying alloy. For Cu-rich Cu92Pt8 catalysts, we observe substantial restructuring of the near-surface region, including the cyclic formation and reduction of Cu2O, pronounced Cu leaching from depths of several tens of nanometres, and the progressive emergence of a Pt-rich ≈Cu15Pt85 phase that stabilises the surface against further oxidation. These structural changes coincide with a ca. 5-fold increase in current density and a ca. 100 mV increase in onset potential during activation, after which the electrochemical response becomes stable. Pt-richer alloys exhibit markedly reduced restructuring, with compositional changes largely confined to the top ≈20-30 nm of the catalyst. Analysis of peak broadening via Williamson-Hall plots reveals that dealloying and surface oxidation are associated with increased microstrain, which subsequently relaxes as a Pt-rich surface configuration is established. Beyond revealing the non-equilibrium interplay of oxidation, segregation and realloying that governs the performance and durability of Cu-Pt catalysts for glycerol electrooxidation, our methodology and cell design provide a flexible, broadly applicable platform for operando, depth-resolved diffraction studies of electrochemical interfaces in energy and biomass-conversion reactions.

papers.title: The helium ground-state energy to 60 significant figures on a laptop
papers.abstract: We report a variational upper bound on the nonrelativistic, infinite-nuclear-mass ground-state energy of helium whose first 60 significant figures are converged, E0 = −2.903 724 377 034 119 598 311 159 245 194 404 446 696 925 311 117 290 339 042 34 Eh, 16 more than the best previous record. The calculation runs on a laptop and the method, which we call FLAKE (Fock-log anisotropic Kronecker eigensolver), combines four ingredients. (i) A change of variables making Schwartz’s Hylleraas-type basis with logarithms an exact tensor product, so the Hamiltonian is a sum of 27 Kronecker products of small matrices. (ii) Exact, arbitrary-precision orthonormalisation of the small radial and angular Gram factors removes all cancellation from the large computation. (iii) Fixed-point products at about 280 bits are split without error into ordinary double-precision matrix multiplications. (iv) The variational space is anisotropic: it carries extra radial degree and a tower of (ln s)p functions only at low angular order, as dictated by channelresolved convergence rates. Every energy quoted is certified by an independent arbitrary-precision evaluation of the Rayleigh quotient of the explicit trial function. The remaining error is estimated from geometric convergence laws that predicted subsequent energy increments to within 2%.

papers.title: Density Functional Theory Bond Dissociation Energies of Model Compounds Relevant to LDL Oxidation: Bis-Allylic C–H, Phenolic O–H and Hydroperoxide O–H Bonds
papers.abstract: Background: Oxidative modification of low-density lipoprotein (LDL) contributes to atherogenesis, with polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) as its main chemical target. Vitamin E is an effective chain-breaking antioxidant in vitro, yet large clinical trials showed no cardiovascular benefit. We calculated bond dissociation energies (BDEs) of model compounds to quantify the underlying thermodynamics. Methods: Density functional theory calculations (PySCF; B3LYP/6-311+G(d,p)//B3LYP/6-31G*, scaled zero-point energy, 0 K) were performed for butane (secondary C–H), 1,4-pentadiene, phenol, catechol and methyl hydroperoxide. Vitamin E was not calculated at the relaxed level; published values were used. A truncated tocopherol model (5,7,8-trimethylchroman-6-ol) was run at screening level only (B3LYP/6-31+G*, unrelaxed geometries, no zero-point correction), with phenol at the same level. Results: The bis-allylic C–H bond of 1,4-pentadiene (68.2 kcal/mol) was 28.3 below the secondary C–H bond of butane (96.5). Catechol O–H (73.4) was 8.4 below phenol (81.8). The hydroperoxide model (79.6) fell 2.2 below phenol, whereas experimental values place the two within about 1 kcal/mol, comparable to their uncertainties, so phenol is a weak test of the order; catechol was 6.2 below the hydroperoxide, as expected. In screening calculations the tocopherol model was 9.0 below phenol. Published values place α-tocopherol O–H at about 77 to 78 kcal/mol, about 10 below phenol, the same direction as our screening gap. For the four bonds with experimental references, computed values were 1.7 to 8.6 kcal/mol below them; no direct experimental value exists for the bis-allylic C–H. Gaps and ordering, not absolute values, are therefore interpreted. Conclusions: The calculations quantify the thermodynamic basis for PUFA vulnerability and for the stronger hydrogen donation of polyphenol-type O–H bonds. They do not by themselves show donation to peroxyl radicals. Bond energies cannot explain the clinical trial results; kinetics, LDL localization and tocopherol-mediated peroxidation must be considered. No clinical outcomes or biomarkers were computed.

papers.title: The Pnictogen Oracle Provider: Multi-Fidelity Graph Landscapes To Benchmark Molecular Optimization
papers.abstract: The informed discovery and inverse design of new molecules and materials is among the most active applications of data-driven procedures, such as statistical learning, to chemical problems. These approaches involve two key aspects: the dataset, and the exploration algorithms. Here, we cover both of these dimensions by introducing POP (Pnictogen Oracle Provider), a platform comprised by an extensive graph database and an optimization toolkit. The database contains almost 200,000 structures for phosphines, amines and arsines at different fidelity levels, explicitly including failed calculations and enforcing a topology based on substituent-level mutation operations. On the other hand, the software toolkit streamlines the application of optimization algorithms (search policies and predictive oracles) to such databases, pushing forward the development of benchmarks. We explore the baseline application of a varied set of such methods—evolutionary algorithms, Bayesian Optimization, LLM-based procedures and multifidelity approaches—to the optimization of a key property: the HOMO-LUMO gap across each of the three ligand families. In this manner, we reveal the relevance of graph topology in the guidance of these algorithms, as well as the performance differences these baseline methods depending on the particularities of each of the ligand families.

papers.title: A Solution-Gated Graphene Transistor Sensor for the Detection and Quantification of Guanine Quadruplexes.
papers.abstract: SGGT G4 Detection 2 ABSTRACT. We report the design, realization, and testing of a Solution-Gated Graphene Transistor Sensor aimed at detecting and quantifying guanine quadruplexes. By using all-atom molecular dynamic simulations complemented with free energy methods we rationally design the architecture of the sensors, exploiting an economic and easy-available G4 ligand. The prototype of the sensor has shown the capacity to provide a linear response depending on the G4 concentration, hence showing the proof of concept of its applicability for G4 detection. The proposed sensors may allow the rapid detection of guanine quadruplexes in complex matrices, without relying on the use of antibodies or complex experimental apparatus.

papers.title: A soluble conductive chromium coordination polymer with radical ligands and non-integer redox states
papers.abstract: There are few conductive metal-organic materials that are solution processible or that feature electron-accepting conductive units. Thus, a soluble, semiconductive coordination polymer (1n+)x (n = 1 – 3) was developed by linking CrIII ions with electron-deficient back-to-back bis-terpyridine (btpy) ligands. CrIII promotes reduction of these ligands under mild conditions (starting at −0.16 V vs. Fc+/0), providing the first extended material with btpy•− or btpy2− units. Interestingly, (1n+)x undergoes non-integer redox changes (∣Δn∣ < 1) in DMF solution, representing emergent electronic behavior that leads to a moderately high solid-state conductivity of 3.9 x 10−3 S cm−1 when n = 1.5. These solution-phase/solid-state correlations present a promising way to examine and tune the electronic properties of metal-organic radical materials.

papers.title: Memory-Augmented Generative Design of Octahedral Co(II) Complexes with Targeted Zero-Field Splitting
papers.abstract: The discovery of coordination complexes with targeted magnetic anisotropy remains challenging because the enormous chemical space of ligands and coordination environments makes propertydirected molecular design difficult to achieve by conventional screening. Here, we introduce a memoryaugmented generative framework for the inverse design of octahedral Co(II) complexes with targeted zero-field splitting (ZFS). A chemically curated dataset of ~6000 Co(II) complexes, was used to establish a broad electronic-structure landscape spanning positive and negative ZFS regimes. Building on this chemical space, a generative strategy was developed in which ligand structures are iteratively mutated, recombined, and selected according to their predicted magnetic properties, while an elitememory mechanism preserves high-performing molecular motifs and guides subsequent generations toward increasingly favorable candidates. This enables targeted exploration of ligand combinations and coordination environments associated with large negative ZFS while simultaneously controlling rhombicity. The generated complexes were subjected to independent CASSCF calculations, including spin–orbit coupling, to directly validate their magnetic properties. Notably, the generative framework identified candidates with strongly enhanced axial anisotropy, including a representative complex exhibiting D ≈ −223 cm-1 after ab initio validation. The validated candidates reproduced the targeted ZFS with deviations of approximately 15–18 cm-1. These results establish a generative, memory-guided route from ligand design to electronically validated magnetic complexes, providing a practical strategy for discovering previously unexplored Co(II) molecular magnets and advancing molecular-magnet design from screening toward property-directed generation.

papers.title: Composition-Dependent Remodeling of the ABCB1Disordered Linker by Plasma-Generated ReactiveMixtures
papers.abstract: Multidrug resistance (MDR) mediated by the efflux transporter ABCB1 (P-glycoprotein) remains a major barrier in cancer chemotherapy. Because classical active-site inhibitors have largely failed clinically due to off-target toxicity, disrupting the interdomain mechanical coupling required for transport has emerged as an attractive alternative. Cold atmospheric plasma (CAP) generates coexisting reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (RONS) capable of sensitizing chemoresistant cells, yet how multicomponent reactive mixtures dynamically perturb the intrinsically disordered NBD1–TMD2 linker, a vital mechanical relay in ABCB1, remains unresolved. Here, we investigate the conformational and mechanical response of the structurally tethered ABCB1 linker exposed to binary and ternary mixtures of H2O2, NO, and O2 using all-atom molecular dynamics simulations. Characterization across a six-descriptor dynamical panel, synthesized into an Integrated Control-Relative Restriction Score (ICRRS), reveals that linker remodeling is governed by chemical composition rather than total molecular loading. Increasing molecular burden does not induce monotonic rigidity; instead, distinct mixture combinations selectively direct the linker toward divergent, polarized states of conformational restriction or conformational release. Crucially, benchmarking against isolated-species counterparts revealed pronounced composition-dependent contrasts, wherein co-solutes redirect local torsional kinetics, spatial breadth, and effective tethered stiffness. These findings establish that coexisting plasma-derived species selectively reconfigure the conformational state of the ABCB1 disordered relay. By demonstrating that mixture biophysics overrides concentration-dependent loading, this work provides an atomistic foundation for how multicomponent plasma biophysics can mechanically modulate ABCB1 allostery, offering new biophysical perspectives for overcoming P-glycoprotein-mediated chemoresistance.

papers.title: Aerobic ethanol oxidation by magnetic inductive heating of Pd NPs supported onto Ni foam
papers.abstract: Selective aerobic oxidation of ethanol to acetic acid is an attractive example of the conversion of biomass-derived alcohol value-added chemicals. In this context, conventional liquidphase processes often rely on harsh conditions, long reaction times, inefficient external heating and limited catalyst recovery. Herein, a radically new strategy for acetic acid synthesis from ethanol is proposed and demonstrated. The catalyst used is designed not only as the active phase for chemical transformation, but also as the element responsible for local heat generation. Pd nanoparticles were immobilised onto magnetically-responsive Ni foam, affording a macroscopic, flow-compatible architecture that overcomes key limitations found for dispersed or powdered systems, including aggregation, active-phase loss and difficult reuse. Using a low amplitude alternating magnetic field of 9.2 mT, which corresponds to a lower magnetic flux density value than normally used for dispersed magnetic nanocatalyst, the Pd@Ni-foam system reached 90 % ethanol conversion after 8 h, while the acetic acid selectivity was >98 % already after 2 h reaction time. In analogous conditions, conventional heating was significantly less effective than magnetic induction, highlighting the advantage of delivering thermal energy directly at the Pd/liquid interface, thereby preserving ethanol availability at the active sites while limiting substrate evaporation. The structured catalyst showed direct reusability without regeneration, and analysis of the recovered catalyst revealed neither Pd NPs sintering, nor detectable Pd loss. By combining catalytic activity, lowfield magnetic responsiveness, stability, reduced bulk heating and continuous flow operation within a single tuneable material, a new approach to heterogeneous catalysis has been introduced, opening a modular route toward electrified, intensified and more efficient liquidphase transformations of renewable and volatile substrates, such as ethanol.

papers.title: Pd-catalyzed Cycloadditions of 5-Vinyloxazolidine-2,4-diones: A Diastereo- and Enantioselective Access to Spirooxindoles
papers.abstract: In this manuscript, we report a straightforward route to spirooxindoles by Pd-catalyzed cycloadditions of 5-vinyloxazolidine-2,4-diones with isatins. After a screening of chiral ligands, DTBM-SEGPHOS was selected to induce high diastereo- and enantiocontrol of the two newly created tetrasubstituted stereocenters. Our investigation demonstrated broad functional group tolerance under the reaction conditions. Overall, this work represents a rare example of Pd-catalyzed cycloadditions involving 5- vinyloxazolidine-2,4-diones and electrophilic C=O bonds.

papers.title: A species-resolved well-balanced lattice Boltzmann framework for Maxwell–Stefan diffusion in non-ideal multiphase multicomponent transport
papers.abstract: Simulating non-ideal multiphase multicomponent transport requires coupled solution of phase equilibrium, hydrodynamics, and multicomponent diffusion. Recent thermodynamically consistent and well-balanced lattice Boltzmann formulations have addressed multiphase equilibria, but their integration with multicomponent diffusion is less developed. In this work, a speciesresolved well-balanced lattice Boltzmann framework is developed to incorporate Maxwell–Stefan diffusion into non-ideal multiphase multicomponent transport. The formulation evaluates thermodynamic driving forces from chemical potentials and introduces pairwise interspecies resistance at the species-momentum level while preserving the well-balanced nature of the underlying multiphase model. Asymptotic analysis shows that the species-level force balance reduces to the Maxwell–Stefan constitutive relation under quasi-static diffusive conditions. The framework is assessed by equilibrium and phase separation tests, linear modal benchmarks, Arnold–Toor cross-diffusion cases, local Maxwell–Stefan diagnostics, and a buoyancydriven bubble dissolution illustration. The equilibrium tests recover the theoretical equilibrium compositions with nearly uniform chemical potentials and very low spurious velocities. The modal benchmarks reproduce the predicted exponential decay rates with errors below 0.2% for ideal mixtures and about 0.1–0.5% for non-ideal mixtures, while the Arnold–Toor and local diagnostic tests capture characteristic Maxwell–Stefan diffusion behavior. These results support the proposed framework as a thermodynamically consistent and well-balanced lattice Boltzmann approach for non-ideal multiphase multicomponent transport.

papers.title: GMAP: A General Purpose Hamiltonian Mapping Program for Computational Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Vibrational and electronic spectra provide useful information about structure, dynamics, and function in the condensed phase. Electrostatic mappings have proved to be powerful tools for predicting and interpreting both vibrational and electronic spectra. Numerous special purpose programs exist; however, a general purpose framework is still missing. In this paper, we present a new general purpose mapping program for bridging the gap between structural and dynamical information obtained in molecular dynamics simulations and programs for calculating spectroscopic observables. It comes with a number of preexisting maps to, for example, predict the amide I vibrational spectrum of proteins or to model the electronic Qy band of strongly coupled chlorophyll molecules in photosynthetic systems. The program applying mappings connecting structural or electrostatic properties with excitation frequencies, transition dipoles, and couplings is designed so that the user can easily adapt existing maps or add new maps for desired chromophores.

papers.title: Tracking Surface Charge of Gold Single-Crystal Electrodes with Diffuse Layer Force Microscopy
papers.abstract: Electrochemistry is a powerful approach for the interconversion of electrical and chemical energy. This is enabled by the nanoscale confined potential difference occurring at an interface, such as that between a solid and a liquid. As such, the structure of this region of separated charge, or electrical double layer, inherently includes molecular scale ordering in the liquid, as well as atomic scale details of the electrode, making it challenging to obtain a detailed picture of the potential-dependent state of electrochemical interfaces. In this work, we locally measure the long-range electrostatic interaction force (on the order of the screening length) between single-crystal gold electrodes and a microscale probe. Using such force spectroscopy, we observe three distinct electrochemical phenomena through the interaction force, i.e. non-faradaic charging of the interface and the potential of zero free charge, potential-induced surface reconstruction, and electrochemical oxidation of the gold surface. The results are interpreted within the Derjaguin-Landau-Verwey-Overbeek framework, relating the force measurement to the surface charge and the electrochemical state of the interface.

papers.title: Aza-Michael Addition of Aliphatic Amines to Weakly Polarised Alkenes via Organobase Catalysis
papers.abstract: The direct addition of aliphatic amines to alkenes offers an atom-economical route to valuable N-alkyl amines, but remains challenging for weakly polarised alkenes. This is because C–N bond formation is poorly driven thermodynamically and difficult to achieve without strongly activating the alkene or generating more reactive nitrogen species. Here we report an organobase-catalysed strategy that enables anti-Markovnikov addition of secondary aliphatic amines to weakly polarised (hetero)aryl alkenes. Kinetic studies and calculations support a mechanism in which the organobase promotes C–N bond formation through hydrogen bonding and noncovalent stabilisation of the addition transition state, followed by rapid deprotonation of the addition complex. The developed conditions were also applicable to challenging C–C bond forming Michael addition reactions with enolate nucleophiles. These findings demonstrate that organobase catalysis can overcome the intrinsic kinetic and thermodynamic challenges associated with closed-shell additions to weakly activated alkenes.

papers.title: High-Sensitivity, Dual Ratiometric and Turn-on ABATaRs for Multiplexed Temporal Imaging of Ferroptosis Hallmarks in Living Cells
papers.abstract: We present a computationally-guided workflow for designing dual turn-on and ratiometric Raman sensors. The workflow has been used to rationally design activity-based alkyne tagged Raman, ABATaR , sensors that overcome the inherently low Raman sensitivity via strategic placement of electron-donating and electron-withdrawing groups. An ABATaR sensing scaffold designed via the workflow afforded ~ 9000 times higher Raman scattering cross-section than the dimethylsulfoxide C-H stretching-mode. The sensitivity of the scaffold was compared to that of 5-ethynyl-2'-deoxyuridine ( EdU ) to determine Raman intensity versus EdU , RIE, a parameter used to benchmark Raman probes. An RIE value of 170 was obtained which is one of the highest amongst previously reported monoyne and diyne-based Raman probes. The sensitive ABATaR -scaffold was developed into a dual turn-on and ratiometric Fe 2+ -sensor that was applied to distinctly quantify endogenous cellular labile Fe 2+ ion levels. In a key result, live-cell, temporal imaging with the Fe 2+ - ABATaR sensor revealed that intracellular labile Fe 2+ levels progressively increase with ferroptosis while the total Fe-level remains constant. To demonstrate the generalizability of the design workflow, we synthesized an orthogonal ABATaR -sensor for H 2 O 2 . The H 2 O 2 -sensor was applied together with the Fe 2+ -sensor along with inherent Raman peaks for cytochromes to enable simultaneous, multiplexed spontaneous Raman imaging of three distinct ferroptosis hallmarks—labile Fe 2+ , H 2 O 2 , and redox-sensitive cytochrome Raman signals—in living cells. Importantly, the ability to pre-design orthogonal ratiometric Raman sensors and simultaneously track three regulators of ferroptosis via discrete non-overlapping Raman peaks highlights the tremendous potential of Raman sensors toward attaining live cell multiplexed imaging and quantification.

papers.title: Predicting Water-Induced Demixing of Ionic Liquid Mixtures with Associative Electrolyte PC-SAFT
papers.abstract: Ionic liquids (ILs) can be mixed with other ILs to fine-tune their physicochemical properties. While ILs have been long considered inseparable, recent studies have demonstrated that the controlled addition of water enables the selective recovery of the constituent salts, opening new opportunities for sustainable IL recycling and separation. The rational design of these IL mixtures remains challenging due to the lack of predictive models capable of accurately capturing the interplay between competing short- and long-range interactions in IL-based systems, particularly in multi-IL systems, thereby limiting our ability to guide both the selection of optimal IL components and the development of efficient post-mixing recovery strategies. We propose in this work an associative electrolyte PC-SAFT (aePC-SAFT) model, that incorporates, in a physically balanced manner, the short-range dispersion and hydrogen bonding interactions, as well as the long-range Coulomb interactions. Ion-specific parameters are obtained from homologous series of [CnC1Im][NTf2] (1-alkyl-3-methylimidazolium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide) and [C4C1Im][OAc] (1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium acetate), and subsequently transferred to functionalized ILs, including [C3OC1Im]+ (1-methoxyethyl-3-methylimidazolium), based on the liquid-liquid equilibria (LLE) and density of their mixtures with water and hydrocarbons. Without additional parameter adjustment, the model accurately predicts the LLE of binary and ternary IL-water systems, including the ether-functionalized ILs. This work establishes a robust, predictive, and physically grounded framework for modeling the thermodynamic behavior of ILs, enabling the rational design and optimization of separation processes in IL-based systems.

papers.title: Group-aware validation sharply reduces the apparent accuracy of extraction-category classification in public cannabis laboratory data
papers.abstract: Published models that classify cannabis products from cannabinoid and terpene profiles report near-perfect accuracy: above 95% for resin type, 100% for chemovar class. These figures come from random cross-validation or Kennard-Stone partitioning, which hold out no plant, producer or laboratory. We quantify the cost on a task with explicit group structure. On 33,229 public laboratory-result rows for cannabis concentrates that name a producer, nearly all from Nevada, each with a source-declared extraction category (non-solvent against solvent-based), a gradient-boosted classifier scores 78.5% balanced accuracy and a ROC AUC of 0.89 under random five-fold cross-validation. Holding out the producer leaves 54.0% and 0.62. A signal survives: the pooled held-out AUC is 0.61, with a producer-level bootstrap interval of 0.535 to 0.698. But the reported model's pooled balanced accuracy does not separate from chance (51.6%, interval 47.3 to 56.6); it keeps about 30% of its above-chance AUC, and an unweighted logistic regression 41 to 53%. A designed experiment shows the same direction: with the random split averaged over 200 seeds, 162 HPLC-assayed samples fall from 54.3% to 38.9% under leave-one-variety-out with gradient boosting and from 51.8% to 46.3% with logistic regression, against 33.3% chance. In the market data the same profiles identify the producer at 67.1% against a 14.4% baseline and the laboratory at 92.3% against 40.3%. We conclude that the declared extraction category is only weakly recoverable from these analyte panels for an unseen producer, and that a random split overstates it by 8 to 26 points of balanced accuracy depending on the model and subset. We did not rerun the published studies.

papers.title: Automated Extraction and FAIRification of Chemical Structures from Scientific Publications
papers.abstract: Chemical structures are published predominantly as images, which makes them inaccessible for database indexing, structure-based search and computational reuse. While Optical Chemical Structure Recognition and PDF-extraction tools attempt post-publication recovery, they cannot restore the information lost during image rendering. To address this, we present BChemXtract, an open-source Java library that extracts chemical structures directly from the CDX and CDXML files that authors already submit with their manuscripts. BChemXtract parses the CDX object hierarchy to isolate chemical fragments from graphical annotations and expands abbreviations using a community-curated lookup table. The structures are then converted via the Chemistry Development Kit into standard machine-readable formats. BChemXtract is integrated into the production workflow of the Beilstein Journals, where extracted structures are manually validated before being embedded in article metadata as Schema.org JSON-LD, deposited in PubChem and offered for download. Applied to the 2993 ChemDraw figures and schemes of volume 20 of the Beilstein Journal of Organic Chemistry, it yielded 23,320 structures with InChIs in under two minutes. On a 225-file benchmark corpus, it generated valid InChIs for 98.2% of extracted unique substances, compared with 14.2% for Open Babel, at comparable per-file speed. BChemXtract makes published chemistry FAIR at the point of publication without altering author workflows. It is available under the MIT license together with a web application and the benchmark corpus.

papers.title: Tyr10 Modifications and Peptide Context Rewire GLP-1 Modulation of Amyloid-β42 Assembly
papers.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) is best known as a receptor agonist, yet its peptide-level behavior in protein-rich environments remains poorly defined. Here, a GLP-1-directed photoaffinity probe recovered a predefined Aβ42 spike-in from cell lysates, while endogenous actin and α-synuclein were detected in the recovered fractions. This observation motivated chemically defined assembly studies with the actinlinked β-thymosin reference TMSB4Y. Thioflavin T (ThT) kinetics and endpoint electron microscopy (EM) revealed no single pro- or antiassembly response. GLP-1 advanced the ThT-positive transition of Tyr10-unmodified Aβ42, whereas TMSB4Y attenuated it.
