Phosphorylation or nitration at Tyr10 changed both the direction and timing of these effects, and GLP-1 added after assembly had begun redirected established trajectories in a Tyr10-modification-dependent manner. Ser18 O-GlcNAcylation of GLP-1 provided an orthogonal perturbation, suppressing the Tyr10-unmodified response while enhancing the nitrated trajectory and delaying the phosphorylated one. Together, capture in a complex protein background and assembly in defined mixtures identify GLP-1 as a context-sensitive modulator of Aβ42 assembly rather than a fixed promoter or inhibitor.

papers.title: Paper2CIF: An AI Agent for Reconstructing Atomistic Models to Discover Structure-Reactivity Relationships
papers.abstract: Reinterpreting published chemical findings requires explicit atomic structures that connect experimental observations with reactivity. Here we report Paper2CIF, an artificial intelligence (AI) agent that reconstructs sample-specific atomic structures from published chemical evidence for structure-reactivity relationship investigations. Across 171 interdisciplinary articles, Paper2CIF achieves 97.08% phase identification accuracy and 91.23% final structural accuracy, with correct structures satisfying all applicable reported constraints, including composition, site occupancy, and local coordination. Calculations on reconstructed BiVO4 structures reveal distortion-dependent spatial contributions to the transition dipole, guiding targeted synthesis toward enhanced near-edge photon conversion. The resulting BiVO4-based Z-scheme pair exhibits a 3.47-fold increase in apparent quantum yield from 4.51% to 15.64% at 475 nm, compared with a 1.03-fold increase from 18.51% to 19.02% at 365 nm. The solar-to-hydrogen efficiency increases from 0.969% to 1.448% for overall water splitting. Paper2CIF establishes atomic reconstruction as a common basis for deriving chemical mechanisms from published evidence and translating them into experimentally testable principles for materials synthesis.

papers.title: Metal-Free Photoinduced Divergent Activation of N2O and H2 Employing Main-Group Radical Pairs
papers.abstract: Activating robust small molecules like nitrous oxide (N2O) and molecular hydrogen (H2) without transition metals is a key challenge in sustainable chemistry. To address this, we developed an efficient photochemical platform that uses silylphosphanes to divergently activate both the gases. Under photoirradiation, the silylphosphane’s P-Si bond undergoes rapid homolytic cleavage, releasing highly reactive silyl and phosphinyl radicals. When exposed to N2O, these independent radicals act parallelly to drive a double-deoxygenation cascade, yielding the corresponding tetra-aryldiphosphine dioxide and siloxane. Remarkably, this same transient radical pair can also activate H2 under exceptionally mild conditions. Supported by control experiments and DFT studies that confirm a purely radicaldriven mechanism, this work highlights main-group radical pair as a powerful, sustainable alternative to precious-metal catalysis.

papers.title: Unveiling Photoluminescent N-Heterocyclic Silylene-Silver(I) Amides as Dual-Function Photosensitizers and Third-Harmonic Generators
papers.abstract: N-Heterocyclic silylenes (NHSis) have evolved from laboratory curiosities to versatile ligands for small-molecule activation and homogeneous catalysis, yet their potential in photophysics and optical materials remains unexplored. Here, we report for the first time a series of luminescent NHSi-ligated Ag(I) amide complexes (2–4) exhibiting remarkable thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) and dual-emissive behavior. The NHSi→Ag–diphenylamine complex (2) displays pronounced TADF with an exceptionally small singlet–triplet energy gap (ΔES–T ≈ 0.006 eV) and a short delayed-fluorescence lifetime (τTADF ≈ 0.35 μs at 300 K), indicative of efficient reverse intersystem crossing (RISC) driven by NHSi-to-metal amide charge transfer. Complexes 3 and 4 exhibit dual emission and serve as efficient photosensitizers for singlet oxygen (1O2) generation. Remarkably, these complexes (2-4) demonstrate coherent photon up-conversion via third-harmonic generation (THG), representing the first such observation in main-group organometallic chemistry. These findings unveil a new class of main-group metal complexes as promising photosensitizers and third-order nonlinear optical materials.

papers.title: Hydrogenolysis of N-Cbz-Protected Amines Mediated by Spherical SiliaCat Pd(0)
papers.abstract: The deprotection reaction of N-benzyloxycarbonyl (N-Cbz)-protected amino groups in organic compounds can be efficiently achieved by hydrogenolysis mediated by the sol-gel-entrapped spherical catalyst SiliaCat Pd(0). The heterogeneous catalyst combines high catalytic activity and chemoselectivity with low Pd loading, a nonpyrophoric nature, and excellent reusability. Investigation of the effects of solvent, substrate concentration, Pd loading, temperature, and catalyst particle size revealed that 100 µm spherical SiliaCat Pd(0) provides a favorable balance between rapid reaction kinetics and practical catalyst properties for batch applications. The catalyst was successfully reused over ten consecutive reaction runs, maintaining complete conversion and high isolated yields. A broad substrate scope was demonstrated, with tolerance toward methyl esters, Boc-protected amines, pinacol boronate esters, and an aliphatic bromide, while debromination of an aryl bromide revealed a limitation of the method. Comparison of the 100 µm spherical sol-gel catalyst with several commercial heterogeneous Pd catalysts demonstrates its high catalytic activity and selectivity under mild reaction conditions.

papers.title: Mechanochemical nitrogen fixation into amides and nitriles.
Cation Mixing Controls Photocatalytic Activity of Ionic Carbon Nitrides by Switching Exciton Character and Electron Localization
An Annotation Consistency Checker for Evidence-Based Evaluation of Untargeted LC-MS/MS Metabolite Annotations
papers.abstract: Untargeted LC-MS/MS metabolomics routinely produces complex annotation landscapes in which individual spectra can yield multiple candidate metabolite annotations. Although spectral similarity provides an essential foundation for library-based annotation, determining whether a candidate annotation is consistent with the available evidence and whether alternative explanations remain plausible requires integration of multiple lines of evidence. In current practice, this evaluation is largely embedded in expert judgment, making annotation review difficult to teach, standardize, and reproduce. Here, we introduce an annotation consistency checker that aids this expert review process by generating a user-inspectable report for spectral library matches. The framework integrates complementary evidence dimensions, including spectral agreement, structural relationships among candidate annotations, and competing library matches to highlight annotations that are supported by, or inconsistent with, the available data. Biological context is provided separately to aid interpretation of metabolite occurrence across organisms, tissues, and sample types but is not incorporated into the annotation score. By enabling systematic evaluation of multiple evidence streams, this approach provides a transparent workflow that helps users critically assess metabolite annotations, reduce overinterpretation of spectral matches, and make informed decisions beyond only accepting the top-ranked library match.

papers.title: Structural Description of Two-Dimensional Nanoscale Networks Using Graph Theory and Graph Growth Algorithms
papers.abstract: Nanostructured networks stand out among other nanostructures for their unique combinations of properties and easily scalable energy-efficient synthesis. Their structural organization is, however, difficult to describe using traditional approaches based on crystallinity. Although revealing distinct structural patterns, the nanoscale networks also have a substantial degree of randomness. Two-dimensional (2D) nanostructured networks self-assembled from nanoparticles present a unique opportunity to develop the methodology for structural description of such materials. We describe nanostructured networks as sets of nodes and edges with corresponding weights taking advantage of the mathematical apparatus of Graph Theory (GT). Being extracted from electron microscopy images, the GT descriptors readily identify nanoscale networks obtained under different chemical conditions. Also important is that among the prior studies the GT description of properties has been extensively discussed, while better understanding of adequate GT descriptors is lagging. All GT descriptors were found to be scale-dependent, with average nodal degree, centrality metrics, multi-fractal dimension, and Ollivier-Ricci curvature following smooth superlinear or sublinear trajectories over several thousands of nodes. Statistical analysis of topological and metric parameters of nodes and edges enables development of topometric graph growth algorithms (TOGGA) that capture the structural uniqueness of each nanoscale network. Similarly to the infinite tiling of unit cells in crystals, TOGGA models enabled the extrapolation of nanoscale network structure, commensurate with both micro- and macroscale samples over 10 million nodes and 20 million edges. The predictions of electric transport through the networks comparable in size to experimental samples enable identification of knowledge gaps for rapid design of conductive nanoscale networks. TOGGA models can be used to map out experimentally realistic structures for inverse design of nanoscale networks.

papers.title: An Evidence-Graded Framework for Pharmaceutical Route Selection and Process-Risk Prioritization: A PN6047 Case Study
papers.abstract: Purpose: To develop and demonstrate an evidence-graded framework for screening discovery-scale synthetic routes before experimental process development, using the publicly disclosed route to PN6047, a clinical-stage δ-opioid receptor agonist, as a case study. Methods: No synthesis was performed. Operations exemplified in two patent documents were inventoried; each transformation and its conditions were graded A–D by the strength of public evidence; documented regulatory and hazard attributes were flagged; two process-oriented variants were screened by step count, flags and an evidence-weighted validation burden; and a twelve-item risk register was ranked, with the sensitivity of the prioritization to the author-assigned ratings tested by perturbation. Results: The exemplified route (milligram to gram scale; final N-functionalization isolated in 16% by preparative HPLC) carries 11 documented flags, including an ICH Q3C Class 1 solvent, palladium and a benzotriazole-derived coupling reagent. Variants R1 and R2 carry 3 flags each but a higher validation burden (11 and 15 against 2, linear scale): fewer documented flags did not mean lower development uncertainty. Two risks, impurity purge when crystallization replaces chromatography and the undisclosed route to the vinyl bromide, stayed in the top three in about 87% of perturbations, conditional on the initial risk model. Conclusion: The framework converts public route information into an auditable experimental-prioritization strategy while explicitly separating documented process liabilities from unvalidated alternatives. It does not select a best route; it shows where the evidence is strong or assumed and which experiments carry the highest information value.

papers.title: Designing Alloying Interlayers for Metal Anodes in Batteries: Does Nanostructuring Improve Reversibility?
papers.abstract: Metal anodes have been extensively explored as candidates for high-energy rechargeable batteries. However, uncontrolled electrodeposition of metals such as Zn often produces porous, disconnected “dead” metal that limits reversibility. A common mitigation strategy is to introduce an alloying functional layer, which is in general assumed to perform better when nanostructured due to its increased specific surface area and the diffusion scaling relation 𝜏~ 𝐿 2 𝐷 ⁄ . Here, we directly interrogate how the characteristic feature size of an alloying interlayer governs reversibility, using Ag functional layers with building blocks at three representative length scales: 100 nm, a few μm, and 100 μm, approximately. Combining operando visualization with ex-situ structural characterization, we find that Ag layers composed of few-μm particles exhibit the highest Zn plating and stripping reversibility. Coarse, 100-μm Ag particles provide poor areal coverage, such that beneficial Ag–Zn alloying is confined to isolated regions and does not effectively regulate deposition. In contrast, nanostructured Ag reacts rapidly and nearly completely, transforming into bulk intermetallic phases with large volume change that crack and delaminate from the current collector. Few-μm Ag features, on the one hand, provide sufficient surface coverage to promote uniform nucleation; on the other, Ag particles at this few-μm length scale prevent excessive intermetallic conversion and the associated mechanical failure. These results challenge the conventional wisdom that nanostructured layers are inherently more effective and reveal a previously overlooked mesoscopic design window for alloying interlayers. By explicitly linking alloying-layer feature size to diffusion-controlled phase transformation, mesoscale mechanical stability, and electrochemical behavior, this work identifies surface topography as a key design parameter for stabilizing multivalent metal anodes of high-energy batteries.

papers.title: Temperature-dependent Hydrocarbon Chain Packing in Fatty Acid Protocell Membranes at Mineral Interfaces
papers.abstract: Fatty acid vesicles generated through water-rock interactions have been proposed as plausible models of protocells on early Earth. However, how mineral surfaces influence membrane properties over a wide range of temperatures remains unclear. Here, we investigate the temperature-dependent phase transition and hydrocarbon chain packing of vesicles composed of decanoic acid (DA) and 1-decanol (DOH) in contact with FeS, a key hydrothermal vent mineral. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed that DOH incorporation enhances orientational ordering of the hydrocarbon chains, forming more densely packed and thermally stable membranes. This enhancement in molecular ordering induced by DOH incorporation was confirmed experimentally by in situ temperature-controlled micro-Raman spectroscopy and cross-polarized optical microscopy. Upon contact with FeS, DA/DOH vesicles preferentially adhered to FeS surfaces and underwent pronounced structural deformation in response to microscale mineral topology. Despite this deformation, the DA/DOH vesicles retained their liquid-crystalline membrane state. These results demonstrate that FeS surface reorganizes hydrocarbon chain packing in fatty acid membranes, suggesting that mineral-associated protocells possess structurally and dynamically distinct membrane states from free-floating vesicles under the thermally dynamic HV environments.

papers.title: Multi-fidelity machine learning interatomic potential for the energetics and finite temperature structure of Pt surfaces and nanoparticles
papers.abstract: Accurate accounting of exposed facets and surface sites is central to understanding metal nanoparticle catalysts, but modelling their structure at finite temperatures is computationally expensive. We benchmark the universal interatomic potential UMA (Universal Model for Atoms, Open Catalyst 2020 task) against Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof density functional theory (PBE-DFT) for Pt. UMA underestimates the surface energies of all 13 facets by 11-17 % and the excess energies of 28 differently shaped nanoparticles, each containing less than 500 atoms, most strongly for small particles. We distill UMA into a compact Deep Potential model by pre-training on UMA labelled bulk and slab data, then fine-tune it on a small PBE-DFT dataset that includes nanoparticles. The resulting multi-fidelity machine learning interatomic potential (MF-MLIP) gives a surface-energy root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 2.8 meV Å−2, 21 % lower than a DFT only model trained on the same data. On six nanoparticles, the MF-MLIP improves force accuracy over UMA, reducing the force RMSE by 29-52 %, with the largest gains at surface, edge and vertex atoms. Molecular dynamics at 500 K shows Pt(111) retaining its termination while Pt(100) and Pt(110) change strongly. At 500-700 K, the nanoparticles lose vertex sites and gain edge sites, and some restructure away from their ideal shapes. On the same CPU hardware, the MF-MLIP runs molecular dynamics simulations 60-100 times faster than UMA.

papers.title: Coordination-Insertion Copolymerization of Norbornene with α-Olefins using Half-Titanocene Phosphinimide Catalyst
papers.abstract: We previously reported the controlled coordination-insertion polymerization of 2-norbornene (NB) and 5-alkyl-2-norbornenes using a phosphinimide-ligated half-titanocene catalyst (1), affording high-molecular-weight polymers. In this study, the copolymerization of NB with α-olefins, including 1-octene (2), 1-octadecene (3), and 10-undecen-1-ol (4), was investigated to explore the monomer scope and functional group tolerance. Copolymers with Mn values ranging from 2.0 to 20 kg/mol were obtained in moderate to high yields. NB was consumed more rapidly than 2. Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) analysis of the copolymers suggests that an α-olefin-derived titanium alkyl species undergoes chain transfer via a σ-bond metathesis with NB, affording the 2-norbornenyl moiety at the initiating chain end. In addition, copolymers containing up to 7 mol% of 4 were obtained through protecting the hydroxyl group with methylaluminoxane (MAO) prior to polymerization. Collectively, catalyst 1 exhibited broad reactivity, including the coordination-insertion and the σ-bond metathesis reactions, while remaining catalytically active in the presence of the alkoxyaluminum species.

papers.title: On the impact of methodological configurations and data variations on chemical recycling life cycle assessment studies
papers.abstract: The comparability of Life Cycle Assessment studies on chemical recycling processes for plastic waste conversion is challenging due to the wide range of investigated feedstocks, datasets, and methodological choices. Thus, this paper investigates the impact of various degrees of freedom within peer-reviewed Life Cycle Assessments of chemical recycling processes on the proposed environmental impact. In detail, methodological degrees of freedom, such as system boundary depth, functional units, allocation methods, and the utilization of substitution credits, as well as data-related degrees of freedom, including the use of plant-level, model-based, literature-derived, or third-party data at different data scales, such as experimental, laboratory, or pilot scale, are considered. Among the investigated Life Cycle Assessment studies, none of them applied the same combination of methodological choices, highlighting the methodological uniqueness of each study. However, changes in either methodological or data-related degrees of freedom substantially affect Life Cycle Assessment results in both magnitude and interpretation: without changing the methodology, data-related degrees of freedom shift the global warming potential for 1 kg of treated waste from 2.5 kg CO2-eq. below that of incineration as the reference waste treatment process to 0.5 kg CO2-eq. above. Utilizing the same database, methodological differences as reported in the investigated studies shift the global The underlined authors contributed equally and share first authorship. warming potential from 2.9 below to 0.3 kg CO2-eq. above the global warming potential of incineration. The same trend is found when comparing the products of chemical recycling to the fossil-based production routes, where the main levers affecting the results were identified as the declaration of products, the handling of side streams, and the choice of energy sources. These findings show that LCA results should not be interpreted on the basis of individual values alone, but in the context of methodological choices, data sources and quality, and sensitivity to both data and methodological assumptions. Without transparency regarding these aspects, reported values are of limited interpretive value and may offer unwanted possibilities for selective interpretation and may ultimately increase the risk of greenwashing in the communication of chemical recycling performance.

papers.title: Origin of the Difference between Kohn-Sham and ∆SCF Band gaps for Delocalized Electron–Hole Excitations in Hybrid-Functional Supercell Calculations
papers.abstract: We examine the relationship between ground-state generalized Kohn–Sham (GKS) band gaps and self-consistent ∆SCF excitation energies for delocalized electron–hole excitations in finite periodic supercells. For a vertical excitation at the undistorted ground-state geometry, these two quantities are expected to coincide when the promoted electron and hole remain Bloch-like. This is mostly true with semilocal functionals, but not with hybrid functionals for which the difference increases linearly with the fraction of exact exchange. The origin of this difference is derived from two equivalent viewpoints: the total-energy change associated with the ∆SCF excitation and the occupation-dependent orbital gap shift arising from the self-consistent potential response. The residual energy arises from the orbital-dependent exact-exchange selfenergy associated with the electron-hole pair and decreases approximately as 1/N

papers.title: Structure-Activity Relationship Studies of the Complement Regulator-Recruiting Peptide 5C6
papers.abstract: Active recruitment of host complement regulators to biomedical surfaces emerges as a therapeutic strategy to prevent adverse immuno-inflammatory reactions to biomaterials and organ transplants. Coating with the macrocyclic peptide 5C6, which binds and recruits the central complement regulator factor H (FH), was shown to protect clinically relevant surfaces from complement attack. While we previously identified general determinants for the 5C6-FH interaction, more granular structure-activity relationship (SAR) studies have hitherto been missing. In the absence of published target structures, we employed a panel of focused amino acid substitutions combined with biomolecular interaction studies to achieve an SAR profile of 5C6. We identified three positions that are particularly amenable to affinity optimization and combined several changes to produce a next-generation 5C6 analog with enhanced target residence time and serum stability. Biomaterial-related assays suggest that such analogs may confer benefits under stress conditions, providing a path for the further development of 5C6-based coatings.

papers.title: Earth-abundant 3d metal-catalyzed enantioselective catalysis towards the functionalization of E/Zalkenes mixtures.
papers.abstract: Enantioselective catalysis transforming alkenes to chiral molecules have been a breakthrough in the field of organic synthesis. Though a major challenge persists. The “privileged” chiral catalyst capacities depend on the geometry of the olefin substrate which can be either E or Z. Enantioselective catalysis allowing to convert both alkene stereoisomers to a single chiral molecule promises sustainable synthetic routes and novel mechanistic strategies towards chiral molecule synthesis. Enantioselective methods towards the functionalization of E/Z-alkenes, which has largely taken advantages of the recent development of earth-abundant 3d metal catalysis, are covered in this revue. An emphasis on the mechanisms accounting for the observed stereoconvergence and enantioselectivity is proposed.

papers.title: Multinotch Isolation Enables Efficient Native Top-down Mass Spectrometry of Proteins in Complex Mixtures.
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of intact proteoforms and their complexes directly from heterogenous biological samples is essential to understand their role in health and disease. While native top-down mass spectrometry (nTDMS) workflows enable this, the extreme molecular complexity of biological samples inadvertently results in overlapping signals which confounds protein identification. One approach to resolving this complexity is gas-phase ion-ion reactions which separate analytical targets according to their original charge state. Charge reduction techniques coupled to mass spectrometry resolve signal overlap in m/z space, when ions differ in charge, and so they are especially useful in the analysis of large biomolecules like proteins that form multiple charge states during electrospray ionisation. Previously, we investigated multistage nTDMS of intact proteins sampled directly from tissue sections where the first experiment stage was separation by charge reduction, followed by collisional activation for sequence ion production. The specificity of product ion spectra was improved but at the expense of signal intensity owing to inefficient use of charge-reduced product ions. Here we establish the use of synchronous precursor selection (SPS) for nTDMS via multinotch isolation in a linear ion trap, enabling simultaneous isolation of multiple targets in m/z space and thereby increasing the number of ions available for fragmentation. We implemented SPS for nTDMS across three charge reduction techniques and collision, electron and photon mediated fragmentation methods on commercial and modified mass spectrometers. Improvements to the signal-to-noise ratio of product ions resulted in greater sequence coverage for example intact proteins and complexes up to ~44 kDa using the SPS workflow. We provide a freely-available SPS target calculator, Novalap, that enables simple SPS method development. SPS nTDMS is a methodological breakthrough for proteoform identification in complex mixtures, where specificity is essential, sequence coverage is desired and ion abundance is at a premium.

papers.title: Probing Benzoxazine Dimer Formation Using Methyl-Blocked Derivatives as Mechanistic Probes
papers.abstract: The early-stage dimer formation of 1,3-benzoxazine (PH-a) was investigated as a diagnostic system for understanding the ring-opening polymerization (ROP) mechanism using a coupled FAIMS-IRMPD-MS/MS platform. High-field asymmetric waveform ion mobility spectrometry (FAIMS) resolved the protonated PH-a dimer into three distinct populations. A series of methyl-blocked benzoxazine derivatives was used to systematically eliminate individual reactive sites and assign each FAIMS population to a specific reaction route via tandem MS fragmentation patterns and IRMPD action spectroscopy, supported by theoretical vibrational spectra obtained by DFT calculations. Four dimer formation pathways were confirmed: phenolic aromatic substitution at the ortho and para positions, and arylamine aromatic substitution at the ortho and para positions of the aniline ring. Phenoxy- and nitrogen-mediated attack routes were not observed. Each pathway yields dimers in either a closed-ring (CRB) or open-ring (ROP) form, a structural duality with direct implications for the crosslinking topology and network heterogeneity of the resulting polybenzoxazine.

papers.title: Designing organic photoredox catalysts as a fragment-based puzzle solved by reinforcement learning
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is a promising strategy for identifying optimal solutions in vast search spaces. We have developed a framework in which the design of organic photoredox catalysts (OPCs) is deliberately formulated as a fragment-based puzzle that is well suited to RL. In this framework, an RL agent sequentially selects and orders molecular fragments and attempts to identify fragment combinations that afford high rewards, as calculated based on the similarity between the properties of the generated molecules and those of 4CzIPN, a well-known OPC. In addition to the rediscovery of a previously reported high-performance OPC, experimental validation of the proposed candidates revealed a TADF emitter with redox potentials similar to those of 4CzIPN, as well as an OPC with superior catalytic activity in several photoreactions.

papers.title: Birefringence Breaks Symmetry-Protected Fluorescence Trapping in Laser-Cooled Crystals
papers.abstract: Total internal reflection traps light inside high-index emitters, and in laser-cooled crystals the trapped fluorescence limits how far purification lowers the parasitic heat load. The symmetry of the crystal shape is known to govern this trapping. Here we show that the dielectric tensor supplies a second, intrinsic symmetry, and we unify the geometric and dielectric symmetries in a single conservation law. A fluorescence photon stays trapped when every facet operation conserves a wave-vector component that keeps it inside total internal reflection. Mirror facets of a cuboid conserve three components and trap 17.2% of all directions. Brewster end facets, or mode conversion between ordinary and extraordinary waves at facets containing the optic axis of uniaxial Yb:YLF, leave one component and reduce the trapped set to a universal shell of 3.45% of directions. Sub-degree misorientation of the optic axis, subnanometer facet roughness or an asymmetric cut releases this shell, and the release rate determines how strongly purification lowers parasitic loss. Released Yb:YLF crystals keep nearly linear purity leverage at 77 K and tolerate about ten times more cold background and up to 240 times more facet absorption than the same crystals with mode-conserving reflection. Birefringence releases trapped light on the smoothest facets, where surface absorption is lowest. Crystal symmetry, set jointly by shape and dielectric tensor, thereby becomes a design parameter for optical refrigeration toward liquid-nitrogen temperature and for uniaxial scintillators, light-emitting diodes and other facet-bounded emitters that trap light by total internal reflection.

papers.title: Optimization of Sodium-Catalyzed Si–N Bond Formation Through a Comparative Study of Group 1 Alkoxides
papers.abstract: A systematic comparison of group 1 tert-amylate (OtAmyl) salts as precatalysts for Si–N heterodehydrocoupling is reported with a focus on NatOAmyl. The heavier alkali metals provide good to excellent conversions with all substrates screened, including tertiary silanes and secondary amines, which are challenging substrates in prior literature reports. Although the activity of NatOAmyl is limited in comparison to rubidium and cesium congeners, this can be improved with judicious solvent choice, particularly DMSO. The overall findings support that a single inexpensive and sustainable catalyst can be primarily used for Si–N bond formation; however, if the substrates are particularly challenging, CstOAmyl will provide high conversion. This analysis provides a systematic approach for pragmatic catalysts to engage in bond formation with abundant silicon and nitrogen that serves synthesis and materials chemistry.

papers.title: Total Synthesis of Site-Specifically Modified bHLHLz Transcription Factors Reveals Insights into the Regulatory Role of Posttranslational Modifications in the Myc–Max–Mad Network
papers.abstract: The Myc–Max–Mad bHLHLz transcription factor (TF) network regulates the expression of ~15% of the human genome, and its dysregulation is implicated in nearly 70% of human cancers. Although its activity is primarily governed by competition for dimerization partners and occupancy of shared DNA target sequences, the molecular mechanisms controlling oligomerization and DNA binding remain elusive. Here, we employed total protein synthesis and combinatorial assembly to define how posttranslational modification (PTM) patterns regulate the Myc–Max–Mad TF network. Using native chemical ligation, we prepared a library of site-specifically modified Myc, Mnt, Mad, and phosphorylated or acetylated Max analogs. Remarkably, the isolation of homogeneous TFs enabled the combinatorial generation of all 24 heterodimeric complexes, allowing systematic analysis of dimerization and DNA-binding activity across the network. Our findings provide direct evidence that although Max phosphorylation and acetylation do not significantly affect its oligomerization with the Myc transcriptional activator, these modifications enhance its dimerization with the transcriptional repressors Mnt and Mad. Moreover, we found that Max-PTMs modulate DNA-binding activity by both specific PTM patterns and combinations, as well as the identity of the TF partner. Together, these findings demonstrate that PTM-dependent modulation of DNA-binding activity within the Myc–Max–Mad network constitutes a key regulatory layer governing gene expression.

papers.title: Alkyl-BODIPYs as a Self-Photoredox Catalyst for their Oxidative Hydroxymethylation
papers.abstract: The adoption of photocatalytic approaches for utilising small organic molecules in self‑catalysed reactions offers opportunities in green organic synthesis. We report that alkylated boron‑dipyrromethenes (BODIPYs) act as self‑photoredox catalysts for their own oxidation under mild visible‑light conditions. Using an imidazolinium salt (NHC-H) as a quencher, alkylated BODIPYs are oxidised cleanly to the corresponding hydroxymethyl derivatives in a one‑pot process. Luminescence studies, including Stern–Volmer analysis, support a reductive‑quenching pathway in which the NHC-H transfers an electron to photoexcited BODIPY to give a BODIPY radical anion. The method proceeds without external photocatalysts or stoichiometric oxidants and shows good functional‑group tolerance, highlighting the potential of these chromophores both as substrates and catalytic light absorbers. Moreover, the synthesized molecules were demonstrated to behave as effective passivating agents for layered Mn2+

papers.title: Structural Convergence of MD simulations on RNA Motifs: A tRNA case study
papers.abstract: A detailed understanding of the structural dynamics of diverse RNA architectures is critical for elucidating the chemical basis of cellular function and expanding the use of RNA in medicine and biotechnology. While classical molecular dynamics (MD) simulations can provide this much-needed atomic information, sampling requirements remain poorly characterized for RNA systems. In the present study, we compared the conformational ensemble sampled by five independent 5 μs trajectories and 60 independent 500 ns replicas for unmodified Escherichia coli tRNAPhe under three (monovalent, crystallographic-Mg2+, and 6 Mg2+) environmental conditions, yielding 165 μs of aggregate sampling. Although the global L-shaped tRNA fold was retained across all simulations, structural convergence was strongly motif-dependent. Mean base-pair and base-step descriptors of the rigid acceptor and anticodon stem-loop duplex regions were reproduced with modest replication across metal environments. In contrast, the dynamic anticodon loop exhibited substantial trajectory-to-trajectory heterogeneity. A stacking-based analysis identified diverse loop conformations with counterparts in experimentally determined tRNA structures, showing that ensembles of independent classical MD replicas can sample diverse experimentally observed conformations without enhanced sampling. While fewer long trajectories incompletely sampled the heterogeneous loop conformational space, ensembles of many shorter replicas are key to exploring the conformational dynamics of RNA motifs like hairpins. Inclusion of Mg2+ also shifted the sampled conformational ensemble, underscoring the importance of mimicking the experimentally-relevant ionic environment. Overall, our findings offer practical guidelines for MD simulation setup, including trajectory length, replica number, and divalent ion conditions, for studies of RNA systems featuring similar tertiary architectures.

papers.title: Chemically modified hydrogels to improve geothermal reservoir performance by enabling flow control via size-shifting microspheres
papers.abstract: Thermal short circuits, where fluids preferentially connect injection and production wells, are a leading cause of premature enthalpy decline in geothermal reservoirs. These pathways accelerate cooling, reduce effective heat transfer area, and limit reservoir lifetime. We propose a temperature-responsive hydrogel microsphere suspension as an “active tracer” that dynamically redirects flow away from cooled short-circuit channels while also tracing fluid flow via fluorescence spectroscopy. Highly idealized reservoir simulations with field-informed permeability distributions indicate that a yieldstress fluid with temperature-responsive behaviors may improve reservoir thermal lifetime by a factor of at least 24 to 59x while maintaining acceptable hydraulic performance. To develop a candidate “active” tracer intended to satisfy the assumptions of the idealized simulations, we synthesized poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (pNIPA) microgels, characterized their swelling and rheological behavior, and conducted a large-scale laboratory experiment in an analog parallel-plate that demonstrates short-circuited flow behavior. These lab-scale results demonstrate that injected microgels clog cooled short circuits via swelling and diverted flow into hotter regions. This proof-of-concept establishes an attractive pathway for employing engineered materials to actively manage flow and extend geothermal reservoir lifetimes.

papers.title: VISION-BASED DRY-MATERIAL INVENTORY ESTIMATION IN AUTONOMOUS LABORATORIES: RGB SEGMENTATION VERSUS RGB-D SURFACE RECONSTRUCTION
papers.abstract: Reliable dry-material inventory monitoring is needed for autonomous laboratory operation, but the suitability of a non-contact method depends on material behaviour, optical access, calibration requirements and the quantity to be estimated. We compared two vision-based approaches—material-specific RGB/YOLO level estimation and visible-surface reconstruction from an Intel RealSense D405—across three materials (black polypropylene pellets, wood powder, and microcrystalline cellulose fine powder) in small transparent laboratory tubes representative of common dosing instruments, with the aim of informing a practical, evidence-based framework for choosing between such methods in laboratory automation and similar industrial contexts. Software-coordinated records linked the two camera channels to a nominal mass-fraction inventory reference and a manual-height baseline. Across six runs and 133 paired, reference-eligible material states, D405 achieved lower error than YOLO in every run (mean absolute error of 3.26 vs. 7.14 percentage points), though YOLO offered higher valid-result coverage (97.2% vs. 95.1%). Both methods showed increased error under repeated surface disturbance, with YOLO degrading more sharply than D405. An exploratory correction fitted using the first observation at each mass level substantially improved YOLO but did not surpass D405’s uncorrected accuracy, while a single global correction worsened both methods—indicating that simple corrections do not transfer robustly across conditions. The results support a method-selection framework based on error, availability, viewing geometry, calibration-state representativeness and total resource requirements. Conclusions are limited to the tested materials and setups, and the mass-fraction reference is an operational inventory proxy rather than a direct measurement of true occupied volume.

papers.title: Predictive Model for Acid-Catalyzed SN1 Solvolysis Racemization of Chiral Alcohols in Water
papers.abstract: We have developed a predictive model for assessing the racemization risk of drug candidates featuring chiral alcohol motifs, addressing an important concern in drug discovery and development. Specifically, it predicts the activation free energy of stereoisomerization through the acid-catalyzed SN1 solvolysis mechanism based on the calculated electronic reaction energy associated with carbocation formation, the assumed rate-determining step. At the core of the framework is a linear regression model relating the calculated electronic reaction energy difference between the chiral alcohol and the carbocation intermediate to the activation free energy derived from experimental racemization kinetics. The resulting model showed a strong correlation and high statistical significance (R2=0.92, p=1.9 ∗ 10−8), reproducing the activation free energy with a root-mean-square error of 4.1 kJ/mol. Thus, the model has the potential to enable high-throughput assessment of racemization risk in drug candidates, supporting the development of safer pharmaceuticals and more efficient drug development pipelines.

papers.title: A Redox-Non-Innocent Catecholate Shifts the Oxidation State Break in the Actinides
papers.abstract: Realizing the full potential of actinide-based systems requires strategies to differentiate elements whose similar chemical properties complicate their selective use. Redox-active ligands offer a promising approach: their ability to participate in electron transfer provides a means to tune the oxidation states and electronic structures of both lanthanides and actinides. To explore this approach, we conducted a theory-guided study of (Tp*)2An(dtbsq) complexes (1-An; An = U, Np, Pu, Am, Bk; Tp* = [HB(C3N2Me2H)3]-; dtbsq•− = [C6O2 tBu2H2]-), which contain a redox-active semiquinone ligand. This study reveals a shift in the preferred actinide oxidation state from An(IV) to An(III) between the chemically similar elements Np and Pu. Such an effect is made possible due to differential stabilization of oxidation states by the ligated redox-active ligand. Structural and spectroscopic data are consistent with this trend, as exemplified by the experimentally characterized complexes 2-U ([(Tp*)(Bp*)UIV 2(dtbc)3], Bp* = [H2B(C3N2Me2H)2]-, dtbc = [C6O2 tBu2H2]2-) and 1-Pu [(Tp*)2PuIII(dtbsq)]. In these systems, the radical ligand is reduced to a catecholate only in the presence of UIII but it remains in its radical form with PuIII. Electronicstructure calculations for (Tp*)2An(dtbsq) (An = U, Np, Pu, Am, Bk) reveal tunable AnIII/IV oxidation states—supported by highly multiconfigurational ground states—and oxidation-statedependent covalency. This study advances our fundamental understanding of actinide bonding and highlights oxidation-state control as a promising strategy for tuning reactivity and selectivity across f-block chemistry.

papers.title: Bio-derived ionic conductive Guar Gum hydrogels as distributed circuit elements for analogue signal processing: the case of Resistor-Capacitor filters
papers.abstract: Developing functional electronic materials from renewable resources is a key challenge toward more sustainable electronics. Here, we report on a bio-derived ionic conductive hydrogel based on guar gum and demonstrate its direct integration as a functional circuit element for analogue signal processing. Ionic conductivity is introduced by incorporating sodium chloride into the polysaccharide matrix and systematically tuned through the glycerol and salt contents. Increasing glycerol loading enhances conductivity, while varying NaCl concentration produces a non-monotonic response, with maximum conductivities in the 10-2 S cm-1 range and an optimum salt-loading window. The conductive formulation is subsequently combined with pristine guar gum, used as a dielectric, to fabricate guar gum-based resistor-capacitor elements. Their integration into low-pass and high-pass filters demonstrates frequency-selective operation in the audio range, with cut-off frequencies of 658 and 576 Hz and transition slopes of −17 and +15 dB dec-1, respectively. These results demonstrate that guar gumbased ionic hydrogels can move beyond conventional roles as substrates or electrolytes and directly perform circuit-level functions, providing a simple materials platform for low-frequency analogue electronics.

papers.title: Process and Systems Modeling of Hydrothermal Liquefaction for Fuels and
papers.abstract: 17 Hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) can convert wet organic waste into fuels and bioproducts, but 18 variation in feedstocks and operating conditions can propagate from product yields to system 19 performance and deployment. This study linked machine learning based HTL yield prediction with 20 process simulation, techno-economic analysis (TEA), life cycle assessment (LCA), uncertainty 21 analysis, and surrogate modeling. A literature data set of 402 experiments was used to predict 22 biocrude, aqueous, gas, and solids yields, with 71.8% of predictions within ±5 wt% of experimental 23 values. The predicted yields reproduced 77.1% of internal rate of return (IRR) and 83.2% of 24 GWP100 estimates within ±5% and ±10 kg CO2e/kg, respectively, and were integrated into two 25 deployment configurations (centralized and decentralized HTL) and two product pathways 26 (biobinder/biofuel and sustainable aviation fuel [SAF]). Process and system scale analyses 27 showed that operating conditions strongly affecting HTL performance could have weaker or 28 competing economic effects due to tradeoffs among product yields, water handling, energy 29 requirements, and capital costs. Across representative feedstocks, decentralized biobinder 30 systems achieved median IRRs up to 35.8%, compared with up to 8.0% for decentralized SAF 31 systems. Feedstock price, followed by biocrude quality, and biocrude yield emerged as the 32 leading economic drivers. Monte Carlo filtering identified waste tipping fee thresholds $25.1–33 196.7 per wet metric tonne for achieving the 10% IRR target. These results show that existing 34 tipping fee structure can support HTL deployment in some cases, while higher tipping fees or 35 additional financial incentives can expand viability and enable higher investment returns. 36

papers.title: Machine Learning of Methacrylated Dextran Phase Separation for Prediction, Transferability, and Adaptation
papers.abstract: Thermoresponsive polymers are promising materials for separations, sensing, drug delivery, and other biomedical applications, but their phase behavior depends on numerous polymer and solution variables, which creates a formulation space that is impractical to explore exhaustively by experiments. Here, we develop machine-learning (ML) models for predicting the lower critical solution temperature (LCST) of methacrylated dextran (Dex-MA), a biocompatible polysaccharide-based polymer, using 403 unique experimentally measured formulations spanning polymer molecular weight, degree of methacrylation, concentration, salts, surfactants, and other additives. The dataset is nonuniformly sampled because of practical synthesis constraints and application priorities. Despite this nonuniformity, descriptor-and molecular-embedding-based XGBoost and multilayer perceptron (MLP) models achieved mean absolute errors of 3.6 o C to 3.7 o C and 5.4 o C to 5.7 o C, respectively, for within-domain LCST prediction and mean phase-behavior classification accuracies of 89.4–89.6% and 85.3–86.6%, respectively. However, strong within-domain performance did not uniformly transfer to unseen formulation domains. Systematically withholding entire polymer, surfactant, and salt domains produced domain-dependent losses in predictive accuracy; for example, withholding 86 and 250 kDa Dex-MA increased LCST prediction errors to 11.4 o C and 17.5 o C, respectively, whereas errors for held-out surfactants were 5.6–7.2 o C. Progressive incorporation of target-domain measurements recovered predictive accuracy, but the recovery rate varied substantially with additive and salt identity and polymer molecular weight. This work provides a framework not only for predicting thermoresponsive-polymer phase behavior but also for evaluating model transferability to new formulation domains and guiding experimental data collection for model adaptation.

papers.title: QMzyme: A Python Package for Automated and Systematic QM-based Enzyme Modeling
papers.abstract: We introduce QMzyme, a Python package to automate the generation of Quantum mechanics (QM)-based enzyme models. QM calculations on enzymes are computationally challenging because full enzyme systems typically contain thousands of atoms, placing accurate QM treatments beyond practical computational limits.Therefore, QM-based enzyme studies rely on identifying a subset of atoms that captures the essential chemistry of the reaction environment, enabling tractable yet chemically meaningful calculations. However, constructing these reduced models requires numerous user-defined decisions, including selection of the starting structure, identification of atoms to include in the QM region, and definition of truncation strategies for QM-only models, all of which can substantially influence the resulting calculations. QMzyme aims to provide the community with a flexible and extensible framework for automated, systematic generation of QM-based enzyme models, enabling researchers to more rigorously evaluate how model construction decisions influence computational outcomes while improving reproducibility and transparency across workflows. By facilitating high-throughput generation and analysis of QM enzyme models, QMzyme supports largescale, data-driven investigations of enzyme structure, function, and reactivity. This effort is especially crucial for the creation of large, chemically consistent datasets that can support emergent artificial intelligence and machine learning approaches for accelerated digital discovery in enzymology and biocatalysis.

papers.title: Probing Oxygen Transport in β-Cyclodextrin–Cyclohexane Crystal Nanochannels by Luminescence Quenching from Nanoseconds to Seconds
papers.abstract: Molecular transport in nanochannels can deviate from normal diffusion and exhibit different regimes depending on the observation timescale. However, resolving them from nanoseconds to seconds remains challenging. Here, oxygen transport in β -cyclodextrin–cyclohexane supramolecular crystals containing solvent-filled nanochannels is probed using room-temperature phosphorescence and fluorescence of aromatic luminophores. Their emission lifetimes, ranging from approximately 50 ns to 15 s, provide intrinsic time windows spanning more than eight orders of magnitude. Comparison of fluorescence and phosphorescence quenching for the same guests provides an internal control for probe identity. The effective bimolecular quenching rate constants decrease by approximately five orders of magnitude. Between approximately 50 ns and 10 ms, the dependence follows a power law, k q ∝ τ 0 -0.8 , followed by a nearly lifetime-independent plateau. The theory of diffusion-controlled reactions relates this dependence to the time-dependent oxygen flux and indicates subdiffusive transport at intermediate times with an effective anomalous exponent of approximately 0.4. A random-barrier model with quenched disorder provides a physical interpretation of this regime and its crossover to normal transport at long times. Thus, molecular excited states with different emission lifetimes enable luminescence quenching to resolve distinct temporal regimes of molecular transport under nanoscale confinement.

papers.title: From Static Material Design to Predictive Open-Loop Control via Chemistry–Architecture Coupling in a Moving-Boundary Reaction–Diffusion Framework

Development of A Modeling Framework for Characterizing Protein–Polymer Bioconjugates with Enhanced Sampling Molecular Dynamics Simulations
papers.abstract: Protein–polymer bioconjugates represent a class of biomaterials that leverages the molecular specificity of proteins and the tunability of synthetic polymers. Strategic conjugation of polymers to protein surfaces can enhance key biomolecular properties such as structural stability and target affinity while preserving the biological functions of the native protein. The rational design of these hybrid biomolecules demands a detailed understanding of the underlying molecular mechanisms governing protein–polymer interfacial behavior. Critically, strong interfacial interactions can impose substantial energetic barriers that hinder conformational sampling in molecular dynamics (MD) studies of this system. Enhanced sampling methods are highly effective for overcoming such limitations in the simulation of biomolecular interfaces. However, the opportunity to apply enhanced sampling methods toward navigating the complex interfacial landscapes of protein–polymer bioconjugates has yet to be realized by the field. In this study, we showcase the development of a molecular modeling framework that leverages enhanced sampling to extensively characterize protein–polymer bioconjugates. To validate this framework, we constructed two bioconjugate models of hen egg-white lysozyme grafted with activated methoxy polyethylene glycol (mPEG) chains of varying lengths at multiple surface-exposed lysine sites. We then performed all-atom MD simulations of these PEGylated constructs, augmented with well-tempered metadynamics (WTM) to fully explore their conformational landscapes under multi-site polymer conjugation. This approach yielded converged free energy surfaces (FES) characterizing the thermodynamic favorability of grafted mPEG chain conformations at each conjugation site. We also identified key protein contact residues and site-specific non-bonded interactions responsible for bioconjugate stabilization. This study demonstrates a novel application of enhanced sampling methodologies in bioconjugate systems for characterizing site-specific conjugation effects on protein–polymer interfacial energetics and structural dynamics in the context of protein surface chemistry. More broadly, applying this methodological framework across diverse polymer chemistries and protein variants can elucidate molecular design rules for engineering bioconjugates with precise properties and functions for applications spanning biotechnology, energy, and health.

papers.title: First-principles data for solid-solution Nb–Zr, Ta–Zr, and V–Zr binary alloys with body-centered-cubic structures
papers.abstract: We present three open-access datasets containing density functional theory (DFT) calculations for refractory solid-solution binary alloys niobium–zirconium (NbZr), tantalum–zirconium (TaZr), and vanadium–zirconium (VZr) in 128-atom body-centered-cubic (BCC) supercells. These datasets extend our previously published first-principles collections for NbTa, NbV, TaV, and NbTaV alloys and were generated with the same automated high-throughput workflow based on the Vienna Ab-Initio Simulation Package (VASP). For each of the three NbZr, TaZr, and VZr systems, we uniformly sample 31 chemical compositions across the full composition range in 4-atom increments. For every composition we construct 100 distinct disordered atomic configurations by randomizing the element assignments on the BCC lattice sites. All structures are fully relaxed, and the released data include complete input files, detailed VASP outputs for each relaxation stage, and derived physical quantities such as ground-state formation energy and root mean-squared displacement (RMSD) relative to an ideal BCC reference. These Zr-containing binaries are motivated by our earlier demonstration that graph neural networks (GNNs) trained on binary NbTa, NbV, and TaV data can interpolate formation enthalpies and structural descriptors in ternary NbTaV alloys while dramatically reducing the required number of ternary DFT calculations. The new NbZr, TaZr, and VZr datasets increase the diversity of available binary training data, in particular in systems with larger size mismatch and stronger lattice distortion due to Zr, and are intended to support the development of transferable machine learning (ML) interatomic models for accelerated exploration of high-dimensional multicomponent alloy spaces.

papers.title: Thioiminium Salt Catalyzed Chemoselective Late Stage Halogenation Using N-Halosuccinimides
papers.abstract: C−H halogenation plays a central role in drug discovery. It enables rapid molecular diversification and provides a direct means to tune the metabolic and biological properties of drug candidates. However, selective halogenation of less reactive arenes remains challenging, particularly when aromatic and benzylic C−H bonds coexist in the same molecule. Here, we introduce a thioiminium salt-based Lewisbase catalyst that activates readily available N-halosuccinimides for selective aromatic and benzylic halogenation with complementary control. Notably, the method enables late-stage aromatic bromination of natural products, pharmaceuticals, peptides and heterocycles and can be extended to aromatic chlorination using N-chlorosuccinimide. The practicality of this method is demonstrated by four gramscale syntheses, catalyst recycling and post-synthetic diversification. Mechanistic and computational studies reveal distinct electrophilic and radical pathways, with the catalyst counter anion acting as a molecular switch for chemoselectivity between aromatic and benzylic bromination.

papers.title: Structuring High-Entropy Oxides at the Nanoscale: Ordered Mesoporous (CrMnFeCoNi)Ox Thin Films for High-Performance Oxygen Evolution Reaction Catalysis
papers.abstract: The synthesis of high-entropy oxides (HEOs) with nanoscale architectures is challenging, since both the peculiar crystalline structure with statistical element occupancy and the desired nanomorphology must be controlled. Here, ordered mesoporous (spinel) (CrMnFeCoNi)Ox HEO thin films were prepared via soft-templating and dip-coating under tailored synthesis conditions, and the influence of calcination temperature on their structural evolution and alkaline oxygen evolution reaction (OER) performance was investigated. Electron microscopy revealed a temperature-dependent development of an ordered mesoporous architecture with 15–20 nm pores using polyisobutylene-block-poly(ethylene oxide) (PIB-b-PEO) as structure-directing agent. Energy-dispersive spectroscopy and inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy demonstrated a near-equiatomic, spatially homogeneous distribution of all transition metals at the surface and in the bulk. Transmission electron microscopy and X-ray diffraction revealed a temperature-induced transition from an amorphous to nanocrystalline cubic spinel structure at 600 °C. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy indicated a transformation from a high-valence, defective/hydroxylated surface composition rich in Cr6+, Mn3+, Co2+, and Ni2+ species at 300–400 °C to more low-valence surface states with increased lattice-oxygen contribution at 500–600 °C. The mesoporous HEO thin film annealed at 400 °C for 5 min exhibited one of the best OER performances ever reported (η10 = 273 mV at 10 mA cm−2 and Rct = 3.9 Ω at 1.5 V vs. RHE) in alkaline electrolyte. Overall, the structural evolution and OER performance of HEO thin films follow a temperature-dependent activity trend based on the balance and interplay of surface area, crystallinity, oxygen defects, and catalytically active species at the surface, highlighting the necessity of precise control of the synthesis conditions and formulation of structure-property relationships for improving the OER performance of compositionally complex catalysts.

papers.title: A Response Surface Methodology Framework for Targeted MALDI‑TIMS Optimization and in‑Tissue Metabolite Resolution
papers.abstract: Differentiating hexose‑phosphate isomers directly within tissue is essential for understanding glycolytic and pentose‑phosphate pathway activity, particularly in the kidney, where these metabolites play central roles in energy balance, redox regulation, and stress response. However, their high structural similarity and low endogenous abundance make on‑tissue discrimination analytically challenging. To address this, we systematically optimized MALDI‑TIMS‑TOF parameters using response surface methodology (RSM), developing a predictive model that revealed positive linear and negative quadratic effects of ramp time, a positive linear dependence on TIMS pressure, no significant contribution from the mobility window, and no factor interactions. Balancing analytical sensitivity and mobility resolution identified 720 ms ramp time and 2.5 mbar TIMS pressure as optimal conditions for targeted hexose‑phosphate separations. Under these optimized conditions, MALDI‑TIMS MSI of mouse kidney with lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced injury uncovered an endogenous feature with the same nominal mass as hexose phosphates but with mobility distinct from all tested standards, including glucose-6-phosphate, glucose-1-phosphate, fructose-6-phosphate and mannose-6-phosphate. This molecule showed differential localization between cortex and medulla and responded to LPS‑induced metabolic stress, revealing unanticipated biochemical heterogeneity within the hexose‑phosphate mass range. Together, these findings demonstrate that RSM‑guided TIMS optimization enhances the resolving power of mobility‑based separations and expands the discovery potential of MALDI‑TIMS MS for uncovering molecular complexity directly within biological tissues. INTRODUCTION Sugar phosphates are central intermediates that connect glycolysis, gluconeogenesis, the pentose phosphate pathway, and glycogen metabolism, thereby sustaining energy production and redox balance in mammalian tissues1. In the kidney—one of the body’s most metabolically demanding organs—hexose phosphates play essential roles in proximal tubular glucose handling and phosphate‑dependent metabolic regulation2. Among these metabolites, glucose‑6‑phosphate (Glc6P) links glycolysis to NADPH‑producing pathways important for maintaining tubular antioxidant defense3, fructose‑6‑phosphate (Fru6P) modulates carbohydrate flux in renal epithelial cells2, and glucose‑1‑phosphate (Glc1P) contributes to glycogen turnover and metabolic buffering during renal stress4, 5. Perturbations in these tightly regulated metabolites accompany inflammation and acute kidney injury1, 6, 7, underscoring the need for analytical strategies that can distinguish sugar‑phosphate isomers directly in tissue. Differentiating sugar‑phosphate isomers remains analytically challenging because their high polarity and minimal structural differences limit the resolving power of conventional approaches. Chromatographic strategies—including hydrophilic interaction liquid chromatography (HILIC),

papers.title: Active synthesizability prediction for a virtual space of 395 million catalyst candidates with small data
papers.abstract: N-heterocyclic carbenes (NHCs) are well established as catalysts and ligands in many chemical transformations. Recently, interest has grown in pyridine[1,5]imidazolium salt pre-catalysts, stable precursors to NHCs, because they are relatively easy to synthesize and highly adaptable. This work introduces a data-driven workflow to identify which pyridine[1,5]imidazolium salts are readily synthetically accessible, starting from exploratory synthesis attempts for 127 compounds. Our approach relies on a feedback loop with a supervised machine learning model to estimate and dynamically update the synthesizability for a combinatorial space of about 394 million pre-catalysts derived from commercially available precursors. Our final model estimates that 4.78% of the entire space are feasible, mapping the space of readily accessible candidates and providing a valuable set for future inverse design studies. We validated the prediction performance of our approach based on both literature data and a holdout set occupying extremes of the combinatorial space.

papers.title: How does spatio-temporal optimisation affect the siting and operation of direct air capture systems?
papers.abstract: The climate crisis is driving the urgent development of negative emission technologies, such as adsorption-based direct air capture (DAC). Although DAC holds promise, it remains costly and requires further technological innovation, design optimisation, and supply chain development to scale effectively and achieve meaningful climate impact. DAC performance is influenced by both local ambient (e.g., temperature, humidity) and energy conditions (e.g., upstream emissions, costs). Previous studies have typically evaluated DAC systems under constant ambient and energy conditions, used static models that do not provide temporally resolved results, or restricted their analysis to limited case studies. These restrictions may lead to an incomplete assessment of DAC performance and suboptimal decision-making. This study presents the dynamic DAC + energy supply (DACES) optimisation framework, which explicitly accounts for spatial and temporal variations in ambient and energy conditions, and demonstrates its application to the province of Alberta, Canada using highresolution data from 2024. The DACES model can address two essential questions without reverting to static modelling or time-averaged input assumptions: (i) which locations are better suited for DAC deployment than others and (ii) how DAC should be operated. Coupled with a genetic algorithm that minimises net carbon capture costs, the DACES model answers these questions while maintaining computational tractability. The results demonstrate that spatio-temporal optimisation—through the selection of more favourable DAC locations combined with adaptive cycle designs—reduces estimated costs by up to 20 %. Specifically, the use of dynamic conditions in the decision-making process favours the positioning of DAC systems in northern Alberta, whereas constant conditions would have placed them several hundred kilometres further south. An analysis of 32 external conditions across different stages of the cycle identified ambient temperature at the start of adsorption, relative humidity at the end of adsorption, and upstream emissions and costs at the start of desorption as the parameters most influential to cycle performance. Results further show that, for optimal cycle designs, the system should (i) align cycle design with the minima of these parameters at their respective stages, since they determine the extent of pre-desorption conditions and the associated costs of net removal during desorption; and (ii) introduce strategically timed waiting periods between DAC phases to align operation with external conditions, trading DAC productivity for reduced regeneration energy. Overall, the findings highlight that accounting for spatio-temporal variability and optimising cycle design at the individual-cycle level can considerably enhance DAC performance and reduce operational costs.

papers.title: VIBE-VIEW and QVF: portable visualization and checksummed archives for quantum chemistry
papers.abstract: Quantum-chemistry results often span separate files for structures, orbitals, scalar fields, and spectra. We present VIBE-VIEW, a viewer for molecular and periodic calculations, and QVF (Quantum Visualization Format), its producer-neutral archive format. QVF combines visualization data with provenance, citations, and optional job specifications and run records in one ZIP file. A JSON manifest declares payload formats and SHA-256 checksums, with dtypes and shapes for numeric arrays. Consumers verify payload integrity before use and explicitly report unsupported extensions. A published schema, extension registry, and twelve-archive conformance corpus support independent implementations. VIBE-VIEW provides renderers or panels for 41 of 42 canonical kinds, with bonds incorporated into structure rendering. Browser, desktop, terminal, headless, notebook, and Python interfaces support inspection and figure generation from the same archive, without requiring installation of the original producer. A water calculation demonstrates the workflow. VIBE-VIEW is licensed under MPL-2.0; the QVF specification and reference writer toolkit use Apache-2.0. Graphical TOC summary. QVF combines molecular and crystal structures, orbitals, spectra, and calculation provenance in one checksummed file. The VIBE-VIEW application opens these archives through interactive and scripted interfaces, supporting inspection and figure generation without installing the original calculation program.

papers.title: Solid-state NMR and first-principle calculations reveal the structure and dynamics of Li-N-H materials
papers.abstract: Lithium-nitrogen-hydrogen (Li-N-H) materials are promising for hydrogen storage, solid-state batteries, and lithium-mediated ammonia synthesis, yet their local structures and proton dynamics remain poorly understood because of compositional disorder and limited sensitivity of conventional diffraction methods. Here, we combine multinuclear solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy (1H, 7Li, 14N, and 15N ssNMR) with first-principles calculations to resolve the atomic environments and dynamics of Li3N, LiNH2, and Li1+xNH2-x (. 7Li NMR and density functional theory calculations identify distinct lithium sites in coexisting α- and β-Li3N phases and in tetragonal LiNH2. 1H and 15N NMR, together with 1H-detected 14N spectroscopy, reveal two distinct domains in synthesized lithium-rich Li1+xNH2-x that are not resolved by laboratory X-ray diffraction. Comparison with calculated NMR parameters assigns these domains to LiNH2 and Li2NH, respectively. Variable-temperature 1H-1H exchange spectroscopy shows that correlations between the two domains arise predominantly from spin diffusion rather than interdomain proton exchange, indicating nanoscale structural heterogeneity within a solid solution. Local proton motion occurs within the Li2NH environment and is restricted in the LiNH­2 domains. These results establish a molecular-level relationship between local structure and proton mobility in Li-N-H materials, providing insights relevant to hydrogen storage, solid-state batteries, and ammonia synthesis.

papers.title: TRMC and NEXAFS Reveal Fast Electron Transfer to Ce3+/Oxygen-Vacancy Traps in Non-Covalent CexOy/C3N4 Interface for Photocatalytic H2
papers.abstract: Earth-abundant photocatalysts for solar H₂ struggle to absorb deep visible light and separate charges at the same time. Here we show that a small amount of reduced ceria on carbon nitride achieves both. Non covalent CexOy/C3N4 heterostructures with 4% and 7% cerium oxide were compared with CeO2 and C3N4 references for H₂ evolution at 410 and 465 nm. The key turns out to be not how much ceria is added, but in which state and how well it is spread. At 4%, ceria forms finely dispersed, oxygen-deficient nanoparticles rich in Ce3+/oxygen-vacancy (Ov) defects, as revealed by Ce M4,5- and O K-edge NEXAFS and supported by XPS, which shows reduced cerium, no fluorite lattice oxygen and the highest surface exposure of Ce. At 7%, the particles agglomerate. These defects extend light absorption into the visible range and act as electron traps: time-resolved microwave conductivity and photoluminescence reveal faster, productive electron transfer from C3N4 to ceria at 4%. As a result, the 4% composite delivers ~682 µmol g-1 h -1 (AQY ~0.57% at 410 nm), outperforming all other samples at both wavelengths. With a surface area similar to C3N4, the gain is electronic and defect-driven, not textural.

papers.title: High-Spin Diradical-Dominated Chemiluminescence
papers.abstract: We report a quantum-chemical investigation into the chemiluminescence mechanism of cyclometalated Ir (III) Schiff base complexes, promising chemiluminophores for biological imaging. The reaction proceeds via ring-opening of a key oxaziridine intermediate to yield a singlet diradical, which undergoes rapid intersystem crossing (ISC) to its triplet counterpart, followed by deprotonation to generate the emissive triplet product. Within this process, the Ir (III) center not only activates the imine via Lewis-acid coordination but also reverses the singlet-triplet energy ordering of the diradical intermediate, rendering the triplet diradical thermodynamically favored with an equilibrium population of ca. 86% at ambient temperature. The heavy-atom effect of iridium provides substantial spin-orbit coupling; combined with a low-lying minimum-energy crossing point (MECP, 1.7 kcal mol -1 ) and large Franck-Condon-weighted density of states, this accelerates ISC to a rate of 1.5 × 1011 s -1 . Notably, the two radical centers are separated by an 𝑠𝑝3-hybridized carbon, and the intervening C-H bond is strongly polarized by the adjacent O-centered radical, rendering deprotonation nearly barrierless. These collective computational findings establish design principles for two distinct goals: stabilizing diradical species to extend their lifetimes for EPR characterization, and informing the rational development of non-precious-metal chemiluminescent systems.

papers.title: Tension-Limited Leaflet-Asymmetry Budding Predicts the Size and Rate of Tumour Ectosome Shedding
papers.abstract: In fatty-acid protocells, growth by outer-leaflet monomer uptake generates a transbilayer area imbalance that is relieved by shedding nano-vesicles once the reduced imbalance ∆a exceeds a critical value ∆ac = O(1), as described by area-difference elasticity (ADE). It is tempting to read modern tumour ectosome shedding as the same physics. We show that the naive transfer fails, and derive the version that does not. A protocell is tensionless; the plasma membrane of a cancer cell is not, and its apparent tension (σ ∼ 10−5–10−4 N m−1) imposes an area cost that is absent from the protocell treatment. Replacing the shape-instability criterion with an explicit energy balance for bud formation, we obtain a budding threshold in the differential leaflet tension, ∆τc = √ 8κσ/h, and a parameter-free bud radius at threshold, r∗ = √ 2κ/σ,

papers.title: Fundamental Limitations of Cu(II)-based Oxides for Photoelectrochemical Nitrogen Reduction
papers.abstract: The photoelectrochemical (PEC) nitrogen reduction reaction (N 2 RR) offers a potentially sustainable route to ammonia (NH 3 ) synthesis. However, reliable evaluation of PEC N 2 RR activity remains challenging due to contamination-induced false positives and competing reactions. Here, we comparatively investigate p -type CuBi 2 O 4 and the previously reported PEC N 2 RR-active photocathode CuO, using an ultra-clean, contamination-controlled measurement system. Despite favorable band energetics and measurable photocurrents, neither material exhibits statistically significant NH 3 production, suggesting that the previously reported activity of CuO most likely originated from contamination-induced false positives rather than genuine N 2 reduction. Density functional theory further shows that the first proton-coupled electron transfer step toward *NNH formation remains kinetically prohibitive, even on oxygen-deficient surfaces, strongly favoring the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). In addition, both photocathodes undergo surface reduction and photocorrosion. Nevertheless, comparative analysis reveals fundamentally different degradation pathways on the two photocathodes. While CuBi 2 O 4 retains its bulk structural integrity under photocathodic conditions, CuO undergoes extensive reduction, restructuring, and dissolution. Together, these findings highlight the importance of contamination control in evaluating aqueous PEC N 2 RR, as well as the challenges of overcoming vigorous competition with HER and photocorrosion processes using Cu(II)-based oxides.

papers.title: Autonomous Robotic Workflow for Solution-Based Synthesis and High-Temperature Thermal Processing toward Self-Driving Laboratories
papers.abstract: The growing need has pushed the development of autonomous laboratory automation for high-throughput materials research. Although self-driving laboratories (SDL) and automated liquid handling have advanced significantly, robotic material handling remains poorly integrated with high-temperature thermal processes. In this study, a solution-based synthesis autonomous robotic process was designed, developed, calibrated, and validated. Two cooperative robotic arms, a bespoke pneumatic pipetting end-effector, an RS485-controlled syringe pump, a modular crucible assembly, and automated furnace control were all integrated into the developed platform via a centralised Python-based architecture that uses Modbus TCP and RTU communication. The system handles liquid dispensing, sample mixing, robotic transfer, furnace loading, thermal treatment, controlled cooling, and sample retrieval on an independent basis. Deionised (DI) water, ethanol, and zirconium (Zr) acetate solution were used to calibrate the dispensing system to assess performance across liquids with various physical characteristics. With dispensing accuracy of 98.4%, all liquids showed excellent linearity between scheduled and dispensed quantities. After fluid-specific calibration, an error propagation study showed strong mechanical repeatability and predictable systematic error buildup, validating the system's capability for dependable automated precursor production. The independent synthesis of gadolinium zirconate (Gd2Zr2O7), a highly sought-after thermal barrier coating (TBC) composition for the next generation of aero gas turbines, was used to test the entire operation. The robotic platform effectively completed precursor dispensing, solution homogenisation, furnace processing at 1600 °C, controlled cooling, and sample recovery.

papers.title: Reversible Ion Transport Through an Irreversibly Percolating Li <sub>2</sub> S Interphase at the Li/Li <sub>6</sub> PS <sub>5</sub> Cl Interface
papers.abstract: Interfacial resistance growth between Li metal and sulfide solid electrolytes is a leading cause of failure in solid-state batteries, yet the atomic-scale processes that govern this growth under an electrochemical driving force are poorly resolved. Herein, we combine a fine-tuned machine-learning interatomic potential with dynamically updated atomic charges to simulate the Li/Li 6 PS 5 Cl interface for nanoseconds under both field-free and electric-field-driven conditions. Without a field, the electrolyte decomposes spontaneously into a Li 2 S-rich interphase whose thickness follows square-root-of-time kinetics, consistent with diffusion-limited growth. Applying a field to the same initial interface accelerates this growth nearly seven-fold and converts the entire electrolyte slab within ∼100 ps. In both cases, the Li 2 S-like product forms a single connected network, while Li 3 P-and LiCl-like decomposition products remain confined to small, disconnected clusters. Although reversing the field reverses the direction of Li flux almost immediately, the percolating Li 2 S network persists unchanged and the argyrodite coordination does not recover. This decoupling shows that structural memory, not instantaneous transport direction, determines the interphase that Li ions actually cross. Because this connectivity survives stripping, our results suggest that anode-interface resistance and reactivity in solid-state batteries are set early in cycling and are not reset by current reversal.

papers.title: Adaptation of a retrosynthetic tool to project-specific chemistry: oligomer synthesis case study
