This work highlights the potential of MAHG crystals for the rapid detection of DHB via colorimetric changes and their separation in water, offering a promising approach for industrial applications dedicated to hydroquinone and catechol production.

papers.title: Kinetically Synchronized Aqueous Co-precipitation and Hydrothermal Crystallisation of (Mg1−xCox)CO3 Rhombohedral Solid-Solution Nanoparticles: Thermodynamic Feasibility, Ethylene Glycol Kinetic Control, and Prospective Functional Applications
papers.abstract: Cobaltoan magnesite, (Mg1−xCox)CO3 (R3c; x = 0–1), has previously been accessible only under extreme solid-state conditions (≥600 °C, ≥15 kbar; Goldsmith & Northrop, 1965) or over geological timescales in supergene ore environments (Barton et al., 2014). We report the first deliberate laboratory synthesis of phase-pure (Mg,Co)CO3 solid-solution nanoparticles at 250 °C under autogenous pressure (~40 bar) via a modified polyol-assisted aqueous coprecipitation route. Thermodynamic feasibility is established through saturation-index analysis (SI(CoCO3) = +10.6, ΔG° = −60.5 kJ mol−1; SI(MgCO3) = +2.6, ΔG° = −14.8 kJ mol−1), confirming that both carbonate end-members are thermodynamically driven to precipitate from solution at ambient conditions and that the hydrothermal step supplies kinetic — not thermodynamic — activation energy. The principal kinetic challenge, the seven-order-ofmagnitude disparity in solubility products (Ksp(CoCO3) = 10−13 vs. 6.8×10−6 for MgCO3), is surmounted by ethylene glycol (EG) coordination of Co2+, confirmed in situ by a spontaneous pink→blue colour transition upon EG addition, which elevates the desolvation activation barrier and synchronises Co2+ and Mg2+ precipitation rates. Convergent evidence from five independent characterisation techniques confirms the R3c solid-solution product: (i) PXRD with Vegard's Law analysis of the composition-sensitive (113) reflection yields x(Co) ≈ 0.73 (Sample 3, pre-hydrothermal) and x(Co) ≈ 0.44 (Sample 4, post-hydrothermal); (ii) FTIR reveals a single ν2(CO32−) band at 870 cm−1, intermediate between MgCO3 (880) and CoCO3 (860 cm−1) endmembers — a necessary and sufficient criterion for isomorphic solid-solution identification by infrared spectroscopy; (iii) SEM-EDX shows a continuous unimodal composition distribution (x(Co) = 0.27–0.73) with no bimodal clustering indicative of phase separation; (iv) UV–Vis spectroscopy identifies characteristic Co2+ ligand-field and charge-transfer transitions with a direct optical band gap of ~3.1–3.4 eV; (v) DLS confirms near-monodisperse product (PDI = 0.053, Dh = 306 nm) following hydrothermal treatment, representing an 83% reduction in polydispersity relative to the amorphous precursor (PDI = 0.314). Prospective applications spanning heterogeneous catalysis, Li-ion battery cathode precursors, CO2 mineralisation, photocatalysis, and pH-responsive drug delivery are evaluated on the basis of the crystal chemistry and mixed-metal composition of the product phase.

papers.title: High-Throughput Compositional Tuning of Thin-Film (La,Ca)MnO <sub>3</sub> Perovskites as Bifunctional Oxygen Catalysts
papers.abstract: Systematic investigations of composition-dependent performance in thin-film material libraries help to understand how descriptors influence performance and enable materials optimization. The fundamental challenges of such studies are the discrete synthesis of multiple compositions within one material family and the subsequent characterization steps, which are time-consuming and limit experimental throughput. In this work, the A-site-substituted thin-film (La,Ca)MnO 3 (LCMO) material family is studied for oxygen electrocatalysis performance. Discrete synthesis is circumvented by a combinatorial pulsed laser deposition approach, enabling the synthesis of the full material family within a single deposition. High-throughput characterization methods, including X-ray diffraction, spectroscopic ellipsometry, and Raman spectroscopy, allow assessment of structural, optical, and vibrational properties. Electrocatalytic performance, including oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) activity and stability in terms of dissolution, is probed using a scanning flow cell coupled with inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (SFC-ICP-MS). Principal component analysis (PCA) is used to identify correlations between structural, optical, and vibrational descriptors and electrochemical performance. The analysis reveals distinct composition-property-performance relationships, demonstrating that the A-site composition of LCMO governs activity. This work establishes a workflow that combines combinatorial synthesis, physicochemical and functional characterization, and multivariate data analysis to identify performance-relevant descriptors in oxide electrocatalysts.

papers.title: From Retrosynthetic Prediction to the Bench: Experimental Evaluation of Computer-Generated Synthetic Routes
papers.abstract: Retrosynthesis tools propose bond disconnections and precursor assignments, but the chemist must still evaluate these choices and select reaction conditions and purification before a route can be run. In this work, we examine 53 PostEra Manifold and AiZynthFinder proposals for three small organic targets by combining chemist assessments with selected synthesis outcomes. Proposals were rejected or deprioritised for different reasons: incorrect connectivity, unsupported transformations, or extra steps and costly precursors in routes that would otherwise work. For a methoxy-substituted biaryl ketone, a Suzuki–Miyaura coupling using the chemist-preferred assignment of coupling partners gave 94% isolated yield. For a naphthylphenol, coupling with 2hydroxyphenylboronic acid gave 92% isolated yield with an aryl bromide and 7% with the corresponding chloride under the same procedure. The chloride result supports the chemist’s preference for the bromide, whereas the 92% yield shows that the earlier concern about this boronic acid, based on its behaviour in water, was not limiting under the tested conditions. We therefore propose that each generated route be judged on four separate points: whether it gives the correct target, whether the transformation is chemically supported, whether the route is practical, and whether it has been tested experimentally.

papers.title: Electron Paramagnetic Resonance on a Tip Reveals Thickness-Dependent Spin Heterogeneity in Two-
papers.abstract: Direct characterization of the spin centers that provide the magnetic states of low-dimensional magnetic materials is key to understand whether the magnetic properties arise from defects, interfaces, or surface-specific coordination environments, and how they can thus be employed in devices. The spectroscopic technique par excellence for this purpose is electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) which has seen recent expansion to single spins but remains challenging for nanostructures on insulating surfaces. Here, we overcome this limitation and demonstrate local spin-resonance spectroscopy of nanoscale systems on insulators. We achieve this by combining EPR detection with scanning microwave microscopy (SMM) at X-band frequencies of ≈9.3 GHz, with resonant spin absorptions identified as local field-dependent microwave losses, available by mapping the complex admittance under a swept magnetic field. We demonstrate the potential of the technique on single flakes of the two-dimensional Fe–Ni Hofmann clathrate. The new technique reveals a thickness-dependent evolution from bulk-like toward low-dimensional spinresonance behavior, allowing the investigation of flakes from ≈5-15 nm to >100–200 nm thick, in conditions inaccessible to other surface EPR methods. The observed thickness-dependent response is consistent with increasing contributions from surface, interface, and undercoordinated Fe environments. These new developments allow a unique route to probe dimensional effects in magnetism, make surface effects and defects accessible in insulators, and open the possibility of directly observing EPR not just on atoms and molecules, but on single electronic nanodevices, such as Single Electron Transistors and quantum dots.

papers.title: Redox-mediated water electrolysis for on-demand hydrogen production and low-grade heat harvesting
papers.abstract: Hydrogen is widely regarded as a key energy carrier for a sustainable, decarbonized economy; however, conventional and decoupled water electrolysis remain highly electricity-intensive because of the thermodynamic water-splitting voltage and sluggish reaction kinetics. Here, we report a thermally regenerative electrochemical cycle (TREC)-based decoupled water electrolysis strategy that incorporates low-grade waste heat to enable hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) at cathodic potentials more positive than 0 V versus RHE (after IR correction). We establish a theoretical framework for integrating TREC into water splitting. By leveraging the negative temperature coefficient of the Fe(TiPA) complex, this TREC-base HER process delivers an absolute electricity savings of 7.9% compared to conventional alkaline HER. Operating alongside a highly stable ferrocyanide/ferricyanide anolyte, the flow system exhibits near-97% Faradaic efficiency and exceptional structural reversibility over prolonged cycles. Combined with the temporal flexibility to exploit off-peak electricity arbitrage, our design achieves a 33.1% reduction in overall hydrogen production costs, establishing a commercially viable and scalable paradigm for energy-efficient green hydrogen generation.

papers.title: Engineering Fe-based OER electrocatalyst stability through alloy-driven modulation of Fe-O bond covalency and hydroxyl coverage
papers.abstract: Fe-based oxyhydroxides are earth-abundant alternatives to costly Ir and Ru catalyst for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), but their stability in alkaline electrolyte limits their applicability at scale. We show that alloying FeOOH with 4+ ions (My = Se, Sn, Ti, Hf) controls dissolution through the electronegatiity of the alloyed element. In 1 M KOH at 10 mA cm-2, all four alloys exhibited slower steady-state (8–48 h) Fe dissolution rates relative to pure FeOOH; and corresponding first-order rate constants fit to transient mass loss data (enabled by XRF) decrease as My becomes less electronegative. FeTiOOH (of particular note for its affordability relative to Ru and even Ni) dissolves about eight times more slowly than FeOOH; with the steady state rate of Fe mass loss suggesting an electrode half-life of about one month. The particular stability of more electropositive alloys (FeTiOOH and FeHfOOH) is achieved following a transient of about 8 h in which labile sites are stripped away (preferentially dissolved); and this restructuring manifests as an increase in the apparent charge transfer resistance and a decrease in the electrochemically active surface area as the electrode approaches steady state. As a result, more stable FeTiOOH and FeHfOOH anodes exhibit reduced OER activity relative to FeOOH (overpotentials 556, 412 and 370 mV). Nonetheless, these findings identify electropositive alloying as a route to stabilize earth-abundant Fe anodes for the oxygen evolution reaction. In a forthcoming publication, we will employ liquid-phase XPS to demonstrate that the alloy-modulated rates of Fe dissolution are mediated through two coupled effects: the oxidation state and hydroxyl coverage of the surface, and the electron density on lattice oxygens.

papers.title: Cooling-induced liquid–liquid separation promotes monazite precipitation through segregation of rare earth elements
papers.abstract: Monazite, (Ce,La,Nd)PO4, is a major source of rare earth elements (REEs), which play a vital role in green technology and electronics industries. Investigation into mechanisms of monazite formation from silicic melts provide valuable insights into its stability and behavior at varying temperature. This knowledge is crucial for improving the efficiency of REE extraction from mine slags, which could potentially contribute to expanding demand for critical materials. The present study leverages high-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy to characterize the behavior of monazite during slag cooling and the PARROT module available in Thermo-Calc software to predict thermodynamic conditions that control monazite crystallization within the system SiO2‒P2O5‒Ce2O3. Using an objective optimization technique that incorporates experimental data from various sources, the study provides a representation of phase equilibria. The mechanisms of monazite formation are examined, with CePO4 identified as a stable phase at specific compositions and temperature ranges. A relative enrichment in REE and P is, however, insufficient to ensure monazite crystallization. Local composition, degree of supersaturation, nucleation barriers, and cooling rate also impact on whether a chemically segregated domain crystallizes or becomes kinetically arrested as glass. Although seamless extrapolation of the three component binary systems to the SiO2‒Ce2O3‒P2O5 ternary is currently precluded by a lack of reliable experimental data or ab-initio computational constraints, this optimization work enhances understanding of phase behavior, with relevance for potential REE recovery from copper slags, a largely untapped source of critical materials.

papers.title: First principles study of stability, electronic and optical properties of Diphenylhexatriene under pressure
Electronic and Steric Effects on the Photoswitching and Thermal Relaxation of Ortho-Substituted Pyrazole Azo Phthalimides
papers.abstract: A series of ortho-substituted phthalimide–azopyrazole photoswitches bearing CH3, CF3, tert-Bu, and Ph groups was developed to determine how local steric and electronic perturbations control photochemical addressability and thermal Z→E relaxation. The substituents strongly altered the preferred irradiation wavelength while producing modest differences in the attainable Z-rich photostationary states. The CF3 derivative underwent E→Z photoisomerization at 530 nm, whereas the other derivatives were switched at 370 nm. TD-DFT analysis attributes this spectral differentiation to orbital reordering, configuration mixing, and redistribution of oscillator strength within the low-energy excited-state manifold. Thermal Z→E half-lives span more than three orders of magnitude, from 112 s for the CH3 derivative to 73 h for the CF3 derivative. Eyring analysis reveals predominantly entropic differentiation among the CH3, tert-Bu, and Ph derivatives, whereas CF3 persistence is primarily enthalpic. Adiabatic S0 calculations reproduce the experimental stability order but do not account for the substantially negative experimental activation entropies. Relaxed T1 scans and optimized S0/T1 crossing points identify accessible twisted crossing regions. The combined results support a multidimensional relaxation landscape in which CNNC torsion, azo-nitrogen bending, and changes in N=N bond character constitute coupled coordinates whose energetic and configurational accessibility is reshaped by ortho substitution.

papers.title: Stepwise reduction of a porphyrin nanowire: minimal structural reorganization up to the open-shell tetraanion
papers.abstract: π-Conjugated porphyrin oligomers serve as molecular wires: they exhibit high single-molecule conductance and excellent cycling kinetics as organic active electrode materials. These applications require systems in which charge/discharge cycles cause minimal changes in molecular geometry. Here, we use a butadiyne-linked porphyrin dimer as a model compound to show that its chemical reduction with alkali metals leads to subtle changes in the bond lengths in the resulting multiply charged anions, as revealed crystallographically. The small structural changes are consistent with a low inner-sphere reorganization energy, as expected for an efficient redox-active molecular wire. π-Bond Delocalization Function (π-BDF) analysis shows that successive reduction increases π-electron delocalization within the porphyrin cores, while the involvement of the butadiyne linker is strongly charge- and spin-state-dependent. The previously unknown, structurally characterized tetraanion has an open-shell singlet diradical ground state with a thermally accessible triplet state, separated by 14.2 kJ mol −1 , as established experimentally by EPR spectroscopy and supported by DFT calculations. The two open-shell states retain nearly identical covalent-delocalization topologies and differ primarily in the organization and coupling of their two unpaired electrons. Prolonged reaction with lithium metal leads to demetallation of these zinc porphyrins and cleavage of the butadiyne, forming an acetylene-appended porphyrin monomer.

papers.title: Analysis of the pH-Dependent Phase Behavior of Amorphous Solid Dispersions Using in situ Stimulated Raman Scattering Microscopy
papers.abstract: In this study, in situ stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy was employed as a novel analytical method to investigate the pH-dependent phase behavior of amorphous solid dispersions (ASDs) during hydration. Ibuprofen–poly(1-vinylpyrrolidone-co-vinyl acetate) (IBU-PVPVA) ASDS were used as model systems. The ASDs underwent multiple structural changes including polymer swelling, gel-layer formation and phase separation. To monitor these processes, binary IBU-PVPVA ASDs with six drug loadings were studied under four pH conditions using in situ hyperspectral stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy with spectral focusing, further augmented with correlative confocal reflection imaging. Spectral imaging data analysis was performed with classical least squares, preceded by multivariate curve resolution-alternating least squares estimation. Supportive solid-state analysis was performed using modulated temperature differential scanning calorimetry, polarized light microscopy, thermogravimetric analysis, and spontaneous Raman spectroscopy combined with principal component analysis. The results show that in situ SRS microscopy enables detailed real-time visualization of pH-dependent structural evolution in ASDs during hydration. The phase behavior was found to be affected by the environmental pH and buffering conditions, expected to ultimately determine drug release performance.

papers.title: The Problem of NMR Data Analysis in Synthetic Chemistry: Why Is It Important to Understand Spectra?
papers.abstract: High-resolution NMR (nuclear magnetic resonance) is one of the key methods for establishing the structures of organic compounds. Modern instrumentation and reference data provide a sufficient range of experiments for unambiguous assignment. However, in practice these resources are applied selectively. An assignment is commonly treated as complete once it no longer contradicts the expected structure. It is complete only when the spectrum as a whole has been explained, including signals at odds with that structure. The discussion is built on six papers retracted between 2020 and 2025, in which the reported structure was incorrect and the original assignment rested on NMR data. These cases are not used to estimate how often such errors occur, but to illustrate types of error that keep recurring in the literature. The same errors are then shown in a paper where the structure is correct and firmly supported by orthogonal methods. Two criteria are proposed for assessing a reported spectrum without access to the raw data. The first is the resolution indicated by the multiplet of the residual solvent signal. Therefore, this multiplet should remain visible in spectra reproduced in the Supporting Information. The second is the internal consistency of the reported data. The stated multiplicity must match the number of coupling constants. The notation must also make sense for the structure: simple descriptions such as “d” or “t” are not valid, for example, for the signals of a monosubstituted or unsymmetrically 1,4-disubstituted benzene ring. Automated approaches inherit rather than remove this difficulty: their output is accepted with the same confidence.

papers.title: Lighten Learners’ Cognitive Load or Create Conceptual Understanding: Looking Beyond Le Chatelier’s Principle.
papers.abstract: Here we explore a novel approach to teaching the effect of temperature on exothermic and endothermic reactions. We contend that Le Chatelier’s Principle is best used as a predictive tool. Insights from teacher practice, personal experience and action research are shared. This narrative is a reflective professional journey supported by empirical evidence from action research (n = 17). The insights gained offer strategies to build conceptual understanding by applying Johnstone’s Triangle to reactions like the Haber process. We discuss an approach to making connections among the reaction profile, the overall equation and the Boltzmann distribution curve.

papers.title: A New Route to Macrobicyclic Dibridgehead Diphopsphines P((CH <sub>2</sub> ) <sub>n</sub> ) <sub>3</sub> P; Reductive Demetalation of Cage-Like Fe(CO) <sub>3</sub> Adducts
papers.abstract: When THF solutions of cage-like trans-Fe(CO) 3 (P((CH 2 ) n ) 3 P) ( 1 , n = a /10, b /12, c /14, d /16, e /18) are exposed to a potassium mirror, reduction occurs to give ferrate salts of the formula 2K + [(R 3 P)(CO) 3 Fe] 2– , as supported by IR data. Following additions of excess CO and methanol, the dibridgehead diphosphines P((CH 2 ) n ) 3 P ( 1a-e ) are isolated as white solids in 61-98% yields (average 80%) as mixtures of in/in and out/out isomers that interconvert by homeomorphic isomerization. This protocol represents an alternative to a photochemical demetalation that requires PMe 3 , as well as oxidative recipes that give dibridgehead diphosphine dioxides 1a-e ·2O with byproducts that are difficult to remove. The practicality of the new route is demonstrated by a half gram-scale synthesis of 1b .

papers.title: Structural and Electrochemical Evaluations of Li4Ti5O12 Composite Anodes with an Organic Ionic Plastic Crystal Solid Electrolyte
papers.abstract: Li 4 Ti 5 O 12 (LTO) is a commercialized anode active material for battery applications. Using LTO in solid-state batteries (SSBs) is expected to overcome some issues associated with anode active materials working at a low electrode potential, such as graphite and Si. Li+-containing organic ionic plastic crystals (OIPCs) reportedly have issues with these materials, including low Coulombic efficiency and achievable capacity relative to the theoretical value. This study explored the LTO−OIPC composite anode and evaluated its surface structure and electrochemical performance. It was found that the OIPC electrolyte (with carbon black) connects LTO secondary particles to facilitate ion/electron conduction. Although the capacity of the composite anode increased gradually up to ca. 15 cycles, it was close to the theoretical value (175 mAh/g) after stabilization. While applying a vacuum-drying temperature that is higher than the melting point of the Li+-containing OIPC (>140 °C) to the composite anode adversely affected initial battery performance, it provided multiple benefits thereafter, including more efficient charge transfer and higher discharge capacity than the one vacuum-dried at 50 °C. The best-performing cell contained the 150-°C-dried one, cycled at 1C for 400 cycles. The results provide insights into further development of OIPC-containing electrodes for SSBs.

papers.title: Improved electrostatic machine learning embedding ML/MM scheme for a phosphoryl transfer reaction
papers.abstract: The promise of hybrid machine learning/molecular mechanics (ML/MM) simulations is to provide QM/MM-quality free energy profiles at a fraction of the cost. One of the challenges is to accurately treat the interaction between the ML subsystem and the MM environment. Here we test the Electrostatic ML Embedding (EMLE) scheme on a minimal model of RNA cleavage in water, which is already challenging due to a doubly charged reactant dissociating into two anions. The original scheme, a MACE potential embedded by an independent EMLE model, is compared with a new EMLE–MACE architecture, in which a single equivariant network predicts the gas-phase energy together with the atomic charges, valence widths, polarizabilities and static dipoles required by the embedding. The models were trained by active learning against M06-2X/def2- TZVP data, with structures selected by query-by-committee from the ML/MM dynamics itself. About 1500 single point calculations were sufficient for stable 100 ps umbrella sampling simulations in 73 windows along the reaction pathway. The EMLE–MACE profile reproduces the reference DFT/MM profile within its sampling error, including a metastable pentacoordinate intermediate. Energy decomposition shows that the static dipoles are essential: without them the static error stays above chemical accuracy even for an ideally trained model, due to the irreducible error of approximating electron density with spherical atoms.

papers.title: Two-Electron Photoreduction of Pd(II) Oxalates: In Crystallo Synthesis and Catalysis
papers.abstract: Discovery and optimization of cross-coupling catalysts require catalyst activation strategies that balance the operational simplicity of air-stable precatalysts with the need for air-sensitive, lowcoordinate and -valent intermediates for substrate activation and turnover. Here we introduce a general approach for on-demand catalyst activation via two-electron photoreduction of air-stable phosphine-ligated palladium(II) oxalates. The platform exploits rapid ligand exchange at (MeCN)2Pd(ox) to enable modular assembly of catalyst photoprecursors from a single precursor. In crystallo photochemistry and single-crystal Raman spectroscopy of phosphine-supported Pd oxalates establish that photoactivation proceeds via the extrusion of two molecules of CO2 and provide the Uirst crystallographic characterization of a Pd–CO2 adduct. Two-electron photoactivation translates to the solution phase to provide a platform to access Pd oxidative addition complexes (OACs) and to generate poison-free, on-cycle catalyst intermediates. The combination of rapid and quantitative ligand exchange coupled with facile two-electron photoreduction enables application in highthroughput experimentation (HTE) workUlows and on-plate ligand screening. Photogenerated catalysts are competitive with state-of-the-art precatalysts in both C–N cross-coupling and a newly developed base-free Suzuki reaction. These results establish Pd oxalates as general, photoactivated precursors to unsaturated catalyst intermediates that unlock streamlined, combinatorial workUlows for catalyst discovery and data-driven optimization.

papers.title: Synthesis of nitride materials by atmospheric pressure metathesis
papers.abstract: Nitride materials have many important technological applications, yet they remain underexplored compared to other classes of compounds, as reflected by the smaller number of reports in databases and literature. The primary reason for this is the difficulty of synthesizing nitrides, which must outcompete energetically stable molecular N 2 and oxide compounds. As a result, bulk synthesis of nitrides often requires high pressure or corrosive fluxes in addition to oxygen-free conditions. We present our perspective on the metathesis technique as an accessible method for synthesizing nitrides at or below atmospheric pressure for the broader chemistry community. To highlight the advantages of this synthesis approach, we also review traditional methods for bulk nitride synthesis, including high pressure techniques, sodium and halide fluxes, and gas- and liquid-ammonia-based routes. We provide a brief tutorial on metathesis reactions including tips and tricks to help researchers get started. Finally, we discuss the future outlook for metathesis reactions, with an opportunity for precise structural selection during nitride synthesis through the controlled formation of stable and metastable polymorphs within the multidimensional potential-energy landscape of material nucleation and growth.

papers.title: Surface-Aware Generative Design of Selective Inhibitors for Protein–Membrane Adsorption
papers.abstract: Peripheral membrane proteins (PMPs) bind membrane surfaces through interfacial binding sites (IBSs) that are critical for stable membrane association and proper orientation of catalytic active sites. Dysregulated PMP–membrane interactions can enhance catalytic activity and contribute to diseases including cancer, but many PMPs remain difficult therapeutic targets because their active sites lack well-defined pockets or become accessible only upon membrane binding. In this work, we developed a multistage computational framework that integrates MaSIF-PMP, a surface-centered geometric deep learning model for IBS prediction, with a generative diffusion model to design protein binders that target PMP IBSs and inhibit membrane adsorption. Candidate binders were ranked using MaSIF-PMP prediction scores and geometric descriptors, then validated by molecular dynamics and enhanced sampling simulations. Applied to three disease-relevant PMPs, the framework identified selective binders that disrupted membrane association while minimizing off-target membrane interactions, providing a potential strategy for designing PMP membrane-adsorption inhibitors.

papers.title: Few-Shot Early-Release Adaptation Enables Generalizable Prediction of PLGA Drug Release
papers.abstract: Reliable prediction of long-term drug release remains challenging for formulations developed under experimental conditions that differ from those represented in literature-derived training data. Standard formulation descriptors capture important physicochemical and formulation characteristics, but they do not fully represent study-specific factors that shape the realized release trajectory. Here, we develop a machine-learning-based few-shot adaptation strategy that combines formulation descriptors with sparse early release measurements to forecast the remaining release trajectory under previously unseen experimental settings. Using a public dataset comprising 321 formulations, 4,913 release measurements, and 113 source studies, we evaluate the framework using strict study-grouped validation. Zero-shot prediction shows limited generalization to new experimental domains, whereas incorporating only a few early observations produces a marked and reproducible improvement in predictive performance. Across repeated held-out study splits, two early measurements increase mean pooled from −0.084 to 0.333 and reduce formulation-level MAE by approximately 30%, with further improvements as additional observations are incorporated. Although absolute predictive accuracy remains moderate, the improvement is consistent across repeated splits and demonstrates that limited target-specific information can substantially reduce the generalization gap. These findings show that sparse early release measurements can serve as an effective calibration signal for machine-learning models, providing a practical strategy for improving long-term drug-release forecasting under previously unrepresented experimental conditions.

papers.title: AI Agents for CRISPR Diagnostics: From Automation to Bounded Autonomy
papers.abstract: Recent years have witnessed rapid advances in clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) diagnostics, artificial intelligence (AI), and self-driving laboratories for automation. CRISPR diagnostics have emerged as a promising strategy for earlier disease detection, with Cas12a and Cas13a targeting DNA and RNA, respectively, and converting that recognition into collateral reporter cleavage. In parallel, different subsets of AI have advanced rapidly, with machine learning (ML) interpreting biosensor readouts, and large language models (LLMs) and AI agents applied to automation. Laboratory automation and self-driving platforms reduce the workload of human experimentalists and enable scale-up, having run long unattended campaigns in materials discovery. However, how these advances in AI, CRISPR diagnostics and automation could be integrated to enable a future of autonomous biosensing remains unresolved. In this perspective, we evaluate CRISPR diagnostics as autonomous systems, where analytical metrics alone cannot ensure robustness, failure-mode predictability, recoverability and auditability. We then propose a bounded-autonomy layer in which multimodal evidence, scored by ML, gates a Sense, quality control (QC), Decide, Act and Report loop, with guardrailed LLM agents invoked only when QC flags a run, selecting pre-validated actions under deterministic validation. By tying detectable failure modes to validated recovery actions, we outline a path toward bounded autonomy in CRISPR diagnostics, where a device unable to act safely abstains and escalates.

papers.title: Base-Dependent Lewis Acidity in Substituted Boranes: Revisiting Intrinsic Acidity through DFT and Machine Learning
papers.abstract: The Lewis acidity of boranes is strongly influenced by the electronic nature of their substituents and is commonly assessed through interactions with representative Lewis bases. However, the extent to which the relative Lewis acidity ordering of substituted boranes depends on the identity of the interacting Lewis base has not been systematically investigated. In this work, Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations combined with machine learning (ML) analysis were employed to quantify substituent effects and base dependence in borane–Lewis base interactions. A dataset comprising 816 trisubstituted boranes generated from 16 representative substituents was examined in interaction with five Lewis bases (H2O, NH3, C5H5N, P(CH3)3, and Cl−), yielding 3927 computed adduct formation free energies. The results show that electron-withdrawing substituents generally enhance, whereas electron-donating substituents attenuate, the Lewis acidity of boranes. However, the magnitude of these substituent effects depends on the identity of the interacting

papers.title: Beyond the Ligand Applicability Domain: Generalization and Local Resolution in Structure-Aware Foundation Models for Affinity Prediction
papers.abstract: Structure-aware foundation models that jointly represent proteins and ligands promise to extend affinity prediction beyond the chemical applicability domains of conventional ligand-based models, but whether they provide sufficient resolution to guide fine-grained medicinal-chemistry decisions remains unclear. We evaluatedBoltz-2across12kinasetargetsusinghistoricalbioactivityreconstruction,binding-pocket randomization, cross-target selectivity analysis, and chemical-series evaluation. Across chemically diverse compounds in temporally reconstructed evaluation sets, Boltz-2 and target-specific ligand-based machine learningshowedcomparablemeanglobalrankingacrosstargets,withsubstantialtarget-dependent differences (mean Kendall’s τ = 0.40 vs 0.31). Randomizing the binding pocket reduced mean τ from 0.33 to 0.14, while predictions were centered near −7.64 kcal/mol and retained correlated compound profiles acrossproteins.Together,theseresultssuggestastrongligand-conditionedsignal,withadditional predictive information contributed by the protein pocket. Despite this protein sensitivity, compound-level selectivitypredictionremainedweak(meanτ=0.17),andtheexperimentallystrongesttargetwas recovered for only 18.9% of compounds. Ranking also weakened within 72 temporally classified chemical series and varied substantially among series (protein-balanced mean τ = 0.18 for Boltz-2 and 0.09 for ligand-based models). These results show that structure-aware models can recover affinity information beyond relationshipscaptured by conventionalligand-based approaches whilerevealingaresolution boundary between broad prioritization and the local energetic discrimination required for selectivity and analogue ranking. At their current demonstrated resolution, such models appear best suited to broad compound or series prioritization and complementary hypothesis generation. Extending their use to fine analogueranking,selectivityoptimization,andinterpretationofsmallaffinitydifferenceswillrequire prospective evidence of reliable local resolution.

papers.title: Inconsistent odor-threshold measurements limit prediction from molecular structure
papers.abstract: Existing work treats odor detection threshold prediction as a supervised regression problem, assuming published thresholds are clean targets. In current public datasets, they are not: values come from different measurement sources and often disagree for the same molecule. Across the three largest public air-phase compilations, thresholds for identical molecules differ systematically by median factors of 3 to 11. Individual source studies vary around a compound’s underlying threshold by about 1.4 log 10 units, so under an independent-source approximation, a new study is expected to differ from the compiled value by about 1.6 log 10 units. This exceeds the best structure-based model’s error against that value (root-mean-square error 1.34), meaning the model matches the published compilation more closely than a new experiment would be expected to. Although averaging multiple studies makes the compiled value more precise, its remaining uncertainty still accounts for at least one-third of the model’s prediction-error variance, and a single source-study threshold has estimated reliability near 0.5. Changing the molecular representation, by comparison, changes root-mean-square error by only about 0.2 log 10 units. We therefore introduce a joint calibration model that places the compilations on a common scale, estimates source-specific offsets and noise, and improves cross-compilation prediction over a simple fixed-offset correction while providing calibrated uncertainty. These results show that progress in odor detection threshold prediction depends not only on better molecular models, but also on better measurements and methods that account for disagreement across data sources.

papers.title: Homogeneous Electrochemical Hydrogenation of 1-Octene with [( <sup>iPr</sup> PNP)CoCl] and Water
papers.abstract: Here we present the electrochemical hydrogenation (ECH) of 1-octene to n -octane using the homogeneous complex [( iPr PNP)CoCl] [CoCl] and water as the source of hydrogen atoms. We showcase how tuning only electrode surface area, as well as supporting electrolyte type and concentration can drastically increase the reaction selectivity for ECH over parasitic H 2 evolution from initially 9% to eventually 82% faradaic efficiency, without traditional chemical reaction optimization or catalyst tuning. The ECH process runs via a single electron path of hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) rather than hydride transfer according to quantum chemical calculations. Two consecutive HAT cycles must be completed to hydrogenate one substrate molecule, which renders the process more sensitive to mass transport effects and reaction design than hydride transfer mediated ECH with two electrons transferred in one step. Mechanistically, upon an initial one-electron reduction of [CoCl] , the complex undergoes HAT at one of its benzylic C–H positions to afford a dearomatized ligand structure. A key step of the active ECH cycle is then the oxidative addition of H 2 O to a Co(I) intermediate, affording a fleeting Co(III)-hydroxy-hydride, which immediately undergoes HAT to the substrate, forming a more stable Co(II)–OH species. A proton coupled electron transfer regenerates Co(I) for the next cycle. Using Bu 4 NOH in water as hydrogen atom source proved the resilience towards high pH values and suggests that the process does not rely on high proton activity in the electrolyte.

papers.title: Decoupling Dissolution from Water Oxidation at Single-Faceted High-Entropy Perovskite Electrodes
papers.abstract: High-entropy oxides (HEOs) are promising anode materials for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) due to their wide compositional space and electronic flexibility. However, their electrochemical dissolution and OER remains concurrent, preventing decoupled analysis of dissolution kinetics and stability. Here, we present a combined atomic force microscopy (AFM) and scanning electrochemical cell microscopy (SECCM) strategy to decouple lattice dissolution from water oxidation under well-defined reaction conditions. Structurally analogous, atomically flat, single-faceted (001) ABO 3 perovskite electrodes, La 1- x Sr x (Cr 0.2 Mn 0.2 Fe 0.2 Co 0.2 Ni 0.2 )O 3 with x = 0 and x = 0.3, serve as model systems to probe dissolution and OER kinetics in acid. Pipette probed localized cyclic voltammetry and chronoamperometry reveal that the measured current contains contributions from both OER and lattice dissolution, the latter producing nanoscale dissolution pits beneath the SECCM droplet. By correlating pit-growth kinetics with total OER charge as a function of pulse duration (τ), overpotential (η), and pH, we quantitatively separate dissolution from OER. The proportional scaling between dissolution charge and total charge indicates that OER and dissolution proceed within a common kinetic regime, sharing a common intermediate. A rate-law-based analysis yields the standard dissolution rate constant ( k d 0 , cm/s), transfer coefficient ( α ), and proton reaction order ( b ), for the dissolution of the 001 facet of both HEO-P. Our results unravel how aliovalent A -site substitution (30% Sr 2+ ) alters dissolution kinetics, charge partitioning between dissolution and OER, and thickness-dependent stability, thereby enabling quantitative disentangling of the intrinsic activity and stability of HEO electrodes.

papers.title: Active-Space Selection in Nonadiabatic Dynamics Simulations of Dense Manifolds of Excited States: When Local Diabatization Needs Great Care
papers.abstract: Local diabatization (LD) propagates electronic amplitudes using time-overlaps of adiabatic states and is robust to wavefunction phase arbitrariness, root character transport, and rotations within near-degenerate manifolds. However, when truncated dynamical bases are not numerically supported by the consecutive-geometry overlaps, polar orthogonalization underlying the LD approach can enforce unitary evolution in unresolved directions leading to unphysical population transfer. This work introduces an active-space screening protocol based on singular values of time-overlap matrices. Candidate spaces proposed from persistent energy gaps and state character are accepted only when every singular direction remains above the user-defined threshold and can then be tested for physical convergence across nested active spaces. Three-state and 30-state models, controlled overlap-failure tests, and atomistic (TiO2)2 and C20 trajectories show that formal rank and increasing state count alone do not guarantee reliable LD dynamics. Smaller, well-supported spaces can outperform the nominal full space when the latter is ill-conditioned.

papers.title: Transition from Anisotropic to Isotropic Crystal Growth Enables Ultrahigh-Rate Zn Metal Anodes in Batteries
papers.abstract: Achieving controllable crystallization under dynamic, far-from-equilibrium conditions remains a fundamental challenge underlying many technologically important processes, including highpower batteries based on metal anodes. Recent studies have identified crystal anisotropy as a key factor governing electrodeposit morphology. Departing from conventional wisdom, we find that suppressing highly anisotropic facet-dependent growth by slowing interfacial kinetics results in more isotropic, morphologically uniform electrodeposition. Taking Zn as an example, we use a nonaqueous Zn(Otf)2 in acetonitrile electrolyte to promote the formation of dense irregular-shaped nuclei in sharp contrast to the faceted nuclei formed in conventional aqueous Zn(Otf)2 and ZnSO4 electrolytes. 3-D profilometry shows the isotropic growth of Zn in the organic electrolyte leads to significantly flatter deposit morphology compared to the aqueous electrolytes. We rigorously characterize the electrochemical properties of the Zn(Otf)2 in acetonitrile electrolyte and compare it to aqueous Zn(Otf)2 and ZnSO4 electrolytes, using a combination of ultra-fast scan cyclic voltammetry on an ultra-microelectrode (UME) and interfacial molecular dynamics simulations. Our measurements show the plating/stripping kinetics in the organic electrolyte are reduced by over 100-fold relative to the aqueous electrolytes, while the transport properties are only slowed by 3 to 4-fold. Using a two-step Butler-Volmer model, we find slow interfacial kinetics in the organic electrolyte eliminate the facet-dependent rate-determining step present in aqueous electrolytes, directly linking sluggish kinetics to isotropic growth. The uniform morphology and the suppression of Zn corrosion reactions in the organic electrolyte lead to over a 10-fold improvement in cycling stability over benchmark aqueous Zn electrolytes, both at moderate current densities (1 mA/cm2) and ultra-fast current densities (200 mA/cm2). Taken together, these results highlight the viability of using a fully organic Zn electrolyte for Zn batteries and Zn electroplating systems, challenging the prevailing assumption that organic electrolytes are inferior under fast cycling conditions. Moreover, the demonstrated correlation between interfacial kinetics and electrodeposit morphology offers a generalized framework for morphological control in metal deposition.

papers.title: Data-Driven Prospective Design of Phase-Inversion Conductive Polymer Membranes
papers.abstract: Conductive polymer membranes combine separation and electrical functionality, but their design remains challenging because performance emerges from coupled effects of composition, fabrication, and operating conditions. Here, we assembled 396 membrane records from 77 publications and developed target-specific machine-learning models for pure-water permeability (PWP), solute rejection, and electrical conductivity. Weighted artificial neural network ensembles for PWP and rejection and XGBoost for conductivity achieved fixed-holdout R2 values of 0.855, 0.896, and 0.914, respectively, with distinct SHAP feature-contribution patterns across the three targets. We then coupled the predictive models with residual Gaussian-process uncertainty estimation and sequential Monte Carlo expected hypervolume improvement to search a 3,024-member PANI–DBSA/PES design space and identify 12 formulations for prospective experimental evaluation. Atomistic molecular dynamics simulations provided complementary mechanistic insight: increasing PANI from 0.47 to 1.89 wt% decreased the first-shell hydration number around DBSA sulfonate sites from 1.02 to 0.74, while the apparent finite-time water diffusion coefficient declined from 0.6910-10 m2∙s-1 in neat PES to 0.3710-10 m2∙s-1 at 1.89 wt% PANI. Together, these results connect literature-derived learning, uncertainty-aware formulation selection, and molecular-scale interpretation, providing a systematic framework for prospective conductive membrane design

papers.title: Case Studies of Homemorphic Isomerization: Interconversion of In/Out Isomers of Bicyclo[6.5.1]tetradecane and Related Bicyclic Hydrocarbons
papers.abstract: Homeomorphic isomerization is equivalent to turning a molecule inside out in the same manner as a reversible article of clothing. Manifestations include the interconversion of (a) in,in and out,out isomers, or (b) in,out and out,in isomers of bicyclic molecules, but without inverting the configurations of the bridgehead atoms. In this preprint, this topological process is probed computationally for the title molecules. For the in,in/out,out manifold, the CH 2 tether is able to transit through the CH(CH 2 ) 6 CH tether with a barrier of ~26 kcal/mol, in good agreement with an experimental measurement. The geometries of the ground and transition states are analyzed in detail and the process of isomerization is visualized in animations.

papers.title: Integrated Process Environmental and Economic Modeling of Electrically Assisted Forward Osmosis Microbial Desalination for Water and Struvite Recovery
papers.abstract: Electrically assisted forward osmosis (eFO) coupled with a microbial desalination cell (MDC) integrates water recovery, nutrient recovery, desalination, and bioelectricity utilization. This study coupled a previously validated hybrid mechanistic–data-driven model with cradle-to-grave life cycle assessment (LCA) and techno-economic analysis (TEA) to evaluate the sustainability of eFO–MDC across operating conditions and scale-up scenarios. Operational electricity was the dominant environmental hotspot, accounting for 90.7% of the positive life-cycle GWP burden, whereas manufacturing impacts were concentrated in the MDC cathode and energy-management unit. Model-coupled LCA showed that hydraulic throughput strongly governed treatment-normalized impacts, while applied voltage produced comparatively small changes in GWP relative to its effect on nutrient recovery. TEA identified capital intensity, pumping, and treatment scale as the principal economic drivers, with combined scale-up and capital reduction lowering processing cost by 67.8%. Overall, eFO–MDC sustainability depends primarily on improving throughput and energy efficiency while reducing capital intensity during scale-up.

papers.title: Enhancing double-duplex invasion by using multiple parallel-stranded peptide nucleic acids
papers.abstract: Peptide nucleic acids (PNAs) enable sequence-specific recognition of double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) via invasion complex formation. Here, we report a strategy using multiple parallel-stranded PNAs to enhance invasion efficiency. Cooperative binding of PNAs at adjacent target sites markedly improved invasion efficiency and enabled sequence-specific recognition of plasmid DNA under physiological conditions.

papers.title: Understanding the Dynamics of C-OH Bond Activation over Mo <sub>2</sub> C under Hydrodeoxygenation Reaction Conditions
papers.abstract: Hydrodeoxygenation (HDO) of biomass to value-added chemicals using transition metal carbides (TMCs) serves as a two-fold solution to overreliance on fossil-based feedstocks and excessive usage of noble metal catalysts. Specifically, Mo 2 C and W 2 C have emerged as viable alternatives to noble metal catalysts for HDO reactions. However, the underlying reaction mechanisms and structure-activity relationships for TMC catalysts are still not fully understood. Our previous mechanistic studies (Meena et al. ACS Catalysis, 2023, 13, 13446–13455), based on static DFT calculations and microkinetic modeling, indicated that C-OH bond dissociation (C 4 H 9 OH⋆ →C 4 H 9 ⋆ + OH⋆) is the rate-determining step (RDS) of HDO reaction over Mo 2 C. Nevertheless, these static calculations, which neglect thermal fluctuations, cannot fully capture the catalysts’ behavior under working conditions. To address this limitation, here, we present a comprehensive computational investigation of the RDS under more realistic reaction conditions using ab initio Molecular Dynamics simulations combined with the path metadynamics enhanced sampling technique. Path metadynamics runs reveal that the Mo 2 C surface is stable at the reaction temperature and no significant surface reconstructions take place. Further, the C-OH activation barrier obtained at 623 K using path metadynamics (38 kcal/mol) is higher than that from static DFT calculation (30 kcal/mol), likely emphasizing the significance of entropic contributions. The comparison of the barriers of C-OH activation over Mo 2 C and Zr- and Co-doped Mo 2 C surfaces revealed similar activity trends compared to that from static DFT, i.e., Zr doping improves the activity and Co doping inhibits the activity

papers.title: On the Mechanism of Catalytic Chain Transfer Photopolymerization (CCTP2): the Good, the Bad and the Ugly
papers.abstract: Previously, the addition of catalytic quantities of cobalt(II) complexes to standard methacrylatebased formulations was found to reduce the crosslinking density, glass transition temperature, modulus and stiffness of the resultant photopolymeric materials proportional to catalyst loading. We have dubbed this technique catalytic chain transfer photopolymerization (CCTP2), which is conceptually and mechanistically linked to its predecessor catalytic chain transfer polymerization (CCTP), but uses photoinitiation, multifunctional methacrylate monomers, and creates crosslinked 2 materials. Expansion of this technology has been met with issues related to non-linear catalyst performance, limited methacrylate conversion, and long exposure times. These roadblocks prompted us to develop a working mechanistic model for CCTP2 using a combined experimental and computational approach, which is presented here. We anticipate that understanding the good, the bad, and the ugly of this catalytic process will inform future catalyst development, formulation chemistry, and broader applications of this technique towards the synthesis of functional materials and stereolithography.

papers.title: Electrochemical Detection of Ethanol in Liquid Samples and Simulated Breath: Investigating Calibration, Selectivity, and Preconcentration
papers.abstract: Advances in miniaturized and point-of-care electrochemical sensors have expanded their applications in healthcare, environmental monitoring, and public safety. Consequently, it is important to study the principles of these technologies in an undergraduate setting. This experiment uses screen-printed electrodes for electrochemical detection of ethanol and introduces students to electrocatalysis, calibration curves, chemical interference, selectivity, and preconcentration. Students use cyclic voltammetry and chronoamperometry to make calibration curves and determine ethanol concentrations in ethanol standards and diluted beer and wine samples. Glucose interference is investigated, and a simulated breath experiment demonstrates how selecting breath as the analytical sample and condensing it can eliminate interference while simultaneously preconcentrating ethanol. The activity provides an opportunity to discuss blood alcohol concentration (BAC), breath alcohol concentration (BrAC), and modern alcohol-sensing technologies. This experiment is suitable for upper-level undergraduate courses in analytical chemistry, physical chemistry, and electrochemistry.

papers.title: Atomic Level Characterization of PolyGlycine Assembly
papers.abstract: Polyglycine peptides can adopt polyproline II (PPII) helical conformations that assemble into honeycomb-shaped oligomers. These polyglycine II (PGII) helical bundles, which are also found in several natural proteins, lack apolar groups and cannot be stabilized by hydrophobic interactions. Thus, their folding must differ from that of typical globular proteins for which hydrophobic interactions promote structure formation. Despite their fundamental interest and relevance for molecular pathology, the atomic level details on how these PGII assemblies form are scarcely explored. To elucidate this process, we used CD and NMR spectroscopies to show that oligoglycine peptides with a few terminal Asp residues readily form oligomers rich in PPII helix at low pH and cool temperatures. Next, to test whether these structures can emerge without a preformed template, we performed ten independent, unbiased, multi-microsecond, all-atom molecular dynamics simulations starting from dispersed, terminally capped nonaglycine monomers in water. We observed PPII helical bundle formation through an oligomeric intermediate that is relatively poor in nematic order and H-bonds.

papers.title: Mechanism-grounded fragmentation trees enable explicit chemical reasoning for electron ionization mass spectrum prediction
papers.abstract: Developing predictive models that connect molecular structures with measured spectra while preserving interpretable links to ion formation and fragmentation chemistry remains a central challenge in predictive spectroscopy. Here we present FragTreeMS, a mechanism-grounded framework that decomposes electron ionization (EI) mass spectrum prediction into fragmentation tree generation and repair followed by pathway- conditioned intensity learning. FragTreeMS organizes source-mechanism-product relations into traceable fragmentation trees and uses candidate-guided self-review to identify and recover plausible omissions before intensity prediction. The repaired fragmentation tree provides the pathway from the molecular root to each retained product ion, and these pathways are directly used for intensity prediction. FragTreeMS improves product ion recovery and complete spectrum similarity relative to direct spectrum prediction and established EI-MS baselines. The inferred ion formation processes and associated putative structural fragments are explicitly represented and visualized, advancing mass spectrum prediction toward interpretable chemical reasoning.

papers.title: Exploring intermediates in mechanochemical cycle and mechanism of regulation of full-length Dynein
papers.abstract: Cytoplasmic dynein is a complex hexameric AAA+ motor protein essential for intracellular transport, yet the structural mechanisms and domain cooperativity driving its mechanochemical cycle remain incompletely understood. In this study, we utilize a dual-basin structure-based model (SBM) to simulate the full-length dynein cycle in the presence of microtubules. Rather than a single concerted transition, our results reveal that dynein moves through discrete, on-pathway conformational intermediates, including a transient, ADP-bound state that bridges the pre- and post-powerstroke configurations. We identify four key regulatory interfaces (AAA1-subdomains, AAA1–AAA2, AAA3–AAA4, and AAA5–AAA6) that function as checkpoints to couple the AAA+ ring changes to power- and recovery stroke. Crucially, we elucidate the regulatory roles of the non-dominant domains: suppressing AAA3 disrupts recovery-stroke progression and linker relocation, while suppressing AAA4 selectively impairs linker stabilization and docking. Together, these findings demonstrate that dynein's force generation relies on a highly coordinated allosteric network across the entire AAA+ ring.

papers.title: Water-Responsive Shape-Memory Origami Enabled by a Washi–Bulk pNIPAAm Hydrogel Hybrid Sheet
papers.abstract: Origami transforms two-dimensional sheets into complex three-dimensional forms through folding and has evolved from a traditional art into a versatile design principle for deployable and reconfigurable structures. Here, we develop a water-responsive shape-memory origami sheet by combining highly concentrated poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (bulk pNIPAAm) hydrogel with Japanese kozo paper. Bulk pNIPAAm undergoes pronounced hydrationinduced softening and recovers its permanent shape upon rehydration, whereas the paper scaffold enables the hydrogel to be fabricated and handled as a thin, foldable sheet. Rather than programming only individual active creases, the hybrid sheet allows complex folded three-dimensional configurations to be programmed directly as permanent shapes. Two complementary programming strategies are demonstrated: photopolymerization of precursorimpregnated paper in a pre-folded configuration and post-fabrication programming by local photopolymerization at selected creases. Kozo washi-based hybrid sheets exhibited more than 90% recovery within several seconds in a simple folding test, and Miura-fold, crane, dolphin, and kirigami structures recovered their memorized geometries after unfolding and dehydration-induced temporary fixation. Finally, simply pouring warm water onto a flowershaped structure triggers spontaneous blooming without full immersion. This approach transforms a bulk shape-memory hydrogel into a fold-programmable sheet material and

papers.title: Self-quenched growth of monodisperse SnO2 nanocrystals—insensitive to synthesis conditions
papers.abstract: Metal oxide thin film fabrication from colloidal nanocrystal dispersions separates the materials synthesis from the device (layer) fabrication, enabling fast solution processing. However, nanocrystal ink syntheses can be still too complex to be truly scalable for large-area ultra-lowcost applications such as solar modules. Here, we present a self-quenched (by precipitation) nanocrystal synthesis at room temperature. The synthesis is independent of the precursor concentrations, precursor addition speed (injection vs. slow addition), mixing dynamics of the solutions, reaction duration, and temperature. Crystalline and monodisperse tin(IV) oxide nanocrystals (<3 nm diameter) are obtained with a near-unity reaction yield. After purification, the nanocrystal surface is modified with acetate ligands and brought into a colloidal dispersion, again with near-unity yield. Nip perovskite solar cells containing tin oxide nanocrystal thin films 2 achieve power conversion efficiencies of at least 21%. This method introduces a highly scalable SnO2 nanocrystal ink synthesis, which may be applicable to other metal oxides for coating technologies such as displays, windows, and perovskite solar modules, as well as the deposition on polymer films.

papers.title: Beyond Organic Molecules: MetalLipoDB, a Lipophilicity Dataset for Metal Complexes and Machine Learning Benchmarks
papers.abstract: Lipophilicity governs the uptake, distribution and toxicity of drug candidates, yet the experimental logP datasets used to build predictive models contain almost exclusively organic molecules. Here we present MetalLipoDB, a manually curated dataset of 5158 experimental logP and logD values of complexes of 23 metals from 1192 articles, including 556 entries for multinuclear and heterometallic complexes, annotated with the measurement conditions and counterions. The dataset quantifies the inter-study reproducibility of these measurements (0.56 log units) and serves as a benchmark for machine learning, with a mean absolute error of 0.72–0.75 for complexes from unseen articles. For articles with at least four measurements, anchoring the predictions to three measured complexes of the series reduced the error on the remaining complexes from 0.73 to 0.51. MetalLipoDB, the code and an interactive web application (https://biometaldb.streamlit.app/) are openly available to support the design of metal-based drugs.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Guided QSAR Modeling and Virtual Screening of Medicinal Plant-Derived Phytochemicals for the Identification of Potential hDHFR Inhibitors
papers.abstract: Human dihydrofolate reductase (hDHFR) is a well-established anticancer drug target due to its essential role in folate metabolism and DNA synthesis. This study employed integrated machine based structural-activity relationship, virtual screening, and molecular docking to identify potential hDHFR inhibitors from medicinal plant-derived phytochemicals. A curated dataset of 1,368 compounds was obtained from ChEMBL and presented using Morgan fingerprints and RDKit molecular descriptors. Four regression model algorithms, including RF, XGBoost, LightGBM, and SVR were developed and optimized. Among them, SVR achieved the best score with a test R2 of 0.669 and a Spearman coefficient of 0.789. The SVR model was then used to screen the drug like phytocompounds collected from medicinal plants. The top-ranked compounds were subsequently evaluated through molecular docking against hDHFR (PDB ID: 1U72). Several phytochemicals exhibited stronger binding affinities than the reference inhibitor methotrexate. Among them Withaferin A showed the strongest docking score (-11.68 kcal/mol). These findings highlight the potential of combining machine learning and structure based virtual screening to identify promising hDHFR-targeted lead compounds for further validation.

papers.title: Parallel Production of Uniform Artificial Multicellular Models Using Vibration-Induced Local Microvortices
papers.abstract: In this study, we propose a facile and efficient method for constructing artificial multicellular models via vibration-induced flow (VIF), a local fluid flow induced around vibrating microstructures. By applying circular vibration to a substrate with a cylindrical micropillar array, uniform micro-vortices were generated, into which giant unilamellar vesicles (GUVs), as artificial cells, rapidly accumulated at the center. We show that by modifying two GUV populations with complementary single-stranded DNAs, we can promote specific adhesion between GUVs, leading to uniform parallel aggregates. Furthermore, the pillar-array design controls the size of GUV aggregates. Finally, we embedded nanopore-forming α-hemolysin with Spytag and SpyCatcher system in GUV populations, allowing the lumens of assembled GUVs to channel with one another and enable close-proximity molecular communication. This technology will contribute to future research on fabricating artificial multicellular models with complex functions.

papers.title: Practical In Situ Generation of Phosphorus Pentafluoride as a Metal-Free Potent Lewis Acid
papers.abstract: Metal-free potent Lewis acids are of great interest in the pharmaceutical and food industries to avoid metal contaminants. Phosphorus pentafluoride (PF 5 ) is a potent Lewis acid, but its practical use is severely restricted by its gaseous state and corrosiveness. Here we report a simple and convenient method for either the rapid or slow in situ generation of PF 5 from widely available and easy to handle hexafluorophosphate (PF 6 − ) salts and either aluminum chloride (AlCl 3 ) or boron trifluoride etherate (BF 3 ·Et 2 O), respectively. The potency of PF 5 in Lewis acid catalysis is demonstrated in the tandem Friedel–Craft alkylation of thiophene derivatives with ketones, where PF 5 outperforms conventional Lewis acids such as BF 3 ·Et 2 O, AlCl 3 , and SnCl 4 .

papers.title: Experimental Inter-Report Scatter Bounds Machine-Learning Accuracy for TADF Singlet–Triplet Gaps—Structure and Semi-Empirical Features Reach the Same Limit
papers.abstract: The singlet–triplet gap ∆ESTis the screening parameter for thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF), yet independent experimental reports of the same compound scatter by 0.072 eV RMS, and the per-molecule median regressed on is known only to 0.049 eV, about half of any model’s error. This label noise sets a ceiling on every predictor, yet the models sit below it: neither noise nor capacity alone accounts for the remaining error. Against that ceiling, two-dimensional structure predicts as accurately as a semiempirical excited-state calculation: on 231 donor–acceptor molecules (212 Bemis–Murcko scaffolds, scaffold cross-validation), random forests from Morgan fingerprints (MAE 0.091 eV) and RDKit descriptors (0.100 eV) match natural-transition-orbital descriptors from a GFN2-xTB/sTDA excited state (0.096 eV) to within 0.017 eV on paired folds, so the excited-state step buys no accuracy. Two further results are specific to this corpus. First, under a source-paper split the accuracy advantage over a mean-value baseline disappears, but the excited-state descriptors keep the rank correlation the fingerprints lose (paired ∆ρ = 0.19 on a single split, 95 % CI narrowly excluding zero): they order candidates across laboratories without predicting the gap. Second, the leakage that inflates many computed-gap models is learner-dependent—given the S1 and T1 energies as features, a linear model returns ∆EST ≡ ES1 − ET1 exactly (R2 = 1.000) while an axis-aligned forest on the same features recovers only R2 = 0.59 and clears cross-validation unremarked. Progress past the ≈ 0.1eV ceiling needs a curated, solvent-controlled, single-source experimental benchmark—one that would also expose the remaining modelling headroom. Data, models, and code are available (Zenodo DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.17436069).

papers.title: Atomically Precise Platinum Nanocluster Catalysts for Efficient Hydrogen Production via Methylcyclohexane Dehydrogenation
papers.abstract: In hydrogen storage technologies with liquid organic hydrogen carriers, the development of efficient catalysts for methylcyclohexane dehydrogenation is highly important. In this study, we developed atomically precise platinum nanocluster catalysts supported on Al2O3 (Ptx/Al2O3; x = 17, ~51). Comprehensive characterization demonstrated that the catalysts remained highly monodisperse and of uniform particle size (0.86 or 1.15 nm), and maintained a cationic electronic state (Ptδ+) even after thermal treatment. Remarkably, the Pt17/Al2O3 and Pt~51/Al2O3 catalysts exhibited a mass activity up to 7.9 and 8.2 times higher than that of conventional nanoparticle catalysts. Furthermore, by effectively suppressing undesirable cracking pathways at a low operating temperature of 250 °C, the catalyst achieved both high selectivity (byproduct yield < 3%; below the detection limit) and durability. These findings pave the way for practical guidelines in advanced catalyst design.

papers.title: Continuous-wave laser ablation enables high-resolution ambient mass spectrometry imaging
papers.abstract: Continuous-wave lasers are generally not considered for applications demanding precision ablation, because sustained heating in bulk tissue causes extensive thermal damage. Here we show that this limitation does not apply to thin sections: a 2.91 µm continuous-wave laser leaves no resolvable heat-affected zone beyond the ablation track on 10 µm thick cryosections, a confinement consistent with heat sinking vertically into the glass slide rather than diffusing laterally. This defines a distinct sampling regime in which confined material removal by a continuous-wave mid-infrared laser preserves the sample morphology for post-hoc staining and optical imaging while generating a laminar plume well suited for aspiration into the atmospheric inlet of a mass spectrometer. Here we demonstrate matrix-free ambient mass spectrometry imaging at 3 µm pixel size with a fibre-delivered beam, uniting few micron scale sampling, broad chemical coverage, and same-section co-registration on a readily adoptable platform assembled entirely from commercial components.

papers.title: Growth-Triggered Nano-vesicle Budding via Leaflet Area Asymmetry in Fatty-Acid Protocells
papers.abstract: Fatty-acid vesicles growing by monomer uptake, as demonstrated experimentally for Szostak-type protocells, insert new amphiphiles predominantly into the outer leaflet. Because transbilayer flip-flop is not instantaneous, this generates a growing area mismatch between the two leaflets. We show, using the area-difference-elasticity (ADE) framework for vesicle shape, that this mismatch crosses a threshold beyond which the vesicle relieves it by shedding small, high-curvature nano-vesicles rather than by symmetric division–with no external mechanical forcing required. A leaflet-resolved kinetic model shows that sustained parent growth over many such cycles requires the shed nano-vesicles to be compositionally enriched in the destabilizing (outer-leaflet) material rather than ordinary bilayer: a specific, falsifiable prediction. For illustrative growth and flipflop rates the model predicts nano-vesicles of radius 60–90 nm, above the stability floor of fatty-acid vesicles. This mechanism, and its central prediction, match independent experimental observations on fatty-acid and lysolipid-containing vesicles. In an earlier work [1] we explored periodic environmental mechanical forcing (tidal, geyser and vortex-driven shear) as an alternative trigger for vesicle instability; that mechanism rests on poorly constrained assumptions about Hadean orbital dynamics and produces, in its simplest form, no resonance, only a low-pass response. The present mechanism requires no assumption about the early Earth’s mechanical environment at all.

papers.title: A Highly Proton-Tolerant Multicenter Borane/Phosphazene Catalytic System for Efficient PO/CO2 Copolymerization toward CO2-Based Poly(carbonate-ether) Polyols
papers.abstract: Low-molecular-weight CO2-based poly(carbonate-ether) polyols from ring-opening copolymerization (ROCOP) of propylene oxide (PO) with CO2 are highly desired as soft blocks to synthesize sustainable polyurethanes. However, such process remains great challenges because of the demanding of highly proton-tolerant catalysts. Herein, we report a binary organocatalysis system based on a nanoscopic multicenter borane Lewis acid (POSS-B8) combined with various organobases for the tunable ROCOP of PO and CO2. The confined POSS-B8 framework not only endows excellent tolerance to proton but enables cooperative activation of PO and CO2, thereby facilitating PO/CO2 ROCOP while effectively suppressing the formation of cyclic propene carbonate (cPC). Remarkably, the binary system can tolerate high loadings of chain-transfer agents (up to 400 equivalents), affording low-molecular-weight polycarbonate polyols (0.6 kDa) with narrow dispersity (Ð = 1.16). By tuning POSS-B8 loading and CO2 pressure, both the carbonate content (19-64 mol%) and glass transition temperature (-58.6 to 4.7 °C) of resulting polymers can be modulated. This metal-free and tunable platform offers a versatile strategy for the preparation of CO2-based poly(carbonate-ether) polyols with controlled structure and strong potential for industrial applications.

papers.title: A field-deployable method for measuring picomolar mercury levels in natural waters
papers.abstract: Measurements of mercury (Hg) at sub- to picomolar concentrations in natural waters often rely on cold vapor atomic fluorescence spectrometry (CVAFS), which provides the sensitivity required for trace detection. However, CVAFS instruments are not well suited for routine field deployment and require compressed high-purity argon or helium gas to operate, limiting their use in remote regions and locations without established analytical infrastructure. Cold-vapor atomic absorption spectrometry (CVAAS) offers a robust alternative but generally lacks the sensitivity required for low-level natural waters. Here, we optimized and tested the Nippon Instruments EMP Gold+, a purge-and-trap preconcentration system coupled to a portable CVAAS detector, to address this analytical challenge. We developed protocols for total Hg (THg) and dissolved gaseous Hg (DGM) and evaluated their performance in seawater during field deployments in Monterey Bay, California, USA and the Gulf of Guinea, Ghana. The optimized methods achieved detection limits of 0.97 pM for THg and 0.25 pM for DGM. THg measured in the Gulf of Guinea agreed closely with laboratory CVAFS measurements (R 2 = 0.953, slope = 1.11), with field matrix-spike recoveries of 90.6-96.2%. In Monterey Bay, portable DGM measurements reproduced the vertical structure observed independently for dimethylmercury using gas chromatography coupled to CVAFS. We demonstrate that this new approach can support direct measurements in regions where compressed gases and specialized analytical infrastructure are unavailable and provide rapid screening to guide subsequent sampling for more detailed Hg speciation.

papers.title: Spin-dependent thermoelectric transport properties of DPH-based molecular device
Energy ordering of singlet and triplet excited states in s-indacene, Pentalene, Cyclobutadiene derivatives in singlet fission : A model exact and density matrix renormalization group study
Nucleotide-mediated catalytic peptide synthesis from aminonitriles
papers.abstract: Aminonitriles are accessible from simple feedstock compounds and their hydrolysis offers an abiotic route to life’s amino acids on the early earth. However, controlled aqueous polymerisation of amino acids into peptides remains challenging. Here we show that peptides can be directly generated and elongated by aminonitriles when the latter are coupled to nucleotides as a phosphoramidate. Upon thiol catalysis and pH shifts, a series of selective reactivities drives iterative peptide bond formation in water. The high energy nitrile bond of aminonitriles circumvents amino acids’ need for concurrent activation chemistry in peptide elongation. Coupling the building blocks of life’s central biopolymers in this manner provides a pathway for early integration of peptides into biology.

papers.title: RealBind: a leakage-controlled benchmark for experimental PXRD and Raman structure retrieval
papers.abstract: We present RealBind, a benchmark for retrieving crystal structures from experimental powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) and Raman spectra. It contains 3,288 curated candidate structures, of which 1,468 have linked measured PXRD patterns, and 16,005 experimental Raman spectra, of which 10,547 are linked to structures. We provide quality-control records, prototype-held-out and composition-held-out splits, and evaluation protocols that state candidate-library size and the chemical information available at retrieval time. On a 492-candidate prototype-held-out library, a contrastive model trained on simulated PXRD reaches 78.5% Recall@10 on simulated queries but 5.3% on measured queries; physics-inspired corruption raises measured-query Recall@10 to 34.4%. A model-free correlation against simulated candidate patterns, with no preprocessing beyond the common Q-grid resampling and the measuredwindow mask, achieves 82.8% Recall@10 on the same test library. In a separate split comparison, 44% of random-split test structures have a structure-matched training counterpart; measured-query Recall@10 is 59.1% on that split versus 20.7% on the prototype-held-out split, although test populations and libraries also differ. Holding the trained model and 420 queries fixed, restricting the candidate library and pre-screening candidates by the ground-truth element set of the query’s structure, used as an oracle chemistry-conditioned diagnostic, raises Recall@10 from 27.1% to 99.1%; 37.6% of filtered queries have a single candidate. A Raman-to-structure baseline reaches 34.7% Recall@10 on heldout mineral spectra against 979 candidates in the pooled evaluation and 45.7% on the 485-candidate test-only library, which includes no validation structures. RealBind provides an experimental test bed for comparing learned methods with simple simulation-based matching under explicit, leakage-aware protocols.

papers.title: μ-Oxo-Bridged Iodine(III) Reagents Enable Catalyst- and Light-Free Fluoro(halo)methyl Radical Generation
papers.abstract: While conventional radical fluoroalkylation typically requires exogenous catalysts or photoactivation to overcome significant kinetic barriers, here we report bench-stable μ-oxo-bridged iodine(III) reagents that release fluoro(halo)methyl radicals upon heating without an external catalyst, additive, or light. The resulting radicals initiate cascade cyclizations of methacrylamides and methacrylohydrazides to afford fluorinated oxindoles, pyrazolones, and related heterocycles. Variation of the fluorinated carboxylate ligand within the iodine(III) reagent framework controls the identity of the transferred C1 fragment, thereby providing chlorofluoromethyl, bromofluoromethyl, difluoromethyl, and monofluoromethyl products from a common reagent architecture. The transformation is compatible with structurally diverse and natural-product-derived substrates and proceeds efficiently upon scale-up.
