By encoding the required bond lability directly into the iodine(III) framework, this strategy establishes a general platform for the catalyst-, additive-, and light-free generation and incorporation of fluorinated C1 radicals into complex molecular frameworks.

papers.title: RGST-ΔSCF: Response-Guided Construction and Tracking of Excitation-energy-Resolved states along surface Reaction Pathways
papers.abstract: Illumination can promote or inhibit catalytic reactions, yet the origin of their excitation-energy dependence remains unclear. Here, constrained ΔSCF calculations and spin- and k-resolved wavefunction-overlap tracking are used to follow nonequilibrium electronic configurations across four excitation-energy intervals along H2-dissociation pathways at doped Cu/ZnO interfaces. The preferred pathway switches from final-state-referenced configurations at low excitation energies to initial-state-referenced configurations at higher energies, with dopant-dependent crossover energies and nonmonotonic barrier responses. Metal-site dopants regulate reactivity primarily through excitation-induced reconstruction of collective metal-H bonding, whereas support-site dopants act through pathway-dependent interfacial spin redistribution. Neither excitation energy nor the magnitude of charge, bonding, or spin redistribution alone universally predicts catalytic promotion; the response depends on its direction, localization, and differential coupling to the initial and transition states. Application to Ag-mediated O2 dissociation further demonstrates that population-dependent interfacial reorganization, rather than net adsorbate charge alone, controls bond activation.

papers.title: Active Noise Cancelling in Point-of-Care Testing
papers.abstract: Point-of-care testing (POCT) holds great potential to improve diagnostic accessibility because of its low cost, portability, user-friendliness, and rapid turnaround times. However, the limited analytical precision and high error rates of most POCT platforms usually caused by the assay noises at the POC settings frequently create diagnostic ambiguity and lead to further confirmatory testing. Consequently, these limitations restrict broader clinical translation. To address this issue, we introduce an active assay noise canceling approach, using the deep-learning-based Whole-Process Analysis (WPA), a universal, device-adaptable software paradigm without altering assay hardware or chemistry. Instead of relying on static endpoint readouts, WPA uses a deep-learning architecture to continuously capture the spatiotemporal evolution of the entire POCT assay process. The architecture decodes dynamic, high-dimensional "assay noise footprints" and algorithmically compensate for the signal variations caused by assay noises. We demonstrated the proof of concept, we chose the lateral flow assay (LFA) as a model, which is a leading POCT platform. We validated WPA for xylazine LFA across 251 patient urine samples, benchmarking against gold-standard liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). WPA drastically decreased signal variations among different clinical samples and compressed the diagnostic gray zone, delivering 94.02% accuracy (95% CI: 90.33%-96.62%), 71.15% sensitivity (95% CI: 56.92%-82.87%), and 100% specificity (95% CI: 98.16%-100.00%), compared with human reading, which achieved 89.2% accuracy (95% CI: 84.74%-92.79%), 48.1% sensitivity (95% CI: 34.01%-62.37%), and 100% specificity (95% CI: 98.16%-100.00%). By computationally untangling true analyte signals from assay noises in POC settings, WPA provides a transformative, device-adaptable pathway to improve POCT accuracy and precision without altering assay hardware or chemistry.

papers.title: GCI-TPs: Identifying Potentially Hazardous Transformation Products of Global Chemical Inventory Compounds
papers.abstract: Environmental contamination from an ever-increasing number of chemicals is a subject of high concern, with over one hundred thousand discrete chemicals listed in a recently compiled open global chemical inventory (GCI). As these compounds enter the environment, they often form transformation products (TPs) which may have persistent, mobile and toxic (PMT) properties. Despite this, less than 1% of compounds have openly available TP information. Although TP prediction can fill some data gaps, the models are prone to combinatorial explosion, and predicted TPs must be prioritized. This study implemented multi-step environmental biotic and novel abiotic TP prediction of the ZeroPM GCI chemicals using BioTransformer 4.0, combined with toxicity and mobility models to prioritize which TPs are potentially persistent, mobile and toxic. The resulting GCI-TPs database, contains over 13 million predicted TPs, including 5481 compounds labeled as potential dead-end compounds (compounds that are not predicted to transform further), of which 478 were predicted to be either PMT or PvM compounds. From this, 38 substructures that can act as flags for potential PMT-TP formation were identified. The dead-end PMT-TPs are available on the NORMAN Suspect List Exchange and through the GCI-TPs website (https://gcitps.lcsb.uni.lu/).

papers.title: Accelerating discovery of phosphorescent blue OLED emitters using chemical foundation models
papers.abstract: In OLED displays, phosphorescent emitter molecules are used for red and green but not for blue pixels. Iridium organometallics are promising phosphorescent emitters, but a molecule satisfying the requirements of color, brightness, and stability has not yet been developed. One strategy to discover an emitter is virtual screening, in which computational predictions are used to prioritize candidates for synthesis. Due to the computational difficulty of screening with first-principles methods such as density functional theory (DFT), empirical machine-learning methods have been used for virtual screening. Recently, machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) have provided fast proxies for DFT energies. This suggests that virtual screening could be conducted with ML proxies for DFT calculations rather than empirical ML, but this has not yet been applied to OLEDs. We show on a dataset of experimental values extracted from the literature that for emission wavelength, MLIP-based predictions are not inferior to empirical ML. Using an MLIP, we screened millions of molecules for blue emission. Although blue emission is not sufficient for an emitter, our results suggest that further development of virtual screening could focus on machine learned proxies for DFT prediction pipelines rather than models trained to experimental data.

papers.title: Data-Driven Discovery of Boronic Acid Catalysts for Amidation Reactions
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly recognized as a powerful tool for catalyst optimization in organic synthesis. Yet, applications are often restricted by the need for large datasets, programming expertise, and specialized knowledge in model development. Boronic acidcatalyzed amidation reactions represent an attractive target for AI-guided optimization because of their synthetic relevance, detailed mechanistic understanding, and the need for improved catalysts for amidations. Here, an AI-guided workflow for catalyst optimization in boronic acidcatalyzed amidation reactions was established using the large-language model ChatGPT for code generation and workflow development. A dataset was generated by high-throughput screening of 459 arylboronic acids and combined with DFT-derived steric and electronic descriptors of the catalysts for model training. The model enabled the identification of the unprecedented catalyst FIBA with higher activity than the benchmark catalyst MIBA. In addition, detailed data analysis of the highly active but poorly predicted diboronic acid catalyst DBA led to the identification of a distinct activation mode involving higher-order boronate aggregates that activate and preorganize the amine nucleophile. Thus, improved catalyst performance and new mechanistic insight were obtained through an AI-guided workflow.

papers.title: Giant barocaloric effect from spin crossover in a green nitroprusside framework†
papers.abstract: The interest in spin crossover for solid-state cooling is growing. We investigate the spin crossover transitions of [Fe(pyridine)2Fe(CN)5NO] and [Fe(pyrazine)Fe(CN)5NO] by single-crystal X-ray diffraction, high-pressure X-ray diffraction, magnetometry, and high-pressure calorimetry. The dehydrated form of the latter compound shows a reversible cooling effect (∆Tad,rev) of ∼15K at 1.2 kbar. This is high in the context of other reported spin-crossover barocalorics, and competitive within the field at large. The excellent performance results from a large barocaloric coefficient (dT1/2/dp = 35K kbar−1). In addition, the one-pot synthesis is simple and free from toxic solvents.

papers.title: Towards Zero-Waste PFAS Treatment Train: Regeneration of Ion Exchange Resins in Supercritical CO <sub>2</sub> Coupled with Supercritical Water Oxidation
papers.abstract: Ion-exchange resins (IXRs) are often used to remove PFAS from aqueous matrices; however, spent media generate secondary waste that must be disposed of. We demonstrate a waste-treatment strategy that combines IXR regeneration in a supercritical carbon dioxide (scCO 2 ) environment followed by destruction of PFAS-containing regenerants via supercritical water oxidation (SCWO). Screening of co-solvent formulation showed that HCl-amended ethanol/water mixture effectively extracted PFOA from both macroporous and gel-type resins marketed for single use. Macroporous IXR maintained sorbent capacity over five adsorption-regeneration cycles. Further optimization identified conditions for solvent reduction: an EtOH/H 2 O/HCl regenerant yielded regeneration efficiencies of ~97.6% for the gel-type and 99.7% for the macroporous resins within 60 minutes at flow rates corresponding to 9 BV. Comparison of the regenerant’s water content provided insights into the regeneration mechanism, progressing via (i) ion exchange in an H 2 O-rich hydration layer at the IXR surface followed by (ii) PFOA transport in the scCO 2 /EtOH-rich gas-like bulk flow. Downstream SCWO treatment of the regenerant shows complete PFOA defluorination. This treatment train advances sustainable PFAS management by combining sorbent reuse, reduced demand for non-toxic organic solvents, and end-of-life treatment of concentrated PFAS residuals.

papers.title: Spatially Refined Analysis of Emission Burdens and Equity from Light-, Medium-, and Heavy-Duty Vehicle Traffic in the United States
papers.abstract: We estimate block-level emission intensities of nitrogen oxides (NO X ) and fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) from on-road vehicle traffic for every census block in the United States, combining MOVES-based emission factors with street level traffic data. We use this spatially refined, computationally efficient, and policy-sensitive metric to evaluate emissions burden. Despite comprising less than 11% of vehicle kilometers traveled, we find that medium- and heavy-duty trucks account for 46% of NO X and 50% of PM 2.5 emission burden nationally — with PM 2.5 burden from trucks dominated by exhaust emissions while tire and brake wear constitute nearly half of light-duty vehicle PM 2.5 burden. People of color face emission burdens averaging 40% above the national mean, with Asian populations exceeding 60%, and lower-income populations face 20–25% higher burdens. Statistically significant racial-ethnic or income disparities are present in 85–89% of US counties. Critically, these disparities are not confined to large metropolitan areas. They are widespread across both urban and rural counties nationwide. We also show that spatial aggregation substantially attenuates estimated disparities of burdened groups, underscoring the importance of spatially refined analysis.

papers.title: Excited-State Planarization Couples Charge-Transfer Character and Spin-Orbit Coupling to Enable High Efficiency Solvatochromism in an Anti-Kasha Donor-Acceptor Phosphor
papers.abstract: A single, synthetically controllable structural coordinate capable of simultaneously enhancing charge-transfer (CT) character and spin-orbit coupling (SOC) is highly sought after in purely organic chromophore design, yet has not been demonstrated. We show that excited-state planarization (ESP) in an anthracene-anthraquinone donor-acceptor emitter is exactly such a coordinate, governing one electronic variable, the CT weight of the emissive singlet, that simultaneously sets SOC into an acceptor-localized triplet channel in a near-linear, quantified relationship (R2 = 0.997), and we propose this as a general, transferable design principle for donor-acceptor chromophores. The resulting CT character exhibits a Solvatochromic response that exceeds current literature values for a neutral, purely organic, small-molecule donor-acceptor chromophore, with a slope of 25,384 cm-1 per unit Δf and R2 = 0.928 across a nine-solvent panel, which is the best yet reported. Finally, the compound exhibits genuine room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) despite an anomalously small experimental singlet-triplet gap (0.08 eV), with emission confirmed, computationally and experimentally, to originate from the second triplet state rather than the lowest, a definitive instance of anti-Kasha phosphorescence; we provide a plausible, computationally supported mechanism for this behavior, in which reverse intersystem crossing (RISC) suppression is the most plausible explanation.

papers.title: Ligand Engineering for Ultrahigh-Light-Yield Lanthanide Complex Scintillators
papers.abstract: Scintillators featuring high light yield and low detection limit are critically important for high-energy radiation detection. Lanthanide complexes are attractive candidates due to their strong X-ray absorption, facile synthesis, and high photostability. However, their practical application has long been hindered by relatively low light yield. Here, we show that ligand engineering is a general and effective strategy for realizing lanthanide complex scintillators with ultrahigh light yield. By precisely tuning the π-conjugation extent of the β-diketone ligands across a rationally designed series of Tb(β-diketone)3·2H2O complexes, we identify Tb(acac)3·2H2O as an exceptional scintillator, whose exciton utilization efficiency is near-unity (99.3%). Under X-ray excitation, polycrystalline Tb(acac)3·2H2O delivers a light yield of 134,400 photons/MeV, which further increases to an unprecedented 180,000 photons/MeV in its single-crystal form. Ultrafast spectroscopic investigations directly reveal the underlying energy transfer mechanism of lanthanide complexes, highlighting the decisive role of the energy gap between ligand triplet states and lanthanide excited states, and establishing a broadly applicable ligand-engineering design principle for developing highly efficient lanthanide complex scintillators. We further demonstrate the practical utility of ultrahigh-light-yield Tb(acac)3·2H2O in X-ray intensifying screens, enabling at least a fivefold reduction in irradiation time compared with radiography performed without an intensifying screen. Overall, these results establish ligand engineering as a powerful paradigm for molecular scintillator design and open new opportunities for advanced radiation detection and imaging technologies.

papers.title: Toward transparent rigid packaging from sugarcane bagasse: a consistency-testing framework for nanocellulose–chitosan sheets
papers.abstract: Transparent rigid packaging is dominated by fossil-derived polymers, whereas fiber-based packaging is opaque. Dense cellulose nanofibril (CNF) and nanocrystal sheets are transparent as flat films, but whether transparency, wet stiffness and a three-dimensional shape can coexist in one sugarcane-bagasse-derived package has not been established, and one reported attempt to mold transparent CNF objects failed through drying shrinkage. This paper reports no experiments. It applies three consistency screens to a proposed bagasse CNF–chitosan–wax architecture: an optical screen derived from Debye–Bueche scattering theory, a wet-stiffness screen and a geometric forming screen, each propagated through a seeded Monte Carlo analysis over ranges traced to cited literature or explicitly stated assumptions. Under the stated optical-screen assumptions, a 100 µm wall at 10% haze and 5% voids requires a correlation length of about 10 nm or less, and because stiffness fixes a minimum wall thickness, the liquid the package must resist feeds back into the optical budget. Chitosan raises modeled wet stiffness mainly through cross-linking (median gain +1.1 GPa with it, -0.1 GPa without), but its gain in an acidic liquid is small and of uncertain sign. A tray, bowl and cup need total strain tolerances of 0.26, 0.67 and 1.10; no combination of the assumed ranges forms the cup (best case 0.96), which would need a flange wrinkling strain above 0.64. Pass shares depend on the priors, whereas the thresholds, the cup bound and the rank ordering do not. Barrier performance is untested, so every feasibility result is provisional.

papers.title: Surpassing the sensitivity limit and thermal quenching barrier in NIR luminescent thermometry in monazite BiPO4 concentrated with Nd
papers.abstract: Non-contact thermometry in the near infrared (NIR) region could enable minimally invasive thermal mapping in biological applications. Yet, existing probes often face trade-offs among sensitivity, brightness, and thermal stability. Here, we developed a single-ion Nd3+-based NIR thermometer, Bi1-xNdxPO4 (x = 0.20-0.40), via integrating several key structure-property considerations. The optimized composition Bi0.70Nd0.30PO4 in monazite structure , synthesized by a high-temperature solid-state reaction, delivers an ultra-high relative sensitivity of 6.62 %K-1 with temperature resolution of 0.29 K at 313 K, while exhibiting no measurable thermal quenching up to 673 K. Remarkably, its NIR-I emission is detectable even under an excitation power as low as 30 μW, highlighting efficient emission at ultra-low excitation. By integrating high sensitivity, thermal robustness, and low-power operation into a single Nd3+-emitting platform, this work establishes a materials design route toward practical NIR thermometry for biological and other demanding environments.

papers.title: FoldX interface ΔΔG depends on which structure it starts from, and a learned predictor does not: a cautionary analysis on glutaryl-CoA dehydrogenase
papers.abstract: FoldX and related methods are widely used to interpret missense variants, and their sensitivity to the input structure is documented: repair of the coordinates is mandatory, averaging over structural ensembles improves agreement with experiment, and the uncertainty of a FoldX folding ΔΔG has been put at roughly ±3 kcal/mol, with binding stability worse. What has not been asked is whether that uncertainty is spread evenly over a protein. We took 258 ClinVar missense variants in glutaryl-CoA dehydrogenase, a homotetramer, verified every reference residue against the 1SIQ structure and computed ΔΔG for the 124 classified pathogenic. Eighteen variants were then recomputed on three molecular dynamics snapshots of the same complex: six interface variants selected on their monomer-to-tetramer difference, six interface variants drawn at random, and six at least 10 Å from any contact. The displacement between the crystal-based value and the relaxed-frame mean had a median of 1.10, 1.38 and 0.20 kcal/mol in the three groups (random interface against distant, Mann-Whitney p = 0.0130), while frame-to-frame scatter was indistinguishable between them (Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.385). The variation is therefore positional, and it is not explained by noise in the mean. SAAMBE-3D, a learned interface predictor, run on the same eighteen variants and the same four structures, moved by a median of 0.075 kcal/mol at the interface and by nothing at all away from it, so the instability is largely a property of FoldX. It also depends on magnitude: G171R, scored at +22.53 kcal/mol, moved 2.7%, whereas A421V moved from +0.18 kcal/mol, which reads as tolerated, to +4.37 ± 2.22. Along the way we found that ThermoMPNN given a chain selector on a tetramer returns values identical to the isolated monomer at all 7,800 scanned positions. For variant interpretation the consequence is specific: at a subunit interface, in the range where a classification is actually in doubt, a single starting structure does not support a single number.

papers.title: Sulfur-Driven Surface Reconstruction of Nickel into NiOOH for Enhanced Electrooxidative Lignin Depolymerization
papers.abstract: text Finding strategies to maximize the density of catalytically active sites is pivotal to enhancing the electrooxidative depolymerization of lignin. Here, we present a Ni 3 S 2 precatalyst grown on nickel foam that, upon electrochemical activation, self-reconstructs into a NiOOH electrocatalyst with a high density of Ni 3+ active sites. This proliferation of active sites drastically increases the anodic currents for the oxygen evolution reaction as well as for benzyl alcohol oxidation. Operando Raman spectroscopy confirms the formation of the active NiOOH phase at low operating potential, while depth-profiling analysis reveals that this active phase extends tens of nanometers deep before transitioning to the underlying sulfide core. Electrooxidation of veratrylglycerol-beta-guaiacyl ether, a model dimer bearing a β-O-4 interunit linkage, selectively yields veratric acid and veratraldehyde, confirming the C α -C β bond cleavage. Applied to organosolv lignin extracted from pine wood, the electrocatalyst achieves substantial depolymerization, reducing the average molecular weight three-fold and releasing vanillic acid and vanillin as major monomeric products, reaching 22.4 % of the theoretical maximum monomer yield. Overall, this self-reconstructed architecture offers a compelling route for boosting the activity of oxyhydroxide-based electrodes while retaining their intrinsic selectivity.

papers.title: Water-Soluble Isocyanides for Passerini-Mediated Peptide Modification and Ligation
papers.abstract: Protein solubility is a key factor of peptide and protein modification and downstream application, yet chemical functionalization under aqueous conditions often compromise solubility. Here, we introduce a new class of ionic, water-soluble isocyanides for the functionalization of peptide carboxyl groups under aqueous conditions. By combining strong hydrogen-bonding motifs with ionic functionalities, these reagents provide enhanced water solubility while enabling modulation of peptide isoelectric points. The isocyanides were synthesized via a concise route and applied successfully in Passerini multicomponent reactions without observable precipitation. The resulting esterified peptides remained water-soluble even for highly hydrophobic sequences. They also served as competent substrates for omniligase-1-mediated ligation, with polar cationic modifications showing particularly favorable performance. These results demonstrate that rational isocyanide design can overcome solubility losses associated with peptide esterification, expand the scope of isocyanide-based ligation chemistry in aqueous environments, and provide a platform for tuning protein surface charge.

papers.title: Transition-Metal-Controlled α-C–H Acidity in Keto–Enol Tautomers: A DFT Study of Metal, Tautomer, and Substituent Effects
papers.abstract: Metal coordination provides an effective strategy for modulating the acidity of otherwise weak C–H bonds and controlling proton-transfer reactivity. Herein, we use density functional theory to investigate the effects of metal identity, tautomeric state, and substituent electronics on α-hydrogen acidity in metal-coordinated keto–enol systems. A systematic set of approximately 128 Au(III)-coordinated structures containing electron-donating and electron-withdrawing substituents was examined, with multiple coordination geometries and tautomeric forms considered to identify the thermodynamically preferred states. Au(III) coordination substantially enhances α-C–H acidity, with many systems exhibiting highly favorable deprotonation and strongly acidic computed pKa values. Electron-withdrawing substituents generally increase acidity, whereas electron-donating groups reduce it, although deviations observed for OMe and CF3 highlight the additional roles of charge delocalization and electrostatic stabilization. Kinetic analysis further reveals a strong dependence on tautomeric state: deprotonation of Au(III)-coordinated enol structures proceeds through barrierless pathways, whereas the corresponding keto structures require activation barriers of approximately 37–46 kcal mol−1. Comparative calculations with Co(III)-and Rh(III)-porphyrin complexes show substantially weaker acidification than Au(III), with both metals preferentially stabilizing the keto tautomer. These results demonstrate that metal identity, tautomeric structure, and substituent effects collectively govern α-C–H acidity and proton-transfer reactivity, highlighting the distinctive ability of Au(III) to promote α-hydrogen acidification in keto–enol systems.

papers.title: Ligand Design Principles Enabling High Efficiency Aqueous Iron Electrodeposition at Ambient Temperature
papers.abstract: Aqueous iron electrodeposition is an attractive route to enabling lower temperature, more modular ironmaking compared to conventional blast furnaces, but existing approaches require extreme pH, elevated temperatures and exhibit low Faradaic efficiency (FE) at elevated current density. A central challenge is the lack of design rules linking electrolyte chemistry to Fe2+ stability, FE and deposit purity. Here we demonstrate that pH-dependent electrolyte stability follows a volcano-type dependence on ligand functional group chemistry that is governed by a competition between metal–ligand complexation and ligand–solvent interactions. We determine α/β-hydroxycarboxylates optimize this balance and identify glycolate as a highly efficient coordinating ligand – enabling dense, ~99% pure iron deposits with >90% FE at thicknesses >100 μm and current densities approaching 1 A cm-2 under benign operating conditions (25ºC and pH 3.5). More broadly, these molecular design principles provide a framework for aqueous electrolyte development that should be transferrable to other electrochemical metal production processes.

papers.title: Graph-based machine learning model for adsorption energy prediction of CO2 hydrogenation intermediates on metal oxide catalysts
papers.abstract: Mixed metal oxide catalysts are highly active for CO2 hydrogenation to methanol and typically more selective than classical Cu-based catalysts. Adsorption energies of key reaction intermediates can serve as activity descriptors for high-throughput screening of metal oxide-dopant combinations, but this requires numerous computationally demanding density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) and adsorption energy prediction models offer faster alternatives, yet current architectures struggle with the structural and electronic complexity of mixed metal oxides introduced by dopants, oxygen vacancies, and diverse adsorption motifs. In this work, a graph-based Gaussian process regression (GPR) model is developed, combining graph representations of adsorption structures with node-level electronic descriptors. Trained on 638 adsorption structures of CO and all formate-pathway intermediates on pristine and Zn-doped ZrO2 and HfO2, as well as pristine In2O3 surfaces, the model achieves a test-set mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.16 eV. Leave-one-feature-out analysis identifies the d-band center, surface work function, and adsorbate LUMO energy as the dominant descriptors governing the prediction accuracy. Coupling the model with UMA small v1.2-D3 establishes an efficient workflow for rapid structural relaxation and accurate adsorption energy prediction, enabling high-throughput screening of mixed metal oxide catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation to methanol.

papers.title: Activationless Charge Transport in Heliobacterial Reaction Centers: Polarizable Cofactors Coupled to Strong Intraprotein Electric Fields
papers.abstract: We study rate-limiting steps of electron transfer following photoinduced charge separation to the primary acceptor A0 in a heliobacterial reaction center (HbRC). Two steps involved are electron transfer to the iron-sulfur cluster (ISC) FX of HbRC, followed by electron transfer to the FA ISC of a ferredoxin protein in solution. Ferredoxin forms a stable binding configuration with the reaction center as established by Brownian dynamics simulation. Molecular dynamics simulations are used to calculate the reaction times of ∼ 0.1µs (A0 → FX) and ∼ 3− 5µs (FX → FA). These two steps are the slowest in the overall electron transport in HbRC. Electron transfer to ferredoxin is irreversible since the calculated time of recombination to the closest A0 cofactor is ∼ 70 ms. All reactions show near-zero activation barriers when cofactors’ polarizabilities are included in the calculations. The overall robust operation of solar energy conversion in HbRCs is allowed by combining cofactors’ polarizabilities with strong local intraprotein electric fields.

papers.title: On how cell shape determines bactericidal effects of nanopatterned surfaces
papers.abstract: Nanopatterned surfaces inactivate bacteria by mechanically deforming adherent cells, yet design guidelines remain inconsistent and studies rarely isolate the role of cell shape. Here, we show how cell shape governs responses to nanopatterned surfaces. We develop a thermodynamic model coupling envelope stretching and bending with cell-surface adhesion to compare spherical and rod-shaped bacteria with identical cross-sections. We find that nanopatterning increases strain for both shapes, while cell shape changes how cells attain that strain. We show that spherical and rod-shaped cells adopt different adhesion geometries and energy balances even when they experience similar strains. Rod-shaped cells reach higher strains at lower nanopillar densities over much of the design space, while nanopillar radius and density tune cell shape-dependent strain differences. We identify nanopatterns that preferentially strain either shape or balance their responses using Pareto analysis. Together, our results establish cell shape as a key design consideration for tailoring bactericidal nanopatterned materials.

papers.title: Synthetic Methodologies to Access Fused Six-Membered Phosphorus Heterocycles
papers.abstract: π-Conjugated molecules are essential in a wide range of modern technologies: organic electronics, sensing and biomedical applications. The incorporation of heteroatoms into fused aromatic systems represents a key strategy to modulate their optoelectronic properties. While nitrogen, sulfur and oxygen have been extensively investigated in this context, phosphorus remains far less explored, despite offering a unique combination of properties: tunable oxidation states, rich coordination chemistry, non-planar geometry at heterocyclic rings, and a strong ability to lower the LUMO energy of π-systems. These properties make six-membered phosphorus heterocycles especially attractive building blocks with capabilities that other heteroatoms simply cannot provide. However, the synthetic methodologies available to incorporate these heterocycles into large fused π-conjugated architectures remain underdeveloped, hampering broader exploration of their extraordinary potential. In this review, we aim to offer synthetic and organometallic chemists a starting point to identify current limitations and develop new, more versatile strategies for incorporating these heterocycles into fused architectures, and, in turn, a practical guide for materials scientists seeking to design new π-extended phosphorus systems. In particular, we provide a systematic catalog of the cyclization reactions reported to date for the preparation of six-membered phosphorus heterocycles fused at different positions to aromatic rings, organized around five model structures according to the bond(s) at which fusion takes place, from metal-free strategies to the transition-metal-mediated C-P bond-forming methodologies that have driven much of the recent progress. We anticipate that this overview will encourage new, more efficient synthetic routes to fused phosphorus heterocycles, broadening access to this underexploited class of π-extended systems.

papers.title: Electronic Structure, Bonding Topology, and Photophysical Properties of the Low-Valent Beryllium Cluster CpBe2NO: A Multireference and Real-Space Wavefunction Analysis
papers.abstract: A comprehensive ab initio investigation of the cyclopentadienyl-beryllium nitrosyl complex (CpBe2NO) was conducted using complete active space self-consistent field (CASSCF), strongly contracted n-electron valence state perturbation theory (SC-NEVPT2), complete active space second-order perturbation theory (CASPT2), and symmetry-adapted cluster/similarity transformed equation-of-motion domain-based local pair-natural orbital coupled-cluster (STEOM-DLPNO-CCSD) methods, in conjunction with quantum theory of atoms in molecules (QTAIM) and real-space wavefunction topology analyses. The singlet–triplet energy gap indicates a triplet ground state at the CASSCF level. Relaxed CASPT2 potential energy surface scans along the Be–Be internuclear coordinate establish an equilibrium singlet bond distance of 2.200 Å, a dissociation energy (De) of 21.11 kcal mol-1, and a harmonic vibrational frequency (ωe) of 593.75 cm-1. Active-space natural orbital populations and QTAIM bond critical point (BCP) decompositions demonstrate pronounced multireference character and multi-center metallic bonding. STEOM-DLPNO-CCSD excited-state calculations map vertical transition energies, oscillator strengths, and unrelaxed dipole moments across the low-lying singlet manifold. Real-space descriptors—including the electron localization function (ELF), localized orbital locator (LOL), reduced density gradient (RDG), and interaction region indicator (IRI)—further elucidate the electronic shell structure and attractive metallic interaction basins.

papers.title: Hybrid-CatBoost: an empirical comparison of molecular representations for aqueous-solubility prediction on the TDC benchmark
papers.abstract: Aqueous-solubility prediction depends on both molecular representation and the definition of the target. We compared fingerprint, descriptor, hybrid, and graph-based representations on the TDC Solubility_AqSolDB benchmark using five official scaffold splits and a fixed test set of 1,997 records. Hybrid-CatBoost achieved a five-run test MAE of 0.749631 ± 0.016216 TDC logS units, compared with 0.764558 ± 0.009666 for descriptor-only CatBoost. However, the corresponding validation improvement was small (ΔMAE = −0.004932) and occurred in only two of five matched splits. Errors increased toward both target extremes and showed opposite-signed residual biases. These results indicate that descriptor-based models capture most of the predictive signal in this benchmark, while the added Morgan fingerprint provides only a modest and split-dependent benefit. Interpretation is limited by incomplete assay metadata and the use of a single fixed test set, which does not provide external validation.

papers.title: Electrochemical passivation of LiFePO4 cathodes by polaron crystallization during cell cycling
papers.abstract: The nature of intermediate phases during LiFePO 4 cycling and their role in limiting lithium transport remain unresolved. Building on our pioneering application of operando 57 Fe nuclear resonance vibrational spectroscopy to working batteries, we combine this element-specific probe with machine-learning-based spectral analysis to resolve and quantify a vibrational signature of an intermediate component distinct from the LiFePO 4 and FePO 4 end-members. Its maximum molar fraction reaches nearly 20% at cycling rates of C/10, C/5 and C/2, revealing a rateindependent formation of intermediate phase. The intermediate exhibits additional distinct feature in the Fe-projected phonon density of states, suggesting localized Fe 3+ hole-polaron environments, which is supported by atomistic simulations. These observations motivate a working hypothesis linking the persistence of the intermediate to restricted lithium transport. We propose that local accumulation of hole polarons along with elastic stress at phase interface promotes their crystallization into an ordered superstructure at the advancing phase boundary. Ordering restricts polaron motion and through lithium ion–polaron coupling reduces lithium-ion mobility across the intermediate layer. This layer could therefore to certain extent passivate individual particles against further delithiation, allowing transformation to proceed elsewhere in the electrode. The proposed mechanism offers an explanation for the nearly rate-independent intermediate phase fraction and identifies polaron ordering as a potential target for improving high-rate performance, for example through dopants that inhibit polaron crystallization.

papers.title: Computational shielding of chikungunya viral prefusion with permeable cyclic-minipeptides
papers.abstract: Permeable cyclic-minipeptide-conformer candidates were computationally co-generated with the aim of shielding the protected prefusion-loops (FL) of the envelop E2E1 protein heterodimers of chikungunya virus (CHIKV). This work attempts to prevent some of the earliest pH-dependent dissociation E2E1 events which trigger CHIKV fusion/ infectivity by fully exposing their FL. To co-generate de novo candidates, a minimized prefusion CHIKV E2E1 (minE2E1) model including minimal E2-protective and E1-FL sequences was targeted by BoltzGen. The advantages of the cogenerated top-affinity nanoMolar candidates include higher affinities compared to previous neutralizing peptides, easier chemical synthesis, low antigenicity and strong conformer stabilities. Top-affinity parents were computationally mutated to derive thousands of membrane-permeable candidates conserving their cyclization, targets and affinities. A few membrane-permeable top-affinity candidates may serve for experimentally-guided validation of possible inhibition of CHIKV fusion and infection.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Powered Simulations of Confinement-Driven <sup>129</sup> Xe Nuclear Spin Relaxation
papers.abstract: The rate at which a nuclear spin returns to equilibrium encodes the dynamics of its surroundings, information the chemical shift, a time-averaged quantity, cannot provide. Building on a previous dual-model machine learning framework, combining a fine-tuned atomistic foundation model (FT-AFM) for molecular dynamics (MD) with an NMR-ML model predicting the 129 Xe magnetic shielding tensor, we compute the chemical shift anisotropy-driven 129 Xe spin-lattice ( T 1 ) and spin-spin ( T 2 ) relaxation times of xenon confined in carbon nanotubes by extending the Redfield theory treatment to arbitrary nanotube orientations relative to the external magnetic field. Across various temperatures, nanotube diameters, and Xe loadings, both relaxation times evolve non-monotonically in several cases, and for systems whose Xe densities match those of experimental free xenon gas, confinement shortens T 1 by up to fivefold. We also show that T 1 provides an indirect NMR probe of single-file Xe diffusion. This work establishes FT-AFMs and NMR-ML models as a fast, accurate, and general route to the nuclear spin relaxation of confined Xe across a broad range of porous materials.

papers.title: Developing An Entirely Mechanochemical Synthesis of Cram’s Cavitands and Carcerands
papers.abstract: We report the development of an entirely mechanochemical synthesis of a set of iconic and complex supramolecular targets, Cram’s carcerands and cavitands, using a sequence of mechanochemical, liquid-assisted steps. By demonstrating how mechanochemical methods can be adapted to each segment of carcerand synthesis, this work highlights the benefits and opportunities mechanochemistry offers for simpler, high-yielding synthesis of complex targets. This work exploits grinding based on dual asymmetric centrifugal motion, which provides high autogenous frictional heating to drive chemical reactivity and, in some cases, permits thick and resinous reaction systems to mix without solidifying. The analogous media-free approach provided efficient mixing when heating was not required. Using these methods, we show that a set of phenolic cavitands, which are crucial precursors to a wide set of carcerands and hemicarcerands, can be synthesized rapidly, in high yields, using minimal organic solvent, and with improved operational simplicity, and that the final capsule-like carcerands can also be assembled mechanochemically, despite the common expectation that effectiveness of such supramolecular transformations requires high dilutions.

papers.title: Talking to instruments: device-integration standards for self-driving laboratories
papers.abstract: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) are rapidly outgrowing the single-instrument prototype, scaling into multi-instrument and multi-site platforms that run autonomous discovery across chemistry, materials science, biotechnology, pharmaceutical re-search and adjacent domains. What now decides whether an SDL can scale, share its integrations and federate experiments is no longer the algorithms or the robots, but the software layer that orchestrates heterogeneous devices. Today that layer is the bottleneck: a fast-growing ecosystem of open-source orchestrators in which most have built device integration on their own bespoke conventions instead of adopting a formally governed standard. The result is predictable and costly. Integrations do not transfer between laboratories, orchestrators cannot interoperate and many new SDLs rebuild their device-control layer from scratch. Crucially, this is an engineering coordination problem, not a fundamental scientific one and therefore among the most tractable bottlenecks in autonomous science. We map the device-integration standards landscape onto the open-source orchestrator ecosystem, compare the leading options and give scenario-driven guidance on when to use each. We then translate the requirements of autonomous operation into a concrete deliverable: a set of testable engineering criteria and a weighted procurement scorecard that defines an autonomous-ready control interface and gives institutional buyers the leverage to demand it; these requirements do not change as orchestration turns agentic: whether an instrument is driven by a program or by a language-model agent through a model-facing protocol, it is only as safe and reliable as the interface it exposes. Adopted at scale, these requirements turn device integration from a burden repaid lab by lab into shared infrastructure,

papers.title: SMILES serialization changes activity-cliff annotations in the MoleculeACE benchmark
papers.abstract: MoleculeACE is a widely used benchmark that annotates activity-cliff compounds in 30 ChEMBL datasets and reports that machine-learning models predict them poorly. Its “soft consensus” criterion admits a compound pair when any of three similarities reaches 0.9: ECFP4 Tanimoto similarity, Tanimoto similarity of anonymized molecular graphs, or normalized Levenshtein similarity between SMILES strings. The first two are computed after parsing; the third operates on the supplied strings, which the benchmark code does not canonicalize. This study held molecules, potencies, thresholds and code fixed and varied only how the same molecules werewritten. A re-implementation reproduced the distributed labels exactly in 27 of 30 datasets, and canonical round-tripping changed amedian of 0.00% of labels. Re-serializing themolecules with two independent cheminformatics toolkits, with every rewritten string verified to encode the original molecule, changed a median of 8.98% (Indigo) and 9.48% (Open Babel) of compound labels; Kekulé SMILES from RDKit changed 5.23%, and randomized SMILES 17.05%. The graph-derived criteria were invariant across all rewrites. Because MoleculeACE stratifies its train/test split on the cliff label, changing the labels caused split membership to approach that of an independent redraw (31.3% of compounds reassigned, against a 32.21% ceiling). An end-to-end repair, with serialization-invariant labels, re-derived splits and retrained descriptorbased models, moved the pooled cliff penalty by −0.006 to +0.020 log units; every confidence interval included zero against a minimum detectable effect of 0.041–0.057, and for SVM the shift fell within the variability of same-definition split redraws of comparable magnitude. The distributed annotation is therefore reproducible but not invariant to valid serialization. Benchmarks that retain string-based criteria should specify and enforce the canonicalization contract (toolkit, version and output mode); otherwise, labels should be defined on parsed molecular representations. Serialization-invariant labels, splits and per-molecule predictions are released.

papers.title: Raman Spectroscopy Reveals Isotope-specific Hydrogen Bond Kinetics in a Spherical Droplet leading to Preferential Evaporation of D2O in H2O-D2O Mixture
papers.abstract: The evaporation of a spherical droplet having a pure solvent or a mixture of isotopic forms is fundamental to atmospheric physics, and critical for studying interfacial fluid dynamics, and hydrogen-bond kinetics. Understanding the hydrogen/deuterium bonded structural dynamics at molecular level during evaporation of isotopic water mixture (H2O/D2O) is important for understanding non-equilibrium phase transitions. In this work, we investigated real-time evaporation kinetics of spherical water droplets on superhydrophobic surface by time - dependent Raman spectroscopic method. Specifically, the results give an account for the variation of each H - or D-bonded clusters (ranging from fully tetrahedral ice-like structure to free water molecule) with time in the mixture from the time - dependent intensity change of each distinct vibrational stretching band of O-H or O-D. For pure H2O, the O-H peak intensities for all the clusters were decreasing with time, whereas for pure D2O, the ice-like structures vanished quickly with simultaneous increase in the free D2O molecules. In the mixture of H2O-D2O, based on Raman signal of each species, our experimental measurements suggested that the species having O-D or D2O was evaporating faster in comparison to the species having O-H or H2O. The results were also supported by the molecular dynamics simulation, which revealed that the bulk D2O was moving to the surface, and evaporating faster than H2O molecules.

papers.title: A Biobased Epoxy Resin with Sequential Thermoplastic-to-Thermoset Curing Enables Removable-to-Permanent Adhesive Bonding
papers.abstract: Adhesives are commonly designed either as reworkable thermoplastics or permanently crosslinked thermosets. Here, sequential thermoplastic-to-thermoset curing enables a simple two-component formulation based on a bio-based epoxy resin to function first as a removable hot-melt adhesive and subsequently as a permanent structural adhesive. Reaction of diglycidyl ether of vanillyl alcohol (DGEVA) and anilinium methanesulfonate at 110 °C produces a thermoplastic intermediate that is solid at room temperature but flows upon reheating and dissolves in selected solvents. This intermediate forms load-bearing joints that can be thermally debonded and rebonded or disassembled by dissolution. Further heating induces crosslinking and converts the same adhesive layer into a permanent epoxy network, increasing the apparent lap-shear strength nearly eightfold and rendering the joint resistant to disassembly under the same solvent conditions. This curing sequence therefore assigns reworkability and high-strength permanent bonding to successive adhesive states within the same formulation.

papers.title: Computational assessment, against criteria specified in advance, of a Na+/Ag+ ion-exchange route to Ag2MgSiO4, a predicted wurtzite-derived silver silicate
papers.abstract: Many metastable inorganic compounds exist only because a synthetic route delivers them, and database screening is poorly placed to find them. Topotactic ion exchange is such a route: at low temperature it swaps the mobile cation of a known parent for another, ideally while the framework stays intact, yet it is rarely assessed computationally before synthesis. We test whether a simple exchange-energy criterion, specified in advance and checked against independent calculations, can nominate a credible target. Computed with a machine-learned interatomic potential, the criterion reproduced the sign of 42 published DFT exchange enthalpies (36/36 for |∆H| ≥ 10 kJ mol−1) and selected Ag2MgSiO4, to be made from Na2MgSiO4 in molten AgNO3. Density functional theory gives an exchange energy of about −58 kJ mol−1 per Ag, within the ±10 kJ mol−1 window around three reported preparations of silver silicates and germanates from sodium parents in molten AgNO3, and an energy above the hull (0.038–0.042 eV atom−1) like that of known silver silicates. The Pna21 structure is dynamically stable in the harmonic approximation (0 K). Calculated Ag+ hop barriers are comparable to or lower than those of a reported Ag+ conductor, and the HSE06 gap, calibrated on one literature value, is about 3 eV, at the violet edge of the visible range. These are 0 K predictions; no synthesis was attempted, and the closest precedent is Ag2MnSiO4, so a single exchange experiment can confirm or refute them (incomplete exchange or changes in particle size and shape are reported in some precedents).

papers.title: TiO2 as active site and protective layer on Sn doped spinel cobalt oxide for acidic OER
papers.abstract: Green hydrogen is expected to play a major role in the decarbonisation of hard-to-electrify sectors such as shipping, aviation, steel, and fertiliser. Cost effective acidic water electrolysis to produce green hydrogen requires active, stable non-noble metal oxide catalysts, however non-noble metal oxides tend to be unstable at oxidative potentials in acidic media. In this work we show that Sn doped Co 3 O 4 exhibits improved activity, while using an ultrathin TiO 2 overlayer improves stability greatly without hindering activity. The maximal activity, at 5% Sn content, was comparable to the state-of-the-art for non-noble PEM anode catalysts, while the maximal stabilising effect produced by the overlayer was more than eightfold.

papers.title: Metal-Free Traceless Directing Group-Assisted Cascade Cyclisation of 2-Alkynylquinazolinones for the Synthesis of Enpyrroloquinazolinones and Their Anticancer Activity
papers.abstract: Pyrroloquinazolinones, representing the pharmacological scaffold of the natural product Luotonin A, exhibit significant biological activities. Distinguishing from metal-catalysed methodologies, this study delineates a metal-and photocatalystfree strategy for the synthesis of enpyrroloquinazolinone derivatives via a cascade Michael addition-cyclisation-denitrative aromatisation, involving 2-alkynyl quinazolinones and nitroalkenes, which renders the nitro group into a traceless directing group. The resultant enpyrroloquinazolinone analogues underwent systematic evaluation for their anticancer efficacy and potential to activate caspases 3/7 against A549 (NSCLC) and SW480 (colorectal) cancer cell lines. Furthermore, molecular modelling indicates that these enpyrroloquinazolinones possess substantial potential as effective inhibitors of topoisomerase I, providing a promising foundation for the continued development of topoisomerase I inhibitors for therapeutic interventions.

papers.title: Off-line LCxLC-Mass Spectrometry Workflow using CID and EAD for the Quantification and Comprehensive Structural Double Bond Characterization of Glycerophospholipids in Plasma Samples
papers.abstract: Here we describe an automated workflow using a PAL Robotic Tool Changer (RTC) system for plasma lipid sample preparation and off-line two-dimensional liquid chromatography (LCxLC) separation. The orthogonal chromatographic platform couples hydrophilic interaction liquid chromatography (HILIC) in the first dimension with rapid reversed-phase liquid chromatography (RPLC) in the second dimension, facilitated by automated fraction collection at 10-second intervals into 96-well plates. Lipid profiling and structural identification strategies were evaluated using collision-induced dissociation (CID) and electron-activated dissociation (EAD) across data-dependent acquisition (DDA), dataindependent acquisition (DIA / SWATH), and high-resolution multiple reaction monitoring (HRMRM) modes. Standard Reference Material NIST SRM 1950 (Human Plasma) was employed for lipid quantification and double-bond characterization of phosphatidylcholines (PCs). By combining automated modified Matyas liquid-liquid extraction, and off-line LCxLC, a total of 115 PC’s lipids could be detected in SRM 1950 plasma sample. For 74 PC’s including isomers, double assignments could be proposed based on the EAD spectra.

papers.title: An Ion-Pair Complex-Enabled Photoinduced Cleavage of the Trifluoromethyl Thianthrenium Salt
papers.abstract: Trifluoromethyl thianthrenium salts represent valuable reagents in photocatalysis; however, their activation traditionally necessitates external one-electron donors, such as photocatalysts, electron-donor-acceptor complexes. Direct photoexcitation can proceed without exogenous one-electron donors, thereby circumventing the stringent redox potential constraints inherent in the ground and excited states of conventional photocatalytic systems. Such direct excitation facilitates a transition of substrates to an electronically excited state, promoting homolytic cleavage to release the CF 3 • radical. Nevertheless, this process typically requires near-ultraviolet excitation (390 nm) to attain the high-energy excited singlet state of the substrate. In this study, we report a pioneering strategy involving the design of an acid-base ternary ion-pair complex utilising trifluoromethyl thianthrenium salts. In contrast to conventional ion-pair complex catalysis, this methodology eliminates the requirement for a photocatalyst and bypasses the single electron transfer process. This conceptual advancement lowers the activation energy to the excited singlet state of TT-CF 3 OTf, enabling the generation of CF 3 • species via homolytic cleavage under industrially preferred 450 nm excitation. As a proof of concept, the ion-pair complex was utilised to facilitate the trifluoromethylative difunctionalisation of diverse alkenes. This method yields pharmaceutically significant compounds and natural products with moderate to high yields. Both DFT calculations and experimental results demonstrate the formation of an ion-pairing complex, with binding constants K a of 4.36 in acetonitrile and 2.28 in chloroform, the latter increasing to 4.20 upon the addition of KOAc. This methodology exhibits substantial potential for future applications within biological and biochemical contexts.

papers.title: Decoupling Thermal Kinetics and Structural Evolution in HfO2 RRAM via Broadband Impedance Spectroscopy: A SPICE Model for Analog Applications
papers.abstract: The integration of HfO2-based resistive random-access memory (RRAM) into analog circuits and neuromorphic hardware requires accurate, physics-based small-signal models. In this work, we employ broadband impedance spectroscopy to physically isolate the distinct structural and kinetic components governing the alternating current (AC) response of TiN/Ti/HfO2/W memristive devices, thereby providing such a model. Measurements were performed over a wide temperature range (77 K to 350 K), across multiple device areas, and at various resistance states controlled by compliance current. The AC response reveals distinct relaxation processes, which are accurately described by an electrical equivalent circuit that isolates the individual electrical signatures of the filament constriction, the interfacial boundary, and the bulk conductive path. The low-frequency relaxation, attributed to the filament constriction, exhibits a strong exponential temperature dependence, allowing for the extraction of the thermal activation energy associated with trap-assisted charge transport within the oxygen vacancy-rich gap. In contrast, the bulk-related response is temperature-independent but strongly depends on the resistive state. The model is further validated by the scaling of the high‑frequency pole with device area, confirming its geometric origin. As a result, our model decouples the thermal kinetics from the structural evolution of conductive filaments in emerging non-volatile memories. Finally, to demonstrate the practical utility of this model, it is implemented in LTSpice to design all-memristive analog filters and a neuromorphic signal mixer. This approach takes advantage of the properties of both pristine and programmed devices to eliminate the need for conventional passive components.

papers.title: Physics-Guided Soft Sensing under Sparse Laboratory Measurements and Temporal Regime Shifts in Industrial Monoammonium Phosphate Production
papers.abstract: Industrial plants collect high-frequency telemetry while critical quality variables may be measured only every few hours. We study soft sensing for an industrial monoammonium phosphate process using 260,642 one-minute records and 1,325 paired laboratory observations. The grey-box model reconstructs latent acid properties from conductivity and combines them with material-balance calculations to estimate molar ratio and downstream density. Validation is entirely chronological: nine pre-gap rolling tests, a short-term regime-transfer test, a strict external post-gap test on 438 future laboratory pairs, and ten post-gap rolling comparisons. To prevent uncontrolled extrapolation, the conductivity input to the fitted latent-property mappings is limited to the range observed in the corresponding training data. Ridge and LSBoost remain more accurate than the physics-guided model, particularly in the independent long-horizon evaluation. The results show that physical structure improves interpretability but does not by itself ensure temporal robustness, motivating regime-aware monitoring, recalibration, and fallback logic for industrial virtual telemetry.

papers.title: Guiding chromatographic purification through data-driven condition recommendations
papers.abstract: Purification is essential for isolating compounds for reliable characterization and subsequent experiments; however, suitable chromatographic conditions are often still selected through trial and error. Herein, we present a data-driven framework that recommends a stationary phase or separation mode, solvent, and solvent ratio to support thin-layer chromatography (TLC) screening and column chromatography (CC) purification. Using purification records from publications and laboratory notebooks, we developed models to predict TLC and CC conditions. Models using product structures alone or in combination with reactant and agent information were compared across prediction tasks and data sources. Experimental evaluation of 11 previously unreported compounds demonstrated that ranked recommendations could guide TLC screening and the selection of CC purification conditions. Additionally, a web application was developed to provide users with flexible access to the prediction models. The proposed framework supports the selection of practical purification conditions and provides a foundation for integrating purification planning into future autonomous experimental workflows.

papers.title: Decoding Polyurethane Breakdown: A QM/MM MD Exploration of UMG-SP3 Urethanase Catalysis
papers.abstract: Polyurethane (PU) low-cost production and versatility propelled its widespread daily usage. However, due to a lack of efficient end-of-life waste treatment options, this recalcitrant polymer tends to accumulate, becoming hazardous. Enzyme depolymerization emerged as a promising 2 alternative to tackle this global problem. Accordingly, three metagenome-based urethanases were discovered (UMG-SP1, 2 and 3). Despite several efforts being made to understand their catalysis, none of the studies accounted for full protein sampling. To address this, we employed an umbrella sampling-based quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics methodology to explore UMG-SP3catalyzed urethane bond hydrolysis. Our results revealed that the hydrolytic mechanism occurred in two sequential stages: i) acylation; and ii) deacylation. The first stage was rate-limiting, with an energetic barrier of 21.6 kcal.mol-1, corresponding to the formation of the acyl-enzyme state and the release of an alcohol (leaving group). Remarkably, the energetic barrier was in agreement with the previously reported values for the UMG-SP2 homolog. In addition, the enzyme shown preference for the cleavage of the C-O bond instead of the C-N bond. However, we observed that the overall reaction was endergonic, with a product-state Gibbs free energy of 8.3 kcal.mol-1. UMG-SP3 has previously been shown to be less stable than the other UMG-SPs. As a result, its more mobile active site may be less effective at stabilizing the released product, increasing the associated free energy. Hence, to improve the likelihood of industrial implementation, the mechanistic data should be leveraged to rationally engineer a more stable and efficient enzyme. Altogether, these findings can pave the way for improving enzymatic depolymerization of PU.

papers.title: Reductive Deoxygenation of Benzylic Alcohols by Low-Valent Titanium Alkoxides
papers.abstract: 2 ABSTRACT: Reductive deoxygenation of benzylic alcohols is a valuable transformation that yields alkylated aromatic compounds. Even though hydroxyl group in these substrates is considered as activated, general mild methods for their reduction remain elusive. While many existing protocols require acidic reagents or additives detrimental for functional groups, milder alternatives are efficient only with 1° benzylic alcohols and diarylmethanols. Here we report that low-valent titanium alkoxides promote deoxygenation of 1°, 2° and 3° benzylic alcohols under basic conditions compatible with acetal, alkene, ester, amide, nitrile, aryl halides and benzyloxy groups. The low-valent titanium reagents were generated in situ by the reduction of Ti(OiPr)4 either with a dihydrobenzimidazol derivative under irradiation with blue light or with pieces of sodium metal. Mechanistic studies revealed that the deoxygenation step is promoted by Ti(III) alkoxides, while OH-groups of the substrate serve as a source of H-atoms.

papers.title: Toward a New Paradigm for Renewable Biopolymer Selection: A Structure–Processing–Architecture–Property–Scalability Framework (Alginate, Cellulose, Lignin, Chitosan, and Starch)
papers.abstract: Renewable biopolymers are increasingly explored as alternatives to fossil-derived materials, yet bio-based origin alone does not determine performance or commercial relevance. This review compares alginate, lignin, cellulose, chitosan, and starch through an integrated structure–processing–architecture–property–scalability framework. Molecular functionality — carboxylate-rich, aromatic, hydroxyl-rich, amine-rich, crystalline, branched, and charged structures — is linked to processing pathways and to the resulting coatings, fibers, crosslinked networks, porous structures, carbon materials, and composite architectures. A dedicated cross-cutting discussion then argues why the three comparison axes dominant in the existing literature, chemistry, biodegradability, and application category, each fail, on their own, to predict which material and processing combination is actually useful for a given job, and what a comparison needs to include instead. The review closes with application-specific design rules to support material and processing selection for sustainable packaging, thermal insulation, water purification and separations, CO2 capture, energy storage and electrocatalysis, biomedical scaffolds and controlled release, and construction materials.

papers.title: Decoding the Sequence Determinants of DNA Cleavage in Histidine-Containing Copper(II) Metallopeptides
papers.abstract: The increasing global incidence of cancer, emerging viral infections, and antimicrobial resistance highlights the urgent need for innovative therapeutics with novel mechanisms of action. Nucleic acids, central to genetic information processing, are promising targets for therapeutic intervention through selective cleavage. Inspired by the biological activity of DNases and RNases, peptide-based metallonucleases—particularly those containing histidine—have emerged as versatile agents with tunable activity and potential applications in treating genetic diseases, including cancer. By analyzing a set of six copper(II) complexes with different histidine-containing tripeptides, this work investigates how peptide sequence influences several factors determining DNA-cleavage efficiency, such as speciation and conditional affinity at physiological pH, coordination mode, DNA binding, and ROS production. These findings offer a new framework for designing peptide-based copper nucleases and possibly identify a non-ATCUN sequence as a promising lead structure.

papers.title: Dopant-Controlled Gas Adsorption and Electronic Response in AlN-and BP-Doped Two-Dimensional Fullerene Networks: A DFT and Ab Initio Molecular Dynamics Study
papers.abstract: Using density functional theory (DFT) and ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD), we investigated the structural stability, electronic properties, and gas adsorption behaviour of AlN-and BP-doped quasi-2D C60 fullerene networks (C58AlN and C58BP). Both heteroatom-pair substitutions maintain structural and thermal stability. Dopant chemistry strongly governs adsorption preferences: C58AlN exhibits robust binding (CO2:-2.79 eV, H2O:-1.27 eV, N2:-0.50 eV), whereas C58BP shows weak interactions. Charge analysis confirms significant electronic redistribution during adsorption. Crucially, adsorption strength does not dictate sensing performance; N2 triggers the highest conductivity modulation despite weaker adsorption. Overall, heteroatom-pair engineering offers a valuable strategy to tune gas capture and sensing capabilities in fullerene-based 2D materials.

papers.title: Membraneless microdroplets generate thermodynamically distinct states of water under fully hydrated conditions
papers.abstract: Water is indispensable for life, yet aqueous environments can thermodynamically disfavor dehydration-driven condensation reactions relevant to prebiotic polymer formation. Whether hydrated, dynamically reorganizing compartments can establish hydration thermodynamics distinct from the surrounding solution remains unclear. Here, we show that membraneless polyester microdroplets derived from prebiotically plausible α-hydroxy acids sustain spatially organized hydration environments during thermal structural reorganization. Combining high-speed scanning ion conductance microscopy, spatially resolved Raman spectroscopy and temperature-dependent wide-angle X-ray scattering, we resolve dynamic interfaces, spatial hydration gradients and reversible polymer organization. Crucially, Raman-derived average hydrogen-bond coordination within the droplets remains lower and markedly less temperature-dependent than in the corresponding aqueous solution. Van’t Hoff analysis of intact versus broken hydrogen bonds reveals attenuated apparent enthalpic and entropic contributions to redistribution. Together, these findings demonstrate that dynamically reconfiguring polymer-rich compartments can maintain distinct hydration thermodynamics during thermal perturbation, linking the physical chemistry of water with soft compartmentalization under hydrated conditions.

papers.title: What sixty studies of V2O5 supercapacitor electrodes can and cannot tell us: a validated dataset with study-grouped analysis
papers.abstract: Vanadium pentoxide (V 2 O 5 ) is one of the most studied electrode materials for supercapacitors. Hundreds of studies report its specific capacitance, but it is not clear whether these data can be combined to predict the performance of a new electrode. To examine this, 974 records from 60 published studies were collected into one dataset, and each record was linked to its source. Within each study, the data behave as expected. Capacitance decreases as the charge-discharge rate increases, and this decrease is well described by a simple power law. Adding a composite partner or a dopant raises the capacitance by about 1.6 times compared with pure V 2 O 5 tested in the same study. Between studies, however, the picture is different. The median capacitance reported for pure V 2 O 5 differs up to 27 times from one study to another. A model trained on some studies could not predict the values reported in others (R 2 = 0.11), although a random split of the same data suggested good accuracy (R 2 = 0.76). One likely reason is that key electrode details, such as mass loading and active mass, are reported for only about one fifth of the records. A short list of details that future studies should report is proposed. The dataset and scripts are openly available.

papers.title: Cu(II) complexes based on morpholine-substituted thiosemicarbazones show reduced toxicity in normal cells
papers.abstract: Three novel Cu(II) complexes with 3,4-dimethoxybenzylidene-substituted thiosemicarbazones were synthesized and evaluated for anticancer, antibacterial, and antioxidant activities. Our recent structure-activity relationship studies showed that Cu(II) complexes containing 3,4-dimethoxybenzylidene-substituted ligands can display potent anticancer activity, reaching single-digit IC 50 values, which prompted further investigation of this structural motif. The complexes examined here showed moderate antibacterial activity and distinct antioxidant profiles in the ABTS, DPPH, and ORAC-FL assays. Among them, the morpholine-containing complex Cu(dm-TSC-morph) 2 showed the most favorable anticancer selectivity, retaining low-micromolar activity against SK-MEL-28 and A-375 melanoma cells (IC 50 = 6.58 ± 0.71 and 9.20 ± 1.52 μM, respectively) while exhibiting lower toxicity toward BJ, HUVEC, and HEK-293 cells, with selectivity indices up to 4.88. Studies of mechanism of action revealed that Cu(dm-TSC-morph) 2 induced intracellular oxidative stress in melanoma cells. These findings identify the morpholine-containing derivative as the most promising compound in the analyzed series and support further development of selective Cu(II) thiosemicarbazone complexes.

papers.title: Reaction-Network Kinetics of Lignin Hydrothermal Liquefaction: Effect of Cu Incorporation Strategy
papers.abstract: Cu-based catalysts can enhance bio-oil production during the hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) of lignin; however, the influence of Cu incorporation strategy on individual reaction pathways remains insufficiently understood. In this study, experimental HTL of lignin under direct Cu-assisted and Cu-impregnated conditions was investigated over 200–320 °C and residence times of 5–25 min, together with a five-pathway lumped kinetic model. Apparent kinetic parameters were estimated by nonlinear regression of the experimental product yields. The model captured the principal evolution of residual solid, bio-oil, water-soluble fraction, and gas over the investigated conditions. The maximum bio-oil yield was obtained at 280 °C and 15 min, increasing from 24.87% for the direct process to 28.74% for Cu-impregnated lignin. Kinetic analysis revealed pathway-dependent effects of Cu impregnation. At 280 °C, the apparent residual-solid-to-bio-oil rate constant (k1) increased from 0.0211 to 0.0402 min-1, whereas the fitted contribution of the direct residual-solid-to-gas pathway (k3) was substantially lower following Cu impregnation. The apparent bio-oil-to-gas rate constant (k4) also increased at elevated temperatures, indicating stronger secondary conversion of bio-oil under more severe conditions. Arrhenius analysis further showed differences in the apparent activation energies and pre-exponential factors of the dominant pathways. Overall, the results demonstrate that Cu impregnation modifies the apparent distribution of reaction pathways rather than uniformly increasing all fitted rate constants, providing a quantitative kinetic framework for understanding the influence of Cu incorporation strategy on lignin HTL.

papers.title: SCO ATLAS: Mapping Spin-Crossover Thermodynamics across Experimentally Grounded Fe(II)N6 Complexes
papers.abstract: Research on the Spin-crossover (SCO) phenomenon has generated extensive experimental and computational data, distributed across hundreds of different sources, limiting systematic comparison and data reuse. Here, we introduce the SCO ATLAS, a data infrastructure that connects experimental sources with quantum chemistry computations and derived analyses, and we demonstrate its use through a first analysis devoted to the gas-phase thermodynamics of transition metal complexes (TMC) based on Fe(II)N6. Currently, the ATLAS includes 723 CSDderived crystallographic systems, from which 602 unique TMCs were retained for analysis. We map the thermodynamic landscape governing their molecular spin-state stability, identify the ranges of electronic and vibrational contributions compatible with SCO near room temperature, and show that ligand denticity modulates both components. Normal-mode analysis traces the denticity dependence of the vibrational entropy primarily to changes in ligand motion and the first coordination sphere. The homoleptic complexes are organized into 96 ligand families, with family identity accounting for approximately one-third of the within-denticity variation in ∆Helec. Across the complete dataset, ∆Helec is most strongly associated with the HS Fe–N distance. The released data, calculations and analysis tools provide a reusable framework for navigating SCO chemical space and developing future extensions of the ATLAS.

papers.title: Dual-Ligand Engineering of a Stable and High-Utilization Iron Complex Anolyte for Alkaline All-Iron Flow Batteries
papers.abstract: Alkaline all-iron flow batteries offer a low-cost and inherently safe approach to large-scale energy storage, but Fe-complex anolytes remain limited by insufficient coordination stability, solubility, and utilization at high concentrations. Here, we develop a dual-ligand Fe(TEA)(PS) anolyte using triethanolamine as the primary ligand and pyridine-3-sulfonate (PS) as the secondary ligand. The secondary ligand reinforces the Fe coordination environment through pyridyl-N coordination while introducing a hydrophilic sulfonate group. Computational calculations and Fe K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy reveal an enlarged molecular configuration and a more saturated coordination environment. Fe(TEA)(PS) exhibits a reversible Fe(III)/Fe(II) redox couple at -0.87 V versus SHE and a solubility of 1.41 M in 2 M NaOH. The resulting full cell achieves 95.12% electrolyte utilization at 1.0 M and a peak power density of 422.8 mW cm -2 . It retains 98.28% of its capacity over 1200 cycles at 100 mA cm -2 . Moreover, a cell containing 0.8 M Fe(TEA)(PS) maintains 96.87% capacity after 1800 cycles, corresponding to a decay rate of only 0.0017% per cycle. These results establish second-ligand engineering as an effective strategy for developing stable, highly soluble, and highly utilized Fe-complex anolytes for alkaline all-iron flow batteries.

papers.title: Interaction effects and droplet dynamics in chitosan-coated nanoemulsions via echo-Diffusing Wave Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: In this work, interaction effects and droplet dynamics in chitosan-coated nanoemulsions were investigated via echo-Diffusing Wave Spectroscopy (DWS). Medium-chain triglyceride (MCT) nanoemulsions containing 5–10% (w/w) oil were prepared with and without chitosan. Experimental photon transport mean free paths, were compared with non-interacting, hard-sphere, and excluded-annulus scattering models to evaluate the contribution of inter-droplet correlations. Intensity correlation functions were analyzed against scaled delay time, to account for differences in photon transport, while mean squared displacements (MSDs) were used to characterize inferred droplet motion. Chitosan incorporation produced non-monotonic changes in photon transport and correlation relaxation, while generally reducing the apparent droplet displacement. The excluded-annulus model provided a useful first approximation of selected intermediate-concentration formulations but was not able to capture the full concentration dependence, highlighting the limitations of representing the hydrated chitosan layer as a fixed exclusion boundary. The findings reveal a concentration-dependent interplay between longer-range interactions governing inter-droplet organization and hydrodynamic coupling and shorter-range interactions involving the hydrated polymer layer. This study demonstrates the value of echo-DWS for investigating interaction effects in polymer-coated nanoemulsions and provides a physical framework for their rational design as drug-delivery carriers.

papers.title: Laser ablation rapid evaporative ionisation mass spectrometry imaging with few-micrometer sampling pixels
papers.abstract: Achieving sub-cellular resolution in ambient, matrix-free mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) remains challenging because reducing the sampling area often compromises ion yield and image fidelity. Here, we demonstrate an infrared laser–driven ambient MSI platform that mitigates these limitations through low-fluence, picosecond pulsed, highrepetition-rate laser ablation with a custom 2.94 μm light source with near-diffraction limited beam quality. This approach produces well-confined ablation features with diameters of 5μm to 10 μm. Coupling the laser ablation plume to a rapid evaporative ionisation mass spectrometry (LA-REIMS) interface and a commercial time-of-flight mass analyser provides multiplexed ion maps of metabolites, phospholipids, and other small molecules in a single acquisition. This configuration enables routine 3 μm-pixel size imaging of fresh-frozen tissue sections, as well as imaging of formalin-fixed, paraffin embedded biopsy samples, all without additional preparation steps. Oversampled images preserve sub-cellular morphology and yield molecular distributions that correlate with fluorescence and histological features. Together, these results define a robust operational regime for high-fidelity, matrix-free MSI in the few-μm pixel range, where high infrared beam quality and stable, low-fluence, high repetition rate picosecond laser sampling underpin gentle ablation and efficient ion formation via REIMS, enabling sub-cellular molecular mapping in a clinically compatible, fully ambient format.

papers.title: A Decision-Making Framework for Renewable Biopolymer Selection: Integrating Structure, Processing, Properties, Scalability, Techno-Economics, and Life-Cycle Assessment
