papers.abstract: Renewable biopolymers are often compared by feedstock origin, biodegradability, or isolated material properties. These comparisons do not, by themselves, support an engineering decision because a useful material is not a polymer in isolation: it is a biopolymer processed into a defined architecture for a specified application and manufactured under practical constraints. This study presents a semi-quantitative multi-criteria decision-making framework for selecting renewable biopolymer systems across alginate, cellulose, lignin, chitosan, and starch. The framework evaluates a material–processing route–architecture–application decision unit through five linked dimensions: molecular functionality, processing compatibility, resulting architecture, applicationrelevant performance, and scalability. Scores are accompanied by evidence-confidence flags and are tested under three application-specific weighting scenarios — balanced, performance-led, and manufacturability-led — so that the framework reports conditional candidates and genuine ranking reversals rather than a universal material ranking. Sustainable packaging coatings and films, thermal-insulation panels and porous materials, and adsorption-based water treatment using biopolymer sorbents are used as contrasting demonstration cases. For packaging, barrier performance under relevant humidity, mechanical integrity, food-contact compatibility, converting compatibility, and end-of-life are prioritised. For insulation, thermal conductivity at realistic moisture content, density, dimensional stability, drying intensity, moisture management, and manufacturability are prioritised. For water treatment, adsorption capacity and selectivity, regeneration and reuse, aqueous-state stability, and feedstock cost and availability at scale are prioritised. The method explicitly separates reported evidence from missing evidence, and the worked sensitivity analysis finds genuine ranking reversals for packaging and insulation alongside a stable, target-class-specific robust result for water treatment. Available technoeconomic and life-cycle evidence is incorporated as illustrative, application-specific data points rather than as a substitute for a dedicated assessment. The framework provides a reproducible bridge between qualitative renewable-biopolymer reviews and application-specific materialsystem design.

papers.title: Single-Polynucleotide Encapsulation in Lipid Nanoparticles via Single-Step Assembly at Physiological pH
papers.abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are the leading nonviral platform for polynucleotide delivery, but structural heterogeneity and poorly controlled loading states limit quantitative structure–function analysis and rational formulation design. Standard protocols use rapid mixing under acidic conditions followed by buffer exchange, reflecting the assumption that ionizable lipid protonation is required for nucleic acid complexation. Here, we show that lipid–polynucleotide nanoparticles can instead be assembled directly at near-physiological pH through a single rapid micromixing step. Under near-stoichiometric lipid-to-polynucleotide conditions, rapid solvent exchange yields a homogeneous nanoparticle population without acidic formulation or post-assembly pH adjustment. Small-angle X-ray and neutron scattering (SAXS and SANS), together with cryogenic transmission electron microscopy (cryo-TEM), reveal a common core–multishell architecture consistent with encapsulation of one polynucleotide strand per particle. In situ SAXS shows that the final structure is established within submillisecond timescales during solvent exchange, indicating rapid cooperative coassembly rather than postmixing restructuring. Systematic variation of mixing conditions, stoichiometry, PEGylated lipid content, ionic strength, and pH demonstrates that this structural regime is selected by the assembly pathway rather than composition alone. The nanoparticles remain structurally stable over extended periods and retain intracellular delivery activity, while providing a constrained system for probing formulation-dependent effects. These results establish physiological-pH assembly as a route to pathway-selected single-polynucleotide nanoparticles and identify loading state as a design variable alongside composition, size, and surface chemistry. More broadly, they highlight assembly history as a determinant of nanoparticle structure and pathway-directed assembly as a strategy for controlling soft nanomaterial heterogeneity at its origin rather than after formation.

papers.title: Synthesis of Buprenorphine from Morphine
papers.abstract: Buprenorphine is a WHO essential medicine widely used to treat pain and opioid addiction, which is currently manufactured from thebaine, a morphinan alkaloid obtained from the poppy plant. However, thebaine has a low abundance in natural poppy strains, its production is geographically concentrated, and recent years have seen global shortages. These factors present a potential vulnerability in the buprenorphine supply chain. Herein, we report the synthesis of buprenorphine from morphine, the most abundant and cheapest poppy alkaloid. To streamline the synthesis, with practical manufacture in mind, our route combines multiple transformations into several one-pot sequences. The synthesis of buprenorphine from a more available starting material may help to ensure continued supply of this critical therapeutic.

papers.title: Shaping single crystals through a controlled non-classical crystallization pathway
papers.abstract: The ability to program the shape of single crystals through molten-state processing has transformed the manufacturing of inorganic materials, yet this strategy is fundamentally incompatible with most organic-based crystals, which decompose before melting. Here, we show that a non-classical crystallization pathway can overcome this limitation by generating a moldable dense-liquid intermediate during the growth of peptide-based metal-organic frameworks (MOFs). By engineering a reaction environment in which precursor concentration and reagent diffusion are controlled while suppressing convection, we selectively activate a liquid-liquid phase separation process to produce a confined dense-liquid phase that can be shaped prior to crystallization. Repeated diffusion-limited chemical perturbations subsequently transform this intermediate into single crystals that faithfully preserve the geometry of the confined environment in which they form, enabling non-equilibrium morphologies inaccessible by conventional synthesis. We further show that crystal shape influences mechanical properties, demonstrating that controlling crystallization pathways provides a route to tailor function without altering chemical composition.

papers.title: The assembled catalytic triad of Ideonella sakaiensis PETase is metastable in apo molecular dynamics simulations across multiple control conditions
papers.abstract: Active-site geometry is routinely reported from molecular dynamics of engineered variants of Ideonella sakaiensis PETase (IsPETase) as evidence that a design preserves catalytic capability. We simulated wild-type IsPETase and six length-matched linker fusion constructs, four replicates each, for 350 ns at 343 K under a preregistered analysis plan. Twenty-six of 28 trajectories began with the Ser133 OG to His210 NE2 distance inside the competent range, below 0.35 nm, and two began marginally above it. All 28 ended outside that range without recovery. The median time to crossing, from the onset of free dynamics, was 4.06 ns, with a range spanning more than four orders of magnitude. Triad loss was not generally accompanied by global destabilisation. The loss persisted when the system was built from the crystal structure rather than a predicted model, when both native disulfide bonds were present, and at 300 K. Changing the catalytic histidine protonation state did not restore persistent catalytic geometry. A post hoc control under a second protein and water parameter set also left the competent range in all four replicates, but reached separations of 0.48 to 0.90 nm rather than the 1.9 to 2.1 nm seen under CHARMM36m. Because the endpoint failed in the wild-type control, the intended comparison of linker family and length could not be completed. Active-site distances from apo IsPETase simulations should not be interpreted as evidence of catalytic competence without a wild-type control and replicate sampling.

papers.title: Diabat 2.0: A Comprehensive Diabatization Toolkit for Multichromophoric Systems
papers.abstract: The construction of physically meaningful quasi-diabatic states and the evaluation of their electronic couplings are essential for describing nonadiabatic processes in molecular aggregates and other multichromophoric systems. Existing software implementations, however, are often restricted to dimers, two-state models, or particular types of quasi-diabatic states. Here, we present Diabat 2.0, a comprehensive toolkit for multistate diabatization in multichromophoric systems. It constructs the adiabatic-to-diabatic (ATD) transformation based on the adiabatic-state wave functions and energies obtained from external quantum chemistry calculations, yielding quasi-diabatic states and their electronic couplings in a nearly black-box manner. Diabat 2.0 implements several advanced ATD methods, including a general approach that can reliably construct quasi-diabatic states with diverse charge and excitation distributions without prescribing state types. This enables Diabat 2.0 to support diabatization in a broad range of scenarios that involve not only conventional charge-transfer, locally excited, and correlated triplet pair states, but also a variety of exotic states, such as mixed radical-triplet states, trion states, radical-coupled triplet-pair states, and charge-localized dicationic states. These capabilities are demonstrated in applications to several multichromophoric systems that pose substantial challenges to existing software.

papers.title: Neural Kinetics: Learning Kinetics as Transport in Compositional Space
papers.abstract: Complex bio-derived and fossil mixtures contain thousands of molecules whose individual structures and reaction pathways cannot be fully resolved, making conventional mechanism-based kinetic modelling impractical. A reaction network detailed enough to describe every formula-level transformation would contain far more reactions and parameters than the available data can constrain. We propose to overcome this limitation by representing mixtures directly as abundance fields on a compositional grid indexed by molecular descriptors, specifically carbon number (#C) and double-bond equivalent (DBE), and by learning a time-conditioned, chemistry-informed operator that maps the initial composition to predict a later state. The evolution rates of the chemical space are learned by a two-dimensional Fourier neural operator (FNO) acting jointly on a set of heteroatom classes, with normalized time and compositional coordinates appended as input channels. Because experimental data are limited, we enlarge the training set with synthetic trajectories generated from the measured samples, pre-train on this ensemble, and then calibrate a small subset of parameters on the measured distributions. We tested the framework on a case of oxidation of a complex hydrocarbon mixture that is tracked by FTICR-MS over sixty seconds of reaction. On an independent sample the framework, that we named NeuralKinetics, reproduced the measured endpoint class composition within a mean absolute error of approximately one percent and arranged the heteroatom classes correctly on the compositional grid. The second test was an entirely different system: litter decomposition in a peatland warming experiment, also followed by FTICR-MS but over two years. The developed operator accurately predicted the endpoint class composition of the held-out sample proving that the framework is flexible enough to adapt to diverse reactive systems.

papers.title: Non-Covalent Interactions Directed Azobenzene Crystals: Photoisomerization-Induced Melting and Melt-Mediated Polymorphism
papers.abstract: Azobenzene molecular crystals have emerged as a compelling class of stimuli-responsive materials, yet the structural factors that determine whether a given crystal bends, melts, or remains entirely inert under UV irradiation are far from understood. Here, we investigate a series of eight structurally homologous 2,2′-dihydroxyazobenzene derivatives (Azo-0 to Azo-7) in which terminal functional groups (‒OH vs. ‒OMe) and pendant alkyl spacer length are independently varied, allowing the contributions of intramolecular conformation, intermolecular packing topology, and lattice compliance to be disentangled. Single-crystal Xray diffraction (SCXRD), UV-vis spectroscopy, differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), together with thermal-stage polarized optical microscopy, reveal two mechanistically distinct melting pathways. The central finding is that an intramolecular O-H···N hydrogen bond, present in four derivatives (Azo-0, Azo-1, Azo-3, Azo-5), forms a pseudo-six-membered chelate ring that locks the azobenzene core in its planar trans conformation, fully suppressing photoisomerization in both solution and solid state. Removal of this intramolecular constraint through ‒OMe substitution liberates the azobenzene core in Azo-2, Azo-4, Azo-6, and Azo-7, enabling efficient and fully reversible cis-trans photoisomerization with visible-light-driven recovery. Critically, irradiation of these unlocked crystals below their equilibrium melting points (Ts < Tm) triggers rapid, cooperative crystal-to-liquid transitions that are absent in the dark and under 456 nm light irradiation, establishing photoisomerization-induced lattice strain—not photothermal heating—as the operative mechanism. The sole outlier, Azo-5, melts under intense UV irradiation through a purely photothermal pathway, consistent with its locked conformation and strong 370 nm light absorption. Additionally, Azo-7 undergoes a thermally driven solid, liquid, solid polymorphic transformation: melt-recrystallization converts the high-melting polymorph Azo-7α (Tm ≈ 59 °C) into a structurally distinct, lower-melting polymorph Azo-7β (Tm ≈ 42 °C), demonstrating that thermal history is itself an independent handle for programming crystal packing. These findings translate directly into three molecular design principles for photomechanical organic crystals: phenolic OH gates the photoisomerization switch via intramolecular hydrogen bonding; alkyl chain length tunes lattice compliance and packing dimensionality; and melt-mediated crystals provide access to structurally and thermally distinct polymorphic forms.

papers.title: Multiscale Insights into CO2 Chemisorption and Proton Transfer in Choline-Imidazolate based Deep Eutectic solvents: Exploring the Effect of Primary, Secondary and Tertiary Alkanolamine on Reaction Pathways and Product Distribution
papers.abstract: Understanding how solvent composition governs competitive CO 2 chemisorption within solvents is essential for the rational design of solvents for CO 2 capture. In this work, we combine density functional theory (DFT), classical molecular dynamics (cMD), and microkinetic modeling to investigate CO 2 chemisorption in choline-imidazolate based systems containing different alkanolamine hydrogen bond donors (HBDs): monoethanolamine (MEA), diethanolamine (DEA), and methyldiethanolamine (MDEA). By systematically characterizing the thermodynamics, kinetics and liquid structure influence, our results show that within these systems, choline is the preferred CO 2 -binding site unless a HBD is present. Accordingly, the MEA system shifts almost entirely to amine-centered carbamate formation, the DEA system retains carbamate dominance but with stronger competition from choline-centered capture, and the MDEA system which additionally includes water shifts back toward choline-centered carbonate together with a competitive water-assisted bicarbonate pathway. The findings illustrate how CO 2 chemisorption in multicomponent liquids is controlled by a combination of intrinsic reaction thermodynamics, liquid-structure, and CO 2 concentration. More broadly, this work provides insights that will facilitate molecular-level design of solvents for CO 2 uptake and regeneration.

papers.title: Unveiling the Potential of Biomass-Accessible Bifuran Unit in Conjugated Polymers: Synthesis, Thermal Properties, Photophysics, and Comparative Study with Phenylene and Thiophene Analogues for OLED Applications
papers.abstract: The bifuran unit is a biomass-accessible building block for organic electronic materials; however, its application in electroluminescent devices remains largely unexplored. In this study, polycondensation reactions of a bifuran diboronic ester with nine aryl dibromides were examined. The obtained polymers (PBFAr)s showed strongly comonomer-dependent yields and solubilities. Detailed solution-state and device characterization was focused on the soluble fluorene-containing polymer PBFAr1. For comparison, analogous polymers containing phenylene (PSPhAr1), biphenyl (PBPhAr1), and bithiophene (PBTAr1) units were also synthesized. In chloroform solution, PBFAr1 and its bithiophene-based analogue PBTAr1 exhibited photoluminescence quantum yields of 43% and 39%, respectively. Kelvin probe measurements indicated an energy-level alignment with the ITO anode that may facilitate hole injection. Solution-processed OLEDs with an ITO/PEDOT:PSS/emissive polymer/LiF/Al architecture were fabricated, and the PBFAr1-based device exhibited cyan electroluminescence at 484 nm, demonstrating that PBFAr1 can function as an emissive layer in a solution-processed OLED. These results demonstrate the potential of bifuran-based conjugated polymers as emissive materials for further development in organic optoelectronic applications.

papers.title: Magnetic control of lipid–peroxyl termination yield under spin relaxation: from an optimised dipolar-scale field to a falsifiable kinetic criterion
papers.abstract: Lipid peroxidation, the radical-chain oxidation of membrane lipids, terminates in part through spin-selective encounters between lipid-peroxyl radicals. We ask how far a shaped magnetic field can steer this branch under spin relaxation and how that change propagates to the oxidation flux. Gradient-projection and bang–bang Pontryagin controls were evaluated with a stochastic-Schrödinger treatment of dipolar fluctuations and an independent Brownian-dynamics model. A best-found dipolar-scale field raises the triplet-initialised singlet termination yield from ΦS|T = 0.220 at 50 µT to 0.562 (+155%), with the bang–bang solution corroborating at 0.522; a bandwidth-filtered proxy retains 0.270. Under Brownian dynamics the control advantage remains positive throughout the sampled rotational-correlation-time range, and one field transfers across eight microdomain-size–diffusion parameter sets. Closing the spin calculation to classical autoxidation kinetics gives Ceff = −f/(1+f), where f is the fraction of peroxyl loss proceeding through bimolecular termination. Two limiting descriptions of the productive encounter population bracket the predicted suppression of oxidation flux in antioxidant-free liposomes at approximately 21–37%, and at approximately 4–10% for the bandwidth-filtered field. α-Tocopherol attenuates the response as interception comes to dominate, providing an internal experimental control. These values describe an elementary encounter and a minimal kinetic model, not whole-cell lipid peroxidation.

papers.title: Provenance-Aware Quality Control for Heterogeneous Bioactivity Data
papers.abstract: Background. Machine-learning models for proteins increasingly train on large, pooled collections of laboratory measurements-binding affinities such as IC50, Ki, Kd and EC50 (numbers that describe how tightly a molecule binds its target), togetherwith biophysical readouts from techniques such as surface plasmon resonance (SPR), bio-layer interferometry (BLI) and isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC). These measurements arrive in different units, from different assay formats, fitted with different models, and at different levels of quality. Pooling them without care injects substantial noise. The per-record quality flags that some databases attach are incomplete, and they do not travel with the data once records from several sources are combined. What has been missing is an open, model-agnostic layer that turns raw measurements into records a downstream pipeline can consume directly: unit-normalized, quality-checked, and carrying their own uncertainty and provenance. What we built. biophys_interop is an open Python toolkit and data schema. It maps any supportedmeasurement to a single canonical record spanning 24 measurement types (modalities), converts units to a common standard, and runs a registry of 72 deterministic, method-aware quality-control (QC) rules. Every rule cites a reason from the measurement literature, recommends a concrete action, and returns a simple pass / warn / fail flag together with a calibrated uncertainty. The library is small and has few dependencies. We are deliberate about what our validation does and does not cover: two broadly applicable affinity rules (a plausible-value-range rule and an exact-duplicate rule) are tested at scale against an independent curator’s labels; the remaining method-specific biophysical rules are offered as a literaturegrounded, executable registry-useful and auditable, but not claimed as validated here, because no public database publishes the per-record ground-truth flags that would be needed to score them. Results. Using ChEMBL’s own data_validity_comment and potential_duplicate annotations as an independent ground truth, transparent rules on the standardized record reproduce two of ChEMBL’s three curator flag families on 175,387 held-out records across 30 human targets, with no trained model (value-range rule: Matthews correlation coefficient [MCC] 0.61; duplicate rule: MCC 0.65). The thresholds transfer cleanly to a completely separate set of targets (train on 15, test on 15 disjoint targets; 88,443 held-out records; MCC 0.73 and 0.64). Going beyond the curator, the layer flags 929 internally inconsistent records that ChEMBL did not flag, and a comparison against the independent BindingDB database exposes 38 disagreements of 100-fold or more, 89% of them unmarked by either database. A domain expert who checked a 24-record sample against the primary literature confirmed 16 of 24 (67%) as genuine data errors, including 11 of 12 cross-database conflicts. We reproduce the known cross-assay noise regime reported by Landrum and Riniker, and show that a comparability gate based on assay metadata more than halves the median disagreement between records (0.51-> 0.21 log units). Finally, feeding the calibrated signal into a downstreammutation-effect (ΔΔG) predictor gave no reliable improvement; we report this negative result in full. The toolkit, the rule registry, the cleaned datasets, and one-command reproduction scripts are released openly. Conclusions. Once heterogeneous public measurements share one representation, simple transparent rules can catch data problems-matching expert curators at scale on the rule families we tested, and catching errors those curators missed. The result is a reusable, auditable data layer for protein machine learning, rather than a new predictive model. Keywords: bioactivity data; data curation; quality control; ChEMBL; BindingDB; data standardization; FAIR data; machine learning; interoperability; reproducibility

papers.title: Sisyphus: A Topology-Compiled Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetic Platform with Structure-Only Input and Bayesian Parameter Refinement
papers.abstract: Physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models provide a mechanistic framework for drug disposition, but compound-specific parameterization remains a practical constraint when experimental absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) measurements are unavailable. Sisyphus is an open-source platform that compiles ordinary differential equations from a typed physiological graph and uses molecular structure plus dose to generate oral maximum plasma concentration (Cmax) predictions. Seven fitted models support ADME estimation and a four-track geometric blend of mechanistic, direct machine-learning, clearance-based, and distribution-based predictions. This revision reconciles the manuscript with public training snapshots and a source audit of clinical reference records. Of 107 repeatedly accessed development compounds, 73 retain evaluable reference Cmax values. The hybrid prediction has a geometric mean absolute fold error (AAFE) of 2.830 (conditional bootstrap 95% confidence interval 2.30-3.52), with 43.8% of predictions within twofold; engine-only and direct machine-learning AAFE are 3.872 and 3.049. These data do not establish independent generalization or superiority of the hybrid. The user-facing residual band is development-derived and is not valid split-conformal calibration. A selected ten-compound measured-input diagnostic lowers engine AAFE from 6.708 to 5.968, while new same-model synthetic experiments illustrate Bayesian updating with explicit effective-sample-size and interval diagnostics. Neither experiment establishes clinical accuracy. A previously reported temporal cohort has been consumed by repeated analysis, and no untouched external performance estimate is available. The platform's contribution is the integration of topology-compiled simulation, structure-driven parameterization, and experimental observation-informed refinement, together with an auditable account of data provenance and limitations. Negative development experiments identify unsuccessful tested strategies; they do not demonstrate an intrinsic structure-only accuracy ceiling or a verified bioavailability-specific cause of error.

papers.title: Efficient Microwave-Enhanced Solid Phase Peptide Synthesis of Secretin Hormones Amenable for Rapid Library Design and Lead Optimization
papers.abstract: Microwave-enhanced solid phase peptide synthesis of complex, therapeutically relevant, aspartimide-prone secretin hormones was achieved under optimized conditions with economical and commercially available protected amino acids. In order to determine robust and general methods, standard Fmoc SPPS conditions, Oxyma-buffered deprotection solution, Fmoc-(Dmb)Gly-OH, Fmoc-Asp(OMpe)-OH, and combinations thereof were systematically evaluated for crude purity using LC-MS. Aspartimide formation was significantly reduced, and syntheses were completed in a single run without the need for expensive, commercially inaccessible, or diversity-limiting peptide fragments or pseudoprolines, supplying methods amenable for rapid library generation, hit-to-lead endeavors, and lead optimization.

papers.title: Cation-Deficient Tantalum Oxide–Zinc Tantalate Nanocomposite for Photocatalytic Carbon Dioxide Conversion
Thickness dependent HER activity of individual MXene flakes revealed by SECCM
papers.abstract: MXenes, 2D transition metal carbides, provide unique properties for a large range of applications including electrocatalysis and energy storage. Specifically, Ti 3 C 2 T x , has shown activity for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). MXenes are conductive, present a rich surface chemistry and do not contain rare and expensive elements. They are promising for next generation catalyst materials. Here, we study the HER activity of individual single-layer and multilayer Ti 3 C 2 T x flakes, using SECCM and ex situ AFM. Our results show that multilayer flakes have a much larger overpotential, revealing that the reaction proceeds more slowly in the interlayer volume compared to the open basal plane of a single layer. This opens avenues of optimization for MXene catalyst layer formulation that have not been considered before.

papers.title: Photosensitizer-free infrared-light-induced radical reactions
papers.abstract: Infrared (IR) light is a source of mild energy that facilitates selective chemical reactions in a deeply penetrative manner. However, harvesting IR light through electronic excitation is challenging, and thus organic photoreactions at wavelengths over 1000 nm are scarce even with specialized photosensitizers. Herein, we report radical reactions driven by IR-A (~1000 nm) or IR-B light (~1500 nm) via vibration-mediated photolysis in the absence of a photosensitizer. The developed method promotes diverse transformations, including iodination, alkylation, and selenation reactions, with wider scope, higher selectivity, and deeper penetration through reaction media, compared with those of conventional irradiation with visible light. Applications include irradiation through obstacles, one-pot sequential transformations, and flow chemistry in opaque tubing. Experimental and spectroscopic studies reveal that the absorption of IR light via vibrational modes promotes photolysis that triggers radical chain reactions.

papers.title: N-aminated N-heterocycle based hydrazones as widely tunable photoswitches
papers.abstract: Photoswitches based on E/Z isomerism around a C=N bond have found wide-reaching applications in materials science and biology. Herein, we report a new class of hydrazone photoswitch based on aminated nitrogen heterocycles, the N-aminated N-heterocyclic hydrazones (NaNs). These photoswitches can be synthesised in a single step, achieve near quantitative photoswitching, offer visible light (470 nm) response, have thermal half-lives of up to 958 hours at room temperature and quantum yields of up to 70%. We have investigated the impact of different structural features on switch properties by studying a library of 30 derivatives with varied N-amino N-heterocyclic components and varied aldehyde components. These have been extensively studied in the solution and solid state, towards understanding structure-activity relationships for rational NaN photoswitch design. The stability of the metastable state facilitated the growth of the Z-isomer crystals for an anthracene derived NaN, and we observed both E/Z isomerisation and dimerisation of the anthracene, depending on irradiation duration. Furthermore, we demonstrate a member of the library undergoes E→Z photoisomerisation in the solid state, displaying single crystal to single crystal switching. We anticipate that the simple synthesis of these compounds, combined with their tuneable properties, will ensure that they find widespread application across numerous fields.

papers.title: Sulfilimine benziodoxolones: stable electrophilic bifunctional reagents for nitrogen incorporation
papers.abstract: We report the design and scalable synthesis of novel sulfilimine-based hypervalent iodine reagents (INSert, based on the I-N=S motif), that are bench-stable, non-explosive and can act as bifunctional electrophilic nitrogen donors. Their distinctive architecture combines a benziodoxolone moiety to induce electrophilicity at the nitrogen atom, with a sulfilimine group as a versatile, latent synthetic handle for downstream diversification. We first demonstrate the utility of this reagent class through the formal anti-Markovnikov hydrosulfilimination of alkenes via alkyldimethylborane intermediates, followed by subsequent transformation of the resulting N-alkylsulfilimine into various nitrogen-containing scaffolds. We also report preliminary N-insertion reactions with an indole and an imidazole. These results clearly show that the reagents’ modular iodinane-sulfilimine architecture can open new avenues for the incorporation of nitrogen into organic molecules through multiple distinct reaction manifolds.

papers.title: Spatially programmed MOF-coated microchannels for capillary-driven microvolume analysis
papers.abstract: Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) and covalent organic frameworks (COFs) offer chemically and geometrically programmable pore environments that have been exploited as coatings for capillary- and fiber-based microextraction. However, most formats still rely on discrete adsorbent handling or external fluid actuation, poorly suited to the microliter sample volumes typical of biological specimens. Here we report glass microcapillaries bearing a spatially programmed, nanometer-thick MOF film that simultaneously drives fluid uptake by capillary action and performs localized analyte enrichment within a single, self-contained channel. Retaining the adsorbent as a conformal film rather than a particulate phase removes the need for separate adsorbent handling. It also concentrates chemical functionality at the fluid-contacting surface, enabling efficient enrichment from a few microliters without external pumps. We demonstrate this approach by enriching and quantifying the inflammation-associated metabolites kynurenine and quinolinic acid from microliter volumes of mouse blood serum, achieving clear discrimination between inflammatory and control conditions. These MOF-coated microcapillaries offer an integrated route to low-volume biofluid analysis in settings where sample availability and external fluid handling are limiting.

papers.title: Molecular Dynamics Simulations of the Outer-Sphere Reorganization Energies of Aqueous Oligothiophenes
papers.abstract: The outer-sphere reorganization energy (λout) contributes directly to the activation barrier for hole transfer in aqueous organic mixed ionic–electronic conductors, yet it is usually estimated from dielectric continuum models rather than computed explicitly. Here, λout is computed for doped oligothiophenes in explicit aqueous electrolyte by all-atom molecular dynamics with an electronic continuum correction, using vertical-energy-gap fluctuation estimators and thermodynamic integration. Increasing the degree of polymerization from one to six decreases λout from 0.84 to 0.55 eV owing to hole delocalization; λout saturates beyond the trimer and remains comparable to the inner-sphere reorganization energy (0.48 eV for the hexamer). Across side-chainfunctionalized thiophene monomers, λout varies by ≈0.2 eV and scales with the square of the doping-induced change in molecular dipole moment, whereas for trimers and hexamers it converges to ≈0.53 eV irrespective of whether the side chain is neutral, cationic, or anionic. These results identify backbone delocalization as the principal determinant of λout for aqueous conjugated oligomers.

papers.title: Checkmate for CHK2: Discovery of First-in-Class Covalent CHK2 Inhibitors with High Potency and Selectivity
papers.abstract: Checkpoint kinase 2 (CHK2), a serine/threonine kinase encoded by CHEK2, plays a key role in the DNA damage response (DDR), acting downstream of ataxia-telangiectasia mutated (ATM) kinase in the ATM–CHK2–p53 signaling axis. Despite considerable interest in CHK2 as a potential therapeutic target, our understanding of its biological functions and therapeutic potential remains constrained by the limited availability of potent and selective chemical probes. While several non-covalent CHK2 inhibitors have been developed, their utility for interrogating CHK2 biology is often limited by suboptimal kinase selectivity. Moreover, selective covalent inhibitors that enable robust and sustained pharmacological perturbation of CHK2 have not been reported. To address this gap, we developed the covalent CHK2 inhibitor (R)-12b, which selectively targets Cys231 at the P3 position of the glycine-rich loop (P-loop). Covalent binding of (R)-12b induces a repositioning of the P-loop, leading to an outward displacement of the N-lobe and expansion of the ATP-binding pocket. (R)-12b exhibits nanomolar biochemical and cellular potency, good in vitro metabolic stability, moderate covalent bond-formation kinetics, and a highly favorable kinome-wide selectivity profile. Together, these properties establish (R)-12b as a first-in-class selective covalent CHK2 inhibitor and a valuable chemical tool for exploring CHK2 biology and further elucidating its therapeutic potential.

papers.title: Small-Angle X-ray Scattering and Rheology Reveal the Onset of Interparticle Correlations during Nanoparticle Immobilization in Polystyrene
papers.abstract: The immobilization of nanoparticles in polymer matrices is a key strategy to suppress Brownian motion while preserving nanoparticle functionality. In this work, monodisperse iron oxide nanoparticles with mean diameters of 6.4, 7.1, and 8.8 nm were synthesized via thermal decomposition of an iron–oleate complex and immobilized in a styrene matrix by radical polymerization. TEM and SAXS confirm that particle size and morphology remain unchanged, whereas interparticle correlations and larger-scale clusters develop during immobilization. Combined in-situ SAXS and rheological measurements reveal that the timing of structure formation is governed by polymerization kinetics. At 80 °C, rapid polymerization leads to the early development of structure factor contributions and a steep viscosity increase. At 60 °C, polymerization proceeds substantially more slowly, allowing the early stage of structure formation to be resolved in which interparticle correlations develop before the viscosity increases steeply. Larger nanoparticles follow the same sequence of structural changes with a progressively earlier onset, indicating that particle size affects the timing of structure formation. These findings indicate that interparticle correlations form as the medium surrounding the still mobile nanoparticles changes during polymerization, with polymerization kinetics setting the time scale until the solidifying matrix freezes in the structure.

papers.title: Resolving Water-Oxidation Kinetics by Combining Operando Spectroscopy with O2 Evolution Rates over Seven Orders of Magnitude
papers.abstract: Electrocatalytic water oxidation is central to renewable energy conversion, yet the origin of its potential–current response remains challenging to define. Classical electrode kinetics attributes the empirical exponential increase in current with potential to the linearly lowering of the activation barrier with applied potential, as described by Butler–Volmer formalisms, while potential-dependent coverage of active surface states has also been considered as an important factor in electrocatalytic kinetics. However, direct quantitative experimental links between the state evolution, activation-energy changes, and the macroscopic potential-current response remain limited. Here, by combining temperature-dependent electrochemistry with operando optical spectroscopy, we show that the apparent activation energy decreases approximately linearly with the coverage of electrophilic *O active states on iridium oxide catalysts. Potential-current data across more than 7 orders of magnitude, obtained from microelectrode and electrochemical mass spectrometry, reveal a continuously evolving Tafel slope from ~20 to 160 mV dec-1, which is not captured by the simplest version of Butler-Volmer equation. In contrast, a second-order coverage-dependent barrier model, employing *O active state densities determined from optical spectroscopy, is found to give a good fit to the global potential-current response, with the coverage dependence of the activation barrier being in good agreement with that measured directly from temperature-dependent data. More complex models are also discussed. These results link water oxidation kinetics to the accumulation and interaction of active states, providing a framework for understanding kinetics of multistep electrocatalytic reactions.

papers.title: Analytic Nuclear Gradients and Derivative Couplings for SA-QED-CASSCF
papers.abstract: Exploring the potential energy surfaces of molecules in optical cavities requires analytical derivatives. We present analytical nuclear gradients and nonadiabatic derivative couplings for state-averaged quantum-electrodynamics complete-active-space self-consistent field theory (SA-QED-CASSCF) forthe coherent-state Pauli–Fierz Hamiltonian, including the coupledperturbed response of the QED-Hartree–Fock reference and the photon contribution to the coupling that arises because the coherent-state displacement depends on the geometry. The derivatives agree with finite differences to within 10−6 atomic units (5×10−6 for the state of smallest weight in an unequal average) for equal, unequal and zero-weight state averaging, and with independent codes without the cavity. With them we locate a polariton-induced conical intersection in LiH, where the cavity makes the molecular orientation a second coordinate and a reflection combined with photon parity makes the crossing symmetry-allowed. In ethylene, the S0/S1 conical intersection persists under coupling and keeps its twisted–pyramidalized geometry, and it becomes more accessible from the Franck–Condon point, because the dipole self-energy raises the diffuse π → 3s state more than the crossing pair. Capturing the partial return of this penalty through the bilinear coupling requires the polarization-axis partner orbital in the active space, a rule for polaritonic CASSCF in general.

papers.title: Probing local structure and hydrogen incorporation in solution-processed thin-film solid electrolytes
papers.abstract: Solution processing of functional thin films offers significant benefits, yet characterising their local structure and bulk composition remains challenging. Here, we investigate the composition-structure-property relationships of nanocomposite Na-Al-P-O (NAPO) thin-film solid electrolytes using impedance spectroscopy, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy and time-of-flight elastic recoil detection analysis (ToF-ERDA). An invariant activation energy of ≈0.8 eV across NAPO compositions was observed despite a ≈20-fold variation in ionic conductivity, suggesting that these differences arise primarily from changes in the concentration of mobile Na⁺ in the amorphous matrix. NMR measurements revealed highly disordered Al environments that were correlated with increased conductivity, evidence for multiple Na environments with differing mobilities, as well as a reduced local energy barrier to Na + hopping of ≈0.5 eV for two compositions. ToF-ERDA measurements showed that the elemental distributions were homogeneous, alongside significant H incorporation, identified as hydroxyl groups bound to Al and P via NMR. The H content increased as the ionic conductivity decreased in the NAPO system. Comparison with related, but ionically insulating compositions showed that H is a universal component of solution-processed materials. Although the protons were not mobile in these systems, H is proposed to occupy mobile sites within the framework that would otherwise host mobile ions such as Na + . Thus, our work suggests that promoting local disorder and minimising H incorporation are key design strategies for enhancing ionic conductivity in solution-processed amorphous solid electrolytes.

papers.title: A review on foundation models for polymer informatics
papers.abstract: Foundation models have emerged as a powerful paradigm for learning transferable knowledge from broad, heterogeneous data and adapting them to diverse downstream tasks, driving a growing interest in AI-accelerated scientific discovery. In polymer science, this paradigm offers a promising route beyond conventional machine learning methods that are often confined to isolated tasks and struggle to generalize under data scarcity and across heterogeneous downstream settings. Polymer foundation models (PFMs), however, are not merely general scientific foundation models applied to polymer datasets. They must address representation, generation, transfer, and evaluation challenges specific to polymer informatics. This review synthesizes recent progress in PFMs for representation learning and generative modeling, spanning models designed for polymer systems and those adapted from general foundation models. We organize this review around two stages: (1) polymer modeling as the foundation, covering representations, datasets, model architectures, and pretraining objectives; and (2) downstream applications, evaluation, and adaptation. By synthesizing recent progress, open challenges, and future directions, this review outlines a roadmap toward robust and generalizable foundation models for polymer informatics.

papers.title: Light-Driven Dissolution of Ultrasmall Maghemite Nanoparticles: The Role of Ligand and Photon Energy
papers.abstract: Light-controlled conversion of iron oxide nanoparticles into redox-active soluble iron offers a route toward externally triggered, image-guided ferroptosis strategies, but the physicochemical factors governing this process remain poorly understood. Here, visible-light-driven dissolution of ultrasmall citrate-stabilized maghemite nanoparticles (3.4 ± 0.8 nm) is shown to arise from a competition between iron release and nanoparticle aggregation. The process involves iron oxide reduction, ferrous iron release, citrate detachment and oxidation, and subsequent nanoparticle aggregation. The effects of citric acid and photon energy are systematically examined, revealing their key roles in regulating dissolution and aggregation. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and spatially resolved diffuse reflectance are used to monitor these changes in biologically relevant environments, including tissue-mimicking phantoms. MRI contrast evolves predictably with irradiation time, supporting the use of these particles as responsive imaging probes. In glioblastoma cells, green-light irradiation of internalized maghemite nanoparticles induces mitochondrial cytochrome oxidation. Cell-viability assays further reveal a non-monotonic concentration dependence under blue and green light, with lower nanoparticle concentrations producing stronger cytotoxic effects. These results establish a light-controlled, ligandassisted dissolution/aggregation strategy in which photon energy and ligand availability govern iron release, colloidal stability, imaging response, and light-induced cellular toxicity.

papers.title: Correlative Potential and Impedance Microscopy Reveals Particle-Level Degradation and Transport Heterogeneity in Solid-State Composite Cathodes
papers.abstract: The electrochemical performance of composite cathodes in all-solid-state batteries is governed by local reaction and transport processes; however, directly linking cell-level electrochemical responses to individual activematerial particles and local microstructural features remains challenging. Here, we investigate a composite cathode in sulfide-based all-solid-state cells using correlative microscopy combining Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) and scanning impedance microscopy (SIM). Following high-voltage degradation, KPFM revealed that some cathode active-material particles exhibited smaller changes in contact potential difference (CPD) between the charged and discharged states or deviations from the overall trend. Furthermore, a particle-by-particle correlation was observed between the charge–discharge CPD response and the corresponding low-frequency local AC voltage response measured by SIM. Analysis of the SIM spatial distributions using a transmission line model further provided a framework for interpreting changes in the relative contributions of electronic transport, ionic transport, and cathode active material/solid electrolyte interfacial impedance between the charged and discharged states and following high-voltage degradation. This approach provides a basis for linking particle-level reaction heterogeneity to local transport networks in composite cathodes.

papers.title: A Charge-Directed Electrocyclic Ring Opening of Azomethine Ylides as a Route to 2-(N-Acylamino)-1,3-dienes
papers.abstract: The electrocyclic ring opening of azomethine ylides driven by charge neutralization leads to 2-N-acylamino-1,3-diene products. The requisite azomethine ylide is formed by deprotonation of an oxazolinium ion, which is formed by O-silylation of a readily available oxazolidinone starting material. Computational studies indicate that the deprotonation event is the rate limiting step of the sequence providing a short-lived ylide intermediate that opens spontaneously via a low-barrier (1.7 kcal/mol) transition state leading to an enecarbamate product that is about 48 kcal/mol lower in energy than the ylide intermediate. Charge minimization biases the equilibrium position of the electrocyclization reaction leading to the ring-opened product. This transformation provides a straightforward route to 2-Nsubstituted-N-acylamino-1,3-dienes which were used in subsequent Diels-Alder cycloaddition reactions to give cyclohexenecarbamate products.

papers.title: Growth and crystallization of solution-processed TIPSpentacene on ultra-thin ferroelectric HZO gate dielectrics
papers.abstract: The solution processed organic thin film growth on the ferroelectric Hf0.5Zr0.5O2(HZO) thin films was investigated using the most commonly used TIPS-pentacene toward memory device applications. The molecular orientations, surface morphologies, and crystallinity of TIPS pentacene deposited on HZO were comparable to those of fabricated thin films on SiO2. In particular, 2D-GIXD results showed that TIPS-pentacene on HZO crystallized by annealing at 150°C exhibited higher crystallinity and molecular orientation than that on SiO2. Preliminary electrical measurements revealed that TIPS‑pentacene/HZO stacks exhibited strong channel conduction with negligible gate modulation, indicating that interfacial electronic states at the HZO surface dominate charge transport.

papers.title: Excitonic Coupling Suppresses Phonon-Induced Polariton Group Velocity Renormalization
papers.abstract: Exciton-polaritons can transport electronic excitation energy ballistically over distances far exceeding those accessible to bare excitons, yet their measured group velocities are often substantially lower than those predicted from the bare polariton dispersion. Recent experiments have shown that excitonic transfer coupling of the materials coupled inside the cavity can reduce the magnitude of group velocity renormalization, even though it does not impact the measured optical dispersion relation of polaritons. We derive an analytical, finite-temperature theory for the phonon-renormalized lower polariton group velocity that explicitly considers the impact of exciton transfer coupling. Our theory suggests that phonon-mediated virtual scattering of polariton states into dark states and back makes the magnitude of the group velocity renormalization sensitive to the dark exciton dispersion at large momentum. We use mixed quantum–classical dynamics simulations to corroborate the analytical predictions, capture experimental trends in layered halide perovskites, and show that stronger excitonic coupling helps preserve the ballistic character of polariton propagation. These results identify the excitonic transfer integral as a molecular design variable for preserving fast, coherent polariton transport under strong light–matter coupling.

papers.title: Super-Reaction Enhancement of Polariton-Mediated Electron Transfer
papers.abstract: We investigate the enhancement of polariton-mediated electron transfer (PMET) using a general super-reaction mechanism where multiple donor sites locally couple to individual acceptors. We demonstrate that this enhancement extends to the collective light-matter coupling regime with a large number of acceptors and cavity-coupled donors. We use analytic rate theory and quantum dynamics simulations to show that the local super-reaction mechanism serves as an additional enhancement to the delocalized driving force enhancement of PMET. We further incorporate bath-induced disorder in the donors to investigate precisely how collective light-matter coupling protects the coherent super-reaction enhancement against disorder. The results show that ET from bright polariton states, that are separated enough from the dark state manifold, is enhanced by the super-reaction mechanism in any ET regime, offering another avenue to realize cavity modification of photochemistry.

papers.title: Dynamic Flow Experimentation for Data-Rich Polymer Synthesis
papers.abstract: Growing global challenges in healthcare, energy, sustainability, and technology have motivated increased automation and robotics to accelerate material discovery and development. Continuous droplet flow chemistry has provided a solution to non-uniform mixing and transport phenomena and provides the advantages of batch reactions for screening individual reaction conditions and reagent compositions. Dynamic experimentation in flow chemistry enables the exploration of a broad design space while minimizing the use of reagents and time by continuously varying reaction parameters (such as temperature, concentration, reaction time). Here, an automated polymer synthesis platform with dynamic experimentation capabilities was implemented. The platform leveraged syringe pumps, a custom uniform irradiance photochemical reactor with tunable temperature control, inline Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), and an online benchtop nuclear magnetic resonance spectrometry (NMR) at 80 MHz for automated and data-rich polymer synthesis. The combination of inline FTIR, online NMR, and offline (500 MHz) NMR enabled cross-validation between analytical techniques, and parity plots comparing data between the techniques had an R 2 value greater than 0.99 for the dynamic experiment exploring the PET-RAFT homopolymerization of methyl acrylate. Dynamic experimentation was also used to explore the copolymerization of methyl acrylate and dimethylacrylamide. The obtained rich data were used to generate accurate Gaussian process regression models for the polymerization reactions with R 2 values greater than 0.9 for parity plots of the model vs experimental monomer conversion values. The Gaussian process regression model of the copolymerization was used to understand copolymerization reaction kinetics by determining reactivity ratios under various light intensity and temperature conditions.

papers.title: High-Resolution 3D Laser Printing of Microalgae-Derived Materials for Photodynamic Therapy
papers.abstract: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) offers localized, controllable cancer treatment through reactive oxygen species (ROS) generated by light-activated photosensitizers. Three-dimensional (3D) printing of PDT-active materials has emerged as a powerful tool for fabricating customized structures with controlled architecture and composition. However, conventional PDT materials often require complex, multi-step syntheses with low yields. Consequently, integrating natural photosensitizers into biocompatible matrices represents a crucial step towards sustainable PDT. Here, microalgae-derived materials are investigated to fabricate high-resolution scaffolds via 3D laser printing while retaining the intrinsic photoactive properties of chlorophyll. Within these matrices, native chlorophyll derivatives fulfill a triple light-induced function: driving microalgal lipid biosynthesis, initiating additive-free 3D laser printing, and acting as immobilized photosensitizers. Fluorometric assays confirm robust ROS generation upon red-light irradiation of the 3D printed microalgae-derived material. The photodynamic efficacy of these scaffolds is evaluated in melanoma cells to demonstrate their therapeutic potential. In vitro studies reveal significantly reduced cell viability upon irradiation, while maintaining cytocompatibility under dark conditions. Furthermore, the microalgae-derived materials enable the fabrication of scaffolds with varied complex geometries and feature sizes while retaining photodynamic activity. These findings demonstrate a highly versatile, biobased strategy combining natural photosensitizers with 3D laser printing to produce functional platforms for precision PDT.

papers.title: Basis-Set Limit Wavefunction Energies of Massive Water Clusters: Resolution of a Challenge for Many-Body Expansion
papers.abstract: The many-body expansion (MBE) offers a route to high-level wavefunction energies of systems beyond the reach of conventional calculations, but its practical convergence is entangled with basis set superposition error (BSSE), electrostatic embedding, and the scarcity of direct supersystem benchmarks at large size. Here, we show that as the complete-basis-set (CBS) limit is approached, electrostatically embedded three-body MBE, EE-MBE(3), provides accurate absolute and relative HF, RI-MP2, and CCSD(T) energies across water clusters of varying sizes. Critically, the largesystem conclusions are tested against direct same-level supersystem references rather than lowerlevel or extrapolated benchmarks. A distributed canonical RI-MP2 implementation enables a systematic HF/RI-MP2 campaign for 64 and 128 waters with cc-pVXZ and aug-cc-pVXZ basis sets (X = D, T, Q), with three configurations at each cluster size/basis set point. The largest calculation, (H2O)128/aug-cc-pVQZ, contains 22,016 spherical primary basis functions and, to our knowledge, is the largest reported MP2 calculation performed without a local-correlation approximation. At augcc-pVQZ, EE-MBE(3) maintains per-water errors within the 0.09 kcal mol-1 dynamical-accuracy

papers.title: Herzberg–Teller eﬀect as a phonon-assisted optical transition in molecules
papers.abstract: This study derives expressions for the photophysics of a molecule exhibiting the Herzberg–Teller (HT) effect. The derivation is based on Fermi’s golden rule, and the Longuet-Higgins representation, where the electron–photon and vibronic couplings are treated as perturbations, is used. All the vibrational modes are included, thus enabling the assignment of vibronic progressions in the spectrum originating from Franck–Condon factors. A forbidden transition is regarded as the photon absorption or emission accompanied by phonon absorption or emission, clarifying the contribution of vibronic structures to the transition. The derived expressions are applied to the absorption from S0 to S1 and fluorescence from S2 to S0 for azulene, a molecule known to exhibit the HT effect. Using the S4 state as an intermediate state, the calculated fluorescence spectrum and rate constant agree well with the experimental results. The in-plane stretching vibration of the five-membered ring contributes to phonon emission, whereas that at the junction of the five-and seven-membered rings contributes to the acceptance of the excess excitation energy. Furthermore, the vibronic coupling density analyses reveal that the vibronic couplings originate from the five-membered ring. This study presents a theory that allows for a detailed assignment of vibronic structures involved in the HT effect, providing design guidelines for HT molecules.

papers.title: Thioalkyltetrazines Synthesis from Aldehyde Precursors and Application in Ag-Mediated Liebeskind-Srogl Coupling
papers.abstract: Tetrahydrotetrazines are readily prepared from aldehydes, but have minimal precedent as precursors to tetrazines of value to bioorthogonal chemistry applications. Formaldehyde and glyoxylate esters undergo condensation with ([1,1'-biphenyl]-4-ylmethyl)thiocarbohydrazide bromide to give practical access to new thioalkyltetrazines as crystalline solids. 3-(([1,1’-biphenyl]-4-ylmethyl)thio)-tetrazine (h-Tz) was used for the synthesis of monosubstituted tetrazines via silver-mediated Liebeskind-Srogl coupling. Tetrazine-3-carboxylic esters were also synthesized using this method, further expanding the library of functional tetrazines for bioorthogonal chemistry applications.

papers.title: High-resolution mass spectrometry revealed that amino acid-based surfactants as a potential contributor to bacterial regrowth in tap water
papers.abstract: Microbial regrowth in tap water poses a potential threat to public health. Although biodegradable organic matter (BOM) supports microbial proliferation, specific BOM components remain largely unknown. This study evaluated the bacterial growth potential and explored BOM components in tap water samples collected from a hospital and a university. In the hospital sample, indigenous microbial communities grew up to 107 cells/mL after several days of incubation. Amplicon sequencing revealed that abundance of Methylotenera mobilis increased significantly. By solid-phase extraction followed by liquid chromatography high-resolution mass spectrometry (LC/HRMS), 36 putative BOM components were screened from 5,787 dissolved organic matter components. Tandem mass spectrometry and co-chromatography identified C18H36N4O3 as lauroyl arginine, an N-acyl amino acid and amino acid-based surfactant. N-lauroylglycine, and N-myristoylglycine were identified as BOM components from the university tap water sample. Further incubation experiments revealed that some bacterial species can use these three compounds as sole carbon sources. Our findings demonstrate that compound-level characterization using LC/HRMS can reveal previously unrecognized contaminants, with potential implications for biological stability and drinking water distribution system management.

papers.title: A Framework for Quantifying and Attributing Molecular Standardization Reproducibility in Cheminformatics Pipelines
papers.abstract: Molecular structure standardization, which normalizes salts, charge states, tautomers, isotopes and stereochemistry to a canonical form, is mandatory in essentially every cheminformatics pipeline. The protocols used to perform it nonetheless vary across tools, databases and configurations. Disagreement between standardization pipelines is documented at production scale, but existing analyses compare one pipeline against one reference, so they cannot identify which normalization decision produced a given disagreement. We present a measurement framework that treats standardization reproducibility as a quantifiable property of a dataset. Given an arbitrary set of protocols, the method determines whether they agree on each molecule's standardized identity, then attributes each disagreement to a specific normalization operation by systematic ablation. Agreement is evaluated under two identity conventions, canonical SMILES and InChIKey, which we show are not interchangeable. We applied the framework to a seeded random sample of 4,972 ChEMBL structures using three protocols that bracket the plausible range: a minimal one, one approximating the ChEMBL curation pipeline, and a deliberate upper-bound stress case. They agreed on 54.1% of molecules under canonical-SMILES identity (95% CI 52.8–55.5%) and 57.7% under InChIKey identity (56.3–59.0%). Ablation attributed divergence mainly to stereochemistry handling (66.6% of divergent molecules) and tautomer canonicalization (22.1%). Disabling stereochemistry removal, a step no major public pipeline performs, raises agreement to 75.5% and leaves tautomer canonicalization responsible for 87.4% of what remains. The cause spectrum is thus a property of the protocols compared and the dataset audited, not an intrinsic ranking of operations. A hand-assembled benchmark inverts it entirely, which argues for auditing the dataset actually in use instead of relying on published rates. Extending the comparison to the pipelines databases actually run, namely ChEMBL's own curation code and MolVS in two configurations, yields two further results. Our composed ChEMBL-like protocol reproduces ChEMBL's production pipeline on 99.8% of structures, so conclusions drawn from the composed protocols transfer to the real one. And two configurations of a single standardizer agreed with each other on only 56.0% of structures, while two independently developed standardizers agreed on 77.2%. Configuration choice within one tool spans a wider range of outcomes than the choice between tools, so naming the software used is not sufficient provenance. To test whether such divergence carries a practical cost, we applied the same protocols to 27,152 IC50 measurements across four targets. Grouping by standardized identity is what deduplication does, so protocol choice silently changes a dataset. The most aggressive protocol removed up to 9.5% of compounds by merging, fusing into single training labels compounds whose measured activities differed by up to three log units, a thousandfold difference in potency on a cardiac-safety endpoint. Cross-validated model performance was nonetheless statistically indistinguishable across protocols on all four targets, under both random-split and generalization-stressing scaffold-split cross-validation.

papers.title: A Blood–Brain Barrier-on-Chip Approaching In Vivo Tightness for Quantitative Ultrasound-Mediated Opening
papers.abstract: The blood–brain barrier (BBB) remains one of the greatest obstacles to the treatment of neurological diseases, preventing the delivery of nearly all large therapeutics and most small molecules to the brain. Although ultrasound-activated microbubbles offer a promising strategy for transient BBB opening, quantitative in vitro models capable of reproducing physiological barrier properties while allowing controlled ultrasound studies remain scarce. Here, we report a human BBB-on-chip that combines near-physiological barrier tightness with real-time quantitative permeability measurements under ultrasound exposure. We identify the key physical parameters governing barrier formation, demonstrating that microenvironment geometry and hydrogel confinement play a decisive role in establishing a functional endothelial barrier. The optimized platform exhibits permeability coefficients for 10 and 70 kDa dextran that approach in vivo values despite relying on a simple endothelial monoculture under static conditions. To quantitatively characterize barrier integrity, we compare three permeability formulations commonly used in the literature and introduce a complementary impermeability index describing barrier dynamics. Finally, we demonstrate that ultrasound-activated microbubbles increase barrier permeability by more than sixfold, enabling the extravasation of fluorescent tricaprylin nanodroplets into the hydrogel compartment.

papers.title: Motional Mode Conversion in the Orbitrap
papers.abstract: Resonant coupling between motional modes has played an important role in trapped-ion physics and Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance (FTICR) mass spectrometry, enabling ion manipulation, cooling, centering, and precision measurements. In contrast, controlled mode conversion in the Orbitrap mass analyzer has received little attention. Here we develop a general theory of motional mode conversion in the Orbitrap and identify three classes of resonant transfer: radial-axial (), azimuthal-axial (), and radial-azimuthal () conversion. Coupling potentials for the three conversion processes are derived from symmetry considerations and analyzed using an action-angle description of Orbitrap dynamics. Numerical simulations demonstrate coherent transfer between the participating motional modes and confirm the predicted resonance conditions. A central result is that conversion processes involving the radial mode require rotating-frame formulations to maintain phase coherence with the instantaneous radial motion direction of the ion in orbit, whereas azimuthal-axial conversion can be described directly in the laboratory coordinate frame. The simulations further demonstrate two potentially useful ion-manipulation techniques. Radial-azimuthal and radial-axial conversions provide two complementary routes to Orbitrap circularization, whereas radial-axial and azimuthal-axial conversions provide two complementary routes to axial centralization. These operations may be combined with azimuthal dipolar excitation/de-excitation, or additional mode-conversion steps to prepare ions in standardized trajectories prior to image-current detection of the azimuthal rotation. The concepts developed here establish a theoretical foundation for additional active control of Orbitrap ion motion beyond the methods provided by traditional dipolar excitation and suggest new opportunities for ion manipulation.

papers.title: Extending Hertzian Contact Area Theory to Plastic Deformation of Glassy Polymer Particles
papers.abstract: Quantifying the mechanical response of polymer particles under compression is fundamentally hindered by a deceptively simple problem: the contact area between the particle and compression plate can rarely be directly measured during deformation. Since Hertz formulated his contact theory in 1881, widely used Hertzian and adhesive contact models have remained largely confined to the elastic regime, leaving the plastic deformation behavior of polymer particles fundamentally out of reach. Here, we extend the original Hertzian contact area relation from elastic deformation to plastic deformation by combining it with the Boyce–Parks–Argon constitutive model. The contact area predicted by the model agree well with those obtained directly from all-atom molecular dynamics simulations of poly(methyl methacrylate) and poly(methyl acrylate) particles. When the framework is applied to experimental compression data of polystyrene and acrylic particles, it identifies clear yield points and shows that crosslinking density and particle-size effects can be understood within the established framework of bulk polymer mechanics. The framework provides a route to the intrinsic mechanical properties of polymer particles beyond the yield point without direct measurement of the contact area, supporting the rational design of particles with tailored mechanical properties.

papers.title: A Silica-Supported Tungsten-Iridium Hydride Catalyst with Enhanced Arene H/D Exchange performances
papers.abstract: Despite extensive exploration of reaction conditions, the direct synthesis of a molecular tungsten-iridium complex from Cp*IrH 4 and W(≡C t Bu)(Np) 3 remained elusive. However, we discovered that the silica-supported tungsten alkylidyne species, (≡SiO)W(≡C t Bu)(CH 2 t Bu) 2 , readily reacts with Cp*IrH 4 , enabling the formation of heterobimetallic surface species, (≡SiO)W(CH 2 t Bu) 2 (H) n IrCp*. This result demonstrates the power of Surface OrganoMetallic Chemistry (SOMC) as a unique synthetic method for assembling heterobimetallic architectures that are otherwise inaccessible or unstable under homogeneous conditions. Preliminary catalytic evaluations in H/D exchange of arenes reveal that this silica-supported W–Ir material shows the best performance within the series, exhibiting higher activity than Hf–Ir and Ta–Ir analogs.

papers.title: Synthesis and Reactivity of Fluorene-Bridged Cyclic Diaryliodonium Salts
papers.abstract: Spirocyclic organic compounds play a significant role in organic materials, particularly in the field of optoelectronics. In this study, novel spiro-bridged cyclic diaryliodonium salts were synthesised in yields of up to 78%. The structure of the parent salt was confirmed by X-ray crystallography, and the salt was functionalised in iodine-chalcogen exchanges towards highly valuable xanthene derivatives in up to 88% yield.

papers.title: Isolation and bonding analysis of copper(I)-xenon complex stabilized by weakly coordinating alkoxyaluminate anion.
papers.abstract: The first crystalline Cu(I)-Xe complex, Xe-Cu[Al(OR F ) 4 ], 1 , (R F = C(CF 3 ) 3 ), forms as a salt of the weakly coordinating perfluorinated alkoxyaluminate upon ligand exchange between elemental xenon and Cu(I)-N 2 complex, Cu(N 2 )[Al(OR F ) 4 ]. Despite the lack of relativistic character of the copper ion, 1 is obtained under ambient Xe pressure and at room temperature. The crystal structure reveals that it is a molecular compound where xenon is a terminal ligand to copper with steric factors causing a Cu-Xe bond elongation in comparison with known gas-phase Xe-Cu(I) species. Extensive computational analysis facilitates the interpretation of spectral properties and gives insight into the nature of the bond between Xe and Cu[Al(OR F ) 4 ]. EDA-NOCV and NPA indicate that electrostatic forces between Xe and Cu[Al(OR F ) 4 ] have the largest share of its energy, though orbital interactions between the 5p orbital of Xe and the hybridized 4s/3d orbital of Cu as well as dispersive forces are also significant. Though the Xe-Cu[Al(OR F ) 4 ] bond is fairly weak in comparison with Au + -Xe in the known [Xe-AuAsF 3 ] complex, the isolation of 1 is possible thanks to the use of the weakly coordinating anion and solvent, which are worse ligands to copper than Xe atom.

papers.title: Wavelength-Sequential Generation of Multi-Emissive Fluorophores for Site-Selective Fluorescence Nanoscopy
papers.abstract: Photoactivatable fluorophores are indispensable tools for super-resolution microscopy, but their performance is often hindered by the need for caging group chemistry, ultraviolet activation, interfering triplet-state photochemistry, and most importantly resulting in a single emissive scaffold. Here, we report a hydroacridine-based fluorophore that addresses the often encountered limitations by providing caging-group-free activation using visible light. A heteroatom-engineering strategy enables rapid singlet-state proton-coupled electron transfer, converting a blue-emissive precursor into two highly fluorescent acridinium states with distinct green (ΦF ≈ 0.80) and red (ΦF ≈ 0.78) emission by a two-step photoconversion using blue and green light sequentially. The process operates efficiently under physiological conditions without involving triplet biradical intermediates, enhancing compatibility with live-cell imaging. The fluorophore architecture further supports organelle-targeted imaging and photoinduced intracellular redistribution, enabling multicolour visualization from a single molecular scaffold, serving both spatial and temporal control over the photoactivation. These findings provide new strategies for heteroatom-controlled visible-light photoactivation and fluorophore design, providing a new platform for next-generation super-resolution imaging.

papers.title: Drawing the Bow: Bending Peropyrene for Singlet Fission
papers.abstract: Singlet fission (SF) can overcome efficiency limits in solar cells by converting one photon into two triplet excitons. Only a few organic chromophores, however, possess triplet energies compatible with Si- and GaAs-based semiconductors commonly used in photovoltaic devices. Peropyrene fulfills these energetic requirements, but excimer formation in its unsubstituted form stabilizes the singlet excited state. This lowers its energy below the threshold required for SF, necessitating control over intermolecular interactions. Contorting chromophores reduces their ability to achieve effective π-surface overlap with neighboring molecules, but the most common strategy, twisting, comes at the cost of a lower triplet energy. We overcome this trade-off by bending peropyrene into a bow via selective π-radical cascade reactions. This approach enables progressive deformation to the limit attainable with this method, a regime hitherto inaccessible by strategies developed for shorter and longer homologs. Bending reorganizes the solid-state crystal packing and reduces the extent of red-shifted emission in concentrated solution and in the solid state, consistent with reduced excimer stabilization. Calculations show a slight increase in triplet energy, desirable for improved compatibility with relevant semiconductors.

papers.title: Chiral Intramolecular Ether–Borane FLPs for Asymmetric Ketone Hydrogenation
papers.abstract: Asymmetric hydrogenation of ketones remains challenging in frustrated Lewis pair (FLP) catalysis, largely because the low basicity of ketones places stringent demands on both H 2 activation and stereocontrol. Here we introduce binaphthyl ether–boranes (BINEBs), a new class of chiral intramolecular FLPs featuring a bis-ether Lewis base tethered to a strongly Lewis acidic borane on an axially chiral binaphthyl scaffold. BINEBs catalyze the asymmetric hydrogenation of a broad range of aromatic ketones, delivering chiral secondary alcohols with high enantioselectivities. This platform also enables the first metal-free kinetic resolution of cyclic α-haloketones using H 2 as the reductant, providing enantioenriched cis-halohydrins with selectivity factors (s) exceeding 200. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations support a multifunctional role for the key intramolecular bis-ether motif: it mediates heterolytic H 2 cleavage and, following proton transfer to the ketone, remains engaged through hydrogen bonding, orienting the substrate for stereoselective hydride transfer. This study illustrates how covalent Lewis acid–base preorganization can enhance substrate recognition and stereocontrol, providing catalyst design principles that may open opportunities in asymmetric FLP hydrogenation and Lewis acid catalysis.

papers.title: When Philicity Fails: Mechanistic Control of Ambiphilic Metal–Superoxo Reactivity
papers.abstract: A fundamental challenge in oxygen activation chemistry is understanding the factors that govern the switch between electrophilic and nucleophilic reactivity in metal–superoxo intermediates. Notably, only four ambiphilic metal–superoxo systems have been reported to date, yet the origins of their ambiphilic behavior remain poorly understood, limiting the rational design of catalysts with predictable and tunable reactivity. Here, we systematically investigate these four reported complexes, [(L 1 ) •+ Co II –O2 •⁻ ] – ( 1b ) (where L1 = (N • ( o -PhNC(O) i Pr) 2 ) 2– ) , [(L 2 )Mn III –O 2 •– ] ( 2b ) (where L 2 = BDP Br P = 2,6-bis((2-( S )-di(4-bromo)phenylhydroxylmethyl-1-pyrrolidinyl)methyl)pyridine) 2– ), [(L 3 )Fe III (O 2 •⁻ )] 2− ( 3b ) (where L 3 = TAML = Tetra Amido Macrocyclic Ligand) 4- and [(L 4 )Co III –O 2 •⁻ ] ( 4b ) (where L 4 = BDPP = 2,6-bis((2-(S)diphenylhydroxylmethyl-1-pyrrolidinyl)methyl)pyridine) 2– ) , using density functional theory to elucidate their O 2 activation and reactivity toward electrophilic and nucleophilic substrates. O 2 activation preferentially proceeds through inner-sphere pathways, in which electron transfer and M–O 2 bond formation occurs concomitantly, with ligand-to-O 2 electron transfer for 1a and metal-to-O 2 electron transfer for 2a – 4a . For PPA deformylation, coordinatively saturated complex 2b favor α-hydrogen atom abstraction, whereas the open, four-coordinate 1b preferentially undergoes nucleophilic addition. In contrast, oxygen-atom-transfer reactivity toward triphenylphosphine does not follow electrophilicity alone: despite the higher intrinsic electrophilicity of [(L 5 )Cu II –O 2 •– ] + (L 5 =TMPA = tris(2-pyridyl methyl)amine); ( 5b ), 1b exhibits a lower activation barrier (68.4 vs 81.4 kJ/mol) owing to stronger orbital interactions and reduced deformation requirements. Collectively, these results establish that metal–superoxo reactivity is governed by the interplay of coordination environment, philicity, orbital interactions, steric effects, and deformation energy. These insights provide a framework for rational catalyst design in which reactivity can be tuned by optimizing the complete electronic and structural reaction landscape rather than maximizing philicity alone.

papers.title: Overcoming the Density Limitation of Polyhydroxyurethane Self-Blown Foams through Sol–Gel Chemistry
