papers.abstract: Non-isocyanate polyurethane foams (NIPUFs), particularly polyhydroxyurethane (PHU) foams prepared by cyclic carbonate aminolysis, are promising safer alternatives to conventional polyurethane foams. Although water-induced CO 2 self-blowing can now be achieved from room-temperature formulations within minutes, access to foams with densities below 150 kg·m -3 remains a significant challenge. Herein, we introduce alkoxysilanes as additives for the fabrication of NIPUFs with ultra-low densities (30–50 kg·m -3 ). The strategy synergistically combines CO 2 generation from cyclic carbonate hydrolysis with in situ alcohol formation through alkoxysilane hydrolysis and condensation. Without external physical blowing agents, surfactants, or foam stabilizers, hybrid foams with densities of 28–35 kg·m -3 were obtained, entering the range of conventional lightweight foams. The resulting open-cell foams showed high porosity, complete cyclic carbonate conversion, and tunable mechanical properties depending on amine structure. Their rebound resilience was also strongly and reversibly modulated by humidity, increasing from 0–9% in the dry state to 37–56% at 90% RH and recovering upon drying. This work demonstrates a simple and versatile alkoxysilane-assisted self-co-blowing strategy toward low-density NIPU cellular materials with humidity-responsive mechanical functionality.

papers.title: Lookahead Bayesian Optimisation for Molecular Growth in Self-Driving Laboratories
papers.abstract: Self-driving laboratories can autonomously execute iterative design-make-test-analyse cycles, but molecular optimisation presents a distinctive challenge: selecting which compound to elaborate determines not only the next experiment, but also the chemical space accessible in subsequent rounds. Conventional molecular Bayesian optimisation typically evaluates compounds without considering how their selection changes what can subsequently be synthesised. Here, we introduce Lookahead Bayesian Optimisation (LABO), which instead values candidate molecules according to the predicted value of the synthetically accessible chemical space they unlock, enabling optimisation to account for future experimental opportunities. We evaluate LABO in simulated five-round molecular optimisation campaigns across 30 lead-like starting compounds and five kinase targets. LABO outperformed established molecular optimisation strategies from the literature across all 30 optimisation landscapes, as well as random, greedy and Bayesian optimisation controls. LABO was shown to improve ligand-lipophilicity efficiency by 1.25 units over random selection, equivalent to approximately 18-fold greater potency at equal lipophilicity, and by 0.34 units (2.2-fold) over greedy elaboration. These results demonstrate a general principle for autonomous molecular optimisation: under synthetic constraints, the value of a molecule depends not only on its predicted properties, but on the future experiments that selecting it makes possible. By explicitly incorporating this future experimental value into molecular selection, LABO provides a framework for planning successive rounds of molecular growth in self-driving laboratories.

papers.title: A field-deployable method for measuring picomolar mercury levels in natural waters
papers.abstract: Measurements of mercury (Hg) at sub- to picomolar concentrations in natural waters often rely on cold vapor atomic fluorescence spectrometry (CVAFS), which provides the sensitivity required for trace detection. However, CVAFS instruments are not well suited for routine field deployment and require compressed high-purity argon or helium gas to operate, limiting their use in remote regions and locations without established analytical infrastructure. Cold-vapor atomic absorption spectrometry (CVAAS) offers a robust alternative but generally lacks the sensitivity required for low-level natural waters. Here, we optimized and tested the Nippon Instruments EMP Gold+, a purge-and-trap preconcentration system coupled to a portable CVAAS detector, to address this analytical challenge. We developed protocols for total Hg (THg) and dissolved gaseous Hg (DGM) and evaluated their performance in seawater during field deployments in Monterey Bay, California, USA and the Gulf of Guinea, Ghana. The optimized methods achieved detection limits of 0.97 pM for THg and 0.25 pM for DGM. THg measured in the Gulf of Guinea agreed closely with laboratory CVAFS measurements (R 2 = 0.953, slope = 1.11), with field matrix-spike recoveries of 90.6-96.2%. In Monterey Bay, portable DGM measurements reproduced the vertical structure observed independently for dimethylmercury using gas chromatography coupled to CVAFS. We demonstrate that this new approach can support direct measurements in regions where compressed gases and specialized analytical infrastructure are unavailable and provide rapid screening to guide subsequent sampling for more detailed Hg speciation.

papers.title: Uncertainty Quantification for Aquatic Ecotoxicity Prediction
papers.abstract: Aquatic ecosystems are threatened by thousands of chemicals whose hazard is often unknown. Laboratory tests of individual chemicals on individual species establish, for example, the Lethal Concentration for 50% of test individuals (LC50), but for most chemicals in use such data exist for only a small fraction of species. A growing body of research applies machine learning to bridge these gaps. Before such models can be relied on in regulatory and environmental management contexts, they must not only be accurate in general, but also quantify how far individual predictions can be trusted. We address this by training a Bayesian Factorization Machine (BFM) on ecotoxicity test data. The BFM matches the accuracy of the current state of the art in predicting LC50 values, and additionally quantifies the uncertainty of every prediction, separating the part arising from a lack of data (epistemic) from the part that is irreducible, reflecting inter-test and biological variability (aleatoric). We then show how this uncertainty propagates into environmental quality assessment: Species Sensitivity Distributions (SSDs) become ensembles of plausible curves rather than single fits, and the hazardous concentrations derived from them carry credible intervals that are widest for the data-poor chemicals where conventional SSDs are least reliable.

papers.title: DNA binders based on the integration of duocarmycins into minor groove-targeting polyamides have potent and selective anti-trypansosomal activity
papers.abstract: Duocarmycins are attractive DNA alkylating agents due to their high potency; however, increasing their selectivity has always been a challenge. Here, we describe the integration of the duocarmycin subunits DSA and CI into minor groove-targeting polyamides, compounds that can ‘read’ DNA sequences. The synthesis of a CI analogue suitably substituted for solid phase synthesis using Fmoc-chemistry is described. The synthesis of the hybrid compounds is achieved using solid phase methods on chloro-trityl resin. The resulting hybrids display sequence-selective DNA alkylation, depending on the enantiomer and position of the duocarmycin unit as might be expected, except for the compounds with a central DSA alkylation subunit, which act more similarly to reversed analogues. The CI hybrids with a central unit are relatively unreactive with DNA and modelling studies suggest that the CI subunit is sub-optimally located for alkylation in these structures. Investigations against the parasite T. brucei, responsible for African trypanomiasis, highlight compounds with nanomolar potency and high selectivity (SI >300), showing that the integration of duocarmycins into the backbone of polyamides has promise for developing gene-targeting small molecule anti-parasitic agents.

papers.title: Spin-dependent thermoelectric transportproperties of DPH-based molecular device
Fourteen-Membered Macrocyclic Copper Complex for Highly Selective Electrochemical Nitrate Reduction to Ammonia
papers.abstract: The selective electrochemical reduction of nitrate (NO3−) to ammonia (NH3) represents a promising route for sustainable NH3 production. However, achieving high NH3 selectivity remains challenging due to competing reactions. Additionally, many reported catalysts rely on noble metals and often require relatively elevated catalyst loadings to achieve high apparent activity, while most systems operate only at relatively low current densities. Herein, a fourteen-membered macrocyclic copper complex supported on Ketjenblack (Cu-14MR/KB) is reported as a cathode catalyst for the highly selective electrochemical reduction of NO3− to NH3. With a low Cu loading of 1.34 μmol cm−2, Cu-14MR/KB delivered a high Faraday efficiency for NH3 synthesis of up to 94.8% at a current density of −26.3 mA cm−2 and maintained high NH3 selectivity over a wide current density range from −26.3 to −150 mA cm−2. Notably, at −150 mA cm−2, Cu-14MR/KB achieved an NH3 yield rate of 604 μmol cm−2 h−1 with an NH3 Faraday efficiency of 86.4%. Furthermore, a more contracted Cu–N4 coordination environment was revealed in Cu-14MR than in CuPc, with a shorter Cu–N bond distance, suggesting relatively stronger Cu–N interactions. This work provides an efficient strategy for high-performance NO3− electroreduction using a low-loading and non-noblemetal catalyst.

papers.title: Additive Manufacturing of Polyvinylidene Fluoride (PVDF) Toward High Performance with AI-Driven Workflows
papers.abstract: Polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) is a high-performance fluoropolymer known for its chemical resistance, mechanical strength, thermal stability, and piezoelectric and dielectric behavior, making it an ideal material for additive manufacturing (AM). The first part of this paper provides an overview and demonstration of this potential, with the first section reviewing PVDF materials, crystallographic phases, and fused deposition modeling (FDM) processing. This perspective provides practical guidance for optimizing PVDF AM for engineering applications, as well as the potential for artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) workflows to inform future research.

papers.title: Hydrogen-Assisted Reduction of Metal Oxides: Reaction Mechanisms, Process Optimization, and AI/ML-Enabled Pathways for Sustainable Materials Processing
papers.abstract: Hydrogen reduction of metal oxides has been identified as a promising approach for producing some engineering (metallic) materials, both through primary production and the reprocessing of waste materials. Such an approach offers a viable promise for the production of value-added materials in a sustainable manner. Unlike in other reduction processes, where obnoxious gases get 2 released as byproducts, hydrogen reduction, on the other hand, generate water vapor as the clean principal byproduct. Such an approach renders the overall mcheaping process inexpensive because of the use of metal oxides as the cheap feedstocks. However, the manufacturing process offers several challenges, upscaling being one of the major ones. In the present review, an attempt has been made to assess the overall reduction process in an integrated manner, which relates thermodynamic principles, reduction mechanisms, reactor-scale phenomena, and specific application requirements. The principles of thermodynamic constraints related to oxide reducibility are described in relation to the role of reduction temperature, gas compositions, and the gas-solid reaction mechanisms to determine rate-controlling processes, diffusion coefficients, and the role of catalysis for the production of metallic materials by primary manufacturing processes and environmental remediation. There is also the consideration of an enabling role of automation, modeling, and digital twin technologies. The manuscript describes practiced hydrogen reduction processes to produce some of the specific metals, such as iron, nickel, cobalt, and refractory metals, but also the need to improve hydrogen access, efficiency, scalability, and ensure catalyst longevity. Enhanced research in hydrogen, renewable power coupling, AI-assisted process control and reactor design are some of the aspects that have been observed to be the major enablers. The manuscript not only describes the status and future projections but also provides a roadmap for improving the status quo.

papers.title: Deoxygenative Dialkylation of Vinylic Epoxides to Chiral Alkanes by Double SN2’
papers.abstract: Chiral alkanes bearing two contiguous tertiary all-carbon stereocentres are important motifs in bioactive molecules, natural products and functional compounds, yet their stereocontrolled synthesis remains challenging. Here we report their modular preparation through the formal deoxygenative dialkylation of enantioenriched vinyl epoxides. Two consecutive organocopper-mediated S N 2′ substitutions enable stereospecific transfer of the starting stereochemical information followed by diastereoselective installation of the adjacent stereocentre. The sequence can be performed in one pot, providing densely substituted hydrocarbon frameworks with high regio- and stereocontrol. The method accommodates diverse, including sterically demanding, alkyl substituents, extends to cyclic substrates, and leaves a terminal alkene for downstream diversification. Vinyl epoxides thus provide a stereochemically encoded platform for straightforward access to complex chiral alkanes.

papers.title: Energy ordering of singlet and triplet excitedstates in s-indacene, Pentalene,Cyclobutadiene derivatives in singlet fission : A model exact and density matrixrenormalization group study
A bipartite quantum-acoustic architecture stabilizes multi-exciton solitons at 323 K
papers.abstract: A fundamental thermal paradox has constrained the physical viability of quantum coherent Davydov solitons in protein α-helices for over 50 years. At 323 K (0.0278 eV), ambient thermal noise disrupts the localized amide I self-trapping resonance, rapidly scattering multi-quanta excitations into delocalized thermal states on femtosecond timescales. This long-standing decoherence gap is resolved by a non-equilibrium, bipartite quantum-acoustic stabilization matrix which induces a transverse acoustic viscoelastic phonon gap, extending exciton coherence lifetimes from 6.5 fs to 42.6 fs by acting as a macroscopic low-pass filter. Utilizing non-Markovian open quantum system simulations, we demonstrate that a highly polarizable variable-dipole linactant at the lipid raft interface induces localized electrodynamic Stark defects, breaking lattice translation symmetry to anchor the wave packet. Sustaining this protective boundary against passive diffusive loss mandates a strict kinetic equilibrium that arrests uncoupled proton leaks, directly coupling the continuous, hydrogen-bonded α-helices of eukaryotic F/V-type rotary c-rings to a hyper-rigid viscoelastic membrane locked in a far-from-equilibrium state. Finally, we present a definitive pathway to bypass thermal decoherence by establishing three physical boundary conditions to translate these biological principles into a predictive blueprint for synthetic quantum-acoustic metamaterials.

papers.title: Fusion-Number-Dependent Emergence of 16π-Electron Antiaromatic Circuits in Thienocyclopenta-Fused Pyrenes
papers.abstract: Antiaromatic 4nπ-electron circuits provide a powerful strategy for narrowing the HOMO–LUMO gaps of π-conjugated molecules, yet their contribution is often attenuated or obscured in stable polycyclic frameworks by competing local aromatic stabilization. Here we report a systematic series of thienocyclopenta-fused pyrenes containing one ( 1TP ), two ( trans -2TP and cis -2TP ), or four ( 4TP ) fused thienocyclopentadiene units, designed to evaluate the stepwise contributions of embedded 16π-electron circuits. The molecules were synthesized through Suzuki–Miyaura coupling followed by palladium-mediated annulation. Notably, 4TP was isolated as an air- and ambient-light-stable green solid, and its structure was confirmed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Comparative 1 H NMR analysis revealed a progressive upfield shift of diagnostic protons upon increasing the number of fused thienocyclopentadiene units, indicating the emergence and amplification of a paratropic ring-current effect. Theoretical calculations supported the emergence and strengthening of 16π-electron antiaromatic contributions in the two 2TP isomers and 4TP . Frontierorbital calculations and cyclic voltammetry further showed that the LUMO level is substantially stabilized whereas the HOMO level remains nearly unchanged, resulting in a systematic decrease in the HOMO–LUMO gaps. These results establish thienocyclopenta fusion as an effective molecular design strategy for controlling the antiaromatic contribution of 16π-electron circuits within a stable carbon-rich π-framework.

papers.title: Pore-network homogeneity for mechanically reliable powder-compacted solid-electrolyte separators
papers.abstract: All-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) with alloy anodes require solid-electrolyte (SE) separators that sustain ion transport while accommodating repeated electrode-derived mechanical loads. However, the mechanical state of powder-compacted separators is commonly inferred from bulk porosity, averaged mechanical properties, or cell-level stack pressure changes, obscuring spatially heterogeneous local responses. Here, we show that pore-network homogeneity is a key determinant of the mechanical reliability of sulfide solid-electrolyte separators by governing local mechanical heterogeneity and stress localization. FIB-SEM tomography and spatially resolved nanoindentation reveal that a highly densified separator with a broad particle-size distribution (PSD) retains clustered pore-rich and mechanically compliant regions, whereas a narrower-PSD separator exhibits a more homogeneous pore network and local mechanical response. Despite comparable cell-level pressure evolution, the two separators show markedly different cycling stability. Post-cycling microscopy reveals cracking and interfacial delamination in the heterogeneous separator, while microstructure-resolved simulations reveal stronger local stress amplification consistent with these observations. Controlled digital structures with identical D50 and porosity further isolate PSD-dependent changes in pore architecture and stress distribution. These findings establish pore-network homogeneity as a key design criterion for mechanically reliable solid-electrolyte separators beyond ionic conductivity and bulk densification.

papers.title: pH-responsive nanopores enable programmable transmembrane potential
papers.abstract: Biological ion channels achieve highly selective, ultrafast ion transport through stimulus-responsive gating, in which conformational changes triggered by chemical cues such as pH that modulate channel permeability with exquisite precision. Replicating this coupled chemical-structural functionality in synthetic membranes remains a fundamental challenge, particularly for scalable platforms relevant to energy harvesting, desalination, and chemical sensing. Here, we report a bioinspired polymer-metal-organic framework (MOF) composite membrane in which an amino acid (histidine) functionalized MOF nanopores serve as synthetic proton-gated anion channel. The histidine modified, spatially confined ion transport pathway exhibited selective Cl- diffusion at pH 4, enabling pH programmable control of transmembrane potential. Micrometer-scale percolated transport networks within the composite membrane, architecturally inspired by ion channels embedded in lipid bilayers, translate localized αNH2(histidine)-anion specific interaction into macroscopic, anion selective transmembrane potential output. This work establishes a generalizable design strategy for coupling chemical gating with macroscopic ion transport in synthetic membrane systems, with direct implications for ion separations, sensing and osmotic energy generation.

papers.title: A quantitative roadmap from catalyst benchmarks to commercial hybrid electrolysis
papers.abstract: Hybrid water electrolysis replaces the sluggish oxygen evolution reaction with the oxidation of an organic substrate, producing hydrogen alongside another value-added chemical. In its most efficient form, the electrochemical oxidative dehydrogenation (EOD) of aldehydes, hydrogen evolves at both electrodes with specific electricity consumption down to 4 kWh kg−1 totalH2 , tenfold lower than conventional water electrolysis. Yet whether such efficiency gains translate into commercial viability has never been tested, as the field lacks standardized performance metrics, limiting catalyst comparability and industrial viability assessment. We propose three performance metrics: Anodic Hydrogen Productivity (AHP), Specific Electricity Consumption (SEC), and Deactivation Rate (DR), and benchmark all reported EOD systems as a case study. A techno-economic analysis links these metrics to net present value and reveals a roadmap to commercial viability: (i) Feedstock selection is the primary economic determinant; (ii) Catalyst stability is the foremost bottleneck, with DRs exceeding tolerable values by three orders of magnitude; (iii) Current density is a linear lever on economics; (iv) Energy efficiency, the property most intensively optimized by the field, matters least, contributing under 1% of net present value for high-value products. This offers quantitative benchmarks for catalyst and process development toward commercially viable EOD. Because the metrics depend only on measurable cell performance, benchmarks and roadmap transfer directly to other hybrid electrolysis concepts.

papers.title: Nucleus-Independent Chemical Shifts in disordered nanoporous carbons are governed by the long-range magnetic response of the carbon framework
papers.abstract: Nanoporous carbons are widely used in energy storage, gas storage, and separation technologies due to their high surface area, porosity, and electrical conductivity. Understanding atomic-scale structure is critical for interpreting performance, yet disorder greatly complicates characterization. NMR chemical shifts of adsorbed molecules have emerged as a probe of structural disorder, but how nucleus-independent chemical shifts (NICS) relate to structure in realistic, disordered carbons remains poorly understood. Here, we generate realistic nanoporous carbon structures using molecular dynamics simulations and compute pore-averaged NICS using density functional theory, reproducing experimentally observed negative values across commercial nanoporous carbons. We find a moderate correlation between sp 2 domain area and NICS, indicating that domain size alone is a poor predictor of the observed shifts, while NICS value also weakly correlate with heteroatom content and 6-membered ring fraction. Instead, decomposing local shielding from non-local contributions shows that the framework's bulk magnetic susceptibility, which implicitly encodes domain size, packing arrangement and defects, dominates the pore-averaged response. These results reframe NICS as a reporter of the framework's collective magnetic susceptibility, rather a local probe of isolated aromatic environments. This position NMR as a quantitative tool for characterizing functional disorder in nanoporous carbons and will help establish a link between framework architecture and performance.

papers.title: Directional Control of Droplet Motion via Geometric Gating
papers.abstract: We explore new methods for inducing the movement of water droplets on elastomeric substrates, such as polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS). Our approach builds upon the well-known phenomenon that water droplets move easily across these substrates when swelled with silicone oil. While designing shallow open channels and traps on a PDMS film offers a simple way to control a droplet's trajectory by tilting the substrate in two orthogonal directions, this method is poorly suited for manipulating multiple droplets simultaneously. To address this limitation, we introduce two new methods. The first method utilizes a piano-concave PDMS platform with a radius of curvature significantly larger than the size of the droplet and its translation distance. When the system's configuration is altered, this curved substrate consistently guides the droplet along a curved geodesic. The second method incorporates diode-like gates on the PDMS. These gates are created on either flat or piano-concave PDMS films by embedding thin, rigid plates into the elastomer prior to crosslinking, followed by swelling in silicone oil. This process generates sigmoidal steps that restrict droplet motion to a single direction. Finally, we demonstrate how combining these two strategies enables various forms of directed motion for both single and multiple droplets.

papers.title: Carboxyl–Group Removal and Return: Mechanistic and Strategic Advances in Decarboxylation–Carboxylation
papers.abstract: Carboxylic acids are ubiquitous functionalities and indispensable synthetic linchpins in organic chemistry. In recent years, strategies involving the removal, exchange, or recycling of the carboxyl group, particularly decarboxylation and carboxylation have gained remarkable momentum, partly driven by the imperative to valorize carbon dioxide generated in chemical transformations. Beyond simple CO2 extrusion, tandem decarboxylation–carboxylation and related cyclic processes have emerged as powerful yet underexplored approaches for constructing carboxylic acids in a single operation. This review highlights recent advances (2000–2026) in decarboxylation–re-carboxylation chemistry, with an emphasis on mechanistic understanding, reactive intermediates, and the strategic use of CO2 as a transient functional handle. We introduce a unified conceptual framework that classifies carboxyl–group transfer based on the identity of the carbon shuttle, the timing and mode of carboxyl reintroduction, and the nature of reactive intermediates. Subsequent sections discuss three major mechanistic archetypes: CO2–cycling decarboxylation–re-carboxylation, ester–cycling decarboxylation–re-esterification, and non-in situ carboxyl transfer using exogenous CO2 or alternative carboxyl sources. By delineating key developments and conceptual trends, we aim to inspire further innovation in exploiting carboxyl–group recycling as a platform for sustainable molecular synthesis.

papers.title: DeMiR: Density-Matrix-Informed Representations for Molecular Property Prediction
papers.abstract: The Hohenberg–Kohn theorem, which states that all physical quantities in the ground state are functionals of the electron density, suggests that much of a molecule's behavior is encoded in its electronic structure. This study proposes DeMiR, a model that treats electron density matrix prediction as a pretraining task. DeMiR reconstructs cc-pVDZ/B3LYP density matrices for molecules ranging in size from QM9-scale molecules to drug-like molecules with up to 146 atoms, achieving median NMAE values of 1.0% and 2.16%, respectively. At the atomic level, the model's embeddings contain electronic structure information: per-atom electronic observables are predicted with an R² of 0.94 by a linear probe, whereas Uni-Mol reaches 0.84 and a randomly initialized model of the same architecture only 0.63. The embeddings also remove 44.9% of the residual error left by a geometry-based descriptor, showing that this information is not linearly accessible from an explicit geometric descriptor. At the molecular level, transfer depends on the label type. Where electronic structure directly determines the property, transfer holds: on an external experimental pKa test set, fine-tuned DeMiR achieves an MAE of 1.143, significantly outperforming a randomly initialized control with the same architecture and training budget (1.397), and performing on par with or better than chemical foundation models pretrained on far larger datasets. In contrast, for labels such as pIC50 and ADMET, DeMiR shows no consistent advantage over existing general-purpose foundation models, as two-dimensional substructures and physicochemical descriptors have already saturated predictive performance. This study presents the scope within which a connection between electron density prediction capability and molecular property prediction capability holds, along with its boundaries.

papers.title: Hybrid Organosilicon Polymers Integrating Latent Si–Si Chromophores and Orthogonal Si–O–C Reactivity
Resolving Kinase Resistance Landscapes via Antisymmetric Siamese Graph Networks and Co-Folding Ensembles
papers.abstract: Acquired clinical resistance to small-molecule kinase inhibitors arising from single-point mutations within the ATP-binding cleft presents a critical challenge in precision oncology. Conventional computational modeling relies either on rigid docking—which overlooks induced structural alterations—or computationally demanding alchemical free energy perturbation (FEP) methods that cannot scale across wide mutational panels. In this work, we present an end-to-end computational methodology integrating multi-state conformational ensemble generation via the generative biomolecular co-folding engine Boltz with a continuous distance-aware Siamese Graph Neural Network (GNN). Crucially, we introduce an unconstrained bias-free difference head that strictly enforces thermodynamic antisymmetry (f (0) ≡ 0.0 kcal/mol), eliminating trivial baseline drift. Under rigorous 5-fold cross-validation on experimentally characterized kinase resistance pairs, the model achieves an out-of-fold root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 1.637 kcal/mol (MAE = 1.459 kcal/mol, Pearson R = 0.239, Spearman ρ = 0.260). Across a prospective panel of 52 clinical kinase-inhibitor complexes, the architecture structurally rationalizes key resistance patterns, resolving the steric disruption of the ABL1 T315I gatekeeper mutation circumvented by ponatinib and the covalent ablation of EGFR C797S against osimertinib.

papers.title: Electrochemically Controlled Crystallization Using Selective Bipolar Membrane Electrodialysis
papers.abstract: Nitrogen and phosphorus nutrient recovery from wastewater represents a critical frontier for circular fertilizer manufacturing and effective water treatment. Conventional chemical precipitation remains hindered by the need for expensive reagent consumables. Here, we examine an integrated, chemical-free electrochemical mixer (ECM) system that leverages selective bipolar membrane electrodialysis (SBED) to achieve precise struvite (MgNH4PO4 · 6H2O) crystallization. We furthermore demonstrate how control over current density (1–5 mA cm−2), specific charge loading (20–40 C m−3), and hydraulic retention time (τ = 2.3–6.9 s) enhances downstream crystallization yield, purity, and morphology. Shortening retention promotes boundary-layer convection, reducing in-cell scaling energy penalty (∆E) by 86% and total stack energy consumption by 22%. Operating within an optimized pH window (7.7 < pH < 9.0) governs crystal morphology and allows for 91% yield of highly pure struvite (> 97%), bypassing competitive newberyite crystallization. We unify the ECM transport kinetics and crystallization thermodynamics into a single dimensionless descriptor—the crystallization index—which establishes a linear correlation to predict the product yield based on upstream transport dynamics. Steady specific energy consumption of 9.38 ± 0.9 kWh kg−1 − struvite through autonomous in-situ acid flushing confirms system stability with minimal scaling. Finally, techno-economic analysis evaluates the levelized cost of struvite produced as $996 t−1, which is a reduction in operating expenditures by a maximum of 89% compared to commercial phosphorus recovery installations. Ultimately, the ECM eliminates crystallization chemical dependencies and reduces membrane scaling bottlenecks, establishing a highly tunable and efficient separations reactor with precise control of crystal products.

papers.title: Minimum Knowledge Collaboration enables joint materials development through protected optimization
papers.abstract: Materials companies must jointly develop products that meet competing requirements while keeping their formulations, processes and models private. Sample exchange alone can leave their searches poorly coordinated. We introduce Minimum Knowledge Collaboration (MKC), which connects private Bayesian optimizers through bounded candidate descriptions and company-specific search directions. Mathematical analysis links representation error, feasible private responses and information-limited search. In 256 controlled synthetic programs, all methods pursued the same reachable product target, defined as 100%. After 64 complete-product tests, MKC reached 92.4%, the information-rich reference 93.8%, and reusable better, neutral or worse feedback 6.0%. By 2,048 tests, ternary feedback reached MKC's result in 30 of 32 simplest bilateral programs; attainment across all 1,024-candidate programs was 12.5%. A cross-study scenario calculation gave a 0.0063% complete-state reconstruction index. This assumption-based design screen complements the measured reconstruction results. MKC demonstrates coordinated product development with bounded disclosure and supports industrial evaluation.

papers.title: Polymorph Influence on Sequential Anion Exchange Doping and Charge Transport in Poly(didodecyl-quaterthiophene) (PQT) for Organic Thermoelectrics
Transition-State Steric Fields Capture Geometric Signatures Associated with Electronic Perturbations in Asymmetric Catalysis
papers.abstract: In data analysis of molecular catalysis, molecular shape can be represented by voxel descriptors generated by mapping molecular structures onto a three-dimensional grid according to atomic van der Waals radii. Such voxel representations of molecular shape can be treated as steric molecular fields and are generally used as steric descriptors. However, because electronic perturbations can lead to systematic changes in molecular geometry, steric fields constructed from transition-state (TS) structures may also capture geometric signatures. We therefore examined whether steric fields derived from TS geometries can capture such structural changes associated with electronic perturbations in asymmetric catalysis. Using DFT-calculated TS structures from three asymmetric Michael addition systems, we generated two voxel-based molecular-field representations, steric fields and NPA-charge fields, for the major and minor TS pathways and used them to construct regression models with calculated enantioselectivity (ΔΔ G ‡ ) as the target variable. The resulting steric- and NPA-charge field models showed similar pathway-dependent trends in cross-validated coefficients of determination (q 2 ). The NPA-charge fields revealed distinct charge responses across the three reaction systems, and the associated changes in TS geometry were captured by the steric fields. These results indicate that TS-derived steric fields can encode not only molecular shape but also the geometric changes associated with electronic perturbations, providing simple and interpretable descriptors for data analysis in asymmetric catalysis.

papers.title: Hypoboric Acid Catecholate (HAC) Catalysis for Stereoselective Decarboxylative Borylation of Redox-Active Esters
papers.abstract: The Hypoboric Acid Catecholate (HAC) is a new class of diboron reagent bearing a borylcatecholato and a boronic acid moiety. Herein, we demonstrate that HACs can also be expontaneously formed in situ from collections of catechols and hypoboric acid. These HACs catalyze the decarboxylative borylation of redox-active esters, providing superior reactivity and selectivity. Equilibrium and kinetic NMR experiments indicate that the catalytic turnover is enabled by the high affinity of catechols for hypoboric acid and their low affinity for boronic acids that is uncovered herein. The catalytic system operates in mild conditions and is robust towards air and moisture, demonstrating its utility in the synthesis of important medicinally-relevant boronates. The enhanced selectivity is sourced in the regioselective radical capture by HAC intermediates at their customized borylcatecholato moiety, which can easily be stereoelectronically tailored for specific applications. These features of the catalytic approach with unsymmetrical HACs presented herein contrast with current state-of-the-art methods based on stoichiometric symmetrical diboron reagents.

papers.title: Glycine specifically labelled proteins to enhance solution NMR of methylene groups
papers.abstract: Specific isotopic labelling of proteins has greatly advanced biomolecular NMR. Protein domains, individual residues or certain chemical groups with specific patterns of isotopes can be incorporated to optimize the use of NMR pulse schemes. Here, we describe a novel cell-free protein expression protocol that allows specific isotopic labelling of glycine residues, whilst all other amino acids are independently labelled. This technique enables us to prevent amino acid scrambling and cross-protonation from the solvent resulting in high labelling selectivity of glycine residues as attested by quantification of 15N amide scrambling and residual Ca protonation. We then highlight the potential applications of these samples in the field of biomolecular NMR. We produced a 1 H, 13 C glycine specifically labelled sample of a subunit of the heavy metal ATPase HMA8, in a completely perdeuterated 2 H background and demonstrate how the CH 2 -TROSY experiment recorded on such a sample improves the spectral quality of glycine residues.

papers.title: Selective Operando Visualization of Ultrathin Lithium in Li-Metal Batteries by Neutron Capture Imaging
papers.abstract: Operando visualization of ultrathin lithium is essential for understanding plating and stripping in lithium-metal batteries, but existing neutron imaging techniques lack sufficient sensitivity for ultra-thin lithium layers formed at crucial early stages. Here we introduce neutron capture imaging (NCI), which selectively detects tritons generated by neutron capture in 6 Li. Ex situ measurements of electrochemically plated and thermally evaporated 6 Li demonstrate sensitivity around 10 nm for a 1.5 h acquisition and two-dimensional imaging with around 100 μm lateral resolution. Simulations indicate that the resolution could approach 25 μm through optical optimization. Operando measurements in an asymmetric Cu|| 6 Li cell reveal spatially heterogeneous lithium plating and stripping in agreement with electrochemical data. Our results establish NCI as a high-sensitivity, near-zero-background tool for operando studies of lithium metal batteries, opening new possibilities for resolving early-stage deposition, dead lithium formation, and interfacial dynamics with broad applicability to ultrathin reactive lithium layers in electrochemical systems.

papers.title: Mousanes: Convergent Synthesis and Diversification of Serially Spiro-Fused Cyclobutanes
papers.abstract: Connecting cyclobutanes through successive spiro junctions offers a way to restrict the relative positions and orientations of functional groups along a saturated framework. Here we describe a convergent synthesis of mousanes, dispirodecane scaffolds comprising three cyclobutanes. A functionalized methylenecyclobutene is prepared on decagram scale by elimination of an iodo-bicyclo[1.1.1]pentanederived precursor. This 1,3-diene undergoes regioselective, triplet-sensitized [2+2] homodimerization to construct the central cyclobutane and both spiro junctions. Hydrolysis and stereoconvergent hydrogenation provide a bifunctional mousane on multigram scale, from which amino acid, diamine, diol and differentially functionalized derivatives are prepared. Calculations suggest that regioselectivity is established during the initial C–C bond-forming step and show that mousane stereochemistry controls terminal geometry. The exo,exo framework has dimensions comparable to short hydrocarbon linkers but displays a narrower calculated range of terminal-vector orientations. We illustrate the use of these building blocks through incorporation into drug analogues and a BRD4-targeting heterobifunctional ligand directed degrader.

papers.title: Ultra-Low CoNi Alloy Nanoparticle Loaded Polypyrrole Nanospheres as Oxygen Electrocatalysts in Alkaline to Near-Neutral Zinc-Air Batteries
papers.abstract: Dearth of a wide-range pH-adaptable bifunctional oxygen electrocatalyst is a bottleneck in the advancement of efficient metal-air batteries as catalysts optimized for alkaline media often lose effectiveness under near-neutral conditions. Herein, we report an ultralow (~1 atomic%) amount of CoNi alloy loaded polypyrrole-derived graphitic nanoparticle (CoNiPpy) system as a pH-adaptable oxygen electrocatalyst for high energy density and durability in near-neutral zinc-air batteries (ZABs) with 100% coulombic efficiency. The efficient activity of CoNiPpy towards oxygen reduction and oxygen evolution reactions (ORR and OER) is established, with CoNiPpy showing a lower overpotential than the benchmarked Pt-IrO2 catalyst combo in both alkaline and near-neutral electrolytes. When employed as the air cathode in rechargeable ZABs, CoNiPpy outperforms Pt/C benchmarks, sustaining > 650 cycles in alkaline electrolyte and >1100 cycles for ~200 h in near-neutral electrolyte. Stable operating voltages of 1.435 V and 1.235 V are achieved in alkaline and near-neutral ZABs respectively. Series connected cells further power a 33 mW lighting load for more than 1 h and operate portable sensors, demonstrating functionality beyond conventional electrochemical benchmarking. Detailed full-cell analysis demonstrates that, rather than relying on high metal loadings, trace CoNi incorporation into a conductive N-containing carbon framework can enable a single bifunctional air cathode to operate across both alkaline and near-neutral ZAB chemistries. The findings further emphasize that appropriate electrolyte selection plays an important role in full-cell performance and guiding the development of scalable zinc-air battery systems.

papers.title: Surface hydroxyls act as key intermediates in the selective oxidative dehydrogenation of 2-propanol on Co3O4
papers.abstract: Transition-metal oxides typically catalyze aerobic oxidation reactions with high activity even at low temperatures, but rarely with high selectivity. Owing to the complexity of competing surface processes on such catalysts, the rational design of selective low-temperature catalysts still requires a deeper mechanistic understanding of the active surface and reaction intermediates. In this work, we combine operando modulation-excitation infrared spectroscopy with density functional theory and molecular dynamics to mechanistically investigate 2-propanol oxidation over Co3O4 with a focus on surface hydroxyls, acting as hydrogen acceptors during alcohol adsorption. We identify two chemically distinct hydroxyl populations: linear hydroxyls, which actively participate in acetone formation and can be considered part of the active surface ensemble, and bridged hydroxyls, which behave largely as spectators. Together, these results provide a molecular-level mechanistic picture of alcohol oxidation on Co3O4 and establish the dynamic role of surface hydroxyl species as active players in heterogeneous oxidation catalysis.

papers.title: Harnessing π-d magnetic interactions in Co porphyrins by metal-ligand coordination
papers.abstract: π-Multiradicalic compounds fabricated by on-surface synthesis have emerged as a powerful platform to interrogate spin interactions at the atomic scale. However, the introduction and role of unpaired d-electrons on such systems, and the study of π-d electronic interactions, are still incipient. In this context, a crucial point is the tunability of the inherent magnetic properties of such π-d architectures by incorporation of peripheral metal-organic coordination, which at the same time allows creating self-assembled architectures. Herein, to this aim we exploit an ex-professo synthesized Zn-porphyrin (1) equipped with two carbonitrile-dimethyl-phenyl moieties at its trans-meso positions, which forms π-extended metallo-organic nanostructures featuring unpaired π-electrons through cyclodehydrogenation and concomitant carbonitrile-gold coordination. Transmetallation of such Zn-based nanoarchitectures with Co atoms gave rise to the several Co-based porphyrin multiradicalic species featuring both unpaired π and d electrons, including porphyrin monomers (CoPor M) and dimers (Co-Por D) as well as one-dimensional porphyrin nanochains (1D CoPor NC) and nanotapes (1D CoPor NT). Scanning probe spectroscopy combined with theoretical calculations reveal that the carbonitrile-gold coordination environment dramatically alters the magnetic structure of the cobalt center as compared to analogue porphyrin species lacking the CN group. On the one hand, in both CoPor M and 1D CoPor NC the cobalt atom presents a S=3/2 ground state versus the S=1/2 case for Co porphyrins analogues lacking the nitrile moiety. Additionally, no Kondo interactions are detected at the metal center, as a consequence of a diminished magnetic interaction of CoPor M and 1D CoPor NC with the Au(111) substrate. On the other hand, CoPor D presents two radical electrons distributed between the cobalt atoms and the carbon π-system which interact ferromagnetically yielding a S=1 ground state. Our findings demonstrate how metal-ligand coordination can be used to harness the magnetic interactions within surface-supported multiradicalic molecular systems.

papers.title: A robust multiwell workflow for quantitative and nontargeted chemical exposomics at cohort scale
papers.abstract: Chemical exposomics enables comprehensive profiling of environmental substances and their metabolic perturbations, providing new opportunities to uncover environmental drivers of disease. To realize its full potential in human exposome initiatives, more reproducible high-throughput workflows are needed that combine sensitive quantitative targeted analysis with nontargeted molecular discovery in small serum volumes. We describe a 96-well phospholipid depletion workflow using 100 µL of serum and liquid chromatography – high-resolution mass spectrometry to quantify 247 priority pollutants, drugs and metabolites while confidently annotating hundreds of additional exogenous and endogenous molecules. In contrast to evaporation-to-dryness workflows, adding a small volume of dimethyl sulfoxide retained more analytes and improved recovery (99% median target recovery), with negligible effect on sensitivity (0.5 ng/mL median method limit of quantification), resulting in robust within-laboratory reproducibility across four operators over 1.5 years (18% median relative standard deviation). Application to 718 human serum samples confirmed scalability while maintaining reproducible quantitation and molecular discovery (761 annotated substances) at the cohort scale.

papers.title: Plasmonic Coupling Within Atomically Precise Nanocluster Dimers for Engineering Hot-Carrier Generation and Molecular Activation
authors: Sharma S. R. K. C. Yamijala
papers.abstract: Activating the exceptionally strong N≡N remains a fundamental challenge due to the chemical inertness of molecular nitrogen (N2). Plasmonic nanoclusters offer a promising approach by generating localized electromagnetic fields and energetic hot carriers that can drive bond activation at ambient conditions. Here, we combine real-time time-dependent density functional theory with Ehrenfest molecular dynamics to reveal how plasmonic coupling between tetrahedral Ag20 nanoclusters governs N2 activation and dissociation. Systematic variation of the intercluster separation shows that a 6 Å nanogap maximizes near-field enhancement and hot-electron transfer to the adsorbed N2, accompanied by N-N activation. Consequently, N2 dissociation is achieved at incident field strengths as low as 0.5 VÅ–1, whereas larger-gap dimers exhibit substantially lower activity. Similarly, isolated N2 remains intact under comparable conditions. These findings establish nanogap engineering as an effective strategy for optimizing plasmon-driven N2 activation and provide design principles for developing efficient plasmonic catalysts.

papers.title: From Rotor to Motor: Dissecting Design Principles for Light-Driven Directional Motion
papers.abstract: Research on molecular motors continues to expand as increasing attention is devoted to dynamic and out-of-equilibrium chemical systems. Among the different classes of artificial molecular machines, light-driven motors are the most extensively present, yet the fundamental principles governing their directional motion remain difficult to disentangle, particularly for non-specialists. This work applies these concepts in a tutorial setting by gradually implementing molecular features to a base scaffold that turns it from a bistable system into an experimentally observable light-driven molecular motor. In doing so, it demonstrates how directional bias emerges as soon as relaxation of a high-energy state is coupled to a mechanical movement (a power stroke), while the motor performance can be addressed through modification of the underlying energy landscape. In addition, we show a practical workflow for benchmarking new motor candidates along with the experimental determination of their kinetic and thermodynamic parameters. To complement this study, we provide procedures for undergraduate students to synthesize and operate a molecular motor in practical courses.

papers.title: Phase-Controlled Efficient Nitrate-to-Dinitrogen Electroreduction on an α-Co/NC@CNT Electrified Membrane Platform
papers.abstract: Selective electrochemical conversion of nitrate (NO 3 - ) to dinitrogen (N 2 ) is attractive for nitrate remediation but remains challenging because competing hydrogenation pathways often yield reduced nitrogen products. Here, we develop a self-supported flexible electrified membrane (α-Co/NC@CNTFEM) by integrating phase-defined hexagonal close-packed (HCP) α-Co/nitrogen-doped carbon (NC) into a conductive carbon nanotube (CNT) framework. The resulting membrane combines a uniformly integrated catalytic phase with a thin, interconnected porous architecture suitable for flow-through electrochemical operation. At an initial nitrate concentration of 10 mg L -1 , α-Co/NC@CNT-FEM achieves 96.5% nitrate conversion, 81.5% N 2 Faradaic efficiency, and 97.9% N 2 selectivity, exceeding the corresponding mixed-phase Co NP /NC@CNT-FEM and bare CNT-FEM. The enhanced N 2 selectivity is associated with the coupled effects of the phase-defined α-Co, N-doped carbon matrix, and flow-through CNT microenvironment, which may favor N–N coupling while suppressing excessive hydrogenation. Moreover, our results also reveal that stable nitrate removal on this platform is maintained over 10 consecutive cycles. This work demonstrates crystal-phase engineering coupled with electrified membrane design as a materials strategy for selective nitrate-to-N 2 conversion.

papers.title: Substituent-Controlled Divergent Photocyclization of Aza-1,5 Dienes to Access Three Distinct Cyclic Frameworks
papers.abstract: Rigid, three-dimensional cyclic scaffolds are highly valued in medicinal chemistry, yet selectively accessing dis tinct cyclic frameworks from a common class of simple acyclic precursors remains a significant challenge. Herein, we report a precious-metal-free photochemical cyclization of aza-1,5-dienes that enables the substituent-controlled, divergent synthe sis of three distinct cyclic frameworks: bridged bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes, fused bicyclo[2.2.0]hexanes, and six-membered lac tams. N-Aryl-substituted substrates preferentially undergo 5-exo-trig cyclization to afford bridged bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes, whereas substrates bearing electron-withdrawing N-substituents such as acetyl or tosyl groups favor the 6-endo-trig pathway to furnish fused bicyclo[2.2.0]hexanes. Notably, this strategy was further extended to the synthesis of six-membered lactams from N-methyl-substituted aza-1,5-dienes under photosensitizer-free conditions. This work establishes a mild, substituent controlled strategy for skeletal divergence, enabling the selective synthesis of structurally diverse cyclic scaffolds of potential value in medicinal chemistry.

papers.title: Protein Language Model-Boosted Prediction of Isoelectric Point
papers.abstract: pH plays a key role in many biological processes. When the solution pH equals the isoelectric point (pI) of a protein, the protein carries zero net charge, which minimizes its solubility and thus promotes aggregation. Here we present ESMpI, a sequence-based protein pI predictor that combines optimized pKa values of seven ionizable residue types and two terminals with embeddings from a pre-trained protein language model. Benchmarked against experimental protein pI values, ESMpI outperforms other state-of-the-art methods, including structure-based approaches that derive the pI of a protein from residue-specific pKa calculations. Finally, ESMpI requires only sequence information, making it well suited for high-throughput proteomescale analyses and protein engineering.

papers.title: Stereochemical Control of Static Strength and Dynamic Fracture for Efficient Atomization of Supramolecular Gel Propellants
papers.abstract: Supramolecular gel propellants immobilize liquid fuels through the efficient self-assembly of low-molecular-weight gelators, enabling storage-stable networks at minimal additive loading while remaining susceptible to rapid disruption during atomization. However, the multiscale relationships linking molecular design, supramolecular organization, rheology, and atomization remain poorly understood. Here, four glutamic acid-derived low-molecular-weight gelators were developed by varying molecular chirality, steric hindrance around hydrogen-bonding sites, and alkyl-chain length to regulate their assembly in aviation fuel JP-10. Comparison of racemic and enantiopure analogues highlighted stereochemical coherence as a key determinant of higher-order non-covalent assembly. G4, bearing an N-acetyl headgroup, an enantiopure L-glutamic acid configuration, and C18 alkyl chains, exhibited the highest gelation efficiency and formed ordered lamellar packing and an interconnected helical nanofiber network. The resulting G4@JP-10 gel combined a high yield stress of 718.50 Pa with a low critical strain of approximately 40%, resisting the onset of flow under weak perturbations while showing limited tolerance to large deformation under strong external shear. The test results of low-field nuclear magnetic resonance (LF-NMR) indicated weak network-imposed restriction of JP-10 molecular motion, while the shear-disrupted G4 sample exhibited the lowest average surface tension of 28.34 mN m-1, reducing capillary resistance to new gas–fuel interface formation. Consequently, G4 achieved a Sauter mean diameter (SMD) of 5.38 μm at a N2 pressure of 0.6 MPa, lower than that of neat JP-10 under identical conditions. This work reveals the unique advantages of chiral supramolecular gels for propellant atomization and establishes comprehensive structure–property relationships that bridge molecular structure and assembly behavior with rheological characteristics and atomization performance.

papers.title: Bonding, Biradicaloid Character, and Real-Space Topology of the Dinitrosyl Beryllium Dimer Be2(NO)2: A Multiconfigurational and Energy-Decomposition Study
papers.abstract: The structural, vibrational, thermodynamic, multiconfigurational electronic structure, biradicaloid character, charge-transfer bonding, and real-space topological properties of the dinitrosyl beryllium dimer, Be2(NO)2, are investigated using density functional theory (DFT) at the TPSS/def2-TZVP-D4 level, complete active space self-consistent field (CASSCF) coupled with N-electron valence state second-order perturbation theory (NEVPT2), STEOM-DLPNO-CCSD, and multi-wavefunction topological analyses via Multiwfn. Energy Decomposition Analysis combined with Natural Orbitals for Chemical Valence (EDA-NOCV) and Quantum Theory of Atoms in Molecules (QTAIM) reveal that the stability of this unique main-group cluster is governed by strong electrostatic interactions, pronounced charge-transfer components, multi-centre core bonding, and synergistic orbital back-donation channels. Natural orbital occupation numbers and narrow singlet–triplet gaps further confirm significant biradicaloid character.

papers.title: Consecutive hydrodefluorination for the regioselective synthesis of partially fluorinated arenes
papers.abstract: Fluorinated arenes are critically important motifs in drug discovery, often exhibiting superior bioactivity compared to their non-fluorinated counterparts. While advances in fluorination methods have improved access to monofluoroarenes, the synthesis of di- and trifluoroarenes remains challenging. Here, we present a powerful method for access to partially fluorinated arenes via consecutive hydrodefluorination of perfluoroarenes, executed in one ‘pot’. This method utilises hydridosilicates as the reducing species, which are formed in situ by the combination of phenylsilane and cesium carbonate in dimethylsulfoxide. These conditions avoid precious metal catalysts and exotic reagents, exhibiting exceptional regioselectivity and control over the degree of defluorination. Through an in-depth mechanistic study, we found that hydridosilicates can perform hydrodefluorination by two distinct mechanisms, one thermal and one photochemical. These mechanisms are complementary in substrate scope—together, they enable a method with notable generality.

papers.title: Photoresponsive Dynamics in HABI-Carbamate-Silsesquioxane Hybrid Polymer Networks with Tunable Thermomechanical Properties and Shape-Memory Behaviors
papers.abstract: Photoresponsive polymer networks that reversibly modulate their mechanical properties under light irradiation are promising materials for advanced actuators and shape-memory systems. Herein, we report the synthesis of a new family of hexaarylbiimidazole (HABI)-carbamate-siloxane hybrid polymer networks containing methyl, phenyl, vinyl, acrylate, methacrylate, and isooctyl organotrialkoxysilane structures. The polymers were prepared through simultaneous urethane formation and siloxane condensation. We characterized all synthesized compounds by ATR-FTIR, 1H NMR, 13C NMR, solid-state 13C NMR, 29Si NMR, LC-HRMS, UV−Vis spectroscopy, thermogravimetric analysis, and dynamic mechanical analysis. Chemical characterization confirmed successful incorporation of HABI moieties, formation of carbamate linkages, and cross-linked siloxane networks. The organotrialkoxysilane substituents significantly influenced the thermal and mechanical properties of the polymer networks. Methacrylate- and acrylate-containing polymers showed the highest thermal stability (Td5% = 237 °C and 207 °C, respectively), while ceramic yields increased from 7% for the pristine network to 15%- 19% for the modified systems. Dynamic mechanical analysis revealed pronounced, reversible light-induced changes in storage and loss moduli arising from reversible HABI C−N bond cleavage and recombination, with the vinyl-containing polymer exhibiting the largest storage modulus variation (8 × 103 MPa). Several polymers also demonstrated reproducible light-assisted shape-memory behavior, with the acrylate-, methacrylate-, methyl-, and isooctyl-containing systems showing the most distinct responses. These HABI-carbamate-siloxane hybrid networks provide a versatile platform for developing mechanically tunable, photoresponsive materials for smart polymer and shape-memory applications.

papers.title: Effects of Zinc Leachate on the Structure and Activity of Semaglutide
papers.abstract: Semaglutide is among the most prescribed Glucagon-like peptide-1 agonists (GLP-1As) for treatment of type II diabetes and obesity in both oral (Rybelsus®, Wegovy®) and injectable (Ozempic®, Wegovy®) formulations. Injectable semaglutide is often manufactured in prefilled syringes, which facilitate convenient storage and independent dosage for patients. Recently, potential leaching of zinc from the elastomer of the inner needle shield has been evaluated for pharmaceutical antibody formulations. The leached zinc ion may impose a risk of drug aggregation, particle formation, and needle clogging. In the present study, we experimentally examined the effects of Zn2+ on structure and in vitro activity of semaglutide. Our findings indicated that addition of Zn2+ induced a rapid increase in semaglutide’s α-helicity, followed by a gradual decrease in ellipticity under thermal stress at 37 °C. The zinc-stressed semaglutide did not cause cytotoxicity or loss of in-vitro activity, potentially due to the reversibility of their structural changes upon dilution. Moreover, we observed a protective role of phosphate, the formulation buffer of Ozempic and Wegovy, against Zn2+-induced stress. This work provides new insights for evaluating and mitigating the potential risk of zinc leaching in the injectable formulations of GLP-1 therapeutics.

papers.title: Mathematical Modeling of Coupled Electronic and Ionic Transport Mechanics in Flow-Electrode Capacitive Deionization
papers.abstract: Flow Capacitive Deionization (FCDI) is an electrochemical ion removal technology well-suited for continuous desalination of brackish waters, as well as ion-specific removal. Despite over a decade of research into FCDI, few researchers have probed the transient and spatially dependent mechanisms of ion transport and electro-adsorption within flow electrodes. In this study, transport equations describing the advection of overpotential along with the flowing electrode are coupled with the Nernst-Planck equations governing ion transport within the ion exchange membranes, water channel, and slurry electrolyte. The effect of flow velocity on electrical potential profiles and active regions of capacitive electro-adsorption are illustrated using 2-dimensional Finite Element Analysis (FEA) simulations. The model is then validated against a representative experimental cell using experimentally determined slurry properties and membrane properties as model inputs. The model shows general agreement with experimental data despite a high variability in experimental results. Finally, an empirical correlation for slurry conductivity, capacitance, and velocity, is fitted to non-dimensionalized simulation results, yielding power model correlations analogous to the Nusselt number and Peclet numbers in conductive heat transfer, Nu c ∝Pe c 0.258±0.002 . The result is a useful tool for predicting FCDI cell performance based on material inputs and operating parameters. This model serves as valuable groundwork for the expansion of FCDI modeling capabilities and subsequent optimization of operational parameters and cell geometries.

papers.title: A Stereochemical Blueprint for Thermoresponsive Polymers
papers.abstract: Predicting polymer structure-property relationships is challenging due to the vast chemical expanse of polymer design space and the limited availability of high-quality datasets that effectively span the design space. Here, we present a physics-informed framework that integrates high-throughput molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with machine learning to predict the lower critical solution temperature (LCST) of stereochemically diverse poly(Nisopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAM) systems using 5632 MD simulation trajectories, corresponding to a cumulative simulation time of 2816 µs. We use validated MD simulations to generate descriptors that capture local hydration and conformational environments, enabling the extraction of molecular features directly linked to thermoresponsive behaviour. The resulting model accurately reproduces subtle experimentally observed LCST variations arising from changes in tacticity, demonstrating that sequence derived features and simulation-derived hydration descriptors encode the molecular information required to resolve compositiondependent phase behaviour. Beyond LCST prediction, the framework provides mechanistic insight into the molecular origins of thermoresponsive behaviour of PNIPAM, revealing that meso and racemic dyads undergo distinct backbone rotational mediated collapse pathways, with meso dyads requiring backbone rotation through partially hydrated intermediates, whereas racemic dyads collapse within a fixed backbone rotational conformation through closure of the isopropyl-isopropyl distance. These findings establish a transferable simulation-machinelearning strategy for linking polymer structural information to macroscopic properties and accelerating the discovery of functional polymer materials.

papers.title: Mechanochemical Activation of Strontium for the Selective Cross-Coupling of Chlorosilanes
papers.abstract: Silicon-containing compounds are important in both academic and industrial settings, and the reductive coupling of chlorosilanes is a widely used approach for the formation of Si–Si bonds. However, despite its long history, this strategy for the formation of Si–Si bonds has remained largely limited to homocoupling, while a general synthetic method for selective heterocoupling has yet to be established. Previous strategies have relied on the stepwise generation of silicon nucleophiles or electrochemical methods. Here, we demonstrate that mechanochemical activation of strontium metal by ball milling enables the one-pot, cross-selective coupling of a broad range of chlorosilane pairs. Notably, after screening group 1 and group 2 metals, strontium was found to exhibit higher reactivity under mechanochemical conditions than commonly used metal reductants such as lithium and sodium. Importantly, no reaction occurs when strontium is employed under conventional solution conditions, highlighting the crucial role that mechanical activation plays in the reaction. Finally, this method is also applicable to the cross-coupling of chlorosilanes with chlorogermanes, thus establishing a practical and operationally simple protocol for the formation of E–E (E = Si, Ge) bonds.

papers.title: Peptide-Directed Ligand Design Enables Chemical Disruption of the Nrf2/MafG Coiled-Coil Transcription Factor Complex.
papers.abstract: Transcription factor protein interactions remain among the most challenging targets in chemical biology, particularly those driven by leucine zipper coiled coil assemblies. For this challenge we developed a peptide-directed ligand design strategy identifying inhibitors of the Nrf2/MafG transcription factor complex, a key driver of cytoprotective signalling and cancer chemoresistance. MafG-derived α-helical peptides bind Nrf2 and disrupt formation of the Nrf2/MafG/DNA complex. Guided by structural modelling, peptide-small molecule hybrids were subsequently developed that preserved inhibitory activity while reducing peptide content. Lead hybrids inhibited Nrf2/MafG/DNA assembly, suppressed Nrf2-dependent transcriptional responses, reduced HO-1 and NQO1 gene expression, NQO1 enzymatic activity, and decreased nuclear localisation of Nrf2 in A549 cells. Disruption of Nrf2/MafG signalling restored sensitivity to gemcitabine in an intrinsically chemoresistant lung cancer model. This provides a new approach for the modulation of coiled-coil transcription factor interactions and new chemical probes for Nrf2-dependent chemoresistance in cancer biology.

papers.title: A Fragment-Based Mechanistic Potential for Noncovalent Systems: Combining Conceptual DFT and Quantum Chemical Topology Domains
papers.abstract: Within a framework combining conceptual Density Functional Theory (cDFT) with the computational efficiency of the quantum chemical topology (QCT) description of matter, we introduce a mechanistic potential designed for the fast exploration of intermolecular potential-energy surfaces between rigid molecular fragments. The proposed strategy deliberately retains only a minimal set of physically interpretable contributions, namely electrostatics, charge transfer, and dispersion. All electronic properties are evaluated once for the isolated rigid fragments and subsequently propagated using the Kabsch algorithm during their relative translations and rotations, so that the potential energy depends only on the six intermolecular degrees of freedom. The proposed workflow is illustrated using a set of noncovalent and donor-acceptor complexes displaying different degrees of directionality and intermolecular overlap. In the long-range regime, the effective potential mimics a substantial part of the orientational selectivity and correctly identifies the main low-energy regions and interaction-energy minima. This behavior is illustrated for weakly bound systems, hydrogen-bonded and donor–acceptor complexes, σ-hole interactions, the guanine–cytosine pair, and the CO2 molecule confined within a (H2O)20 clathrate cage. Deviations from reference DFT profiles become more pronounced at shorter intermolecular separations, where Pauli repulsion and polarization contributions, which are not explicitly included in the model, become significant. The resulting approach therefore provides a fast, computationally inexpensive, and physically interpretable tool for the prescreening and exploration of intermolecular potential-energy surfaces, allowing favorable orientations and low-energy structures to be identified prior to more demanding electronic-structure calculations. More generally, this mechanistic strategy may provide a useful route for the modeling and exploration of increasingly complex non-covalent molecular and supramolecular systems.

papers.title: Discovery of new octadecanoids in γ-linolenic acid rich oils
papers.abstract: 17 novel hydroxy fatty acids derived from LA, ALA, and GLA were characterized in evening 2 primrose, borage and hemp oil. Structural characterization was based on semi-synthetic 3 standards generated by autoxidation, photoxidation and enzymatic conversions, combined 4 with LC-MS and GC-MS analysis with multiple derivatization strategies. Novel oxylipins 6-5 HODE and 7-HODE, presumably formed as site-products of Δ6-desaturase, showed 6 characteristic patterns in GLA-rich oils: 6-HODE occurred at high levels in in evening primrose 7 oil (23 ± 1 mg/100 g) and in borage oil (84 ± 7 mg/100 g), whereas 7-HODE (28.7 ± 8 0.6 mg/100 g) was abundant in hemp oil. These novel oxylipins occurred in similar 9 concentrations in both cold-pressed and refined oils and did not relate to the oxidation status. 10 Although, the occurrence of autoxidatively formed hydroxy-LA, ALA and GLA correlated with 11 peroxide value. Overall, these findings highlight novel oxylipins as promising markers of oil 12 quality and authenticity. 13 14 15 16

papers.title: Accuracy in Homonuclear Distance Determinations by Solid-State NMR Spectroscopy: The Benefits of Fast Magic-Angle Spinning up to 100 kHz
papers.abstract: Homonuclear distance measurements by solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy under magic-angle spinning (MAS) conditions are key to structural analysis in complex materials. While a wide variety of dipolar recoupling techniques involving the excitation of double quantum (DQ) coherences is available, the excitation efficiency is critically affected by the chemical-shift anisotropy (CSA) and the (often unknown) relative orientations between chemical-shift and dipolar-coupling tensors of the involved nuclei. Here, we demonstrate that a previously reported DQ-based sequence, Constant-Time Dipolar Recoupling Effects Nuclear Alignment Reduction (CT-DRENAR), enables robust and highly accurate homonuclear distance determinations for 19F and 31P nuclei under fast MAS conditions up to 100 kHz. We establish a numerical simulation approach to investigate the uncertainties in such distance measurements arising from the orientational effects and show that they become negligible when the MAS frequency exceeds approximately twice the spectral dispersion due to the CSA. Using this numerical simulation approach for data analysis, 31P–31P and 19F–19F effective distances in crystalline model systems with shortest internuclear contacts of 3–5 Å and CSA magnitudes exceeding 100 ppm are determined with accuracies of 0.1–0.5 Å. The experiment is applied to probe the conformational change of a phosphine ligand upon ruthenium coordination in a heterogeneous solid molecular ruthenium-polyphosphine catalyst. These results demonstrate the suitability of CT-DRENAR as a reliable strategy for precise homonuclear distance measurements in complex functional materials.

papers.title: Solving density-of-states occupation in disordered systems using neural networks
papers.abstract: Describing density-of-states occupation with high precision in disordered systems is crucial for modeling charge transport and understanding doping mechanisms or interfacial energy-level alignment. Beyond fundamental insight from a mechanistic understanding of these physical phenomena, accurate modeling is pivotal for optimizing technological applications in optoelectronic and thermoelectric devices. However, the required calculations are computationally demanding and inherently complex, preventing systematic computational-experimental approaches. Here, we leverage neural networks to perform these calculations precisely and efficiently. We first demonstrate this approach for the Fermi-Dirac occupation of Gaussian densities of states, achieving accelerations of up to three orders of magnitude, a substantial advantage for advanced modeling workflows that require repeated evaluation of the underlying integrals. We then introduce a neural network for doped molecular materials, such as organic semiconductors, that directly predicts doping levels and Fermi level shifts, circumventing conventional recursive schemes and accelerating computations by nearly five orders of magnitude.

papers.title: d10 Coinage Metal Organic Chalcogenolates: Tuning Dimensionality and Properties through Phenylthiolate Functionalization
papers.abstract: Metal–Organic Chalcogenolates (MOCs) based on d 10 coinage metals constitute a versatile class of coordination polymers combining anisotropic structures with diverse functional properties. In this review, we examine a series of 23 Cu(I), Ag(I), and Au(I)-based MOCs obtained from eight functionalized thiophenolate ligands. The systematic comparison of these compounds highlights how the metal identity, ligand functionalization, steric hindrance, and secondary interactions govern the coordination modes and, most importantly, the dimensionality of the resulting networks. The 1D and 2D MOCs provide a particularly relevant platform to establish relationships between network dimensionality and physical properties. Their photoluminescence and electrical properties reveal distinct trends across the Cu, Ag, and Au series, with dimensionality playing a key role in both light emission and charge transport. The review further discusses the dynamic behavior of these materials, including ligand-exchange processes and reversible transformations between different structural and physical states. Their ability to form fibers, thin films, glasses, and composite materials further illustrates the versatility of MOCs beyond their crystalline structures. Selected examples of optical thermometry, optoelectronics, phase-change materials, sensing, and catalysis demonstrate their emerging functional potential. Overall, this review emphasizes dimensionality as a central structural parameter for understanding structure–property relationships and guiding the design of functional MOCs.

papers.title: Photocatalytic performance of silver clusters on anatase TiO2 for bisphenol A degradation in water under solar light
papers.abstract: The increasing occurrence of bisphenol A (BPA) in water sources raises significant environmental and health concerns, demanding efficient and sustainable remediation strategies. In this work, we investigate the photocatalytic degradation of BPA using silver metal clusters (Ag5) supported on anatase TiO2 under simulated solar irradiation. The deposition of Ag5 clusters significantly enhances visible-light absorption, promotes charge separation and improves photocatalytic performance, achieving an apparent rate constant (kobs) of 0.0142 min-1, corresponding to a ~43% improvement compared to bare TiO2. In addition, the Ag5@TiO2 catalyst exhibits higher photocatalytic activity, demonstrating the beneficial effect of Ag5 clusters incorporation. HPLC-MS analysis enabled the identification of intermediate degradation products. Compared to literature reports on modified TiO2-based photocatalysts, the present system demonstrates competitive performance even at significantly lower catalyst loadings. These results highlight the potential of Ag5@TiO2 photocatalysts as highly efficient alternatives for removing endocrine-disrupting compounds from water.

papers.title: Computational assessment of a proposed Na+/Ag+ ion-exchange route to Ag2MgSiO4, a predicted wurtzite-derived silver silicate
papers.abstract: Low-temperature ion exchange can provide a route to metastable inorganic compounds that are not favoured by equilibrium synthesis. We assess the proposed preparation of Ag2MgSiO4 from Na2MgSiO4 in molten AgNO3, using exchange energies, reported preparation controls and lattice-dynamical calculations. MLIP screening agrees in sign with the selected published DFT references, but the reaction set is linked by reciprocal reactions and thermodynamic cycles and is not an independent sample of synthesis outcomes. All screened Na-parent/AgNO3 exchanges pass the energy criterion; the Mg compound was carried forward by literatureguided judgement, not uniquely selected by that criterion. PBE gives exchange energies of about −58 kJ mol−1 per Ag and restricted O-balanced hull energies of 0.038–0.042 eV atom−1, comparable with reported silver silicates under the same calculation protocol. The exchange energies use an AgNO3 reference polymorph whose effect has not been tested with the same PBE settings. Corrected-code phonons support the Pna21 structure at the commensurate points and under the sampled tolerance, but stability beyond the chosen supercell and sampling is not established. A reanalysis of the archived outputs exposes limitations in the functional-property calculations: sparse path images do not establish DFT migration barriers, and incomplete exact-exchange sampling and single-reference gap shifting do not establish visible-light absorption. No synthesis or property measurement was performed. Ag2MgSiO4 remains a computational candidate for testing an exchange route; a failed experiment under one set of conditions would not by itself exclude the compound.

papers.title: Stacking Interactions of Druglike Heterocycles with Histidine
papers.abstract: Histidine side chains are prevalent in binding sites and can engage in stacking interactions with heterocyclic ligand components. However, efforts to harness these interactions for molecular recognition are often hampered by an incomplete understanding of the factors that control the strength and preferred geometries of these interactions. To this end, we provide a comprehensive computational analysis of stacked dimers of druglike heterocycles with the three protomers of the histidine side chain.
