The data show that the strengths of these stacking interactions span a considerable range, offering a potentially fruitful means of modulating binding. While the strength of stacking interactions with the neutral Nδ−H and Nε−H tautomers are strongly correlated, stacked dimers of aromatic heterocycles with the imidazolium form follow a qualitatively different trend. Moreover, the impact of placing heteroatoms at a given position depends on the protomeric state, highlighting potential challenges in designing heterocycles to stack strongly with binding site histidine side chains. Ultimately, we provide simple predictive models of the maximum possible stacking strength of mono- or bicyclic heterocycles with the three protomers of histidine based on readily computed heterocycle descriptors. We also interpret these results within the framework of our recently introduced model of heteroatom effects in parallel-displaced stacking interactions (J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2025, 147, 32273), which provides a means of predicting the preferred orientation of heterocycles stacked with histidine.

papers.title: Structure-Based Design of Potent Pan-YTHDF Ligands
papers.abstract: N6-Adenosine methylation (m6A) is the most abundant post-transcriptional modification of mRNA. The reader proteins YTHDF1, YTHDF2, and YTHDF3 recognize m6A-RNA in the cytosol. Here, we present a protein structurebased medicinal chemistry campaign that resulted in the pan-YTHDF inhibitor 34, which shows for YTHDF2 an equilibrium dissociation constant (Kd) of 0.14 µM determined by calorimetry. Compound 34 binds the three YTHDF paralogs with comparable affinity, while being selective against YTHDC1 and YTHDC2. The high-resolution crystal structures of the complex of YTHDF2 with six members of the series validate the structure-based design. Using the structural information, we designed the advanced compound 31 (IC50 = 0.22 μM for YTHDF2, according to TR-FRET) and a negative control, i.e., its methylated analogue 31b (IC50 > 100 μM for the three YTHDF paralogs, according to TR-FRET). The cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) provides evidence of YTHDF2 target engagement in cells for the advanced compounds 34 and 31, while the negative control 31b is inactive in CETSA. Compounds 34 and 31 at low-µM concentration inhibit the proliferation of the acute myeloid leukemia (AML) cell lines MOLM-13 and THP-1. Importantly, the inhibition of the YTHDF readers by 31 increases the level and stability of the transcript of tumour necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 1B. This renders THP-1 cells more sensitive to tumour necrosis factor-α-induced toxicity. Thus, ligand 34 and the pair 31 and 31b are tool compounds for studying the biological roles of the cytosolic YTHDF readers and their involvement in AML.

papers.title: Quantum Subspace Expansion for Molecular Excited States: Representability, Stability, and Practical Considerations
papers.abstract: Accurate treatment of excited states remains challenging for classical electronic-structure methods, motivating quantum algorithms that may provide more favorable resource scaling. We systematically assess the practical performance of Quantum Subspace Expansion (QSE) for low-lying electronic states across 28 organic molecules from the Thiel benchmark set. Statevector simulations reveal that QSE representability depends strongly on the target state, active space, and molecular electronic structure, with multiconfigurational character emerging as an important factor. In several cases, the one-body QSE subspace cannot adequately represent the target states, while explicit double-excitation operators improve representability at the cost of a larger operator space. Analysis of the QSE overlap matrix shows that although eigenmodes with small eigenvalues drive numerical instability, they cannot be discarded indiscriminately without compromising spectral accuracy. Under finite-shot sampling, energy errors exhibit an empirical scaling of approximately n_{\mathrm{orb}}^2/\sqrt{N_{\mathrm{shots}}} , which, combined with the growth in measurement groups, yields a total measurement cost of approximately \mathcal{O}(n_{\mathrm{orb}}^{11}) for constant accuracy under our direct-estimation protocol. These results expose a central tension between representability, numerical stability, and measurement cost. Encouragingly, we find that the projected matrices exhibit recurring structural patterns, while the finite-shot perturbations in the Hamiltonian and overlap matrices show nontrivial covariance, suggesting opportunities for more efficient structure-aware measurement and reconstruction strategies. Overall, our results provide an assessment of QSE across chemically-relevant organic molecules, identifying present limitations while highlighting potential routes toward more practical future implementations.

papers.title: Highly Luminescent Alkyl- and Alkoxy-Terminated Silicon Quantum Dots via Aging Following Single-Step Plasma Synthesis and Functionalization
papers.abstract: Nonthermal plasma synthesis enables the continuous production and immediate surface functionalization of silicon quantum dots (Si QDs) in a single, flow-through reactor. While this process occurs on a millisecond timescale, the resulting nanocrystals are often limited by low photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQY) due to persistent surface defects. In this work, we demonstrate that a minimal post-treatment, aging the Si QDs in specific solvents, can enhance the PLQY to ~50%, approaching the performance of much more complex solution-phase methods. We find that the choice of the surface ligand and solvent is critical: hexanol-terminated Si QDs exhibit significantly higher initial and final PLQYs than decene-terminated particles, likely due to the faster reaction of alcohols with electrophilic surface sites in the gas phase. Among the solvents investigated, chloroform consistently yields the highest PLQY. Furthermore, we show that light irradiation at 400 nm and 633 nm drastically accelerates the Si QD aging process, reducing the aging time from hundreds of hours to under 20 hours. This practical “synthesize and forget” strategy offers an efficient pathway for optimizing high-PLQY Si QDs for applications in optoelectronics and bioimaging.

papers.title: Assessing the state of the art in ADMET prediction: Lessons from the OpenADMET-ExpansionRx community blind challenge
papers.abstract: Computational blind challenges are essential for advancing drug discovery, especially in research areas with limited public data, such as absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, toxicity (ADMET) prediction. In this paper, we present the results of our latest community blind challenge, organized in collaboration with Expansion Therapeutics (ExpansionRx). Participants were tasked with predicting nine distinct ADMET endpoints routinely evaluated during lead optimization of compounds in drug discovery programs. Following unprecedented engagement from the global community, this challenge provided valuable insights into the state of the art in machine learning for ADMET modeling. Evaluating submissions against a realistic, challenging dataset from active ExpansionRx drug discovery programs revealed that message-passing neural networks and chemical foundation models dominated among the top performers. Furthermore, the results highlighted the power of proprietary industry datasets and a critical need to optimize predictive workflows for different endpoints independently via multitasking and task-affinity grouping. We also demonstrate how hosting our open-source blind challenge infrastructure on a flexible platform like Hugging Face was pivotal for driving community engagement and visibility. Ultimately, blind challenges supported by robust infrastructure, widespread dissemination, and rigorous post-challenge analysis are fundamental to maximizing the utility of public data releases. We anticipate that these community benchmarks will continue to drive the advancement of ADMET models, enabling their deployment in both early- and late-stage drug discovery.

papers.title: Treatise on Present Practice and Perspectives of MDGC
papers.abstract: The state of affairs of multidimensional gas chromatography (MDGC) at present is no more than an implementation of a two-dimensional form (2D-GC) reducing the domain to the setup known as GCxGC. Introduced in 1991 with great expectation, however, GCxGC still happen to fall short of realizing the anticipated capabilities despite continuous efforts made over the elapsed 35 years. This got quantitative formulation in regard of separation performance as early as 2008, proving that it failed to be competitive with a well-governed 1D-GC. The present paper highlights further limitations of GCxGC: inadequate operation burdened with shortcomings are presented via examples taken from GCxGC literature; crowning the list with the inability to meet fundamental requirement that if a compound can be analyzed by 1D-GC it must remain analyzable by MDGC. The repertoire of the intertwining issues, each of which unavoidably rigs or even hamstrings the others, highlights that GCxGC has a built-in self-limiting feature. Attempts to overcome confinements via loosening the binding conditions turned GCxGC back to the form it emerged from decades ago, yet without getting rid of the hampering curbs. The unfavorable overall picture forces to consider viabilities of other concepts, with focus on avoiding errors and pitfalls of GCxGC while fulfilling basic requirements of MDGC. In our view, there are two alternatives. One is ZGC, principle of which was introduced in 1989, requirements and potential of which are presented here in more detail; the other is a concept called Quantum-GC, which is presented as an introductory approach.

papers.title: Predicting Thermophysical Properties of Halide Salts Using On-the-Fly Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials Across Multiple Exchange-Correlation Functionals
papers.abstract: In silico modeling of molten salts is pivotal for the development of emerging carbon-free energy technologies, where accurate knowledge of thermophysical properties is essential for understanding and predicting material behavior under operating conditions. However, the accurate prediction of these properties using first-principles methods remains computationally intractable because of the large length scales and long timescales required to adequately describe molten-salt systems. In addition to these computational limitations, the choice of exchange-correlation (XC) functional is crucial for accurately predicting thermophysical properties. Here, we employ machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) to investigate the thermophysical properties of NaBr, KCl, and AgCl, which represent alkali- and transition-metal halides, across their solid and liquid phases. We systematically benchmark ten XC functionals for NaBr over a temperature range of 600–1400 K and subsequently assess the transferability of the best-performing functional to KCl and AgCl. The MLIPs enable simulations at length and timescales beyond the practical limits of conventional ab initio molecular dynamics, thereby facilitating the prediction of key thermophysical properties, including density and ionic self-diffusion coefficients. In addition, the simulations capture the first-order solid–liquid phase transition, allowing the behavior of these salts to be examined across both phases within a unified computational framework. Our results show that the BEEF-vdW functional provides accurate predictions of the optimized lattice constants of NaBr and KCl and consequently reproduces their experimental solid- and liquid-phase densities. For molten NaBr, the predicted Na⁺ and Br⁻ self-diffusion coefficients agree with experimental measurements to within approximately 6%, demonstrating the ability of the MLIP-based approach to reproduce experimentally relevant transport properties. However, the transferability of an XC functional is found to be system-dependent. Although BEEF-vdW performs well for NaBr and KCl, it inaccurately predicts the density of AgCl, which is associated with its inaccurate prediction of the lattice constant. In contrast, PBE-D3 provides excellent agreement with the experimental density of AgCl, with deviations of approximately 5% across both the solid and liquid phases. This work establishes a foundation for the high-throughput generation of reliable molten-salt thermophysical databases using general machine-learning potentials, enabling simulations beyond the computational limitations of first-principles methods.

papers.title: Features of the Gibbs Equation (∆G = ∆H - T∆S) Applied to Solvation, Vaporization, and Complexation Thermodynamics
papers.abstract: The Gibbs equation (∆ G = ∆ H – T ∆ S ) remains a cornerstone of chemical thermodynamics. Yet the scope and origins of the widely observed correlations between the enthalpies (∆ H ) and entropies (∆ S ), or Gibbs energies (∆ G ) and enthalpies, have long been debated. This study systematically analyzes over 4,500 experimental thermodynamic values at 298.15 K to establish quantitative principles governing the ∆ G vs. ∆ H relationship across solvation, vaporization, and molecular complexation processes. By classifying systems according to hydrogen-bonding capabilities, we demonstrate that non-associated solute–solvent pairs universally follow a baseline linear correlation (the Barclay–Butler line). Systematic deviations from this baseline are quantitatively attributed to distinct physical contributions: conformational flexibility in long-chain aliphatics (hindered internal rotation), a constant entropic penalty per directional hydrogen bond, and predominantly entropic solvophobic effects in associated solvents. Through thermodynamic transformations, these solvation/vaporization rules are extended to yield a universal linear ∆ G –∆ H relationship with an invariant slope of 0.660 for both solution- and gas-phase molecular complexation, encompassing hydrogen bonding, charge transfer, and dispersion interactions. The framework is successfully applied to α -cyclodextrin host–guest systems, where it can be used as a diagnostic tool for detecting anomalous or non-inclusion binding modes and for deeper analysis of the complexation mechanism. Ultimately, this work transforms the Gibbs equation into a predictive instrument, enabling accurate estimation of enthalpies from single-temperature Gibbs energy measurements and providing a unified, mechanism-independent foundation for analyzing intermolecular interactions in systems of varying complexity.

papers.title: Integrating Ion Mobility–Resolved Tandem Mass Spectrometry and Microcrystal Electron Diffraction for Structural Elucidation
Light Intensity Switches Photocurrent Polarity via Surface States in Single-Component Semiconductors
papers.abstract: Understanding and regulating photocurrent generation in semiconductors, particularly the control of polarity, is central to photoelectrochemical (PEC) system design. While engineered heterojunctions enable wavelength-dependent polarity switching, they require complex architectures. Light intensity, by contrast, is far more readily tuned but has long been limited to modulating photocurrent magnitude. Herein, we report that surface states, which participate in photoinduced carrier transfer, can mediate light-intensity-dependent photocurrent polarity reversal in single-component semiconductors of both n- and p-type (e.g., carbon nitride, CdTe quantum dots, and BiOI). Mechanism studies reveal that in the photocurrent switching potential (E ps ) region, where the built-in potential is attenuated, surface state occupation, dictated by illumination intensity, governs the direction of charge transfer. This surface-state-mediated mechanism establishes light intensity as an orthogonal dimension for adaptive photoresponsivity, bypassing the need for heterojunction engineering. As a proof of concept, a dopamine PEC biosensor built on this principle achieves exceptional selectivity without conventional biorecognition units, where photocurrent polarity itself serves as the recognition dimension.

papers.title: Magnetron Sputtering of Conformal Tungsten and Copper Coatings onto Glass Microsphere Powder via Agitation
Local-Environment Populations Govern Size-Dependent OER Activity in Supported Subnanometer IrO𝑥 Clusters
papers.abstract: Proton-exchange-membrane water electrolysis is constrained by the high Ir demand of the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER), motivating supported subnanometer IrO𝑥 clusters that maximize Ir utilization. At this scale, however, changing cluster size simultaneously alters structure, oxygen coverage, and the distribution of nonequivalent active sites, making it difficult to identify the physical origin of size-dependent activity. Here, we combine systematic structure sampling, density functional theory, implicit solvation, and site-resolved microkinetics to resolve OER thermodynamics across Ir𝑛O𝑥 (𝑛 = 1–30) clusters supported on anatase TiO2(101). The resulting activity landscape is strongly heterogeneous and nonmonotonic with cluster size, with substantial activity variations even among sites on the same cluster. This heterogeneity can be traced to the local oxygen coordination of the active Ir–∗O motif. Increasing oxo-proximal coordination, quantified by CNO,co(Ir∗), raises the ∗OH-to-∗O free-energy cost while lowering that of ∗O-to-∗OOH formation, thereby controlling the energetic balance between the two steps surrounding ∗O. Electronic-structure analysis associates this coordination dependence with charge redistribution at the binding Ir center, changes in Ir–O bonding, and reorganization of the Ir 5d–O 2p electronic structure. Steady-state microkinetics preserves the thermodynamic activity hierarchy, with ensemble rates governed primarily by the most active sites at each cluster size. Single-Ir dissolution thermodynamics further shows that higher local oxygen coordination is associated with greater resistance to Ir loss, extending the significance of local coordination from OER energetics to dissolution stability. These results establish local-environment populations as the structural origin of size-dependent catalytic behavior in subnanometer IrO𝑥 clusters, revealing local coordination rather than cluster size alone as the key structural variable underlying activity and stability.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Accelerated Inverse Design of Sequence-Controlled Terpolymers
papers.abstract: Sequence-controlled polymers hold immense potential for advanced materials design, yet discovering their experimental recipes is bottlenecked by the high-dimension kinetic parameter space of multicomponent copolymerization. Traditional ordinary differential equation (ODE) solvers provide rapid macrokinetic predictions but are fundamentally blind to explicit backbone microstructures. To bridge this gap, we use a stochastic simulation algorithm (SSA) engine to generate high-throughput terpolymer sequence data from a physically constrained parametric sweep across a 9-dimensional kinetic space, charting how feed stoichiometry and kinetic propensities dictate macromolecular structure. Information-theoretic analysis and t-SNE dimensionality reduction of the resulting 27-component triad frequency matrices for each simulation reveal profound microstructural degeneracies, demonstrating that traditional ensemble descriptors, such as the Harwood run number, are fundamentally incapable of describing sequence specifics. To accelerate optimization, we establish a digital twin strategy utilizing an XGBoost regressor to instantaneously predict localized chain-end propagation probabilities based on target sequence motifs. Finally, we demonstrate a closed-loop inverse design strategy that passes the 2 machine learning predictions to a deterministic root-finding optimizer, isolating exact initial monomer feeds and reactivity ratios needed to create them. By training an ML surrogate using explicit chain sequences from SSA, this framework provides a powerful alternative to classical macrokinetic equations, establishing an immediate, predictive tool to accelerate the discovery and reliable synthesis of sequence-controlled functional macromolecules.

papers.title: Site-Selective Radical Carbonylation of Aryl Thianthrenium Salts with Gaseous CO in Flow
papers.abstract: Site-selective carbonylation of complex arenes remains challenging, particularly when carbon monoxide must intercept short-lived radical intermediates. Here, we report a photoredox carbonylation of aryl thianthrenium salts with gaseous CO and Michael acceptors in continuous flow. Pressurized gas–liquid flow facilitates the interception of photogenerated aryl radicals by CO, generating acyl radicals that subsequently engage diverse Michael acceptors to furnish 1,4-dicarbonyl derivatives. The method is compatible with a broad range of functional groups, heterocycles, pharmaceuticals, and natural-product-derived substrates, and its synthetic utility is demonstrated through a three-step synthesis of fenbufen from biphenyl and diversification of a salicin-derived 1,4-diketone into several heterocycles. This strategy combines siteselective arene thianthrenation with flow radical carbonylation, providing a versatile approach to the late-stage installation of carbonyl-containing motifs in complex molecules.

papers.title: Deposition-Dependent Excitonic Properties of Spin-Coated CsPbBr3 Thin Films Revealed by Temperature-Dependent Optical Spectroscopy.
papers.abstract: Temperature dependence of the optical properties of CsPbBr3 perovskites prepared by spin coating is studied. Absorbance and photoluminescence spectra were acquired at controlled temperature varying from room temperature to 20 K. In the case of absorbance, the Elliott model for excitonic absorbance was considered, allowing obtaining parameters such as bandgap energy, exiton binding energy, and Stokes shift, among others. The bandgap energy increases with temperature, against what is observed in conventional tetragonal semiconductors. The exciton binding energy also increases with temperature as expected from its dependence with reduced exciton effective mass and dielectric constant. The Stokes shift follows Guriolli´s model for carrier thermalization in photoluminescence spectra, indicating the free excitonic recombination as its origin. Other models were also studied, such as the Segall function for the Full Width at Half Maximum of the photoluminescence spectra, which shows that the dominant term at higher temperatures is the exciton optical phonon coupling. Arrhenius function for the area of the photoluminescence spectral intensity indicates two channels of exciton dissociation. At low temperatures the Urbach energy is very low, and gives phonon energies compatible with the one obtained from Segall model. It was observed that certain parameters, such as the excitonic binding energy and the Urbach energy, show appreciable variation with the number of cycles of the sample synthesis process. The sample synthesized with 5 cycles presents an optimal balance between low disorder, less exciton-phonon coupling and favorable excitonic parameters.

papers.title: Mining the cysteine-motif repertoire of airway mucins reveals redox-active mucolytic peptides
papers.abstract: Muco-obstructive lung diseases are characterized by hyper concentrated airway mucus in which gel-forming mucins form mechanically reinforced polymer networks. Thiol-based mucolytics can reduce disulfide bonds within these networks, but clinically used monothiols show limited potency, whereas stronger reducing agents are constrained by instability and toxicity. Here, we systematically mined the major airway mucins MUC5B and MUC5AC for closely spaced cysteine motifs and screened the resulting mucin-derived peptide library for redox activity, oxidation stability, solubility, epithelial compatibility, and mucolytic activity. The identified Cys–[X]n–Cys peptides displayed pronounced sequence- and pH-dependent thioldisulfide exchange capabilities, with many peptides reacting faster than monothiol controls and several exhibiting reactivity approaching or superior to dithiothreitol (DTT). Reactivity was governed by the combined effects of thiol number, apparent thiol pKa, and local motif architecture rather than by a single physicochemical descriptor. Analysis of free-thiol stability and oxidation products further revealed sequence-dependent access to distinct intra- and intermolecular disulfide states. Together, these measurements provide a systematic sequence-redox framework for understanding how closely spaced cysteine motifs tune thioldisulfide exchange, with implications for the design of redox-active peptides and for understanding how local cysteine sequence environments may contribute to oxidative protein folding. Developability profiling identified soluble, reduced-thiol-stable, and epithelialcompatible candidates. Selected peptides reduced high-molecular-weight MUC5B multimers in cystic fibrosis mucus and MUC5AC multimers in asthma mucus, with activities in the range of DTT and greater than NAC under the tested conditions. These peptides were active in both pathological and healthy mucus, while showing compound-dependent differences in their concentration-response profiles across mucus environments. Our findings point at airway mucins as a source of redox-active peptide candidates with potential for mucolytic therapy and provide a broadly applicable resource for relating cysteine-motif sequence to disulfideexchange behavior.

papers.title: Descriptor-Dependent Metal–Ligand Covalency Across a Matched Mn–Cu Coordination Series
papers.abstract: Metal–ligand covalency is central to the electronic structure of first-row transition-metal complexes, but different descriptors do not necessarily measure the same component of bonding. Here, we examine descriptor agreement and disagreement across a matched series of neutral fourcoordinate complexes, MCl2L2, where M = Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, or Cu and L = NH3, pyridine, PMe3, or an N-heterocyclic carbene. Multiple spin states and tetrahedral or square-planar starting geometries were screened using PBE0-D4 and TPSSh-D4, followed by large-basis single-point calculations and QTAIM analysis. Mn, Fe, Co, and Cu show consistent spin and geometry assignments across both functionals, whereas Ni displays a ligand-dependent d8 spin/geometry crossover. Targeted CAS(8,5)-FIC-NEVPT2 calculations indicate near-degenerate singlet and triplet structures for Ni–NH3, favor singlet square-planar structures for Ni–PMe3 and Ni–NHC, and strongly favor the triplet distorted structure for Ni–pyridine. Across the full series, ρBCP, HBCP, delocalization indices, Mayer bond orders, normalized M–L distances, and spin populations reveal related but non-equivalent trends. PMe3 and NHC show comparable basin sharing and normalized bond contraction but differ in how their bonding is represented by local and population-derived descriptors: NHC is emphasized by ρBCP and HBCP, whereas PMe3 is emphasized by Mayer bond order. These results show that first-row metal–ligand covalency is neither a transferable ligand constant nor a single scalar property, but a state- and metal-dependent bonding response better represented by a multidimensional descriptor fingerprint.

papers.title: Dihydrogen Phosphate as a Hydrophilic Co-Anion in Multicomponent Cholinium Ionic Liquids for Directional Solvent Extraction
papers.abstract: Directional solvent extraction (DSE) recovers water from brine with low-temperature heat, and its output depends on how much water the solvent takes up on heating and releases on cooling. In an ionic liquid (IL) solvent, adding a hydrophilic co-anion is one way to tune this behavior. Here we screened co-anions X in 5:1 mixtures of cholinium bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)imide ([Choline][NTf2]) with [Choline][X] and selected dihydrogen phosphate. We followed liquids with nominal [NTf2] : [H2PO4] ratios of 5:1, 10:1 and 20:1 over five extraction cycles and determined the freshwater yield (FWY) of each run from the mass of the phase collected after cooling. Every run with these liquids had an FWY above the ≈ 0.30 wt% ◦C−1 reported for 1-ethyl-3-methylimidazolium bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)imide and the ≈ 0.31 wt% ◦C−1 reported for a hydroxide-containing cholinium formulation. FWY was 0.35–0.38 wt% ◦C−1 in the first cycle. When the recovered liquids were reused, it rose to 0.55–0.58 wt% ◦C−1 in the second or third cycle and then declined to 0.40–0.49 wt% ◦C−1 in the fourth and fifth cycles. In molecular dynamics simulations, dihydrogen phosphate interacted strongly with water, as reported for hydroxide, and was enriched around water relative to its share of the anions.

papers.title: Drugon: Phase-Encoded Morgan Fingerprints Match Pretrained Chemical Transformers in Low-Data Affinity Prediction
papers.abstract: Pretrained chemical language models such as ChemBERTa and MoLFormer have become the default choice for molecular property prediction. However, they require large training sets to fine-tune effectively, and their computational footprint is substantial. We present Drugon, a compact alternative based on a Phase-Encoded Morgan fingerprint combined with a LightGBM regressor. Drugon requires approximately 15,000× fewer parameters and 40× less training time than fine-tuned transformers, while achieving higher predictive accuracy on three independent ChEMBL targets (n = 1378 to 2000). On the c-Abl dataset (CHEMBL4550), Drugon reaches a Pearson r = 0.749 under 5-fold cross-validation, compared with 0.605 for fine-tuned ChemBERTa and 0.551 for MoLFormer. Across all three targets, phase encoding provides a consistent, non-negative improvement over the classical binary Morgan fingerprint (∆r ∈ [0.000, 0.026]). Our results suggest that, in the low-data regime (n < 2000), fingerprint-based methods remain the most efficient and interpretable

papers.title: Flash Communication: On-Complex Assembly of Organic Azide Ligands
papers.abstract: Organic azides can serve as precursors to reactive metal nitrenes. Transition metal complexes of organic azide ligands are typically prepared by coordination of pre-synthesized organic azides to appropriate metal complexes. Here, we report on-complex assembly of organic azides by alkylation of metal complexes featuring inorganic azide ligands. This strategy, which we demonstrate in the context of Rh2 complexes, avoids isolation and handling of organic azides and thus provides access to complexes of volatile, potentially explosive organic azide ligands.

papers.title: From Computation-Ready to Claim-Ready: An Evidence Framework for MOF Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Scientific data are routinely transformed so they can be stored, joined and used by machine-learning models. These steps enable scale, but they can also remove the context that tells us what a prediction means and how far it can be trusted. Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) make this problem especially clear: one nominal material may appear as an experimental crystal, an activated simulation structure, a charge-assigned model or a row of descriptors, while information about protonation, counterions, coordination environment or measurement conditions may disappear along the way. We introduce claim readiness: a framework for asking whether the evidence preserved through a data pipeline is sufficient for the scientific claim made at the end of it. By tracing chemical evidence, identifier joins and evaluation choices, we show that data can be highly usable for machine learning yet incomplete for chemistry-sensitive interpretation, and that a model can still be useful for ranking candidates even when its value-level accuracy decreases under a harder split. The wider lesson is not specific to MOFs: trustworthy scientific machine learning requires a traceable connection between the representation used by the model and the evidence needed to support the resulting claim. Highlights • Claim readiness matches scientific claims to evidence preserved in data pipelines • Model-ready materials data can lose chemistry needed for interpretation • Data joins change which materials enter representation comparisons • Harder data splits reduce accuracy while useful candidate ranking can remain

papers.title: Modulating Geometric Frustration in COFs through Linker Flexibility for Enhanced Glucosamine and Galactosamine Adsorption
papers.abstract: Geometric frustration remains largely unexplored in covalent organic frameworks (COFs), where reticular synthesis typically relies on highly symmetric and geometrically compatible building blocks. Departing from these conventional geometrical constraints can introduce additional accessible and reactive sites, providing opportunities to tune material properties for applications such as catalysis, sensing, and adsorption. Herein, we introduce geometric frustration into COFs using an asymmetric tetradentate thiophene-based aldehyde linker possessing unconventional bite angles of approximately 68°, 69°, 68°, and 154°. Condensation of this linker with three linear diamines of varying rigidity, namely 1,4-phenylenediamine, trans-1,4-cyclohexanediamine, and benzidine, yielded the corresponding COFs THPD, THCH, and THBZ. Structural characterization using PXRD, BET analysis, FT-IR spectroscopy, and solid-state NMR revealed significant structural disorder within the frameworks. To further elucidate their structural organization, multiple sulfur-orientation-dependent structural models were constructed and analyzed using periodic density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Correlating linker distortion, quantified through root-mean-square deviation (RMSD), with relative framework energies revealed stabilization through intermediate distortion states rather than fully relaxed geometries. The aromatic linker-based systems accumulate substantially larger strain energies than the cyclohexanediamine-based framework, demonstrating that linker flexibility governs strain accommodation within the COFs. These distortions strongly influence framework accessibility and amino sugar adsorption, with the moderately frustrated THCH framework exhibiting significantly enhanced guest uptake relative to the more rigid frustrated systems and a non-frustrated reference COF. Collectively, this work demonstrates that geometric frustration can be systematically embedded and modulated within COFs through linker design, while establishing RMSD-based structural analysis as a quantitative tool for identifying and comparing geometrically frustrated systems.

papers.title: The Development and Optimization of Biogenic Molecularly Imprinted Sensors for the Sensitive and Selective Electroanalytical Quantitation of Met-Enkephalin
papers.abstract: Elucidating the roles of endogenous peptides such as Met-enkephalin in a spatiotemporal manner necessitates sensitive and selective measurement tools capable of measuring peptide dynamics in situ. In this work, we develop novel molecularly imprinted polymers on carbon fiber microelectrodes using the amino acid methionine as a functional monomer. We have coined these new materials biogenic molecularly imprinted polymers (bio-MIPs). Electroanalytical sensors are made by integrating these bio-MIPs with carbon fiber microelectrodes through electropolymerization. Using electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, we examined how tuning different parameters in cyclic voltammetry and chronoamperometry during polymerization affected the surface and performance of imprinted sensors. These sensors demonstrated comparable selectivity to prior o-phenylenediamine/aniline sensors but with six-fold greater redox response to the same concentration of Met-enkephalin. The bio-MIPs sensors were also created with 1000-fold less monomer and template peptide concentrations than previous ones using non-biogenic monomers such as o-phenylenediamine and aniline. Electrochemical impedance data demonstrate that the best performing bio-MIPs sensors had comparable conductivity as the bare electrode and an increase in electroactive area compared to the bare carbon fiber microelectrodes, with thinner polymeric coating resulting in better redox signal overall. This work lays the groundwork for new molecular recognition elements using electroactive amino acids as functional monomers for imprinting.

papers.title: A Multiscale Assessment of Oil-in-Water, Water-in-Oil, and Bicontinuous Structures in 2-Butanol/Water/Citric Acid surfactant-free microemulsions
papers.abstract: Surfactant-free microemulsions (SFMEs) are attracting growing interest as sustainable alternatives to conventional microemulsions, yet their structural organization remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigate a novel green SFME based on water, 2-butanol, and citric acid, combining dynamic light scattering, small-angle X-ray scattering, fluorescence spectroscopy, confocal laser scanning microscopy, and rheology to probe its organization from the nano- to the microscale. Samples located near the phase boundary exhibited a complex multiscale structure. Scattering measurements revealed the coexistence of nanometric and submicrometric-to-micrometric domains, while direct confocal observations confirmed the presence of micron-sized aggregates in optically transparent formulations. Fluorescence spectroscopy indicated that the local hydrophobic environment remained essentially unchanged across compositions, suggesting that structural evolution is mainly governed by changes in domain size and connectivity. As the oil-to-water ratio approached unity, the scattering behaviour deviated from that observed for the other formulations, indicating the emergence of a distinct structural regime. Combined scattering, microscopy, and rheological analyses identified this region as consistent with a bicontinuous organization already present below the macroscopic phase-separation temperature. Temperature-dependent experiments further revealed domain growth and enhanced viscoelastic contributions preceding visible phase separation. These findings demonstrate that transparent water/2-butanol/citric acid SFMEs can host pre-ouzo, ouzolike, and bicontinuous structures, providing new insight into the structural complexity of sustainable hydrotrope-based microemulsions.

papers.title: QMzyme: A Python Package for Automated and Systematic QM-based Enzyme Modeling
papers.abstract: We introduce QMzyme, a Python package to automate the generation of Quantum mechanics (QM)-based enzyme models. QM calculations on enzymes are computationally challenging because full enzyme systems typically contain thousands of atoms, placing accurate QM treatments beyond practical computational limits.Therefore, QM-based enzyme studies rely on identifying a subset of atoms that captures the essential chemistry of the reaction environment, enabling tractable yet chemically meaningful calculations. However, constructing these reduced models requires numerous user-defined decisions, including selection of the starting structure, identification of atoms to include in the QM region, and definition of truncation strategies for QM-only models, all of which can substantially influence the resulting calculations. QMzyme aims to provide the community with a flexible and extensible framework for automated, systematic generation of QM-based enzyme models, enabling researchers to more rigorously evaluate how model construction decisions influence computational outcomes while improving reproducibility and transparency across workflows. By facilitating high-throughput generation and analysis of QM enzyme models, QMzyme supports largescale, data-driven investigations of enzyme structure, function, and reactivity. This effort is especially crucial for the creation of large, chemically consistent datasets that can support emergent artificial intelligence and machine learning approaches for accelerated digital discovery in enzymology and biocatalysis.

papers.title: Probing Oxygen Transport in β-Cyclodextrin–Cyclohexane Crystal Nanochannels by Luminescence Quenching from Nanoseconds to Seconds
papers.abstract: Molecular transport in nanochannels can deviate from normal diffusion and exhibit different regimes depending on the observation timescale. However, resolving them from nanoseconds to seconds remains challenging. Here, oxygen transport in β -cyclodextrin–cyclohexane supramolecular crystals containing solvent-filled nanochannels is probed using room-temperature phosphorescence and fluorescence of aromatic luminophores. Their emission lifetimes, ranging from approximately 50 ns to 15 s, provide intrinsic time windows spanning more than eight orders of magnitude. Comparison of fluorescence and phosphorescence quenching for the same guests provides an internal control for probe identity. The effective bimolecular quenching rate constants decrease by approximately five orders of magnitude. Between approximately 50 ns and 10 ms, the dependence follows a power law, k q ∝ τ 0 -0.8 , followed by a nearly lifetime-independent plateau. The theory of diffusion-controlled reactions relates this dependence to the time-dependent oxygen flux and indicates subdiffusive transport at intermediate times with an effective anomalous exponent of approximately 0.4. A random-barrier model with quenched disorder provides a physical interpretation of this regime and its crossover to normal transport at long times. Thus, molecular excited states with different emission lifetimes enable luminescence quenching to resolve distinct temporal regimes of molecular transport under nanoscale confinement.

papers.title: Scalable Multiplexed Electrochemical Aptasensor Enabled by Chitosan for Heavy Metal Ion Detection: Advancing Electrode Functionalization and Reusability
papers.abstract: The rapid and reliable detection of heavy metal ions in water remains a critical challenge for environmental monitoring and public health protection. While recent advances in aptamer-based electrochemical sensors for heavy metal detection emphasize miniaturization and improved electrode modification techniques to achieve higher sensitivity, striking a balance among the sensor's analytical performance, ease of fabrication, and scalability remains a major challenge, often resulting in trade-offs between sensitivity and scalability. Herein, we have developed a sensitive, multi-analyte aptamer-based electrochemical sensor by modifying micro structured electrodes with chitosan, which adheres to their inherent functional groups, thereby simplifying sensor preparation. The target-specific aptamers are immobilized via glutaraldehyde-mediated crosslinking chemistry. Using a differential pulse voltammetry measurement technique the sensitivities of the sensor for specific heavy metals was found to be 21.7, 15.18, and 9.25 ΔI per decade change in concentration per unit area for Pb(II), As(III), and Cd(II), respectively. The limit of detection for the developed sensor is observed to be 1.03 ng/L for Pb(II), 0.45 ng/L for As(III), and 3.03 ng/L for Cd(II) in water. Further, the sensor's reusability has been analysed using a chelation mechanism in combination with potential stripping voltammetry. The sensor was effectively regenerated and reused across four consecutive cycles, thereby reducing the cost per test.

papers.title: A PN adamantanoid ligand for reticular materials
papers.abstract: Despite their functional advantages, ligands featuring inorganic elements are rare in reticular chemistry, as are three dimensional ligands. We report the synthesis and characterisation of a phosphorus-nitrogen (PN) cage-based tetra-benzoic acid – P 4 (BA) 4 – and its application to the synthesis of crystalline materials PNMOF-1 and PNHBP-1 . These results debut framework materials based on PN cages and expand the scope of 3-dimensional inorganic ligands for reticular chemistry beyond carboranes and silsesquioxanes.

papers.title: Revealing the Deactivation Mechanism of Aconitase at the Atomistic Level by Multiscale Simulations
papers.abstract: Mitochondrial aconitase is a key enzyme of the citric acid cycle that converts citrate to isocitrate at its [4Fe−4S] cluster cofactor. It is widely conserved across vertebrates and also found in numerous other organisms. Oxidation of the [4Fe−4S] cluster by reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (ROS/RNS) leads to the release of one Fe center, denoted as Fe α . The remaining [3Fe−4S] cluster is catalytically inactive, meaning aconitase oxidation leads to enzyme deactivation. Aconitase deactivation regulates the citric acid cycle and mitochondrial respiration, which leads to decreased ROS and RNS formation. Thus, aconitase serves as a redox sensor that prevents high ROS and RNS concentrations. The deactivation process is well characterized on the macroscopic scale, meaning that the deactivation kinetics and the thermodynamics of oxidation are known. However, little is known about the deactivation mechanism at the microscopic scale. In the present study, multiscale simulations were performed to elucidate the deactivation mechanism of aconitase on the atomistic level. Density functional theory calculations showed that the oxidized [4Fe−4S] cluster is roughly 70 kJ mol -1 to 100 kJ mol -1 less stable than the reduced cluster with respect to Fe α release. Molecular dynamics simulations with the hybrid quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics approach suggested that His167 and Asp165 facilitate Fe α release by coordinating to Fe α and weakening the Fe−S bonds in the cluster. The corresponding mechanism was supported by comparing simulated and experimental redox potentials of intermediate states. Classical molecular dynamics in combination with umbrella sampling showed that Fe α release is followed by the formation of two salt bridges near the active site, namely Glu640−Arg447 and Asp568−Arg452. Moreover, salt bridge formation is associated with a protein closing movement.

papers.title: Photo-oxidation of Dilute Methane in Dairy Barn Air: Pilot Scale Optimization
papers.abstract: Low concentration (below 1000 ppm) methane emissions from point sources such as cattle barns remain a significant source of greenhouse gas emissions, and have proven hard to mitigate. Previously, a novel method for methane photo-oxidation using UV light to produce chlorine radicals from chlorine gas, which subsequently oxidize methane, was proposed. Here we present the first real-world experimental results from a pilot scale Methane Eradication Photochemical System (MEPS) deployed at a dairy farm in Denmark. Utilizing electrolysis generated chlorine and UV light, chlorine radicals were produced in a confined photoreactor to effectively oxidize methane. The system demonstrated methane oxidation with a specific energy of 0.32 kWh/gCH4 and 75 % methane removal efficiency at an inlet concentration of 89 ppm. To better understand the operational parameters, the reactor was operated at a variety of different methane concentrations, UV irradiance, airflow rates, and chlorine concentrations. Statistical evaluation indicated that increasing UV power and Cl2 concentration synergistically minimizes specific energy while maximizing removal efficiency. The ability to achieve low specific energy and high removal efficiency underscores the system’s viability. By addressing agricultural emissions, this technology offers a tangible pathway for mitigating atmospheric methane and limiting global temperature overshoot in the 21st century.

papers.title: Machine Learned Interatomic Potentials and MultiobjectiveBayesian Optimization for Hydroxylamine Electrosynthesis overSubstituted COF-366
papers.abstract: Electrochemical nitrogen oxide reduction to hydroxylamine (NH2OH) couples substrate entry, branching among nitrogen–oxygen intermediates, and product release. This study develops a catalyst discovery workflow combining machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) with multiobjective Bayesian optimization (MOBO). The candidate space comprises 40 substituted COF-366 structures formed from eight metal centers and five linkers. Three thermodynamic quantities jointly define the optimization objectives: formation of the nitrite-derived *NO2 surface state, the first hydrogenation branch of *NO, and release of *NH2OH. The Universal Model for Atoms (UMA) evaluates candidate structures and key reaction states under consistent settings. We then compare G*NO and G*NHO as one-dimensional physical descriptors for Gaussian process (GP) models and expected hypervolume improvement (EHVI) search. With the same initial set, Matérn 5/2 kernel, and EHVI settings, G*NO recovers two preferred Mn candidates in fewer iterations and yields faster hypervolume growth, showing more efficient multiobjective search. The complete 40-candidate thermodynamic landscape further shows that Mn's relatively favorable baseline for substrate entry leaves more room for linker-induced tradeoffs. The vinyl2 and OMe2 linkers improve NH2OH release while maintaining acceptable substrate entry, thereby identifying favorable metal–linker combinations. Local electronic-structure analysis shows similar Mn charge, spin population, and electrostatic potential around vinyl2-Mn and OMe2-Mn. A free-energy pathway for vinyl2-Mn favors N–O bond retention through *NHO toward NH2OH and supports favorable product release. This work illustrates a catalyst discovery strategy that uses mechanistic descriptors as coordinates for multiobjective search and identifies how metal centers and linkers jointly regulate the nitrite-to-hydroxylamine reaction network.

papers.title: ProtMutMap: Predicting Protein Binding Free Energy Changes Using Multiple-Mutation Networks
papers.abstract: Predicting changes in binding free energy ΔΔ G caused by multiple mutations at protein−protein interfaces requires accounting for nonadditive interactions between mutations, which an additive approximation based on single mutations cannot capture, and for the dependence on the computational pathway in stepwise approaches that introduce mutations sequentially. Here, we propose ProtMutMap, a method that integrates information from multiple pathways in a network whose nodes represent target variants and variants containing subsets of their mutations, and whose edges represent free energy perturbation (FEP) calculations for residue substitutions. ProtMutMap simultaneously estimates the binding ΔΔ G of each variant from all edge values using Huber loss. We compared ProtMutMap with the additive approximation and the stepwise method at 30 evaluation points, including intermediate variants, using a multiple-mutation dataset comprising 7 protein complex systems derived from SKEMPI2. ProtMutMap achieved a root mean squared error (RMSE) of 1.13 kcal/mol, lower than that of either comparison method. ProtMutMap also yielded lower prediction errors than Rosetta flex ddG. These comparisons with experimental values demonstrate that integrating multiple pathways through variants containing subsets of the target mutations improves binding ΔΔ G predictions for protein variants with multiple mutations.

papers.title: Ethanol-Oriented CO2 Hydrogenation for Alcohol-to-Jet Sustainable Aviation Fuels: Catalyst Design and Fixed-Bed Performance Benchmarking
papers.abstract: Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) is expected to play a central role in aviation decarbonization because long-range flights will continue to depend on energy-dense, infrastructure-compatible liquid fuels. Among available SAF pathways, alcohol-to-jet (ATJ) routes connect oxygenated intermediates with established upgrading technologies for jet-range hydrocarbons. In this context, alcohol-oriented thermocatalytic CO 2 hydrogenation could provide an upstream platform for SAF production when coupled with low-carbon H 2 . However, catalytic studies have largely been evaluated using reaction-centered metrics, while the downstream implications of alcohol identity have received less critical attention. This Review positions ethanol synthesis within the broader landscape of methanol and higher alcohol synthesis and examines how alcohol identity affects carbon-chain construction, deoxygenation and hydrogen requirements, separation burden, and pathway compatibility. Ethanol is adopted as the central reference intermediate because it balances upstream synthetic accessibility with downstream ATJ relevance. To establish a data-centered benchmark, ethanol-forming catalyst performance reported over the past two decades under continuous-flow fixed-bed conditions is critically compiled and normalized. Where the source data permit, EtOH selectivity is recalculated on a common total-carbon basis and catalyst-mass-normalized EtOH space-time yield (STY) is derived using a consistent definition. Comparison of noble-metal, Co-based, Cu-based, and Fe/Zn/alkali multielement and tandem catalysts reveals a common design logic in which multifunctional site ensembles, engineered interfaces, and promoter/support effects define the ethanol-forming window. By linking fixed-bed catalytic evidence with downstream ATJ requirements, this Review provides a framework for evaluating CO 2 -to-ethanol catalysts as components of SAF-oriented alcohol platforms.

papers.title: Hydrophobic Interaction as the Resolution of Interfacial Frustration
papers.abstract: The hydrophobic effect is one of the central organizing principles of molecular biology, underpinning protein folding, molecular recognition, membrane self-assembly and many forms of biomolecular recognition. Contemporary statistical-mechanical frameworks explain much of its thermodynamics, including the dependence of hydration on solute size, density fluctuations and interfacial formation. The remaining conceptual challenge is not the absence of successful theories, but the lack of a common spatial language to describe how heterogeneous non-polar interfaces perturb the collective state of water. In this paper, I propose interfacial frustration as such a descriptor, presenting it as a spatially distributed measure of the mismatch between the preferred state of hydrogen bonded water and the geometric constraints imposed by a non-polar interface. I propose that hydrophobic association can be viewed as a solvent-mediated reduction of this mismatch, while retaining the established thermodynamic description in terms of free energy (G), enthalpy (H), entropy (S) and density fluctuations. Hence, the proposed framework is intended as a complementary representation, and not a replacement of existing theories like Lum-Chandler-Weeks (LCW) theory. The spatial pattern, overlap, and non-additivity of interfacial frustration can provide a common descriptor for geometry dependent association and the crossover from localized hydration to collective interfacial drying. I also develop a more tentative extension to protein dynamics, in which hydration coupled fluctuations at and around hydrophobic cores may modulate distal conformational ensembles. The proposed framework generates explicit operational definitions, comparative predictions and falsification criteria that distinguish it from explanations based solely on surface area, local density or generic conformational entropy

papers.title: Non-Orthogonal Exciton Theory Including Charge Transfer Effects for Strongly Coupled Chromophores
Quantum Sensing of Lithium Ions with Defect-Engineered Recognition Pockets in a TEMPO-Modified Covalent Organic Framework
papers.abstract: Nuclear-spin quantum sensing requires coherent molecular electron spin qubits embedded in analyte-recognizing local environments that bring target nuclei into their short-range hyperfine detection volume. Here, we introduce TA-TEMPO, a covalent organic framework in which dilute nitroxide radicals and Li + -binding triazine moieties form defect-engineered recognition pockets for room-temperature 7 Li sensing. Optimizing radical density preserves spin coherence while maximizing the 7 Li/ 1 H response acquired by hyperfine spectroscopy. TA-TEMPO detects Li + in a tetrahydrofuran solution of LiBr with a sensitivity of 1.0 × 10 −4 mol·L −1 at room temperature, a 50-fold improvement over the previous benchmark, and enables quantum sensing across several lithium-based electrolytes. Control experiments and density functional theory calculations show that triazine sites preferentially bind Li + over Na + and position it near nitroxide radicals, accounting for selective detection in a large excess of Na + . These results establish chemically programmed host-guest recognition as a strategy to integrate sensitivity, selectivity, and coherent spin readout in porous molecular quantum sensors.

papers.title: AnhDis: A Scheme for Anharmonic Nuclear Ensembles and Absorption Spectra
papers.abstract: The Nuclear Ensemble Approach (NEA), typically implemented using the harmonic Wigner approximation, has shown significant limitations when applied to molecules with pronounced anharmonicity. The harmonic model frequently samples unphysical regions of the potential energy surface, resulting in artificial spectral broadening and spurious transitions. In this work, the Anharmonic-Distribution (AnhDis) scheme is presented. The method is based on constructing mode-resolved potential energy surfaces through explicit scans, represented in the present implementation by quartic polynomial fits, although higher-order expansions or other one-dimensional potential energy functions can be employed when required. By solving the resulting one-dimensional vibrational Hamiltonians, physically consistent nuclear distributions that account for anharmonic confinement and wave functions asymmetry are obtained. Temperature effects are incorporated through Boltzmann weighting of the vibrational eigenstates. AnhDis significantly improves upon harmonic sampling while maintaining the computational feasibility required for large-scale systems. Validation against higher-level reference approaches and experimental data across atmospherically relevant molecules demonstrates that the proposed method captures absorption spectral profiles while reducing harmonic-induced artifacts.

papers.title: Simplified Time-Dependent Density-Functional Theory for Noble Metal Nanoclusters: Progress Toward the Tamm–Dancoff Approximation
papers.abstract: We investigate the optical and plasmonic properties of noble metal nanoclusters containing up to a few hundred atoms using the simplified time-dependent density functional theory (sTDDFT) framework. Extending our previous work based on the Tamm--Dancoff approximation (sTDA), we assess the impact of solving the full Casida equation on the computed photoabsorption spectra. Compared with sTDA, the full sTDDFT formalism yields enhanced plasmon-band intensities and systematically red shifts plasmon-band positions, while preserving the overall spectral profile in the 2--5 eV range at a still affordable computational cost. We further show that global and range-separated hybrid functionals are essential for a reliable description of plasmon resonances. Benchmarking against damped complex-polarizability TDDFT (polTDDFT) demonstrates that sTDDFT provides an efficient and reliable alternative for describing the optical response of noble metal nanoclusters.

papers.title: Chemically fueled amplification of supramolecular asymmetry with double chiroptical inversion
papers.abstract: Amplification of asymmetry in supramolecular polymers is typically studied under equilibrium conditions in apolar solvents, while examples in aqueous media, under non-equilibrium conditions or under temporal chemical control remain scarce. Here we demonstrate chemically fueled amplification of supramolecular asymmetry in water using perylene diimide (PDI) derivatives. The chemically fueled reaction cycle uses sodium dithionite to reduce and depolymerize kinetically stable helical aggregates, while subsequent oxidation by dissolved oxygen restores them. This transient disassembly–reassembly process yields amplification of asymmetry in Majority Rules ( MR ) experiments that is absent in the kinetically trapped system. In Sergeants-and-Soldiers ( SaS ) experiments, the fueled cycle shows an unusual composition-dependent response characterized by a double helical inversion as a function of sergeant fraction. A phase model captures the emergence of three composition regimes and rationalizes the observed CD response. Overall, we show how chemical fuels can regulate asymmetry amplification in aqueous supramolecular polymers and highlight the role of phase competition in complex chiral self-assembly.

papers.title: Electrochemically Stabilized Iron Foam Enables Selective and Durable Nitrate-to-Ammonia Conversion at Industrial Current Densities
papers.abstract: We report the synthesis of Fe foams by dynamic hydrogen bubble template (DHBT)-assisted electrodeposition and their electrocatalytic performance for the selective reduction of nitrate to ammonia, a strategy that mitigates nitrate pollution while providing a decentralized route for ammonia production. Fe-foam_90s@Ti achieves a Faradaic efficiency of up to 97% and a partial current density for ammonia formation approaching -1 A cm -2 without externally imposed convection. Operando Raman spectroscopy tracked the potential-dependent reduction of surface Fe oxides and, together with identical-location scanning electron microscopy (IL-SEM), supported the assignment of metallic Fe as the catalytically active state for selective ammonia formation. Potential-dependent ICP-MS and ion chromatography analyses identified an operating window with minimal Fe dissolution, in which the corrosion-prone catalyst can be electrochemically stabilized through cathodic protection. The catalyst was further implemented in a laboratory-scale flow-cell electrolyzer under galvanostatic conditions, demonstrating its compatibility with continuous-flow operation. Together, these results establish DHBT-derived Fe foams as promising electrocatalysts for high-rate ammonia electrosynthesis and support their further evaluation in scaled flow-cell systems.

papers.title: Gas Phase Structures of Cationized Imidacloprid and Cationized Chlorpyrifos
papers.abstract: Neonicotinoids and organophosphates are important analytes due to their use as insecticides and environmental profiles. Cationized imidacloprid and chlorpyrifos as prototypical examples of these were analyzed with drift tube, traveling wave, trapped ion, and cyclic ion mobility mass spectrometry, with experimental collision cross sections ( Exp CCS N2 ) derived for each to help understand their gas phase structures. The Exp CCS N2 of potassiated imidacloprid and chlorpyrifos are reported for the first time. The cross-platform Exp CCS N2 for [imidacloprid+K] + is 160−165 Å² and for [chlorpyrifos+K] + is 175–176 Å². Consistent assignment of [imidacloprid+H] + structure is achieved based on current work, literature interlaboratory CCS values, DFT energetics, predicted CCS ( Calc CCS N2 ) and literature IRMPD spectroscopy. Imidacloprid coordinates cations at the pyridinic N, with a varying degree of nitroguanidine interaction that depends on the cation. Sodiated and potassiated imidacloprid ions have a 10-membered ring structure where the overall size depends more on the non-covalent interactions than the incorporated cation size. Chlorpyrifos also coordinates cations at the N, but consistently forms 6-membered ring structures. Overall size trends for sodiated and potassiated species follow the cation size trends, revealing the change in size due to incorporated cation. The consistency of interlaboratory results and current results also support confident assignment for the protomer of [chlorpyrifos+H] + .

papers.title: Unlocking chromophore excited state modulation in photoactive biohybrids using protein conformational dynamics
papers.abstract: Photoactive biohybrids offer a promising platform for photonic applications by merging the functional versatility of synthetic molecules with the tunable structure and dynamics of proteins. While unexpected excited-state relaxation in biohybrids has been attributed to complex protein motions, the intentional design and exploitation of such dynamics remain largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrated that the conformational landscape of biohybrids can be systematically tuned by exploiting the intrinsic flexibility of a de novo α3 protein scaffold. We develop the unfolding-refolding method to synthesize a series of four new thermodynamically stable biohybrids. Based on this approach, we showed that single-point aromatic mutations modulate the conformational exchange of our biohybrids on the microsecond timescale. By combining spectroscopic, structural, and computational studies, we showed that the engineered conformational dynamics correlate with changes in chromophore triplet-state relaxation. While environmental factors, such as polarity or steric forces within the protein pocket, can contribute to photoresponse, the observed trends highlight conformational dynamics as a key parameter linking protein structure to excited-state behavior. These findings reveal an unexplored strategy for controlling biohybrid photoresponses through engineered conformational changes, thereby opening new avenues for designing biohybrids with tunable photophysical properties.

papers.title: Drop-in Silver Nanogap−Cellulose Concentrator for Surface-Enhanced Raman Monitoring of Water Contaminants
papers.abstract: Organic contaminants in natural waters threaten ecosystems and human health, motivating integrated strategies for trace-level monitoring. Although surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) offers molecular specificity and trace-level sensitivity, many platforms require separate preconcentration, provide limited control over analyte delivery to plasmonic hot spots, and lose performance in complex water matrices. Here, a poly(ether-block-amide) (PEBAX)-coated Ag nanogap–cellulose concentrator is reported, coupling self-driven interfacial enrichment with Raman readout through an amphiphilic, chemically heterogeneous, mixed-polarity interface. The engineered interface enabled charge-diverse partitioning of cationic and anionic molecular probes down to 10 -10 M across a broad pH range. Relative to the uncoated sensor, interfacial enrichment coupled to Ag nanogaps lowered SERS detection limits by up to 3,100-fold, reaching 1.1 × 10 -11 M for crystal violet and 2.3 × 10 -9 M for methyl orange. In untreated tap and lake water, the coated sensor resolved crystal violet and methyl orange fingerprints that were weak or variable on the uncoated sensor and identified acetamiprid and thymol within 30 min. These results show that coupling interfacial concentration with nanogap-mediated molecular readout establishes an integrated route for passive monitoring of trace contaminants in complex water matrices.

papers.title: Critical assessment of published Kalina cycle studies: cycle configuration, state-point reporting and optimisation bounds
papers.abstract: The Kalina cycle is widely proposed for converting geothermal, solar and waste heat, including in systems that also supply cooling, fresh water or hydrogen. It differs from an ammonia–water Rankine cycle in two respects established in its original formulation: a separator that produces a working solution richer in ammonia than the basic solution, and internal recuperation of turbineexhaust heat. Three operational criteria were derived from these features: non-zero mass flow in both separator outlets, a working-to-basic ammonia mass-fraction difference of at least 0.05, and non-zero recuperator duty. These criteria, a ten-item reporting checklist and a comparison of reported optima with the published search bounds were applied to 88 full-text journal articles, 84 of which designate a cycle as a Kalina cycle. In 17 of the 84 studies (20%; 95% CI 13–30%), at least one designated Kalina layout contained no recuperator or no separator. At the operating point of the principal results, all three criteria were demonstrably satisfied in 19 studies (23%), at least one was violated in 20 (24%), and 45 (54%) reported insufficient data for a decision. A complete state-point table was reported in 20 of the 88 studies. Of 40 optimisations performed with a named algorithm, 22 reported both bounds and optimal values; in 18 of these, at least one optimum coincided with or exceeded a bound, including all 14 single-objective cases. Agreement between an initial and a blinded repeat scoring was substantial (κ = 0.69–0.77). A verification procedure and a minimum reporting set are proposed.

papers.title: Designing Ideal Denoisers for Chromatographic and Spectroscopic Signals
papers.abstract: Modern instrumental analyses have different types of noise superimposed on the true signal, from low frequencies (baselines and colored noise) to very high-frequency components like sharp spikes. Convolution based denoisers or frequency domain filters inadequately handle colored noise and induce baseline oscillations while broadening narrow peaks. Herein, two new dataadaptive denoising methods are developed for chromatographic and spectroscopic data. The goal is to suppress noise without appreciably distorting peak shape or quantitative information (area, location, and variance). The proposed methods are posed as optimization problems inspired by the Bohlmann-Whittaker smoother. The objective function consists of a data fidelity term and adaptive second difference and bi-scale log-cosh penalties. The latter term suppresses pink or colored noise effectively, while adaptive functions protect narrow and weak peaks. The second method is designed for intensity-dependent additive and proportional noise and combines an inverse hyperbolic sine variance-stabilizing transformation with adaptive second-difference regularization. Non-uniform sampling rates are tolerated by this second smoother. In simulated chromatograms containing white and pink noise, the proposed adaptive method reduced the reconstruction error by approximately 40-50% relative to Gaussian weighted moving average and penalized least squares smoothing. The resolution of closely spaced peaks was maintained, and a weak peak with a weak peak with a signal-to-noise ratio near 5 was recovered. The proposed denoisers were evaluated on real data from GC-IMS, LC-MS/MS, Raman spectra relevant to planetary studies, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy of graphitic surface, and overloaded LC-MS instruments as test cases with and without baseline correction. Most denoiser parameters are derived from noise estimated from a single chromatogram or spectrum; no training or learning algorithms are required. The denoisers are fast and can be extended to 2D data.

papers.title: “Head-cut” 2DLC–HRMS (RPLC → HILIC) enhancing non-targeted chemical coverage in environmental exposomics.
papers.abstract: Chemical coverage remains a major limitation in environmental non-target analysis (NTA), as conventional one-dimensional liquid chromatography (1D-LC) provides incomplete retention and separation across the broad physicochemical space encountered in complex samples. Here, we developed an online “head-cut” two-dimensional liquid chromatography–high-resolution tandem mass spectrometry (2DLC–HRMS/MS) approach combining reversed-phase liquid chromatography (RPLC) and hydrophilic interaction liquid chromatography (HILIC), using a dual-trap system combining porous graphitic carbon and trimodal ion-exchange sorbents, to recover complementary regions of environmental chemical space within a single analysis. Trapping and modulation were first evaluated using a representative set of contaminants of emerging concern (CECs), evidencing that the combined complementary trapping materials achieves quantitative transfer (40-100%) of chemically diverse polar and mobile analytes to HILIC. Feature-based NTA performance of the optimized 2DLC method was comparatively evaluated in river water and effluent wastewater and compared with the corresponding 1D-HILIC and 1D-RPLC. “Head-cut” 2DLC yielded approximately 2.3–2.6-fold more blank-corrected ESI(+) and ESI(−) features than either individual 1D separation. Beyond feature level coverage, DIA componentization demonstrated that precursor-associated MS/MS information increased and successfully distributed across both 2DLC chromatographic domains. Fragment Ambiguity Score (FAS) analysis of ESI(+) data further confirmed the occurrence of low-ambiguity, structurally informative fragments within the expanded separation space. These results demonstrate that wide-interaction recovery of the RPLC blind spot can extend measurable chemical space and access to fragmentation information relevant for structural annotation, supporting “head-cut” RPLC→HILIC–HRMS/MS as a promising strategy for increasing chemical coverage in environmental NTA.

papers.title: Towards Environmentally Friendly Removal of Acrylate-Based Impregnation from Commercial Carbon Fiber Roving
papers.abstract: Carbon fibers face a growing use in industry due to their exceptional mechanical and light-weight properties. Particularly they are used as carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) in lightweight mobility, wind turbines and as concrete reinforcements to create light-weight and durable structural components. To fully enable their environmentally friendly use, full life cycles and end-of-life scenarios have to be developed. Therefore, energyand cost-effective carbon fiber retrieval from polymer impregnated commercial samples needs to be investigated. In this study, we investigate a commercially available CFRP roving with an industrial acrylate-based impregnation, commonly used in construction as concrete reinforcements. The impact of several chemical solvents was assessed identifying acetic acid as a highly effective and environmentally friendly agent. To further reduce the concentration of acetic acid, electrochemical dissolution was tested where the carbon fiber was used as a working electrode in an electrochemical cell. Applying a voltage as low as 1.5 V vs. Ag|AgCl, the acetic acid concentration required to dissolve the polymer could be reduced by 33% compared to pure chemical treatment, while the tensile strength of the carbon fiber was maintained.

papers.title: A Giant Fluoride-Bridged Rare-Earth Cluster with Moderate Hydrophobicity and Bright Luminescence Develops High-Resolution Latent Fingerprints
papers.abstract: Visualization of latent fingerprints (LFPs) at high resolution plays a vital role in crime scene investigation. The key to obtain high resolution image of LFPs is to design a developer that has strong contact with LFPs and bright luminescence. Since LFPs comprise both hydrophilic components (e.g., inorganic salts and water from sweat) and hydrophobic components (e.g., fatty acids and squalene from sebum) designing luminescent materials with appropriate hydrophobicity holds significant importance. Here we show that a family of fluoride-bridged rare-earth (RE) clusters with a common formula of [RE 26 (µ 3 -F) 40 (µ-F) 4 (µ 6 -F)(piv) 31 (H 2 O) 8 (cyclen) 2 (DCA) 2 ]·DMF (abbr. REFC-26, RE = Nd, Eu, Gd, Tb, Dy and Er) can achieve this goal. REFC-26 has not only the largest nuclearity among air-stable fluoride-bridged RE clusters known to date, but also both hydrophobic and hydrophilic functional groups on the surface. Coupled with the excellent luminescent properties of EuFC-26 and TbFC-26, these clusters effectively suppress background interference, yielding high-contrast and high-resolution fingerprint images. The resolution reaches a precise identification of level 1-3 features that range from macroscopic ridges to microscopic sweat pores even after the LFPs are aged for 30 days. Such a remarkable performance outperforms most LFP developers and may open a new photographic developer design based on luminescent RE clusters.

papers.title: Reviving Fused-ring Currents on Pentagonal Bipyramidal Cages
papers.abstract: The coexistence of 2D π-aromaticity and 3D σ-aromaticity within a single edge-fused molecule remains an open question, as the two aromatic subsystems are often assumed to be electronically incompatible. Here we fuse benzene, C 7 H 7 + and C 7 H 7 – onto the pentagonal-bipyramidal B 7 H 5 /C 2 B 5 H 5 fragment and systematically vary the fusion-edge composition (B–B, B–C, C–C), evaluating the 2D ring with GIMIC bond currents, NICS, ISE and EDDB. The 3D cage aromaticity remains essentially intact in aromatic cases, whereas the fate of the 2D ring depends strongly on the ring type and the fusion edge. Benzene fusion gives only weakly aromatic 2D rings, while C7H7 + fused through boron-rich edges develops a desymmetrized through-edge current path and sustains strong diatropic circuits up to 13.2 nA/T, restoring magnetic communication between the 2D ring and the 3D cage. Adding two electrons instead produces local paratropic circuits on the 2D rings via a HOMO-to-LUMO rotational transition. Throughout these systems the four descriptors diverge within both aromatic and antiaromatic series.

papers.title: Asymmetric Electrical Double Layer Charging in Ionomers under Pure Water
papers.abstract: Electrode interfaces with ionic polymers (ionomers) create local microenvironments in membrane electrolysis and other applications, yet the formation and dynamics of electrical double layers (EDLs) at ionomer|electrode interfaces are incompletely understood. Unlike traditional aqueous electrolytes with both mobile cations and anions, ionomer interfaces couple mobile counterion motion to the slower response of tethered polymer-backbone ionic groups. Studying these solid|ionomer interfaces, with pure water feed as in many technology applications, is more difficult than with conventional electrolytes due to the lack of a liquid supporting electrolyte for simple integration of counter and reference electrodes. Here, we use a membrane-electrode-assembly-inspired architecture with a lateral ionomer strip and a salt-bridged reference electrode to independently track anodic and cathodic potentials while sweeping the voltage between the two Pt-solid|ionomer interfaces in pure water. We quantify electrode-resolved non-faradaic charging and show that fixed polymer charges and mobile counterions contribute differently to interfacial capacitance. In anion-exchange ionomers, mobile Cl- responds rapidly, whereas fixed quaternary ammonium groups relax more slowly, producing a capacitance asymmetry. This asymmetry weakens when sufficient time is allowed for relaxation and is suppressed by supporting electrolyte. When Nafion cation-exchange ionomer is used instead, the results show a reversal in the sign of the asymmetry. Supporting molecular dynamics simulations establish coupled counterion motion and tethered-charge relaxation as governing features of pure-water ionomer EDLs. The work thus provides a framework for studying and ultimately designing ionomer microenvironments for membrane electrolysis and other applications. The Bigger Picture Pure-water-fed membrane electrolyzers rely on ionomers to carry charge to catalyst surfaces. Unlike soluble liquid electrolytes, ionomers contain mobile counterions and oppositely charged groups fixed to a polymer chain. The details of how these charges form electrical double layers under positive and negative polarization are not fully understood. We developed a model cell with a solid ionomer electrolyte that senses each electrode potential separately during cell operation.
