This transformation relies upon stoichiometric, low-cost Fe(acac)3 to interconvert an olefin into an alkyl radical via MHAT, which is then trapped by a sulfinylamine (e.g. TrNSO) to deliver S(IV) species, with exclusive Markovnikov selectivity. These sulfinamides serve as diversifiable lynchpins for readily accessing their aza-S(VI) congeners. Furthermore, we demonstrate this transformation’s practicality at preparative scale (>20-grams of product), enabling access to complex organosulfur modalities using inexpensive reagents and simple conditions.

papers.title: Coherent Recrossing Challenges Mechanistic Interpretations from Surface Hopping
papers.abstract: Surface hopping is widely used to assign mechanisms in ultrafast molecular photodynamics, yet the resulting mechanistic picture can become strongly method-dependent when electronic coherence survives across recurrent nonadiabatic interactions. We identify this regime, which can arise in dense excited-state manifolds, as coherent recrossing. Using semiclassical analysis of the prototypical Tully dual avoided-crossing model, we disentangle three controlling ingredients: phase accumulation between nonadiabatic events, electronic decoherence, and the relative phase information encoded in the nonadiabatic coupling. We then examine [3.3]paracyclophane, comparing surface hopping with ab initio multiple spawning (AIMS) using the same Hamiltonian, initial conditions, and coupling treatment. AIMS predicts prolonged multistate population sharing with state-selective electronic coherence, whereas the tested surface-hopping variants yield dynamics qualitatively distinct from AIMS. Landau–Zener surface hopping (LZSH) does not propagate electronic amplitudes and consequently cannot retain phase memory between successive nonadiabatic events, preventing it from describing interference that depends on such memory. Fewest-switches surface hopping (FSSH) and local-diabatization surface hopping (LDSH), with and without standard decoherence correction, reveal a fourth controlling ingredient that emerges in the multistate regime: the state-pair selectivity of the retained coherence. The tested FSSH and LDSH treatments retain coherence less selectively than AIMS and fail to reproduce its population dynamics, ranging from rapid S1 funneling to excessively broad population sharing. However, because FSSH and LDSH propagate electronic amplitudes and therefore retain phase information, their description of coherent recrossing can in principle be improved through more appropriate treatments of decoherence.

papers.title: Assigning the Low-Energy Excitons in Far-Red Photosystem II through Atomistic Modeling
papers.abstract: Far-red light photoacclimation of cyanobacteria extends the spectral range of oxygenic photosynthesis through the incorporation of chlorophylls (Chls) d and f into natural Photosystems, but the energetic organization of these pigments remains poorly understood. Here, we combine electronic-structure calculations with atomistic QM/MM and polarizable QM/MM approaches to determine the site energies, electronic couplings, and excitonic structure of the far-red PSII from Synechococcus sp. PCC 7335. In particular, we use benchmark calculations against spin-component-scaled CC2 to assess the accuracy of long-range corrected density functionals for describing the relative energetics of Chls a, d and f. Our calculations reveal that the energetic tuning of the far-red pigments is governed primarily by protein electrostatics, whereas structural distortions and environmental polarization make comparatively minor contributions. We found significant excitonic interactions within the subset of CP47 chlorophylls, while the reaction-center Chl d remains largely localized. The resulting excitonic Hamiltonian quantitatively reproduces both the far-red absorption spectrum and the sequence of exciton energies extracted from two-dimensional electronic spectroscopy, enabling a first-principles assignment of the low-energy excitons to specific Chl f and Chl d pigments. These results provide an atomistic picture of the far-red excitonic landscape and establish a quantitative basis for future simulations of excitation-energy transfer and charge separation in far-red photosystems.

papers.title: Testing for the presence of Endocrine Disrupting Chemicals in Locally Available Perfumes in Pakistan Through GC-MS Analysis and Implications for Public Health Policy
papers.abstract: Introduction Many conventional perfumes contain Endocrine Disrupting Chemicals (EDCs) like phthalates, synthetic musk, and parabens – often hidden under the ingredient label ‘fragrance’ or ‘parfum.’ Daily exposure to EDCs, through inhalation and skin contact, is very harmful, resulting in multiple health issues in infants, children, and adolescents undergoing critical developmental stages. In Pakistan, consumers remain considerably unaware, making this a serious problem. Perfumes are typically produced by unauthorised local manufacturers who do not follow standard protocols. Local brands are not bound by any explicit ingredient labelling laws. Currently, little to no research is done in this area. Methods In the months of March to April 2026, four local perfumes were arbitrarily purchased from the Pakistani consumer market in Lahore. The four perfumes were de-identified them and randomly coded them from 1 to 4. The perfumes were sent to the Industrial Analytical Centre in Karachi and analysed qualitatively and quantitatively using Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry for EDCs. Results Analysis showed that four perfumes contained Citral, three contained hydroxycitronellal, two contained Benzyl Salicylate, and two contained Benzyl Benzoate: all of which are established, potent EDCs and restricted according to the IFRA Standards (51st Amendment). 3 perfumes also had notes of synthetic musk, a strong EDC that is prohibited under the IFRA Standards. One perfume did not mention its ingredient list at the back, a practice that is detrimental to consumer awareness and should not be happening in the first place. Conclusion/Discussion These results, supporting the initial claim, raise a dire need for the government to monitor perfume products in the market. Strict public policy is required to target the lack of awareness by mandating that the packaging clearly indicates the levels of chemicals present. Any perfume containing excessive amounts of chemicals should be restricted for manufacturing and sale.

papers.title: PervoTransformer: Multi-Scale Transformer-Based Device Design and Atomistic Modeling of Perovskites
papers.abstract: Perovskite solar cell design involves a large and highly coupled space of material compositions, layer structures, and physical parameters, making systematic exploration of complete device architectures computationally challenging. This work introduces PervoTransformer, a transformer-based framework that represents complete device architectures as sequences and learns device-level behavior directly from this representation. A RoBERTa model is fine-tuned on SCAPS-generated device sequences spanning six perovskite families, including MAPbI3, FAPbI3, CsPbI3, and their Sn-based analogs. The model simultaneously predicts multiple performance metrics, including power conversion efficiency (PCE), short-circuit current density (Jsc), open-circuit voltage (Voc), and fill factor (FF), demonstrating the ability of transformer encoders to capture coupled, nonlinear dependencies across complete device stacks. To explore configurations beyond the training distribution, a GPT-2 model is fine-tuned using the same device-sequence representation to generate candidate architectures with new combinations of compositional and physical parameters. Generated configurations are screened for validity and uniqueness and subsequently evaluated using the fine-tuned RoBERTa model, enabling efficient exploration of under-sampled regions of the device design space. In parallel, machine-learned interatomic potentials based on the MACE framework are fine-tuned for CsSnX3 (X = Cl,Br, I) using available DFT data, enabling efficient structural relaxation and exploration of lead-free Sn-based perovskites. The resulting multiscale framework combines sequence-based transformer models for device-level design with machine-learned interatomic potentials for atomistic materials exploration, while retaining first-principles calculations for detailed physical validation. This approach provides a scalable strategy for navigating the coupled materials and device design spaces of perovskite solar cells while reducing reliance on computationally expensive simulations during initial exploration.

papers.title: BULK VERSUS SURFACE CHARGE RECOMBINATION KINETICS IN POLYMER HETEROJUNCTION NANOPARTICLE PHOTOCATALYST DISPERSIONS
papers.abstract: Organic donor-acceptor heterojunction nanoparticles have emerged as promising photocatalysts for solar hydrogen production, combining efficient light harvesting, donor-acceptor charge separation, and the generation of long-lived charge carriers. However, the identity of the charge populations responsible for photocatalytic turnover remains unresolved. Here, we study photogenerated polarons in aqueous oligo(ethylene glycol)-functionalized IDTBT:IDTBR-based heterojunction nanoparticles using transient absorption spectroscopy (TAS) and photoinduced absorption spectroscopy (PIAS) to probe, respectively, the transient polarons generated under pulsed excitation and long-lived polarons that accumulate under continuous illumination. By directly correlating spectroscopic signatures with photocatalytic hydrogen evolution, we show that the steady-state PIAS response tracks photocatalytic activity, establishing long-lived accumulated charges as the reactive population governing photocatalytic turnover. Excitation-fluence studies further demonstrate that the contrasting TAS and PIAS responses originate from distinct trapped-charge populations, with decay times at matched charge densities being five orders of magnitude faster for TAS compared to PIAS. We attribute the exceptionally long lifetimes measured in PIAS to the synergistic effects of donor-acceptor charge separation, progressive trap filling under continuous illumination, and dielectric stabilisation provided by the aqueous glycol-functionalized environment, which together suppress charge recombination and enable long-lived charge accumulation under operating conditions. These findings identify operando PIAS as a powerful approach for probing catalytically relevant charge populations and provide mechanistic design principles for engineering organic semiconductor photocatalysts with enhanced solar fuel performance.

papers.title: In-column Synthesis and Atomic-resolution Electron Microscopic Analysis of Metastable Reactive Nitrides
papers.abstract: Metastable and air-sensitive compounds are challenging to synthesize and characterize because their formation often requires harsh conditions and their structures can rapidly evolve upon exposure to the environment. Here, we demonstrate that a high-vacuum environment inside a transmission electron microscope (TEM) column can serve simultaneously as a reaction platform and an atomic-scale analytical tool for generating and interrogating such materials. Electron-beam irradiation on sodium azide (NaN3) produces crystalline sodium nitride (Na3N) at room temperature, despite the conventional decomposition of NaN3 into sodium and nitrogen. The formation of Na3N is supported by high-resolution TEM, electron diffraction, and energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, which reveal correlated structural and compositional changes through irradiation. The resulting Na3N subsequently undergoes oxidation through an amorphous intermediate to form polycrystalline Na2O. The high-vacuum environment sufficiently suppresses this reaction to resolve its otherwise unachievable microscopic mechanisms. Extending this approach to potassium azide (KN3), we observe a transient crystalline phase that is most consistently indexed as K3N, a nitride known to be thermally unstable even under room temperature. Its transient appearance and decay indicate a dynamic balance between electron-beam-induced formation and degradation. These results establish in-column electron-beam chemistry as a route to metastable nitride formation while enabling multimodal characterization of highly reactive products. More broadly, this strategy offers a means of exploring nonequilibrium metastable compounds that are difficult to access using conventional synthesis and characterization workflows.

papers.title: Playing Domino with Carbon: Electrochemical CO2 Reduction to Methanol with Cobalt Phthalocyanine
papers.abstract: Electrochemical reduction of carbon dioxide to methanol represents one of the most demanding transformations in CO 2 conversion, requiring the management of a six-electron, six-proton sequence while suppressing competing pathways toward carbon monoxide, formate, and hydrogen evolution. Among molecular electrocatalysts, cobalt phthalocyanine (CoPc) has emerged as a unique molecular platform capable of extending CO 2 reduction beyond CO through a domino-like cascade of protoncoupled electron transfer steps. Its square-planar Co-N 4 coordination environment provides metalcentered redox couples that enables CO 2 activation at the Co(I) state and stabilizes key intermediates within a narrow adsorption-energy window compatible with further hydrogenation. This review examines the fundamental and applied aspects of CoPc-mediated electrochemical CO 2 and CO reduction to methanol. The effects of ring substitution, axial ligation, and support-induced distortions on redox potentials, orbital interactions, and intermediate binding energetics were analyzed. Particular attention was devoted to solvation-coupled proton-coupled electron transfer, cation effects, and electric double-layer structure, which collectively governed CO retention and sequential hydrogenation toward CH 3 OH. Immobilization strategies on carbon nanotubes and related supports were discussed in relation to molecular dispersion, electronic coupling, and stability under flow-cell operation. Finally, scalability and sustainability are assessed through life-cycle considerations and green-chemistry metrics applied to phthalocyanine synthesis and device integration. Despite these advances, the field remains limited by catalyst deactivation, incomplete comparability among electrochemical setups and the frequent lack of standardized metrics for methanol quantification under device-relevant conditions. By connecting molecular design interfacial microenvironment, reactor architecture and sustainable catalyst synthesis, this review identifies the key directions required to move CoPc-based systems from promising molecular models toward technologically credible CO 2 -to-methanol electrolysis.

papers.title: Scientific World Models: Toward Closed-Loop Scientific Intelligence
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence is moving from task-specific scientific tools toward foundation models, generative design, research agents, and autonomous laboratories. Despite this progress, most systems remain organized around isolated predictions or local workflows. They rarely maintain an evolving account of scientific objects, predict the consequences of interventions, or learn systematically from computational and experimental evidence. This article introduces scientific world models as a core paradigm for closed-loop scientific intelligence. A scientific world model reconstructs the physical state of a scientific object and its corresponding epistemic state—what is known, uncertain, or contested—from partial, multimodal, and instrument-mediated observations. It models action-conditioned state transitions, explores plausible futures under scientific constraints, and supports the selection of measurements, simulations, experiments, and process interventions according to scientific value, information gain, cost, feasibility, and risk. The new evidence then updates the state, hypotheses, and subsequent actions. On this basis, we propose a three-layer architecture of scientific perception, cognition, and action. Perception turns the physical world into traceable scientific observations and state representations. Cognition combines data-driven models with scientific laws, mechanistic knowledge, and simulation to interpret current states and reason about possible futures. Action connects model reasoning to computation, instruments, experiments, and physical processes. We further distinguish the scientific world model core from foundation models, scientific agents, digital twins, and autonomous laboratories, and outline domain instantiations, maturity levels, evaluation criteria, and open technical challenges. This framework provides a common basis for developing scientific AI systems that can observe, reason, act, and improve through evidence.

papers.title: Comprehensive Quantum Chemical Interaction Analysis of Whole Protein–Ligand Structures in BindingDB Using the Fragment Molecular Orbital Method
papers.abstract: Understanding protein–ligand interactions based on their electronic states is important for elucidating molecular recognition and supporting structure-based drug discovery. In this study, we performed fragment molecular orbital (FMO) calculations, a quantum chemical approach, for a comprehensive set of experimentally determined protein–ligand complexes derived from BindingDB. Ligand–amino acid residue interactions were quantitatively characterized using inter-fragment interaction energies (IFIEs) and pair interaction energy decomposition analysis (PIEDA), and were compared with molecular mechanics (MM) interaction energies. The comparison revealed residue- and interaction-dependent differences between the FMO and MM descriptions, with particularly distinct behavior for interactions involving aromatic residues. Comprehensive IFIE/PIEDA analysis further revealed characteristic energetic contributions associated with amino acid residue type and ligand charge, including dispersion contributions involving aromatic residues and charge-transfer contributions associated with hydrogen-bonding interactions. A case study of MAPK14 demonstrated that the resulting dataset can identify residue regions commonly involved in ligand recognition and distinguish residue-level interaction patterns among individual ligands. These results provide a systematic quantum chemical perspective on diverse protein–ligand interactions and establish a quantum chemical resource for complementing structural, experimental, and conventional MM-based analyses.

papers.title: Direct Access to α-Chiral Amino-Oxetanes via Boron-Assisted Aziridine Ring-Opening
papers.abstract: α-Chiral amino-oxetanes represent a high-value yet synthetically difficult to access scaffold class in medicinal chemistry, combining the favorable pharmacokinetic properties of the oxetane ring with an additional degree of molecular complexity and three-dimensionality. Here we report the first synthetic route to α-chiral amino-oxetanes bearing boron and silicon substituents via a boron-assisted aziridine ring-opening strategy. Treatment of multichiral borylated and silylated oxetanyl-aziridines with simple carboxylic acids proceeds under mild, base-free conditions with full regio- and diastereoselectivity, affording densely functionalized products in excellent yields. The methodology accommodates over 30 structurally diverse carboxylic acids, including complex building blocks and Nprotected amino acids, and extends to azetidine analogs in a scalable protocol. Mechanistic investigations combining density functional theory computations and kinetic studies reveal a novel boron-assisted activation mode: reversible proton transfer from the carboxylic acid to the aziridine nitrogen generates a reactive aziridinium/carboxylate ion pair, which undergoes rate-determining SN2 attack facilitated by boron-oxygen coordination, lowering the activation barrier by more than 10 kcal·mol-1. This work expands the boron- and silicon-enriched chemical space accessible for drug discovery while simultaneously establishing a versatile platform for the synthesis of densely functionalized, stereochemically complex amino-oxetane scaffolds.

papers.title: Chemical Generalization Boundaries in Fire-Extinction Prediction from a Public Surfactant Formulation Database
papers.abstract: Machine-learning models of firefighting surfactants can appear persuasive when repeated measurements or closely related formulations occur on both sides of a random split. We reconstructed the public Hinnant surfactant workbook at cell-level provenance and evaluated fire extinction with explicit failure labels and a hierarchy of increasingly stringent chemical splits. The reconstructed data contain 917 heptane and 595 gasoline fire tests; heptane extinction comprised 733 successes, 179 documented failures, and 5 unlabeled observations, whereas gasoline comprised 554 successes and 41 failures. Structure-based analyses retained 114 formulations built from 50 single-structure and 22 polydisperse represented materials. For the fixed Extra Trees/combined representation, pooled heptane success ROC–AUC was 0.812 for row-random, 0.813 for replicate-disjoint, 0.805 for formulation-disjoint, and 0.783 for component-set-disjoint evaluation. At the prespecified 0.55 Tanimoto stress threshold, 114 formulations formed seven families of sizes 87, 11, 10, 3, 1, 1, and 1; only five families had labeled heptane observations. A fixed FireSuppressionFP/Extra Trees leave-one-family-out stress test gave pooled ROC–AUC 0.557. The three unique historical family partitions gave macro, size-weighted, and pooled ROC–AUC values of 0.694, 0.572, and 0.557, respectively; model-seed repeats were not counted as independent partitions. Extinction-time prediction remained limited: formulation-disjoint MAE was 38.9 s with pooled R2 0.306, while the family stress test yielded MAE 45.8 s and pooled R2 0.076; the partition-macro family R2 was -0.105. Thus, extinction success generalized across unseen formulations and component sets within represented chemistry, but coarse-family extrapolation was unstable and poorly constrained. Results are retrospective associations for 19 cm liquid-pool fires, not prospective validation or evidence of wildland-fire performance.

papers.title: Bridging Azahelicene Enables Circularly Polarized Luminescence in a Dinuclear Ytterbium(III) Single-Molecule Magnet
papers.abstract: Modern coordination chemistry employs increasingly sophisticated building blocks to design compounds and molecule-based materials with unusual combinations of properties relevant to emerging technologies. A notable example is the incorporation of helicenes as chiral ligands in luminescent and magnetic lanthanide complexes, which can give rise to circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) or magneto-chiral dichroism (MChD). Lanthanides are particularly wellsuited for CPL owing to their intraconfigurational 4 f -4 f transitions with long excited-state lifetimes and sharp, well-defined emission bands. Herein we present a new low-coordinate Yb III dinuclear complex [{Yb(BHT) 3 } 2 (azahelicene)] (BHT = 2,6-di-tert-butyl-4-methylphenolate; azahelicene = benzo[4,5]imidazo[1,2-a]benzo[4,5]imidazo[2,1-k][1,10]phenanthroline), where the two Yb III luminophores are bridged by the optically pure azahelicene ligand as the source of chirality. Additionally, the reported compound is a single-molecule magnet (SMM) thanks to the synthetic strategy that enables control of the coordination sphere around the Yb III ion. The combined experimental and theoretical magneto-optical studies conducted for both enantiomers of [{Yb(BHT) 3 } 2 (azahelicene)] reveal a direct link between the crystal structure, the related crystalfield splitting, and the observed magnetic and chiroptical properties. First of all, the introduction of the azahelicene into the coordination sphere of the achiral luminescent Yb(BHT) 3 parent compound was achieved with the retention of its SMM behavior. Most importantly, however, its incorporation as an integral component of the molecule enabled the observation of circularly polarized near-infrared (NIR) emission from Yb III . Three CPL bands were detected in the NIR, including the most intense signal at 978 nm with the luminescence dissymmetry factor glum = |0.035|, as well as a rare CPL emission above 1050 nm.

papers.title: Solid-state Electron Transfer Mechanism Study in Mechanochemistry through Time-Resolved Multimodal Monitoring
papers.abstract: Mechanochemical reactions can access unusual and useful reactivity, but the electron-transfer steps that govern many of these mechanochemical transformations have remained difficult for time-resolved monitoring. Here we establish a time-resolved strategy for resolving mechanochemical electron transfer by integrating in-situ powder X-ray diffraction with ex-situ quantitative electron paramagnetic resonance, solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance, and magnetometry. Using the formation of a sodium anion complex (sodide) as a model reaction, we show that a mechanically driven disproportionation proceeds through a stepwise pathway involving an electride intermediate. This finding provides direct mechanistic insight into how electrons move through reactive solids under mechanochemical condition. More broadly, it establishes a general experimental blueprint for identifying electronically distinct transient intermediates in mechanochemical redox chemistry.

papers.title: Finding the Right TEMPO: Multi-Objective Virtual Screening and Experimental Validation of TEMPO Derivatives for Aqueous Redox Flow Battery Catholytes
papers.abstract: We formulate the discovery of aqueous redox flow battery catholytes as a multi-objective optimization problem and introduce a virtual screening framework that simultaneously considers redox potential, chemical stability, and synthetic accessibility. Applied to a library of 182 TEMPO derivatives, the workflow identified a diverse set of high-ranking candidates, including the previously unexplored methyl carbamate-TEMPO (MC-TEMPO) and diethylamino-TEMPO (DEA-TEMPO). Furthermore, the screening revealed a moderate correlation between redox potential and predicted degradation resistance, indicating an intrinsic trade-off between these properties. For established TEMPO derivatives, the framework reproduced relative performance trends reported within independently studied series. Across the broader library, the highest-ranked candidates reflected a non-intuitive balance of electrochemical performance, stability, and synthetic accessibility rather than optimization of redox potential alone. MC-TEMPO and DEA-TEMPO were subsequently synthesized and experimentally characterized, providing a prospective test of the computational predictions. Cyclic voltammetry validated the redox potential predictions, with measured values closely matching the calculated values. During 130 h potentiostatic holds under sustained oxidizing conditions, MC-TEMPO showed no measurable electrochemical or molecular degradation, whereas DEA-TEMPO underwent a substituent-specific degradation pathway not captured by the initial screening model. Together, these results show that multi-objective catholyte discovery can prioritize molecules that would be overlooked by redox-potential optimization alone and provides a framework for the computationally guided design of organic redox flow battery catholytes.

papers.title: Perovskite Photovoltaics in 2025: The certified frontier held while verification stayed scarce
papers.abstract: This review assembles the complete 12-month publication record retrospectively, rather than through sequential monthly monitoring. The corpus holds 7931 publications meeting the topical scope criteria, of which 450 were examined in close detail across date-resolved monthly cohorts, alongside 1089 publications dated only to the calendar year. Within this literature, only 66 investigations reported an independently certified power conversion efficiency (PCE), which peaked at 33.15% for the year. Certified values moved from 30.26% in the first month recording a verified metric to 30.1% in the last, a net displacement of-0.16. Buried contact modification with carbazole self-assembled monolayers (SAMs), low-dimensional capping heterostructures, and additive-directed crystallization drove the performance records in both monolithic tandem and single-junction architectures. Mechanistic consensus breaks down over whether these surface modifiers permanently eliminate deep electronic traps or merely impose transient electrostatic potential shifts. Several groups attribute suppressed non-radiative recombination and stabilized open-circuit voltage (Voc) to chemical defect healing, while competing investigations demonstrate that asymmetric interfacial dipoles create electrostatic crosstalk, transport barriers, and unshielded internal fields that accelerate halide segregation. Carrying these interfacial treatments to scalable modules incurs a severe area penalty, with sharp efficiency deficits as aperture dimensions expand toward the maximum reported area of 764 cm2. In blade and slot-die deposition, the molecular attributes that minimize interface recombination in spin-coated cells directly impair meniscus translation, because hydrophobic self-assembled monolayer (SAM) terminal groups form precursor micellar aggregates that induce solvent dewetting, pinhole formation, and lateral nucleation gradients across wide substrates. Operational stability data remain deficient across the publication record. Merely 15 studies documented operational lifetimes, the longest reaching 3200 h, and only 24 articles followed standardized International Summit on Organic Photovoltaic Stability (ISOS) procedures. Most stability assessments evaluated unencapsulated storage in inert atmospheres, or omitted continuous maximum power point tracking (MPPT) under elevated operating temperatures, which leaves lifetime projections uncalibrated against operational degradation modes. Abstract-level reporting frequencies confirm the same verification gap: statements of independent certification occurred in just 5.8% of evaluated abstracts across the year, varying between 3.4% and 7.6% across monthly cohorts. Champion efficiency claims therefore rest predominantly on unverified, small-area laboratory cells that remain susceptible to spectral mismatch and calibration artifacts. Read across device architectures, the high open-circuit voltages obtained through contact engineering are frequently purchased with accelerated chemical and electronic degradation. Phosphonic acid anchor groups corrode reactive nickel oxide hole-transport layers under operating bias, and low-dimensional perovskite capping overlayers introduce anisotropic out-of-plane transport barriers that accumulate photogenerated carriers, lowering the kinetic activation barrier for electricfield-driven halide migration and phase demixing. In narrow-bandgap tin-lead absorbers, evidence settling whether stannous oxidation stems from autonomous chemical redox reactions or from downstream lattice microstrain remains thin, since chemical reducing agents delay degradation without resolving the underlying mechanical distortion. Establishing whether passivating molecules permanently eliminate deep recombination centers, or merely raise temporary barriers that disguise latent operational instabilities, requires synchronized operando spectroscopic and impedance measurements under simultaneous electrical bias and thermal stress.

papers.title: Molecular Dynamics Studies of Model Ionizable Lipids in an mRNA Vaccine
papers.abstract: Effective COVID-19 mRNA vaccines encapsulate nucleoside-modified messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA), which encodes the prefusion-stabilized SARS-CoV-2 spike protein, inside lipid nanoparticles. Endosomal acidification motivates the study of ionizable lipid protonation. Here, we isolate how protonation changes hydration, solvent preference, and structural organization of ALC-0315 in simplified model environments. Through molecular dynamics simulations, we identify clear protonation-dependent differences in lipid orientation, hydration, and collective organization across three model systems. At a water/hexane interface, the protonated amine headgroup shows a stronger preference for the aqueous phase, reflecting enhanced interactions with water molecules. In 20-lipid assemblies, the protonated assembly remains more hydrated and aqueous-associated over the simulated trajectory, whereas the neutral assembly migrates toward and spreads along the water/hexane interface. In pure ALC-0315 bilayer simulations, protonation strengthens amine hydration and alters bilayer-scale structural organization, with the observed morphology depending on the pressure-coupling protocol. Collectively, these findings demonstrate how protonation of ionizable amine headgroups can remodel ALC-0315 assemblies through strengthened lipid–water interactions. These simplified systems provide molecular-level insight into protonation-dependent ALC-0315 behavior, while not directly modeling the full multicomponent LNP, the endosomal membrane, or mRNA release.

papers.title: Argon Coordination to the 3d Transition-Metal Monohalides: A Systematic Study of σ-Acceptor Accessibility in Ar–MX (M = Sc–Cu; X = F, Cl, Br)
papers.abstract: Argon is generally regarded as chemically inert, yet direct Ar–metal coordination has been established for several late transition-metal complexes. Here, we systematically investigate Ar coordination across the 3d transition-metal monofluorides, MF (M = Sc–Cu), and subsequently extend the analysis to the corresponding chlorides and bromides. Density functional theory, population analysis, energy decomposition, and multireference calculations reveal a pronounced and nonmonotonic variation in Ar-binding propensity across the MF series. Ar binding is characterized by Ar 3pσ donation into a metal-centered σ-acceptor manifold of mixed 4s and 3dz2 character. In predominantly single-reference systems, the metal 4s population of bare MF provides a simple descriptor of the accessibility of this manifold: low 4s occupation is generally associated with Ar coordination, whereas high 4s occupation is associated with dissociation. Consistent with this picture, single-reference calculations give shortrange Ar-bound minima for MnF and FeF on lower-spin DFT surfaces with reduced 4s occupation, although these solutions are SCF-unstable and require multireference confirmation. The same metaldependent trend is largely retained for the chlorides and bromides, with additional modulation by the M–X framework. Sc halides mark the multireference limit of the simple 4s-based description.

papers.title: In situ Ni(II) to Ni(0) Reduction Enables Catalytic H2 Generation from Fe(II)-bearing Minerals
papers.abstract: Mechanistic insight into the catalysis of stimulated mineralogical hydrogen production may advance its realization as a scalable, emissions-free hydrogen source. Though enhanced H 2 generation from Ni(II)-catalyzed Fe(II) mineral oxidation has been posited to occur at Ni(II) sites co-precipitated on the Fe(II) mineral surface, operando insight into the active catalyst for H 2 production remains limited. Here, we combine potentiometry and time-resolved mass spectrometry to perform operando studies of exogenous Ni(II) speciation during hydrogen evolution from the coupled oxidation of the ferrous mineral Fe(OH) 2 to Fe 3 O 4 in anoxic water. By studying Fe(II) and Ni(II) systems in isolation, we first establish the thermodynamic competency of Fe(II) for reduction of Ni(II) to Ni(0) in circumneutral aqueous solutions; we then demonstrate that this occurs in situ. We further show that this conversion generates the active Ni(0) catalyst for H 2 evolution coupled to Fe(OH) 2 oxidation, despite the low reductive overpotentials generated by Fe(II). Over the course of the reaction, increasing solution potential due to increasing Fe(III) speciation re-corrodes Ni(0), rendering it undetectable in post-mortem product analysis. Data from Ni(II)-catalyzed hydrogen production from siderite (FeCO 3 ) suggests this in situ reduction of Ni(II) to Ni(0) may be a general mechanistic motif for H 2 generation across ferrous minerals. Insight into this in situ phenomenon is expected to contribute to the mechanistic picture of stimulated mineralogical hydrogen production and guide its optimization – with additional implications for the dynamic speciation of other exogenous metal catalysts for reduction reactions driven by Fe(II) oxidation.

papers.title: A Biomimetic Ion-Selective Transistor-Coupled Droplet Bilayer for Integrated Chemical Sensing, Synaptic Plasticity, and Associative Learning
papers.abstract: Integration of sensing, memory, and learning within a single device remains a major challenge for bioinspired electronic interfaces. Here, we report a transistor-coupled droplet bilayer (TCDB) in which selective ion transport across a biomimetic lipid membrane directly controls the electronic state of an organic electrochemical transistor (OECT). Incorporating valinomycin ionophores into the droplet interface bilayer membrane enables the selective transport of K + ions while suppressing the response to other cations. Increased concentration of valinomycin in the membrane decreases the resistance of the membrane to K + ions, producing correspondingly faster and stronger transistor gating responses. Using this membrane-mediated gating mechanism, the TCDB distinguishes K + concentrations from 3.5-20 mM through concentration-dependent response kinetics. Beyond sensing, the finite ion transport and relaxation times impart history dependence to the transistor's response, producing a ~330 mV hysteresis window, reversible analog conductance programming, paired-pulse facilitation, post-tetanic potentiation, and spike-rate- and timing-dependent plasticity. Repeated stimulation further extends the lifetime of programmed conductance states, directly linking selective ion transport dynamics to short-term memory. We further demonstrate, for the first time in a TCDB, a dual-gate architecture comprising two independently addressable lipid bilayers coupled to a shared OECT channel. The dual-gate TCDB integrates multiple ionic inputs within a common channel and enables associative learning through the temporal pairing of independent gate stimuli. Together, these results establish membrane resistance, selective ion transport, and ionic relaxation as physical parameters that simultaneously govern chemical sensing, memory, and synaptic adaptation, providing a biomimetic route toward ion-selective neuromorphic devices in which sensing and information processing arise from the same membrane-mediated ionic dynamics.

papers.title: A Flexible Framework for Course-Based Undergraduate Research Experiences
papers.abstract: Course-based undergraduate research experiences (CUREs) broaden access to the high-impact practice of undergraduate research. Unfortunately, many faculty lack a clear roadmap for developing a CURE. To address this barrier, we present a series of modular activities, the CURE "Flexi-Framework", which guides faculty through the process of creating a CURE based on their own research. Within the framework, students progress through four phases of scientific research: (I) Obtaining, Evaluating, and Organizing Information; (II) Asking Questions and Planning Investigations; (III) Investigation, Data Analysis, and Iteration; and (IV) Justification and Communication through a written report and/or oral presentation. Each phase consists of assessable, workshop-style activities that can be adapted to different research topics while maintaining the CURE-defining elements of collaboration, discovery and relevance, and iteration. Over the past decade, the Flexi-Framework has been used to implement multiple upper-division CUREs across three institutions and several subdisciplines of chemistry. Assessment using the Classroom Undergraduate Research Experience Survey and the Laboratory Course Assessment Survey demonstrates student-reported gains and course design elements consistent with national CURE benchmarks. The CURE Flexi-Framework thus provides a validated, adaptable pathway for integrating research into coursework, lowering the barrier to adopting CUREs across institutional and disciplinary contexts.

papers.title: In silico evaluation of novel isosteres against PTPN1 and estrogen receptor alpha: molecular docking, ADMET profiling, and quantum chemical analysis
papers.abstract: A series of novel cyclic alkene template (CAT) isosteres (CAT-0 to CAT-7) were designed and evaluated through an integrated in silico workflow combining molecular docking, density functional theory (DFT) based electronic structure analysis, ADMET prediction, CYP450 profiling, and preliminary synthetic feasibility assessment. Two biologically relevant protein targets, protein tyrosine phosphatase 1B (PTPN1) and estrogen receptor alpha (ERα/ESR1), were investigated to explore the potential biological activity profiles of the designed compounds. Docking studies were performed using the 2HNP and 3ERT crystal structures for PTPN1 and ERα, respectively. Validation of the docking protocols through reproduction of the corresponding co-crystallized ligand poses yielded RMSD values below 2 Å, supporting the reliability of the docking procedures. CAT-3, CAT-4, and CAT-7 were identified as the most promising candidates based on their predicted binding affinities across the two targets. Electronic structure analysis suggested that variations in electrostatic potential distribution and frontier orbital characteristics may contribute to differences in binding behavior within the series, supporting the isosteric design strategy. ADMET and toxicity predictions indicated generally favorable drug-like properties, with most compounds exhibiting acceptable gastrointestinal absorption and low predicted CYP450 inhibitory activity, suggesting a limited risk of CYP-mediated drug–drug interactions. However, variability in blood–brain barrier permeability and model-dependent toxicity endpoints highlights the inherent uncertainty of in silico ADMET predictions and warrants cautious interpretation of absolute values. Among the designed compounds, CAT-3 emerged as the most balanced lead candidate, combining favorable docking performance, acceptable predicted pharmacokinetic properties, and improved synthetic accessibility relative to CAT-4 and CAT-7, which, despite strong predicted affinities, present greater synthetic constraints. Its structural relationship to trodusquemine further supports its relevance as a promising scaffold. Overall, CAT-3 represents the most favorable compromise between predicted biological activity and practical feasibility within the series. Nevertheless, given the limitations of empirical scoring functions, rigid receptor approximations, and predictive ADMET models, these findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating. Further validation through molecular dynamics simulations, MM-GBSA free energy calculations, and experimental assays will be required to confirm the predicted biological relevance of the CAT series.

papers.title: Determination of Asbestos Fibre Release Potential from Contaminated Craft Sand and Sand-Based Toys
papers.abstract: Over the last century, human exposure pathways for asbestos have changed from those associated with direct interaction with the minerals (e.g. mining) to secondary exposure from a variety of asbestoscontaining materials, including those linked to para-occupational, domestic and environmental pathways. In 2025, the discovery of asbestos in children’s toy sand products caused panic, stress and fear amongst the community. Although there is no safe level of asbestos exposure, these products were deemed to be low risk by some due to uncertainty around whether fibres could become airborne during play. In this experimental study, contaminated sand samples were “played with” inside a Class A asbestos enclosure by an asbestos technician wearing protective equipment. Air samples collected were analysed using a combination of light and electron microscopy undertaken by two independent laboratories. 90% of tested craft sands released asbestos fibres into the air during play activities. Some fibres met the criteria for respirability. Air samples taken during experiments using moulding sand samples did not show any airborne asbestos fibres; however, analytical detection limits for this study were high. This demonstrates that the potential risk from asbestos in the product can create a real risk from fibres in the air; however, the magnitude of this risk has yet to be determined by further research. Nevertheless, no amount of risk of asbestos exposure through toys is acceptable so the most practical way to eliminate this risk would be to avoid the use of artificial sand products in toys or similar consumer products.

papers.title: Polyanion-Based Compounds for Rechargeable Magnesium Batteries
papers.abstract: Rechargeable magnesium metal batteries represent a compelling post-lithium energy storage technology owing to the abundance of terrestrial magnesium reserves, their current cost-effectiveness and intrinsically higher safety relative to lithium systems, coupled with their capacity to deliver high volumetric energy density. However, this promise and beyond remains constrained by the stringent requirement that rapid and reversible Mg 2+ transport can be achieved in concert with electrochemical and thermodynamic stability across both electrodes and electrolytes. Within this context, polyanion compounds, such as phosphates, silicates, and borates, have emerged as a pedagogically rich and technologically versatile class of materials. Polyanion-based compounds offer high redox voltages, exceptional thermal and chemical robustness, and a plethora of crystallographic chemistries that permit rational tuning of Mg 2+ migration pathways. This Review surveys polyanion-based positive electrodes and solid electrolytes for rechargeable magnesium batteries, with emphasis on computational prediction, mechanistic elucidation, synthetic methodology, advanced structural and spectroscopic characterisation, and the prospects for all- solid-state magnesium batteries capable of operating under high‑temperature conditions.

papers.title: Screening Protein Conformational Responses by Molecular Friction Sensing
papers.abstract: Small-molecule drugs often act by stabilizing specific protein conformations, yet most biophysical screening platforms report binding affinity or kinetics without directly capturing structural response. Here we introduce molecular friction sensing (MFS), a screening-compatible approach that detects ligand-induced changes in protein conformation through changes in hydrodynamic drag exerted on electrically switchable DNA origami nanolevers. Across a diverse protein panel and under physiological conditions, the method quantitatively reports protein size and resolves ligand-dependent conformational shifts with sub-Angström sensitivity. In maltodextrin-binding protein, cognate and non-cognate maltodextrins produced distinct friction signatures that mirrored their biological roles. In a carbonic anhydrase screen, molecular friction sensing identified compound-dependent conformational responses among SPR-validated binders, revealing that affinity and kinetics do not predict structural outcome. Molecular friction sensing therefore adds a structural dimension to interaction analysis and provides a route to prioritize drug candidates by the conformations they induce.

papers.title: Internal conversion in functionalized poly-chlorinated trityl radicals can be tuned by a characteristic high-frequency mode
papers.abstract: We provide a theoretical analysis of trends in radiative losses by internal conversion (IC) in a series of doublet radical emitters and triplet diradicals derived from the poly-chlorinated trityl moiety. Minimizing radiative losses in these systems by molecular design is of current interest to opto-electronics and quantum technological approaches. Our results clearly indicate that IC in the doublet emitters as well as in different diradical architectures is governed by a characteristic high-frequency mode, which is associated with a quinoidal distortion. For the doublet emitters, we can establish that deliberate design allows to deactivate this mode as decay channel, resulting in a significantly reduced IC rate and an improved internal fluorescence quantum yield. We propose an analogous design principle for highly fluorescent triplet diradicals, and discuss the role of a high fluorescence efficiency in the context of quantum applications.

papers.title: Time-Resolved Raman Spectroscopy of Nitrate Electroreduction Reveals Dynamic Interfacial Adsorbate Evolution
papers.abstract: Nitrate electroreduction offers a pathway for coupling wastewater remediation with sustainable ammonia production, yet its mechanistic details under operating conditions remain poorly understood. In this work, we directly resolve the dynamic evolution of nitrate-derived intermediates at electrified interfaces, addressing a key limitation in understanding dynamic reaction pathways. We employ time-resolved surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (TR-SERS) to monitor the interfacial behavior of NO 3 – and NO 2 – during nitrate reduction on roughened silver electrodes and observe potential-dependent vibrational shifts attributed to systematic changes in adsorption modes under increasingly cathodic potentials. Density functional theory calculations further support the vibrational assignments and provide insight into preferred binding motifs across the applied potential range. By tracking the time evolution of adsorbates, this approach provides insights into the sequence of adsorption and transformation steps on silver. The combined experimental and computational analysis contributes to a molecular-level understanding of nitrate electroreduction and provides a framework for probing dynamic reaction intermediates in nitrogen conversion electrocatalysis.

papers.title: StateFlux: DFT-Validated Quantum Reactivity across Predicted Metabolic State Networks Shows Limited Incremental Value for Broad Toxicity Prediction
papers.abstract: Mechanistic molecular representations are increasingly used to supplement parent structure with protonation, metabolism, and quantum-chemical reactivity, but added physical detail does not necessarily provide predictive information beyond structure. StateFlux represents each drug as a network of chemical and predicted metabolic states with node-level GFN2-xTB properties and edge-resolved changes in ionization potential, electron affinity, electrophilicity, solvation, and local reactivity. On a locked DILIrank 2.0 development set (n = 376; 156 positive and 220 negative), 10 × 5 scaffold-grouped validation gave AUROC/AUPRC values of 0.8249/0.7727 for ECFP, 0.8049/0.7430 for ECFP + FluxCore, and 0.8010/0.7261 for ECFP + StateFluxCore. Strict temporal and scaffold-novel tests showed no consistent gain, and an independent 5,367-compound genotoxicity transfer benchmark reproduced the pattern (AUROC 0.7765 for ECFP versus 0.7732 for StateFluxCore). To separate limited predictive utility from inaccurate low-cost quantum chemistry, 24 parent-to-metabolite transformations were evaluated with 144 ωB97X-D/6-31+G*/SMD single-point calculations. GFN2-xTB closely tracked DFT changes in electrophilicity (Pearson r = 0.963; MAE = 0.408 eV; 79.2% sign agreement). Thus, transformation-induced quantum reactivity can be consistent with higher-level DFT without providing reliable incremental information for broad toxicity classification. Quantum-chemical fidelity and predictive utility should therefore be evaluated as separate claims in chemical machine learning.

papers.title: Vapor Pressure of Octafluorocyclobutane (RC-318) from 234 K to 387 K Measured with a Variable-Volume View Cell
papers.abstract: Saturated vapor pressures of octafluorocyclobutane (c-C4F8, RC-318) were measured at 32 temperatures from 234.33 K to 387.01 K, corresponding to pressures from 20.62 kPa to 2.698 MPa. Measurements were performed in a variable-volume cell with sapphire windows, enabling direct observation of the vapor–liquid meniscus and visual confirmation of the two-phase state at each point. The highest measurement was obtained 1.36 K below the reported critical temperature (Tc = 388.37 K). Temperature was measured with a platinum resistance thermometer traceable to the ITS-90, and pressure was measured with a calibrated transducer. The combined expanded uncertainty in the saturation pressure, U(ps) (k = 2), was estimated to be 0.2–0.6% over the measured range. The data were correlated with a four-term Wagner equation constrained to the critical parameters of Douslin et al.,[3] giving an average absolute relative deviation (AARD) of 0.23%, a root-mean-square relative deviation of 0.34%, and a maximum absolute relative deviation of 0.82%. The measurements agree with the reference equation of state of Platzer et al.[28] with an AARD of 0.27%. Combined with saturated-phase molar volumes from the reference equation of state, the correlation gives an enthalpy of vaporization that decreases from about 25.4 kJ·mol−1 at 234 K, through 23.3 kJ·mol−1 at the normal boiling point, and approaches zero at the critical point. These measurements provide a modern, internally consistent vapor-pressure data set for a high-GWP fluorinated gas that is widely used in semiconductor processing and has also been investigated for dielectric applications.

papers.title: Tafel curvature analysis in electrocatalysis: theoretical foundations and microkinetic simulations
papers.abstract: A curved Tafel plot records how an electrocatalytic interface changes its response to potential. Its shape contains the signatures of adsorption, interactions between adsorbates and redistribution of reaction flux, yet these signatures are often compressed into a few fitted slopes. Here we develop Tafel curvature analysis as a quantitative framework for interpreting these transitions. Analytical adsorption theory and reversible microkinetic simulations connect the second derivative of logarithmic current to surface-response identities and experimentally testable features. For a turnover law with a constant explicit potential sensitivity, curvature eliminates both the current prefactor and the linear activation term. Ideal Langmuir adsorption then gives a direct susceptibility relation, a fixed amplitude–width relation and a signed-area sum rule. Competitive adsorption extends this result to a weighted squared response of the entire population vector. Lateral interactions reshape this response and produce a precisely located splitting transition: in the pair-dependent Frumkin model, two curvature peaks emerge above a repulsion parameter of 4/3 even though the surface has a single adsorbate population. Parallel currents generate a complementary positive contribution equal to the variance of their local slopes. These relationships organize the behavior of three catalytic networks. Hydrogen oxidation separates population response from pathway redistribution. CO oxidation predicts an activity-dependent curvature-peak displacement and exposes the kinetic influence of a sparsely occupied intermediate through its product-exit probability. For a four-state oxygen-reduction cycle, an exact decomposition links curvature to reversible driving, population motion and dispersion among elementary-rate products; a shared potential factor explains the zero-curvature limit. Together, the models show how curvature sign, area, width and peak motion characterize kinetic transitions and guide the choice of concentration and spectroscopic measurements. A synthetic measurement study further demonstrates recovery of single and split curvature features from discrete noisy currents by local polynomial regression, with propagated uncertainty and an explicit resolution–noise tradeoff. Tafel curvature thus turns variation in kinetic sensitivity into a set of quantitative physical relationships and practical tests of electrocatalytic surface dynamics.

papers.title: In situ monitoring of solvent dependent CsPbBr3 nanorod growth from lead halide precursors
papers.abstract: CsPbBr 3 nanocrystals are promising semiconductors for numerous optoelectronic applications due to their high quantum yield and impressive tunability. Most recently, one-dimensional perovskite nanorods and nanowires have attracted attention for their advanced luminescence properties such as light polarization and lasing. Such applications require precise morphological and surface chemistry control, both of which are difficult to obtain using conventional synthesis pathways. A novel approach is to use preformed lead halide clusters as nucleation sites, decoupling nucleation and growth to lower dispersity. In this work, we utilize preformed PbBr 2 clusters in 1-octadecene as precursors for anisotropic growth of CsPbBr 3 nanorods. Using in situ UV-Vis absorbance and photoluminescence spectroscopies, we monitored the different morphologies and phases formed during the growth of CsPbBr 3 . We investigate the impact of the solvent on precursor chemistry, final nanorod structure, as well as the growth pathway to reach those structures. Our results show that for growth occurring in toluene, the lead halide precursors are isolated octahedra favoring a classical diffusion mechanism and nanorods with less defined width. When the reaction occurs in 1-octadecene, the precursors form preassembled monolayers, promoting oriented assembly and giving rise to distinct, coexisting, two and three monolayer thick nanorods. Sequential crystallization of Cs 4 PbBr 6 was observed in toluene because of the increasing ligand concentration during nanorod growth. Cs 4 PbBr 6 crystals could then be converted into two monolayer thick nanorods through the addition of a small volume of ethanol. These results shed light on the importance of solvent choice on lead precursor chemistry to obtain homogeneous size-controlled nanorods.

papers.title: Parahydrogen-induced 15N polarization of nitrate ion
papers.abstract: Parahydrogen-induced polarization (PHIP) represents a cost-effective hyperpolarization technique providing dramatic increase of the NMR spectroscopy sensitivity. In particular, hyperpolarized metabolites are employed in various in vivo applications, including cancer diagnostics and grading. In this proof-of-concept study, we present an extension of the PHIP methodology to a key nitrogenous metabolite, the nitrate anion. We report an approach for the production of hyperpolarized nitrate solutions utilizing PHIP by means of the side-arm hydrogenation of propargyl nitrate ester. Through the sequential optimization of hydrogenation, polarization transfer, and hydrolysis procedures, we obtained hyperpolarized nitrate anion with 15 N polarization levels estimated as >2%.

papers.title: Charge-Encoded Anion Sublattices Drive Ordering and Phase Selection in Layered Chalcogenides
papers.abstract: Predicting the sites where anions order in a crystal, and when that ordering drives structural rearrangement, remains a challenge in mixed-anion chemistry. Here we show that both are linked to the distribution of charge on the anion sublattice of ACuMIVQ3 chalcogenides. Bader analysis of four competing polymorphs reveals that the sequencing of polyhedra controls the range of charge across anion sites (Δq) and programs each structure with a distinct charge-encoded anion sublattice. Thirteen new mixedchalcogen compounds were prepared, and the anion site occupancies were determined through single crystal X-ray diffraction. While sulfoselenides tend to adopt structures with small Δq, where they form near-ideal solid solutions, greater anion disparity in the selenotellurides and sulfotellurides leads to enhanced ordering, which drives formation of alternate structures with higher Δq. These structures provide terraced charge landscapes with more strongly differentiated sites, suggesting that structure selection depends on how well the anion sublattice matches the chemical disparity of the anion mixture. This trend culminates in KCuZrTeSeS, where S, Se, and Te order across three distinct sites in the Pnma structure, a phase not adopted by any single-anion end member, and the first demonstration of site-selective ordering of all three chalcogens in a single material. An enrichment factor connecting site occupancy with Bader charge further shows that the most electronegative chalcogen in a given mixture preferentially occupies the highest-charge site. Together, the results establish charge-encoded anion sublattices as a framework for predicting anion ordering and phase selection in extended solids.

papers.title: Photochemical CO Evolution in a Quinone-Based Electrochemical CO2 Capture System
papers.abstract: Quinone-based electrochemical CO2 capture in aprotic organic solvents relies on the redox-controlled formation of quinone–CO2 adducts. Understanding how these bound species respond to light is essential for identifying competing reaction pathways that may alter carrier stability and the chemical outcome of capture. Here, we investigate the photochemical behavior of electrochemically reduced 9,10-phenanthrenequinone (PAQ) in DMSO under CO2 and N2 using visible-light irradiation (440 nm). Electrochemical and spectroscopic measurements reveal light-responsive behavior of the reduced-PAQ/CO2 system. CO evolution is observed during irradiation under CO2, with earlier quantifiable detection and greater accumulation than under N2. Water addition strongly suppresses CO evolution, suggesting that water-induced changes in reduced-PAQ speciation affect the CO-forming pathway. Together, these observations suggest that reduced-PAQ speciation influences CO formation, with light-induced transformation of PAQ–CO2-bound species as a plausible contributing pathway. These findings highlight photochemical stability and waterdependent speciation as important considerations in the design of quinone-based CO2-capture systems.

papers.title: Nitrogen basicity dictates Fe-N-C-catalyzed aerobic oxidation activity
papers.abstract: Iron-metalated nitrogen-doped carbon (Fe-N-C) materials rival platinum-based electrocatalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) in fuel cells, and O2 reduction is proposed to occur at atomically dispersed Fe atoms coordinated by nitrogen within the graphitic material (FeNx). In recent years, similar catalysts have been shown to be effective for aerobic oxidation of organic substrates, often under non-aqueous conditions that are very different from electrocatalytic ORR conditions. Such reactions have been the focus of limited mechanistic attention, and little is known about the active sites and/or catalyst features that contribute to improved activity. Here, we investigate Fe-NC-catalyzed aerobic oxidation of hydroquinone to benzoquinone and two other organic reactions. The FeNx site density is found to have little influence over catalytic activity. Instead, we find that the basicity of nitrogen atoms in the Fe-N-C surface is the dominant feature that correlates with catalytic activity, with diagnostic insights gained from binding isotherm measurements with pivalic acid. Fe-N-C catalytic activity is shown to correlate directly with the pivalic acid binding constant (Kads) across a series of different catalysts. These insights provide a valuable foundation for future development and optimization of improved aerobic oxidation catalysts.

papers.title: Restored operation lifetime of Au@ZnO NW gas sensors for H₂S detection due to reversible sulfurization with NO₂ and O₃
papers.abstract: The nanomaterial system of gold functionalized zinc oxide nanowires (Au@ZnO NWs) shows extraordinary sensing ability towards trace amounts of hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S), meeting the requirements for early medical diagnostics via exhaled human breath. An interplay of morphological and chemical sensitization of ZnO NWs with Au nanoparticles (Au NPs) enables the selective detection of H 2 S concentrations at the ppt (parts-per-trillion) concentration level at room temperature. Exceptional sensitivity and selectivity are achieved through dissociative chemisorption of H 2 S on both the Au NP surface, and the ZnO NW [10-10] side-factette. Unfortunately, this interaction leads to the sulfurization of the sensor, deteriorates the gas sensitive surface of the nanomaterial system and significantly shortens the lifetime of Au@ZnO NW gas sensors. In this work, we investigate and successfully demonstrate a complete reversal of the sensor’s deterioration, which is achieved by flushing the affected nanomaterial with potent oxidants, namely NO 2 and ozone (O 3 ). Gas sensing performance is assessed in current-over-time measurement ( I - t ) of Au@ZnO chemically sensitive field effect transistors (ChemFETs). Here, functionalized nanowires form the gas-sensitive open gate. We present the initial deterioration of sensors caused by sulfur poisoning of the nanomaterial system, followed by a recovery treatment with either NO 2 , or O 3 . We systematically compare the morphological and chemical effects of each treatment and evaluate the viability of each method by using SEM micrographs, energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) data and detailed X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analysis. Results indicate that the NO 2 treatment can lead to a complete decomposition of the gassensitive open gate upon prolonged exposure. In contrast, O 3 found to provide a damage-free treatment that completely restores the sensors' sensing properties after less than 30 min of continuous exposure. ( I - t )-measurements verify a sufficient recovery of the initial sensor sensitivity and signal properties after O 3 treatment, which directly extends the operational lifetime of an Au@ZnO NW gas sensors for H 2 S detection.

papers.title: Glucose Dehydrogenase Engineered for the Noncanonical Coenzyme NMN Outperforms Its Natural NAD-Dependent Activity
papers.abstract: Engineering redox enzymes to utilize noncanonical coenzymes is critical for advancing in vitro enzymatic biocatalysis and in vivo bioorthogonal chemistry. However, engineered NAD(P)-dependent dehydrogenases had universally underperformed on small noncanonical coenzymes compared to their wild-type (WT) counterparts on natural NAD(P). Here we developed an Iterative (one-site) Mutagenesis and Evolutionary Strategy (IMES) to evolve a flavin-free, NAD-dependent glucose dehydrogenase (GDH) on nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN + ). By integrating rational design, directed evolution, and a novel high-throughput screening method, we obtained the variant M3 (E44H/P191T/V187M). For the first time, an engineered dehydrogenase achieved catalytic efficiencies with NMN + that surpassed those of the WT enzyme with its natural coenzyme NAD + . Specifically, variant M3 exhibited a 3.2-fold higher specific activity and a 2.06-fold greater catalytic efficiency ( k cat / K m ) with NMN + than the WT GDH with NAD + . Furthermore, we established functional NMN-recycling cascades by coupling the NMNH-generating M3 variant with four NMNH-consuming redox enzymes, including flavin-free alcohol dehydrogenase and mannitol dehydrogenase, as well as two flavin-dependent enzymes (i.e., an oxidase and a transhydrogenase). This study establishes an NMN-based cascade redox system applicable to both in vitro biocatalysis and in vivo bioorthogonal chemistry. Replacing NAD with the smaller, lower-cost NMN coenzyme greatly reduced the economic burden of cofactor supply, paving the way for more efficient and cost-effective enzymatic biocatalysis.

papers.title: Heterogeneous Catalysts as Electrochemical Cells: Completing the Circuit using Proton Buffers in Nonaqueous Media
papers.abstract: Thermochemical redox reactions with heterogeneous catalysts often proceed by an "electrochemical" mechanism that features coupled redox half-reactions. Studies supporting this mechanism have typically been performed with water as the solvent; however, many organic oxidation reactions feature non-aqueous solvent. Here, we analyze the aerobic oxidation of hydroquinone with iron-containing nitrogen-doped carbon (Fe-N-C) catalysts in acetonitrile. Addition of proton buffers significantly accelerates the reaction, and mechanistic data indicate the buffers support proton transfer between the two redox half-reactions, proton-coupled oxidation of the hydroquinone and O2 reduction, which take place at different active sites on the catalyst surface. Kinetic studies of the thermochemical aerobic oxidation reaction are complemented by electrochemical studies, including linear-sweep voltametric analysis of both independent half-reactions. Collectively, the data provide a selfconsistent mechanistic picture that highlights the importance of proton management in supporting thermal heterogeneous catalytic redox reactions in non-aqueous solvent.

papers.title: Zwitterion Doping to an Organic Ionic Plastic Crystal Electrolyte: A Strategy to Improve Ionic Conductivity without Compromising Melting Point
papers.abstract: Li+-containing organic ionic plastic crystals (OIPCs) show great promise as solid electrolytes for solid-state batteries. However, their ongoing issue is a decrease in the melting point with an increase in the Li+ concentration, requiring a new strategy to improve ion-transport properties without compromising the operating temperature range of the electrolytes as a solid. Herein, we address this by incorporating a small portion of zwitterions into an OIPC matrix, N,Ndiethylpyrrolidinium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide ([C2epyr][FSI]). The effect of zwitterion incorporation on physicochemical properties depends on the type of zwitterion. If its structure is similar to the host OIPC, it improves ionic conductivity without narrowing down the temperature range as a plastic crystal, which is supported by minimal destruction to the host crystalline lattice without obvious formation of new crystalline phases. The cycle test of solid-state Li | LiFePO4−[C2epyr][FSI] cells with various concentrations of the pyrrolidinium-based zwitterion in the cathode layer showed the most stable discharge capacity of 150 mAh/g at 0.1C, 50 °C for the cell with 8.70 mol% of the zwitterion, without any sign of capacity decay. Impedance analysis unveiled the positive effect of the zwitterion addition at this concentration regime, which stabilizes cathode-electrolyte interphase and charge transfer at the LFP interface.

papers.title: Harnessing Machine Learning and Composite Quantum Chemical Methods for Computing Accurate Bond Dissociation Energies of PFAS
authors: Sharma S. R. K. C. Yamijala
papers.abstract: Designing efficient degradation pathways for per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) requires access to accurate bond dissociation energies (BDEs). Composite quantum chemical methods such as G4 provide high accuracy (<1 kcal mol–1) but are limited to small molecules. Density functional theory (DFT) can handle larger systems, but its results vary significantly with the choice of functional and basis set, raising concerns about reliability. Fragment-based methods like the connectivity-based hierarchy (CBH) and its modified form (mCBH) offer G4-level accuracy at DFT cost, but only when using large fragments. Since obtaining G4 energies for large fragments is computationally demanding, these methods are not practical for building large BDE databases. To address this limitation, we introduce a machine learning (ML)-enhanced CBH approach. Here, a regression model is trained on G4-calculated energies of small fragments and is used to predict PFAS BDEs. This strategy achieves near-G4 accuracy without requiring G4 calculations on large fragments. Across diverse PFAS with varying chain lengths and functional groups, our ML-augmented fragmentation-based methods either match or outperform the accuracy of both the mCBH-3 and CBH-3 approaches (both of which require larger fragments), demonstrating that chemical accuracy can be achieved with smaller fragments. By integrating fragment-level quantum data with ML, this hybrid framework provides an efficient pathway for generating reliable BDE datasets and accelerating the discovery of effective PFAS degradation strategies.

papers.title: Reading the charge state of hydrogenated nanodiamonds: the 1330 cm-1 Fano feature as an interfacial probe
papers.abstract: Hydrogenated nanodiamonds combine unusual electrokinetic charging with electronic properties that are highly sensitive to their surrounding environment, yet the relationship between molecular adsorption, interfacial charge and carrier state remains poorly understood. Here, a homologous series of anionic and cationic surfactants with C3–C16 alkyl chains is used as a controlled molecular perturbation of oxidized and hydrogenated detonation (DND) and high-pressure high-temperature (HPHT) nanodiamonds. By combining ζ-potential measurements, FTIR spectroscopy and electrical transport, we examine how surfactant polarity and chain length affect these chemically and structurally distinct interfaces. Particular attention is given to the ~1330 cm-1 Fano-type infrared feature of HPHT H-ND, which we establish here as a spectroscopic probe of changes in its interfacial electronic state. The comparison reveals a marked contrast between the comparatively electrostatically hard H-DND interface and the electronically responsive HPHT H-ND surface, where molecular interactions can substantially modify the charge-transfer state. More broadly, the results show that molecular adsorption, electrokinetic charge and electronic carrier response need not evolve in parallel, supporting the Fano-type feature as a sensitive readout of molecularly regulated hydrogenated nanodiamond interfaces.

papers.title: Sugar and Amino Acid Combinations Generate Aroma Compounds Associated with Cereal and Roasted Notes in Beer
Chemical tuning of framework libration as a design principle for Na-oxide superionic conductors
papers.abstract: Most design principles for superionic conductors (SICs) are derived from known SICs and evaluated on static structures, which can miss transport enabled by finite-temperature framework motion. Both limitations are particularly severe for Na-oxides, a low-cost, stable chemistry with only a few known SIC frameworks. Here we establish a Na-oxide design principle that links local Na-site geometry to framework dynamics using chemical substitution and compositional modification strategies. Using molecular dynamics simulations with a Na-oxide-specialized machine-learning interatomic potential, we screen all 8,504 Na-oxides in the Materials Project and identify six superionic frameworks, four of them previously unreported. The highest extrapolated room-temperature conductivity reaches 29 mS cm -1 . We identify a finite-temperature Na-site size window of 1.2–1.5 Å that favors Na hopping and show that the framework motion required to access this window depends on the initial geometry: larger-amplitude libration opens initially small sites, whereas smaller-amplitude libration preserves initially larger sites. Thus, stronger framework motion is not universally favorable for ion transport. Furthermore, we show that libration is governed by polyhedral connectivity and can be tuned through Na content and cation substitution within a fixed framework. Our findings extend Na-oxide design principles from static structure to framework dynamics and indicate that frameworks overlooked at their default compositions can become conductive once the framework dynamics are tuned.

papers.title: Volcanic ash: a broad-scope natural pesticide for global utilization in agriculture
papers.abstract: Overabundant volcanic dust, in the form of volcanic ash or micronized volcanic rock, is a broad-scope natural pesticide. Its physical mechanism of action is chiefly based on adhesion of cuticle and death induction via dehydration, thereby ensuring lack of ecological toxicity. After decades of modest scholarly and industrial interest following the 1972 discovery of the insecticidal mechanism of action of volcanic ash, the first volcanic rock-based pest control formulations were commercialized in Europe in the early 2020s. Applied in agriculture, volcanic dust acts as pesticide, fertilizer, biostimulant and soil conditioner supporting its widespread utilization both by farmers living nearby active volcanoes and basalt quarries and by others in regions where volcanic ash or micronized volcanic rock will be regularly shipped.

papers.title: The Sombor deletion correction term: extremal structure, exact coincidence classification, and the information content of edge decks, with applications to chemistry
papers.abstract: The Sombor index SO(𝐺) = ∑𝑢𝑣∈𝐸 √𝑑2𝑢 + 𝑑2𝑣is a distinguished member of the family of edge-additive degree-based topological indices. We study what happens to SO when an edge is deleted. Summed over all edges, the deletions obey the exact identity ∑𝑒 SO(𝐺 − 𝑒) = (𝑚 − 1) SO(𝐺) − 𝐶(𝐺) with a single correction term — an edge-additive index with an irrational kernel, which we call the Sombor deletion correction term 𝐶 . The paper develops the theory of 𝐶 along three axes. Structure (Sections 2–3): 𝐶 is a linear functional of the edge-type counts, with sharp two-sided bounds against Zagreb-type polynomials and a star-maximisation theorem with full equality characterisation, closed forms for regular graphs and products, and non-expressibility certificates against (𝑛,𝑚,𝑀1,𝑀2, 𝐹 , SO), the degree sequence, and small spectra. Exact algebra of the drops (Section 4): the per-edge drops Δ𝑒 = SO(𝐺) − SO(𝐺 − 𝑒) lie in a fixed multiquadratic field, a normal-form procedure decides their equalities exactly, and an exhaustive computation classifies all coincidences up to degree bound 8 — cross-type coincidences form exactly two families (based on √ 20 and √ 52), within-type coincidences are governed by a diagonal-union theorem and telescoping identities, and the all-degree classification is conjectural. Deck information (Sections 5–7): over all 288,266 graphs on 𝑛 ≤ 9 vertices and all 89,402 chemical graphs on ten vertices, the Sombor deck and the edge-type deck induce the same partition (53,984 classes); 𝐶 is injective modulo matching components on both ranges, but fails in general: an explicit collision with value 20 √ 2 − 4 √ 5 is constructed. On the 18 octane isomers 𝐶 separates 16 structures and raises a boiling-point regression from 𝑅2 = 0.559 (SO alone) to 0.814 (with 𝐶), an exploratory signal. All claims are proved, exhaustively verified, or machine-checked in Lean 4 (Section 8).

papers.title: First-Principles Magnetic Anisotropy and Statistical-Mechanical Prediction of Magnetic Alignment in Aromatic PET-Type Polymer Domains
papers.abstract: Gauge-including-atomic-orbital (GIAO) density functional theory calculations at the B3LYP/6-31+G(d,p) level are used to determine the molecular magnetic susceptibility tensors of a hydroxyl-terminated poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) oligomer series - PET1/BHET, PET2, and PET3 - and the results are carried through an explicit statistical-mechanical model of field-induced domain alignment.
