The isotropic molecular response becomes increasingly negative with oligomer length, while the chemically defined axial anisotropy along the terephthalate backbone remains approximately constant at 15–16 atomic units, showing that total diamagnetic response and magnetic anisotropy are governed by distinct structural features. A continuum orientational model based on the ratio λ = VΔχB2/(2μ0kBT) of magnetic to thermal energy is used to obtain the exact Boltzmann orientational distribution and the second-rank order parameter S, together with an overdamped-rotation estimate of the characteristic alignment time. Because a molecular susceptibility tensor is not automatically a bulk volume susceptibility, the continuum values reported here are explicitly identified as provisional, density-based phenomenological estimates rather than validated bulk quantities. The central physical result is that the coherently rotating domain volume, through its cubic scaling of the magnetic energy, dominates the alignment behaviour far more strongly than the modest variation in molecular anisotropy across the oligomer series, so that the crossover field for a given domain scales as B ∝ a-3⁄2. The framework separates a complete first-principles molecular-response and statistical-mechanics treatment from a deliberately provisional molecular-to-bulk conversion, and it identifies the specific calculations — conformer sampling, a structural-axis re-analysis for PET3, a method-sensitivity benchmark, and a validated coarse-graining scheme — required before the predicted alignment fields and order parameters can be compared quantitatively with experiment.

papers.title: Lithium-Lithium Correlations and the Emergence of Transport Properties in Solvate Ionic Liquid Electrolytes
papers.abstract: Solvate ionic liquids (SILs), equimolar mixtures of lithium salts and chelating glymes, are promising electrolytes for energy storage due to their high thermal stability and low vapor pressure. However, the low lithium transference numbers and modest ionic conductivities of SILs limit device performance. Here, long-timescale molecular dynamics simulations combined with transport characterization identify the Li+-Li+ structural decorrelation as the key descriptor governing ion transport in SILs composed of lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and glymes of various lengths. These SILs have extended ionic networks in which anions bridge multiple Li+ centers, generating long-lived structural correlations. SIL ion transport is initiated by speciation exchange, which disrupts the ionic network and leads to structural decorrelation on nanosecond timescales. Decreasing glyme chain length increases anion bridging, slows structural decorrelation, and decreases ionic conductivity, while increasing lithium transference. These results establish structural decorrelation as a key descriptor of transport in SILs. While the anion-mediated decorrelation is demonstrated for SILs, this framework is general and can be applied to any high concentration electrolyte in which transport emerges from the reorganization of correlated ionic networks.

papers.title: A Crystalline Aminoborane Radical Defines a New Stabilization Strategy and Enables Dihydrogen Activation and Transformation
papers.abstract: Borane radical anions are highly reactive open-shell species, yet their application in dihydrogen activation remains rare. Persistent borane radical anions have primarily been accessed through π-conjugation and kinetic protection. Here, we introduce an adaptive stabilization strategy in which a Zr center dynamically adjusts its coordination geometry to stabilize the boron-centered radical or to disengage from the boron center when reactivity is required. This strategy enables access to an aminoborane radical anion and its boron-centered reactivity toward dihydrogen activation and transformation. D2 labeling further confirmed the dihydrogen activation process and demonstrated that the activated hydrogen can be transferred to organic substrates. Theoretical calculations elucidate the adaptive B–Zr orbital interaction responsible for radical stabilization and the mechanism of H2 activation.

papers.title: Scalable Multiplexed Electrochemical Aptasensor Enabled by Chitosan for Heavy Metal Ion Detection: Advancing Electrode Functionalization and Reusability
papers.abstract: The rapid and reliable detection of heavy metal ions in water remains a critical challenge for environmental monitoring and public health protection. While recent advances in aptamer-based electrochemical sensors for heavy metal detection emphasize miniaturization and improved electrode modification techniques to achieve higher sensitivity, striking a balance among the sensor's analytical performance, ease of fabrication, and scalability remains a major challenge, often resulting in trade-offs between sensitivity and scalability. Herein, we have developed a sensitive, multi-analyte aptamer-based electrochemical sensor by modifying micro structured electrodes with chitosan, which adheres to their inherent functional groups, thereby simplifying sensor preparation. The target-specific aptamers are immobilized via glutaraldehyde-mediated crosslinking chemistry. Using a differential pulse voltammetry measurement technique the sensitivities of the sensor for specific heavy metals was found to be 21.7, 15.18, and 9.25 ΔI per decade change in concentration per unit area for Pb(II), As(III), and Cd(II), respectively. The limit of detection for the developed sensor is observed to be 1.03 ng/L for Pb(II), 0.45 ng/L for As(III), and 3.03 ng/L for Cd(II) in water. Further, the sensor's reusability has been analysed using a chelation mechanism in combination with potential stripping voltammetry. The sensor was effectively regenerated and reused across four consecutive cycles, thereby reducing the cost per test.

papers.title: Three-dimensional fluorescence lifetime imaging of a molecular rotor at complex interfaces of grease
papers.abstract: Fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) maps local physicochemical properties on a confocal laser-scanning microscope. Soft materials are a promising target for FLIM, given their demand for multi-scale microanalysis; of particular interest are the interfacial properties of complex fluids, which remain underexplored. Here, we demonstrate three-dimensional FLIM mapping at complex interfaces of grease as a model system. In grease, tens-of-nanometer-scale thickener fibers form a three-dimensional network in the base oil, and the extent to which fiber–oil interactions alter the local oil properties is an open question. Our bulk measurements confirm that the fluorescence lifetime of a molecular-rotor dye dissolved in the oil is coupled to the local viscosity. Three-dimensional FLIM reveals that the lifetime of the molecular rotor significantly increases at the fiber–oil interfaces. Phasor analysis and pixel-level fitting show that the interfacial state arrests the rotation of the molecular rotor, so the interface is solid-like rather than viscous. Its physicochemical origin may offer a new handle for designing grease materials. Beyond the ~200 nm resolution of our images, the lifetime-domain separation of the two states resolves their coexistence within a single diffraction-limited voxel. Three-dimensional high-resolution FLIM will broaden the mapping of interfacial properties in soft complex materials.

papers.title: Geminal Metalloid Substituents Enable Stereoselective Geometric Isomerization of Highly Substituted Alkenes via Energy-Transfer Catalysis
papers.abstract: Controlling alkene geometry with high stereochemical precision remains a fundamental challenge in synthetic chemistry, particularly for highly substituted systems. Here we report a stereoselective photoisomerization of gem-diborylalkenes in which visible light enables efficient E→Z interconversion of geminal metalloids-substituted carbon–carbon double bonds through a triplet energy-transfer (EnT) mechanism, overcoming the long-standing limitation of stereoselective photoisomerization of highly (tetra)substituted alkenes. A broad range of tri- and tetra-substituted alkenes are converted to the thermodynamically less stable Z-isomer with up to 99:1 selectivity. Mechanistic studies and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that stereocontrol arises from both interplay between excited-state deconjugation due to steric bulkiness and substratephotocatalyst interactions. Sequential functionalizations of both geometrically defined diborylalkene isomers are also demonstrated, enabling the stereodivergent construction of complex stereodefined alkenes. Beyond facilitating stereoselective geometric isomerization of tri- and tetrasubstituted alkenes, this work establishes (gem)-dimetalloid alkenes as light-programmable scaffolds and introduces a general strategy for boron-mediated photochemical control of alkene stereochemistry with implications for molecular and materials design.

papers.title: Understanding the steric demand of the reactions of nickel(0) complexes with aryl halide substrates
papers.abstract: Nickel complexes are able to undergo reactions with organohalides by a variety of fundamental steps, which can be either one-electron or two-electron in nature. Two electron processes are typically some flavour of oxidative addition (OA), but various mechanisms have been proposed for the one-electron reactions, including inner-sphere halogen atom abstraction (HAA) and outer-sphere single electron transfer (SET). It was recently proposed that the steric bulk of a substrate can be used as an indicator of whether HAA is feasible, and therefore that SET was in operation for a specific and bulky substrate. However, the steric requirements for HAA by nickel have not yet been systematically assessed. Here we report a structured assessment of how HAA feasibility might vary with ligand and substrate steric impact. We find that HAA by [Ni(PMe 3 ) 3 ] is feasible even for sterically very hindered substrates. Systems with ferrocene-derived bisphosphine ligands tend to prefer HAA when the ligand and/or the substrate are very sterically bulky.

papers.title: Revisiting Artifact Suppression in Electrospray Ionization Deconvolution
papers.abstract: Charge state assignment is a critical step in many workflows for intact protein analysis by mass spectrometry. Computational deconvolution algorithms are increasingly used to automate data analysis, but conventional approaches can present artifacts. Here, we explore several approaches to remove artifacts by limiting the charge state assignments for each data point. One approach removes satellite charge states surrounding local maxima. Another removes harmonics at double a more probable charge assignment. The last two limit either the total number of allowed charge state assignments or the minimum relative charge state assignment probability for a given data point. These new features are as effective as the prior SoftMax artifact removal in UniDec, but they enable easier tuning by the user. Although the new set of features introduces additional complexity and an expanded number of parameters, these tools enable users to more precisely reduce artifacts in deconvolution results.

papers.title: Solvent organization and QM–MM nonbonded interactions govern excitation energies of cationic Methylene Blue: a multiscale Dual-MD/ML and QM/MMPol benchmark
papers.abstract: Methylene blue (MB) has been utilized as a therapeutic agent and has been in clinical and research use for more than a century. The cationic nature of MB+ and the mutual polarization between solute and solvent constitute not just higher-order corrections but dominant contributions; accordingly, polarizable embedding approaches have been shown to substantially modify computed absorption characteristics of dyes in condensed phases, but it is still a challenge to reproduce the MB+ absorption spectrum. Here, we benchmark three multiscale simulation workflows, differing in force-field parametrization and configurational sampling strategy. In parallel, we evaluate five density-functional approximations to describe the electronic structure and to compute the associated absorption spectra of the solvated system. Consistent with experimental observations, methylene blue exhibits pronounced sensitivity to the local solvation environment, and the results indicate that the Dual-MD protocol is compatible with both conventional Born–Oppenheimer molecular dynamics (BOMD) and machine-learning (ML)-based potentials. Moreover, upon inclusion of explicit water molecules in the QM region, fully hybrid functionals yield excitation energies in excellent agreement with experiment.

papers.title: United Complexes or [2]Catenanes: Curvature-Controlled Cooperative π-Coordination Mimicking θ-Curve Motifs
papers.abstract: Control over the solid-state self-assembly of (M 3 L 2 ) 2 -type entangled complexes (M = Cuᴵ, Agᴵ) and interlocked [2]catenanes was achieved through structural modification of the curved tripodal arms of triarylmethane-based ligands (L). When 3-pyridyl groups served as terminal coordination donors on appropriately curved tripodal arms, cooperative metal–acetylene π-coordination, reminiscent of the secondary cross-linking found in nontrivial θ -curve motifs of entangled proteins, generated additional intercomponent connectivity and bridged the two M 3 L 2 cages to form a “united” complex. In contrast, incorporation of 4-pyridyl donors reduced the curvature of the tripodal arms and afforded a normal [2]catenane lacking such inter-cage cross-linking. Furthermore, insertion of an m -phenylene–ethynylene spacer produced a unique dissymmetric [2]catenane in the crystalline state. These results demonstrate that subtle changes in ligand geometry can regulate secondary connectivity while preserving the underlying (M 3 L 2 ) 2 entangled framework, thereby providing access to distinct interlocked architectures. The introduction and control of θ -curve-like secondary linkages thus offer a new design principle for coordination-driven nanostructures based on molecular entanglement.

papers.title: Conjugated Helicene Oligomers Displaying an Odd-Even Conformational and Aggregation Effect
papers.abstract: Helicenes attract attention due to their spring-shaped structures and conjugated backbones. Synthesizing longer helicenes allows for structure-property relationship investigation as additional coil layers are achieved. Therefore, developing helicenes as building blocks for oligomers and polymers will increase understanding of property tuning upon chain extension. We report the synthesis of discrete oligomers using the helicene N[5]HDI from lengths n=1 to n=5. Selective bromination of the oligomers allows for extension to longer oligomers, as well as the potential to use them as monomer units in polymerizations. The oligomers exhibit an odd-even effect, where odd oligomers prefer a ‘coiled’ conformation, while even oligomers prefer a ‘snake’ conformation. This results in improved orbital overlap and effective conjugation in odd oligomers, and small changes in electronics but increased aggregation in even oligomers. The synthesis and structure-property tuning of N[5]HDI oligomers is an important step toward incorporating helicenes into polymers with enhanced mechanical and electronic properties.

papers.title: Decoupling the Thermal Service Limit from Degradability in 3D Printable Covalent Adaptable Networks via Nanohybridization
papers.abstract: Covalent adaptable networks (CANs) represent a critical advancement in sustainable polymers, yet their deployment is frequently constrained by a trade-off between high thermal service limit and on-demand degradability. Herein, we report an organic-inorganic hybrid polymer architecture that decouples thermomechanical robustness from chemical responsiveness. By integrating rigid polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane (AcryloPOSS) nanoclusters into a dynamic lipoic acid-based CAN-type matrix, the POSS cages function as steric nanoscale shields that restrict polymer chain mobility. This structural confinement yields a high activation energy for disulfide exchange (204.9 ± 22.5 kJ mol-1), thereby suppressing macroscopic creep and maintaining network integrity up to 250°C, matching the performance of non-degradable commercial thermosets. Furthermore, the hybrid network exhibits chemical stability over a wide pH range yet undergoes complete dissolution in highly alkaline solutions within 24 hours, decomposing into the building blocks of the hybrid polymer. Utilizing digital light processing 3D printing, we demonstrate a dual-curing strategy to fabricate geometrically complex, high-resolution polymeric objects that balance exceptional durability with closed-loop end-of-life deconstructability.

papers.title: Fundamental Determinants of Misranking in Affinity-Based Ligand Ranking
papers.abstract: Affinity-based prioritization depends on preserving the relative order of ligands, which is distinct from determining each equilibrium dissociation constant, K d , accurately. Errors that substantially bias individual K d values do not necessarily alter ranking if they affect ligands similarly, whereas smaller differential errors can reverse the order of ligands whose true affinities are close. Here, we establish a quantitative framework for understanding this distinction in full-titration binding assays. First-principles analysis of equilibrium 1:1 binding shows that the target-to-affinity ratio, T 0 / K d , governs the amplification of concentration errors into fitted-affinity errors, while the true affinity ratio between two ligands defines the margin that differential errors must overcome to produce rank inversion. Controlled end-to-end simulations extend this analysis to additive and nonadditive response models and map the regimes in which affinity ranking becomes vulnerable. The results show that ranking progressively destabilizes as local affinity separation decreases and T 0 / K d increases. They further demonstrate that ligand-specific signal nonadditivity can introduce differential distortions that impair ranking even when concentration-dependent error amplification is weak, whereas response transformations shared across ligands have substantially less effect on their relative ranking. Library-scale simulations additionally show that strong overall rank correlation can coexist with substantial errors in recovering the highest-affinity candidates, indicating that global rank statistics alone may not adequately assess prioritization performance. We translate these findings into a practical workflow emphasizing appropriate concentration design, validation of response additivity, control of ligand-to-ligand variability, and selection-focused performance metrics for reliable affinity ranking.

papers.title: ATP-Driven Electron Transfer in the DCCP:DCCP-R Protein: A Synergy of Conformational Shift and Asp–Arg Bridge Protonation for Redox Modulation
papers.abstract: Most enzymatic systems that couple ATP hydrolysis to low-potential electron transfer (ET) typically rely on: (i) large conformational changes that tune the redox properties of the reductase Fe-S cluster, and (ii) redox state-dependent dissociation of the reductase subunit to ensure directionality. The double-cubane cluster protein (DCCP) and its reductase (DCCP-R) operate through a distinct mechanism, as the complex remains associated and the crystal structures reveal only subtle nucleotide-dependent conformational changes. These include the formation of Asp–Arg salt bridges by two aspartates (Asp113), located next to the [4Fe4S] cluster at the DCCP:DCCP-R interface. Infrared spectroscopy further showed that protein scaffold rearrangements are rate-limiting and likely involve carboxylate protonation dynamics. In addition, direct electrochemistry revealed an unusually high midpoint potential for a low-potential [4Fe4S] cluster. DFT modeling demonstrated that the ATP-dependent conformational change is coupled to the protonation status of Asp113 in proximity to the [4Fe4S] electron relay. This coupling modulates the cluster redox behavior in an electrostatic proton-coupled ET (PCET) manner, providing a thermodynamic basis for electron transfer to the low-potential [8Fe9S] cluster in DCCP.

papers.title: Auditing LLM Chemical Priors for Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization of Chemical Reactions: A Validity, Alignment, and Diversity Benchmark
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as priors for cold-starting Bayesian optimization (BO) of chemical reactions, yet their benefit–risk profile in multi-objective reaction optimization remains poorly characterized. We present a systematic benchmark asking when LLM knowledge helps, is neutral, or hurts multi-objective BO (MOBO). Across seven public reaction benchmarks (6,384 candidate experiments), we compare nine strategies—including LLM-initialized BO, an LLM-only initializer, and established baselines (TSEMO, EDBO+-style scalarization, LLAMBO)—with 20 seeds per configuration (1,120 main-grid plus 360 ablation campaigns), scored by hypervolume completion and its sampling-efficiency integral (AUC), with paired Wilcoxon tests and two-family Benjamini–Hochberg correction against a random-init BO control. Three regimes emerge. On Suzuki–Miyaura, LLM initialization significantly improves sampling efficiency (ΔAUC +2.0 points, q = 0.026; alternative backbone +2.7 points, q = 1.4 × 10⁻⁴). On Buchwald–Hartwig, LLM priors are statistically indistinguishable from random. On a process-development coupling, LLM initialization significantly harms efficiency (ΔAUC −11.1 points, q = 0.0016) despite a 0% out-of-pool rate, whereas the Suzuki benefit coexists with a 45% out-of-pool rate—the prior’s direction, not its syntactic validity, controls the outcome. Diversity-based initialization (farthest point sampling) matches or exceeds LLM initialization wherever LLMs help, and no LLM-derived benefit exceeds what the knowledge-free diversity control already provides. A five-category diagnostic protocol intercepts 100% out-of-pool suggestions on the flow cases at zero experimental cost. LLM priors are not yet a reliable default for multi-objective reaction optimization; we provide a cost-free pre-campaign screening heuristic for deciding when to trust them.

papers.title: Signal Additivity as a Practical Criterion for Validating Kd Determination: Reconciling Conflicting Backscattering Interferometry Results
papers.abstract: Backscattering interferometry (BSI) enables label-free, immobilization-free detection of molecular interactions in free solution, but published studies report conflicting outcomes, including saturable, nonsaturating, and poorly reproducible responses. Here, we develop a signal-additivity framework that distinguishes interaction detection from determination of the thermodynamic equilibrium dissociation constant, K d , and provides a basis for reconciling these reports. For a two-state system at fixed total target concentration, quantitative K d analysis requires the final referenced and control-subtracted response to be an affine function of equilibrium complex concentration over the fitted range. A general refractive-index expansion shows that nonlinear self-and crosscomponent contributions can survive control subtraction and generate composition-dependent residual signals. Illustrative simulations with a known input value, K d,true , show that such residuals can produce smooth, apparently saturable curves with biased apparent dissociation constants, K d,app , or strong concentration-range dependence of K d,app . Concentration-design analysis further illustrates, for a specified ligand-dependent residual model, a trade-off between upper-isotherm coverage and high-concentration residuals. Reinterpretation of representative BSI studies indicates that specificity, reproducibility, and apparent saturation support interaction detection but do not independently establish signal additivity. We therefore propose a workflow based on matched controls, concentration-range analysis, residual inspection, parameter-stability assessment, and binding-model evaluation, with measurements at different target concentrations when feasible. Although developed here using BSI, the underlying criterion applies more broadly to affinity studies in which a processed response is assumed to report equilibrium binding populations. BSI-derived values should be reported as K d,app unless signal additivity, adequate isotherm coverage, concentration accuracy, and binding-model adequacy are independently supported.

papers.title: Controlled Assembly and In Situ Reconfiguration of Multiphase DNA Droplets in a Vibration-Induced Local Vortex Microfluidic Platform
papers.abstract: Liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) of sequence-designed DNA nanostructures offers a powerful route toward dynamic artificial cells and intelligent molecular robots. However, conventional bulk synthesis suffers from stochastic polydispersity in terms of droplet size and topology, and physical compartmentalization restricts continuous chemical exchange with the external environment. This study reports an upgraded vibration-induced local vortex (VILV) microfluidic platform featuring secondary trapping pillars that decouple a localized microvortex-driven assembly from a global convective flow. This architecture enables highthroughput parallel manufacturing of uniform multiphase DNA droplets and their anchoring within micropillar arrays without washout. By systematically tuning the stoichiometry of the interphase hexavalent DNA linker, precise array-wide programming of the surface valence of the multiphase droplets is achieved, driving predictable structural transitions from monovalent Janus artificial cells to highly connected multivalent patchy networks. Notably, under continuous open perfusion, introducing invader strands rationally engineered to mimic clinically diagnostic microRNA (miRNA) biomarker sequences triggers toehold-mediated strand displacement (TMSD) across phase boundaries. This non-invasive tracking demonstrates linker-density-dependent morphological alterations. This study establishes a versatile foundation for mass-producing synthetic organelles and one-pot molecular diagnostic devices by bridging uniform multiphase artificial cell manufacturing with sequence-specific miRNA responsiveness under continuous fluidic flow.

papers.title: Decoding Residue-level Energetic Rewiring in PROTAC Ternary Cooperativity
papers.abstract: Binding cooperativity is a defining determinant of the stability, selectivity, and degradation efficiency of PROTAC-mediated ternary complexes, yet its molecular origin remains poorly understood because existing computational approaches largely provide only global affinity estimates. Here we present MASIC (Multimeric Alanine Scanning with Interaction Convolution), a thermodynamically grounded end-point free energy framework that enables quantitative residue-level analysis of cooperativity in multimeric protein-protein-PROTAC systems. MASIC establishes a unified formulation linking end-point free energy theory, alanine-scanning interaction entropy, and multimeric cooperativity, while introducing a statistically robust interaction-convolution strategy that overcomes the finite-sampling instability of conventional interaction-entropy estimators. Beyond quantifying overall cooperativity, MASIC provides, to our knowledge, the first residue-resolved cooperativity landscapes of PROTAC ternary complexes and introduces the concept of cooperativity hotspots, identifying residues that govern cooperative stabilization rather than binding affinity alone. Extensive validation across diverse experimentally characterized PROTAC systems, including BRD9-VHL, BRD4-CRBN and FKBP12-CRBN, demonstrates accurate prediction of experimental cooperativity and consistently outperforms established structure-based approaches. Residue-level analyses reveal previously inaccessible many-body interaction networks underlying synergistic and antagonistic cooperativity, providing mechanistic insight into ternary-complex formation. Together, MASIC establishes a general framework for dissecting cooperative molecular recognition in multimeric biomolecular assemblies and provides a foundation for the rational design of next-generation targeted protein degraders.

papers.title: Continuous Solar-Adaptive Electrochemical Stripping for Circular Nitrogen Recovery from Urine
papers.abstract: Solar electrochemical stripping (ECS) is a low-carbon circular economy approach to recover ammonia from wastewater that faces challenges in scale up and intermittent energy supply management. We present a novel autonomous solar-adaptive multistage ECS system that removed > 94% of nitrogen from a continuous flow of influent urine and recovered >75% of nitrogen as ammonium sulfate fertilizer in over 80 hours of off-grid operation. To control urine flow rate, we identified a load ratio that maximizes nitrogen extraction across fluctuating solar power inputs. The first demonstrated multistage electrode stack configuration of ECS increased the system’s volumetric urine treatment capacity by 2.7x and revealed that hydraulic coupling of stages in series can increase nitrogen removal by 16.5% compared to parallel operation for the same urine flow rate and energy efficiency. Using these findings, ECS was operated as a three-stage configuration in real sunlight on two sunny days and one partially cloudy day, allowing current density to range from 4.7 mA/cm2 to 10.4 mA/cm2 proportionally to incident sunlight. Urine flow varied accordingly from 0.82 L/day to 1.92 L/day. Even as input power fluctuated, the system achieved consistent nitrogen extraction that varied less than 7% at steady state. This solar-adaptive (i.e., flexible) operation scheme would require 55% less battery storage than an equivalent constant operation scheme. Ultimately, this work elucidates a pathway to valorize alternative sources of ammonia nitrogen at the water-energy nexus, leverages demand-side response to support electrical grid stability, and reduces the need for renewable energy battery storage.

papers.title: Nanocraft: Nanocrystal Assembly and Functionalization Toolkit
papers.abstract: Nanoparticles find broad applications in optoelectronics, catalysis, and nanomedicine. While machinelearning and computational screening can accelerate their design, the structural chemical space of these materials remains underrepresented in current databases. Obtaining realistic atomistic models requires the proper representation of both the inorganic core and its surface chemistry, which are commonly treated through disjoint workflows relying on separate tools. We present Nanocraft, an open source Python toolkit for the generation and functionalization of nanocrystals and nanoparticles. Operating locally through an accessible Jupyter Notebook interface, Nanocraft does not require advanced coding skills and enables the rapid generation and manipulation of large datasets by varying core stoichiometries, shapes, ligand types and surface coverage. The toolkit provides automated surface passivation based on local oxidation states and enables facet selective ligand attachment within a single framework. Its structure generation pipeline accepts crystallographic CIF files or XYZ supercells and exports the resulting structures in XYZ format for direct use in molecular dynamics, density functional theory, and machine-learning workflows. We demonstrate Nanocraft’s capabilities by constructing a dataset of thiolcapped CdSe quantum dots. Both Nanocraft and the supporting information, including a User Guide, are available at https://github.com/jgrll/Nanocraft/.

papers.title: Active Atom Identification for Information-Dense Training of Machine-Learning Potentials in Catalysis
papers.abstract: Machine-learning potentials (MLPs) extend atomistic simulations beyond the size and time scales accessible to density functional theory while retaining near-first-principles accuracy. However, their reliability depends on training data that cover the relevant potential-energy surface (PES). In heterogeneous catalysis, local changes at active sites may be obscured by redundant nonactive atoms when configurations are selected using global metrics. This limitation calls for an atom-resolved criterion for identifying where chemically relevant configurational information is concentrated. Here we introduce Active Atom Identification (AAI), an algorithm that measures local structural evolution and identifies active atoms that contribute most to configurational diversity. Building on this atom-resolved information, we develop IDEAL (Information-Dense Extraction and Adaptive Learning), which integrates data generation, active-learning selection and dataset refinement into a unified workflow for MLP construction. For CO2 adsorption at Ag/H2O interfaces, a model trained on an IDEAL-selected subset comprising 44% of the original dataset, reaches the accuracy of the full-dataset model. The broad applicability of IDEAL is further demonstrated in two additional applications: database refinement for solid-state electrolytes and transfer learning between zeolite-supported Rh clusters and their hydroxylated analogues. These results validate local structural evolution as an effective criterion for constructing information-dense MLP datasets in complex atomistic systems.

papers.title: Asymmetric Anti-Hydrogenation of Tetrasubstituted Alkenes
papers.abstract: Asymmetric alkene hydrogenation is a foundational method for constructing chiral molecules, with broad applications in pharmaceutical synthesis, natural-product synthesis and materials science. However, the stereochemical outcomes accessible through conventional asymmetric hydrogenation are constrained by its underlying mechanism. Established catalysts, including complexes of iridium, rhodium, ruthenium and platinum, typically deliver both hydrogen atoms to the same face of an alkene to give syn-hydrogenation products. The complementary process, in which hydrogen atoms are stereoselectively delivered from opposite alkene faces, would provide direct access to complementary stereochemical products, but remains poorly developed. Here we show that engineered heme proteins catalyze asymmetric anti-hydrogenation of unactivated cyclic tetrasubstituted alkenes. These genetically encoded catalysts operate through a cooperative radical mechanism in which an active-site iron hydride delivers a hydrogen atom to one face of the alkene to generate a transient carbon-centered radical, which is subsequently quenched from the opposite face by a distal cysteine residue. The spatially separated hydrogen-atom donors thereby enable sequential stereodetermining events, furnishing anti-hydrogenated products with high diastereo-

papers.title: Reinterpreting Simulation Results for New Materials Applications with a Large Language Model
papers.abstract: In materials discovery, computational results generated for one application may retain value for deciding what to investigate next. Here we use a large language model to reinterpret archived adsorption calculations in the context of framework chemistry and pore structure across three metal–organic framework case studies. Xenon affinity directly guided Xe/Kr selection, while dilute-limit methane affinity transferred more effectively than finite-pressure uptake. We then asked whether archived results could suggest new applications without a predefined target. CO2 results prompted four separation directions, CO2/N2, CO2/CH4, C2H2/CO2, and C2H6/CO2, none of which was recovered when the same materials lacked the archived CO2 information. Nine of 15 CO2-informed material–application pairs ranked in the top quarter of corresponding classical screening distributions. Archived simulations can therefore guide what to investigate next, from selecting materials for a known target to opening a new application.

papers.title: Conformational control for selective CO2-to-isocyanate conversion in a series of dizinc macrocycle complexes
papers.abstract: Understanding how ligand architecture and conformational flexibility govern reactivity and selectivity in dinuclear metal complexes is essential for the rational design of catalysts. Macrocyclic ligands provide a unique platform to control metalmetal distance as well as the geometry of reactive intermediates; however the relative importance of these factors remains unclear. Herein, we report a series of dinuclear zinc complexes supported by bis(imino)diphenylamido macrocyclic ligands with tunable ring sizes, which exhibit divergent selectivity in CO 2 -to-isocyanate transformations. Varying the linker length between the binding pockets dictates the conformation of key siloxide intermediates, and thus their ability to react further with CO 2 , leading to either isocyanate or silyl ether products. These results establish liganddriven conformational control as a key design principle governing reactivity in dinuclear metal complexes, beyond simple metalmetal distance considerations.

papers.title: Target-Specific De Novo Drug Design via Fine-Tuned Language Models and Molecular Docking, Molecular Dynamics Simulation Validation
papers.abstract: De novo drug design remains an expensive and low-yield process, particularly for targets with limited bioactivity data. In this study, we fine-tuned the Qwen 2.5 0.5B model to treat ligand design as a sequence-to-sequence task from protein amino acid sequences to molecular SELFIES representations. A curated and balanced dataset derived from ChEMBL was used to reduce target-level data imbalance, followed by systematic evaluation using beam search and stochastic sampling. The fine-tuned model demonstrated strong ligand generation capability across multiple targets, achieving high validity, uniqueness, and novelty. Comparative analysis revealed that beam search favored conservative exploitation of learned chemical space, whereas sampling enabled broader exploration and higher novelty. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and MM/PBSA binding free-energy calculations for representative targets showed that generated compounds formed stable complexes with energetically favorable binding profiles comparable to known inhibitors. Notably, target-specific fine-tuning under extreme low data conditions, enabled through molecular representation augmentation, successfully guided ligand generation toward relevant structural frameworks. Our work suggests that small language models can be effectively fine-tuned for structure-aware, target-specific ligand design, even under limited bioactivity information.

papers.title: Role of Interfacial Silica in the Local Structure, Strain, and Propane Dehydrogenation Activity of Dispersed Ga3+ Sites
papers.abstract: Understanding the structure of the active sites in supported Ga-based propane dehydrogenation (PDH) catalysts is essential, as the Ga–O coordination environment and the nature of neighboring atoms (e.g., Al or Si from SiO2 or Al2O3 supports) strongly influence the catalytic properties. Here, we prepared Ga3+ sites dispersed on Al2O3 and SiOx-Al2O3 supports using atomic layer deposition, tailoring the thickness of the grown SiOx layer and the acidity at the Ga-SiOx-Al2O3 interface. Comparing the propene selectivity and Ga-normalized propene formation rates of the prepared materials reveals that, for the Al2O3 and SiOx-Al2O3 supports, catalytic activity decreases as Si content increases, which correlates with a decrease in the relative abundance of weakly Lewis acidic tetracoordinate Ga3+ sites in the local coordination environment with Al3+ atoms ([4]Ga(Al) and [4]Ga(Al/Si) sites), driving the PDH activity of those catalysts. In comparison, a reference catalyst with Ga3+ sites dispersed on SiO2 is more active and features the highest abundance of strongly Lewis acidic tetracoordinate Ga3+ sites in the local coordination environment of Si4+ atoms ([4]Ga(Si) sites), which drive its PDH activity. Solid-state 71Ga nuclear magnetic resonance studies at ultra-high field (28.2 T) highlight that the distorted coordination geometry of [4]Ga(Si) sites is characteristic of the silica support, and notably less frequent for dispersed [4]Ga(Al) and [4]Ga(Al/Si) sites on alumina and SiOx-Al2O3.

papers.title: An Ab Initio-Kinetic Framework for Predicting Electrochemical Passivation of Materials
papers.abstract: Recent years have seen a strong push towards data-driven discovery of materials in many areas, from structural alloys to energy devices to quantum materials. However, many applications involve prolonged exposure to aqueous and/or acidic electrochemical conditions that can promote material degradation. Despite the critical role of stability in determining material performance, there is a lack of models that are capable of predicting a material’s corrosion-passivation behavior without relying on empirical parameters or fitting. In this work, we address this gap by developing an ab initio kinetic model (AKM), which integrates an existing empirical passivation growth theory, the Point Defect Model (PDM), into a non-empirical first principles-based framework. We redefine the five primary inputs of the PDM, previously ad hoc or experimentally-fitted, into ab initio -calculable parameters, entirely removing their empirical dependence. We then apply AKM to predict the passivation growth of six common metal-film systems. In comparison to experiments reported in the literature, we obtain a strong qualitative trend and reproduce the correct orders of magnitude, without any a priori experimental inputs. We further investigate passive-film formation in the Cu-CuO x system through a detailed computational case study, establishing guidelines for selecting appropriate surface terminations, oxygen vacancy configurations, and point defect concentrations. Sensitivity analyses further reveal that, within the PDM framework, the electrical driving force has a greater influence on passive-film growth than the chemical driving force. This work represents a vital step towards the development of high-throughput predictive modeling of materials’ electrochemical stability in applications where materials are exposed to aqueous media.

papers.title: Optimizing mechanical properties and ionic conductivity of hybrid hydrogel electrolytes for flexible zinc-ion batteries
papers.abstract: Wearable electronics require energy storage systems that combine mechanical flexibility, safety, and electrochemical performance, making aqueous zinc-ion batteries using hydrogel polymer electrolytes (HPEs) a promising approach. However, achieving hydrogels with both high mechanical toughness and ionic conductivity remains a major challenge. Herein, a zwitterionic poly(sulfobetaine methylacrylate)-tetraethylene glycol dimethacrylate (PSBMA-EG) hydrogel was combined with a silica network to form an organic/inorganic hybrid electrolyte. The results demonstrated the successful synthesis and cross-linking of the organic and inorganic networks using 3-(trimethoxysilyl)propyl methacrylate (TMSPMA) as a coupling agent. The acrylate-to-silica ratio (Ac:Si), as the composition-dependency, was varied to investigate its effect on the morphology, swelling behaviour, and glass transition temperature of the obtained hydrogels. Typically, increasing the Ac:Si ratio resulted in more homogeneous and porous structures with higher water uptake. The mechanical and electrochemical properties were evaluated using uniaxial compression and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), respectively. The HPE with the optimized combination of properties was obtained at an Ac:Si ratio of 2:1, exhibiting a toughness of 152.41 ± 30.12 kJ m –3 and an ionic conductivity of 118.01 ± 28.04 mS cm –1 .

papers.title: Prediction of organic additive-induced rheological enhancement of CTAB solutions using machine learning methods
papers.abstract: Various organic additives can induce structural rearrangement of surfactant micelles in aqueous solutions, leading to enhanced rheological properties, namely an increase in viscosity, appearance of viscoelasticity, and non-Newtonian behavior. This phenomenon can be exploited in several industries to obtain strong gels. The selection of proper additives and their concentrations remains largely empirical owing to the high number of factors influencing structural rearrangement. This paper aims to employ machine learning (ML) methods to predict whether an enhancement of rheological behavior will occur in cetyltrimethylammonium bromide solutions (CTAB) upon addition of an organic compound. Five different shallow ML algorithms were tested along with graph neural networks (GNNs), using a dataset of 605 data points collected from the literature. Two types of descriptors (RDKit and PaDEL) were applied. Shallow ML algorithms achieved a maximum precision of 0.85 under cross-validation with a random fold split, and this performance did not deteriorate significantly when a structure-based split was applied (0.82). The random forest algorithm was selected based on its comparatively stable performance. GNN achieved a precision of 0.85 (random split) and 0.80 (structure-based split). Analysis of relative contribution of system properties and molecular features to the predictions of shallow and GNN models is consistent with the known physicochemical basis. Experimental validation of ML methods on four prospective compounds unseen during training was carried out. Comparison with ML predictions demonstrated that both models can correctly identify compounds that promote rheological enhancement, but tend to overpredict positive outcomes. However, this drawback may be partially mitigated by applying a pessimistic consensus, and then the accuracy of 0.84 and the precision of 0.73 are achieved for evaluation on the experimental dataset. The present work demonstrates that ML methods can be applied to address the problem of surfactant self-aggregation in solution upon addition of organic additives with room remaining for performance improvement.

papers.title: A PN adamantanoid ligand for reticular materials
papers.abstract: Three dimensional linkers are rare in MOF chemistry, as are linkers featuring inorganic elements. Here we report the synthesis and characterisation of a novel phosphorus-nitrogen (PN) cage-based tetra-benzoic acid (P4BA4) and its use for the synthesis of crystalline framework materials PNMOF-1 and PNHOF-1. These results expand the toolkit of 3-dimensional inorganic linkers beyond the current state of the art defined by carboranes and silsequioxanes.

papers.title: GCCDDCs Enable Tumor-Selective Lysosomal Degradation and Payload Delivery via GC-C-Mediated Trafficking
papers.abstract: Degrader–drug conjugates (DDCs) represent an emerging class of therapeutic agents that integrate the mechanism of targeted protein degradation with enhanced drug delivery, offering a promising strategy for precision cancer therapy. We herein report the rational design of GC-C–targeted degrader–drug conjugates (GCCDDCs), a bifunctional modality that promotes selective PD-L1 degradation while concurrently delivering a cytotoxic payload to GC-C–expressing cancer cells. Utilizing the GC-C agonist linaclotide as a targeting moiety, we first engineered GC-C–mediated lysosome-targeting chimeras (GCCTACs), which effectively induced degradation of both extracellular and membranebound proteins in a selective manner. By conjugating a PD-L1-targeting degrader to the microtubule-disrupting agent MMAE, the resulting GCCDDCs exhibit potent antitumor efficacy through coordinated immune checkpoint degradation and direct cytotoxicity. The development of GCCDDCs expands the pharmacological toolbox for targeted protein degraders (TPDs) and X–drug conjugates (XDCs), thereby offering broad utility in chemical

papers.title: Deciphering Ionic Conductivity Differences in Linear Carbonate Electrolytes: Conformational Shrinkage and Solvation Structure in Dimethyl vs Diethyl Carbonate
papers.abstract: Dimethyl carbonate (DMC)-based electrolytes consistently show higher ionic conductivity than diethyl carbonate (DEC)-based ones despite their comparable viscosities and dielectric constants. Here, classical MD simulations with LiPF 6 as the salt are used to elucidate the molecular origins of this difference. LiPF 6 -DMC electrolytes contain a larger population of solvent-separated ion pairs (SSIPs), whereas LiPF 6 -DEC electrolytes exhibit a higher population of ion aggregates (AGGs). Among various species, SSIPs make the dominant contribution to ionic conductivity, accounting for the higher conductivity of DMC-based electrolytes. Both solvents exist predominantly in two conformations, cis-cis (CC) and cis-trans (CT), defined by the torsional angle about the C-O bond; the former is largely non-polar, while the latter has a substantial dipole moment of nearly 4 D. In both electrolytes, the CT fraction increases with salt concentration, consistent with the stronger ion-dipole interactions of the CT conformer with ions and the fractions are comparable for DMC and DEC. Nevertheless, DMC retains a larger fraction of lithium ions as SSIPs. Although CT-DMC and CT-DEC have nearly identical polarities, more CT-DMC molecules coordinate Li + than CT-DEC molecules do. This difference arises from their distinct conformational sizes: CT-DMC has a volume approximately 8% smaller than that of CC-DMC, whereas the corresponding decrease for DEC is only about 2%. The smaller relative size of CT-DMC permits more of it to coordinate Li + to yield effective electrostatic shielding. This, in turn, leads to a larger SSIP population and higher ionic conductivity of LiPF 6 -DMC relative to LiPF 6 -DEC.

papers.title: From Metal-Organic Precursors to Coalesced Thin Films: A Predictive, End-to-End Atomistic Framework for MOCVD Multilayer TMD Growth
papers.abstract: Metal-organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) enables scalable synthesis of layered two-dimensional semiconductors such as transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), yet the atomistic mechanisms linking precursor chemistry to multilayer nucleation and film evolution remain elusive, limiting synthesis control. Here, we establish a predictive mechanistic framework for multilayer TMD growth using MoS 2 as a representative system. Combining density functional theory, ReaxFF molecular dynamics, machine learning, and experimental validation, we reveal how metal antisites occupying chalcogen vacancies intrinsically form through surface interactions and serve as transient nucleation centers under experimentally relevant conditions. These defects stabilize epitaxial registry through covalent bonding and ultimately diffuse into the epilayer to form van der Waals interfaces. During this process, H 2 S vapor pressure influences metal-organic precursor decomposition by lowering the complete Mo(CO) 6 decomposition temperature, thereby promoting nucleation-center formation. This framework shifts layered-material synthesis from empirical trial-and-error toward predictive control, providing a computational route for growth of next-generation two-dimensional materials.

papers.title: Surface charge mosaic of a water-soluble Au25(p-MBA)18 nanocluster induced by environment’s pH
papers.abstract: Water-soluble monolayer-protected gold nanoclusters (AuNCs) are widely regarded as promising nanomaterials for biological and biomedical applications, yet the impact of environment’s pH on their surface charge distribution is poorly understood, hampering efforts to rationally design the cluster size and ligand chemistry for optimizing reactivity and solvation. To investigate the pH-effect, we used constant-pH molecular dynamics simulation method for statistical sampling of ligand charge distributions in a water-soluble gold nanocluster protected by para-mercaptobenzoic acid ligands, Au25(p-MBA)18, in a wide pH range of 1 to 11. The results showed three macroscopic pKa values for the ligand layer: 2.25 ± 0.01, 5.68 ± 0.02, and 6.23 ± 0.04, and indicated anticooperative deprotonation behavior with Hill coefficients ranging from 0.74 to 0.34. The ligand layer pattern and interligand interactions through π–π stacking explained the observed order of the ligand deprotonation. These results uncover ligand-specific deprotonation behavior of Au25(p-MBA)18, enabling precise tuning of its functional performance across diverse applications in biological environment.

papers.title: Structural and Spectroscopic Characterization of Self-Sufficient Cytochrome P450 Fusion Enzymes: CYP102A1 and CYP116B
papers.abstract: Cytochrome P450 (CYP) monooxygenases are heme-thiolate enzymes that catalyze diverse oxidative transformations essential to metabolism, detoxification, and biosynthesis. While most CYPs rely on separate redox partner proteins for electron delivery, a subset-known as self-sufficient or fusion P450s-incorporate the reductase domain(s) directly within a single polypeptide, enabling efficient intramolecular electron transfer and, in some cases, exceptionally high catalytic turnover. This review examines two representative self-sufficient P450 systems, CYP102A1 (P450 BM3) and CYP116B, summarizing spectroscopic evidence (UV-Vis, EPR, and resonance Raman), supported by available crystal structures, to compare how their distinct domain architectures shape heme electronic structure and catalytic mechanism. CYP102A1, a fused FAD/FMN-heme flavocytochrome from Bacillus megaterium, undergoes pronounced substrate-induced conformational rearrangement and low-spin/highspin switching, properties that are further tunable through active-site mutagenesis (e.g., A82F, F87V, F393 variants) and that underlie its status as the most extensively studied and engineered P450 scaffold. In contrast, CYP116B enzymes, which transfer electrons through a defined FMN-[2Fe–2S]-heme pathway, maintain a comparatively rigid, conserved low-spin heme environment that is less dynamically coupled to substrate binding, although engineered variants (e.g., CYP116B5-SOX) demonstrate their potential for peroxide-driven biocatalysis. Together, these comparisons illustrate how differences in fusion architecture translate into distinct strategies for electron transfer and catalytic control, offering complementary design principlesstructural plasticity in BM3 versus a stable redox scaffold in CYP116B-for engineering nextgeneration self-sufficient P450 biocatalysts.

papers.title: Site-Specific Anchoring and Spectral Signatures of Single Atoms, Pairs and Chains for Cs supported on γ-Al2O3 from Atomic-Scale Imaging and 133Cs NMR
papers.abstract: γ-Al2O3 is one of the most widely used supports in heterogeneous catalysis. While the surface of the support provides the anchoring sites for active sites or active phases, e.g. nanoparticles, important for the reactivity and the stability of catalysts, the surface organisation of γ-Al2O3 remains elusive owing to its complexity and heterogeneity. The surface is proposed to host specific anchoring sites depending on the exposed crystalline facets as well as the specific edges between (110) and (100) facets, which are home to distinctive Al coordination environments. Additionally, while alkali metals are essential promoters in heterogeneous catalysis, the way they bind to oxide supports and organise at their surfaces remains poorly understood. In particular, Cs/γ-Al2O3 systems are of practical importance in CO2 conversion processes, where the loading and dispersion of Cs strongly influence activity, yet the nature of the surface Cs species and how their spatial arrangement governs this promoting effect remain poorly understood. Thus, these two interconnected challenges give the opportunity to use specifically designed system to be addressed together. Here, we generate atomically dispersed Cs sites on the surface of well-defined γ-Al2O3 supports with specific crystalline facet organization, according to tailored nanocrystal morphologies. Taking advantage of the high-contrast of Cs (Z=55), we quantify its spatial distribution and specific location by atomic-resolution HAADF-STEM imaging over hundreds of atoms on various support morphologies. Furthermore, we use 133Cs ssNMR and DFT calculations to elucidate the Cs speciation associated with specific anchoring sites. Our work reveals the formation of Cs chains along the (110)/(100) edges of needle-shaped crystals, whereas rhomboids, terminated exclusively by (111) facets, show no such feature. 133Cs NMR and DFT rationalize this behaviour, identifying Cs pairs as the stable configuration at (110)/(100) edges. These results established the specificity of edge anchoring sites, together with bringing details on how Cs binds to surface of relevant oxide support, opening doors to a better understanding of its promotional effect in various catalytic processes, where the spatial distribution of alkali metals is thought to be a crucial factor.

papers.title: Broadly Accessible and Highly Active Hydrophosphination Catalysis with Simple Calcium Compounds in DMSO Solution
papers.abstract: Highly earth-abundant and simple calcium precatalysts are reported that address the long-standing challenge of broad scope in hydrophosphination catalysis. With more than 120 examples of hydrophosphination reactions, calcium catalysts are the broadest in scope, including traditional styrene substrates and activated alkenes (Michael acceptors), conjugated dienes, heterocumulenes, alkynes, unactivated alkenes, and even naturally occurring alkenes. Reactions are optimized to maximum conversion, and few examples have less than 90% conversion, making these the most active catalysts to date. Two features contribute to this exceptional scope and activity. The first feature is solvent. Reactions run in DMSO experience a step up in relative rate compared to those in lower-dielectric solvents. Second, more challenging substrates are readily accessed under photocatalytic conditions, a feature already established for calcium precatalysts. The simple precatalyst, Ca(HMDS) 2 (THF) 2 (HMDS = – N(SiMe 3 ) 2 , 1 ), works for all reactions described, and mechanistic evidence points to a nucleophilic attack for amenable substrates. This work highlights critical advances in hydrophosphination (solvent effects, s-block catalysts, and photocatalysis) to yield an abundant metal (calcium) in green solvent with low energy input to achieve hydrophosphination of the widest scope of substrates under operationally simple conditions.

papers.title: Aminomutase-Inspired Methylene Insertion for α-to-β Homologative Transposition of Amino Acids
papers.abstract: A versatile method for the preparation of synthetically valuable β2-homologated amino acid esters from simple α-amino acid esters is described. Inspired by pyridoxal 5′-phosphate-dependent aminomutase enzymes, the described strategy exploits a straightforward protocol for substrate activation, alkylation, and migration leveraging a bio-inspired 3-exo-trig radical cascade. This approach enables a novel homologative strategy towards β-amino acids via methylene insertion into the Cα–N bond of α-amino acids. A broad substrate scope is demonstrated, and key activator electronic factors are elucidated through experimental and computational mechanistic studies. By engaging α-amino acids directly, the method provides unique access to β2-homologated amino acids.

papers.title: Treatise on Present Practice and Perspectives of MDGC
papers.abstract: The state of affairs of multidimensional gas chromatography (MDGC) at present is no more than an implementation of a two-dimensional form (2D-GC) reducing the domain to the setup known as GCxGC. Introduced in 1991 with great expectation, however, GCxGC still happen to fall short of realizing the anticipated capabilities despite continuous efforts made over the elapsed 35 years. This got quantitative formulation in regard of separation performance as early as 2008, proving that it failed to be competitive with a well-governed 1D-GC. The present paper highlights further limitations of GCxGC: inadequate operation burdened with shortcomings are presented via examples taken from GCxGC literature; crowning the list with the inability to meet fundamental requirement that if a compound can be analyzed by 1D-GC it must remain analyzable by MDGC. The repertoire of the intertwining issues, each of which unavoidably rigs or even hamstrings the others, highlights that GCxGC has a built-in self-limiting feature. Attempts to overcome confinements via loosening the binding conditions turned GCxGC back to the form it emerged from decades ago, yet without getting rid of the hampering curbs. The unfavorable overall picture forces to consider viabilities of other concepts, with focus on avoiding errors and pitfalls of GCxGC while fulfilling basic requirements of MDGC. In our view, there are two alternatives. One is ZGC, principle of which was introduced in 1989, requirements and potential of which are presented here in more detail; the other is a concept called Quantum-GC, which is presented as an introductory approach.

papers.title: GXNU MolStudio: An Integrated Open-Source Platform for Molecular Visualization and Quantum Chemical Analysis
papers.abstract: We report GXNU MolStudio, an open-source, bilingual (Chinese/English) desktop application that integrates real-time molecular visualization with a broad suite of quantum chemical analyses in a single interactive environment. MolStudio embeds a purpose-built OpenGL 3.3 renderer that presents molecules, orbitals, and property-colored isosurfaces in a publication-ready style, and couples it to scripted invocations of the external wavefunction analysis program Multiwfn. The current version provides 14 panels (11 analysis panels plus 3 workflow panels) covering: orbital browsing and isosurface generation (including spin-density visualization for open-shell systems); six atomic charge schemes (ADCH, Hirshfeld, Mulliken, CM5, SCPA, and VDD); Mayer bond orders; NBO donor–acceptor (E(2)) analysis; electrostatic potential (ESP) surfaces with extrema and surface-area distributions; IGMH/IRI weak-interaction analysis; QTAIM topology; ETS-NOCV energy decomposition; molecular planarity parameters (MPP); IRC energy/bond-order profiles; distortion–interaction (DI) decomposition; the energetic span model (ESM); and activation strain scans along the IRC (ASM), multi-CUB overlay, and IRC splitting. All panels share one canvas and one atomic-picking protocol, so that results from different analyses can be compared immediately on the same structure. A retained VMD/Tachyon channel delivers ray-traced journal-quality figures in more than 30 curated styles. MolStudio is distributed as Python source (PyQt5, Python ≥ 3.8) and as a standalone Windows executable, under the GNU General Public License, version 3 (GPLv3only). Its rendering pipeline is a Python port of the GPLv3-licensed IboView engine — a derivative relationship that is declared explicitly in Section 7 and itemized in the code repository — and all third-party components are credited. The software is freely available at https://cnb.cool/chem311/GXNU-MolStudio.

papers.title: Orange hydrogen production with fayalite slag: identifying reaction bottlenecks
papers.abstract: Orange hydrogen (H2) is generated through stimulated water–rock reactions, analogous to natural hydrogen formation via serpentinization, and offers a potential pathway for clean H2 production from Fe(II)-bearing minerals and mineral side streams. Here, we investigate orange H2 production based on fayalite slag, an Fe(II)-rich metallurgical waste that has not previously been studied for this purpose. H2 generation from fayalite slag was evaluated in a stirred hydrothermal reactor pressurized with Ar and experiments were carried out at initial pressures of 5, 50, and 100 bar and temperatures of 160 and 230 °C. The highest H2 production was observed at 230 °C and an initial pressure of 5 bar in 1 M KOH (pH 14) after 48 h, reaching 0.45 g H2 kg-1 fayalite slag, corresponding to ⁓7.2% of the theoretical maximum H2 yield. During the reaction, the fayalite content decreased, while magnetite and a K-bearing mica phase formed as secondary products. These secondary phases may have limited further reaction by reducing water access to Fe(II)-bearing regions. This is evidenced by the fact that H2 generation plateaued after 48 h of reaction time. Overall, the results show that fayalite slag is a potential feedstock for orange H2 production under comparatively mild hydrothermal conditions, while also indicating that secondary phase formation and surface passivation are important reaction bottlenecks.

papers.title: The first approach to highly substituted dihydroimidazotriazolones and their controlled post-transformations
papers.abstract: A novel class of azido-modified α , β -unsaturated Ugi adducts (enamides) has been explored as a versatile platform for post -Ugi transformations. While intramolecular azide-alkyne cycloadditions of Ugi-derived peptidomimetics have been extensively studied, the corresponding azide-alkene cycloadditions on similar scaffolds have remained unexplored. In this work, we report a systematic investigation of intramolecular azide-alkene cycloaddition involving activated enamide moieties derived from Ugi adducts. Enamides readily undergo catalyst-free intramolecular [3+2] cycloaddition under mild conditions to afford the previously unknown 3,3a,4-trisubstituted-3a,4-dihydro-3 H -imidazo[1,2-c][1,2,3]triazol-5(6 H )-one scaffold in high yields. This novel fused heterocyclic system was fully characterised and proved to be a highly versatile intermediate for divergent post -Ugi transformations. Fused dihydrotriazoles transformed into 3,5-dihydroimidazol-4-ones via an elimination of N 2 supplemented by acylamide migration. Additionally, base- or acid-mediated cascades enabled efficient one-pot access to aromatised 1,2,3-triazoles and open-chain triamides, respectively. In total, 4 generations of structural isomers and 2 other classes of compounds were involved in the work. The methodologies developed highlight the synthetic value of azido-modified enamides as divergent intermediates, providing rapid and controlled entry to structurally diverse nitrogen-rich heterocycles and peptidomimetics from simple Ugi adducts derived from α , β- unsaturated aldehydes.

papers.title: Per-axis failure of the minimum-image convention in GCMC screening of MOFs for hydrogen storage
papers.abstract: Grand canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) simulations underpin machine-learning-accelerated screening of metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) for hydrogen storage, yet published workflows differ widely in simulation rigour. Minimum-image violation in GCMC screening of MOFs biases uptake but preserves rankings, and the error is predictable before any simulation is run. Here, the cost of the single-unit-cell shortcut (one crystallographic cell regardless of the interaction cutoff, violating the minimum-image convention) is quantified across a screening library for the first time. Uptakes of 85 CoRE MOF 2019 frameworks were computed with a converged per-framework supercell protocol and repeated in a single cell. Deliverable capacity rankings are found to be remarkably stable (Spearman ρ = 0.996, bootstrap CI [0.989, 0.998]; top ten recovered exactly, no capacity forfeited), while absolute uptakes fall by up to 30%. The total replication factor m predicts the error poorly: frameworks needing only 4 × 1 × 1 replication lose as much uptake as 36× cases. The error tracks the worst single axis nmax, exposing rod secondary-building-unit frameworks (MOF-74 among them) as the class at risk; intermediate-supercell ladders confirm this directly, the same volume increase recovering 2.4% or 16.4% of the deficit according to which axis receives it. Stated without reference to the cutoff, a single cell is safe for ranking whenever every perpendicular width exceeds one cutoff radius, while absolute capacities require two. Recomputing only the frameworks with nmax ≥ 3, one in three of the set, brings the largest remaining error down to 1.3% while still saving 18% of the campaign

papers.title: Programmable Oxidation in Flow on Interdigitated Lateral Catalytic Condensers
papers.abstract: Heterogeneous catalysis remains fundamentally limited by the intrinsic static electronic and physical structure of the catalyst surface during reaction that restricts catalytic rates and limits reactions to equilibrium. To circumvent these limitations, a catalytic condenser enables the non-Faradaic dynamic modulation of surface binding energies through an external potential. Here, we describe an interdigitated (IDT) internal ion gel catalytic condenser within a continuous flow reactor for the electronic control of thermochemical carbon monoxide oxidation on Pt active sites. The device utilizes a thermally stable, high-capacitance ion gel electrolyte (PA6,6/[EDMIM][TFSI]) to establish an electric double layer at the metal-electrolyte interface, enabling both charge condensation and a strong electric field at the Pt active sites. Field strength was measured by Stark tuning of 4-mercaptobenzonitrile (4-MBN) on a model Ag electrode, with field strengths on the order of ~1 V nm -1 shifting a voltage-dependent nitrile response up to ~4 cm -1 /V at negative applied potential. By applying a bias of ±1 V at 180°C, the device both increases and decreases the catalytic turnover frequency of CO oxidation. These results support surface-charge modulation as the origin of catalytic rate enhancement for the non-Faradaic dynamic tuning of thermochemical reaction rates.

papers.title: Sensory Roles of 2-Methyl-3-furanthiol, 3-Methyl-2-buten-1-thiol, and 2-Furfurylthiol in Beer :Olfactometric Evidence and Trace-Level Quantification by Complementary GC-MS Methods
Clearing a benchmark's resolution limit is necessary and not sufficient: measured floors for structure-based virtual screening, and five interventions on a second target
papers.abstract: A virtual screening improvement is normally reported as a difference in AUROC between two protocols, each run once, on one benchmark. Two questions are almost never asked: whether the benchmark can resolve a difference of that size, and whether the difference survives a second target. We ask both, and the answers are not the same. The resolution is measurable and predictable. Fifteen replicates of an identical AutoDock Vina protocol on a 755-compound SARS-CoV-2 Mpro panel, varying only --seed, give an AUROC standard deviation of 0.00441 and a one-sided 95% chi-squared bound of 0.00644. Twelve replicates on an 886-compound Factor Xa panel give 0.00682. AUROC variance scales as 1/n, verified within a target (755 to 339 compounds, ratio 1.14) and, on a prediction fixed in advance, across targets (0.00459 predicted, 0.00427 measured, ratio 0.93). A floor can therefore be quoted for a panel that has not been re-measured. It is specific to the method, the protocol and the panel, and borrowing is expensive. Three substitutions we made and corrected cost factors of 4.0 (one method's floor used for another), 2.2 (the sd of a residual charged against a margin), and 1.5 (a floor moved between panel sizes). The floor is only weakly specific to the AUROC level: across simulated panels from 0.28 to 0.90 it varies by 12%, so a floor measured where a method performs poorly is conservative elsewhere. The metric matters more than any of it. On the same replicates, EF@1% has a coefficient of variation 8.6 times AUROC's: a floor of 0.38 against a mean of 2.28, and a third of the value on a smaller panel. Enrichment at an early cutoff is what screening papers usually report, and it is the quantity a benchmark of this size resolves worst. BEDROC (alpha = 20) sits between the two. Clearing the floor does not make a result real, and that is the paper's central claim. Of five interventions measured on Mpro, three clear the floor by wide margins. Re-measured on a second target, none of the four testable ones replicates. The largest (replacing the scoring function on identical poses: +0.140 on Mpro, twenty-two times that panel's floor, with its whole 95% interval above it) comes back at -0.058 on Factor Xa: a reversal of sign, with the interval clear of that target's own floor. Of the two mid-sized effects, one falls to about a quarter of its Mpro value and one changes sign; neither is resolvable. The smallest effect reproduces almost exactly (+0.0082 against +0.0096) and is unresolvable on both. A resolution limit is a necessary filter and a poor certificate. We recommend measuring it, reporting it with its panel size, and treating a result that clears it as eligible for belief rather than established. VERSION NOTE Supersedes v2. The two resolution limits reported in v2 measured the wrong quantity -- one was implementation variance between two scoring-function builds, the other an intervention effect used as its own threshold -- and they were the decision rule for every intervention in that version. They are replaced by seed replication of an unchanged protocol. Four interventions are additionally re-measured on a second target: none replicates, and the largest (+0.140 on Mpro) reverses sign to -0.058 on Factor Xa. A mechanistic explanation offered for that reversal was tested and withdrawn as inconclusive.

papers.title: TLQ Method: A Tandem Mixing–Linear Deduction–Quantile Weighted Median Framework for Robust Metabolite Screening and a General Diagnostic Indicator for Measurement Reliability
papers.abstract: Untargeted metabolomics is constrained by inter-individual variability, difficulty in detecting low-abundance metabolites, and matrix effects. Post-acquisition corrections are limited when biological variation is large, signals approach detection limits, or matrix effects are strong. We propose the TLQ method, consisting of Tandem Mixing, Linear Deduction, and Quantile Quality-Weighted Median. Tandem Mixing compresses between-group matrix differences and enhances low-abundance signals via equal-volume mixing of paired samples. Linear Deduction removes background and back-calculates the treatment signal, yielding a deduced fold change closer to the true treatment-to-control ratio. The third module performs robust screening using a quality-weighted median with Bootstrap confidence intervals. A candidates-of-interest mechanism improves coverage without compromising accuracy. The modules can be deployed flexibly (paired mode, P_R mode, or standalone third module). We also propose a general group-level diagnostic indicator (GDI) framework. GDI compares pooled and individual estimates and normalizes their discrepancy against a stochastic expectation, making systematic distortion quantifiable. GDI is platform-independent and serves as an independent reliability annotation layer in the TLQ method..

papers.title: Rapid chromatography combined with trapped ion mobility mass spectrometry for analysis of derivatized small molecules
A Simple Model to Predict Complex Coacervation: Forces as Drivers of Phase Change and Structuration
papers.abstract: Biomolecular condensate formation or coacervation has come to the fore as an extremely attractive research area over the past few years, as these condensates have been conjectured to be the most primitive sort of protocells. One of the most studied coacervation process is the complex coacervation between polyelectrolytes and oppositely charged small molecules. Among these structures, a very well tested system is the poly-L-Lysine/Adenosine Tri Phosphate (pLL/ATP) coacervate. To understand the condensation process, one needs to unravel the forces which dictate the behaviour of pLL dispersed in water at various temperatures and for various monomer charge fractions which are positively charged. Unlike most simulations which have been performed for biologically relevant proteins, here we have used an included solvent Monte Carlo approach on 10-bead flexible strands as the model pLL molecules, where each bead stands for 3 lysine monomers. Initially we have established the 10-bead model for pLL molecules. We have shown that at high pH, when the positive charges are largely neutralized due to deprotonation of the amine groups in the lysine monomers, the strands show a clear tendency to form bundles of rigid and vertically elongated pLL molecules driven by intermolecular attractions caused by hydrophobic repulsion from the aqueous medium. On switching off the hydrophobic interaction, we see no bundle formation and the screened coulomb repulsions dominate pushing the strands away from each other, underscoring the essential role of hydrophobic interaction in pLL structuration. We see a similar tendency to move away from each other by keeping the charges fixed at high reduced temperatures as well. These results agree nicely with experimental observations of the different phases of pLL, in particular the formation of fibrils at high pH and room temperature. Once we established the pLL model, we introduced negatively charged single ATP beads. Based on the screened coulomb attractions between the polymers and the molecules, we could predict the crossover point where the repulsive regime gets converted into an overall attractive one leading to nucleation and growth, resulting into coacervation. We could, therefore, correlate the ATP/pLL ratio to the forces dictating the phase separation process – for the first time to the best of our knowledge. Additionally, we could find the radial charge and ATP and pLL bead density distributions which allows us to understand the internal structures of the condensates.

papers.title: Simultaneous selective recognition of two different anions within a hydrogen/halogen bonding cage
papers.abstract: The search for selective anion receptors that can function in water is a longstanding challenge in supramolecular chemistry, motivated by anions’ fundamental roles (and potential applications) in biological, environmental and industrial processes. Here we incorporate halogen and hydrogen bond donors into an easy-toprepare organic cage molecule and demonstrate that this can bind anions at either or both of a halogen bonding pocket and hydrogen bonding pockets depending on the nature of the anions and the solvent. The halogen bonding pocket comprised of six bromopyridinium donors is a potent host for iodide anions, and can selectively bind this guest in water as strongly as biological iodide binders ( K a = 43,000 M –1 measured by 1 H NMR spectroscopy) with the exclusion of other halide anions. In DMSO/water mixtures, the hydrogen bonding pockets are able to recognise chloride anions, resulting in the formation of well-defined mixed anion iodide/chloride complexes with an iodide bound in the centre of the cage and chlorides in the peripheral binding sites. This demonstrates the exquisite selectivity afforded by halogen bonding systems and reveals a general route to a range of supramolecular anion hosts that bind multiple guests in different locations.

papers.title: Comparative Study of Y2O3, ZnO, and CeO2 Additions to Magnesium Aluminosilicate Glasses: Composition–Structure–Property Relationships
papers.abstract: The development of high-modulus glasses is essential for advanced lightweight applications, requiring a fundamental understanding of how different oxide components dictate elastic performance.
