This self-sustaining cycle achieves approximately 80% TOC removal of phenol in a scaled-up 15 L reactor under natural sunlight and sustains approximately 65% TOC removal over 20 consecutive cycles for real pharmaceutical wastewater, with only 1.2% iron loss per cycle and near-zero sludge generation. This work transforms a canonical kinetic barrier into a self-regenerating catalytic platform, uncovering a hydration-driven photochemical route that offers sustainable, sludge-free, sunlight-driven water purification.

papers.title: Machine Learned Interatomic Forces as Inference-Time Physical Guidance for All-Atom Diffusion Peptide Design
papers.abstract: Diffusion-based biomolecular generative models can efficiently explore peptidereceptor sequence-structure space, but the learned generative distribution does not explicitly represent the underlying atomistic potential-energy landscape. As a result, generated complexes may contain locally unfavorable atomic arrangements even when they remain plausible under the learned structural prior. Here, we develop an inferencetime physical guidance framework that couples machine learned interatomic potential (MLIP)-derived forces to the all-atom reverse diffusion trajectory of RFDiffusion3 for receptor-conditioned peptide design. Rather than applying energy minimization after generation, atomistic physical information is introduced before the joint sequencestructure trajectory termination. MLIP-derived forces therefore provide atomic coordinate corrections that are propagated through subsequent denoising steps, allowing physical information to influence not only atomic geometry but subsequent residue selection. The framework requires neither retraining nor modification of the pretrained diffusion model and uses late-stage force guidance, adaptive step-size control, and geometry-preserving projection to retain the underlying generative prior. Across eight receptor systems for peptide designs, MLIP guidance reduced peptidereceptor steric clashes by 24.7% and intrapeptide clashes by 37.4%, while promoting more hydrogen-bond-compatible interface geometries. Guided structures shifted toward more favorable energetic regions in both the guiding MACE potential and an independent MM/GBSA evaluation, with 82.4% of retained structures exhibiting more favorable MM/GBSA energetic estimates. These improvements were achieved with a median peptide backbone deviation of only 0.051 Å. Importantly, 95.0% of generated peptide sequences were preserved, whereas 5.0% underwent residue substitutions, demonstrating that physical guidance can feed back into sequence-structure generation without globally overriding the learned RFDiffusion3 distribution. This distinguishes inference-time physical guidance from post-generation relaxation, which optimizes only the coordinates at fixed chemical identity. More broadly, the results establish a general strategy for coupling pretrained biomolecular generators with differentiable atomistic energy models, enabling physical information to participate directly in molecular generation rather than serving only as a post hoc filter or refinement step.

papers.title: Continuous carbon capture and release using an aqueous oxygen-tolerant redox electrolyte in symmetric flow cells
papers.abstract: Electrochemical CO2 capture provides a promising pathway for carbon management under ambient conditions, yet practical deployment remains limited by system complexity and energy losses associated with oxygen sensitivity, crossover, and overpotentials. Here we report a fluoflavine disulfonate (FFDS)-based symmetric flow reactor for continuous electrochemical CO2 capture. The symmetric configuration generates spatially separated alkaline catholyte and acidic anolyte through a proton-coupled electron transfer process, enabling simultaneous electrochemical regeneration of sorbent, CO2 absorption as (bi)carbonate, and CO2 release. The system demonstrates excellent stability and high oxygen tolerance under simulated flue gas conditions. Furthermore, the CO2 release rate can be regulated by varying the applied current density. Proton crossover is identified as a parasitic transport pathway that compromises energy efficiency. Its impact can be mitigated through buffer regulation and ultimately eliminated by using an industrial packed column to maximize gas–liquid contact. An isolated dual-loop cycling mode further enables simultaneous CO2 capture and release throughout charge–discharge cycling, improving electron utilization under pure-CO2 release conditions. A preliminary techno-economic analysis identifies electricity consumption as the dominant cost contributor, while the cost associated with the redox-active molecule is negligible. Overall, this work establishes a compact, modular, plug and play symmetric electrochemical platform for continuous CO2 enrichment under near-practical operating conditions.

papers.title: A Non-Nuclear Attractor-Mediated 𝟑𝒄–𝟐𝒆 𝝈-Aromatic Core in Triberyllium Hexaoxide
papers.abstract: Low-valent main-group clusters that activate small molecules represent an intriguing frontier in modern coordination and cluster chemistry. Herein, the structural topology, correlated electronic structure, excited states, and real-space chemical bonding of the cyclic triberyllium hexaoxide complex Be3(O2)3 are investigated using meta-GGA density functional theory (TPSS), domain-based local pair natural orbital coupled-cluster theory [DLPNO-CCSD(T)], local energy decomposition (LED), similarity transformed equation-of-motion coupled-cluster theory (STEOM-DLPNO-CCSD), and the Quantum Theory of Atoms in Molecules (QTAIM). The cluster features an equilateral triangular Be3 core (d(Be–Be) = 2.103–2.105 Å) coordinated radially to three end-on dioxygen units (d(O–O) = 1.297 Å). High-level DLPNO-CCSD(T)/def2-TZVP benchmarks establish a correlation energy of −1.751222 Eh and a total electronic energy of −494.527653 Eh. Extended transition state natural orbitals for chemical valence (ETS-NOCV) analysis reveals that core-to-ligand assembly is driven by strong orbital stabilization (ΔEorb = −503.51 kcal/mol) overcoming Pauli steric repulsion (ΔEPauli = +767.52 kcal/mol), mediated by dative charge flow into the dioxygen π* manifold. Topological gradient vector field analysis demonstrates that the Be3 ring lacks classical pairwise Be–Be bond critical points; instead, gradient trajectories converge into a central Non-Nuclear Attractor (NNA) at the ring centroid. Real-space electron localization function (ELF), localized orbital locator (LOL), source function integrations, and delocalization indices (Σ δ(Be, Bq) = 0.971 e) confirm that the Be3 core is sustained by a central three-center two-electron (3c–2e) σaromatic bond.

papers.title: Alkynyl Flexion as a Design Principle for Cryoelastic Phosphorescent Crystals
papers.abstract: Achieving cryogenic mechanical flexibility and persistent phosphorescence simultaneously is challenging because cooling suppresses molecular motion, favoring long-lived emission while limiting the structural adaptability required for elastic deformation. Alkynyl-engineering enables the C≡C unit to function beyond its conventional role as a conjugated linker, with directional C≡C···π-hole interactions serving as a key determinant of crystal packing and mechanical response. Three positional isomers, p-TPA-TRZ, m-TPA-TRZ, and o-TPA-TRZ, were designed to examine how molecular geometry controls this interaction topology while retaining the same TPA donor, TRZ acceptor, and alkynyl linker. These isomers yield six distinct single crystal forms, each exhibiting unique packing structures, emission properties, and mechanical responses. Flexible crystals consistently display C≡C···π-hole contacts that extend into alkynyl-directed interaction networks, whereas the non-flexible crystals lack this topology. The results demonstrate that specific intermolecular interactions can generate emergent crystal-level mechanical behavior through their geometric organization and propagation across the lattice. Remarkably, the flexible crystals retain their mechanical adaptability at 77 K, with persistent phosphorescence. These results establish a molecular-tocrystal design principle in which alkynyl-directed C≡C···π-hole interactions organize crystal packing to generate emergent cryogenic elasticity and persistent phosphorescence.

papers.title: Solid-state synthesis of high-purity mixed-chalcogenide perovskites
papers.abstract: Recently, chalcogenide perovskites that are fully inorganic and composed of earth-abundant elements are emerging as non-toxic alternatives to established lead-halide perovskite materials. However, chalcogenide perovskite compositions relevant for optoelectronic applications such as solar cells remain largely unexplored due to the complex, high-temperature synthesis routes involved and difficulties in obtaining high purities. Here, we present a new solid-state synthesis route for facile fabrication of mixed-chalcogenide perovskite powders BaZr(S 1−x Se x ) 3 , where 0 ≤ x ≤ 0.3. We obtain high-purity chalcogenide perovskite powders at moderate temperatures (600 ◦ C) and short reaction times (24 hours). We demonstrate that precursor selection and chalcogen stoichiometry can effectively be used to control the perovskite composition. By increasing Se content (x), the band gaps of the mixed-chalcogenide perovskites can be controllably tuned from 1.83 to 1.58 eV, spanning the desired range for single-and multi-junction solar cells. Broadly, our findings establish a generalisable synthesis method for preparing several mixed-chalcogenide perovskite compositions, including BaZr(S 1−x Se x ) 3 and BaHf(S 1−x Se x ) 3 .

papers.title: Super Sensitization Near-Infrared Ln-MOF with ultra high quantum yield 19.51% as Ratiometric Temperature Sensing Platform
papers.abstract: ： Temperature sensing plays a pivotal role in environmental, biomedical, and industrial applications. While most luminescence-based sensors operate in the visible spectrum, their effectiveness is limited in scenarios requiring deep tissue penetration or low background interference. Near-infrared (NIR) luminescence sensing address these limitations yet its development is hampered by low quantum yields and severe thermal quenching of rare-earthdoped materials. These limitations lead to sensing instability across broad temperature ranges, compromising their real-time monitoring capabilities in complex environments. In this work, we report a Yb3+/Nd3+ dual-emission rare-earth MOF integrated with Au nanoparticles to harness surface plasmon resonance (SPR) effects. By synergistically combining SPR-induced electromagnetic field enhancement with fluorinated ligands that effectively suppress vibrational quenching, the quantum yield was enhanced from 11.32% to 19.51%, enabling stable, high-sensitivity near-infrared temperature sensing across a wide operational window 2 / 39 covering 78-348 K. This strategy effectively addresses long-standing trade-offs between quantum efficiency and thermal stability, providing a generalizable platform for high-precision thermal sensing in biomedical and catalytic systems.

papers.title: Computer Learning Can Streamline Development of Lipid Nanoparticle Vaccine Delivery Constructs
papers.abstract: Lipid nanoparticle (LNP) delivery constructs provide a precise and targeted therapeutic platform for nucleic-acid and subunit vaccines. By shielding fragile antigens and genetic cargo from premature degradation, these constructs help vaccines overcome the physiological barriers that separate an injection site from its intracellular target, increasing specificity, potency, and the precision of controlled release. This capability has broadened the range of immunomodulatory targets in the fight against infectious disease and has opened the door to vaccines that treat tumors and cancer. Increasingly, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are being applied to predict the LNP formulations that maximize mRNA-vaccine efficacy, and the same computational strategies are now being extended across diverse vaccine modalities. By approximating in vivo pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics, in silico methods promote rational, data-driven design that is reshaping the drug-development pipeline. In this Review we summarize current literature on the optimization of LNP delivery constructs for vaccine therapeutics using ML, survey the rapid clinical translation of LNP-mRNA technology since 2021, and discuss the limitations and predictive capabilities of computer-simulated experimental models.

papers.title: Lighting the Way to Sustainability with Refractory Plasmonic Materials
papers.abstract: The search for plasmonic materials that combine strong light-matter interactions with stability under demanding operating conditions has driven growing interest in transition metal nitrides and carbides. These refractory materials offer tunable optical properties, thermal and chemical stability, and diverse electronic structures that distinguish them from conventional noble-metal plasmonic materials. This Review examines the development of refractory plasmonic materials from their fundamental photophysical properties and synthesis to their use in water-energy systems, climate-resilient infrastructure, and solar-driven chemical transformations. Attention is given to how composition, stoichiometry, particle morphology, and surface chemistry influence localized surface plasmon resonance, hot-carrier dynamics, and photothermal conversion. We critically assess the sustainability of refractory plasmonics beyond noble-metal replacement, considering resource availability and criticality, synthesis and processing requirements, material complexity, and functional lifetime. Finally, we outline key challenges and emerging opportunities in positioning refractory plasmonic materials as the cornerstone of a sustainable economy.

papers.title: Chiral Doping of Two-Dimensional Molecular Crystals for Circularly Polarized Photodetection
papers.abstract: 2 Abstract Circularly polarized (CP) photodetection is essential for applications such as quantum communication, biomedical imaging, and secure optical encryption. Direct CP photodetection using chiral organic materials has attracted growing interest owing to their structural tunability and solution processability; however, it requires both strong chiroptical response and efficient charge transport. Two-dimensional molecular crystals (2DMCs) are attractive photoactive systems with ordered molecular packing and favorable charge transport, but lack intrinsic chirality. Here, we develop a chiral doping strategy to introduce chiroptical activity into 2DMCs for efficient CP photodetection. An achiral diphenyl-substituted boron–nitrogen-embedded anthracene derivative bearing hexyl side chains is designed as the host, while chiral molecules with the same conjugated backbone and chiral side chains serve as dopants. The resulting doped films combine chiroptical response with ordered molecular packing. The corresponding phototransistor devices exhibit favorable charge transport and ultraviolet CP photodetection performance, with a maximum mobility of 0.45 cm 2 V −1 s −1 , a maximum responsivity of 8.2×10 2 A W −1 , and an average photocurrent dissymmetry factor of 0.17, representing competitive performance among reported direct organic CP phototransistors. Furthermore, CPlight-based information encoding and decoding are demonstrated. This strategy endows 2DMCs with chiroptical activity, providing a platform for CP photodetection and chiral optoelectronic applications.

papers.title: Nanodiscs can preferentially enrich transmembrane proteins in a bottom-up proteomic analysis workflow
papers.abstract: Membrane proteins are critically important pharmaceutical targets and thus their analytical characterization is vital to drug development efforts. However, compared to cytosolic proteins, membrane proteins are generally more difficult to purify and/or analytically characterize in part due to their amphipathic nature. Nanodiscs (NDs) have become a popular membrane mimetic system offering a well-defined lipid bilayer environment to stabilize membrane proteins for in vitro analyses. NDs based on membrane scaffold proteins (MSPs) offer advantages in terms of their amenability to purification and control over lipid composition. Here we investigated the utility of MSP NDs having different diameters and lipid compositions to enrich membrane proteins isolated from cells for bottom-up proteomic characterization. Specifically, we coupled a robust ND formation and purification workflow with liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) analysis to determine the identity and relative abundance of proteins incorporated into NDs made using different synthesis conditions. We found that the ND diameter had an effect on the relative enrichment of detected proteins and protein classes; however, lipid composition did not have a significant effect. The data indicated that this ND-based approach selectively allowed for the detection of membrane proteins and membrane associated proteins over cytosolic protein contaminants. Furthermore, we found that transmembrane proteins, which are particularly hard to extract and analyze using traditional membrane mimetics, were significantly enriched when using NDs compared to detergent micelles. These results suggest that MSP ND-based approaches could be applied to the selective enrichment of membrane proteins from cells in a manner that could be enabling for both proteomic and other analytical characterization approaches.

papers.title: Reversing Benzene Bioisosterism through Photocatalytically Divergent Double Strain-Release Skeletal Remodeling
papers.abstract: Highly functionalized two-dimensional molecular frameworks are vital in drug discovery, but their regioselective synthesis remains challenging. Here, we present a photocatalytic method that reverses the conventional paradigm of replacing planar aromatic rings with three-dimensional C(sp3)-rich bioisosteres. Instead, this technique converts bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) back into highly functionalized benzenes. This process creates a reversible link between three-dimensional and planar chemical spaces via divergent double-strain-release steps. By tuning the photocatalyst to favor either energy transfer or electron transfer pathways, distinct regioselective skeletal rearrangements were achieved from common BCB precursors. The method works with many functional groups and substitution patterns, enabling direct synthesis of densely functionalized benzenes that are otherwise difficult to produce regioselectively. Combined experimental and computational data revealed the reaction mechanisms in which photoinduced energy or electron transfer produces intermediates that undergo strain release and radical rearrangement in sequence. These results demonstrate strain-release skeletal remodeling as a way to switch between three-dimensional and planar chemical spaces, providing a complementary strategy to traditional benzene bioisosterism.

papers.title: Computational corroboration, at the sign level, that R-phenibut is the GABA-B eutomer: a two-sided alchemical transfer free-energy validation
papers.abstract: Phenibut (β‑phenyl‑γ‑aminobutyric acid) is taken as a racemate, but its two enantiomers are not equivalent at its principal target, the GABA‑B receptor complex. This study asks one narrow question: which enantiomer is the eutomer at GABA‑B, and can a physics‑based relative binding free energy (RBFE) method answer it within a stated uncertainty? Calculations used the open‑source Alchemical Transfer Method (ATM) in AToM‑OpenMM at the orthosteric site of the 4MS4 Venus‑flytrap domain, on a 22‑state λ‑ladder with replica exchange and autocorrelation-corrected UWHAM estimation. The method was licensed on a two‑sided edge first: R‑phenibut → arbaclofen (H→Cl) returned ΔΔG = −1.890 ± 0.368 kcal/mol against a measured bracket of ≈ −1.6 to −2.0, correct in sign and inside the bracket. That edge is a substitution, not a stereoinversion, so no enantiomer edge here is validated two‑sided. Three independent seeds are reported as separate rows andarenot averaged: ΔΔG(R→S) =+1.673± 0.321,+0.633±0.302 and+0.783±0.304 kcal/mol. All three are positive, soR‑phenibut is theeutomer at GABA‑B. The claim is the sign, not the magnitude. The magnitude moves the other way. Seeds 2 and 3 agree to 0.150 kcal/mol while seed 1, the first completed, lies about 1 kcal/mol above both and is the one that does not replicate. The between‑seed scatter (SD 0.562) exceeds every individual corrected error, so single‑run bars understate the true uncertainty; two pre‑registered tests for a sampling defect in seed 1 both returned negative, so the spread is carried as genuine between‑run variance. Against the one‑sided experimental floor ΔΔG ≥ +1.42 kcal/mol, seeds 2, 3 and the three‑seed mean (+1.03) fall below, so the protocol under‑predicts the magnitude. With zero completed λ round trips these ± are statistical‑only lower bounds that exclude force‑field error, and the seeds share one force field, one protonation assignment and one receptor structure, so the sign rests most firmly on the experiment together with the validation edge. The same machinery fails at phenibut’s second target, α2δ‑1. The H→Cl edge is wrong‑signed (−0.805 ± 0.303 against experimental +1.13), and a gabapentin → pregabalin control lands at +12.846 ± 0.449 against an expected≈−0.21—a ~13 kcal/mol miss that passes every standard convergence gate. An initial attribution to a broken λ‑ladder splice did not survive a direct test of the saved trajectories and is withdrawn; the failure mechanism is unresolved. No α2δ‑1 number is biology, and no two‑target sign‑inversion claim is made. The contribution is the pairing: a licensed regime and a documented‑failure regime, each reported with its full uncertainty.

papers.title: Chemical Structures Cleaning Center: An Open Web Service for Automated Chemical Databases Curation
papers.abstract: Chemical database curation is an essential step in chemoinformatics workflows. Omitting this process or using inadequate curation protocols adversely affects structure-dependent computational methods that rely on high-quality data, such as quantitative structure–activity relationship models, physicochemical property prediction, and molecular similarity calculations. Although database curation is compulsory as machine learning, chemoinformatics, and computational chemistry in general rely on data quality, existing public databases curation pipelines are predominantly developed in coding environments like Python and hosted on different servers. While efficient, these tools often present a steep learning curve for researchers without programming expertise or domain specialists seeking to integrate chemoinformatics into their projects. To bridge this gap, herein we present Chemical Structures Cleaning Center, an automated, user-friendly, and open-access web application designed for streamlining chemical database curation. The tool builds upon well-validated and used protocols to curate chemical libraries. To illustrate the platform's utility, we used a small chemical database containing reference compounds to test various pipeline tasks, such as counterion desalting, duplicate detection, small-molecule salt handling, preservation of complex stereochemical integrity, and reduction of metal-organic salts. The curation pipeline provides references to relevant manuscripts highlighting the importance of chemical database curation. The web page is freely available at https://huggingface.co/spaces/Dannmarquez16/Chemical-Structures-Cleaning-Center

papers.title: A Reported Featurizer Ranking Instability Is Noise Between Inseparable Arms
papers.abstract: Representation comparisons are commonly published from one split at one seed on uncurated public sets. Repeating one, the count of endpoints whose best featurizer changes with the split read three, one, one and three under two choices, seeds and deduplication, and every reorder lay between arms whose intervals overlap. Only the fingerprint baseline separated anywhere, by being worse; duplicates placed up to 3.8% of random-split test rows in training. A four-step remedy is given.

papers.title: Cationic Conductive Aluminum Metal-Organic Framework Couples Ion Exchange and Redox Chemistry for Oxyanion Detoxification
papers.abstract: We report Al-HOTP, [Al 3 (HOTP) 2 (H 2 O) 6 ][Al 3 (HOTP)(H 2 O) 12 ] (SO 4 ) 2 (HOTP = 2,3,6,7,10,11-hexaoxytriphenylene), a cationic two-dimensional electrically conductive metal-organic framework (MOF) that couples counterion-exchange chemistry with a redox-active framework for oxyanion capture and detoxification. While triphenylene-based honeycomb conductive frameworks are well established, the Al-based analog reported here is, to the best of our knowledge, the first of its kind, and demonstrates how cationic ion-exchange chemistry can be combined with framework-mediated redox activity for multifunctional water remediation. Al-HOTP efficiently removes permanganate (MnO 4 − ) and dichromate (Cr 2 O 7 2− ) from water while promoting their conversion to lower-valent, less toxic Mn(IV)- and Cr(III)-containing species. The framework removes approximately 95% of MnO 4 − and 90% of Cr 2 O 7 2− from 30 ppm solutions within 5 min and exhibits an experimentally demonstrated uptake capacity of up to 1600 mg g −1 for MnO 4 − and 300 mg g −1 for Cr 2 O 7 2− . To the best of our knowledge, the MnO 4 − adsorption capacity is the highest reported for a MOF-based permanganate adsorbent. Mechanistic studies support a cooperative capture-and-reduction mechanism in which sulfate-to-oxyanion exchange promotes initial uptake, followed by electron transfer from the redox-active HOTP ligands to the captured oxyanions. The resulting framework oxidation increases the demand for charge-compensating anions, enabling additional uptake beyond the initial sulfate-exchange capacity. Beyond batch uptake, Al-HOTP maintains efficient contaminant removal over 36 consecutive filtration passes and can be integrated into an FTO-based electrode for proof-of-concept electrochemical detection of both oxyanions. Overall, this work establishes the coupling of permanent cationic character with framework redox activity as a design strategy for integrating high-capacity capture, reductive detoxification, regeneration, and device functionality for multifunctional water remediation.

papers.title: EVALUATING MOLECULAR DYNAMICS FRAMES FOR BINDING AFFINITY PREDICTION AND VIRTUAL SCREENING
papers.abstract: Motivation: Machine-learning scoring functions are typically trained on static crystallographic structures, although protein-ligand recognition is inherently dynamic. It remains unclear whether MD derived conformations provide transferable information or instead shift the training data away from experimentally observed binding geometries. Results: We generated 20 ns molecular dynamics trajectories for 2,502 protein–ligand complexes and evaluated five scoring function architectures trained on crystallographic structures and MD-derived frames using four different sampling protocols. Across the CASF-2016 and CASF-2013 affinity benchmarks, MD-only training generally reduced predictive performance, whereas augmenting crystallographic structures with MD data improved four of the five architectures. Averaged across models, benchmarks, and sampling protocols, augmentation increased PCC by 0.072 and reduced RMSE by 0.165 relative to MD-only training. A nearest-neighbor analysis showed that the benefits of augmen-tation were not restricted to complexes similar to frames, arguing against a simple similarity-based explanation. The results suggest improvements were connected with exposing models to controlled structural perturbations around experimentally observed binding poses. Overall, MD conformations were most effective as augmentation rather than replacement for crystallographic training data. Availability: MD frames used for model training are available at: (https://zenodo.org/ records/20443988).

papers.title: Stochastic Trace Estimation Method for Ring-Polymer Instanton Theory
papers.abstract: Evaluation of the fluctuation factor can become a computational bottleneck in ringpolymer instanton calculations, particularly at low temperatures where large numbers of ring-polymer beads are required. Conventional evaluation involves diagonalization of the full ring-polymer Hessian, with a computational cost that scales as O(P 3D3) for P beads and D physical dimensions. Here, we develop a matrix-free stochastic trace estimation approach that avoids full Hessian diagonalization. The log-determinant entering the fluctuation factor is evaluated using stochastic Lanczos quadrature, while a preconditioned Davidson algorithm is used to obtain the required low-lying eigenpairs. Control-variate and subspace-projection techniques are used to reduce the variance and improve the efficiency of the stochastic estimator. The approach is tested for proton transfer in malonaldehyde, the CH4 +H → CH3 +H2 hydrogen-abstraction reaction, and intramolecular proton transfer in dinitro-HBQ. For these systems, the calculated log(Finst) agrees with full diagonalization to within an absolute error of ≈ 0.1, while the variance is reduced by up to approximately two orders of magnitude. The matrixfree formulation shows O(P ) to O(P logP ) scaling with bead number, providing a practical alternative to full diagonalization when large numbers of ring-polymer beads are required and potentially facilitating applications to larger molecular systems.

papers.title: AI-Driven Optimization of Electrochemical Fertilizer Processes
papers.abstract: Conventional fertilizer production relies on centralized, fossil-fuel-intensive processes such as Haber–Bosch ammonia synthesis, with high energy demand and associated carbon emissions. Electrochemical routes to nitrogen and phosphorus fertilizers offer a potentially decentralized, renewable-powered alternative, but their practical performance remains limited by the interaction of catalyst structure, electrolyte composition, reactor architecture, and operating conditions. These variables do not act independently: fertilizer synthesis is fundamentally a coupled, high-dimensional optimization problem that is difficult to address by varying one factor at a time. This chapter argues that artificial intelligence becomes genuinely useful for this problem not as an isolated computational tool, but as a layer connecting experimental and sensor data with prediction, optimization, and control. The chapter examines four electrochemical fertilizer pathways nitrogen reduction, nitrate reduction, urea synthesis, and phosphorus recovery alongside the functional materials and electrode architectures used to catalyze them. It then considers the reactors, analytical instrumentation, and real-time, in-situ sensors that generate the data on which these AI applications depend, treating this measurement infrastructure as inseparable from AI-enabled optimization. Three distinct roles for AI and machine learning are developed: discovering and screening catalyst candidates across combinatorial design spaces; predicting process behavior under coupled and time-varying operating conditions; and identifying and maintaining optimal conditions through Bayesian optimization, multi-objective search, and autonomous control. Techno-economic and life-cycle assessment are introduced as additional decision criteria, since chemical performance alone cannot define an optimal process once cost and environmental impact are considered. A fully integrated, autonomous electrochemical fertilizer platform has not yet been demonstrated in the literature reviewed here. Instead, the chapter shows that individual components of such a system, together with several partial integrations from adjacent process industries, already exist and provide a technically credible foundation for future integration. Data scarcity, the DFT–experiment gap, sensor reliability, reproducibility, interpretability, and scale-up nevertheless remain major barriers to realizing this integration in practice.

papers.title: Direct generation of a prototypical n-pentyl peroxy radical reveals how mixedfate chemical regimes shape product distributions
papers.abstract: Organic peroxy radicals (RO2) are key branch points in atmospheric oxidation with competing fates in the troposphere: reaction with NO, reaction with HO2, self-/cross-reaction with another RO2, and isomerization. RO2 often react in mixed-fate regimes, yielding product distributions with a complex dependence on reactivity conditions. In traditional environmental chamber experiments, not all RO2 fates are equally accessible, and chemical regimes favoring RO2 self-/cross-reactions and isomerizations are poorly characterized. Here, we access these conditions in an environmental chamber via 1-iodopentane photolysis, monitoring product distributions with NH4 + chemical ionization mass spectrometry. We tune the relative importance of these reaction pathways by varying the initial conditions, spanning bimolecular lifetimes from ~100-2000 s. Across conditions, the major observed C5 product, C5H10O3 (~40-60% yield), requires at least one RO2 isomerization to form, demonstrating the importance of downstream RO2 unimolecular reactions even if they are not the major fate of upstream RO2. Model mechanisms partially reproduce observed product distributions but cannot quantitatively capture variations with changing RO2 fate. Discrepancies suggest poorly-understood RO2 cross-reactions substantially influence product distributions. Conditions favoring RO2 isomerization unintuitively enhance both fragmentation and accretion via downstream functionalized alkoxy and peroxy radical chemistry. Results illuminate important gaps in existing atmospheric reaction mechanisms when predicting product distributions in mixed-fate chemical regimes.

papers.title: Atomic Chalcogen Substitution Modulates Photophysical Properties and Electronic Structure in Donor–Acceptor Covalent Organic Frameworks
papers.abstract: While chalcogen substitution has recently emerged as a means for tuning the properties of covalent organic frameworks (COFs), its influence on the intrinsic photophysical and charge-transport properties of isoreticular donor–acceptor COFs remains largely unknown. Here, an isoreticular series of novel donor–acceptor COFs was constructed from a tetrathienonaphthalene-based (TTNTA) node and linear donor–acceptor–donor linkers containing oxygen (O), sulfur (S), or selenium (Se) within their acceptor cores. Highly crystalline COFs with identical topology and comparable structural order were obtained, while the synthesis of preferentially oriented thin films enabled direct comparison of chalcogen-dependent optoelectronic properties. Time-resolved photoluminescence measurements revealed progressively shorter emissive-state lifetimes from the O- to the S- and Se-containing COFs. Optical-pump terahertz-probe spectroscopy showed a parallel decrease in effective charge-carrier mobility across the same series, with the O-containing COF exhibiting the highest value of 0.19 ±0.02 cm 2 V −1 s −1 . Density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent DFT calculations further revealed that valence-band dispersion originates from coupling between TTNTA- and linker-derived states and that the low-energy absorption involves linker-centered mixed excitations with progressively decreasing oscillator strength from O to Se. Collectively, these findings establish systematic structure–property relationships between acceptor-core chalcogen substitution and the photophysical and electronic properties of donor–acceptor COFs, providing mechanistic insights into their composition-dependent behavior and guidance for the design of future COF-based semiconductors.

papers.title: Direct Observation of Ligand Exchange Dynamics on Atomically Precise Gold Clusters
papers.abstract: Ligand exchange reactions provide a route to modify the monolayers of atomically precise gold clusters, but the structural dynamics of the process remain poorly understood. In this work, we use collision-initiated direct dynamics driven by a semiempirical electronic-structure method to study ligand exchange on Au38(PET)24, where PET denotes 2-phenylethanethiolate. The incoming ligands are thiophenol and two para-substituted derivatives, each considered in both its thiol and thiophenolate forms. The trajectories resolve the proposed associative mechanism as a sequence of ligand addition and elimination, followed by substantial restructuring of the core-monolayer interface and incorporation of the incoming ligand into the monolayer. The displaced PET ligand remains associated with the cluster, making desorption a distinct subsequent step required to form fully separated products. Comparisons among the incoming ligands show that both protonation state and para substitution influence how far the trajectories progress. These simulations provide a direct atomistic view of ligand exchange and show that the process involves extensive reorganization of the cluster–monolayer interface.

papers.title: GXNU MolStudio: An Integrated Open-Source Platform for Molecular Visualization and Quantum Chemical Analysis
papers.abstract: We report GXNU MolStudio, an open-source, bilingual (Chinese/English) desktop application that integrates real-time molecular visualization with a broad suite of quantum chemical analyses in a single interactive environment. MolStudio embeds a purpose-built OpenGL 3.3 renderer that presents molecules, orbitals, and property-colored isosurfaces in a publication-ready style, and couples it to scripted invocations of the external wavefunction analysis program Multiwfn. The current version provides 14 panels (11 analysis panels plus 3 workflow panels) covering: orbital browsing and isosurface generation (including spin-density visualization for open-shell systems); six atomic charge schemes (ADCH, Hirshfeld, Mulliken, CM5, SCPA, and VDD); Mayer bond orders; NBO donor–acceptor (E(2)) analysis; electrostatic potential (ESP) surfaces with extrema and surface-area distributions; IGMH/IRI weak-interaction analysis; QTAIM topology; ETS-NOCV energy decomposition; molecular planarity parameters (MPP); IRC energy/bond-order profiles; distortion–interaction (DI) decomposition; the energetic span model (ESM); and activation strain scans along the IRC (ASM), multi-CUB overlay, and IRC splitting. All panels share one canvas and one atomic-picking protocol, so that results from different analyses can be compared immediately on the same structure. A retained VMD/Tachyon channel delivers ray-traced journal-quality figures in more than 30 curated styles. MolStudio is distributed as Python source (PyQt5, Python ≥ 3.8) and as a standalone Windows executable, under the GNU General Public License, version 3 (GPLv3only). Its rendering pipeline is a Python port of the GPLv3-licensed IboView engine — a derivative relationship that is declared explicitly in Section 7 and itemized in the code repository — and all third-party components are credited. The software is freely available at https://cnb.cool/chem311/GXNU-MolStudio.

papers.title: Programmable aggregation of photosensitizer in multi- organelles for cancer therapy
papers.abstract: The precise spatiotemporal control of subcellular drug distribution remains a central therapeutic challenge. Here, a stimulus-responsive aggregation-induced emission (AIE) photosensitizer (TBPBB) is utilized to achieve controllable aggregation switching between two distinct organelles that enables sequential dual-organelle destruction. Actively delivered to tumors by hypoxia-tropic Bacillus subtilis, TBPBB first aggregates at mitochondria, generating reactive oxygen species (ROS) under light exposure, triggering bond cleavage to form a second AIE species (TBP) that re-aggregates at lipid droplets and generates ROS more efficiently. The sequential targeting and destruction of dual organelles, together with ROS-triggered bacterial lysis, induce ferroptosis, apoptosis and antitumor immunity, collectively amplifying therapeutic efficacy. In a breast cancer model, this system achieves a 92.4% tumour growth inhibition with negligible organ toxicity. This paradigm establishes a generalizable strategy for programmable aggregation of therapeutic agents and multi-organelle destruction, readily adaptable to other organelle pairs by substituting the stimuli-responsive moieties or targeting fragments.

papers.title: High-Field Spin Dynamics of Photoexcited Pentacene at 9.2 T by Time-Resolved Pulsed EPR and Vector DC Magnetic-Field Sensing
papers.abstract: Photoexcited triplet spin states of pentacene molecules are promising for dynamic nuclear polarization (DNP) and quantum sensing, yet their spin properties at high magnetic fields remain largely unexplored. Here, we study the high field spin dynamics of the photoexcited pentacene using highfrequency time-resolved pulsed electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) at 260 GHz (∼ 9.2 T). Using pulsed EPR synchronized with optical excitation, we determine triplet sublevel populations, decay rates, spin relaxations, and the g-tensor. The transient triplet remains a strongly non-Boltzmann sublevel population, with a dominant |TX⟩ population of 0.86 ± 0.05, while the triplet lifetimes, spin-lattice relaxation, and coherence remain favorable for triplet-DNP and quantum sensing applications. We further develop a vector DC magnetic-field sensing protocol that combines the transition resonances of the two crystallographically inequivalent pentacene sites with orientation-dependent triplet decay to determine the field magnitude and orientation. These results establish the high-field spin properties of photoexcited pentacene and provide a foundation for its triplet-DNP and quantum sensing at high magnetic fields.

papers.title: Accessing an Extreme Steric Regime of C–O Atropisomerism through Overcrowded Iodane-Mediated Rearrangement
papers.abstract: C–O atropisomerism in aryl ethers is intrinsically difficult to stabilize because oxygen provides limited steric leverage and the two C–O bonds may undergo concerted rotation (gearing). Here, we report that the reaction of an overcrowded (diacetoxyiodo)arene with cyclic 1,3-diketones generates aryliodonium ylides that undergo spontaneous rearrangement to furnish highly congested atropisomeric aryl vinyl ethers. These compounds occupy a previously unexplored steric regime of C–O atropisomerism and display configurational stability that strongly depends on the cyclic 1,3-diketone framework. Whereas the cyclopentane-1,3-dione derivative exhibits an enantiomerization barrier of 32.9 kcal mol–1, the corresponding cyclohexane-1,3-dione and dimedone derivatives reach barriers approaching 40 kcal mol–1. The alkenyl C–I bond serves as both a major contributor to atropostability and a synthetic handle for systematic modulation of the enantiomerization barrier through deiodination and cross-coupling. Computational studies revealed a striking energetic separation between gearing and enantiomerization. Even in this extreme steric regime, gearing remains accessible with barriers of ~15 kcal mol–1 and is only weakly affected by the iodine substituent, whereas enantiomerization requires substantially higher-energy rotational pathways. These findings provide a mechanistic picture of molecular motion under extreme steric constraints and establish overcrowded iodanemediated rearrangement as a route to previously inaccessible C–O atropisomeric architectures.

papers.title: Suberin-Cutin inspired copolyester films as bio-based packaging materials
papers.abstract: Fossil-based plastics are widely used in packaging because of their low cost, processability, and exceptional barrier performance. However, their nonrenewable origin, short lifespan, and resistance to degradation in the environment present major challenges. Suberin and cutin are two types of biopolyesters found in plants, which can be used as renewable feedstock for the synthesis of bio-based plastics. Here, we extracted suberin monomers from birch bark and combined them with two building-blocks monomers found in cutin; a long chain ω-hydroxy fatty acid and a diacid, to produce cross-linked semi crystalline polyester films by melt polycondensation and thermoforming. Increasing the cutin monomer content promoted crystallization and increased the films’ stiffness and strength. Additionally, it reduced water vapor transmission rates and oxygen permeability, reaching properties comparable to short chain polyesters such as polylactide and poly ε-caprolactone. All films blocked the UV radiation below 400 nm. The resulting properties highlight suberin/cutin-based plastics as a potential future green packaging material.

papers.title: MACHINE LEARNING FOR CELLULOSE MEMBRANES: A REPRESENTATION–MODEL–TASK FRAMEWORK FOR SMALL-DATA REGIMES
papers.abstract: Cellulose membranes are a small-data problem with a chemically ambiguous object. A polymorphic matrix, three chemically inequivalent hydroxyls at C2, C3 and C6, and a two-stage fabrication route make representation — not model architecture — the binding constraint on machine learning in this field, and this is why the toolkit that succeeded for gas-separation polymers and thin-film-composite membranes does not transfer to cellulose unchanged. This review organises the methodology around that claim. It first sets out why cellulose membranes remain of interest and where they fail, then shows that the existing computational treatment of cellulose is stratified into layers — first-principles, atomistic, coarse-grained, pore-scale, phenomenological, process-level — that do not connect, so that no chain of models runs from a synthesis recipe to a measured permeance. That specific structural gap, rather than the absence of cellulose studies in the machine-learning literature, is the argument for a data-driven approach. The representation–model–task framework is then executed task by task across property prediction, synthesis optimisation with Bayesian optimisation, inverse design, microstructural analysis and fouling forecasting, with four mandatory decisions — representation, model, task, validation — made explicit for each, and interpretability treated as a validation instrument whose attributions are falsifiable by synthesis. Cellulose/iron-oxide composites for oil–water separation serve as a running example throughout. Data resources are assessed for cellulose coverage rather than catalogued; methodological pitfalls are given cellulose-specific manifestations and mitigations; and under-explored niches are classified by operational criteria under a stated, repeatable search protocol.

papers.title: Switching from orthosteric to allosteric inhibition: Discovery of N-aryl-1H-azaindole-derived allosteric
papers.abstract: The cytosolic protein tyrosine phosphatase SHP2 is an emerging therapeutic target due to its central role in oncogenic receptor tyrosine kinase and immune checkpoint signaling. Although allosteric SHP2 inhibitors have entered clinical trials, they often lack efficacy as single agents and display reduced potency against activated SHP2 mutants. New allosteric SHP2 inhibitor chemotypes and a deeper understanding of allosteric SHP2 modulation are therefore needed. Herein, we report N -aryl-1 H -azaindazoles as a novel class of allosteric SHP2 inhibitors. A scaffold-hopping strategy led to the conversion of an orthosteric SHP2 inhibitor into an allosteric inhibitor. Structure-activity relationship studies, including a systematic investigation of the scaffold, led to the identification of compound 67 . Compound 67 inhibits SHP2 through an exclusively allosteric mechanism and shows potent activity across various cancer cell lines, including AML cells overexpressing the activated SHP2 E76K mutant. X-ray crystallography and computational analyses elucidated key molecular determinants underlying the steep structureactivity relationships of this inhibitor series, providing a structural basis for further optimization.

papers.title: Hidden Diversity in Myxobacterial Lasso Peptides: An Atypical RiPP Recognition Element and Host-Mediated Loss of the Lasso Tail
papers.abstract: Cystonodins and soranginodins are the first lasso peptides identified from the phylum Myxococcota and reveal unexpected diversity in lasso peptide biosynthesis. Whereas the soranginodin pathways combine canonical fused RREproteases with precursor peptides retaining the YxxP motif, the cystonodin pathway contains McyB, a functional fused RRE-protease with a shortened N-terminal domain that adopts an atypical RRE architecture, retaining the characteristic β-sheets but lacking much of the canonical αhelical region. A targeted bioinformatic survey of apparent standalone lasso proteases identified 52 cryptic RREprotease fusions; subsequent structural analysis revealed both typical and atypical fused RREs architectures, exposing a blind spot in RRE detection and BGC annotation. We additionally identified several C-terminally truncated cystonodin congeners, including an unprecedented tail-less variant consisting solely of the macrolactam ring. In vitro reconstitution and biochemical characterization implicate endogenous host protease(s) in these cleavage events. Together, these findings highlight the value of integrating structural information into genome-mining workflows and expose host-dependent remodelling as a potential pitfall of

papers.title: Modulating Phoretic Interactions through Molecular Recognition
papers.abstract: Molecular recognition allows living systems to convert chemical information into physical behavior. Synthetic active matter lacks an analogous mechanism by which chemical information modulates phoretic interactions, which are determined instead by physicochemical properties. Here, we harness host-guest chemistry within coordination cages to enable the transduction of molecular recognition into non-equilibrium responses. We employ guest molecules as chemical signals which tune a tracer’s zeta potential upon binding within cages adsorbed to the particle interface. Phoretic mobility of these tracers is controlled via ionic diffusiophoresis. Experiments across multiple guests reveal a direct relationship between binding affinity, surface potential, and interaction sign, i.e. convergence toward or divergence away from the center of a gradient. We also present a predictive theoretical framework that quantitatively maps guest properties onto the sign and magnitude of phoretic interactions. These results establish molecular recognition as a chemical code for modulating interactions in active matter.

papers.title: Solid-Phase Standard Enthalpies of Formation from SMILES with a Calibrated Per-Molecule Uncertainty: Application to a 13 606-Compound CHONFCl Inventory
papers.abstract: The standard enthalpy of formation of a solid, ∆fH ◦(s, 298 K), governs the detonation performance and the thermal hazard of an energetic material, yet it is measured for only a few hundred compounds, and 30 % of the compounds measured more than once carry determinations that disagree by more than 20 kJ mol−1. I report a route from a SMILES string to ∆fH ◦(s, 298 K) that returns, together with the value, a molecule-specific standard deviation calibrated against experiment. The gas-phase enthalpy is obtained from the ANI-2x neural network potential evaluated on a connectivity-based hierarchy (CBH-2, with CBH-1 fallback) isodesmic balance in which the nitro group is treated as a single pseudo-atom, without which the balance cannot be closed on a charge-separated nitrogen; a rigid-rotor harmonic-oscillator correction supplies the thermal terms. The sublimation enthalpy is a 32-descriptor additive model fitted to 229 measurements harvested from the NIST Chemistry WebBook. Two systematic shifts that survive leave-one-out validation are removed. The uncertainty is a heteroscedastic Gaussian variance model. The whole chain is validated by a nested leave-one-out procedure in which the sublimation model, the acceptance threshold, the systematic shifts and the variance model are all re-estimated without the compound they predict, and that compound’s own gas-phase reference is withheld: over 281 compounds the mean absolute error is 26.1 kJ mol−1, the mean |z| is 0.80 against 0.80 expected for a well-calibrated Gaussian, and the coverage is 71.2 % at one standard deviation and 93.6 % at two, against 68.3 % and 95.4 % expected. For scale, independent experimental determinations of the same solid deviate from their own median by 7.6 kJ mol−1 on average, so two determinations of one compound typically differ by about twice that. The procedure was applied to an inventory of 13 606 CHONFCl compounds; 13 267 (97.5 %) were predicted in 314 core-hours on a single desktop machine, the remainder being open-shell radicals outside the domain of ANI-2x. I state explicitly, and quantify, the size beyond which the uncertainty model itself extrapolates.

papers.title: Hypervelocity impact mass spectrometry enables membrane phospholipid detection in ocean-world plumes
papers.abstract: Saturn's ocean moon Enceladus and Jupiter's moon Europa expel subsurface material into space, enabling direct sampling of potentially habitable ocean environments without landing on their surfaces. Previous spacecraft analyses of plume ice grains revealed salts, simple organic compounds, and degraded macromolecular material, but no unambiguous molecular biosignatures. A fundamental question is whether diagnostic components of living cells can survive hypervelocity impact ionization during spacecraft flyby sampling. Here, we demonstrate that phospholipid membranes produce distinct and diagnostic negative-ion signatures following hypervelocity impacts of nanometer-sized ice particles at velocities up to 3.7 km s⁻¹. Using artificial vesicles composed of the phospholipid 1-palmitoyl-2-oleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine (POPC), we obtained single-particle time-of-flight mass spectra containing characteristic phosphate-derived and fatty-acid fragment ions together with higher-mass species. Assignments were supported by collision-induced dissociation measurements using high-resolution Orbitrap mass spectrometry. The persistence of these membrane-specific anions demonstrates that hypervelocity impact ionization preserves molecular signatures diagnostic of phospholipid bilayers, identifying cell membranes or their components as a detectable class of biosignatures for plume-sampling missions. Our results provide an experimental framework for interpreting complex negative-ion spectra from future ocean-world missions, including Europa Clipper and proposed Enceladus missions, and highlight the scientific value of high-resolution negative-ion impact mass spectrometry for the search for extraterrestrial life.

papers.title: Influence of Electrode Potential on Biased Reaction Sampling: NVT, NVTΦ or µVT?
papers.abstract: Incorporating applied electrode potential into density functional theory molecular dynamics simulations of solid-liquid interfaces has developed remarkably in recent years. Current approaches based on constant-charge or constant-potential schemes remain limited in their ability to accurately describe the physical electrode-electrolyte interface, as they can create artificial effects, such as inducing a dipole, shifting the target potential of the simulation, or requiring instantaneous relaxation of the interface. In this work, the effect of applying the fluctuation-dissipation theorem to the applied potential on reaction barriers in ab initio slow-growth molecular dynamics simulations is investigated. Three simulation schemes are compared: the NVT ensemble (constant charge), the µVT ensemble (constant potential), and NVTΦ, realized through FLEX++, a Python wrapper for VASPsol++ that controls the number of electrons at each simulation step according to the fluctuation-dissipation theorem. The reaction barrier of the Volmer step of the HER on Au(110)/water and Cu metal leaching from a CuN4HC single-atom catalyst during CO2RR are calculated as test cases. For the Volmer step, the reaction barrier increases with the applied potential for all ensembles, but each simulation repetition yields a considerably different barrier for the NVT and µVT ensembles, whereas NVTΦ yields a more consistent estimate. The reason is that FLEX++ maintains the electrode potential more consistently along the reaction coordinate, while letting the electrode potential vary to accommodate the reaction event. These differences in barrier height between the repetitions originate from the covalent bonds and H-bond network around the O donating the H in the Volmer step. For Cu metal leaching, NVTΦ shows an increased barrier of 0.1 eV, on average, over standard NVT. This decreased NVT barrier is rationalized by a lack of charge fluctuations that would otherwise destabilize the solvated leaching metal complex, if present.

papers.title: Accelerated Hygrothermal Aging of an Epoxy Barrier Coating: Correlating Laboratory Degradation with Performance
papers.abstract: This study investigates the hygrothermal aging behavior of a commercial an epoxy barrier coating. The coating was subjected to water immersion and dry-heat exposure at 20–80 °C for up to 14 months, and changes in water uptake, tensile properties, and thermal transitions were monitored by gravimetric measurements, tensile testing, dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA), and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC). After two months, combined water and elevated-temperature exposure produced larger reductions in tensile modulus and strength than dry aging, while drying substantially restored the mechanical properties. This indicates that moisture-induced plasticization and swelling account for a major fraction of the early property loss. Longer exposure produced more severe mechanical deterioration, and at 60 °C the material continued to gain mass for up to eight months before subsequent weight loss, consistent with a transition from predominantly diffusioncontrolled water uptake toward degradation-associated behavior. In contrast, DMA and DSC glass-transition temperatures varied only modestly with aging temperature. The results show that mechanical measurements provide a more sensitive indicator of hygrothermal performance than Tg alone for this coating. The study provides material-level evidence relevant to the assessment of rubber-toughened epoxy barrier coatings under combined heat and moisture exposure.

papers.title: Mature complexes carry more G protein class information than partner free GPCR structures
papers.abstract: GPCR structures are widely used to infer G protein coupling and pathway selective pharmacology, but mature receptor G protein complexes may contain structural information acquired or stabilized after partner selection. We asked how much G protein class information is present independently of the bound transducer. We analyzed 1,360 experimental class A GPCR structures using structural bioinformatics, molecular recognition descriptors and receptor grouped machine learning. Every receptor with both a strict partner free active structure and a G protein bound structure entered the matched analysis; activation and evolutionary transfer served as controls. Twelve receptors met the strict criteria. Bound endpoints gave a larger G protein class margin in 11 of 12 receptors (mean difference 0.389, 95% CI 0.095 to 0.682; exact sign flip P = 0.030), with macro ROC AUC 0.795 versus 0.619. A four feature geometry classified activation at ROC AUC 0.996 across 1,336 structures from 199 receptors. Across 207 receptor transducer units, class information was distributed across sequence and structural properties, strongly shaped by evolutionary relatedness, and no universal cross family interface rule emerged. Mature GPCR complexes therefore contain receptor compatibility plus information associated with the selected and stabilized transducer. Similarity to a G protein bound endpoint supports compatibility with that signalling state but does not by itself establish intrinsic coupling preference, a distinction relevant to pathway selective drug discovery.

papers.title: Orange hydrogen production with fayalite slag: identifying reaction bottlenecks
papers.abstract: Orange hydrogen (H2) is generated through stimulated water–rock reactions, analogous to natural hydrogen formation via serpentinization, and offers a potential pathway for clean H2 production from Fe(II)-bearing minerals and mineral side streams. Here, we investigate orange H2 production based on fayalite slag, an Fe(II)-rich metallurgical waste that has not previously been studied for this purpose. H2 generation from fayalite slag was evaluated in a stirred hydrothermal reactor pressurized with Ar and experiments were carried out at initial pressures of 5, 50, and 100 bar and temperatures of 160 and 230 °C. The highest H2 production was observed at 230 °C and an initial pressure of 5 bar in 1 M KOH (pH 14) after 48 h, reaching 0.45 g H2 kg-1 fayalite slag, corresponding to ⁓7.2% of the theoretical maximum H2 yield. During the reaction, the fayalite content decreased, while magnetite and a K-bearing mica phase formed as secondary products. These secondary phases may have limited further reaction by reducing water access to Fe(II)-bearing regions. This is evidenced by the fact that H2 generation plateaued after 48 h of reaction time. Overall, the results show that fayalite slag is a potential feedstock for orange H2 production under comparatively mild hydrothermal conditions, while also indicating that secondary phase formation and surface passivation are important reaction bottlenecks.

papers.title: Transport and mechanical properties of pseudo-zwitterionic polymer electrolytes from non-equilibrium molecular dynamics simulations
papers.abstract: Pseudo-zwitterionic polymer electrolytes (PZPEs) are promising multifunctional copolymers for solid-state batteries, where efficient ion transport must be balanced against mechanical robustness. Here, we used non-equilibrium molecular dynamics (NEMD) simulations to determine how polymer composition, LiTFSI concentration, and copolymer sequence govern coupled transport and mechanical properties in MIL:PEGMbased PZPEs. A calibrated field-driven NEMD protocol enables ionic conductivity to be obtained within a few nanoseconds while preserving the equilibrium salt-concentration dependence. It is found that Li+ self-diffusion decreases with increasing salt concentration in PEGM-rich systems but can increase in MIL-rich systems, accompanied by a shift toward TFSI− rich coordination. Onsager analysis further shows that cation–anion correlations strongly influence electrophoretic mobility. The resulting conductivity–modulus maps reveal a clear trade-off: PEGM-rich systems are more conductive but softer, whereas MIL-rich systems are stiffer but less conductive. NEMD simulations suggest that salt concentration and copolymer sequence provide additional handles for tuning this balance.

papers.title: Manufacturing process modeling of bilayer cathode for graded thick electrode design
papers.abstract: The energy density and rate capability of lithium-ion batteries can be improved through the design of bilayer and compositionally graded architectures for thick electrodes. For this, manufacturing steps such as drying and calendering are key considerations, since they determine the final electrode microstructure and therefore affect its electrochemical performance. Here, we extend our previously developed processcoupled coarse-grained molecular dynamics and discrete element method manufacturing computational workflow from single-layer LiNi0.33Co0.33Mn0.33O2 cathodes to bilayer cathode architectures. The model accounts for active material particles with realistic shapes obtained from X-ray micro-computed tomography. We use bilayer cathodes with different layer formulations as study cases. The Our simulation results show that the initial through-thickness heterogeneity can be preserved after slurry drying but is progressively reshaped during calendering. The layer-averaged porosity contrast can be weakened or even reversed under compression. This indicates a transition from porosity heterogeneity arising from slurry drying to residual porosity governed more by formulation-dependent particle packing. Meanwhile, the interfacial mixing region between the two layers broadens and the effective tortuosity factor increases sharply in the low-porosity regime. These results demonstrate that bilayer electrode design should be treated as a process-history-dependent engineering problem rather than as a static layer stacking one.

papers.title: Design of High-Ionic-Conductivity Doped Li2ZrO3 Cathode Coating with Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
papers.abstract: Li2ZrO3 (LZO) is a promising cathode coating material for all-solid-state batteries, but its intrinsically low ionic conductivity limits rate performance. Here, we investigate the effects of Y3+, Al3+, Nb5+, and Ta5+ doping and amorphization on the Li+ conductivity of LZO using density functional theory (DFT) and machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs). Among the dopants studied, Y3+ substitution exhibits the most favorable defect formation energies. Molecular dynamics simulations using a fine-tuned moment tensor potential (MTP) reveal that 6%-Y-doped crystalline LZO (c-LYZO) achieves a maximum room-temperature ionic conductivity of ∼2mS cm−1, an order of magnitude improvement over undoped LZO. Amorphization was also found to enhance the conductivity of undoped LZO but the effect is attenuated in doped LZO. We show that amorphous LYZO exhibits more spatially fragmented, trapping-dominated Li transport than its crystalline counterpart. These results identify Y-doped LZO as a potential high-conductivity cathode coating and provide a design framework that balances dopant chemistry, defect type, doping concentration, and structural order.

papers.title: Microstructural Evolution of Coffee Beans during Aqueous-based Decaffeination
papers.abstract: Aqueous decaffeination removes caffeine before roasting but may also alter the green-bean microstructure that contributes to subsequent heat and mass transfer. This study used X-ray micro-computed tomography (µ-CT) to quantify time-dependent changes in the three-dimensional pore structure of intact Colombian Arabica coffee beans treated using a laboratory-scale protocol termed the Thame Water Method (TWM). Two beans were imaged in their raw states. One was subsequently imaged after 8 hr of treatment, while the second was imaged after 5 min and 30 min of treatment. Pore number decreased in both treatment windows, falling by approximately 22% after 30 min and 68% after 8 hr. During 30 min short-duration treatment, mean pore diameter and resolved porosity increased, whereas both decreased following prolonged treatment of 8 hr. A numerical model informed by the measured microstructures predicted slower heating for the 30 min microstructure and faster heating for the 8 hr microstructure relative to the raw bean under the same roasting profile. These findings show that aqueous decaffeination can alter the physical starting structure of green coffee beans and suggest that these changes may influence subsequent heating transfer during roasting. The TWM provides a µ-CT-compatible platform and a methodology to investigate structural changes produced by other decaffeination processes. A more complete understanding could ultimately support decisions about how decaffeinated coffee is processed and roasted for optimal cup quality.

papers.title: Simultaneous quantification and natural abundance δ15N analysis of protein-bound amino acids in human lung tissue by GC-C-IRMS
papers.abstract: Compound specific isotope analysis in natural abundance provides a tracer free approach to investigate metabolism, but its application to amino acids in complex human tissues remains limited by derivatization requirements and the need for high precision isotope ratio measurements. Here, we developed and validated a Gas Chromatography–Combustion–Isotope Ratio Mass Spectrometry (GC-C-IRMS) method using methyl ester–pentafluoropropionyl (Me-PFP) derivatization for simultaneous quantification and δ15N analysis of protein-bound amino acids in human lung tissues. The method provided 12 measurable chromatographic signals corresponding to 13 amino acids, with satisfactory isotopic precision from standards to biological matrices, and derivative stability for 22 days in standards and for approximately 28 days in lung cancer tissue sample at −20 °C. Application to 12 paired tumor and adjacent non-tumor samples showed negative median tumor–adjacent δ15N shifts for glycine and hydroxyproline. Exploratory histology stratified analysis further suggested opposite δ15N shifts for alanine and tyrosine between adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma. These results demonstrate the suitability of a Me-PFP GC-C-IRMS workflow for combined quantitative and natural abundance nitrogen isotopic profiling of amino acids in human lung tissues.

papers.title: Analytic Energy Gradients for Unrestricted Mixed-Reference Spin-Flip Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory
papers.abstract: Analytic nuclear gradients for individual low-lying singlet and triplet states within mixed-reference spin-flip time-dependent density functional theory (MRSF-TDDFT) based on an unrestricted Kohn–Sham (UKS) reference (UMRSF-TDDFT) were derived and implemented. The mixed-reference response restores the missing spin-complementary configurations and substantially attenuates the effects of the unequal UKS α/β orbitals. Relative to the restricted-open-shell (RO)-MRSF gradient, the major change is that the UKS reference supplies independently optimized α and β spatial-orbital sets. Corresponding orbitals in these generally unequal sets must first be paired by an orbital alignment. Differentiation of this additional alignment generates two contributions absent from RO-MRSF: spin-resolved alignmentinduced orbital-gradient terms ∆G f ,σ align in the orbital gradient and an explicit overlap contribution −Tr(W alignSξ ). The aligned response is also nonstationary to relevant occupied–occupied (α) and virtual–virtual (β ) rotations, requiring an independent-spin, full-block Z-vector. When the SOMOs are exactly degenerate, we select the minimum-norm solution of the response equation, which leaves the gradient unchanged. Compared with the RO-MRSF gradient, the formal scaling is unchanged, but the independent α/β response approximately doubles the principal coupled Z-vector dimension. Despite substantial differences between UKS and restricted-open-shell Kohn–Sham (ROKS) frontier orbitals, the UMRSF and RO-MRSF structures and potential-energy surfaces show close agreement.

papers.title: Mechanochemical Degradation of Activated Carbon-Adsorbed PFAS and Fluorinated Gases
papers.abstract: Fluorochemicals are widely used in modern society due to their unique and valuable properties. From the perspective of sustainable fluorine resource utilization, technologies that enable the recovery and reuse of fluorine from waste or captured fluorochemicals are crucial. However, efficient strategies for recovering fluorine from these materials remain limited. Herein, we report a mechanochemical strategy for the direct conversion of activated carbon-adsorbed PFAS and fluorinated gases into potassium fluoride (KF), a valuable fluorination reagent, by ball milling with potassium metal. The process proceeds rapidly and efficiently under solvent-free conditions. The method is applicable to a variety of PFAS, including perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), perfluoroheptanoic acid (PFHpA), and perfluorobutanesulfonic acid (PFBS), as well as fluorinated gases such as SF6, HFC-125, and HFC-23. This work provides a sustainable strategy toward a fluoro-circular economy through the recovery of fluorine as a valuable chemical resource.

papers.title: Fully Reversible High-Capacity Ammonia Storage in a Series of Phase-Transformable Molecular Nickel Thiocarboxylates
papers.abstract: Ammonia (NH 3 ) is an indispensable chemical commodity in modern society, but its nature as a toxic and corrosive gas makes its storage and transport difficult. Here, we report non-porous molecular nickel thiobenzoate [Ni 2 (PhCOS) 4 ] and derivatives, as a distinct class of phase-transformable adsorbents for reversible and high-density ammonia storage in ambient conditions. Despite lacking intrinsic porosity, [Ni 2 (PhCOS) 4 ] presented excellent sorption capacity of 23.5 mmol/g (effective reversible capacity: 22.0 mmol/g) at 298 K and 1 bar. The multi-sigmoidal adsorption profile, arising from solid-state chemical transformation into well-defined compounds of formulas {Ni 2 (PhCOS) 4 (NH 3 ) n } (n = 1, 8 and 16), provides a large pressure-swing working capacity (11.4 mmol/g between 0.1 and 1.0 bar) and enables complete, energy-efficient regeneration under remarkably mild conditions (60–80 °C). The transformation was associated with drastic changes in the coordination environment of Ni centers yet was fast and fully reversible. Phase transformation-induced self-fragmentation generates hierarchical diffusion pathways, driving rapid kinetics (50% uptake in 95 s). Furthermore, the complex demonstrates outstanding ambient moisture tolerance, 10-cycle durability, scalable one-pot synthesis exceeding 60 g (81% yield), and practical cartridge-level storage (+36wt% mass increase), demonstrating dynamic molecular complexes as a practical platform for gas management.

papers.title: Mechanochemical Birch-type hydrodefluorination of polytetrafluoroethylene: amine-controlled hydrogenation versus carbonization
papers.abstract: Reductive defluorination of polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) can efficiently recover fluoride but commonly converts the carbon component into poorly defined carbonaceous solids. Herein, we report a mechanochemical Birch-type hydrodefluorination using lithium and ethylenediamine (EDA) that couples C-F bond cleavage with hydrogen incorporation. Milling at 30 Hz and room temperature released fluoride in 98% yield within 10 min, as independently determined by quantitative 19F NMR spectroscopy and ion chromatography. The pale-brown residue contained 0.6 wt% fluorine, 78.4 wt% carbon, and 12.3 wt% hydrogen, corresponding to an atomic H/C ratio of 1.88. FTIR and Raman spectroscopy, differential scanning calorimetry, solid-state 13C-MAS NMR, and powder X-ray diffraction showed loss of the PTFE C-F fingerprint and emergence of a CH2-rich structure with polyethylene-like thermal and crystalline features. The product is therefore assigned as a polyethylene-like material rather than chemically pure polyethylene. In the absence of EDA, fluoride was again obtained in 98% yield, whereas the solid product was a black, disordered sp2rich carbon. Coarser PTFE powders likewise tended to afford darker solids despite nearly quantitative fluoride recovery. These results demonstrate that fluoride yield alone is not a measure of hydrodefluorination selectivity and that EDA controls the competition between hydrogen incorporation and carbonization. The method converts PTFE into an inorganic fraction containing LiF and a hydrogen-rich carbon material potentially suitable for downstream polyolefin valorization.

papers.title: Classical infrared correlation rules as diagnostic tests: likelihood ratios from 6,663 experimental spectra
papers.abstract: Infrared correlation tables give, for each functional group, a wavenumber window and an adjective. They do not say how often a band is found in that window when the group is absent, and that is the number that decides whether the observation is evidence. We treated every published rule as a diagnostic test. A set of 101 rules for 60 functional groups, transcribed from one widely used interpretation course and frozen before any confirmatory analysis, was scored on 1,539 ATR spectra of synthesised compounds from the Chemotion repository and replicated on 5,124 transmission spectra from the NIST Chemistry WebBook, with the deposited structure as ground truth and sensitivity, specificity and likelihood ratios as the metrics. The main result is a division of the spectrum into two regimes. Above 1500 cm−1 most rules carry real evidence (median positive likelihood ratio 2.8 and 3.0 in the two collections, up to 43 for the saturated ester carbonyl); in the fingerprint region, at or below 1350 cm−1, band position alone is close to uninformative (median 1.1 and 1.2), because almost every spectrum has a band in almost every window. The rankings agree across the two collections (Spearman 0.79; 87% of rules within a factor of two). The audit also measures what the tables leave unsaid: intensity qualifiers cost more sensitivity than they buy specificity (the nitrile band reaches the stated intensity in one nitrile in ten), the benzene substitution patterns do not reach a likelihood ratio of 5 in either collection, and several rules are far more useful for ruling a group out than for ruling it in. We provide the quantified table, the frozen rule set and the scripts so that the audit can be extended to further rules and collections.

papers.title: Emerging Paradigms in Electrochemical Water Treatment: Advanced Electrode Materials, Resource Recovery, and Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Electrochemical water treatment offers a versatile approach to contaminant removal and resource recovery, although its practical performance depends on electrode properties, wastewater composition and operating conditions. This review critically examines the principal electrochemical treatment methods, including electrochemical oxidation and reduction, electro-Fenton processes, electrocoagulation, electroflotation, electrodeposition and electrodialysis. Their reaction pathways, treatment capabilities and limitations are discussed, with particular attention to the distinction between pollutant degradation, separation and recovery. Electrode development is examined through boron-doped diamond, mixed metal oxides and two-dimensional materials, including graphene derivatives, MXenes, transition-metal dichalcogenides and black phosphorus. The discussion considers how surface chemistry, electronic structure and electrode architecture influence charge transfer, reactive-species generation and ion transport, while addressing stability, material release and performance in complex wastewater matrices. Commercial implementation is assessed in relation to energy consumption, electrode lifetime, reactor design, maintenance requirements and integration with existing treatment infrastructure. The review also explores the application of machine learning to predict treatment performance, identify influential operating variables and guide material selection and process optimization. Particular emphasis is placed on data quality, model interpretability and validation beyond laboratory datasets. By connecting treatment mechanisms, electrode engineering and data-driven optimization, this review identifies the evidence and development priorities needed to advance electrochemical technologies towards reliable, economically viable water treatment.

papers.title: Boundary-driven phase transformation in layered 3R In2Se3 captured by long range machine learning molecular dynamics
