papers.abstract: Layered In2Se3 switches between closely related crystalline van der Waals states, but its atomistic thermal pathway in rhombohedral 3R geometries remains unresolved because middle-Se motion within each quintuple layer (QL), inter-QL glide, freesurface morphology, and weak interlayer binding evolve together. Here we develop a PBE+D3(BJ)-trained MACERSGA interatomic potential that adds a reciprocal-space gated-attention long-range correction to a short-range MACE backbone. Compared with MACE trained on the same data, MACERSGA reduces test-set energy and force RMSEs by 83.8% and 17.7%, respectively, while preserving the PBE+D3(BJ) exfoliation binding curves of α-and β-like structures. Large-cell molecular dynamics examines 1QL vacuum slabs, 3QL vacuum slabs, and periodic 3QL cells containing one full 3R repeat. Heating and cooling ramps at 5 and 1 K ps−1, supported by fixed-temperature holds, reveal a boundary hierarchy in the finite-rate structural-change window. The 1QL vacuum slab shows structural change first, followed by the 3QL vacuum and periodic 3QL cells. The 3QL vacuum slab also undergoes substantially larger inter-QL glide than the periodic cell. Cooling the α-heated structures directly tests whether the transformed states retain boundary-specific structural memory on the simulated timescale. Upon cooling, both 3QL systems retain transformed local environments near θ ≈ 57◦ at room temperature rather than returning to high-θ α, yet preserve distinct inter-QL registries and out-of-plane morphologies inherited directly from their boundary-specific heating pathways. These results show how nanoscale boundary conditions shape transformation pathways and retained interlayer registry in layered In2Se3, revealing structural memory relevant to nonvolatile crystalline memory and neuromorphic switching concepts.

papers.title: Atomistic Probability Kinetic Modeling of Polymer Functionalization: A Framework for Post-Functionalization and Upcycling of Polymers
papers.abstract: Post-functionalization and the upcycling of post-consumer waste are valuable strategies for enhancing the material properties and value of polymers, but predictive modeling of these reactions is limited because of their inherent randomness. We present a mathematical framework to describe the effect of polymer functionalization reactions on downstream material properties or products using a combinatoric atomistic probability distribution (APD). The APD is derived generally to predict the spacing of subchains, Δ, between substituents or at chain ends when S substituents are randomly distributed along a polymer chain of length L. This approach is applied to a model upcycling system: the functionalization of polyethylene (PE) via sulfonation and subsequent H 2 O 2 -driven oxidative depolymerization. By coupling the APD with models for downstream depolymerization of sulfonated PE and hydroxyl radical-mediated decomposition kinetics, we develop a kinetic probability distribution (KPD) that explicitly describes the resulting degradation products. This approach results in dimensional reduction by requiring 14 total parameters for an N-species system (N = 6 here), while traditional modeling approaches require 4N + 7 (31 in our case). Probability parameters obtained from the KPD enabled the calculation of product and CO 2 carbon yields within ~10% of experimental values. This framework presents a novel approach to incorporating the underlying randomness governing polymer functionalization reactions, vastly reducing the parameter space and improving targeting of more economically relevant products during upcycling.

papers.title: Enantioselective Synthesis of Carbazole-Thioisatin Spirocycles via NHC-Catalyzed Remote N–H Activation
papers.abstract: An enantioselective NHC-catalyzed strategy for the synthesis of spirocyclic carbazole derivatives was developed through oxidative remote N–H activation of readily available 1-formylcarbazoles. Catalytic generation of aza-ortho-quinone methides enables efficient annulation with thioisatins, underexplored electrophiles in asymmetric NHC catalysis. The protocol is also compatible with conventional isatins, affording structurally diverse spirocyclic heteroaromatic products in acceptable to good yields (up to 76%) and enantiomeric ratios up to 98:2 er. The utility of the method was demonstrated on gram-scale, while successful coupling with an acyclic ketone further illustrates the broader synthetic potential of this remote N–H activation process.

papers.title: Direct Ink Writing (DIW) of Mechanically Graded and Programmable Crosslinked Polymers with Seamless Interlayer Fusion
papers.abstract: Direct ink writing (DIW) enables the fabrication of complex polymer architectures under mild processing conditions, yet the production of mechanically graded multimaterial structures remains limited by weak interfacial adhesion and by the restricted availability of printable thermoset feedstocks. Here, we introduce a high internal phase emulsion (HIPE)-based printing platform for the fabrication of mechanically programmable crosslinked polymers with seamless interlayer integration. Oil-in-water HIPE inks were formulated from methacrylated dextran (DexMA) in the continuous phase and mixtures of methyl methacrylate and hexyl methacrylate in the dispersed phase, yielding printable precursors that generate crosslinked networks spanning elastic moduli from below 1 MPa to above 150 MPa after curing. Rheological and morphological analyses demonstrated that the different formulations possess comparable printability despite their markedly different final mechanical properties. Photo-rheological experiments revealed a two-stage curing process, consisting of rapid DexMA crosslinking followed by slower polymerization of the monomer-rich phase, providing a temporal window that promotes molecular interpenetration across adjacent deposited filaments. This mechanism enables the formation of intermolecularly fused interfaces rather than conventional layer-by-layer contacts. Monomaterial and multimaterial constructs were fabricated and mechanically characterized under compression. While multimaterial architectures exhibited compressive moduli comparable to intermediate-composition controls, they displayed substantially enhanced toughness and enabled programmable deformation and recovery behaviors. The ability to sequentially combine mechanically distinct formulations within a continuous crosslinked network, while maintaining robust interlayer cohesion, establishes HIPE-based DIW as a versatile strategy for the fabrication of mechanically graded thermoset architectures whose performance emerges from the interplay between material composition and spatial design.

papers.title: Acylals Derived from Acrylic Anhydride as Latent Anhydride Crosslinkers for Catalyst-Free Vitrimers
papers.abstract: Carboxylic anhydrides are attractive dynamic covalent bonds that undergo rapid bond exchange without external catalysts. In this study, acylals prepared from acrylic anhydrides and aromatic aldehydes were employed as latent carboxylic anhydride crosslinkers to introduce dynamic anhydride linkages into polymer networks via postpolymerization heat treatment. Model experiments using small molecules suggested that acylals themselves undergo bond exchange, although the exchange is considerably slower and proceeds via a dissociative mechanism. In contrast, carboxylic anhydrides undergo rapid bond exchange via an associative mechanism. Polymers containing acylal crosslinks exhibited slow stress relaxation and required a high temperature (220 °C) for reprocessing. Heat treatment converted the acylal crosslinks into carboxylic anhydride crosslinks, resulting in substantially faster stress relaxation, improved reprocessability, and decrosslinking via hydrolysis. The heat-treated network exhibited catalyst-free stress relaxation with an Arrhenius temperature dependence, demonstrating the formation of a carboxylic anhydride-based vitrimer.

papers.title: Data-driven models for performance prediction in a microalgae-based wastewater treatment process
papers.abstract: Microalgae-based wastewater treatment has the potential to advance tertiary phosphorus recovery while producing biomass for resource valorization. The development of reliable near-term prediction models can help reduce system upsets, support proactive process control, and optimize resource utilization. In this study, Light Gradient-Boosting Machine (LGBM), Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models were comparatively evaluated for predicting effluent ammonium, nitrate, and orthophosphate concentrations and biomass dynamics in a full-scale (568 m 3 ·d -1 ) microalgal system using 25 months of operational and microalgal community structure data. LSTM consistently achieved the highest prediction accuracy while effectively capturing system upset events. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis provided interpretable insights into feature importance across both feature and temporal dimensions, with SHAP-guided feature reduction substantially reducing computational requirements without compromising predictive performance. Benchmarking against the mechanistic process model further identified the complementary application niches of mechanistic and data-driven approaches, providing practical guidance for model selection.

papers.title: Room-temperature relithiation of chemically delithiated LMFP cathode materials as a model for direct recycling
papers.abstract: Room-temperature direct relithiation is an attractive strategy for the regeneration of olivine-type cathode materials, but its applicability to LiMn 0.6 Fe 0.4 PO 4 (LMFP) remains largely unexplored. Here, chemically delithiated LMFP powders were used as model materials to evaluate the feasibility and limitations of direct regeneration under mild conditions. Different delithiation levels were obtained using Ferric nitrate or Nitronium tetrafluoroborate as oxidizing agents, enabling selective oxidation of Fe 2+ or combined oxidation of Fe 2+ and Mn 2+ depending on the oxidizing strength. The structural and redox evolution from pristine to delithiated and relithiated states was followed by X-ray diffraction, X-ray absorption spectroscopy, Mössbauer spectroscopy, Raman spectroscopy, and electrochemical testing. Relithiation was carried out at room temperature using lithium iodide in organic media, including acetonitrile and ethanol. The results show that LMFP can be efficiently relithiated when lithium loss is mainly associated with Fe 2+ oxidation, with substantial recovery of the olivine structure and electrochemical activity. However, higher delithiation levels involving Mn oxidation lead to incomplete regeneration, likely due to manganese dissolution and irreversible local structural changes. These findings demonstrate that LMFP cannot be considered as a simple extension of LFP in direct recycling processes. Instead, manganese-containing olivine cathodes require specific regeneration strategies adapted to their redox chemistry and degradation pathways. Studies on real end-of-life LMFP electrodes will be required to validate the conclusions obtained from these model materials.

papers.title: Uni-Macro-FRPN: Full-Resolution and Cross-Scale Learning for Polymers
papers.abstract: Polymer properties emerge from interactions across scales, yet existing polymer models typically preserve either detailed monomer chemistry without an explicit polymer graph or polymer connectivity with simplified monomer representations, due to computational constraints, as polymers typically contain tens of thousands of atoms. We present Uni-Macro-FRPN (FRPN), a Full-Resolution Polymer Network that retains both detailed atom-level and monomer-level features and explicit polymer structure information within a unified framework. Two Transformers jointly learn atom-informed monomer semantics, sequence order, and chain topology from BigSMILES-derived representations. On the Block Copolymer Database (BCDB) lamellar-versus-non-lamellar classification task, FRPN achieves 86.4% accuracy and 90.6% ROC–AUC, establishing state-of-the-art performance. Ablation results indicate that the gain is not explained solely by increased parameter count. On a linear homopolymer benchmark, monomer-centric learning remains competitive, highlighting a boundary case where polymer-scale organization is simple. To test generalization beyond linear polymers, we further construct an all-atom molecular-dynamics benchmark of 1640 datapoints spanning diverse monomer chemistries, sequence orderings, chain topologies, and physical properties. FRPN achieves the strongest overall performance on this topology-rich benchmark, with diagnostics supporting the benefit of jointly modeling monomer chemistry and polymer structure. Taken together, FRPN provides a practical route for moving polymer representation learning beyond monomer-centric representations. The leading performance of FRPN also suggests a promising direction for polymer informatics: future polymer prediction models should treat polymers not only as collections of monomer descriptors, but as complete multiscale chemical and topological objects.

papers.title: Resolving Positional Markush Structures for Chemical Reaction Extraction
papers.abstract: The automated extraction of chemical reaction data from scientific literature remains very challenging mainly due to the visual complexity and heterogeneity of published graphical schemes. In particular, substrate scopes containing positional Markush structures pose a significant challenge for current Optical Chemical Structure Recognition (OCSR) and reaction-extraction systems, as their resolution requires combining molecular recognition with precise spatial reasoning. Herein, we introduce a deterministic, coordinate-based extraction pipeline designed to resolve positional Markush structures in reaction schemes. Building upon a fine-tuned version of the graph-prediction OCSR module MolScribe, our approach uses deterministic geometric rules based on 2D molecular coordinates to infer R-group attachment points and generate topologically valid molecular representations. To evaluate this approach, we introduce two curated benchmarks: MIPub-2k (Molecular Images from Publication - Université Bourgogne Europe) comprising 2,128 literature-derived molecular image crops for OCSR evaluation and MIReactPub (Markush template-based Image of Reaction from Publication – Université Bourgogne Europe) comprising 450 reactions from 23 schemes containing positional Markush structures for reaction-level assessment. The complete pipeline achieves an end-to-end F1 score of 0.46, increasing to 0.54 for schemes without textual-dependent ambiguities. Slightly reorganizing figures doubles the F1 score, demonstrating the robustness of the underlying geometric resolution while highlighting the substantial impact of visual heterogeneity in published literature on end-to-end performance. By explicitly encoding chemical and spatial constraints, our proposed approach provides a transparent and reproducible framework for resolving complex molecular representations from literature images. The resulting open-source pipeline and benchmarks provide a specialized component that can be further integrated into automated workflows for large-scale chemical information extraction.

papers.title: Azopyrazole boronic ester crosslinks with long thermal half-lives for phototunable viscoelastic hydrogels
papers.abstract: Covalent adaptable networks (CANs) based on boronic acid–ester exchange undergo rapid network reconfiguration in ambient conditions, making them useful materials for biomedical applications. The combination of photoswitches and dynamic bonds imparts reversible spatiotemporal control over mechanical properties for smart and responsive materials. Here, we report azopyrazole boronic acids that undergo rapid photoisomerization to their metastable Z isomers, which have extremely long thermal half-lives (over a year at 25 °C) and a 3-fold enhancement in binding affinity for diols compared to the E isomer. When incorporated into hydrogels, these photoswitchable dynamic bonds enable reversible changes in stiffness and stress relaxation time with at least 6 cycles of visible and UV light. Despite only containing dynamic crosslinks, these hydrogels are comparable in stiffness to our previously reported hybrid materials containing dynamic azobenzene boronic ester and static bis(acrylamide) crosslinks. This work demonstrates an alternative strategy to tuning boronic acid-ester equilibria with light while maintaining strong binding in both isomers.

papers.title: Concise Total Synthesis of (–)-5-epi-Cycloclavine via Metal- and Base-Free Diastereoselective Intramolecular Cyclopropanation of N-Sulfonylhydrazone-Derived Donor Carbene
papers.abstract: A metal- and base-free intramolecular cyclopropanation based on nonstabilized donor carbenes generated in situ from N-sulfonylhydrazones has been developed, enabling the construction of the highly strained aza[3.1.0]bicyclic core of (–)-5-epi-cycloclavine with concomitant complete stereocontrol of two all-carbon quaternary stereocenters. Combined with the straightforward introduction of methacrylic acid as four-carbon fragment from readily available enantiopure functionalized tricyclic indole derivative (4-amino Uhle's ketone), this strategy enabled a concise diasteroselective synthesis of the five-fused rings system present in (–)-5-epi-cycloclavine.

papers.title: Coordination Alone Does Not Passivate Surface Halide-Vacancy States in Lead Halide Perovskites
papers.abstract: Molecular passivation of halide vacancies at lead-halide perovskite surfaces is conventionally attributed to Lewis-base coordination of undercoordinated Pb2+ sites. Density functional theory with spin–orbit coupling on FA0.75MA0.25PbI3 (001) shows this premise is electronically insufficient. Across ten additives, no coordination metric predicts which additives passivate: molybdic acid coordinates at 2.346 Å (−1.14 e) yet leaves the localized Pb(6p) defect trap intact (p = 0.128; +0.29 eV in HSE06), whereas permanganic acid coordinates at 2.156 Å (−1.06 e) and clears it (p ≤ 0.002). The outcomes exhibit discrete bimodal separation (Ashman’s D = 23.11) governed by specific interfacial chemistry: proton transfer forming a hydridic Pb–H bond (H2SO4, p = 0.008) or charge-transfer depopulation into an accessible acceptor manifold (HMnO4). This mechanism rationalizes the observed processing sensitivity of phosphate additives. Screening additives by coordination geometry cannot identify passivants; targeting proton delivery or redox-accessible acceptor levels can.

papers.title: Accelerating the Design of New Natural Deep Eutectic Solvents with Supervised Variational Autoencoders
papers.abstract: The rational design of natural deep eutectic solvents (NaDESs) is hindered by the vast combinatorial space arising from the possible combinations of hydrogen bond donors and acceptors. This enormous design space limits the systematic experimental exploration of their physicochemical properties. In this work, we propose a supervised variational autoencoder (SVAE) framework to efficiently explore this chemical space by coupling generative modeling with property prediction. The model is trained on a curated dataset of deep eutectic solvents to learn simultaneously the latent structural representations and correlations with target properties, including melting point, density, and viscosity. The SVAE generates virtual NaDES candidates characterized by molecular descriptors, component ratios, and target property values. To associate these virtual candidates with real molecules, a descriptor matching strategy is applied using the COCONUT natural product database. The resulting NaDES candidates are subsequently validated using predictive models trained on experimental DES data. The results show strong agreement between the SVAE-generated target property values and the corresponding predictions of the regression models (R2 = 0.89, RMSE=21.7 K for melting point; R2 = 0.91, RMSE = 0.04 g·cm-3 for density; and R2 = 0.89, RMSE=0.47 cP for ln(viscosity)). This workflow demonstrates how guided generative models can be combined with machine learning models to accelerate the discovery of sustainable solvents. Beyond NaDESs, the proposed strategy provides a general and transferable framework for the rational design of other chemical systems, where combinatorial complexity limits conventional experimental approaches.

papers.title: Orthogonal-Solvent Sequential Depositionfor Chiral Induction in Polymer Films andCircularly Polarized Light-Emitting Diodes
papers.abstract: Solution-processed chiroptical polymer films are commonly prepared by blending a fluorescent polymer with a chiral inducer, which restricts material selection to components soluble in a common formulation solvent. Here we decouple the two solvent requirements by sequentially depositing poly(9,9-dioctylfluorene-alt-bithiophene) (F8T2) from chlorobenzene and a chiral inducer from ethanol, followed by thermal annealing. With (R)-(−)-1,1′-binaphthyl-2,2′-diyl hydrogen phosphate (R-DbHP), the sequential film reaches a peak apparent absorption dissymmetry factor of 0.35, compared with 0.09 for the best tetrahydrofuran-blend film under separately optimized conditions. The chiroptical response develops during annealing and is largely retained after ethanol treatment reduces the characteristic absorbance of the inducer overlayer. The strategy transfers to a second inducer, R-5011, and the resulting emissive layers operate in circularly polarized light-emitting diodes (CP-LEDs), giving electroluminescence dissymmetry factors of 0.79–0.83 at the emission maximum across four devices. The largest CD-derived values are designated apparent because their raw ellipticities exceed the nominal full-scale range; front/back measurements and an in-range concentration series characterize the signal while not excluding all polarization artifacts. Orthogonal-solvent sequential deposition thus provides a processing route to chiroptical polymer films and CP-LEDs without requiring the polymer and inducer to share a casting solvent.

papers.title: Can AI Help Chemists To Solve NMR?
papers.abstract: Chemists read 1 H and 13 C NMR daily, and it is tempting to paste the peak lists into a large language model. Given only those two peak lists for 105 molecules balanced by molecular complexity and compound classes, six frontier LLMs (Claude Opus 4.8, DeepSeek V4 Pro, Gemini 3.1 Pro, GPT-5.5, Grok 4.3, Qwen3.7-Max) and four specialized solvers (BLIND, NMRMind, NMRPeak, NMR-Solver) were compared. The best LLM (Gemini 3.1 Pro) solved 24% of structures, the best specialized model (BLIND) solved 69% of them. All models drift toward smaller molecules and drop groups silent in ¹H NMR like halogens, nitriles, diazo.

papers.title: Domino and Cascade Reactions in Sustainable Synthesis: Activation Modes, Assessment Boundaries, and the Molecular-Process Discrepancy
papers.abstract: Domino and cascade reactions construct molecular complexity through sequential transformations and can reduce intermediate isolation. Their contribution to sustainable synthesis depends on whether these advantages persist when precursor preparation, catalyst production, reaction operation, and product recovery are included. This targeted narrative review examines thirteen mechanistic examples across seven activation or propagation modes and develops the molecular-process discrepancy (MPD) as a framework for testing that translation. MPD connects a specific reaction-level claim to the additional material and energy requirements introduced by expanding the assessment boundary. It complements atom economy, process mass intensity, E-factor, life-cycle assessment, and process benchmarks without replacing their measurements. Four case studies distinguish the roles of feedstock and product recovery in Ambrox synthesis, oxidant substitution in coumestan formation, advanced-substrate preparation in lasalocid A biosynthesis, and operational consolidation in oseltamivir synthesis. Together, they show why atom conservation, selective ring construction, and fewer isolations provide different forms of efficiency that must be evaluated separately. The analysis identifies precursor access, dilution, separation, catalyst lifetime, and heat, light, or oxygen delivery as specific targets for process improvement. MPD provides a procedure for determining whether a proposed cascade advantage is retained, attenuated, reversed, or unresolved across explicit assessment boundaries.

papers.title: Q-Chem/CP2K software interface for projection-based, pseudoperiodic wavefunction-in-DFT embedding
papers.abstract: We report an implementation of projection-based quantum embedding that combines periodic density functional theory in the CP2K code with correlated wavefunction calculations in the Q-Chem program. Using this interface, correlated wavefunction methods can be applied to a subset of the molecular orbitals, selected in an automated manner based on a user-defined list of nuclei, wth an embedding potential that provides electronic coupling to the remaining orbitals that comprise the environment. Our implementation uses exact projection, without the need for any level-shift operator, and is “pseudoperiodic” in the sense that periodic boundary effects are implicit in the orbitals used in the (non-periodic) wavefunction calculation. Convergence tests demonstrate that computed properties are faithful to the corresponding periodic quantities, provided that the high-level subsystem is spatially localized and small, relative to the periodic simulation cell. Spectroscopic examples for aqueous chromophores demonstrate converged results using a very limited subset of the water molecules in the simulation cell, decoupling the choice of excited-state method and basis set from the functional that is used to propagate ground-state ab initio molecular dynamics. Solvatochromic shifts for aqueous uracil are converged using equation-of-motion coupled-cluster theory, without the need for solvent molecules in the wavefunction calculation, and the embedded calculation captures solvent effects that are absent in gas-phase “microhydration” studies.

papers.title: Atomic Environment Aware Lennard-Jones Parameterization for Electrostatic Embedding ML/MM Simulations
papers.abstract: Hybrid machine learning/molecular mechanics (ML/MM) methods have emerged as a powerful approach to multiscale modelling. Recent advances have focused on electrostatic embedding schemes, in which atoms in the ML region are polarized by the surrounding MM environment. Consequently, ML/MM electrostatics have been the subject of extensive study, whereas dispersion and close-range repulsive interactions remain comparatively underexplored. In analogy to established QM/MM practice, exchange-repulsion and dispersion interactions are commonly described using Lennard-Jones (LJ) 12-6 potentials with parameters transferred from existing force field libraries. However, such transferable parameters may be suboptimal for ML/MM interfaces, where consistency with the electrostatic embedding model is desirable. Here, we develop methodologies for deriving dynamic LJ parameters based on the exchange-hole dipole moment (XDM) model and the Fedorov polarizability scaling relation. Moreover, we propose a one-shot procedure for fine-tuning LJ parameters to experimental free energies. Focusing on the electrostatic machine learning embedding (EMLE) scheme, we show that these approaches yield EMLE models with competitive accuracy relative to conventional force fields and mechanical embedding schemes, while additionally providing chemically environment-aware LJ parameters. This capability offers a route to improved accuracy in demanding applications such as reactive modelling, where dispersion coefficients may depend strongly on the local chemical environment.

papers.title: Direct Synthesis of Ag-In-Zn-S Quantum Dot Inks for Solution-Processed Optoelectronics
papers.abstract: Non-toxic I–III–VI quantum dots (QDs) hold strong potential for optoelectronics but are hindered by complex synthesis and post-processing requirements. Here, we demonstrate a direct synthesis of Zn-alloyed AgIn 5 S 8 (AIZS) QDs that produces high-quality inks in N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF). The colloidal stability originates from a synergistic solvation layer comprising surface-bound oxygen-coordinated In/Zn–DMF complexes, co-adsorbed butylamine, and residual iodide anions. The resulting QDs exhibit strong n-type character and photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of ca. 43%. Proof-of-concept Quantum Dot Ligh emitting Diodes (QDLEDs) were fabricated based on this material, demonstrating the feasibility of processing functional emitting layers directly from polar inks.

papers.title: Beyond Swelling: Electrochemical Doping Tunes the Balance between Ion Compensation and Exchange in a Hydrated Organic Mixed Ionic–Electronic Conductor
papers.abstract: Organic mixed ionic–electronic conductors (OMIECs) couple electronic doping to ion compensation and water reorganization. As doping increasing, molecular reorganization within the polymer–ion–water environment is thought to underlie the often nonmonotonic response of OMIEC devices, yet this process is essential for the understanding of structure-function relationship in related OMIEC devices but remains unclear. Current experimental investigations cannot reveal this molecular-level reorganization, and the conventional simulations cannot realistically capture how the microstructure evolves with doping. To address these limitations under experimentally relevant electrochemical conditions, we develop an ion-regulated quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) grand-canonical molecular dynamics framework that operates at constant electrochemical potential and samples OMIECs across experimentally relevant doping levels.

papers.title: Ultra-thin WS2 growth by ALD from bis(tert-butylimido)bis(dimethylamido)tungsten and 1,2-ethanedithiol and detailed surface mechanism
papers.abstract: A molecular layer deposition/atomic layer deposition (MLD/ALD) strategy using bis(tert-butylimido)bis(dimethylamido)tungsten (BTBMW) and 1,2-ethanedithiol (EDT), the latter serving as a safer organic alternative to H2S, leads to the formation of ultrathin WS2 films via a molecular/hybrid tungsten organothiolate intermediate. A multiscale approach, involving Si/SiO2 wafers, silica nanobeads, and molecular models, provides mechanistic insight into the early stages of growth. It reveals a complex surface chemistry involving ligand exchange, partial reduction of tungsten, and degrafting processes with regeneration of Si-OH groups. Despite this complexity, the process evolves toward a self-limiting and reproducible growth regime. Annealing studies on Si/SiO2 wafers and silica nanobeads allow tracking the transformation of the organothiolate intermediate into crystalline WS2 and confirm that WS2 formation proceeds through a progressive and controlled conversion of the deposited phase into lamellar WS2 domains. The mechanistic study also suggests that the degrafting-induced mobility of thiolate species during deposition may contribute to the lateral growth observed during annealing.

papers.title: Modulation of Crystal Habit and Preferred Orientation of Aspirin: Combined Effects of Solvent and a Metallic Mesh Template during Evaporative Crystallization
papers.abstract: Polymorphism plays a significant role in crystal engineering, as it can directly influence the physicochemical properties of active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs). Aspirin (ASA) is one of the extensively studied model compounds in small-molecule polymorphism due to its pharmaceutical relevance. To date, ASA has been reported to exist in four polymorphic forms, Forms I, II, III, and IV. Like polymorphism, preferred (or preferential) orientation is another important characteristic in solidform screening that increases the risk of misidentifying pharmaceutical compounds as polymorphs. Here, we report evaporative crystallization of Form I ASA, with and without a metallic mesh template, in solvents of different polarities, exhibiting preferred orientation driven by the resulting crystal morphology 2 while retaining Form I. It was observed that the solvent and/or template independently/combinedly, along with grinding, has induced the preferred orientation of Form I ASA modulated by crystal habit during some crystallization conditions. Consequently, this study may provide a rationale for preventing the misidentification of crystal polymorphs during pharmaceutical manufacturing and development.

papers.title: In-situ Electrochemical Spectroscopic Ellipsometry Characterization of Polymer and MXene Films
papers.abstract: In-situ electrochemical spectroscopic ellipsometry (EC-SE) can enable real-time monitoring of optical properties and thickness changes of surfaces and thin films. This method can provide a broad range of information on the evolution of the microenvironment of an electrode during electrochemical reactions. However, to avoid modeling artifacts, accurate data analysis is critical. Here, we outline key steps in data analysis that can help prevent overfitting and misinterpretation of results. For example, determining the refractive index of the electrolyte at the air/electrolyte interface, along with measurements of the electrode’s dielectric data in dry conditions, can yield more accurate results than simultaneous fitting of all parameters for the electrolyte and electrode. We also present detailed modeling strategies tailored to fitting in-situ cyclic voltammetry (CV) data on various types of thin films, by providing two distinct examples: the thickness change of catalyst polymer films due to swelling by the electrolyte, and the simultaneous change in thickness and optical properties of Ti3C2Tx MXene films due to both reversible (electrochromic effect) and irreversible (degradation) processes. These details can help guide the informed selection of models in similar conditions by providing practical guidelines. The step-by-step approach to modeling can be more broadly adopted to enhance the accuracy and reproducibility of EC-SE experiments for interfacial studies relevant to energy conversion and storage, as well as other electrochemical reactions.

papers.title: Not comparing like with like: a measurement-conditions audit of the solid polymer electrolyte literature
papers.abstract: Ionic conductivities of solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) are routinely compared across publications as though they were measured the same way. We tested that assumption by building a measurement-conditions annotation layer over the largest open compilation of SPE conductivity data (16,009 measurements from 214 source papers), recording for each source study how the measurement was actually made. Fifty-eight papers spanning 1986–2020 and 20 journals were annotated across 59 fields, covering 11,394 measurements, or 71.2% of the compilation. Every condition was extracted twice independently and all substantive disagreements were adjudicated against the source PDFs. Three findings follow. First, 22.5% of the compilation’s measurements come from systems containing no polymer at all—salts in molecular solvents or ionic liquids, classified from the declared composition alone. These sit a median 2.6 orders of magnitude above solvent-free SPEs while being measured 35 řC cooler, and they inflate any pooled statistic drawn from the dataset. Second, refitting each formulation’s temperature series and extrapolating to 25 řC shows that among genuinely solvent-free polymer electrolytes, 50.1% reach 10−4 S cm−1 at the temperature reported but only 3.4% do so at 25 řC, a median loss of 2.54 orders; 97.5% of their best-reported values are taken at ≥60 řC. Pooling classes understates this attrition because liquid systems barely lose anything on cooling. Third, the conditions needed to reproduce or even recompute a conductivity are frequently absent: film thickness is not recoverable for 60.7% of papers, electrode area for 68.4%, per-point equilibration time for 77.2%, and only 5 of 57 papers report a measured residual water content.

papers.title: Are we measuring the right thing? Evaluation practice for machine-learned transition states and reaction barriers
papers.abstract: Machine-learned models of chemical reactivity are now reported with structural deviations below 0.1 Å, barrier errors near 1 kcal/mol and search success rates above 90 %. These figures come from different tasks, reference quantities and denominators, and this review asks what they certify. Its evidence base is five molecular datasets of small-molecule organic saddle points computed with density-functional theory, one catalysis benchmark, and the models scored on them; enzymatic, condensed-phase, photochemical and solid-state barriers are outside its scope. We argue that a reported accuracy is a distance to a reference, summarised by one statistic, on one split, and that each of these choices can materially change apparent performance. A prior question is whether the electronic-energy barrier that is scored is the quantity the application uses. Five of the six datasets rely on proxy verification rather than an intrinsic reaction coordinate calculation at the final labelled level, while the sixth shows that exhaustive verification is feasible at scale. We then ask whether summary statistics carry the information a task consumes, whether one held-out set measures transfer along the relevant axis, and how the error of the reference compares with the thresholds used to rank methods. The kinetic and label-error results are existence proofs on named systems: they show that a mean error is not a universal certificate, not how often current models fail. We propose eight core reporting items with pass conditions and task applicability, a conditional grid in the supporting information, and four missing measurements, including a design for validating a sensitivity-weighted barrier error against downstream kinetic observables. No new electronicstructure, machine-learning or simulation calculation was performed.

papers.title: Spatially resolved 3D aging model linking interdependent degradation mechanisms to knee and end-of-life prediction
papers.abstract: Forecasting battery lifetime and degradation is valuable but difficult because lithium-ion batteries age through complex, non-linear processes. Physics-based models are often preferred for their mechanistic insight into key aging modes. This work introduces a 3D+1D electro-thermal-aging model coupling multiple degradation phenomena to capture lithium inventory loss (LLI), loss of active material (LAM), and impedance increase at the cell level. The model integrates a DFNbased electrochemical component with a thermal model, alongside an aging component considering solid electrolyte interface (SEI) growth, lithium plating, and transition-metal dissolution, migration, and deposition as side reactions. We calibrated the model using data from an industrial graphite/LFP cell cycled under three CCCV protocols from 10 °C to 60 °C and C/3 to 6C. The spatially resolved 3D model predicts the nonlinear capacity "knee" and sudden-death behavior, linking them to interconnected knees of LLI and impedance increase caused by localized transport limitations, matching experimental degradation rates. Our findings indicate that knee point and sudden death result from gradual yet abrupt lithium loss due to continuous lithium plating and impedance rise restricting lithium availability. This study emphasizes the need to explore how aging processes influence the knee point, helping forecast and extend battery lifespan.

papers.title: Evaluation of log D and pKa predictions for the SAMPL8 blind challenge
papers.abstract: The goal of the Statistical Assessment of Modeling of Proteins and Ligands (SAMPL) challenge is to improve the accuracy of computational methods used in drug discovery and design by providing a platform to benchmark different methods and draw the community’s attention to specific areas of improvement. The SAMPL8 physical properties challenge focused on the prediction of pKa and log D for multi-protic compounds with two or more widely separated polar groups. Here, we present an overview of the results from the SAMPL8 challenge. We adopted two different workflows to compare experimental and predicted pKa data due to the presence of multiple macroscopic pKa values for individual compounds. These multiple pKa values meant that it was often unclear which of the microscopic transitions contributed to the observed macroscopic pKa. We find that the performance of different methods for pKa predictions is heavily dependent on how we pair predicted pKa values with measured ones–that is, the underlying mechanism. In contrast to some previous challenges, where analysis focused on pairing calculated pKa values with those which were experimentally closest, we here instead use alternate approaches, presenting two different methods of evaluating pKa predictions. Our first approach uses community consensus, pairing the most popular predicted transition(s) with the experimental value. The second involves selecting the correct transition based on additional experimental data–specifically, pH-dependent solubility curves. We used these two approaches to compare SAMPL submissions from participants using a wide variety of different methods. Results showed that while the numerical predictions for pKa values were often reasonable, different participating methods might disagree about the mechanism behind the pKa, indicating that pKa prediction methods may need to focus more on correct prediction of protonation states, not just pKa values. In the log D analysis we find that most methods performed better in prediction of log D for the octanol-water solvent combination, likely due to the greater abundance of training data for these solvents.

papers.title: Fracture mechanics favors lower-than-expected stack pressures in halide solidstate batteries
papers.abstract: All-solid-state batteries promise safer, more energy-dense storage than cells built on liquid electrolytes. Among solid-state electrolytes, halide electrolytes offer high ionic conductivity, anodic stability, and room-temperature processability, yet stable cycling is typically achieved under stack pressures of tens to hundreds of megapascals, for reasons that remain unclear. Here we identify the unusually high susceptibility of brittle halide electrolytes to fracture as the mechanism underlying and show that stack pressure—conventionally applied to suppress mechanical damage—can instead promote it by enhancing strain transfer from the active materials to the surrounding electrolyte. Operando scanning electron microscopy captures crack initiation and propagation within electrolyte domains in composite cathodes driven by active material volume changes, while nanoindentation reveals an exceptionally low fracture toughness of 0.23 MPa·m1/2 for the representative halide electrolyte Li3YCl6, substantially lower than the 0.7−1.0 MPa·m1/2 for typical sulfide and oxide electrolytes. Pressure-dependent electrochemical and morphological analyses show that, although modest pressure is sufficient to maintain interparticle contact, increasing pressure beyond this level promotes electrolyte fracture and accelerates capacity loss. Guided by this insight, we demonstrate an anode-free halide pouch cell that retains 85% of its capacity over 200 cycles at C/3 under only 2 MPa. Together, these findings show that the high stack pressures widely used in halide solid-state batteries primarily compensate for the consequences of electrolyte fracture rather than reflecting the pressure intrinsically required for stable operation, establishing a mechanical basis for low-pressure halide solid-state batteries.

papers.title: QM_eMMa: An Open GPU-Accelerated Framework for Ab Initio QM/MM Molecular Dynamics and Enhanced Sampling
papers.abstract: Ab initio QM/MM molecular dynamics can describe chemical processes accurately, but its practical use is limited by the cost of repeated electronic-structure calculations and by overhead in coupling molecular-dynamics and quantum-chemistry programs. We present QM_eMMa, an open interface that couples AMBER to PySCF/GPU4PySCF while keeping the electronic-structure engine and GPU context active throughout a simulation. The converged electronic density is reused between consecutive MD steps, with automatic recovery through a cold-start SCF calculation when needed. We first optimized the workflow with a GH125 α-mannosidase model. Removing repeated interface overhead increased throughput by approximately 26%. Systematic energy and force comparisons then identified a less expensive numerical setting that retained the accuracy required for MD and increased throughput by a further 23% in independent GH125 simulations. The same protocol enabled stable DFT/MM dynamics of a larger enzymatic QM region containing 115 electronic centers and sustained 145 ps of ab initio well-tempered metadynamics, recovering the principal α-mannose conformational basins observed previously. Finally, a reactive aqueous SN2 benchmark showed that the optimized and stricter protocols gave activation and reaction free energies differing by only 0.73 and 0.01 kcal mol-1, respectively, while the optimized calculation remained faster. QM_eMMa therefore provides a practical open framework for single-GPU DFT/MM dynamics and enhanced sampling, with numerical approximations selected through explicit validation of energies, forces, dynamics, and chemical reactivity.

papers.title: Multimodal LLM-Assisted Diagnosis of Cryptic Failure Modes in High-Throughput Experimentation: A Case Study in Gold Nanorod Synthesis
papers.abstract: Self-driving labs typically optimize experiments within a predefined design space. Yet high-throughput campaigns can fail for reasons outside this design space, in-cluding reagent state, stock solution quality, and handling history. Here, we present a case study of a five-plate high-throughput gold nanorod synthesis campaign in which a multimodal large language model (LLM) helped diagnose such cryptic failure modes. We used low-cost camera images for rapid assessment of seed and synthesis state, with UV–vis spectroscopy when the images were insufficient for failure diagnosis. The campaign included an abnormal seed batch, a visually plausible synthesis with hidden spectroscopic defects, and a plate-wide failed synthesis in which most wells showed weak spectra with a strong rise toward the near-infrared. In response, the LLM intervened by questioning the seed preparation step and reagent handling instead of optimizing the screened concentrations of silver nitrate and ascorbic acid. To quantify recovery, we defined a UV–vis spectral roughness metric based on local spectral interpolation across the synthesis grid. The final synthesis had the lowest roughness, Rspec = 0.636 compared with ∼ 0.772 for earlier successful runs, and the highest median longitudinal-window absorbance. Our results show the potential of multimodal LLMs upstream of autonomous optimization in self-driving labs to identify when an experiment has failed for reasons outside the nominal design space and when additional characterization is needed before optimization should continue.

papers.title: Synthesis of Dihydro-indolo-oxazines via a RedOx‑Neutral, Gold‑Catalyzed Hydride‑Transfer Process
papers.abstract: RedOx neutral gold-mediated processes are particularly valuable for C-H bond functionalization. When these transformations proceed stepwise via intramolecular hydride transfer to an electrophilic Gold(I) center, their efficiency critically depends on the nature of the hydride donor. We report herein that, in contrast to tertiary amines, which strongly coordinate to gold and thereby tend to inhibit catalysis, benzyl ethers can serve as effective hydride donors, enabling a smooth catalytic C-H functionalization sequence. This reactivity is illustrated by the synthesis of a series of dihydro-indolo-oxazines, obtained in moderate to high yields under mild catalytic conditions.

papers.title: Unravelling concomitant pseudopolymorphs of 5,10,15,20-meso-tetrakis(4-hydroxy-3,5-dimethoxyphenyl)porphyrin: structural insight in to a guest free and two solvated forms by using MicroED
papers.abstract: Crystal structures of three concomitant pseudopolymorphs of 5,10,15,20-meso-tetrakis(4-hydroxy-3,5-dimethoxyphenyl)porphyrin (1), comprising a solvent free form and two solvates, were elucidated by three-dimensional rotational electron diffraction (3DED/MicroED). This finding presents structural insight of 1 and highlights the potential of MicroED in resolving complex pseudopolymorphic mixtures from a single batch of sample. The ability of porphyrins to spontaneously organize into a highly ordered supramolecular architecture via noncovalent interactions has made them attractive building blocks for functional materials. Such assemblies are fascinating because they can be prepared relatively easily, are biomimetic in nature and exhibit excellent solution processability. Moreover, they give rise to diverse solid state arrangements in response to environmental factors, particularly solvents. This structural versatility has enabled their exploration in a wide range of applications

papers.title: Uncovering the Relative Importance of Chemical Emissions Arising from the Application as Polymer Additives
papers.abstract: Polymers can act as “Trojan Horse” releasing toxic chemical additives into ecosystems and individual organisms. However, the extent to which additive use contributes to the overall emissions and environmental burdens of multifunctional chemicals remains poorly understood. Here, we use polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), polybrominated diphenyl ethers (PBDEs), and short-, medium-, and long-chain chlorinated paraffins (SCCPs, MCCPs, and LCCPs) as case studies to quantify the contribution of polymer additive use to their global historical emissions and environmental burdens. We revisit their global emission inventories and derive emissions exclusively associated with additive use using the CiP-CAFE model. The total emissions and those arising from additive use are both fed into the BETR-Global model to quantify the environmental burden attributable to additive applications. Additive applications are estimated to account for 38%, 84%, 14%, 26%, and 9% of cumulative global emissions of PCBs, PBDEs, SCCPs, MCCPs, and LCCPs, respectively. Additive and non-additive applications differ substantially in their release characteristics, including emission factors during use and end-of-life management, the mode of emission, temporal delays, and spatial distributions. By 2025 (for PCBs and PBDEs) and 2020 (for SCCPs, MCCPs, and LCCPs), 24%, 92%, 51%, 42%, and 13% of the global environmental burden, respectively, can be attributed to additive use, with disproportionately larger contributions in more dispersive environmental compartments, particularly the atmosphere and seawater, and therefore also in remote polar and oceanic regions.

papers.title: Shaping Tumor Targeting: How Nanoparticle Morphology Influences Penetration and Accumulation in 3D Breast Cancer Models
papers.abstract: Efficient nanomedicine delivery to solid tumors requires both tissue penetration and cellular accumulation, yet how nanocarrier architecture governs these processes remains poorly understood. Here, molecular polymer brushes spanning hydrodynamic radii (Rh) of 10–45 nm and aspect ratios of 1.2–8.1, with identical polysarcosine surface chemistry, are used to investigate transport in two extracellular matrix (ECM)-embedded breast cancer tumoroids: BT549 and MDA-MB-468 cells, separately. Passive transport reveals tumor entry as a major 2 barrier, while diffusion inside the tumoroid depends much less on particle morphology. While all particles enter the tumor spheroids, the smallest, near-spherical PeptoBrush (PB50, Rh = 10 nm) is the most efficient architecture for tumor penetration, which underlines that in an orientation of worm-like PeptoBrushes does not occur at the matrix tumor interphase under the experimental conditions. Functionalization of PB50 with an average of two cetuximab molecules strongly enhances EGFR-mediated tumor-cell association and accumulation while preserving deep tissue penetration. Time-resolved imaging reveals initial peripheral enrichment followed by progressive penetration toward the tumoroid core, consistent with a transient binding-site barrier. These findings distinguish two complementary determinants of intratumoral distribution in the extracellular matrix tumoroid model: nanocarrier morphology governs passive penetration, whereas antibody-mediated recognition drives cellular binding and tumoroid accumulation.

papers.title: Complementary chemical probes and substrates reveal split subsite specificity in a fungal GH12 glucanase
papers.abstract: Xyloglucans are structurally heterogeneous polysaccharides in which xylosylation patterns vary along the β-(1,4)-glucan backbone. Because endo-glycanases engage substrates across both sides of the scissile bond, we hypothesised that GH12 substrate selectivity may vary across the catalytic cleft. We combined activity-based profiling of basidiomycete secretomes with defined fluorogenic substrates, oligosaccharide product mapping and structural analyses. TlGH12A, a previously characterised endo-β-glucanase, reacted with a xyloglucan-configured cyclophellitol probe despite showing no detectable activity on polymeric xyloglucan. Complementary analyses revealed that substrate recognition differs across its catalytic cleft. TlGH12A hydrolysed XXXG-4MU approximately 60-fold more efficiently than GGGG-4MU, demonstrating a strong negative-subsite preference for xylosylated glucan. Crystal structures showed xylosylated glucan occupying subsites −4 to −1, whereas unbranched glucan occupied the positive subsites. Comparison with ligand-bound GH12 xyloglucanases identified steric constraints that may restrict positive-subsite accommodation of Xyl substituents. Sequence-network, phylogenetic and structural-modelling analyses suggest that this architecture recurs among Basidiomycota GH12 endoglucanases. Complementary probes, hydrolysable substrates and structural analyses resolved the basis of this previously unrecognised distribution of specificity in TlGH12A. These findings reveal how substrate recognition can vary across a GH12 catalytic cleft, with implications for understanding fungal plant cell wall deconstruction and for identifying and engineering glucan-active enzymes with distinct substrate specificities.

papers.title: Computational Fluid Dynamics-Informed Machine Learning-Enabled Digital Twin for Vapor Maldistribution Prediction in Structured Packed Distillation Columns
papers.abstract: Vapor maldistribution in structured-packed distillation columns reduces separation performance. While experimental measurements are essential for characterizing column hydrodynamics, they often lack the resolution to capture velocity distributions or to systematically quantify how column geometry and operating conditions affect vapor maldistribution throughout the packed bed. High-fidelity, first-principles computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations can provide detailed spatial flow information, but their high computational cost limits the rapid evaluation of alternative column designs and operating conditions. To address this limitation, a CFD-informed machine-learning (ML) reduced-order model (ROM) framework was developed to rapidly predict vapor flow uniformity in structured-packed distillation columns. 3D CFD simulations were performed for 13 column geometries by varying column diameter, inlet diameter, nozzle-to-packing clearance, and vapor mass flow rate, yielding a dataset of 65 simulation cases for parametric analysis and ML model training. Vapor maldistribution was quantified using the area-weighted coefficient of variation (CoV) of streamwise velocity across 13 packing layers. CFD results indicated that vapor maldistribution was most pronounced near the packed-bed entrance and progressively decreased through the packing. Higher vapor flow rates and smaller inlet diameters generally increased maldistribution in the inletdominated region, while the effect of nozzle-to-packing clearance depended on column geometry and scale. For instance, increasing the inlet diameter reduced the Layer-1 CoV from 51.01% to 30.73% in the 47.75-in. column and from 48.82% to 22.32% in the 120in. column. A Gaussian process regression (GPR)-based ROM was subsequently trained using the CFD dataset and evaluated through leave-one-geometry-out cross-validation. Across 65 held-out cases and 845 packed-layer predictions, the ROM achieved a mean absolute error of 0.851, a root mean squared error of 1.524, and a coefficient of determination of 0.980. Prediction errors were primarily concentrated in the lower packing layers, where the flow was strongly influenced by the inlet geometry, and decreased substantially farther downstream. The resulting CFD-informed ML framework offers a computationally efficient digital-twin development workflow for predicting vapor maldistribution in previously untested column geometries and, within the investigated design space, enables rapid geometry screening and design optimization of structuredpacked distillation columns.

papers.title: Cooperative Electronic Programming by Phenanthroline Pockets, Ethynyl Bridges, and Pyrene Cores in a One-Dimensional Covalent Organic Framework for Chemoselective Nitrate-to-Ammonia Electrosynthesis
papers.abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) offer molecular precision, yet their catalytic function is often treated as though the metal center operates independently of the scaffold that surrounds it. Here, we introduce TU-24, a one-dimensional COF in which phenanthroline pockets, ethynyl bridges, and pyrene cores are deliberately integrated to co-program coordination geometry, frontier electronic structure, and reaction progression for nitrate-to-ammonia electrosynthesis. Molecular deconstruction reveals noninterchangeable functions: the pyrene core supplies frontier-accessible π states, the ethynyl linkage preserves electronic communication, and the phenanthroline motif tunes the near-Fermi-level manifold while creating an accessible N,N coordination pocket. Postsynthetic Cu incorporation preserves the crystalline architecture while generating spatially dispersed, approximately four-coordinate Cu–N/O sites electronically distinct from metallic Cu and bulk copper oxides. TU-24-Cu delivers 92.0% NH3 Faradaic efficiency at −0.7 V versus RHE and an areal NH3 yield of 1.71 mg h-1 cm-2 at −0.8 V, while strongly suppressing nitrite release. Operando ATR-SEIRAS and density functional theory converge on a deep-reduction pathway involving hydrogenated N–O intermediates, with the framework favoring the lower-energy *NHO channel and adaptively weakening Cu–N binding as hydrogenation advances. These findings establish a broader design principle: COF electrocatalysis can be programmed not merely by installing an active site, but by electronically wiring that site to a framework that governs intermediate retention, pathway branching, and forward continuity across a multielectron reaction network.

papers.title: Group-Invariant Certificates and Solvers for Diversity Selection in Combinatorial Libraries
papers.abstract: Selection of massive, mutually non-redundant subset of highly scoring compounds from a combinatorial library is a standardized design in early stage drug discovery. It is usually solved by heuristics that return a ranking of capable candidates, however there is no quality guarantee. We formulate and introduce a method as maximum weighted independent set with a parameter soft redundancy penalty on a Cayley graph over the abelian group ℤ𝑛, 𝑞—where 𝑛 is the number of substitution positions and 𝑞 the number of substituents per position. The formulation rests on one explicit and falsifiable modelling commitment: pairwise redundancy should depend only on the group difference of two compounds. Under this commitment the interactionmatrix is diagonalised by the group characters, its spectrum is available in closed form via Krawtchouk polynomials, and classical coding-theoretic bounds (Hoffman ratio, Delsarte linear programming) apply verbatim to the unweighted problem. Our contribution is an interface rather than new bound technology: we derive two valid upper bounds for the weighted objective, report the resulting a posteriori approximation-ratio lower bound 𝜌lower = 𝑓(𝑆)/𝑈 , and introduce a coset-decomposition family of certificates that recouples the weight term with the combinatorial structure. On synthetic libraries the spectral certificate yields a mean quality floor of 59.3%, the Delsarte version 67.7%, and the coset family a further 3.3 points. A gap decomposition against exhaustively computed optima shows that 77% of the residual gap is bound looseness rather than solver suboptimality, which redirects effort to the certificate side. On the solver side, group invariance permits column generation in𝑂(𝑁)without ever materialising the 𝑁 × 𝑁 matrix, and evaluation of all 𝑁 translates of a linear code by a single group Fourier transform in𝑂(𝑁 log𝑁); exhaustive enumeration of cyclic codes combined with this step doubles the quality floor relative to a lookahead greedy at 𝑁 = 8192 while running four times faster. We report three negative results that we believe are useful to record: Pólya-based budget allocation is significantly worse than uniform allocation (𝑡 = −4.65), non-coordinate conjugacy classes of index-2 subgroups are systematically looser, and orbit-level selection never wins. All experiments use synthetic libraries; no chemical validation is claimed.

papers.title: Aged Hops Increase 3-Methyl-2-butene-1-thiol (MBT), β-Ionone, and Branched-Chain Esters in Beer
Report – 4th Ontologies4Chem Workshop
papers.abstract: The Ontologies4Chem workshop series brings together developers and users of chemical ontologies to align ontology initiatives with shared standards and approaches to semantic interoperability. The 4th Ontologies4Chem Workshop, organized by TIB in collaboration with the Beilstein-Institute, the NFDI4Chem Consortium, the NFDI4Cat Consortium, and the Physical Sciences Data Infrastructure (PSDI) took place from November 11 to 13, 2025 in Limburg an der Lahn (Hessen, Germany). The programme covered chemical ontologies and their applications on the first day, the ontological representation of chemical reactions and experimental workflows on the second, and the reuse and further development of ChEBI as the central resource for chemical entities on the third. Talks on RO-Crate, DCAT-AP+, and chemDCAT-AP added the provenance and packaging layer that complements ontologies in FAIR data workflows. A central outcome of the workshop is the introduction of the Ontologies4Chem Canon, a vision of a living, community-curated body of the essential ontologies for chemistry together with their design patterns and the discourse around them. It rests on modular, OBO-aligned design, reuse before creation, the IUPAC Gold Book as source of definitions, and ODK-based development and deployment pipelines, provided by the NFDI4Chem Terminology Service and related internally through SSSOM mappings. The hacking sessions initiated the migration of the CHEMINF ontology to an ODK-based infrastructure and led to a decision, taken together with the ChEBI team, to reincorporate disjointness axioms into the ChEBI release cycle. Presentations on ontology pre-training, ChemLog, and Chebifier 2 showed how ontologies and machine learning reinforce each other. A panel discussion with the ChEBI team identified sustainable, community-driven governance and funding as the decisive challenges for the field.

papers.title: Towards Universal Calibration for Infrared Spectroscopy with Probabilistic Interference Removal
papers.abstract: Structured interferences from substrates, matrices, and instrumental artifacts in mid-infrared (IR) spectra often overlap with analyte features and introduce errors in quantitative analysis. Existing correction methods rely on heuristic parameter selection and frequently perform suboptimally when applied across a diverse set of samples. We present a probabilistic framework, Variational-Inference-based Background Elimination in Spectroscopy (VIBES), for automated estimation of regularization hyperparameters from the data that enables removal of such interferences. Background contributions are modeled using covariance structures learned from analytical blank measurements, analyte signals as residual components from background removal under appropriate probabilistic assumptions that promote robustness and hyperparameters calibrated by maximizing a variational approximation to the model evidence. VIBES is demonstrated on two types of transmission-mode measurements with different types of background variations and analyte features, and shows capability to isolate the analyte absorption spectrum with high correlation (r > 0.95) between absorbance and mass loading across sharp and broad peak spectra. Interference-corrected spectra are furthermore shown to be consistent with absorption coefficients derived from complex refractive indices acquired from other measurement modalities. The possibility for quantitative extraction of analyte spectra in the presence of various interferences suggests a path toward development of universal calibrations for mid-IR spectroscopy.

papers.title: Carbonylative Cross Couplings Promoted by a Metal Carbonyl Complex in Catalytic Amounts
papers.abstract: Carbon monoxide is a highly valuable building block that enables the rapid construction of complex molecules like pharmaceuticals from simple and commercial precursors. However, the handling of CO requires special and elaborate precautions, since it is a highly toxic and odourless gas supplied in pressurized gas cylinders. To improve operations with carbon monoxide several CO surrogates including Mo(CO) 6 have been introduced, which form CO in enclosed gas reactors on demand. Herein, we report on the discovery of Fe 2 (CO) 9 as a highly efficient CO surrogate, which unlike preceding works is capable to transfer 8 out of 9 CO ligands onto the molecule of interest. This enables the application diiron nonacarbonyl in “catalytic amount” of 15 mol% with regard to the aryl halide coupling partner (100 mol%). The high synthetic value of the novel approach is witnessed by three different carbonylative cross couplings, syntheses of four pharmaceuticals and a head-to-head comparison with Mo(CO) 6 as gold standard.

papers.title: Certified Zero-Frequency Response and a Fourth-Order Mechanism Test for Nonlinear Soft-Constrained Langevin Dynamics
papers.abstract: Eliminating stiff internal coordinates can preserve equilibrium while changing kinetics, and a finite-time coarse-graining error does not by itself control a zero-frequency transport observable. We study a reversible overdamped Langevin model with constant microscopic mobility and nonlinear soft constraints, Uϵ(x, y; γ) = V (x− Fγ) + |y − g(x)|2 2ϵ , where V may be nonquadratic and nonconvex. An exact coordinate transformation factorizes the equilibrium measure but produces a nontrivial kinetic metric. For any mean-zero source depending only on x, we prove a direct zero-frequency comparison between the full microscopic inverse response Rϵ and the constrained geometric response R0: 0 ≤ R0 −Rϵ ≤ ϵmT 2 Eπ∥Dw0∥2F , where w0 is the source-specific corrector derived from the effective Poisson equation. The bound contains no inverse global spectral gap. For a one-dimensional translated potential, the conjugateforce friction closes explicitly and admits a certified first finite-stiffness correction with two-sided O(ϵ2) remainder bounds. We then derive a mechanism test: any autonomous hidden-history model for which two-time forces are conditionally standard Gaussian with history-dependent correlation must have a nonnegative connected fourth quantity K4(t). A fully reversible nonlinear constant-mobility Langevin model violates this condition: K4,ϵ(t) < 0 for a nonzero short-time interval at every finite ϵ, while its constrained limit satisfies K4(t) < 0 for every t > 0. The all-time sign is certified by a five-dimensional outward-rounded interval Schur test controlling the infinite even sector of the generator. Integer interval arithmetic, independent primal–dual calculations of the full two-dimensional process, and a reversible finite-volume discretization provide mutually distinct checks. These results are a controlled response and model-discrimination theory for a specified soft-constrained class; they do not constitute a general theory of glass formation or a bulk shear-viscosity prediction.

papers.title: Large Language Models in Chemistry and Materials Science: A Comprehensive Survey
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are expanding the scope of artificial intelligence in chemistry and materials science by connecting scientific knowledge, heterogeneous data, computational tools, and experimental workflows. This article presents a comprehensive survey of the foundations, representations, methods, applications, and evaluation of LLM-centered scientific systems. We develop a non-exclusive representation-by-mechanism taxonomy linking text, molecular and crystal structures, spectra, images, and numerical properties with model adaptation, cross-representation grounding, external knowledge and tools, and workflow coordination. Within this framework, we synthesize prompting, domain pre-training and fine-tuning, preference alignment and verifier-driven reinforcement learning, multimodal integration, and retrieval- and agent-based approaches. Applications span literature understanding, property prediction, molecular and materials design, synthesis planning, characterization, hypothesis generation, and closed-loop discovery. By linking method choices to input information, task definitions, and validation conditions, the framework clarifies which reported results can be compared and what scientific claims they support. We organize representative datasets and benchmarks and introduce an evaluation matrix connecting task performance with information fidelity, uncertainty, chemical and physical validity, and workflow reliability. Detailed supplementary cases document the settings and evidence underlying key comparisons. Finally, we identify research priorities in integrated scientific representations, efficient adaptation, reusable knowledge and tool interfaces, and verifiable human-machine collaboration. By linking methodological developments to scientific objectives, this survey provides a conceptual map and practical guidance for developing and assessing LLM-enabled chemical and materials discovery.

papers.title: Antimicrobial Resistance Breakers That Specifically Restore Efficacy of Polymyxins
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a global threat to human health and prosperity. Antimicrobial resistance breakers (ARBs), molecules that reverse AMR e.g., by blocking enzymes involved in bacterial membrane remodelling, are an attractive solution to restore the efficacy of existing antibiotics. We have identified several hits from in silico screening that restore polymyxin B (PmB) efficacy at concentrations of 250-500 µM in the clinically relevant ESKAPE pathogen Enterobacter bugandensis. The compounds act in tandem with PmB, but not with other antibiotics. They have no significant antibacterial effect themselves and may therefore be regarded as true resistance breakers. Preliminary results suggest that at least two of the three hit compounds may act via covalent bond formation with a target enzyme.

papers.title: Neutron Crystallography Maps the Interaction Landscape of Pseudomonas aeruginosa LecA with Deuterated Aromatic β-Galactoside
papers.abstract: Aromatic derivatives of β-galactosides are potent inhibitors of the LecA lectin, a key virulence factor of Pseudomonas aeruginosa, involved in host recognition, tissue adhesion and biofilm formation. This opportunistic bacterial pathogen is considered a serious global health threat, particularly due to the emergence of multidrug-resistant strains. Anti-adhesive and anti-biofilm compounds represent promising alternatives or complements to conventional antibiotic therapies. The design of such pathoblockers requires detailed structural insights into their interactions with the target protein. Neutron macromolecular crystallography (NMX) provides complementary structural information to X-ray diffraction (XRD), by enabling the localization of hydrogen atoms, but typically requires the use of deuterium-labeled molecules. We developed a unique approach combining bacterial production of deuterated galactose and its functionalization with a deuterated phenyl group, resulting in the first synthesis of perdeuterated phenyl-β-galactoside, PheβGal-d16. The structure of the deuterated bacterial receptor LecA in complex with PheβGal-d16 was determined using neutron diffraction, providing experimental localization of hydrogen atoms involved in hydrophobic contacts with the Pro38 and Gln53 residues, and in the unusual T-shaped π-stacking interaction with His50. These observations rationalize the 10-fold affinity increase measured for an aromatic β-galactoside compared to galactose.

papers.title: Exploration of Low-Crystalline NiPd(CN)4 by Ab Initio Global Structure Search
papers.abstract: For poorly crystalline inorganic materials, it is often difficult to uniquely determine the crystal structure from diffraction measurements alone. In this study, we identified the crystal structure of a newly synthesized metal cyanide NiPd(CN) 4 by combining experiments with ab initio calculations. The observed powder X-ray diffraction pattern could not be explained by any previously reported analogous structures, while magnetization measurements indicated the presence of a finite local magnetic moment in the ground state. Using these experimental constraints as clues, we obtained a relaxed tilt structure with distorted square-planar coordination through heuristic structure modeling, and discovered a µ-bridged structure, in which Ni adopts a six-coordinate octahedral environment, through ab initio global structure search. The candidate structures were comprehensively validated through comparisons between theory and experiment for powder X-ray diffraction, Raman scattering, XAFS, STEM, and UV–vis spectroscopy, and the µ-bridged structure was found to reproduce the experimental results well. Based on these findings, we conclude that the µ-bridged structure is strongly suggested to be the realized structure of NiPd(CN) 4 .

papers.title: A conformational filter protocol for structures with topological symmetry
papers.abstract: This paper presents an efficient conformational filter protocol for handling structures with topological symmetry implemented in the open-source molecular modelling program curcuma. This approach addresses the challenge of comparing molecular conformations in which symmetrically equivalent atoms may have different indices in the structure files. Descriptors that are independent of the storing order of the atoms (energy differences, rotational constants, and Vietoris-Rips (VR) persistence barcodes) are used to efficiently predict potential structural similarities before performing computationally expensive permutations on selected structure pairs using distinct permutation approaches implemented in curcuma or the external tool molalign. The filter protocol operates in three phases: 1) initial RMSD-based filtering and data-set-specific training of the atom index-independent descriptor thresholds, 2) permutation-based filtering using parameterised descriptors, and 3) final filtering using stored permutation vectors. Our evaluation using 395 complex conformations optimised at different levels of theory shows that although conformational geometries typically remain similar across different theoretical methods; their relative energies can vary significantly between different levels of theory. This highlights the importance of efficient conformational filtering in identifying structurally unique conformers, particularly when faster semiempirical quantum chemical methods are used, which might incorrectly evaluate certain conformers as energetically unfavourablein contrast to slower more accurate quantum mechinal methods. A key finding is that performing all possible RMSD calculations does not necessarily yield the optimal filtering result, as the final outcome depends significantly on the specific order of the structure comparisons.

papers.title: Reply to a comment ‘On the futility of the Fuoss–Kirkwood relation’ by Gradišar & Boškoski
papers.abstract: A recent comment on our previous paper (Electrochem. Commun. 164 (2024) 107731) regarding the futility of the so-called Fuoss-Kirkwood (FK) relation presents an appreciated opportunity for clarification and further argumentation. In this reply, we provide additional arguments suggesting that the commenting authors are misguided in concluding that this relation is valid, and that, when correctly applied, the FK relation can be straightforwardly employed to derive analytical expressions of the real-valued distribution of relaxation times (DRT) for model impedances that are explicitly known in closed form and do not possess ω-domain singularities. Moreover, we present analytical expressions of the DRT for the impedances of the Cole-Cole (CC) and Havriliak-Negami models, which are generally complex-valued, and validate their accuracy by incorporating them into the DRT integral equation with a Debye kernel, utilising the proven sifting property of the δ distribution.

papers.title: Strategic Bromine Substitution in Aryl Aminoboranes Unlocks Photochemical Route to Narrow-Band Emitting Azaborines
papers.abstract: The development of UV/deep-blue emitters with high color purity remains a central challenge in OLED research, where conventional fluorophores suffer from broad emission and triplet-harvesting systems compromise stability. Here we show that strategic ortho-bromine substitution in bis-aryl aminoboranes unlocks an intramolecular photo-cyclization that allows direct access to azaborine frameworks under mild conditions and near quantitative yield. The high triplet energy of the aminoborane precursors enables efficient population of the T1 state, triggering ring closure and suppressing the twisted intramolecular charge-transfer (TICT) behavior characteristic of the open scaffolds. The resulting azaborines display deep-blue to near-UV emission, with remarkably narrow bandwidths (FWHM down to 0.09 eV in solution and 0.04 eV in glassy matrix) and localized excited states (LE). A systematic library screening unveils the modularity of this approach and shows that cyclization rate correlate with spin-orbit coupling (SOC) and triplet-state localization on the B-N bond. This work establishes the first photochemical route to azaborines and provides a synthetically versatile platform for high-purity emitters, suited for next-generation optoelectronic applications.
