papers.title: Why Electrochemical–Thermal–Mechanical Understanding is Needed to Explain Knees in Lithium-Ion Batteries Degradation
papers.abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are essential to modern life, spanning portable electronics, electric vehicles and grid storage. Yet, their degradation mechanisms remain incompletely understood, particularly the sudden capacity drops known as knee points. In this study, commercial Samsung 50S cells are degraded under various cooling setups and charge/discharge rates, revealing consistent knees in slow-discharge cells even above 80% of initial capacity, while fast-discharge cells degraded beyond 60% without knees. Using a multiphysics characterisation approach, we decipher the origins of these knees: attainment of lower voltages enhances silicon activity, triggering a chain of mechanisms that culminate in sudden failure. Specifically, recurring SEI reformation drives a dual pathway: gas release displaces electrolyte, inducing localised current concentration, overcharge and a first pattern of lithium plating, while simultaneous electrode thickening deforms the jelly roll. This mechanical effect, combined with geometrical heterogeneities from the welded tab design, produces a second pattern of lithium plating in later ageing states, identified as the primary cause of the knees. These findings elucidate the complex coupling of multiscale degradation mechanisms and demonstrate that robust state-of-health monitoring must be holistic, incorporating indicators beyond traditional temperature, capacity and resistance.

papers.title: Interfacial Solvent Engineering of Zinc Porphyrin Hydrogen-Bonded Organic Frameworks Enables Aggregation-Enhanced Electrochemiluminescence for Synthetic Cannabinoid Sensing
papers.abstract: Zinc porphyrin hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (ZnTCPP HOFs) are prone to uncontrolled short-range π–π stacking at solid/liquid interfaces, which leads to aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ) and consequently limits their electrochemiluminescence (ECL) efficiency. Current strategies for suppressing ACQ primarily depend on covalent or coordination bonds and often involve laborious synthesis. Addressing this challenge from the perspective of colloid and interface science, this study introduces a chitosan (CS)–DMF counter-solvent precipitation strategy. This approach reorganizes the hydrogen-bond network and fosters electrostatic association between CS and the carboxyl groups of ZnTCPP HOFs, thereby facilitating a controlled transformation of bulk crystals into micro/nano-aggregates. This synergistic effect suppresses short-range π–π stacking while enhancing long-range aggregation-induced emission (AIE), leading to a significant improvement in ECL efficiency without the need for an additional co-reaction promoter. On this basis, an aptamer-based ECL sensor was developed for the ultrasensitive detection of 5F-EDMB-PINACA, achieving a limit of detection of 8.61 × 10 -16 g/L and a linear range spanning nine orders of magnitude. These findings underscore the efficacy of colloidal-interface regulation in ECL sensing.

papers.title: RaX-DT: An Open-Source Platform for Automated Molecular Docking Workflows and Reproducible Pipeline Validation
papers.abstract: Automated molecular docking workflows often fail not at the scoring engine but at the interfaces between ligand preparation, protein preparation, binding-site definition, and post-processing. We present RaX-DT, an open-source, Docker Compose–deployable platform that integrates these steps in a single web application and an optional conversational assistant. RaX-DT automates 3D ligand generation, tautomer/protonation-state handling, protein cleaning, binding-site definition via P2Rank, Fpocket, or user-specified coordinates, GNINA-based docking, and interactive result visualization. Because end-to-end automation can introduce silent failures, we validated the assembled workflow on 231 protein–ligand co-crystal structures from DUD-E and LIT-PCBA rather than treating the docking engine in isolation. Of these, 186 structures completed successfully; the top-ranked pose reproduced the crystallographic pose within 2.0 Å for 65.1% of completed structures, and the best of the five top-scoring poses reached 77.4%. Validation also exposed a box-placement defect that would have produced plausible-looking but invalid output, underscoring the value of pipeline-level quality control. RaX-DT is released under the MIT license and is intended to improve accessibility, reproducibility, and transparency in routine docking workflows.

papers.title: Designing Cure Kinetics in Polyester Networks: Tuning Initiator Content to Control Gelation and Glass-Transition Development
papers.abstract: Unsaturated polyester networks remain widely used in composite manufacturing, construction, and infrastructure, and yet the practical relationship between initiator content and cure trajectory is not always reported consistently across industrial formulations. Using a field-representative unsaturated polyester systems, real-time gelation/exotherm were tracked with differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) to map how initiator type and content govern gel time, exotherm behavior, and the thermal state of the cured network. Across the compositions examined, gel time varied roughly four-fold, from approximately 10–12 minutes to 44–45 minutes, and peak exotherm temperature reached approximately 123–137 °C. Across an extended 0.8–4% peroxide range, the first-scan glass transition (Tg1) rose from 46.15 to 56.38 °C and residual cure enthalpy (ΔH) fell from 33.35 to 15.67 J/g, while the fully cured glass transition (Tg2) rose sharply to approximately 100–103 °C at intermediate peroxide content before declining to 84.74–89.20 °C at 3–4%. These results indicate that additional initiator can accelerate cure and reduce measured residual reaction while not necessarily improving the final thermal state of the network.

papers.title: A theory of inner-sphere reorganization energy for electrocatalysis
papers.abstract: In Marcus theory, reorganization energy links thermodynamics and kinetics for outer-sphere electron transfer, in which the redox centre exchanges an electron without changing its bonding to the electrode. Most electrocatalytic elementary steps are instead inner-sphere processes: the reacting intermediate is part of the interface, and surface bonding changes with charge transfer. A general thermodynamic definition of the full nonequilibrium preparation cost of such a bonded interface is lacking, leaving equilibrium descriptors and measured rates without a common theoretical basis. Here we define this quantity thermodynamically and provide a first-principles procedure for its calculation. A Legendre transform of fixed-potential thermodynamics yields an internal free-energy surface in which interfacial polarization and surface bond state are coupled variables, while electrode potential remains an external control. For a specified elementary event, inner-sphere reorganization energy is the finite free-energy cost of preparing a product-like interface before relaxation. Writing this cost as a Bregman difference separates it from the reaction driving force and relates it to a weighted integral of local interfacial stiffness. The classical Marcus expression is recovered as the one-dimensional harmonic charge-only limit of this framework. Applied to Volmer hydrogen oxidation on

papers.title: Quantifying Validation-Induced Optimism in Machine Learning for Food Spectroscopy: An Empirical Multi-Dataset Benchmark
papers.abstract: Background: Evaluating machine-learning regression models in food spectroscopy using random row-wise cross-validation ignores hierarchical experimental structures (replicate scans, aliquot extractions, packaging batches, instruments, and harvest campaigns). While theoretical warnings caution against sample leakage, the chemometric literature lacks a multidataset empirical quantification of validation-induced optimism, its impact on model selection, and its underlying physical mechanisms. Methods: We executed an empirical multi-dataset benchmark across four benchmark food spectroscopy collections encompassing 12,706 source spectra/records, with 6,376 spectra evaluated in primary regression workflows: Cargill corn near-infrared (NIR; n = 240 spectra across 80 physical grain samples and 3 spectrometers; targets: moisture and protein), edible vegetable oils Raman (Gilbraith , 2024; n = 215 spectra across 52 distinct reference titration determinations; target: peroxide value), mango fruit dry matter NIR (Anderson , 2020; n = 4,233 calibration spectra across 5 cultivars and n = 1,448 external harvest season spectra; target: dry matter content), and Tecator meat NIR (n = 240 spectra with 24 duplicate pairs [48 rows participating in identical pairs], leaving 216 unique spectral profiles; targets: fat and moisture). Six regression algorithms—partial least squares (PLS), Ridge regression, support vector regression (SVR-RBF), Random Forest, XGBoost, and k-nearest neighbours (kNN, serving as a diagnostic sentinel)—were evaluated across four hierarchical validation tiers: Level 1 (random row-wise cross-validation), Level 2 (sample-aware group cross-validation, reference-valuegrouped validation, or deduplicated validation), Level 3 (cultivar-aware validation), and Level 4 (external instrument and seasonal holdout). Model specifications were held fixed across validation tiers to isolate validation design as the sole manipulated factor, and all spectral standardisation was strictly fitted within training partitions to eliminate unsupervised leakage. Results: Transitioning from random row-wise to structured validation systematically eroded apparent predictive performance across all 36 random-to-structured model–task contrasts, yielding a median validation-induced optimism ΔR2 of 0.0170 (mean 0.3290, interquartile range [0.0084, 0.3985]) and a median root-mean-square error inflation ratio (RR_RMSE = RMSE_structured / RMSE_random) of 1.1395 (mean 1.4277, IQR [1.0417, 1.4374], range [0.9406, 5.2645]). Degradation was especially pronounced under external domain transfer (median ΔR2 = 0.6399, median RR_RMSE = 1.8199). In edible oils containing replicate scans sharing identical titration reference values, random cross-validation produced catastrophic performance inflation for non-linear models: kNN collapsed from an apparent R2 of 0.8865 (RMSE 5.40 meq O2/kg) to −2.1443 (RMSE 28.43 meq O2/kg; RR_RMSE = 5.265), and Random Forest collapsed from R2 = 0.8437 to −0.5806 (RR_RMSE = 3.180). This replicate leakage completely inverted algorithm rankings (Spearman ρ = −0.886, p = 0.019; Kendall τ = −0.733, p = 0.056). Algorithm robustness under external transfer was domain-specific: Ridge was the most resilient model under Mango seasonal transfer (R2 = 0.6690, compared to R2 ≈ 0.13–0.17 for tree ensembles), whereas uncalibrated Corn instrument transfer caused severe degradation in linear models (Ridge R2 = −30.04, PLS R2 = −37.05) due to uncorrected spectrometer baseline shifts. In contrast, non-linear models exhibited smaller relative degradation under sensor transfer. Cross-partition nearest-neighbour spectral similarity dropped by up to 0.0164 under domain transfer. Across tasks, this similarity drop showed an exploratory positive association with kNN error inflation (Pearson r = 0.739, Spearman ρ = 0.912), consistent with a spectral-proximity mechanism whereby high optical similarity enables flexible models to interpolate training points rather than learning transferable chemical relationships. Conclusions: Random row-wise validation creates severe validation-induced optimism, distorts algorithm rankings, and rewards models that memorise experimental artefacts. Reporting standards, mandatory specimen-level split manifests, and the routine inclusion of kNN as a diagnostic canary are essential to restore methodological integrity and field deployability to machine learning in food analysis.

papers.title: DeepEnzyKat: Turnover number prediction through enzyme-substrate interaction modeling and adaptive expert ensembles
Transferable Graph Neural Network Surrogates for Molecular Dynamics Across Crystal Symmetries
papers.abstract: We present a transferable graph neural network (GNN) surrogate framework for molecular dynamics (MD) that directly predicts atomic displacements and propagates atomistic configurations without explicit force evaluation or numerical time integration. The central objective of this work is to establish whether a common GNN formulation can represent atomic dynamics across materials with fundamentally different crystal symmetries and coordination environments. The same network architecture, feature representation, graph construction, and training protocol are applied without symmetry-specific modification to face-centered cubic (FCC) aluminum, body-centered cubic (BCC) iron, and hexagonal close-packed (HCP) magnesium. Across these distinct elemental and crystallographic systems, the framework achieves position-prediction errors on the order of 10−4 Å 2 and supports stable autoregressive propagation to nanosecond time scales. The predicted trajectories preserve thermodynamic stability, characteristic coordination-shell structure in the radial distribution functions, and temperature-dependent mean-squared-displacement behavior. In particular, the framework captures the closely spaced coordination shells of BCC iron and the anisotropic coordination environment of HCP magnesium without introducing lattice-specific representations. These results demonstrate that direct GNN-based atomic propagation can be formulated as a transferable framework across different elements, lattice symmetries, and coordination geometries, providing a pathway toward generalizable surrogate models for accelerated molecular dynamics.

papers.title: Zeolite-Mediated Three- and Pseudo-Five-Component Reactions Involving α-Ketoglutaric Acid, Aromatic Aldehydes and 5-Aminotetrazole
papers.abstract: We report previously undescribed multicomponent reactions of α-ketoglutaric acid, aromatic aldehydes, and 5-aminotetrazole that provides access to two distinct types of products. Notably, these transformations require the presence of 4A or 3A molecular sieves, and the formation of the target compounds is condition-controllable: the process can proceed through a pseudo-five-component pathway, yielding tetrahydropyrido[3,4-d]tetrazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidinone derivatives – the first examples of this heterocyclic framework – or can be directed toward a three-component condensation that affords dihydrotetrazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidine dicarboxylic acids. The latter were identified as key intermediates in the pseudo-five-component transformation, enabling the synthesis of pyrido[3,4-d]tetrazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidine systems via a two-step Doebner-type and Castagnoli–Cushman-type/decarboxylation sequence with an expanded range of possible substrates, thereby combining tetrazole, dihydropyrimidine, δ-lactam, and triazole pharmacophore motifs within a single fused framework.

papers.title: Alternative synthetic pathways to selected molecular fluorophores present in citric acid-based carbon dots
papers.abstract: Molecular fluorophores (MFs) are an integral part of many raw reaction mixtures prepared during the synthesis of carbon dots (CDs) from small organic molecules by the bottom-up methods. Despite their significant contribution to the luminescence of as-prepared CDs, the investigation of optical properties of MF is complicated by the pH dependence, possibility of formation of tautomers, low yields and complicated isolation. In this review, we summarize the structure of MFs detected in CDs prepared from citric acid (and various dopants), whose structure contains pyridin-2(1 H )-one ring annulated to 5- or 6-membered heterocycles. These compounds are closely related to citrazinic acid (CZA). The second part of the review deals with the alternative synthesis pathways towards ring-fused 2-pyridones, that could be used to prepare analogous compounds without the drawbacks related to the direct synthesis from CA (formation of carbonaceous matrix along with MFs resulting in low yields). MFs prepared by alternative pathways, free from polymerized and carbonized particles, could be used as standards towards better understanding of optical properties of CDs.

papers.title: Redirecting Iodine Oxidation in Thyroxine by O-Phosphorylation
papers.abstract: nachtsheim@uni-bremen.de Abstract O-Phosphorylation of a thyroxine derivative redirects mCPBA oxidation from the internal iodine to a terminal one. A two-step oxidation-hydrolysis sequence delivers the phosphate-stabilised aryl(hydroxy)iodonium salt, whose regiochemistry is established by 3 J-CP-coupling.

papers.title: Direct Alkylarene Desaturation via Base-Promoted Halogen Transfer
papers.abstract: We report a method to prepare alkenes through the base-promoted oxidative desaturation of alkylarenes and related weakly acidic functional groups. This process operates via a tandem deprotonative-halogenation and elimination sequence using haloarene halogen-transfer reagents. The use of potassium tert-butoxide with haloarene oxidants provides a simple means to desaturate a broad range of alkylarenes, acids, esters, and amides, as well as to aromatize saturated heterocycles. A critical feature for reaction success is the generation of tert-butanol from the tert-butoxide base which buffers the reaction solution to prevent anionic alkene polymerization. The utility of this approach is enhanced by its direct sequencing with additional base-promoted processes, such as hydrofunctionalization, to access formal homobenzylic C–H functionalization products.

papers.title: Multimodal Representation Learning for Exploring Natural Product Chemical Space
papers.abstract: Natural products represent a major source of therapeutic molecules, yet their structural diversity and limited biological annotations pose substantial challenges for computational exploration and discovery. Here, we develop a multimodal molecular representation framework that integrates chemical language, molecular fingerprints, physicochemical descriptors, and molecular graphs into a unified latent space for natural product discovery. Using structurally out-of-distribution molecular spaces, we show that molecular representation and sampling strategy jointly determine which regions of chemical space are explored. Multimodal pretraining captured chemically informative representations that enabled exploration of structurally unseen natural products, while comparisons with singlemodality representations showed that representation advantages depended on the discovery objective rather than being universally superior. The pretrained representation was transferable across anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activity predictions, and its integration with active learning enabled data-efficient exploration of biologically active molecules. Prospective evaluation of structurally unseen natural products further connected model-guided exploration with experimental antioxidant activity. These findings establish molecular representation and sampling as coupled determinants of chemical-space exploration and show

papers.title: Electrochemically Hole-catalyzed Dearomative (3+2) Cycloaddition of Nitroarenes
papers.abstract: We report the first electrochemically hole-catalyzed (3+2) dearomative cycloaddition of nitroarenes, including benzene-based derivatives. Enabled by a hole-transfer chain process, the reaction proceeds through the anodic generation of a non-stabilized azomethine ylide from a readily available precursor, providing efficient access to structurally complex pyrrolidines from a broad range of electron-deficient nitroarenes. Remarkably, full conversion is achieved using catalytic amounts of electricity (0.1 F mol-1), resulting in high TONe (222) and Faradaic efficiency (925%). This work expands the scope of hole electrocatalysis beyond electron-rich olefins and establishes a new platform for electrochemical dearomative cycloadditions. The scalability of the method was further demonstrated under continuous-flow conditions.

papers.title: Crowding-induced interfacial aggregation underlies enzyme concentration-dependent inhibition during poly(ethylene terephthalate) depolymerization
papers.abstract: Enzymatic depolymerization of poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) using PET hydrolases (PETases) offers a sustainable route for plastic recycling, yet high enzyme loadings paradoxically reduce degradation efficiency. The molecular basis of this enzyme concentration-dependent inhibition (ECDI) has remained unresolved. Here, by exploiting host-dependent differences in folding quality of a sequence-identical PETase, we show that ECDI is driven by crowding-induced interfacial aggregation, which progressively destabilizes PET-bound enzymes. By establishing aggregation propensity as a tractable design parameter, we demonstrate a complementary multi-level engineering framework operating at the sequence, folding, and reaction-environment levels that suppresses interfacial aggregation and improves PET depolymerization across multiple PETases. Our findings reveal how enzyme–enzyme interactions can govern catalytic performance at heterogeneous solid–liquid interfaces, providing a mechanistic basis for designing high-performance biocatalytic systems under high-enzyme-loading conditions.

papers.title: Cuban Bentonite/Polymer Nanocomposites: A Sustainable Alternative for Food Packaging
papers.abstract: The environmental impact of conventional polymers has driven the search for sustainable food packaging alternatives. Clay incorporation into polymers matrices has shown to enhance optical, mechanical, and barrier properties. This study evaluates Cuban natural bentonite as a reinforcing phase in hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC), carboxymethylcellulose (CMC), polyvinyl alcohol (PVA), and polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP), plus their mixtures (PVA/PVP and PVA/CMC). Films were cast and characterized by XRD, ATR-FTIR, SEM, and water resistance tests; opacity was measured by UV-Vis spectroscopy accounting for thickness. Results indicate that polymer dispersion depends on temperature (CMC fastest). Bent/HPMC films stood out for their superior opacity and water resistance, while Bent/PVA/PVP and Bent/PVA/CMC showed predominantly exfoliated structures, favorable for food packaging applications.

papers.title: Nanoscale stacking disorder and Jahn-Teller distortion in Brochantite, Cu4SO4(OH)6, revealed by 3D electron diffraction
papers.abstract: Characterization of functional materials often neglects explicit modeling of structural disorder because of its complexity and the limitations of conventional experimental methods. Yet disorder can strongly affect material properties, and understanding its role is essential for establishing reliable structure-property relationships. Here, we address the long-standing structural complexity of brochantite, one of the most common basic copper sulfates, using 3D electron diffraction (3D ED) complemented by laboratory and synchrotron single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Measurements on dozens of crystals reveal nanoscale disorder, a new orthorhombic polytype, and a broad range of stacking-fault probabilities. The results demonstrate pronounced structural heterogeneity in brochantite and allow us to examine how different sulfate environments and stacking configurations correlate with the magnitude and orientation of Jahn-Teller distortions. High-pressure measurements further show that these distortions respond to changes in layer geometry and compression. Additionally, single-crystal X-ray investigations show unusual twinning in brochantite, whereas 3D ED data collected for nanocrystals supply individual crystal structures that are averaged out in larger crystals.

papers.title: Black-Body-Based Scatter Removal Procedure for Quantitative Neutron Radiography at the MARS Beamline (CG-1D), HFIR
papers.abstract: Quantitative neutron imaging is fundamentally limited by scattering artifacts, low neutron flux, and wavelength-dependent attenuation, which restrict accurate transmission measurements. This work presents the first implementation and validation of the blackbody (BB) based scatter removal procedure (Carminati et al., 2019) for quantitative neutron radiography of engineering materials at the MARS beamline (CG-1D), High Flux Isotope Reactor (HFIR), Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL). The scatter removal pipeline was applied to a series of single crystal nickel (Ni) and polycrystalline austenitic (γ-phase) 316L stainless steel samples pre-charged with hydrogen gas (H2) at pressures of 1.5, 5, 12.5, and 20 kpsi. The BB correction removed a spatially varying scatter contribution of up to 8% of the local transmission that was not eliminated by conventional open-beam normalization. After scatter removal and subtraction of the metal-matrix attenuation, the resulting H attenuation coefficient, µH, increased monotonically with H concentration in both materials. Ni exhibited a higher H attenuation response than 316L stainless steel, consistent with differences in H solubility and trapping behavior. Pixel-wise maps further revealed concentration-dependent spatial heterogeneity, including localized regions of elevated µH in Ni at the highest H concentration. At the lowest concentrations, uncertainty in the interpolated scatter field exceeded the spatial-sampling uncertainty and established the effective detection floor of the measurement. Independent validation experiments were performed at the VENUS beamline of the Spallation Neutron Source using a H-free 316L stainless steel sample as a control and a water column with a known H number density as a reference standard. The corrected measurements recovered the expected zero H signal in the control and the H attenuation of the water reference, demonstrating that the pipeline can distinguish H attenuation from matrix and scatter contributions across independent beamline conditions. These results establish a validated workflow for removing sample dependent scatter and enabling quantitative analysis of neutron radiography data acquired at cold-neutron imaging beamlines.

papers.title: Perovskite Photovoltaics in January-June 2026: The Certified Frontier From Cell to Module
papers.abstract: Over an evaluation period spanning 6 months, the metal halide perovskite literature expanded by 3328 indexed publications. Of these, 884 were examined closely for physical claims, interfacial mechanisms, and stability validation across distinct device architectures. Across single junction devices, the certified power conversion efficiency (PCE) ceiling advanced to 27.6%, yet mechanistic investigations diverged over the operational function of low-dimensional capping heterostructures. Several studies concluded that wide-bandgap surface caps suppress non-radiative recombination and impede halide migration without hindering transport, while competing evidence demonstrated that disordered organic spacer phases create severe charge-transport barriers, accumulate photogenerated carriers under illumination, and penalize fill factor (FF). In all-perovskite tandems, performance ceilings remained governed by the chemical vulnerability of narrow-bandgap (NBG) mixed tin-lead sub-cells. Chemical hardness engineering and nucleation control synchronized crystallization and suppressed localized tin-rich defect segregation. Physical evidence that this arrests autonomous divalent-to-tetravalent tin oxidation cascades during continuous operation remains thin and contested. Monolithic hybrid tandems paired with silicon or chalcogenide bottom absorbers established the issue-wide ceiling of 34.85% certified PCE, and exposed an acute mechanistic dispute over buried hole-selective layer (HSL) contacts. One body of work holds that dense intermolecular pi-pi stacking and strict crystalline order within self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) are required to align interfacial energy levels and eliminate pinholes. A second holds that crystalline domains induce nanoscale grain boundaries and thermal dewetting, so that sterically hindered, amorphous molecular geometries preserve conformal passivation more reliably. Translating these absorbers into perovskite solar modules (PSMs) incurred a steep area penalty, with certified PCE falling to 26.8% at the largest reported aperture area of 655.2 cm2. Reports conflict over whether that penalty is dominated by non-radiative recombination at laser scribing margins, by convective drying instabilities generating coffee-ring solute segregation, or by heterogeneous out-of-plane residual lattice strain across the bulk film. Operational stability verification remains sparse and fragmented across all architectures: only 39 publications designated a standardized consensus protocol from the International Summit on Organic Photovoltaic Stability (ISOS), and only 39 studies reported an operational lifetime metric, with the longest duration reaching 4100 h under continuous illumination. Reporting rigor varies widely across device families, in that 52.1% of published abstracts state an efficiency value, yet only 8.5% report independent certification, representing just 114 certified works across the surveyed corpus. Progress in perovskite photovoltaics has therefore decoupled from uncertified efficiency metrics, and has shifted toward coupled ionic-electronic degradation under operating electrical and thermal stress. Resolving buried contact degradation between out-of-plane molecular desorption and lateral field-induced dewetting requires operando bias-dependent sum-frequency generation and conductive atomic force microscopy. Settling open-circuit voltage (Voc) losses demands operando drive-level capacitance profiling (DLCP) coupled with depth-resolved photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) mapping, to distinguish true defect passivation from electrostatic band realignment.

papers.title: Enhancing Linear B-Cell Epitope Prediction via Evolutionary Scale Modeling (ESM-2) and Hybrid Feature Integration
papers.abstract: Experimental identification of B-cell epitopes is time-consuming and resource-intensive, motivating the adoption of computational prediction approaches. This study examines the progression of sequence-based strategies by contrasting traditional machine learning methods (SVM, XGBoost, etc.) and early deep learning techniques (CNN, RNN, etc.) with sophisticated protein language models such as ESM-2. By systematically evaluating multiple feature encodings, including amino acid composition, dipeptide composition, k-mer tokenization, and evolutionary embeddings, we established that capturing both global semantic context and local sequence motifs is essential for robust predictive performance. Optimal performance was achieved using a hybrid framework that combined 15B-parameter ESM-2 embeddings with k-mer features. This hybrid approach achieved an AUC of 0.743 and an MCC of 0.333 on independent validation using an Extra Trees classifier, and an AUC of 0.738 and an MCC of 0.356 using an XGBoost classifier on the same dataset. Our findings indicate that transformer-based embeddings yield enhanced protein representations; however, their predictive efficacy is optimized when integrated with local motifs and ensemble learning, presenting a scalable, high-accuracy alternative to conventional and standalone deep learning frameworks.

papers.title: Synthesis and Ambiphilic Reactivity of a Monocoordinate Carbazolyl Gallylene
papers.abstract: Monocoordinate Lewis base-free gallium(I) complexes are rare due to their high propensity for disproportionation and oligomerization. Herein, we report the synthesis and structural characterization of a monomeric, monocoordinate gallylene stabilized by a bulky 1,8-bis(3,5-ditert-butylphenyl)-3,6-di-tert-butylcarbazole ligand. Taking advantage of the substantial kinetic shielding provided by the flanking aryl substituents, the compound can be isolated as a solvent free, one-coordinate main-group carbenoid. With a lone pair and two vacant p-orbitals, this compound features an ambiphilic character which was experimentally probed through coordination to both Lewis-acidic transition-metal fragments (M(CO) 5 ; M = Cr, Mo, W) and strong σ-donor Lewis bases, including the N-heterocyclic carbene ( IPrMe NHC) and 4-dimethylaminopyridine (DMAP). Furthermore, the Ga(I) complex shows oxidative addition of methyl iodide and phenanthrene-9,10-dione. Conversely to other monocoordinate gallylene compounds its carbometallation reactions are kinetically and thermodynamically unfavored.

papers.title: Study of neutron-induced effects on cultural heritage linen fabrics using fluorescence spectroscopy
papers.abstract: This study investigates how the fluorescence of linen changes when it is irradiated with a focus for the first time on the distinction between neutron from pure gamma ray irradiation. Earlier studies showed that when linen was subjected to both neutron and gamma irradiation, its visible and ultraviolet (UV) fluorescence increased as the radiation dose increased. However, the spectroscopic reason was not explained, and the specific contributions of neutrons versus gamma rays were not addressed. In this work, a particular linen is used as a control, and the changes caused by irradiation are characterized and analyzed using steady-state and time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy, as well as total UV fluorescence photography. The tests reveal that only neutrons, and not gamma rays, increased UV fluorescence in linen. The different ways in which the two forms of radiation interact are highlighted. In addition, the spectral ratio between the yellow band and the blue band areas, as well as the time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy, could indicate that the linen was exposed to neutrons. The results support cluster-triggered emission (CTE) as the main cause of cellulose autofluorescence as a constituent of linen, and also a relative increase of CTE with the neutron dose. Finally, the underlying mechanisms of the visual fluorescence perception are analyzed, and the observed effect is explained by calculating the L dimension of the fluorescence spectra using the CIE L*a*b* color space. This work proposes a simple device for detecting neutron irradiation in place in cultural heritage linen fabrics, with potential applications in conservation and forensic analysis.

papers.title: Linear I···I contacts in a platinum(IV)-diiodo porphyrin: Emergent type III halogen–halogen interactions
papers.abstract: This study presents experimental and theoretical evidence for unusual intermolecular I···I interactions between axially coordinated iodide ligands in a Pt(IV) porphyrin. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals that PtI2T[3,5-diOMe]PP, where T[3,5-diOMe]PP is the 5,10,15,20-tetrakis(3,5-dimethoxyphenyl)porphyrinato dianion, crystallises in the uncommon P4/n space group, in contrast to the I4/m space group frequently observed for related metalloporphyrins, and adopts an eclipsed columnar packing arrangement, with co-crystallised dichloromethane (DCM) molecules occupying the space between successive porphyrin layers. The iodide ligands form linear I···I contacts that propagate into a one-dimensional supramolecular network. Comparison with the axial-iodide-free PtT[3,5-diOMe]PP and the related OsI2T[2,4,6-triMe]PP, where T[2,4,6-triMe]PP is the 5,10,15,20-tetrakis(2,4,6-trimethylphenyl)porphyrinato dianion, demonstrates how axial iodide coordination, peripheral substitution, and the local solvent environment influence the resulting crystal packing and macrocyclic conformation. Molecular surface electrostatic potential (MESP), quantum theory of atoms in molecules (QTAIM), natural bond orbital (NBO), and Hirshfeld surface analyses were employed to investigate the nature of the intermolecular contacts. QTAIM analysis identifies the I···I contacts as weak, closed-shell interactions, while NBO analysis reveals a significant donor–acceptor component involving iodide lone pairs and neighbouring Pt–I or Os–I antibonding orbitals. The magnitude and distribution of these interactions depend on the local supramolecular environment, with co-crystallised DCM contributing additional C–H···I contacts and altering the electronic environment of these ligands. Together, these results demonstrate that the I···I interactions cannot be considered in isolation, but instead form part of a broader network of cooperative intermolecular contacts that governs the crystal packing of the Pt(IV) porphyrin.

papers.title: LANGER: Lanthanide Affinity Network via Graph and Evolutionary Representations
papers.abstract: The transition to sustainable energy relies heavily on rare earth elements (REEs), yet their separation remains a critical industrial bottleneck due to their nearly identical physicochemical properties. The discovery of lanmodulin (LanM), a highly selective REE-binding protein, has inspired bio-based separation strategies; however, predicting binding affinity between different LanM variants and REEs remains a significant computational challenge. Here, we present LANGER, a multimodal deep learning framework for predicting REE protein binding affinity (Kd) by synchronously integrating global evolutionary context, continuous ionic chemistry, and local three-dimensional coordinate geometry. Our architecture combines ESM2 protein sequence embeddings, REE physicochemical descriptions, and geometric graph learning (GGL) features derived from topologies extracted from protein-ion complexes. Using a comprehensive dataset of 616 evaluated LanM homologs against 15 REE ions, we demonstrate the robustness of this framework across two rigorous evaluation settings. In a cluster-based validation analysis designed to test extrapolation to held-out LanM sequence clusters, LANGER achieved a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.212 and a concordance index (CI) of 0.757. More importantly, in a rigorous evaluation protocol that completely excludes individual ions from the training phase, the fully integrated multimodal framework achieved high predictive accuracy (RMSE = 0.119, Pearson correlation coefficient r = 0.860, CI = 0.800), demonstrating its unique ability to transfer learned physicochemical trends to unseen lanthanide elements. This work establishes a scalable, computationally accurate structure recognition platform for the discovery and design of data-driven REEselective proteins.

papers.title: Quality control measurement science: Point-of-care opioid compounding and personalized pain management
papers.abstract: Traditional "one-size-fits-all" pharmacotherapy often fails to address the complex, highly individualized needs of patients undergoing opioid tapering, pain management, and withdrawal. While distributed and point-of-care (POC) additive manufacturing—such as 3D printing, semisolid extrusion, and drop-on-demand (DoD) deposition—enable agile, patient-specific dosing and multi-drug formulations, they introduce critical quality control (QC) challenges in facilities that often lack extensive laboratory infrastructure. We employed a quality by design (QbD) approach to identify the critical relationships between input materials, process parameters, and critical quality attributes (CQAs) and investigated a tiered series of atline, inline, and final-product QC measurement technologies for personalized pain management and opioid-tapering therapies. Using precision DoD liquid dispensers, various tunable dosage forms were produced, including injectable saline solutions, semi-solid extruded tablets, and oral films. These vehicles carried full and partial opioid agonists, opioid antagonists, and adjuvant withdrawal medications (fentanyl, buprenorphine, methadone, oxycodone, naloxone, diphenhydramine, promethazine, and 2 bupivacaine). The performance, speed, and selectivity of four analytical techniques were explored: microdrop UV-Vis spectroscopy, liquid chromatography-UV (LC-UV), handheld Raman spectroscopy, and chromatography-free direct analysis in real time triple quadrupole mass spectrometry (DART-TQ-MS). We characterized and quantified each manufactured dosage form by either single-point calibration (i.e., against a reference standard [RS] or quality control standard) or linear least squares regression. Analytical control strategies for quality control require balancing throughput, analytical capabilities and limitations, and specific medicine considerations. This work defined robust metrological pathways for safe, compliant, and personalized point-ofcare pharmaceutical production, bridging clinical pain management and opioid tapering guidelines with manufacturing quality assurance.

papers.title: Counter-Intuitive Orthogonal Catalysis for In-Situ Functionalization of High-Performance Self-Blown Non-Isocyanate Polyurethane Foams
papers.abstract: Rigid foams earn their place in structural applications through a specific balance of stiffness and density. Reproducing that balance without isocyanates has proven far harder than replacing the chemistry itself. Water-blown polyhydroxyurethane (PHU) foams are the most credible isocyanate-free alternatives to conventional polyurethanes, but toxic base catalysts and weak mechanical properties have stalled their adoption. Brønsted acid catalysis, long dismissed on the expectation that amine protonation suppresses urethane formation, proves effective instead: a dynamic equilibrium of transient protonation and thermal amine regeneration widens the rheological window for water-driven CO 2 release while carrying the network to full conversion. Acidic conditions additionally activate vinyl ethers, converting the pendant and vicinal hydroxyls responsible for moisture plasticization into acetal crosslinks. The resulting poly(hydroxyurethane)–polyacetal (PHU–PAC) foams show a sixteenfold (16x) higher rubbery modulus, a fourfold higher compressive modulus (4 → 18 MPa), and halved water uptake relative to the PHU benchmark. Normalized peak heat release rate falls nearly eightfold below that of a commercial PU foam, and on an Ashby plot of specific strength versus stiffness, PHU–PAC approaches HDPE and PVC. Addressing catalyst tractability, moisture uptake, and mechanical performance in one formulation, acid-catalyzed PHU–PAC reframes non-isocyanate foams as tunable structural materials and positions catalyst design as a lever for the next generation of sustainable cellular materials.

papers.title: Performance Self-Blown Non-Isocyanate Polyurethane Foams
papers.abstract: Rigid foams earn their place in structural applications through a specific balance of stiffness and density. Reproducing that balance without isocyanates has proven far harder than replacing the chemistry itself. Water-blown polyhydroxyurethane (PHU) foams are the most credible isocyanate-free alternatives to conventional polyurethanes, but toxic base catalysts and weak mechanical properties have stalled their adoption. Brønsted acid catalysis, long dismissed on the expectation that amine protonation suppresses urethane formation, proves effective instead: a dynamic equilibrium of transient protonation and thermal amine regeneration widens the rheological window for water-driven CO2 release while carrying the network to full conversion. Acidic conditions additionally activate vinyl ethers, converting the pendant and vicinal hydroxyls responsible for moisture plasticization into acetal crosslinks. The resulting poly(hydroxyurethane)–polyacetal (PHU–PAC) foams show a sixteenfold (16x) higher rubbery modulus, a fourfold higher compressive modulus (4 → 18 MPa), and halved water uptake relative to the PHU benchmark. Normalized peak heat release rate falls nearly eightfold below that of a commercial PU foam, and on an Ashby plot of specific strength versus stiffness, PHU–PAC approaches HDPE and PVC. Addressing catalyst tractability, moisture uptake, and mechanical performance in one formulation, acid-catalyzed PHU–PAC reframes non-isocyanate foams as tunable structural materials and positions catalyst design as a lever for the next generation of sustainable cellular materials.

papers.title: Additive manufacturing of micro-architected carbide ceramics via molten salt conversion
papers.abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) enables complex micro-architected geometries in metals 1–3 , polymers 4 and oxide ceramics 4–6 , yet its extension to non-oxide ceramics remains constrained by optical opacity and high-temperature densification. Carbide ceramics are challenging for particle-based vat photopolymerization (VPP), where strong absorption limits curing, while pressure-assisted densification, often required for high density, is incompatible with delicate architectures. A general route to fabricate dense micro-architected carbide ceramics without conventional sintering remains unavailable. Here we demonstrate molten salt-assisted additive manufacturing of carbide ceramics (MOSAIC), an AM framework that decouples geometric shaping from carbide formation. Thermoset polymer architectures fabricated by VPP are pyrolysed into architected glassy-carbon templates and converted into carbide ceramics through molten-salt-mediated reaction with transition metals. MOSAIC produces micro-architected TiC, VC, Cr 3 C 2 and TaC with relative densities above 95% and features down to ~20 µm, and extends to WC, ZrC and Mo 2 C. Conversion depth can be controlled from ~1 µm to tens of micrometres, yielding solid carbide struts or hollow architectures after carbon removal. Controlled oxidation converts these structures into TiO 2 , Cr 2 O 3 , V 2 O 5 and Ta 2 O 5 while preserving topology. By separating architecture definition from ceramic formation, MOSAIC enables photopolymerization-based manufacturing of transition-metal carbides and derivative oxides across micrometre-scale features and millimetre- to centimetre-scale architectures.

papers.title: Investigating pH Effects on the Photoswitching of Furanyl-Indolinium Heteroarylstilbenes
papers.abstract: Cationic heteroarylstilbenes, such as the furanyl-indolinium chromophore, represent a class of watersoluble, visible-light-responsive photoswitches. However, their photochemical behaviour under physiologically relevant pH conditions remains insufficiently understood. In this study, four derivatives were synthesized and systematically investigated, with particular emphasis on their photoswitching properties at three pH values using phosphate-buffered media. The visible-light-induced E/Z photoisomerization kinetics were analysed by UV/Vis spectroscopy, while the structures of the resulting isomers were confirmed by NMR spectroscopy. A key result is the pronounced pH dependence of the thermal Z→E back-isomerization in phosphate buffer, whereas the photoinduced E→Z switching is only weakly affected. The apparent thermal recovery is superimposed by a competing dark-decay process, which was quantified independently to separate concurrent degradation from the actual thermal back-isomerization kinetics. The derivatives differ in their chemical stability. The methyl-substituted derivative is comparatively robust, whereas the nitro-substituted derivative shows pronounced degradation. These results show that water solubility alone does not guarantee robust photoswitching under biologically relevant conditions and that both pH-dependent switching kinetics and chemical stability must be considered in the design of cationic heteroarylstilbene photoswitches.

papers.title: Fiber-Scale Discrete Element Modeling Approach for Microstructural Evolution in Carbon Felt Electrode Manufacturing
papers.abstract: Porous carbon components strongly influence transport, kinetics, and performance in electrochemical energy devices, like electrodes in redox flow batteries or gas diffusion layers in proton exchange membrane fuel cells. Yet quantitative links between industrial felt manufacturing and the resulting microstructure remain insufficiently understood. Recent studies have explored alternative bottom-up fabrication strategies to achieve greater microstructural control, while computational optimization often considers stochastic microstructures without accounting for manufacturability. Consequently, the extent to which conventional manufacturing processes can tailor microstructure remains unclear. Here, we develop a discrete element method framework that resolves fiber-scale interactions and microstructural evolution during mechanical processing of oxidized polyacrylonitrile precursor felts. The framework represents successive stages of fiber generation, web formation, web laying, needle punching, and calendering. At each stage, the evolving three-dimensional microstructure is resolved and quantified using fiber- and pore-scale descriptors, including pore-size distributions, fiber-orientation tensors, and transport-related properties. The simulations reveal process–structure–transport relationships, identifying key parameters governing pore-throat size, fiber reorientation, and effective diffusivity. These findings define the microstructural design space accessible through conventional felt manufacturing and provide a basis for future process optimization and integration with subsequent thermal-processing stages.

papers.title: Macromolecular Size Matching in Stabilizing Corrugated Chiral Plasmonic Nanostructures
papers.abstract: Chiral plasmonic nanoparticles derive strong chiroptical responses sensitive from their corrugated, high-curvature surfaces, but these same features are thermodynamically unstable. Surface functionalization using macromolecules could broaden their utility by enabling improved colloidal compatibility, secondary functionalization, stimuli responsiveness and and assembly into higher-order structures. However, as the chiroptically active surface feactures are often only a few nanometer in size, inadequate size matching leads to structural instability, causing particle surfaces to flatten and consequently diminishing their chiroptical properties. Here, we show that chain-length-selective polymer functionalization stabilizes the fine groove structures of chiral gold nanorods. We identify a threshold behavior of hydrodynamic diameter below which polymer coils can penetrate and anchor within the grooves, preserving structural integrity and chiroptical activities. Guided by this principle, we establish a sequential functionalization strategy using polymers of two distinct sizes to produce chiral AuNRs with stable chiroptical performance. Our results establish a general design rule for integrating versatile macromolecular architectures with chiral nanoparticles and expand the engineering space for nano-optical applications.

papers.title: Conformational ensembles of the TDP-43 NTD-RRM1-RRM2 domains interacting with GU-rich RNA determined by MD simulations and SAXS data
papers.abstract: TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43) is a crucial regulator of RNA metabolism whose pathological aggregation is a hallmark of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), frontotemporal dementia (FTD), and Alzheimer’s disease. Binding to GU-rich RNA sequences via its RNA recognition motifs (RRM1 and RRM2) is known to antagonize aggregation, yet the molecular mechanisms by which RNA modulates TDP-43 conformational and supramolecular organization remain poorly understood. This limitation arises from the challenges related to the structural resolution of the inter-domain dynamics by experimental methods due to the protein intrinsically disordered regions, notably the linker connecting the N-terminal domain (NTD) to RRM1. To address this gap, we performed a combined all-atom (AA) and coarse-grained (CG) molecular dynamics (MD) investigation of a TDP-43 NTD–RRM1–RRM2 monomer in both the absence and presence of GU-rich RNA. AA simulations were carried out using the protein AMBER03ws and RNA AMBERχOL3 force fields to accurately capture protein–RNA 1 interactions. In parallel, we developed a MARTINI 3–compatible CG model for GU–rich RNA and performed CG simulations to access longer timescale conformational dynamics and extend structural trends observed with atomic accuracy. Small-angle X–ray scattering (SAXS) data were integrated to refine the conformational ensembles generated by both AA and CG simulations using the genetic algorithm judging optimization of ensembles (GAJOE). Across resolutions, our results consistently show that RNA binding reshapes the conformational ensemble of TDP-43. RNA association promotes closer packing of the RRM domains while subtly modulating the spatial arrangement of the NTD. Importantly, the ensemble refinements improve the agreement with experimental SAXS data without altering the underlying residue-level protein–protein and protein–RNA interaction network, suggesting that the conformational dynamics of the NTD-RRM1 intrinsically disordered linker is not affected by the RNA binding. As a first step toward the modeling of TDP-43–RNA oligomeric assemblies, this work establishes a validated multi-scale framework for studying the impact of RNA binding on TDP-43 self-assembly and supramolecular organization. By bridging AA atomic details, CG conformational sampling, and integration of experimental data for ensemble refinement, our approach provides accurate insight into how RNA binding regulates domain organization and conformational heterogeneity of TDP-43, shedding light onto its role in proteinopathies.

papers.title: Auto-healing Co(II)-based metallosupramolecular hydrogel of 3-amino-1-propanol as Low Molecular Weight Gelator: Investigations of morphological features, rheological dynamics, and stimuli-responsiveness
papers.abstract: In the present work, a stable, green-coloured metallohydrogel was fabricated under ambient conditions through the spontaneous self-assembly of cobalt(II) nitrate hexahydrate, Co(NO3)2·6H2O, as the metal source with 3-amino-1-propanol acting as a low-molecular-weight gelator (LMWG) in aqueous medium. The synthesized metallogel was characterized using rheological analysis i.e.; strain sweep, frequency sweep and thixotropy. Surface morphology and network texture were probed by FESEM, elemental composition was verified by EDX analysis, and the gel's stimuli-responsive were subsequently evaluated.

papers.title: Pyrrole-Imine Dimer Stabilized Bis(germaamides) with two Ge(E)N(SiMe3)2 moieties (E = S, Se)
papers.abstract: Bis(germaamides) and their thio- and seleno- analogs are unknown. This work reports the isolation and characterization of the first examples of thio- and seleno-analogs of bis(germaamides) 7 and 8 containing two Ge(E)NR2 moieties (E = S, Se; R = SiMe3). These compounds were obtained by oxidizing the bulky pyrrole-imine dimeric ligand-stabilized bis(aminogermylene) 5 with elemental sulfur and selenium. This study also highlights the first-ever application of the bulky pyrrole-imine dimeric ligand 3 to simultaneously stabilize two low-valent centers (germylenes or stannylenes). Furthermore, the bonding in the thio- and seleno-bis(germaamides) 7 and 8 was investigated in detail using single–crystal X-ray diffraction and DFT calculations.

papers.title: Addressing the nature and reductive stability of alkylthiol-modified Cu electrode surfaces
papers.abstract: Cu surfaces modified with molecular adsorbates are being used in electrocatalyic processes (e.g., CO2 reduction (CO2RR)) to improve performance, but the nature and stability of molecular adsorbates (e.g. thiols) on Cu remain poorly understood owing to the sensitivity of Cu to oxidation and the complex chemical nature of the interface. To address these challenges, alkylthiol modification of 10 monolayers of electrodeposited Cu onto single-crystal Au bead electrodes has been prepared and studied using electrochemistry and in-situ fluorescence imaging. Under rigorous O2-free and H2O-free conditions, oxide-free Cu surfaces were produced. Modification of these oxide-free surfaces with alkylthiols resulted in a Cu2S overlayer. Oxide-free Cu surfaces modified with alkylthiol in the presence of trace H2O or O2 was found to have an increased amount of Cu2S, identified by electrochemistry and ex-situ Raman. The reductive stability of the alkylthiol modified Cu surface was investigated using a fluorophore-labelled DNA-alkylthiol adsorbate and in-situ fluorescence microscopy. Oxide-free Cu surfaces modified with alkylthiols produced a surface that was slightly more reductively stable (by-0.1 to-0.2V) when compared with alkylthiol self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) on Au, but do not show the characteristics of an alkyl-thiol SAM. Under similar modification procedures but using slightly oxidized Cu surfaces, the adsorbates were not removed using reducing potentials more negative than hydrogen evolution, suggesting a multilayer adsorbate structure composed of Cu2S with non-specifically adsorbed species. Thus, Cu surfaces prepared in the presence of trace O2and H2O may have a Cu-sulfide overlayer rather than a Cu-alkylthiol monolayer, even at reducing potentials typical of CO2RR or other electrocatalysis processes. More generally, the quantitative methodology that we developed for studying Cu electrodes is a framework for gaining insight into the preparation and molecular modification of other non-noble metal electrodes of interest for electrocatalysis.

papers.title: Reducing Synthetic Complexity: A Fluorine-Free Benzodithiophene-Thienopyrrolodione Donor Polymer by Direct Arylation Polycondensation for Organic Photovoltaics
papers.abstract: Synthetic complexity is a decisive aspect for absorber material availability in organic photovoltaics (OPVs). By using direct arylation polycondensation (DAP), a new route to the donor polymer PBDT-T2-TPD is presented. DAP allows to reduce the amount of toxic chemicals and simplifies the reaction scheme at the same time. Furthermore, this new route allows to vary the molar mass of PBDT-T2-TPD and thus enables the investigation of chain length-dependent OPV parameters in devices with the non-fullerene L8-BO as acceptor. An increasing molar mass results in an improvement of the open-circuit voltage, the fill factor and the power conversion efficiency, while the short-circuit current density saturates after an initial increase. These changes arise from reduced non-radiative voltage losses and enhanced mobility–lifetime products. The performance of the best performing DAP material is at least as

papers.title: Why Molecular-Scale Occupancy Fluctuations Appear Gaussian without Being Bulk-Like
papers.abstract: Molecular-scale occupancy distributions in water and hard-sphere fluids can appear remarkably Gaussian. Using classical density functional theory with an external field conjugate to the occupancy, we calculate occupancy cumulants for spherical volumes in a hard-sphere fluid and reproduce the variance and small, oscillatory third moment reported previously in Monte Carlo simulations. This agreement shows that the density functional captures the correlations responsible for the phenomenon and allows the role of excluded-volume packing to be isolated. By comparison with the Poisson limit and by varying both observation-volume size and bulk density, we show that excluded-volume correlations strongly suppress the higher cumulants. The resulting skewness and excess kurtosis remain nonzero and oscillatory, but they become small as the observation volume increases. However, over the same molecular-scale range, the finite-volume variance remains strongly scale-dependent and does not attain the extensive scaling set by the bulk compressibility. The early onset of near-Gaussianity is therefore governed primarily by molecular packing: it does not demonstrate that the fluctuations have reached the thermodynamic Gaussian limit, nor does it support a distinct small-cavity regime governed by bulk-like Gaussian fluctuations.

papers.title: Dissecting the Roles of Optimal Tuning, Solvation, and Vibrational Corrections in Excited-State Redox Potential Prediction for Organic Photoredox Catalysts
papers.abstract: Department of Chemistry, Emory University Abstract Reliable computational prediction of excited-state redox potentials is central to the rational design of photoredox catalysts and requires accurate treatment of both ground-state redox thermochemistry and excited-state energetics. Although time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) provides a practical computational framework, it remains unclear whether these two components should use the same range-separation treatment and how the tuning of 2 range-separated hybrid (RSH) functionals, solvent response, and vibrational corrections affect that choice. We address these questions using a controlled benchmark of 16 structurally related N-aryl phenoxazine photocatalysts with experimental data obtained in dimethylacetamide, comparing default range-separation parameters with gas-phase tuning (GPγT) and two solution-phase tuning schemes based on equilibrium (PVγT) and nonequilibrium (SVγT) polarizable continuum models. The optimal treatment is quantity dependent: default ω values give the lowest errors for ground-state oxidation potentials, whereas solution-phase tuning with PVγT or SVγT reduces the mean absolute errors (MAEs) of transition energies to 0.10–0.13 eV; combining these component-specific treatments with zero-point or full vibrational corrections yields excited-state oxidation-potential MAEs of 0.11–0.13 V, although the required frequency calculations substantially increase the computational cost. These results reveal that applying a single range-separation treatment throughout the calculation is suboptimal and provide a physically motivated, quantity-specific computational strategy for solution-phase excited-state redox predictions that can now be tested across broader photocatalyst classes and solvent environments. 1 Introduction Photocatalysis has emerged as a versatile strategy for promoting chemical transformations through photoinduced electron transfer (PET) under mild conditions.1-8 Although ruthenium and iridium complexes have traditionally been widely used as photoredox catalysts (PCs),5, 9-12 organic PCs are emerging as cheaper and greener alternatives because their photophysical and redox properties can be systematically tuned through molecular design.2, 4, 8, 13-19

papers.title: Influence of Structural Flexibility on Ion-Receptor Interactions in Octamethyl Calix[4]pyrrole Complexed with Prolinate
papers.abstract: We present cryogenic ion vibrational spectroscopy of deprotonated L-proline ([Pro-H]-) complexed with octamethyl calix[4]pyrrole (omC4P). Density functional theory calculations reveal two low-energy binding motifs. In the lowest energy structure, the carboxylate group interacts with only three NH groups of omC4P, with the NH group of the fourth pyrrole pointing away from the binding site. In another geometry, slightly higher in energy, the ion binds to all four NH groups. The experimental IR spectrum matches the lowest energy isomer, featuring a free NH stretching signature at 3439 cm-1 alongside strongly red-shifted NH stretching modes involving the three strong hydrogen-bonding NH groups. This three-point binding motif represents a departure from the typical four-point binding observed with smaller anions, demonstrating how the charge distribution of the guest and the structural flexibility of the receptor affect binding of larger anions. Despite the reduced number of hydrogen bonds, the three-point binding motif is lower in energy due to shorter, stronger hydrogen bonds, and it is the dominant motif of [Pro-H]-·omC4P in vacuo.

papers.title: When the lower-barrier pathway yields the minor enantiomer: reversibility and intermediate stability in pyrroloindoline synthesis
papers.abstract: In this work, we present a computational study that provides evidence for the origins of selectivity in the enantioselective synthesis of pyrroloindolines catalyzed by iminium ions. Through a conformational search combined with DFT calculations, we obtained the catalytic energy profile, which shows that the enantioselectivity is not determined by the barriers of the enantiodetermining C–C bond-forming step. A microkinetic model built on this profile reproduces the experimental enantiomeric excess and identifies the origin of the selectivity: under conditions in which the steps preceding product release are reversible, the catalyst-bound intermediate I9 accumulates preferentially along the S pathway, where it is markedly more stable than its R counterpart. The selectivity therefore reflects a thermodynamic contribution operating at the level of the diastereomeric on-cycle intermediates rather than a difference in activation barriers. We stress that this outcome is not accessible from the free energy profile alone: a simple inspection of the activation barriers predicts the opposite sense of induction, and only the explicit kinetic treatment reproduces the experimental results. Previous studies have suggested that control of the E/Z ratio of the iminium ion intermediate was related to catalytic selectivity; here we show that the stereoinduction originates from the predominance of the E isomer of the iminium ion. Furthermore, for the C–C bond-forming step, we identify the regions of the system involved in the noncovalent interactions that govern selectivity. Finally, by introducing substituents on the substrate, we observe a decrease in the activation barrier associated with the iminium ion–substrate interaction when electron-donating groups are present in the nucleophile.

papers.title: Experimental Data Analysis and Improved Cytochrome P450 Site-of-Metabolism Prediction for Drug Discovery
papers.abstract: Cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzymes mediate the oxidative metabolism of most marketed drugs, making early prediction of their sites of metabolism (SoMs) essential for addressing metabolic liabilities. In this work, we present a substantial update to our hybrid docking/quantum mechanics SoM prediction tool IMPACTS (J. Chem. Inf. Model., 2012, 52, 2471-2483). This update is evaluated on newly curated, fully annotated datasets containing over 2,400 datapoints and spanning nine human isoforms; these datasets are released to the community in MOL2 and JSON formats. Technical implementations presented in this work include 1) development of a three-dimensional solvent-accessible surface area correction to the precomputed activation energies, 2) design and integration of a highly efficient L-BFGS optimizer, and 3) elimination of a filter that had been historically used to remove unproductive binding modes. We follow these updates with extensive benchmarking and analysis on the newly curated datasets, where we show 1) achievement of a global Top-2 accuracy of ~75% across the nine isoforms and 2) the effective computational cost using the new optimizer was less than 1 minute per metabolite for eight of the nine isoforms. Finally, we present six real-world case studies comprised of approved drugs and discontinued clinical candidates. These case studies illustrate both the practical value and the remaining limitations of our approach.

papers.title: Collaborative Laboratory Edge Networks
papers.abstract: Chemistry language models now predict reactions and retrosynthetic routes with useful accuracy, but they assume that proprietary reaction records can be pooled into a central cluster and that inference runs on abundant accelerators. Neither assumption holds in pharmaceutical and fine-chemical practice, where yield records cannot leave the plant network, the points of use are heterogeneous resource-limited sites, and different laboratories occupy disjoint regions of chemical space. We present ChemFedFusion, a heterogeneity-aware framework for federated chemistry-model training and offloading over collaborative laboratory edge networks. ChemUCP is a chemistry-aware utility–cost predictor that scores a task–node pair by expected chemistry gain, expected latency, and an explicit out-of-distribution risk of emitting unparsable or unreliable chemistry, using a dual-channel tokenizer and a scaffold-coverage encoder that is corrected online from execution feedback. CSAW replaces sample-count aggregation with the product of a scaffold-space complementarity term, a site reliability term, and a weakened volume guard, amplifying rare chemistry while suppressing noisy sites. ARCO couples offloading and aggregation through a shared adaptation matrix and an event-driven asynchronous aggregator with a staleness bound, so that successful offloads teach the aggregator which node is competent for which chemistry task. On Mol-Instruction and USPTO-50K, ChemFedFusion reaches 0.883 Exact and 51.36% Top-1, and on the FedChem suite it reduces regression RMSE by up to 9.99% and classification ROC-AUC improvements are consistent across all nine datasets and three heterogeneity levels. The framework reduces convergence rounds by 22.4% and raises the fraction of answers that are both on time and chemically valid by 8.8 percentage points. A failure analysis shows that the remaining errors are dominated by synthetically infeasible routes that parse correctly, which no validity-based router can detect.

papers.title: Helical Polymers for Artificial Cell Engineering: Backbone-to-Droplet Reorganization in Polyacetylene-based Microdroplets
papers.abstract: Biomolecular condensates provide a powerful framework for constructing artificial cells with crowded interiors and dynamic molecular organization. However, most synthetic condensates rely on flexible or intrinsically disordered macromolecules, leaving the role of conformationally defined synthetic polymers in liquid-liquid phase separation largely unexplored. Here, we introduce cationic helical polyacetylenes as structurally defined building blocks for coacervate-based artificial cells and investigate how their conformation governs condensate properties. Complexation with ATP generates spherical, liquid-like microdroplets that sequester small organic molecules and proteins from the surrounding solution while supporting enzymatic transformations. These coacervates exhibit substantially greater resistance to increasing ionic strength than those formed with their linear counterparts, a behavior associated with changes in the polyacetylene backbone upon ATP complexation. Moreover, combining helical and linear polyamines induces the heterogeneous partitioning of a hydrophilic molecular guest, accompanied by a transition from spherical to amorphous condensates. Together, these findings establish a direct link between polymer secondary structure and condensate stability, morphology, and molecular organization, highlighting conformationally defined synthetic polymers as versatile building blocks for artificial cell engineering.

papers.title: Direct visualization of heterogeneous molecular diffusion and interfacial barriers during condensate ripening
papers.abstract: Ripening processes are ubiquitous in various multiphase systems, such as emulsions, crystals, alloys, and biomolecular condensates. This phenomenon significantly affects the morphology of a system and its resulting properties through the growth of dispersed domains at the expense of others without direct contact. Though ripening has been studied for centuries, a molecule-level visualization of this process has never been captured, significantly hindering our fundamental understanding. Here, we use single-molecule tracking techniques to visualize and quantify the diffusion dynamics of poly-L-lysine (PLL) during a rapid ripening process, where ATP droplet condensates transform into fibrillar crystals. We successfully observe preferential motion of PLL within both the dilute and condensate phases toward growing crystals and uncover previously unknown molecular dynamics near interfaces. At condensate interfaces, PLL molecules encounter energetic barriers that trap their motions and restrict their escape from condensates. Near crystal fibers, we discover clear heterogeneity in molecular dynamics, which can be classified into Brownian, confined, and superdiffusive motions. To explain this result, simulations and a physical model reveal the formation of water lubrication layers on crystal fibers, which enables PLL molecules to slide along fibers with superdiffusive motion before crossing the layer and becoming immobilized on fibers with confined motion. These results provide molecular-level insight for understanding the fundamental ripening process and answering open questions across diverse nonequilibrium systems.

papers.title: From Automated Beamlines to Autonomous Science
papers.abstract: Autonomous experimentation is emerging across materials synthesis, synchrotron and neutron characterization, real-time analysis, and scientific decision-making. Yet increasingly capable artificial intelligence does not by itself create autonomous science. Scientific user facilities must also provide machine-operable experiments, machine-readable and interoperable data and interfaces, persistent provenance across the experimental lifecycle, scientific capabilities that can be discovered and orchestrated across instruments and facilities, and access models compatible with iterative experimental campaigns. We argue that these infrastructure requirements should be treated as a coupled scientific design problem. Their value is not limited to higher throughput: reducing the latency between observation, interpretation, decision, and the next measurement can make metastable states, competing phases / phase coexistence, degradation, failure pathways, phase boundaries, and other difficult-to-access phenomena experimentally observable. Drawing on recent demonstrations in autonomous laboratories and advanced characterization, along with discussions from the 2026 Advanced Light Source Automation and Self-Driving Labs Workshop, we outline a practical progression from automated instruments to distributed autonomous discovery ecosystems that link synthesis, synchrotron and neutron characterization, computing, theory, and human scientific judgment.

papers.title: The first approach to highly substituted dihydroimidazotriazolones and their controlled post-transformations
papers.abstract: A novel class of azido-modified α , β -unsaturated Ugi adducts (enamides) has been explored as a versatile platform for post -Ugi transformations. While intramolecular azide-alkyne cycloadditions of Ugi-derived peptidomimetics have been extensively studied, the corresponding azide-alkene cycloadditions on similar scaffolds have remained unexplored. In this work, we report a systematic investigation of intramolecular azide-alkene cycloaddition involving activated enamide moieties derived from Ugi adducts. Enamides readily undergo catalyst-free intramolecular [3+2] cycloaddition under mild conditions to afford the previously unknown 3,3a,4-trisubstituted-3a,4-dihydro-3 H -imidazo[1,2-c][1,2,3]triazol-5(6 H )-one scaffold in high yields. This novel fused heterocyclic system was fully characterised and proved to be a highly versatile intermediate for divergent post -Ugi transformations. Fused dihydrotriazoles transformed into 3,5-dihydroimidazol-4-ones via an elimination of N 2 supplemented by acylamide migration. Additionally, base- or acid-mediated cascades enabled efficient one-pot access to aromatised 1,2,3-triazoles and open-chain triamides, respectively. In total, 4 generations of structural isomers and 2 other classes of compounds were involved in the work. The methodologies developed highlight the synthetic value of azido-modified enamides as divergent intermediates, providing rapid and controlled entry to structurally diverse nitrogen-rich heterocycles and peptidomimetics from simple Ugi adducts derived from α , β- unsaturated aldehydes.

papers.title: A bench-scale, continuous reactor for reductive polyolefin depolymerization
papers.abstract: Catalytic deconstruction of polyolefins is central to chemical recycling, but most laboratory studies use batch reactors that obscure kinetics and limit reproducibility. Flow operation enables rigorous measurement of rates and selectivities, yet processing viscous polymer melts at small scales remains challenging. Here we present a laboratory-scale flow reactor that couples a hydraulic melt pump to a stirred-tank vessel, enabling continuous and semi-continuous operation at high pressure. The system achieves pseudo-steady state, where volatile production rates reflect C–C scission kinetics, validated by a first-principles model. Using this reactor with H-ZSM-5, we demonstrate three features of polyethylene hydrocracking difficult to probe in batch systems, namely that alkene selectivities exceed batch reactions by nearly tenfold, hydrogen availability within the melt governs the balance between alkene and alkane products, and catalyst acidity and crystallite size jointly tune this product balance through intermediate diffusion from the zeolite. This reactor provides a platform for kinetic and mechanistic studies of catalytic polymer deconstruction.

papers.title: Atomic Orbital Interactions in [CeX6]2– (X = F, Cl, Br): Consequences for X-Ray Absorption Spectroscopic Analysis
papers.abstract: Metal–ligand bonding in [CeX 6 ] 2– complexes (X = F, Cl, Br) is investigated using density functional theory (DFT) and pre-bonding analysis. The analysis quantifies atomic orbital (AO) energies and overlaps in the complexes, with a focus on the mixing between Ce 4f AOs with halide 𝑛p donor AOs. Results indicate that decreasing Ce–ligand AO overlap from X = F to Br is compensated by improved AO energy matching, leading to increased 4f-based ligand-to-metal donation across the series. Population analysis derived from pre-bonding data rationalizes recent experimental X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) findings. Effective orbital overlaps extracted from XANES data using a simplified AO bonding model based on the Wolfsberg–Helmholtz (WH) relation are compared directly with pre-bonding overlaps. The consequences of using ionization potential (IP) based AO energies in the experimental data workup and other assumptions inherent in the bonding model are also scrutinized. Using consistent pre-bonding AO energies in the model requires a WH constant of 𝐾 ≃ 3 to reproduce the calculated overlaps for 4f-based interactions. Combining IP-based AO energies with a conventional value 𝐾 = 2, as done in prior studies, is shown to yield comparable overlaps due to a cancellation of errors. Overall, pre-bonding analysis provides a framework rooted in first-principles theory for connecting AO interactions in the molecule with experimental bonding trends.

papers.title: Chemical Synthesis of the endogenous metabolite Phosphocitrate and Its Structural Isomer Phosphoisocitrate
Transitional Band Gaps During Polarization Switching in Wurtzite Ferroelectrics
papers.abstract: The electronic band gap ( E g ) is commonly treated as a static materials property associated with an equilibrium crystal structure. Yet in functional materials whose operation involves field-driven structural transformations, the relevant electronic structure may evolve as the atoms traverse different configurations, with consequences for materials design and device reliability. Wurtzite ferroelectrics provide a compelling setting to examine this idea because polarization reversal requires substantial atomic rearrangement and unusually large electric fields that can approach dielectric breakdown.
