Here, using first-principles calculations, we track E g along atomistically resolved polarization switching minimum energy pathways in experimentally established Al 1−x Sc x N, Ga 1−x Sc x N, and Al 1−x B x N ferroelectric alloys. As cation-centered tetrahedra rearrange and invert during switching, the band gap decreases substantially relative to the equilibrium polar state, with reductions reaching approximately 30-40% in some compositions. Importantly, the minimum E g does not necessarily coincide with zero polarization or with the highest-energy configuration along the switching pathway, demonstrating that the energetic and electronic structure landscapes do not map trivially onto one another. Extending the analysis to 24 chemically diverse wurtzite compounds reveals transitional E g reductions ranging from negligible to nearly 50%. These results identify the minimum E g sampled along the switching trajectory as an important, material-specific descriptor of electronic robustness. The results also suggest an intrinsic contribution to transient excess conduction during switching and motivate future studies connecting transitional electronic structure to conductive domain walls and memristive behavior in ferroelectrics.

papers.title: A Vanadium(II) Photosensitizer Delivered by Human Serum Albumin for Photodynamic Therapy
papers.abstract: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is an established clinically approved treatment; however, the development of next-generation photosensitizers remains constrained by the reliance on scarce precious-metal scaffolds and poor pharmacological properties. Earth-abundant first-row transition metals offer an attractive alternative, but their application in PDT remains underexplored. Herein, we report the first vanadium(II) photosensitizer for PDT and show that its biological activity can be unlocked through loading into human serum albumin (HSA), a strategy intended to improve its pharmacological properties. The resulting HSA-bound complex showed negligible dark toxicity and induced pronounced light-dependent cytotoxicity upon blue- and red-light irradiation in human colon carcinoma cells. Mechanistic studies revealed that the HSAbound complex preferentially accumulates in lysosomes, where red-light irradiation triggers singlet oxygen generation and promotes apoptosis. This work establishes vanadium(II) complexes as a new class of photosensitizers for photodynamic therapy and opens new opportunities for the design of first-row transition-metal photosensitizers with improved photophysical properties.

papers.title: Nanothermodynamic Generalization of the Young–Laplace and Young Equations for Sessile Droplets with Line Effects
papers.abstract: Thermodynamic investigations of wetting phenomena require that we handle the nanoscale. By combining Hill’s small-system thermodynamics with a Gibbsian composite-system description, we formulate the equilibrium thermodynamics of a sessile nanodroplet. We consider a one-component liquid droplet resting on an ideal, flat, inert solid substrate and in contact with reservoirs that fix the temperature and chemical potential. Finite-size effects are retained in the liquid bulk phase, the liquid–vapor interface, and the three-phase contact line, while the solid–vapor and solid–liquid interfaces are assumed to follow regular thermodynamics and treated macroscopically. The distinction between integral and differential pressure, surface tension, and line tension is used to derive nanothermodynamic generalizations of the Young–Laplace and Young equations. The resulting equations account for the size-and shape dependence of the finite thermodynamic contributions and recover the classical equilibrium equations in the macroscopic limit.

papers.title: Dielectric Nanolensing: How a Wavelength-Scale Lens Carries Hidden Detail into an Ordinary Microscope and What Chemistry Should Build Next
papers.abstract: Dielectric nanolensing has evolved from a wavelength-scale molecular lens into a broad family of microsphere, particle-lens, scanning, arrayed, and computational platforms. Breakthrough advances now include white-light nanoscopy, immersed high-index imaging, large-field scanning, non-destructive semiconductor metrology, living-cell optics, nanolithography, and substrate-free Raman analysis. This Perspective explains, in accessible terms, how a lens placed in the specimen’s near field can redirect otherwise inaccessible spatial information into light collected by an ordinary objective. It then reconciles curvature, solid immersion, nanojets, Mie and whispering-gallery modes, and Fano interference as condition-dependent contributions rather than competing universal explanations. The central opportunity is forward-looking: chemistry can control complex refractive index, shape, assembly, environment, and the nanometre-scale lens-specimen gap, while quantitative transfer measurements can replace incomparable resolution claims. Together, these developments point toward scalable, calibrated nanolenses for imaging, metrology, and chemical analysis.

papers.title: Making Analytic Double-Hybrid DFT Gradients Practical: A High-Performance Multi-GPU RI Implementation
papers.abstract: Double-hybrid density functional theory (DHDFT) constitutes the fifth rung of the DFT Jacob's ladder and ranks among the most accurate broadly applicable density-functional methods, but its use for molecular structure and dynamics remains limited by the substantial computational cost of analytic nuclear gradients. Here we present the first fully GPU-accelerated implementation of analytic gradients for DHDFT within a Gaussian atomic-orbital framework. The implementation, developed in the Extreme-scale Electronic Structure System (EXESS), employs resolution-of-the-identity (RI) techniques throughout the calculation and evaluates all main algorithmic components of gradient on GPUs, including the modified Z-vector response and the explicit nuclear derivative of the exchange-correlation potential. The distributed multi-GPU formulation supports basis functions through g angular momentum and is performance-portable across NVIDIA and AMD GPUs. Gradients for B2PLYP and revDSD-PBEP86-D4 are validated against numerical differentiation and the established CPU implementation in ORCA. For sufficiently large calculations, EXESS sustains more than 50% of the theoretical peak double-precision throughput and exhibits effective multi-GPU strong scaling. Calculations are demonstrated through 80 atoms at quadruple-ζ quality and 212 atoms at double-ζ quality. Relative to ORCA on a modern Sapphire Rapids CPU, a single NVIDIA H200 GPU reduces wall time by approximately 10x-675x. These results make large-basis analytic DHDFT gradients practical for geometry optimisation and exploration of molecular potential-energy surfaces.

papers.title: Seedless one-pot synthesis of high aspect ratio chiral gold nanofibers
papers.abstract: Chirality, a fundamental characteristic of nature, plays a decisive role in molecular recognition, catalysis, and cellular organization. Translating this asymmetry into synthetic systems has the potential to unlock new functionalities at the interface of nanoscience and biology. Here, we report the synthesis of high-aspect-ratio chiral gold nanofibers, a class of one-dimensional chiral plasmonic materials, fabricated via a seedless, soft-templated, ligand-assisted growth method using D/L-cysteine as chiral inducers. Small-angle X-ray diffraction and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy results support the hypothesis of a soft template-mediated growth mechanism. The resulting chiral gold nanofibers exhibit pronounced, mirror-symmetric circular dichroism signals and characteristic plasmonic resonances, confirming their intrinsic structural chirality. Further, 4D scanning transmission electron microscopy analysis indicates that the atoms arrange in a chiral fashion, resulting in the observed topographical chirality of the gold nanofibers. Altogether, this effort establishes a simple and scalable route to fabricate chiral gold architectures with potential applications in asymmetric catalysis, optical sensing and bio-instructive scaffoldings.

papers.title: VIBE-QC: an open-source, general-purpose electronic-structure code for molecules and solids developed with generative AI
papers.abstract: We present VIBE-QC, a general-purpose open-source electronic-structure code for molecules and solids, developed almost entirely through generative-AI-assisted programming (“vibe-coding”) under expert human direction. The molecular stack provides Hartree–Fock and Kohn–Sham DFT over the full LIBXC library, analytic gradients and Hessians, Møller–Plesset theory and double hybrids, coupled cluster with local-correlation variants, multireference methods, excited states, dispersion, continuum solvation, effective core potentials, and semiempirical methods. The periodic stack treats one-, two-, and three-dimensional systems at multiple 𝒌 through three Fock-build routes. Production claims are validated by out-of-process cross-code comparisons against established reference programs, reaching the nanohartree scale for mean-field methods and 3.3 × 10−7 𝐸h for conventional CCSD(T); external parity for periodic total energies is open work at this release, tracked in the public issue tracker. VIBEQC adds a container-based results-storage and visualization format (QVF), an interactive viewer (VIBEVIEW), and a job queue (VIBE-QUEUE), under the MPL-2.0 license. Graphical TOC summary. VIBE-QC is an open-source, general-purpose electronic-structure code for molecules and solids that was built almost entirely through generative-AI-assisted programming under expert direction, and validated capability-by-capability where production status is claimed. It spans Hartree–Fock through coupled cluster, multireference, and excited states for molecules, and three periodic Fock-build routes for solids, and ships its own modern file format (QVF), viewer (VIBE-VIEW), and cluster-aware queue (VIBE-QUEUE).

papers.title: Enhancing Grignard reactions via anion borrowing in deep eutectic /organic biphasic media
papers.abstract: The rational optimization of the Grignard reaction remains a considerable challenge for synthetic chemists. When assessing nucleophilic additions to unsaturated organic molecules, it has been shown that improved performance can be achieved using deep eutectic solvents (DESs). In this case, a solution of the Grignard in THF is added to the DES containing the substrate under vigorous stirring. In this study, we determine the underlying causes for this beneficial effect by combining ab initio molecular dynamics, QM/MM simulations, and enhanced sampling, using i -PrMgCl and acetophenone as reagents, THF as the organic solvent, and a 1:2 solution of choline chloride:glycerol as the DES. Our results show an increased preference for the Grignard reaction over the formation of by-products originating from a β-H transfer from the isopropyl group with the DES/THF media. This enhanced selectivity stems from the formation of chlorinated dimagnesium entities at the DES interface. While the reaction of a neutral Grignard in bulk THF kinetically favours the β-H transfer, the chlorine enrichment originating from the DES is shown to make the two reactions kinetically more equivalent, and to drastically favor the thermodynamic preference for the Grignard product, a result of increased intramolecular stabilizing interactions. This result is in line with experimental evidence of increased selectivity in the presence of various halide salts. This mechanistic interpretation paves the way for the rational improvement of Grignard reagents, allowing an even broader application of these compounds in these non-conventional solvents.

papers.title: Molecule–Metal Nanostructure Interactions in Plasmonic Chemistry
papers.abstract: Plasmonic chemistry converts metal nanostructures into photocatalysts via three interconnected channels at the molecule–metal interface: enhanced near fields, non-equilibrium charge carriers, and localized heat. This review focuses on this interfacial perspective. We show how adsorbates and ligands do more than just stick to nanoparticles – they reduce plasmon lifetimes, change work functions, modify the density of states, and impact the energy and charge flow during various physical processes. Ultrafast thermalization under pulsed excitation and steady state conditions under continuous illumination open up different pathways for chemical reactions. Although the plasmonic metal is crucial, surface-bound molecules actively participate by scavenging charge carriers, affecting selectivity and stability, and even undergoing chemical transformations. These aspects are crucial for controlling product distributions and enabling novel chemical pathways by exploiting excited-state pathways inaccessible through thermal energy. Together with the nanoscale properties of plasmonic nanostructures, chemical reactions can be confined to nanoscale hot spots shaped by geometry and polarization. These insights inform the development of practical design principles for antenna–reactor hybrids and novel plasmonic materials in which absorption, carrier localization, and interfacial alignment are precisely engineered. Finally, we identify key open questions and the need for operando interfacial techniques to transform these insights into practical tools for selective, solar-driven synthesis.

papers.title: Incoherent Transport Signatures in Ferrocene and Ferrocenium-based Molecular Wires
papers.abstract: Molecular wires incorporating redox units are foundational to single-molecule electronics, yet the molecular designs and environment which govern whether charge-transport proceeds predominantly via phase-coherent quantum tunnelling or thermally activated incoherent hopping remains debated. By synthesising bench-stable Fe(III) ferrocenium wires ( ex-situ oxidation) and comparing their molecular conductance against electrochemically gated Fe(II) analogues ( in-situ oxidation) within scanning tunnelling microscopy break-junctions, we identify distinct experimental signatures of coexisting transport regimes. For both ferrocene and ferrocenium systems, while phase-coherent tunnelling through frontier molecular orbitals dominates at low bias, favourable environmental reorganisation energetics trigger efficient, two-step sequential processes at high biases. These findings resolve a long-standing mechanistic question in metallocene molecular electronics and highlight how two-terminal measurements alone are insufficient to resolve such ambiguities. Our combined electrochemical approach provides a pathway to more robust characterisation of transport phenomena in molecular junctions.

papers.title: Tokenising quantum data for label-efficient training of molecular models
papers.abstract: A model of molecular energies is limited by how much reference data can be afforded, because every training example is itself an expensive calculation. The practical question is therefore not “how accurate can this get” but “how much accuracy do I get per labelled molecule.” We built a representation of a molecule’s quantum features, which we call a quantum token and which a model consumes alongside whatever representation it already uses. The energy of a molecule in a given orbital basis is a linear functional of its one-and two-particle reduced density matrices, so those matrices, rather than the atomic coordinates, are the object the answer is actually computed from. A cheap calculation already produces an approximate one, and the token is a fixed-length encoding of it. It is not a token in the language-model sense: it is a vector of real numbers, not a discrete symbol drawn from a vocabulary, and the name refers to a unit of quantum information minted once and reused by many downstream models. No quantum hardware is involved: an ordinary classical model is trained on these features to predict the residual of the cheap calculation, the part a fast method gets wrong. Only the features are quantum. Holding the learner, the scaffold-disjoint split and the training-set size fixed and varying only the input features, adding the token to a production descriptor makes it 4.4–5.3× more accurate at equal training data, and a model given 50 labelled molecules is more accurate than the same model given 16,000 without it. At 20 to 52 heavy atoms, the size of drug candidates and the range where these models are applied in drug discovery rather than on public benchmarks, 93.7% of molecules fall within chemical accuracy, against 65.0% for the strongest classical descriptor and 4.4% for the uncorrected cheap method.

papers.title: Anomalous Hall Conductivity from Berry Curvature at the Dirac Point in AlPd5I2 Monolayer
papers.abstract: The anomalous Hall effect (AHE) in non-magnetic materials is a powerful transport probe of the Berry curvature (BC) of Bloch electrons and a key component of next-generation spintronic devices. In this work, I present a first-principles study of the anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC) in monolayer AlPd5I2, a two-dimensional material hosting a Dirac-type crossing located close to the Fermi energy. Density functional theory (DFT) with spin-orbit coupling (SOC) is performed using Quantum ESPRESSO and maximally localized Wannier functions (Wannier90). The electronic structure reveals a Dirac point at the S point, split by SOC into a gapped state with a large BC. The Fermi level is located slightly above the gap, yielding a metallic state with a very high AHC. The AHE is traced directly to the intense BC hotspots at the SOC-induced gap at the Dirac point. My findings establish the AlPd5I2 monolayer as a promising system for investigating BC dominated transport and large Hall responses.

papers.title: Mechanistic regimes for electron transfer at bio–nano interfaces
papers.abstract: Bioelectronic medicine increasingly operates at interfaces whose dimensions approach redox molecules, electrical double layers and structured electronic states. The central problem is therefore not to identify a size at which electrochemistry becomes quantum, but to determine which physical description explains a response. This challenge is acute for nanoscale bipolar electrodes, where conductor-scale potentials predicted from uniform-field models can be extremely small despite faradaic and biological activity. Local field concentration, double-layer overlap, ion-concentration polarisation, altered reorganisation energetics, stochastic molecular dynamics and electron tunnelling offer coexisting explanations. We propose a falsifiable framework that distinguishes continuum/device, interfacial/cellular, stochastic/few-molecule and quantum-informed regimes by perturbing local potential, field and length, molecular coupling, confinement and electronic structure. Quantum capacitance, bipolar electrochemistry, tunnelling junctions, activationless electron transfer and multiscale modelling illustrate these tests. Size determines when effects may become important; mechanism must be assigned from discriminating behaviour, not from size or endpoint response alone.

papers.title: In-Situ and Label-Free Quantification of BSA Adsorption on Mesoporous Silica Nanoparticles via Orthogonal Analysis in Analytical Ultracentrifugation
papers.abstract: Understanding the bio–nano interface requires precise, in-situ and label-free tools to characterize the protein corona. While hydrodynamic techniques like dynamic light scattering (DLS) and nanoparticle tracking analysis (NTA) are widely used, they face inherent limitations: DLS provides ensemble-averaged signals and often requires specific optical models, whereas NTA’s temporal resolution limits its accuracy for ultra-small particles. Here, we demonstrate the power of custom-built multiwavelength analytical ultracentrifugation (MWL-AUC) as a superior orthogonal platform to characterize the bovine serum albumin (BSA) corona on mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs). By integrating three independent analytical dimensions, i.e. in-situ supernatant depletion, density-based sedimentation analysis, and multiwavelength spectral decoupling, we achieved precise quantification of both the total adsorbed BSA and its spatial distribution. This approach enables a quantitative mapping of protein localization that transcends mere qualitative observations of aggregation. Specifically, we show that the compositional information from spectral decoupling provides a robust cross-validation for the effective density analysis, which fundamentally dictates the precision of the derived spatial distribution. This study establishes a self-validating framework for the precise characterization of protein corona on porous nanostructures, offering vital insights for the rational design of nanocarriers in complex biological environments.

papers.title: From Rim to Core: Nitrile Coordination Creates an Electronic Gradient across Cu12 Nanocluster Nodes for CO2-to-Formate Electrosynthesis
papers.abstract: Atomically precise copper nanoclusters offer an opportunity to program catalysis across individual metal positions, yet reticulation has largely been used to stabilize clusters rather than differentiate them electronically. Here, nitrile coordination converts a Cu12S9 nanocluster node into a radially polarized catalytic ensemble in Cu12TPN MOF. Single-crystal analysis resolves a thiolate-supported Cu12 architecture whose four terephthalonitrile linkers selectively address peripheral Cu sites. Bader analysis reveals an electronic gradient from electron-deficient nitrile-bound rim sites (~+0.57 |e|) to an electron-rich Cu–S/Cu interior (~+0.32–0.37 |e|). This coordination-encoded asymmetry translates directly into CO2 reduction, delivering 63.32% Faradaic efficiency for HCOOH with negligible CO formation. Density functional theory identifies a 0.91 eV energetic separation favoring O-bound *OCOH over *COOH at the pathway bifurcation, while H adsorption remains unfavorable. Post-electrolysis spectroscopy confirms persistence of the cluster-derived environment. These results establish reticulation as an electronic programming strategy within, rather than merely around, atomically precise nanocluster nodes. Atomically precise metal nanoclusters (NCs) occupy an unusual catalytic regime in which composition, metalmetal connectivity, ligand coordination, and individual surface sites can all be resolved at the atomic level.1-24 Unlike nanoparticles with distributed surface sites, NCs provide finite multinuclear ensembles in which structural and electronic perturbations can be traced from specific coordination events to catalytic consequences. Copper nanoclusters are especially attractive in this regard because the adaptable coordination chemistry of Cu(I), flexible Cu–S bonding, and short Cu···Cu contacts permit substantial redistribution of geometry and electron density within a single cluster.25-42 Yet this same adaptability makes it difficult to preserve atomically defined Cu ensembles under catalytic conditions.

papers.title: Chemical synthesis of an atomically precise 2.5-MDa protein capsid and its mirror image
papers.abstract: Protein capsids perform a broad range of biological functions 1–4 and can be engineered 5 as delivery vehicles, 6 nanoreactors, 7 biosensors, 8 and vaccines. 9 However, because the protein building blocks that make up these capsids must be expressed in biological systems, their composition is largely restricted to the canonical amino acids, limiting functionality. Assembling capsids from chemically synthesized proteins could circumvent this limitation but has not been accomplished due to a combination of technical challenges. Here we demonstrate the complete chemical synthesis of the 14.1-kDa coat protein of bacteriophage Qβ and its assembly into 180-subunit 2.5-MDa capsids. We exploit the expanded chemical palette afforded by total synthesis to produce mirror-image capsids composed entirely of unnatural D-amino acids. We determine the structures of the L- and D-capsids to 3-Å resolution by cryo-EM and verify their stereochemistry by cryo-ET. D-capsids elicit antibody titers 100-fold lower than their L-counterparts in mice, with the D-capsid response dominated by IgM antibodies. We demonstrate functional delivery in vivo using synthetic L-and D-capsids loaded with luciferase-encoding mRNA. By combining biological self-assembly with chemical synthesis, our results establish a route to producing a new class of programmable nanomaterials for diverse applications.

papers.title: Dynamic Coordination Enables Moisture-Tolerant Organoaluminum Catalysis for Controlled Ring-Opening Polymerization
papers.abstract: Reconciling high catalytic activity with air/moisture stability remains a fundamental challenge in the development of efficient organometallic catalysts for the ring‑opening polymerization (ROP). In this contribution, we present a dynamic Lewis-base coordination strategy that regulates the coordination environment of an organoaluminum catalyst to balance these competing requirements. A structurally simple organoaluminum catalyst featuring a dynamic THF ligand, MeAl(BHT)2(THF) (BHT = 2,6-di-tert-butyl-4-methylphenoxy), is easily prepared from commercially available trimethylaluminum, 2,6-di-tert-butyl-4-methylphenol and tetrahydrofuran (THF) without tedious purification. In contrast to the parent MeAl(BHT)2, MeAl(BHT)2(THF) exhibits substantially enhanced air/moisture tolerance while retaining good catalytic activity and controllability toward the ROP of a diversity of lactones and lactide. Notably, MeAl(BHT)2(THF) enable controlled ROP of commercially as-received monomers without prior drying or purification. In particular, MeAl(BHT)2(THF) achieves a high turnover frequency (TOF) of 8400 h-1 for the bulk ROP of l-lactide conducted at 180 °C in air. The single-crystal structural analysis and in-situ NMR experiments collaboratively confirm the dynamic coordination and dissociation of the THF ligand, which accounts for the balance of high activity and moisture tolerance. This dynamic ligand strategy affords a robust organometallic catalyst with facile preparation, good activity and ambient stability, facilitating practical scalable aliphatic polyester synthesis.

papers.title: Enhancement of Sensory Hop Aroma by Extending the Whirlpool Settling Time
Rapid, High-Yielding, and Broad-Scope Silicon-Noded Single-Atom Ligation Platform
papers.abstract: The node–module logic underpins DNA, RNA, and metal–organic frameworks. In small-molecule synthesis, SuFEx and PFEx exploit sulfur or phosphorus as single‑atom nodes for 10 modular ligations but are largely confined to amine and phenol modules. Silicon‑based ligation would offer a viable alternative, as both alcohols and phenols can serve as reliable modules, yet it has lacked efficient and controllable platforms. Herein, we report a silicon-noded ligation platform using bis(2,4,6-trimethoxyphenyl)silanes (bis(TMP)silanes) as the ligation hubs, enabling rapid, high-yielding ligation of both alcohol and phenol modules with broad functional-group tolerance.

papers.title: Operational insights from the front lines of OpenADMET: lessons from our blind challenges
papers.abstract: The gap between reported machine learning (ML) model performance in drug discovery and the experience of using these models in live discovery projects remains a major hurdle for the field, because the retrospective nature of most benchmarks makes it difficult to objectively assess progress. To address this gap, OpenADMET has hosted a series of blind challenges to benchmark and advance predictive modeling in absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET). In this Perspective, we distill the operational, strategic, and community-level lessons from our first four blind challenges, providing a practical blueprint for designing and running collaborative machine learning competitions in the life sciences. In addition, we open-source our blind challenge infrastructure and data-validation tools to lower the barrier to entry for hosting rigorous, community-driven competitions and to foster a sustainable framework for collective learning in computer-aided drug discovery.

papers.title: Water Layering and Orientation Modulate Lanthanide Hydration in Carbon Nanotubes
papers.abstract: Nanoscale confinement can reorganize water molecules and alter ionic hydration, offering a potential route to separating chemically similar ions. We use molecular dynamics simulations with the MACE-MH-1 foundation machine-learning interatomic potential to investigate the hydration of eight trivalent lanthanide ions (Ln 3+ : La 3+ , Pr 3+ , Nd 3+ , Gd 3+ , Tb 3+ , Dy 3+ , Tm 3+ , and Lu 3+ ) in carbon nanotubes (CNTs) with diameters of 1.09–1.49 nm. We first evaluate MACE-MH-1 for Ln 3+ hydration in bulk solution. The OMOL model of MACE-MH-1 reproduces the reported Ln–O distances and coordination-number trends and is therefore used for the CNT simulations. The hydration factor, which measures first-shell orientational order, varies nonmonotonically with CNT diameter and reaches a minimum in CNT(9,9), which also accommodates the most first-shell water molecules. This minimum coincides with the emergence of a central water population and reflects two combined effects: difference in preferred orientation between first-shell and surrounding water molecules and increased hydrogen-bond coupling between them. However, different Ln 3+ ions respond similarly to confinement, suggesting that CNT confinement alone may offer limited selectivity for their separation.

papers.title: Growth and Postsynthetic Modulation of Morphology-Encoded Plasmonic Chirality
papers.abstract: Establishing how nanoscale morphology gives rise to plasmonic chirality requires understanding both its development during nanoparticle growth and its response to subsequent structural modification. Here, we investigate these complementary processes within a single nanoparticle platform through cysteine-directed Au growth followed by Ag overgrowth. Initially achiral Au bipyramids evolve into irregular, faceted nanoparticles displaying strong bisignate circular dichroism (CD), with L- and D-cysteine producing approximately mirror-related responses. Varying the relative proportions of the cysteine enantiomers systematically controls the sign and magnitude of the CD response, with near cancellation for the racemic mixture. Time-resolved measurements reveal that the positive and negative CD bands develop with comparable sigmoidal Avrami-type kinetics, quantitatively capturing the emergence of plasmonic chirality during growth. Once chirality is established, subsequent Ag deposition without additional cysteine progressively blue-shifts the plasmonic response and attenuates the CD of both enantiomeric nanoparticles without sign reversal. This attenuation accompanies the transformation of the irregular, faceted Au exterior into a smoother and more rounded Ag-rich outer morphology. Together, these observations connect the emergence and postsynthetic attenuation of plasmonic chirality and highlight the importance of the asymmetric nanoparticle exterior in sustaining morphology-encoded chiroptical activity.

papers.title: MaRs: A Universal Python Library for Steady-State and Time-Resolved EPR Simulations
papers.abstract: MaRs is an open-source Python library for the simulation and fitting of electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectra. MaRs supports simulations of field-swept and frequency-swept continuous-wave EPR, accounting for various spin-sublevel polarizations. Moreover, MaRs is capable of simulating complete 2D time-resolved EPR spectra (in field-time domain). The latter can be computed in different levels of theoretical complexity. First, the time evolution can be computed either with kinetic rate equations, which describe population transfer, or in full Liouville space, which captures coherence dynamics. Second, the relaxation pathways in timeresolved simulations can be specified either through intuitive rate parameters that are automatically expanded into the Lindblad master-equation form, or derived microscopically using the Bloch-Redfield formalism. To handle physically complex relaxation scenarios, MaRs provides automatic thermal-balance enforcement and composition operations that allow multicomponent relaxation models to be assembled from simple building blocks. Built on PyTorch (popular platform for machine learning development), MaRs leverages operations on both CPU and CUDA (GPU) backends. We demonstrate MaRs time-resolved EPR capabilities as well the differences and limitations of each built-in approach to time-domain simulations on the examples of coupled triplet-doublet pairs and systems exhibiting the reverse intersystem crossing phenomenon. Separately, we validate stationary EPR simulations across diverse spin systems, including high-spin complexes, achieving excellent agreement with established packages. We also show the possibilities of parameter fitting framework, applicable to all spectrum types implemented in MaRs, that supports multiple optimization strategies and uncertainty quantification.

papers.title: Preclinical and Pilot Human Evaluation of [18F]NIDF-1, an N-Protonation-Guided Tau PET Tracer
papers.abstract: Hyperphosphorylated tau aggregates are a pathological hallmark of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and an important target for positron emission tomography (PET) imaging. Guided by the hypothesis that N-protonation enables electrostatic interactions with negatively charged sites associated with tau hyperphosphorylation, we designed and synthesized a focused series of azaindole derivatives and identified NIDF-1 as a lead compound by competitive autoradiography on AD brain sections (IC50 = 22.1 ± 6.8 nM). NIDF-1 showed low amyloid-β (Aβ) cross-reactivity and limited off-target toward monoamine oxidases (MAO). [18F]NIDF-1 exhibited favorable brain kinetics in rodents, with an initial brain uptake of 7.57% ID/g in mice and a peak brain mean standardized uptake value (SUVmean) of 2.20 in Sprague–Dawley (SD) rats, followed by rapid clearance (2-to-60-min brain uptake ratios of 18.46 and 3.30, respectively). Autoradiography confirmed preferential binding to ADassociated tau pathology. In a pilot human PET study, [18F]NIDF-1 showed higher cortical retention in an AD participant than in a healthy control. These findings identify [18F]NIDF-1 as a promising tau PET tracer with favorable tau binding affinity, brain kinetics, and encouraging initial human imaging results, while supporting N-protonation as a useful design consideration for tau-targeted imaging agents. KEYWORDS: N-Protonation, Tau PET tracer, Azaindole, Alzheimer’s disease

papers.title: Historical Side Information and the Reversal of Open-System Dynamics
papers.abstract: Microscopic reversibility guarantees the existence of a time-reversed trajectory for a globally reversible dynamical system, but does not by itself guarantee that a later controller possesses the physical information required to identify and implement that trajectory. For an open system, distinctions between different microscopic histories may become encoded in environmental correlations whose physical carriers disperse, degrade, or become inaccessible, even though the corresponding information remains present in the global state. We formulate this distinction in terms of the physically accessible state of the controller and introduce a task-dependent measure of historical reversal information: the additional physically realizable information required to achieve a prescribed reversal accuracy. For continuous systems, a local Gaussian model yields a rate–distortion lower benchmark whose high-resolution behavior separates a geometrical contribution from a dynamical amplification term. For chaotic dynamics, the latter can acquire a Pesin-type form proportional to the relevant positive Lyapunov exponents. We then distinguish practical loss of accessibility from causal inaccessibility. When carriers of reversal-relevant information cross a causal horizon, subsequent information backflow to the controller is excluded. Finally, we consider a finite physical memory and show, in a minimal model, that memory saturation followed by logical erasure links the loss of accessible historical distinctions to Landauer entropy production. If the corresponding erasure heat is transferred across a horizon, this yields a lower bound on the associated horizon-entropy and area increase. The resulting framework separates global information preservation from local physical recoverability and shows how openness, dynamical instability, finite record capacity, and causal structure can jointly limit the reversal of a particular realized history without violating microscopic reversibility.

papers.title: When Is a Molecule a Duplicate? Identity Policy Determines What a Benchmark Audit Finds
papers.abstract: Reports of duplicate or redundant records in molecular machine-learning benchmarks are routinely presented as properties of the datasets. They are not. A duplicate count is the output of an operational definition of molecular identity applied to a dataset, and different defensible definitions return different answers from the same file. We audited seven MoleculeNet [3] benchmarks (52,144 records) under a four-level identity hierarchy — canonical molecular graph, fragment parent, charge-normalised parent and tautomer-normalised parent — with the Standard InChIKey as an orthogonal comparator rather than a rung, and with derived identity withheld outside a declared domain of applicability. Duplicate-group counts moved with the level in every benchmark, and for three the audit changed its answer to whether the benchmark contains duplicate compounds at all. Domain choice mattered as much: HIV reports 330 duplicate groups at the tautomer-normalised level when identity is asserted for every record, against 124 on the declared domain. A post hoc sensitivity analysis found that domain under-covered main-group and f-block metal-associated structures, giving 109 without displacing 124 as the prespecified result. Of 295 merge events, 179 were decidable from structure alone and 116 were policy-dependent; across that complete census, 19 events (16.4%; 41 records) received a different benchmark-equivalence decision from transition-appropriate official-InChI arbitration under an endpoint rulebook fixed before final classification, all 19 in one benchmark's stereochemical subset. We publish the identity policy as an executable, fingerprinted contract reproducing every reported count exactly (434/434), so the assumptions behind an audit statistic can be inspected and re-executed rather than inferred.

papers.title: Biosynthetic Plausibility Mapper: Reaction-Aware Prioritization of Plant Metabolite Candidates Using Curated Pathway Context
papers.abstract: Untargeted plant metabolomics can generate numerous structurally plausible annotations and candidate structures, but structural similarity alone does not establish whether a compound is consistent with the biosynthetic context represented by the detected metabolome. Integrating curated biochemical relationships with chemical similarity could therefore provide an additional, interpretable layer for candidate prioritization. Here, we present Biosynthetic Plausibility Mapper (BPM), an opensource cheminformatics application that maps user-provided plant metabolite annotations onto a locally constructed PlantCyc-derived knowledge base and explicitly distinguishes detected compounds, curated pathway context, and computationally prioritized candidates. BPM integrates chemical-identity reconciliation, curated reaction and pathway relationships, structural similarity, and global-context coherence into a decomposable candidate-ranking framework. In pathway-based benchmarking against hard structural decoys, BPM v3.1 achieved AUROC and AUPRC values of 1.000 and ranked the reference compound first in all 20 trials. In a more stringent adversarial benchmark containing biosynthetically plausible alternatives, v3.1 improved AUROC from 0.920 to 0.985, AUPRC from 0.574 Biosynthetic Plausibility Mapper to 0.837, and Top-1 accuracy from 65% to 90% relative to v3. A compact phenylpropanoid–flavonoid example illustrates the separation of experimental annotations, curated context, and prioritized hypotheses, while a larger Arabidopsis occurrence dataset demonstrates application to 864 mapped compounds within a 6,714-node network. BPM therefore provides an interpretable framework for converting annotated plant metabolite lists into ranked biosynthetic hypotheses without conflating computational plausibility with compound identification. By combining curated biochemical context with structural evidence and exporting prioritized candidates for targeted interrogation of LC–MS/MS data, BPM provides a practical link between metabolite annotation, biosynthetic interpretation, and subsequent experimental investigation.

papers.title: Self-Salting Coacervates: Interfacial Tension Reveals a Critical-Like Self-Suppression of Complex Coacervation
papers.abstract: Complex coacervation, the associative liquid\liquid phase separation of oppositely charged polyelectrolytes, is a widely used physicochemical model for the principles underlying biomolecular condensates and for applications in encapsulation and underwater adhesion. Coacervation is typically controlled through the ionic strength of an added salt, while the role of polyelectrolyte concentration itself has received much less attention. Here we show that increasing polymer concentration can itself progressively suppress complex coacervation in a charge-stoichiometric, salt-free poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride)/sodium polyacrylate system. As the polymer concentration increases, the coacervate phase swells while the fraction of polymer recovered in it stays nearly constant, and the compositions and densities of the coacervate and supernatant phases progressively converge. At a polymer concentration of 400 mM, the macroscopic phase boundary vanishes and the system reaches a homogeneous, self-suppressed coacervation state. Over this range, the liquid\liquid interfacial tension decreases continuously toward zero, following a critical-like power law with an exponent of 1.43±0.03, close to the classical mean-field value of 3/2. These results show that polyelectrolyte concentration is not merely a compositional variable but can itself drive coacervation toward a critical-like, homogeneous state by increasing salt-like screening from polymer-derived counterions, analogous to the effect of added salt.

papers.title: Sampling Budget as a Confound in Dimensionality-Reduction Analyses of Molecular Simulation
papers.abstract: A common claim in molecular simulation is that projecting a trajectory reveals N metastable states. Here N is operationally the number of Gaussian-mixture components selected in a low-dimensional embedding, without a kinetic model it should be read as an apparent-basin count, not a validated metastable-state count. Across two potentials with basin counts fixed by construction and two independent 100 ns alanine-dipeptide simulations, the BIC-selected component count rises strongly with sampling budget (Spearman rho = 0.87-0.97 across systems and methods) although the reference landscape is unchanged. The trend persists under uniform thinning of a common reference trajectory, where coverage is approximately matched, and under IID Boltzmann sampling in the exact synthetic latent coordinates, which removes time correlation and projection learning. Other criteria exhibit different failure modes: AIC is frequently ceiling-censored or non-monotone, ICL never reaches the tested ceiling but remains method-dependently inaccurate, and silhouette and the simple elbow diagnostic are largely insensitive. BIC-selected recovery often peaks at an intermediate budget and then declines even while recovery at the reference component count is flat or improves. One exception is explicit, alanine TICA seed 1 shows no decline within the tested range because its high-recovery crossover occurs at the last budget. We recommend reporting sampling-budget curves, treating mixture components as candidate states until kinetically validated, and using ICL only as a less-ceiling-prone sensitivity analysis rather than a general default.

papers.title: SimSJSAlert: A Similarity-Augmented Multi-View Learning Framework with Scaffold Alerts for Drug-Induced Stevens-Johnson Syndrome Risk Assessment
papers.abstract: Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS) is a rare, life-threatening adverse drug reaction for which early identification of high-risk drugs remains challenging. In this study, we developed an explainable quantitative structure-toxicity relationship (QSTR) framework for SJS prediction using a multi-view learning framework with 21 molecular representations, including molecular descriptors, fingerprints, transformer-based embeddings, and a molecular similarity representation. Model development and evaluation were designed in accordance with the OECD principles for QSAR validation, incorporating scaffold-aware validation, external evaluation on pharmacovigilance negative-signal compounds, and structural interpretation by integrating SHAP with Bemis-Murcko scaffold enrichment analysis. The proposed framework achieved robust sensitivity and specificity, with molecular similarity consistently improving the identification of SJS-associated compounds. Furthermore, a consensus prediction and scaffold-based prioritization strategy identified several high-risk drugs from the 1 external negative-signal dataset, including cefprozil, tetracycline, and omadacycline, highlighting their potential association with SJS and warranting further pharmacovigilance and experimental investigation. To facilitate practical application, this was deployed as a freely accessible web server, SimSJSAlert (https: //sim-sjs-alert.streamlit.app/), enabling rapid drug-induced SJS risk assessment. The proposed framework combines predictive performance, interpretability, and accessibility to support early SJS risk assessment, pharmacovigilance signal prioritization, and safer drug development.

papers.title: Synthetic Mutagenesis of Tyrosine into Proline Mimetics Enables Late-Stage Backbone Editing of Peptides
papers.abstract: The biological and physicochemical properties of peptides are strongly influenced by their backbone conformations. However, installing conformationally restricting units generally requires peptide redesign and resynthesis using noncanonical amino acids. Here, we report a late-stage backbone-editing method that converts a native amino acid residue into a proline-mimetic structure. Treatment of the dearomatized intermediate generated by tyrosine-selective oxime conjugation in a basic aqueous buffer induced intramolecular 1,4-addition of the backbone amide nitrogen, thereby converting the tyrosine residue into a cyclic proline-mimetic unit within the peptide backbone. This transformation proceeded efficiently under mild aqueous conditions and was applicable to several bioactive peptides. Multidimensional NMR analyses established the structures of the resulting products, while conventional molecular dynamics and REST2 simulations demonstrated that the installed proline-mimetic backbone reduced the local conformational freedom of the peptide. Evaluation using a β-hairpin model peptide further demonstrated that the proline-mimetic structure enhanced resistance to proteolytic degradation. This method constitutes a chemical mutagenesis strategy that directly converts a native tyrosine residue into a backbone conformational control unit without reconstructing the parent peptide sequence. By connecting residue-selective side-chain modification with backbone editing, this strategy provides a new design concept for the late-stage conformational and functional diversification of peptides.

papers.title: Coordinate bonding, cluster delocalization and topological criticality in a cyclic trimeric beryllium–dinitrogen complex
papers.abstract: Fixation and coordination of molecular dinitrogen (N2) by main-group clusters offer fundamental insight into non-classical multi-centre bonding and light-metal activation pathways. Here we report a combined density-functional and ab initio study of the cyclic cluster Be3(N2)3. Geometry optimization and frequency analysis establish a stable, closed-shell Cs-symmetric trimer containing an isosceles triangular Be3 metal core coordinated end-on by three terminal N2 ligands. Energy decomposition analysis coupled with natural orbitals for chemical valence (ETS-NOCV) shows that the Be3⋯(N2)3 interaction is dominated by orbital contributions (≈60 % of attractive forces), supplemented by electrostatic attraction that together overcome Pauli repulsion. Quantum theory of atoms in molecules (QTAIM) identifies two non-nuclear attractors along the apical–basal Be–Be edges, while electron localization function (ELF) and localized orbital locator (LOL) basin analyses reveal a distinct heart-shaped trisynaptic valence basin V(Be,Be,Be) populated by ≈1.8–2.0 electrons. These topological signatures establish multi-centre σ-aromatic delocalization as the structural foundation of the central metallacycle and demonstrate that light alkaline-earth elements can support non-classical N2 coordination frameworks.

papers.title: Machine-learning force-field scoring rivals free-energy perturbation for congeneric ligand ranking across public benchmarks
papers.abstract: Relative binding free-energy (RBFE) methods such as free-energy perturbation (FEP) set the accuracy standard for ranking congeneric ligands in structurebased drug design, but their computational cost limits throughput. Machine-learned force fields (MLFFs) now approach quantum-chemical accuracy at a small fraction of that cost, raising the question of whether they can recover much of RBFE’s ranking accuracy while remaining computationally efficient. We introduce a static-score methodology called taqo and benchmark 10 MLFF variants spanning 6 model families (UMA, MACE, Orb, eSEN, AIMNet2, AllScAIP), together with a classical molecular-mechanics force field, on a uniform staticpocket protocol, correlated against experiment across 22 benchmark systems.We find that the ten MLFFs cannot be resolved from one another at this sample size, while every one of them significantly outranks the classical force field reference, at a few seconds per ligand on a single GPU. Against published OpenFE and FEP+ results on the same systems and the same ligand sets, taqo is statistically indistinguishable from OpenFE and significantly below FEP+, at roughly three orders of magnitude lower cost. On the congeneric JACS subset taqo and FEP+ are statistically indistinguishable. On the same benchmark poses taqo outperforms classical docking scores and is statistically indistinguishable from deep-learning affinity models, without any affinity-specific training. Together these establish MLFF interaction-energy scoring as a practical high-throughput approach for lead optimization.

papers.title: A substrate-first-enzymology deep-learning framework for transforming new-to-nature chemicals
papers.abstract: Enzyme activity data favor familiar substrates and positive outcomes, creating survivorship bias that limits predictions for new-to-nature chemistry. Here we introduce substrate-first enzymology: a chemically diverse substrate array is designed to broaden coverage of a predefined, synthetically relevant chemical space, independently of expected activity. Alcohol dehydrogenases (ADHs) are systematically assayed against this array using a unified high-throughput assay. The enzyme–substrate matrix records activity labels and turnover frequency ( k cat ) values; substrate-resolved profiles form an ADH k cat atlas. A deep learning model trained on these data classifies activity and predicts k cat for active pairs. The model outperforms existing approaches under matched training and evaluation conditions and prospectively prioritizes active substrates from underrepresented chemical space. Without binding-pocket annotations, the model’s attention mechanism highlights substrate reactive centers and catalytically relevant residues. By designing substrate coverage before measurement and retaining both positive and negative outcomes, this framework reduces historical sampling bias and supports interpretable k cat prediction beyond historically sampled chemistry.

papers.title: Thermodynamics-Driven Treatability Investigation of Energy-Storage-Related Emerging PFAS
papers.abstract: Bis-perfluoroalkyl sulfonimides (bis-FASIs), widely used in lithium-ion battery electrolytes, are increasingly detected in the environment, yet their transformation and treatability remain poorly understood. Here, density functional theory (DFT) calculations were integrated with experiments to determine how molecular structure controls bis-FASIs degradation. During electrochemical oxidation (EO) and UV/sulfite (UV/S) treatment, degradation and defluorination generally increased with perfluoroalkyl-chain length, with bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)imide (bis-FMeSI) being the most recalcitrant homolog. Although both processes nearly completely transformed bis-FMeSI, its fluorine fate differed markedly. EO produced trifluoromethanesulfonate (TFMS) at nearly stoichiometric yield, whereas UV/S generated both TFMS and trifluoromethanesulfonamide (TfNH 2 ). Marcus-theory calculations established the redox thresholds for one-electron transfer, while electronic-structure analysis showed that oxidation and reduction generate distinct states that follow different bond-cleavage pathways. Further transformation of TFMS and TfNH 2 required redox conditions beyond those attainable within the aqueous-phase stability window, causing their accumulation and limiting defluorination. To overcome this constraint, we demonstrated a cross-media approach in which bis-FMeSI and TFMS were adsorbed from water onto granular activated carbon and subsequently destroyed by additive-free ball milling with stainless-steel media, achieving complete degradation and near-quantitative recovery of organofluorine as fluoride. This cross-media strategy provides a potential solution for PFAS resistant to aqueous-phase treatment.

papers.title: Computational investigation of the first most (𝝅; 𝝅∗)𝟏; (𝒏; 𝝅∗)𝟏;(𝝅; 𝝈∗)𝟏 and (𝒏; 𝝈∗)𝟏 electronic states of all possible positional isomers of iodinated BODIPY
papers.abstract: Photochemistry of all possible positional isomers of iodinated -BODIPY has been explored employing state of the art two-component relativistic sf-X2C-S-TD-DFT-SOC method. Vertical excitation energies; oscillator strength and spin–orbit couplings of first most promising electronic states have been computed. Effect of number of iodine atoms attached to BODIPY moiety and their topology on magnitude of vertical excitation energies have been explained in detail. Slater–Condon rules and El–Sayed rules which are special case of former have been effectively employed to explain magnitude of spin–orbit couplings between states of different multiplicities. Coupled states exhibiting anomalies from conventional El–Sayed rules have been explained with the help of orbitals involved in respective states. Effect of non-planarity of BODIPY ring on magnitude of spin–orbit couplings between states of different multiplicities have also been discussed. Most effective positions on BODIPY moiety that can turn in to effective photosensitizer by attaching iodine atoms on them has been explored and explained.

papers.title: Closed-loop optimization in an industrial R&D lab
papers.abstract: In industrial research and development, autonomous closed-loop reaction optimizers have the potential to significantly accelerate processes, but they must be robust and flexible, encompassing both hardware and software components. This paper presents a versatile system developed and deployed within a research unit of an industrial R&D lab, designed to address a variety of industry-relevant challenges rather than functioning as a one-off demonstrator. Unlike traditional systems that may focus on specific chemical processes, our approach facilitates the optimization of reactions across multiple organic synthesis research groups. We illustrate the system’s capabilities through three case studies, showcasing its adaptability and effectiveness in real-world applications. By prioritizing configurability and reusability, this work aims to contribute to a more sustainable and efficient approach to chemical engineering practices in industrial settings where interdisciplinary collaboration is key.

papers.title: TLQ Method: A Tandem Mixing–Linear Deduction–Quantile Weighted Median Framework for Robust Metabolite Screening and a General Diagnostic Indicator for Measurement Reliability
papers.abstract: Untargeted metabolomics is constrained by inter-individual variability, difficulty in detecting low-abundance metabolites, and matrix effects. Post-acquisition corrections are limited when biological variation is large, signals approach detection limits, or matrix effects are strong. We propose the TLQ method, consisting of Tandem Mixing, Linear Deduction, and Quantile Quality-Weighted Median. Tandem Mixing compresses between-group matrix differences and enhances low-abundance signals via equal-volume mixing of paired samples. Linear Deduction removes background and back-calculates the treatment signal, yielding a deduced fold change closer to the true treatment-to-control ratio. The third module performs robust screening using a quality-weighted median with Bootstrap confidence intervals. A candidates-of-interest mechanism improves coverage without compromising accuracy. The modules can be deployed flexibly (paired mode, P_R mode, or standalone third module). We also propose a general group-level diagnostic indicator (GDI) framework. GDI compares pooled and individual estimates and normalizes their discrepancy against a stochastic expectation, making systematic distortion quantifiable. GDI is platform-independent and serves as an independent reliability annotation layer in the TLQ method..

papers.title: Deciphering Charge-Transfer and Triplet-Multiplet Excited States in Substituted MnIII and CrIII Phthalocyanines: Insights from UV-Vis-NIR, MCD, and Theory
papers.abstract: Charge-transfer (metal-to-ligand, MLCT, ligand-to-metal, LMCT, and interligand, (LLCT) and intraligand (π−π* and triplet-multiplet) transitions observed in the UV-vis-NIR and magnetic circular dichroism (MCD) spectra of high-spin Pc tBu Cr III Cl, Pc tBu Mn III Cl, and Pc OBu Mn III Cl (Pc tBu is the dianion of the 2,9(10),16(17),23(24)-tetra-tert-butyl-phthalocyanine and Pc OBu is the dianion of the 1,4,8,11,15,18,22,25-octa-n-butoxy-phthalocyanine) complexes were analyzed with the help of group theory combined with time-dependent density functional theory and ab initio (CASSCF and NEVPT2(13e,14o)) calculations. The energy shift between tert-butylated and butoxylated Pc rings, the energy shift between Mn and Cr centers, and the change in solvent donicity between dichloromethane/chloroform (DCM / CHCl 3 ) and N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) were used to systematically perturb the energies of electronic transitions. It was demonstrated that the triplet-multiplet transitions dominate the NIR region of the UV-vis-NIR and MCD spectra, while LMCT bands dominate the “phthalocyanine window” (350-550 nm) region of the UV-vis-NIR and MCD spectra. Like other trivalent transition-metal phthalocyanines, MLCT transitions were predicted in the UV region of the UV-vis-NIR and MCD spectra. General trends in triplet-multiplet transitions across d 1 -d 9 configurations as well as the function of axial ligands for a given metal are delineated and parameterized. These studies will be used for further understanding of wavelength-dependent photochemical activity and the effects of structural substitutions on electrocatalytic and photocatalytic transformations.

papers.title: N-Phosphoryl Imines Enable Intermolecular Aza Paternò–Büchi Reactions with Unactivated and Activated Alkenes
papers.abstract: Intermolecular aza Paternò–Büchi (aPB) reactions provide a direct and convergent approach to azetidines through the photocycloaddition of imines and alkenes. However, reactions involving unactivated alkenes remain challenging, particularly with acyclic imines, whose excited states are susceptible to rapid nonradiative relaxation and competing photochemical pathways. Here, we report N-phosphinyl imines as readily accessible and stable photoreactive partners for visiblelight-mediated intermolecular aPB reactions with unactivated alkenes. Triplet sensitization using thioxanthone as an inexpensive organic photocatalyst enables productive [2+2]-cycloaddition across a range of alkenes, establishing a new reagent platform for intermolecular aPB chemistry to expand the accessible reactivity of acyclic imines with unactivated alkenes.

papers.title: Carbon dioxide expanded ionic liquid mixtures for changing reaction outcomes and efficient separation
Do topological and quantum-inspired molecularrepresentations add value? Evidence from Africannatural-product-inspired antimalarial chemical space
The CO₂ Concentration Inversion Effect: *CO Generation Rate and *CO C–C Coupling Efficiency as Dual Kinetic Descriptors for Catalyst-Dependent C₂₊ Selectivity in Dilute CO₂ Electroreduction¹
papers.abstract: The electrochemical reduction of dilute CO₂ (5–33% v/v) to multicarbon (C₂₊) products offers a sustainable route to directly utilize industrial exhaust, bypassing energy-intensive CO₂ capture and purification. Our systematic investigations from 2023 to 2026 reveal a counter-intuitive paradigm: under dilute CO2 feed ranging (e.g. from 25% to pure CO2), the C2+ selectivity of copper-based catalysts not only matches but can surpass the pure CO2 baseline. Here, we define the CO₂ Concentration Inversion Effect: a kinetic regime where the FE(C₂₊)/FE(C₁) ratio under dilute CO₂ feed exceeds that under pure CO₂ at identical potentials. This non-monotonic selectivity demonstrates that C₂₊ formation is governed by a catalyst-tunable balance between *CO supply and coupling kinetics. Critically, we introduce two quantitative kinetic descriptors that jointly govern the fate of *CO intermediates: the *CO production rate (the total flux of *CO supplied to the surface) and the C-C coupling efficiency of *CO (the fraction of that *CO consumed by C-C coupling). While the definitions of these descriptors are general, their joint systematic quantification and mechanistic application as a dual-descriptor framework represent a significant advance. We demonstrate that C2+ selectivity is synergistically controlled by both the *CO generation rate and the *CO C-C coupling efficiency, both of which are modulated by applied potential and local reaction environments. In-situ FT-IR spectroscopy and systematic pH-dependent measurements reveal that the coupling efficiency is primarily governed by CO2 concentration rather than bulk pH, although the boundaries of the inversion window (Cmin, Cpeak, Cmax) shift with electrolyte conditions. Notably, we resolve a mechanistic decoupling between microscopic coupling efficiency and macroscopic FE(C2+)/FE(C1) ratios: while coupling efficiency reflects the intrinsic branching ratio of *CO intermediates, the macroscopic selectivity is optimized at an intermediate *CO supply where the absolute flux and suppression of competing C1 pathways dominate. This framework, validated across diverse catalyst families including B-doped Cu, Ag@Cu2O, and Cu(OH)2-derived Cu, establishes five key advances: (i) the explicit definition of coupling efficiency as a quantitative ratio, alongside *CO production rate; (ii) its absolute quantification across CO2 concentrations; (iii) cross-system validation of the dual-descriptor framework; (iv) the elucidation of the decoupling between efficiency and selectivity at high *CO coverage; and (v) their use as design criteria for catalyst optimization. This framework suggests that optimizing the *CO supply-coupling balance at dilute concentrations may offer distinct advantages for carbon upcycling compared to incremental improvements under pure feeds.

papers.title: Active control of crystal nucleation and growth using operando X-ray imaging
An open implementation of MSEVB for reactive force field simulation with simple energy-based coupling
papers.abstract: Chemical reactivity modelling in large systems over extended timescales is computationally and theoretically challenging; ab initio methods are too expensive, while classical force fields cannot handle bond breaking/formation. Existing solutions like reactive force fields require extensive expertise to develop, and machine-learned approaches often need prohibitively large, high-quality datasets for training. These barriers have hindered the modelling of reactive chemical processes. Multi-state empirical valence bond (MSEVB) theory offers an alternative by enabling conventional unreactive force fields to be mixed in a controlled manner to selectively describe chemical reactions. However, existing MSEVB implementations are often field-specific, have license-restricted distribution, or rely on complex parameterisation schemes. This work presents a new open-source, general MSEVB implementation, designed to make reactive modelling more accessible to non-experts. Specifically, the implementation here focused on simple energy-based coupling, thereby eliminating the need for complex geometry-based coupling approaches, significantly lowering the barrier to entry for reactive force field development. This generalised approach is demonstrated to reproduce proton transfer behaviour in Y-doped and undoped BaZrO3, bulk water and liquid imidazole, as well as other forms of reactivity, such as electron migration in LiCoO2. We demonstrate that only two fitted parameters are needed to accurately model symmetric transfer across the three chemically diverse proton-conducting systems studied

papers.title: Hierarchical Dimensionality Evolution of Ionic Transport in Superionic Copper Iodide
papers.abstract: Superionic conductors exhibit liquid-like ion transport within a rigid solid framework enabled by dynamical sublattice decoupling. In copper iodide (CuI), fast ion conduction emerges through structural transitions that reshape the local energy landscape, yet the microscopic evolution of diffusion topology across phase transitions remains insufficiently understood. By integrating machine-learning Molecular Dynamics (MLMD) with lattice dynamics, we elucidate the temperature-dependent ionic transport mechanism in CuI. The superionic transition in CuI manifests as a hierarchical evolution of transport dimensionality, progressing sequentially from localized vibrations to 1D channel transport, 2D in-plane diffusion, and ultimately isotropic 3D migration. This hierarchical evolution is driven by transverse acoustic phonon softening, which modulates migration barriers through direction-selective geometric confinement via a triangular-gate regulation mechanism.

papers.title: Sensitized near-infrared luminescence in sulfur-coordinated lanthanide complexes for machine learning-enhanced thermometry
papers.abstract: Lanthanide (Ln 3+ ) coordination complexes featuring only Ln–S bonds have optical properties uniquely modulated by soft donor atoms. Yet, these complexes and their applications are underexplored, due to the stricter environmental control required for their typical preparation relative to complexes containing Ln–O bonds. Herein, we show that Ln-S coordination is ideally suited to generate information-rich near-infrared (NIR) photoluminescence, laying the optimal ground for machine learning-driven optical sensing. We prepared three new homoleptic complexes with general formula [K(2.2.2-cryptand)][Ln( L ) 4 ] (Ln = Nd 3+ ( 1-Nd ), Gd 3+ ( 1-Gd ), or Yb 3+ ( 1-Yb ); L = 2,6-bis-(4- tert -butylphenyl)phenyldithiocarboxylate). In all complexes, the Ln 3+ ion is dodecahedrally coordinated to eight sulfur atoms, generating a crystal field that deviates from the ideal anisotropic case and leads to substantial mixing of the crystal-field states, as revealed by magnetic measurements and ab initio calculations. Temperature-dependent photoluminescence and optical absorption measurements allowed identifying the electronic transitions and energy transfer mechanisms underpinning the complexes’ optical properties, which are dominated by ligand sensitization of the Ln 3+ emission. Survey of the photoluminescence-vs-temperature (calibration) datasets indicated the amenability of 1-Nd and 1-Yb to luminescence thermometry. Chiefly, the complex spectral variations induced by thermal changes can be comprehensively analyzed via principal component analysis, thus extracting global optical features with readout precision that is one order of magnitude higher than classical, local spectral features. More broadly, this study demonstrates that spectral complexity in molecular systems sets the necessary preconditions for advanced optical sensing supported by machine learning algorithms.

papers.title: MPID Polarizable Force Field: GPU Implementation and Biomolecular Simulations
papers.abstract: The multipole and induced dipole (MPID) model provides a sophisticated description of electrostatics through permanent atomic multipoles up to the octopole level and point induced dipoles, but its high computational cost has limited its routine application to biomolecular simulations. Here, we present a GPU-accelerated implementation of the MPID model in OpenMM. The implementation produces energies and forces fully consistent with those obtained from CHARMM and enables routine microsecond-scale molecular dynamics simulations of explicitly solvated protein systems. Moreover, force field parameters were transferred directly from the Drude oscillator model to the MPID framework without reparameterization, yielding the MPID-2019 protein force field. Tests on five proteins show that MPID-2019 reproduces a range of NMR observables, including scalar couplings and relaxation order parameters. These results demonstrate that MPID-2019 is a valid polarizable force field readily applicable to protein simulations and that the effective equivalence of the induced dipole and Drude oscillator formalisms can be established at the biomolecular level.

papers.title: Nickel-Catalyzed Formal [3+2+2] Cycloadditions of Bis(trimethylsilyl)cyclopropanone withDiynes: A Concise Approach to Functionalized Azulene Derivatives
papers.abstract: consequently, developing efficient methods for their preparation is important. Herein, we report the development of formal [3+2+2] cycloaddition chemistry involving 1,6-diynes and cis-2,3-bis(trimethylsilyl)cyclopropanone as a new synthetic approach to functionalized azulene derivatives. The azulene framework is efficiently constructed using the developed reaction, with synthetically versatile functional groups introduced in a single operation. An unusual rearrangement process consistent with a formal [1,7]-silyl migration from the C7 to C6 position of the azulene framework was observed during the course of the transformation. The synthetic utility of the method was demonstrated by further transforming the resulting silylated azulene derivatives into a variety of 1functionalized azulenes. This study provides a new strategy for constructing and functionalizing azulene skeletons as well as new insight into the reactivities of cyclopropanone-derived intermediates.

papers.title: Fully bio-based precursor for photocurable networks: synthesis and photopolymerization of furan-vegetable oil derivative
papers.abstract: The development of fully bio-based photocurable resins represents a promising sustainable alternative to conventional petroleum-derived materials. In this study, novel furan-based macromonomers were synthesized via a two-step synthetic route. The first step involved the transesterification of dimethyl 2,5-furandicarboxylate (DMFDCA) with dilinoleic diol (DD) using various catalysts, followed by methacrylation with methacryloyl chloride to introduce terminal vinyl functionalities. The chemical structures of the intermediates and final macromonomers were confirmed by 1 H NMR and FT-IR spectroscopy. Rheological characterization was conducted to evaluate flow behavior and processability. Thermal properties and phase behavior were investigated by differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), revealing an amorphous and flexible polymer architecture with thermally induced crosslinking at elevated temperatures. Photopolymerization kinetics were analyzed using photo-DSC with different type-I photoinitiators under controlled UV irradiation conditions, while network formation was further evaluated through gel fraction analysis of photocured samples prepared under ambient conditions. Additionally, cytocompatibility studies were performed to assess the potential suitability of the materials for biomedical applications. Overall, this systematic investigation provides valuable insights into the design and synthesis of renewable, photocurable furan-based materials for advanced biomedical applications and sustainable manufacturing.

papers.title: CO2 Electrosorption: Electric Field Effect on the Metal–CO2 Interfacial Dipole
papers.abstract: CO2 electrosorption at metal electrodes is a critical step controlling the subsequent electrochemical reduction process, yet its physicochemical origin remains debated. The field-induced stabilization of adsorbed CO2 – the field effect − is commonly attributed to the interaction between the applied electric field and the adsorption-induced molecular dipole of CO2 . In this study, we employ density functional theory with an applied electric field to re-examine this paradigm by studying CO2 electrosorption on (111) surfaces of Ag, Au, Cu, Ir, Pb, and Pt. We show an electric-field-driven transition between physisorbed and chemisorbed CO2 . Physisorption preserves a near-linear geometry with negligible charge transfer and weak field dependence, whereas chemisorption involves pronounced bending and substantial electron transfer from the metal. Collectively, we demonstrate that the field effect arises from the interaction between the electric field and the interfacial metal–CO2 dipole formed upon charge transfer, rather than the molecular CO2 dipole alone, as conventionally assumed.

papers.title: Accessing room-temperature phosphorescence via a modular quinoline-amine scaffold
papers.abstract: Cinchona alkaloids have played an important part in the history of fluorescence studies and the recent discovery of their long-lived emission makes them a useful tool for exploring new applications in labelling and tagging. Furthermore, they are excellent model systems for exploring the fundamental nature of charge transfer due to the through-space charge transfer between the nitrogen atom on the cage and the quinoline aryl group. However, the synthetic routes and pathways to modification are cumbersome and new synthetic routes are required. Here we demonstrate new synthetic pathways to create a wide range of unnatural quinine analogues giving control over the chromophore point of attachment and N-aryl distance. Furthermore the molecules demonstrate long-lived emission confirming that we are capturing some of the novel photophysical properties of their natural analogues.

papers.title: Hydrogenation of C–C Multiple Bonds with Simple Calcium Salts
papers.abstract: Hydrogenation is among the most widely used transformations in chemical synthesis, yet it typically relies on precious transition-metal catalysts, pressurised hydrogen gas and an excess of solvents. Here we report a solvent-free, transition-metal-free hydrogenation method based on mixtures of simple, commercially available calcium salts (CaH 2 with Ca(OH) 2 or CaCO 3 ). Under mechanochemical conditions, calcium hydride reacts with calcium hydroxide or carbonate to generate H 2 in situ, eliminating the need for an external hydrogen source. The system efficiently hydrogenates alkenes, alkynes and aromatic hydrocarbons, including tetrasubstituted alkenes and benzene. Mechanistic studies support reversible hydrocalciation at the calcium hydride surface followed by irreversible hydrogenolysis with in situ generated H 2 . The method was demonstrated to be general, with the hydrogenation of 16 examples proceeding with an average of 74% yield, providing a safe, cheap and practical alternative to transition metal-catalysed hydrogenation of carbon-carbon multiple bonds.

papers.title: Dinuclear Gold Photocatalyzed Atom-Transfer σ-Bond Metathesis and Sequential Heck-type Coupling
papers.abstract: A dinuclear gold photocatalytic approach for strain-release σ-bond metathesis has been developed by combining inner-sphere electron transfer (ISET) and radical ligand transfer (RLT) mechanisms. This strategy facilitates atom-transfer reactions via C–I bond cleavage, radical translocation, and ligand transfer, yielding a wide range of spirocyclobutyl oxindoles with excellent substrate diversity and atom economy. Additionally, the produced C(sp 3 )–I bond functions as a versatile handle for selective Heck-type coupling with alkenes. Mechanistic investigations indicate a combined ISET-RLT pathway, where sequential excitation and excited-state aurophilic interactions between high-valent gold centers weaken the Au–I bond and enable ligand transfer. Gramscale synthesis and further derivatizations highlight the synthetic utility of this methodology.

papers.title: Accurate modeling of ion-protein binding in solution: molecular mechanics force field innovation and validation on Mg2+
papers.abstract: Multivalent ions bind to proteins to control many biological processes. Molecular simulations can effectively supplement experiments to resolve underlying mechanisms, but suffer from reliability and feasibility issues in describing ion-protein binding in the condensed phase. Here we present a molecular mechanics based generalizable solution to this long-standing challenge. Using the divalent Mg 2+ as a model, we demonstrate that our approach yields unprecedented accuracy in describing its binding to proteins in solution – compared to high level quantum mechanics, the mean error in local interaction energies is 0.5%, and the binding modes and binding free energies match experiment. Our study also shows that key to achieving this accuracy requires a delicate balance between the large repulsive and attractive forces at short distances near ions for which explicit modeling of polarization is essential. Overall, our work lays foundation for future development of molecular simulation methods for ions and opens the way to quantitatively study Mg-dependent mechanisms in hundreds of enzymes and proteins.

papers.title: Hierarchical Encoding of Digital Data on DNA Origami Nanostructures with Topological Barcodes
papers.abstract: DNA data storage has emerged as a promising route to managing the exponential growth in global data production. While sequence-based DNA data storage offers unprecedented storage densities, the high costs of DNA synthesis make it prohibitively expensive. As a more cost-efficient alternative, data can be stored in DNA origami nanostructures (DONs), which however comes with the disadvantage of dramatically reduced data densities.
