This work aims to increase the amount of data that can be stored in one DON sample by introducing topological barcodes to identify different data subsets by atomic force microscopy (AFM). Two barcoding approaches are compared based on either different DON shapes or a single shape with different notches that are generated by omitting groups of edge staples. Although the correct identification of barcodes is more difficult for the notch designs than for the DON shapes, the notch-based barcoding approach achieves more consistent and reliable data readout. At the same time, the notch-based barcoding approach is substantially more cost-efficient as it uses only a single set of staples, whereas the shape-based approach requires one staple set for each DON shape. Notch-based topographic barcodes thus represent a viable, low-cost approach for indexing data subsets in DON-based data storage.

papers.title: Hybrid Physics–Diagnostic Estimation of Liquid Loading for Wet-Gas Flowmeter Correction: A Model-Based Uncertainty Framework
papers.abstract: The established wet-gas corrections express the indicated gas rate as the true rate multiplied by an over-reading factor that depends on the Lockhart–Martinelli parameter. At most production metering stations that parameter is not measured, so the correction cannot be closed from the meter signal alone. This paper treats liquid loading as a latent variable to be estimated rather than treating the over-reading as a quantity to be learned. A thermodynamic prediction from composition, pressure and temperature is combined with a structurally distinct estimate from flowmeter diagnostic signals already transmitted at the station, and their disagreement is quantified by an estimator consistency index governing whether the correction is applied. The study is computational: no wet-gas loop data were used, the diagnostic estimator is specified but not fitted, and every figure below is a modeled uncertainty rather than a measured accuracy. In a Monte Carlo study of 300,000 simulated realizations over a rich-gas envelope (60–85 kg/cm2, 30–60 °C), three results follow. Inverse-variance fusion degrades the estimate unless the thermodynamic estimator declares an allowance for upstream carryover it cannot observe; with that allowance and an asymmetric weighting, the simulated 95% band falls from ±5.45% to ±4.28%. The consistency index is a specific detector of that failure mode: carryover occurs in 25% of realizations but in 94% of those rejected. Because the two estimates are not statistically independent, the covariance term must be retained in the index; omitting it progressively disables the acceptance test. A falsifiable experimental protocol is specified.

papers.title: Comparative Characterization of Nitrogen–Nitrogen Bond-Forming Piperazate Synthases to Improve Activity and Precision
papers.abstract: Piperazate synthases (PZSs) have recently gained attention as enzymes that catalyze the formation of nitrogen-nitrogen bonds, offering a sustainable alternative to traditional synthesis of substituted hydrazines. Although progress has been made in elucidating their structure and mechanism, an exhaustive study characterizing multiple PZSs regarding their activity or tendency toward side reactions under varying conditions has yet to be conducted. In this study, we profiled the activity of eight purified PZSs under 80 different conditions each, covering pH, buffers, salinity, temperature dependence, and thermal stability, using automated liquid handling and a colorimetric substrate consumption assay. We also performed kinetic and structural analysis of the two most promising PZSs and used LC-MS to quantitatively investigate the substrate scope and side reactions. Among the investigated enzymes, we identified two highly active synthases, SbPZS from Streptomyces sp. B93 and SgPZS from Streptomyces griseochromogenes. Both enzymes tolerated a broad range of reaction conditions, but differed in their side-product formation rates. We found this tendency to be sequence-dependent and controlled by pH. These findings provide detailed information regarding the in vitro applicability of PZSs and will improve their use in (chemo-)enzymatic cascades for synthesizing pharmaceutical building blocks.

papers.title: Failure-Mode-Driven Methodology to Unravel Interfacial Chemical Bonding in Laser-Welded Polyamide-6.6–Titanium Interfaces
papers.abstract: The demand for hybrid polymer-metal assemblies is growing worldwide, addressing challenges in fields such as biomedical implants. Among assembling techniques, laser welding is gaining attention for its quick processing, minimal pretreatment, high design freedom, and reproducibility. While these assemblies show strong mechanical resistance, understanding the root causes of adhesion—particularly potential chemical bonds at the interface—remains challenging, especially for thick assemblies. Previous work suggests breaking assemblies and dissolving the remaining polymer on the metallic surface to access the interface, an approach effective for cohesive failure modes. Here, we explore assemblies with mixed or adhesive failure modes using this breaking-and-dissolving combination. Results suggest that the methodology for accessing interfaces should be adapted to the assembly's failure mode: breaking and dissolving for cohesive failure, but breaking alone for mixed or adhesive failure. Both approaches were tested on laser-welded thick polyamide-6.6/titanium assemblies exhibiting a mixed failure mode. Interfaces were analyzed using XPS and ToF-SIMS. The methodology successfully provided access to interfacial molecular information, supporting previous findings that show the formation of a C-O-Ti bond at the interface resulting from laser welding.

papers.title: There is Room in the Middle: Unidirectional Energy Transfer in Plasmonic Nanohybrids through Intermediate Coherence
papers.abstract: Plasmon-induced resonance energy transfer (PIRET) is less well-known than hot carrier and polaritonic photocatalysis. The small dipole moment of individual excitons means donors and acceptors are weakly coupled in molecular energy transfer, so it is considered not efficient as hot carrier photocatalysis. And unlike the detailed quantum descriptions for polaritons in vibrational and electronic strong coupling, there is not a clear mechanistic model for PIRET. Here, we establish the underlying mechanism of PIRET and show energy transfer efficiencies of up to 75%. Gold nanorod (AuNR)-methylene blue polymer nanohybrids with identical plasmon resonance energies but with systematically varied core sizes enable direct comparison of the competing roles of oscillator strength and dephasing. Operando single-particle spectroelectrochemistry is used to quantify PIRET efficiencies. Open-quantum and classical electrodynamics simulations reveal that smaller AuNRs have an advantage because they combine stronger eigenmode-normalized local coupling with slower plasmon dephasing. PIRET efficiency increases from 30% to 75% with optimized AuNR sizes. The unique oscillator properties of AuNRs establish intermediate coherence, between more familiar weakly and strongly coupled regimes, as an effective route to unidirectional plasmon-to-exciton transfer. Intermediate coherence is a kinetic gate for PIRET, creating an efficient way to transform light into chemical degrees of freedom through which further photocatalysis is possible.

papers.title: A Molecular Generation–Validation Workflow Combining Reversible Junction Tree Reinforcement Learning and Semi-empirical Quantum Chemistry: A Case Study on Molecular Solar Thermal Fuels
papers.abstract: Molecular generative models can rapidly explore chemical space, but conventional metrics alone do not establish whether proposed structures possess application-relevant physical properties. To address this limitation, we developed an integrated generationvalidation framework coupling Reversible Junction Tree Reinforcement Learning (RJT- RL) with automated density-functional tight-binding (DFTB) evaluation. Azobenzenebased molecular solar thermal fuels served as a representative case study. RJT-RL was guided by maximum Tanimoto similarity to a reference dataset, while reference and generated molecules were evaluated under identical DFTB calculation conditions to obtain the energy difference between the cis and trans isomers (∆ E iso ) and the S 0 → S 1 excitation energy (∆ E ex ). As training progressed, the ∆ E iso distribution extended toward higher values, while ∆ E ex values were more concentrated within the visible-light window, yielding candidates within the selected joint screening region, although neither descriptor was included in the reward. These results show that automated semi-empirical post-generation validation can identify candidates with targeted property combinations and reveal information beyond conventional molecular generation metrics.

papers.title: From Fluorine Substructures to Compound Identities: Bayesian Analysis of Multidescriptor 19F NMR Measurements in Multiple Solvents
papers.abstract: Targeted liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry quantifies only a few dozen fluorinated analytes and requires an authentic standard for each, so most of the organofluorine in environmental extracts is never assigned to a structure. Fluorine-19 NMR is an attractive complement because every fluorine nucleus responds independently of ionization and in proportion to its abundance, but existing 19 F libraries record chemical shift alone, in inconsistent solvents, and without the statistical search tools needed for 25 identification. Here we report a 19 F NMR spectral library of 163 fluorinated compounds—PFAS, pesticides, pharmaceuticals, and other fluorinated species—measured under three defined solvent conditions and annotated at the level of the individual fluorine nucleus with chemical shift, scalar coupling, multiplicity, and transverse relaxation time. We introduce the solvent-induced shift vector (SISV), the change in chemical shift of a resonance between solvent systems, as a descriptor that discriminates local fluorine environments that a single-solvent shift cannot resolve. Annotated resonances are mapped onto HOSE substructure codes and searched with a Bayesian framework that reports a likelihood ratio for each candidate structure together with an explicit ambiguity count, so that evidence strength and identification specificity are reported separately. Validation against synthetic mixtures establishes which descriptors contribute discriminating information and where the spectrum supports only a substructure class; application to an industrial wastewater extract demonstrates candidate prioritization under realistic, nonideal matrix conditions.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Dopant Discovery toward Air-Stable Sulfide Solid-State Electrolytes
papers.abstract: Sulfide solid-state electrolytes (SSEs) are highly promising candidates for all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs), but the severe degradation triggered by moisture exposure remains a major obstacle to their large-scale application. Despite compositional doping could effectively enhance the air stability, there is currently no relevant screening strategy to support the efficient exploration of dopants. Herein, we develop an artificial intelligence-assisted dopant screening platform for air-stable sulfide SSEs (LPSC). Retrieval-augmented system combined with large language model could effectively prescreen the dopants that enhance both the ionic conductivity, and interfacial compatibility of the electrolyte. More importantly, the impact of dopants on the air stability of electrolytes was quantified by the minimum Gibbs free energy change () of the hydrolysis reaction, which could be predicted by a composition-based machine learning model. Guided by this strategy, several promising dopants, including BiF3, CoF3, InF3, and SnF4 were successfully identified. As a proof of concept, LPSC-BiF3 electrolyte demonstrates superior air stability, delivering a high ionic conductivity retention of 91% after exposure to air with 10% RH for 6 h. Consequently, the exposed LPSC-BiF3 electrolyte enabled excellent cycling stability in Li-In||NCM811 full cells. The proposed screening strategy significantly promotes the exploration of high-performance dopants for air-stable sulfide SSEs.

papers.title: Enhancing Aromatics Production in Zeolite-Catalyzed Lignin Pyrolysis by Establishing Structure-Acidity-Performance Relationships
papers.abstract: Selective pyrolysis of lignin into aromatics remains a major challenge due to its high oxygen content and structural complexity. Solid acid catalysts, like zeolites, are well known as effective catalysts for pyrolysis processes. However, the role of acid site density and strength in controlling aromatic yields in lignin pyrolysis remains insufficiently understood. Here, three zeolite framework topologies, namely FAU, MFI, and BEA, with distinct acidity profiles were systematically evaluated for lignin pyrolysis to disentangle zeolite framework topology and acidity effects. Significant variations in bio-oil and non-oxygenated aromatics (benzene, toluene, xylene (BTXs), and napthalenes) yields demonstrated that framework topology-dependent acid site strength plays a more dominant role than acid site density (bulk/external) in enhancing aromatics yield. Thermogravimetric analysis revealed that primary lignin depolymerization is not responsible for the product distribution variations observed. Instead, secondary reactions of oxygenated lignin fragments with acid sites dictate the overall deoxygenation performance. H-ZSM-5 exhibited the highest aromatics yields (100–132 mg g-1lignin), followed by H-Beta (35–52 mg g-1 lignin) and H-Y (8–22 mg g-1 lignin) zeolites. These values correspond to 4 to 16 % of theoretical maximum BTXs ring utilization efficiency (RUE), a benchmark that we propose to evaluate catalyst efficiency in lignin pyrolysis, defined as the ratio of experimentally obtained BTXs to the theoretical maximum based on phenylpropanoid units (C9) in lignin. Regeneration studies revealed gradual catalyst deactivation due to the conversion of strong acid sites (SAS) to intermediate acid sites (IAS) resulting in lower BTXs RUE per cycle. Overall, this work highlights the role of zeolite framework topology-driven confinement effects in controlling the acid site strength and thereby, governing lignin pyrolysis performance.

papers.title: Nucleation of Condensates and Voids: A Generalised Critical Cluster Equivalence Principle for Phase Separation in Liquid Mixtures
papers.abstract: The assembly, number density, and size distribution of biomolecular condensates are central to their biological functions, but the nucleation kinetics that precede growth and coalescence remain difficult to characterise experimentally and in simulations. In this work, we develop a theoretical framework to apply the critical cluster equivalence principle (CEP), which builds on the thermodynamic equivalence between stable clusters in confined systems and critical clusters in open systems, to multicomponent liquids undergoing phase separation into solvent-and solute-rich phases. We first test the proposed approach in a symmetric Lennard-Jones mixture, where nucleation rates agree with large-scale Yasuoka–Matsumoto simulations and the predicted critical cluster sizes match independent seeding results. We then use the validated approach to investigate a homopolymeric chainsolvent system, introducing concepts intrinsic to biomolecular condensates such as chain rigidity and connectivity. Here, the CEP predicts the coexistence composition and interfacial tension for both the forward nucleation of dense condensates and the reverse formation of dilute voids, indicating that the curvature dependence is consistent in both directions, thereby uncovering a forward/reverse relationship that has primarily been studied for single-component droplets and bubbles, now demonstrated for a compositionally mixed liquid phase separation. Overall, the CEP-based workflow employs smaller systems and shorter simulations than conventional nucleation methods. These findings indicate a comprehensive methodology for quantitatively examining biomolecular condensate nucleation in explicit solvent.

papers.title: Predicting spatiotemporal coke growth in an industrial ethane cracker with a hybrid mechanistic–neural surrogate of its plant-tuned SPYRO model
papers.abstract: Coke accumulation on radiant coils sets the run length of steam-cracking furnaces, yet the thickness field cannot be measured in service, and rigorous simulators are proprietary and non-differentiable. We introduce a grey-box surrogate of a plant-calibrated SPYRO model for an industrial ethane cracker, forecasting the complete coke field across 52 axial segments over a 90-day run. It learns the coking rate as an explicit Arrhenius core modulated by a positive neural component and coke self-feedback, integrated over time to inherently ensure monotonic growth. On six held-out cases outside the training window in at least two operating variables, it reaches 0.034 ± 0.001 mm mean absolute error (R² = 0.9994, five seeds) with zero monotonicity violations; ablations show the guarantee costs no accuracy. Plant infrared data reproduce the encoded temperature trend. We close with limitations (unidentifiable embedded kinetics, narrow validity window, exogenous wall temperature) and demonstrate an online-estimator deployment using the analytic Jacobian.

papers.title: Excitation-Energy Accuracy Does Not Guarantee Observable Fidelity: Rethinking Validation of Excited-State Quantum Algorithms
papers.abstract: Excitation-energy accuracy is currently the dominant validation criterion for excited-state quantum algorithms. We show that this practice can conceal severe failures in physically relevant observables. Using quantum equation-of-motion (qEOM) as a representative case study, we demonstrate that excitation-energy accuracy and observable accuracy can become effectively decoupled. While both qEOM and Quantum Subspace Expansion (QSE) yield highly accurate excitation energies, their predictions for dipole moments differ dramatically, establishing observable fidelity as an independent benchmark dimension that cannot be inferred from energy agreement alone. To investigate the origin of this discrepancy, we introduce anti-Hermitized qEOM (AqEOM), an a posteriori anti-Hermitian transformation applied to the qEOM-derived state-transfer operator before direct property evaluation. Across multiple systems, AqEOM substantially improves dipole moments, state-overlap diagnostics, and reduced density matrix-based observables while leaving the underlying excitation-energy description essentially unchanged. These results demonstrate that excitation-energy accuracy does not guarantee observable accuracy and that energy-only validation can overlook significant failures in physically relevant properties. AqEOM provides a concrete mechanistic demonstration of this principle, highlighting observable fidelity as an independent benchmark dimension for excited-state quantum algorithms.

papers.title: Nanovehicles Equipped with Triptycene-Fused Unidirectional Light-Driven Molecular Motors
papers.abstract: The integration of molecular motors into increasingly complex functional architectures while preserving their dynamic behavior represents an important challenge in the development of molecular machinery. Herein, we report a modular synthetic platform for motorized nanovehicles based on a triptycene-fused overcrowded alkene molecular motor, orthogonal axles, trimethyladamantane-based wheels, and an optional flagellum-like appendage. Three nanovehicle architectures of increasing structural complexity were assembled using a convergent synthetic strategy. The photochemical and thermal behavior of the parent molecular motor was investigated by NMR and UV–vis spectroscopy, supported by X-ray crystallography and density functional theory calculations, and shown to proceed through a unidirectional four-stage rotary cycle. Importantly, the characteristic photoisomerization and thermal helix inversion processes were retained after incorporation of the motor into the nanovehicle framework. Furthermore, selected nanovehicle was immobilized on gold surfaces, where differential UV–vis spectroscopy demonstrated preservation of the photochemical and thermal responses observed in solution. The close correspondence between solution-phase and surface-confined behavior indicates effective decoupling of the motor unit from the metallic substrate by the trimethyladamantane wheels. These results establish a versatile platform for the construction of motorized nanovehicles and provide a foundation for future studies of molecular machines operating at interfaces.

papers.title: Hyperlocal PM2.5 Exposure and Health Burden Disparities Revealed by a Taxi-Based Mobile Monitoring Platform in Shenzhen
papers.abstract: Although fine particles (PM 2.5 ) concentrations in China have declined over the past decade, exposure disparities persist at hyperlocal scales. We conducted a six-month mobile monitoring campaign in Shenzhen, where four taxis with calibrated low-cost sensors gathered 24.6 million 1 Hz measurements (~3,700 hours) across 550 km² and 7.3 million residents. We developed a novel application of a multi-source XGBoost (MS-XGB) framework that integrates mobile and fixed-site station data to reconstruct a road-network PM 2.5 dataset at 30 m × 1 h resolution, filling 98% of missing observations. Validation demonstrates strong agreement with both mobile observations (R 2 = 0.97) and data from fixed regulatory monitoring stations (Pearson r = 0.82). We used the road-network dataset to generate a 100 m × 100 m population grid exposure map and benchmarked it against two conventional exposure assessment approaches that rely solely on fixed-site regulatory stations. Relative to MS-XGB, conventional methods systematically underestimated long-term PM 2.5 exposure, with grid-level differences of up to 15 μg/m³. Population-weighted mean exposure was higher in urban villages (16.51 µg/m³) than in other urban areas (14.41 µg/m³), with hotspots 52.5% more likely to occur in urban villages. In Longhua, high exposure was concentrated specifically in urban villages, indicating that district-level averages can mask substantial intra-district heterogeneity. In Nanshan, 40% of elderly residents live in high-exposure areas, compared with 34% of children aged 0–14 and 33% of adults aged 15–59, suggesting that older adults bear a disproportionate exposure burden and face elevated health risks. Our findings demonstrate that mobile-monitoring-based hyperlocal exposure assessment is essential for revealing true PM 2.5 exposure inequalities across population groups and spatial environments that are overlooked by conventional fixed-site approaches.

papers.title: Uni-Macro-FRPN: Full-Resolution and Cross-Scale Learning for Polymers
papers.abstract: Polymer properties are governed by interactions across scales. Existing polymer models commonly retain either monomer chemistry without the polymer graph, or the polymer graph with simplified monomer chemistry. Here, we present Uni-Macro-FRPN (FRPN), a Full-Resolution Polymer Network unifying atom-level and within-monomer structural encoding with an explicit monomer-instance graph of a polymer chain. Its two Transformers jointly learn atom-informed monomer semantics, sequence order, and chain topology. Using BigSMILES to construct monomer semantics and polymer graphs, FRPN achieves 86.4% accuracy and 90.6% ROC–AUC on Block Copolymer Database (BCDB) lamellar-versus-non-lamellar classification, outperforming the evaluated baselines and supporting joint reasoning over monomer semantics and chain structure. Ablation results support a contribution from joint representation beyond the tested increases in parameter count. On the linear homopolymer benchmark, monomer-centric learning remains competitive, identifying a boundary case in which polymer-scale organization is relatively simple. In addition, existing models are primarily developed around linear polymers. To test whether this full-chain representation generalizes beyond linear polymers, we construct an all-atom moleculardynamics (MD) benchmark of 1640 datapoints spanning diverse monomer chemistries, sequence orderings, chain topologies, and physical properties. FRPN achieves the strongest overall performance on this topology-rich benchmark, and the accompanying diagnostics suggest a benefit from jointly modeling monomer chemistry and polymer structure within one architecture. Taken together, FRPN provides a practical route for moving polymer representation learning beyond SMILESbased descriptions by using BigSMILES to connect monomer semantics with explicit polymer-chain topology, and establishes a foundation for full-chain, cross-scale polymer modeling. Its leading overall performance among the evaluated models on both the real-world BCDB benchmark and the topology-rich MD benchmark further suggests a promising direction for polymer informatics: future polymer prediction models should treat polymers not only as collections of monomer descriptors, but as complete multiscale chemical and topological objects.

papers.title: Glycan-binding agglutination assays reveal key binding epitope of unknown lectins in Acinetobacter baumannii
papers.abstract: Acinetobacter baumannii infections are associated with high mortality rates and an even higher prevalence of antimicrobial resistance. Understanding the lectin-glycan interactions mediating A. baumannii adhesion to cells will facilitate their exploitation in strategies to develop improved approaches to diagnosis and treatment. In this work, we use an established low-cost glycan-based agglutination assay to undertake a systematic structure-activity relationship screen of glycan ligands, and identify selective adhesion to α-GalNAc that is dependent upon both stereochemistry and presentation. Our work demonstrates how this approach can rapidly identify glycan motifs important to adhesion of understudied pathogens such as A. baumannii, information that is both therapeutically exploitable and furthers understanding of bacterial virulence.

papers.title: What survives? Semantic eligibility, distribution shift and metric interpretation in external validation of ADMET predictors
papers.abstract: Machine-learning models for absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion and toxicity (ADMET) are usually reported on benchmark splits drawn from the same curated collections used to train them. External validation is rarer, and when it is attempted, the assumption that a public dataset carrying a matching endpoint name is a valid comparator for a model output is seldom examined. We applied a pre-specified, fail-closed semantic eligibility screen — ten declared gates covering biological endpoint, matrix, species, assay family, measurement direction, result semantics, units, transformation, classification threshold and positive class — to twelve candidate pairings between three public experimental datasets and the outputs of ADMET-AI 2.0.1. The screen was executed before any metric was computed. Three pairings were accepted; nine were rejected, each with a recorded reason, and no classification endpoint qualified. On the three accepted pairings, after excluding exact structure overlap with the endpoint training source and with the reconstructed regression multitask universe, performance was poor to moderate: human liver microsomal clearance R² = −0.156 (95% CI −0.217 to −0.108; n = 366), logD at pH 7.4 R² = 0.368 (0.261 to 0.456; n = 474), and human plasma protein binding R² = 0.642 (0.543 to 0.732; n = 178). The model nevertheless outperformed both a training-set-mean baseline and a 1-nearest-neighbour Morgan/Tanimoto baseline on every accepted endpoint, including microsomal clearance, where the mean baseline gave R² = −0.270 and the nearest-neighbour baseline R² = −0.278. Two mechanisms accounted for the pattern. Label-distribution shift between the reconstructed training labels and the external labels was severe for clearance (Kolmogorov–Smirnov D = 0.446) and mild for logD (D = 0.095). Prediction-range compression was extreme for clearance, where predictions had 9% of the observed standard deviation and a calibration slope of 0.037, and moderate for logD (0.781; slope 0.545) and plasma protein binding (0.725; slope 0.599). Chemical novelty explained little (Spearman ρ between maximum training similarity and absolute error, −0.13 to −0.28). Conclusions were unchanged by structure-level aggregation, a structure-clustered bootstrap, restriction to stereochemically unambiguous records, and the inclusion of low-clearance measurements that the original benchmark had excluded before inference. We conclude that assay semantics must be screened before external metrics are computed, and that under strong label-distribution shift R² alone misrepresents model utility; rank correlation, bias, calibration slope and baseline-relative performance should be reported alongside it.

papers.title: Bio-Based Levoglucosenone Enables Regioisomer-Driven Inversion of Optical Activity in Polymers via Stereoselective Thia-Michael Addition of 1,2- and 1,3-Benzenedithiols
papers.abstract: Levoglucosenone (LGO), a biobased platform molecule derived from cellulose waste, offers a versatile scaffold owing to its cyclic acetal bridge and reactive enone functionalities. Building on our previous work on stereoselective polymer formation from LGO, this study explores the incorporation of regioisomeric benzenedithiols (1,3- and 1,2-) via thia-Michael addition to afford structurally defined LGO-based monomers. These monomers were subsequently polycondensed with dicarboxylic dihydrazides to yield degradable polyhydrazones with well-defined stereochemistry. Notably, the regioisomeric structure of benzenedithiols induces a striking inversion of optical activity in the resulting polymers, demonstrating that the sign of the optical rotation can be controlled through monomer connectivity. This finding highlights a new strategy for tuning polymer properties from a single bio-based building block. The physicochemical, thermal, optical, and aqueous degradation properties of the resulting polymers were comprehensively characterized. In addition, the synthetic procedures have been optimized to improve sustainability by replacing hazardous solvents with greener alternatives.

papers.title: Processing–structure–property relationships of Y2O3- and ZnO-modified MgO–Al2O3–SiO2 glasses for high-modulus fiber drawing
papers.abstract: Magnesium aluminosilicate (MAS) glasses are attractive candidates for high-modulus (HM) reinforcing fibres but are prone to crystallisation, which restricts the usable forming window. Four MAS compositions modified with Y2O3 (T9, V9) or a combined Y 2 O 3 /ZnO addition (T10, V10) were investigated on a single experimental platform to define the window for crystallisation-free fibre drawing. Two base glasses were compared: an MgO-rich, Al 2 O 3 -lean variant (T series) and an Al 2 O 3 -rich, MgO-lean variant (V series). Compositions were verified by ICP-OES/MS, and characterised by dilatometry, DSC, rotational viscometry with Vogel–Fulcher–Tammann fits, gradient-furnace liquidus measurement and X-ray diffraction. The V series shows a glass transition 30–40 K above the T series and a 20 % lower thermal expansion coefficient. Substituting half of the Y 2 O 3 by ZnO lowers the glass transition by 13–30 K and raises the liquidus of the Al 2 O 3 -rich base from 1311 to 1340 °C. The DSC crystallisation onset lies a near-constant 33–37 K above the glass transition across all four glasses, indicating a kinetic barrier set by the MAS network rather than by the modifiers. All four were drawn into fully amorphous continuous fibres from nozzle temperatures only 40–69 K above their liquidus, and remain calorimetrically indistinguishable from the parent glass; V10, drawn 40 K above the highest liquidus, is the most stringent case. Crystallisation-free forming is therefore controlled by the rapid quench inherent to filament drawing rather than by a positive thermodynamic margin. The results support Y 2 O 3 -rich, Al 2 O 3 -rich compositions for HM-MAS fibre scale-up.

papers.title: Polymer-Assisted One-Dimensional Dissolution in N‑Methylformamide Unlocks Highly Ordered Hybrid Bragg-Stack Clay-Poly(Ethylene Glycol) Oxygen Barriers
papers.abstract: One-dimensional (1D) dissolution is a gentle and thermodynamically driven process that enables the spontaneous and utter delamination of layered materials into nematic suspensions of individual high aspect ratio nanosheets. This process is primarily known and extensively explored for aqueous systems. Examples of 1D dissolution in organic solvents are scarce and require selected organocations or complexation of the interlayer cation. This work demonstrates synergistic delamination of synthetic sodium fluorohectorite (NaHec; Na0.5inter [Li0.5Mg2.5]oct <Si4>tet O10F2) in N-methylformamide (NMF) using poly (ethylene glycol) (PEG), which concomitantly acts as a complexing agent driving delamination and as the polymer matrix for a composite. Upon spray coating, the polymer is directly incorporated into a highly ordered hybrid Bragg-stack nanocomposite. The performance as a gas barrier was investigated for a range of PEG chain lengths [MW = 200, 400, 1500, 10000 g mol-1] using O2‑transmission rate measurements. With increasing MW, substantially reduced oxygen permeabilities (23°C, 75% r.h.) were observed, reaching values as low as 0.029 cm3 µm m‑2 d‑1 bar‑1, demonstrating the power of non-aqueous preparation of NaHec-PEG hybrid Bragg-stack nanocomposites.

papers.title: Coverages and Configurations of CO* and H* on Pt(111) under Realistic Reaction Conditions
papers.abstract: Lateral interactions between co–adsorbed species can produce non-random spatial organization that governs the availability of reactive motifs relevant to catalytic behavior. For CO* and H* co–adsorbed on Pt(111), these interactions determine how the two species distribute across the surface and therefore which local CO*–H* configurations are available under reaction conditions. In this work, we combine density functional theory, cluster expansions, and grand canonical Monte Carlo simulations to determine how CO* and H* organize on Pt(111), and subsequently use electronic surface charge as a controlled perturbation to examine how this organization responds to changes in the underlying energetics. On neutral Pt(111), CO*–H* first-nearest-neighbor interactions are strongly repulsive (0.42 eV), CO*–CO* first-nearest-neighbor interactions are moderately repulsive (0.12 eV), and H*–H* interactions are comparatively weak. These interactions cause CO* to nucleate into islands that grow and coalesce with increasing CO* coverage, while H* preferentially occupies regions outside CO*-rich domains. Consequently, the abundance of CO*–H* nearest-neighbor configurations varies non-monotonically with CO* coverage, reaching a maximum at intermediate coverage before decreasing as CO* islands grow and the adsorbates become increasingly segregated. Positive surface charge strengthens CO* adsorption but also increases CO*–CO* repulsion, producing higher CO* coverages, a broader distribution of CO* island sizes, and larger low-coverage regions between islands where H* can adsorb away from CO*. This suppresses CO*–H* nearest-neighbor configurations relative to the neutral surface. Negative charging weakens CO* adsorption, producing lower CO* coverages, higher H* coverages, and less consolidated CO* islands, thereby increasing the prevalence of mixed CO*–H* local environments. At intermediate CO* coverage, CO* islands enter a regime of accelerated growth and coalescence that coincides with a shallow plateau in H* coverage. This coincidence suggests that the onset of CO* island coalescence is accompanied by a reorganization of the co-adsorbed layer. Further, it illustrates the strong influence of lateral interactions on the formation of potentially reactive motifs, highlighting how they become influential in determining catalytic reactivity.

papers.title: Morita-Baylis-Hillman Allyl-Aryl Sulfoxides for the Dual Functionalization of Indoles via Interrupted Pummerer Rearrangement: Unlocking its Anticancer Potential
papers.abstract: Employing Morita-Baylis-Hillman derived trisubstituted allyl aryl sulfoxides for a one-step dual vicinal functionalisation of indoles for the first time towards the synthesis of 3-aryl-thio-2-allyl indoles. The reaction proceeds via sulfoxide activation, nucleophilic attack of indole and a charge-accelerated [3,3]sigmatropic rearrangement. Selected compounds from the synthesized library showed significant anticancer activity against MDA-MB-7 cell lines with low toxicity towards normal MCF-10A cell line highlighting their potential as anticancer agents.

papers.title: Origin-of-life chemistry is a problem of chemical composability
papers.abstract: Life is usually described by biological functions such as metabolism, replication and evolution. A complementary chemical question lies upstream: what properties of a chemical world make such functions physically realizable? No single interaction strength, solvent property or temperature can answer this because persistence, exchange, reaction, transport and driven organization impose competing requirements. Compatibility may occur under one condition or across an ordered environmental history, provided useful states survive between stages. Autonomy emerges not through environmental independence, but as more constraints coordinating chemical flux are generated and maintained by the system itself. We propose a chemistry-first diagnostic programme mapping molecular failure modes, constructive trajectories and system-generated constraints across scales, from molecular interactions to reaction networks and selfmaintaining organization.

papers.title: The importance of nanoscale phenomena in electrolyte behavior: acetonitrile-aqueous zinc sulfate electrolytes
papers.abstract: Electrolytes composed of mixed solvents are of significant scientific and technological importance in lithium-ion and beyond–lithium-ion batteries, and more broadly across physical chemistry. Their emergence has highlighted the importance of multiscale phenomena, particularly the development of nanoscale solution heterogeneities. It is therefore essential to assess how these inhomogeneities and nanoscale aggregates influence solvation, transport, and electronic properties. Here we investigate the solution structure and transport properties of aqueous zinc sulfate electrolytes with acetonitrile (ACN) additives, where the addition of ACN leads to improved cyclability. Using complementary anomalous small-angle X-ray scattering, X-ray pair distribution function, electrochemistry, and NMR, we identify the presence of salt-rich-water-rich and salt-poor-ACN-rich nano-heterogeneities, and at higher ACN concentrations, liquid-liquid phase separation. We find that the size of zinc-sulfate ion clusters in the water domains increases slightly upon ACN addition, while the ACN-rich domains grow much larger as phase separation is approached. The inverse Haven ratio, determined using the ionic conductivity and diffusivity, is much less than unity and decreases slightly on addition of ACN, which shows ion-ion interactions. We speculate that the increased ion-ion interactions with increased ACN is a result of a reduction in free water, the increase in zinc sulfate cluster size and/or an increase in solution tortuosity. This work highlights key phenomena to consider when engineering new water-organic-salt electrolyte systems and establishes a phase diagram for water-ACN-ZnSO4 that can guide advances, such as self-adaptive electrolytes.

papers.title: Multiscale Insights into CO2 Chemisorption and Proton Transfer in Choline-Imidazolate based Deep Eutectic solvents: Exploring the Effect of Primary, Secondary and Tertiary Alkanolamine on Reaction Pathways and Product Distribution
papers.abstract: Understanding how solvent composition governs competitive CO2 chemisorption within solvents is essential for the rational design of solvents for CO2 capture. In this work, we combine density functional theory (DFT), classical molecular dynamics (cMD), and microkinetic modeling to investigate CO2 chemisorption in choline-imidazolate based systems containing different alkanolamine hydrogen bond donors (HBDs): monoethanolamine (MEA), diethanolamine (DEA), and methyldiethanolamine (MDEA). By systematically characterizing the thermodynamics, kinetics and liquid structure influence, our results show that within these systems, choline is the preferred CO2-binding site unless a HBD is present. Accordingly, the MEA system shifts almost entirely to amine-centered carbamate formation, the DEA system retains carbamate dominance but with stronger competition from choline-centered capture, and the MDEA system which additionally includes water shifts back toward choline-centered carbonate together with a competitive water-assisted bicarbonate pathway. The findings illustrate how CO2 chemisorption in multicomponent liquids is controlled by a combination of intrinsic reaction thermodynamics, liquid-structure, and CO2 concentration. More broadly, this work provides insights that will facilitate molecular-level design of solvents for CO2 uptake and regeneration.

papers.title: Efficient Free-Energy Landscape Construction Using Graph-Based Active Path Sampling
papers.abstract: Constructing free-energy landscapes without prior knowledge of their structure often requires dense sampling of the configuration space, leading to prohibitive computational costs. Here, we introduce an efficient graph-based active-learning framework that adaptively constructs free-energy landscapes while preserving the connectivity required for free-energy determination. The method employs a Gaussian-process surrogate to identify informative configurations and connects each newly sampled set of points to the existing sampled region through a shortest-path search on a graph, enabling efficient, connected exploration required for accurate free-energy determination. We validate the framework using analytical two-and three-dimensional model energy landscapes as well as a many-body free-energy landscape derived from molecular dynamics simulations of polymer-grafted nanoparticles in a polymer melt. Across all cases, the method accurately recovers the multidimensional landscape at much lower effective sampling cost than dense or predetermined grid-based sampling, with sampling efficiency quantified by the cumulative length of the connected sampling tree constructed during active learning. More broadly, this work establishes a general framework for data-efficient exploration of high-dimensional free-energy landscapes in molecular and materials simulations.

papers.title: Resolving Positional Markush Structures for Chemical Reaction Extraction
papers.abstract: The automated extraction of chemical reaction data from scientific literature remains very challenging mainly due to the visual complexity and heterogeneity of published graphical schemes. In particular, substrate scopes containing positional Markush structures pose a significant challenge for current Optical Chemical Structure Recognition (OCSR) and reaction-extraction systems, as their resolution requires combining molecular recognition with precise spatial reasoning. Herein, we introduce a deterministic, coordinate-based extraction pipeline designed to resolve positional Markush structures in reaction schemes. Building upon a fine-tuned version of the graph-prediction OCSR module MolScribe, our approach uses deterministic geometric rules based on 2D molecular coordinates to infer R-group attachment points and generate topologically valid molecular representations. To evaluate this approach, we introduce two curated benchmarks: MIPub-2k (Molecular Images from Publication - Université Bourgogne Europe) comprising 2,128 literature-derived molecular image crops for OCSR evaluation and MIReactPub (Markush template-based Image of Reaction from Publication – Université Bourgogne Europe) comprising 450 reactions from 23 schemes containing positional Markush structures for reaction-level assessment. The complete pipeline achieves an end-to-end F1 score of 0.46, increasing to 0.54 for schemes without textual-dependent ambiguities. Slightly reorganizing figures doubles the F1 score, demonstrating the robustness of the underlying geometric resolution while highlighting the substantial impact of visual heterogeneity in published literature on end-to-end performance. By explicitly encoding chemical and spatial constraints, our proposed approach provides a transparent and reproducible framework for resolving complex molecular representations from literature images. The resulting open-source pipeline and benchmarks provide a specialized component that can be further integrated into automated workflows for large-scale chemical information extraction.

papers.title: Analytical topological bounds and favorable elastic paths in discrete molecular networks
papers.abstract: The mechanical response of discrete networks is fundamentally governed by their underlying connectivity. While traditional matrix-based approaches successfully capture global mechanical responses, their utility is delimited by an 𝒪(𝑁3)computational cost that limits direct access to specific topological pathways and localized load transmission. Here, we formulate a graph-theoretical framework that determines the effective elastic constant of molecular networks through analytical topological rules, bypassing global matrix diagonalization. Central to this formulation is the concept of favorable elastic paths—the specific topological highways that actively transmit mechanical force between terminal vertices. For series-parallel architectures, we compute effective stiffness via recursive edge reductions characterized by excluded minors. To quantify localized mechanical contributions, we introduce a normalized Relevance Ratio and a hierarchical (𝑘, 𝑑)-subgraph classification based on graph distance and vertex connectivity. For complex, non-reducible topologies, we leverage Menger's theorem to derive rigorous topological upper and lower bounds for the effective stiffness using purely combinatorial opera tions. By mapping atoms and bonds to vertices and edges, we demonstrate how discrete connectivity dictates continuum mechanical response. This topology-driven approach provides a computationally efficient (𝒪(∣ 𝐸 ∣)) and analytically transparent baseline, opening new avenues for the algorithmic screening and targeted chemical functionalization of complex biopolymer networks and mechanical metamaterials.

papers.title: ElastoGraph: An Open-Source Algorithmic Framework for the Topological Assessment of Molecular Stiffness Applied to Polysaccharide Networks
papers.abstract: The prediction of mechanical properties at the molecular scale relies on matrix-based approaches, such as the diagonalization of large Hessian matrices in elastic network models (ENMs) or molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. These methods exhibit O(N3) computational complexity and map molecular connectivity to macroscopic stiffness through numerical operations that do not explicitly resolve load-transmission pathways. Here, we present 2 ElastoGraph, an open-source Python framework that shifts the analytical focus from numerical prediction to the topological mapping of elastic paths—the specific routes through which mechanical force is transmitted between terminal vertices. The algorithm achieves three objectives: (i) it identifies and prunes mechanically irrelevant subgraphs (r = 0) via cut-vertex analysis, isolating the subset of elastic paths that contribute to load transmission; (ii) it hierarchically classifies these paths using a k–d subgraph ranking based on graph distance and vertex-connectivity, providing a prioritized map of topological targets for chemical functionalization; and (iii) it computes effective elastic constants for series-parallel architectures through recursive edge reductions in O(N) time, while establishing rigorous topological bounds for non-series-parallel networks. Applied to the load-bearing backbones of cellulose and β-chitin, the framework reveals that under uniform edge weights both polysaccharides are topologically isomorphic, yielding an identical effective stiffness. However, the integration of a chemical parameterization module breaks this degeneracy: assigning relative stiffness values of k = 1.0 to covalent bonds and k = 0.10 to hydrogen bonds in cellulose, versus k = 0.15 for hydrogen bonds in β-chitin, yields differentiated mechanical profiles (keff = 0.45 for cellulose and keff = 0.52 for β-chitin). The framework computes these results in less than 0.01 s, representing an approximate 50-fold speedup compared to standard Hessian inversion on comparable synthetic networks. This framework complements molecular dynamics simulations by providing an interpretable topological baseline that identifies which bonds are worth functionalizing to tune macroscopic stiffness. Quantitative validation against experimental nanomechanical data will be the subject of future work. Beyond polysaccharides, this topology-driven framework is extensible to protein domains, DNA nanostructures, metal–organic frameworks, and two-dimensional materials, providing an interpretable baseline for the rational design of mechanically tunable molecular 3 systems across structural biology, soft matter, and nanotechnology. The source code, documentation, and benchmark datasets are freely available at https://github.com/yeyrecanals/ElastoGraph

papers.title: Unmasking the Non-Covalent Nature of HA–Dopamine Assemblies: Insights from 1H NMR Degradation Tracking and Multidimensional NMR
papers.abstract: Hyaluronic acid (HA) is a polysaccharide with diverse clinical and industrial applications. One of the key challenges is its sensitivity to enzymatic degradation. Chemical modifications offer a potential for modulating enzymatic susceptibility, as well as other functional properties. We report an NMR-based examination of the effect of HA modifications on hyaluronidase degradation. Chemical modification of HA with dopamine (HADN) has been widely reported, based on 1-ethyl-3-(3 dimethylaminopropyl) carbodiimide hydrochloride (EDC) chemistry. We describe a 1H NMR strategy for a convenient and sensitive analysis of hyaluronidase degradation rates. Surprisingly, HADN exhibited a degradation profile nearly identical to that of native HA, while methacrylated HA resisted degradation. The finding that HADN showed no protective effect prompted a rigorous re-investigation of HADN using 2D NMR. Our findings revealed that HADN is not a covalent conjugate, but a non-covalent and reversible system involving an unexpected EDC-dopamine adduct. Thermal and alkaline stress facilitate the release of dopamine from the non-covalent HADN complex. Our data highlight risks in the use of EDC-based conjugation experiments applied to many types of polysaccharides. Our NMR methods provide a robust platform for the dynamic comparison of degradation rates of HA, and identify a fingerprint test for characteristic residual EDC adducts.

papers.title: Per-axis failure of the minimum-image convention in GCMC screening of MOFs for hydrogen storage
papers.abstract: Grand canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) simulations underpin machine-learning-accelerated screening of metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) for hydrogen storage, yet published workflows differ widely in simulation rigour. Minimum-image violation in GCMC screening of MOFs biases uptake but preserves rankings, and the error is predictable before any simulation is run. Here, the cost of the single-unit-cell shortcut (one crystallographic cell regardless of the interaction cutoff, violating the minimum-image convention) is quantified across a screening library for the first time. Uptakes of 85 CoRE MOF 2019 frameworks were computed with a converged per-framework supercell protocol and repeated in a single cell. Deliverablecapacity rankings are found to be remarkably stable (Spearman ρ = 0.996, bootstrap CI [0.989, 0.998]; top ten recovered exactly, no capacity forfeited), while absolute uptakes fall by up to 30%. The total replication factor m predicts the error poorly: frameworks needing only 4 × 1 × 1 replication lose as much uptake as 36× cases. The error tracks the worst single axis nmax, exposing rod secondary-building-unit frameworks (MOF-74 among them) as the class at risk; intermediate-supercell ladders confirm this directly, the same volume increase recovering 2.4% or 16.4% of the deficit according to which axis receives it. Stated without reference to the cutoff, a single cell is safe for ranking whenever every perpendicular width exceeds one cutoff radius, while absolute capacities require two. Recomputing only the frameworks with nmax ≥ 3, one in three of the set, brings the largest remaining error down to 1.3% while still saving 18% of the campaign

papers.title: Agentic Workflow for High-Throughput Synthesis Campaigns: Mapping the Persistent Phosphor Ca2ZnSi2O7:Eu2+,Nd3+
papers.abstract: The structural and spectroscopic record of a high-throughput synthesis campaign exceeds what experimenters can closely and accurately analyze with conventional tools alone. We report a workflow built for this problem: a language model agent operates an automated Rietveld phasesearch pipeline, Crystalyze Match, built on the open-source DARA engine, and then interprets the phases, optical spectra, and synthesis metadata. We demonstrate this workflow on a 48 sample campaign for the persistent phosphor Ca 2 ZnSi 2 O 7 :Eu 2+ ,Nd 3+ (doped hardystonite), a water-stable candidate alternative to SrAl 2 O 4 :Eu 2+ ,Dy 3+ for luminescent road markings. Within the campaign’s lifetime, the workflow mapped two decomposition pathways, incomplete reaction and zinc volatilization, that validate the two-step synthetic approach. The workflow also identified the fate of the rare-earth dopants: a silicate oxyapatite, Ca 2 (Eu,Nd) 8 (SiO 4 ) 6 O 2 , missed by prior manual analysis, is present in every doped sample. Human adjudication proved necessary as the search first scored the oxyapatite through a lanthanide-free proxy structure that scatters too weakly to register at low fractions, and a corrected-model re-screen of all 48 patterns recovered it. Though the rare-earth dopants appear to end up in the oxyapatite phase, emission rises monotonically with Eu content, and the material shows the target persistent luminescence, so where the emitting Eu 2+ resides remains unresolved. Our work highlights that human review and re-screening after every structure-model revision dramatically improve the trustworthiness of campaign-scale claims.

papers.title: Enzymatic routes to site-specific protein-nucleic acid conjugates
papers.abstract: Nature rarely joins nucleic acids to proteins covalently, yet synthetic protein-nucleic acid conjugates enable diverse applications from nanotechnology to therapeutics, which require or benefit from defined, stable, one-to-one linkages of known geometry. Here I evaluate biochemical routes to such conjugates against four ideals: enzymatic bond formation, addressability on both partners, minimal engineering of the protein of interest, and scarless linkage to unmodified nucleic acid. With an eye on biochemical mechanisms, I cover both established tools and natural systems that might become one. The available methods fall into two broad architectures. In cis, the enzyme itself becomes part of the product, allowing native chemistry on unmodified nucleic acid but requiring a folded fusion, usually at a terminus. In trans, a separate enzyme modifies the target protein and leaves a short motif, but the burden often shifts to the nucleic acid, which must carry a reactive group. No current method satisfies all four ideals, and the trade-offs largely reflect the substrate class recognized by the bond-forming enzyme. Nucleic-acid readers offer the most direct route to scarless, fully enzymatic conjugation but their requirement for large fusions limit protein-side addressability. Small-molecule readers invert this profile, enabling compact tags and greater placement flexibility at the cost of synthetic handles and a chemical final bond. Peptide readers combine short tags with enzymatic ligation but constrain attachment geometry and linkage chemistry. Site-specific, minimally invasive, scarless, and fully biochemical ProNAc formation therefore remains a tetralemma, with enzymatic activation of nucleic acids offering a promising route toward resolving it.

papers.title: Dynamic Parameter Screening for Accelerated Mechanistic Analysis
papers.abstract: Mechanistic studies are essential for the continued advancement of the chemical sciences however; classical approaches remain laborious and material intensive. Graphical reaction analysis techniques such as RPKA and VTNA have substantially reduced this burden, yet the time and resources required to comprehensively study increasingly complex reactions remain high. Medium- and high-throughput batch and flow kinetic methods have been developed to further streamline data acquisition, but their widespread adoption is limited by the need for specialized equipment or expertise. Here we introduce dynamic parameter screening (DPS), in which a single batch reaction is monitored continuously while sequential reagent and catalyst additions are used to probe kinetic impacts of multiple species within one experimental setup. Using the palladium-catalyzed Kumada–Tamao–Corriu cross-coupling as a model system, we compared DPS with traditional one-factor-at-a-time approach across three catalytic systems (PdCl2(dppf)·CH2Cl2, PEPPSI-iPr, and XPhos Pd G2). DPS afforded essentially identical qualitative and quantitative (kinetic modeling) conclusions except for the case of XPhos Pd G2. This latter system exhibited multiple kinetic regimes where the traditional approach revealed the global impact of reagent concentrations, whereas DPS provided complementary, higher-resolution insight into reagent effects within a specific kinetic regime. The insights obtained from DPS guided a simple slow-dosing strategy that markedly improved reaction rates even at reduced catalyst loadings. DPS therefore provides a practical, low-barrier route to high-resolution kinetic information that is fully compatible with conventional modeling, broadening access to mechanistic understanding in resource-limited settings.

papers.title: Topochemical Fluorination of the Ruddlesden−Popper In/Sb-Mixed Oxide Ba2In0.5Sb0.5O4; Staged Anion Insertion and Structural Evolution toward the Fluorine-Rich Oxyfluoride Ba2In0.5Sb0.5O2F4
papers.abstract: Layered Ruddlesden–Popper (RP) oxides provide a versatile platform for topochemical anion modification, enabling access to metastable mixed-anion phases with tuneable structural and electronic properties. In this work, we present a comprehensive investigation of how mixed B -site (indium and antimony) chemistry influences topochemical fluorination of Ba 2 In 0.5 Sb 0.5 O 4 using polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF). Powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) reveals anisotropic lattice expansion, dominated by elongation perpendicular to the perovskite layers, with minimal change in the in-plane lattice parameters. Fluorination proceeds through a composition-dependent multiphase regime in which several tetragonal ( I 4 /mmm ) RP components with progressively expanded c and slightly contracted a lattice parameters coexist, representing a distribution of fluorination states, followed by convergence to a single dominant fluorine-rich tetragonal phase at high fluorine content. Coupled X-ray/neutron Rietveld refinement establishes the end member as the anion-saturated oxyfluoride Ba 2 In 0.5 Sb 0.5 O 2 F 4 , and locates the three fully occupied anion sites of the tetragonal I 4 /mmm framework. The preferred O/F distribution, with oxide at the equatorial site and fluoride at the apical and interstitial sites, is supported by bond-valence-sums (BVSs) analysis of the refined interatomic distances and the corresponding global instability indices (GIIs), together with charge balance, since O and F cannot be reliably distinguished from their neutron scattering lengths alone. X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) measurements support the retention of the formal In 3+ and Sb 5+ oxidation states upon fluorination.

papers.title: Effect of Na substitution on P2−NaxMn2/3Ni1/3O2 cathodes for Na-ion batteries: A DFT study of structural stability, ion mobility and local charge compensation.
papers.abstract: Layered oxides emerge as promising materials as cathode in sodium ion batteries due to the possibility to avoid critical metals and the direct industrial transferability in lithium-ion battery factories. A key point is that the layered structure can host a wide range of cations, enabling the substitution as a strategy to improve key factors such as structural stability, electronic conductivity, ion mobility, etc. For that, it is important to determine how the different substituents can affect these factors, to then mitigate side reactions and improve the desired mechanisms. In the present work, the effect of the co-interlayering ions on the open circuit voltage, structural stability, cation mobility, and electronic structure has been investigated for P2−Na x Mn 2/3 Ni 1/3 O 2 cathodes through Density Functional Theory. Calculated substitution thermodynamics indicate that P2 − Na x Mn 2/3 Ni 1/3 O 2 (x = 2/3, 1/8) can accommodate K + , Ca 2+ , Mg 2+ , and Zn 2+ at the Na site. Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations reveal that all dopants preserve the structural integrity of the layered framework while inducing distinct local dynamical responses, with Mg and Zn producing the most rigid local environments and K the highest lattice flexibility. CI-NEB calculations show that K facilitates the Na-ion hopping, and Ca preserve it with Na-ion migration barriers comparable to those of the pristine material, whereas Mg and Zn significantly increase the activation energy for Na intersite-hopping. Electronic structure analysis reveals a markedly different behavior between isovalent and aliovalent substitutions, with divalent dopants enhancing oxygen participation in charge compensation and locally promoting Mn 3+ -like electronic configurations at high Na contents. These results provide atomistic insight into how Na-site chemistry governs the balance between ionic transport, electronic structure, and structural stability, offering practical guidelines for the design of high-performance layered sodium-ion cathodes.

papers.title: IntegroPectin in aqueous solution: a multi-scale computational investigation of solvation, conformational dynamics, and thermodynamic partitioning of a naringeningalacturonic acid–rhamnose glycoconjugate
papers.abstract: A novel class of flavonoid-pectin bioconjugates sourced via cavitation of citrus processing waste, citrus IntegroPectin pectic polymers exhibit a complex structural synergy between the pectic backbone and co-extracted flavonoids imparting these biopolymers with broad scope biological activity. Using a reductionist approach, we explore the hydration behavior of Model A — a neutral naringenin-esterified disaccharide (GalA(1→2)Rha) modeling the structure of grapefruit IntegroPectin via a multiscale computational workflow spanning isolated-molecule DFT, topological analyses, mixed implicit–explicit iterative micro-solvation, explicitsolvent molecular dynamics, and continuum thermodynamics. The solvation of Model A (naringenin–galacturonic acid–rhamnose) is governed by a rigid, preorganized conformation in which the most electrostatically attractive sites are topologically saturated by intramolecular hydrogen bonds. Water therefore occupies a hierarchy of available rather than optimal sites, forming an anisotropic percolating network whose electronic, geometric, topological, and spectroscopic signatures are mutually consistent across four levels of theory and three timescales. Analysis points to a genuine decoupling between the spatial and electronic descriptions of hydration that neither a purely energetic nor a purely geometric analysis could reveal alone.

papers.title: A traceable agentic framework for chemistry research query and analysis with ThermoML database
papers.abstract: Reliable use of thermophysical databases in exploratory chemistry requires resolving heterogeneous identifiers, reconciling experimental conditions, and preserving numerical provenance across large, nested records. We present a hierarchical large language model (LLM) agent framework, implemented with a custom ReAct reasoning engine, that translates naturallanguage research questions into traceable retrieval and analysis workflows over the NIST ThermoML database. The framework combines hierarchical canonical identifiers, queryconditioned evidence compaction, deterministic inspection ledgers and numerical-grounding gates, and tool-assisted Redlich–Kister fitting. Five case studies are discussed in detail, representing chemistry tasks spanning data-rich and data-sparse retrieval, binary-mixture correlation, and open-ended cosolvent screening. For an ethanol–water equimolar density query, the system reduced ~190k characters of search output to 2k and precisely recovered a measured density of 859.3 kg m-3 at an ethanol mole fraction of 0.498, 298.15 K, and 100 kPa. For methanolethanol viscosity, it selected condition-aligned mixture and pure-component records, examined the fitting results at different orders, and produced a 2nd-order Redlich–Kister fit with 𝑅 = 0.982. Results for an open-ended iron-electrodeposition electrolyte design query synthesized evidence from approximately 12k measurements across 200 data blocks. However, with numerical grounding disabled for this specific case, the answer contained severe numerical hallucinations despite qualitatively coherent reasoning. These cases establish the feasibility of agent-assisted ThermoML research and identify identity management, evidence compaction, and deterministic numerical provenance as central design requirements for reliable chemistry-database research agents with some level of abstraction chemistry reasoning.

papers.title: Programmable Oxidation in Flow on Interdigitated Lateral Catalytic Condensers
papers.abstract: Heterogeneous catalysis remains fundamentally limited by the intrinsic static electronic and physical structure of the catalyst surface during reaction that restricts catalytic rates and limits reactions to equilibrium. To circumvent these limitations, a catalytic condenser enables the non-Faradaic dynamic modulation of surface binding energies through an external potential. Here, we describe an interdigitated (IDT) internal ion gel catalytic condenser within a continuous flow reactor for the electronic control of thermochemical carbon monoxide oxidation on Pt active sites. The device utilizes a thermally stable, high-capacitance ion gel electrolyte (PA6,6/[EDMIM][TFSI]) to establish an electric double layer at the metal-electrolyte interface, enabling both charge condensation and a strong electric field at the Pt active sites. Field strength was measured by Stark tuning of 4-mercaptobenzonitrile (4-MBN) on a model Ag electrode, with field strengths on the order of ~1 V nm -1 shifting a voltage-dependent nitrile response up to ~4 cm -1 /V at negative applied potential. By applying a bias of ±1 V at 180°C, the device both increases and decreases the catalytic turnover frequency of CO oxidation. These results support surface-charge modulation as the origin of catalytic rate enhancement for the non-Faradaic dynamic tuning of thermochemical reaction rates.

papers.title: Dynamic Covalent Approaches to Responsive Electropores for Iontronics
papers.abstract: Regulating ion transport across biomimetic membranes is fundamental to the design of adaptive neuromorphic and iontronic systems. Electroporation provides a powerful means to establish conductive pathways without biological pore-forming agents, yet these pores are inherently transient and stochastic, limiting their ability to achieve non-volatile, reconfigurable conductance. Here, we show stable, chemically responsive electropores in nanoparticle-surfactant bilayers assembled via dynamic covalent diketoenamine chemistry. The lifetime of electropores is modulated via electrical stimuli, allowing the bilayer to emulate synaptic behaviors ranging from short-term plasticity to long-term potentiation. While interfacial jamming structurally stabilizes conductive pathways against line-tension-induced closure, amine-mediated bond exchanges provide a distinct chemical trigger to unjam interface and actively reseal the pores. By evaluating a series of 1-alkylamines, we find that additive lipophilicity governs the interfacial chemo-response, with high partition coefficients being essential for triggering pore resealing. By integrating photo-caged polymeric amines into the surrounding oil phase, we achieve in situ optical resetting of transmembrane ion conductance, bypassing physical intervention and slow passive diffusion of exogenous chemical triggers. Our findings establish dynamic covalent nanoparticlesurfactants as a robust architecture for engineering stable, responsive electropores in biomimetic membranes, providing a foundation for adaptive neuromorphic and iontronic systems.

papers.title: Stage-Defined Prenyltransferase Integration for Hybrid RiPP Biosynthesis
papers.abstract: Combining biosynthetic enzymes from distinct ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptide (RiPP) families offers a route to hybrid RiPPs but poses challenges in coordinating noncognate enzymatic transformations. Here, leveraging the temporal control enabled by in vitro biosynthesis, we first explored stage-defined integration of a cyanobactin prenyltransferase (PTase) into thiopeptide biosynthesis, a highly coordinated multienzyme pathway involving interdependent transformations of a single precursor peptide. Whereas early- and intermediate-stage prenylation interfered with thiopeptide maturation, late-stage prenylation of fully matured thiopeptides proceeded efficiently, enabling the production of diverse prenylated thiopeptides. We then extended this late-stage strategy to structurally distinct RiPPs, nonribosomal peptides, and artificial cyclic peptides using multiple cyanobactin PTases. Stage-controlled integration of non-cognate tailoring enzymes thus provides access to hybrid peptidic natural products.

papers.title: Unexpected effects of the addition of copper(II) bisphenanthroline complexes in Chan-Lam couplings
papers.abstract: The effect of the addition of bis(2,9-dimethyl-1,10-phenanthroline)copper(II) chloride and bis(1,10-phenanthroline)copper(II) chloride on Chan-Lam couplings with copper acetate and a previously reported coordination complex LCuCl were investigated with respect to their potential role as redox shuttles in the catalytic cycle. In neither case action as a redox shuttle was observed. While no effects were observed in reactions catalysed by LCuCl, addition to reactions catalyzed by copper acetate gave more complicated results, sometimes with drastically increased activity. Detailed investigations found that (i) ligand exchange results in the formation of a more active mono-phenanthroline copper complex and (ii) formation of mixed chloride/acetate salts lead to significant increases in activity. This result could not be generalized for a wider range of N-nucleophiles or observed for anion combinations other than chloride/acetate.

papers.title: Water-Gated Molecular Bistability in Tetrazolate MOFs
papers.abstract: Stimuli-responsive metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) offer opportunities to couple structural transformations with switchable electronic states, yet reproducing spin-crossover (SCO) behaviour across different frameworks and metal centres remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate a conserved watergated switching mechanism in a family of flexible tetrazolate MOFs comprising Fe(II), Co(II), and mixed Fe/Co frameworks. Dehydration induces framework contraction, metal–N bond shortening, ligand immobilization, and a shift toward low-spin states, while rehydration restores the initial structure and physical properties. Remarkably, despite their markedly different initial spin-state populations, upon dehydration of Fe- and Co-based frameworks, Raman spectroscopy reveals an identical 13 cm-1 shift of a tetrazolate/phenyl-ring vibration, identified as a spin state marker band. This molecular fingerprint is also retained in the mixed-metal solid solution, demonstrating that the structural and vibrational response is conserved upon metal substitution and mixing. These results identify water desorption as the thermodynamic trigger, and the flexible tetrazolate network as the mediator that couples guest removal to metal-centre spin transition, providing a transferable strategy for water-gated spin switching in flexible tetrazolate frameworks.

papers.title: Investigation of α-Silylalcohols as Chiral Umpolung Carbanion Surrogates through Stereospecific 1,2-Brook Rearrangement
papers.abstract: We report the investigation of the enantiospecific trapping of chiral α-silyl secondary alcohols through stereospecific 1,2-Brook rearrangement of the lithium alkoxide. The reaction proceeds through a chiral polarityreversed carbanion intermediate that can be trapped faster than racemization in many cases. Weinreb amides were applied as electrophile to access enantioenriched α-hydroxyketones in good yields and variable enantiopurities. Substituent effect studies showed that product enantiopurity was a function of the rate of electrophilic trapping of the intermediate chiral carbanion with faster trapping rates affording higher chirality transfer. The chiral α-silyl secondary alcohols were conveniently accessed in high enantiopurity using Noyori asymmetric transfer hydrogenation (ATH) with low catalyst loading (0.5 mol % Ru).

papers.title: Development of Efficient Blue OLEDs: A Systematic Investigation of the Effect of the Nature of the Host on Exciton Dynamics in Operating TADF Devices
papers.abstract: The continuing demand for sharper and brighter displays is driving the development of efficient blue organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs). However, achieving high maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE max ) and low efficiency roll-off is still a major challenge for blue-emitting devices. Herein, we report highly efficient blue multi-resonant thermally activated delayed fluorescent (MR-TADF) OLEDs showing EQE max of 32.5% and relatively moderate efficiency roll-off (EQE: 26.3% at 100 cd m -2 and 14.6% at 1000 cd m -2 ). Several host:emitter combinations were explored to correlate the nature of the emissive layer formulation to the 2 differences in device efficiencies. Here, the photophysical measurements did not adequately explain the differences in device performance; however, direct measurement of exciton dynamics in operating OLEDs and single-carrier devices revealed that charge accumulation at the interface between the transport layer and host resulted in increased exciton-polaron annihilation and the loss of efficiency. This highlights the importance of measurements on operating devices, as the differences in efficiency between devices could not be explained by conventional photophysics alone.

papers.title: Screening Natural and Modified Nucleobases to Create Alkylation-Resistant Nucleic Acids Toward Sensing Applications
papers.abstract: Alkylating agents play critical roles in medicine and chemical defense but also pose significant hazards by modifying DNA and disrupting cellular function. Their reliable detection is therefore critical, yet current analytical methods are often limited by poor selectivity, need for extensive sample preparation, or poor compatibility with complex matrices. Nucleic acid sensors, such as aptamers, offer a promising route to achieve selective sensing. However, alkylation of nucleobases can compromise DNA three-dimensional structure and binding abilities. To address this limitation, we sought to develop DNA sequences that are resistant to alkylation. We first evaluated the reactivity of modified nucleobases toward a panel of alkylating agents. Although the N7 position 2 of guanosine and N3 position of adenosine have been reported to be among the primary alkylation sites, their analogues 7-deaza-2′-deoxyguanosine and 3-deaza-2′-deoxyadensoine were still found to be reactive. In contrast, 7-deaza-2′-deoxyinosine and 7-deaza-2′-deoxyadenosine were resistant to all alkylating agents tested. Using these resistant nucleobases as substitutes for all guanosine and adenosine residues, respectively, we screened polymerases and found that Therminator DNA Polymerase enabled enzymatic synthesis of fully alkylation-resistant DNA. This work establishes a chemical framework for the development of robust, DNA-based sensors for alkylating agents in biomedical and defense applications.

papers.title: Azopyrazole boronic ester crosslinks with long thermal half-lives for phototunable viscoelastic hydrogels
papers.abstract: Covalent adaptable networks (CANs) based on boronic acid–ester exchange undergo rapid network reconfiguration in ambient conditions, making them useful materials for biomedical applications. The combination of photoswitches and dynamic bonds imparts reversible spatiotemporal control over mechanical properties for smart and responsive materials. Here, we report azopyrazole boronic acids that undergo rapid photoisomerization to their metastable Z isomers, which have extremely long thermal half-lives (over a year at 25 °C) and a 3-fold enhancement in binding affinity for diols compared to the E isomer. When incorporated into hydrogels, these photoswitchable dynamic bonds enable reversible changes in stiffness and stress relaxation time with at least 6 cycles of visible and UV light. Despite only containing dynamic crosslinks, these hydrogels are comparable in stiffness to our previously reported hybrid materials containing dynamic azobenzene boronic ester and static bis(acrylamide) crosslinks. This work demonstrates an alternative strategy to tuning boronic acid-ester equilibria with light while maintaining strong binding in both isomers.

papers.title: Carbonyl node and decarbonylation bottleneck: A mechanistic basis for staged gas release in coal
papers.abstract: Coal spontaneous combustion begins with low-temperature oxidation, in which multiple functional groups participate concurrently, and their coupled evolution ultimately determines the formation of diagnostic gases. However, how these pathways interact and translate structural oxidation into staged gas release remains poorly resolved. Here, the oxidation pathways associated with methyl, hydroxyl, ether, and carbonyl functionalities in Liuqiao (LQ) coking coal are integrated into a unified reaction network. Site-specific lead compounds representing the corresponding local coal environments were constructed, and Laplacian bond order (LBO) was used to identify preferred activation sites.
