Density functional theory calculations characterized the elementary reaction pathways, with transition states verified by intrinsic reaction coordinate analysis where applicable. LBO identified distinct activation centers for each functionality, while the three supply pathways exhibited closely convergent propagation barriers of 16.84, 17.71, and 17.68 kcal/mol, indicating concurrent operation with contributions governed primarily by functional-group abundance rather than strong kinetic selectivity. Peroxide homolysis acts as a kinetic gate at 33.50 kcal/mol, whereas carbonyl formation is facile and decarbonylation constitutes the downstream bottleneck at 22.47 kcal/mol. This network architecture predicts that carbonyl species should accumulate before substantial CO release. In-situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (DRIFTS) and TG-MS confirm this prediction, showing carbonyl accumulation preceding the staged evolution of H2O, CO, and CO2. These results establish carbonyl as a key structural reservoir linking low-temperature oxidation chemistry to gas evolution and provide a mechanistic basis for interpreting gas-based indicators of coal spontaneous combustion.

papers.title: Formation of the titanium oxyl at an electrochemical interface: limiting the role of solvent re-orientation in strong electric fields
papers.abstract: The oxidation of water at surfaces requires reactive and metastable intermediates such as surface adsorbed and often electron deficient oxygen. An outstanding question is whether forming these intermediates depends primarily on the energetics of adsorption associated with the reorganization of bonds at a vacuum interface, or whether it must include contributions from the re-orientation of water dipoles and ions within the aqueous electrolyte that could lower the free energy. Time-resolved mid-infrared experiments in an attenuated total reflection geometry have detected the terminal oxygen, the titanium oxyl, by a vibration that forms underneath it. The vibration was shown to couple to the librational modes of water by a Fano resonance. Here, we show that the picosecond formation of the titanium oxyl’s vibration is invariant across interfaces that change the density of librational modes (air, pH 7, pH 13, and pD 13), as detected by significant modifications of the coupled line-shape. Across the interfaces, we report a common rate constant (0.56 +/- 0.08 ps) and half rise (1.76 +/- 0.39 ps). This demonstrates that the reorganizational energy associated with solvent re-orientation is limited to affecting the ultrafast (400 fs) time resolution of the experiment characteristic of activation-less reactions and bond-reorganization. Furthermore, the formation kinetics are well-fit by a logistic function that describes an autocatalytic reaction and the surface population of titanium oxyl with excitation is well modelled by the Langevin equation. Both suggest that the invariant picosecond rise is due to a re-orientation of the titanium oxyl and its p-polarized vibrational dipole with respect to the strong Helmholtz electric field common to the probed interfaces.

papers.title: Chemistry-Informed Multimodal Model for Structure Elucidation in Automated Reaction Discovery
papers.abstract: Rapid and reliable structure elucidation remains a central bottleneck in automated reaction discovery, where highthroughput experimentation can generate large numbers of crude reaction mixtures faster than they can be interpreted. Gas chromatography coupled with mass spectrometry (GC-MS) provides rapid and information-rich analytical data, but identification of unknown reaction products still relies heavily on expert interpretation or spectral library matching, limiting applicability to novel compounds. Here we introduce Dynamic Mass-Aware Identification from Reaction Knowledge (DynaMAIK), a multimodal transformer framework for reaction-aware structure elucidation from GC-MS data. DynaMAIK combines electron ionization mass spectra with reaction context encoded as reactant and reagent SMILES to predict product structures and molecular formulas. Trained on more than three million reaction–spectrum pairs derived from curated reaction databases, spectral simulation and experimental spectra, DynaMAIK achieved 87% top-1 and 94% top-10 structure accuracy on a held-out experimental test set. Comparisons with spectrum-only and reaction-only models, together with ablation and scrambling experiments, show that spectral evidence and reaction-derived context provide complementary constraints for product identification. Application to high-throughput thiolation reactions demonstrates accurate product assignment directly from experimental screening data. DynaMAIK establishes context-aware GC-MS interpretation as a scalable route toward automated analytical feedback in reaction discovery workflows.

papers.title: Deriving New Model Hamiltonians for [2Fe-2S] Iron-Sulfur Clusters
papers.abstract: Iron–sulfur clusters are common bioinorganic cofactors found in many enzymes. Their open-shell electronic structures, characterized by strongly interacting d-electrons and a dense manifold of near-degenerate electronic states, often require computationally expensive multiconfigurational ab initio methods for their accurate treatment. Therefore, model Hamiltonians using a limited number of physically meaningful parameters are often used to describe their electronic structure properties. The Heisenberg-Dirac-Van Vleck Hamiltonian and the canonical Heisenberg double exchange model, which have traditionally been used to describe the electronic spectra of iron–sulfur clusters, can describe the lowest-energy state of each spin multiplicity. However, these models are limited to a relatively small set of spin degrees of freedom and cannot describe the full range of low-energy electronic excitations and therefore are not sufficient to reproduce the complete low-energy electronic spectrum. This motivates the development of more general model Hamiltonians for these systems. In this work, we employ the density matrix downfolding (DMD) method to derive an improved model Hamiltonian for the [Fe 2 S 2 (SCH 3 ) 4 ] 2-/3- cluster, which serve as models of the active site of ferredoxins containing the [2Fe–2S] motif. A generalized Hubbard-like Hamiltonian derived using DMD provides a substantially improved description of the low-energy spectrum using a relatively small number of physically meaningful parameters. Our matching pursuit analysis further shows that the exchange coupling parameter is selected only at a late stage of the optimization, while most of the exchange interaction is captured by the hopping and electron-electron interaction terms.

papers.title: Active Confinement Catalysis Powered by Mechanical Force.
papers.abstract: The design of artificial enzyme mimics has long been guided by the paradigm of crafting static pockets for transition-state stabilization, a process reliant on stochastic molecular diffusion. These passive events impose a rate limit, and a strict criterion for substrates with suitable size and electronic matching. Inspired by biological ion pumps that drive uphill ion transport using chemical fuels, we propose that mechanical force can power an active, out-of-equilibrium catalytic pumping cycle. We herein report a solid-state mechanochemical strategy where mechanical input drives a confinement catalyst 1 ( Pd 2 L 2 ) from a closed to an open “active” state, while simultaneously pumping substrate molecules into its active site for catalytic events. This dynamic catalyst exhibits substrate size and shape recognition, and its mechano-pump mechanism is quantitatively validated by Michaelis-Menten saturation kinetics, where catalytic efficiency scales directly with the applied force. Moreover, the active-pump action overcomes inherent electrostatic repulsion, enabling cationic substrates, normally excluded from the cationic host catalysts, to be efficiently drawn in and engaged in catalytic turnover. This force-induced pumping catalysis concept is smoothly extended to photochemistry. By combining a photosensitizing unit and an active confinement catalyst, an active pumping mechano-photoredox C-H oxidation process is developed. This work establishes mechanical force not merely as a synthetic tool, but as a fundamental design parameter for catalysts, opening a pathway to life-like chemical control in which energy transduction, not just static structure, dictates function.

papers.title: Mechanical State Selection in Mechanochemical Bond Activation.
papers.abstract: Mechanochemical reactivity provides a distinctive mode of energy input, wherein mechanical force performs work on molecular structures to access reactivity beyond conventional thermal activation. Yet a fundamental understanding of how transient mechanical impacts translate into productive molecular activation remains lacking, particularly under the stochastic conditions of ball milling. By promoting direct homolytic bond scission, mechanoradical chemistry provides an ideal platform to interrogate the role of mechanical force in triggering chemical reactions. However, the resulting highly reactive radical species are often short-lived and elusive, making their formation and reactivity difficult to quantify. Here we use a mechanoradical-chain C-S coupling reaction to amplify otherwise transient initiation events into a measurable kinetic response. Time-resolved kinetics reveal a pronounced force-dependent induction period, while theoretical calculations show that productive C-I homolysis requires a specific loading trajectory. These findings indicate that mechanical force does not simply promote bond cleavage in proportion to its magnitude; rather, individual impacts sample a distribution of mechanical states, with only a small subset being competent for chemical activation. This selective sampling of mechanically competent states provides a mechanistic basis that controls the initiation, propagation and extinction of mechanoradical chains, enabling sustained out-of-equilibrium radical reactivity under intermittent mechanical driving, including with otherwise inaccessible insoluble poly(disulfides) in a diffusion-limited setting.

papers.title: Mild Organic Acid Induced Acidochromism of Spiropyran
papers.abstract: Mild organic acid induced acidochromic transformation of spiropyran is presented herein. Benzoic acids bearing electron-withdrawing substituents efficiently induced the acidochromic transformation of spiropyran, which was monitored using UV–visible and NMR spectroscopy. Kinetic studies revealed a zero-order dependence of the reaction rate on the concentration of benzoic acids. Furthermore, control experiments and DFT calculations demonstrated the pivotal role of the methoxy (–OMe) substituent on the spiropyran core, which facilitates acidochromism by bringing organic acids into close proximity via hydrogen-bonding interactions. Furthermore, biologically relevant acids, including citric acid and tartaric acid, were also found to effectively induce the acidochromic transformation.

papers.title: Interfacial Chain Mobility in Polymer–Silica Elastomers Governs the Balance between Biocompatibility and Tissue-Like Mechanics
papers.abstract: Soft biological tissues combine biocompatibility, viscoelastic energy dissipation and J-shaped nonlinear elasticity, yet the molecular principles for reproducing these properties in artificial soft materials remain unclear. Here we identify interfacial chain mobility, rather than interaction strength, as a key parameter governing tissue-like mechanics in composite elastomers. Using non-aggregated silica particles dispersed in biocompatible PMEA and PMEO2MA networks, we decouple polymer–particle interactions from filler aggregation. Strong multipoint interactions in PMEO2MA create a constrained interphase that suppresses chain mobility and promotes premature stiffening. By contrast, moderate PMEA–silica interactions preserve interfacial mobility while enabling efficient stress transfer. This balance produces J-shaped elasticity through finite chain extensibility and pronounced hysteresis through reversible interfacial stress transfer. Our results reveal complementary molecular origins of nonlinear elasticity and energy dissipation, establishing interfacial chain mobility as a design principle for biointegrated soft materials combining flexibility, damping, biocompatibility and tissue-like mechanical performance.

papers.title: Computational Discovery and Characterization of Cancer-associated Variants in DNA Transaction Enzymes: Impact of a Glioma–associated mutation on Thymine-DNA Glycosylase
papers.abstract: DNA transaction pathways play a fundamental role in maintaining genome integrity through the regulation of DNA replication, repair, recombination, and epigenetic modification. When these pathways are disrupted, it can lead to genomic instability and contribute to disease initiation and progression. Genome-wide association studies and follow–up analysis from data generated by these studies continue to identify numerous disease-associated variants, although functional characterization of missense mutations arising from these variants remains a challenge. In this study, we employed a hypothesis-driven computational framework to identify statistically significant cancer-associated variants in DNA transaction genes across four different cancer phenotypes using genome-wide association study databases. Bioinformatics analyses were used to prioritize missense variants based on their statistical significance. Among the identified variants, the thymine DNA glycosylase (TDG) missense variant rs4135113 was selected for detailed structural characterization because of the critical role of TDG in base excision repair and active DNA methylation. Classical molecular dynamics simulations were performed to investigate the impact of the resulting TDG variant on its structure and dynamics. In addition, the impact of biologically relevant post-translational modifications on both wild-type TDG and variant proteins were investigated. Our results uncover 74 previously unreported cancer–associated SNPS for the four tested phenotypes, including 7 pleiotropic variants. Additionally, our atomistic analysis of a glioma–associated TDG variant provides a detailed insights into how a cancer-associated variant in TDG may impact its function and highlight the importance of combining bioinformatics with molecular simulations to connect genetic data with underlying biological mechanisms.

papers.title: Per-Stage Controls and Failure Modes in a Co-Folding Virtual Screening Cascade for the Keap1–Nrf2 Interaction
papers.abstract: Virtual-screening cascades assembled from co-folding and learned-affinity models are now routine, and each stage is usually trusted on the strength of its own score. We measured, stage by stage, whether those scores carry the information a practitioner would attribute to them, using the Keap1–Nrf2 protein–protein interaction and a 130,793-compound make-on-demand library as the test bed. Most measurements are negative, and none of the failure modes is specific to one of the two models tested. Two independently developed affinity models order activity-cliff pairs above chance (about 68% of 181 pairs) but carry no information about the size of the potency gap, and both couple to molecular weight; the built-in molecular-weight correction rescales without de-biasing. Neither model resolves enantiomers, including the model that generates an explicit high-confidence three-dimensional pose. Pose-model confidence is only weakly informative about geometric validity, so an explicit validity check is required rather than optional. Training-free guidance is required for stereochemical fidelity in pose generation, and diffusion steps can be halved without detectable loss. A seeded matched-decoy gate validates the pose-and-energy stage where no single physicochemical descriptor does, and the pose model reproduces all five co-crystal references below 2 Å, three of them released after its training cutoff. Single-structure MM-GBSA ordering is not validated by ensemble refinement, and the two solvation models disagree both on the ordering and on which candidates are separable at all. The control suite is released as a reusable artifact.

papers.title: Cumulative Charge as a Workload-Aware Comparison Coordinate for Pulsed High-Current OER Stability
papers.abstract: The interpretation of electrode degradation under dynamic electrolysis is complicated by the fact that degradation rates expressed per unit time depend not only on the degradation response but also on the electrochemical workload imposed during the test. Here, we investigate this effect for porous NiFe OER electrodes operated in an alkaline gas-diffusion-electrode half-cell configuration under pulsed galvanostatic operation at 1-3 A·cm-2. Two pulse protocols, corresponding to 86% and 96% active operation time, were evaluated using 36 electrode tests from two independent deposition batches. Degradation was quantified both per unit elapsed time and per cumulative areal charge using iR-corrected electrode potentials, sample-level regression, random-effects pooling, and batch-aware statistical analysis. In the time domain, the degradation rate increased substantially with current density, from 19.2 ± 4.7 to 53.4 ± 23.6 mV·h-1 for the 86% active-operation protocol. In contrast, the charge-normalized voltage loss remained approximately constant at 5.6-6.2 mV·(kC·cm-2)-1 over 1-3 A·cm-2 for the same protocol. The 96% protocol showed a similar overall reduction in apparent current-density dependence after charge normalization, although the 2 A·cm-2 condition exhibited a distinct deviation. Furthermore, at 3 A·cm-2, increased non-linearity, signal variability, and post-electrolysis structural damage indicated a transition to a failure-prone operating regime in which linear charge-normalized degradation was no longer sufficient to describe electrode behavior. Our results demonstrate that elapsed-time degradation rates can overstate apparent current-density and duty-cycle effects during pulsed high-current electrolysis. The charge-normalized voltage loss therefore provides a useful workload-aware descriptor for comparing degradation within the stable operating regime, while high-current failure processes require separate consideration.

papers.title: From Silicon to Carbon: Experimental Validation of Generative AI-Derived CNS Drug Candidates — A Systematic Review (2021–2026)
papers.abstract: Background Generative artificial intelligence has gained traction as an approach for designing novel CNS-relevant drug candidates, yet the extent to which computationally generated molecules undergo experimental validation remains poorly characterised. Methods A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines using a prospectively registered protocol (OSF: https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/JE2DY). PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, arXiv, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched to March 2026. Eligible studies applied generative AI approaches to CNS-relevant targets and reported experimental wet laboratory validation. Titles and abstracts were screened independently by three reviewers; full-text screening, extraction, and quality appraisal were performed independently in duplicate. Findings were synthesised narratively; no meta-analysis was performed. Results Six studies met the inclusion criteria from 374 identified records. All performed in vitro validation; two additionally provided in vivo evidence. Despite CNS-focused objectives, one of six experimentally validated blood–brain barrier permeability. Three studies confirmed their primary computational predictions experimentally, whereas three showed partial confirmation. Validation rates, calculated as confirmed active compounds divided by compounds tested, ranged from 26 to 100 percent; these rates reflect differing selection stringency and are not directly comparable. Publicly accessible code was unavailable in four of six studies. Conclusions Among studies reaching experimental validation, blood–brain barrier confirmation, in vivo evidence, and code availability remain the exception. Because eligibility required reported validation, these findings describe successful translations and cannot estimate failure rates; they nonetheless indicate that validation depth, rather than molecular generation, is the current constraint in this field.

papers.title: Self-Salting Coacervates: Interfacial Tension Reveals a Critical-Like Self-Suppression of Complex Coacervation
papers.abstract: Complex coacervation is typically controlled via salt concentration, while the role of polymer concentration itself has received much less attention. Here, we show that increasing polyelectrolyte concentration can progressively suppress complex coacervation in a charge-stoichiometric, salt- free PDADMAC/PANa system. As polymer concentration increases, the coacervate phase swells while the polymer recovery stays nearly constant, and the compositions and densities of the coacervate and supernatant phases progressively converge. At = 400 mM, the macroscopic phase boundary vanishes and the system reaches a homogeneous, self-suppressed coacervation state. Over this range, the liquid–liquid interfacial tension decreases continuously toward zero following a critical-like power law with an exponent of 1.43 ± 0.03, close to the classical mean-field value of 3/2. These results show that polymer concentration is not merely a compositional variable, but can itself drive coacervation toward a critical-like, one-phase state by increasing salt-like screening from polymer-derived counterions, analogous to the effect of added salt.

papers.title: Disentangling element‑specific pathways in solvothermal formation of platinum-group metal complex solid solutions
papers.abstract: Platinum‑group metal (PGM) complex solid‑solution nanoparticles exhibit unique catalytic properties due to a homogeneous atomic‑scale distribution of multiple elements within a single crystalline phase. Despite their importance, the mechanisms governing their solvothermal formation remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate the solvothermal synthesis of multicomponent Pt–Ir–Pd–Rh–Ru nanoparticles by in situ powder X‑ray diffraction, enabling time‑resolved monitoring across a wide compositional space of ternary and quaternary alloys. Lattice‑parameter evolution confirms incorporation of all elements into a common fcc phase with a systematic iridium deficiency. Crystallite size correlates with elemental heat of fusion, identifying lattice energy as a key parameter controlling particle growth. Formation pathways are strongly element specific: Pd‑free systems form homogeneous alloys directly, whereas Pd‑containing systems follow a two‑step mechanism involving initial Pd‑rich crystallisation and diffusion‑controlled alloying when Pt is present. Pd without Pt yields inhomogeneous multiphase products, contradicting the assumption that Pd seeding is required for homogeneous PGM alloy formation. Overall, this study demonstrates how in situ X‑ray diffraction can accelerate materials discovery while also providing general mechanistic insight into multicomponent solvothermal alloy formation.

papers.title: Toward Environmentally Stable Transition-Metal Dichalcogenides: Defect-Selective Docking of Au Nanoparticles on MoS2, MoSe2, and MoTe2
papers.abstract: Defect sites in two-dimensional (2D) transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) can enhance surface reactivity and charge-transfer interactions, but the same exposed metal centers can accelerate degradation under environmental conditions. Selective functionalization of these sites therefore offers an opportunity to improve TMD stability without sacrificing the broader functionality of the 2D surface. Herein, we use density functional theory to examine Au 55 nanoparticle (NP) attachment to pristine and chalcogen-vacancy-containing MoS 2 , MoSe 2 , and MoTe 2 , with emphasis on the interplay between surface diffusion, NP capture, and interfacial bonding. Au 55 preferentially binds chalcogen vacancies across all three TMDs, supporting defect-directed nanoparticle functionalization as a route toward selective passivation. However, the specific surface behavior is strongly material dependent: vacancy binding is strongest for MoSe 2 , whereas surface diffusion is most facile on MoS 2 and vacancy docking is kinetically most accessible on MoTe 2 . Surface-diffusion barriers of 0.34, 0.38, and 0.46 eV are obtained for MoS 2 , MoSe 2 , and MoTe 2 , respectively, while the direct vacancy-docking barriers are 0.59, 0.68, and 0.31 eV. The resulting vacancy-bound complexes exhibit large detachment barriers, indicating stable localization under ambient conditions. Au decoration also produces distinct work-function and charge-transfer responses across the TMD series. These results demonstrate that defect-directed Au NP functionalization is potentially general across TMDs, while its effectiveness remains intrinsically material dependent. The distinct interplay of nanoparticle mobility, vacancy capture, interfacial bonding, and electronic response provides a basis for tailoring NP–TMD interfaces for applications that rely on controlled surface reactivity and charge transfer, including gas sensing, photocatalysis, and environmental contaminant conversion, while enhancing environmental stability.

papers.title: Fully Deuterated [9]Cycloparaphenylene: Vibrational Modulation for Enhanced Solid-State Fluorescence
papers.abstract: Fully deuterated [9]cycloparaphenylene ([9]CPP- d 36 ) was synthesized by gold-mediated macrocyclization. Although the molecular geometry and π-electronic structure of [9]CPP were retained, the framework vibrational frequencies were lowered. Solid-state [9]CPP- d 36 showed a higher fluorescence quantum yield than [9]CPP (0.46 vs 0.34), demonstrating H/D substitution as a vibrational-modulation approach for enhancing nanohoop fluorescence.

papers.title: Data-Driven Exploration of Literature-Derived Catalyst and Reaction Spaces for the Vapor-Phase Aldol Condensation of Acetate with Formaldehyde
papers.abstract: Emerging catalytic processes are often characterized by sparse, heterogeneous, literature-derived datasets, limiting the applicability of conventional predictive machine learning. Herein, we demonstrate a robust approach for extracting mechanistic insights from such challenging datasets using interpretable machine learning. A database comprising 375 observations from 71 publications on the vapor-phase thermocatalytic aldol condensation of acetate with formaldehyde to acrylate was compiled, including catalyst composition, reaction conditions, and catalytic performance. Unsupervised clustering identifies three catalyst families: titanium and vanadium phosphorus oxides, alumina-supported Cs- and Ba-based catalysts, and silica-supported Cs-based catalysts. The small dataset size, restricted catalyst diversity, and inter-study variability result in substantial model overfitting and constrain the accurate prediction of catalyst performance. Robust model development relies on regularized tree-based estimators, publication-grouped cross-validation, and sensitivity analysis across model architectures and random initializations. SHAP analysis identifies liquid hourly space velocity and reactant molar ratio as the dominant operational variables governing acrylate productivity. The presence of water, methanol, or ester-based acetate precursors lowers productivity, while reaction temperature exhibits limited influence. Metal phosphorus oxide and silica-supported Cs materials are ranked as the most and least active catalyst families, respectively. Despite catalyst deactivation being the major limitation, time-on-stream profiles remain largely underreported. Correlation analysis associates the deactivation of metal phosphorus oxide and alumina-supported catalysts primarily with acrylate productivity, consistent with acrylate polymerization, whereas silica-supported Cs catalysts exhibit greater variability, suggesting additional deactivation pathways. Overall, this work provides a transferable framework for extracting reliable insights from sparse literature-derived datasets using interpretable machine learning and robust validation.

papers.title: Beyond Recognition Chemistry: Ion Sensing through Intrinsic Electrochemical InterfacialResponse
papers.abstract: Reliable ion sensing across multicomponent and dynamically changing environments is important in environmental monitoring, industrial process control, and biological analysis. In conventional electrochemical sensors, ion selectivity is typically achieved through redox reactions, ion-selective membranes, or molecular recognition layers, requiring ion-specific chemistry or materials to distinguish the target species. Yet dissolved ions also modify the intrinsic electrical structure of the electrode–electrolyte interface through differences in valence, hydrated size, mobility, polarizability, hydration energetics, and ion–surface interactions. These effects alter solvent organization, charge screening, ion accumulation, dielectric response, and transport within the electric double layer, creating composition-dependent electrical signatures without deliberately introduced receptors. Exploiting these intrinsic responses therefore offers an alternative basis for extracting ion-specific information from the interface itself. This review critically examines recognition-free ion sensing based on such intrinsic interfacial processes, with particular emphasis on non-Faradaic approaches. We first establish the physical origins of ion-dependent interfacial structure and examine how these differences are translated into measurable electrical responses, including capacitance, impedance, electronic channel modulation, ionic transport, and electrokinetic signals. The evolution of recognition-free sensing is then evaluated according to increasing analytical capability, from ion-dependent response and discrimination to single-analyte and multicomponent quantification. This analysis reveals that quantitative capability has advanced substantially, particularly through multidimensional electrical measurements and machine learning, but remains concentrated largely in simple solutions and controlled mixtures. Translation to complex and real matrices therefore represents a major unresolved frontier. Future progress will require deeper understanding of competitive multicomponent interfaces, deliberate control of interfacial properties, informative perturbation of the sensing environment, and data-driven analysis that remains connected to underlying physicochemical processes. Recognition-free sensing thus provides a route toward quantitative ion analysis in which analytical information is encoded by the interface itself rather than imposed exclusively through molecular recognition chemistry.

papers.title: Terminal 4-Cyanophenyl Functionalization of Helical Nanographenes: Mechanistic Insights into Columnar Assembly and Near-Infrared Chiroptical Modulation
papers.abstract: We report a primary helical nanographene terminally functionalized with 4-cyanophenyl groups. This terminal substitution dictates columnar solid-state assembly and selectively stabilizes frontier orbitals deriving narrow HOMO–LUMO gap. It also induces redshifted absorption and amplifies circular dichroism via transition moment density redistribution, providing rational design principles for helical π-systems.

papers.title: The infinitesimal surgeon: nanomachines and upconversion nanoparticles
papers.abstract: The concept of the infinitesimal machine surgeon: a tiny nano-sized machine with moving parts “akin to a little knife”; which is guided to a biological target; and which is human controlled via an electromagnetic input; was loosely envisaged by Feynman two influential lectures in 1959 and 1983. In this perspective, we examine how chemistry – not physics - may be on the cusp on creating a true infinitesimal machine surgeon. We extract four key criteria for an infinitesimal machine surgeon. We set out how nanomachines – light activated molecular rotors – can trigger cell death via mechanical action, and highlight the recently demonstrated combination of nanomachines and photonic upconversion nanoparticles (UCNPs), which enable control of nanomachines with near-infrared (NIR) light. This advancement conceivably enables the ability to control nanomachines in deep tissue (> 1 cm) using diffuse NIR illumination, surpassing depth limits of conventional and two photon excitation (2PE) of nanomachines. We set out directions for future development of nanomachines and UCNPs, for deep-tissue applications, including opportunities for targeted delivery and multi-modal tracking. With sufficient development, we expect the conjunction of UCNPs and nanomachines can fulfil all four criteria to be considered an infinitesimal machine surgeon.

papers.title: Zirconium Oxynitride for the Oxygen Evolution Reaction
papers.abstract: Zirconium oxynitride (Zr2ON2) has been proposed as a support material for iridium-lean oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts, with Zr2ON2 representing a middle ground between conductive but readily oxidized ZrN and acid-stable but insulating ZrO2. Using density functional theory (DFT), we assess the stability of Zr2ON2 under operating conditions and consider it as a host for singleatom Ir catalysts. Substituting Ir into the Zr2ON2(111) surface creates active sites with theoretical OER overpotentials as low as 0.31 V, aided by a stabilization of the OOH∗ intermediate. Although Zr2ON2 is stable, or at worst marginally metastable, on the Zr–N–O convex hull, computational Pourbaix analysis shows it to be unstable in aqueous environments across pH and potential. These conditions drive N to leave as N2 or as dissolved species, leaving behind either dissolved Zr or ZrO2. Previously reported stable operation of Zr2ON2-based electrodes may therefore be reconciled with a self-passivating ZrO2 surface layer.

papers.title: Benchmark Label Definition, Not Model Capability, Explains a Machine-Learning Advantage over TD-DFT for λmax Prediction
papers.abstract: Machine-learning models trained on literature-mined UV-Vis data are frequently reported to outperform time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) for predicting absorption maxima (λ max ). Such comparisons usually evaluate the model on held-out molecules from the same corpus that supplied its training labels, and they set experimental labels of heterogeneous transition type against computed vertical excitations of a single electronic transition. Using a Gaussian process (GP) with 256-bit Morgan fingerprints, trained on 6,878 curated compounds from the Beard literature-mined database, the study shows that two features of the benchmark, rather than model capability, govern the reported margin. On leakage-free in-corpus holdouts the GP outperforms the quantum-chemical references (RMSE 87.3 vs 108.7 nm against TD-DFT, n = 36; 81.6 vs 117.1 nm against sTDA, n = 1,011), and the advantage survives Bemis–Murcko scaffold splitting. Applied unchanged to genuinely external corpora, the same model keeps working where the label convention is compatible with training (R² = +0.209 on 5,811 compounds) and fails where it is not (R² = −0.269 with a +53.5 nm offset on 318 photoswitches labelled specifically to the E -isomer π→π* transition); chemical novelty alone does not break it, reassigning the label does. Against published ωB97X-D3 vertical excitations on 5,501 training-disjoint compounds, the calculations are the more accurate predictor once each method’s removable offset is discounted (≈58 vs 95 nm residual scatter) and correlate with experiment nearly twice as strongly (r = 0.85 vs 0.46). On the transition-specific corpus, CAM-B3LYP/6-31G** reaches 25.4 nm against the GP’s 80.9 nm. The 57–65 nm quantum-chemical underestimation seen in-corpus reappears out of sample at −61.9 nm against independently computed values, supporting a definitional rather than a functional origin. GP predictive uncertainty is poorly calibrated in all external regimes and does not reliably identify high-error predictions; its apparent correlation with error reflects the label variance of the evaluation set rather than structural distance from the training distribution. For this model class, reported margins over quantum chemistry should therefore be regarded as properties of the benchmark—its label definition and its same-corpus provenance,not of the method, unless the benchmark is external and its label convention is stated.

papers.title: Three-Component Alkene Difunctionalization Enabled by Continuous-Flow Generation of the NCF3 Anion
papers.abstract: Multicomponent alkene difunctionalization provides an efficient route to molecular complexity by forging multiple bonds in a single operation. Although radical-polar crossover chemistry has greatly expanded the scope of these transformations, the use of highly reactive fluorinated nucleophiles remains largely unexplored because of their limited accessibility and poor stability. Here, we report the first three-component alkene difunctionalization employing the NCF3 anion as the nucleophilic reaction partner. The key to this transformation is the on-demand generation of the NCF3 anion in continuous flow, followed by its direct merger with visible-light photoredox catalysis. This strategy enables the coupling of a diverse range of radical precursors with styrenes and the flow-generated NCF3 anion through the sequential combination of radical and polar reactivities under mild photochemical conditions. The protocol accommodates extensive variation of the radical precursor, the alkene component and the NCF3 anion itself, and is applicable to the late-stage diversification of pharmaceuticals and agrochemicals. More broadly, this work demonstrates how continuous-flow generation of reactive intermediates can unlock multicomponent reaction manifolds that remain inaccessible using conventional batch methods.

papers.title: Hydridoaluminastibanes: A New Class of Al–Sb Bonded Main-Group Compound
papers.abstract: Reactions of an Al(I) center with Sb–Cl, Bi–Cl and, notably, Sb–H reagents afford a family of Al(III) complexes featuring structurally characterized, pnictogen–halide and –hydride bonds. The Sb–H reaction is particularly striking, simultaneously forging Al–Sb and Al–H bonds to give the first hydridoaluminastibane establishing the previously unknown Al(Sb)(H) functional group. These results introduce pnictogen hydride oxidative addition as a new strategy for Al–Sb bond formation and expands the reactivity landscape of hydrostibination.

papers.title: Polymer Informatics Atlas: Property-Specific Representations, Chemistry-Aware Generalization, and Reliability-Aware Machine Learning Across Five Polymer Properties
papers.abstract: Polymer-property machine learning is often evaluated as if representation choice, random-split accuracy, chemical extrapolation, transfer learning, uncertainty, and chemical interpretation were a single problem. Here, these questions are separated in a six-stage Polymer Informatics Atlas built from 7,973 unique RDKit-valid polymer repeat units in the NeurIPS Open Polymer Prediction 2025 dataset. Thirty-six interpretable composition/structure descriptors and radius-4, 2,048-dimensional count Morgan fingerprints were evaluated independently and as a hybrid representation for glass-transition temperature (Tg), fractional free volume (FFV), thermal conductivity (Tc), density, and radius of gyration (Rg). Frozen property-specific models achieved untouched random-holdout R2 values of 0.608, 0.704, 0.825, 0.920, and 0.703, respectively. However, chemistry-separated testing changed this interpretation substantially: Tc fell to R2 = 0.326, whereas density remained comparatively robust at R2 = 0.874. Representation-block permutation showed that density was predominantly captured by interpretable global chemistry, while Tc and Rg depended more strongly on local/topological structure; Tg and FFV required mixed information. Masked multitask learning on the overlapping Tc-Density-Rg block used incomplete labels more efficiently than complete-case training, but gains over matched single-task neural networks were small and seed dependent. Five-member ensembles combined with splitconformal calibration produced 90% nominal intervals with empirical coverages of 95.7% (Tc), 92.3% (density), and 98.5% (Rg). Finally, 28 predictive Morgan indices were decoded to atom-centred environments after exact fingerprint-regeneration audits, and an integrated descriptor/fingerprint manifold was used for chemical-space visualization, archetype selection, and an illustrative high-Tc/low-density Pareto analysis. The results support a property-specific, domain-aware view of polymer informatics in which predictive accuracy is reported together with chemical support, uncertainty, and explicit claim boundaries rather than as a single global score.

papers.title: Photosensitive Phenothiazine-Fused [4]Helicenes
papers.abstract: Here, we report the synthesis and photoreactivity of a phenothiazine fused [4]helicene, namely 3,13dimethoxybenzo[4,5]quinolino[3,2,1-kl]phenothiazine (MBQP). Comprehensive photophysical studies reveal that MBQP exhibits a high photoluminescence quantum yield of 60.3% and strong circularly-polarized luminescence, with high glum of 2.0 × 10-3 in DMSO. Besides its excellent chiroptical properties, MBQP can undergo a photoinduced chloroformylation reaction upon 365 nm irradiation in chloroform, enabling direct functionalization of the helicene framework. Notably, the emission of resulting photoproducts redshift to ~500, 550, and 660 nm, together with quantum yields up to 77.2%, demonstrating that the photochemical transformation can simultaneously functionalize the helicene framework and improve its luminescence performance. This work provides a straightforward example for the facile synthesis and post-functionalization of color-tunable chiral materials.

papers.title: Bottom-up design of the operating window for direct urea synthesis from first-principles molecular thermodynamics
papers.abstract: Urea, among the most widely utilized foods for crops, is mass-produced via the carbon-and energy-intensive Bosch–Meiser process. However, its operating condition is settled empirically, vulnerable to undersampling and suboptimal production, and its molecular mechanism is not well understood. Here we present a bottom-up design of the operating condition driven by first-principles molecular modeling. Using a machine learning force field trained on first-principles calculations of urea and relevant species, we explored the free energy surface of the reaction space from reactant to product across temperatures. We found a strong thermodynamic preference for acyl substitution over competing pathways, with a free energy minimum around 420 K arising from the balance between carbamic acid’s protonation ratio and solvation number, which respectively increase and decrease with temperature. And we confirmed that the optimal condition originates from near-critical behavior, showing a fixed ratio to the critical temperature below unity. The maximum-yield temperatures of simulation and experiment correspond when scaled to their critical temperatures, suggesting this combined approach for engineering the operating condition.

papers.title: Visible-light-driven C2-phosphonylation of tryptophan in peptides and proteins
papers.abstract: Tryptophan (Trp) residues are comparatively rare in proteins but are frequently positioned at sites that control folding, molecular recognition, ligand binding, and enzymatic activity. Direct chemical modification of Trp therefore offers a powerful strategy for perturbing protein structure and function. However, methods for installing compact, highly polar functionality onto native Trp residues under mild, protein-compatible conditions remain limited. Here we report a visible-light-driven reductive platform for the C2-selective phosphonylation of Trp-containing peptides and proteins using oxime phosphonates as radical precursors. The reaction proceeds under mild conditions, tolerates diverse peptide sequences containing nearly all proteinogenic amino-acid side chains, and enables late-stage modification of Trp-containing synthetic peptides or peptides derived from structurally complex bioactive molecules. The method further extends to native proteins in aqueous buffer, with LC-MS/MS analysis confirming site-selective modification across a range of protein substrates. Collectively, these results establish photochemical Trp-phosphonylation as a versatile method for peptide diversification, protein conjugation, and chemical control of biomolecular function in situ.

papers.title: Decoupling Nanofiller Dimensionality and Electronic Character in Gel Polymer Electrolytes for Supercapacitors
papers.abstract: Gel polymer electrolytes bridge the gap between the mechanical compliance needed for flexible supercapacitors and the ionic transport required for competitive rate performance, and nanofiller incorporation is a widely adopted route to improving both. However, because most studies examine individual nanofillers in different polymer hosts under varying conditions, the relative contributions of filler geometry and intrinsic electronic character remain entangled. Here, a chemically crosslinked poly(vinyl alcohol)-poly(ethylene glycol) gel electrolyte was used as a common matrix to compare four nanofillers at identical loading, spanning a 2 × 2 design of dimensionality (1D versus 2D) crossed with electronic character (insulative versus conductive): halloysite nanotubes (HNT), multiwalled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs), hexagonal boron nitride (hBN), and reduced graphene oxide (rGO). The 1D-filled electrolytes reached ionic conductivities of approximately 39 mS cm −1 , compared with 26 mS cm −1 for the 2D-filled membranes and 15 mS cm −1 for the neat electrolyte. Thus, the 1D-filled electrolytes were approximately 50% more conductive than their 2D counterparts and this difference was largely independent of whether the filler was insulating or conductive. In symmetric supercapacitor cells, however, the capacitance ranking did not follow this conductivity trend. The MWCNT composite delivered the highest specific capacitance of 151 F g −1 and energy density of 13.5 Wh kg −1 , yet the insulating hexagonal boron nitride (94 F g −1 ) outperformed the conductive reduced graphene oxide (76 F g −1 ), demonstrating that cell-level charge storage is governed by the combined influence of ionic transport, filler-matrix interactions, and interfacial ion accessibility rather than any single filler descriptor. These findings provide a framework for rational nanofiller selection in gel polymer electrolytes based on both geometry and electronic classification.

papers.title: From Static Material Design to Predictive Open-Loop Control via Chemistry–Architecture Coupling in a Moving-Boundary Reaction–Diffusion Framework
papers.abstract: Bioactive silicate ceramics, wollastonite (CaSiO3), diopside (CaMgSi2O6), and apatite–wollastonite glassceramics constitute a unique class of bone-regeneration materials whose therapeutic action is intrinsically coupled to their own degradation. Yet the field continues to design these materials as static objects, optimizing initial composition, porosity and elastic modulus while evaluating outcomes at fixed endpoints, tacitly ignoring the central fact that the physicochemical microenvironment they create evolves continuously and irreversibly. We argue that this temporal evolution is not a side effect but the therapeutic mechanism itself, and that it can be engineered predictively. This review consolidates and mathematically hardens the emerging paradigm of spatiotemporal trajectory engineering: the pre-encoded, open-loop programming of a degrading scaffold’s full physicochemical trajectory through coupled control of ceramic network chemistry and pore-network architecture. Three advances over prior treatments are delivered. First, the solid-state chemistry foundation is deepened: Qn speciation from 29Si MAS-NMR is mapped onto hydration versus hydrolysis activation barriers; the incongruent dissolution cascade (cation exchange → silica-gel layer → hydroxycarbonate apatite nucleation) is formalized as a coupled surface–gel-layer–precipitation problem; and the autocatalytic OH−-feedback loop that drives local pH spikes is quantified, together with surface-specific XPS O 1s BO/NBO deconvolution as the front-tracking metric. Second, the static reaction–diffusion model is upgraded to a moving-boundary erosion formulation: an explicit porosity-evolution law, a dynamically self-consistent effective diffusivity, and interstitial convective (Brinkman) transport are introduced, yielding a two-dimensional Damköhler–Péclet regime map that delineates four phenomenologically distinct trajectory regimes, reaction-limited, diffusion-limited, convective washout, and convection-amplified dosing, plus a coupled design corridor where trajectory classes diverge maximally. Third, biological admissibility is replaced from discrete endpoint thresholds to a continuous phase-indexed Regenerative Target Zone (RTZ) envelope incorporating M1-gating, M2-switch, and HCA-maturation kinetics; and the computational pipeline is extended with functional data analysis (fPCA, DTW), neural ordinary differential equations, physicsinformed neural networks, Hamiltonian Monte Carlo credible tubes, and Bayesian-optimal experimental design. The resulting framework is fully specified, falsifiable, and implementable with open-source tools and standard instrumentation. It reclassifies the design problem from optimizing a material to programming an evolving microenvironment, and because the temporal program is pre-encoded without biological sensing, it qualifies as a passive implant under current regulatory frameworks.

papers.title: Sustainable time-temperature integrator for perishable fresh foods based on polymer/graphene blends
papers.abstract: Monitoring the thermal history of perishable food products along the cold chain is critical to guarantee quality and safety for consumers. Time-temperature integrators (TTIs) offer solutions to guarantee cold chain efficiency, improve safety, and reduce food waste. Here, we present a sustainable TTI device based on the irreversible dehydration of a hydrogel, made of reduced graphene oxide and PEDOT:PSS, when exposed to varying environmental conditions. Dehydration kinetics of the hydrogel are investigated over a range of temperatures and relative humidity relevant to food-storage applications. The TTI response is quantified by the mass loss evolution which is interpreted by means of a kinetic model leveraging the initial hydrogel mass, the temperature and the relative humidity. The Arrhenius-like energy barrier is greater than the water binding enthalpy within the hydrogel, and the dehydration rate of the TTI device is finely tuned through the initial mass to mimic the microbial growth curve on fresh sea bream fillet. Deviations of the TTI from its evolution upon optimum conditions reveal the occurrence of a breach in the cold chain. We demonstrate that it is possible to translate the TTI assessment on a smartphone by imaging the evolution of shrinking of the projected area.

papers.title: Unusual reactivities of “NONO” calix[4]arene aluminum complexes
papers.abstract: Reaction of dibenzylaminocalix[4]arene, L1H2, with aluminum alkyls did not lead to deprotonation of both phenolic groups but provided aluminum or aluminate complexes containing phenolic OH or anilinium NH2 + groups in the presence of aluminum alkyl groups. Upon heating aluminum complexes L1AlMe and L1AlCl were obtained. Reaction of L1AlMe with amines led to amido complexes, either of the ancillary amine or the aniline moiety of L1. Further reaction with isopropanol yielded L1AlOiPr. Heating in the absence of amine afforded the phenyl complex L1AlC6D5 by activation of the NMR solvent. Reaction with two equivalents of AlMe3 led to -H abstraction from methyl to form methylene-bridged (L1-2H)(AlMe)2CH2. Reactions of bis(S,S-2-(dimethylamino)cyclohexyl)amino) calix[4]arene, L2H2, with AlEt2Cl or AlMe3 led directly to the anilido complex (L2-H)Al. Reaction with two equivalents of AlMe3 yielded (L2-2H)Al2CH2 after -H abstraction from methyl. Both compounds reacted with isopropanol to form L2AlOiPr. Isopropoxide complexes L1AlOiPr and L2AlOiPr were moderately active in lactide polymerization (yielding essentially atactic polylactide) and the Meerwein-Ponndorf-Verley reduction of benzophenone. Reaction of methylene-bridged (L2-2H)Al2CH2 with benzophenone afforded diphenylethylene in transition-metal-free methylenation.

papers.title: ChiroptMap: Orbital-Cube-Free Transition-Moment Density Maps from Gaussian and ORCA
papers.abstract: Earlier cube-based workflows generated electric-and magnetic-dipole transition-moment maps from molecular-orbital cubes exported with Gaussian cubegen from formatted-checkpoint data. ChiroptMap instead evaluates canonical orbitals and analytical derivatives blockwise from Gaussian WFX or an ORCA output/JSON/WFX bridge, eliminating intermediate orbital cubes while retaining final visualization cubes and S1–S6 CPL CSV values. Across ten Gaussian S1 TDA/TD-DFT cases, the median MDTM norm discrepancy decreased from 1.214% to 0.0541%, whereas EDTM recovery was unchanged; five S1/TDA cross-engine benchmarks gave mean field differences of 1.061% (electric) and 1.774% (magnetic), and the retained footprint decreased by 99.17%. Independent coefficient-print and spatial-grid tests support IOp(9/40=4) for the tested state while requiring both sources of numerical convergence to be assessed.

papers.title: From Computational Chemistry to Generative Models: A Survey of AI-Driven Small-Molecule Drug Discovery
papers.abstract: Small-molecule drug discovery requires navigating enormous chemical space to identify candidates that are simultaneously potent, selective, synthetically accessible, and acceptable across pharmacokinetic and safety profiles; modern generative AI extends a long computational medicinal chemistry lineage that began with QSAR, pharmacophore modeling, and early structure-based de novo design. This survey focuses primarily on developments from 2017 to 2025, with the literature updated through 31 January 2026. Using a medicinal-chemistry lens, it first establishes the shared machinery of the field: molecular representations such as SMILES, SELFIES, graphs, fingerprints, three-dimensional coordinates, voxels, and latent vectors; commonly used datasets and benchmarks; and graph neural network encoders, including message-passing, directional, and equivariant architectures. We compare five principal generative mechanisms—autoregressive models, variational autoencoders, generative adversarial networks, normalizing flows, and diffusion models—together with reinforcement learning as a major goal-directed optimization framework. Across these approaches, we show that current methods offer complementary rather than interchangeable trade-offs, and we highlight recurring challenges, including validity versus synthesizability, limited prospective experimental validation, mode collapse and diversity loss, stereochemical and physical realism in three-dimensional design, computational cost, data scarcity, and the emerging convergence toward scaffold-conditioned generation, hybrid architectures, developability-aware optimization, and molecular foundation models.

papers.title: Synthesis of 5-Aminoisoxazolidines from Azetidine Nitrones via Formal Ring Expansion
papers.abstract: A formal ring-expansion reaction of azetidine nitrones has been developed for the synthesis of 5-aminoisoxazolidines. Nucleophilic addition of an amine, alcohol or water to an azetidine nitrone is proposed to initiate azetidine nitrone ring-opening followed by cyclization to the corresponding 5-membered ring. A variety of examples are presented highlighting the scope of the method as well as the differences in stereochemical preference between primary aniline and secondary amine nucleophiles. A two-step, one-pot process is also described for the direct conversion of N-alkenylnitrones to 5-aminoisoxazolidines.

papers.title: Regularized Alternatives to Conventional Density Fitting: Tikhonov Regularization with Discrete Picard Condition
papers.abstract: Density fitting (DF) reduces the computational cost of correlated electronic-structure methods but can become unstable when the fitting metric contains small eigenvalues or near-linear dependencies. We introduce a set of protocols based on Tikhonov regularization (TR) combined with the Discrete Picard Condition (DPC) to adaptively determine an effective truncation of the auxiliary space in DF-MP2. Truncation indices are selected using either a two-line L-curve fit or local sharp-corner protocols. The TR-DPC approaches are evaluated against conventional DF-MP2 and Cholesky decomposition (CD) across the S22 benchmark set and an AlkB hydrogen-atom-transfer reaction. The three-point sharp-corner methods provide the best overall accuracy among the TR-DPC protocols, while the two-line method is less accurate but more robust for reduced or poorly matched auxiliary spaces. CD provides the closest agreement with conventional DF-MP2; however, for the systems examined here, it generates more Cholesky vectors than the number of functions in the corresponding DF auxiliary basis and is accompanied by greater computational cost. TR-DPC provides a useful alternative by reducing the effective auxiliary representation while maintaining small, often sub-kcal mol⁻¹, errors, providing a balance between accuracy, representation size, and computational cost.

papers.title: Evaluating a Lightweight Neural Network for Aggregate Isotope Distribution Prediction
papers.abstract: Isotope distribution prediction is an important part of mass spectrometry data analysis. A variety of strategies have been developed, including brute-force polynomial methods and Fourier-transform (FT) convolution methods. Here, we present a novel neural network (NN) approach to isotope prediction. These NN-based tools are distributed in a new package, IsoGen, alongside FT-based tools. We show that NNs perform as well as existing approaches when predicting isotope distributions for molecules with natural isotope ratios. We then demonstrate the capability of NNs for transfer learning, a method by which existing models that have been trained to perform one task can be reused as a starting point to train models to perform a second task. Here, a NN that has been trained to predict isotope distributions for molecules with natural isotope ratios can be retrained to predict distributions for molecules with perturbed isotope ratios. We also demonstrate that these training distributions do not need to be produced theoretically but may be extracted from experimental data where the underlying isotopic composition is not known. Overall, NNs provide a robust method for isotope prediction that can be extended to applications where the isotope distributions can be measured but not easily predefined.

papers.title: Temperature-and pressure-dependent water stabilization of CO dimerization on Cu(100)
papers.abstract: The electrochemical CO(2) reduction reaction offers a pathway to producing fuels and high-value chemicals from waste CO2 using renewable electricity. Among known catalysts, only copper in aqueous electrolytes enables the formation of C2+ products with high activity. The process of the C-C coupling is believed to be limited by the dimerization of two adsorbed *CO to form a *OC-CO* intermediate. Experimental strategies to improve selectivity toward C2+ products have recently focused on increasing temperature and pressure in the system, but the origins of these effects remain poorly understood. In this work, the thermodynamic and kinetic stability of the *OC-CO* dimer at the electrochemical interface of Cu(100) has been investigated, as a function of temperature and pressure using machine-learning interatomic potentials trained on DFT data. Extended molecular dynamics simulations with an explicit aqueous interface show that increased water density stabilizes the *OC-CO* intermediate through increased hydrogen bonding between interfacial water and the dimer. In contrast, temperature has no direct effect on the CO–CO association barrier, but instead indirectly influences reactivity by destabilizing *CO adsorption. Introducing a potassium cation leads to a large reduction in the interface work function, but only minor changes were observed in the energetics of the dimer formation. No correlation between cation-dimer distance and energetics is observed, suggesting a limited role of local field effects. These results identify hydrogen bonding as the key factor governing the stabilization of the *OC-CO* intermediate under experimental conditions. This work demonstrates how machine-learning interatomic potentials can facilitate systematic analysis of dynamic interfaces, and can be a powerful tool in theoretical exploration of electrolyte effects on reaction intermediates across extended time and length scales.

papers.title: Domino and Cascade Reactions in Sustainable Synthesis: Activation Modes, Assessment Boundaries, and the Molecular-Process Discrepancy
papers.abstract: Domino and cascade reactions construct molecular complexity through sequential transformations and can reduce intermediate isolation. Their contribution to sustainable synthesis depends on whether these advantages persist when precursor preparation, catalyst production, reaction operation, and product recovery are included. This targeted narrative review examines thirteen mechanistic examples across seven activation or propagation modes and develops the molecular-process discrepancy (MPD) as a framework for testing that translation. MPD connects a specific reaction-level claim to the additional material and energy requirements introduced by expanding the assessment boundary. It complements atom economy, process mass intensity, E-factor, life-cycle assessment, and process benchmarks without replacing their measurements. Four case studies distinguish the roles of feedstock and product recovery in Ambrox synthesis, oxidant substitution in coumestan formation, advanced-substrate preparation in lasalocid A biosynthesis, and operational consolidation in oseltamivir synthesis. Together, they show why atom conservation, selective ring construction, and fewer isolations provide different forms of efficiency that must be evaluated separately. The analysis identifies precursor access, dilution, separation, catalyst lifetime, and heat, light, or oxygen delivery as specific targets for process improvement. MPD provides a procedure for determining whether a proposed cascade advantage is retained, attenuated, reversed, or unresolved across explicit assessment boundaries.

papers.title: Comparative Study of Y2O3, ZnO, and CeO2 Additions to Magnesium Aluminosilicate Glasses: Composition–Structure–Property Relationships
papers.abstract: The development of high-modulus glasses is essential for advanced lightweight applications, requiring a fundamental understanding of how different oxide components dictate elastic performance. To maximize stiffness, oxides must be strategically introduced to enhance both network connectivity and volumetric packing density; hence, Y 2 O 3 , ZnO, and CeO 2 are investigated here due to their high single-bond dissociation energies and strong cationic field strengths. Magnesium aluminosilicate glasses (MAS) modified with Y 2 O 3 , ZnO, and CeO 2 were systematically investigated to establish composition–structure–property relationships. A constrained ternary mixture design (Y 2 O 3 –ZnO–CeO 2 = 14 wt.%) was used to span the compositional space efficiently. The measured Young’s modulus ranged from 97.5 to 113.8 GPa, while the specific modulus varied between 36.6 and 41.7 ×10 6 N·m/kg. The highest values were obtained for compositions adding Y 2 O 3 alone or Y 2 O 3 –ZnO. Raman spectroscopy revealed systematic changes in the Si–O stretching band, including shifts in band position and variations in band width depending on composition. These changes indicate structural reorganization of the glass network. A moderate correlation between Raman peak position and Young’s modulus confirms that structural connectivity effects contribute to stiffness, although additional factors such as packing density and cation field strength are also relevant. The results demonstrate that Y 2 O 3 is the most effective oxide for increasing stiffness, ZnO exhibits composition-dependent behaviour, and CeO 2 reduces the specific modulus. The combined analysis provides an experimental and structural basis to designing high-modulus glass systems.

papers.title: Globally Aromatic 10-Boratetraoxacorroles: Boron-Doped Macrocyclic Chromophores with Intense Red-to-Near-Infrared Emission
papers.abstract: Neutral, globally aromatic boron-containing macrocycles are exceptionally rare, with the 10-bora-21,22,23,24-tetraoxacorroles reported herein representing only the second class of such compounds known to date, following the 5-bora-21,22-dioxaporphyrin we recently described, and are also the first neutral, globally aromatic boracorroles. Here, we present a furan-based 10-bora-21,22,23,24-tetraoxacorrole and an oxadiborepin-fused derivative thereof. The global aromaticity of both macrocyclic boranes in the neutral state is supported by experimental data and NICS and ACID cal­culations. They exhibit intense absorption spanning the ultraviolet to near-infrared (NIR) regions of the electromagnetic spectrum. Notably, the novel boracorroles display bright red and red-to-NIR fluorescence, achiev­ing quantum yields more than twice (Φ fl = 35–46%) that of conventional triphenylcorrole (Φ fl = 19%). DFT analysis reveals that the frontier orbital en­ergies are strongly modulated by the meso- B atom, generating a large HOMO to HOMO−1 energy gap and, consequently, mark­edly enhanced Q-band extinction coefficients arising from the predominantly single-configurational character of the S 0 →S 1 transition (HOMO to LUMO). Incorporation of the BOB bridge in the oxadiborepin-fused derivative significantly stabilizes the LUMO, giving rise to red-shifted absorption and emission alongside distinct electrochemical behavior. In addition, the BOB unit further amplifies the global aromaticity of the boracorrole, underscoring efficient π-conjugation across this heteroatomic bridge.

papers.title: AQ-GNoME: an Aqueous Stability Augmentation of the GNoME Database
papers.abstract: Aqueous stability is a fundamental requirement for materials used in electrochemical energy technologies, yet no systematic Pourbaix stability screening has been performed for Google DeepMind’s GNoME database of more than 520,000 novel inorganic crystals. Here, we introduce AQ-GNoME, an aqueous-stability augmentation of the GNoME database, enabling systematic shortlisting of GNoME candidates for electrochemical applications. The database additionally includes machine-learning-based substitutional-disorder predictions and Herfindahl–Hirschman Index supply-risk metrics, thereby supporting structural-order and supply-risk based filtering. User-defined criteria across electrochemical potential and pH, elemental composition, structural order, and supply concentration reduce the database to a manageable, project-specific shortlist. We apply AQ-GNoME to identify GNoME materials relevant for further investigation in electrochemical CO2 reduction (eCO2RR) and acidic oxygen evolution (OER), focusing on candidates absent from the Materials Project and ICSD. For eCO2RR, combining aqueous stability criteria with a compositional heuristic intended to mimic copper’s selectivity, we identify 8 ordered multimetallic candidates. For acidic OER, combining stability and supply-concentration criteria, we identify 39 Ir-lean oxides, of which 26 are metallic under HSE06 DFT. AQ-GNoME therefore provides a practical framework for electrochemical materials discovery within GNoME, reducing the search space from more than half a million compounds to experimentally tractable candidate sets.

papers.title: A Library of Iron and α-Ketoglutarate Dependent Dioxygenases Enables the Synthesis of Six Fungal Natural Products
papers.abstract: Achieving selective oxygenation chemistry offers a powerful strategy for streamlining routes to complex target molecules, yet the development of site-selective C-H functionalization reactions remain a significant challenge. Several enzyme families are capable of catalyzing C-H hydroxylation reactions and, in principle, provide an attractive solution for achieving selective oxidative transformations. In practice, however, the difficulty of identifying a biocatalyst suited to a specific synthetic target often renders chemoenzymatic strategies impractical. For example, biosynthetic enzymes such as CitB and ClaD can mediate site-selective benzylic hydroxylation, enabling access to select natural products that share structural features with their native substrates. Nonetheless, such approaches typically lack generality and do not readily extend to broader collections of natural products. Here, we explore the previously unstudied natural sequence space of the hydroxylases CitB and ClaD to generate a bespoke panel of uncharacterized enzymes that collectively expand the scope of this chemoenzymatic strategy. Development of this curated biocatalyst panel enabled the synthesis of six natural products, demonstrating that assembling this enzyme collection effectively derisks the use of biocatalysis in synthetic campaigns.

papers.title: Chemoenzymatic synthesis of (E,E,Z)-humulene derived natural products
papers.abstract: Among the >300 skeletally distinct products derived from farnesyl pyrophosphate (FPP) reported to date, meroterpenoids derived from the humulene core are of great interest due to their potent biological activities. Whereas the most available (E,E,E)-humulene core and derivatives thereof have been well-studied, comparatively little is known of the chemistry and biological properties of the related (E,E,Z)-core and natural products derived from this humulene isomer. Herein, we detail the first synthesis of (E,E,Z)-(10S)-hydroxyhumulene and elaborate this macrocycle through a chemoenzymatic route to (±)-deoxyeupenifeldin and neosetophomone B, and further accomplish the chemical synthesis of pughiinin A. The (E,E,Z)-(10S)-hydroxyhumulene was accessed via a selective oxidative double-bond isomerization from the (E,E,E)-humulene core. Additionally, when studying this macrocycle in subsequent hetero-Diels Alder (hDA) cycloadditions, it was observed that the (E,E,Z)-core imparted more biased diastereoselectivity when compared to previous studies of the corresponding (E,E,E)-core. Our findings demonstrate scalable access to (E,E,Z)-(10S)-hydroxyhumulene and the ability to build meroterpene natural products from this humulene isomer.

papers.title: Constructing safe and highly potent antiviral neutralising nanodevices using a ferritin-based plug-and-play molecular assembly platform
papers.abstract: Viral infections are a global threat. Vaccines and antiviral drugs take years to develop, and few options exist for rapid response to viral outbreaks. To address this gap in pandemic preparedness, we advance a “plug-and-play” nanocage assembly platform for constructing antiviral nanodevices (AVNs), defined as nanocages that physically bind viral surface glycoproteins and block entry and infection. Using a multidisciplinary approach combining molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, biochemical assays, Cryo-EM structural analysis, and antiviral assays, we show that different antiviral lectins can be genetically fused to assembly precursors designed by linking two ferritin subunits with an intrinsically disordered peptide (IDP) containing an enterokinase cleavage site. The resulting precursors significantly improved (>2-fold) lectin binding to glycans and assembled into AVNs with a core structure resembling a ferritin nanocage. We show that AVNs have potent activity against influenza A virus (IAV) (IC50 values < 1 nM), with no toxicity observed in ex vivo precision-cut lung slices (PCLS). Our data revealed insight into precursor design rules and suggest a stepwise mechanism of nanocage assembly. These findings pave the way for using AVNs to develop novel antiviral preventive strategies and provide fundamental insights into nanocage assembly.

papers.title: Understanding Differential Chemical Activities of Eutectic Gallium Indium (eGaIn) Thin Films with Fluorinated Analytes using Raman Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Gallium oxide (Ga2O3) forms on the surface of eutectic gallium indium (eGaIn) alloy in air; In the presence of water, it transforms to gallium oxide monohydroxide, GaO(OH). During such transformation, it is challenging to differentiate the activities of the oxides while adsorbing solutes from the solvent. Herein, we address this challenge by investigating the temporal evolution of eGaIn thin films during adsorption of dilute organofluorines in water. We identify five hours as the stability threshold to obtain a water-modified thin film. Leveraging both fresh and five-hour-modified films in parallel, we distinguish water-specific changes and differentiate the signals uniquely caused by fluorinated analytes. The modified GaO(OH) interface demonstrates increased hydrophilicity for microdroplet studies and structural stability under high-energy (20 kV) electron beam irradiation. We leverage Frontier Molecular Orbital (FMO) theory to predict that the GaO(OH) surface is also a reactive catalytic interface. In the presence of the GaO(OH) surface and UVA irradiation, short-chain (HFBA) and long-chain (PFOA) fluorinated compounds exhibited altered interfacial activity. We leveraged Raman spectroscopy throughout our study to differentiate the in situ activities of Ga2O3 and GaO(OH). Our investigations will be useful for differentiating fresh and modified oxide dynamics during in situ interfacial studies or wet chemical measurements.

papers.title: Dynamic Oxygen-Vacancy Redistribution Regulates the Structural Evolution and Stability of Supported Au Nanoparticles
papers.abstract: Supported metal nanoparticles (NPs) on reducible oxides are widely employed as heterogeneous catalysts, where the metal-support interaction plays a pivotal role in determining catalytic activity, stability, and resistance to sintering. Oxygen vacancies (Ovs) in cerium oxide (CeO2-x) are known to modify the electronic and structural properties of the support; however, how their redistribution regulates the structural evolution and stability of supported metal nanoparticles at the atomic scale remains poorly understood. Here, by combining molecular dynamics simulations, density functional theory calculations, and experimental observations, we show that Ovs are preferentially distributed in the second oxygen layer rather than the outermost surface and undergo temperature-dependent redistribution. Increasing Ov concentration induces a pronounced size-dependent structural reconstruction of supported Au NPs, with smaller NPs exhibiting greater flattening associated with enhanced interfacial electron transfer. Meanwhile, vacancy-enhanced metal-support interactions restrict NP mobility and improve resistance to sintering. Under H2O-containing conditions, water dissociation further stabilizes the NPs through surface H species while triggering extensive oxygen redistribution within the CeO2-x lattice. The second oxygen layer accommodates substantial changes in oxygen population while preserving a relatively stable electronic environment, highlighting its role as a dynamic oxygen reservoir. These results establish a unified picture in which oxygen-vacancy dynamics couple support restructuring with the morphology and mobility of supported Au NPs, offering an atomic-scale basis for designing sintering-resistant metal/oxide catalysts.

papers.title: Bayesian reaction optimization with fixed MaleCNS features: performance, wiring controls, and reward–aversion diagnostics
papers.abstract: Connectome-derived features provide one possible representation for reaction optimization, but their utility need not depend on measured neuronal pairing. We examine a Bayesian predictor using fixed mushroom-body features derived from MaleCNS connectivity, with observed prediction errors separated into engineered reward and aversion signals. An offline evaluator returns only selected recorded outcomes. We distinguish this predictor from earlier models that modify KC–MBON efficacy incrementally or reconstruct it from observed response ranks. The rank comparison changes both the learning head and acquisition rule. In the exploratory predictive-model evaluation, the mean best response over post-initial observations exceeded rank reconstruction by 0.486 percentage points on C–N coupling and 3.346 on Suzuki–Miyaura coupling. Differences from development-tuned Gaussian-process optimization were smaller, and their cluster-bootstrap intervals included zero. Native-versusrewired intervals also included zero. C–N responses were analytical yields; Suzuki responses were UV-area percentages. High/low response diagnostics separate input-dependent KC activity from outcome-dependent prediction updates: circuit activity remains fixed under an identical-cue outcome intervention. Reused datasets and input ensembles, and one rewired graph restrict inference. These results support evaluating anatomical representation, learning rule, search performance, and prediction accuracy separately; they establish neither statistical equivalence nor a unique advantage of native connectivity.

papers.title: Fluorinated Olefins as Traceless Linchpins for Modular Non-Directed C–H Alkenylation Reactions
papers.abstract: Palladium-catalyzed non-directed C–H olefination provides an attractive strategy for the direct functionalization of simple arenes, yet its modularity is typically limited by the need for prefunctionalized olefin coupling partners. Here, we report an unconventional tracelesslinchpin strategy using bromo-difluoromethyl-substituted olefins for the modular synthesis of cinnamic acid esters. In contrast to the expected formation of fluorinated alkenes, the fluorinated olefin undergoes palladium-catalyzed non-directed C–H functionalization followed by defluorinative transformation in the presence of alcohols, furnishing the corresponding cinnamic acid esters. The method tolerates a broad range of fluorinated and non-fluorinated alcohols as well as structurally diverse arenes, providing access to products in generally good to excellent yields and useful regioselectivities. The modular nature of the transformation further enables the late-stage functionalization of pharmaceutically relevant molecules and the direct synthesis of drug–drug and drug–natural product conjugates. Mechanistic studies support an initial C–H functionalization with the fluorinated olefin, followed by subsequent conversion of the resulting intermediate into the corresponding cinnamic acid esters.

papers.title: The impact of configurational disorder on electronic structure of perovskite oxides
