papers.abstract: Compositionally complex perovskite oxides provide a broad design space for catalytic materials, yet the electronic consequences of configurational disorder remain insufficiently understood. Here, we use high-throughput density functional theory calculations to systematically investigate how B-site compositional complexity modifies the local electronic structure of perovskite oxides across single-metal, binary, and quinary compositions. We analyze electronic descriptors relevant to catalytic activity, including transition-metal eg occupancy, d-band center, oxygen p-band center, and metal–oxygen d–p overlap. Based on data mining of DFT electronic structures for 4,035 compositionally disordered perovskites, we demonstrate that configurational disorder gives rise to distributions of local electronic states originating from heterogeneous coordination environments. As a result, transition metals with electronic and oxidation-state flexibility can access substantially broadened electronic configurations. Compositional complexity also expands the range of accessible metal–oxygen interactions, although the magnitude and direction of this effect vary among constituent elements. These results establish a distribution-based description of electronic structure for compositionally disordered perovskites and highlight local-environment statistics as a key dimension for understanding and tuning the catalytic electronic structure of disordered oxides.

papers.title: Electrochemical Metastability of Au–Pd Alloy Nanoparticles: Interplay between Alloying, Surface Structure, and Halide-Induced Dissolution
papers.abstract: Understanding the dissolution of alloy nanoparticles in corrosive environments is essential for designing stable electrocatalysts. In this study, we investigate the corrosion behavior of AuxPdy nanoparticles in halide-containing electrolytes using cyclic voltammetry combined with ICPMS quantification of dissolved metals. The results demonstrate that metal dissolution depends on the complexing strength of the halide ions. Alloying Pd with Au significantly suppresses Pd dissolution within the potential range where Au remains stable against dissolution. Conversely, increasing the Pd content shifts Au oxidation to lower potentials, suggesting that while Au stabilizes Pd, Pd reduces the electrochemical oxidation stability of Au. The experimental results are interpreted using DFT simulations based on a previously proposed model for predicting dissolution thermodynamics. Together, the experimental and theoretical results provide mechanistic insight into the metastability of alloy electrocatalysts and the critical role of electrolyte composition in governing metal dissolution.

papers.title: Particle-Size Modulated MOFs for Fluorescent PFAS Sensing
papers.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) require sensitive and accessible detection technologies to complement conventional laboratory-based analytical methods. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as promising fluorescence sensing platforms owing to their high surface areas, tunable pore environments, and versatile host-guest interactions. To date, efforts to improve MOF-based PFAS sensing have primarily focused on framework chemistry and pore engineering, while the role of particle size has remained largely unexplored. Here, we systematically investigate the influence of particle size on PFAS fluorescence sensing using NU-1000 as a model fluorescent MOF platform. A series of NU-1000 particles with sizes ranging from approximately 300 nm to 10 μm were synthesized while maintaining comparable crystallinity, porosity, morphology, and chemical composition. Fluorescence measurements revealed a pronounced particle-size dependence, with smaller particles exhibiting substantially enhanced responses toward perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS), and perfluorodecanoic acid (PFDA). Reducing the particle size from 2 μm to 300 nm lowered the limits of detection by approximately one-half, from 311.4 to 153.8 ppb for PFOA, from 282.0 to 145.3 ppb for PFOS, and from 615.4 to 269.4 ppb for PFDA. Mechanistic investigations showed that the observed size effect does not arise from differences in PFAS uptake. Instead, decreasing particle size increases the surface-to-volume ratio, resulting in a larger fraction of surface-accessible Zr6 adsorption sites and emissive TBAPy linkers that induces more efficient fluorescence signal generation. Consequently, PFAS adsorption events are converted into more substantial fluorescence responses despite comparable overall uptake. These findings identify particle size as a previously overlooked design parameter governing MOF-based fluorescence sensing and demonstrate that particle-size engineering offers a simple, effective, and broadly applicable strategy for enhancing sensing performance without altering framework chemistry or pore architecture.

papers.title: Covalently Functionalized Two-Dimensional Red Phosphorus Nanosheets: Efficient Platform for Broad-Spectrum Biofilm Eradication
papers.abstract: Red phosphorus (RP) has gained considerable attention owing to its high chemical stability and narrow band gap, making it a promising material for applications in photocatalysis, energy storage, and related areas. Covalent functionalization has emerged as an effective approach to enhance the surface reactivity, dispersibility, and chemical stability of nanomaterials. Herein, we report covalently modified RP nanosheets prepared using aryl diazonium molecules as organic ligands. The functionalized RP nanosheets (f-RPNS) exhibit better colloidal stability and dispersibility compared to pristine RP nanosheets. The in vitro antibiofilm studies of f-RPNS, with and without NIR irradiation, demonstrated that the covalently modified RPNS can eradicate drug-resistant bacterial biofilms even in the absence of photothermal treatment. We highlight the potential of f-RPNS across various biomedical fields, particularly in biofilm eradication.

papers.title: Bioisosteric Design of Novel Flavonoid-Derived Aromatase Inhibitors to Reduce Estradiol Biosynthesis in ER+ Breast Cancer
papers.abstract: Estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) breast cancer is a hormonal cancer in which tumor proliferation is dependent on estrogen via androgen-to-estrogen conversion, facilitated by the aromatase enzyme (CYP19A1). Aromatase inhibitors (AIs) are often first-line treatments for ER+ breast cancer, yet the three FDA-approved agents present potentially mitigable pharmacological issues and distinct side-effect profiles. To expand structural diversity and improve pharmacological properties, a computational hit-to-lead pipeline was executed. A virtual hit screen of ten selected natural flavonoids against human aromatase (PDB ID: 3S79) across 100 dockings revealed Chrysin consistently outperformed other flavonoid ligands on all measured thermodynamic metrics, with 51% of poses scoring an energy (ΔG) ≤ -5.9 kcal/mol. Using target-based and bioisosteric substitution, a lead series of Chrysin-based analogs called Arcflavonoids (ARC) was engineered in PyMOL. SwissADME predicted the optimized ARC series was leadlike and features reduced cross-inhibition of the major drug-processing CYP450 enzymes, relative to existing commercial AIs. Utilizing comparative molecular docking against both historic and current-generation AIs, we observed that all leads demonstrated steroidal cleft coordination and no heme-iron interaction. Through steroidal cleft interaction, a top lead, ARC48, achieved a predicted ΔG < -10.00 kcal/mol and an inhibition constant (Ki) of 10.34 nM. This optimized, non-steroidal series offers a promising strategy to mitigate adverse reactions from historical AIs.

papers.title: Theoretical insights into B-site homonuclear dual-atom doping in LaMnO3 for CO chemical looping combustion
papers.abstract: Perovskite oxides have emerged as promising oxygen carriers (OCs) for chemical looping combustion (CLC), where their catalytic behaviour can be effectively regulated through compositional engineering. In this work, a first-principles-based strategy was developed to uncover the role of B-site homonuclear dual-atom incorporation in modulating the CO oxidation activity of LaMnO3. Twenty-four doped configurations were systematically screened, leading to the identification of eight energetically favourable structures for subsequent catalytic investigation. Detailed electronic-structure analyses revealed that dual-atom doping alters CO adsorption characteristics and facilitates surface oxidation processes. Kinetic evaluation demonstrated that four doped systems, namely V2–LaMnO3(O1), V2–LaMnO3(O2), Ni2–LaMnO3(O1), and Ni2–LaMnO3(O2), outperform pristine LaMnO3, with Ni2–LaMnO3(O2) achieving the lowest CO oxidation barrier of 0.666 eV, corresponding to a 67% reduction. The structural stability of these highly active catalysts under CLC operating temperatures was further verified by ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations. Furthermore, descriptor analysis established that dopant-induced charge-transfer energy and Bader charge transfer provide reliable criteria for predicting catalytic performance. These findings elucidate the electronic origin of enhanced CO oxidation induced by B-site homonuclear dual-atom doping and offer a rational framework for designing advanced perovskite OCs for efficient CLC.

papers.title: Explicit and Parallelised Octupole and Hexadecapole Moment Interactions in Flexible Smooth Particle Mesh Ewald
papers.abstract: Long-range electrostatic interactions have long been known to be important in the accurate simulation of biomolecular systems and molecular crystals. Despite this fact, these interactions are absent in many machine learning force fields aiming to improve upon classical potentials. In the worst cases, this omission can lead to serious discrepancies with experimental results. FFLUX is a machine learning force field that predicts atomic energies and multipole moments up to the hexadecapole moment on-the-fly during molecular dynamics simulations. The predicted multipole moments are fed into an adapted smooth particle mesh Ewald algorithm allowing long-range electrostatic interactions to be calculated. Here we present refactoring of the Ewald routines and a new implementation of routines handling interactions involving octupole and hexadecapole moments. The new implementation leads to a speed-up of up to 10.5 times in serial compared to our previous implementation. Additionally, a hybrid parallelisation scheme using a combination of Message Passing Interface and OpenMP is made available to these high-electrostatic-rank calculations. This parallelisation offers speed-ups of up to two orders of magnitude, improving the feasibility of bulk simulations with high-rank electrostatic interactions using FFLUX force fields.

papers.title: Area-Selective Deposition of WS2 via Sacrificial ZnS Conversion at Low Temperatures
papers.abstract: 2D transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) offer a promising path forward as standard silicon technology approaches its physical scaling limits. However, integrating TMDCs into semiconductor manufacturing requires precise, back-end-of-line (BEOL)-compatible deposition methods. Area-selective deposition (ASD) enables direct bottom-up patterning, yet achieving surface-selective growth of tungsten disulfide (WS 2 ) under low thermal budgets remains a significant challenge. Here, we demonstrate a thermally driven ASD route for ultra-thin WS 2 films at 400°C, using tungsten(VI) sulfide tetrachloride (WSCl 4 ) and H 2 S as precursors and leveraging the unique reactivity of the halogenated, sulfur-containing metal precursor to drive selective ligand exchange and conversion. This approach uses a sacrificial, ultra-thin ZnS template layer to guide spatial selectivity. The process selectively converts pre-deposited ZnS into high-quality WS 2 at 400°C while completely suppressing growth on adjacent dielectrics. Applied to 200 mm undoped silicate glass (USG) / Si(100) wafers, this precursor combination yields pure, smooth, ultra-thin (< 10 nm) crystalline WS 2 films with predominantly horizontally oriented layers. The surface conversion mechanism shows remarkable chemical contrast, with high selectivity (S > 0.994) over 1200 deposition cycles, with USG as a non-growth area (NGA). Electrical measurements on tungsten-contacted transmission-line structures show functional behavior, yielding a layer resistivity of 2.9 × 10 7 µΩ·cm and a specific contact resistivity of 5.4×10 -3 Ω·cm 2 for ~7.5 nm WS 2 films. By leveraging sacrificial template conversion to enable highly selective, low-temperature thermal ASD of WS 2 , this work provides a scalable, chemistry-driven, direct, bottom-up integration of 2D materials into future advanced semiconductor device architectures.

papers.title: Information Thresholds in Adaptive Quantum Control of Nonadiabatic Molecular Dynamics:
papers.abstract: Ultrafast photochemical reactions can undergo strongly nonadiabatic dynamics near conical intersections, where electronic and nuclear degrees of freedom become coupled and conventional descriptions based on electronic populations alone may become insufficient for control. This paper proposes an information-aware framework for adaptive quantum control in which the information supplied to a controller is treated as an explicit experimental variable. Using a benchmark four-mode linear vibronic-coupling model of pyrazine, the proposed computational study compares control performance across a hierarchy of information levels, from final reaction outcomes and electronic populations to nuclear observables, electronic coherences, and complete quantum-state information. The central hypothesis is that the minimum information required to achieve a specified control fidelity depends on proximity to the nonadiabatic branching region. This is formalized through an information-threshold function relating control fidelity to conical-intersection proximity, with particular emphasis on the marginal benefit of coherence and nuclear information. The manuscript provides a reproducible computational protocol, including pulse parameterization, optimization, information ablation, control objectives, validation criteria, and falsification tests. No simulations or new numerical calculations are reported; the numerical predictions are explicitly identified as hypotheses requiring future computational testing.

papers.title: A residue-50 crystallographic B-factor scalar tracks catalytic-efficiency ordering across HG Kemp eliminase evolution
papers.abstract: Active-site pre-organisation is a well-characterised contributor to enzyme catalysis, and progressive rigidification of catalytic residues during HG-series Kemp eliminase evolution — including decreasing structure-normalised B-factor Z-scores at the position-50 residue — has already been reported directly from room-temperature crystallography (Broom et al., 2020). The contribution here is therefore not that observation, but a bounded quantitative test of how completely a single compact scalar recovers catalytic-efficiency ordering within an HG Kemp eliminase series, together with an explicit account of where that scalar fails to transfer. In the primary HG dataset — five room-temperature structures from the directed-evolution series plus the separately engineered variant HG4 — the residue-50 side-chain scalar correlated with log10(kcat/KM) at r = −0.9899 (p = 1.52 × 10-4) and reproduced the catalytic-efficiency ordering of the archived scalar values exactly (Spearman ρ = −1.000; exact two-sided permutation p = 0.0028). Restricting the analysis to the five evolutionary-series variants gave r = −0.9893. The association is robust to the choice of published kinetic dataset. In four independently designed HG variants the multi-residue active-site scalar was directionally negative (r = −0.7759) but weak on a rank basis (ρ = −0.400; exact two-sided p = 0.75) and is treated as neither replication nor support of comparable weight. Application of the same extraction logic to an independent KE07 scaffold failed a pre-committed robustness criterion and is reported as a negative transfer result. Two distinct sensitivities are separated there: a normalization correction, and an additional dependence on which deposited structure represents each variant across all 48 pre-declared combinations. We do not claim that the specificity of the primary single-residue scalar has been established: the archived negative controls were computed on a four-residue active-site average, not on the primary scalar, and their generating workflow is not fully archived. B-factors are treated throughout as operational crystallographic observables rather than as measurements of solution dynamics. The result is a narrowly scoped, reproducible descriptive reanalysis of public data with a clearly documented limit on transfer — not a causal mechanism, a specificity demonstration, or a generalisation to other reaction classes.

papers.title: Surface-Induced Constraint Release in Confined Polymer Films: A Computational Phenomenological Study
papers.abstract: Thin polymer films exhibit thickness-dependent viscoelastic behavior attributed to enhanced segmental mobility near free surfaces, a phenomenon recently linked to surface-induced constraint release (SICR) in entangled polymer melts. While self-consistent theoretical treatments of this mechanism exist, computationally lightweight phenomenological models that isolate the role of specific structural assumptions remain comparatively underexplored. This work showcases a developed closed-form, depth-resolved generalized Maxwell model in which local relaxation times are derived from a depth-dependent entanglement molecular weight profile, motivated by reptation scaling () and literature-reported surface entanglement enhancement ratios. With this framework, we directly compare two assumptions for combining depth-dependent relaxation behavior into an effective film modulus: a depth-independent linear superposition, and an entanglement-coupled, double-reptation-inspired mixing rule. Holding the underlying relaxation-time profile identical between both models, we find that the choice of coupling mechanism alters the predicted storage modulus by up to ~40%, with the divergence peaking at an intermediate film thickness rather than increasing monotonically as films thin. This work shows that the peak location is associated with, though not fully predicted by, the frequency-dependent heterogeneity of local relaxation times across the film. These results indicate that depth-coupling assumptions in phenomenological thin-film rheology models are not a minor implementation detail, but materially and non-trivially shape predicted thickness-dependent behavior, with implications for how such models should be constructed and interpreted going forward.

papers.title: Intramolecular Alkene Protonation Enables Stereoconvergent Catalysis Through Tertiary Carbenium Ions
papers.abstract: Enantioselective trapping of tertiary carbenium ions is often complicated by competing E1 elimination. Here, we show that a chiral oxazaborolidinium ion catalyst promotes ground-state intramolecular proton transfer from a phenolic OH group to an adjacent alkene, generating a catalyst-associated tertiary carbenium ion for enantioselective trapping. This activation mode allows alkenes formed by E1 elimination to regenerate reactive cations during the stereoconvergent conversion of racemic tertiary alcohols. Hydride and carbon trapping afford enantioenriched diarylalkanes and products bearing acyclic all-carbon quaternary stereocenters in up to 99% yield and 99% ee. Experimental and computational studies support competition between direct cation trapping and elimination followed by alkene protonation, with the balance depending on nucleophile reactivity. These findings establish intramolecular alkene protonation as a strategy for incorporating elimination into productive asymmetric catalysis.

papers.title: Synthesizing N-indole Carbamates via CO2 Valorization in o-difluorobenzene driven by pKa Values of N-H Covalent Bonds
papers.abstract: A green synthetic route for accessing N -indole carbamates, a key building block of bioactive molecules, can be achieved using indole and CO 2 . However, using strong bases results in low yields and reduced functional group tolerance, making it more challenging to develop milder reactions. The proton transfer from indole N-H bond to base is one of the essential steps in synthesizing N-indole carbamates, which is highly dependent on the driving force ΔG PT and their corresponding p K a values in the solution-state. In this study, the optimized condition was experimentally approved and driven by the ΔG PT values derived from the experimentally determined pKa values of 31 N–H covalent bonds in six polar fluorinated arenes, resulting in synthesizing N-indole carbamates in o-difluorobenzene promoted by MTBD via CO 2 valorization at room temperature, which is free of catalysts or additives and exhibits excellent functional group tolerance with moderate to excellent yields. Compared to commonly used organic solvents like THF and acetonitrile, the ΔG PT can be significantly reduced in o-difluorobenzene. And DFT analysis revealed that o-DFB can regulate the reaction mechanism through a pathway in which indole anionic intermediate formed before the activation of CO 2 .

papers.title: Free Amino Acids Decrease Beer Foam Stability
papers.abstract: Basic amino acids have previously been reported to impair beer foam adhesion and lacing. This study examined whether adverse effects of free amino acids on beer foam stability extend to non-basic amino acids. Concentration ranges (ΔC = Cmax − Cmin) were determined for individual amino acids in more than 200 production lots of a single Japanese pilsner brand collected across factories in 2016. Individual amino acids were added to fresh commercial beer at two supplementation levels, 2ΔC and 4ΔC, and foam stability was evaluated using the NIBEM-30 method. Compared with matched controls, lysine and histidine lowered NIBEM values at both supplementation levels, while arginine lowered the value at the higher level. A mixture of these basic amino acids also lowered NIBEM values. Crucially, reductions were also observed following supplementation with non-basic amino acids, including glutamine, glycine, proline, and γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA). In a separate evaluation, increasing laboratory ambient temperature from 20 to 27 °C shortened the measured collapse time by 19 s at a constant beer temperature of 20 °C, emphasizing the importance of controlling the measurement environment. These findings indicate that amino acids capable of reducing beer foam stability are not confined to basic amino acids: certain non-basic amino acids can also reduce foam stability under the tested supplementation conditions. 日本語要旨：塩基性アミノ酸は、ビールの泡の付着性およびレーシングを損なうことが従来報告されている。本研究では、遊離ア ミノ酸によるビールの泡安定性への悪影響が、非塩基性アミノ酸にも認められるかを検討した。2016年に複数の工場から収集した、 日本の単一ピルスナーブランドの200ロットを超える製品を対象として、各アミノ酸の濃度範囲（ΔC＝最高濃度－最低濃度）を求め た。新鮮な市販ビールに各アミノ酸を2ΔCおよび4ΔCの2水準で添加し、NIBEM-30法により泡安定性を評価した。対応する対照と比 較して、リシンとヒスチジンは両添加水準でNIBEM値を低下させ、アルギニンは高い添加水準で低下させた。これらの塩基性アミ ノ酸の混合物もNIBEM値を低下させた。特に、グルタミン、グリシン、プロリン、γ-アミノ酪酸（GABA）などの非塩基性アミノ酸 の添加でも、NIBEM値の低下が観察された。別途行った評価では、ビール温度を20 °Cに一定に保った状態で実験室の室温を20 °Cか ら27 °Cに上げると、測定された泡の崩壊時間が19秒短縮し、測定環境を管理する重要性が示された。これらの結果は、ビールの泡 安定性を低下させうるアミノ酸が塩基性アミノ酸に限られず、今回の添加条件では、一部の非塩基性アミノ酸も泡安定性を低下さ せうることを示している。

papers.title: Octahedral Ligand Field as Magnetic Coordinate Frame in a Luminescent DyIII Single Molecule Magnet
papers.abstract: The synthesis of lanthanide complexes with low coordination numbers is challenging because the large ionic radii of lanthanide ions generally promote the formation of highly coordinated species. Achieving lower coordination geometries requires introducing significant steric hindrance. We report two low coordinated, almost perfectly octahedral lanthanide complexes [LnIII(Ph3PO)4(HBS)2](OTf) (Ln = DyIII (1), YbIII (2) and NdIII (3), Ph3PO = triphenylphosphine oxide; HBS = 4-hydroxybenzenesulfonate). Their magnetic and temperature-dependent luminescent properties have been systematically investigated showing field induced Single Molecule Magnet behavior and f-f optical transitions. To rationalize these properties with Complete Active Space Spin Orbit Configuration Interaction calculations, we have extended our program to compute magnetic dipole oscillator strengths. We showed that the octahedral ligand field acts as the magnetic main axes, that small geometric distortions induce significant anisotropy and simulated luminescent and magnetic data in very good agreement with experiment.

papers.title: Biosynthetic Plausibility Mapper: Reaction-Aware Prioritization of Plant Metabolite Candidates Using Curated Pathway Context
papers.abstract: Untargeted plant metabolomics can generate numerous structurally plausible annotations and candidate structures, but structural similarity alone does not establish whether a compound is consistent with the biosynthetic context represented by the detected metabolome. Integrating curated biochemical relationships with chemical similarity could therefore provide an additional, interpretable layer for candidate prioritization. Here, we present Biosynthetic Plausibility Mapper (BPM), an open-source cheminformatics application that maps user-provided plant metabolite annotations onto a locally constructed PlantCyc-derived knowledge base and explicitly distinguishes detected compounds, curated pathway context, and computationally prioritized candidates. BPM integrates chemical-identity reconciliation, curated reaction and pathway relationships, structural similarity, and global-context coherence into a decomposable candidate-ranking framework. In pathway-based benchmarking against hard structural decoys, BPM v3.1 achieved AUROC and AUPRC values of 1.000 and ranked the reference compound first in all 20 trials. In a more stringent adversarial benchmark containing biosynthetically plausible alternatives, v3.1 improved AUROC from 0.920 to 0.985, AUPRC from 0.574 to 0.837, and Top-1 accuracy from 65% to 90% relative to v3. A compact phenylpropanoid–flavonoid example illustrates the separation of experimental annotations, curated context, and prioritized hypotheses, while a larger Arabidopsis occurrence dataset demonstrates application to 864 mapped compounds within a 6,714-node network. BPM therefore provides an interpretable framework for converting annotated plant metabolite lists into ranked biosynthetic hypotheses without conflating computational plausibility with compound identification. By combining curated biochemical context with structural evidence and exporting prioritized candidates for targeted interrogation of LC–MS/MS data, BPM provides a practical link between metabolite annotation, biosynthetic interpretation, and subsequent experimental investigation.

papers.title: Iso-co-humulone Does Not Necessarily Contribute to the Roughness of Beer Bitterness
papers.abstract: [Conclusion] Iso-co-humulone does not necessarily contribute to the roughness of beer bitterness. The long-repeated rule that a high cohumulone proportion produces rough, harsh, or lingering bitterness should not be accepted as a general law of brewing and should not be used by itself to judge hop quality or to predict the sensory quality of beer. [Background] The cohumulone–roughness hypothesis has been reproduced for decades in brewing literature, referenceworks, trainingmaterials, andhop-selectionpractice, despite limiteddirect evidence and timeintensity findings inconsistentwith a simple universal rule. This persistence is consequential: brewers, particularly those entering the field, may reject otherwise suitable hops or misdiagnose rough bitterness solely from a cohumulone specification. [Methods] Fractions containing iso-co-humulone, iso-normal-humulone, or iso-ad-humulone (each combining its cis and trans forms) were added separately to unhopped beer at 25 BU. Lingering bitter aftertaste was evaluated blind by six trained panelists on a nine-point anchored scale and by a lipid-membrane taste-sensing system. In a separate 3,000-L brewing comparison, the iso-co-humulone proportion was increased from 28.2% to 39.8%; eight trained panelists performed blind paired comparisons of lingering aftertaste and bitterness crispness (kire). [Results]Mean lingering-bitterness scores were 4.9, 6.2, and 6.9 for iso-co-humulone, iso-normal-humulone, and iso-ad-humulone, respectively. Corresponding taste-sensor aftertaste responses were 0.24, 2.89, and 2.73. In the brewing comparison, aftertaste choices were divided 4:4, whereas seven of eight panelists selected the higheriso-co-humulone beer as having greater crispness (one-sided exact p = 0.035; two-sided p = 0.070). [Interpretation] Roughness was not measured as a separate multidimensional attribute, and the brewing comparison was not independently replicated. Nevertheless, the convergent model-beer, sensor, and brewing observations contradict the necessary-persistence premise of the traditional roughness rule and do not justify treating a high iso-co-humulone proportion as automatic evidence of rough beer bitterness. A cohumulone percentage on a hop specification is not a sensory verdict.

papers.title: Reconciliation Through Integration: A Source-Level Bayesian Framework for Developing Measurement-Integrated Methane Inventories
papers.abstract: Bottom-up (BU) inventories and top-down (TD) aerial measurements at midstream natural gas facilities frequently diverge, and this discrepancy remains a central challenge for methane accounting in the sector. Previous approaches typically reconcile this divergence by treating BU and TD data as independent estimates of a single true quantity to be adjusted toward agreement, rather than as evidence that each capture only part of a more complex underlying system. This complexity arises from methane emissions being strongly governed by equipment operational state and therefore instantaneous aerial “snapshots” translate poorly to annual inventories. We argue instead that BU and TD are complementary sources of evidence that should be integrated. We present a source-level Bayesian framework that constructs BU prior distributions for each emission source category and updates them with attributed aerial detections through an empirical data-augmentation procedure. The resulting posterior distributions were propagated through unit-level activity data and source-specific information via Monte Carlo simulation to produce annual estimates. Across 64 compressor stations, measurement-integrated annual estimates were 84% higher than the BU inventory, a difference driven almost entirely by compressor vents (rod packing and seal vents), and leakage through blowdown and isolation valves, which together accounted for 90% of the asset-level revision. The revision was heterogeneous across stations and source categories, emphasizing the importance of source-level, station-specific integration when developing an emissions inventory.

papers.title: From 4D to 2D: Efficient computation of the electron correlation energies of atoms in molecular systems
papers.abstract: The accurate modeling of (bio)molecular systems remains a major challenge in computational chemistry. In recent years, machine learning potentials (MLPs) have emerged as a promising approach, combining the efficiency of classical force fields with near quantum-mechanical accuracy. Among these, the physics-informed MLP FFLUX employs the Interacting Quantum Atoms (IQA) energy partitioning scheme to decompose molecular energies into atomic contributions derived from quantum mechanics for machine learning. However, incorporating two-electron correlation energies into IQA, and consequently into FFLUX, is currently unfeasible for larger systems en masse, due to the steep computational scaling associated with the necessary storage and evaluation of the two-particle density matrix (2PDM). In this work, we introduce a proof-of-concept workflow that employs density fitting (DF) to compress the 2PDM into a two-index representation, thereby accelerating the IQA partitioning of two-electron correlation energies. By expressing traditionally four-centre electron repulsion integrals in terms of auxiliary basis functions, the DF approximation enables a size reduction of the 2PDM from O(N^4) to O(NDF^2), where N is the number of basis functions and NDF is the size of the auxiliary basis set. The method proposed here is demonstrated using coupled cluster singles and doubles densities. The resulting reduction in computational cost and memory requirements enables correlated IQA analyses for significantly larger systems than previously accessible. Thus, this development provides an important step towards incorporating explicit electron correlation and hence dispersion directly into FFLUX atomic ML models, thereby improving both their physical robustness and transferability. This advance will eliminate the need to artificially add empirical potentials, or a posteriori dispersion correction.

papers.title: SimSJSAlert: A Similarity-Augmented Multi-View Learning Framework with Scaffold Alerts for Drug-Induced Stevens-Johnson Syndrome Risk Assessment
papers.abstract: Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS) is a rare, life-threatening adverse drug reaction for which early identification of high-risk drugs remains challenging. In this study, we developed an explainable quantitative structure-toxicity relationship (QSTR) framework for SJS prediction using a multi-view learning framework with 21 molecular representations, including molecular descriptors, fingerprints, transformer-based embeddings, and a molecular similarity representation. Model development and evaluation were designed in accordance with the OECD principles for QSAR validation, incorporating scaffold-aware validation, external evaluation on pharmacovigilance negative-signal compounds, and structural interpretation by integrating SHAP with Bemis-Murcko scaffold enrichment analysis. The proposed framework achieved robust sensitivity and specificity, with molecular similarity consistently improving the identification of SJS-associated compounds. Furthermore, a consensus prediction and scaffold-based prioritization strategy identified several high-risk drugs from the 1 external negative-signal dataset, including cefprozil, tetracycline, and omadacycline, highlighting their potential association with SJS and warranting further pharmacovigilance and experimental investigation. To facilitate practical application, this was deployed as a freely accessible web server, SimSJSAlert (https: //sim-sjs-alert.streamlit.app/), enabling rapid drug-induced SJS risk assessment. The proposed framework combines predictive performance, interpretability, and accessibility to support early SJS risk assessment, pharmacovigilance signal prioritization, and safer drug development.

papers.title: Synthetic Mutagenesis of Tyrosine into Proline Mimetics Enables Late-Stage Backbone Editing of Peptides
papers.abstract: The biological and physicochemical properties of peptides are strongly influenced by their backbone conformations. However, installing conformationally restricting units generally requires peptide redesign and resynthesis using noncanonical amino acids. Here, we report a late-stage backbone-editing method that converts a native amino acid residue into a proline-mimetic structure. Treatment of the dearomatized intermediate generated by tyrosine-selective oxime conjugation in a basic aqueous buffer induced intramolecular 1,4-addition of the backbone amide nitrogen, thereby converting the tyrosine residue into a cyclic proline-mimetic unit within the peptide backbone. This transformation proceeded efficiently under mild aqueous conditions and was applicable to several bioactive peptides. Multidimensional NMR analyses established the structures of the resulting products, while conventional molecular dynamics and REST2 simulations demonstrated that the installed proline-mimetic backbone reduced the local conformational freedom of the peptide. Evaluation using a β-hairpin model peptide further demonstrated that the proline-mimetic structure enhanced resistance to proteolytic degradation. This method constitutes a chemical mutagenesis strategy that directly converts a native tyrosine residue into a backbone conformational control unit without reconstructing the parent peptide sequence. By connecting residue-selective side-chain modification with backbone editing, this strategy provides a new design concept for the late-stage conformational and functional diversification of peptides.

papers.title: Dearomative Multifunctionalization of Benzene Rings Enabled by Electron-Transfer Catalysis
papers.abstract: Transforming simple benzene-ring-containing compounds from bulk chemicals into complex three-dimensional molecules with diverse functionalities and controllable stereochemistry under mild, scalable conditions remains a long-standing goal in synthetic chemistry. Dianions generated from aryl carbonyl compounds by two-electron transfer are promising precursors for dearomative difunctionalization. However, previous methods1 for generating dianion intermediates require harsh conditions and are incompatible with functionalized electrophiles, while competing benzylic functionalization via ketyl radical anions2,3 further limits their application. A key challenge is therefore to rapidly convert radical anions into higher-energy dianions using a mild reducing agent, outcompeting nucleophilic reactions of radical anions while ensuring electrophile compatibility. Here we report an ultrafast electron-transfer catalytic mode employing a bipyridine-based catalyst that rapidly acquires electrons from magnesium metal and transfers them to aryl ketyl radical anions, enabling the efficient in situ generation of dianion intermediates from simple aryl ketones under mild conditions. Using chlorosilanes as electrophiles, we obtain dearomatized bis-silylated products bearing conjugated enol silyl ether and allylsilane motifs in up to 98% yield. These products serve as versatile platform molecules for dearomative multifunctionalization, enabling the highly stereoselective synthesis of complex compounds with multiple stereocentres.

papers.title: A Simple and Green One-Pot Synthesis of 2-Arylbenzimidazoles from Alcohols Using MnO2/I2
papers.abstract: A straightforward and green synthetic method has been developed to prepare functionalized 2-arylbenzimidazole derivatives from readily accessible starting materials (arylmethyl alcohols and o-phenylenediamines) via a two-step, one-pot reaction. In the first step, arylmethyl alcohols are oxidized using MnO2 (4-8 equiv.) under both solvent-free and toluene-mediated conditions. subsequently, the aromatic aldehyde undergoes a 10 mol% iodine-catalyzed condensation with o-phenylenediamine in toluene at 100 °C under open-air conditions, leading to the production of 2-substituted benzimidazoles. The one-pot direct conversion of benzyl alcohols to 2-arylbenzimidazoles proceeds efficiently, affording the desired benzofused imidazoles in good to excellent yields, up to 91%. The sustainable method exhibits broad substrate scope, tolerating a wide range of functional groups. Mechanistic studies support a plausible imine formation pathway, followed by cyclization and oxidative aromatization under open-air conditions. This work highlights the synthetic utility and potential of the developed green method for future applications in organic synthesis and medicinal chemistry.

papers.title: Polymorphous Structural Landscapes Drive Broadband Optical Response in Water-Stable Mixed-Halide Antiperovskites
papers.abstract: Silver chalcohalide antiperovskites have emerged as low-toxicity semiconductors with strong near-infrared absorption, although their unusual composition-dependent optical properties, including inverse bandgap bowing, remain poorly understood. Here, Ag3SI1-xBrx solid solutions were synthesized by a solvent-free mechanochemical route and investigated by structural and optical characterization, ultrafast spectroscopy, and first-principles calculations. While all compositions retain an average cubic Pm-3m structure and exhibit a Vegard-like lattice contraction with increasing Br content, strongly nonlinear optical behavior and multiple absorption onsets are observed. First principles calculations reveal that these alloys are more appropriately described by an ensemble of electronically distinct low-energy configurations arising from an underlying polymorphous energy landscape. This configurational diversity redistributes band-edge spectral weight, enables quasi-direct transitions at Γ, and provides a microscopic explanation for the broadband absorption and anomalous bandgap evolution. Transient absorption spectroscopy further supports the presence of different compositiondependent electronic environments and reveals prolonged carrier lifetimes for mixed-halides, consistent with alloy-disorder-induced localization. From an applicative perspective, these materials show remarkable water stability and efficient photothermal energy conversion enabling their use in a proof-of-concept solar water evaporation setup. These findings establish Ag3SI1-xBrx antiperovskites as water-stable, low-toxicity, broadband-absorbing materials and demonstrate the importance of polymorphous local structure in governing their optical response.

papers.title: Comprehensive Strategies in the Synthesis of Noncanonical Cyclic Peptides Containing Biaryl-Bridged Linkages
papers.abstract: CONSPECTUS: The development of synthetic methodologies for natural products and the establishment of chemical supply routes for complex compounds, which advanced significantly in the twentieth century, provided organic chemists in both academia and industry with considerable confidence and assurance. These achievements offered humanity a systematic framework and a degree of sustainability in the supply of complex organic molecules. Established synthetic strategies enabled access, to a certain extent, to diverse bioactive compounds such as terpenes, alkaloids, and peptides. The isolation of bioactive natural products has often been compared to the extraction of crude oil, and we are repeatedly taught that the major bioactive natural products or their core scaffolds have already been “almost completely isolated.” Yet such a sense of accomplishment is frequently illusory. In reality, isolation techniques for bioactive natural products have advanced dramatically over time, and reports of newly isolated bioactive compounds continue to appear with vigor. In recent decades, the rapid progress of genome mining since the early 2000s has enabled the computational analysis of genetic information to uncover novel bioactive substances with pharmaceutical potential. This technology revealed that many organisms harbor, within their genomes, numerous beneficial bioactive compounds that are not produced under conventional environmental conditions. Consequently, a surge of discoveries—akin to a gold rush—has been reported. Among these natural products are compounds with previously unknown and distinctive scaffolds, many of which lack established synthetic supply routes. Notable examples include cihunamide B, lapparbin, micitide 982, rubrin, scabrirubin CB-4, and cyctetryptomycin A, all of which represent recently isolated noncanonical cyclic peptides characterized by biaryl-bridged linkages. Most of these compounds were discovered through genome mining and are distinguished by rigid architectures in which two aromatic rings, such as tryptophan and tyrosine, are covalently linked within the cyclic peptide framework. The presence of multiple highly conjugated sp2 carbons imparts pronounced linearity to the cyclic peptide backbone, concomitantly increasing structural strain. As a result, conventional strategies for cyclic peptide synthesis—such as intramolecular amide coupling, intramolecular Ullmann coupling, or intramolecular oxidative cyclization—are inadequate for constructing these highly strained biarylbridged cyclic peptides. We have recently established a general modular synthetic approach for these noncanonical cyclic peptides, enabling their supply on the gram scale. Most notably, this methodology not only permits the synthesis of naturally occurring biaryl-bridged linkages but also allows the deliberate incorporation of diverse, artificially designed aromatic motifs into arbitrary peptide linkers. Within the vast genetic “ocean” encoded in microbial genomes, numerous cryptic natural products with unprecedented scaffolds are expected to remain undiscovered. The systematic synthetic strategy we present herein provides a general and coherent framework that enables access to these compound classes, which until now have been exclusively available through microbial biosynthesis. Moreover, recent advances in photochemical and electrochemical methodologies, particularly inexpensive and mild radical reactions, have proven to be highly effective approaches for the synthesis of these previously unexplored natural products. These cutting-edge single-electron processes are not merely substitutes for classical two-electron name reactions; rather, they have emerged as powerful tools for navigating the genomic “ocean” and uncovering new chemical space.

papers.title: Towards an Accurate Atomistic Description of Procaine Crystals: Force Field Development and MD Simulation of Solid-to-Liquid Phase Transitions
papers.abstract: Rational design of crystalline materials is crucial for material science and pharmaceutical development, requiring molecular modeling as a powerful complementary tool. This study employs molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate the thermal stability, structural evolution, and melting mechanisms of crystalline procaine base across a temperature range of 23 to 373 K. To evaluate potential finite-size and boundary effects, two distinct computational setups were considered: a bulk crystal model under periodic boundary conditions (System I, 600 molecules) and an isolated nanocrystal in vacuum (System II, 1188 molecules). Both systems demonstrate well-preserved long-range positional ordering from 23 to 313 K, followed by the appearance of a plastic crystalline state with enhanced rotational freedom between 323 and 333 K. At 343 K, a heterogeneous, surface-initiated phase transition to an isotropic melt occurs, which closely matches the experimental melting point of procaine free-base of 334-337 K. MD analysis reveals remarkably slow melting kinetics at 333-343 K, where a crystalline core persists for over 300 ns before complete melting at 500 ns. We found that the thermal breakdown of the crystal lattice strongly correlates with a breakage of the intermolecular hydrogen-bonding 3D network between procaine molecules. Radial distribution function (RDF) analysis shows a sharp shift in the primary amino nitrogen correlations (N10···N10) towards short-distances upon melting, whereas short-range hydrogen-bond N10···O9 distances remain spatially invariant in the liquid phase. Mean square displacement (MSD) of procaine molecules demonstrates a dramatic transition from restricted lattice vibrations below 333 K to active fluid diffusion above 343 K. These findings are accompanied by rotational autocorrelation functions transition from long-time orientational persistence in the solid state (23-333 K) to rapid exponential relaxation in the melt (343-373 K). Finally, unconstrained melting of System II produces a spherical nanodroplet driven by surface tension minimization, confirming that the performance of the developed OPLS-AA FF model.

papers.title: Electrosynthesis of Bis-spirocycles via a Radical Strain-Release Dearomatization Cascade
papers.abstract: This report presents an electro-oxidative approach to synthesize functionalized bis-spirocycles by combining the strain-release reactivity of bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) with arene dearomatization in a radical cascade. Various radical precursors can undergo this transformation under mild, oxidant- and mediator-free conditions, allowing efficient production of complex, three-dimensional bis-spirocyclic structures with high functional-group tolerance. Mechanistic investigations indicate an anodically driven radical cascade, involving radical addition to the BCB, strain-release ring opening, and subsequent ipso-dearomatization.

papers.title: Rhodium-Catalyzed Stereoselective Access to Polysubstituted Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes Bearing Quaternary Bridge Carbons
papers.abstract: Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) are unique strained carbocycles that have emerged as attractive buildingblocks in synthetic and medicinal chemistry owing to their unique reactivity. Despite recent advances in the preparation of polysubstituted BCBs, the stereoselective synthesis of bridge-substituted derivatives remains a significant challenge, particularly when quaternary stereocenters are involved at these positions. Herein, we report a rhodium-catalyzed [2+1] cycloaddition of cyclopropenes and diazo compounds that provides direct access to stereodefined bridge-substituted BCBs. The reaction proceeds with complete diastereocontrol across a broad range of substrates and enables the construction of densely functionalized frameworks bearing up to four stereocenters. The methodology can also be extended to enantioenriched cyclopropenes, providing optically active BCBs with complete enantiospecificity. DFT calculations are consistent with the stereochemical outcome and the synthetic utility of the resulting BCBs is demonstrated by transformations leading to fused tricyclic architectures and polysubstituted cyclobutenes and cyclobutanes.

papers.title: Three-photon Absorption Cross-Sections of Serotonin, Fluorescein, Rhodamine 6G, and Some Fluorescent Protein Chromophores
papers.abstract: Interest in studying, enhancing the performance, and engineering of three-photon absorption (3PA) responsive molecular probes and bio-molecular systems, such as fluorescent proteins (FPs), has increased significantly over the last decade. 3PA has a deeper penetration than one-and two-photon absorption (1PA and 2PA, respectively). In particular, FPs can display 3PA within the deep tissue imaging window (1600-1870 nm). Experimentally, the 3PA ability (measured in terms of the 3PA cross-section, σ 3PA ) of a set of red fluorescent proteins (RFPs) has been reported before. On the other hand, just a handful of computational studies have determined the 3PA response and, in even fewer cases, determined the σ 3PA of selected FPs. By means of time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) here we determine the σ 3PA of fluorescein, rhodamine 6G, serotonin, and a curated set of isolated FP chromophores for which their computationally determined 1PA and 2PA have been reported previously. The results from this investigation are in reasonably good agreement with their experimentally determined σ 3PA . We expect that in the future, our results for FP chromophores could be improved by the inclusion of effects of the protein, which are well-known to play important roles in determining the magnitude of 1PA, 2PA, and 3PA cross-sections. Finally, this investigation contributes to the understanding of multi-photon absorption photophysics of existent FPs and, furthermore, assists in the future engineering of new 3PA responsive FPs and FP chromophores.

papers.title: Red TADF Pyridoquinoxaline-Annulated Curved Nitrogen-Doped PAHs and their use in OLEDs
papers.abstract: Curved nitrogen-doped polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons offer a rigid and nonplanar framework for investigating how donor identity regulates the balance between locally excited and charge-transfer states in thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) emitters. Here, a pyrido[2,3b]quinoxaline unit was integrated into a dibenzo[b,f]azepine-based polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon scaffold and functionalized with one of 3,6-di- tert -butylcarbazole ( TBCzPyN-PAH ), diphenylamine ( DPAPyN-PAH ), 9,9-dimethyl-9,10-dihydroacridine ( DMAcPyN-PAH ), or phenoxazine ( PXZPyN-PAH ) donor moieties. The resulting series provides a common acceptor framework in which the electronic and conformational properties of the peripheral donor affect the 2 energies of the excited states. Donor substitution tunes the emission maximum in toluene from 528 to 697 nm. In 2 wt% doped films in CBP, these compounds emit from 519 to 622 nm with PLQY of up to 58%. Temperature-dependent time-resolved photoluminescence confirms TADF for all investigated compounds except for the DPA derivative. Across the TADF-active series, the singlet–triplet energy gap, Δ E ST , decreases from 0.22 to 0.03 eV and the delayed fluorescence lifetime shortens from 8.5 ms to 29 μs. Vacuum-deposited OLEDs with TBCzPyN-PAH showed EQE max , of 21.6% at an electroluminescence maximum of 538 nm, whereas the device with PXZPyN-PAH emitted at 606 nm and showed a lower EQE max of 7.2% but with a milder efficiency roll-off.

papers.title: Red TADF Pyridoquinoxaline-Annulated Curved Nitrogen-Doped PAHs and their use in OLEDs
papers.abstract: Curved nitrogen-doped polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons offer a rigid and nonplanar framework for investigating how donor identity regulates the balance between locally excited and chargetransfer states in thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) emitters. Here, a pyrido[2,3b]quinoxaline unit was integrated into a dibenzo[b,f]azepine-based polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon scaffold and functionalized with one of 3,6-di-tert-butylcarbazole (TBCzPyN-PAH), diphenylamine (DPAPyN-PAH), 9,9-dimethyl-9,10-dihydroacridine (DMAcPyN-PAH), or phenoxazine (PXZPyN-PAH) donor moieties. The resulting series provides a common acceptor framework in which the electronic and conformational properties of the peripheral donor affect the 2 energies of the excited states. Donor substitution tunes the emission maximum in toluene from 528 to 697 nm. In 2 wt% doped films in CBP, these compounds emit from 519 to 622 nm with PLQY of up to 58%. Across the TADF-active series, the singlet–triplet energy gap, ΔEST, decreases from 0.22 to 0.03 eV and the delayed fluorescence lifetime shortens from 8.5 ms to 29 μs. papers.title: Mechanistic Insights into Light-Alkane Formation from Photoexcited Uranyl complexes
papers.abstract: This work describes a uranyl-catalysed photo-induced methodology for generating methane from acetic acid. The reaction proceeds in water as the only solvent, with roughly 10 vol % acetic acid — a composition mimicking ommercial vinegar — and only 1 mol % of UO 2 (NO 3 ) 2 , a by-product of the nuclear fuel cycle. The mechanism underlying this transformation was examined in detail through luminescence measurements, EPR spectroscopy, isotope-labelling experiments, and speciation studies. DFT calculations show that the process involves an unstable intermediate, U V O 2 + -AcOH template, which is prompt to disproportionation into inactive U IV and appears to be responsible for the low TON, which is reported. However, the speciation studies also suggest that the equatorial environment of UO 2 2+ would stabilize this UV intermediate and therefore influence the CH 4 production as well as decreasing the potential additional competitive paths, leading to greater selectivity.

papers.title: All-Dielectric Metasurfaces in Fundamentals, Materials, and Emerging Applications
papers.abstract: The field of optics is undergoing a transformative shift, pushed forward by the demand for miniaturized, lightweight, and highly functional components. Dielectric metasurfaces have emerged as a transformative platform in modern photonics, offering unprecedented control over the amplitude, phase, polarization, and frequency of light within an ultrathin, planar architecture. Unlike their metallic predecessors, all-dielectric metasurfaces exploit Mie resonances, bound states in the continuum, and multipolar interference to achieve low-loss, high-efficiency optical functionalities across the visible, near-infrared, and terahertz spectral ranges. This review covers the field systematically, starting with the common working principles of dielectric metasurfaces and the physical mechanisms that make them so versatile. We then discuss the most widely used material platforms, including their optical properties and practical trade-offs, followed by an overview of the fabrication techniques available today. We look at both traditional top-down methods, such as electron-beam lithography, and emerging high-throughput approaches like nanoimprint lithography and photochemical deposition. We also examine the design strategies and element geometries used to build optical functionality into these surfaces, from simple phase-shifting pillars to more complex resonant architectures. Finally, this review examines the broad range of applications these structures enable, from metalenses and holography to nonlinear optics, biosensing, and terahertz generation. By identifying the key open challenges in fabrication scalability, broadband operation, and active tunability, this review aims to serve both as a reference resource for specialists and as an entry point for researchers from adjacent disciplines, charting a clear roadmap for the next decade of flat-optics research.

papers.title: BondNet: Noise-Robust Molecular Bond Perception from 3D Coordinates with Explicit Hydrogen Context
papers.abstract: Recovering molecular graphs from atomic identities and 3D coordinates is a key step in coordinate-first molecular modelling and generation. We present Bond-Net, a two-stage framework in which a PaiNN model first predicts connectivity on a distance-derived candidate graph and a topology-aware network then classifies heavy–heavy bond types. Explicit hydrogens participate in message passing as local valence context but are excluded from bond-type supervision and scoring. On a fixed 26,940-molecule GEOM-DRUGS validation cohort, the near-clean model achieves pipeline macro-F1 = 0.9994 and correctly types every reference heavy–heavy bond in 99.4% of molecules. A historical ablation shows that removing hydrogen context reduces macro-F1 by 6.7 percentage points and the exact-type rate to 19.7%. With Gaussian coordinate-noise augmentation and candidate graphs rebuilt from the perturbed coordinates, BondNet retains pipeline macro-F1 = 0.9859 and a true-bond exact-type rate of 87.7% at σ = 0.1 Å; its stricter HH-graph exact match is 83.0% because extra predicted bonds are also penalized. BondNet’s pipeline macro-F1 exceeds RDKit DetermineBonds at every tested noise level on the common denominator. Residual strict-label disagreements are concentrated in resonance-ambiguous N–O and carboxyl motifs. An exact-molecule-leakage-controlled diversity study further shows that a curated multi-source set of 80,000 molecules transfers better than both a same-size random GEOM subset and a 3.4× larger single-source set. 1 Scientific Contribution. BondNet isolates geometric connectivity from topology-aware bond typing and quantifies how explicit-hydrogen context and noise augmentation affect robust graph recovery. The study also provides atom-pair-matched baselines, explicitly reports tool failures, and introduces an exact-molecule-leakage-controlled comparison of training-set diversity and scale.

papers.title: Single-Ion Hydration Through the Lens of Data-Driven Many-Body Potentials
papers.abstract: Single-ion hydration provides a stringent test of molecular models because local ionwater interactions, collective polarization, nuclear quantum effects, and long-range electrostatics all contribute to experimentally measurable structure, spectra, and thermodynamics. Here we discuss how data-driven many-body potentials, in particular MB-pol for water and MB-nrg for hydrated ions, provide a physically transparent route from correlated electronic structure data to predictive simulations of ion hydration from clusters to bulk water and aqueous interfaces. We emphasize how this framework transforms single-ion hydration from a parameterization problem into a hierarchy of many-body observables, and we outline opportunities for connecting simulations directly with interfacial spectroscopy, hydration free energies, and complex electrolyte environments.

papers.title: Trapacycle: A Chiral Rhombic Macrocycle
papers.abstract: The development of a new class of macrocycles is a primary issue in supramolecular chemistry. We here report the synthesis, spectroscopic properties, and host-guest functions of chiral, rhombus-shaped macrocyclic oligoimides 1, denoted as trapacycles. Trapacycle (+)-1 could be readily synthesized by the condensation of 9,10-dihydro-9,10-ethanoanthracenebased tetracarboxylic dianhydride 2 with (1S,2S)-cyclohexane-1,2-diamine D-tartrate. Its enantiomer (–)-1 could be analogously accessed from 2 and (1R,2R)-cyclohexane-1,2-diamine L-tartrate. The solid-state crystalline structures of 1 showed intrinsic rhombic shape pores and extrinsic pores. These pores were found to accommodate guest solvent molecules. Furthermore, 1 adsorbed iodine vapor in the solid state and accommodated naphthalenes in organic solvents.

papers.title: Full-scale Hazardous Waste Incineration of PFAS in Fluorotelomer-Based Aqueous Film-Forming Foam
papers.abstract: In the absence of full-scale incineration studies into the impacts of temperature on thermal destruction of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), globally evolving regulatory guidelines have been inconsistent. In this study, we incinerated a fluorotelomerization-based aqueous film-forming foam (AFFF) concentrate at different temperatures and feed rates of up to 1500 kg/h in one of the largest hazardous waste incinerators in the world. At secondary combustion chamber temperatures as low as 950 °C and 2 seconds gas residence time, the destruction and removal efficiency for the main AFFF component 6:2 fluorotelomer sulfonamide alkylbetaine (6:2 FTAB, a.k.a. Capstone B) exceeded 99.999999% at the highest AFFF feed rate. Non-polar volatile fluorinated compounds targeted by Other Test Method 50 (OTM-50) were below method detection limits, while PFAS concentrations in ashes and scrubber waters were practically indistinguishable from baseline conditions when no fluorine-containing waste was incinerated. PFAS stack emissions into the atmosphere during AFFF treatment were substantially lower than volatile PFAS emissions from a typical landfill. Quantum chemical modeling suggested that a similar treatment efficiency may be expected for perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS)-based electrochemical fluorination foams. The findings of our study suggest that hazardous waste incineration may be effective at temperatures well below the 1100 °C required by some current regulations, minimizing fuel consumption, equipment wear, and undesirable side reactions during thermal PFAS destruction.

papers.title: The nature of metal-ligand interactions in different metalloporphyrin · · · hydrogen cyanide complexes: Limitations of DFT exchange-correlation functionals.
papers.abstract: The weak intermolecular interaction energies of various metalloporphyrin (MP, M = Cr, Fe, Co, Ni, Zn) and hydrogen cyanide complexes along the axial metal-ligand bond have been computed using different wavefunction-based theoretical level (MP2, CCSD and CCSD(T)). The domain-based local pair natural orbital (DLPNO) method was applied at all three theoretical levels, as well as in the case of the MP2 theory, the spin-component and spin-opposite scaled frameworks were also taken into account. The nature of the interactions was analyzed by decomposing the intermolecular interaction energy into physically meaningful components (Electrostatic, Exchange, Dispersion, Non-dispersion and Perturbative triple) using the local energy decomposition (LED) method in the framework of the CCSD(T) theory. The potential energy curves were also compared with the results obtained using density functional theory ((DFT), considering sets of widely used exchange-correlation (XC) functionals, as well as the r2SCAN functional family. The behavior of DFT functionals is highly heterogeneous. For dispersion-dominant Ni, Zn and Mg cases of the interaction, the functionals underestimate the potential energy curves obtained by the CCSD and CCSD(T) methods. For the less dispersion-dominant Fe and Cr cases, where larger non-dispersion and triple perturbation (T) contributions were obtained, however, they overestimate the reference potential energy curves. This under-and overestimation can be linked to the exact exchange and correlation term used in the XC functional. Employing the MP2based component with a higher weight makes the XC functional’s behavior much more balanced. Overall, it was found that, the CAM-B3LYP, Pr2SCAN69, and our newly defined SCS1-r2SCAN0-2 (or r2SCAN0-2*, where the initail “SOS” form was replaced with “SCS”) functionals showed the most efficient performance.

papers.title: Diffusion-Model-Guided Adaptive Sampling of Rare Conformational States in Adenylate Kinase
papers.abstract: Efficiently exploring the rare conformational states of biomolecules remains a central challenge in molecular dynamics simulation. Here we show, using adenylate kinase as a methodological testbed, that the static structural scores conventionally used to prioritize diffusion-modelgenerated candidates have essentially no power to predict which candidates actually reach a kinetically rare state upon subsequent simulation (AUC = 0.500, 95% CI [0.251, 0.749]). Motivated by this finding, we introduce two adaptive strategies — direct PCA-distance targeting and replication of confirmed-hit structures — that achieve significantly higher rare-state hit rates and dwell times than extended conventional molecular dynamics or random-initialization sampling under matched computational budgets, while also enabling, for the first time, statistically stable estimation of rare-macrostate populations. These results show that structural novelty and kinetically meaningful entry into a rare state are not the same property, providing concrete design guidance for generative-model-driven adaptive sampling in other biomolecular systems.

papers.title: Reductive Electrophotocatalysis: Fundamentals, Mechanistic Frameworks, and Synthetic Applications
papers.abstract: Reductive electrophotocatalysis has emerged as a powerful synthetic platform that combines electrochemistry and photoredox catalysis to achieve exceptionally strong reduction potentials under mild conditions. Through sequential electrochemical reduction and photoexcitation, highly reactive excited-state radical ions are generated, which can activate challenging substrates that are often difficult to address with conventional catalytic methods. Consequently, this approach has unlocked a broad range of previously unattainable reductive transformations. This review seeks to provide a comprehensive overview of the fundamental principles, catalyst design strategies, and mechanistic aspects of reductive electrophotocatalysis, with particular emphasis on the ongoing debate surrounding the identity of the reducing species responsible for substrate activation. Special attention is devoted to the four mechanistic pathways currently proposed in the literature: (i) direct electron transfer from the excited photocatalyst radical anion, (ii) substrate activation facilitated by pre-association between the photocatalyst radical anion and the substrate (iii) reduction through solvated electrons or related electron-pool mechanisms, (iv) reduction mediated by catalyst-derived or modified photocatalyst species. In addition, representative electrophotocatalyst systems and their applications in reductive bond activation will be critically evaluated. Finally, future opportunities for the development of sustainable, selective, and scalable electrophotocatalytic methodologies will be highlighted, with particular focus on advancing mechanistic understanding.

papers.title: Total Synthesis: Backbone of Organic Chemistry, a Discipline in Decline?
papers.abstract: Total synthesis has long been regarded as the intellectual backbone of organic chemistry, driving reaction discovery, stereoselective methodology, and molecular design. Yet its place within the contemporary discipline is actively debated, largely on the basis of editorial opinion rather than evidence. In this Perspective we bring quantitative data to that debate. We examined the annual share of articles carrying the phrase “total synthesis” in their titles across four leading journals—Angewandte Chemie International Edition, Journal of Organic Chemistry, Organic Letters, and Tetrahedron Letters—from 1959 to 2025. The share rose through the late twentieth century to a peak of about 4.79% in 2009, then fell to 1.85% by 2025, a relative decline of roughly 61%. Structural-break analysis places a consistent inflection near 2020, and an AIC-selected ARIMA(0,1,0) model with drift projects continued decline to about 1.40% by 2030. Crucially, the fall is relative rather than absolute: the annual number of total syntheses has held broadly steady while overall journal output has expanded dramatically. We argue that total synthesis is not disappearing but being diluted and redefined, and we outline how researchers, editors, and funding agencies might sustain it as a driver of innovation.

papers.title: A spectral reset law explains and predicts periodic recurrence in the elements
papers.abstract: The recurrence of chemical properties is the defining feature of the periodic system, yet it is conventionally explained only indirectly, through inferred electron configurations and heuristic filling rules rather than being directly derived from atomic observables. Building on an empirical spectral framework in which elements occupy a bounded spectral space defined by two measured frequencies, the K-edge frequency (𝜈 max ) and the first ionization frequency (𝜈 ion ), we show that recurrence arises from simple quantitative constraints operating directly on these observables. As 𝜈 max increases across the elemental sequence, 𝜈 ion rises toward the upper boundary of the spectral space. At this limiting condition, a spectral mode bifurcates and 𝜈 ion undergoes a sharp reset toward a nearly invariant baseline, cancelling the accumulated rise to within 1%. Repetition of this rise–split–reset structure partitions spectral space into successive bounded intervals that emerge as periods, with lower and upper edges corresponding to elements conventionally classified as Groups 1 and 18, respectively. The rise–split–reset structure yields the recurrence 𝜈 ion (𝑛 + 1) = 𝜈 ion (𝑛) + Δ𝜈 ion (rise) − Δ𝜈 ion (reset) , with |Δ𝜈 ion | = 𝐴𝜈 𝑚𝑎𝑥 𝑏 , so that successive period anchors recur at the same relative position in spectral space. Across the four experimental period boundaries, reset magnitude scales linearly with the spectral splitting amplitude (𝑅 2 = 0.962), empirically linking the recurrence to the mode differentiation that establishes the periods. Seeded with a single measured value (lithium), the recursion regenerates the experimental G1 and G18 period anchors with a median error of 1.4%, and extrapolates beyond the known table to hypothetical periods 8 and 9, including element 119 at 𝜈 ion = (1.12 ± 0.33) × 10 15 s −1 (4.6 ± 1.4 eV). These results establish periodic recurrence as a quantitative, generative spectral structure in measurement space and show that ionization frequencies are not independent quantities, but are determined sequentially from a single seed and a pair of spectral scaling power laws with only two measured observables.

papers.title: Unlocking PEG-400: A Sustainable Reaction Medium for Phthalocyanine Synthesis and Pd-Catalyzed C–C Bond Formation
papers.abstract: In this work, we demonstrate that poly(ethylene glycol)-400 (PEG-400) can efficiently replace conventional and hazardous solvents such as N,N-dimethylaminoethanol (DMAE) and N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) in the synthesis of phthalocyanines, a class of functional molecular materials widely investigated for optoelectronic and energy-related applications. Used at a loading as low as 1.0 equivalent relative to the phthalonitrile precursor, PEG-400 enables cyclotetramerization reactions under operationally simple and comparatively safer conditions, providing isolated yields of 50-83% across a range of metalated and metal-free derivatives and substitution patterns. The robustness of the protocol was further demonstrated at the multigram scale, affording cobalt phthalocyanine in 79% yield, with 88% of the PEG-400 recovered from the reaction mixture. Remarkably, PEG-400 proved compatible with sequential cyclotetramerization followed by Sonogashira or Suzuki coupling without isolation of the macrocyclic intermediate, affording functionalized products in up to 75% yield and enabling pot-economical access to more complex derivatives. E-factor and Process Mass Intensity (PMI) analyses quantitatively support the improved material-efficiency profile of the method when compared to representative literature procedures. Overall, these results establish PEG-400 as a versatile and sustainable medium for the resource-efficient synthesis and functionalization of phthalocyanine derivatives.

papers.title: Instantaneous Mechanical Programming of Polymer Microparticle Shape and Surface Architecture
papers.abstract: Structurally anisotropic polymer microparticles with controlled surface topographies are essential for applications in selfassembly, interfacial engineering, and responsive materials. However, practical methods for fabricating such complex morphologies remain limited. Here, we demonstrate an instantaneous mechanically driven strategy for simultaneously programming particle shape and surface architecture through a refined rubbing process. By optimizing particle plasticization, pressure distribution, and stress transmission, spherical polymer particles were transformed into cylindrical particles within only 10 s. Patterned silicon substrates enabled direct mechanical transfer of periodic surface structures, while variations in substrate topology and deformation pathway produced diverse anisotropic architectures. This simple mechanically driven process provides a straightforward platform for programming hierarchical polymer microparticle architectures.

papers.title: Rapid, Reliable and Accurate XPS Depth-Distribution Functions from the Berger–Doggett method
papers.abstract: Two complementary rapid Monte Carlo methods for emission-depth distributions were introduced for Auger electron spectroscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy in 1993; the statistical weights method and the Berger-Doggett method. The statistical-weights method samples both elastic scattering directions and the distances between elastic events; the Berger–Doggett method conditions on the angular history and analytically averages over all such distances. These were much faster (by orders of magnitude) than previous methods and no less accurate. Besides reducing variance, the two methods should provide an unusually strong independent cross-check in their common domain of a homogeneous sample. As computer resources have progressively increased over the last 30 years, longer Monte Carlo runs have become practical, and in those a numerical instability can arise in the Berger-Doggett approach that we solve in this paper. We reformulate the original integral recurrence as a lower-bidiagonal system of linear ordinary differential equations with mixed boundary conditions. An ordered Schur decomposition selects the bounded invariant subspace and the required fluences are obtained from the action of a matrix exponential, avoiding the chance near-co-linear direction cosines that would occasionally frustrate the method published in 1993, and now allows very long Monte-Carlo runs to be performed quickly and reliably. In controlled tests the original method accumulated a relative error of 7.6 × 1010 at a cosine separation of 10−14, whereas the new formulation remained within 2.3 × 10−16 of a 120-digit reference. In a 500 angle-history recalculation using contemporary NIST SRD 64 elastic data, at a typical C 1s kinetic energy the old method gave a relative error of 6.2 × 1012 in the coefficient recurrence even though its closest pair of direction cosines differed by 1.15 × 10−4; the new formulation agreed with a 160-digit result to 1.6 × 10−16. This removes the need for extended or arbitrary precision without changing the underlying transport model. Routine Berger-Doggett calculations can now be done on a typical PC reliably and almost instantly, supporting also the statistical weights method by making it easier to verify implementations of it. This should be a significant step towards the automated extraction of all the information possible from nondestructive XPS depth-profiling. As an example of its wide applicability, the calculation confirms the physical basis of a previously proposed coaxial XPS geometry, producing a depth-distribution function with a subsurface maximum. Its considerable breadth, however, suggests enhanced subsurface selectivity rather than any general resolution of the ill-conditioning of depth-profile reconstruction.

papers.title: Mixed thiolate/alkoxide antimony cages for stable reversed-bilayer vesicle self-assembly
papers.abstract: A new two-step synthesis produces moisture-stable antimony and arsenic dithiothreitol cages. Structural analysis reveals that the Sb compounds self-assemble into reversed bilayers, consistent with pnictogen-bonded vesicle formation in organic media. The Sb assemblies more efficiently encapsulate and protect rhodamine B than the arsenic analogue or a topological mimic that lacks pnictogen-bonding capability. This work provides a synthetically accessible tool for partitioning organic media to allow for orthogonal reactivity.

papers.title: Nano-Focusing of Fiber-Guided Vortex Beam using Plasmonic Nanoantennas
papers.abstract: Optical vortex beams carrying orbital angular momentum (OAM) and cylindrical vector beams (CVBs) enable unique functionalities in optical communication, sensing, and chiral light-matter interactions. However, their use at the nanoscale is hindered by a spatial mismatch between the micron-scale beam and nanoscale targets, limiting light-matter coupling. In this study, we investigate a fiber-integrated plasmonic platform that confines fiber-guided vortex modes to subwavelength dimensions using a radially symmetric gold nanorod array on a polarization-maintaining ring-core vortex fiber facet. Full-vectorial finite-element simulations examine the coupling of radially polarized (TM 01 ), azimuthally polarized (TE 01 ), and circularly polarized (CP) OAM modes to the nanostructure array. The simulations predict symmetry-selective field enhancement and confinement to a ~300 nm central region (spatial confinement factor ~13), while preserving the polarization state, and helical phase of the OAM beam. The TM 01 mode yields the strongest enhancement through symmetry matching with the radial array, the CP-OAM modes show comparable enhancement and helicity-independent confinement, and the TE 01 mode couples weakly.
