Experimentally, we fabricate the nanostructure array on the fiber facet and characterize the transmitted modes in the far-field, where polarization-projection and coaxial interference measurements verify stable far-field propagation with nominal circular-polarization and topological charge magnitude | l |. These results establish a compact, scalable platform for predicted subwavelength confinement of structured light toward nanoscale light-matter interaction and chiral sensing.

papers.title: Adaptive Voiding Enables Interfacial Morphological Control at Low Stack Pressure in Solid-State Batteries
papers.abstract: Solid-state batteries with alkali metal anodes offer high energy density and improved safety, but their performance is hindered by void formation at the metal-solid electrolyte interface during metal stripping, leading to impedance rise and increased probability of dendrite formation upon plating. Here, we demonstrate that low concentrations (<5 vol%) of potassium metal added to industrial-grade lithium metal creates a dispersed Na-K liquid phase that suppresses voiding and enables stable, high-capacity stripping at practical current densities and stack pressures below 1 MPa. We furthermore identify a low-frequency oscillatory impedance attributed to “adaptive voiding”—the cyclic expansion and contraction of interfacial voids arising from an interplay between void growth and lithium deformation. This behavior, revealed by cryo-PFIB imaging and electrochemical analysis, offers a diagnostic signature for evaluating interfacial stability. These findings highlight new opportunities for designing robust, high-capacity SSBs operable under realistic mechanical constraints by controlling dynamic interfacial morphologies.

papers.title: Comprehensive Chemical Space Exploration in De Novo Drug Design: An Algorithmically Constrained, Parallel Dual-Paradigm Framework Validated on BACE1
papers.abstract: Isolated de novo drug design paradigms carry inherent vulnerabilities: ligand-based (LBDD) models risk unreliable extrapolation beyond their training domain, while structure-based (SBDD) genetic algorithms accumulate molecular size-bias across evolutionary generations. Furthermore, on structurally complex targets, deploying either paradigm in isolation risks systematically excluding viable chemical space. Here, we introduce a dual-paradigm framework addressing both failure modes through two novel algorithmic constraints: a Zoned Applicability Domain (AD) integrated as a live reinforcement learning reward gradient, and the Size-Independent Ligand Efficiency (SILE) metric deployed as a generational fitness function. A convergent validation cascade - pharmacokinetic filtering, exhaustive docking, and molecular dynamics - is architecturally positioned to eliminate artifacts these constrained engines may still produce. We evaluated this workflow on β-secretase (BACE1), deliberately selected because its electrostatic catalytic dyad and hydrophobic sub-pockets present divergent reward landscapes. Ablation studies confirmed the Zoned AD suppressed out-of-domain artifacts to enrich extrapolation, while SILE prevented meaningless molecular bloat compared to baseline models. The LBDD pipeline autonomously rediscovered 10 withheld experimental inhibitors, while the SBDD pipeline successfully decoupled docking affinity from molecular size, with both yielding leads with thermodynamic profiles comparable to the clinical reference verubecestat. Critically, the campaign demonstrated a fundamental algorithmic divergence: LBDD generates data-driven compounds inheriting the binding topology of known inhibitors, while SBDD explores pocket-complementary space with substantially different binding mechanisms. This suggests that parallel deployment of constrained paradigms may be necessary for systematic coverage of a target's viable binding space.

papers.title: van der Waals-Guided Nanopatterning Perovskite Nanocrystal Superlattices for Active Light-Emitting Metasurfaces
papers.abstract: High-resolution nanopatterning of self-assembled colloidal nanocrystal superlattices is crucial for their integration into miniaturized devices and integrated photonics. However, conventional top-down lithography often compromises supercrystallinity and dissolves constituent nanocrystals. Here, we introduce a non-destructive, bottom-up approach for the site-specific nucleation and growth of perovskite superlattices. Guided by the Lifshitz theory of van der Waals forces, we engineer a sharp permittivity contrast within nanotemplates to manipulate localized dewetting dynamics. This tailored interaction landscape establishes deep thermodynamic sinks that selectively drive the site-specific nucleation of CsPbBr3 nanocrystals. Corroborated by molecular dynamics simulations, we reveal that these dynamic energy sinks strictly restrict the rotational degrees of freedom of incoming nanocrystals, ultimately promoting highly ordered, face-to-face superlattice packing. This approach yields uniform, large-area arrays with subwavelength feature sizes and periodicities down to 200 and 350 nanometers, respectively, achieving an unprecedented array density exceeding 8 x 106 mm-2. Deterministic control over superlattice dimensions and array periodicity enables precise momentum-space engineering of radiation patterns, realizing highly directional light-emitting metasurfaces with an ultranarrow beam divergence of only 8.5°. Finally, we demonstrate the monolithic integration of these arrays into subwavelength electrically-driven active light-emitting metasurfaces, unlocking robust on-chip light modulation. This work establishes a robust pathway for translating the extraordinary properties of perovskite superlattices into next-generation on-chip nanophotonics.

papers.title: Interfacial Position Governs the Dual Functionality of Carbazole Layers in Cu2O Photocathodes
authors: Víctor A. de la Peña O’Shea
papers.abstract: Organic-inorganic hybrid photoelectrodes offer a promising strategy to improve charge separation in photoelectrochemical (PEC) systems, yet the influence of the spatial position of ultrathin organic interlayers remains poorly understood. Herein, we integrate electropolymerized carbazole-based conjugated porous polymers (CPPs) into Cu2O photocathodes by positioning the polymer either beneath or on top of the semiconductor. Both hybrid architectures exhibit en-hanced PEC performance compared with bare Cu2O, with the highest photocur-rent achieved when the polymer is deposited as an ultrathin overlayer. A combi-nation of electrochemical impedance spectroscopy together with femtosecond and nanosecond transient absorption spectroscopy reveals that the carbazole interlayer performs two distinct functions depending on its position within the hybrid architecture. When located beneath Cu2O, the polymer primarily facili-tates directional hole extraction and charge separation. In contrast, when depos-ited on top of Cu2O, the ultrathin polymer predominantly passivates surface defects, suppressing interfacial recombination and extending charge-carrier life-times while preserving efficient interfacial charge transfer. The triscarbazole-based polymer consistently exhibits slightly improved charge-transport proper-ties compared with its biscarbazole analogue. These findings demonstrate that the functionality of ultrathin organic interlayers is governed not only by their molecular structure but also by their spatial position within hybrid photoelec-trodes. More broadly, this work establishes interfacial positioning as a simple yet powerful design principle for engineering charge-carrier dynamics in organic-inorganic photoelectrochemical systemsgoes here.

papers.title: Nonlinear Optical Response in Water-Soluble Ionic Carbon Nitride Photocatalysts: A Two-Photon Absorption Study
papers.abstract: The two-photon absorption in water-soluble ionic PHI photocatalysts is investigated by single-beam z-scan. A systematic variation of sample concentration and laser irradiance shows that nonlinear absorption in the material is governed by trap states, the nature of which is controlled by the type of cation.

papers.title: A Systematic Approach to Batch Active Learning for Material Optimization
papers.abstract: Closed-loop automated experimentation platforms are accelerating materials characterization and discovery, but their efficiency hinges on a question that automation alone does not answer: given a fixed evaluation budget, which experiment configurations should be run next? Batch active learning addresses this by selecting a group of candidates at each iteration, yet the design choices that govern its efficiency, how many candidates to acquire per cycle, and how to balance exploitation against exploration remain poorly understood. Here, we present a systematic in-silico benchmark of batch active learning across optimization landscapes, prediction models, and dimensionalities, introducing composite metrics that track optimization progress and surrogate accuracy as co-equal outcomes. We find that an exploitative-dominant strategy with a small fixed exploratory minority matches or exceeds purely exploitative configurations while outperforming purely exploratory ones across landscapes, models, and dimensionalities, and that batchand cycle-efficient regimes are distinct and constraint-dependent. We further validate these findings on an automated coacervate condensate optimization platform, confirming their transfer to a real, noisy materials system.

papers.title: Order in Disorder: Exciton Dynamics Reveal Short-Range Molecular Packing in Small-Molecule Ionic Isolation Lattices Fluorescent Nanoparticles
papers.abstract: Organic fluorescent nanoparticles (NPs) enable exceptional brightness through high dye loading, yet the fundamental relationship between local molecular organization and exciton dynamics remains elusive because short-range packing in densely packed assemblies is difficult to resolve using conventional structural characterization techniques. Here, femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy reveals hidden short-range orientational order within globally disordered small-molecule ionic isolation lattice NPs (SMILES NPs) and establishes how this local organization governs exciton transport and fluorescence loss. Within locally ordered domains, fluorophore orientations are isotropically distributed within a two-dimensional plane perpendicular to the local stacking axis. Such local structural organization enables ultrafast exciton migration, followed by efficient energy funneling into non-emissive traps on a ~100 ps timescale, defining a kinetic window for exciton harvesting. Guided by this mechanistic insight, we introduce an emissive acceptor that captures excitons through sub-50 ps energy transfer, outcompeting trap-assisted quenching and producing binary SMILES NPs with a brightness per volume of 8700 M -1 cm -1 nm -3 , among the highest reported in the deep-red/near-infrared region. Collectively, this work establishes exciton dynamics as powerful probe of short-range molecular organization in dense molecular nanostructures and provides a molecular-packing-driven framework for controlling exciton transport and energy flow, offering general design principles for next-generation ultrabright emitters.

papers.title: Subtle differences in interlayer energetics dictate facet-dependent elastic and plastic flexibility in a molecular crystal
papers.abstract: Mechanically flexible molecular crystals hold promise for emerging functional materials such as optoelectronics and piezoelectrics. Here, we report a rare example of facet-dependent elastic and plastic bending in a molecular crystal. Synchrotron micro-focused X-ray diffraction mapping (µ-XRD) and X-ray quantum crystallography (QCr) reveal distinct domain-level structural changes during plastic versus elastic deformation and variations in intermolecular interactions across the slip planes that govern these distinct mechanical responses. Potential energy densities evaluated at the interaction regions from QCr models, along with the subtle difference in interlayer binding energies (ΔE = 2.2 kJ mol-1) reveal more robust interactions that underpin the elastically bending facet. µ-XRD mapping uncovers the atomistic origin of elastic deformation in terms of molecular reorientation (Δθ = 0.38°) and packing density gradients in the bent region, whereas plastic deformation proceeds via irreversible molecular slippage, quantified by a 5-fold increase in crystal mosaicity (from 0.06° to 0.30°). These findings correlate subtle electron-density and energetic features with the domain-level changes underlying this rare phenomenon.

papers.title: Single-particle FRET reveals ligand configurations on colloidal perovskite quantum dots
papers.abstract: The functionality of colloidal quantum dots (QDs), whether in fundamental studies, optoelectronics, or emerging quantum technologies, critically depends on their surface chemistry, with organic ligands influencing nearly every aspect of their behavior. Whereas the inorganic core can be comprehensively characterized at atomic resolution, ligands remain dibicult to probe owing to their low atomic contrast and soft, disordered structure. Here, we empower single-particle photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopy to resolve ligand conformations at sub-nanometer resolution. Tagging ligand tails with organic dyes enables measuring their distance from the QD via Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET). Single-particle, single-molecule FRET experiments performed on lead halide perovskite QDs reveal nanometer-scale variations in dye-surface distances, both within individual particles (0.81 ± 0.22 nm on average) and between QDs with varied ligand chemistries (from 0.25 nm to 1.02 nm). Supported by atomistic modelling, our experiments tie variations in the local ligand environment to this conformational diversity. A powerful yet accessible spectroscopic method for interrogating the complex surface chemistry of QDs is highly relevant to QD-based optoelectronics, quantum applications, and photocatalysis.

papers.title: Linking electronic and geometrical structure to local magnetism in lanthanide hexacyanoferrates by paramagnetic solid-state NMR
papers.abstract: Lanthanide hexacyanoferrates, LnFe(CN)6·xH2O, combine the structural versatility of cyanidebridged frameworks with the strong spin–orbit coupling and crystal-field effects of lanthanide ions. Yet, the local (ion-specific) origins of the magnetic response of these materials remain difficult to resolve by conventional solid-state chemistry techniques. Here, we report the 1H and 13C solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectra of LnFe(CN)6·xH2O (Ln = La to Yb), with assignments supported by first-principles calculations and optical spectroscopy. We interpret the 1H NMR spectra in terms of free (interstitial) and bound (Ln-coordinated) water environments within the porous framework. The 1H shifts and shift anisotropies scale approximately linearly with the lanthanide Bleaney coefficients, establishing a direct and quantifiable link between 1H spectra and single-ion anisotropy. Using 13C NMR spectra, we are able to isolate the impact of Ln composition, despite the Ln contribution comprising only a small fraction (up to 3%) of the total paramagnetic NMR shift. The 13C shift anisotropy also tracks linearly with the Bleaney coefficients, whilst the trend against the isotropic shift is weaker, underlining the site-specific effect of Fermi contact and dipolar contributions to the total shift. Together, out results establish solid-state NMR spectroscopy as a sensitive and quantitative probe of single-ion anisotropy in cyanide-based frameworks.

papers.title: Nitrile Geometry as an Architectural Code for Cu10 Nanocluster Metal–Organic Frameworks
papers.abstract: Atomically precise nanoclusters offer molecularly defined metal architectures, yet their conversion into extended frameworks remains difficult because reticulation must impose long-range order without erasing the structural adaptability of the multinuclear node. Here, we show that nitrile geometry can function as an architectural code for Cu10 nanocluster metal–organic frameworks (NCMOFs). Rather than relying on conventional pyridyl donors, we employ sterically minimal aryl nitriles whose weaker donor character is coupled to sharply defined coordination vectors. Natural population analysis confirms that nitrile N atoms are substantially less electron-rich than representative pyridyl donors, establishing a distinct electronic regime for cluster reticulation. Using terephthalonitrile (TPN), isophthalonitrile (IPN), and 1,3,5-tricyanobenzene (TCB), we obtain four crystallographically distinct frameworks— Cu10TPN-1D, Cu10IPN-2D, Cu10IPN-1D, and Cu10TCB-2Dthrough diffusion-controlled assembly of a common Cu–thiolate precursor. Single-crystal structures reveal that the Cu–N interface remains comparatively constrained, while Cu···Cu, Cu–S, and especially Cu–O metrics reorganize to accommodate different linker vectors and lattice demands. Strikingly, the same 120° IPN linker yields either 1D or 2D connectivity depending on the crystallization medium, demonstrating that linker geometry defines an accessible connectivity landscape rather than a predetermined topology. These results establish a broader design principle for NCMOFs: directional information can be encoded in a weakly donating linker, while structural compliance is retained within the nanocluster node, enabling adaptive multinuclear units to translate molecular geometry into distinct reticular states.

papers.title: Stannylene Ambiphilicity Enables Formation of a Trimetallic Complex
papers.abstract: Low-valent heavier group 14 tetrylenes combine a stereochemically active lone pair with a vacant p-orbital at a single centre, resulting in a unique ambiphilic reactivity profile. However, exploiting these donor–acceptor properties to construct transition-metal complexes featuring bridging tetrylene units remains largely unexplored. Here we report a flexible pincer ligand in which an N,O,N pocket stabilises the monomeric stannylene [(PNONP)Sn] (Sn1) that itself presents a P,Sn,P pocket for nickel coordination and can be employed, either stepwise or in one pot, to afford the isolable NHC-stabilised tin–nickel heterobimetallics [(PNONP)SnNi(NHC)] Sn4a,b (NHC = N-heterocyclic carbene). Reaction of Sn4a with W(CO)6, envisaged as a simple test electrophile for the tin-centred lone pair, instead proceeds via unanticipated NHC-to-CO exchange and the resulting NHC-free tin–nickel-carbonyl fragment self-associates to give the dimeric complex [(PNONP)SnNi(CO)]2 (Sn5). Treatment of Sn4a with [(p-cymene)Ru(Cl)2]2 affords the target heterotrimetallic Ni–Sn–Ru complex [(PNONP)Sn{Ru(Cl)2(p-cyemene)}Ni(IiPr2Me2)] (Sn6), in which tin bridges the metal centres in a genuinely push–pull fashion, representing the first structurally authentification of such a bonding mode for a heavy tetrylene.

papers.title: Intelligent Microscopy for Materials: Leakage-Controlled SEM Morphology Classification with Calibration, Explainability, and Artifact Perturbation
papers.abstract: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) image classification is increasingly used to organize large microscopy archives, but high predictive accuracy alone does not establish that a model is scientifically reliable. Duplicate images, class imbalance, acquisition annotations, poorly calibrated confidence, and post hoc use of test data can all make performance appear stronger than it is. This study develops a leakage-controlled and reliability oriented workflow for ten-class SEM morphology classification using the public NFFA-EUROPE 100% SEM Dataset v2.0. The 21,169 source images were audited before modelling. Full-file MD5 screening removed 332 exact duplicates,while a perceptual-hash/structural-similarity pipeline identified 92 high-confidence near duplicate groups and removed 95 additional redundant images, producing a final modelling cohort of 20,742 images. A single stratified 70/15/15 train/validation/test split was then frozen for all experiments. Three model families were evaluated under this protocol: a1,041-feature hand crafted image descriptor with classical machine learning, a convolutional neural network trained from scratch,and an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18. On the held-out test set, the selected ResNet-18 achieved 0.942802 accuracy, 0.930980 balanced accuracy,and 0.931633 macro-F1, compared with 0.7789/0.6713/0.6890 for the classical baseline and 0.7947/0.8421/0.7425 for the scratch CNN.Validation-fitted temperature scaling reduced test expected calibration error from 0.018974 to 0.011369 without changing predicted classes. Grad-CAM provided coarse spatial checks of model attention, while a controlled chromatic-annotation-region perturbation experiment showed a larger mean absolute class-probability change than equal-area translated controls (0.032554 vs 0.002420; Wilcoxon p = 1.07 x 10^-26), but only 4 of 172 targeted images changed predicted class. Selective prediction further increased retained-image accuracy to 0.980007 at approximately 90% coverage while rejecting 68.54% of all test errors. Together, these results support a predominantly morphology-driven transfer model with measurable localized artifact sensitivity and show how dataset integrity, calibration, perturbation analysis, and confidence-based review can complement headline accuracy in materials microscopy.

papers.title: Toward Property-Directed Catalytic Skeletal Editing of Functional Organic Materials
papers.abstract: Late-stage skeletal editing has emerged as a useful strategy in synthetic and medicinal chemistry for altering molecular frameworks by atom insertion, deletion, replacement, or bond reorganization. Functional organic molecules and materials are commonly optimized through peripheral substitution and de novo framework construction. Direct modification of an existing skeleton provides a complementary means of tuning electronic structure, molecular shape, chirality, packing, and processability. Herein we examine catalytic skeletal editing with an emphasis on functional organic materials, specifically π-conjugated molecules, dyes, polymers, and covalent frameworks. Representative examples are evaluated in terms of catalytic status and experimentally demonstrated properties. Key requirements for broader application include site selectivity, element transfer, catalyst compatibility, and control of editing extent in extended materials. The emerging opportunity is to move skeletal editing from reaction-centered diversification toward catalyst-controlled, property-directed modification.

papers.title: Vicinal Chlorination of Dehydrogenated Polyethylene Toward Applications of Waste Polyolefins
papers.abstract: Post-polymerization vicinal chlorination of unsaturated polyolefins provides access to linear poly(ethylene-co-1,2-dichloroethylene) polymers that are inaccessible through conventional polymerization or post-polymerization routes. Herein, Cl 2 (g), generated in situ from N-chlorosuccinimide (NCS) and hydrochloric acid (HCl), was used to selectively convert alkene sites in polycyclooctene (PCOE)-derived polyolefins into vicinal chloride subunits. Partial hydrogenation of PCOE afforded substrates containing 4–25 mol% residual C=C, which upon chlorination, yielded polymers with controlled levels and distributions of vicinal chlorides along a linear polyethylene backbone. Incorporation of chlorides into the PCOE-derived polymers disrupts crystal formation and reduces the glass transition and melting temperatures. For the 25 mol% vicinal chloride, the polymer affords precise placement of chlorides along the polymer backbone and transforms the orthorhombic crystal structure, typical of polyethylene (PE), to a triclinic crystal structure, suggesting the incorporation of Cl atoms to the crystallites. This method was further extended to dehydrogenated post-consumer HDPE from milk jugs, affording vicinal chlorinated polyethylene containing ~ 1.1 mol% vicinal Cl, while maintaining the original polymer chain architecture and molecular weight. These results establish vicinal chlorination of unsaturated PE as a strategy for tuning polymer properties and provide a platform for upcycling PEs into value-added functional materials.

papers.title: Use of Gas Chromatography, Nuclear Magnetic Resonance and Fluorescent methods to Estimate Enantiomeric Excess in Asymmetric Transfer Hydrogenation.
papers.abstract: The use of Gas Chromatography, Nuclear Magnetic Resonance and fluorescent methods to estimate ee are described, using asymmetric transfer hydrogenation (ATH) of acetophenone derivatives as a platform for the methodology. The use of rapid analysis processes may facilitate the screening samples through a simple process without having to use chiral HPLC or GC when generating an approximation of enantioselectivity.

papers.title: Origin of the Exceptional Activity in Molybdenum-Catalysed Dinitrogen Reduction with Samarium Diiodide and Water
papers.abstract: Molybdenum complexes supported by phosphine–ligand–phosphine (PLP) pincers, combined with samarium diiodide and water, convert dinitrogen to ammonia under mild conditions with nitrogenase-like activities. Using explicitly correlated coupled-cluster calculations, spin–orbit corrections, and realistic concentration and speciation models, we elucidate the cleavage mechanism from N 2 -bound Mo(I) complexes to ammonia release. Dimerisation proceeds through pentacoordinate Mo(I)–N 2 complexes, and N 2 activation is controlled by terminal N 2 dissociation, which converts a [Mo]–N≡N–[Mo] unit into cleavage-ready [Mo]=N=N=[Mo] before spin crossover and bond scission. The resulting nitrido intermediates are reduced by outer-sphere, Sm-mediated concerted proton-coupled electron transfer (cPCET). This pathway avoids the high-energy charge-separated intermediates of stepwise PT/ET and the loss of strong azaphilic Sm(III)–N interactions upon Sm–OH formation in inner-sphere alternatives. Aggregation into ammonia-binding Sm(III) hydroxide oligomers and precipitation stabilise the product states and render reduction effectively irreversible. These features explain the exceptional activity of Mo/SmI 2 /H 2 O systems. The first cPCET is rate-determining under typical conditions, whereas N 2 activation becomes limiting at low catalyst concentrations or with electron-withdrawing ligands. Pincer geometry and π-acidity facilitate cPCET, but efficient catalysis requires ligands that avoid over-stabilising low Mo oxidation states during N 2 activation while accommodating changing coordination numbers across the cycle.

papers.title: Molecular rotor-regulated target-selective photoinactivation of myostatin
papers.abstract: Photoinactivation allows precise spatiotemporal control of biomolecules in biological systems. Among the photoinactivation strategies, photooxygenation is advantageous, as it can be readily induced with a photosensitizer upon photoirradiation in biological environment. However, its utility is limited by poor target selectivity arising from the excessive generation and high reactivity of reactive oxygen species. Here, target-selective photoinactivation of myostatin is achieved using a target-binding ligand functionalized with a molecular rotor-based photosensitizing unit whose photooxygenation activity is enhanced upon binding to the target protein. A novel molecular rotor-based photosensitizer was developed and conjugated to a myostatin-binding peptide. The resulting functionalized peptide selectively oxygenated and inactivated myostatin under near-infrared irradiation. Treatment with the peptide followed by irradiation decreased endogenous myostatin levels in skeletal muscle, leading to increased muscle weight and muscle fiber size. This target-selective photoinactivation strategy may expand the applicability of photoresponsive approaches for the treatment of various diseases, including muscular dystrophy.

papers.title: Concise Total Synthesis of (–)-5-epi-Cycloclavine via Metal- and Base-Free Diastereoselective
papers.abstract: A metal- and base-free intramolecular cyclopropanation based on nonstabilized donor carbenes generated in situ from N-sulfonylhydrazones has been developed, enabling the construction of the highly strained aza[3.1.0]bicyclic core of (–)-5-epi-cycloclavine with concomitant complete stereocontrol of two all-carbon quaternary stereocenters. Combined with the straightforward introduction of methacrylic acid as four-carbon fragment from readily available enantiopure functionalized tricyclic indole derivative (4-amino Uhle's ketone), this strategy enabled a concise diasteroselective synthesis of the five-fused rings system present in (–)-5-epi-cycloclavine.

papers.title: Inter-Phase Chirality Transfer in 2D and Quasi-2D Perovskite Heterostructures
papers.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) chiral metal halide perovskites (CMHPs) emerged as promising materials for spintronics. These 2D semiconductors comprise single layers of corner-sharing metal halide octahedra (n = 1) intercalated by organic cations, which limits charge mobility and spin lifetime. In comparison, quasi-2D analogs, with two or more octahedra layers (n ≥ 2), exhibit higher charge carriers mobility, augmented spin lifetime, and tailorable bandgap. Nonetheless, the few reports on quasi-2D CMHPs in the literature often describe time-consuming synthesis and materials presenting poor chiroptical properties after processing. We address this limitation by designing heterostructure thin films comprising a chiral n = 1 phase with a non-chiral n = 2 phase. Circular dichroism (CD) manifestation in the non-chiral phase confirms chirality transfer in the heterostructures. We found that chirality transfer depends on the intermolecular interaction of the chiral and non-chiral cations, being effective when R-/S-𝛼-methylbenzylammonium (MBA) in the chiral phase is combined with benzylammonium (BZA) in the non-chiral phase. Chirality transfer is weak when n-butylammonium (BA) is used in the non-chiral phase. We attribute this difference to a more effective intermixing enabled by 𝜋-𝜋 stacking in the MBA/BZA heterostructure. This inter-phase chirality transfer strategy opens a new avenue for spintronic materials design.

papers.title: Immunometabolic Signaling Networks in HIV Persistence: From Cellular Metabolism to Reservoir Control
papers.abstract: Combination antiretroviral therapy (cART) successfully suppresses systemic HIV-1 replication, yet latent reservoirs persist in long-lived memory CD4+ T cells, myeloid lineages, and specialized anatomical sanctuaries. While previous immunometabolic studies have documented altered bioenergetic profiles in infected host cells, the upstream signaling mechanisms that govern these metabolic states and drive viral fate remain incompletely defined. Here, we present a comprehensive framework positioning intracellular immunometabolic signaling networks—specifically PI3K–AKT–mTOR, AMPK, and HIF-1α—as central transducers linking extracellular microenvironmental signals to cellular bioenergetics, epigenetic remodeling, and viral persistence. We evaluate how the interplay between mTOR-, AMPK-, and HIF-1α-associated signaling influences metabolic and transcriptional states that may shape the balance between active viral expression and deep transcriptional latency. Furthermore, we examine how oxygen-sensing through HIF-1α, tissue-specific nutrient microenvironments (in GALT, lymph nodes, and the CNS), and mitochondrial ROS signaling shape reservoir longevity, clonal expansion, and resistance to apoptosis. Finally, we discuss therapeutic strategies, contrasting traditional "shock and kill" approaches with "metabolically reprogram and kill" modalities designed to lower the threshold for latency reversal. Understanding and therapeutically manipulating the signaling–metabolism–latency axis may provide new strategies for disrupting viral reservoirs and promoting durable HIV remission.

papers.title: Reversible solidification of liquid organic hydrogen carriers
papers.abstract: Liquid organic hydrogen carriers (LOHCs) are a promising option for hydrogen storage, but their transportation and long-term storage are complicated by sloshing, leakage, evaporation, and the associated safety issues. They are hard to gelate or solidify using conventional gelators due to factors such as steric hinderance and/or the lack of pi-pi conjugation within their molecular structure. Here, we report a one-pot reversible solidification strategy that converts hydrogenated LOHCs into free-standing monolithic solids without compromising their hydrogen-storage performance. The solidified carriers can prevent sloshing during transportation and potential leakage upon tank fail. The vapor pressure and fire intensity of LOHCs are reduced by 66% and 16.5%, respectively. As a result, their mass retention rate increased by 2.8-fold after one week of open storage and their mass loss rate is reduced by 3.4-fold after 24 hours of vigorous vibration compared with regular LOHCs.

papers.title: A tertiary network couples hydrophobic substitutions to terminal contacts in an IDP
papers.abstract: Conformational ensembles of intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) are sensitive to changes in amino acid sequence. Even chemically conservative substitutions can alter global properties and interactions far from the mutation site, but how these effects propagate across the sequence remains unclear. Here, we investigated six chemically conservative substitutions at site 66, in addition to the naturally occurring Val66 sequence of the intrinsically disordered Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor (BDNF) prodomain to understand how a substitution near the center of the sequence affects the termini. Using 896 µs of all-atom explicit-solvent enhanced molecular dynamics simulations and Blobulation, we find that each substitution affects ensemble compactness, which was reflected in contacts between the terminal hydrophobic blobs. For five of the seven sequences, we identified contact associations consistent with an indirect pathway connecting the mutation site to the termini through an intermediate hydrophobic blob. Our findings provide a mechanistic framework for understanding how chemically conservative substitutions produce sequence-dependent changes in IDP ensembles and establish an approach for identifying direct and indirect interaction pathways through which the effects of a mutation propagate.

papers.title: Engineering chirality in threaded BODIPYs
papers.abstract: In this article, we explore the possibility of introducing chirality at different structural levels within boron-threaded BODIPYs. Three strategies were investigated, involving a chiral macrocycle, a stereogenic boron center and an axially chiral BODIPY dimer. In the latter case, double threading through boron coordination was achieved for the first time. The optical and chiroptical properties of the three chiral systems were investigated. While the chiral macrocycle leads to the most pronounced chiroptical response with clear evidence of chirality transfer to the BODIPY, all three architectures display measurable electronic circular dichroism and circularly polarized luminescence. These results demonstrate that chirality can be deliberately positioned at distinct structural levels of threaded BODIPYs, providing a modular platform to investigate the interplay between molecular architecture and chiroptical properties.

papers.title: Machine-Learning Models Bypass Charge Computation for Modeling 14N Quadrupolar Relaxation in Ionic Liquids
papers.abstract: Modeling the electric field gradient (EFG) in molecular dynamics (MD) simulations enables the prediction of nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) relaxation rates thus allowing to unravel the underlying relaxation-active molecular motion. Here, we compare the linear-response Sternheimer model with a novel machine-learning (ML) approach to simulate 14 N quadrupolar T 1 relaxation in the ionic liquid 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium tetrafluoroborate ([BMIM][BF 4 ]). Improving the parametrization of the Sternheimer model at the low-symmetry nitrogen sites required an electron density-based charge-partitioning scheme. In contrast, the parameter-free ML descriptor directly captured the EFG dynamics, providing a flexible methodology for computing EFG tensors in complex ionic systems. In the extreme-narrowing regime, both models predicted relaxation rates in excellent agreement with experimental measurements. Finally, using a regularized inverse Laplace transform, we deconvolute the dynamics of the EFG tensor and of the cation inertia tensor, and identify molecular rotation as the dominant mode responsible for 14 N quadrupolar relaxation.

papers.title: Structural characterization of fully chemically modified siRNA with lipid conjugate and divalent architecture
papers.abstract: The development of delivery platforms, including lipid conjugates and multivalent scaffolds, has accelerated the emergence of extrahepatic-targeting small interfering RNA (siRNA). These molecular architectures have advanced multiple clinical-stage siRNA candidates targeting the central nervous system (CNS) and other extrahepatic tissues, underscoring an urgent need for analytical methodologies capable of resolving conjugate-derived fragmentation pathways and symmetric multivalent structures that complicate their characterization by tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS). Here, we develop complementary MS/MS and data-interpretation strategies for structural characterization of lipid-conjugated and fully chemically modified divalent siRNA using ion-pair-free hydrophilic interaction liquid chromatography (HILIC). Conjugate-derived fragmentation pathways were first established using a lipid-conjugated oligonucleotide standard via collision-induced dissociation (CID), higher-energy collisional dissociation (HCD), and ultraviolet photodissociation (UVPD), and the resulting framework was then applied to characterize a human Huntingtin (HTT)-targeting lipid-conjugated siRNA. For analysis of a symmetric divalent siRNA, a customized terminal fragment-based data-processing strategy was developed that preserved the complete molecular architecture and enabled assignment of terminal fragment ions from both halves of the construct without relying on internal fragments. This workflow provided comprehensive sequence characterization of divalent siRNA while substantially improving recovery of informative 3ʹ-terminal fragment ions compared with the conventional static 3ʹ-modification method. Collectively, the lipid-fragmentation framework and terminal fragment-based interpretation approach provided a robust analytical platform for structural characterization of increasingly complex conjugated and multivalent RNA therapeutics.

papers.title: Photocatalytic synthesis of functionalized polymers on primary human T cells
papers.abstract: Polymers can be designed to impart new functions to the surfaces of tissues and cells, making them valuable tools for bioengineering applications. Existing grafting-to methods suffer from low polymer grafting efficiencies – due in part to challenging-to-control lipid anchoring strategies. One solution to these limitations is to adopt a grafting-from approach, where polymers are synthesized at defined initiation sites on the cell surface. Previous studies have highlighted the value of cytocompatible photocatalyzed grafting-from polymer chemistries or site-specific covalent anchoring of initiation sites; however, unification of these features remains unexplored. Further, no grafting-from technologies have been applied to surface engineering of primary human cells. To address this gap, we have combined Photo-Induced Electron-Transfer Reversible Addition-Fragmentation Chain-Transfer (PET-RAFT) chemistry with site selective surface anchoring of a custom traceable oligomeric polymer initiation site. We show that our approach enabled efficient grafting-from chain extension of functionally diverse polymers anchored on cell surface carbohydrates (glycans). The approach was compatible with both an immortalized human cell line and primary human immune cells (T cells). This technology provides a framework for site-selective modification of primary cell surfaces without genetic manipulation.

papers.title: A scalable framework for goal-driven task-based simulations
papers.abstract: Realistic surfaces of active materials that involve the motion of atoms or ions in their function typically change their (sub-)surface composition and geometry under operating conditions due to varying environmental stimuli, degradation or healing processes, but also just while exhibiting their intended function, making it difficult to build simulation models that remain valid as the system evolves. Such problems often demand large-scale computation together with efficient data processing, so scalable task execution and data-efficient synchronization become critical. We present a scalable computational framework that supports large collections of independent computation tasks with incremental result aggregation. We demonstrate the framework using adaptive kinetic Monte Carlo (akMC) as a showcase application, where transition-state searches are performed on-the-fly. The new framework employs a hierarchical orchestrator–worker architecture implemented with modern MPI constructs and operates efficiently from single workstations to multi-node high-performance computing systems. It integrates well-established simulation engines such as LAMMPS and supports multi-core CPU and GPU parallelism within each task. Performance is demonstrated using classical, machine-learning, and GPU-accelerated interatomic potentials. Benchmarks show strong scaling across multiple compute nodes with several hundreds of CPU-cores, efficient utilization of multi-core executors and GPU sharing. The results indicate that the framework provides an efficient solution for rare-event and mesoscopic simulation workflows.

papers.title: Aqueous Crystallization Unlocks Tunable Structural Color from Isoxanthopterin
papers.abstract: In nature, some animals generate reflective tissues through the controlled precipitation of organic matter. Whether assembled as amorphous structures within the lumen of butterfly wing scales to produce color, or as spherulitic nanomaterials within the epithelial cells of certain vertebrates and crustaceans to enhance visual acuity, certain biomolecules exhibit a conserved capacity to template structures whose refractive index and morphology directly govern optical properties. One such example, isoxanthopterin, produces some of the most reflective structures found in biology yet remains largely unexplored as an engineered material, owing in part to its limited solubility. We investigate the chemical principles underlying isoxanthopterin assembly in aqueous solution and show that the balance between electrostatic repulsion and hydrogen bonding governs crystal formation, with pH tuning this balance to modulate size and, in turn, bulk optical properties. These structural and optical differences reveal simple design principles for engineering color from a single starting biomolecule, informing the design of future aqueous-based optical materials

papers.title: In Situ and Operando Neutron Powder Diffraction of NaxNiO2: a Case Study for Sodium-ion Batteries
papers.abstract: Neutron powder diffraction (NPD) is a non-destructive technique uniquely suited to investigating industrially relevant sodium-ion cathode materials. Unlike X-ray diffraction, it offers excellent contrast between neighbouring transition metal ions and is sensitive to lighter elements such as O/Na, which are key to revealing superstructural orderings characteristic of sodium cathodes. However, in situ/operando NPD battery studies are hindered by sample quantity requirements, and lack of suitable sample environments. Using a cell developed at ISIS Neutron and Muon Source, we observed no detrimental effects from prolonged vacuum exposure required for Time-of-Flight NPD. We collect/analyse data in two modes: operando, in which the electrochemical structural evolution is tracked, and in situ, wherein higher signalto-noise data is collected during voltage holds, for phase-pure samples at set voltage cutoffs. Using Na x NiO 2 as a model system, we present a methodology to account for the complex background profile characteristic of electrochemical environments enabling, for the first time, quantitative Rietveld refinements against in situ electrochemical NPD, and providing a systematic framework for future studies. Structural models are refined against in situ data and benchmarked against combined refinement of ex situ SXRD/NPD measurements. This work unlocks potential for previously inaccessible insights into structure-property relationships and degradation, helping to facilitate the development of next-generation cathodes with enhanced useful lifetime, capacity, and performance.

papers.title: Integrated CO2 removal and NH3 recovery from wastewater using a bidirectionally productive electrochemical pH swing
papers.abstract: Electrochemical pH-swing processes based on proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) offer a promising route for selective chemical separation from aqueous media. Yet in all previous systems only one half of the pH swing performs a separation, while the reverse half is expended solely to regenerate the state of charge of the active electrode or electrolyte. Using a synthetic mimic of domestic wastewater as the input feed, we demonstrate a bidirectionally productive electrochemical pH-swing generated by a phenazine-carbon nanotube PCET-active composite electrode in an aqueous flow cell, in which both the acidifying and alkalizing half-cycles perform useful chemical separation. Electrode oxidation acidifies the wastewater to convert dissolved inorganic carbon into CO 2 (aq) for removal, whereas the subsequent reduction alkalizes the feed, converting NH 4 + to NH 3 (aq) for recovery using membrane stripping. An experimentally validated reaction-transport model establishes the pH-swing sequence as a key design parameter, with oxidation before reduction enabling integrated CO 2 removal and NH 3 recovery, whereas the opposite sequence prioritizes NH 3 recovery through near-complete NH 4 + -to-NH 3 conversion. The system achieved batchwise NH 3 recovery using the reduction–oxidation sequence over 31 cycles spanning 43 h, establishing operational stability over a duration not previously demonstrated for PCET-driven nutrient recovery. The oxidation–reduction sequence achieved average energetic costs of 219.9 kJ mol -1 CO 2 removed and 12.2 kWh kg -1 N recovered, with corresponding separation rates of 4.47 μmol CO 2 h -1 cm -2 and 5.33 g N m -2 day -1 , respectively. By making both directions of an electrochemical pH swing productive, this work reframes electrode regeneration as an opportunity for a second separation, and points toward wastewater treatment plants as distributed sites for combined nutrient recovery and carbon removal.

papers.title: Nitroarylphosphines: An Overlooked Family of Ligands
papers.abstract: Homoleptic tris(nitroaryl)phoshines are very rare, “explosive-looking” molecules that have until now never been fully characterized. We show that they are accessible from nitroarylphosphine oxides and are, perhaps surprisingly, sufficiently thermally stable to be handled at ambient temperature and used as ligands. We show experimentally and computationally that they display significantly modulated electronic properties and we demonstrate several examples of their coordination complexes, thus showing the nitro group is an overlooked tuning tool in phosphine coordination chemistry.

papers.title: Breath Acetone Sensor for Subclinical Ketosis Detection in Dairy Cows
papers.abstract: Subclinical ketosis (SCK) in dairy cows is a prevalent metabolic disorder that can reduce milk production, impair animal health, and causes substantial economic losses. Current diagnostic approaches are invasive and poorly suited for routine and autonomous on-farm detection. Here, we demonstrate non-invasive breath acetone sensing for monitoring metabolic changes associated with SCK in dairy cows. Breath samples (n = 235) were longitudinally collected over 35 days from seven dairy cows (five SCK-induced and two controls) using a custom-designed sampling mask. A chemoresistive sensor based on WO3 nanoparticles exhibited high selectivity toward acetone over interferents (e.g., ethanol, acetic acid, methane and isoprene) at their typical concentrations in cow breath and barn air. Good agreement (R2 = 0.81) with proton-transfer-reaction time-of-flight mass spectrometry was obtained for acetone quantification over a concentration range of 54 – 4,500 ppb. Time-resolved measurements revealed that the sensor captured dynamic post-partum acetone changes, including rapid increases, late-onset elevations, and stable low-level profiles. These trends were consistent with blood β-hydroxybutyrate and milk acetone measurements, supporting the physiological relevance of breath acetone as a non-invasive biomarker of SCK. These results demonstrate the potential of chemoresistive breath acetone sensing as a practical approach for longitudinal, on-farm monitoring of dairy cows for SCK detection.

papers.title: Nanothermodynamic Generalization of the Young–Laplace and Young Equations for Sessile Droplets with Line Effects
papers.abstract: Thermodynamic investigations of wetting phenomena require that we handle the nanoscale. By combining Hill’s small-system thermodynamics with a Gibbsian composite-system description, we formulate the equilibrium thermodynamics of a sessile nanodroplet. We consider a one-component liquid droplet resting on an ideal, flat, inert solid substrate and in contact with reservoirs that fix the temperature and chemical potential. Finite-size effects are retained in the liquid bulk phase, the liquid–vapor interface, and the three-phase contact line, while the solid–vapor and solid–liquid interfaces are assumed to follow regular thermodynamics and treated macroscopically. The distinction between integral and differential pressure, surface tension, and line tension is used to derive nanothermodynamic generalizations of the Young–Laplace and Young equations. The resulting equations account for the size-and shape dependence of the finite thermodynamic contributions and recover the classical equilibrium equations in the macroscopic limit.

papers.title: Extended QM/Me: Quantum-Mechanical Explicit Solvation at Solid–Liquid Interfaces
papers.abstract: We extend the subtractive QM/Me embedding scheme from vacuum to liquid environments: the adsorbate and explicit solvent are treated by a periodic quantum-mechanical layer above a classical metal bath, avoiding the need for metal–solvent interaction parameters. For methoxy on Pt(111) in water (3070 quantum atoms), the performance of three tight-binding Hamiltonians for adiabatic solvation shifts is assessed. The embedding provides analytic energy gradients and substantially reduced computational cost compared to a fully quantum-mechanical model.

papers.title: Benzimidazole Modification of DNA Aptamers for Ultra Responsive Protein-Induced Fluorescence Enhancement
Do crown ethers fully dissociate ion pairs in aqueous solution?
papers.abstract: In alkali fluoride solutions, crown ethers are widely assumed to generate "naked" anions by capturing cations, yet direct evidence for complete ion-pair dissociation is limited. We combine 19F Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) and multiscale modeling on aqueous NaF and KF with 18crown-6 (18C6). Fluoride diffusion slows on crown addition, scaling linearly with the crownbound cation fraction across both salts and extrapolating to zero without complexation. The 19F chemical shifts independently establish this retained ion pairing. For KF, the signal moves away from the free-ion baseline, the wrong direction for liberation. While NaF responds more weakly, the theoretical chemical shift profile shows that the crown-bound cation carries a shielding contact (CIP) region and a deshielding solvent-shared (SIP) region whose cancellation flattens the response. Molecular dynamics confirm reduced but persistent contact pairing. Crown ethers thus suppress contact pairing while retaining both solvent-shared and residual contact associations with the sequestered cation.

papers.title: Concerted, Facile CO2 Hydrogenation in Ni-MOF-74 Revealed by Machine Learning Interatomic Potential-Based Enhanced Sampling Simulations
papers.abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) with open metal sites are promising heterogeneous catalysts, but the atomistic and dynamic details that govern their reactivity are difficult to access experimentally due to spatiotemporal resolution limits. Computational studies, predominantly gas-phase density functional theory (DFT) calculations, have been used to study MOF-catalysed reactions, but typically rely on reduced cluster models of the metal center that neglect confinement effects or treat the framework as rigid during the reaction, limiting realistic modeling of catalysis at finite temperature and pressure. Here, we investigate, as a prototypical reaction, CO2 hydrogenation inside Ni-MOF-74 using machine learning interatomic potentials-based molecular dynamics and on-the-fly probability-based enhanced sampling (OPES) simulations, which delineate dynamic adsorption of CO2 and H2 in a flexible MOF and provide the underlying free energy for the CO2 reduction reaction. OPES simulations further reveal that H2 first adsorbs and undergoes heterolytic dissociation at the Ni-O site with a free energy barrier of ∼16 kcal mol−1, forming a proton and hydride species. Subsequent reduction of CO2 to HCOOH proceeds via a concerted mechanism, involving simultaneous hydride and proton transfer through a single transition state with a relatively low activation barrier of ∼6 kcal mol−1. These results demonstrate that explicit treatment of framework flexibility and thermodynamic conditions is essential to accurately capture reaction mechanisms and energetics in porous catalysts. Our integrated MLIP-OPES approach provides a generalizable computational framework for studying complex chemical transformations under confinement in MOFs and related framework materials.

papers.title: A Hidden Acid–Base Ion Pair Scaffolds Organic-Rich Atmospheric Nucleation
papers.abstract: New particle formation is widely observed in organic-rich atmospheric environments where sulfuric acid and basic vapors appear scarce, yet what initiates nucleation and what role trace inorganic acid–base species play remain unclear. Guided by laboratory experiments and field observations, we resolve this ambiguity with a bottom-up framework bridging molecular energetics and nucleation kinetics, tracking nucleation from molecular origin to measurable formation rates. We uncover a hidden pathway in which a multifunctional oxygenated organic molecule (OOM) hydrogen-bonds simultaneously to sulfuric acid and ammonia, inducing proton transfer and stabilizing a charge-separated HSO 4 - –NH 4 + ion pair. This ion pair forms a localized electrostatic scaffold that recruits additional OOMs into a charge-assisted hydrogen-bond network, yielding stable embryonic clusters. Remarkably, a single ion pair unlocks this mechanism, indicating that even trace inorganic species can be indispensable nucleation triggers. Operating across diverse biogenic and anthropogenic OOM systems, ion-pair-scaffolded nucleation may be ubiquitous in the atmosphere.

papers.title: Understanding and quantifying interfacial ion exchange in hybrid electrolytes
papers.abstract: In pursuit of practical solid-state lithium batteries with low cost and scalable manufacturing, hybrid electrolytes that combine Li + -conducting inorganic electrolyte particles with liquid or polymer electrolytes have emerged as a promising strategy. 1-2 In these systems, Li + needs to transport through the interface between the percolating organic electrolyte matrix and the dispersed inorganic particles. However, interfacial Li + transport dynamics remain poorly understood largely due to lack of reliable experimental measurements. 3-4 Here, we introduce two straightforward nuclear magnetic resonance techniques − spin saturation transfer and selective inversion-recovery − to directly and unambiguously quantify Li + exchange in hybrid electrolytes. This enables us to build a new theoretical framework based on the exchange kinetics to analyze Li + transport in organic-inorganic hybrid electrolytes. By studying several representative hybrid electrolytes, we demonstrate that the ratio of inorganic particle radius and ionic Kapitza length predicts whether the incorporation of Li + -conducting particles into organic electrolytes will lead to hybrid electrolytes with improved conductivity. This study thus provides quantitative measurements and physical scaling principles to systematically design hybrid electrolytes for solid-state batteries.

papers.title: Coordinate bonding, cluster delocalization and topological criticality in a cyclic trimeric beryllium–dinitrogen complex
papers.abstract: Fixation and coordination of molecular dinitrogen (N2) by main-group clusters offer fundamental insight into non-classical multi-centre bonding and light-metal activation pathways. Here we report a combined density-functional and ab initio study of the cyclic cluster Be3(N2)3. Geometry optimization and frequency analysis establish a stable, closed-shell Cs-symmetric trimer containing an isosceles triangular Be3 metal core coordinated end-on by three terminal N2 ligands. Energy decomposition analysis coupled with natural orbitals for chemical valence (ETS-NOCV) shows that the Be3⋯(N2)3 interaction is dominated by orbital contributions (≈60 % of attractive forces), supplemented by electrostatic attraction that together overcome Pauli repulsion. Quantum theory of atoms in molecules (QTAIM) identifies two non-nuclear attractors along the apical–basal Be–Be edges, while electron localization function (ELF) and localized orbital locator (LOL) basin analyses reveal a distinct heart-shaped trisynaptic valence basin V(Be,Be,Be) populated by ≈1.8–2.0 electrons. These topological signatures establish multi-centre σ-aromatic delocalization as the structural foundation of the central metallacycle and demonstrate that light alkaline-earth elements can support non-classical N2 coordination frameworks.

papers.title: Cooperative Inorganic-Organic Binding Sites in Zeolite Adsorbents Enhance CO <sub>2</sub> Capture and Water Resistance
papers.abstract: Optimization of amine-based adsorbents for carbon capture technologies requires next-generation materials capable of handling a broad range of operating conditions with high amine efficiency. The current disadvantages of liquid amine absorbents motivate the design of porous solid analogues as alternatives. Here we present a bifunctional zeolite comprised of silanol defects and grafted amines that cooperatively bind CO 2 with 97% amine efficiency. We use a borosilicate beta zeolite as a parent material and generate a high density of silanol defects through facile post-synthesis demetalation, followed by amine functionalization. Spectroscopic techniques and density functional theory calculations confirm that silylpropylcarbamate species enhance CO 2 binding through an activated process with optimal performance at 100℃, which markedly reduces the temperature swing for regeneration without loss in performance after multiple cycles. Systematic analysis of carbon capture performance reveals that CO 2 sorption capacity doubles when shifting from high to low temperature, and is positively influenced by humidity.

papers.title: Connected, but for how long? A residual-lifetime criterion for the hydraulic–diffusive boundary in polyamide reverse-osmosis membranes
papers.abstract: The mechanism of water transport through the polyamide active layer of reverse-osmosis membranes is again contested: a 2023 claim that transport is governed by pore flow rather than solution-diffusion reopened a debate many considered settled, and a two-phase treatment has since shown the two descriptions are not mutually exclusive once their coefficients are matched. That reconciliation, however, answers a phenomenological question, not a structural one: whether a genuine, pressure-bearing continuous water phase exists is a separate, testable claim about the material. This Perspective argues that settling it requires two conditions prior work has largely treated as one — an instantaneous through-connected topology, and its survival over the transport timescale — and that the second condition has so far been estimated the wrong way: from the total lifetime of a connectivity interval rather than the residual lifetime seen by a water molecule arriving at a random instant, the same statistical root as the inspection paradox. A dynamic accessibility measure, Adyn = θ·SR(τtr), is proposed to close this gap, built on an intensive areal connectivity measure θ and a residual-lifetime survival function SR rather than an assumed exponential decay. A minimal structural surrogate places the connectivity transition at a model water-accessible volume fraction of 0.14–0.17, close to atomistic estimates for real polyamide, and a comparison of accessible simulation timescales with the residence time implied by realistic operating conditions shows why molecular dynamics alone cannot currently resolve the question. A concrete, falsifiable test agenda is proposed.

papers.title: Integrating Theory–Experiment Active Learning and Mechanistic Insights for High-Entropy Alloy Design Toward Efficient Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution
papers.abstract: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) offer diverse local coordination environments for modulating hydrogen adsorption and water activation in alkaline hydrogen evolution, but their highdimensional compositional space remains difficult to explore efficiently. Theory-experiment closed loops can accelerate this search, yet theoretical prior and candidate sampling are commonly coupled, obscuring their individual contributions. Here, we developed a theory-experiment activelearning (TEA) framework that independently varies theoretical priors and candidate sampling strategies for AuCuPdPtIr HEAs. Under identical experimental throughput, the theoretical prior provided transferable performance trends across composition space, whereas the proposed adaptive sampling strategy broadened effective compositional coverage. After three iterations involving 120 compositions, the framework identified Au16Cu5Pd35Pt35Ir9, which required only 16 mV overpotential to reach 10 mA cm-2 in 1 M KOH. An anion-exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE) cell using this catalyst as the cathode reached 1 A cm-2 at 1.647 V and 60 °C and operated stably for 1000 h. Model interpretation, operando infrared spectroscopy, machine-learning-potential molecular dynamics (MLP-MD) simulations, and charge-density analysis further associated Ir/Cu-related local environments with a weaker interfacial hydrogenbond network and more Volmer-like water configurations. This work connects controlled module comparison, data-efficient compositional optimization, and interfacial-water mechanisms, providing a general strategy for complex multicomponent electrocatalysts.

papers.title: From Computational Chemistry to Generative Models: A Survey of AI-Driven Small-Molecule Drug Discovery
papers.abstract: Small-molecule drug discovery requires navigating enormous chemical space to identify candidates that are simultaneously potent, selective, synthetically accessible, and acceptable across pharmacokinetic and safety profiles; modern generative AI extends a long computational medicinal chemistry lineage that began with QSAR, pharmacophore modeling, and early structure-based de novo design. This survey focuses primarily on developments from 2017 to 2025, with the literature updated through 31 January 2026. Using a medicinal-chemistry lens, it first establishes the shared machinery of the field: molecular representations such as SMILES, SELFIES, graphs, fingerprints, three-dimensional coordinates, voxels, and latent vectors; commonly used datasets and benchmarks; and graph neural network encoders, including message-passing, directional, and equivariant architectures. We compare five principal generative mechanisms—autoregressive models, variational autoencoders, generative adversarial networks, normalizing flows, and diffusion models—together with reinforcement learning as a major goal-directed optimization framework. Across these approaches, we show that current methods offer complementary rather than interchangeable trade-offs, and we highlight recurring challenges, including validity versus synthesizability, limited prospective experimental validation, mode collapse and diversity loss, stereochemical and physical realism in three-dimensional design, computational cost, data scarcity, and the emerging convergence toward scaffold-conditioned generation, hybrid architectures, developability-aware optimization, and molecular foundation models.

papers.title: Targeted mitigation strategies for critically polluted PM2.5 regions in India using spatially constrained airsheds
papers.abstract: Air pollution in India is a regional problem, yet the current air quality management policy is largely city-centric. Here, we developed an airshed management framework that emphasizes cooperative action for PM2.5 pollution mitigation. This framework identifies air pollution control areas (APCAs) for targeted emissions control across four critically polluted regions in the Indo-Gangetic Plain by mapping sectoral emissions from administrative units to pollution levels to meet specified air quality targets. We find that the dominant emission sectors differ across APCAs, such as agriculture, transport, and domestic to micro, small and medium-scale industry, highlighting the inadequacy of broad regional airshed management and the need for tailored air quality management plans. This framework yields differentiated policy guidance at the airshed and sub-airshed scales for the districts that constitute an APCA, leading to a spatially fine-tuned and implicitly minimal-effort mitigation plan. The developed framework is generalizable worldwide to polluted regions at any PM2.5 level.

papers.title: Metabolic Competition Reshapes the Performance of Engineered Polyketide Synthases
papers.abstract: Directed evolution is widely used to enhance enzymatic performance and evolve new-to-nature reactivities, typically in vitro or in model microbial systems. However, variants selected in a model host may not retain their relative performance in the intended production organism. Here, we engineered a single 2-pyrone synthase (2PS) scaffold by directed evolution in Escherichia coli ( E. coli ) and evaluated the resulting variants in both E. coli and planta. In E. coli, engineered 2PS variants showed distinct chemoselectivities, giving access to precursors for kavalactones and raspberry ketone from one protein scaffold. The best variant achieved >98% conversion of p -coumaric acid to >200 µg/mL bisnoryangonin. In planta, however, variant performance was reordered: the top-performing microbial variant was outperformed 2.7-fold by one with lower activity in E. coli . We traced this host-dependent shift to competition for the shared p -coumaroyl-CoA pool and identified cinnamoyl-CoA reductase from Nicotiana benthamiana ( Nb CCR) as a key competing enzyme. Introducing Nb CCR into E. coli recapitulated the variant rank order observed in planta, demonstrating that metabolic competition can reshape the performance of engineered enzymes across hosts. These results also suggest that reconstructing key competing pathways of the target host in a tractable microbial system can provide a practical strategy for engineering enzymes for otherwise difficult-to-evolve production hosts. Finally, 2PS variants enabled the chemoenzymatic synthesis of natural and fluorinated kavalactones with up to 64% isolated yield over two steps.

papers.title: An Atomistic Workflow for Determining Acid-Base Prototropic Tautomer Microstate Populations
papers.abstract: We present a new cheminformatics package, Protomer Enumerator & Automatic Calculator for Energies (PEACE), which lists the prototropic forms of a given acid or base, and predicts which of these microstates are likely to be present in solution. The workflow enumerates prototropic tautomers, and orchestrates inexpensive semi-empirical quantum chemical simulations to evaluate their single-point energies, solvation free energies, entropic contributions, and ultimately their solution-phase energies. The relative population of each tautomer is then calculated. PEACE includes automatic error checks, tautomer screening, and conformational effects to improve speed and accuracy. It can be run in several solvent systems and on charged solutes. Herein, we demonstrate the workflow’s efficacy on numerous practical benchmarks including on druglike molecules. The workflow is freely available for use through the command line with minimal package dependencies.

papers.title: Efficiency and Accessibility Are Not Enough: Chemical-Validity Filtering in High-Throughput Screening of Organic Photovoltaic Materials
papers.abstract: Descriptor-based screening for organic photovoltaics ranks molecules on computed properties such as frontier-orbital energies and synthetic accessibility, but such descriptors do not test whether a highly ranked molecule is a chemically sensible material. We screened 17,458 molecules from the PubChemQC database using PCESAScore—Scharber-model efficiency minus the RDKit synthetic-accessibility score—and examined what the metric actually returns. Seven molecules cross the viability threshold, but three are not organic semiconductors (molecular oxygen, a magnesium carbonate salt, a quinhydrone cocrystal) and three more carry reactive groups (two azides, one nitroso). A transparent chemicalvalidity filter and a reactive-group screen reduce the viable set from seven to four to a single stable candidate. The top-ranked molecule, an azidotriazine, reaches a 36.1% nominal efficiency—above the Scharber model’s single-junction ceiling—from a 0.91 eV gap, and carries a 9.26 D dipole and a negative computed reorganization energy: signatures of an unusable material, not a lead. Across the dataset, heteroatom composition correlates only weakly with orbital energies (|r| ≤ 0.34), so no simple design rule holds. Descriptor-based materials screens require an explicit chemical-validity and stability gate; the gap between the pre-and post-gate viable sets is a result in itself.

papers.title: Which state are you converging? A spin audit of sample-based quantum diagonalization benchmarks on iron–sulfur clusters
papers.abstract: Sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD/QSCI) diagonalizes the Hamiltonian classically in determinant subspaces selected from quantum-circuit samples. Its iron–sulfur demonstrations underpin claims of utility-scale quantum chemistry, and a recent critique disputes them at matched subspace dimension. Both sides compare energies; neither reports which spin state was computed. Our spin audit uses the exact determinant-space ⟨S²⟩, the invariant spectrum of the S² block over quasi-degenerate manifolds, and higher moments (⟨S⁴⟩ to ⟨S⁸⟩) bounding the spin-sector weights. We apply it to the public [2Fe-2S] and [4Fe-4S] benchmarks, IBM's released qiskit-addon-sqd pipeline and published hardware data. No audited execution returned the named singlet at competitive energy; for published states unavailable to direct audit, the energy-only records do not establish singlet identity. Under the audited HCI protocols, selected-CI growth approaches a spin-contaminated state (⟨S²⟩ ≈ 4.7 on [2Fe-2S]) whose samples keep the contamination. Spin-inversion completion leaves the energy and ⟨S²⟩ of these states unchanged. The released [2Fe-2S] hardware samples give no energy advantage over the released uniform-random control. A scalar mean does not identify these states: two audited arms share ⟨S²⟩ ≈ 2.00, but one is a triplet eigenstate (Var(S²) = 3×10⁻⁶) and the other a 2:1 singlet–quintet mixture whose third moment bounds its triplet weight below 10⁻⁴. At the largest published dimension (5.625×10⁷ determinants, reconstructed here from the released support), the lowest root, 170 mHa below the published energy, has ⟨S²⟩ = 1.3711, unchanged under an 18.6-fold residual tightening to 1.1% of the 0.285 mHa gap. Its first two moments, with Var(S²) = 6.9, exclude any decomposition confined to S ≤ 2. Near-singlet character appears only as a non-stationary superposition, because determinant selection does not commute with S². Energy-only benchmarks therefore do not establish convergence to the named state. We recommend reporting spin moments with every energy and controlling spin during selection.

papers.title: There is no knee in Ragone: clarifying battery energy and power fade using Ragone plots
papers.abstract: Ragone plots provide a compact representation of energy storage performance by relating accessible energy to power. Despite this, battery degradation is often described using simplified metrics such as “energy fade” and “power fade”, which obscure changes in the overall performance envelope. Here, we propose a shift towards a Ragone-based analysis of degradation, enabling a more comprehensive assessment of battery health. We use physics-based models to simulate ageing under a range of operating conditions and degradation modes, and evaluate Ragone plots over the course of ageing. Each degradation mechanism leaves a distinct signature in the Ragone plots, which can be directly associated with energy and power fade, as well as with specific internal states of the battery. We also show that the widely reported “knee” in reference performance tests is an artefact of testing protocols, rather than an intrinsic feature of battery behaviour, underscoring the advantages of Ragone-based characterisation. Finally, we introduce a systematic empirical method to extract energy and power fade from Ragone plots. These results demonstrate that Ragone analysis provides a more powerful framework for diagnosing, interpreting, and ultimately mitigating battery degradation in practical applications.

papers.title: Tetraethylammonium Cations Enable C2+ Product Formation in Acidic CO2 Reduction
papers.abstract: Cation effect is essential to obtain selectivity towards carbon dioxide (CO 2 )​ reduction reaction (CO 2 ​RR) over the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in acidic media. Selectivity towards CO 2 RR has been largely attributed to the coordination between alkali cations and CO 2 -derived intermediates. Here, we provide a different perspective by demonstrating that tetraethylammonium (Et 4 ​N + ), a weakly coordinating cation, can also effectively suppress the HER in acidic media, favoring CO 2 ​RR on both Ag and Cu electrodes. The generation of both C 1 ​ and C 2+ ​ products on Cu indicates that the direct participation of alkali cations as co-catalyst is not a prerequisite for CO 2 activation or C-C coupling. We find that CO 2 ​RR is independent of the bulk pH in the presence of 1 M Et 4 ​N + , as evidenced by similar selectivity across acidic, neutral, and alkaline media. In addition, rigorous impurities control reveals that millimolar-levels of triethylammonium chloride (Et 3 ​NHCl) substantially promote HER on Cu catalyst, hence calling for careful impurity control. Overall, this work reveals the use of Et 4 ​N + as an valuable platform to investigate the effects of cations or impurities for CO 2 ​RR.

papers.title: Influence of Non-Polar Amino Acids on the Phase Transitions of Atmospheric Aerosol Particles
papers.abstract: The fate of aerosol particles in the atmosphere depends in part on their composition, morphology, and phase transitions. Studies of aerosol phase transitions have focused on aerosol particles with organic compounds consisting of C, H, and O atoms, although a substantial fraction of organic compounds contain heteroatoms such as sulfur and nitrogen. In this study, non-polar amino acids were used to study the effect of organonitrogen compounds on the phase transitions of droplets using optical microscopy. The ternary internal mixtures used were composed of ammonium sulfate (AS), a non-polar amino acid, and either 2-methylglutaric acid (2MGA) or 1,2,6-hexanetriol (126HT) (model oxidized organic compounds). The morphology, phase transitions, and spatially resolved chemical composition were characterized using optical and Raman microscopies. A suppression of the separation relative humidity was observed when the concentration of amino acid was more than 50% of the organic compound by weight. For some systems, the amino acid crystallizes, while the oxidized organic compounds and ammonium sulfate undergo liquid-liquid phase separation, yielding a three-phase system. Trends in the efflorescence relative humidity depend on the solubility of the amino acid. These studies are important in understanding the impact of organic-organic interactions as well as organonitrogen compounds on the phase transitions of aerosol particles, which have consequences for heterogeneous chemistry and cloud droplet nucleation in the atmosphere.

papers.title: Spacing Over Sequence: Design Considerations for Polystyrene-binding Polypeptides
papers.abstract: Plastic-binding polypeptides have emerging applications in biosensor design, materials functionalization, and nanoplastic capture, and the rational design of new sequences requires the development of structural and sequence-based design principles. Here, we demonstrate a computational workflow combining atomistic molecular dynamics simulations and enhanced sampling to evaluate polypeptide binding to polystyrene, a common commodity plastic. We investigate two candidate sequences previously proposed as polystyrene binders, both enriched in either aromatic or cationic residues expected to interact with polystyrene's aromatic rings. We find that the two sequences bind stably through apparent π-stacking and cation-π interactions. These binding modalities rely on proper residue spacing; not all cationic residues on a polypeptide bind unless separated by linking residues as demonstrated by our “arginine claw” motif. We also determine that the presence of the polypeptide does shield the polystyrene from contacts with solvent, though it does not promote further self-collapse of the oligomer. Our analysis demonstrates how sequence composition coupled with sequence orientation enables multiple binding modalities, determining motifs such as the “arginine claw” and aromatic ring distribution that can be leveraged in future polypeptide design.

papers.title: In Situ Co-Activation–Nucleophilic Aromatic Substitution (ISCA–SNAR): Synthesis of a-Aryl-a-Heteroarylmalononitriles.
papers.abstract: We report the discovery of a fundamentally unique nucleophilic aromatic substitution (S N Ar) reaction. It was found that a-arylmalononitriles and haloheterocycles undergo a mild, additive- and base-free C–C bond forming reaction via in situ co-activation (ISCA) to a carbanion and a pyridinium, which rapidly react through a neutral and low-barrier Meisenheimer complex to ultimately yield the S N Ar product.
