This study includes a background analysis of ISCA-S N Ar and a-aryl-a-heteroarylmalononitriles, discovery and optimization of efficient coupling conditions, a study of various physical organic parameters governing the transformation, scope of the reaction, and select malononitrile functional group interconversions. These detailed studies lay the groundwork for developing this, and related reactions, for use in high-value organic synthesis.

papers.title: Dielectric Nanolensing: How a Wavelength-Scale Lens Carries Hidden Detail into an Ordinary Microscope, and What Chemistry Should Build Next
papers.abstract: Dielectric nanolensing has evolved from a wavelength-scale molecular lens into a broad family of microsphere, particle-lens, scanning, arrayed, and computational platforms. Breakthrough advances now include white-light nanoscopy, immersed high-index imaging, large-field scanning, non-destructive semiconductor metrology, living-cell optics, nanolithography, and substrate-free Raman analysis. This Perspective explains, in accessible terms, how a lens placed in the specimen’s near field can redirect otherwise inaccessible spatial information into light collected by an ordinary objective. It then reconciles curvature, solid immersion, nanojets, Mie and whispering-gallery modes, and Fano interference as condition-dependent contributions rather than competing universal explanations. The central opportunity is forward-looking: chemistry can control complex refractive index, shape, assembly, environment, and the nanometre-scale lens-specimen gap, while quantitative transfer measurements can replace incomparable resolution claims. Together, these developments point toward scalable, calibrated nanolenses for imaging, metrology, and chemical analysis.

papers.title: Redox-Promoted Reactivity of Uranium, Neptunium, and Plutonium Diamide Complexes
papers.abstract: The chemically active 5 f orbitals of the early actinides give rise to a number of accessible oxidation states, as well as contribute to complex redox behavior that is sensitive to changes in the coordination environment of the metal. Understanding how these electronic and coordination effects translate into structural transformation remains a central challenge in fundamental actinide chemistry. Herein, we present a crystallographic and spectroscopic investigation of redox-promoted reactivity in uranium, neptunium, and plutonium complexes supported by malonamide and diglycolamide ligands, which provide flexible O-donor coordination environments for investigating structural chemistry of early actinides as a function of the oxidation state. A series of molecular [An VI O 2 (ma)(NO 3 ) 2 ], [An VI O 2 (tmma)(NO 3 ) 2 ], and [An VI O 2 (tmdga) 2 ](NO 3 ) 2 complexes across the U−Np−Pu series has been prepared and structurally characterized, providing a platform for examining chemical transformations induced by ligand degradation and electron transfer (ma = malonamide; tmma = N,N,N′,N′ -tetramethylmalonamide; tmdga = N,N,N′,N′- tetramethyldiglycolamide). Aging these complexes in acidic media leads to the formation of unexpected products spanning multiple oxidation states, including oxalate-bridged actinyl dimers generated through oxidative degradation of diglycolamide ligands, mixed-valent Pu(IV)/Pu(VI) molecular ion pairs, and neptunium species that evolve from monomeric Np(VI) complexes to mixed-valent Np(V)/Np(IV) assemblies featuring Np V =O yl −Np IV actinyl–actinide interactions before complete reduction to Np(IV) products. Complementary single-crystal Raman spectroscopy provides vibrational fingerprints of the actinyl units and coordinated ligands, supporting the structural assignments and enabling comparisons across the U–Np–Pu series. These results demonstrate that diamide ligands may serve as both coordination platforms and active participants in redox chemistry, giving rise to reaction pathways that generate previously inaccessible molecular species.

papers.title: Hydrogen diffusion on metals: Full-Dimensional Ring Polymer Molecular Dynamics Rate Calculations
papers.abstract: The diffusion of hydrogen atoms on nine different metals: Co, Ni, Cu, Rh, Pd, Ag, Ir, Pt, Au, has been simulated by ring polymer molecular dynamics. For Co, the (0001) surface facet has been chosen, while for all other metals, (100) surfaces are investigated. For the nine systems, message-passing atomic cluster expansion (MACE) machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) were set up by means of self-consistent biased fine-tunings. The H diffusion was sampled first with the MACE MP-0 foundation model by means of umbrella samplings along the diffusion path; then, a subset of sampled structures was recalculated by periodic density-functional theory (DFT) and the MACE was fine-tuned with the obtained reference data. This was repeated once to correct for biases of the foundation model concerning the sampling of configuration space. Thorough benchmarking revealed that the fine-tuned MLIPs were reliable and of high quality, also for situations not covered by the training set. The fine-tuned MACE MLIPs were then used to sample the full-dimensional diffusion rate constants with the Caracal program for temperatures between 20 and 300 K, in 10 K steps, and from them obtain the temperature-dependent diffusion coefficients. Crossover temperatures to the deep tunneling regime were calculated as well.

papers.title: Cross-Conjugation Effect in Benzotrithiophene-Based Covalent Organic Frameworks
papers.abstract: Bandgap engineering in covalent organic frameworks (COFs) is critical for their optoelectronic and photocatalytic applications, but it remains far less developed compared to linear p-conjugated polymers. Here, we demonstrate that permutation of π-conjugation pathway provides a general strategy to tune the electronic structure of covalent organic frameworks (COFs). An asymmetric benzotrithiophene ( A BTT) node enables a more efficient electron delocalization compared to its commonly used symmetric analogue ( S BTT), resulting in ∼0.05–0.2 eV band-gap contraction and improved charge-transport properties in corresponding COFs, with electrical conductivity up to 1.6×10 –1 S cm –1 in iodine-doped films.

papers.title: Small Organic Molecules Regulate Transport-Limited Dendrite Growth in Aqueous Zn Battery Anodes
papers.abstract: Understanding electrochemical crystal growth at high rates and under far-fromequilibrium conditions is important for a broad range of industrial processes, including metal electrowinning, semiconductor plating, and electrochemical energy storage. In particular, transport-limited metal electrodeposition, which often produces aggressive dendritic morphologies, plays a critical role in the behavior of fast-charging battery anodes. Although small organic molecules such as urea are known to influence electrodeposition, their effects have primarily been studied at moderate current densities well below the mass-transport limit. Here, we investigate how urea affects Zn metal growth in concentrated aqueous battery electrolytes (10 M ZnCl2) under explicitly transport-limited conditions. Using operando visualization together with ex situ characterization, we find that urea transforms Zn dendrite structure once its concentration exceeds a threshold. In the absence of organic additives, Zn forms quasi-single-crystalline, needlelike dendrites whose crystallites exhibit apparent orientational correlation across the entire dendrite, over length scales of centimeters. This behavior suggests sustained growth from a small number of initially nucleated crystals. In contrast, above 5 wt.% urea, the dendrites initially lose their long-range orientational correlation before reverting to needle-like propagation. We attribute this transition to urea adsorption on the Zn surface, which modifies the relative kinetics of nucleation and crystal growth. Comparisons with structurally related small molecules indicate that molecular symmetry and functional group selection play an important role in governing this behavior: asymmetrical acetamide yields needle-like growth similar to the additive-free baseline, whereas retaining symmetry with methyl groups using acetone provides a dense morphology that extends cell lifespan. These findings provide new insight into the molecular regulation of electrochemical crystal growth under far-from-equilibrium conditions and may inform strategies for controlling Zn deposition in fast-charging aqueous batteries.

papers.title: Force-Programmed Evolution of Topological Freedom in Slide-Ring Polymer Networks
papers.abstract: Force-adaptive polymer networks, whose mechanical response evolves under load, offer a route to structural materials that combine high stiffness and strength with efficient energy dissipation.[1,2] Most existing force-adaptive systems achieve this through mechanochemical reactions that generate reactive intermediates and thereby stiffen or rearrange the network,[3-5] a strategy that is intrinsically limited by diffusion, reaction kinetics, and the irreversible consumption of the reactive species. Here we pursue a fundamentally different strategy, in which a force-triggered transformation regulates the topological freedom of a slide-ring crosslink[6,7] rather than driving a chemical reaction. We integrate a mechanophore directly into the stopper of a rotaxane crosslinker, in which a cyclobutane formed by the [2+2] photodimerization of two cinnamate units[8,9] acts as the bulky stopper that confines a 24-crown-8 macrocycle on a dibenzylammonium axle.[10,11] Under load, retro-[2+2] cycloreversion reduces the steric dimension of the stopper and thereby expands the sliding space accessible to the macrocycle, so that a single covalent event gates a large slidingdissipation channel rather than dissipating energy directly. We incorporated this crosslinker into a segmented polyurethane and evaluated it against an orthogonal three-member sample set (R, C1, C2) of identical crosslinker content that decouples whether the stopper can open from whether the macrocycle can slide. The optimal composition, R3, reaches a toughness of about 215 MJ m-3 and a tensile strength of about 38 MPa—up to 9.4 and 5.6 times the toughness and strength of the openbut-cannot-slide control (C1), and far exceeding the constitutively sliding control (C2). Smallstrain dynamic mechanical analysis confirms that the mechanophore is silent at low strain, whereas gradient cyclic loading reveals a force-activation fingerprint: the dissipation ratio of R3 rises from below both controls at 100% strain to above them at high strain, crossing over near 300–400%. Infrared spectroscopy detects the regenerated cinnamate C=C band only after stretching and only in the cyclobutane-bearing samples,[8,9] and an annealing-reload test shows that the extra dissipation of R3 is largely recoverable with the smallest permanent damage of the three, consistent with a reversible sliding channel that shields the matrix.[12,13] These results establish a general design principle in which the structural precision of a mechanochemical transformation programs the evolution of topological freedom during deformation.

papers.title: Dynamic Parameter Screening for Accelerated Mechanistic Analysis
papers.abstract: Mechanistic studies are essential for the continued advancement of the chemical sciences however; classical approaches remain laborious and material intensive. Graphical reaction analysis techniques such as RPKA and VTNA have substantially reduced this burden, yet the time and resources required to comprehensively study increasingly complex reactions remain high. Medium- and high-throughput batch and flow kinetic methods have been developed to further streamline data acquisition, but their widespread adoption is limited by the need for specialized equipment or expertise. Here we introduce dynamic parameter screening (DPS), in which a single batch reaction is monitored continuously while sequential reagent and catalyst additions are used to probe kinetic impacts of multiple species within one experimental setup. Using the palladium-catalyzed Kumada–Tamao–Corriu cross-coupling as a model system, we compared DPS with traditional one-factor-at-a-time approach across three catalytic systems (PdCl2(dppf)·CH2Cl2, PEPPSI-iPr, and XPhos Pd G2). DPS afforded essentially identical qualitative and quantitative (kinetic modeling) conclusions except for the case of XPhos Pd G2. This latter system exhibited multiple kinetic regimes where the traditional approach revealed the global impact of reagent concentrations, whereas DPS provided complementary, higher-resolution insight into reagent effects within a specific kinetic regime. The insights obtained from DPS guided a simple slow-dosing strategy that markedly improved reaction rates even at reduced catalyst loadings. DPS therefore provides a practical, low-barrier route to high-resolution kinetic information that is fully compatible with conventional modeling, broadening access to mechanistic understanding in resource-limited settings.

papers.title: Sensory Roles of 2-Methyl-3-furanthiol, 3-Methyl-2-buten-1-thiol, and 2-Furfurylthiol in Beer :Olfactometric Evidence and Trace-Level Quantification by Complementary GC-MS Methods
Direct Synthesis of Covalent Organic Framework Monolayer via Ullmann Coupling on Non-metallic Substrates
papers.abstract: Two-dimensional covalent organic framework monolayers are promising porous materials for electronic and optoelectronic applications owing to their periodic nanoporous architectures and tunable electronic structures. However, on-surface Ullmann coupling used to construct such frameworks typically relies on catalytic single-crystal metal substrates, whose strong electronic coupling can obscure the intrinsic properties of the molecular layer and complicate device integration. Here, we demonstrate substrate-engineered Ullmann coupling of 1,3,5-tris(4iodophenyl)benzene toward monolayer two-dimensional covalent organic networks on nonmetallic substrates. On inert highly oriented pyrolytic graphite, externally deposited Fe species promote C–I bond activation and covalent coupling, whereas FeO thin films enable network formation without additional metal deposition through defect-derived Fe active centers. Density functional theory calculations reveal that the energetically favored pathways on HOPG, FeO, and Au(111) all involve transient metal-centered intermediates that facilitate dehalogenation and C–C bond formation, although the catalytic centers originate from different sources. Bias-dependent scanning tunneling microscopy further shows that substrate coupling governs the visibility of frontier electronic states: weakly interacting HOPG preserves orbital-like features that closely resemble calculated frontier states of the freestanding framework, whereas stronger interactions on FeO and Au(111) progressively perturb or screen these states. These results establish nonmetallic substrates as viable platforms for on-surface Ullmann coupling and highlight substrate engineering as a strategy for accessing intrinsic electronic properties of two-dimensional covalent organic materials.

papers.title: Low-threshold Deep-red Organic Laser Dye Based on a Vinylene-bridged Benzothiadiazole Dimer in a Donor–Acceptor–π–Acceptor–Donor Framework
papers.abstract: Organic laser dyes emitting at long wavelengths often suffer from high amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) and lasing thresholds because nonradiative relaxation is promoted by the energy-gap law. Herein, a deep-red-emitting laser dye, trans - BTDA , is developed using a donor–acceptor–π–acceptor–donor framework combining triphenylamine donors and a vinylene-bridged benzothiadiazole (BTD) dimer as the acceptor–π–acceptor core. The π-extended BTD dimer narrows the energy gap, while mixed locally excited and charge-transfer character with favorable orbital overlap contributes to a large radiative rate constant ( k r ). In thin films, trans - BTDA exhibits deep-red ASE at 652 nm with a low threshold of 3.54 μJ cm –2 , while trans - SBA , containing a stilbene unit instead of the BTD dimer, exhibits blue ASE at 476 nm with a threshold of 0.81 μJ cm –2 . Both dyes also achieve low-threshold distributed feedback lasing at 651 and 473 nm, with thresholds of 0.85 μJ cm –2 and 0.33 μJ cm –2 , respectively. Minimal spectral overlap between the ASE and ground- and excited-state absorption spectra indicates low optical losses. trans - BTDA further shows favorable photostability under continuous excitation, even for the red emitter. In conclusion, the vinylene-bridged BTD dimer enables sharp deep-red emission with a large k r and low ASE and lasing thresholds.

papers.title: Achieving Sustained Conformational Exploration with Continually Adaptive Local Memory Sampling
papers.abstract: Enhanced sampling techniques aim to expedite the exploration of molecular conformations and their associated transitions. The extended adaptive biasing force method (eABF) is an enhanced sampling technique that applies a biasing force to targeted collective variables (CV), which serves to overcome energy barriers that would normally delay conformational transitions. With eABF, the biasing force is adaptively constructed to nullify the average force acting along the CV, effectively removing barriers to promote accelerated transitions. However, the eABF biasing force can become unresponsive to CV-coupled environmental dynamics, leading to hindered CV sampling. Therefore, in order to promote persistent CV transitions, we developed the continually adaptive local memory (CALM) sampling method, designed to sustain adaptation of the eABF biasing force. This is achieved by maintaining a limited sampling memory, which allows for CV moves to continually synchronize with coupled environmental dynamics. Herein, we show CALM effectively accelerates conformational sampling of alanine dipeptide and deca-alanine in vacuum and also deca-alanine and the mini-protein chignolin in explicit water. As a result of maintaining biasing force adaptability, we illustrate how CALM promotes sustained CV transitions via access to hidden conformational pathways that are not accessible via eABF.

papers.title: Leveraging Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials into Fitting Fast and Accurate AMBER-Compatible Precise Force Field
High-Entropy Catalysts for Lithium-Sulfur and Room-Temperature Sodium-Sulfur Batteries: Electronic Descriptors, Performance, and Design Challenges
papers.abstract: Lithium-sulfur (Li-S) and room-temperature sodium-sulfur (RT Na-S) batteries offer high theoretical energy density at low materials cost, but the insulating nature of sulfur, the shuttling of soluble polysulfides, and sluggish multistep redox kinetics limit their practical use. Catalysts that anchor polysulfides and accelerate their conversion are a widely investigated remedy, and the field is moving from single-metal catalysts toward high-entropy catalysts (HECs) built from five or more principal elements. This review is organized around the electronic descriptors, principally the d-band center and its refinements, that are used to connect multi-element composition to polysulfide adsorption and to reaction barriers. We define configurational entropy quantitatively, separate genuine HECs from lower-order multimetal catalysts, survey the alloy, oxide, sulfide, and single-atom families with attention to mechanism and limitations, and treat the still under-demonstrated RT Na-S case explicitly. We then examine the first-principles workflow required for chemically disordered surfaces and the emerging, mostly non-sulfur, use of machine learning (ML). Our central conclusion is that the d-band center is a useful but non-universal descriptor whose predictive value depends on local coordination, oxidation state, surface reconstruction, solvation, and polysulfide coverage, and that direct evidence for entropy-derived synergy, and for high-entropy catalysis in RT Na-S specifically, remains incomplete.

papers.title: Machine-learning force-field scoring rivals free-energy perturbation for congeneric ligand ranking across public benchmarks
papers.abstract: Relative binding free-energy (RBFE) methods such as free-energy perturbation (FEP) set the accuracy standard for ranking congeneric ligands in structurebased drug design, but their computational cost limits throughput. Machine-learned force fields (MLFFs) now approach quantum-chemical accuracy at a small fraction of that cost, raising the question of whether they can recover much of RBFE’s ranking accuracy while remaining computationally efficient. We introduce a static-score methodology called taqo and benchmark 10 MLFF variants spanning 6 model families (UMA, MACE, Orb, eSEN, AIMNet2, AllScAIP), together with a classical molecular-mechanics force field, on a uniform staticpocket protocol, correlated against experiment across 22 benchmark systems.We find that the ten MLFFs cannot be resolved from one another at this sample size, while every one of them significantly outranks the classical force field reference, at a few seconds per ligand on a single GPU. Against published OpenFE and FEP+ results on the same systems and the same ligand sets, taqo is statistically indistinguishable from OpenFE and significantly below FEP+, at roughly three orders of magnitude lower cost. On the congeneric JACS subset taqo and FEP+ are statistically indistinguishable. On the same benchmark poses taqo outperforms classical docking scores and is statistically indistinguishable from deep-learning affinity models, without any affinity-specific training. Together these establish MLFF interaction-energy scoring as a practical high-throughput approach for lead optimization.

papers.title: Predicting Thermophysical Properties of Halide Salts Using On-the-Fly Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials Across Multiple Exchange-Correlation Functionals
papers.abstract: In silico modeling of molten salts is pivotal for developing emerging carbon-free energy technologies. Accurate prediction of their thermophysical properties using first-principles methods remains computationally intractable owing to the large length and timescales required. Further, the choice of exchange-correlation (XC) functional critically governs the predictive accuracy of thermophysical properties. Here, we train machine learning force fields to investigate the thermophysical properties of NaBr, KCl, and AgCl, representing alkali- and transition-metal halides, across their solid and liquid phases, systematically benchmarking ten XC functionals for NaBr (600-1400 K) and testing the transferability of the best-performing functional to KCl and AgCl. These MLIPs enable prediction of densities and ionic diffusion coefficients at length and timescales beyond ab initio simulations, while capturing the first-order solid-liquid transition. We find that BEEF-vdW accurately predicts the optimized lattice constants of NaBr and KCl, consequently reproducing experimental solid and liquid densities, with Na+ and Br- self-diffusion coefficients agreeing with experiments to within ~5%. However, we find that the BEEF-vdW functional inaccurately predicts AgCl density owing to its inaccurate lattice constant, whereas PBE-D3 yields excellent density agreement (~5% deviation) across both phases. This work establishes a foundation for high-throughput generation of molten-salt thermophysical databases using general machine learning potentials.0

papers.title: Tree-Based Classification of Functional Groups from IR Spectra: Feature Importance Corroborates Quantum-Chemical Fragment Frequencies
papers.abstract: Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy is a widely used analytical technique for identifying functional groups in chemical compounds, but its interpretation remains labor-intensive and reliant on expert knowledge, especially for complex or multicomponent samples. This study presents a tree-based Random Forest (RF) machine-learning framework, successfully developed to predict the presence of specific functional groups (FGs) from an infrared spectra database. Stratification was employed to address positive class imbalance, maintaining the F1-score drop under 12% across models. All models achieved strong overall performance, with accuracy, F1-score, ROC-AUC, and out-of-bag (OOB) scores exceeding 0.8. Of the 46 FGs modeled, 43 demonstrated acceptable performance, while only three underperformed, as categorized by their Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) and precision-recall area under the curve (PR-AUC) scores. Threshold tuning further improved model performance, yielding up to a 9% increase in MCC score. Finally, feature importance extracted from the trained models exhibited strong interpretability, correlating with theoretically predicted IR spectra and bridging experimental data with theoretical chemical significance. These results establish a robust, interpretable framework with potential for integration into intelligent monitoring and process optimization systems.

papers.title: Thermodynamics-Driven Treatability Investigation of Energy-Storage-Related
papers.abstract: Bis-perfluoroalkyl sulfonimides (bis-FASIs), widely used in lithium-ion battery electrolytes, are increasingly detected in the environment, yet their transformation and treatability remain poorly understood. Here, density functional theory (DFT) calculations were integrated with experiments to determine how molecular structure controls bis-FASIs degradation. During electrochemical oxidation (EO) and UV/sulfite (UV/S) treatment, degradation and defluorination generally increased with perfluoroalkyl-chain length, with bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)imide (bis-FMeSI) being the most recalcitrant homolog. Although both processes nearly completely transformed bis-FMeSI, its fluorine fate differed markedly. EO produced trifluoromethanesulfonate (TFMS) at nearly stoichiometric yield, whereas UV/S generated both TFMS and trifluoromethanesulfonamide (TfNH 2 ). Marcus-theory calculations established the redox thresholds for one-electron transfer, while electronic-structure analysis showed that oxidation and reduction generate distinct states that follow different bond-cleavage pathways. Further transformation of TFMS and TfNH 2 required redox conditions beyond those attainable within the aqueous-phase stability window, causing their accumulation and limiting defluorination. To overcome this constraint, we demonstrated a cross-media approach in which bis-FMeSI and TFMS were adsorbed from water onto granular activated carbon and subsequently destroyed by additive-free ball milling with stainless-steel media, achieving complete degradation and near-quantitative recovery of organofluorine as fluoride. This cross-media strategy provides a potential solution for PFAS resistant to aqueous-phase treatment.

papers.title: Reading the whole corpus: a reproducible cross-sample Raman workflow for materials characterisation, with a spectral 3D Gaussian splatting representation for hyperspectral maps
papers.abstract: Raman mapping produces a hyperspectral cube, and turning that cube into numbers depends strongly on a chain of preprocessing choices. Two further problems appear once a laboratory holds many maps rather than one: the corpus is analysed one file at a time, and the analysable corpus is only the subset somebody remembered to export by hand from the instrument’s proprietary format. We present RAMANSP, a compact open framework providing typed spectral containers, composable preprocessing protocols and an analysis layer, and extend it in three directions. First, a direct reader for the undocumented Horiba LabSpec 6 container, reverse engineered here and verified bit identical against the instrument’s own text export, which removes the manual export step and takes this corpus from 1 usable map to 23. Second, a cross-sample knowledge graph linking every acquisition by spectral similarity, shared unmixing endmembers and disorder-metric proximity, with each metric edge carrying the preprocessing protocol under which it was computed. Third, and as the main methodological contribution, spectral 3D Gaussian splatting: a map V (x,y,ν) is represented by a differentiable field of anisotropic ellipsoids, each localising a domain in the two spatial axes and a band along the wavenumber axis, fitted by first-order descent on closed-form gradients, entirely in NumPy on a CPU. On an anonymised corpus of 108 acquisitions the graph recovers 23 communities at modularity Q = 0.65 and flags 5 groups of byte-identical duplicates, and across 6 maps the field reconstructs held-out wavenumber channels to within 0.70 to 1.34 of each map’s own measurement noise at 8.1 to 37.7× compression, that is, essentially to the noise floor.

papers.title: Carbonyl Recycling Limits Productive Ethanol Formation during Syngas Conversion on Rh(211): A First-Principles Microkinetic Analysis
papers.abstract: Higher alcohol synthesis from syngas on Rh involves a highly branched and reversible reaction network in which formation of a C–C bond does not necessarily result in productive higher-alcohol synthesis. Here, a thermodynamically consistent first-principles mean-field microkinetic model is constructed to determine how carbon is partitioned among methane, methanol, ethanol, and highercarbon intermediates under steady-state conditions. Across a 100-point temperature–pressure domain, the model exhibits a pronounced activity–selectivity trade-off: conditions that increase turnover progressively favor methane and methanol over ethanol. Reaction-flux analysis reveals that CO insertion provides the dominant entry into the C 2 carbonyl manifold, but 79–94% of this carbonyl flux is recycled toward the C 1 pool across representative kinetic regimes rather than converted productively to ethanol. Consequently, the elementary C–C coupling reactions carry substantial flux while exhibiting relatively small degrees of rate control. Instead, downstream ethoxy hydrogenation becomes increasingly rate controlling, while methane formation and oxygen-removal chemistry strongly influence ethanol productivity. CHO insertion, despite its favorable intrinsic forward barrier, changes from a productive C–C-forming pathway at low activity to a net recycling pathway at high activity, demonstrating that isolated activation barriers do not determine steady-state pathway utilization. Methanol additionally constitutes a major competing sink for oxygenated C 1 carbon. These results show that improving Rh-based higheralcohol synthesis requires not only promoting C–C coupling but also suppressing carbonyl recycling and kinetically trapping C 2 intermediates along the productive ethanol pathway.

papers.title: Azobenzene-Mediated Reversible Conformational Switching in 9,9′-Bifluorenylidene-Based Molecular Machines
papers.abstract: Intrinsically dynamic molecules offer attractive building blocks for molecular machines, yet controlling their conformational motion with external stimuli remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we report Azo–BF–Azo, a photoresponsive molecular machine in which an intrinsically dynamic 9,9′-bifluorenylidene (BF) core is coupled to two visible-light-responsive tetra-orthofluorinated azobenzene (Azo) units that act as molecular actuators. Irradiation at 525 nm induces trans-to-cis photoisomerization of the Azo units, accompanied by a shift of the BF framework from the closed toward the open conformation, whereas irradiation at 456 nm reverses Azo isomerization and restores the BF-closed state over time. DFT calculations reveal that the extended trans-Azo units favor intramolecular π–π interactions that stabilize the closed BF conformation, while their conversion to the folded cis state disrupts these interactions and alters the steric environment surrounding the BF core. Variable-temperature NMR spectroscopy provides experimental support for the role of these intramolecular interactions in regulating the BF conformational equilibrium. The photoinduced state additionally undergoes spontaneous thermal relaxation, recovering approximately 65% of the initial state. Together, these results demonstrate that local photoisomerization of peripheral Azo actuators can reshape the conformational landscape of an intrinsically dynamic BF core through the cooperative modulation of steric and intramolecular π–π interactions. This work provides a strategy for converting intrinsic molecular dynamics into externally programmable motion and establishes a design principle for constructing integrated molecular machines in which one type of molecular motion regulates another.

papers.title: Backbone Editing of Natural Rubber for Sustainable Flexible Electronics
papers.abstract: Sustainable electronics offer a path to reducing the environmental burden of electronic waste, but achieving closed-loop recyclability in flexible organic devices remains challenging because most stretchable substrates and elastomers are non-recyclable, petroleum-derived thermosets. Natural rubber ( cis -1,4-polyisoprene), a renewable and mechanically compliant biopolymer, is an attractive alternative for sustainable electronics, yet its chemical inertness has limited its use in advanced functional materials. Here we report a photoredox-catalyzed strategy for the selective functionalization of cis -1,4-polyisoprene, enabling modular installation of functional groups without crosslinking or degradation. This approach yields functional polyisoprene with luminescent and flame-retardant properties and, through dynamic ionic crosslinking, produces elastomers with tensile strengths up to 20 MPa and stretch ratios of 22. We further prepare a recyclable composite using functional natural rubber and PEDOT:PSS, stabilized by ionic interactions rather than permanent vulcanized networks, that retains mechanical and electrical performance over multiple recycling cycles. Its application in robotic motion sensing and electronic skin exemplifies a fundamental design principle for sustainable flexible electronics.

papers.title: Coordination–Diffusion Coupling (CDC) in Dual-Anion Ionic-Liquid/Carbonate Electrolytes: Molecular Origins of Lithium-Ion Self-Diffusion
papers.abstract: Understanding lithium-ion motion in concentrated ionic-liquid electrolytes requires a description that connects local coordination structure to long-range diffusion. Here we combine dispersioncorrected density functional theory (DFT), natural bond orbital (NBO) analysis, and classical molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to examine [EMI][TFSI]/LiFSI/EC/DMC electrolytes at 298 K. The calculations show that [TFSI]- and [FSI]- possess distinct interaction landscapes: six low-energy [EMI][TFSI] conformers span 0.676–5.170 kJ mol-1 in relative energy and −41.22 to −48.64 kJ mol-1 in interaction energy, whereas the corresponding [EMI][FSI] conformers span 0.163–5.849 kJ mol-1 and −34.62 to −44.19 kJ mol-1, respectively. In the condensed phase, Li+ coordination evolves from predominantly carbonate-mediated solvation in the 0% ionic-liquid system to mixed carbonate/anion coordination at 42.9% ionic-liquid content and exclusively anion coordination in the 100% ionic-liquid system. The Li+ self-diffusion coefficient is nonmonotonic across the reported compositions, decreasing from 28.66 × 10-12 m2 s-1 in the carbonate-rich system to 19.88 × 10-12 m2 s-1 at 42.9% ionic-liquid content and increasing to 27.00 × 10-12 m2 s-1 in the pure ionic-liquid system. FSI- also diffuses faster than TFSI- in the systems for which both are present. These results support a mechanistic picture in which Li+ motion is governed not solely by bulk solvent properties but by the persistence and reorganization of its local coordination environment. Building on this observation, we formulate a Coordination–Diffusion Coupling (CDC) framework that combines Shannon coordination entropy with trajectory-derived coordination exchange kinetics and a complementary timescale ratio between translational displacement and coordination-shell residence. The framework is presented as a physically motivated descriptor for interpreting and ultimately screening electrolyte compositions. Importantly, the present study does not directly calculate electrochemical stability, interfacial decomposition, or a local dielectric constant; those properties are therefore treated as design considerations rather than demonstrated outcomes.

papers.title: Epitaxial Growth, Electronic Transitions, and Size-Dependent Cavity Modes of WS2@ReSe2 Core–Shell Nanotubes
papers.abstract: WS2@ReSe2 core–shell nanotubes were synthesized by van der Waals epitaxy, representing the first highly crystalline nanotubular architecture incorporating ReSe2. High-resolution electron microscopy and 4D-STEM diffraction reveal the epitaxial growth of crystalline ReSe2 multilayers that conformally wrap multiwall WS2 nanotubes while maintaining atomically sharp interfaces. Raman and photoluminescence spectroscopy confirm electronic coupling between the constituent phases. Cryogenic low-loss EELS resolves excitonic transitions in both WS2 and ReSe2 and reveals additional interface-localized subgap excitations associated with cavity-confined modes enabled by the hollow nanotube geometry and strongly diameter-dependent. Cathodoluminescence directly visualizes simultaneous emission from both the WS2 core and ReSe2 shell. These findings establish ReSe2 as a new member of the inorganic nanotube family and demonstrate the potential of anisotropic core–shell nanotubes as platforms for investigating strain-induced optoelectronic phenomena. While the work primarily focuses on synthesis and basic characterization, it invites follow-up to explore its application potential in devices, photodetectors, or optoelectronics.

papers.title: The Interference Index: Quantifying and Improving Error Cancellation in Machine-Learned Thermodynamic Stability Predictions
papers.abstract: Machine-learned formation enthalpies for inorganic materials approach density functional theory (DFT) accuracy, yet thermodynamic stability predictions derived from them can remain unreliable, a gap commonly associated with error cancellation in DFT that independent per-compound training does not reproduce. We introduce the interference index ξ, a dimensionless measure of how strongly errors reinforce or cancel in linearly derived quantities. Its root-mean-square average, ξrms, provides a reaction-size-independent null reference, with ξrms = 1 for the isotropic null model. Across seven published models benchmarked on Materials Project compounds, error-cancellation behaviour is distinct from per-compound accuracy and becomes progressively less favourable with increasing formation-enthalpy accuracy among the compositional models. We then introduce iiLoss, a reaction-aware objective that favours cancellation of formation-enthalpy errors rather than directly minimising decomposition-enthalpy error. On Materials Project data, iiLoss reduces decomposition-enthalpy error by 21% and improves thermodynamic stability classification by 6.8% in F1 score, outperforming direct supervision on decomposition enthalpies. These results show that error cancellation can be quantified and directly optimised to improve derived thermodynamic predictions.

papers.title: Kinetic Mechanism Development and Pollutant Chemistry in NH3/H2/CH4 Combustion
papers.abstract: Ammonia (NH 3 ) is a promising carbon-free fuel, but because it is difficult to combust, blending ammonia with co-fuels such as H 2 and CH 4 is one approach to improve combustibility. However, the underlying chemical interactions, particularly coupled carbon–nitrogen (C–N) pathways, become increasingly complex as fuel composition expands. Existing kinetic mechanisms are typically constructed by manually merging NH 3 and hydrocarbon sub-mechanisms, often with limited systematic treatment of C–N cross chemistry and frequently involving empirical tuning of kinetic parameters. In this work, a comprehensive kinetic mechanism for NH 3 /H 2 /CH 4 combustion is developed using the Reaction Mechanism Generator without any empirical parameter tuning. The mechanism builds upon a previously validated NH 3 /H 2 model and a recent, high-quality hydrocarbon mechanism. C-N chemistry is obtained from the literature when available and automatically constructed with Reaction Mechanism Generator when not. For select important reactions, we calculated kinetic parameters in this work. The developed mechanism is validated against laminar-burning velocities, ignition-delay times, and flow-reactor and jet-stirred-reactor measurements, showing good agreement over a wide range of conditions. Using the validated model, pollutant formation and consumption pathways for NOx , N 2 O, HCN, and CO are systematically investigated across the ternary composition space.

papers.title: EA-Derived Carbon Dot Fluorescence Sensor Array for Simultaneous Discrimination and Quantification of Amlodipine, Losartan, Atorvastatin, and Clopidogrel
papers.abstract: A three-channel fluorescence sensor array based on Echium amoenum-derived carbon dots (EA-CDs) was developed for the simultaneous discrimination and quantitative determination of amlodipine (AML), losartan (LOS), atorvastatin (ATO), and clopidogrel (CLO). The EA-CDs were synthesized through a hydrothermal method and exhibited nanoscale dimensions, excitation-dependent photoluminescence, abundant oxygen- and nitrogen-containing surface functional groups, and a fluorescence quantum yield of 41.55%. To generate differential sensing responses, Mg 2+ and Al 3+ were introduced as auxiliary metal ions, forming three sensing channels consisting of EA-CDs (S1), EA-CDs–Mg 2+ (S2), and EA-CDs–Al 3+ (S3). The four target drugs produced distinct fluorescence fingerprints that enabled effective discrimination using principal component analysis (PCA) and hierarchical cluster analysis (HCA). Optimization studies identified pH 7, 250 μM Mg 2+ , and 750 μM Al 3+ as the most suitable sensing conditions, and clear discrimination was maintained over drug concentrations of 2–50 μg/mL. The sensor array also exhibited good selectivity toward the target drugs in the presence of common interfering species. Quantitative analysis provided drug-dependent calibration responses with coefficients of determination ranging from 0.912 to 0.97. Recovery values ranged from 97.60% to 104.67%, with relative standard deviations of 0.45–3.20%, demonstrating acceptable accuracy and precision. These results indicate that the proposed EA-CD/Mg 2+ /Al 3+ fluorescence sensor array provides a simple and effective platform for multicomponent discrimination and quantitative analysis of antihypertensive and cardiovascular drugs.

papers.title: Domain-Informed AI Multimodal Foundation Model for Materials Science
papers.abstract: Accelerating materials discovery can unlock progress on clean energy, sustainable construction, medicines, and electronics, yet the machine-learning pipelines meant to drive that acceleration remain fragmented, unimodal, and narrowly scoped. Large multimodal foundation models, pretrained broadly and reused across tasks, offer an alternative paradigm. Materials-specific foundation models already exist and have delivered genuine advances, most notably universal interatomic potentials and domain language models, but those surveyed here remain either unimodal or physics-agnostic, and building a model that reasons jointly across the full range of materials data requires more than scaling them up. This review examines what such a model would demand in order to deliver reliable, physically consistent property prediction and candidate generation that transfer across chemistries, length scales, and data regimes, and how close the field is to meeting those demands. We survey the data infrastructure and unimodal precursors already in place, analyze the recent landscape of foundation models for materials, and argue that a credible model must be domain-informed; because most materials knowledge is formalized as physical laws, we concentrate on its physics-informed subset. Organized around four pillars, we review multimodal data integration, model architecture and pretraining, parameter-efficient specialization to low-data industrial problems, and validation, deployment, and continuous improvement. A recurring finding is that physical grounding and multimodality have so far advanced on separate lines. Beyond reviewing this landscape, we use the state-of-theart analysis to propose guidelines for further developments, arguing that a physically grounded multimodal backbone would let discovery in data-rich sectors transfer to data-poor ones.

papers.title: Investigating the ‘Water Paradox’: Theoretical Evidence for Electric Field-Mediated Catalysis of Peptide Bond Formation
papers.abstract: A key question in origins of life chemistry – sometimes termed the ‘Water Paradox’ – is how complex biomolecules can form via condensation reactions in aqueous environments. This problem is exemplified by the formation of peptides, which is a challenging reaction in bulk water because high free energy barriers and small thermodynamic driving forces hinder polymerization. Recent experiments suggest that peptide polymerization is more facile at air-water interfaces, possibly due to the presence of intrinsic interfacial electric fields. Here we explore the viability of electric field catalysis of peptide bond formation using quantum mechanical simulations of the dimerization of glycine zwitterions. Our results suggest that oriented electric fields reduce the high barrier, six-step mechanism in bulk water to a simpler four-step process with substantially lower reaction barriers. Furthermore, our modeling indicates that the reverse reaction – peptide hydrolysis – is not catalyzed because the oriented electric field causes a spatial separation between the reacting water and the peptide bond, making the initial hydrolysis step less accessible. These results complement experimental findings and provide a compelling mechanism that supports the hypothesis that interfacial electric fields could play a central role in prebiotic peptide synthesis.

papers.title: Increasing Trifluoroacetic Acid Concentration in Austrian Groundwater and Its Associations with Agricultural Indicators
papers.abstract: Trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) is an extremely persistent and highly mobile substance that is accumulating in the environment as a result of continued emissions from diverse sources. Yet time trend data for TFA in groundwater remain scarce, despite growing concern about TFA as a persistent groundwater contaminant. We analyzed temporal trends in official Austrian monitoring data from 2018–2019 and 2024, comprising 98 baseline sites and 107 sites in 2024, including 16 sites sampled in both periods. TFA increased at all paired sites; mean concentrations rose from 1.36 to 2.86 µg/L (+110%) and median concentrations from 1.01 to 2.05 µg/L (+103%). Across the complete, largely non-paired datasets, mean concentrations were 0.78 and 2.42 µg/L and median concentrations were 0.39 and 1.40 µg/L, respectively. This comparison supports the hypothesis of a broader upward shift in TFA groundwater concentration on a national scale. To assess agriculture as a possible source, we tested associations with agricultural contamination indicators. TFA was associated with nitrate and pesticide burden, but not with other monitored PFAS. This supports an agricultural contribution in the most impacted regions. Given TFA's persistence and limited removal by conventional water treatment, limiting further emissions from TFA-forming pesticides and other sources, such as fluorinated gases, is important to prevent further accumulation.

papers.title: Finite-Field Second Hyperpolarizability via Adaptive Bayesian Quantum Phase Estimation for Early Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computers: Ground-State Energies Beyond Chemical Accuracy
papers.abstract: The static second hyperpolarizability governs third-order nonlinear-optical responses but is difficult to compute by first-principles methods because finite-field extraction requires a fourth-order energy derivative. The resulting error amplification demands sub-µHa ground-state energies, far beyond conventional chemical accuracy. Standard multi-qubit QPE can in principle meet this precision but requires a wide ancilla register, while single-ancilla iterative QPE (IQPE) is limited by a binary-grid quantization floor. We develop an adaptive Bayesian QPE (BQPE) workflow that uses a single ancilla, terminal measurements, and real-time classical feedback to estimate the eigenphase through a continuous posterior rather than a fixed binary grid. For a linear H4 chain in the STO-3G basis, represented by a six-qubit parity Hamiltonian with one ancilla, BQPE reaches a ground-state energy error of ≈ 10−7 Ha at controlled-U depth mmax ≈ 215, about two orders of magnitude below the IQPE floor. Propagated through the finite-field stencil and Richardson extrapolation, these energies recover the second hyperpolarizability within ±10% of the FCI reference over the stable field-strength plateau, whereas IQPE at the same depth fails to do so. These results indicate that grid-free Bayesian phase estimation can make nonlinear-optical properties accessible on early fault-tolerant quantum computers.

papers.title: Atomistic Mechanism of the Spontaneous Formation of Ferroelectric Nematic Order from an Isotropic Liquid
papers.abstract: Ferroelectric nematic (N F ) liquid crystals have fluidity with macroscopic polar order, yet the transition pathway at the molecular scale by which an isotropic liquid spontaneously develops long-range ferroelectric order remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrated that microsecond-scale, unbiased all-atom molecular dynamics simulations can reproduce the spontaneous development of strong, system-wide polar order from an initially isotropic state. For DIO, highly polar local domains emerged upon cooling but remained nanoscopic because slow molecular diffusion kinetically suppressed their further growth. In contrast, UUZU-2-N, which exhibits an enantiotropic N F phase at relatively high temperatures, underwent progressive polar-domain growth and coalescence, ultimately reaching a nearly monodomain state with a polar order parameter of . The calculated spontaneous polarization reached 6.7 μC/cm 2 , in reasonable agreement with experiment. Notably, nematic orientational order developed rapidly, whereas long-range polar order emerged over several microseconds through much slower domain coarsening. The spontaneous development of strong polar order was also reproduced for C2-BOE. Further structural analyses revealed characteristic offset configurations and head-to-tail correlations between neighboring molecules. In comparison with molecular electrostatic distributions, it is suggested that longitudinally asymmetric and modulated charge distributions contribute to the stabilization of these polar arrangements. These results provide an atomistic mechanism connecting molecular electrostatics, local packing, domain coarsening, and macroscopic polarization in the N F liquid crystals.

papers.title: The Design and Application of Diureido Functionalized Spiroligomers as Diphosphate Receptors
papers.abstract: Spiroligomers are rigid, stereochemically defined scaffolds that can be programmed to display functional groups in precise three-dimensional constellations. We utilize this scaffold to position two urea groups in a preorganized geometry for anion binding. Among the receptors synthesized, the spiroligomer with RRRR-configuration displayed the strongest affinity for hydrogen pyrophosphate H2PPi (H2P2O7

papers.title: Geometry-Dependent Redistribution of Exocytotic Spike-Shape Populations Revealed by Ultrafast Disk and Nanotip Acetylcholine Biosensors
papers.abstract: Measurements of sub-millisecond acetylcholine (ACh) exocytosis have only recently become possible through the development of ultrafast electrochemical ACh biosensors. These biosensors convert transient presynaptic ACh release events into sub-millisecond amperometric spikes that can be analyzed at the single-event level. Although both disk and nanotip electrode geometries have been incorporated into ultrafast ACh biosensors, it remains unclear whether sensor geometry influences quantal measurements and the observed distribution of exocytotic spike shapes. Amperometric recordings were obtained from single cholinergic cells and analyzed using a spike-shape classification system consisting of eight distinct event categories, including low sharp, high sharp, increasing, decreasing, plateau, high spike, overlap, and funky events. Although disk and nanotip biosensors produced comparable estimates of vesicular release content and global spike kinetics, detailed spike-shape classification revealed a geometry-dependent redistribution of the detected exocytotic event populations. Nanotip biosensors detected a significantly higher proportion of high sharp events and lower proportions of morphologically more complex full-release events and overlap events than disk biosensors. The reduction in complex full-release events was not driven by a single subtype but instead reflected distributed changes across multiple event categories. These findings demonstrate that electrode geometry can influence the apparent composition of the detected exocytotic spike populations without substantially altering estimates of vesicular release content or global spike kinetics. The results provide new insights into how nanoscale sensor geometry shapes electrochemical observations of neurotransmitter release and highlights the importance of considering biosensor geometry when interpreting single-cell exocytosis measurements.

papers.title: Case Study of Bayesian Batch Optimization Strategies for Heterogeneous Catalysts in CO2 Hydrogenation
papers.abstract: High-throughput and automated experimentation platforms combined with artificial intelligence are increasingly used to accelerate catalyst discovery. Batch Bayesian optimization (BO) (i.e., the simulta neous selection of multiple candidate experiments per iteration) is widely adopted for navigating large compositional spaces; however, its practical behavior under realistic high-throughput and batch con straints remains poorly understood. In this work, we performed a case study on four BO strategies to optimize the catalyst composition for the hydrogenation of CO2 to methanol. For each BO strategy, 48 catalysts were synthesized by co-precipitation, utilizing an automated synthesis platform, and evaluated in high-throughput fixed-bed reactors over seven batch iterations. The composition space comprised up to four metallic elements selected from a pool of nine. Although all BO strategies identified competitive catalyst formulations, most optimization trajectories rapidly converged toward distinct local optima that were strongly influenced by the initial random design and exhibited limited global exploration of the compositional space. This case study provides practical insights into the limitations of BO for batch catalyst optimization and highlights their strong dependence on the initial random design, parameter space definition, and batch execution strategy.

papers.title: P,T-odd sensitivity parameters of laser-coolable SrOH from relativisticcoupled-cluster theory
papers.abstract: Ultracold molecules have attracted significant interest as promising platforms for exploring fundamental physics and quantum information science. As progress toward precision measurements with the ultracold SrOH molecule is currently underway [{\it Phys. Rev. Lett. 134, 083401 (2025)}], we present a four-component relativistic coupled-cluster (RCC) study of various parity- and time-reversal-violating (P,T-odd) interactions in the ground electronic state of SrOH. In particular, we extend the application of the Z-vector (energy-derivative) approach within the RCC framework to a polyatomic molecule for the calculation of P,T-odd molecular sensitivity parameters. We obtain the following molecular parameters for SrOH: $E_\text{eff} = 2.12 \pm 0.27$~GV/cm, $W_S = 1.89 \pm 0.21$~kHz, and $W_M = (2.04 \pm 0.12) \times 10^{32}$~Hz/e$\cdot$cm$^2$. These parameters provide essential molecular inputs for the design and interpretation of precision experiments with SrOH. We find that the P,T-odd sensitivity parameters of SrOH are comparable to those of the isoelectronic diatomic molecule SrF. However, the polyatomic structure of SrOH offers enhanced capabilities for suppressing systematic errors, making it a particularly promising candidate for high-precision searches for P,T violation.

papers.title: Vacancy-Controlled Stabilization and Reactivity of Single Metal Atoms on Titanium Nitride and Titanium Oxynitride
papers.abstract: Titanium nitride (TiN) and titanium oxynitride (TiON) are attractive conductive supports for single-atom electrocatalysts, but the role of surface vacancies in balancing metal stabilization and catalytic reactivity remains unclear. Here, we used density functional theory to screen the formation of Ag, Au, Co, Cu, Ir, Ni, Pd, Pt, Rh, and Ru single atoms on pristine and vacancy-containing TiN and TiON surfaces, and their reactivity toward the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Vacancy formation generally strengthens single-atom anchoring, but the corresponding changes in hydrogen adsorption are strongly metal- and defect-dependent, showing that a stronger metal–support interaction does not necessarily imply improved HER activity. Combining hydrogen adsorption thermodynamics with electrochemical dissolution stability identifies Pd atoms trapped in Ti vacancies (VTi) as the most promising candidates. Importantly, Pd@VTi shows nearly identical hydrogen adsorption energetics and dissolution potentials above 0 V vs. SHE for TiN and both investigated TiON configurations, indicating remarkable insensitivity to the local O/N arrangement. Electronic-structure analysis, ab initio molecular dynamics, and surface Pourbaix calculations further support the viability of these configurations. These results highlight cation-vacancy-confined Pd as a robust HER motif on compositionally variable Ti(O)N supports.

papers.title: Preserving topographic information stored on DNA origami nanostructures in harsh environments by ultrathin Al2O3 films
papers.abstract: Structure-based DNA data storage uses DNA origami nanostructures (DONs) to arrange chemical entities into bit arrays that can be read out by atomic force microscopy (AFM). Here, we investigate the potential of ultrathin Al 2 O 3 films to preserve topographic information stored on streptavidin (SAv)-decorated DONs in harsh environments. SAv-decorated DONs immobilized on Si wafers are coated with 4.7 nm thick Al 2 O 3 films by low-temperature atomic layer deposition (ALD) at 58 °C. Although the film thickness is comparable to the diameter of the SAv molecules, AFM-based data readout is not compromised by the Al 2 O 3 film. Nevertheless, the film stabilizes the SAv-decorated DONs against harsh environmental conditions. Heating to 200 °C, O 2 plasma treatment, and chemical denaturant exposure results in severe damage of the uncoated samples, which may even lead to the complete disappearance of the DON shapes. In contrast, the coated samples retain recognizable DON shapes with isolated topographic SAv features after all treatments. Although the mean SAv occupancy decreases slightly after these treatments, it remains between 76% and 81%. These results demonstrate that ultrathin ALD-grown Al 2 O 3 films can preserve topographic information in structure-based data storage even under harsh conditions. Furthermore, the conditions tested here are much harsher than any environmental conditions that information-carrying DONs will likely experience during archival storage, rendering ALD coating a straightforward and low-cost approach for preserving topographic information during long-term storage.

papers.title: Machine Learning Assisted Raman Spectroscopic Identification of Edible Oils in Fried Food Matrix
papers.abstract: Identification of the type of cooking oil used in ready-to-eat (RTE) foods is paramount, as it directly impacts consumers’ health. Comprehensive evaluation of existing protocols reveals a pressing need for developing rapid methodologies with improved operational efficiency. This proof-of-concept study reports development of one such rapid, solvent-free analytical framework by coupling Raman spectroscopy with machine learning. It demonstrates the feasibility of oil type identification from fried food matrices without solvent extraction. Five edible oils (sunflower, soybean, groundnut, palm, and vanaspati) and one complex food matrix (potato chips) were chosen for the study. Five types of paper based absorbents were screened for most effective isolation of the oil from the potato chips. Seven supervised classification algorithms, Logistic Regression, SVC (RBF/Linear), LightGBM, Random Forest Classifier, XGBoost, and KNN were evaluated using stratified five-fold cross-validation. Model performance was assessed using four key metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Coarse hyperparameter tuning was employed to further enhance the model performance. Comparative analysis of the tested algorithms revealed SVC (RBF) to achieve the best prediction accuracy (97% for oils and 89.8% for chips). The framework reduces the total analysis time from hours to minutes by replacing conventional oil extraction with the newly optimized sampling technique. This new sampling strategy was validated using cross-correlation analysis and non-negative least squares (NNLS) spectral decomposition. The high correlation coefficient (ρ= 0.91) and high spectral contribution (56%) of oils in the chips spectra confirmed the preservation of the oil fingerprints within the chips spectra.

papers.title: Surface Geometry Governs Cation Effects via Nonlocal Solvent Gating
papers.abstract: Catalyst structure and electrolyte composition are commonly regarded as independent descriptors governing electrocatalytic behavior. Here, we show that surface geometry governs cation effects through catalyst–electrolyte coupling that we term nonlocal solvent gating. Constant-potential ab initio molecular dynamics simulations and free-energy sampling reveal contrasting cation (Li+, K+, Cs+)-dependent CO2 reduction activity on single-crystal and polycrystalline Au. On relatively flat Au(100) and Au(111), cation hydration controls the contact-water structure, and the solvent penalty for CO2 approach decreases with increasing cation size. In Au(110) grooves, surface-registered water instead reverses the cation response. Remarkably, an Au(110)-like groove embedded within an otherwise flat Au(111) terrace induces the same reversed cation trend even at geometrically pristine terrace sites away from the groove, demonstrating that a local surface motif can regulate electrolyte effects nonlocally through the interfacial solvent. An additional calculation for Rb+ supports this mechanism, yielding an intermediate groove-induced cavity penalty. This nonlocal coupling provides a mechanistic basis for the experimentally observed volcano-shaped cation dependence on flame-annealed polycrystalline Au, which cannot be explained by independent single-facet responses. These results establish interfacial water as a medium through which surface geometry and electrolyte composition become intrinsically coupled, extending conventional local-site descriptions of complex electrocatalytic interfaces to include nonlocal solvent-mediated effects.

papers.title: π-Interaction-Guided Tuning of Ferrocene Redox Mediators for Shono-Type Allylation of N-Aryl Amines
papers.abstract: The development of Shono-type oxidation reactions for late-stage functionalization has recently focused on the expansion of compatible nucleophiles; however, a central limitation is N-aryl, or aniline-derived, substrates due to oxidative sensitivity that leads to decomposition under direct electrolysis. Redox mediators have recently been employed to drive Shono-type oxidation reactions at lower overpotentials but are underdeveloped with aniline-type substrates. We demonstrate that electron-transfer (ET)-based ferrocene (Fc) mediators are capable of driving a rare Shono-type allylation reaction using simple allyl trifluoroborate salt with a variety of N-aryl substrates. Computational data probing the nature of ET from substrate to Fc+ suggests a distinct π-interaction, leading to our evaluation of phenyl-appended Fc (FcPh) for enhanced reactivity. We find that FcPh improves reaction efficiency across structurally diverse N-aryl substrates under controlled potential electrolysis (CPE) at applied potentials differing only by 20 mV, illustrating a distinct handle for tuning Fc redox mediators via proposed non-covalent interactions. DFT supports a working model for “out-ofcage” and “in-cage” single electron transfer (SET)pathways that provides a rationale for observed trends. In the presence of benzene co-solvent, the advantage of FcPh is suppressed, supporting the proposed role of π-interactions between FcPh and N-aryl substrates. These results highlight mediatorbased π-interactions as a strategy for tuning mediation efficiency without substantial alteration of mediator redox potential.

papers.title: Computational investigation of the first most (𝝅; 𝝅∗)𝟏; (𝒏; 𝝅∗)𝟏;(𝝅; 𝝈∗)𝟏 and (𝒏; 𝝈∗)𝟏 electronic states of all possible positional isomers of iodinated BODIPY
papers.abstract: Photochemistry of all possible positional isomers of iodinated -BODIPY has been explored employing state of the art two-component relativistic sf-X2C-S-TD-DFT-SOC method. Vertical excitation energies; oscillator strength and spin–orbit couplings of first most promising electronic states have been computed. Effect of number of iodine atoms attached to BODIPY moiety and their topology on magnitude of vertical excitation energies have been explained in detail. Slater–Condon rules and El–Sayed rules which are special case of former have been effectively employed to explain magnitude of spin–orbit couplings between states of different multiplicities. Coupled states exhibiting anomalies from conventional El–Sayed rules have been explained with the help of orbitals involved in respective states. Effect of non-planarity of BODIPY ring on magnitude of spin–orbit couplings between states of different multiplicities have also been discussed. Most effective positions on BODIPY moiety that can turn in to effective photosensitizer by attaching iodine atoms on them has been explored and explained.

papers.title: Potency Prediction via Probabilistic Modeling of Dose–Response Curves
papers.abstract: Predicting molecular potency from chemical structure is an important task in drug discovery, and is almost universally framed as scalar regression on the half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) derived from a dose–response experiment. This formulation collapses the full experimental signal into a single number and implicitly assumes well-behaving data, even though real assay measurements might be imbalanced, noisy, and potentially censored. Because public bioactivity datasets report only the summary pIC50, the alternative of predicting the entire dose–response curve has remained essentially unexplored. Here, using an in-house dataset containing the full curves, we present a novel probabilistic approach to potency prediction that models the entire dose–response curve as the cumulative distribution function of a latent concentration variable. We benchmark it against two alternative curve-prediction models—a multi-task regression over the concentration grid and a parametric four-parameter logistic model—and against descriptor-and graph-based scalar baselines. The probabilistic model achieves the best performance on all metrics, demonstrating the competitiveness of curve-level modeling over the scalar formulation. Its advantage is two-fold. First, it exposes useful curve information, such as slope, asymptotes, and shape, that is otherwise lost in the scalar collapse. Second, it learns directly from raw measurements rather than a fitted summary statistic that itself carries uncertainty and noise. Altogether, these results show that modeling the full dose–response curve offers a robust and information-preserving alternative to conventional scalar potency prediction.

papers.title: IntelliPore: A Foundation Model for Gas Adsorption in Porous Materials
papers.abstract: Porous materials, such as metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), covalent organic frameworks (COFs), and zeolites, hold great promise for energy and environmental applications, particularly in gas storage and separation technologies. However, their rapidly expanding design space, driven by experimental synthesis and computational modeling, challenges traditional exploration methods. Machine learning has emerged as a promising alternative, yet current approaches are typically developed for specific adsorption properties or material families. Consequently, each new property or material class requires training a new model from scratch using large amounts of labeled data, which are often not available. Inspired by the emerging foundation-model paradigm that has transformed computer vision and natural language processing, we introduce IntelliPore, a foundation model tailored for gas adsorption in porous materials. By pretraining on 12.5 million publicly available adsorption data from MOFs and COFs, IntelliPore learns transferable knowledge across adsorption tasks and material classes, enabling generalization to previously unseen materials such as zeolites and porous polymer networks. It demonstrates strong few-shot learning capabilities, substantially improving sample efficiency compared with the traditional approach of training from scratch. Furthermore, it achieves state-of-the-art performance in adsorption property prediction with exceptional parameter efficiency, requiring only 0.86 million parameters—two orders of magnitude fewer than existing leading models. To facilitate broader adoption, IntelliPore is made publicly available to the research community and accessible through a web application. Collectively, these advances establish IntelliPore as a practical foundation for data-driven adsorption modeling in porous materials and represent a step toward the emerging paradigm of foundation-style models in materials science.

papers.title: Descriptor-Based Pre-Training Improves Reaction Property Prediction
papers.abstract: Pre-training graph neural networks on large unlabeled datasets has substantially improved molecular property prediction, yet pre-training approaches for reaction property prediction remain underexplored. We introduce CheMeleon-Rxn, a pre-trained reaction graph neural network that adapts the CheMeleon framework to condensed graphs of reaction (CGR) and demonstrates that descriptor-regression is an effective pre-training strategy for low-data reaction property prediction. An O(10M)-parameter D-MPNN encoder was pre-trained on ∼2 million reactions by regressing onto dense reaction descriptors pooled from classical molecular descriptors, then fine-tuned on small reaction property prediction datasets. Across regression tasks spanning gasphase activation energies, reaction enthalpies, experimental yields, and rate coefficients, CheMeleon-Rxn is best or statistically tied-for-best on seven of eight tasks. It outperforms the same encoder trained from scratch, as well as classical-descriptor, fingerprint, and pre-trained-fingerprint baselines. We further tested the pre-training strategy across various graph neural network architectures and found that its benefit holds for other edge-aware backbones such as GINE, and that it is robust to the choice of descriptor set, pooling operation, and other pre-training hyperparameters. We visualized and analyzed the CheMeleon-Rxn embeddings, which reveal chemically coherent structure in the learned reaction representation space. The CheMeleon-Rxn code has been released publicly (https://github.com/MSDLLCpapers/chemeleon-rxn) to encourage adoption and extension by the community. The model weights will be released upon publication.

papers.title: Bio-based carbon dot-loaded polyethylene films for smart packaging applications
papers.abstract: Innovative packaging solutions, namely smart packaging, have recently been explored to combat challenges in the food system, such as reducing food waste, preventing foodborne diseases, and food fraud. One of the most interesting materials recently explored in this context is carbon dots (CDs), which could be used to develop traceability and anti-counterfeiting solutions. As such, this work aimed to use bio-derived CDs to develop extruded CD-loaded low-density polyethylene (LDPE) films foreseeing its use as invisible tags in food packaging. Bio-derived CDs were produced via hydrothermal synthesis using sodium alginate and urea and present a spherical morphology, a size of 5.6 ± 1.7 nm, display blue fluorescence (λexc=~335 nm; λem=~410 nm), and a quantum yield of 5.53 %. Surface analysis of the CDs shows that nitrogen incorporation was successful, with the CDs composed of carbon, oxygen, nitrogen, and sodium. The CDs exhibited excitation-dependent emission consistent with their complex surface chemistry and demonstrated high biocompatibility (>90% in a cytotoxicity assay). Chemical and optical characterisations (XRD, Raman, FTIR, XPS) seem to indicate that the produced CDs are carbonised polymer dots (CPDs). LDPE Films were produced via blown-film extrusion and characterised regarding their morphology, fluorescence, transparency, mechanical and barrier properties, as well as their migration behaviour. Transparent and mechanical properties remained mostly unchanged and migration of CDs from the LDPE films was absent, while CD-loaded films displayed blue fluorescence under UV light (365 nm). Overall, the CD-loaded films displayed a similar behaviour to the control across all assays, indicating that the CD incorporation does not induce significant changes to the LDPE films. The highest loading of CDs in LDPE films displayed blue fluorescence, confirming their potential for use as traceability, recyclability, and anti-counterfeiting solutions.

papers.title: Unusual reactivities of “NONO” calix[4]arene aluminum complexes
papers.abstract: Reaction of dibenzylaminocalix[4]arene, L1H2, with aluminum alkyls did not lead to deprotonation of both phenolic groups but provided aluminum or aluminate complexes containing phenolic OH or anilinium NH2 + groups in the presence of aluminum alkyl groups. Upon heating aluminum complexes L1AlMe and L1AlCl were obtained. Reaction of L1AlMe with amines led to amido complexes, either of the ancillary amine or the aniline moiety of L1. Further reaction with isopropanol yielded L1AlOiPr. Heating in the absence of amine afforded the phenyl complex L1AlC6D5 by activation of the NMR solvent. Reaction with two equivalents of AlMe3 led to -H abstraction from methyl to form methylene-bridged (L1-2H)(AlMe)2CH2. Reactions of bis(S,S-2-(dimethylamino)cyclohexyl)amino) calix[4]arene, L2H2, with AlEt2Cl or AlMe3 led directly to the anilido complex (L2-H)Al. Reaction with two equivalents of AlMe3 yielded (L2-2H)Al2CH2 after -H abstraction from methyl. Both compounds reacted with isopropanol to form L2AlOiPr. Isopropoxide complexes L1AlOiPr and L2AlOiPr were moderately active in lactide polymerization (yielding essentially atactic polylactide) and the Meerwein-Ponndorf-Verley reduction of benzophenone. Reaction of methylene-bridged (L2-2H)Al2CH2 with benzophenone afforded diphenylethylene in transition-metal-free methylenation.

papers.title: Depleting Nucleation: Out-of-Equilibrium Effects of Monomer Consumption and System Adiabaticity on the Activation Energy Barrier
papers.abstract: This work challenges two common assumptions of Classical Nucleation Theory (CNT), namely, isothermal conditions and a constant supply of monomers, which can lead to inaccuracies in predicting nucleation rates in small, well-insulated systems. Given the contemporary focus on synthesizing nanoparticles and nanocrystals for various industrial applications, a re-examination of how these factors impact the activation energy of nucleation is warranted. A more accurate relationship is proposed to account for the selfheating that occurs in thermally insulated systems. Furthermore, to address the effect of monomer consumption by cluster formation, the Gibbs-Thomson equation is incorporated into the existing theoretical framework to describe the increase in the activation energy that accompanies supersaturation relief. The newly proposed equation simultaneously helps reconcile the recent observation that the CNT-predicted energy barrier is systematically underestimated by a factor of approximately 1.78 [Skrdla, P. J. "A Theoretical Approach for Modeling Non-steady-state Nucleation Kinetics in Solutions and Melts." J. Phys. Chem. C 130 (2026): 3614–3623]. Although the condensation of water is used as a case study, the methodologies presented are broadly applicable to any nucleating system operating under the constraints of finite volume and adiabaticity.

papers.title: Self-assembling redox films from marine polysaccharides: chitosan-1,8dihydroanthraquinone-based hydrogel and LbL-films with alginate
papers.abstract: A biosourced and biodegradable redox polymer was synthesised that is capable of forming stable, physically crosslinked films. This is achieved either by gelation upon a change in solvent or by layerby-layer electrostatic assembly with a negatively charged polyelectrolyte. The obtained films undergo reversible twoelectron reduction at mildly negative potentials in aqueous solution.

papers.title: Automatic Text-fishing, Unification, and Normalization Application in Python (aTUNApy): a tool to build molecular databases
papers.abstract: The construction and maintenance of chemical databases from the scientific literature remain labor-intensive, largely because relevant information is dispersed across thousands of publications and compounds are reported under inconsistent nomenclature. Here we present aTUNApy (automatic Text-fishing, Unification, and Normalization Application in Python), an open-source tool that couples large language model (LLM)-based extraction of compound information from PubMed abstracts with nomenclature harmonization through PubChem and SMILES standardization with RDKit. aTUNApy retrieves articles for a user-defined query, extracts compound names together with user-specified attributes such as bioactivity, mechanism or source, and maps each mention to a unique PubChem identifier, collapsing synonyms onto a single canonical entry. Four LLM families are supported: GPT, Claude, LLaMA and Gemini. We benchmarked all four against a manually curated reference set of 507 articles, including 100 negative controls, covering 148 unique compounds. Claude achieved the highest performance (precision 0.98, recall 0.95, F1 0.97), while Gemini reached comparable precision (0.98) and the lowest hallucination rate (0.2%) at no API cost, reducing a five-day manual curation task to minutes or hours of automated processing. Finally, to demonstrate end-to-end utility, we applied aTUNApy to 8,273 articles from PubMed and Web of Science to build NutriEpiDB, a database of 653 dietary compounds with reported epigenetic effects across 917 food sources.
