Yet, if limited to the first two processes, accounting for ca. one lithium per formula unit, the pristine crystalline reflections are recovered exactly in position and profile on relithiation, excluding amorphization and particle-size reduction. We propose a description of the intermediate as a paracrystal, retaining the parent antiperovskite topology while losing periodicity through aperiodic displacive relaxation. 57 Fe Mössbauer isomer shifts evolve continuously through intermediate values rather than as coexisting Fe 2+ and Fe 3+ populations, indicating mixed-valent iron, and saturate near Fe 2.8+ placing the onset of anion redox earlier than the prevailing sequential cation-then-anion picture. Cells limited to 2.6 V retain >90 % of capacity over 150 cycles, against <70 % at 3.0 V. Reversible cycling of Li 2 FeOS therefore rests on a mixed-valent, paracrystalline intermediate, and capacity fade follows once sulfur oxidation is driven beyond it.

papers.title: Observation-Guided Computation: Sequential Reobservation for Robust Chromatographic Peak Detection
papers.abstract: Chromatographic peak detection is the bottom-most step of the data-processing chain, yet almost every classical detector defines its decision variables in units of signal amplitude, so those variables co-vary with baseline drift, injection amount, and detector gain, and a single-pass decision is made once against an unchanged trace. We reframe detection not as a better criterion but as a change in the computational organization of observation, and we do so in three ordered layers. Layer 1 — Observation-Guided Computation (OGC) is a sequential computational framework — an analytical data-interpretation principle rather than a new peak detector — built around the Observation Deviation (OD) measure established in our companion work13. OGC does not introduce another peak criterion or redefine OD; it embeds OD as an observation measure into an observe–detect–reconstruct–flatten–reobserve loop, so the observation condition is updated after each detected structure. Within a working window the trace is normalized to a unitless observation space, scored by OD against a single dimensionless threshold, and all final boundaries are re-anchored on the raw signal. OGC is deliberately independent of any particular candidate generator: it can be composed from any apex finder, and six heterogeneous engines all converge to a common performance plateau. Under one frozen configuration OGC reaches interval-coverage F1 = 1.000 on three of four synthetic benchmark sets with zero false positives, converts six heterogeneous apex-finder engines into region locators that all converge to F1 ≈ 1.000 (lifting bare derivative and moving-average detectors, unusable at F1 ≤ 0.090, by up to +0.967), is invariant to four orders of magnitude of dynamic range, and identifies high-confidence observable structures on two real GC–MS chromatograms where no global prominence fraction could serve both. Layer 2 — OGC-Net asks whether the representation of chemical observation can itself be learned: it algorithm-unrolls OGC's recursive loop into a differentiable K = 5-round network of 160,516 parameters. It runs a 150-point segment in 13.9 ms (batch 1) to 0.92 ms (batch 128) on CPU and, evaluated under the identical matching protocol, beats the frozen deterministic OGC by +0.116 peak-level F1 precisely on the harder, deployment-identical windowed distribution (0.6944 vs 0.5782). Layer 3 — OGC-Web delivers OGC-Net as a single offline, zero-backend HTML file whose forward pass is a pure-JavaScript port with base64-embedded weights, reproducing the peak-level agreement with the OGC reference client-side. Our central message is that chromatographic observation can be quantified and computationally organized as a sequential process, and that learning the framework — not fitting output labels — is the stronger objective when a deterministic gold-standard algorithm already exists.

papers.title: PARAM-DOCK: An Integrated Framework for Parallel Multi-Protein–Multi-Ligand Docking and Scoring for Scalable Structure-Based Drug Discovery
papers.abstract: Molecular docking is a central component of structure-based drug discovery, but practical docking studies often require several independent programs for receptor and ligand preparation, binding-site definition, docking, visualisation, interaction analysis, and downstream compound assessment. This fragmentation becomes particularly limiting when multiple protein targets and multiple ligands must be evaluated in the same study. Here, we present PARAM-DOCK, an open-source molecular docking engine and integrated web workflow implemented in Python with Numba-compiled numerical kernels. PARAM-DOCK supports parallel multi-protein-multi-ligand docking and automates major pre-processing and post-processing steps within a single platform. The docking engine combines a seven-term empirical scoring function with an iterated local search strategy in which Monte Carlo perturbations are followed by bounded quasi-Newton minimisation using analytical gradients. Final pose selection can additionally incorporate binding-basin population and pocket-complementarity descriptors when they are informative. The web platform integrates molecular preparation, docking setup, pose ranking, 2D and 3D protein-ligand interaction analysis, comparative score and interaction heatmaps, molecular visualisation, and ADMET prediction. PARAM-DOCK was benchmarked against Vina using matched receptor and ligand PDBQT files, identical search boxes, symmetry-corrected RMSD evaluation, and identical hardware. On the 285-complex CASF-2016 core set, PARAM-DOCK achieved a Pearson correlation of 0.631 for scoring power and a mean within-target Spearman correlation of 0.579, compared with 0.604 and 0.528 for Vina. In de novo redocking of 255 complexes, PARAM-DOCK placed the top-ranked pose within 2.0 Å in 68.6% of cases and recovered a near-native pose among nine outputs in 84.3%, compared with 74.1% and 93.7% for Vina. Conditional on generating a near-native pose, PARAM-DOCK ranked it first in 81.4% of complexes versus 79.1% for Vina. These results indicate competitive scoring and ranking performance, while conformational sampling remains the main area for further improvement.

papers.title: Robust Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning Improves Joint Predicted-Potency and Drug-Likeness Yield in EGFR Molecule Generation
papers.abstract: Optimizing a molecular generator against a single activity-model estimate can reward structures for which that estimate is unreliable. We extended our published ChemBERTa–reinforcement-learning (RL) workflow for human epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) with scaffold-separated activity modeling, empirically calibrated lower scores, bounded chemistry rewards, and matched-seed evaluation. From ChEMBL 37, we curated 6,476 unique structures with Reference/unspecified biochemical EGFR IC50 measurements; 4,491, 680, and 1,305 structures were assigned to scaffold-disjoint training, calibration, and test sets. The random-forest reward model achieved a test mean absolute error of 0.610 pIC50 units and R2 = 0.615. Uniform or potency-enriched masked-language-model continuation was crossed with three RL rewards, with three seeds and 600 generation attempts per combination. The locked LCB-versus-mean-only comparison changed GNN potency-screen yield by +0.28 percentage points (95% descriptive t interval,-1.10 to +1.66) across three seed-cluster means. In the pipeline-level comparison with the published-form baseline, Robust-LCB increased the GNN joint-screen yield in all six matched blocks; averaged across the two MLM arms, the yield rose from 0.72% to 1.22%. Two structures passed the full RF–GNN consensus funnel. These results support a pipeline-level increase in joint predicted-potency and drug-like yield, while the incremental contribution of the lower-score term alone remains uncertain. These comparisons describe computational variability; activity estimates for generated molecules require biochemical testing.

papers.title: Spin-polarized low-density asymptotics of RPA-screened second-order exchange in the uniform electron gas
Operando Cross-Sectional Nanoscale Imaging of Na Anode Formation in Zero-Excess Solid-State Batteries: Coupled Phase–Stress Evolution and X-ray Beam Effects
papers.abstract: Zero-excess solid-state sodium batteries plate Na during charging, which places severe demands on the mechanical stability of the evolving anode and its interfaces. This work resolves the spatiotemporal evolution of phase formation and mechanical stresses across buried interfaces in a Na-Pb model system using a custom-built operando cell for cross-sectional X-ray nanodiffraction with a beam of 150 nm in diameter. The operando phase maps reveal that Na, Pb/NaPb3, and NaPb/Na9Pb4 phases coexist spatially during plating, contradicting the predominantly sequential pathway reported for liquid-electrolyte Na-Pb systems. The temporal evolution of the deviatoric in-plane stress reveals an increasingly compressive state within the solid-state electrolyte, concentrated near the interface and consistent with Na filling residual pores within the ceramic electrolyte, thereby creating local stress concentrations associated with dendritic growth and failure. Unexpectedly, comparison with beam-free reference cells reveals that X-ray exposure measurably suppresses Na plating, evidenced by an altered electrochemical response and substantially reduced Na and alloy formation. Suppressed phase formation at previously unexposed positions further shows that the beam-induced perturbation extends beyond the irradiated region, unlike the predominantly localized effects reported for liquid-electrolyte systems. This non-local response is consistent with radiation-induced charge generation within the ceramic electrolyte and demonstrates that X-ray exposure can directly alter the electrochemical process being probed in solid-state systems under bias.

papers.title: Layered Double Hydroxides with Interlayer Electrons Activate Strong Chemical Bonds
papers.abstract: Layered electrides are an unusual class of materials in which excess electrons occupy interlayer regions and serve as anionic, charge-balancing species. Many prototypical layered electrides are based on subnitrides and subcarbides, motivating the search for new types of host structures. Here, we use density functional theory (DFT) to characterize a class of layered electrides derived from layered double hydroxides (LDHs). Through an anion–electron exchange process, we predict that several LDH compositions can stabilize an electride state wherein significant charge is confined in the interlayer galleries. We evaluate the thermodynamic and finite-temperature stability of the LDH electrides, demonstrating that the balance between stability and interlayer charge can be controlled through partial anion exchange. DFT calculations and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations further reveal that the interlayer electrons impart unique chemical reactivity by facilitating the activation of strong chemical bonds, such as the spontaneous dissociation of Br 2 and the reduction of CO 2 to formate.

papers.title: Fast-Response Operando Mass Spectrometry Demystifies C₂ Product Formation in Cu-Catalyzed CO and CO₂ Reduction: Burst of Ethylene Isotopologues
papers.abstract: It has been a long-standing challenge in electrocatalysis to measure product formation with kinetically relevant time resolution. Here, we couple a real-time gas analyzer mass spectrometer with a modified sampling inlet to a gas diffusion electrode cell, achieving sub-second time resolution for both reactant consumption and product formation. We focus on CO 2 /CO reduction on oxide-derived Cu, motivated by the continuing interest in its reaction mechanism and its high selectivity to ethylene (C 2 H 4 ) formation. Potential step experiments for CO reduction reveal that the initial consumption of CO is fast (< 1 s), but the appearance of C 2 H 4 products can be 10 times slower, which we attribute to the time required for CO storage on the Cu surface and subsequent reconstruction into the active, C 2+ -forming, configuration. Previous studies have reported that the co-feed of 12 CO 2 / 13 CO results in the enhancement of 13 C-containing ethylene isotopologues, but the mechanism causing this remains unknown. Isotopic-labeled gas switching ( 12 CO 2 - 13 CO) experiments yield compelling evidence that 13 C species continue to exist for more than a minute at near proximity to or on the catalyst, even after the supply source has been cut off, evidenced by the significant enhancement of 13 C-containing ethylene isotopologues: pure ( 13 C 2 H 4 ) and mixed ( 13 C 12 CH 4 ), formed through a CO 2 (g)-*CO pathway. Importantly, the size of the C 1 reservoir, the amount of 13 C 12 CH 4 made when CO 2 reacts with it, and the amount of Cu + that is removed are all in the micromole range. Thus, the picture emerges that a monolayer is stripped off from the copper catalyst surface during the CO-CO 2 switch. Tracking of dynamic Cu surface insights (i.e., activation, dissolution and deactivation) provides valuable mechanistic insights for optimizing reaction conditions.

papers.title: Tailoring the Fusogenic Properties of cis-ssPalmO-phe Based Lipid Nanoparticles for mRNA Delivery
papers.abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are widely used for mRNA delivery, yet the effects of helper lipids on mixed bilayers containing redox-cleavable, self-degradable ionizable lipids remain unclear. Here, we conducted atomistic molecular dynamics simulations of bilayers formed from self-degradable lipid cis-ssPalmO-phe, examining 20 compositions with variations in helper-lipid headgroup (PC or PE), acyl chain length (C14-C24), and unsaturation, establishing structure-property relationships governing fusogenicity. We found that 40 mol% DOPC is optimal, with bilayer thickness of 4.60 nm and a diffusion rate of 0.37 ×10−7 cm2 s−1, balancing rigidity and dynamics for effective encapsulation and endosomal escape. PC bilayers are thinner (4.50 to 5.39 nm), more fluid, negatively charged (-0.21 to-2.59 V), enhancing stability and circulation. In contrast, PE bilayers are thicker (4.96 to 5.75 nm), denser, positively charged (up to +1.42 V), promoting curvature for endosomal fusion and cargo release. Higher unsaturation increases diffusion but decreases bilayer order, while saturated long-chain lipids maximize packing and binding energy indicating stability (up to-59.37 kcal mol−1). Tilt-angle analysis shows PC and PE adopt similar orientations and radial distribution functions confirm no clustering in saturated systems. These findings connect lipid chemistry to bilayer structure, offering design insights for degradable LNPs for mRNA and oligonucleotide therapies.

papers.title: Facet Selective Adsorption and Mobility of Anthracene Based Nanocars on Gold Surfaces
papers.abstract: Atomistic molecular dynamics simulations of anthracene-based nanocars (ANTH-R; R= H, Me, Cl) on Au(100) and Au(111) facets in explicit water, investigating the combined effects of facet crystallography, substituent chemistry, and solvation previously unexplored. Binding free energies reveal stronger adsorption on Au(111): ANTH-Me > ANTH-Cl > ANTH-H, with diffusion suppressed upto 100 fold on Au(111). Substituent chemistry influences adsorption geometry and create varied transport regimes providing design principles for nanocar motion under realistic conditions.

papers.title: Unit-Cell Molecular Dynamics Framework for Cross-Linked Hydrogels: Linking Cross-Link Density, Hydration Shells, and Swelling
papers.abstract: Rational design of polyacrylamide (PAAm) hydrogels involves linking local amide–water interactions to macroscopic properties. This study combines molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of “unit-cell” PAAm segments with experimental data to explore how the acrylamide (Ac) to N,N′ methylenebisacrylamide (BAc) molar ratio affects network structure and water dynamics. By modeling PAAm chains at ratios from 4:1 to 7:1, we reframe a covalently cross-linked network using a non-covalently self-assembling unitcell analogy, bridging oligomer-proxy and supramolecular modeling paradigms. Validating our findings against gravimetric swelling, FTIR, SEM, and oscillatory rheology data, we identify a two-stage assembly mechanism. Initially, amide groups undergo intrasegment electrostatic pre-organization, followed by inter-segment hydrogen-bonding.

papers.title: Explainable ML force-field for evaluating protein–ligand binding energy using SO3LR
papers.abstract: Accurate estimation of protein–ligand binding affinities remains central to structure-based drug design. Classical force fields neglect important quantum-mechanical effects, while quantum mechanical and semi-empirical methods remain impractical for large biomolecular systems. Machine-learned force fields (MLFFs) offer an alternative, but their performance may be inflated by training on protein–ligand complexes. Here, we introduce SO3LR-SF, a physics-based scoring function built on the pretrained SO3LR MLFF, combining an equivariant message-passing network for semi-local interactions with physically motivated terms for short-range repulsion, electrostatics, and long-range dispersion. Built on an MLFF that was not trained on protein–ligand complexes, SO3LR-SF provides a stringent test of transferability. On PLA15 (15 active-site models), SO3LR-SF attains a relative interaction error of 5.8% against DLPNO-CCSD(T) references, the lowest of all tested methods. On the FEP benchmark (8 targets, 264 ligands), SO3LR-SF achieves an average Spearman correlation of 0.51, on par with the best semi-empirical quantum-mechanical method tested (0.47, GFN-FF) and with MMGBSA (0.44), and surpassing Glide (0.27). On the Wang dataset (8 targets, 199 ligands), it reaches 0.51, approaching the 0.60 average of molecular dynamics-based free-energy methods at a fraction of their cost. Each complex is scored in 1–10 seconds on 12 CPU cores, an 80- to 300-fold speedup over comparable MLFFs. An 8 Å trimming protocol reduces runtime threefold without loss of accuracy, and a restrained geometry optimization recovers ranking accuracy for targets with strained input structures. A multi-level explainability framework adds energy decomposition, per-atom energy contributions reported either for ligand or as 2D protein–ligand interaction maps, and 3D binding site visualization. We identified two pocket descriptors that flag applicability before scoring, e.g. polar solvent accessible surface area (SASA) ratio correlating strongly (r = 0.81) with performance. Together, SO3LR-SF presents a fast, interpretable, and competitive scoring function for drug discovery that requires no domain-specific training data.

papers.title: Physical Metallurgy of Lithium and Sodium and its Role in Electrochemical Stability of Solid-State Battery Anodes
papers.abstract: Alkali metal negative electrodes in solid-state batteries (SSBs) undergo mechanical deformation during cycling, for which an understanding of their physical metallurgy is critical. Here, we study the link between microstructure and plastic deformation in lithium and sodium. Grain size is controlled through deformation processing, and etching methods are developed to reveal grain boundaries, subgrain boundaries, and dislocation structures. Hall-Petch strengthening with decreasing grain size occurs in both metals. Creep rate in lithium is grain-size-independent above the subgrain size, but increases at small grain sizes where diffusional creep dominates. Oxide dispersion-strengthened behavior is observed in Li. At length scales below the subgrain size, strength increases and creep rates decrease due to dislocation starvation. Solid-state electrochemical cell tests in which lithium of differing foil thickness is stripped under pressure validates length-scale effects. Overall, this work provides a physical metallurgy framework for alkali metal deformation and offers design principles for advanced SSBs.

papers.title: Decoding Membrane Biophysics for Nucleic Acid Delivery: Bridging Bilayer Simulations and Lipid Nanoparticle Functionality
papers.abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are a proven platform for delivering nucleic acids, evidenced by the approvals of patisiran and COVID-19 mRNA vaccines. However, the molecular mechanisms behind lipid organization, cargo encapsulation, and intracellular release remain partially understood. This review links molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of lipid bilayers to functional LNP systems through a three-level framework. (i) Structural observables: area per lipid, bilayer thickness, intrinsic curvature. (ii) Dynamic and mechanical properties: bending modulus (Kc), deuterium order parameter (SCD), lateral diffusion coefficient (DL), potential of mean force (PMF). (iii) Functional delivery outcomes: endosomal escape efficiency, RNA encapsulation, PEG shedding kinetics, cytosolic cargo release. We assess various MD frameworks, including all-atom, classical coarse-grained, and machine learning-based methods, evaluating their accuracy across the scale frontier. The pH-responsive behavior of ionizable lipids is linked to curvature stress, driving transitions from lamellar to inverted hexagonal (HII) phases, crucial for endosomal escape. We also analyze how cholesterol, helper phospholipids, and PEGylated lipids modify membrane mechanics and aid in cargo release. We highlight current limitations like fixed-protonation force fields and inadequate parameterization for new ionizable lipids. Future directions include constant-pH

papers.title: Multigram Synthesis of Heterabicyclo[4.1.1]octanes: Conformationally Restricted Azepane Analogs for Drug Discovery
papers.abstract: A convenient and scalable synthetic approach enabling multigram access to three heterabicyclo[4.1.1]octane families – 2-azabicyclo[4.1.1]octane, 2,5-diazabicyclo[4.1.1]octane, and 2-oxa-5-azabicyclo[4.1.1]octane – is described. Starting f rom readily available cis -1,3-disubstituted cyclobutanes, the target scaf folds were obtained by the common lactamization – amide reduction strategy, providing access to the (mono)protected (di)amines as ready-to-use building blocks. Representative members were characterized by single-crystal X-ray diffraction studies, and basicity (p K a ) and lipophilicity (Log P ) were determined for selected compounds. These rigid f rameworks can be considered as saturated analogs of the azepane, 1,4-diazepane, and 1,4-oxazepane rings.

papers.title: Diffusion-Model-Guided Adaptive Sampling of Rare Conformational States in Adenylate Kinase
papers.abstract: Efficiently exploring the rare conformational states of biomolecules remains a central challenge in molecular dynamics simulation. Here we show, using adenylate kinase as a methodological testbed, that the static structural scores conventionally used to prioritize diffusion-modelgenerated candidates have essentially no power to predict which candidates actually reach a kinetically rare state upon subsequent simulation (AUC = 0.500). Motivated by this finding, we introduce two adaptive strategies — direct PCA-distance targeting and replication of confirmed-hit structures — that achieve significantly higher rare-state hit rates and dwell times than extended conventional molecular dynamics or random-initialization sampling under matched computational budgets, while also enabling, for the first time, statistically stable estimation of rare-macrostate populations. These results show that structural novelty and kinetically meaningful entry into a rare state are not the same property, providing concrete design guidance for generative-model-driven adaptive sampling in other biomolecular systems.

papers.title: A simple demonstration of the importance of purity in nanotechnology with the example of rapid syntheses of gold nanoparticles in water
papers.abstract: A simple and visual demonstration of the importance of purity and the impact of impurities in nanotechnology is described. Stable colloidal gold nanoparticles are simply obtained at room temperature in seconds, adding NaBH4 to HAuCl4 in water without the need for other chemicals. By adjusting the conductivity of the water used, for example by using high purity water, tap water or mixtures of the two in different ratios, the size and stability of the nanoparticles is easily tuned. Size control is easily assessed by the color of the colloids obtained and/or by UV-vis spectroscopy. This undergraduate level demonstration suitable for a wide audience requires only very simple equipment and can be broadly implemented to illustrate the importance of controlled conditions in nanotechnology, raise awareness on the impact of impurities, but also show how to leverage on negative results to turn a drawback into a benefit. Additionally, the concept and the experimental approach proposed integrate well in other pedagogical activities and are a solid foundation to link nanotechnology to other important topics in the education of the chemical sciences.

papers.title: Tandem mass spectrometric analysis of interfacial lipid alkyl chains selectively modified via reactive ion deposition
papers.abstract: The molecular structures of lipids, including branching, double bonds and substitution within the hydrophobic chains, are key aspects in research fields such as biomarkers and signaling, and determine cell membrane properties. Although mass spectrometry has become the dominant method for lipidomics, determining fatty acid chain structures using widely available methods (MSn via CID) remains challenging. In this study, we present reactive ion deposition as a method for chemically modifying interfacial lipids in thin layers. Highly reactive [B12I11]− anions are mass-selected and deposited onto layers containing various fatty acids, phosphatidylserines, phosphatidylcholines and triacylglycerides. Using isotope-labelled compounds, we observed that [B12I11]− selectively binds to the terminal methyl groups of fatty acid hydrophobic n-alkyl chains (≥95%). The molecular structure of the lipid remains intact during covalent binding of the reactive ion on the surface, effectively charge-tagging the lipid at the alkyl chain. Therefore, ESI-MS analysis of the interfacially active layer components is enabled. Collision-induced dissociation of the anionic reaction products reveals structural information about the lipid via MSn spectra regarding both head group and fatty acid chain structure (i.e., branching, double bonds and substituent positions). This method enables not only analysis of lipids molecular structures, but also reveals information about the interfacial composition and molecular orientation of complex samples due to the binding of molecular groups located at the interface of the probed layer.

papers.title: Automated Symbolic Derivation Enables Scalable Ensemble DFT for Strongly Correlated Molecules and Materials
papers.abstract: Strong electron correlation governs the chemistry of bond breaking, polyradicals, and excited states, yet accurately describing it requires computational methods whose cost increases steeply with system size. We present a scalable ensemble density functional theory (eDFT) methodology that extends accurate treatment of strong correlation to molecular systems of realistic size at standard Kohn-Sham DFT cost. Automated derivation of the method’s working equations and a data-driven acceleration scheme enable linear scaling with active-space size while retaining multiconfigurational accuracy. Applied to systems inaccessible to standard Kohn-Sham DFT methods, such as multiple bond dissociation, open-shell polyradicals, and a recently synthesized magnetic quantum material, the framework reproduces experimental magnetic gaps and near-exact wavefunction benchmarks using active spaces up to ten electrons in ten orbitals, thus removing a long-standing barrier to routine simulation of strongly correlated matter.

papers.title: Operando Investigation of the Lithiation Mechanism in CsPbCl3 Perovskite
papers.abstract: Metal halide perovskites offer a structurally responsive platform for lithium-ion battery components, however the interplay between structural transformation and electrochemical functionality remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the lithiation mechanism in all-inorganic CsPbCl3 perovskite as a model system for resolving electrochemically driven phase reconstruction relevant to artificial solid electrolyte interphase concepts. Operando X-ray diffraction combined with electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, reveals that lithiation proceeds via a multistep pathway initiated by irreversible perovskite decomposition, resulting in formation of metallic Pb and mixed Cs–Li–Cl phases. Subsequently, reversible alloying reactions during the first cycle leads to the emergence of Li–Pb intermetallic compounds including LiPb and Li8Pb3. The evolution of diffraction features correlates with pronounced changes in the impedance response, revealing a transition from kinetically hindered conversion to more facile charge-transfer and diffusion-associated processes during alloying. Notably, no reconstruction of the perovskite framework is observed upon delithiation, confirming a conversion–alloying mechanism as the dominant charge-storage pathway. The in situ formation of Cs–Li–Cl phases coincides with marked changes in charge-transfer and diffusion-associated resistances, suggesting that the electrochemically generated chloride-rich products may contribute to the interfacial response of the reconstructed electrode. These results elucidate the lithium storage mechanism in halide perovskite-derived materials and highlight the role of decomposition-driven phase evolution in governing electrochemical performance.

papers.title: Strongly bound excitons limit the photocatalytic efficiency of carbon nitride by hindering free charge carrier generation
A simple visual tool to illustrate the relationship between transcript and protein specificity in human organs
papers.abstract: Today a large amount of high depth quantitative proteomic information exists for nearly every human tissue. Despite this wealth of information simple tools for visualizing protein distribution in the human body are somehow lacking. Due to the challenges in accessing protein measurements directly biologists commonly use accessible web portals which provide RNA transcript read counts, which end up being used as a proxy for protein data. This is unfortunate because it is well established that the correlation between transcript counts and protein concentration in mammalian material is low. This is, however, a relatively vague concept that is difficult to both envision and to explain in the context of the central dogma. One way to rectify this problem would be by making protein quantification data as simple and accessible as RNA read count data. To illustrate how a large amount of proteomic data can be easily visualized, I have constructed an example lightweight HTML page that is small enough to be attached to email even when containing deep proteomic analysis of 29 healthy human tissues. The value of simple proteomic data representation is further demonstrated by overlaying proteins predicted to be organ specific from transcriptomic data. Displayed together, it is possible to rapidly determine which transcript measurements can be trusted to be predictive of protein specificity. All data, code and step-by-step analyses are made available in the Supporting Information and a web instance of the resulting tool comparing two gold standard datasets is hosted at: https://www.orsburnlab.org/protein-specificity.

papers.title: Aqueous-rich flow intensification for enzymatic transesterification of rose geranium oil in a coiled flow inverter microreactor
papers.abstract: Enzyme-assisted valorisation of crude floral oils into high-value fragrance esters is constrained by mass-transfer limitations and limited productivity in conventional batch reactors. Rose geranium oil, a naturally complex and terpene-rich multicomponent feedstock containing geraniol, citronellol and numerous other volatile constituents, was selected to investigate continuous enzymatic transesterification directly from a crude floral oil. Using Pseudomonas fluorescens lipase (PFL), geraniol and citronellol were selectively transesterified within the multicomponent oil, without prior isolation of these constituents. A process-intensified strategy was developed using a coiled flow inverter (CFI) microreactor. Aqueous-rich biphasic slug flow at an aqueous-to-organic ratio of 9:1, providing a specific interfacial area of 2319 m 2 m -3 , increased the apparent volumetric mass-transfer coefficient (kLa) by approximately 5-fold for geraniol and 7-fold for citronellol relative to batch operation. At 60 °C and a residence time of 5 min, the CFI achieved 99 % geraniol and 93 % citronellol conversion at 0.2 M rose geranium oil, while maintaining 91 % and 71 % conversion, respectively, at 1.4 M. Increasing the residence time to 7 min increased citronellol conversion at 1.4 M to 95 %. At 1.4 M, the 2 mL CFI provided calculated productivities of approximately 572 g day -1 for geranyl ester and 422 g day -1 for citronellyl ester, assuming continuous operation for 24 h. These results establish aqueous-rich segmented flow as an effective strategy for intensifying selective enzymatic transesterification within a compositionally complex terpene feedstock. The combination of selective conversion, enhanced interphase mass transfer and high calculated productivity provides a basis for the continuous valorisation of rose geranium oil and other complex floral oils into high-value fragrance esters.

papers.title: Electrolyte-Dependent Electrochemical Performance of a Lead-Free Semiconducting Co(II)-Halide Hybrid for Aqueous Supercapacitors
papers.abstract: Developing affordable and stable electrode materials is crucial for advancing sustainable supercapacitor technologies. In this study, a lead-free Co(II)-halide hybrid material (CoTEA) was synthesized via slow evaporation and evaluated as an electrode for aqueous electrochemical energy storage. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction showed a zero-dimensional structure consisting of isolated tetrahedral units separated by tetraethylammonium cations. Morphological and spectroscopic analyses confirmed the crystalline nature and the Co(II) oxidation state of the material. Optical measurements indicated semiconducting behavior with a band gap of 3.64 eV. The electrochemical response of CoTEA was highly dependent on the electrolyte used. At 5 mV s-1, specific capacitances of 5.01, 22.24, and 21.37 F g-1 were recorded in 1 M H2SO4, 0.5 M Na2SO4, and 6 M KOH, respectively. While Na2SO4 yielded the highest capacitance at the lowest scan rate, KOH demonstrated better rate performance and lower charge-transfer resistance, suggesting more efficient interfacial kinetics. In 6 M KOH, CoTEA achieved a GCD-specific capacitance of 21.41 F g-1 at 0.5 A g-1 and maintained about 85% of its initial capacitance after 3000 cycles. These results underscore the significant impact of electrolyte composition on the charge-storage behavior of CoTEA and present it as a promising, tunable material for aqueous supercapacitor applications.strong influence of electrolyte composition on the charge-storage behavior of CoTEA and highlight it as a promising tunable material for aqueous supercapacitor applications.

papers.title: Condition-Aware and Leakage-Resistant Machine Learning of Short-Peptide Self-Assembly Across Bulk State and Supramolecular Morphology
papers.abstract: Short-peptide self-assembly is governed jointly by molecular structure and experimental environment, yet many predictive workflows treat condition-specific observations as independent samples. Here, a source-audited dataset was reconstructed from PeptideMiner and SAPdb to evaluate bulk-state and supramolecular-morphology prediction under leakage-resistant validation. Peptide identity was defined from sequence,terminal modifications,non-terminal modifications,peptide-system annotations,and conjugate partners; experimental descriptors included concentration, pH, temperature, thermal history, incubation, and explicit solvent composition. A conventional random row split was shown to be strongly non-independent: 87.3% of test molecular identities had already appeared in training and 94.2% of test rows came from molecules represented in training.Accordingly,all primary claims were based on molecular-identity-grouped validation and permanently sealed holdouts containing previously unseen molecular systems. For hydrogel versus non-gel prediction, a tuned Random Forest achieved ROCAUC 0.977, PR-AUC 0.882, balanced accuracy 0.945, F1 0.880, and MCC 0.836 on 115 conditions from 20 unseen molecular identities. Solvent identity and composition formed the dominant transferable feature block,but analyses restricted to fully aqueous conditions demonstrated that non-solvent variables,particularly concentration,pH,temperature,and related processing descriptors,retained substantial predictive information. A harder three-class non-gel/hydrogel/organogel task yielded macro ROC-AUC 0.783 and MCC 0.247 on unseen molecules, with organic non-gelling conditions constituting the dominant error mode. For broad morphology, an Extra Trees classifier achieved macro ROC-AUC 0.980, macro PR-AUC 0.925, and MCC 0.665 on 59 conditions from 14 unseen molecular identities, although spherical/particulate morphology remained comparatively difficult.Fine-grained morphology prediction was not forced when independent class support proved insufficient for stable molecule grouped cross-validation. These results establish that reliable learning of short-peptide self-assembly requires explicit representation of experimental environment, source-level curation, and validation at the level of independent molecular systems rather than condition rows.

papers.title: Argon Coordination to the 3d Transition-Metal Monohalides: A Systematic Study of σ-Acceptor Accessibility in Ar–MX (M = Sc–Cu; X = F, Cl, Br)
papers.abstract: Argon is generally regarded as chemically inert, yet direct Ar–metal coordination has been established for several late transition-metal complexes. Here, we systematically investigate Ar coordination across the 3d transition-metal monofluorides, MF (M = Sc–Cu), and subsequently extend the analysis to the corresponding chlorides and bromides. Density functional theory, population analysis, energy decomposition, and multireference calculations reveal a pronounced and nonmonotonic variation in Ar-binding propensity across the MF series. Ar binding is characterized by Ar 3pσ donation into a metal-centered σ-acceptor manifold of mixed 4s and 3dz2 character. In predominantly single-reference systems, the metal 4s population of bare MF provides a simple descriptor of the accessibility of this manifold: low 4s occupation is generally associated with Ar coordination, whereas high 4s occupation is associated with dissociation. Consistent with this picture, single-reference calculations give shortrange Ar-bound minima for MnF and FeF on lower-spin DFT surfaces with reduced 4s occupation, although these solutions are SCF-unstable and require multireference confirmation. The same metaldependent trend is largely retained for the chlorides and bromides, with additional modulation by the M–X framework. Sc halides mark the multireference limit of the simple 4s-based description.

papers.title: Software Tool for Automated Kinetic Tracking in Mass Spectrometry Data
papers.abstract: Time-resolved mass spectrometry produces large datasets that are challenging to organize and screen for kinetic trends. We present an open-source software tool designed for the exploratory screening and visualization of time-dependent variations in extensive series of mzML measurements. Rather than focusing on automated compound identification, the software's main purpose is to highlight and rank the signals that undergo the most significant changes over time. The software streamlines chronological file organization, replicate aggregation, and trend ranking. To demonstrate its utility, the tool was used to monitor the reaction between aniline and 1-iodobutane. Crucially, the software not only correctly identified the expected mono- and dibutyl derivatives of aniline, but it also revealed the unexpected presence of aniline dimers (m/z 183 and 185), and trimer (m/z 274), and their corresponding butylated products. The automated ranking perfectly captured the consecutive reaction profiles, showing the initial accumulation of monobutyl intermediates and their subsequent consumption into dibutyl derivatives. Without this unbiased screening, these dimeric and trimeric pathways could have been easily overlooked. Ultimately, this tool drastically reduces manual data processing while guiding researchers directly to the most chemically interesting variations.

papers.title: Reliable Structure-Processing-Performance Learning in Organic Photovoltaics: Chemical Generalization, Processing-Aware Prediction and Uncertainty under Domain Shift
papers.abstract: Machine-learning models for organic photovoltaics (OPVs) can achieve strong performance under random train-test splits, but such evaluation may overstate prospective generalization when literaturederived datasets contain repeated publications and material systems. Here, two complementary OPV benchmarks were constructed to separate interpolation from chemical extrapolation: a provenanceclean OPV-DB cohort containing 21,590 experimentally reported devices and a processing-rich Wen-Zhang-Ma cohort containing 994 unique physical processing conditions. Random, publication-heldout, donor-acceptor (D:A)-pair-held-out, acceptor-held-out, and donor-held-out validation regimes were compared, together with structure-only, processing-only, and combined structure-processing representations. Extra Trees performance on OPV-DB declined from R2 = 0.813 under random validation to R2 = 0.362 under donor holdout. In the processing-rich benchmark, adding processing information reduced MAE by 19.5% under random validation but by only 1.0-2.4% under chemically grouped validation. This effect was strongly associated with material-system familiarity: processing reduced MAE by 27.1% for test records whose D:A pair was represented in training, compared with 1.8% for completely unseen pairs. Ensemble dispersion was useful for ranking errors under random validation (Spearman rho = 0.462) but lost reliability under donor holdout (rho = 0.047), where the most uncertain 20% of predictions captured only 16.1% of the largest errors. A cross-dataset transfer audit further showed that a common unmodified RDKit representation covered 73.54% of the processing benchmark and only 38.02% of records with PCE >= 15%, creating substantial chemicalselection bias. These results show that validation design is central to claims of OPV model reliability, that processing information primarily refines predictions within familiar chemistry, and that both uncertainty estimation and transfer benchmarking require explicit domain-shift and representation audits.

Novel green K-based Metal-Organic Framework with high proton conductivity
papers.abstract: Despite growing interest in metal-organic frameworks (MOFs for protonconductivity applications, monovalent-cation-based MOFs remain comparatively underexplored due to the weaker coordination interactions typically associated with these systems. In this work, we report GR-MOF-28, a novel potassium-based naphthalene tetracarboxylate framework synthesized under mild aqueous conditions at room temperature. Structurally, GR-MOF-28 consists of K2O10 dioctahedra interconnected through tetracarboxylate ligands and coordinated water molecules, generating a confined hydrogen-bond network along the crystallographic channels. The material exhibits proton conductivity values up to 4.3·10-2 S·cm-1 under high relative humidity conditions, placing it among the highest-performing K-based MOFs reported to date. Combined electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and molecular simulations support a water-mediated Grotthusstype proton transport mechanism through the confined hydrogen-bond network. In addition, GR-MOF-28 can be incorporated into a conductive polymer matrix without loss of proton transport properties. These results highlight the potential of underexplored K-based coordination frameworks as proton-conducting materials.

papers.title: Interpretable Machine Learning Disentangles Pore Confinement Across Multiple Zr-MOF CO2 Capture Targets
papers.abstract: Pore confinement in zirconium-based metal–organic frameworks (Zr-MOFs) is often described using the cage–window ratio (ΓCW), the largest cavity diameter divided by the pore-limiting diameter (Df), yet whether this composite coordinate carries information beyond Df alone remains unclear. We modeled CO2 uptake, heat of adsorption (HoA), and CO2/N2 selectivity for 239 Zr-containing MOFs at two pressures relevant to vacuum-swing adsorption using structure-grouped machine learning with SHAP interpretation, reaching test R2 values of 0.77–0.88. Although ΓCW correlated positively with all three targets, controlling for Df weakened these associations and reversed their sign, while the reciprocal analysis left the Df associations largely unchanged and a difference-based formulation produced no significant association. Df played different roles across the three targets, indicating that the apparent confinement effect mainly reflects the limiting aperture rather than relative cage–window architecture.
